The system combines front-of-house and back-of-house operations, table and floor-plan management, menu and inventory tools, real-time analytics and multi-location reporting, and a mobile manager app, with an in-house payment processor (EPX). Originally a 500 Global / 500 Startups portfolio company, SALIDO was acquired by First Data and is now backed by North American Bancard (NAB). No public developer API or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: SEI Investments
providers.description: SEI Investments Company (NASDAQ: SEIC) is a publicly traded financial services and technology provider founded in 1968 and headquartered in Oaks, Pennsylvania. SEI delivers end-to-end technology, operations, and asset management solutions to asset managers, banks and wealth managers, financial advisors, and institutional investors. Marquee platforms include the SEI Wealth Platform (front-to-back wealth management technology and outsourced operations), SEI Data Cloud (managed near-real-time data platform), SEI Sphere (managed IT, cybersecurity, cloud, and network operations), and SEI Novus (institutional portfolio analytics). SEI does not run a public developer portal — partner and client integrations are delivered through contractual onboarding to the SEI Wealth Platform, SEI Connect advisor channels, and managed-service engagements rather than self-serve OpenAPI or SDK distribution.

providers.name: Smol
providers.description: Smol is a UK-based direct-to-consumer home-care brand founded in 2018 by Paula Quazi and Nick Green, delivering concentrated, plant-based, cruelty-free cleaning products — laundry capsules, dishwasher tablets, fabric conditioner, surface sprays and personal-care bars — on a flexible subscription that ships refills through the letterbox. The company positions itself as a sustainability challenger to legacy home-care brands, emphasizing reduced plastic, carbon and chemical load, and became a certified B Corporation in July 2022. Backed by Balderton Capital and GV, Smol operates a consumer e-commerce and subscription business; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer program.

providers.name: Speedata
providers.description: Speedata is a Tel Aviv-based semiconductor company that builds the APU (Analytics Processing Unit), a processor purpose-built for accelerating Apache Spark SQL, batch ETL and AI data-preparation workloads rather than graphics or model training. The APU ships as the C200 PCIe Gen5 accelerator card powered by the company's Callisto ASIC, paired with a software layer called Dash that plugs into the Spark Catalyst optimizer and offloads compute-intensive stages to the card with no application code changes. Founded in 2019 by researchers in multi-threaded coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture, the company raised a $44M Series B in June 2025 (total funding ~$114M) from Walden Catalyst Ventures, 83North and Koch Disruptive. Speedata publishes no public web API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surface is a Spark plugin JAR distributed under an early-access program, plus a free browser/CLI Workload Analyzer for estimating acceleration on a customer's own Spark workloads.

providers.name: StanCorp Financial Group
providers.description: StanCorp Financial Group, Inc. (doing business as The Standard) is an insurance and financial services company headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance Company since 2016. Founded in 1906, The Standard offers group and individual disability insurance, group life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance, group dental and group vision insurance, absence management services, retirement plans, individual annuities, and commercial mortgage loan origination. The Standard does not offer a public developer API. Employer and benefits administrator integrations are managed through EDI and proprietary data exchange channels.

providers.name: Starship Technologies
providers.description: Starship Technologies is an autonomous last-mile delivery company that operates a global fleet of self-driving, sidewalk-going delivery robots. Founded in 2014 by Skype co-founders Ahti Heinla and Janus Friis, the company runs commercial robot delivery on university campuses, in residential neighborhoods, on industrial sites and for grocery and restaurant partners across the United States, the United Kingdom, Estonia, Finland, Germany and Denmark, and has completed more than 10 million autonomous deliveries. Its commercial product, Delivery by Starship, is a delivery-as-a-service offering that partners integrate into their own ordering apps: Starship states that its APIs let a partner create delivery jobs, load robots, obtain status updates and handle delivery cancellations, backed by a developer toolkit, documentation, ready-made components and support. That developer surface is not published to the open web — Starship provides it to partners after a commercial conversation via business@starship.co, so no public specification, reference or portal exists to profile.

providers.name: Streamlane
providers.description: Streamlane provides an agentic parcel spend management platform for modern operators, helping retailers and 3PLs unify shipping data, automate invoice audits, and optimize network decisions. Their solution reduces parcel spend by 15‑20% through rate benchmarking, network modeling, and contract negotiation insights.

providers.name: SXD
providers.description: SXD is a New York-based design-technology company founded in 2022 that uses patented artificial intelligence to generate zero-waste apparel patterns for the fashion industry. Its SXD AI platform transforms a sketch or design concept into production-ready patterns that eliminate fabric waste before the first cut, and the company reports up to 69% material savings across more than 35 brand and manufacturing partners. SXD has been recognized with the Global Change Award and a top prize at the SXSW Pitch competition, and is backed by Initialized Capital. SXD does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: TaxNexus
providers.description: TaxNexus is a cannabis tax compliance REST API and financial technology service that automates calculation of state, county, and local cannabis excise taxes across supported jurisdictions including California and Oregon. Cannabis POS and ERP software developers can integrate with the TaxNexus API to calculate excise taxes, track and store tax data, and file monthly cannabis tax returns. The platform serves cannabis businesses, software makers, and accountants seeking to automate real-world cannabis tax compliance problems for recreational and medical cannabis taxpayers.

providers.name: The Meta
providers.description: The Meta is the gaming-performance company behind KovaaK's Aim Trainer (formerly "Kovaak 2.0: The Meta"), a PC esports training platform distributed on Steam that pairs guided, skill-specific training modules with Kovaak's Sandbox aim trainer and its library of 2,600+ user-generated scenarios. The platform lets FPS players measure, diagnose, and improve their mechanical aim and in-game habits, feeding back insights on weaknesses so players can target their practice. Founded by Duncan Haberly, Jay Brown, and Chris Olson and backed by Canaan (Beta Fund), Village Global, Courtside VC, betaworks, GFR, and Akatsuki Entertainment Technology (AET Fund). The Meta operates a consumer game product, a community wiki, and a Discord community; it does not currently publish a public first-party developer API.

providers.name: This Is L.
providers.description: This Is L. (L. Inc.) is a personal-care company making certified-organic cotton menstrual products — tampons, pads, and liners — sold through major U.S. retailers including Target, Walmart, Walgreens, CVS, and Kroger as well as direct-to-consumer at thisisl.com. Founded as a social enterprise and public-benefit corporation with a one-for-one give-back model, L. was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is now a Procter & Gamble brand (its legal, privacy, and vulnerability-disclosure surfaces resolve to pg.com). This is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce business with no public developer API, SDK, or technology platform; enrichment captured its identity, web link-properties, and security posture.

providers.name: Tone
providers.description: Tone is a full-stack royalty management platform for music rights owners — independent labels, distributors, and royalty teams. It centralizes royalty accounting, income tracking, and contract management, then pays artists directly through integrated global payouts. The platform processes large royalty periods quickly, provides near-real-time sales intelligence with timeline views and customizable charts, models deal structures with a contract simulator (reserves, deductions, escalations), automatically associates costs with the applicable royalty periods, and gives artists transparent dashboards into their earnings. In-app artist payouts are powered by Airwallex for secure multi-currency international payments, letting labels pay artists and partners worldwide without juggling separate banking tools. Tone is backed by QED Investors. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC-portfolio lead; Tone is a SaaS application and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Umami Cart
providers.description: Umami Cart is an online platform offering authentic Asian recipes, ingredient guides, and cooking techniques. It covers Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, Indian, Filipino, Malaysian and more cuisines, providing detailed guides, step‑by‑step recipes, and culinary tips tested in a real home kitchen. The site also features a blog, cooking methods, and a marketplace for Asian food products, aiming to explore and celebrate the flavors of Asia for home cooks worldwide.

providers.name: Unitree Robotics
providers.description: Unitree Robotics is a Hangzhou, China-based high-performance robot manufacturer founded in 2016 by Wang Xingxing. The company is a global pioneer in the commercial quadruped (robot dog) market and has expanded into bipedal humanoid robots. Its product line includes the Go1, Go2, and Go2-W quadrupeds for consumers, education, and research; the industrial-grade B1 and B2 quadrupeds for inspection, patrol, and logistics; the H1 full-size humanoid; the G1 humanoid for research and developer experimentation; the R1 humanoid; and the Z1 robotic arm. Unitree also produces in-house components including the L1/L2 LiDAR, hand-grade actuators, and dexterous hands (Dex1-1). Unitree's developer surface is SDK-centric — there is no public REST or gRPC cloud API. Robot control happens on-device over DDS (Data Distribution Service) via the unitree_sdk2 (C++) and unitree_sdk2_python libraries, with high-level message bindings published as unitree_ros and unitree_ros2. The company maintains an active GitHub presence at github.com/unitreerobotics with 46+ public repositories covering SDKs, ROS packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab simulation environments, reinforcement learning frameworks (unitree_rl_gym, unitree_rl_lab), teleoperation tooling (xr_teleoperate, kinect_teleoperate, televuer), imitation learning (unitree_lerobot), a vision-language-action model (unifolm-vla), and a Unitree App Store template repo. Documentation lives at support.unitree.com/home/en/developer. Unitree's revenue model is direct robot hardware sales via shop.unitree.com and partner distribution; there is no metered API service tier.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Workhelix
providers.description: Workhelix is an enterprise platform for measuring and growing the return on investment of AI initiatives. Its Nucleus product connects workforce data and AI usage history to rank AI opportunities by impact, identify high-performing superusers, surface adoption gaps, and estimate time and cost savings. The company was co-founded by economists Erik Brynjolfsson (Stanford) and Andrew McAfee (MIT) with CEO James Milin and research director Daniel Rock (Wharton), is backed by Bloomberg Beta, and serves enterprise customers including Autodesk, Nasdaq, and LogicMonitor. Workhelix publishes no public API or developer program as of July 2026.

providers.name: Yuga Labs
providers.description: Yuga Labs is a leading Web3 creator and brand studio behind iconic NFT collections such as Bored Ape Yacht Club, Mutant Ape Yacht Club, and Otherside. Founded by a group of friends, the company builds cultural experiences, community-driven products, and the ApeCoin ecosystem. It operates at the intersection of blockchain, gaming, and digital art, fostering a vibrant community and expanding the possibilities of on‑chain ownership and storytelling.

providers.name: Yummly
providers.description: Yummly is a recipe and food discovery platform (yummly.com) offering semantic and visual recipe search, personalized recommendations, shopping lists, and guided cooking. Founded in 2009 (Redwood City, CA), Yummly was acquired by Whirlpool Corporation in May 2017 and operated as a wholly owned subsidiary tied to Whirlpool's smart-kitchen strategy. Yummly historically ran a well-known public Recipe API (developer.yummly.com) exposing recipe search, recipe details, and metadata endpoints. That developer program was DEPRECATED - it stopped accepting new signups and was wound down (commonly cited end date of September 30, 2019), and the developer.yummly.com developer portal and api.yummly.com endpoints are no longer available. There is no public Yummly developer API accepting new registrations as of this cataloging (2026-07-03); the APIs below are documented as historical / modeled for archival and migration reference only.

providers.name: Zipcar
providers.description: Zipcar is a Boston, Massachusetts-based car sharing service operating in more than 500 cities across North America and Europe, including major US metros (Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York, Philadelphia, Portland, San Francisco, Seattle, Washington DC) and Canadian cities (Toronto, Hamilton, the Golden Horseshoe). Members reserve vehicles by the hour or day through the Zipcar mobile app, unlock cars with their phone, and pay per usage with gas, EV charging, standard damage protection insurance, and professional maintenance included. Zipcar serves consumer members, universities (Zipcar for Universities), and businesses (Zipcar for Business) with weekday fleet programs. Zipcar is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Avis Budget Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: CAR), which acquired the company in March 2013 for approximately $500 million. Zipcar exposes a REST-based Partner API at api.zipcar.com/partner-api, documented at owa.zipcar.com/documentation, that returns JSON for Location List and Location Detail resources (vehicles available at a lat/long); access is gated and granted on request via developerportal@zipcar.com — there is no public OpenAPI spec, SDK, or self-service developer signup. Zipcar also operates a public GitHub organization (github.com/Zipcar) hosting internal DevOps tooling (Concourse resources, Ansible helpers, BOSH helpers, monitoring agents) rather than client-facing API artifacts.

providers.name: Aante
providers.description: Aante (爱安特) is a Chinese factory-automation (FA) parts distributor and one-stop industrial e-commerce procurement platform, operated by Aante (Changzhou) Precision Machinery Co., Ltd. (爱安特（常州）精密机械有限公司) and headquartered in Changzhou, Jiangsu. Established in 2002 as the successor to Sandi Automation, it sells linear motion, transmission, standard, machined, framing, motion-unit, electrical and pneumatic components across 96 product categories and roughly two million SKUs, distributing 30+ international brands including SMC and THK alongside its own Aante-branded line. It serves customers in semiconductors, new energy, 3C electronics, photovoltaics, LCD, automotive, medical and food manufacturing from three production bases and 30+ service centers, and in 2026 acquired software firm Zhuiguang Geometry to pair components with design software. The storefront at ant-fa.com is a Chinese-language Nuxt commerce site; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Adlai Nortye
providers.description: Adlai Nortye is a global clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, headquartered in Hangzhou, China with US operations in New Jersey, developing differentiated immuno-oncology and precision-targeted cancer medicines. Its pipeline covers two therapeutic areas: precision RAS pathway targeted therapies — the oral pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor AN9025 and the CEACAM5-targeting antibody-drug conjugate AN4035 built on the company's proprietary RASiCA (RAS Inhibitor Conjugated Antibody) platform — and next-generation PD-1/L1 pathway modulating immunotherapies including AN8025, a multi-functional T-cell and antigen-presenting-cell modulating fusion protein, plus the oral EP4 antagonist AN0025 (palupiprant). The company is listed on Nasdaq under the ticker ANL. Adlai Nortye publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Aella Credit
providers.description: Aella (Aella Credit) is a technology-driven microfinance bank licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), building consumer and business financial infrastructure across Africa. Its consumer app offers savings, low-interest and same-day loans, bill payments, and high-yield savings accounts, while its Fintech-as-a-Service platform exposes that infrastructure to businesses through a developer-facing API gateway. Published API capabilities include wallet-as-a- service (create and manage digital wallets with real-time balances and full ledger support), KYC/identity verification via BVN and NIN, bank-account lookup and validation, sub-accounts and pooled fund structures for platforms and marketplaces, and direct-debit recurring collections. A live Aella Merchant API is hosted at api.aellaapp.com and a merchant dashboard at merchant.aellaapp.com, though the provider does not yet publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile was seeded as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: AgriAku
providers.description: AgriAku (PT Agriaku Digital Indonesia) is a Jakarta-based agritech company founded in 2021 that digitizes the distribution of agricultural inputs - seeds, fertilizers, crop protection, nutrients and farm tools - to Indonesia's network of independent farm-supply shops (toko tani). Partner shops order from a catalog of more than 15,000 agricultural products through the AgriAku Mitra Android app, while separate vendor, seller and courier applications cover the rest of the supply chain. The company reports more than 23,390 partners across Indonesia and has raised roughly USD 46M from Alpha JWC Ventures, Go-Ventures and MDI Ventures. AgriAku operates no public developer program: every API host it runs is a private backend for its own first-party mobile and web applications.

providers.name: Alta VR
providers.description: Alta VR (legally Another Axiom LLC) is a virtual reality game studio behind Gorilla Tag, one of the most-played VR titles ever, and the newer social VR world Orion Drift. The studio builds imaginative, physics-driven multiplayer experiences centered on hand-based locomotion and social play across Meta Quest, Steam, and other VR platforms. It runs an Another Axiom Creator Program for community map-building and content creation, and publishes game code and Unity map-export tooling through its public GitHub organization. Alta VR is a portfolio company of a16z. As a VR consumer game studio it does not currently operate a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program; its developer-facing surface is limited to open-source game code, custom map tooling, and creator resources.

providers.name: AlternativeTo
providers.description: AlternativeTo is a crowdsourced software discovery platform that helps users find alternatives to software products based on user recommendations across desktop, mobile, and web applications. The platform does not currently offer a public API, but provides partner integration opportunities for software vendors.

providers.name: Avitide
providers.description: Avitide is a product line of Repligen, a bioprocessing solutions company. It focuses on downstream processing technologies and services for biopharma manufacturing, offering chromatography, filtration, and process intensification solutions.

providers.name: BARK (BarkBox)
providers.description: BARK, Inc. (operating as BarkBox) is a New York-based dog-focused consumer company founded in 2011 by Henrik Werdelin and Matt Meeker, serving over two million dogs monthly through its BarkBox and Super Chewer subscription boxes, the BARK Bright dental line, the BARK Air pet travel experience, and retail distribution. The company went public via a SPAC merger in 2021 (NYSE: BARK). BarkBox does not operate a public developer program or externally documented API portal; its engineering surface is a set of mostly-internal Ruby services and open-source libraries published under the github.com/barkbox organization (including the barkbox_client Ruby API client and cursor-pagination gems). This profile was surfaced as a Slow Ventures portfolio company and enriched with verified public identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Bechtel
providers.description: Bechtel is one of the largest privately held engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) companies in the world. Bechtel does not publish a public developer portal; technology integration is delivered through project-specific data exchanges with owners, joint-venture partners, and subcontractors, the Bechtel supplier portal, and industry-standard construction data exchange formats (IFC, COBie, CDE) over secure project-management platforms.

providers.name: Betr364d
providers.description: Betr is the world’s first real money gaming super app, offering daily fantasy, social sportsbook, social casino, and arcade experiences. Users can download the app to participate in real‑money gaming across a variety of sports and games, with high‑payout potential and a social community. The platform emphasizes responsible gaming and provides extensive help resources.

providers.name: Bilt Rewards
providers.description: Bilt Rewards (Bilt Technologies) is a fintech membership and loyalty program that lets renters and homeowners earn transferable points on rent and mortgage payments, with no fees, and redeem them for travel, everyday purchases, fitness, dining, or credit toward a future home down payment. Members also unlock benefits across 50,000+ neighborhood merchants and can use the co-branded Bilt Mastercard. Bilt operates regulated entities Bilt Payments LLC (money transmission) and Bilt Mortgages LLC (mortgage brokerage). The company is a consumer-facing app and card program; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: BioCentriq
providers.description: Made Scientific, formerly BioCentriq, is a global cell therapy contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) based in New Jersey and part of GC Corporation. It offers end‑to‑end services including process development, GMP manufacturing, aseptic fill‑finish, quality control, regulatory consulting, and workforce development, supporting autologous and allogeneic cell therapies. The company rebranded in 2025 to reflect its expanded capabilities and global reach, providing flexible partnership models for biotech innovators.

providers.name: Blaize
providers.description: Blaize (NASDAQ: BZAI) is an edge AI company headquartered in El Dorado Hills, California that builds a programmable inference platform uniting silicon and software. Its Graph Streaming Processor (GSP) powers the Pathfinder and Xplorer accelerator families — SoM, M.2, EDSFF and PCIe form factors plus the DST developer station and Blaize Inference Server — and its software layer pairs the Picasso SDK (C++, Python, OpenVX, with TensorFlow/PyTorch/ONNX import via NetDeploy) with AI Studio, a code-free environment spanning the full edge AI DataOps/DevOps/MLOps lifecycle. In April 2026 Blaize announced a planned Blaize AI Services platform that packages multimodal inference, business logic and orchestration as modular application-level APIs across vision, video, document, speech and moderation workloads. The developer surface — SDK downloads, repositories and reference material — is served from a self-hosted GitLab at software.blaize.com and requires an account, so no public machine-readable API contract is published.

providers.name: Blocto
providers.description: Blocto is a Web3 smart-contract wallet built by Portto that lets everyday users interact with decentralized applications without managing seed phrases, using a chain-agnostic account-abstraction architecture. For developers, Blocto ships a client-side integration surface — the JavaScript Blocto SDK, a Blocto-flavored Flow Client Library (FCL) fork, plus Go, Swift and Rust SDKs — to connect dApps to the Blocto wallet for authentication, transaction signing and account-proof verification across Flow, Ethereum, Solana, Aptos, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Arbitrum and Optimism. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network from its public developer documentation and GitHub organization.

providers.name: Bloomscape
providers.description: Bloomscape is a direct-to-consumer houseplant company that grows plants in its own greenhouses and ships them fully grown directly to customers' doors, bypassing traditional retail and nursery supply chains. Alongside houseplants, it sells planters, plant-care accessories, and gifting options, and backs every order with its Grow-How team of horticultural experts plus a plant guarantee. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. Bloomscape operates a consumer e-commerce storefront and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile captures its public web, support, and legal properties along with a domain-security probe.

providers.name: BNP Paribas
providers.description: BNP Paribas is a leading international banking group providing a wide range of financial services to individuals, businesses, and institutions worldwide. The company offers APIs through its CIB Developer Portal covering capital markets, payment services, securities services, and open banking integrations for corporate and institutional clients.

providers.name: Booko
providers.description: Booko is an Australian book, eBook, audiobook, DVD, music and collectibles price-comparison service operating since 2007. It aggregates new and used prices across many online retailers and regions, calculates shipping, and converts international prices to the shopper's local currency to surface the cheapest place to buy a title. Booko also offers shopping lists with bundled shipping calculations, barcode scanning, reading lists, price alerts and notifications. It is a consumer-facing comparison site rather than a retailer or a public API provider, earning referral fees from partner shops (including Amazon Associates) when shoppers buy through its links. Booko is a solo developer-run product surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company.

providers.name: Capitolis
providers.description: Capitolis is a financial technology company for the capital markets that helps banks and institutional investors optimize how capital is used across their trading portfolios. Its two flagship offerings are a Capital Marketplace that connects banks with origination capabilities to institutional providers of capital, and a Portfolio Optimization service that offsets redundant and offsetting derivatives positions to reduce capital requirements, counterparty exposure, and systemic risk. By combining technology with financial expertise, Capitolis aims to create a safer, more efficient financial system and broaden access to more diversified pools of capital. The platform is delivered as a secure, login-gated web application to regulated financial institutions rather than as a public developer API.

providers.name: Carwow
providers.description: Carwow is a UK-based online automotive marketplace that helps consumers buy, sell, lease, and finance cars without haggling or hidden fees. Buyers browse new and used car deals, compare dealer quotes, arrange leasing (including salary sacrifice and fleet through Carwow Leasey), find electric-vehicle deals, and access vehicle financing and credit brokering. Sellers get free car valuations, part-exchange, and van sales. Carwow also publishes professional car reviews and ratings, runs a large YouTube channel, and offers comparison tools, EV charging maps, a car history checker, and insurance services. Founded in London and backed by Accel, Balderton Capital, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Carwow operates across the UK and Europe. It maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source engineering tooling but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Cerene
providers.description: Cerene Cryotherapy develops and provides FDA‑cleared cryotherapy devices for the treatment of heavy menstrual bleeding and other gynecological conditions. The company offers a range of clinical solutions, training, and patient resources, targeting healthcare professionals and women seeking minimally invasive therapy. Cerene focuses on evidence‑based outcomes, safety information, and regulatory compliance, operating primarily in the United States.

providers.name: Chai
providers.description: Chai AI provides a platform for creating and deploying AI-powered characters and chatbots. Users can build, customize, and integrate conversational agents across apps, games, and services. The service offers a library of pre-built characters, tools for training, and APIs for real-time interaction, targeting developers and creators looking to add rich, interactive AI experiences.

providers.name: Charta Health
providers.description: Charta Health is a healthcare AI company (founded 2023) that provides AI-powered medical chart review and autonomous coding for provider groups, FQHCs, MSOs, health systems, and payers. Its platform streams charts in from hundreds of EHR, clearinghouse, and billing integrations, then audits every patient encounter pre-billing to generate codes, surface missed revenue and E/M leveling issues, identify HCC risk-adjustment codes with supporting documentation citations, reduce payer audit risk, and deliver data-driven provider feedback. Charta reports outcomes such as an 11% revenue uplift from scaling pre-billing review across 100% of encounters. Integrations are built per customer against the customer's EHR (e.g. athenahealth Marketplace); Charta does not publish a public self-serve developer API or portal.

providers.name: Chobani
providers.description: Chobani is an American food and beverage company founded in 2005 by Hamdi Ulukaya, best known for popularizing strained Greek yogurt in the United States and for operating what it describes as the world's largest yogurt facility in Twin Falls, Idaho. Its portfolio spans Greek yogurt, oat milk, plant-based yogurt, probiotic drinks, nutritional shakes, and — following the 2023 acquisition of La Colombe Coffee Roasters — ready-to-drink coffee. Chobani sells through retail grocery, an away-from-home foodservice channel, Chobani Cafe locations, and a direct-to-consumer shop. Chobani is a privately held consumer packaged goods manufacturer and does not operate a public developer program: it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs, or public webhook surface, and integrates with retail and distribution partners through EDI and private supply-chain connections rather than an open API.

providers.name: CIBC
providers.description: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) is a Schedule I domestic chartered bank and one of Canada's Big Six, formed in 1961 through the merger of the Canadian Bank of Commerce and the Imperial Bank of Canada and headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. Serving roughly eleven million personal, business, commercial, wealth, and capital-markets clients across Personal & Business Banking, Wealth Management, and Capital Markets, CIBC is a participant in the shared Canadian rails, including Interac e-Transfer and Payments Canada settlement systems. Canada has no operational open-banking mandate today: the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement, overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC), is not yet live, so access remains voluntary and fragmented. CIBC runs no first-party public developer portal (developer.cibc.com does not resolve) and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger specifications. Consumer-permissioned data access is aggregator-mediated: CIBC signed a tokenized data-access agreement with U.S. aggregator MX (announced August 2022, MX's first in Canada) to let clients share financial data with third-party apps without exposing banking credentials, and its accounts are also reachable through Plaid (Assets, Auth, Balance). Corporate connectivity is offered through CIBC SWIFT Corporate Access (SCA) file exchange rather than a public REST API, so CIBC's honest public API surface today is aggregator-mediated only, pending the coming Consumer-Driven Banking regime.

providers.name: Circle K
providers.description: Circle K is a global convenience store and fuel station chain operating more than 14,800 stores worldwide including 9,799 locations in North America and 2,697 in Europe across 48 U.S. states and over 30 countries. A subsidiary of Alimentation Couche-Tard, Circle K operates the Inner Circle Rewards loyalty program, the Easy Pay fuel payment system, an EV charging network, and the Circle K PRO Business Fleet Card.

providers.name: Clas
providers.description: Clas is a European industrial equipment supplier offering a wide range of workshop solutions, lifts, compressors, and tools. Their online store provides product catalogs, technical manuals, and a quick‑checkout system for professional users. The site includes detailed product pages, distributor contacts, and support resources, reflecting a mature e‑commerce platform for industrial customers.

providers.name: ClassAction
providers.description: ClassAction operates enjin (集団訴訟プラットフォーム enjin), a Japanese class-action / group-litigation platform that connects consumers who have suffered damages from the same party with registered attorneys to pursue collective lawsuits. Victims report their damages, registered lawyers volunteer to take on cases, and participants share legal costs and evidence so that even small-value claimants can afford to litigate. The service launched in May 2018 and is free for users. This is a consumer-facing legal-tech website with no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: ClearNote Health
providers.description: ClearNote Health (formerly Bluestar Genomics) is a US cancer detection company with offices in San Diego and San Mateo, California. Its proprietary 5hmC epigenomic platform combines cell-free DNA sequencing from a standard blood draw with machine learning to identify DNA-based alterations as cancer develops. The company commercializes Avantect, a suite of early-detection liquid biopsy tests for pancreatic and ovarian cancer that clinicians order through its laboratory, and Virtuoso, a research-use-only epigenomics platform sold to biopharma for drug discovery, therapy response and resistance research. ClearNote Health publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification: the clinician ordering path is a hosted intake form, and its public GitHub organization contains only forks of open-source bioinformatics tooling.

providers.name: Clearwater Paper
providers.description: Clearwater Paper Corporation (NYSE: CLW) is a Spokane, Washington-based manufacturer of bleached paperboard for North American packaging converters and, historically, private-label tissue for retailers. It is a Fortune 1000 company with mills in Idaho, Arkansas and Georgia. Clearwater Paper publishes no public API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable contract: its corporate site is an investor-relations platform with a customer-login landing page that describes, but does not name or link, a secure customer web portal, and the api./developer. hostnames an earlier version of this record pointed at do not exist in DNS. Trading-partner EDI (X12 850/810/856/997) is offered only through third-party VAN and integration vendors, not from a Clearwater Paper developer surface.

providers.name: Commercial Metals Company
providers.description: Commercial Metals Company (CMC) is a Fortune 500 manufacturer, recycler, fabricator and marketer of steel and metal products — rebar, merchant and structural bar, wire rod, performance steel, construction products and ground improvement solutions — running recycling centers, mini-mills, micro-mills and fabrication plants across the United States, Europe and Asia for the construction, infrastructure, energy and manufacturing markets. CMC was an early mover on customer self-service with myCMC, a portal for inventory, pricing, online ordering, material release, document search and real-time order and delivery status, and it runs a business-to-business Systems Integration program whose own one-pager names EDI, API, CSV, XML and flat file across the Quote-To-Cash process. None of it is self-service: no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract is published on any CMC host as of September 2026 — integration is arranged through a CMC sales rep or ecommerce@cmc.com.

providers.name: ConnectDER
providers.description: ConnectDER is a Philadelphia-based clean energy hardware company and the leading US manufacturer of meter socket adapters (MSAs, also called meter collars) for the residential market. Founded in 2011 as Infinite Invention LLC after a DOE SunShot Incubator grant, it builds plug-and-play devices that install at the utility meter socket to interconnect distributed energy resources — rooftop solar, battery storage and EV charging — without panel upgrades, line-side taps or circuit relocations. Its product line is the IslandDER MSA (a microgrid interconnect device for solar-plus-battery and whole-home backup, integrated by SolarEdge, FranklinWH, Lunar Energy, EcoFlow and Fox ESS), the Solar MSA and the EV MSA. ConnectDER helped author UL 414 Supplements A, B and C, the standards governing meter socket adapters, and has surpassed 40,000 devices installed across US utility territories including PG&E, SCE and SDG&E. ConnectDER publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its devices communicate with partner battery systems over discrete hardwired sensing, control and status signals rather than a network interface. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root.

providers.name: Converus
providers.description: Converus provides advanced lie detection technology using eye‑movement analysis, offering products such as EyeDetect, EyeDetect+, and VerifEye for law enforcement, corporate security, and government agencies. Founded in 2014, the company combines AI and neuroscience to deliver rapid, accurate deception detection solutions worldwide.

providers.name: Cornelisnetworks
providers.description: Cornelis Networks provides high‑performance networking solutions for AI and HPC workloads, offering Omni‑Path and Ethernet products such as the CN5000 and CN6000. The company focuses on ultra‑low latency, lossless scale‑out fabrics, and advanced networking hardware for large‑scale compute environments.

providers.name: Deako
providers.description: Deako is a whole-home smart lighting company that designs modular smart switches, dimmers, plugs, and simple switches (motion, timer, nightlight, and fan controls) for residential new construction and retrofit. Its Deako Intelligence platform layers adaptive lighting, follow-me sound, intercom, and parent-care features on top of the hardware, and the devices integrate with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Control4, Clare, and the Matter smart-home standard. Deako sells directly and through a network of homebuilders, electricians, and integrators. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile tracks the company's public web, support, blog, legal, and smart-home integration surface, awaiting any future developer program.

providers.name: Delek US Holdings
providers.description: Delek US Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: DK) is a diversified downstream energy company headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, asphalt operations, renewable fuels, and convenience store retailing. Delek operates four refineries in Tyler and Big Spring (Texas), El Dorado (Arkansas), and Krotz Springs (Louisiana) with combined crude throughput capacity of roughly 302,000 barrels per day. Logistics assets are operated through Delek Logistics Partners (NYSE: DKL). The company provides investor relations and ESG reporting on its public website but does not publish a developer API; partner integrations occur through industry-standard EDI, terminal automation, and ticketing systems.

providers.name: Docura Health
providers.description: Docura Health builds purpose-built software for physicians who prepare medical-legal reports — independent medical examinations (IME), qualified medical examiner (QME), agreed medical examiner (AME), permanent-and-stationary, and supplemental evaluations. The platform organizes complete case files (medical records, audio, and video), generates intelligent chronological summaries that link back to source documents, guides AMA Guides-compliant impairment ratings (5th and 6th Edition), and produces structured reports from customizable templates matched to each evaluator's practice style. Docura is HIPAA compliant with enterprise-grade end-to-end encryption and audit trails, and is backed by Y Combinator. This profile was seeded from a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from Docura Health's public website and trust center; no public developer API or documentation was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Draftea
providers.description: Draftea is a Mexico-based daily fantasy sports and real-money sports gaming platform, billed as the first daily fantasy sports (DFS) product for the Spanish-speaking world. Fans draft lineups of real athletes across soccer, American football (via an NFL partnership), basketball, baseball, and Formula 1, enter paid contests, and compete against other users for cash prizes rather than against a bookmaker. The company operates in Mexico under regulatory approval (DGAJS/SCEVF/P-06/2005-TER), distributes through native iOS and Android apps, and is backed by Sequoia, Kaszek, Bullpen Capital, Stepstone Group, and Courtside Ventures, along with athlete investors. Draftea is a consumer product company and does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and open-source engineering surface.

providers.name: Dwelly
providers.description: Dwelly (legal entity PROSPIRE TECHNOLOGIES LTD, also trading as Dwelly Group) is a UK-based, AI-first lettings and property-management company founded in 2023 by Ilya Drozdov (CEO), Dan Lifshits (CPO) and Dmitry Khanukov (CTO). Rather than selling software, Dwelly grows by acquiring independent UK lettings agencies and succession-planning their owners out, then running the acquired books on its own AI-powered operating platform. That platform automates tenant find (self-service enquiry chat, virtual viewings, verified offers), banking-grade tenant screening (KYC, Right to Rent, referencing), Direct Debit rent collection with automatic reconciliation and arrears handling, maintenance and property management workflows with centralised communications, and continuous lettings compliance. Dwelly is backed by General Catalyst, Begin Capital and S16VC. As of this profile Dwelly publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or technical documentation — the platform is operated internally for its own and its acquired agencies' portfolios.

providers.name: EarLens
providers.description: Earlens Corporation is a privately held medical technology company in Menlo Park, California that makes the Earlens Contact Hearing Solution, a non-surgical, custom-fit direct-drive hearing device. Instead of amplifying sound through a speaker, a custom lens rests on the eardrum and is driven by light from an ear-tip, vibrating the eardrum directly to reproduce a broader frequency range than conventional hearing aids. Founded by Dr. Rodney Perkins, the company holds more than 180 patents, received FDA clearance for its second-generation system in 2019, and was named to TIME's Best Inventions of 2020. Earlens is sold through audiology and ENT providers and publishes a consumer and provider marketing site, patient support documents, and a news section. As of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Eat Just
providers.description: Eat Just, Inc. is a food technology company founded in 2011 by Josh Tetrick and Josh Balk, headquartered in Alameda, California, that makes plant-based alternatives to animal products. Its flagship product is JUST Egg, a liquid and folded plant-based egg made from mung bean protein, alongside JUST Meat, JUST Protein and JUST condiments. Its GOOD Meat subsidiary produces cultivated chicken and in December 2020 became the first company in the world to receive regulatory approval to sell cultivated meat, in Singapore, followed by US FDA and USDA approval in June 2023. The company sells through retail, foodservice, restaurant and industrial channels in North America and Europe. Eat Just publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; this profile records its public web and corporate surface only.

providers.name: Eden
providers.description: Eden is a Latin American healthcare technology company providing cloud-based medical imaging and radiology software for hospitals, clinics, and diagnostic centers. Its platform includes Eden PACS (a cloud picture archiving and communication system and DICOM viewer), Eden Management (scheduling, referral, and operational workflow tools), Eden Intelligence (data-driven analytics for medical institutions), and Eden Creator (an AI assistant for drafting diagnostic impressions). Eden is backed by Sierra Ventures and serves medical institutions across Latin America. No public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Elroy Air
providers.description: Elroy Air develops autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft for defense, commercial, and rapid-response logistics. Its flagship Chaparral is a hybrid-electric aircraft designed to carry up to 300 pounds of cargo across roughly 300 miles with no crew onboard, taking off and landing vertically and cruising autonomously between points. Founded in 2016 and based in San Francisco, the company works with partners including FedEx, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and Lockheed Martin, and was selected for the U.S. Department of Transportation eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. Elroy Air is a hardware and autonomy company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: EnduroSat
providers.description: EnduroSat is a Sofia, Bulgaria-based satellite manufacturer and space service provider working to make space universally accessible by lowering the cost and complexity of accessing space data. The company builds CubeSat and SmallSat platforms (FRAME Max, FRAME L, FRAME S buses and 8U/12U/16U CubeSats), avionics and communication modules (X-Band SDR, S-Band and UHF transceivers, EPS power modules, solar panels, and antennas), and delivers end-to-end Space Service, SpaceOps, and SpaceDev offerings that take customers from idea to orbit in roughly six months. EnduroSat has deployed 100+ satellites with 3,500+ modules in operation, downlinked 500+ TB of data, and serves ~450 customers including NASA, ESA, and IBM Space. It maintains an open-source GitHub organization publishing Cubesat Space Protocol (CSP) implementations and NextGen ground-station and onboard API frameworks. Backed by Founders Fund and GV.

providers.name: Enfusion
providers.description: Enfusion is a cloud-native, front-to-back investment management platform for hedge funds and asset managers, unifying portfolio management (PMS), order and execution management (OEMS), pre- and post-trade compliance, a unified IBOR/ABOR accounting book of record, and analytics on a single SaaS database. It serves over 1,000 clients across 30 countries, offers direct connectivity to 300+ liquidity sources via FIX, and maintains a 4M+ instrument security master. Enfusion was acquired by Clearwater Analytics (CWAN) in 2025; the enfusion.com domain now redirects to cwan.com, where Enfusion is offered as a product line. There is no public developer portal or open API specification: the platform API and knowledge base are gated behind the client web application and Zendesk help center. This profile was surfaced as an ICONIQ Capital portfolio lead and enriched from public marketing, support, and legal surfaces.

providers.name: FMC
providers.description: FMC Corporation (NYSE: FMC) is a global agricultural sciences company headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with roots dating to 1883. FMC develops, manufactures, and sells crop protection chemistries (insecticides, herbicides, fungicides), biological solutions (biopesticides, biostimulants, biofertilizers, pheromones), seed treatments, and precision agriculture technology. Following the 2019 spin-off of Livent (lithium) and the 2021 divestiture of the Health & Nutrition business to DuPont/Eastman, FMC operates as a focused pure-play agricultural sciences company. The 2022 acquisition of Argentine biologicals firm BIOPHERO accelerated FMC's pheromone-based crop protection portfolio (Sofero brand).

providers.name: FundersClub
providers.description: FundersClub is an online venture capital firm and investment platform based in San Francisco that lets accredited investors browse, evaluate, and invest in curated early-stage technology startups through professionally managed, single-purpose venture funds. Founders apply for funding and, once selected, gain access to capital, a partner network, and post-investment support. Backed by a16z, Felicis, and Y Combinator, FundersClub pioneered the online VC model. The company publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks its web, identity, and domain-security surface for the network.

providers.name: Gankster
providers.description: Gankster is a consumer competitive-gaming social platform — a web and mobile "looking for group" (LFG) network that helps players team up, practice, and compete across titles including Valorant, League of Legends, Dota 2, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, and World of Warcraft. It matches players by rank, playstyle, and reputation to find duos, five-stacks, and fill players, and lets teams organize scrims, tournaments, and recruitment. Gankster operates entirely outside the game client (no overlays or client modifications) and ships the Gankster Duos mobile app on iOS and Android. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and raised $4.25M for its all-in-one competitive gaming platform. Gankster does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Gilead Sciences
providers.description: Gilead Sciences is a research-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, and commercializes innovative therapeutics in areas of unmet medical need including HIV, viral hepatitis, oncology, and inflammatory diseases.

providers.name: GlobalFoundries
providers.description: GlobalFoundries is a leading semiconductor foundry providing advanced manufacturing services for a wide range of technologies, including high-performance, power-efficient, and feature-rich solutions. The company serves diverse markets such as aerospace, automotive, data center, IoT, and mobile devices, offering technologies like FinFET, FD-SOI, advanced packaging, and quantum solutions. GlobalFoundries operates multiple fabs worldwide, supporting customers from design to production.

providers.name: Grail
providers.description: GRAIL, Inc. is a healthcare company headquartered in Menlo Park, California, focused on detecting cancer early, when it can be cured. Its flagship product, the Galleri multi-cancer early detection (MCED) test, uses a single blood draw and methylation-based genomic sequencing to screen for a signal shared across more than 50 types of cancer, many of which lack any recommended screening today. GRAIL runs large clinical programs including the PATHFINDER, PATHFINDER 2, and NHS-Galleri studies, and distributes Galleri through health plans, employers, and partners such as Quest Diagnostics and Junction. GRAIL is a portfolio company of investors including GV and SV Angel. It does not publish a first-party public developer API; programmatic access to Galleri ordering is offered through third-party diagnostic infrastructure partners.

providers.name: Hadrian
providers.description: Hadrian (Hadrian Automation) is a Los Angeles-area precision-manufacturing company founded in 2020 by Chris Power, building software-driven, AI-powered factories that produce high-tolerance machined components for the aerospace and defense industrial base — including parts for rockets, satellites, jets, drones, and missiles. The company's core software stack is Opus, described as a full-stack, AI-powered Factory Autonomy platform that interprets legacy engineering designs, automates CNC machining, inspection, tool-path optimization, adaptive programming, scheduling, and quality assurance, and enables new operators to be productive in 30 days or less. Hadrian operates multiple factories — Factory 2 (F2) and Factory X (FX) in Torrance, California, and Factory 3 (F3) in Mesa, Arizona — and offers three commercial models: precision component manufacturing, Manufacturing-as-a-Service (dedicated automation cells for a single customer), and Factories-as-a-Service (turnkey factory design and operation). Customers and partners include major aerospace and defense primes such as Lockheed Martin. Hadrian has also launched an additive manufacturing division to expand U.S. defense production capacity. The Opus platform is internal-only — Hadrian sells finished precision parts and factory capacity, not software access — and there is no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release for Opus or any Hadrian system.

providers.name: Harbor Health
providers.description: Harbor Health is a Central Texas healthcare company building a vertically integrated "pay-vider" model that combines primary care, specialty care, and health coaching clinics with its own commercial and individual health insurance plans, so the same organization both delivers and covers care. Founded in 2022 by Dr. Clay Johnston (founding dean of UT Dell Medical School), Tony Miller, and Eric Scott, the company operates clinics and Express Care walk-in locations across the Austin, Dallas, El Paso, and San Antonio metros, and is pursuing a value-based care model for the commercial market. It is backed by General Catalyst, 8VC, and Alta Partners. Harbor Health publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web properties (member portal, plans, blog, privacy and terms) for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: i-Brain Tech
providers.description: i-Brain Tech is a neuroscience company building a brain-controlled training platform for sports performance. Its core product is a video game driven exclusively by an athlete's brain impulses through motor-imagery and neurofeedback, requiring no physical movement. The platform is applied to three areas: post-injury neuromuscular recovery and return-to-play readiness, player development through cognitive and tactical training without physical strain, and cognitive assessment that surfaces mental resilience, attention, and endurance from real brain data. Elite football clubs including Real Sociedad, Juventus FC, CD Leganes, Olympique Lyonnais, S.L. Benfica, and Seattle Reign FC use the platform. i-Brain Tech is a Techstars portfolio company. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Indrive
providers.description: inDrive is a global ride-hailing, delivery, and urban-services platform built around a peer-to-peer, name-your-price model in which passengers propose a fare and nearby drivers accept, counter, or decline it directly. Founded in 2012 by Arsen Tomsky in Yakutsk, Russia and now headquartered in Mountain View, California, the company operates across roughly 48 countries and more than 1,000 cities, with over 400 million app downloads. Beyond city rides it offers intercity transport, courier and freight delivery, on-demand task services, and driver lending. inDrive was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bond Capital and General Catalyst. inDrive does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; its GitHub organization hosts internal engineering frameworks and an engineering handbook rather than external API definitions.

providers.name: InfiniGods
providers.description: InfiniGods is a gaming studio building fun, free-to-play, Web3-powered mobile games centered around ancient mythologies. Its titles — Immortal Siege, King of Destiny, and InfiniMerge — share interoperable gaming assets, items, power-ups, and currencies that span the InfiniGods Universe (IGU). Players collect blockchain assets such as the Elder Gods (a 4,488-piece Gen 0 NFT collection that unlocks abilities and boosts scoring across all titles) and the InfiniPass VIP membership (early access, bonus play, exclusive NFT drops, and in-game boosts). The company is backed by Pantera Capital. InfiniGods is a consumer game studio with no public developer/API program; this profile captures its public web, legal, community, and code-org surface.

providers.name: Intrinsic
providers.description: Intrinsic is a Mountain View, California industrial robotics software company spun out of Alphabet's X "moonshot factory" and led by CEO Wendy Tan White. Its mission is to make industrial robots radically easier to program, use, and innovate with so that automation is accessible to a much broader range of businesses. Intrinsic's flagship product is Intrinsic Flowstate, an all-in-one web-based developer environment for designing, building, simulating, and deploying production-grade robotics solutions, paired with Intrinsic Intelligence — a portfolio of AI-powered capabilities including pose estimation, motion planning, grasp planning, and sensor-guided control — and IntrinsicOS, a robot operating system that spans cloud to edge. Developers extend Flowstate by writing Skills and Services in Python and C++ via the open-source Intrinsic SDK (Apache-2.0), or compose them visually via behavior trees in the Flowstate Process Editor. The platform integrates deeply with ROS through Intrinsic's 2022 acquisition of Open Source Robotics Corporation (OSRC) — the commercial arm of Open Robotics — while ROS, Gazebo, and Open-RMF stewardship remain with the independent OSRF non-profit. Flowstate is currently in a gated beta / trusted-tester program; production access is granted to enterprise customers, systems integrators, and participants in programs such as the AI for Industry Challenge. Pricing is not publicly disclosed and there is no self-service developer signup.

providers.name: iovation
providers.description: iovation is a device-intelligence and online fraud-prevention service acquired by TransUnion in 2018 and now delivered as TransUnion TruValidate Device Risk (the SDK was formerly branded "FraudForce"). It fingerprints web and mobile devices into an encrypted "blackbox," evaluates it against a shared reputation database of billions of devices plus configurable rulesets, and returns a transaction risk assessment. Device data is collected client-side with first-party JavaScript and native iOS/Android SDKs; server-side integration is a SOAP CheckTransactionDetails call over HTTPS. iovation is used for account takeover, new-account fraud, payment fraud, and bot detection.

providers.name: Isar Aerospace
providers.description: Isar Aerospace is a European space launch service provider founded in 2018 and headquartered in Ottobrunn near Munich, Germany. The company designs and manufactures Spectrum, a two-stage orbital small-lift launch vehicle capable of carrying up to 1,000 kg to low Earth orbit or up to 700 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit, using liquid oxygen and propane propulsion. Spectrum is fully developed and produced in-house with automated, scalable manufacturing including additive manufacturing and carbon-composite structures. Isar Aerospace offers dedicated, lead, and rideshare launch services for small and medium satellites and constellations. Backed by more than EUR 500 million in private capital from investors including Earlybird and HV Capital, the company employs over 400 people from nearly 50 nations and conducted the inaugural Spectrum test flight from Andoya Spaceport, Norway, on 30 March 2025.

providers.name: ivymark
providers.description: ivymark was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found that the repo domain ivymark.com 301-redirects in full to www.ivy.co — Ivy, a business-management platform for interior designers (product sourcing, proposals, invoices, client mood boards, project and time tracking, online payments, and reporting), now operated as part of Houzz Pro. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery surface was found on either ivymark.com or ivy.co, so no API artifacts could be produced this round; only the identity, verified marketing links, and a live domain-security probe are recorded.

providers.name: Jaspersoft
providers.description: Jaspersoft is a business intelligence and embedded analytics platform, now part of Cloud Software Group (formerly TIBCO). Its flagship products are the open-source JasperReports Library — a Java reporting engine (net.sf.jasperreports) — and JasperReports Server, a reporting and analytics server that exposes a REST API (rest_v2) for managing the repository, running and scheduling reports, executing queries, and administering users, roles, and organizations. Developers embed Jaspersoft content into their own applications with Visualize.js and the js-visualize component library, and interact with the server programmatically through official Java and PHP REST clients. Sector: data analytics / business intelligence. Backed by Sapphire Ventures; surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: Junomedical
providers.description: Junomedical (now Qunomedical) is a Berlin-based digital health company founded in 2015 by Dr. Sophie Chung that connects patients with professionally-vetted doctors and clinics for high-quality medical treatments at home and abroad. The consumer platform (qunomedical.com) offers free assessments, price matching, 24/7 patient support, and personalized treatment matching across specialties including plastic surgery, hair transplants, dentistry, oncology, orthopedics, reproductive medicine, and weight-loss surgery, serving roughly 10,000 patients a month. The company also builds Qunosuite, a patient-relationship-management (PRM) SaaS for healthcare providers. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company operates a consumer marketplace and a provider SaaS but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: K Health
providers.description: K Health is a clinical AI and virtual primary care company founded in 2016 and headquartered in New York City. Its platform pairs an AI-led symptom investigation and intake engine with a 24/7 team of credentialed clinicians to deliver primary care, urgent care, mental health, and medical weight management. K Health licenses its clinical AI to health systems — including Cedars-Sinai, Mayo Clinic, Hackensack Meridian Health, Hartford HealthCare, Mass General Brigham, and Northwell Health — where it triages patients, combines intake with EMR data (Epic/MyChart), and automates clinical documentation. The company has raised more than $380M and was valued at roughly $900M as of 2024. K Health is a B2B2C consumer health application with no public developer API; integrations are handled through partners such as Health Gorilla for lab ordering. This profile was surfaced as a ggv-capital portfolio lead and enriched with verified public identity, link, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Kidas
providers.description: Kidas is a Techstars-backed trust-and-safety company that builds white-label scam detection and online-protection solutions for enterprises and consumers. Its ProtectMe platform monitors PC gaming and Discord voice and text channels for cyberbullying, predators, phishing, and scams, and its broader suite adds SMS scam detection, email protection, a scam-screening chatbot, and deepfake/impersonation defense that integrate into existing customer channels. Kidas markets custom builds and lists Aura, Comcast, Overwolf, Razer, Walmart, Intel, and Best Buy among its customers. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Kindara
providers.description: Kindara is a fertility-awareness and reproductive-health company offering a digital fertility charting system across web (app.kindara.com) and iOS/Android mobile apps. It lets users track basal body temperature, cervical fluid, and menstrual cycle data to understand their fertility, time conception, or practice fertility-awareness-based birth control. Kindara pairs its charting app with the Wink basal thermometer and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer-facing femtech product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Kindred
providers.description: Kindred is a members-only home exchange platform where verified members swap their real homes with one another instead of paying for traditional accommodation. The service runs on a credit economy — members earn one night of travel credit for every night they host, and new members start with five nights of credit. Kindred verifies every member and home, provides professional cleaning before and after each stay, and includes up to $100K in damage protection. There are no membership fees; travelers pay only a cleaning and service fee per trip. The platform operates across 190+ cities in North America and Europe and is backed by a16z, Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, Index Ventures, and NEA. Kindred is a consumer travel product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Kraka
providers.description: Kraka Technologies GmbH is a Berlin-based industrial AI company whose platform turns plain video recordings of shop-floor tasks into standardized, multilingual, step-by-step work instructions. Kraka Studio is the core product, extended by Training, Maintenance and Quality modules covering workforce qualification, AI-assisted fault diagnosis and checklist-driven quality control. Kraka positions itself as closing the execution gap between ERP systems that manage data and the work actually performed on the factory floor. Backed by Seedcamp. No public API, developer portal or SDK is published as of July 2026.

providers.name: La Solive
providers.description: La Solive is a French vocational training organization (organisme de formation) preparing career-changers and apprentices for the trades behind building energy renovation and the climate transition. It runs state-recognized, practice-based programs — chef de projet en rénovation énergétique, conducteur de travaux, plombier chauffagiste pompe à chaleur et gaz, technicien de maintenance CVC, installateur de panneaux photovoltaïques, QualiPAC and agent de maintenance du bâtiment — delivered across campuses in Paris, Lyon, Nantes, Marseille, Toulouse and Lille plus a distance-learning track, with Qualiopi certification and France Travail / Mon Compte Formation / Transitions Pro financing. La Solive reports 1,500+ students trained and 500+ recruiting partner companies. It is a Partech portfolio company in the Climate sector. As of this enrichment pass La Solive publishes no public API, developer portal, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; it does publish an /llms.txt agent-readable site index, captured in this repo.

providers.name: LaborUp
providers.description: LaborUp is an AI-powered recruiting platform for American manufacturing, connecting skilled industrial workers — machinists, CNC programmers, welders, and maintenance technicians — with manufacturing employers. The platform combines voice-first AI screening, skills verification, and constraint-aware matching with dedicated recruiter support, and claims 5-10x faster hiring, more than 50% lower cost than traditional staffing agencies, 3x better post-hire retention, and a proprietary network of 25,000+ vetted workers. Founded by Simba Jonga, LaborUp raised $7.74M ($1.935M pre-seed plus a $5.8M seed announced in August 2025) led by NVP with Torch Capital, Threshold, Heartland VC, Daybreak, Westbound, Marketplace Capital, and Market Square Ventures. Early traction is concentrated in the Knoxville, Tennessee manufacturing corridor and in aerospace, shipbuilding, and critical infrastructure. As of July 2026 LaborUp publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification; the product is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application.

providers.name: Lagom
providers.description: Lagom is an open source framework for building reactive microservice systems in Java and Scala, built on top of Akka and Play Framework, designed for distributed architectures.

providers.name: Lyric
providers.description: Lyric is an AI-powered supply chain software company, founded in 2022 and backed by Insight Partners. Its Lyric Studio platform lets enterprises model, plan, and optimize their supply chains across four composable layers — Data (enterprise-grade data management and integrations), Algorithms (advanced supply chain science), Workflows (flexible, composable processes), and Models & Apps (ready-to-use applications). The platform spans network modeling, transportation optimization, inventory management, forecasting, routing, and scheduling. Lyric does not publish a public developer API surface; its product documentation at docs.lyric.tech is gated behind a Lyric Studio login. It does operate a public SafeBase security and trust portal documenting SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR, CCPA, CPRA, and CSA STAR Level 1 posture plus a responsible disclosure program.

providers.name: Matera
providers.description: Matera is a French proptech company providing a digital platform for condominium management (syndic de copropriété), rental property management (gestion locative), and real estate transactions. Founded in Paris, Matera lets co-owners self-manage their buildings with software backed by 200+ in-house accountants, lawyers, and works experts, plus embedded services such as building insurance, legal protection, and a Treezor-powered payment account. It serves 150,000+ co-owners across France and is a certified B Corporation.

providers.name: METYCLE
providers.description: METYCLE is a Cologne, Germany-based digital B2B marketplace and AI-powered trading platform for the international secondary (scrap) metal industry, connecting suppliers and buyers of recycled metals - copper, aluminum, zinc, nickel, lead and magnesium - across borders. Operated by METYCLE GmbH and led by managing directors Rafael Suchan and Sebastian Brenner, the company raised a 14.1M euro Series A round to expand its platform for transparent, sustainable global metal trade and to advance circular-economy sourcing of secondary metals. Its customer platform supports biddable listings, product discovery and trade execution. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record; METYCLE currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: MHub
providers.description: MHub is a Malaysian property-technology (proptech) platform operated by TRB Ventures Sdn Bhd and backed by 500 Global. It gives real-estate developers an integrated system to manage the entire new-property sales cycle — from lead generation, launch, and online booking (Showroom, CRM, SalesCandy) through automated billing and collections (Credit Control), accounting and financial reporting, statutory compliance (HIMS/KPKT registry synchronization and LHDN-compliant e-invoicing), commission control, and handover/defect management. MHub runs a developer portal at developer.mhub.my and an authentication-gated REST API at api.mhub.my for platform integrations.

providers.name: Moleaer
providers.description: Moleaer Inc. is a Hawthorne, California nanobubble technology company that designs and manufactures nanobubble generators — Clear, Bloom, Lotus, Neo, Nexus, Trinity, Freya, Indalo, Titan and XTB, plus the NanoShield service — used to raise dissolved oxygen, act as a chemical-free oxidant, and control algae and biofilm in aquaculture, horticulture and irrigation water, lakes and ponds, wastewater treatment, food and beverage, car washes, mining, and oil and gas. Its only digital surface is a customer-only remote monitoring service, launched in 2020 with industrial IoT provider AMI Global, that reports equipment status and water-quality readings (DO, pH, ORP, temperature, conductivity) into a login-gated portal at www.monitoring-moleaer.com. Moleaer publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification; equipment-level integration is offered through industrial control protocols (SCADA/Modbus/EtherNet-IP) on the generators themselves, not through a web API.

providers.name: Mosaic Tech
providers.description: Mosaic Tech (Mosaic) was a San Francisco-based Strategic Finance Platform, founded in 2019, that connected ERP, CRM, HRIS, billing and data-warehouse systems into a single financial data model for FP&A teams — real-time analytics, agile financial planning, cash-flow forecasting, headcount planning and multi-entity consolidation. HiBob announced its acquisition of Mosaic on 2025-02-13 and closed it on 2025-04-01, folding the product into HiBob's finance/FP&A suite. As of 2026-08-26 the mosaic.tech domain 301-redirects every path to hibob.com, app.mosaic.tech redirects to finance-app.hibob.com, and api.mosaic.tech answers 503 on every path. Mosaic never published a public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification under its own brand — 493 archived mosaic.tech URLs in the Internet Archive contain no /api, /docs, /developers, swagger or openapi path. HiBob's own developer surface is profiled separately.

providers.name: Mubit
providers.description: Mubit is a temporary storage and logistics service based in Guadalajara, Mexico, offering on-demand collection, climate-controlled warehousing, digital photo inventory, and delivery for both individuals and businesses. Customers pay only for the space they use, with free pickup and drop-off, optional professional packing, and 24/7 CCTV-monitored facilities across three warehouses (Colli, Tijera, and Casuarina). Backed by 500 Global and Techstars, the company reports 4,000+ customers and a 4.9-star Google rating, and operates a mobile/web customer portal at clientes.mubit.co for scheduling pickups and deliveries and viewing stored items. Mubit publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Much Better Adventures
providers.description: Much Better Adventures is a B Corp certified adventure travel company that runs 250+ solo-friendly, expert-led outdoor group trips across the world's trails, rivers, coasts and mountains, matching travellers with certified local guides and hosts. It is a consumer-facing booking platform with financial protection via ABTOT/ABTA/ATOL and contributes 5% of every booking to its foundation for conservation. Surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; an enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Nautilus Biotechnology
providers.description: Nautilus Biotechnology is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: NAUT) life-sciences company developing a single-molecule protein analysis platform aimed at unlocking the proteome for basic biology, medicine, and drug discovery. Its Voyager platform pairs a novel single-molecule proteomics instrument with reagents and software to quantify and map proteoforms at scale. The company partners with academic and pharmaceutical researchers on applications spanning biomarker discovery and the drug-development process. Nautilus operates as a research-tools and instrument company; it publishes a corporate site, blog, resource library, and investor relations pages, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Nawah Scientific
providers.description: Nawah Scientific is MENA and Africa's first Cloud Lab, providing analytical testing and R&D services to the region's life science, food, agricultural, and pharmaceutical sectors. Through its online platform researchers and companies can request laboratory analyses, submit and track samples, and access remote scientific instrument time and data services. Headquartered in Egypt with expansion across Saudi Arabia and Rwanda, Nawah operates as a research engine backed by 500 Global.
