Condor advertises 90%+ forecast accuracy, faster month-end close versus spreadsheets, and a compliance-by-design architecture co-developed with Big 4 accounting firms. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published at this time; integrations with systems such as Veeva, Medidata, SAP, and Oracle NetSuite are delivered through the product. Backed by Felicis; raised a $24M Series A.

providers.name: Cotool
providers.description: Cotool is an AI platform for the defensive security "blue team" — AI agents that scale detection, response, and threat hunting across an organization's security stack. Its three products, Detect, Respond, and Hunt, let teams author detections from natural-language descriptions, automate alert response and playbook execution with human-in-the-loop controls, and monitor threat intelligence for relevance and coverage gaps. Cotool's stated mission is to "scale defensive security with tokens," giving defenders machine-speed operational advantages instead of being limited by headcount, improving coverage and cutting mean-time-to-respond (MTTR). Cotool is a San Francisco company backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, WndrCo, and Homebrew. As of this profile it publishes a product and marketing site only — no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or MCP server was found.

providers.name: Deppon Express
providers.description: Deppon Express (德邦快递), operated by Deppon Logistics Co., Ltd., is a major Chinese express delivery and logistics provider specializing in large-parcel (heavy/bulky) express, less-than-truckload freight, full-truckload, air freight, warehousing, supply chain, and cross-border services. Founded from Cui's Freight Company (1996) and incorporated in 2009, it became part of the JD Logistics group in 2022 and ranks among China's largest express carriers by market share. For developers and enterprise partners, Deppon runs the Deppon Open Platform (德邦开放平台, established 2015) at dpopen.deppon.com, offering system-integration APIs for order creation, standard track/tracking queries, and electronic waybill (面单) printing, with access granted to contracted monthly-settlement customers.

providers.name: Dillard's
providers.description: Dillard's, Inc. is a Little Rock, Arkansas department store chain selling apparel, footwear, cosmetics, handbags, menswear and home goods through its stores across the United States and dillards.com. Dillard's publishes no developer program, no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, gRPC or SOAP contract, and no MCP or A2A agent surface — contract discovery on 2026-09-06 found every /.well-known/ and /openapi.json path answering with the storefront single-page-app shell under HTTP 200, matching a nonsense control path. Its two real machine-facing surfaces are a first-party llms.txt at https://www.dillards.com/llms.txt that maps the retail catalog for language models, and an ANSI ASC X12 EDI trading-partner program (810/816/820/832/850/856/860/864/997 over the OpenText/GXS VAN) whose implementation guide and vendor portal are gated behind a login on the Dillard's eBiz extranet.

providers.name: DSpace
providers.description: DSpace is an open‑source digital repository platform used by thousands of academic, non‑profit and commercial organisations to preserve, manage and provide access to digital content. It offers flexible, multilingual support, integrates with services like ORCID and OpenAIRE, and is maintained by a global community under the Lyrasis umbrella.

providers.name: Duetti
providers.description: Duetti is a New York-headquartered music finance and catalog services company founded in 2022 by Lior Tibon and Christopher Nolte that buys music rights directly from independent artists, songwriters and creators. Artists earning at least $2,000 a year from tracks at least six months old can sell masters, publishing shares or a percentage of their royalties for an upfront cash payment — no debt, interest or recoupment — while keeping whatever they do not sell. Alongside the catalog purchases Duetti provides distribution, royalty tracking and claiming, playlisting across a network of owned Spotify playlists, sync placement, paid advertising, influencer and UGC campaigns, and a commissioned remix program. The company has raised more than $435 million, works with 1,100+ music creators, and publishes the Music Economics Report and the Billboard Music Finance Index. Duetti operates artist-facing web applications (DUO onboarding, statements vault, sync portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract as of this profile.

providers.name: E-Peas
providers.description: e-peas is a Belgian fabless semiconductor company founded in 2014 in Louvain-la-Neuve that designs power management integrated circuits (PMICs) for energy harvesting, enabling battery-free and battery-assisted IoT devices to power themselves from ambient energy. Its flagship Ambient Energy Manager (AEM) family harvests from photovoltaic (light), thermal, vibration/piezoelectric, radio-frequency, and hybrid multi-source inputs, and the company also develops ultra-low-power microcontrollers for autonomous data acquisition. e-peas positions itself as a pioneer of the "Ambient IoT" concept serving smart buildings, industrial IoT, consumer electronics, and wearables, with an ecosystem of 30+ partners including Panasonic, TDK, Vishay, and Silicon Labs. This is a hardware/silicon company that does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Emancro
providers.description: Emancro is an AI robotics company automating hospital logistics. Its flagship product, EASO, is described as the world's first fully autonomous robot for hospital medication logistics: it streamlines supply distribution, restocks medication dispensing cabinets, and retrieves medications from pharmacy storage to reduce errors and free clinical staff to focus on patient care. The technology combines vision-language-action (VLA) models with geometric planning, and Emancro is piloting EASO with leading U.S. hospitals. The company is backed by Amplify Partners. Emancro is a physical-robotics and healthcare-AI company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Endel
providers.description: Endel is a wellness technology company that generates personalized, adaptive soundscapes to help people focus, relax, sleep, and stay active. Its patented technology creates endless real-time audio that responds to inputs such as time of day, weather, circadian rhythm, heart rate, and location, delivered across iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, web, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Alexa. Endel is a consumer application; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface, so this repo captures its identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Enter
providers.description: Enter is a Berlin-based residential energy-efficiency company that positions itself as Germany's largest energy advisor, combining on-site building analysis with installation of heat pumps, photovoltaic (solar) systems, battery storage, EV wallboxes, and home energy-management systems. It guides homeowners through energy consulting, subsidy (Foerderung) applications, and financing, and reports 37,000+ completed projects and 150M+ EUR in secured subsidies. Enter is a B2C service provider with no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; it was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Entrepreneur First
providers.description: Entrepreneur First (EF) is a talent investor that backs exceptional individuals before they have a company, pairing them into cofounding teams and providing pre-seed capital, mentorship, and a global network to build technology startups from scratch. Founded in London in 2011 by Matt Clifford and Alice Bentinck, EF runs cohort-based programs across Europe, Asia, and North America and has helped launch hundreds of venture-backed companies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Greylock and added to the API Evangelist network; EF publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Evident Vascular
providers.description: Evident Vascular, Inc. is a San Jose, California medical device company developing the Evident Vascular Guidance System, an AI-powered intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) platform purpose-built for peripheral vascular image-guided therapy, with future capability intended for coronary procedures. The company came out of stealth in 2023 with a $35M Series A led by Vensana Capital and closed a Series B in March 2025 with Shangbay Capital and strategic investors, funding work toward FDA 510(k) clearance and a U.S. launch. The platform pairs an IVUS catheter and console with machine-learning image interpretation intended to improve vessel assessment and streamline the interventional workflow. Evident Vascular is pre-commercial and publishes no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface on its public web surface.

providers.name: Expert Intelligence
providers.description: Expert Intelligence is an AI company building analytical automation for pharmaceutical drug-development laboratories. Its platform turns raw instrument data into signed, regulatory-grade results and surfaces lab-wide trends across instruments, methods, and sites. Two integrated products anchor the offering: EI Flow automates batch analysis by converting instrument output into SOP-aware, signed, explainable results that reach LIMS systems in minutes so analysts review only exceptions, and EI Signal unifies historical data across instruments, methods, and sites to surface drift and anomalies before release. The company promotes exception-based review for higher accuracy, a Limited Sample Model (LSM) approach that needs only 30-50 expert examples, and instrument-agnostic deployment across cloud, on-premises, or hybrid environments. Backed by Sierra Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio and enriched from the company's public website; no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Explomar
providers.description: ExploMar (Changshu, China) designs and manufactures high-power fully-electric outboard propulsion systems for boats, ranging from 70HP to 1200HP. Its product line spans lightweight axial-flux electric outboard motors, high-density marine batteries for long-range and wide-temperature operation, the Smart Captain integrated control system with 200+ diagnostic capabilities, and 5S energy/charging stations (7kW portable through 120kW dual-gun). ExploMar markets an eco-friendly, high-performance alternative to combustion marine propulsion and exhibits at international yachting festivals (Cannes, Monaco, Interboot, Polboat). Backed by DCM Ventures; surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Note: ExploMar is a marine hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time — this profile carries identity and web-property signals only.

providers.name: Forum Mobility
providers.description: Forum Mobility develops, owns, and operates zero-emission heavy-duty trucking infrastructure, bundling electric Class 8 truck leases with charging subscriptions for a single monthly price so freight carriers of every size can electrify without upfront capital. The company builds and runs a network of charging depots — anchored by its flagship FM Harbor site at the Port of Long Beach (44 ports, 360KW fast chargers, 9MW capacity) — with additional depots in development across California and Nevada. Forum Mobility was surfaced as a portfolio company of obvious-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a physical-infrastructure operator with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Fractal Analytics
providers.description: Fractal Analytics Limited (fractal.ai) is an enterprise artificial intelligence services and products company founded in 2000, headquartered in New York with a large delivery footprint in India and roughly 5,000 employees across 18 global locations. Fractal sells AI consulting, data engineering, decision-science and design services to Fortune 500 clients in consumer packaged goods, retail, healthcare and life sciences, technology/media/telecom, financial services, insurance and industrials, and builds products on top of that practice — most notably Cogentiq, its enterprise agentic AI platform (with MCP and agent gateways, low-code agent builder and pre-built domain agents), LLM Studio, and consumer/vertical brands including Flyfish, Asper.ai, Kalaido.ai, Vaidya.ai and iqigai. The company listed on the NSE and BSE under the symbol FRACTAL in February 2026. Its API surface is delivered inside client engagements and gated product tenants rather than through a public developer program: as of this profiling pass Fractal publishes no public developer portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable API contract, and no hosted MCP server or A2A agent card.

providers.name: Freenome
providers.description: Freenome is an early cancer detection company founded in 2014 that develops blood-based screening tests to catch cancer in its earliest, most treatable stages. It combines multiomics laboratory science with artificial intelligence and machine learning to read multiple biological signals from a single blood draw, an approach it calls Personalized Cancer Detection. Its SimpleScreen portfolio includes tests for colorectal and lung cancer, validated through clinical research programs such as the PREEMPT CRC study. Freenome is a clinical diagnostics and life-sciences company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead (backed by a16z, CRV, DCVC, and GV) and enriched with the public identity, legal, and domain-security signals available from its website.

providers.name: Globe Life
providers.description: Globe Life Inc. (NYSE: GL) is a McKinney, Texas insurance holding company and Fortune 1000 constituent. Its wholly owned subsidiaries — Globe Life And Accident Insurance Company, American Income Life, Globe Life Liberty National Division, United American and Family Heritage — sell individual life, accident, supplemental health and Medicare Supplement policies direct to consumers and through captive and independent agents. Globe Life's public digital surface is entirely consumer- and agent-facing: quote tools, the myaccount policyholder portal, an agent locator, the eProvider remittance portal and a mobile app. As of the 2026-09-14 probe Globe Life publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract of any kind; partner and distributor integrations are governed by bilateral carrier agreements rather than by a public developer program.

providers.name: Got
providers.description: Got is a human-friendly and powerful HTTP request library for Node.js with support for streams, retries, and pagination.

providers.name: Healint
providers.description: Healint is a Singapore-headquartered digital health company best known for Migraine Buddy, the world's largest migraine and headache tracking and research platform, used by more than three million people to log attacks, symptoms, triggers, medications, and treatment outcomes. The company applies machine learning, mobile sensor technologies, and analytics to help people manage migraine and other neurological conditions, and to generate real-world evidence for clinicians, researchers, and pharmaceutical partners. Healint and Migraine Buddy are now part of Aptar Digital Health, whose regulated companion apps, patient-support software, and drug-delivery platforms operate across more than 120 countries on HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. Healint does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hedvig
providers.description: Hedvig is a Swedish insurtech offering mobile-first digital insurance to consumers, with more than 200,000 customers managing policies and reporting claims through its app. Products span home and apartment (hemförsäkring), villa, car, pet (dog and cat), accident, student, and travel insurance, with in-app chat support and fast digital claims. Backed by Anthemis and Obvious Ventures, Hedvig operates a consumer app over internal APIs and publishes no public developer API surface; this network profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Helsing
providers.description: Helsing SE is a Munich-based European defense AI company founded in March 2021 by Torsten Reil, Gundbert Scherf, and Niklas Köhler. Helsing builds AI software and autonomous weapons systems for European and allied militaries — reconnaissance-strike software (Altra), electronic-warfare AI (Cirra), an AI fighter pilot (Centaur), loitering-munition strike drones (HF-1 and HX-2), an autonomous combat aircraft (CA-1 Europa), and underwater autonomy (Lura acoustic processing, SG-1 Fathom long-endurance underwater drones). The company is sales-led and government-restricted; there is no public REST API or developer portal. This profile documents the publicly visible product surfaces and partnerships rather than endpoint shapes. Funding totals roughly €1.37B across four rounds, with a $1.2B Series E at an $18B valuation reportedly being finalized as of May 2026. Daniel Ek's Prima Materia is the largest shareholder. Public partnerships include Saab (Gripen E integration of Centaur, including the 2025 Project Beyond combat trial), Airbus, Rheinmetall, the Bundeswehr, and the Eurofighter Typhoon EK programme.

providers.name: Huma Technologies
providers.description: Huma Technologies Inc. operates Huma Finance, described as the first PayFi network — on-chain payment-finance infrastructure that connects global capital to real-world payment assets such as cross-border settlements, card payments, and payroll advances with T+0 on-chain settlement. Huma is offered in two forms: Huma (Permissionless), a retail-open protocol launched April 2025, and Huma Institutional, a permissioned protocol for licensed financial institutions accessing curated payment-financing and RWA opportunities. The protocol runs as smart contracts across Solana, EVM chains, and Stellar (Soroban), has processed over $7 billion in on-chain transactions, and is backed by partners including Solana, Circle, the Stellar Development Foundation, and Galaxy Digital. Developers integrate through the first-party @huma-finance JavaScript SDK, Solana permissionless SDK, Soroban SDK, and embeddable React widgets published on npm.

providers.name: Idecsi
providers.description: IDECSI is a Microsoft 365 and on-premises data security platform focused on Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) and Data Access Governance (DAG). It helps mid-size and large enterprises eliminate access, permission, and sharing risks across Microsoft 365, SharePoint, and file systems, with advanced monitoring, permission analysis, and user-driven security workflows. IDECSI serves large organizations such as L'Oreal, TotalEnergies, SNCF, Renault, and ADP, and aligns with regulatory frameworks including NIS2, DORA, and the EU AI Act. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a marketing site, blog, and help center but no public developer API or specification at this time.

providers.name: INGU
providers.description: INGU is a pipeline integrity technology company delivering inline inspection for oil & gas and water/wastewater pipelines through its Pipers multi-sensor free-floating inspection system paired with AI analytics and GIS-based pipeline viewer software. The platform performs leak detection, deposit and wall-condition assessment, and detection of gas pockets, magnetic features, bends, and hot taps across pipelines of any diameter or material. INGU has inspected over 900 pipelines for operators including Chevron, Shell, TotalEnergies, SUEZ, and Vale. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; the company publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Jaipur Robotics
providers.description: Jaipur Robotics is a Manno, Switzerland based deep-tech company building advanced computer vision and deep learning solutions for the waste-to-energy sector. Its product, Jaipur Intelligence, applies patent-pending image recognition to plant bunkers and truck unloading bays to detect oversized and dangerous items, map the calorific value (LHV) of incoming waste in real time, and track crane operations — helping operators cut emissions, improve waste mixing and combustion stability, and minimize unplanned shutdowns. The company operates a gated customer application at app.jaipurrobotics.com and is backed by Techstars, Innosuisse, Venture Kick, CSEM and others. It currently publishes a marketing site and a customer login only; there is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Juleb
providers.description: Juleb is a Saudi Arabia-based pharma-tech and retail software company providing an integrated cloud platform for the health, retail, and distribution sectors. Its suite spans accounting and financial management, inventory and warehouse management, sales force automation (SFA), point of sale (POS), Rx e-prescription, e-commerce, and DSCSA regulatory compliance. Juleb connects to Saudi compliance systems (ZATCA/Fatoora, RSD, GS1, Wasfaty), e-commerce channels (Salla, Shopify, HungerStation), payment providers (Geidea, Alhamrani), and ERPs (Microsoft Dynamics). Founded by Yousuf Jamjoom and backed by 500 Global, Juleb exposes a REST API (documented at docs.juleb.com) covering inventory, point of sale, prescriptions, and partner/company resources.

providers.name: Layer Health
providers.description: Layer Health is a healthcare AI company building a clinical intelligence platform that reads longitudinal medical records at scale to automate labor-intensive clinical workflows for health systems. Its products span clinical registry abstraction automation (cardiovascular, surgical, and oncology registries), clinical pathways that surface guideline-aligned care opportunities and eligible patients, site-of-care optimization, and automated quality measurement of custom clinical variables. The company positions clinician-validated AI as an embedded workflow layer rather than a standalone tool, citing 50%+ time savings on registry abstraction, and works with health systems including Johns Hopkins Medicine, Intermountain Health, MultiCare, and White Plains Hospital. Backed by GV. As of this enrichment pass Layer Health publishes a marketing and company site only and exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Ledgebrook
providers.description: Ledgebrook is a technology-enabled excess and surplus (E&S) lines managing general agent (MGA) and reinsurance platform headquartered in Massachusetts and founded by Gage Caligaris. It underwrites specialty commercial casualty risk — general liability, professional liability, and cyber — exclusively through wholesale brokers, competing on quote speed rather than direct-to-consumer distribution. Its stack pairs a proprietary underwriting workbench with machine-learning models applied across submission intake, triage, data architecture, and pricing, backed by an engineering, data-science and product organization of 70+ people, with policy administration running on Socotra. Ledgebrook Re extends the business into delegated-authority reinsurance with London and Dubai operations. The company closed an oversubscribed Series C funding round in June 2025 and has appeared on the CB Insights 50 Most Innovative Insurtech Startups list. As of this profiling pass Ledgebrook publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract — its broker quoting platform is a private, credentialed surface.

providers.name: Linc'well
providers.description: Linc'well, Inc. (株式会社Linc'well) is a Tokyo-based healthcare technology company founded in January 2018 whose stated mission is to take healthcare one step further through technology. It operates a healthcare platform that connects medical professionals with patients across online and offline care, organized into three business lines: a telehealth platform licensed to medical institutions, where patients complete everything from booking to consultation on web, smartphone, or tablet, pay by credit card or pay-later, and have medication delivered or dispensed at a local pharmacy; a Smart Clinic clinic-DX service that digitizes core primary-care operations including appointment booking, medical intake, payment, and medical record entry; and a healthcare e-commerce business covering cosmetics, contact lenses, over-the-counter medicines, online medication guidance, and prescription dispensing. Linc'well runs the CLINIC FOR clinic brand and the miteme commerce and pharmacy properties, and is backed by DCM Ventures. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification; integration is a commercial arrangement with medical institutions.

providers.name: Live Oak Bank
providers.description: Live Oak Bank (Live Oak Banking Company) is a digital, branchless, North Carolina state-chartered commercial bank founded in 2008 and headquartered in Wilmington, NC, operating as the primary subsidiary of Live Oak Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: LOB). It is the largest originator of U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) 7(a) loans in the country and serves small businesses in all 50 states with SBA and commercial lending, high-yield business and personal savings, CDs, and business checking with treasury services. Technology-forward for a bank of its size, Live Oak runs a cloud-native Finxact core (now Fiserv) with an Apiture-based digital banking platform, and in 2024 launched an in-house embedded-banking / Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) program that lets software companies deliver Live Oak deposit and payment products to their own customers. Its API surface is real but partner-gated: a production AWS API gateway operates at api.liveoak.bank (returning MissingAuthenticationToken to unauthenticated callers, with Live-Oak-specific lob-identity-id / lob-foreign-entity-id headers), but Live Oak publishes no public self-serve developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, and no public API reference. Consumer-permissioned data access is available through account aggregators rather than a first-party public API, and no FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented.

providers.name: MakerDAO
providers.description: MakerDAO is the decentralized autonomous organization behind the Maker Protocol, an Ethereum-based smart-contract system that lets anyone, anywhere generate the Dai (DAI) stablecoin by locking crypto collateral into Vaults. The protocol governs collateral types, stability fees, the Dai Savings Rate (DSR), collateral liquidation auctions, and oracle price feeds through on-chain governance by MKR token holders. Rather than a hosted REST API, developers integrate directly with the Maker Protocol smart contracts and through the official Dai.js JavaScript / TypeScript SDK, the multicall state-management library, and published developer guides. MakerDAO has since rebranded to the Sky Ecosystem (USDS / SKY). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Paradigm and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Mavenoid
providers.description: Mavenoid is an AI agent platform for product support, helping hardware and consumer-electronics companies deflect and resolve customer issues through self-service troubleshooting across voice, text, image, and video. Its products include Voice Assist (AI call routing and self-service), a Dynamic Help Center that surfaces AI-powered support in search results, an embeddable Virtual Assistant, and an Insights analytics dashboard. Mavenoid connects to CRM, ticketing, ERP, e-commerce, and IoT systems. The company is backed by Creandum and Point Nine. As of this enrichment pass Mavenoid publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or well-known discovery surface; integrations are configured within its product rather than via a documented public REST API.

providers.name: Mazama Energy
providers.description: Mazama Energy is a geothermal energy company reinventing power generation with enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) that tap superhot rock to deliver universal, scalable, clean, and affordable electricity. Its Thermal Lattice sequential-stimulation technology improves connectivity between injectors and producers in super hot reservoirs (SHR). The company is developing the Newberry project in Oregon and runs the Mazama EMPOWER program, and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Headquartered in Frisco, Texas.

providers.name: Mesodyne
providers.description: Mesodyne is an MIT-founded engineering and manufacturing company (established 2018) that builds the LightCell, a patented thermophotovoltaic power generator which converts liquid and gaseous fuels — gasoline, diesel, propane, jet fuel, and hydrogen — directly into silent electricity with more than ten times the energy density of batteries. Designed for military, tactical, drone, and off-grid use, it operates day or night across extreme environments with low heat and emissions signatures and no routine maintenance. Mesodyne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Milu Health
providers.description: Milu Health is a health technology company that pairs a virtual care team with an AI engine to help employees and their families get higher-quality healthcare at a lower cost. Founded in 2023 by Sasha Gribov and Gautam Kumar, Milu integrates directly with electronic health record (EHR) data from tens of thousands of provider groups and health systems to proactively flag medication issues, care gaps, fairly priced and high-quality doctors, incorrect medical bills, and more affordable medications. The platform also ingests an employer's health plan and benefits so it can notify members when an existing benefit could help. Milu is offered through employers and benefits advisors as well as directly to individuals. The company raised a $4.8M seed round led by a16z Bio + Health in March 2024. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; Milu does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Neptune Networks
providers.description: Neptune Networks operates Neptune, an institutional fixed-income pre-trade data platform that delivers real-time dealer axes and bond inventory directly into buy-side workflows. Aggregating structured data from 34 global banks, the network surfaces roughly 110k bonds per day at around $2.2T daily gross notional across 33 currencies, helping asset managers identify liquidity opportunities before they trade. Originally an independent, bank-owned utility backed by Anthemis, Neptune is now operated as RealQ, the data-solutions arm of Liquidnet Fixed Income (part of TP ICAP Group). Connectivity is institutional and permissioned - a browser web app, OMS/EMS integrations, FIX, a REST API, FTP/SSH drop copy, and AWS cloud data transfer - with no public developer portal, published OpenAPI, or open SDKs.

providers.name: Neva
providers.description: Neva is a self-described "builder" agent: an A2A 0.3.0 agent at neva.dt-agent.co.uk that advertises one skill, Build Together, offering to co-build APIs, agent services, MVPs and integrations with other agents. Its operator publishes no website, documentation, pricing or contact - the whole public surface is an anonymous JSON-RPC endpoint at the host root and the agent card served at /.well-known/agent-card.json (and the legacy /.well-known/agent.json), listed on a2aregistry.org since 2026-03-22. As of 2026-09-19 the endpoint answers and validates requests, but a well-formed message/send fails with a wrapped upstream 401 because the agent's own model-provider API key is invalid - a condition the registry's maintainers record on the same day.

providers.name: NewsData
providers.description: NewsData.io provides live breaking news and historical news data going back to January 2018, sourced from over 82,000 sources worldwide. The API supports searching, filtering by source, language, country, and category, and returns results in JSON format suitable for analytics, monitoring, and AI training.

providers.name: Numbi
providers.description: Numbi is a tech-enabled accounting and payroll firm for Colombian companies — especially SAS entities, SMBs, and startups. It pairs expert accountants with automation and AI to run monthly bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and DIAN electronic-invoicing compliance. Numbi is a service rather than software or an ERP: it operates on top of a company's existing accounting systems (Siigo and Alegra) instead of replacing them, ingesting documents (PDFs, XMLs, images) and keeping tax calendars and filings current. Founded in Bogotá and backed by Homebrew and Newtopia VC. No public developer API surface is published as of this pass.

providers.name: Nuvig Therapeutics
providers.description: Nuvig Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 3450 Hillview Avenue, Palo Alto, California, developing next-generation immunomodulators for chronic autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Its lead investigational candidate, NVG-2089, is an engineered Fc fragment designed to selectively engage type II Fc receptors and harness an endogenous regulatory mechanism that resolves autoimmune dysregulation while preserving normal immune function; the first patient was dosed in a Phase 2 trial in chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) in May 2025. The company announced a $161 million Series B financing in December 2024. Nuvig is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, GitHub organization, or machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its public web surface is a corporate WordPress site covering science, pipeline, team, news and careers, from which the only machine-readable artifact published is a Yoast-generated llms.txt.

providers.name: Operator Framework
providers.description: The Operator Framework is a CNCF incubating toolkit for building and managing Kubernetes Operators. It includes the Operator SDK for scaffolding and building operators using Go, Ansible, or Helm, the Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) for installing and managing operators on clusters, and OperatorHub for discovering and sharing operators. The framework codifies operational knowledge into software.

providers.name: Optiwatt
providers.description: Optiwatt is a consumer-centric energy management platform that helps electric-vehicle drivers and homeowners lower their electricity bills by automatically scheduling EV charging and smart-thermostat use for off-peak, low-cost, and low-carbon hours. Its consumer app (getoptiwatt.com) connects to vehicles, chargers, and thermostats via direct OEM integrations such as the Tesla Fleet API and aggregators like Smartcar, while its utility platform (optiwatt.com) orchestrates these distributed energy resources as virtual power plants across demand-response and load-shaping programs for utility partners. Backed by GV. Optiwatt is primarily a consumer of third-party APIs rather than a public API producer; no public developer API or OpenAPI has been found.

providers.name: Passport
providers.description: Passport (Passport Labs) is a mobility management platform for cities, universities, and agencies, covering digital parking payments, enforcement, permits, and curbside management, and is used by 800+ agencies. Passport exposes a partner developer program at developer.passportinc.com whose REST APIs let parking apps, navigation apps, in-car infotainment, and mobility/POS systems create and stop parking sessions, quote and determine rates, bulk-export the parking environment (zones, spaces, rules), receive parking event schemas, and manage enforcement immobilizations. Rates and rules are configured once by Passport's customers and pushed to payment providers via API. Access is gated - partners register an application, are issued OAuth client credentials by Passport's identity provider, and only authenticated partner applications may call the public APIs. No SDK is required. Commercial terms are partnership / agency-contract based rather than publicly listed self-serve pricing.

providers.name: Payna
providers.description: Payna is a compliance operating system for financial licensing that automates applications, renewals, maintenance, and monitoring across all 50 US states and jurisdictions. It tracks state statutes, NMLS procedures, and FinCEN requirements in real time, calculates filing deadlines backward from due dates, scores compliance posture against state examiner playbooks, automates document pre-fill and e-signature, and maintains a timestamped, queryable audit trail for examinations. Payna serves regulated financial sectors including money transmission, lending, mortgage, cryptocurrency/VASP, debt collection, loan origination, and insurance. It is a Y Combinator (W26) company; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Perf.ai
providers.description: PerfAI is an autonomous agentic AppSec and auto-fix platform for AI-built apps, helping teams deliver privacy, security, and governance for APIs and applications.

providers.name: Persefoni
providers.description: Persefoni is a climate management and accounting platform (CMAP) used by enterprises and financial institutions to measure, report, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The platform serves more than 9,000 sustainability teams and covers Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions, financed emissions for financial services (PCAF), and disclosures aligned to SBTi, TCFD, CSRD, SEC, and SASB. Persefoni also ships PersefoniAI and the Persefoni Copilot for in-product carbon accounting expertise. An Integration Hub provides pre-built connectors to enterprise systems (AWS, SAP Concur, Expensify, Navan, Google Sheets, Coupa, NetSuite, Stripe, utilities). Persefoni does not publish a fully open, self-service API portal; programmatic access is delivered through customer and partner channels.

providers.name: Photoneo
providers.description: Photoneo is a Slovak (Bratislava, founded 2013) machine-vision company and a global pioneer of high-resolution structured-light 3D measurement. Its flagship products are the PhoXi 3D Scanner family and the MotionCam-3D, a parallel structured-light camera that captures moving scenes in real-time 3D, together with AI-enabled software such as Bin Picking Studio, Locator, and Palletizing for robotic automation. Rather than a hosted web/REST API, Photoneo exposes a developer surface through the PhoXi Control software and its official C++, C#, and Python device APIs, GenICam/GigE Vision standard connectivity, TCP/IP robot interfaces (UR, ABB, FANUC, Staubli, Mitsubishi, Kawasaki, Yaskawa), and a set of BSD-licensed example repositories on GitHub. Documentation lives in the Photoneo Knowledge Base (docs.photoneo.com) and the 3D scanning wiki. Photoneo (now part of the Brightpick Group) was acquired by Zebra Technologies.

providers.name: Playco
providers.description: Playco is an instant-play gaming company founded in 2020 by Justin Waldron, Michael Carter, Takeshi Otsuka and Teddy Cross, headquartered in Tokyo with teams worldwide. It builds HTML5 games that run inside social and communication platforms without an app install — EverWing on Facebook, Snake Squad on Snap Games, Heads Up! for Zoom, Sway Stories on TikTok and Trip Royale on LINE — and reached unicorn status on a $100M Series A. Its technology stack, described on play.co/tech, is developer tooling rather than a public web API: PixiJS (the open-source HTML5 rendering/creation engine it acquired with Goodboy Digital in 2021), Odie3D (a 3D extension framework), GCInstant (a client-side JavaScript library wrapping platform SDKs and analytics) and Replicant (a backend-as-a-service state manager for instant games). Playco publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract; its public code surface is the play-co GitHub organization, which is the renamed Game Closure organization and carries the legacy devkit HTML5 game platform, js.io and ff.

providers.name: Policygenius
providers.description: Policygenius is an independent online insurance marketplace and licensed brokerage founded in 2014 by Jennifer Fitzgerald and Francois de Lame and headquartered in New York City. The platform lets consumers compare quotes, get unbiased expert advice, and buy life, disability, homeowners, auto, and renters insurance across dozens of carriers, and it operates Policygenius Pro, a turnkey life-insurance fulfillment platform for financial advisors, agents, banks, and credit unions. Policygenius was acquired by Zinnia (an Eldridge company) in 2023. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Policygenius publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; its GitHub organization hosts internal tooling and forks only.

providers.name: Pragmatic
providers.description: Pragmatic Semiconductor Limited is a UK semiconductor manufacturer that designs and produces FlexICs - ultra-thin, physically flexible integrated circuits built on thin-film transistor (TFT) technology rather than conventional crystalline silicon. Founded in 2010 by Richard Price and Scott White and headquartered at Cambridge Science Park with manufacturing at Pragmatic Park in Sedgefield, County Durham, the company operates the Pragmatic FlexIC Foundry, a service that takes third-party custom flexible IC designs from tape-out to delivery in roughly six weeks. Product lines include the FlexIC Platform Gen 3 mixed-signal flexible ASIC design flow, Pragmatic NFC Connect and Pragmatic NFC Protect. The company raised a $231M Series D in 2023. Its only network-reachable API surface is the undocumented, authentication-gated backend of its customer portal; it publishes no developer program, no machine-readable contract and no public API reference.

providers.name: Prisma Photonics
providers.description: Prisma Photonics is an infrastructure-monitoring company that turns existing optical fiber into a continuous sensing network using its Hyper-Scan Fiber-Sensing distributed acoustic sensing technology. The platform measures strain, temperature, pressure, and acoustic signatures at every point along hundreds of kilometers of fiber with sub-meter resolution, and applies AI-driven classification to detect and identify events in real time. It is used to protect and monitor power lines, oil and gas pipelines, perimeters, subsea assets, and smart rail and road infrastructure. Backed by Insight Partners, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Prophetic
providers.description: Prophetic is a San Francisco-based neurotechnology startup, incorporated in January 2023, building the world's first wearable device for stabilizing lucid dreams. Its "Halo" headband pairs EEG sensing with targeted transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) to noninvasively stimulate the prefrontal cortex, driven by an in-house AI model, Morpheus-1, that takes brain activity as its prompt and generates shaped ultrasonic waveforms as output. Backed by BoxGroup and a16z's Scout Fund, Prophetic sells its neuromodulation headbands direct-to-consumer. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Prophetic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic integration surface — it is a consumer hardware and wellness company.

providers.name: Protege
providers.description: Protege (Protege Health Inc.) is a two-sided data platform that connects AI model builders with high-quality, real-world proprietary datasets for pre-training, post-training, fine-tuning, and evaluation. It curates data from hundreds of sources across healthcare, video, audio and speech, motion capture, architecture/engineering/construction, manufacturing, energy, finance, and agriculture, handling licensing and rights protection while fairly compensating data rights holders. Protege also operates DataLab, a research team focused on data-for-AI challenges. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, CRV, Bloomberg Beta, Footwork, Flex Capital, SV Angel, Liquid, and Shaper Capital. As of this enrichment pass Protege publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and web properties.

providers.name: Qasa
providers.description: Qasa is a Swedish digital platform that connects renters and landlords, simplifying the process of finding, listing, and managing rental properties. The service offers a searchable catalogue of over 25,000 homes across Sweden and other Nordic countries, tools for landlords to create listings, and features like premium services, tenant screening, and secure contract handling. Qasa aims to make renting transparent, efficient, and trustworthy for both tenants and property owners, leveraging technology to streamline communication and payments.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: REEV
providers.description: REEV is a medical-technology company developing AI-powered wearable robotics for mobility recovery and neurological gait rehabilitation. Its REEV SENSE platform uses smart shoe- and leg-mounted sensors to analyze gait and visualize biomarkers in a mobile app, and its DREEVEN motorized knee-ankle-foot orthosis (KAFO) delivers robotic walking assistance personalized from REEV SENSE gait data. REEV serves outpatient clinics and rehabilitation centers treating stroke, multiple sclerosis, and paraplegia, and is backed by Techstars, NVIDIA Inception, and Bpifrance.

providers.name: Remedio
providers.description: Remedio is an autonomous cybersecurity remediation platform that detects and automatically fixes misconfigurations, configuration drift, and emerging Shadow AI risks across hybrid IT environments at machine speed. Its platform spans five modules — Baseline (secure configuration baselines), AI Govern (discovery and governance of AI tools, agents, and connections), Fortify (autonomous vulnerability and misconfiguration remediation), Gate (application and software control), and Assure (continuous compliance monitoring) — with predictive impact preview, auditable rollback, and ROI measurement. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Remedio publishes a marketing site and blog but no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Roomstorm
providers.description: Roomstorm is a real-time B2B hotel room marketplace, best known for building the airline industry's first fully automated platform for providing hotel accommodations to distressed passengers during flight disruptions. Founded by Maksim Izmaylov and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2014), the San Francisco company connects airlines, hotels, and travelers so that irregular-operations (IROPS) rebooking, room sourcing, invoicing, and voucher issuance happen programmatically instead of through manual phone calls. Its backend exposes a JSON REST API (documented in API Blueprint) covering authentication, bookings, hotels, rooms, vacancies, organizations, vouchers, and airport search.

providers.name: Rosebud
providers.description: Rosebud is an AI-powered journaling application for personal growth, combining journaling, habit-building, and emotional support in one experience. Users write or speak entries and receive conversational AI feedback, long-term pattern recognition, guided modes (including Internal Family Systems), automated weekly insight reports, and voice journaling, with end-to-end encryption for privacy. It is available on iOS, Android, and the web. Rosebud is a consumer product with no public API, SDK, or developer platform; it is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Initialized Capital, and Khosla Ventures.

providers.name: RPC
providers.description: RPC, Inc. is an oilfield services company providing specialized well services to independent and major oil and gas companies engaged in the exploration, production, and development of oil and gas properties. Operating through subsidiaries including Cudd Energy Services, Patterson Services, Spinnaker Oilwell Services, and Thru Tubing Solutions, RPC offers pressure pumping, wireline, downhole tools, coiled tubing, cementing, snubbing, nitrogen services, well control, rental tools, and tubular services. RPC does not currently offer a public developer API.

providers.name: Saber
providers.description: Saber is a decentralized automated market maker (AMM) on the Solana blockchain, optimized for trading and providing liquidity between mean-reverting assets such as stablecoins and wrapped or pegged tokens. Its StableSwap program delivers low-slippage swaps and capital-efficient liquidity pools. Saber does not expose a REST/HTTP API; developers integrate through its on-chain StableSwap program using first-party TypeScript SDKs (the @saberhq/* packages on npm) and Rust crates (crates.io) that construct and submit Solana transactions. The project also maintains open-source Solana tooling, an asset/pool registry, and on-chain governance. Saber was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Sage Geosystems
providers.description: Sage Geosystems is a Houston, Texas energy company developing "Pressure Geothermal" — an evolution of traditional geothermal that applies subsurface breakthroughs from the oil and gas industry to hot dry rock. Its two-well Power Generation system circulates water through engineered "lung" fractures and extracts heat at surface through a heat exchanger driving an sCO2 turbine, while its single-well EarthStore energy storage system charges and discharges over 8-hour to multi-day timescales for long-duration storage. The company markets to utilities, data centers and government partners rather than to developers: as of this profile it operates a seven-page marketing site with no developer portal, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Sakuu
providers.description: Sakuu Corporation is a Silicon Valley advanced-manufacturing company that builds commercial-scale printing equipment for the battery and supercapacitor industries. Founded in 2016 as KeraCel and renamed Sakuu in 2021, it develops the Kavian platform — a dry-process electrode printing system that produces cathodes and anodes without solvents or drying ovens, covering NCA, NCM, LFP, LTO, graphite and silicon-graphite chemistries as well as sodium-ion, aluminum-ion and solid-state formulations. Kavian was named a TIME Best Invention of 2024 and a Fast Company World Changing Idea of 2025, and the Kavian 2000 platform is sold to battery makers serving AI data centers, energy storage, two- and three-wheel mobility, aerospace and industrial electrification. Sakuu sells capital equipment and process technology; it does not operate a software product, a developer program, or any public API.

providers.name: Scarlet
providers.description: Scarlet is Europe's only Notified Body specialised in software and AI-based medical devices. Operating at scarlet.cc, Scarlet certifies Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and AI as a Medical Device (AIaMD) under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR), streamlining conformity assessment, CE marking, and certificate transfers for manufacturers who ship iteratively and release frequently. Backed by Creandum, Scarlet was built to bring modern, fast-moving regulatory certification to AI and software medical-technology companies. Scarlet is a regulatory and certification services provider; it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Scythe Robotics
providers.description: Scythe Robotics builds autonomous lawn mowers to transform commercial landscaping. Their flagship M.52 robot delivers up to 1.5 acres per hour, reducing crew size and emissions. The company emphasizes sustainable technology, mission-driven teamwork, and community impact, aiming to make outdoor maintenance more efficient and eco‑friendly.

providers.name: ShardSecure
providers.description: ShardSecure is a data security company providing agentless, file-level data protection that keeps sensitive data private, resilient, and compliant across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid or multi-cloud environments. Its platform uses microsharding to cryptographically fragment and distribute data so exfiltrated fragments are unintelligible, adds ransomware detection with self-healing data integrity, and extends to securing AI inference data through an MCP Secure Gateway. ShardSecure is a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public API or developer portal as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Showrunner
providers.description: Showrunner is an AI streaming and animation platform built by Fable Simulation (founded by Edward Saatchi) and billed as the "Netflix of AI." It lets users create and watch AI-generated serialized animated television shows across genres, acting as directors to write, produce, voice, and remix full episodes within simulated worlds such as Sim Francisco, alongside flagship series like Exit Valley. The platform is powered by Fable's proprietary SHOW-2 model and is delivered as a consumer iOS app and Discord community. Showrunner publishes no first-party developer API; its public site is a Wix-hosted marketing property that exposes the standard Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content.

providers.name: Sidecar Health
providers.description: Sidecar Health is a health insurance company founded in 2018 by Patrick Quigley and Veronica Osetinsky and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio. It was built to bring transparency to healthcare pricing, letting members see upfront cash prices for care and share in the savings. After launching with supplemental coverage for individuals, Sidecar established its own insurance carrier in 2021 and today serves large employers with ACA-compliant major medical plans, offered both fully insured and as administrative-services-only (ASO) for self-funded employers. It covers members in 46 states across partners in 50 industries. Sidecar Health operates member, provider, broker, and employer web portals plus a mobile app, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or partner-integration documentation; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Sierra Space
providers.description: Sierra Space is a commercial space and defense technology company headquartered in Louisville, Colorado, spun out of Sierra Nevada Corporation as an independent entity in April 2021 and building on more than three decades of spaceflight heritage. The company designs and manufactures the Dream Chaser reusable lifting-body spaceplane and Shooting Star cargo module, the LIFE expandable space habitat and the Orbital Reef commercial space station developed with Blue Origin, Eclipse-class satellites for national security and on-orbit servicing missions, VORTEX rocket propulsion and hypersonics, space solar arrays and electrical power systems, environmental control and life support systems, and a broad spaceflight hardware catalog spanning valves, regulators, radiators, sensors, actuators, docking and berthing systems, deployable structures and launch adapters. Sierra Space states it has delivered more than 4,000 space systems, subsystems and components across more than 500 space missions. It is a hardware and mission-systems manufacturer rather than a software platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: SM Energy
providers.description: SM Energy Company (NYSE: SM) is an independent oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado. Founded in 1908 (originally as St. Mary Land & Exploration Company), SM Energy focuses on acquiring, exploring, developing, and producing crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids (NGLs) from top-tier assets across the Permian Basin in West Texas and New Mexico, the Maverick Basin in South Texas, the DJ Basin in Colorado, and the Uinta Basin in northeast Utah. The company is a Fortune 1000 member with approximately 1,241 employees and average daily net production of 206.8 MBoe/d. SM Energy completed a merger with Civitas Resources in early 2026. The company does not offer a public developer API; investor data is accessible through financial data APIs and SEC EDGAR.

providers.name: SmartMore
providers.description: SmartMore Corporation (思谋科技) is a Hong Kong- and Shenzhen-headquartered industrial AI and machine vision company founded in 2019, building products and solutions for smart manufacturing and digital innovation. Its flagship SMore ViMo platform bundles ViMo Cloud, ViMo Deeplearning and ViMo Studio into a low-code industrial vision stack covering data management, model training, visual solution design and production-line deployment, and is sold alongside first-party hardware — industrial smart cameras, barcode readers (VS600/VS800P/VS1000/VS2000), vision sensors (VN2000/VN4000) and lenses — through the SmartMoreInside sub-brand. The company also markets digital platforms (Light3D, Data, Gauge, AIoT) and industrial large models (IndustryGPT, SMore LrMo). SmartMore states it has filed 400+ global patent applications with 200+ granted, served 200+ enterprise customers, and reached unicorn status on a Series B that exceeded USD 200 million in 2021, with R&D and business centers in Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Shanghai, Suzhou, Tokyo, Beijing, Hangzhou and Singapore. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; ViMo model export to an SDK is described in marketing copy but is delivered with the licensed product rather than documented publicly.

providers.name: SOLS Energy
providers.description: SOLS Energy is Malaysia's leading residential and commercial solar energy company, on a mission to make green energy a basic human right. It has completed more than 8,900 solar installations across Malaysia spanning residential (Green Homes), commercial (Green Business), and off-grid indigenous community projects (Green Impact), and also offers EV charging (ChargeSingh) and a Solar Academy apprenticeship program. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass SOLS Energy publishes a consumer marketing website (blog, FAQ, contact, privacy and terms pages) but no public developer platform, API, or developer documentation.

providers.name: SpotHopper
providers.description: SpotHopper is a Milwaukee, Wisconsin based restaurant marketing and web technology company, founded in 2015, selling an all-in-one, AI-assisted platform to independent restaurants and multi-location restaurant groups. The platform bundles restaurant website design and hosting (customer sites are served from the spotapps.co domain), SEO and Google Business Profile syncing, menu / specials / event publishing, automated social posting to Facebook and Instagram, email and SMS campaigns, review generation and reputation management, and link-outs to reservation and ordering partners such as OpenTable, Yelp and UberEats. The company markets itself as powering more than 20,000 restaurants. As of the 2026-08-29 enrichment probe SpotHopper publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Star Catcher
providers.description: Star Catcher is a space technology company building the first power grid in space. Its optical power beaming system, the Star Catcher Network, concentrates and transmits solar energy directly to satellites' existing solar arrays, delivering up to 10x more power without any hardware modifications. Founded in 2024 and backed by Initialized Capital, the company holds a world record for optical power beaming and is working to bring shared orbital power infrastructure to satellites supporting universal connectivity, advanced computing, and national security. Star Catcher raised $65 million in May 2026 and plans to bring its technology to orbit. Star Catcher operates physical space hardware and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Strive Health
providers.description: Strive Health is a Denver-based value-based kidney care company that partners with health systems, nephrologists, and payors to deliver comprehensive care for patients across the kidney disease spectrum, from chronic kidney disease (CKD) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) through dialysis and transplant. Its model combines Population Health care teams, Strive Care Partners (nephrologist-led services), Kidney Heroes nurse-practitioner care teams, and the CareMultiplier machine-learning platform for personalized, predictive treatment planning. Strive reports outcomes including higher optimal dialysis starts, reduced hospitalizations and readmissions, and increased home dialysis adoption. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of NEA and Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Strive Health publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Summer
providers.description: Summer (Summer, PBC) is a financial wellness platform that helps individuals, employers, and government organizations manage student loan debt and education expenses. Summer connects members with 150+ federal and state loan programs to lower monthly payments, pursue loan forgiveness (including Public Service Loan Forgiveness), and build tax-advantaged education savings. It is delivered as an employee benefit and through public programs, offering debt optimization, college cost planning, tuition assistance, tax-favorable direct student-loan contributions, and retirement matching of loan payments. Summer reports over $2B in savings delivered and a 97% member satisfaction rate.

providers.name: Swift Charge
providers.description: Swift Charge is an electric vehicle charging company that provides turn-key, fully managed EV charging infrastructure to property owners across the hospitality, education, and multi-family residential sectors, pairing installed charging hardware with a payment application that lets EV drivers locate and pay for charging sessions. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Swift Charge publishes a public marketing and charger-map website but exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile is limited to company identity plus a domain-security probe of its website host.

providers.name: ThinkSono
providers.description: ThinkSono is a medical technology company that develops AI-powered ultrasound software enabling non-specialist clinicians to detect deep vein thrombosis (DVT) blood clots at the point of care. Its real-time AI guidance walks a clinician through capturing and interpreting a compression ultrasound scan, compressing what is typically a full-day specialist referral pathway into an approximately 30-minute point-of-care assessment. The product is positioned for hospital and primary-care settings (including NHS deployments) to reduce DVT diagnostic waiting times. ThinkSono is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. It is a B2B medical-device software business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Tiger New Energy
providers.description: Tiger New Energy is a Bangladesh-based clean-energy company building a battery-swapping network for electric vehicles, primarily electric rickshaws and motorcycles. Drivers swap depleted lithium batteries for fully charged ones at Tiger swapping stations in seconds instead of waiting to recharge, and a "battery passport" tracks each pack's health and lifecycle. The company operates consumer and partner mobile apps (Tiger Driver, Tiger Partner, Tiger Dealer) on iOS and Android. Tiger New Energy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its mobile apps are backed by private, undocumented services.

providers.name: TradeLink
providers.description: TradeLink is a Munich-based logistics SaaS company building the first collaboration platform for supply chain and inbound/outbound logistics. Its cloud software gives warehouses, suppliers, carriers, and dispatchers a shared system for time-slot (dock) booking, dock and yard management, load-carrier and empties management, driver check-in terminals, and analytics insights, replacing phone and email coordination with real-time, transparent workflows. TradeLink integrates with existing ERP and transport-management systems and serves production, retail, and contract-logistics companies across the DACH region and Europe, with customers including MAN, SPAR, Liebherr, and Emons. It is backed by Insight Partners and Point Nine.

providers.name: Ubiquity6
providers.description: Ubiquity6 was a San Francisco augmented-reality startup ("Capture & Edit Reality") backed by Benchmark, First Round, and Index Ventures. It built Display.land, a multiplayer 3D/AR/VR capture and creation platform, acquired Wavy AR, and was acquired by Discord in June 2021, after which its products were discontinued. Ubiquity6 never published a public API or developer program; its GitHub organization survives as a set of open-source computer vision and React Native forks, and a few internal packages remain on npm under the @ubiquity6 scope.

providers.name: UBQ Materials
providers.description: UBQ Materials is a climate-tech company founded in 2012 that converts unsorted mixed household waste, including organics and hard-to-recycle plastics, into UBQ, a climate-positive thermoplastic material that substitutes for oil-based plastics in manufacturing. A Certified B Corporation backed by Battery Ventures, the company operates a full-scale production facility in Bergen op Zoom, Netherlands (opened 2024) with 80,000 tons of annual capacity, plus an R&D center in Tze'elim, Israel. UBQ Materials publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Venwiz
providers.description: Venwiz is a Bengaluru, India based B2B digital platform for the procurement of industrial and infrastructural project services, covering both CapEx and MRO requirements for the manufacturing sector. Founded in 2020 by Rajesh Reddy and Sandesh Paturi, it operates a marketplace that connects industrial buyers with a verified, pan-India database of service vendors, adding vendor discovery, order expediting, project management tooling and vendor intelligence on top. Backed by Accel and other investors (~$11.4M raised), Venwiz digitises what has traditionally been an offline, relationship-driven industrial services procurement process. No public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDK, or documentation surface is published as of this enrichment pass; the public presence is a marketing/content website plus a login-gated application.

providers.name: Vibe Bio
providers.description: Vibe Bio is a biopharma AI company whose VibeOne platform provides AI decision infrastructure for business development and licensing teams, accelerating therapeutic asset diligence by turning unstructured scientific and clinical data into decision-ready outputs across a source, prioritize, evaluate, and decide workflow. The company also operates a venture fund backing founders developing cures for rare and overlooked diseases. VibeOne is offered as a demo-request enterprise SaaS product; no public API or developer platform is published at this time.

providers.name: Vilya
providers.description: Vilya is a computational drug-design biotechnology company pioneering the de novo design of macrocycles — entirely new therapeutic molecules that do not exist in nature. Spun out of the Institute for Protein Design and built on Nobel Prize-winning computational protein-design research from scientific founder Dr. David Baker, Vilya uses AI-driven generative models to generate, predict, and validate novel, chemically diverse macrocycles in silico. Its pipeline advances orally bioavailable macrocycles that aim to combine the target selectivity of biologics with the convenience of small- molecule pills, opening previously untreatable disease areas across oncology and immunology (including an integrin alpha4beta7 program for IBD). Vilya is a private therapeutics company; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: W. R. Grace
providers.description: W. R. Grace & Co. is a global producer of specialty chemicals and specialty materials, providing catalysts and process technologies to refining, petrochemical, and other manufacturers. Grace operates in two segments: Catalysts Technologies (fluid catalytic cracking catalysts, additives, and process technologies) and Materials Technologies (silica-based engineered materials for pharmaceutical, food, coatings, and industrial applications). Grace's Fine Chemical Manufacturing Services division provides active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) development and manufacturing for the pharmaceutical industry. W. R. Grace does not offer a public developer API for software integration.

providers.name: WeGoWhere
providers.description: WeGoWhere is a consumer social-activity coordination mobile app (originally launched as EatMatch) that helps friends discover what the people around them are doing and join those plans in real life. Available on iOS and Android with more than 700,000 active users, the app centers each hangout on a dedicated group chat for attendees plus high-resolution photo and video sharing, spanning activities such as dining, movies, photography, sports, karaoke, and general socializing. Based in Bangkok, Thailand, the company raised US$1.2M in seed funding in 2023 and is backed by 500 Global. WeGoWhere is a consumer mobile product and does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, or SDK.

providers.name: Widgera
providers.description: Widgera is an AI-native business platform that unifies a company's operations into what it calls "One Adaptive OS." Its AI assistants (branded Aiva) learn a business, automate workflows, build internal apps, and run customer interactions across a suite of modules that includes CRM, Chats, Drive, Analytics, and autonomous Agents. Widgera positions itself as the infrastructure layer powering operations for retail, automotive, hospitality, real estate, and service organizations, with a roster of customers across consumer electronics retail, car service, real estate, and wellness. The company is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Widgera runs a private application backend (api.widgera.com) but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site plus Privacy and Terms pages and homepage-published compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR).

providers.name: 24M
providers.description: 24M Technologies is a battery technology company founded in 2010 out of MIT laboratories and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Rather than manufacturing cells at scale itself, 24M licenses its battery materials, cell architecture and SemiSolid manufacturing platform to energy-storage system integrators, EV battery manufacturers and OEMs worldwide. Its product portfolio spans the Eternalyte electrolyte (ultra-fast charging and low-temperature performance), the Impervio separator (thermal-runaway prevention), the LiForever electrode, the 24M ETOP electrode-to-pack architecture, and 24M production equipment. Partners and corporate investors have included Volkswagen Group, Kyocera, Itochu and FREYR Battery. 24M is a hardware, materials and manufacturing company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: 2U
providers.description: 2U, Inc. is an education technology company, founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lanham, Maryland, that partners with the world's top universities and companies to develop and deliver online education programs — from free open courses to bootcamps, certificates, and credit-bearing master's degrees. In 2021 2U acquired edX, which it operates as its global online learning platform and primary consumer brand, offering thousands of courses across subjects such as artificial intelligence, data science, public health, and business. This profile was seeded from a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio-linked lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline. 2U publishes no first-party developer API on its corporate domain (2u.com); its programmatic and integration surfaces live under the edX / Open edX learning platform, and its engineering work is visible in the 2uinc GitHub organization.

providers.name: ABL Space Systems
providers.description: ABL Space Systems is an American launch vehicle company founded in 2017 by Harry O'Hanley and Dan Piemont, headquartered in El Segundo, California, with operations at the Port of Long Beach, Mojave and Kodiak, Alaska. ABL built RS1, a two-stage, kerosene/liquid-oxygen small satellite launch vehicle designed to deliver 1,350 kg to low Earth orbit and 1,000 kg to sun-synchronous orbit, powered by nine in-house additively manufactured E2 engines on the first stage and one on the second. Its companion GS0 ground system packages an entire orbital launch site into standard shipping containers so a pad can be activated anywhere with a flat concrete surface and moved by land, sea or air. RS1 attempted its first orbital flight from Pacific Spaceport Complex Kodiak in January 2023 and was lost shortly after liftoff; a second vehicle was destroyed during preflight static-fire testing in July 2024. In November 2024 the company announced its exit from the commercial orbital launch market, and in February 2025 it rebranded as Long Wall, refocusing on containerized missile defense — the Cyclops exoatmospheric interceptor, RSX low-cost liquid boosters for flight testing and threat replication, and the Ironwood ground support equipment line. ABL/Long Wall is an aerospace and defense hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, machine-readable API contract or developer portal.

providers.name: Aeterlink
providers.description: Aeterlink Corp. is a Tokyo-headquartered deep-tech company, originating from Stanford University research, that develops, manufactures and sells spatial (microwave) wireless power transfer systems under the AirPlug brand. AirPlug delivers power to battery-free IoT sensors and devices at distances of roughly 15-20 meters with bidirectional data communication, and is sold into factory automation, building management and medical implant applications. Founded in August 2020, the company operates offices in Tokyo, Indianapolis and Bangkok, and is active in the international standardization of spatial wireless power transfer. Aeterlink publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; its product materials are distributed by request form.

providers.name: AI Fund
providers.description: AI Fund is a venture studio founded by Andrew Ng that co-founds and scales AI-powered companies alongside entrepreneurs, venture funds, and corporate partners. Backed by more than $370 million from investors including Sequoia Capital, NEA, Nikkei, and AES, it validates, builds, and scales ventures that tackle real-world problems across emergency response, retail, supply chain, government services, and enterprise productivity. Portfolio companies include Workera, Factored, Workhelix, Profitmind, and IrisGo. AI Fund was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Greylock.

providers.name: AIM Intelligent Machines
providers.description: AIM (AIM Intelligent Machines) is a Redmond, Washington robotics and artificial-intelligence company building autonomous earthmoving for mining, construction and defense. Its plug-and-play retrofit kit converts existing heavy equipment — excavators, bulldozers, haul trucks — into self-operating machines regardless of make, model, size or age, while preserving the OEM warranty, pairing rugged onboard hardware and 360-degree camera-based perception with a tablet-based control interface and a "Site Intelligence" analytics dashboard for remote fleet tasking, terrain mapping and productivity reporting. Founded in 2021 by engineers from Waymo, SpaceX, Google, Tesla, Apple, Microsoft, Trimble and Hexagon, AIM is backed by General Catalyst (partners Quentin Clark and Max Rimpel), Khosla Ventures, DCVC, Human Capital, Ironspring Ventures and Mantis, and has announced a strategic partnership with Komatsu and a LiDAR partnership with Ouster. AIM sells through equipment dealers rather than a self-serve product, and as of this pass publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind — its entire public web surface is eight marketing and legal pages.

providers.name: Air Company
providers.description: Air Company (AIRCO) is a carbon conversion technology company founded in 2017 by Gregory Constantine and Dr. Stafford Sheehan. Its patented Carbon Conversion Reactor mimics photosynthesis, combining captured CO2, water and green hydrogen with renewable energy to produce carbon-negative alcohols and fully formulated synthetic fuels. The company licenses its catalytic process technologies and designs deployable production systems, from the container-scale AIRCO MAD Fuel System to the AIRCO SAF Factory.
