The company has flown automated Cessna 208 Caravan demonstrations including a fully uncrewed take-off and landing in 2023, and is pursuing FAA Part 23 supplemental type certification for its automation system. Reliable Robotics has contracts with the U.S. Air Force AFWERX program and the Defense Innovation Unit to evaluate automated cargo and ISR missions on platforms including the Cessna 208, and has partnered with Textron Aviation on certification work. The company's founders are alumni of SpaceX and Tesla autopilot teams. Reliable Robotics is partner- and government-gated and does not currently offer public consumer or developer APIs.

providers.name: Religion of Sports
providers.description: Religion of Sports is an Emmy Award-winning sports media and entertainment production studio founded in 2017 by Tom Brady, Michael Strahan and Gotham Chopra, headquartered in Santa Monica, California and operating as The Religion of Sports Media, Inc. The company produces premium non-fiction film, documentary series and branded content that examine why sports matter, distributed through Netflix, HBO, Paramount+, ESPN, Apple TV+, Showtime, Fox Sports and NBC Sports, with titles including Simone Biles Rising, In the Arena: Serena Williams, Made for March, 5-Star and Alex vs. ARod. It raised a $50M Series B led by Shamrock Capital in June 2022 to build a non-fiction studio arm and expand into new formats and non-sports categories. Its public surface is a marketing and press site; the company operates no developer program, publishes no API documentation, and exposes no machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Sea Group (Sea Limited)
providers.description: Sea Limited is a Singapore-headquartered consumer internet holding company that operates three core businesses across Southeast Asia, Taiwan, and Latin America: Shopee (e-commerce), Garena (digital entertainment and game publishing), and SeaMoney / Monee (digital financial services including SeaBank, ShopeePay, and SPayLater). Sea Limited is publicly listed on the NYSE (ticker: SE). Sea does not publish a unified group-level developer API — each operating subsidiary maintains its own developer platform: Shopee Open Platform (open.shopee.com) for marketplace integrations, Garena for game-platform partners, and SeaMoney / ShopeePay for in-region payment integrations.

providers.name: Signal Advisors
providers.description: Signal Advisors is a financial technology company building an integrated software platform for independent financial advisors and insurance professionals. The Signal Platform consolidates annuity, life insurance, and wealth management workflows into a single system, replacing the traditional Independent Marketing Organization (IMO) model. Product lines include Signal Annuity (quoting, design, and submission), Signal Wealth (portfolio and compliance management), and Signal Life (life-insurance workflow automation), with features such as real-time carrier status updates (TrueStatus), fast commission payouts (TruePay), AI-generated policy summaries, and integrated householding. The company operates a closed, account-based advisor portal and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Sunfire
providers.description: Sunfire SE is a German hydrogen technology manufacturer headquartered in Dresden, Saxony, with additional sites in Berlin and Solingen. Founded in 2010 by Carl Berninghausen, Christian von Olshausen and Nils Aldag, and converted to a European stock corporation (SE) in 2025, the company builds industrial-scale electrolyzers and power-to-X plants that convert renewable electricity into green hydrogen and synthetic fuels. Its Sunfire-HyLink portfolio spans pressurized alkaline electrolysis (HyLink Alkaline 22 at 10 MW and HyLink Alkaline 23 at 50 MW per module, operating at 30 bar(g)) and high-temperature solid oxide electrolysis (HyLink SOEC, 10 MW modules, a claimed world-record 37.5 kWh/kg H2 efficiency), alongside FEED engineering, project delivery, maintenance and remote data-driven monitoring services. Customers and projects include RWE, Salzgitter, Neste, TotalEnergies, BASF, P2X Solutions, Nordic Ren-Gas and the Bad Lauchstaedt Energy Park. Sunfire is an industrial equipment manufacturer: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Supernal
providers.description: Supernal is the Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) company of Hyundai Motor Group, headquartered in Washington, D.C. with engineering operations in California. Supernal is developing the SA-2, an all-electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft unveiled at CES 2024, designed for short urban and regional trips with a pilot and four passengers, targeting commercial entry later this decade pending FAA Type Certification. Supernal leverages Hyundai Motor Group capabilities in design, manufacturing, batteries, motors, and software, and envisions an integrated AAM ecosystem of vertiports, sky corridors, and last-mile connectivity through robotaxis and rideshare. Supernal is hardware- and ecosystem-focused with no public consumer or developer APIs at this stage.

providers.name: Sware (fka BTR)
providers.description: Sware (formerly BTR) is a life sciences software company providing AI-driven GxP validation for regulated life sciences and pharmaceutical organizations. Its Res_Q SaaS platform combines a decade of validation intelligence with a Data Cloud and AI agents that automate validation work, surface insights, and keep every decision explainable, traceable, and reversible. A companion product, GxPNext, delivers agentic validation built for software development so teams can embed GxP validation directly into their applications, ship faster, and simplify customer audits. Sware serves quality, regulatory, and engineering leaders across software validation, AI/ML validation, plant and equipment validation, and medical device / SaMD development, and publishes SOC 2 and ISO 9001 certifications. It is backed by Insight Partners. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI is available today (the Res_Q API page is password-gated), so this profile captures the company's public identity, compliance posture, and domain-security probe.

providers.name: The Feed
providers.description: The Feed is an online sports nutrition store for endurance athletes, stocking products from more than 300 brands across fuel, hydration, supplements, and recovery. Founded by Matt Johnson while managing a Tour de France cycling team, it sells gels, chews, and drink mixes as single servings so athletes can test products without committing to full boxes, offers AutoShip subscriptions and a Feed First membership, and is the official nutrition partner of USA Triathlon. The company builds personalized fueling plans around before/during/after-workout nutrition, tested with input from over 200,000 athletes. It is a consumer e-commerce brand (Shopify storefront) with no public developer API; its machine-readable surfaces are a published llms.txt and a Google Merchant product feed.

providers.name: The Modern Milkman
providers.description: The Modern Milkman is a UK doorstep delivery service that brings farm-fresh milk, groceries and household essentials to customers in returnable and reusable glass bottles or recyclable packaging, with flexible ordering and early-morning delivery. Founded to modernise the traditional milkround, the company focuses on reducing food waste and single-use plastic through a return-and-reuse model, local sourcing, and a subscription-style ordering experience delivered through its website and mobile apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company publishes no public developer API, but does maintain an llms.txt for AI agents, a customer help centre, and a blog. Sector: consumer / direct-to-consumer grocery delivery.

providers.name: Thrasio
providers.description: Thrasio is a consumer products company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Walpole, Massachusetts, that acquires and operates e-commerce-native consumer brands — principally Amazon marketplace sellers — and then scales them with data science, supply-chain and marketing operations. The company states it is one of Amazon's top five sellers, that its products reach more than 80 million households, and that it sells across 150+ retailers. Thrasio is a brand aggregator and operator rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable specifications, and its own marketplace integrations run over Amazon's Selling Partner API rather than over any Thrasio-published interface.

providers.name: Tradeblock
providers.description: Tradeblock (operated by Astrolab, Inc. d/b/a Tradeblock, founded 2019) is a mobile-first, peer-to-peer sneaker trading marketplace that lets collectors use their sneakers as currency. Members build a Closet and Wishlist, browse a feed of public and private trade offers, and swap sneakers with other collectors, balancing uneven trades with cash. Every trade routes through Tradeblock's authentication centers, where shoes are verified for authenticity before shipping to each party. The service also surfaces supply-and-demand signals for individual sneaker models. Tradeblock is a consumer app (iOS, Android, and web) backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Trinity Ventures, and DCVC; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal at this time.

providers.name: TrademarkNow
providers.description: TrademarkNow is an AI-native trademark clearance, screening, and watching platform, now part of Corsearch. It helps brand owners and legal teams create, launch, and defend trademarks globally using neural-network models that analyze phonetics, spelling, meaning, and visuals to surface conflicts across trademark registries. Its modules include ExaMatch for preliminary screening across 190+ registries with phonetic matching, NameCheck for instant trademark risk assessment, LogoCheck for deep-learning image-based logo conflict clearance, and Portfolio Analyzer for portfolio-strength benchmarking and coverage-gap analysis. TrademarkNow is delivered as a SaaS web platform (login at tm.corsearch.com) and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Translucent AI
providers.description: Translucent AI provides an agentic AI platform that acts as a financial operating system for healthcare organizations, unifying claims, labor, clinical output, P&L, budget and forecast, and contract-economics data to deliver real-time financial visibility and automated root cause analysis for finance and clinical teams. The company raised a $27M Series A led by GV, backed by NEA, Virtue, FPV, and Redesign Health. Translucent AI publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Triomics
providers.description: Triomics is an AI healthcare company focused on oncology workflows, using AI agents to transform unstructured electronic health records into structured, actionable datasets for cancer centers and life sciences organizations. Its products include PRISM (AI-powered clinical trial matching), Symphony (visit preparation), Harmony (registry data curation and abstraction), and OncoLLM, a language model that reads entire patient charts to answer oncology-specific questions. The platform ingests HL7, FHIR, CCDA, PDF, and image formats, integrates with Epic, OncoEMR, iKnowMed, and Cerner, and is approved on the Epic App Marketplace. Triomics is deployed at cancer centers including Memorial Sloan Kettering and Mount Sinai, and raised $22 million backed by Battery Ventures, Lightspeed, Nexus, Y Combinator, and Oncology Ventures. Triomics does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Tyffon
providers.description: Tyffon Inc. is a Japanese immersive entertainment company that combines creativity and technology to deliver memorable XR experiences. The studio builds VR, AR, and mixed-reality attractions - including Corridor, Kaiju Haven VR, Floria, and Island Mirrorge MR - operates the Tyffonium attraction brand, licenses its XR content to entertainment venues across Japan, and released the GARA AR platform app. A Techstars portfolio company, Tyffon publishes no public developer portal or API surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: UK Government Open Data
providers.description: UK Government Open Data is a national government open-data portal for United Kingdom running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 57,791 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Upscale AI
providers.description: Upscale AI is a pure-play AI networking infrastructure company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, founded by industry veterans from Palo Alto Networks, Marvell, Cisco, and Google and led by CEO Barun Kar. The company builds a full-stack, open-standards AI fabric spanning silicon, systems, and software — its SkyHammer scale-up ASIC architecture and NVIDIA Spectrum-X/SONiC-based scale-out Ethernet systems connect accelerators, memory, and storage for large-scale AI training and inference. Backed by Mayfield among others (Premji Invest, NVIDIA, Salesforce Ventures, Temasek, Tiger Global), it has raised $500M total at a $2B valuation. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface surface beyond a Webflow-served llms.txt; it sells networking hardware and software evaluated by hyperscalers and neoclouds.

providers.name: Vestwell
providers.description: Vestwell is a New York City-based digital savings and retirement platform (founded 2016) that powers workplace savings programs for employers, financial advisors, financial institutions, TPAs, PEOs, payroll and benefit partners, and government agencies. Its recordkeeping and administration engine supports traditional and Safe Harbor 401(k), Solo-k, Starter-k, pooled/PEP plans, 403(b), 529 education savings, ABLE, emergency savings, student-loan repayment, and tuition reimbursement, as well as state-facilitated ("government savings") retirement programs. Vestwell emphasizes payroll and HR integrations (auto-sync across 190+ payroll providers) rather than a public developer API; onboarding, servicing, and saver access run through its web platform. Surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company and profiled here for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Wiser
providers.description: Wiser Solutions is a retail and commerce intelligence company that provides pricing, market, and MAP (minimum advertised price) intelligence to brands and retailers. Its platform collects online and in-store data, tracking billions of products daily across hundreds of thousands of stores, to power price optimization, competitive price monitoring, promotion and assortment tracking, review analytics, and unauthorized-seller enforcement. Wiser serves hundreds of brands and large retailers and integrates with major eCommerce platforms and marketplaces. As of this profile Wiser publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; integrations are delivered through its platform, dashboards, and partner connectors.

providers.name: World 50 Group
providers.description: World 50 Group is an invitation-only membership community for CEOs, board directors, and C-suite executives from the world's largest and most respected companies. It runs highly curated peer communities organized by role (General Counsel 50, Procurement 50, Human Resource 50, President 50, Innovating 50, and more), the NEXT executive-development platform (Next Director, Next Leader, Next Generation Leadership), and publishes C-suite insights and impact research. Membership is by invitation; members access the community through the World 50 iOS/Android app. The company publishes no public developer program or API surface.

providers.name: 5miles
providers.description: 5miles is a hyper-local mobile marketplace for buying and selling used goods — cars, furniture, electronics, fashion, baby and kids items — and for offering local services such as beauty, auto repair and home cleaning. Founded in 2014 in Dallas, Texas by Lucas Lu and acquired by a China-based buyer in 2020, the company runs the 5miles iOS and Android apps, the 5miles.com web marketplace, and the 5miles Dash bidding site. 5miles operates as an end-user consumer product only: it publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable specification, and its api.5miles.com host serves the company's own mobile and web clients rather than third-party integrators.

providers.name: Accompany Health
providers.description: Accompany Health is a value-based healthcare company that delivers integrated in-home and virtual care to patients with complex, chronic conditions, primarily those covered by Medicaid and Medicare. Its multidisciplinary care teams combine primary care, behavioral health, and social care, wrapping medical treatment with support for the social drivers of health. The company operates in Massachusetts, Michigan (Detroit), and Colorado (Denver), works with health plans and providers, and is HIPAA compliant. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IVP and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing and patient-education website but no public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Admitkard
providers.description: AdmitKard is a Noida, India based study-abroad EdTech company, founded in 2016 by IIT-IIM alumni Piyush Bhartiya and Rachit Agrawal, that guides Indian students through the full overseas-education journey: university and course shortlisting, profile building, test preparation, applications, SOP/LOR support, scholarships, education loans, foreign-exchange remittance, student visas and accommodation. The company is an ICEF-accredited and AIRC-certified agency and raised a Rs 50 crore (about $6M) Series A led by GSV Ventures in 2023. It sells counselling services to students and universities rather than a developer product: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract, and its api.admitkard.com host answers with a Cloudflare 522 origin timeout.

providers.name: Angitia Biopharmaceuticals
providers.description: Angitia Biopharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2018, headquartered at 3027 Townsgate Road, Westlake Village, California, with research and development operations in Guangzhou, China. It discovers and develops biologic therapeutics for serious musculoskeletal diseases, including osteoporosis, osteogenesis imperfecta, bone metastasis, osteoarthritis and muscle disorders. Its clinical pipeline is led by AGA2118 and AGA2115, bispecific antibodies targeting sclerostin and DKK1, alongside AGA111 in lumbar interbody fusion. The company closed a $120 million Series C financing in December 2024 led by Bain Capital Life Sciences. Angitia is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, machine-readable specification, or technology platform of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is an XML sitemap and a robots.txt carrying Cloudflare-managed Content-Signal directives that reserve AI training rights.

providers.name: Anique
providers.description: Anique Inc. is a Japan‑based company that maximizes the value of intellectual property and brands through both real‑world and digital experiences. It operates Anique Shop, Anique Museum, AR and digital collection services, creating limited‑edition merchandise and virtual exhibitions that connect creators with global fans. The company emphasizes creative content, IP‑driven experiences, and supports creators in both physical and digital realms.

providers.name: Apollo Agriculture
providers.description: Apollo Agriculture is an agricultural technology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, that helps small-scale farmers across Africa maximize their profits. Apollo delivers a full-stack service bundling quality farm inputs (seed and fertilizer), flexible input financing and credit, satellite- and machine-learning-driven agronomic advice, crop insurance, and market access, distributed through a network of local agrodealers and mobile technology. The company serves smallholder farmers in markets including Kenya and Zambia and is backed by investors including Anthemis and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile tracks Apollo Agriculture as a company in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API has been identified at this time.

providers.name: AppliedVR
providers.description: AppliedVR is a virtual reality therapeutics company that combines immersive technology with proven cognitive behavioral and behavioral-science techniques to treat medical conditions, with a focus on chronic pain. Its lead product, RelieVRx, is the first FDA-authorized prescription VR device for chronic lower back pain, delivering automated, self-administered cognitive behavioral therapy in the patient's home. AppliedVR also offers the SustainVR and ITx immersive therapeutics platform and the AVR Pathway patient-support system, and validates its products through clinical academic research. The company operates as a regulated digital-therapeutics / medical-device business rather than a developer-facing API platform, so it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Aragen Life Sciences
providers.description: Aragen Life Sciences provides contract research, development, and manufacturing services (CRDMO) for small and large molecule drug discovery and development. The company offers integrated solutions across chemistry, biology, analytical development, and GMP manufacturing, supporting clients from early discovery through commercial production. Their platform includes scientific expertise, global locations, and a resource hub for investors and partners.

providers.name: Arden
providers.description: Arden (Arden AI, Inc.) is an AI-native platform for internal audit and SOX compliance teams, backed by Y Combinator and based in San Francisco. Arden builds AI agents that automatically pull evidence from a company's stack, run end-to-end SOX ITGC and business-process control (BPC) testing, follow up with control owners, and produce reviewer-ready workpapers that external auditors will accept - work that historically ran on spreadsheets and screenshots over weeks. The platform advertises read-only access by default with approval gates before any system writes, integrations across 20+ enterprise systems (Workday, Okta, NetSuite, and others), full-population or sample-based control testing with exception flagging, and full traceability from each conclusion back to the source evidence. Arden targets regulated, compliance-critical institutions performing automated SOX 404(a) testing. Arden does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead and will be enriched further as a public API surface emerges.

providers.name: Artory
providers.description: Artory provides a secure, immutable ledger for recording and verifying the provenance of high‑value assets such as fine art, collectibles, and real estate. By combining blockchain‑based technology with data science, Artory enables collectors, dealers, and institutions to maintain a trusted record of ownership, transaction history, and valuation. The platform supports asset‑level data integration, secure document storage, and API access for partners to query and update asset records, fostering transparency and confidence in the secondary market.

providers.name: Ascena Retail Group
providers.description: Ascena Retail Group was a specialty apparel retailer that operated multiple women's and tween-girl clothing brands through retail stores, outlets, and e-commerce. The company operated brands including Ann Taylor, LOFT, Lane Bryant, Catherines, Cacique, and others. Ascena filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in July 2020 and sold off its brands. Ann Taylor and LOFT were acquired by Sycamore Partners in 2020 and continue to operate. Lane Bryant and Catherines were also sold to new owners. The company did not expose a public developer API during its operation. Current API resources, if any, exist under the successor brand owners.

providers.name: Audiomob
providers.description: Audiomob is an in-game and in-app audio advertising platform that lets mobile game and app publishers monetize their titles with non-interruptive, skippable and rewarded audio ads while advertisers reach engaged gaming audiences at scale. Publishers integrate through the Audiomob Unity plugin or native iOS and Android SDKs (plus a community React Native adapter), add their games to the Audiomob developer dashboard, and configure ad units, an Ad Availability API, and server-to-server webhooks for reward and event tracking. The platform is Open Measurement (IAB Tech Lab) compliant, supports consent management via OneTrust and Sourcepoint, exposes Impression Level Revenue Data (ILRD), and integrates with mediation partners such as AdMob and LevelPlay (MAX) and mobile measurement partners including Adjust, Singular and Tenjin. The current SDK line is SDK 10. Audiomob is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: AutoTrac
providers.description: AutoTrac is a Brazilian fleet management and vehicle tracking technology company with over 30 years of experience. As the national market leader, AutoTrac provides satellite and cellular fleet tracking solutions, real-time telemetry, driver journey management, and management intelligence platforms for logistics, agriculture, maritime, and insurance sectors. The company operates its own terrestrial satellite communication station and data center for nationwide coverage.

providers.name: Beni
providers.description: Beni is a global employee benefits consulting and solutions provider, offering technology-driven services that deliver below-market renewals, strategic benefits solutions, and innovative health plans. The company focuses on real relationships and best-in-class technology to help employers manage fiduciary risk and improve employee satisfaction across multiple industries.

providers.name: Betterhalf
providers.description: Betterhalf is an Indian matchmaking and matrimony mobile application that helps users find genuine and verified profiles for marriage. The app offers in‑app purchases, extensive profile verification, and a focus on Indian cultural preferences. It is available on Android via the Google Play Store and emphasizes privacy and secure matchmaking for its users.

providers.name: BetterNight
providers.description: BetterNight is a San Diego, California virtual-care sleep health company that diagnoses and treats obstructive sleep apnea end to end: telemedicine consults with sleep physicians, home sleep testing devices shipped to the patient, board-certified interpretation and therapy recommendation, home delivery of PAP and oral appliance therapy, and ongoing coaching by sleep specialists and respiratory therapists. It also offers a cognitive behavioral therapy program for insomnia and remote patient monitoring of PAP adherence. The company sells to individuals as well as to physicians, cardiologists, ENT practices, clinics, health plans and ACOs, employers, and DOT/commercial transportation programs. It reports roughly 300 sleep health professionals, Joint Commission accreditation held for over 15 years, and SOC 2 Type II compliance, and in 2026 acquired Coastal Sleep Diagnostics and Epoch Sleep Centers. BetterNight is a healthcare services operator, not an API platform: it publishes no developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Beyond Math
providers.description: BeyondMath is an AI company that has built what it calls the world's first foundational AI model of physics. Its Generative Physics Engine runs full-fidelity, engineering-grade simulations covering fluid, thermal, and structural analysis directly from uploaded geometry, without pre-meshing or preprocessing, and returns results up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD/FEA solvers while generalizing across unseen geometries without retraining. The platform lets engineering teams explore thousands of design variations in minutes rather than months across automotive, aerospace, energy, defense, semiconductor, construction, telecommunications, and electronics. Founded by Alan Patterson (CEO) and Darren Garvey (CTO), the company raised an $18.5M seed round and partners with NVIDIA and AWS. Access is gated behind a waitlist for the Generative Physics Studio; on-premise and private-cloud enterprise deployment is offered. No public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI is published at this time.

providers.name: Biohmhealth
providers.description: BIOHM Health provides probiotic supplements, super greens powders, and colon cleanse products aimed at healing leaky gut and supporting a healthy microbiome. The company operates an e‑commerce storefront offering gut‑testing kits, wellness consultations, and a rewards program for customers seeking digestive health solutions.

providers.name: Blink Health
providers.description: Blink Health is a healthcare technology company that operates BlinkRx, a digital pharmacy platform connecting patients, prescribers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers to simplify prescription access, fulfillment, and affordability. The platform streamlines the path from a provider writing a prescription to a patient receiving medication at a transparent price, with copay support, home delivery, and manufacturer-sponsored programs. Backed by 8vc, Blink Health runs consumer-facing prescription-savings tools and a provider/pharma-facing BlinkRx offering. No public developer API program or documentation was found during enrichment; a live undocumented API host exists at api.blinkhealth.com.

providers.name: BlockSpaces
providers.description: BlockSpaces provides a Bitcoin-native collateral and risk management platform for financial institutions. It offers the ARCC infrastructure that automates contract enforcement, enabling banks and credit unions to offer Bitcoin-backed loans, forwards, and structured products with deterministic settlement. The platform includes APIs for digital asset readiness, collateral management, and integration with existing financial systems, targeting the institutional finance market.

providers.name: BlossomHill Therapeutics
providers.description: BlossomHill Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2020 by drug designer J. Jean Cui, Ph.D. and biotech operator Y. Peter Li, Ph.D., M.B.A. It develops intelligently designed small-molecule medicines for oncology and autoimmune disease, led by BH-30643, a first-in-class macrocyclic non-covalent mutant-selective OMNI-EGFR inhibitor for EGFR- and HER2-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, and BH-30236, a macrocyclic CLK inhibitor for relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia and higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome. The company is a drug discovery business, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: BlueRock Therapeutics
providers.description: BlueRock Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing transformative cell therapies for neurodegenerative and ophthalmic diseases. Leveraging advanced stem cell technologies, the company aims to address unmet medical needs in Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, and retinal disorders, advancing candidates through preclinical and clinical stages to bring innovative treatments to patients.

providers.name: Booosttechnologies
providers.description: Booost Technologies is a Japanese sustainability‑focused enterprise software company offering the Booost Sustainability ERP platform. The platform helps organizations integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) data into their operations, driving scalable growth and net‑zero initiatives across more than 95 countries. With multilingual support and a global client base, Booost delivers a comprehensive suite for sustainability reporting, risk management, and value creation.

providers.name: Bountyjobs
providers.description: BountyJobs is a recruiting marketplace and extended workforce platform that connects employers with over 14,000 vetted search firms, independent recruiters, and provides a purpose‑built Vendor Management System (VMS). It offers solutions for recruiting, contracting, SOW projects, and contingent talent, with integrated analytics, compliance, and a single‑contract, single‑invoice workflow for both employers and agencies.

providers.name: C-Infinity
providers.description: C-Infinity is a Mountain View, California company founded in 2023 that builds foundational AI for mechanical design and manufacturing — AI that reasons about geometry, motion, spatial constraints, and production logic. Its platform, AutoAssembler, connects directly to existing CAD and PLM environments to automate assembly process planning, accelerate engineering change order (ECO) reviews, and generate production-ready assembly work instructions, compressing work that historically took weeks into minutes. The product is described by the company as API-first, with an integration layer that connects upstream to engineering systems and downstream to production, but as of July 2026 C-Infinity publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition — the AutoAssembler application is gated behind a request-a-demo flow and integration is arranged directly with the company. C-Infinity raised a $16M round in April 2026 led by Canaan Partners, with participation from Inventus Capital, Bee Partners, and Radius Capital, and reports deployments across Global Fortune 100 manufacturers as well as small and mid-sized enterprises.

providers.name: Cadence Bank
providers.description: Cadence Bank is a regional U.S. commercial bank headquartered in Tupelo, Mississippi and Houston, Texas, formed in October 2021 when legacy Cadence Bancorporation merged into BancorpSouth Bank (the surviving entity, subsequently renamed Cadence Bank; NYSE ticker CADE). It is a Mississippi state-chartered bank operating roughly 400+ branches across the U.S. South, Midwest, and Texas with about $48-50 billion in assets, offering consumer banking, mortgages, home equity, credit cards, small business and commercial banking, treasury management, and wealth/insurance services. On open finance, Cadence Bank exposes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), which is the honest, prevailing posture for most U.S. regional banks. No documented direct FDX (Financial Data Exchange) membership or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access API was found as of this profile.

providers.name: Cardiointelligence
providers.description: Cardiointelligence (株式会社カルディオインテリジェンス) is a Japanese health‑tech company developing AI‑powered medical devices for cardiac diagnostics. Founded in 2019, it creates AI‑driven ECG analysis tools to support cardiologists, improve arrhythmia detection, and make heart‑disease care more accessible worldwide. The firm collaborates with clinicians and AI specialists, offering explainable AI solutions and pursuing innovative diagnostics for early detection and treatment of cardiovascular conditions.

providers.name: Cavco Industries
providers.description: Cavco Industries, Inc. (Nasdaq: CVCO), founded in Phoenix, Arizona in 1965, designs and builds factory-built housing — manufactured homes, modular homes, park model RVs and vacation cabins — at more than twenty plants across the United States, sold through independent and company-owned retailers under the Cavco family of brands (including Fleetwood Homes and Palm Harbor Homes), with financing through its CountryPlace Mortgage subsidiary and homeowner insurance through Standard Casualty. It is a Fortune 1000 home builder, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK or webhook surface. Its only integration property is a login-gated Angular retailer portal (CavConnect, cavconnect.cavco.com) whose backend host is not publicly resolvable. The developer.cavco.com and api.cavco.com hosts an earlier profile scaffolded do not exist in DNS and were removed from this record.

providers.name: Cerebriai
providers.description: Cerebriai provides a trusted digital workforce powered by AI for travel & expense (T&E) management and procurement. Their platform offers AI agents that automate expense reporting, hotel sourcing, and custom AI solutions for enterprises, delivering frictionless T&E processes, data-driven decision making, and scalable digital employees. The company focuses on integrating AI into business workflows to improve efficiency and reduce manual effort across procurement and travel operations.

providers.name: Compareasiagroup
providers.description: CompareAsiaGroup, now operating as MoneyHero Group, is an Asia‑focused personal finance comparison platform offering users the ability to compare credit cards, loans, insurance and savings products across Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan and the Philippines. The company runs multiple brands and serves millions of users, providing tools, content and partnerships to help consumers make informed financial decisions.

providers.name: Dealertrack
providers.description: Dealertrack is a Cox Automotive brand providing automotive dealership software - a cloud-based Dealer Management System (DMS), digital contracting and F&I tools, and the largest dealer-to-lender credit application network in the United States. Its developer surface is partner-gated. Dealership systems integrate through the Opentrack third-party integration program (real-time, bidirectional REST access to DMS data such as vehicles, customers, deals, repair orders, parts, and general ledger) and through the Cox Automotive Integration Platform partner storefront at developer.coxautoinc.com (OAuth-secured, partner onboarding required). Dealertrack publishes no open, self-service public API; access requires Opentrack certification and annual fees, integration through a certified Opentrack partner, or a Cox Automotive partner agreement. The endpoints described here are modeled from public product and program documentation, not from an open API reference.

providers.name: Denta
providers.description: Denta is a San Francisco-based dental practice management and automation platform, founded by Jack Beecher (Jack Beecher LLC, dba Denta) and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). Positioned as "the dental practice that runs itself," Denta embeds AI into dental organizations to automate back-office operations: it ingests fragmented data from a practice's existing software, provides analytics so dentists can understand their business, and runs in the background to handle administrative work such as insurance payment posting. Its roadmap includes all-in-one native practice management software and an "autonomous dental practice." As of this profile Denta publishes a marketing site, a blog, and login and legal pages, but no public developer portal, API, or OpenAPI surface has been located.

providers.name: Doctolib
providers.description: Doctolib is a European e-health company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Levallois-Perret, France, operating across France, Germany, Italy and the Netherlands. It provides an online medical appointment-booking platform and practice-management software used by patients and by hundreds of thousands of healthcare professionals and facilities. Its product surface spans appointment booking, telehealth/video consultation, patient messaging, clinical software, patient billing, and the Doctolib Connect integration and single-sign-on layer. Doctolib exposes a partner/integration API via an authentication-gated developer portal (developers.doctolib.com); it publishes an RFC 9116 security.txt and runs a public YesWeHack bug-bounty program, an Atlassian Statuspage, and an open-source GitHub organization, but does not publish a public OpenAPI specification, first-party API SDK, or hosted MCP server.

providers.name: End Game Interactive
providers.description: End Game Interactive, Inc. (ENDGAME) is a Bellevue, Washington video game studio founded by Yang C. Liu and Luke Zbihlyj that builds free-to-play, cross-platform real-time multiplayer titles for browser, mobile and desktop — including ZombsRoyale.io, Zombs.io, Spinz.io, BOPZ.io, Fishington, Betrayal, Super Squad, Match City Puzzle and Fate Arena. The studio describes itself as technology-driven, running small agile teams against a proprietary "ENDGAME ENGINE" alongside Unity and Unreal, with AI-assisted pipelines for asset creation, animation, sound design and voicelines. It raised a $3M seed round in 2020 from Makers Fund, Supercell, Kevin Lin and Scooter Braun among others. ENDGAME is a consumer game publisher: as of this profile it operates no public developer program, no documented API, and no machine-readable contract on any of its web properties.

providers.name: Everyday Health
providers.description: Everyday Health is a consumer health media brand founded in 2002 and the flagship property of Everyday Health Group, a division of Ziff Davis (NASDAQ: ZD). The group operates a portfolio of consumer, pregnancy-and-parenting and healthcare-professional brands — Everyday Health, BabyCenter, What to Expect, MedPage Today, Castle Connolly, Diabetes Daily, DailyOM, Lose It!, Migraine Again, theSkimm, HealthCentral and Emma's Diary — and sells pharma commercialization, digital health and wellness, and provider solutions to life sciences companies, hospitals, health systems and clinicians. It is a publisher and advertising business, not an API platform: there is no developer portal, no public API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no SDKs and no hosted MCP or agent surface on any Everyday Health host. This API Evangelist profile captures what the company does publish programmatically — a sitemap index, one public RSS/Media RSS content feed, an auth-gated AWS API Gateway host at api.everydayhealth.com, and an unusually explicit robots.txt that blocks 107 named AI and agent crawlers site-wide while carving out two commercial product-review URLs.

providers.name: Evozyne
providers.description: Evozyne is an AI-native protein therapeutics company founded in 2020 by Paragon Biosciences and headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. It combines generative machine learning with directed evolution and high-throughput biology to design de novo proteins — which it brands Natural Machines — and advance them as engineered protein therapeutics for immune-mediated diseases. The platform pairs AI protein design with wet-lab build-and-test cycles, and the company has collaborated with NVIDIA on model work and with the Gates Foundation on sustainability applications. Evozyne is a drug-discovery organization rather than a software vendor: it publishes a corporate website, a pipeline page, scientific publications and news, but no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Exactera
providers.description: Exactera is a corporate tax technology and advisory company that pairs AI-powered software with expert tax professionals to help multinational corporations manage the full corporate tax lifecycle. Its SaaS platform and services span transfer pricing compliance and benchmarking, R&D tax credits, fixed-asset depreciation, indirect (sales and use) tax advisory, tax provision, and the RoyaltyStat royalty-rate and transfer-pricing data platform. Exactera automates documentation, benchmarking studies, and regulatory reporting so tax and finance teams can reduce audit exposure and meet global compliance requirements. Backed by Insight Partners, the company serves enterprise tax departments and advisory firms worldwide.

providers.name: Feel Therapeutics
providers.description: Feel Therapeutics, an IQVIA business, is a Digital Precision Medicine company on a mission to reinvent how mental health is diagnosed, managed and cared for by bringing objective data, continuous passive measurement and novel digital biomarkers into mental healthcare. Rather than relying on episodic, subjective self-reported questionnaires, Feel develops digital biomarkers from wearable and passive sensor data to enable continuous, objective monitoring. Its solutions span the Feel Digital Precision Medicine Platform (DPMP), Feel DTx precision digital therapeutics, drug-plus / beyond-the-pill programs, and a wearable monitoring device. The company partners with pharma and biotech to advance clinical development, real-world evidence (RWE), and commercialization strategies, and has run 20+ research studies with 3000+ participants.

providers.name: Freeform
providers.description: Freeform is an AI-native advanced manufacturing company founded by former SpaceX engineers, building a network of autonomous factories that sense, learn, predict, and control metal formation for high-performance metal additive manufacturing (metal 3D printing). Freeform integrates hardware, sensors, controls, and software to move parts from prototype to full-scale production for aerospace, defense, aviation, advanced energy, consumer electronics, and automotive customers. It is a physical-AI / advanced-manufacturing business rather than a software API platform, so as of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Gesund
providers.description: Gesund.ai is a governance and validation platform for regulated clinical AI, providing infrastructure to build, validate, deploy, monitor, and update medical AI models across regulatory jurisdictions and stakeholders. Its offerings include an AI CRO (contract research organization) delivering independent validation studies for medical AI models, an AI Factory to accelerate in-house model R&D cycles, and a free Validation Hub for testing models against real-world clinical data. Backed by 500 Global and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company focuses on inspection-ready evidence and FDA/QMSR-aligned regulatory compliance for clinical AI teams. The platform is delivered through a hosted web application and currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Helio AI
providers.description: Helio AI LLC operates Helio.AI, an AI-powered recruiting and applicant tracking (ATS) platform for HR and talent-acquisition teams. It automates the end-to-end hiring workflow — job posting and distribution, resume screening, candidate tracking, real-time analytics, and team collaboration — and pairs the ATS with a gamified personality test to evaluate candidates. The product is offered in multiple languages (English, Russian, Georgian, Armenian, Azerbaijani, and Uzbek) and targets markets across Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Uzbekistan. Helio AI is backed by 500 Global. The company runs its customer application at app.helio-ai.com and does not currently publish a public developer API program or documentation.

providers.name: J Hilburn
providers.description: J.Hilburn is a Dallas, Texas based direct-to-consumer custom menswear brand founded in 2007. It designs and sells made-to-measure suits, shirts, trousers, polos and outerwear through a network of roughly 1,000 independent personal stylists and a small number of studio spaces rather than traditional retail stores. Its public technology surface is consumer- and stylist-facing rather than developer-facing: a catalog and checkout storefront at jhilburn.com, a stylist recruiting and training site at stylist.jhilburn.com, and two iOS applications, J.Hilburn Stylist and J.Hilburn VMA (Virtual Measuring App). J.Hilburn publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API description; the only API surfaces evident from the public web are private, undocumented internal endpoints that the company's own robots.txt disallows crawlers from reaching.

providers.name: Jargon
providers.description: Jargon is a platform for Domain Driven Design for APIs and Enterprise Data Modelling. It provides text-based modelling, template-based API design, real-time validation, version control with breaking change detection, and generation of artifacts including JSON Schema, OpenAPI specifications, and JSON-LD. Jargon supports DevOps-driven collaborative modelling for teams designing and governing domains at enterprise scale.

providers.name: Kartable
providers.description: Kartable is a French online education platform (edtech) delivering standards-aligned learning for students from primary through secondary school (CE1 to Terminale, ages 6-18). It provides more than 1,000 course summaries, thousands of corrected exercises, and quizzes across 16 subjects including mathematics, French, history, physics, and languages, authored by teachers from the French Education Ministry. Its "Alfa" AI tutor answers questions 24/7, generates custom quizzes from photos of coursework, and guides students through homework, while parents follow progress from a dedicated dashboard. Kartable is a consumer subscription product (from EUR 7.99/month) and does not publish a public developer API. Backed by Partech.

providers.name: Kinect
providers.description: Kinect (Kinect AI, Inc.) is an AI revenue platform for direct-to-consumer brands, built around two products that share one brand intelligence: an AI sales rep that converses with shoppers on a brand's own site — grounded in the full catalog, policies, and reviews, selling in the brand's voice and guiding each visitor to the right product — and an agent-ready storefront that makes the brand legible and buyable to external AI (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and emerging buyer agents). Kinect exposes its brand-agent surface through the open Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) at /.well-known/ucp, advertising an MCP shopping service with catalog search and lookup capabilities, and maintains agent-native discovery documents (llms.txt, agents.md, ai-instructions). The company is white-glove and same-day to onboard, measures every deployment behind an A/B split, and is a Y Combinator company (P26) headquartered in San Francisco. Founded by Kratik Agrawal (CEO) and Varun Kandula (CTO).

providers.name: Komprise
providers.description: Komprise is an unstructured data management company whose Intelligent Data Management platform analyzes, tiers, migrates and governs file and object data across NAS, cloud and object storage. The platform spans Komprise Analysis, Elastic Data Migration, Transparent Move Technology, Smart Data Workflows, the Global Metadatabase Service, KAPPA Data Services and Transparent File Tables, giving enterprises a single metadata layer for discovery, classification, sensitive-data detection, ransomware-attack-surface reduction, intelligent tiering and AI data preparation. Komprise publishes an llms.txt bot-access and content policy at www.komprise.com/llms.txt, but its product documentation portal at docs.komprise.com is authentication-gated and no public REST API reference, OpenAPI description, SDK or package was found on any public registry as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Lila Sciences
providers.description: Lila Sciences is an AI company founded in 2023 that is building what it calls Scientific Superintelligence: an autonomous system that runs the scientific method end to end by generating hypotheses, designing experiments, executing them in physical AI Science Factories (autonomous robotic laboratory networks), and learning from the resulting experimental data. Rather than training on internet text, Lila trains a scientific reasoning model on experimental data, coupling it to scalable verifiers and instruments such as molecular dynamics simulators, protein structure predictors, quantum chemistry solvers, and gene editors, then optimizing the policy with reinforcement learning. The company packages this as two commercial offerings: Catalyst, positioned as an operating system for science that accelerates an organization's existing research, and Creation, a partnership model for generating new discoveries, launching products, and founding new companies. Lila works across therapeutics (mRNA, proteins, antibodies, cell therapies, small molecules), advanced materials, chemicals, energy and environment, oil and gas, aerospace and defense, and biotech. It has raised roughly $550M ($200M seed announced March 2025 and a $350M Series A closed in October 2025) from investors including General Catalyst and NVIDIA, at a reported valuation above $1.3B, and collaborates with NVIDIA on the BioNeMo Agent Toolkit. Lila operates from Cambridge MA, San Francisco CA, and London UK. As of this profile Lila publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this entry is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lumilens
providers.description: Lumilens is a San Jose, California photonics company building optical interconnect silicon for AI data centers. Founded in 2024 by Ankur Singla (previously Contrail Systems and Volterra) with Ted Schmidt, Samuel Liu, Ritesh Kapahi and Dave Friedman, it designs co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO) devices that let hyperscalers replace copper interconnect with fiber at 800Gb/s, 1.6Tb/s and beyond, attacking the connectivity bottleneck that now limits GPU cluster scaling more than compute does. The company emerged from stealth in August 2026 with more than $900M raised — including a $700M Series C at a $5.51B valuation led by Atreides Management, Bain Capital Ventures, Meritech, Seligman Ventures and Spark Capital — and says it is already shipping production optical interconnect into hyperscale AI data centers under a multi-billion-dollar customer agreement. Its product is physical silicon sold direct to a small set of very large buyers; as of this profile it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind, and lumilens.com is still an interim recruiting and news site.

providers.name: Mint House
providers.description: Mint House is a US residential-hospitality operator founded in 2017 by Will Lucas that runs tech-enabled apartment-hotel units — full kitchens, workspaces and app-based check-in — in downtown districts of markets including New York, Miami, Nashville, Dallas, Washington DC, Houston, Phoenix and Madison. It raised a $35M Series B in May 2022 led by Mohari Hospitality with Revolution Ventures, Allegion Ventures and Ingleside Investors. In January 2026 Mint House entered an all-equity strategic combination with Kasa; the portfolio now operates as "Mint House by Kasa" and every corporate page on minthouse.com redirects to kasa.com. Mint House is a hospitality operator, not a software vendor: it publishes a consumer booking site and no public API, SDK, webhook or developer program of any kind.

providers.name: Moonhub
providers.description: Moonhub is an AI recruiting platform that deploys proprietary AI agents to source, qualify, engage, and vet candidates across millions of profiles, helping companies hire faster and more cost-effectively. Its agent products (Qualify AI, Engage AI, and Monitor AI) automatically identify qualified candidates, run outreach to convert them into interview-ready applicants, and analyze candidate intent to manage recruiter handoffs. Moonhub is backed by Khosla Ventures, GV, Greycroft, Time Ventures, and AIX Ventures; the Moonhub team joined Salesforce in 2026. The company ships a recruiter web application (recruiter.moonhub.ai) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this profiling.

providers.name: MyARC Fitness
providers.description: MyARC (operated by Vert Analytics Limited) is an all-in-one platform that lets fitness creators and coaches scale their business without writing code. Coaches use MyARC to launch a branded mobile app, automate AI-personalized workout and meal plans for thousands of members at once, run challenges and 1-on-1 coaching, build community, and earn recurring subscription revenue. The consumer-facing MyARC Fitness app ships on iOS and Android with progress tracking and accountability features. As of this profile MyARC exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface — it is a creator-facing SaaS and mobile product, not an API provider. Offices in London, New York, Melbourne, and India.

providers.name: Nexiu
providers.description: Nexiu (Nexiu AI LLC) is a Latin America-focused recruiting automation platform that uses AI agents to source, contact, screen, and schedule high-volume candidates over the official WhatsApp Business API, integrating with Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Meet) and existing ATS systems and job boards. It offers a fully managed pay-per-hire service (Nexiu Managed) and a self-service SaaS platform (Nexiu Platform) for internal talent-acquisition teams, and is backed by 500 Global (500 Latam) and NVIDIA Inception. As of this pass Nexiu consumes third-party APIs (WhatsApp Business, Google, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI) but does not publish a public developer API of its own.

providers.name: Northwood Space
providers.description: Northwood Space is an El Segundo, California ground-infrastructure company for the space industry, founded in 2022 by Bridgit Mendler (CEO), Griffin Cleverly (CTO), and Shaurya Luthra. It designs and delivers rapidly deployable satellite ground stations built on electronically steerable phased-array antennas that track many satellites at once with no moving parts, paired with software ("Portal") that orchestrates every contact, automates scheduling, and moves data from spacecraft to customer. Northwood aims to turn ground infrastructure into cloud-like, on-demand global capacity for defense and commercial operators. The company's software stack is described as developer-oriented with modern APIs and integration hooks, but it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Founders Fund, Washington Harbour Partners, and Alpine Space Ventures; raised a $100M Series B and won a $50M Space Force contract in early 2026.

providers.name: nPlan
providers.description: nPlan applies machine learning to construction project schedules to forecast and de-risk large capital projects. Trained on a large corpus of historical project schedules, its products (nPlan Insights Pro and nPlan Portfolio) analyze programme risk, benchmark schedules against similar projects, and surface the interventions most likely to keep delivery on time and on budget, with a Power BI integration for portfolio-level project controls. nPlan is a private enterprise SaaS company backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: OnKure Therapeutics
providers.description: OnKure Therapeutics (Nasdaq: OKUR) is a publicly traded, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, developing precision medicines for people with cancer. The company designs mutant-selective small-molecule inhibitors against oncogenic drivers in the PI3K pathway; its lead program OKI-219 is a selective PI3K-alpha H1047R inhibitor in clinical development, with additional discovery programs targeting further PI3K-alpha mutations. OnKure became publicly listed through its 2024 combination with Reneo Pharmaceuticals. It is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it operates a corporate and investor relations web presence and publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Oxa
providers.description: Oxa (formerly Oxbotica, rebranded in 2023) is a British autonomous vehicle software company founded in 2014 in Oxford, England by Paul Newman and Ingmar Posner. Oxa builds what it calls Universal Autonomy — self-driving software configurable for almost any vehicle in almost any environment — and sells it as Industrial Mobility Automation for ports, airports, manufacturing yards, solar farms and shuttle networks. Its product line is Oxa Driver (the autonomy stack), Oxa Foundry (a generative-AI training and assurance toolchain, previously marketed as Oxa MetaDriver), Reference Autonomy Designs (modular hardware integration blueprints), and Oxa Hub (a cloud fleet-management suite covering remote assist, task design, workspace mapping, digital twins and in-use monitoring). Oxa Hub is described on the marketing site as offering "an API for optional integration with existing logistics systems", but Oxa publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable specification on any public host. The company raised a $115M Series C in 2023 with participation from Google, and works with Ocado Group, ZF and bp.

providers.name: Phare Health
providers.description: Phare Health builds AI tools for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM), focused on medical coding and clinical documentation improvement (CDI). Its platform analyzes complete electronic health records to generate accurate, compliant medical codes and to catch coding errors before bills are submitted. Products include Phare Audit (a pre-bill safety net that screens encounters for errors), Phare Autonomous (automated coding of simpler cases with explainability), and Phare Analytics (coding workflow and financial monitoring). The UK-founded, General Catalyst-backed company has been acquired by R1 and integrated into its R37 lab division. Phare Health operates as a closed B2B product and publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or status page at this time.

providers.name: Route
providers.description: Route is a post-purchase platform for e-commerce brands that helps merchants own the customer experience after checkout. Its core products are package protection (shipping insurance covering lost, stolen, or damaged orders), AI-driven returns that reduce refunds and returns fraud, and real-time order and package tracking for shoppers. Route serves both merchants and their customers through storefront widgets, a mobile app, and a developer API documented on Stoplight. The company is backed by Craft Ventures.

providers.name: Sentra
providers.description: Sentra is a cloud-native data security platform (DSPM) that discovers, classifies, and governs sensitive data at petabyte scale across cloud and SaaS environments, with a focus on AI-readiness and preventing sensitive data exposure. The platform gives security teams visibility into where data lives, reduces data sprawl, and monitors data access and posture. Sentra was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. It operates a public Trust Center but does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or open documentation; its product documentation is gated behind an authenticated application login.

providers.name: Sett AI
providers.description: Sett AI is a creative performance AI platform for mobile game user acquisition (UA), offering "agentic AI" that helps game studios and performance-marketing teams research, generate, analyze, and deploy video and playable ad creatives at scale to combat creative fatigue. Sett agents connect to ad networks (Meta, Google, AppLovin, Unity, Mintegral) and MMP data to ideate concepts, generate playables and videos, and analyze creative performance. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners; the company raised a Series B bringing total funding to $57M. Sett operates a marketing and product website but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this profiling.

providers.name: SureWaves
providers.description: SureWaves is a broadcast-television advertising technology company that integrates linear TV with digital advertising infrastructure. It provides AI-powered spot and yield management for broadcasters and real-time, pay-for-performance campaign tooling for advertisers, and operates India's largest spot TV network — more than 20 million spots monthly across 550+ local channels reaching 490+ million households. Holder of 50+ patents, backed by Accel, with offices in Bangalore, New York, McLean, Mumbai and New Delhi. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; two enrichment passes (2026-07 and 2026-08) found no public API, developer portal, SDK, package, or machine-readable contract of any kind — the platform is sold as an enterprise engagement behind a "Request Meeting" form. The company does display a SOC 2 Type II badge on its homepage, attested by Prescient Assurance against AICPA SSAE 18.

providers.name: Theator
providers.description: Theator is a surgical intelligence platform that turns minimally invasive surgical video into structured, actionable intelligence. The company processes operative video footage into procedural insights, outcomes data, and surgery-to-text documentation for three audiences: surgeons seeking objective performance feedback, hospital and health-system executives tracking outcomes and efficiency, and revenue-cycle teams improving documentation and coding. Theator is a healthcare technology company backed by Insight Partners and partners with AWS and Oracle Health. It maintains a formal security and compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) published via its trust center. No public first-party developer API, SDK, or documentation surface has been identified; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: Toka
providers.description: Toka is a defense and intelligence technology company, founded in 2017-2018 and headquartered in Maryland with R&D in Israel, that develops signals intelligence, ISR, cyber operations, and force protection capabilities exclusively for militaries, homeland security organizations, intelligence agencies, and law enforcement in the United States and allied nations. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Eclipse Ventures, and Dell Technologies Capital, Toka sells government-facing capability platforms and cyber capacity-building services rather than a public developer or API surface, and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Transposon Therapeutics
providers.description: Transposon Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing transformational therapies for neurodegenerative and aging-related diseases driven by LINE-1 retrotransposon activity. Its lead asset, TPN-101 (censavudine), is a potent oral inhibitor of LINE-1 reverse transcriptase in late-stage development for progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) / frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and Alzheimer's disease. The pipeline also includes follow-on novel nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) and Protein Kinase R inhibitors (PKRi) targeting pathways activated by LINE-1 and implicated in cognitive impairment. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a corporate marketing website only and no public API, developer, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
providers.description: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) is the federal agency responsible for conserving, protecting, and enhancing fish, wildlife, plants, and their habitats for the continuing benefit of the American people. USFWS programs cover migratory birds, endangered species, interjurisdictional fish and marine mammals, and inland sport fisheries. Public-facing data is shared primarily through web tools and downloadable datasets such as the Environmental Conservation Online System (ECOS), Information for Planning and Consultation (IPaC), and the Service Catalog (ServCat) rather than a consolidated public API program.

providers.name: Valar Labs
providers.description: Valar Labs is an AI oncology company building diagnostics that interpret solid tumors from routine pathology slides to predict cancer treatment response. Its proprietary CHAI (Computational Histology Artificial Intelligence) platform analyzes digitized H&E-stained slides — trained on 500,000+ pathologist annotations of tumors and their microenvironment — to help physicians and patients make evidence-based therapy decisions. Products include Vesta Bladder (predicting BCG response in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer), Vesta Prostate, and Vitara Pancreas ChemoPredict (guiding first-line chemotherapy selection in advanced pancreatic cancer). Founded at the intersection of AI and oncology and backed by a16z and DCVC, Valar Labs delivers results within days without requiring additional tissue. The company operates a physician ordering portal at portal.valarlabs.com and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API specification as of this profile.

providers.name: Voya
providers.description: Voya GmbH is a software development and consulting company based in Hamburg, Germany, with nearshore TechHubs in Bucharest and Cluj, Romania. Founded in 2015 as an AI-powered chat-based business-travel booking platform backed by 500 Global, it became a wholly-owned Volkswagen Group subsidiary and has been an independent, founder-led company again since November 2024. Today Voya delivers end-to-end software development, applied AI solutions, and engineering team building for automotive, mobility, and travel clients including Volkswagen, Audi, CARIAD, Deutsche Bahn, and Lufthansa City Center. TISAX certified. Voya publishes no public API or developer portal.

providers.name: VSORA
providers.description: VSORA is a French fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Meudon-La-Foret, France, that designs high-performance AI inference chips. Its Jotunn 8 data-center inference chip (3200 Tflops fp8, 288 GB HBM, built on TSMC 5nm) targets cost- and energy-efficient large-scale AI inference, and its Tyr family (Tyr 2, Tyr 4) targets edge AI and on-device processing. VSORA is a Partech portfolio company and publishes no public web API or developer portal as of July 2026.

providers.name: Wandercraft
providers.description: Wandercraft is a robotics company founded in 2012 by Nicolas Simon, Matthieu Masselin and Jean-Louis Constanza, dual-headquartered in Paris and New York with 175+ AI, robotics and industrial staff. It designs, manufactures and sells self-balancing robotic exoskeletons and humanoid robots. Atalante X is a hands-free, self-balancing overground rehabilitation exoskeleton with 12 motors, used in more than 100 rehabilitation and research centers, CE-marked in 2019 and FDA-cleared for stroke (2022), spinal cord injury (2024) and multiple sclerosis (2025). Eve is the personal self-balancing exoskeleton for wheelchair users, FDA-cleared and commercially launching in the United States in 2026. Calvin-40 is the industrial humanoid built on the same full-body control stack for part handling, flow logistics, picking and kitting in factories and warehouses, deployed at Renault's Douai plant. Renault Group took a stake and joined as industrial partner alongside the June 2025 Series D. Wandercraft publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind: the product is regulated medical-device and industrial hardware, its control software is embedded in the device, and its only public code surface is a single maintenance fork of a third-party C library on GitHub.

providers.name: 8th Wall
providers.description: 8th Wall is a web-based augmented reality (WebAR) platform originally founded in 2016 and acquired by Niantic in March 2022. Following Niantic's 2025 sale of its gaming division to Scopely and the spin-off of Niantic Spatial, Inc. as an independent geospatial AI and XR company, 8th Wall's hosted cloud editor, login, and Niantic Studio services were retired on February 28, 2026 and the platform transitioned to a free, open-source distribution model. Existing published 8th Wall experiences continue to run through February 28, 2027. The 8th Wall stack centers on the XR Engine — a SLAM-based WebAR runtime providing World Tracking, Image Targets, Face Effects, Sky Segmentation, and World Effects — exposed to developers as a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK that integrates with A-Frame, three.js, PlayCanvas, and Babylon.js. The Distributed Engine Binary (released January 2026) ships SLAM under a binary-only license for commercial and noncommercial use, while the surrounding framework, utilities, and example projects are MIT-licensed on the 8thwall GitHub organization. 8th Wall Studio (formerly Niantic Studio) is a real-time visual editor and game engine for authoring 3D and XR experiences that can be deployed to any web host. 8th Wall does not publish a public REST or HTTP API; the developer surface is a client-side JavaScript SDK plus command-line and utility tooling distributed through GitHub.

providers.name: Abbelight
providers.description: Abbelight is a French bioimaging company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Cachan, near Paris, that designs and manufactures single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM) and nanoscopy instrumentation. Its modular SAFe platform — SAFe Excitation, SAFe Detection and the SAFe Nexus optronic control bay — mounts on the camera port of any inverted microscope and upgrades it from diffraction-limited widefield and TIRF imaging to super-resolution techniques including STORM, PALM, DNA-PAINT and spectral demixing. The company also ships the Smart Flow automated sample-preparation system, ready-to-use staining and buffer kits, and the SAFe Neo software suite for 3D quantitative analysis and visualization of localization data. Abbelight sells through account executives and a consumables webshop, and raised a Series B led by AVANT BIO in January 2026. As of this profile it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Acepodia
providers.description: Acepodia is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2017 by Dr. Patrick Y. Yang and Dr. Sonny Hsiao, headquartered in Alameda, California with operations in Taipei, Taiwan. It develops off-the-shelf allogeneic cell therapies for cancer and autoimmune disease built on two proprietary platforms: Antibody-Cell Conjugation (ACC), which uses bioorthogonal click chemistry from Carolyn Bertozzi's Nobel Prize-winning work to attach tumor-targeting antibodies to gamma delta 2 T cells and natural killer cells without genetic engineering, and Antibody-Dual-Drugs Conjugation (AD2C). Its clinical pipeline includes ACE1831, an anti-CD20 gamma delta T cell therapy, and ACE2016, an anti-EGFR gamma delta T cell therapy. Acepodia is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor, and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Adimab
providers.description: Adimab is a private biotechnology company founded in 2007, headquartered in Lebanon, New Hampshire, with a west coast office in Mountain View, California. It operates a proprietary yeast-based antibody discovery and engineering platform that combines fully human synthetic and immune libraries to generate specific, stable and developable IgGs, heavy-chain antibodies (HCAbs), multispecifics, T-cell engagers and T-cell receptors. Adimab deliberately runs no internal therapeutic pipeline, instead partnering with biopharma companies through funded discovery programs, platform transfer and non-exclusive program deals. The company reports more than 140 industry partnerships since 2009, 675+ therapeutic programs initiated, 90+ clinical programs and 6 commercial products. Adimab publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; its capabilities are delivered as laboratory discovery services and licensed platform transfer under partnership agreements.

providers.name: Aer Therapeutics
providers.description: Aer Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in the Research Triangle Park / Raleigh area of North Carolina, developing novel treatments for muco-obstructive lung diseases such as COPD, asthma, cystic fibrosis, and non-CF bronchiectasis. A spinout from Dr. John Fahy's laboratory at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), the company's lead candidate, AER-01 (fexlamose), is an inhaled small-molecule mucolytic designed to break down and liquefy the dense mucus plugs that obstruct airflow in the lungs. Aer closed a $36 million Series A backed by life-science investors including Canaan, OrbiMed, Hatteras Venture Partners, and Pappas Capital. Aer Therapeutics is a private, research-focused therapeutics company and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDKs; this profile captures its corporate identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aktis Oncology
providers.description: Aktis Oncology is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation precision radiopharmaceuticals for the treatment of cancer. The company has built a proprietary miniprotein radioconjugate platform that pairs tumor-targeting miniproteins with targeted alpha-particle emitters, aiming to reach solid-tumor types that have been difficult to address with existing radiopharmaceutical therapies. Aktis focuses on patient populations with significant unmet medical need, advancing a pipeline of targeted alpha-based therapeutic candidates. The company operates from Boston, Massachusetts, with an additional site in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina. Aktis Oncology was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a biotechnology company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Alida Biosciences
providers.description: Alida Biosciences (operating as AlidaBio) is a San Diego‑based biotechnology company founded in 2020 that develops innovative platforms for analyzing RNA modifications. Their EpiPlex™ platform enables high‑throughput profiling of m6A, inosine, pseudouridine and RNA expression in a single workflow, supporting research, diagnostics and therapeutic discovery. The company aims to unlock the epitranscriptomic layer of gene regulation to advance precision medicine.

providers.name: Alliance One International
providers.description: Alliance One International was a global leaf tobacco merchant that purchased, processed, and sold leaf tobacco to manufacturers of cigarettes and other consumer tobacco products. Founded in 2005 through the merger of Dimon Incorporated and Standard Commercial Corporation, Alliance One International became one of the world's two largest leaf tobacco dealers. The company sourced tobacco from major growing regions including the United States, Brazil, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Turkey, and other countries. In 2018, Alliance One International changed its name to Pyxus International, reflecting a broader diversification strategy beyond tobacco into hemp, cannabis, and e-liquids.
