The company focuses on patient-centered innovation, offering a range of devices, accessories, and support services to improve quality of life for individuals with hearing loss.

providers.name: CodeSecure
providers.description: CodeSecure is an application security testing company whose CodeSonar static application security testing (SAST) engine performs deep whole-program analysis of C, C++, Java, and other languages to find bugs, security vulnerabilities, and coding-standard violations, and whose CodeSentry binary software composition analysis (SCA) tool generates SBOMs and detects vulnerabilities in third-party and binary components. CodeSecure merged with AdaCore in 2025, combining SAST and SCA tooling with high-integrity software development for aerospace, automotive, defense, medical, and industrial customers. The tools support SARIF, CWE, MISRA, CERT, and OWASP as well as safety standards such as ISO 26262, IEC 61508, EN 50128, and DO-178C, and integrate with CI/CD, IDE, and issue-tracking pipelines rather than exposing a public developer REST API.

providers.name: Come Bien
providers.description: Come Bien is a Mexican foodtech company operating a digital corporate cafeteria (comedor digital) that delivers fresh, home-style, nutritionally balanced meals to offices without requiring any on-site kitchen installation. Employees choose from a rotating seven-week cyclical menu each day, place their order through the Come Bien app, and receive individually bagged, ready-to-eat meals delivered to the workplace in 100% biodegradable packaging. A dedicated backoffice platform lets employers subsidize, administer, and gain full visibility into their team's food benefit. Backed by 500 Global, the company reports serving 100+ companies, 10,000+ employees, and more than 1.5M orders delivered.

providers.name: Construction Monitor
providers.description: Construction Monitor aggregates building-permit data from county and municipal sources nationwide and resells it as construction leads, contractor intelligence, and historical permit research. Programmatic access is offered through a REST + JSON API backed by Elasticsearch and a weekly data-dump option delivered over secure FTP. Both channels are account-managed; partners receive credentials and a documented endpoint contract directly from Construction Monitor.

providers.name: ContinuumCloud
providers.description: ContinuumCloud is a Tampa, Florida-based provider of cloud software purpose-built for behavioral health and human services organizations. Its integrated suite spans three products: Welligent, an electronic health record (EHR) platform for caseload management, scheduling, clinical documentation and revenue-cycle management; DATIS e3, a unified human capital management (HCM) and payroll system covering recruiting, onboarding, timekeeping, talent management and workforce analytics; and CaredFor, a patient-engagement platform that builds online communities connecting clients, alumni and families. Formerly known as Behavioral Holdings and founded in 2020, the company draws on 25+ years of domain focus and is backed by Battery Ventures. ContinuumCloud does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or MCP server at this time; this profile captures its company identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cowbell
providers.description: Cowbell is a Pleasanton, California-based adaptive cyber insurance provider serving small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) and the middle market with standalone cyber liability coverage, technology errors & omissions (Tech E&O), management liability, and excess cyber products. Founded in 2019, Cowbell pioneered continuous underwriting through its proprietary Cowbell Factors risk benchmarking, which scores organizations against millions of data points to surface vulnerabilities and prioritize remediation. The company pairs its policies with a closed-loop resiliency program (assess-insure-respond-improve) that includes complimentary risk assessments, Cowbell Insights threat detection, incident response planning, cybersecurity awareness training, micro-penetration testing, and vendor risk assessments, plus subscription-based managed detection and response (MDR), penetration testing, identity monitoring (IdentityAI), and Compliance-as-a-Service (COMPaaS). Cowbell operates across the United States (all 50 states plus DC), the United Kingdom, and Australia, is backed by reinsurance partners including Zurich, and offers a public developer program at developers.cowbellcyber.ai exposing REST APIs for agencies, accounts, risk factors, quoting, binding, policy management, and webhooks across its Prime 100, Prime 250, and PrimeOne products. The API surface powers digital aggregator integrations with partners such as Bold Penguin, Herald, Semsee, Sayata, Limit, iBynd, and AmWins. No public OpenAPI specification or open-source SDK is published by Cowbell.

providers.name: Credflow
providers.description: CredFlow AI provides AI‑driven credentialing and payer enrollment solutions for healthcare providers. Their platform automates credentialing software, services, and modules, offering network lookup, payer directory auditing, and AI telecaller agents. The service supports CAQH, Medicare PECOS, and major insurers, handling applications across 22 payer portals with high completion rates.

providers.name: Datalot
providers.description: Datalot (now operating under parent company Centerfield Insurance Services) is an analytics-driven digital customer-acquisition and live lead/call marketplace platform for the insurance industry, spanning auto, home, life, health, Medicare, and commercial lines. It runs digital demand-generation campaigns, qualifies consumers in a real-time marketplace, and routes them by data to carriers and agents, adding agent-presence and telephony management, TCPA/regulatory compliance tooling, and secondary-market handling for unmatched consumers. Named carrier clients include Liberty Mutual, Allstate, Farmers, Progressive, Travelers, Aetna, and Humana. The company is SOC 2 certified. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners; the customer-facing surface is an authenticated carrier/agent portal at app.datalot.com with no public API, SDK, or developer documentation.

providers.name: David AI
providers.description: David AI is an audio data research company building high-quality speech and conversational datasets to bring AI into the real world through voice. Using a rigorous six-step research process (hypothesize, design, experiment, evaluate, productionize, release), the team produces datasets such as Converse (channel-separated two-speaker English conversations), Atlas (multilingual data spanning 15+ languages with dialect and accent metadata), Chorus (multi-speaker conversations for speaker separation and diarization), and Dialog (expert domain conversations). Its data is licensed to Fortune 100 companies and research labs working on speech recognition, translation, synthesis, and conversational AI. Access is arranged through samples, consultation, and a data license agreement rather than a self-serve API. David AI is backed by Amplify Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: EMBL-EBI
providers.description: The European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI) is a world‑leading centre for bioinformatics research and services, providing freely accessible data resources, tools and databases to the global scientific community. It supports a wide range of life‑science research, from genomics and proteomics to structural biology and systems biology, and collaborates internationally to advance open science and data sharing.

providers.name: Eutelsat
providers.description: Eutelsat is a high‑performance multi‑orbit satellite communications operator offering GEO and OneWeb LEO satellite services. It provides resilient, secure connectivity for land, sea and air customers, operating 31 GEO satellites and a constellation of over 600 LEO satellites to deliver broadband and data services worldwide.

providers.name: Finoa
providers.description: Finoa is a Berlin-based, BaFin-regulated digital asset infrastructure provider serving institutional investors, asset managers, family offices, venture capital funds, and regulated crypto service providers. Its platform combines qualified custody, in-custody staking, and prime brokerage across 170+ digital assets and 12 Layer-1 networks, with security and governance controls built for institutional and regulatory requirements. Finoa exposes a gated institutional API surface (api.finoa.io) and a client platform (login.finoa.io / app.finoa.io) rather than a public self-serve developer program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Freightos
providers.description: Freightos (NASDAQ CRGO) operates a global freight booking marketplace and, through WebCargo by Freightos, a rate-management and eBooking platform used by freight forwarders and carriers to price and book air, ocean, and trucking shipments in real time across 55+ carriers. Freightos publishes a developer portal (developers.freightos.com / developer.freightos.com) with freight-rate estimation, HS-code duties classification, and CO2 emissions APIs, plus the public Shipping Calculator on the marketplace. Bookable live rates, eBooking, and shipment tracking are offered to forwarder, carrier, and TMS/ERP partners under commercial agreements. Most developer-portal APIs are documented as beta and provided as-is, and full access is provisioned per partner rather than via open self-service signup.

providers.name: Functionize
providers.description: Functionize is an AI-native intelligent test automation platform that uses generative AI and computer vision to author, run, and self-heal web and mobile UI tests. The Functionize Architect agent generates tests from natural-language prompts, while Smart Test Agents reduce maintenance by adapting to UI changes at runtime. Tests execute against the Functionize Test Cloud and integrate with CI/CD pipelines via the Functionize CLI and a partner-gated REST API. Programmatic surfaces are not publicly documented; access is gated behind a Functionize tenant and a customer support portal at support.functionize.com.

providers.name: Ginkgo Bioworks
providers.description: Ginkgo Bioworks is a synthetic biology company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, that builds a horizontal platform for programming biology. Through autonomous laboratories, foundry services, and AI-powered tools, Ginkgo automates the design-build-test cycle of biological engineering for customers across biopharma, agriculture, industrial biotech, and biosecurity. Its offerings include Build-Your-Own-Lab automation hardware and software, a remotely accessible Cloud Lab, Ginkgo Datapoints screening and data services, Foundry cell-engineering services, and the Catalyst autonomous lab agent. Ginkgo Bioworks (NYSE: DNA) does not currently publish a public self-service developer API; this profile tracks the company's identity and web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GOOD Meat
providers.description: GOOD Meat is the cultivated-meat division of Eat Just, Inc., a San Francisco food technology company. It grows real chicken from animal cells in production bioreactors rather than by raising and slaughtering birds, and it was the first company in the world cleared to sell cultivated meat to consumers — approved in Singapore in December 2020, then cleared by the U.S. FDA in March 2023 and granted USDA label approval and grant of inspection in June 2023. Its products have been served at 1880 and Huber's Butchery in Singapore and at José Andrés' China Chilcano in Washington, D.C., and in May 2024 it became the first cultivated meat sold at retail. GOOD Meat is a consumer packaged-food and foodservice brand: it sells meat, not software. It operates no developer program, publishes no API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable specification, and its parent's GitHub organization carries no public repositories.

providers.name: Gravity
providers.description: Gravity (Gravity Technologies) builds and deploys ultra-fast DC electric-vehicle charging infrastructure for dense urban environments. Its Distributed Energy Access Points (DEAPs) deliver up to five-minute charges from compact, modular hardware that requires minimal real estate and no dedicated utility upgrade, letting operators place high-power charging in garages, curbside, and fleet depots. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDKs at this time, so this profile captures company identity and the domain security surface rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Gyde
providers.description: Gyde is an AI-native health insurance brokerage, founded in 2025 and headquartered in Austin, Texas with an office in New York City. Gyde partners with established insurance agencies through acquisition, embedding AI-powered tools and operational support so brokers can guide clients through insurance, health, and wealth decisions at greater scale. Its products include Gia, an AI assistant that handles client outreach, scheduling, and questions over SMS and voice around the clock, and GydeOS, a broker operating system providing client summaries, conversation transcripts, campaign management, and an AI co-pilot. Gyde launched publicly in January 2026 with $60M in financing led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile tracks its identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Heska
providers.description: Heska is a veterinary diagnostics company that makes in-clinic point-of-care lab analyzers and imaging for veterinary practices - chemistry (Element DC/DCX/RC/RCX), hematology (Element HT5), blood gas and electrolytes (Element POC), immunodiagnostics (Element i), coagulation (Element COAG), and AI-guided urine/fecal/blood-morphology testing (Element AIM) - plus the HeskaView Connect lab data and workflow software. Heska was acquired by Antech Diagnostics, a subsidiary of Mars, Incorporated (Mars Petcare / Mars Science & Diagnostics), in 2023, and now operates as an Antech company. Heska exposes a partner-gated integration API that bidirectionally connects its analyzers to veterinary practice information management systems (PIMS/EMR) - orders flow out to the analyzers and results flow back into the patient record - but there is no public, self-service developer portal, published API reference, OpenAPI, or public pricing. Access is provisioned to approved integration partners (ezyVet, Instinct, Vetspire, NectarVet, Digitail, and others) via API Partner credentials.

providers.name: Homeday
providers.description: Homeday is a German proptech real estate brokerage founded in 2015 and headquartered in Berlin, combining a nationwide network of local partner brokers with digital tools to help owners sell, buyers purchase, and both finance residential property across Germany. Its consumer products include free online and in-person property valuation, full-service sales brokerage, buyer representation, mortgage and financing brokerage through partner banks, and the Preisatlas transparent real estate price map for Germany. Homeday is backed by 500 Global and other investors. The company runs an active engineering organization on GitHub (homeday-de) publishing internal tooling, a Vue component library, design assets, and Ruby clients for third-party real estate APIs (ImmobilienScout24, onOffice), but does not currently publish a first-party public developer API or OpenAPI specification. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with identity, link-property, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Iterative Health
providers.description: Iterative Health is a Boston-based clinical research and healthcare technology company operating a global network of community-based clinical research sites that connect trial sponsors with providers to accelerate enrollment and expand patient access to investigational therapies. Its therapeutic focus spans gastroenterology, hepatology, obesity, and cardiology, and its SKOUT AI tooling (rooted in the company's computer-vision work in GI endoscopy) helps sites and sponsors run research more efficiently. Backed by GV and Obvious Ventures and funded through a $77M Series C, the company partners with provider networks including GI Alliance, One GI, and US Heart & Vascular. As of this enrichment pass Iterative Health publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its public company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Kaizen Labs
providers.description: Kaizen Labs is a New York City based govtech company founded in 2022 that builds modern, AI-native software for America's essential public services. Its modular SaaS platform helps local, state, and federal agencies replace legacy systems and deliver resident-facing digital services across recreation and facility reservations, permitting and licensing, DMV and licensing workflows, parking management, tolls, public transportation fare collection, e-billing and tax payments, citations, and judicial court services. The platform is a single, hyper-configurable framework reported to reach more than 40 million residents across 50+ agencies in 17 states. Kaizen Labs is backed by NEA, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Accel, 776, and Carpenter Capital. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Kaizen Labs delivers bespoke integrations to public-sector customers and does not publish a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Kardome Technology
providers.description: Kardome develops Voice AI technology that lets voice-integrated products hear and understand speech with human-level accuracy in complex, real-world acoustic environments. Its two core technologies are Spatial Hearing AI, which understands the acoustic scene to localize sound sources and attribute speech to the correct speaker, and Cognition AI, which adds contextual awareness so devices understand what people mean in the moment. Kardome targets automotive in-car voice UI and smart-home voice interaction in noisy environments. The company is a Techstars portfolio company, tracked in the API Evangelist network; it licenses embedded voice technology to device makers rather than publishing a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Kepler Communications
providers.description: Kepler Communications operates a cloud-based infrastructure network in space, delivering real-time connectivity, on-orbit edge compute, and hosted payload services for satellite operators and space missions. Its offerings include the Kepler Network for space-based data relay and communications, Kepler Compute for on-orbit processing, and hosted payload services that reduce the cost and technical complexity of operating in orbit. Kepler is backed by Canaan Partners, Costanoa Ventures, and Techstars. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been identified; services are accessed through the Kepler customer portal and an Atlassian-hosted support service desk.

providers.name: Kin Insurance
providers.description: Kin Insurance is a direct-to-consumer home insurance platform founded in 2016 that leverages data and artificial intelligence to provide homeowners insurance in high-risk coastal and weather-exposed markets. The platform uses thousands of property data points for automated underwriting, enabling online quote generation, policy binding, and claims management without the need for traditional agents. Kin offers homeowners, condo, flood, and auto insurance across multiple states with a focus on affordability and accessibility in markets traditionally underserved by major carriers.

providers.name: Laelaps AI
providers.description: Laelaps AI builds field intelligence for critical assets. Its system, LEA, combines autonomous embodied agents (AI-powered robots for site perimeter coverage), video monitoring agents that work on existing camera infrastructure, and fixed and mobile sensing systems under a control center layer that fuses their data into actionable intelligence for human operators; the company says one operator can then protect and operate multiple sites 24/7. Target sites include military bases, power grids, data centers, factories and hospitals, and the control layer supports encrypted, air-gapped on-premises hosting. Founded in 2025 by Dr. Sophia Belser (CEO), Dr. Mania Stamatopoulou (CRO) and Rokas Bendikas (CTO), Laelaps AI is based in Switzerland and operates across Europe; its site lists Speedinvest, Expeditions Fund, Florent Venture Partners, Fund F, ESA BIC and NVIDIA Inception as backers. It publishes a corporate website and an llms.txt but no public developer surface - no documentation, API reference, SDKs or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Latus Bio
providers.description: Latus Bio is a clinical-stage gene therapy company engineering novel adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids to deliver genetic medicines to precise cell types in the central nervous system and peripheral tissues. The company screens tens of millions of novel capsid variants to build a proprietary database of tissue-targeting "delivery zip codes," pairing engineered capsids with optimized routes of administration so therapeutics reach the intended tissue at a fraction of conventional doses and with minimal off-tissue biodistribution. Its lead programs are LTS-201 for Huntington's disease (AAV.DB-3 capsid) and LTS-101 for CLN2 disease, spanning CNS and ocular delivery (AAV.Ep+ capsid). Latus Bio operates offices and laboratories in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania and in Boston's Seaport district, and is backed by DCVC Bio, 8VC, BioAdvance, Samsung Venture Investment, and KDB. Latus Bio is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company; it publishes no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: LivingSocial
providers.description: LivingSocial is a consumer daily-deals and local-experiences marketplace that sells discounted vouchers and offers across travel, events, dining, activities, and products, alongside a coupon and promo-code section for major retailers. Originally a pioneering group-buying company, its brand and marketplace now operate as an affiliate deals and coupons destination. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the public site (livingsocial.com) exposes no developer program, API, or documentation surface: probes of common developer subdomains (developer/api/docs) and /.well-known/ discovery endpoints returned redirects to the consumer site or 404s.

providers.name: Lolli
providers.description: Lolli is a bitcoin and cash-back rewards company founded in 2018 by CEO Alex Adelman, on a mission to make bitcoin accessible to everyone. Through a browser extension, website, and mobile app, Lolli gives shoppers a percentage of their purchase back in bitcoin or cash when they shop online and in-store at 25,000+ merchants including Adidas, Microsoft, Ulta, and Kroger. Merchants pay Lolli for driving sales, and Lolli shares that commission with users as rewards paid into their Lolli wallet. The company reports having distributed over $10 million in bitcoin rewards and onboarded thousands of people into bitcoin for the first time. Lolli is a consumer product; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lumity
providers.description: Lumity is a digital employee benefits broker (part of Alera Group) that acts as an extension of HR teams, combining benefits-administration technology with dedicated benefits experts. Its platform centralizes plan management, eligibility, employee enrollment (web and mobile), renewal strategy and negotiation, year-round employee support, PEO migration, and reporting/analytics with cost forecasting. Lumity markets outcomes such as average cost savings through smarter plan selection and per-employee annual savings. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Threshold Ventures (fintech). Enrichment found no first-party public API, developer portal, or specifications: the employer login portal (er-portal.lumity.com) redirects to the third-party PlanYear platform, and legal pages are served under Alera Group.

providers.name: NerdWallet
providers.description: NerdWallet is a personal finance company that helps consumers make smarter money decisions across credit cards, banking, investing, loans, mortgages, insurance, and taxes. Through its website and mobile apps it offers comparison tools, product marketplaces, educational content, and free credit-score monitoring. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, NerdWallet is publicly traded (NASDAQ: NRDS) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of ivp. As of this enrichment pass NerdWallet publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or well-known API discovery surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Niramai
providers.description: NIRAMAI Health Analytix is a Bangalore, India based deep-tech healthcare company that develops AI-powered, radiation-free breast cancer screening solutions. Its core product, Thermalytix, uses machine learning and deep learning to analyze thermal images of the chest for early-stage tumor detection, complemented by the FDA-cleared SMILE-100 thermal imaging device and the Mythri mobile screening service for primary healthcare settings. The company reports 40+ patents, 55+ clinical publications, and 500,000+ women screened across 22+ countries. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass, Niramai publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: nlyte
providers.description: nlyte is an enterprise Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) software provider, now part of Carrier, that helps organizations discover, model, and manage physical and virtual data-center assets, capacity, power, cooling, connectivity, and operational workflows across facilities. Nlyte products expose REST APIs (including the NgageAPI / Ngauge web service) plus a portfolio of pre-built bi-directional connectors for CMDB, ITSM, service desk, virtualization, and building-management systems. The API is delivered to customers through the Nlyte customer portal rather than a public developer program, so there is no open developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or self-serve sign-up.

providers.name: Ogilvy
providers.description: Ogilvy is a global advertising, marketing, and communications agency network founded by David Ogilvy in 1948 and headquartered in New York City. It is a WPP company (NASDAQ: WPPGY) operating across roughly 132 offices in 83 countries (per ogilvy.com/about; WPP cites 128 offices in 88 countries) with approximately 17,500 employees (per Wikipedia, as of 2022). The network positions itself around "Borderless Creativity," innovating at the intersections of five core capabilities: Advertising, Public Relations & Influence, Consulting, Relationship Design (OgilvyOne), and Health. Ogilvy was named Cannes Lions Network of the Year in 2022 and 2024, D&AD Network of the Year in 2020, and took Network of the Year at The One Show 2026. Long-standing client work includes Coca-Cola, Dove (Campaign for Real Beauty), IBM, American Express, IKEA, Hellmann's, Unilever, KFC, and Cadbury. Ogilvy does not publish a developer portal, public REST APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, status page, changelog, or pricing — its product is creative work delivered to brand clients, not software offered to developers. There is no `github.com/Ogilvy` organization. This repository indexes the public properties (homepage, capabilities, work, ideas/blog, parent company, regional sites, and notable sub-brands) so the API Evangelist network can track the absence of a developer surface and link Ogilvy to its parent WPP and to its practice-area brands (Ogilvy Health, OgilvyOne, Ogilvy PR, Ogilvy Consulting).

providers.name: Omnius
providers.description: omni:us (operated by Qidenus Group GmbH, Berlin) is an insurance technology company building agentic AI for claims processing. Its platform automates end-to-end claims handling — from first notice of loss to settlement — across property, casualty, and marine lines, combining document intake, machine reading of structured and unstructured text, images and handwriting, and decision support trained on millions of annotated claims and insurance documents. Products include No-Touch Claim Automation, an Agentic Co-Pilot for complex claim decisions, Leakage Reduction, and a custom Insurance AI Modeller. omni:us was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company markets an enterprise B2B product sold direct to carriers; it publishes a public marketing site, blog, and legal terms, but exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Optimal
providers.description: Optimal is a preventive-health and longevity company based in Mexico City, backed by 500 Global, operating across Latin America (Mexico, Colombia, and Peru). Optimal offers a consumer blood test that analyzes more than 300 biomarkers and uses AI to surface problems before symptoms appear, positioning itself as a predictive health platform (branded "health OS") that integrates biological data, wearable metrics, behavioral patterns, and medical history into longitudinal health models to identify risk before it becomes disease. The company sells directly to consumers via a web app and subscriptions and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Parkopedia
providers.description: With the roll-out of connected cars, services such as live traffic and live parking have become standard requirements. Parkopedia leads the market in parking data services, with 90 million parking spaces globally across 90 countries, available via the Parkopedia parking API or feed.

providers.name: Phreesia
providers.description: Phreesia is a patient intake, registration, scheduling, payments, and engagement platform for healthcare organizations, powering more than 150 million patient visits annually. It delivers digital check-in, mobile intake and consent forms in 20+ languages, logic-driven patient interviews, real-time insurance eligibility verification, and patient payments, and pushes the resulting data back into the provider's systems of record. Phreesia is not a self-serve public API product - it is an enterprise platform whose integrations are delivered by a dedicated interoperability team using open healthcare standards (HL7v2, FHIR, CCD, CSV) alongside proprietary APIs and data extracts, with bidirectional interfaces into EHR/EMR, PM, HIE, data warehouse, and data lake systems (Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Oracle Health/Cerner, Veradigm, Meditech, ModMed, and more). There is no publicly documented developer portal, API reference, or self-service key registration as of this writing; the API surface below is modeled from Phreesia's published product and integration capabilities, not from public reference documentation.

providers.name: ProductNow
providers.description: ProductNow turns data agents can't reach into living docs — context that travels everywhere. The platform connects to a company's scattered data sources — code repositories, sales systems, financial records, legal documents, and support tickets — and indexes them into searchable documentation that stays current automatically, then surfaces that knowledge to AI agents and teams through Slack, Claude, ChatGPT, and other enterprise tools via Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, with version history, access controls, and knowledge graphs. ProductNow is SOC 2 Type II certified and is backed by Sierra Ventures.

providers.name: QPLIX
providers.description: QPLIX GmbH is a Munich-based wealth management software company offering QPLIX-Q, an all-in-one SaaS platform for professional investors, family offices, asset managers, and banks to consolidate, manage, and report on multi-asset-class portfolios. The platform automates portfolio management, trading and rebalancing, accounting, tax, and client reporting, integrating direct data feeds from 150+ custodian banks (UBS, Julius Baer, Deutsche Bank, and others) and leading market-data providers (LSEG, Moody's, S&P Dow Jones Indices, ISS ESG). QPLIX runs a self-hosted, API-based infrastructure on ISO 27001-certified European data centers, holds an ISAE 3402 attestation, and is registered with Germany's BaFin as an account information service provider (AISP). The company does not publish a public developer API or portal; integrations are delivered as managed add-ons and there is no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Quantum Metric
providers.description: Quantum Metric is a continuous product design and digital experience intelligence platform that captures and quantifies every user session across web and mobile, replaying interactions and surfacing friction, errors, and conversion opportunities in real time so that product, engineering, and customer-experience teams can prioritize work by quantified business impact. The platform exposes data-export and integration APIs to customers within their authenticated instance; during enrichment no public, unauthenticated developer portal or OpenAPI definition was discoverable (developer.quantummetric.com and docs.quantummetric.com redirect to the marketing site and the help center returns a maintenance page).

providers.name: Qwick
providers.description: Qwick is an AI-powered workforce management platform for the hospitality industry, connecting businesses with vetted hospitality professionals ("Pros") for on-demand shifts across 42 states. Its products span the Marketplace (intelligent shift matching), QwickGo (same-day shift posting), Jobs (performance-based hiring with paid working interviews), Compliance (scheduling and time-tracking rules enforcement), and Pay (multi-state W-2 and 1099 payroll). Qwick documents a REST API (v2) plus webhooks for custom integrations exposing shifts, pros, hours, invoices, and compliance data, and pre-built integrations with payroll (ADP, Gusto, Paychex, Paycom), POS (Toast, Square, Lightspeed), HRIS (Workday, BambooHR), scheduling (7shifts, Deputy, When I Work), and SSO (Okta, Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace). It is headquartered in Charleston, SC and backed by Foundry Group.

providers.name: RACE RESULT
providers.description: The RACE RESULT REST interface allows retrieval of data from systems uploading to RACE RESULT servers, including RACE RESULT decoders that upload via TCP and Track Boxes, and supports remote control commands sent to decoders. Communication with the REST API requires API keys for the Customer ID being accessed.

providers.name: Realm
providers.description: Realm is a consumer home-technology company that gives homeowners data-driven insights about their property's value and its renovation potential. The Realm platform combines public property records, permits, zoning, comparable sales, and neighborhood data into personalized recommendations that show which home improvement projects will add the most value, what they are likely to cost, and how they affect a home's estimated worth over time. Marketed at realmhome.com as "Home Renovation Planning & Home Value Insights," the product is delivered as a consumer-facing web and mobile experience rather than a developer platform. Realm was backed by venture investors including DCVC and GGV Capital and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Rivus Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Rivus Pharmaceuticals is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2019, with corporate offices in South San Francisco, California and research operations in Charlottesville, Virginia. Grounded in mitochondrial biology, it develops oral small-molecule controlled metabolic accelerators for obesity and associated cardio-metabolic disease. Lead candidate HU6 is in Phase 2 development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and has reported Phase 2a data in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF); RV-8451, an oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist for obesity, is in IND-enabling studies. Rivus is a therapeutics developer, not a software or technology vendor: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Rohirrim
providers.description: Rohirrim is an AI-native Unified Acquisition Platform that automates and accelerates government procurement for both agencies and contractors. Its UnifiedAcquire product helps government agencies manage procurements from market research through award by automating acquisition documents and centralizing institutional knowledge, while UnifiedRespond (RohanRFP) helps companies identify, match, and draft RFP responses faster and at lower cost. The company targets federal agencies, government contractors, Fortune 500 firms, and healthcare organizations, and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Insight Partners. Rohirrim publishes no public developer API surface today; this profile captures its public web, content, and security-posture footprint.

providers.name: RS Legacy
providers.description: RS Legacy Corporation is the post-bankruptcy successor entity of RadioShack Corporation, the iconic American consumer electronics retailer founded in 1921. RadioShack filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2015, with RS Legacy Corp assuming the remaining obligations. The RadioShack brand was subsequently acquired by Unicomer Group (El Salvador-based) in 2023, which now operates the brand globally in approximately 70 countries including the United States, Canada, Europe, and Latin America. RadioShack continues to sell consumer electronics, components, batteries, cables, and accessories online at radioshack.com and through franchise locations. No public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: Silvr
providers.description: Silvr (Silvr Groupe SAS, Neuilly-sur-Seine, France) was a French fintech that brought Revenue Based Financing to Europe, underwriting non-dilutive growth capital for e-commerce, SaaS and digital SMEs from its own Silvr Analytics scoring model and later broadening into flexible business loans of EUR 5k-10M covering receivables advances, inventory and equipment financing and working capital. Founded in 2020 by Nima Karimi and Gregory Tappero, it raised a EUR 130M Series A plus EUR 200M in debt from Citi and Channel, with ISAI, Serena, XAnge, Otium, Eurazeo and Bpifrance on the cap table. Silvr declared cessation of payments in June 2025; on 2 December 2025 the Nanterre court awarded Karmen the takeover of all Silvr assets except the non-performing loan portfolio, and silvr.co now redirects applicants and logins to app.karmen.io. Silvr marketed an embedded-finance partner API for real-time eligibility, but never published a developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract, and that partner funnel now points at Karmen.

providers.name: SLB (Schlumberger)
providers.description: SLB (Schlumberger) is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The SLB (Schlumberger) API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Slik
providers.description: Slik is a Latin American employee experience (PX) platform that helps organizations measure, analyze, and activate employee engagement in real time. Its Engagement module runs collaborator-journey surveys with real-time reporting, AI-prioritized improvement opportunities, people analytics and prediction, and leader action plans across the selection, onboarding, climate, and wellbeing touchpoints; its Performance module tracks cascading OKRs and continuous feedback outside annual review cycles. Slik distributes surveys and reaches employees through messaging channels including Slack, Google, Microsoft Teams, Workplace, and WhatsApp. Founded in Buenos Aires, Argentina and backed by 500 Global/500 Latam, AVP Ventures, and Vulcano Fund, the platform serves large enterprises such as Burger King, AXA, DHL, Starbucks, and Dole. Slik does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Smalls
providers.description: Smalls is a New York City based direct-to-consumer pet food company founded in 2017 by Matt Michaelson and Calvin Bohn, selling gently cooked human-grade fresh cat food, freeze-dried raw and treats on a personalized monthly subscription that customers build through an onboarding quiz at smalls.com, shipped nationwide and, since 2023, also sold into brick-and-mortar retail and wholesale. The company had raised roughly $34 million as of March 2023 — including a $9M Series A round announced in 2020 and a $19M Series B closed in mid-2022 — from investors including Left Lane Capital, Founder Collective, Digitalis Ventures and R/GA Ventures, and its shares trade on the Forge Global secondary market. Smalls runs its own Remix storefront on Netlify backed by a Contentful CMS rather than a hosted commerce platform, and publishes no first-party developer program: contract discovery in August 2026 found no OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL endpoint, MCP server, A2A agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known documents on any smalls.com host, and no GitHub organization or public client library.

providers.name: Splash
providers.description: Splash is an AI music-creation platform building games and tools for a new generation of creators. Developed by the team formerly known as Popgun AI, it has built proprietary generative-audio technology and high-quality music datasets since 2017, powering features such as Text-to-Singing, Text-to-Rap, and Generative Text-to-Music. Splash's consumer products include the Splash beat-maker app for iOS and Android, SPLASH on Roblox, the WeMix collaborative music experience, and KAIMIX. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Techstars, the Alexa Fund, Bitkraft, King River Capital, and Mawson. Splash publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its public web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sprouts Farmers Market
providers.description: Sprouts Farmers Market is a specialty grocery retailer focused on fresh, natural, and organic foods at affordable prices. Operating primarily in the western United States, Sprouts integrates with third-party platforms including Instacart, DoorDash, and Uber Eats for online grocery delivery. Sprouts uses EDI-based supply chain integrations and participates in Instacart's AI-powered Cart Assistant program. There is no public developer API; integrations are handled through EDI and third-party delivery platform partnerships.

providers.name: Stack AV
providers.description: Stack AV is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania autonomous-vehicle company founded in 2023 by Bryan Salesky (CEO), Peter Rander (President) and Brett Browning (CTO) — the leadership team behind Argo AI — and backed by SoftBank Group. The company develops AI-driven autonomy software and hardware for Class 8 commercial freight trucking, targeting driver shortages, vehicle uptime, safety, operating cost and emissions, and in May 2026 unveiled its first autonomous truck built in collaboration with PACCAR and Peterbilt Motors. Stack AV runs a public open-source engineering organization at github.com/stackav-oss (dltype, conch Triton kernels, clockwork, scene-tokens, push-guard, ai-workloads). It publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract as of August 2026 — the product is an autonomous freight service, not a developer platform.

providers.name: Stockbit
providers.description: Stockbit (PT Stockbit Sekuritas Digital) is an Indonesian retail-investing platform and social community for the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX), letting members discuss, analyze, and trade stocks with real-time market data, fundamentals, trading ideas, news, and sentiment. The product is delivered as consumer iOS and Android apps plus a web experience, with a separate crypto brand (Stockbit Crypto). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Stockbit publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDK, or .well-known discovery surface — the profile is maintained as a consumer-app company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Swiggy
providers.description: Swiggy is an Indian hyperlocal on-demand commerce and food-delivery platform founded in 2014 and headquartered in Bengaluru. Through a single consumer app it connects users with restaurant and merchant partners for food delivery, Swiggy Instamart (quick grocery and essentials commerce), Swiggy Genie (pick-up and drop errands), Swiggy Dineout (restaurant reservations and dining), and the Swiggy One membership program, operating across hundreds of cities in India with a large network of restaurant and delivery partners. Swiggy is a publicly listed company backed by Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners, Norwest Venture Partners and SoftBank Vision Fund. It exposes a login-gated merchant partner portal but does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Taxdoo
providers.description: Taxdoo is a Hamburg-based fintech providing real-time e-commerce accounting software for online retailers and tax advisors. The platform automatically captures sales, fees, payments, invoices, and contracts across 50+ marketplaces, shop systems, and payment providers (Amazon, eBay, Kaufland, Shopify, JTL, PayPal, Stripe, Klarna, Mollie), reconciles them into GoBD-compliant, audit-ready financial data, performs AI-based invoice verification, and exports daily to DATEV. Integrations are delivered as managed no-code connectors; Taxdoo does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API reference. Backed by Accel.

providers.name: Tempus AI
providers.description: Tempus AI (NASDAQ: TEM) is a precision medicine company that has built one of the world's largest libraries of de-identified clinical and molecular data, paired with an operating system to make that data accessible for diagnostics and research, starting with cancer. Its products span genomic profiling (xT / xR), AI-enabled clinical tools (Hub, One, Next), the Lens real-world data and agentic AI platform for life sciences, cardiology and radiology AI (ECG-AI, Pixel), and a consumer health app (Olivia). Tempus does not currently publish a self-serve, documented public developer API; integrations are delivered through enterprise and EHR channels (HL7 / FHIR, e.g. Epic) under partner agreements.

providers.name: Tensordyne
providers.description: Tensordyne (formerly Recogni) builds next-generation AI inference systems from the foundation up — a proprietary logarithmic-math architecture cast into custom 3nm silicon, compute hardware, scale-up interconnect, and system software. Its flagship Napier platform targets the fastest, lowest-cost, most energy-efficient generative AI inference for hyperscaler and neocloud data centers, delivering 608 PFLOPS dense compute per rack in an air-cooled 30 kW pod and supporting MoE models, agentic workloads, and 4K video generation. The stack integrates with PyTorch, Triton, vLLM, and Kubernetes; a developer SDK is announced as coming soon. Backed by Mayfield, Bosch Ventures, Toyota Ventures, GreatPoint Ventures, and Plug and Play, the company has raised more than $211M and operates from Sunnyvale, California and Munich, Germany.

providers.name: Thea Energy
providers.description: Thea Energy, Inc. is a fusion energy company headquartered in Kearny, New Jersey, founded in 2022 on stellarator physics and engineering developed at Princeton University and the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory. Thea is reinventing the stellarator by replacing complex, hand-wound 3D modular coils with a phased array of simple planar electromagnetic coils, moving the complexity of shaping the magnetic field out of the hardware and into a software control stack that can be tuned over an asset's lifetime. Its first integrated machine, Eos, is a steady-state, neutron-producing stellarator; the follow-on Helios is intended to be an electricity-producing plant. The company raised a $100M Series B in May 2026 led by Thomas Tull's US Innovative Technology Fund, and the U.S. Department of Energy has certified its power plant preconceptual design milestone. Thea publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract; its only public software surface is a small set of open-source nuclear-engineering and simulation libraries on GitHub.

providers.name: Uhura Solutions
providers.description: Uhura Solutions is a London-based AI platform for document-driven process automation in financial services, combining fine-tuned large language models, a low-code framework, and a visual workflow engine to deliver intelligent data capture, intelligent document processing, and intelligent process automation for banks and financial institutions including Barclays, Raiffeisen, and Erste Bank. A Techstars portfolio company, Uhura publishes no public developer portal or self-serve API surface; platform access is arranged through sales contact.

providers.name: Withcoverage
providers.description: WithCoverage is a technology-driven risk management and commercial insurance platform that aims to replace the traditional insurance broker for growing businesses. It pairs a team of insurance advisors, claims specialists, and attorneys with an AI-powered digital platform to analyze policies, reduce premiums, manage certificates of insurance, and handle claims proactively as companies scale. Headquartered in New York City and backed by venture investors including 8vc, WithCoverage operates in the insurtech sector. This API Evangelist profile was created as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline; the company currently exposes no public developer API surface (client access is through the app.withcoverage.com web application).

providers.name: Worldover
providers.description: Worldover is the AI operating system for chemicals and cosmetics companies, replacing fragmented ERP, PLM, QMS, LIMS, and regulatory tools with one AI-orchestrated system custom-built around each team's workflows. Powered by Willow, its chemical and regulatory intelligence engine, it runs AI agents for demand planning, regulatory monitoring, quality, formulation R&D, supply chain, SDS authoring, and PLM updates. Headquartered in London and backed by Index Ventures, Chalfen, and EF, Worldover serves beauty brands, manufacturers, ingredient providers, distributors, and pharma and supplements companies. No public developer API is published.

providers.name: Wynn Resorts
providers.description: Wynn Resorts is a developer, owner, and operator of integrated luxury resorts and casinos, with properties in Las Vegas, Boston Harbor, and Macau. The company does not currently publish a public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Xenex Disinfection Services
providers.description: Xenex Disinfection Services is a San Antonio, Texas-based medical technology company founded in 2008 by Johns Hopkins-trained epidemiologists Dr. Mark Stibich and Dr. Julie Stachowiak. Its LightStrike+ pulsed-xenon UV robot is the first FDA-authorized whole-room microbial reduction device, used by hospitals to destroy pathogens like C. difficile on surfaces; the portfolio also includes the LightStrike6 robot, the Deactivate handheld LED unit, and the TrackMate digital cleaning-event tracking system with a client portal at dms.xenex.com. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, but the company does publish an llms.txt company profile on its website.

providers.name: 360leiliang
providers.description: 360leiliang (辅布司 / "Fubusi") is a Chinese S2B self-operated business-to-business e-commerce platform for textile trim and accessories — principally lace, embroidery and knitted narrow fabrics in nylon, polyester, rayon and cotton — sold by the yard to garment manufacturers. The storefront and companion mobile app are owned and operated by 福建东南西北网络科技有限公司 (Fujian Dongnanxibei Network Technology Co., Ltd.) of Mawei District, Fuzhou, Fujian, China; the company was founded in 2014. 360leiliang.com lists per-pattern finished-goods and greige pricing, image-based product lookup, stock and made-to-order availability, and Alipay/WeChat checkout. As of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable contract or SDK; api.360leiliang.com is the private backend for its own clients. It consumes third-party APIs — WeChat login, Alipay, JPush, Vivo/Huawei push — rather than producing one.

providers.name: 4D Molecular Therapeutics (4DMT)
providers.description: 4D Molecular Therapeutics (4DMT) is a late-stage clinical biotechnology company headquartered in Emeryville, California, developing genetic medicines for large-market diseases. The company uses a proprietary directed-evolution platform it calls Therapeutic Vector Evolution to invent customized, proprietary adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene delivery vectors that carry therapeutic payloads to specific tissue types. Its pipeline targets retinal and pulmonary disease, led by 4D-150 for wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema, and 4D-710 for cystic fibrosis lung disease. 4DMT is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: 4R Systems
providers.description: 4R (4R Systems, Inc.) is a Berwyn, Pennsylvania software company founded in 1999 that sells a cloud-based intelligent inventory optimization platform and planning service to retail chains. Its prescriptive-analytics products cover demand planning, replenishment planning, allocation planning, assortment optimization, markdown optimization and vendor order optimization, combining statistical and machine-learning forecasting with a managed "planning as a service" team. Customers reach the platform through a hosted web portal and scheduled data exchanges rather than a public developer API; 4R publishes no developer portal, documentation or machine-readable API contract on its public site.

providers.name: 9 Count
providers.description: 9 Count, Inc. is a Los Angeles (Venice, CA) consumer mobile app studio founded in 2018 by Alex Hofmann, the former CEO of musical.ly, and Joe Viola. The company builds, tests and cross-promotes a portfolio of social-connection applications rather than a single product, iterating on each with usage data and customer feedback. Its flagship is Wink, an AI-assisted friend-making and dating app that matches on personality, stated intent and real-world interests instead of swipe-first selection, and it acquired the LGBTQ+ social and personals app Lex in September 2024. Earlier titles include the dating app Summer, social arcade app Juju and the creator-fan app Popstream. 9 Count has raised roughly $27.5M across three rounds. It is a business-to-consumer studio: its products ship as end-user mobile applications through the App Store and Google Play, and as of a 2026-09-05 probe it publishes no public API, SDK, webhook surface, developer portal or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: 99.co
providers.description: 99.co (99 Group) is a Singapore-headquartered real estate technology company and one of the largest property marketplaces in Southeast Asia. Founded in 2014 by Darius Cheung, Yan Phun and Conor McLaughlin, it operates consumer property portals across Singapore and Indonesia, including 99.co and SRX.com.sg in Singapore and 99.co/id and Rumah123.com in Indonesia. The platform lets buyers, renters and agents search HDB resale flats, executive condos, condominiums, landed homes and new-launch projects for sale and rent, with map-based search, transaction data, agent directories, mortgage tools and nearby-amenity insights (MRT, schools, commute times). 99 Group is backed by investors including Sequoia Capital, 500 Global, Golden Gate Ventures, Quest Ventures and East Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; 99.co exposes consumer web products but publishes no first-party public developer API or portal at this time.

providers.name: Aardvark Therapeutics
providers.description: Aardvark Therapeutics, Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed (AARD) clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel small-molecule therapies designed to inhibit hunger and treat metabolic disease. Its lead candidate, ARD-101, is an oral, gut-restricted agonist of bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) on the luminal side of the intestine, which triggers the release of satiety hormones to suppress hunger signaling; it has been evaluated for hyperphagia associated with Prader-Willi Syndrome, including the Phase 3 HERO trial, as well as in obesity and hypothalamic obesity. The company operates purely as a drug-development organization: its public web presence consists of science, programs, team, news and investor-relations material, and it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Aeroseal
providers.description: Aeroseal is a building-envelope and duct air-sealing technology company headquartered in Miamisburg, Ohio. Its patented aerosol sealing process — developed by Dr. Mark Modera under U.S. Department of Energy research at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory beginning in 1993 and commercialized as Aeroseal in 2010 — injects a fog of non-toxic sealant particles into a pressurized duct system or building envelope, where the particles collect at the edges of leaks and seal them from the inside. The company sells computer-controlled sealing equipment and software to a dealer network under the HomeSeal Connect and AeroBarrier Connect product lines; the on-machine software measures leakage in real time and issues a certificate of completion showing before-and-after leakage rates. Aeroseal reports operations in 27 countries and all 50 U.S. states, and has raised roughly $119M across three rounds, including a $67M Series B in July 2023 backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Climate Investment and OGCI. It is an equipment, materials and contractor-software business rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: AgentPay
providers.description: AgentPay provides pay‑per‑call web extraction, DNS/network intelligence, and document processing tools for AI agents. It offers REST APIs and MCP servers for extracting web pages to markdown, performing DNS and WHOIS lookups, parsing PDFs, RSS/Atom feeds, and generating site sitemaps, all billed per request via x402 on Base or Algorand. No signup required, with free trial credits and transparent pricing.

providers.name: AGTools
providers.description: Agtools, Inc. is an agricultural technology (AgTech) company providing a real-time data analytics and market-intelligence SaaS platform for the global food supply chain. The platform aggregates and curates hundreds of official government, institutional, university, and weather data sources covering 450+ specialty crops and commodities across 189+ countries, exposing 70+ variables and 25+ years of historical records (pricing, supply, demand, exchange rates, weather, CO2 footprint, and transportation costs) through dashboards, daily commodity reports, and a price analyzer so growers, shippers, buyers, and retailers can forecast demand, manage purchase orders, and reduce food waste. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Irvine, California, Agtools is a Techstars Farm to Fork alumnus and Microsoft Machine Learning & AI award winner. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface has been published to date.

providers.name: Aiper
providers.description: Aiper is a consumer robotics company that designs and sells cordless robotic pool cleaners, solar-powered pool skimmers and smart yard-care hardware (the Scuba, Surfer/EcoSurfer, Pilot and IrriSense lines), sold in more than 7,000 stores across 50+ countries with a US base in The Woodlands, Texas. Its devices are paired to the Aiper mobile app, which talks to a regional cloud control plane at apiamerica/apieurope/apiasia.aiper.com plus an AWS IoT MQTT layer. That cloud surface is a private first-party app backend: Aiper publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no SDK and no machine-readable contract, and every anonymous request to those hosts is answered with an authentication error. The only clients that speak it are unofficial, community reverse-engineered Home Assistant and Homebridge integrations.

providers.name: Aiwo
providers.description: Aiwo Limited is a science‑driven longevity hub offering advanced health screenings, personalized treatment plans, tailored supplements, and wellness therapies. Their platform combines cutting‑edge diagnostics with AI‑powered insights to help adults improve health, energy, and lifespan.

providers.name: Akido Labs
providers.description: Akido Labs is a Los Angeles-based healthcare technology company re-engineering care delivery with artificial intelligence. Its flagship system, Scope AI, is a clinical decision support platform trained on large volumes of healthcare data using reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) to help physicians reach efficient diagnoses, order the right diagnostics, personalize treatment, and forecast health risks. Providers use Scope AI through the Akido Chart EMR to expand capacity for primary care and specialty visits. Akido also operates Akido Medical, a care network spanning dozens of locations and hundreds of providers serving hundreds of thousands of patients, with an emphasis on underserved and street-medicine populations. The company is venture-backed (including a Series B led by Oak HC/FT) and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Akili
providers.description: Akili creates digital medicines delivered as video game experiences for people with cognitive impairments. It offers EndeavorOTC™, a game‑based treatment for adults with ADHD, and EndeavorRx®, an FDA‑authorized prescription video game for children with ADHD. The products are available through app stores and require a prescription for use.

providers.name: Alamar Biosciences
providers.description: Alamar Biosciences is a privately held life sciences company headquartered in Fremont, California, building precision proteomics tools aimed at the earliest detection of disease. Its NULISA (NUcleic acid Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay) chemistry and Attobody reagents, run on the ARGO and ARGO HT automated immunoassay systems, deliver attomolar-sensitivity, high-multiplex protein measurement for biomarker discovery, translational research, neurodegeneration and immuno-oncology panels. Alamar publishes no public web API. Its developer-facing surface is open source rather than service based: the first-party NULISAseqR R package (GPL-3) for importing, normalizing, quality-controlling and analyzing NULISAseq XML output, documented at nulisaseqr.alamarbio.com, alongside the NULISA Analysis Software (NAS) that ships with the instruments.

providers.name: Alloy Enterprises
providers.description: Alloy Enterprises is a Burlington, Massachusetts advanced-manufacturing company that makes single-piece aluminum thermal management components using Stack Forging, its patented digital fabrication process. Rather than printing from metal powder, Stack Forging laser-cuts sheets of aluminum and diffusion-bonds them under controlled heat and pressure into monolithic, porosity-free parts carrying complex internal geometries that casting, forging and machining cannot produce. The company sells cold plates, liquid-cooling components, vapor chambers and oscillating heat pipes into data-center cooling, defense electronics, photonics, semiconductor equipment, e-mobility, heavy equipment and industrial fluid-handling markets, and states its parts cut pressure drop by up to 4x and improve thermal resistance by more than 35%. Founded in 2020 and spun out of work begun in Somerville, Massachusetts, Alloy Enterprises was acquired by Johnson Controls in a deal signed 2026-02-18 and closed 2026-05-13, and now operates as part of that company's data-center thermal management business. Alloy Enterprises is a hardware and materials manufacturer: it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, CLI, sandbox, status page or machine-readable specification of any kind. See x-coverage below.

providers.name: Ally Financial
providers.description: Ally Financial (NYSE: ALLY) is a US super-regional, all-digital bank holding company and one of the country's largest auto finance providers, offering online deposit accounts, auto and personal lending, mortgages, credit cards, and self-directed and robo brokerage through Ally Invest. Ally does not operate a live, self-serve first-party public developer portal for its consumer banking products. Programmatic access to Ally Bank account and transaction data is delivered through third-party open-finance aggregators (Plaid and Flinks are documented), and the legacy Ally Invest brokerage REST API (inherited from the 2016 TradeKing acquisition) has effectively been retired as Ally Invest shifted toward managed and robo portfolios.

providers.name: Americaninjuryattorneygroup
providers.description: American Injury Attorney Group is a personal injury law firm serving New York and New Jersey, offering legal representation for car accidents, truck accidents, workers compensation, rideshare incidents, bicycle accidents, construction accidents, pedestrian accidents, motorcycle injuries, medical malpractice, wrongful death, premises liability, brain injuries, birth injuries, and product liability claims. The firm provides free 24/7 consultations and aims to help injured individuals obtain compensation.

providers.name: Amplication
providers.description: Amplication is an open-source backend development platform that generates production-ready microservices — REST APIs, GraphQL endpoints, data models, DTOs, and supporting infrastructure code — from a domain model, embedding organizational best practices and standards so teams avoid repetitive backend coding. The project is TypeScript-based, distributed as @amplication npm packages and an `amp` CLI, and remains actively maintained on GitHub (16k+ stars, v3.15.0). Originally offered a hosted product at app.amplication.com; the hosted service and docs subdomain have since been retired and the amplication.com root now redirects to overcut.ai (the founders' agentic-SDLC venture), while the open-source project, npm packages, and Discord community continue.

providers.name: Analyze Boston
providers.description: Analyze Boston is a municipal government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 231 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Aomstechnologies
providers.description: Aomstechnologies, operating as AMS Technologies, provides optical, thermal management, and electronics solutions for high-mix low-volume markets. They offer custom engineering, production services, and a range of technology products aimed at European industry resilience and innovation.

providers.name: APIDNA
providers.description: APIDNA builds vertically‑trained agentic systems that automate complex workflows across enterprise systems. The platform offers AI agents that execute real‑world tasks, providing high reliability, security (ISO 20022, PSD2, GDPR, SOC 2 Type II), and auditability. It targets industries needing integration across APIs, ERPs, and databases, delivering fast deployment (under 48 hours), 99 % workflow accuracy, and 99.99 % uptime SLA. The company’s website showcases solutions, platform details, and a live agent execution canvas.

providers.name: Arianespace
providers.description: Arianespace is a leading European launch service provider, delivering satellites and payloads to a wide range of orbits using its Ariane family of rockets. Founded in 1980, it operates from the Guiana Space Centre and serves commercial, institutional and governmental customers worldwide, offering flexible launch solutions, ground services and mission support.

providers.name: Arivihan
providers.description: Arivihan is an Indian EdTech company operating an AI-based, fully automated online learning platform that gives each K-12 school student a personalized "tutor in their pocket." It targets low- and middle-income families and students in Tier 2+ cities, delivering interactive, personalized lectures and doubt resolution in vernacular languages at roughly 10% of typical coaching fees. Products include the DoubtBuzzter mobile app and the tutor-prod / InstantGuru doubt-resolution web platform. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and prosus-ventures. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; this remains a consumer-facing product profile.

providers.name: Artiva
providers.description: Artiva Biotherapeutics is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company focused on developing natural killer (NK) cell‑based therapies for autoimmune diseases and cancers. Their lead candidate AlloNK® is an off‑the‑shelf, allogeneic NK cell therapy evaluated in combination with B‑cell‑targeted antibodies, aiming to provide safe, scalable treatments accessible to patients worldwide.

providers.name: AutoGrid
providers.description: AutoGrid Systems is a United States grid-technology company founded in 2011 by Amit Narayan in Redwood City, California, that built AI and machine-learning software for distributed energy resource management (DERMS), virtual power plants, and automated demand response under the AutoGrid Flex platform, selling to investor-owned utilities, retailers, and aggregators rather than to end consumers. It sits on the grid-tech / DERMS layer of the energy value chain - a buyer and orchestrator of utility and device data, not a data custodian - so no Green Button, Consumer Data Right, or smart-meter data-sharing obligation attaches to it. Schneider Electric took control of AutoGrid and then sold it to Uplight in a deal announced 14 December 2023 and closed in early 2024; auto-grid.com now serves only a 270-byte meta-refresh to uplight.com (on an expired TLS certificate as of 27 July 2026) and every developer, docs, api, and data subdomain fails to resolve. Its API posture is therefore honestly none-published - no public developer portal, no OpenAPI, no SDK, no consumer usage API, and no open market data. Its machine-readable contract is instead expressed as protocol conformance, and that is real and still published by the certifying bodies. AutoGrid is a certified OpenADR 2.0a and 2.0b VTN (server) - AutoGrid DROMS and OpenDR Server 2.0, Simple HTTP + XMPP, pull and push - and holds SunSpec Alliance certificate CS-000074 for AutoGrid Flex as an IEEE 2030.5-2018 / CSIP server, tested by Intertek on 12 December 2023 and awarded 22 January 2024. Both surfaces authenticate with mutual TLS x.509 client certificates and were reachable only under commercial contract. The successor surface at docs.uplight.com is real but fully login-gated, redirecting anonymous visitors to a ReadMe dashboard login, and api.uplight.com answers HTTP 401 with "Invalid or no token provided" - partner and customer access only.

providers.name: Automata
providers.description: Automata provides an AI‑ready, software‑defined lab automation platform that orchestrates parallel workflows, delivers real‑time analytics, and integrates genomics, cell biology, and assay screening. Their LINQ suite enables developers to build, run, and monitor complex laboratory processes, accelerating discovery and reducing manual intervention across biotech and life‑science research.

providers.name: Automax Ai
providers.description: Automax AI is a fintech company delivering AI-native residential property appraisals built for modern mortgage lending and the UAD 3.6 standard. Lenders order signed residential appraisals directly from their loan origination system (LOS) and get them back in days rather than weeks, combining AI-assisted market data analysis with licensed appraiser review. The platform pairs a hybrid appraisal workflow (automated mobile data capture of floor plans and photos plus human quality review) with an Appraisal Copilot report-writing and analysis suite, automated appraiser matching and assignment, nationwide licensed-appraiser coverage, and real-time order status tracking. Automax AI is a Y Combinator portfolio company. As of this profile the company exposes web and mobile applications (an appraiser Copilot at copilot.automax.ai and an iOS app) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Betterleap
providers.description: Betterleap is an AI-powered healthcare recruiting platform that automates candidate sourcing, credential verification, and multi-step outreach for talent acquisition teams. Its agentic search lets recruiters describe an ideal candidate conversationally and surfaces qualified matches from a database of 35M+ verified healthcare professionals, with licensing verified through 25+ state board partnerships. The platform autonomously drafts and sends personalized email sequences with follow-ups, integrates with ATS platforms such as Workday, Oracle, and UKG for talent rediscovery and data refresh, and reports recruiting performance and ROI through an insights dashboard. Betterleap is a venture-backed company (a16z portfolio) added to the API Evangelist network; it operates as a SaaS web application and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Blattnertech
providers.description: Blattnertech, operating under the Blattner Company brand, provides engineering and technology solutions across renewable energy, storage, and safety sectors. With over a century of innovation heritage, the firm delivers solar, wind, and storage projects, emphasizing sustainability, community impact, and advanced technical expertise. The company’s portfolio includes large‑scale renewable installations and comprehensive project development services.

providers.name: BlueNalu
providers.description: BlueNalu, Inc. is a San Diego, California cellular aquaculture company founded in 2017 by Lou Cooperhouse, Chris Somogyi and Chris Dammann that produces cell-cultivated seafood — real seafood grown directly from fish cells rather than harvested from the ocean. Its lead product is cell-cultivated bluefin tuna toro, marketed as "Seafood Without Compromise", targeted first at premium foodservice operators in the United States and then internationally. The company has raised approximately $84 million to date, including a Series B and a December 2025 insider-led convertible note and preferred stock financing led by Agronomics, Siddhi Capital and Lewis & Clark AgriFood, and was the first cell-cultivated seafood company admitted to the National Fisheries Institute. BlueNalu is a food and biotechnology producer; it publishes a marketing website and no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Bode
providers.description: Bode is a fashion and lifestyle brand offering clothing, accessories, and home goods. The company operates an e‑commerce site at https://bode.com, but no public API documentation or endpoints were discovered during profiling. This entry remains a stub pending any future API availability.

providers.name: Booksloth
providers.description: Booksloth is a community-driven platform that connects readers through personalized book recommendations, book clubs, and a store offering curated selections. Users can join the BookSloth app to track their reading history, discover new titles, and engage with fellow book enthusiasts. The service provides a blog, mobile apps for iPhone and Android, and integrates social media channels to foster a vibrant literary community. Founded in 2018, BookSloth aims to make reading a shared, enjoyable experience for all.

providers.name: BRINC
providers.description: BRINC builds a connected ecosystem of drones, software, and services purpose-built for public safety in the United States. Its Drone as First Responder (DFR) systems — the Guardian and Responder outdoor drones, the Lemur 2 indoor tactical drone, and the throwable BRINC Ball — pair with LiveOps teleoperations software (livestreaming, two-way comms, evidence management) to put a camera overhead within seconds of a 911 call. BRINC reports deployments across 900+ public safety agencies in all 50 states, sub-70-second average drone arrival times, and a recent $125M funding round. The company also runs its Safeguard upgrade-and-repair program and grant/DFR playbook services. BRINC exposes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface as of this profile; this entry is enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Bubblegoodsinc
providers.description: Bubble Goods Inc. operates an online marketplace offering a curated selection of independent food and beverage products, including snacks, pantry staples, supplements, and beverages. The platform connects small makers with health‑conscious consumers across the United States, emphasizing clean‑ingredient, transparent sourcing, and a wide variety of specialty items. It provides a storefront for independent brands and a shopping experience for customers seeking high‑quality, ethically sourced food products.

providers.name: Caltierrealty
providers.description: CalTier Realty operates a crowdfunding platform offering institutional‑grade multi‑family real‑estate investments to retail investors. The company provides a suite of funds, a REIT, and a learning center, enabling users to invest, track performance, and access educational resources through its web portal and mobile apps. CalTier emphasizes diversification, transparency, and regulatory compliance, with detailed portfolio listings, investor testimonials, and SEC filings publicly available.
