providers.name: Calviri
providers.description: Calviri is a Phoenix, Arizona biotechnology company, founded in 2017, that develops multi-cancer diagnostic tests and therapeutic and preventative cancer vaccines for dogs and people. Its science rests on RNA-Error Derived Neoantigens (REDNs) — abnormal proteins thrown off by the error-prone RNA processing of tumor cells — which Calviri builds as peptides on semiconductor chips and then queries against an individual's blood for antibody responses, using those antibodies as sensitive biomarkers of cancer. Its lead product, StageOne Plus, is a canine multi-cancer blood test designed to detect stage 1 disease before signs appear, alongside a pipeline of canine and human therapeutic and preventative vaccines and a preventative-vaccine trial (VACCS) that enrolled 800+ dogs. Calviri is a life-sciences company with no developer program, no product API and no developer portal; the only machine-readable surface on calviri.com is the Wix-platform-generated llms.txt and the anonymous site MCP endpoint it advertises.

providers.name: Chooose
providers.description: Chooose provides a purpose‑built software platform for scaling Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) programs. Their end‑to‑end solution helps aviation and freight companies plan, procure, report, and manage SAF initiatives, integrating tools for carbon accounting, supplier engagement, and regulatory compliance. The platform is used by industry leaders to accelerate SAF adoption and meet climate targets.

providers.name: COMSOL
providers.description: COMSOL is a Swedish-American engineering software company best known for COMSOL Multiphysics, a desktop platform for physics-based simulation. The platform exposes a unified COMSOL API that powers the GUI, the Application Builder (Java-based Method Editor), LiveLink for MATLAB, LiveLink for Excel, and the LiveLink family of CAD/CAE interfacing products (SOLIDWORKS, Inventor, AutoCAD, Revit, Solid Edge, CATIA V5, MATLAB, Simulink, Excel). COMSOL is primarily licensed desktop software with web deployment via COMSOL Server and standalone applications via COMSOL Compiler. There is no public web REST API and no public GitHub SDK organization; programmatic surfaces are the Java API, the MATLAB LiveLink interface, and the module-specific LiveLink integrations bundled with the licensed product.

providers.name: Conformal Medical
providers.description: Conformal Medical, Inc. is a Nashua, New Hampshire medical device company developing the CLAAS (Conformal Left Atrial Appendage Seal) and next-generation CLAAS AcuFORM left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) systems, foam-based implants intended to seal the left atrial appendage and reduce stroke risk in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation without requiring pre-procedure CT sizing. The company runs the CONFORM pivotal IDE trial and the GLACE study, and publishes a public marketing site segmented for patients, physicians and company/investor audiences. W. L. Gore & Associates completed its acquisition of Conformal Medical on 2026-02-19. Conformal Medical is a regulated medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable specification, and its only software artifacts are clinical-trial companion mobile apps for enrolled sites.

providers.name: Cormint
providers.description: Cormint Data Systems, Inc. is a Texas-based, vertically integrated developer and operator of power infrastructure for large-scale data centers and compute. The company designs, manufactures, deploys and operates its own electrical and site infrastructure in-house — from PDU wiring and PLC controls through transformer integration and substation work — and runs 130 MW energized today at its Fort Blocks site near Fort Stockton in West Texas, with a second 58 MW site (Bobcat) under construction near Orange Grove in ERCOT Load Zone South and a stated pipeline of roughly 370 MW across 707 controlled acres. Cormint built the operating platform in bitcoin mining, where it reports power costs of 2.3–3.1 cents per kWh and a #1 peer ranking on cost efficiency, and is now positioning the same platform for AI and HPC workloads as a colocation and EPC-style infrastructure owner-operator. It is an energy and data-center infrastructure business rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API, and no machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Crave Retail
providers.description: Crave Retail, Inc. builds in-store retail technology that connects shoppers, store associates, and product data across physical touchpoints. Its platform spans Crave Engage (customer-facing digital shopping assistants in fitting rooms, on the sales floor, and on mobile), Crave Assist (store-associate tools for floor visibility, service routing, and item lookup), and Smart Fitting Rooms, the RFID-based connected fitting-room product it started with. Crave reports 3,000+ live touchpoints, 27M+ shopper sessions, and operations across 10+ countries. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and legal web presence but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Credit Karma
providers.description: Credit Karma is an AI-powered personal finance platform founded in 2007 and owned by Intuit since 2020, serving more than 140 million members in the US, UK and Canada. It began as a free credit-score and credit-monitoring destination and has grown into a broad consumer finance marketplace spanning credit cards, personal and auto loans, mortgages, auto and home insurance, banking (checking, savings and credit-builder accounts), tax filing, and identity monitoring. Credit Karma monetizes through personalized recommendations and lead generation rather than a public developer or partner API; it maintains no external consumer-facing API program. It does run an active engineering culture with 29 public open-source repositories on GitHub (Thrift and GraphQL tooling), a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program via HackerOne, and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 security certifications.

providers.name: Crowdplat
providers.description: CrowdPlat, Inc. is a Pleasanton, California company (backed by 500 Global) that operates two platforms combining human expertise with AI. Its crowdsourcing marketplace connects enterprises with vetted specialists across 50+ countries for consulting, software development, R&D, and innovation challenges, delivered with US-based project management and milestone-driven scopes. Its AI Hire platform is recruitment technology that automates candidate evaluation through resume scoring, AI-generated screening questions, video interviews, and LinkedIn job promotion with auto-targeted outreach. Customers include federal agencies and enterprises such as Airbus, PayPal, and EPRI. No public developer/API program is published at this time.

providers.name: CWSI
providers.description: CWSI is a security and compliance partner helping organisations across the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg embrace new technologies with confidence. They provide services in secure AI, data, endpoints, identity and operations, offering assessments, workshops and managed security. Founded in Dublin in 2010, CWSI has grown into a leading Microsoft‑focused security partner.

providers.name: data.gov.uk CKAN Publishing Service
providers.description: data.gov.uk CKAN Publishing Service is a national government open-data portal for United Kingdom running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 57,757 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: DistroKid
providers.description: DistroKid is a Brooklyn, New York based digital music distribution service founded in 2013 by Philip Kaplan that lets independent musicians and labels upload an unlimited number of songs and albums to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, TikTok, Instagram, Pandora, Tidal, Deezer, and dozens of other streaming and download stores for a flat annual subscription fee while keeping 100% of their royalties. By 2020 the platform was distributing roughly a third of all new music released worldwide and serving more than two million artists; Spotify and Insight Partners both hold equity stakes following a 2021 valuation around $1.3B. Around the core distribution product DistroKid has built out a suite of artist services including Teams for automated royalty splits, cover-song mechanical licensing, YouTube Content ID monetization, DistroVid music-video distribution, Upstream label matching, Mixea AI mastering, and DistroKid Direct for fan merchandising and pre-orders. The company has historically operated without a public developer API — integrations with stores, DSPs, rights organizations, and partners are handled through private B2B arrangements, and the only public web endpoints exposed under distrokid.com/api are unauthenticated pre-save widgets used to drive Spotify follow/save campaigns. DistroKid is actively hiring API engineers to scale partner and AI-facing integrations, suggesting a more formal developer surface may emerge, but as of 2026 there is no published OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, sandbox, or developer portal. Third-party reverse-engineered wrappers such as the unofficial Golang `distrogo` library exist but are not endorsed.

providers.name: Divine
providers.description: Divine Research Inc. is a fintech company building blockchain-based unsecured lending for underserved borrowers in emerging markets. Its flagship product, Credit, issues small stablecoin (USDC) loans that start small and can grow to $1,000 as borrowers build trust, with algorithmically set interest rates and default rates that have approached zero. Borrowers access loans through a World MiniApp, while liquidity providers supply capital and earn yield through the Credit Vault at credit.cash. As of late 2024 the platform had issued hundreds of thousands of loans to more than 500,000 borrowers. Divine is backed by Paradigm and was surfaced through its portfolio; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network. Divine currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Exegy
providers.description: Exegy is a St. Louis-based provider of low-latency market data infrastructure, trading platforms, and predictive trading signals for capital markets, backed by Marlin Equity Partners after its 2021 merger with Vela Trading Systems and subsequent acquisitions of Enyx and NovaSparks. The firm sells managed FPGA ticker plants (Exegy Nexus), software feed handlers (SMDS, nxFeed), the Axiom normalized data feed, the Metro options trading platform, and market access products (nxAccess, FrontTrade, SREX). Client access to normalized real-time and historical market data is delivered through the proprietary Exegy Client API (XCAPI), a C++/C#/Java library for Linux and Windows, while Metro exposes the Subway socket API and Freeway algorithmic API - none of which are publicly documented HTTP APIs. All developer documentation sits behind customer logins (Exegy Customer Portal, Object Trading DMA portal, MarketDataPeaks), making this an entirely sales-gated, entitlement-managed offering with no self-serve API surface.

providers.name: Fractile
providers.description: Fractile is a UK-based semiconductor startup, founded in 2022 and headquartered in London with an engineering base in Bristol, designing a new class of AI inference processors. Its architecture physically interleaves memory and compute to overcome the memory-bandwidth bottleneck that limits large language model inference, targeting frontier model serving up to 25x faster and at roughly 1/10th the cost of existing hardware. The company takes a full-stack approach spanning transistor-level circuit design through cloud inference server logic, and in May 2026 raised $220M to build the next generation of inference hardware. Backers include Accel and Felicis. Led by founder and CEO Walter Goodwin, Fractile is a hardware/compute company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Generation Lab
providers.description: Generation Lab is a longevity science company founded in 2023 by Alina Su, UC Berkeley bioengineer Dr. Irina Conboy, and Michael Suswal, and backed by an $11M seed round led by Accel (Accel's first longevity bet). Its flagship SystemAge test measures biological age across roughly 460 biomarkers spanning 19 to 21 physiological systems and organs from an at-home, needle-free blood collection, returning a personalized aging report and science-backed action plan that ranges from lifestyle and supplement guidance to clinical interventions. The test is distributed through 300+ clinic partners across 18 countries and via a patient/provider portal. Generation Lab publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public web, product, and legal surfaces.

providers.description: Greece National Data Portal is a open data portal open-data portal for gr running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 21,931 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Hark
providers.description: Hark is an artificial intelligence lab founded in 2025 by Brett Adcock (founder of Figure AI and Archer Aviation) and headquartered in San Jose, California, building what it calls "the most advanced personal intelligence in the world" — proprietary agentic, multimodal foundation models paired with purpose-built, AI-native consumer hardware intended to act as a universal interface between a person and their digital life, with speech, text, vision and persistent personal memory. The company emerged from roughly eight months of stealth in March 2026 and announced a Series A of more than $700 million at a $6 billion post-money valuation in May 2026, led by Parkway Venture Capital with participation from NVIDIA, AMD Ventures, Intel Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, ARK Invest, Brookfield, Greycroft, Align Ventures, Prime Movers Lab and Tamarack Global. As of August 2026 Hark is pre-product: the platform is in closed beta behind a request-access form, and the company publishes no developer portal, no developer documentation, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable contract of any kind on its own hosts. hark.com is a four-page marketing site (home, careers, privacy policy, and a single announcement article).

providers.name: Iceotope
providers.description: Iceotope Technologies is a Sheffield, UK precision liquid cooling company founded in 2005 as a research-driven "green computing" venture, now supplying chassis-level liquid cooling for AI, HPC, data center and edge infrastructure. Its "direct to everything" single-phase immersion approach removes heat from every component rather than the processor alone, and ships as two product lines: KUL BOX for near-edge AI and HPC deployments, and KUL AI liquid-cooled server chassis for high-density rack environments. The company licenses its thermal IP (228 patents granted, allowed and pending) and works through OEM/ODM partnerships with vendors including HPE, Intel and nVent. Iceotope is a hardware and thermal-engineering business: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Inhabitr
providers.description: Inhabitr is a Chicago-founded furnishing company that operates an AI-assisted furniture rental and procurement platform for commercial real estate and residential customers. Its business side (inhabitr.ai) furnishes hospitality, multifamily, student housing, short-term rental, co-living, senior living and office properties end to end — design, sourcing, procurement, delivery, installation and asset tracking — while its consumer storefront (inhabitr.com) rents furniture, sets and decor to households on flexible terms with a browser-based Home Designer tool. The company describes real-time connectivity to warehouses, manufacturers and retailers as the "furniture cloud" behind its bidding and fulfillment, but it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable contract of any kind as of this profiling pass.

providers.name: Jacobi
providers.description: Jacobi (Jacobi, Inc.) builds a cloud-native, API-first technology platform for multi-asset portfolio design, analytics and client engagement, used by asset managers, wealth managers and RIAs, asset owners and pension funds, and investment consultants and OCIOs. The platform spans portfolio construction and asset-allocation modeling, risk analysis, a Model Portfolio Management Solution (MPMS) covering the model portfolio lifecycle, custom portfolio solutions, an OCIO solution, and the Jacobi Data Engine, which unifies fragmented investment datasets and automates integration, construction, risk and reporting workflows. Jacobi markets an open-architecture API layer and a Python-based Software Development Kit that let analysts and developers build custom models, automate data processes and connect proprietary systems, market data providers, custodians and risk engines. Each client runs on its own private deployment with data segregation, encryption in transit and at rest, fine-grained permissions, enterprise IAM integration, audit logging and continuous monitoring — so the API and SDK surface is provisioned per tenant and is not publicly documented or self-serve. Founded by investment professionals and technologists, headquartered in San Francisco with offices in London and Brisbane; raised a Series A led by QIC in 2022.

providers.name: Japan Post
providers.description: Japan Post (日本郵便株式会社) is Japan's national postal service provider, offering mail, parcel, logistics, financial and insurance services. It operates an extensive domestic and international network, providing online tools for postage calculation, tracking, address lookup, and e‑services for individuals and businesses. The corporation also runs digital platforms for e‑mail, banking, and e‑commerce support, reflecting its modernized operations beyond traditional mail.

providers.name: Kace
providers.description: KACE is the endpoint and systems management product line from Quest Software, originally founded in 2003 as KACE Networks (backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Sigma Partners, and Focus Ventures), acquired by Dell in 2010, and now sold as Quest KACE. The portfolio centers on the KACE Systems Management Appliance (SMA) for inventory, patching, software distribution, scripting, and service desk; the KACE Systems Deployment Appliance (SDA) for OS imaging and provisioning; and KACE Cloud for mobile device management and modern endpoint management. The KACE SMA ships a REST API (JSON and XML) that lets administrators programmatically manage assets, inventory, managed installations, scripting, users, and service-desk tickets on the customer-hosted appliance. This profile enriches the original Norwest portfolio lead with the real Quest KACE identity and its documented API surface.

providers.name: Keep Network
providers.description: Keep Network is a privacy-focused blockchain infrastructure project that merged with NuCypher in 2021 to form the Threshold Network. Its flagship product is tBTC, a decentralized, trust-minimized bridge that tokenizes Bitcoin as the TBTC ERC-20 token so it can be used across Ethereum DeFi without centralized custodians. Keep originally provided off-chain "keeps" — private data containers secured by a threshold ECDSA signing network and a random beacon — enabling confidential data to be used on public protocols. The developer surface is on-chain Solidity smart contracts plus first-party JavaScript/TypeScript client libraries published under the @keep-network npm scope; there is no hosted REST API. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched from the project's public GitHub org, npm packages, blog, and security.txt.

providers.name: Klar
providers.description: Klar is a Mexican digital financial services platform (neobank) headquartered in Mexico City with engineering in Berlin, serving roughly 7 million customers. Regulated by Mexico's CNBV, Klar offers a deposit account with yield, a no-annual-fee credit card, a secured (garantizada) credit card, the metal Platino card, personal loans, investment products, and Chubb-underwritten life and fraud insurance, plus cashback and interest-free-months (MSI) benefits. It also runs Klar Empresarial for business customers, partnered with Uber to launch the Uber Card in Mexico, and announced the acquisition of mortgage fintech Yave. Klar's product surface is delivered entirely through its consumer mobile app and website; as of this profile Klar publishes NO public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or sandbox, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or webhook surface could be found. Third-party access to Klar accounts is generally brokered through Latin American open-finance aggregators (Belvo, Pluggy, Plaid) rather than a first-party Klar API. Klar does operate a public GitHub organization (klar-mx), but its repositories are internal infrastructure and DevOps tooling and forks, not client libraries for a Klar API.

providers.name: Lanch
providers.description: LANCH GmbH is a Berlin-based food-tech startup that builds creator-led virtual restaurant brands for the delivery market. Founded by Nono Konopka and Jonas Meynert and headquartered at Schoenhauser Allee 180 in Berlin, LANCH develops food brands together with German influencers, musicians and athletes, then scales them through franchise partners and ghost-kitchen partners operating out of existing restaurant kitchens. Its two flagship brands are Loco Chicken (halal-certified wings, filets, burgers and chicken-and-waffle creations) and Happy Slice (hand-pulled pinsa-dough pizza, dips and cookies), both distributed through delivery marketplaces including Wolt, Lieferando and Uber Eats. The company is backed by HV Capital and Felix Capital alongside founders of FlixBus, Gorillas, Flaschenpost, Glovo, Foodspring, Foodora, Honest Food and Finleap. LANCH publishes a marketing and partner-recruitment website only; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification or SDK surface.

providers.name: LanzaJet
providers.description: LanzaJet is a sustainable fuels technology company, headquartered at 520 Lake Cook Road, Deerfield, Illinois, that produces and licenses sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and renewable diesel. Founded in 2020 as a spin-out of LanzaTech with Suncor and Mitsui, and later backed by Shell, British Airways, Southwest Airlines, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Breakthrough Energy, Groupe ADP, MUFG and All Nippon Airways, the company commercializes a patented Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ) process that converts ethanol into synthetic paraffinic kerosene through a continuous catalytic reaction, reaching roughly 90% hydrocarbon selectivity to jet fuel and converting about 98% of the ethanol carbon into salable product. The ATJ pathway was approved by ASTM International in 2018. LanzaJet Freedom Pines Fuels in Soperton, Georgia — opened in 2024 — is the world's first commercial ethanol-to-jet SAF plant, producing roughly 10 million gallons of SAF and renewable diesel a year, and the company is developing Project Speedbird in the UK alongside a CirculAir joint solution with LanzaTech that widens the feedstock base to municipal solid waste, agricultural residues and industrial off-gases via gas fermentation. LanzaJet sells technology licenses, project development and engineering services and fuel offtake rather than software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and every /.well-known/ discovery probe against its web host returned 404.

providers.name: MedArrive
providers.description: MedArrive is a healthcare technology company that provides a logistics and workforce platform for in-home care delivery. Its software gives health systems and in-home care providers smart scheduling, real-time provider routing, automated re-routing and patient reminders, and a live command-center dashboard for tracking every provider and visit, alongside a provider mobile app for field teams. The HIPAA-compliant platform is designed to reduce windshield time, cut scheduling effort, and increase daily visit capacity so care teams spend more time with patients and less on logistics. MedArrive is backed by Kleiner Perkins.

providers.name: Mentor Collective
providers.description: Mentor Collective operates an AI Mentorship OS for higher education, powering peer mentoring, student success, and retention programs at colleges and universities. Its platform matches and onboards mentors and mentees, guides conversations with AI prompts, surfaces risk signals and belonging gaps, and turns connection data into real-time retention intelligence for institutions. Backed by Techstars, the company serves higher-education and workforce partners. As of this profile Mentor Collective publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; this repo captures its public web, blog, legal, and domain-security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Metagenomi
providers.description: Metagenomi Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: MGX) is an Emeryville, California clinical-stage genetic medicines company that mines metagenomics — DNA sequenced directly from environmental microbial communities — together with machine learning to discover novel gene-editing machinery from otherwise unknown organisms, then engineers it into in vivo genome-editing therapies. Its published toolbox spans five system classes: programmable CRISPR nucleases, ultra-small nucleases that package into a single AAV vector, base editors the company describes as "the smallest CRISPR base editors known", RNA Mediated Integration Systems (RIGS) for template-encoded edits, and CRISPR Associated Transposases (CASTs) for gene integrations exceeding 10,000 base pairs. The company completed its initial public offering on the Nasdaq Global Select Market in February 2024 at $15.00 per share and partners with Ionis Pharmaceuticals on gene-editing programs including ApoC-III, transthyretin (TTR) and angiotensinogen (AGT). Metagenomi sells therapeutics, not software: metagenomi.co is a seven-page Craft CMS marketing site with no developer program, no API, no SDK and no machine-readable specification of any kind. Its GitHub organization is real and first-party but publishes zero public repositories, and its only first-party software package — the `metagenomi` PyPI library of internal Docker helper scripts — has not shipped a release since July 2019.

providers.name: Mojo Vision
providers.description: Mojo Vision is a Saratoga, California semiconductor and display company building a "wafers-in, wafers-out" micro-LED platform. Founded in 2015, it originally developed the world's smallest, densest dynamic display for an AR smart contact lens, then pivoted in 2023 to commercializing micro-LED displays and optical interconnects. Its platform combines a 300mm silicon architecture with GaN-on-Silicon emitters, proprietary quantum dots and micro-lens arrays, and has demonstrated a monolithic RGB panel at 4µm pixel pitch (6,350 ppi). Target markets are XR and AI-enabled glasses, automotive heads-up displays, large-format displays, and high-density optical I/O for AI infrastructure. Partners include Marvell, DigiLens and CY Vision; investors include Khosla Ventures, NEA, Future Ventures, HP Tech Ventures, Amazon's Alexa Fund and Dolby Family Ventures. Mojo Vision is a hardware/silicon company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Nava Benefits
providers.description: Nava Benefits is a modern employee benefits brokerage that pairs expert human advisors with AI-driven technology to help HR teams manage health insurance renewals, audit billing, control benefits costs, and improve the employee experience. OUTFRONT's digital inventory is made available programmatically through DOOH supply-side partners such as Vistar Media and Place Exchange. OUTFRONT sold its Canadian operations to Bell Media in October 2022 to focus on the U.S. market. providers.name: Overjet
providers.description: Overjet is a dental AI platform that applies FDA-cleared computer vision to dental radiographs (bitewings, periapicals, panoramics, and CBCT) to detect, outline, and quantify oral health conditions - caries, calculus, bone level and bone loss, periapical radiolucencies (PARLs), and anatomical structures - for dental providers, DSOs, and insurance payers. Overjet is not a self-serve public API. Its AI is delivered as OEM/partner integrations embedded into imaging systems and practice management software (Open Dental, Dentrix, Dentrix Ascend/Enterprise, Eaglesoft, Oryx, CareStack, and others) via connector software and DICOM image routing, plus payer-side products for insurance verification and claim review (ReviewPASS). providers.name: Physics Wallah
providers.description: Physics Wallah (PW) is India's leading affordable education technology platform, offering live and recorded courses, test series, notes, and doubt-solving for competitive exams (IIT JEE, NEET, GATE, UPSC), government job preparation (SSC, Banking, Railways, Defence), school boards (CBSE, ICSE, and regional boards), and professional certifications (CA, CS, CFA, ACCA). This profile records that absence honestly rather than describing an API that does not exist.

providers.description: Podchaser provides one of the most comprehensive podcast databases, exposed through a GraphQL API designed to drive podcast discovery for listeners, podcasters, brands, and platform partners. The API surface is GraphQL-only and is therefore not represented as an OpenAPI specification in this index.

providers.name: Pops
providers.description: Pops is a consumer mobile application, built by Undefined Software, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), that lets users create, remix, and share AI-powered mini games with friends. Every play instantly becomes a funny gameplay/reaction video you can send to friends. Pops is available on iOS and Android and is organized around game categories such as arcade, 3D, racing, sports, puzzles, party, and reaction games. It is an end-user social and gaming product with no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Praktika.ai Company
providers.description: Praktika.ai is an AI-powered language-learning application that lets learners have spoken conversations with lifelike AI avatar tutors and receive instant feedback on pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary. The product spans mobile (iOS and Android) and web, with personalized study plans and speaking, listening, reading, and writing exercises across many languages, plus a B2B offering for organizations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Praktika publishes a consumer product only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation were found — so this profile captures the company identity and web properties rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Prime Meridian
providers.description: Prime Meridian (Prime Meridian Labs) is an AI-powered consumer tax preparation and e-filing service that files federal and state income tax returns for free. Users upload their tax documents, answer a few clarifying questions, and the platform's AI generates a plain-language return covering W-2 employment, self-employment (Schedule C), K-1 partnership income, and multi-state situations, then e-files it with the IRS and state authorities in roughly fifteen minutes. The company is backed by General Catalyst and counts former IRS Commissioner Daniel Werfel among its strategic advisors. It is a consumer web application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Prosimo
providers.description: Prosimo is a multi-cloud networking platform that gives enterprises a full-stack cloud transit, security, performance, observability, and cost-management layer across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud. Its Application eXperience Infrastructure (AXI) abstracts cloud-provider networking constructs and ties network transit, micro-segmentation, zero-trust policy, WAF, and observability into an autonomous, ML-driven control plane. Prosimo exposes that control plane programmatically through a first-party Terraform provider (prosimo-io/prosimo) for full lifecycle management of cloud gateways, network and application onboarding, policies, namespaces, and security profiles; a companion Pulumi bridge repository and reusable Terraform modules are published on GitHub. Prosimo was venture-backed by General Catalyst, WRVI Capital, and BlackRock; industry sources report it was subsequently acquired by Palo Alto Networks.

The company reports covering more than one million kilometers and saving over 50 tons of CO2 emissions. Rabbit is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As a consumer mobile-app business, Rabbit publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Recess
providers.description: Recess (Recess Academy, recess.gg) is an online school for gifted and neurodivergent students, including learners with ADHD, dyslexia, autism spectrum, and anxiety. It combines core academics, interest-led classes, small-group coworking sessions with an AI tutor, and a daily community hour, with personalized pacing and world-class mentors. Recess is backed by Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a consumer education web application and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; the only machine-discoverable surface found is a valid RFC 9116 security.txt with a security contact.

providers.name: Responsiv
providers.description: Responsiv is an AI-powered regulatory intelligence and compliance platform that helps organizations monitor regulatory change, translate laws and regulations into clear actionable requirements, identify compliance gaps against existing policies and controls, and track remediation through to completion. The platform continuously monitors 1,000+ regulatory sources across 50+ jurisdictions, routes alerts by business unit, topic, or jurisdiction, maintains an obligations register, and offers agentic legal research with fully cited sources. It serves compliance teams in financial services, health and P&C insurance, and consumer tech. Backed by Greylock. providers.name: Setpoint.io
providers.description: Setpoint is a capital markets operating system for asset-backed finance. It embeds with borrowers and lenders to manage debt facilities — warehouse facilities, forward flow agreements, securitization, and fund/leverage finance — automating collateral verification, data standardization, and reporting across ABS and ABF markets. The platform (Capital OS and Data OS, plus PledgeCheck collateral certification and Setpoint Analytics) manages over $50 billion in financed assets annually. Setpoint is not currently a public API provider; this profile captures the company's identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sidewinder Therapeutics
providers.description: Sidewinder Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Diego, developing a new generation of precision bispecific antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for the treatment of solid tumors. Its engineered biologics bind two complexed targets simultaneously to increase tumor specificity, driving internalization of the antibody-receptor complex and its cytotoxic payload, with the goal of expanding the therapeutic window for hard-to-treat cancers such as colorectal, lung, and head-and-neck squamous cell carcinomas. The company raised an oversubscribed $137M Series B in 2026 (co-led by Frazier Life Sciences and Novartis Venture Fund, with DCVC Bio, OrbiMed, and others) and is advancing its bispecific ADC programs toward clinical development. Sidewinder is a biopharma research company and publishes no public developer or API surface.

Skience is backed by Insight Partners and operates as a private SaaS provider; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, but it does maintain a SafeBase-hosted trust center documenting SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 2 + HITRUST attestations and a responsible disclosure program.

providers.name: Spartan Radar

Spartan sells to commercial-vehicle OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers and fleet operators as embedded software and hardware; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface contract.

Adjacent targets include hydrogen from ammonia e-cracking, syngas, methanol, butadiene and other commodity chemicals, sold as reactor hardware plus a licensing and front-end engineering support package. The platform lets manufacturers evaluate, standardize, and upskill their technician workforce at scale while minimizing disruption to production. Customers include Northrop Grumman, ACC, SUNY, and Dallas College. Backed by 8vc and surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company; TAP currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: ThreatTrack Security

The company traces to Sunbelt Software (founded 1994), which GFI Software acquired in 2010; GFI spun the security unit out in 2013 to form ThreatTrack Security. ThreatTrack was acquired by Ziff Davis / J2 Global in early 2018 and the brand was folded into VIPRE Security Group, so ThreatTrack no longer operates as an independent company. Its historical developer surface was an OEM/on-premise integration API for ThreatAnalyzer (JSON/XML output) and ThreatIQ intelligence feeds rather than a public, self-service developer platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Thyme Care
providers.description: Thyme Care is a value-based oncology care-navigation and support company that partners with health plans, providers, and employers to guide people through a cancer diagnosis and treatment. Thyme Care delivers this through partner programs (Thyme Care Connect, Thyme Care Signal, Thyme Box, and Enhanced Supportive Care) rather than a public developer platform. providers.name: Trace Neuroscience
providers.description: Trace Neuroscience, Inc. is a biotechnology company developing genetic medicines for neurodegenerative diseases. The company sponsors the FUNCtion ALS Phase 1/2 trial (NCT07674667) evaluating TRCN-1023 delivered by intrathecal injection. Trace Neuroscience is backed by GV and does not currently publish a public developer portal or APIs.

providers.name: Tracera

The platform extracts audit-ready metrics from raw data across PDFs, spreadsheets, and ERP systems for 900+ metrics, supports reporting frameworks including CSRD, SEC, GRI, and CDP, and serves Fortune 2000 enterprises across manufacturing, real estate, construction, retail, technology, and healthcare (customers include EnerSys, La-Z-Boy, Sauder Woodworking, and Putzmeister). Founded in 2022 and based in New York, Tracera raised a $12M Series A in April 2025 led by Foundry with Rho Ignition, Tola Capital, and Contour Venture Partners ($17.25M total). The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (seed, 2024) and operates in Israel, the United States, and Italy. TreeX publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.description: Trupanion is a pet medical insurance provider for cats and dogs, best known for its patented software that pays participating veterinary hospitals directly at checkout (VetDirectPay) rather than reimbursing pet owners after the fact. The APIs listed here are modeled from Trupanion's public partner and portal materials, not from an openly documented API reference.

providers.name: TT Labs
providers.description: TT Labs is the company behind VideoPixie, a freelance marketplace that connects clients with professional video creators — videographers, video editors, directors, animators, and motion designers — available for hire. Clients post a project brief in about five minutes and receive competitive bids from vetted creators, then choose a creator based on portfolio and price. VideoPixie serves crowdfunding and Kickstarter videos, product and explainer videos, game trailers, wedding videography, screencasts, and full production campaigns, with example budgets ranging from a few hundred to tens of thousands of dollars. Backed by 500 Global, VideoPixie is a customer-facing marketplace web application (AngularJS) and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Unchained Labs
providers.description: Unchained Labs is a life-science tools company that designs, manufactures, and sells analytical instruments, automation, and consumables for biologics, gene therapy, cell therapy, nanoparticle, exosome, and genomics research. Its product line includes plate-based systems for protein characterization, concentration and quantification (Lunatic and Stunner), protein stability and formulation (Uncle), automated buffer exchange and sample prep (Big Tuna, Little Big Tuna), viscosity measurement, and lipid-nanoparticle synthesis and analysis. The company serves biopharma R&D, process development, and QC labs. Unchained Labs is primarily a hardware, reagent, and lab-software vendor; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, REST/GraphQL surface, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched with verified company identity and link properties from its public website.

providers.name: Upstream Bio
providers.description: Upstream Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 460 Totten Pond Road in Waltham, Massachusetts, founded in 2021 and listed on Nasdaq as UPB since its October 2024 IPO. The company develops treatments for inflammatory disease with an initial focus on severe respiratory disorders, and its strategy is built around a single lead asset: verekitug (UPB-101), described by the company as the only known antagonist in clinical development that targets the receptor for thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP). Verekitug has been advanced into Phase 2 studies in severe asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), with a Phase 3 development strategy announced in 2026. Upstream Bio is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: upstreambio.com is a fourteen-page WordPress marketing site, investor material is served from a hosted Q4-style investor-relations subdomain, and the company publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Velotax

Founded in 2020 by ex-J.P. Morgan bankers Eduardo Esmanhotto and Victor Savioli, it operates as a banking correspondent in partnership with VIA CAPITAL (a Brazilian Central Bank SCD), holds Reclame Aqui's top RA1000 reputation seal, has 3M+ app downloads, and raised a R$125M Series A in 2025 from QED Investors, Valor Capital and Picus Capital. Velotax is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: videogame.ai
providers.description: videogame.ai is an AI-native game development studio that uses fleets of autonomous AI coding agents to build, ship, and operate video games. The company offers full-service game development delivered in days at the cost of a single full-time employee, along with automated live-ops pipelines, a multiplayer engine optimized for AI coding agents, an AI-native asset and media management system, and autonomous generation of ads and creative from game builds. Featured titles include Zero Hour, a narrative game set on a frozen planet, and Imperfect World, an RPG built around time-loop mechanics. Backed by a16z (SR02) and Konvoy. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes a marketing site and contact channel but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Wendys
providers.description: The Wendy's Company is a leading international quick-service restaurant chain operating over 7,000 restaurants worldwide. Wendy's operates digital commerce channels including the Wendy's mobile app, online ordering, and a loyalty rewards program. The company uses AI-powered drive-thru ordering (FreshAI) powered by Google Cloud, and integrates with third-party delivery platforms including DoorDash, Grubhub, and Uber Eats. Wendy's uses PAR Technology for loyalty program advancement and NCR Aloha for POS systems. No public developer API is available; digital ordering is powered through internal platforms and third-party integrations.

providers.name: Westmag
providers.description: Western Magnetics (Westmag) designs and manufactures brushless DC (BLDC) drone motors and robot actuators in South San Francisco, California. Built and scaled in America and NDAA-compliant from day one, Westmag is a vertically integrated motor company spanning design, manufacturing, and supply chain — producing high-volume BLDC drone motors for Group 1, 2, and 3 UAS platforms (20-100mm stators, Kv 100-3,000, outrunner and inrunner) and integrated actuators for humanoid and mobile robots (torque 1-150Nm, 24-48V, gearing 6:1-12:1). Founded by David Hansen (CEO) and Jordan Sanders (COO) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Menlo Ventures, and NFDG. This is a hardware company; it currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Zag Bio
providers.description: Zag Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing thymus-targeted therapies for autoimmune diseases. The company engineers bifunctional antibodies that deliver self-antigens to antigen-presenting cells in the thymus, harnessing the body's natural process of central immune tolerance so developing immune cells learn to recognize, tolerate, and protect the body's own tissues. Its pipeline includes ZAG-101, a candidate for Type 1 Diabetes. Founded and incubated by Polaris Partners, Zag Bio launched publicly in October 2025 with an $80M Series A. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company; as a therapeutics developer it publishes no public API or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: 2NDNATURE
providers.description: 2NDNATURE is a Santa Cruz, California environmental technology company that builds cloud-based stormwater management and water-quality software. Its flagship product, 2NFORM, is GIS-powered MS4/NPDES compliance software that helps municipalities automate stormwater permit reporting, track assets and BMPs, detect illicit discharges, and run construction and post-construction programs. Rainsteward is its corporate water-stewardship platform for reducing costs and maximizing the value of stormwater investments. The company embeds peer-reviewed environmental science into an enterprise SaaS platform and is backed by Techstars. No public developer API program has been identified; the 2NFORM and Rainsteward applications are gated SaaS logins.

providers.name: Acts Retirement-Life Communities
providers.description: Acts Retirement-Life Communities is a not-for-profit operator of continuing care retirement communities (CCRCs) headquartered in West Point, Pennsylvania. Founded in 1972, Acts operates 28 senior living campuses across nine Mid-Atlantic and Southeastern U.S. states (Alabama, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Maryland, New Jersey, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina) and serves approximately 10,000 residents. Its core service lines are independent living for adults 55+, assisted living, memory care, skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, and on-campus health services delivered under the Acts Life Care contract model. Acts publishes no public developer APIs, no OpenAPI specifications, no SDKs, and no developer portal — its digital surface consists of a marketing website, a community directory, an iCIMS-hosted careers portal at careers-actslife.icims.com, and a separate health-services marketing site at actshealthservices.org. This repository documents the organization and its likely senior-living IT vendor stack for ecosystem mapping purposes; it does not document a developer API surface because none is published.

providers.name: ADP Workforce Now
providers.description: ADP Workforce Now is ADP's cloud-based human capital management (HCM) suite for mid-sized businesses, covering payroll, HR, benefits administration, time and attendance, talent management, and analytics in a single platform. The product offers tax filing, compliance reporting, mobile self-service, and marketplace integrations through ADP's developer ecosystem. The ADP Workforce Now APIs (HCM v2) use OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect with mutual TLS client certificates and expose worker, payroll, time, benefits, and talent data through ADP API Central.

providers.name: Afresh Technologies
providers.description: Afresh Technologies builds an AI platform for grocery retail that helps supermarkets and distributors manage fresh food, reducing shrink, improving in-stock rates, and cutting food waste across store ordering, inventory management, production planning, recipe management, and distribution-center buying. Its machine-learning decision engine forecasts demand for perishable, random-weight, and bulk items where operational data is inherently messy, and is also offered as a backend Replenishment API that plugs Afresh's forecasting and ordering logic into a retailer's existing front-end systems without changing in-store associate workflows. The company is based in San Francisco and is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: AlixPartners
providers.description: AlixPartners is a global consulting firm founded in 1981 in Detroit, with over 3,500 people across more than 40 countries, specializing in turnaround and restructuring, corporate performance improvement, M&A, investigations, and digital/AI transformation. AlixPartners does not publish a public developer portal or REST API surface; technology value is delivered through client-specific engagements, proprietary tools such as the AI Profit Engine for retail and the Rapid G&A Diagnostic, and a flagship public thought leadership surface anchored by the annual AlixPartners Disruption Index (3,200+ executives across 11 countries and 10 industries) and the AlixTalks podcast (RSS via Podbean). Public consumption is via the alixpartners.com website, downloadable PDF reports, an email subscription preference center, and the AlixTalks Podbean RSS feed.

providers.name: AnyTax
providers.description: AnyTax provides API‑driven tax solutions, offering tax filing, estimation, and planning services through a white‑label integration. Their platform enables banks, financial advisors, and fintechs to embed tax calculations via REST APIs or SDKs, supporting individuals, freelancers, and small businesses. The service focuses on seamless data connectivity, compliance, and customizable tax products, aiming to make tax processes accessible and automated for any financial platform.

providers.name: Arkoshealth
providers.description: Arkos Health is a healthcare technology company that partners with payers, providers, and patients to deliver value‑based care solutions. Since 2018, it offers integrated clinical services, care coordination, and data‑driven insights through its proprietary Arkos360 platform, aiming to simplify complex healthcare processes, reduce costs, and improve outcomes across its network of providers and members.

providers.name: Arris Composites
providers.description: Arris Composites is a Berkeley‑based advanced manufacturing company that develops high‑performance, lightweight carbon‑fiber composite structures using its patented Additive Molding technology. Founded in 2017, it serves aerospace, defense, consumer products, cycling and other industries with sustainable, high‑strength parts at scale.

providers.name: Artifact
providers.description: Artifact is a consumer service that captures and preserves family stories through professional, guided interviews. The company conducts remote 30-minute interviews with a family member and edits each one into a studio-quality ~20-minute audio episode, hosted on a private webpage where relatives can add photos and share the recording. Episodes are priced per interview, positioning the product as a way to record a loved one's life story and memories. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) in the consumer sector. As of 2026 the company announced it is winding down: new Artifacts are no longer sold, and previously purchased interviews may be scheduled through October 31. The service exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Augury
providers.description: Augury is a New York City-headquartered industrial AI company founded in 2011 by Gal Shaul and Saar Yoskovitz that profiles itself as the leader in Machine Health and Production Health for manufacturing. Its flagship offering pairs purpose-built IoT vibration, temperature, and magnetic sensors — most prominently the Halo Node and earlier Auguscope hardware — with a cloud platform that applies prescriptive AI diagnostics to rotating and electrical equipment, advertised as delivering 75% fewer false alarms than threshold-based vibration systems and trained on more than one billion hours of machine monitoring data. Augury's product portfolio spans Machine Health (predictive maintenance for assets such as motors, pumps, fans, compressors, and gearboxes), Process Health (process optimization software acquired with Seebo in 2022 for yield, waste, and energy improvements), and an Industrial AI Workforce of AI agents that act on combined machine and operational data. The company runs an integration ecosystem branded Augury Plus (CMMS/EAM connectors for SAP PM, IBM Maximo, Infor EAM, MaintainX, and cloud/industrial platforms including Microsoft Azure, PTC, and AVEVA Connect), Augury On (OEM-embedded Machine Health with partners such as Grundfos, Schneider Electric, Trane, Carrier, Bently Nevada, and Baker Hughes), and Augury By (service partners including Accenture, Deloitte, Bain, McKinsey, Sodexo, Aramark, and AECOM). Augury closed a $75M Series F in February 2025 at a $1B+ valuation led by Lightrock with Insight Partners, Eclipse, Qumra Capital, La Maison Partners, SE Ventures, and Qualcomm Ventures, reports a 5x revenue increase since 2021, and serves 170+ global manufacturers across 40+ countries including Heineken, PepsiCo (Frito-Lay), Colgate-Palmolive, Shell, and Hershey's. The company commercializes through hardware-plus-subscription contracts and embedded OEM agreements, references public APIs and certified system integrator partners for custom integrations into customer enterprise systems, and does not publish an open developer portal, OpenAPI description, SDK, or public-facing API reference for the Halo platform.

providers.name: Avaneer Health
providers.description: Avaneer Health provides a real‑time healthcare revenue cycle management platform that connects payers and providers to deliver accurate insurance coverage information instantly. By simplifying data exchange, Avaneer improves outcomes, reduces claim errors, and accelerates care delivery across the healthcare ecosystem.

providers.name: Avride
providers.description: Avride is a leading developer in the autonomous vehicle and delivery robot industry. Founded in 2017, the company builds and operates autonomous cars and delivery robots, serving over 250,000 customers and completing more than 200,000 deliveries. Avride’s technology focuses on safety, scalability, and adaptability across diverse urban environments.

providers.name: Axoni
providers.description: Axoni is a New York-based financial data infrastructure company that provides real-time, automated replication of data between institutions, reducing reconciliations, data pipeline management cost, and operational risk across capital markets. Its platform lets banks, asset managers, and market infrastructure providers rapidly deploy critical financial networks and share post-trade data in real time. Axoni is used by leading institutions including JPMorgan, Deutsche Bank, BlackRock, and Citigroup, and has been recognized by Risk.net, the A-Team Group, and Forbes Fintech 50. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and is backed by a16z and DCVC. Axoni does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs; its documentation surface is access-gated to customers.

providers.name: Boardy
providers.description: Boardy is an AI networking agent — an "AI Superconnector" that facilitates meaningful professional introductions. Users message Boardy (via chat and voice) to describe who they want to meet, and it matches them with relevant people from its network, sharing contact details only after both parties explicitly opt in to connect. Boardy is a free consumer product backed by Creandum; it uses public LinkedIn profile information to facilitate introductions and documents its data handling in a GDPR-aligned privacy policy and terms of service. Boardy publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time — its public surface is a marketing site, legal pages, and an llms.txt for AI agents.

providers.name: BrainCo
providers.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

providers.name: Breezm
providers.description: Breezm is a South Korean eyewear company that offers custom 3D‑scanned prescription glasses. Their platform lets users scan their face online, undergo a detailed 12‑step eye exam, and order personalized frames that are produced using 3D printing and laser cutting. The service emphasizes sustainability by reducing material waste and carbon emissions, and provides a 45‑day guarantee with after‑care support. Founded by Seong‑woo Kim and Hyung‑jin Park, Breezm operates retail locations in Seoul and ships internationally, blending technology with fashion to deliver tailored vision solutions.

providers.name: Bwsensing
providers.description: Bwsensing designs and manufactures high‑precision inertial measurement sensors, inclinometers, IMUs, and related solutions for industries such as construction, energy, transportation, and medical devices. Their products enable accurate orientation, motion tracking, and structural health monitoring, supporting smart infrastructure and autonomous systems. The company emphasizes advanced sensor technology, robust data analytics, and integration with IoT platforms to deliver reliable, real‑time insights for critical applications.

providers.name: Capstack
providers.description: Capstack Technologies operates a digital bank-to-bank marketplace that lets banks, credit unions, and other financial institutions trade whole loans and loan participations, access liquidity, and manage portfolio concentration risk. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Miami, FL, the SaaS platform integrates with originating banks' core banking systems and loan-origination systems (LOS) to surface loans available for syndication, then lets participating institutions search by criteria, ask questions live, and submit bids. It adds loan servicing (payment processing, remittance reporting, loan status tracking) and real-time portfolio analytics, specializing in commercial real estate, multifamily residential, and farmland loans. The marketplace has featured over $2B in assets across 200+ registered banks and credit unions. Capstack is backed by Cowboy Ventures and Citi Ventures. This is a private enterprise platform accessed via a demo/onboarding flow; no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation are published at this time.

providers.name: Cariloop
providers.description: Cariloop provides a Caregiver Support Platform that helps employers offer backup care benefits and guidance to employees managing caregiving responsibilities. The solution includes expert tools, flexible support, and resources to enable working caregivers to manage care with confidence, improving employee wellbeing and retention.

providers.name: Cartwheel Care
providers.description: Cartwheel (Cartwheel Care) is a school-based youth mental health provider that partners with K-12 school districts to deliver rapid-access, evidence-based therapy and psychiatric care to students. Through licensed clinicians it offers individual and group therapy, medication management, and parent guidance, with Care Coordinators contacting families within 24 hours of a school referral and initial appointments typically available within 7-10 days; a course of care generally lasts two to six months. The company is backed by General Catalyst and operates across 25+ school districts in multiple states. Cartwheel publishes no public API or developer surface; its software footprint is a school- and family-facing web application at app.cartwheel.org, hosted on the HIPAA-compliant Aptible platform.

providers.name: CFEX
providers.description: CFEX provides a utility‑grade billing and settlement platform for energy, compute, and AI value chains. Its mission is to streamline granular, contract‑based transactions between buyers and sellers, minimizing errors, lowering costs, and improving auditability. The founding team brings decades of experience in utilities, energy, telecom, and digital media, delivering solutions that monetize goods and services, optimize revenue, and support AI-driven markets.

providers.name: Chainalysis123
providers.description: Chainalysis123 is a leading blockchain data platform providing investigative, compliance, and analytics solutions for law enforcement, financial institutions, and businesses. It offers tools such as Reactor, Wallet Scan, KYT monitoring, and AI-driven agents to trace crypto transactions, assess risk, and prevent fraud across the cryptocurrency ecosystem.

providers.name: Chestnut
providers.description: Chestnut is an AI-native operating system for insurance distribution, built for insurance carriers to manage the entire producer lifecycle. The Seattle-based, Andreessen Horowitz-backed company combines a purpose-built insurance data model with an API-first architecture and an agentic AI layer, providing producer onboarding automation (including NIPR integration), hierarchy configuration, incentive compensation management, debt management, performance tracking, and compensation intelligence. Chestnut positions its platform as a system of record that bridges carriers' operational needs to an agentic AI future, with an API-first, MCP-ready backend. Its public API and developer documentation are gated for carrier customers, so no public specification is available for the catalog at this time.

providers.name: Clearballotgroupinc
providers.description: Clearballotgroupinc is a technology company focused on providing secure, transparent, and verifiable ballot handling solutions for elections and organizational voting. The platform aims to modernize the voting process through digital tools that ensure integrity, accessibility, and auditability, catering to both public sector elections and private organizational decision-making. While detailed public documentation is limited, the company positions itself as a bridge between traditional ballot methods and innovative digital solutions, emphasizing security and compliance with electoral standards.

providers.name: Clicktivated
providers.description: Clicktivated is a video technology platform that turns existing video content into interactive, shoppable experiences without re-shooting or re-editing. Its "Activate, Distribute, Optimize" workflow makes any video clickable the same day, deploys it programmatically across DSPs, SSPs, publishers, and direct site embeds, and captures first-party intent signals - item-level and place-level - to improve targeting, measure lift, and drive better performance. The company serves retail brands closing the gap between inspiration and purchase, and tourism brands converting inspiration into itineraries. Founded as Clicktivated Video, Inc. and backed by Techstars, with offices in Detroit, New York, Dubai, and Sydney.

providers.name: Complete Farmer
providers.description: Complete Farmer is an agritech platform connecting African farmers, buyers, and vendors through a data‑driven marketplace. It offers tools for growers to access inputs, expert support, and market access, while enabling buyers to source high‑quality produce. The solution aims to reduce fragmentation in African agriculture, improve supply‑chain transparency, and foster sustainable growth across the continent.

providers.name: ControlRooms.ai
providers.description: ControlRooms.ai provides an agentic troubleshooting system for energy and chemical plant operations. It uses large harmony models to detect anomalies before traditional alarms fire, offering proactive advice, logging, and AI‑drafted shift summaries. The platform integrates with existing DCS, Teams, and mobile apps to help operators mitigate issues early, improving safety and efficiency across refining, fertilizers, petrochemicals, and related sectors.

providers.name: Cool Planet
providers.description: CoolPlanet is an enterprise energy-management and decarbonisation software company. Its platform, CoolPlanetOS, centralises real-time energy data across multi-site industrial estates, applies AI-driven anomaly detection and efficiency insights, benchmarks performance across facilities, and automates energy and compliance reporting. CoolPlanet pairs the software with consulting and on-site execution services to help manufacturing, pharmaceutical, food and beverage, commercial real estate, mining and shipping enterprises cut energy costs and carbon emissions. Backed by GV (Google Ventures). No public developer API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Course Hero
providers.description: Course Hero is an online learning platform where students and educators access more than 25 million course-specific study resources — practice problems, study guides, class notes, step-by-step explanations, essays, and lab reports — alongside 24/7 tutoring and AI-assisted study tools. Founded in 2006 by Andrew Grauer at Cornell University and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Course Hero is part of Learneo, a family of learning and productivity brands that also includes QuillBot, Symbolab, LitCharts, CliffsNotes, Scribbr, Bartleby, and LanguageTool. Course Hero exposes only internal, undocumented web APIs (under /api/) that power its consumer web and mobile apps; it publishes no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or partner API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital, Sierra Ventures, and SV Angel.

providers.name: CropConex
providers.description: CropConex provides a specialized commodity management software platform that serves as the operating system for global agricultural supply chains. It streamlines trading and logistics operations by unifying inventory, contracts, orders, and payments in a shared workspace. Users can source products, create contracts, coordinate logistics, and manage payments with real‑time visibility, reducing manual work and errors. The platform offers features such as inventory tracking, contract management, compliance tools, and collaborative workspaces for internal teams and external partners, aiming to improve efficiency and decision‑making across the ag supply chain.

providers.name: DataNeuron
providers.description: DataNeuron provides a no-code platform for LLM customization, data annotation, and agentic workflows. It offers tools for data curation, fine-tuning, evaluation, model distillation, and classic NLP pipelines, enabling enterprises to build high-quality datasets and tailor large language models efficiently. The platform includes a knowledge hub, security features, and integrations for rapid deployment.

providers.name: Dewpoint Therapeutics
providers.description: Dewpoint Therapeutics is a biotechnology company applying the emerging science of biomolecular condensates to drug discovery. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, with an additional research site in Dresden, Germany, Dewpoint has built an AI-powered, end-to-end platform (ERSA, powered by ERSAi) spanning target discovery, condensate-modulating (c-mod) drug discovery, optimization, and development. Its pipeline targets previously undruggable diseases across oncology, neurodegeneration, cardiopulmonary, and virology, with collaborations including Bayer, Novo Nordisk, Evotec, and Chemify. Dewpoint is a General Catalyst portfolio company; it operates internal research platforms and the open CD-CODE condensate knowledge platform (condensates.com), but does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Dominion Dynamics
providers.description: Dominion Dynamics Inc. is a Canadian defence-technology company (Kanata/Ottawa, Ontario) building the autonomy stack for the Arctic and other extreme, infrastructure-constrained operating environments. It develops integrated autonomy, edge sensing, communications, and command-and-control systems for defence, security, and critical infrastructure. Its AuraNet platform is a peer-to-peer sensor mesh that fuses EO/IR/SAR imagery, SIGINT/EW/RF signals, telemetry, and structured reporting into a unified local intelligence stream that interoperates with existing allied C2 architectures, and its Aurion product is an open-source government procurement intelligence platform built on Canadian federal open data. Founded by Anduril alum Eliot Pence, the company raised a $139M CAD Series A (2026) led by Georgian. This profile currently has no public developer/API surface; the entry captures the company identity, security.txt, and llms.txt the company publishes.

providers.name: Donnerstag Ai
providers.description: Donnerstag.ai (Donnerstag.ai Technologies GmbH) is a Frankfurt-based enterprise fintech building an AI Reconciliation Layer for enterprise finance. Its platform automates financial reconciliation at the line-item level across accounts payable, accounts receivable, bank, and intercompany flows, adapting to each customer's systems, data sources, workflows, and roles. The stated goal is 100% line-item coverage at T+0 so the financial close becomes a confirmation rather than a month-end scramble, with an immutable audit trail for GoBD, IFRS, SOX, and BEPS. The company serves logistics, payment service providers, retail and e-commerce, manufacturing, human resources, and construction, is EU-hosted in Frankfurt, and is founded by Barbaros Ozbugutu and Volkan Ozkan and backed by Speedinvest. As a solution-and-services provider it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or docs.

providers.name: EcoG
providers.description: EcoG is a Munich-based technology company that builds the software and hardware platform powering electric-vehicle DC fast chargers. Its EcoG OS operating system, Universal Core platform, and controllers let charger manufacturers, charge point operators (CPOs), and EV businesses design, launch, and scale DC charging solutions with reduced complexity, claiming more than 15% market share in Europe with operations across India and North America. For developers, EcoG OS exposes an on-device programmatic surface (an OpenAPI-based application interface, a local web interface, and the LifeC remote management tool) so smart value-added charging applications can be built and run at the device level. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from EcoG's public website; it publishes no public REST API developer portal or specification.

providers.name: Electra Therapeutics
providers.description: Electra Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2018 and pioneering first-in-class antibody therapies directed at signal regulatory proteins (SIRP) for immunological diseases and cancer. Its lead candidate, ELA026 (ipsoprubart), is a monoclonal antibody targeting SIRP-alpha/beta1/gamma on myeloid cells and T lymphocytes to selectively deplete the pathological immune cells that drive the cytokine storm in secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH); it is in the pivotal SURPASS Phase 2/3 study. A second SIRP-targeted program, ELA822, is directed at activated T lymphocytes for immunology and inflammation indications. The company has raised roughly $267M from investors including OrbiMed, Nextech Invest, EQT Life Sciences and Westlake Village BioPartners. Electra publishes a corporate website, pipeline, publications, clinical-trial and news pages, but no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Finom
providers.description: Finom is a European fintech headquartered in Amsterdam that provides business banking, invoicing, and financial management for entrepreneurs, freelancers, and SMEs. Operating as a licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), Finom offers multi-currency business accounts, 24/7 SEPA Instant and SWIFT payments, direct debits, Visa Business physical and virtual cards with up to 3% cashback, compliant e-invoicing (ZUGFeRD, XRechnung), and integrations with accounting platforms such as DATEV, Lexware, sevDesk, Xero, and QuickBooks. It serves Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and the Netherlands with region-specific tooling. Finom does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public discovery, security, and operational surface (llms.txt, security.txt / Intigriti VDP, domain security, status page).

providers.name: Frontier Medicines
providers.description: Frontier Medicines is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering the discovery and development of small-molecule covalent drugs against disease-causing proteins long considered undruggable. Its proprietary Frontier Platform pairs chemoproteomics with artificial intelligence and machine learning and a proprietary Druggability Atlas that maps thousands of novel covalent binding opportunities across the human proteome. Lead precision oncology candidates include FMC-376 (KRAS G12C), FMC-220 (a p53 Y220C reactivator), and FMC-242 (PI3Kalpha-RAS). Founded in 2018 with offices in Boston, Massachusetts and South San Francisco, California, the company is backed by DCVC and other life-science investors. Frontier Medicines was added to the API Evangelist network as a DCVC portfolio company; it publishes no public API or developer surface, so this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Gambit
providers.description: Gambit Security is an Israeli cyber-resilience company, founded in 2024 by Unit 8200 veterans Alon Gromakov (CEO), Sa'ar Elias (CPO) and May Kogan (CTO), that emerged from stealth in February 2026 with $61M in seed and Series A funding from Cyberstarts, Kleiner Perkins and Spark Capital. Its product, Balens, is an AI-native autonomous resilience platform that continuously maps every resource in an environment into end-to-end business applications, revealing dependencies, backup coverage and immutability, detecting infrastructure drift, scoring Cyber Resilience Posture Management (CRPM) and validating real-world recovery paths against ransomware and outages. It also automates compliance evidence for frameworks such as DORA, NIST CSF and SOX. Gambit does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Google Vids
providers.description: Google Vids is an AI-powered video creation and editing application in Google Workspace that enables business users to produce professional videos without design expertise by combining Gemini-assisted outlining, Veo 3 generative video clips, AI avatars, recording studio capabilities, and a royalty-free stock media library. Vids is available on Business and Enterprise Workspace plans as well as Google AI Pro and Ultra consumer plans, with collaboration handled through standard Workspace sharing controls. There is no public developer REST API for Google Vids at this time; this index tracks the product as a documentation-only reference.

providers.name: Hallmark Cards
providers.description: Hallmark Cards, Inc. is a privately held, family-owned greeting card, gift, gift wrap and ornament company headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri, founded in 1910 by J.C. Hall. Its portfolio spans Hallmark greeting cards and Keepsake Ornaments sold through Hallmark Gold Crown stores and mass retailers, the Crayola and Hallmark Business Connections (B2B greeting card programs) subsidiaries, and Hallmark Media (Hallmark Channel, Hallmark+). Hallmark publishes no public developer program: developer.hallmark.com does not resolve, api.hallmark.com serves a stock ASP.NET template with no documented endpoints, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, A2A agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known discovery document was found on any Hallmark host on 2026-09-17. Retail and supply-chain partners integrate through bilateral EDI (Hallmark Global Services) and Hallmark Business Connections' CRM/SSO integrations, none of which are documented publicly.

providers.name: Hessian
providers.description: Hessian is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building a forward-deployed AI agent platform for automating business operations. Its engineers embed on-site to map real workflows, then build and operate custom AI agents on the Hessian platform to run those processes end-to-end — spanning sales proposals, financial reconciliation, data management, and internal-system synchronization.
