Payall markets a lightweight, backward- compatible technical integration and business-friendly APIs (plus bulk/Excel upload) so banks, credit unions, EMIs, and other regulated institutions can offer safe, profitable international transfers. Public developer documentation and an open API specification are not published; the API surface at api.payall.com is authentication-gated.

providers.name: Payment24
providers.description: Payment24 is a white-label payment platform specializing in fuel and fleet payment solutions for oil companies, banks, and retailers, primarily across Africa. Its technology lets clients design and launch branded payment products under their own name — fuel payments and mobile payments, loyalty and rewards, POS terminals, electronic vouchers, B2B and B2C prepaid and store-account cards, EV charging payments, and wet-stock and fuel-in-tank management — alongside banking-grade issuing, acquiring, card management, and merchant management, plus fleet fuel management and telematics. Payment24 operates as a technology partner rather than a public self-serve API provider, so it publishes no open developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Pearl
providers.description: Pearl is a dental AI computer-vision company whose FDA-cleared products - Second Opinion (real-time pathology and restorative detection on 2D and 3D dental radiographs), Practice Intelligence (clinical and operational analytics over full practice-management-system data), and Precheck (AI insurance claim review) - are delivered by embedding Pearl's cloud AI into third-party imaging and practice management software rather than through a public, self-serve developer API. Pearl integrates natively with 40+ imaging/PMS platforms (DEXIS, Carestream, Planmeca Romexis, Dentsply Sirona Sidexis, Apteryx XVWeb, MiPACS, Open Dental, Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Curve, Denticon, Software of Excellence EXACT) and is an authorized vendor in the Henry Schein One API Exchange. There is no publicly documented, self-signup Pearl developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI reference; API access is partner/OEM-gated and arranged through Pearl's integrations and sales teams. The API surfaces below are modeled from Pearl's public product descriptions and integration architecture, not from published Pearl API reference documentation.

providers.name: Pebblely
providers.description: Pebblely creates AI product photos that help you sell more. No Photoshop skills required. The Pebblely API allows programmatic access to AI-powered product photography generation, background creation, and image styling.

providers.name: Perennial Labs
providers.description: Perennial is an on-chain (EVM) perpetual-derivatives protocol — a composable, fully on-chain primitive for permissionless perpetual markets, liquidity provisioning (LPs up to 50x), vaults, collateral accounts, and intent-based order flow with off-chain solvers. Built by Equilibria and backed by Polychain, its developer surface is Solidity smart contracts (MultiInvoker batching) plus first-party TypeScript and Python SDKs and a subgraph, rather than a hosted REST API. The v2 protocol has been audited by Zellic and Sherlock and runs an Immunefi bug-bounty program (up to $500k). The hosted application (perennial.finance) has since been sunset, but the protocol contracts, documentation, and SDKs remain published.

providers.name: Pic Collage
providers.description: Pic Collage (PicCollage) is a consumer photo and video editing mobile app built by Cardinal Blue Software that lets people create collages, greeting cards, and personalized designs from templates, stickers, backgrounds, GIFs, and AI-powered editing tools. It ships on iOS and Android and has been backed by 500 Global. PicCollage exposes no public developer API — its Terms of Service explicitly restrict access to a private, app-only API — so there is no developer portal, documentation, SDK, MCP server, or machine-readable API surface to catalog. This profile captures the company identity and its public web properties.

providers.name: Pinger
providers.description: Pinger, Inc. is a San Jose, California mobile communications company founded in 2005 by former Palm managers Greg Woock and Joe Sipher. It builds consumer and small-business calling and texting apps rather than developer infrastructure: TextFree (launched 2009, the original free texting and calling app with a free US phone number), Sideline (a second phone number for work and privacy, with team number sharing, spam filtering, auto-reply and voicemail transcription) and Index (a dedicated business line with auto-reply, scheduling, broadcast messaging and payment collection). Sideline and TextFree have together been used by more than 100 million people. Pinger publishes no public developer program, API reference, OpenAPI definition or SDK — its integrations run the other way, with Index consuming third-party calendar (Google, iCloud, Outlook) and payment (PayPal, Venmo, Square) services. The one machine-readable artifact it publishes is an llms.txt information sheet on the Sideline domain.

providers.name: Pluto Brand
providers.description: Pluto (Plutopillow) is a Los Angeles-based direct-to-consumer sleep wellness brand best known for the Pluto Pillow, a made-to-order pillow custom-built around each customer's unique sleep profile via an online sleep quiz. The company also sells the PUFF body pillow, the POD travel pillow, and temperature-regulating bedding, and offers a 125-night risk-free trial with free shipping and returns. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, Pluto is a consumer e-commerce brand with no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or partner-integration surface at this time; this profile captures its public web properties for discovery.

providers.name: Quantum Circuits
providers.description: Quantum Circuits, Inc. is a quantum computing hardware company (a Yale University spinout) building superconducting quantum systems with built-in error detection. Its dual-rail cavity qubits pair Quantum Error Detection (QED), Real-Time Control Flow (RTCF), and Error Detection Handling (EDH), and its Aqumen Seeker QPU (introduced November 2024) targets stable, repeatable, fault-tolerant quantum computation. The company engages early users through a Strategic Quantum Release (SQR) program that includes a simulator and access to Aqumen Seeker systems, rather than a public self-serve API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Qwil
providers.description: Qwil (qwil.co) is a financial-technology company and a 500 Global portfolio company. It operates a consumer-facing web and mobile application ("Qwil WebApp" at app.qwil.com) backed by a private, authenticated REST API at api.qwil.co. The platform connects to users' bank accounts through Plaid and uses Firebase Authentication (Google Identity Platform) for identity, with bearer tokens presented to a Django REST Framework API. Qwil does not publish a public API specification, developer portal, or SDK documentation; the API is private and partner-gated. Note that qwil.co is distinct from Qwil Messenger (qwil.io), an unrelated secure client-collaboration platform. This profile was enriched by live probing of Qwil's public network surface; most standard developer artifacts are unavailable because Qwil exposes no public developer program.

providers.name: Rallybio
providers.description: Rallybio Corporation (NASDAQ RLYB) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in New Haven, Connecticut, founded in 2018, developing and commercializing life-transforming therapies for patients with severe and rare diseases. Its pipeline spans maternal-fetal health, complement dysregulation, hematology, and metabolic disorders, led by RLYB116, a differentiated complement component 5 (C5) inhibitor, and RLYB332, a long-acting matriptase-2 (MTP-2) antibody for iron-overload disorders. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a pharmaceutical company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures corporate identity only.

providers.name: Re:Build
providers.description: Re:Build Manufacturing is a U.S.-based industrial engineering and manufacturing company that takes complex products from concept to full-rate production through integrated design, engineering, and scalable domestic manufacturing. Founded to rebuild American manufacturing capacity, the company operates a family of specialized engineering and production businesses across more than 14 U.S. locations, spanning aerospace and defense, electrification, energy and environment, medical devices, and robotics and automation. With 400+ engineers and roughly one million square feet of industrial footprint, Re:Build partners with startups and established manufacturers to develop, industrialize, and produce advanced physical products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment confirms it is an industrial/manufacturing company with no public API, developer, or machine surface at this time.

providers.name: Relay Payments
providers.description: Relay Payments operates a secure digital payment network purpose-built for the freight and trucking industry. Its mobile app and platform let carriers, owner-operators, brokers, and merchants transact contactlessly for diesel fuel, lumper (dock unloading) fees, scales, parking, truck repairs, and freight payments between brokers and carriers, replacing cash, fleet checks, and legacy fuel cards while reducing fraud and streamlining back-office reconciliation. Relay is backed by Ribbit Capital. Partner/system integration is offered under a Relay System Integration Agreement, with developer documentation gated behind partner authentication at docs.relaypayments.com; no public API specification is currently published.

providers.name: Resolution Games
providers.description: Resolution Games is a Stockholm-based studio building games for virtual, augmented, and mixed reality platforms including Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, and PlayStation VR. Its titles include Demeo, Spatial Ops, Blaston, Bait!, and Ultimechs. The company is venture-backed (Creandum, GV, Partech) and runs a consumer-facing games business. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web properties (blog, support, legal pages) for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Revlon
providers.description: Revlon is a global beauty company whose portfolio spans color cosmetics, fragrance, skin care, hair color, hair care, beauty tools, and antiperspirants / deodorants. The company markets Revlon, Elizabeth Arden, Almay, Mitchum, Cutex, Charlie, SinfulColors, and Ultima II, along with a portfolio of licensed prestige and celebrity fragrance brands. Revlon Consumer Products Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the Southern District of New York on June 15, 2022 and emerged on May 2, 2023 as a privately held company controlled by its former lenders (including BrandCo noteholders such as King Street Capital, Glendon Capital, and Angelo Gordon), having cut roughly $2.7 billion of debt from its balance sheet. Today Revlon operates as a private company with reduced leverage, selling through mass-market retail and prestige channels worldwide. Revlon does not publish a public developer API; supplier, retailer, and partner integrations occur through private commercial channels (e-commerce platform integrations, EDI / GDSN feeds for retailers, and the corporate procurement portal).

providers.name: Sail Biomedicines
providers.description: Sail Biomedicines is a Cambridge, Massachusetts preclinical biotechnology company created in October 2023 by Flagship Pioneering through the merger of Laronde and Senda Biosciences, and it is the company this profile's legacy `laronde` slug refers to. Sail combines Laronde's Endless RNA (eRNA) platform — synthetic circular RNA engineered to be translated persistently inside the body — with Senda's programmable lipid and natural nanoparticle delivery chemistry, and layers generative AI on the combined dataset to design what the company calls fully programmable medicines. Its lead effort is in vivo CAR-T for autoimmune disease: instructing a patient's own T cells to reprogram themselves inside the body rather than extracting, engineering and reinfusing them, an approach Sail markets as "immune reset". In July 2026 Johnson & Johnson committed $785 million up front (including a $465 million equity investment) plus up to $140 million in milestones and took an exclusive option to acquire the company for a further $2.58 billion. Sail sells therapeutics, not software: it publishes no API, no SDK, no machine-readable specification and no developer documentation, and it operates no public source-code organization.

providers.name: Sav
providers.description: Sav Technologies Limited operates Sav (sav.money), a UAE-based intelligent financial platform that lets users track, save, invest, and grow their wealth across accounts. Sav offers a suite of consumer products including Gold (physical gold investment from AED 10), MyMoney (financial management and savings), Card (a prepaid card with cashback), Wealth (investing), Sav Pro (premium membership), and an upcoming Credit product. Sav describes itself as extending the APIs and technology components of licensed financial services providers to its users. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass, Sav publishes a consumer app and marketing site but no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Schrödinger
providers.description: Schrödinger is a New York-headquartered (NASDAQ: SDGR) computational science company that develops a physics-based and AI-driven molecular simulation platform used across drug discovery and materials science. Its flagship desktop modeling environment is Maestro (MS Maestro for materials science), which integrates a deep stack of computational tools — Glide (docking), FEP+ (free energy perturbation), Desmond (molecular dynamics), Jaguar (quantum chemistry), Prime (protein structure prediction), BioLuminate (biologics), LigPrep, QikProp, SiteMap, and WaterMap — together with the Schrödinger-maintained PyMOL visualization system. LiveDesign is the cloud-native enterprise design lab where chemists, biologists, and program teams collaborate on molecules, run computational workflows, and integrate experimental data; it exposes a snap-in API framework for connecting in-house and third-party tooling. The Schrödinger Python API (current release 2026-1) is the primary developer surface, providing programmatic access to molecular structures, Maestro automation, jobcontrol, Glide, FEP+, Desmond, Jaguar, MacroModel, Prime, BioLuminate, and LiveDesign integration (login, export, dataset and column management). Schrödinger also ships KNIME extensions, command-line drivers for every computational product, and maintains a meaningful open-source footprint on GitHub — including PyMOL, maeparser, coordgenlibs, sketcher, gpusimilarity, csmiles, and the fixed-data-table-2 React component. The business has two segments — software licensing to global pharma, biotech, and materials companies, and a co-developed and proprietary drug discovery pipeline. There is no public developer signup or self-serve REST API; access to the platform, Python API, and LiveDesign is gated through commercial licensing and the my.schrodinger.com customer portal.

providers.name: SendWave
providers.description: Sendwave is an international money-transfer service operated by Zepz (the fintech group behind WorldRemit) that lets people send money abroad directly from a mobile app, with a focus on low or no transfer fees and fast delivery to recipients across Africa, Asia and Latin America. Funds can be sent to mobile-money wallets, bank accounts and cash pickup in supported corridors. Sendwave is a consumer-facing app (iOS and Android) and is regulated as a money transmitter in the jurisdictions where it operates (NMLS No. 1179663). As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; enrichment therefore captures its public identity, security posture, and support surface only.

providers.name: Slice
providers.description: Slice is an Indian consumer fintech and small finance bank, founded in 2016 as SlicePay by Rajan Bajaj and headquartered between Bengaluru (corporate) and Guwahati (registered). The company originally built a buy-now-pay-later product and a prepaid-card-plus-credit-line offering aimed at students and young professionals — pitched as a credit-card alternative for India's Gen Z — and at its peak was reportedly issuing over 300,000 prepaid cards per month before RBI's 2022 restrictions on credit-linked PPI products forced a pivot. In October 2023 Slice announced a merger with the regulated North East Small Finance Bank (NESFB), the first fintech-into-bank merger in India; the merger received RBI approval in October 2023, CCI approval in March 2024 and NCLT (Guwahati) approval in August 2024, completed on October 27, 2024, and the combined entity was rebranded as Slice Small Finance Bank in May 2025. Today Slice operates a consumer mobile-first neobank — savings accounts, fixed deposits, UPI, a Slice credit card and rewards — alongside a merchant-facing payments stack exposed through a Merchant API (api.nebank.com) covering bank-account validation, payouts, pay-in/collect, refunds, virtual accounts, balance, transactions and webhook notifications. As of late 2024 the company had raised approximately $387M from investors including Tiger Global, Insight Partners and Blume Ventures.

providers.name: So Sure
providers.description: So Sure (wearesosure.com), operated by Open Insurance Services UK Limited, was a UK app-based social insurance provider offering mobile phone and home contents insurance, known for a social/peer insurance model that rewarded claim-free groups. It was an early portfolio company of 500 Global. The company has stopped selling new policies and has transitioned its mobile phone cover to the Huddle Insurance brand while continuing to service existing customers. So Sure publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Souqalmal
providers.description: Souqalmal was a UAE-based personal-finance comparison marketplace that let consumers across the GCC compare and apply for credit cards, personal loans, bank accounts, and insurance products online. The brand has since transitioned to Yabi (yabimoney.com), an AI-powered financial coaching application offering personalized guidance, budgeting tools, spending tracking, credit checks, and financial-education content on iOS and Android. Backed by 500 Global. The souqalmal.com domain now permanently redirects to yabimoney.com. No public developer, API, or partner-integration surface is currently published.

providers.name: Splice
providers.description: Splice is a New York-based music creation platform serving producers, songwriters, and audio creators. Its core offerings are Splice Sounds, a catalog of millions of 100% royalty-free samples, one-shots, loops, MIDI patterns, and presets sold through a credit-based subscription; Splice INSTRUMENT, a creator-first virtual instrument with monthly free drops and unlimited premium presets via subscription; and a Rent-to-Own Plugins marketplace offering pay-as-you-go full-license access to 130+ professional VST/AU/AAX plugins from third-party vendors such as Xfer (Serum 2), Arturia (V Collection 11 Pro), Spitfire Audio (Abbey Road Two), and XLN Audio (RC-20). Splice ships a desktop app, a mobile app, the Splice Sounds Plugin (beta) for in-DAW browsing, and native integrations for Ableton Live 12.3+, Studio One Pro 7, Studio Pro 8+, and Pro Tools 2025.6+. The revenue model is consumer subscriptions (Sounds+ $12.99/mo, Creator $19.99/mo with 200 credits, Creator+ $39.99/mo with 500 credits, INSTRUMENT $12.99/mo) plus rent-to-own plugin payments. Splice does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or partner program; its GitHub organization at github.com/splice contains internal tooling, GitHub Actions, audio engineering exercises, and forks rather than externally consumable APIs.

providers.name: Stage
providers.description: Stage is a code review tool that reorganizes local git changes and pull requests into logical, ordered "chapters" so engineers can review and merge changes far faster — a workflow built for teams shipping large volumes of AI-generated code. Stage ships an open-source (MIT) command-line tool, "stagereview", that runs entirely on the developer's machine and works with any AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, opencode): it diffs the current branch or a GitHub PR, clusters the hunks into narrated chapters with a prologue, and opens them in a local browser SPA for review. The full hosted Stage experience lives at stagereview.app. Stage is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company founded by Charles Pan and Dean Stratakos.

providers.name: Thales
providers.description: Thales is a global technology leader providing advanced solutions for aerospace, defense, security, and digital identity. The company designs and integrates cutting‑edge systems ranging from secure communications and cyber‑defense to critical infrastructure protection and digital transformation services. With a presence in over 50 countries, Thales serves governments, enterprises, and individuals, delivering trusted technologies that safeguard data, assets, and people across complex environments.

providers.name: The Exploration Company
providers.description: The Exploration Company (TEC) is a European deep-tech space startup founded in July 2021 by Hélène Huby and a team of aerospace engineers from Airbus and ArianeGroup. Headquartered in Munich, Germany with sites in Bordeaux, Oberpfaffenhofen, Italy, France, Houston, and the MENA region, TEC develops Nyx, a family of modular, reusable, in-orbit refuelable spacecraft designed to carry cargo — and eventually humans — to low Earth orbit, lunar orbit, and the Moon, serving space stations and long-distance research missions. The company has raised a €40.5M Series A and a €150M Series B and is a certified B Corp. It exposes no public developer API; interfaces are provided to payload customers via a Payload User's Guide.

providers.name: Totus Medicines
providers.description: Totus Medicines is a biopharmaceutical company developing precision oral medicines against historically "undruggable" disease targets. The company's OmniDEL discovery platform screens targets in their normal cellular environment to identify potent, selective covalent small molecules, drawing on precedents like penicillin and AZT. Totus is advancing a pipeline focused on oncology and immunology & inflammation (I&I), including TOS-358, a covalent PI3Ka inhibitor, and a first-in-class covalent IRF5 inhibitor in clinical development. Headquartered in Emeryville, California, Totus was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage drug-discovery company, Totus publishes no public developer API surface; this profile captures its corporate identity, web properties, and security posture.

providers.name: Treasury
providers.description: Treasury (treasury.app) is a consumer investing and personal-finance education platform that bills itself as "the first investing platform built for learning as a community" and a "non-judgmental investing community." It pairs creator-led learning communities (workshops, coaching, and discussion forums), commission-free brokerage investing accounts with fractional and recurring investments, and self-guided courses on investing, personal finance, and retirement. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and other investors, Treasury has introduced tens of thousands of new investors to the market. It has no traditional public REST/OpenAPI developer platform, but it does expose an agent-native surface: a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at treasury.app/mcp guarded by an OAuth 2.1 authorization server (authorization code + PKCE, dynamic client registration, scope mcp:connect).

providers.name: UpSmith
providers.description: UpSmith is a Dallas, Texas-based company backed by a16z that builds AI agents for home services and skilled trades businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical). Its platform texts customers to confirm appointments, follows up on cold estimates, responds to inbound leads around the clock, and reactivates dormant customers, syncing customer records, job details, and booking data with ServiceTitan through ServiceTitan's official APIs. UpSmith consumes partner APIs (a native ServiceTitan marketplace integration) but does not publish a public developer API of its own.

providers.name: Urban Jungle
providers.description: Urban Jungle Services Ltd is a London-based direct-to-consumer insurtech, founded in 2016 by Jimmy Williams and Greg Smyth to sell home insurance to "Generation Rent" — renters, sharers and students the traditional UK market underserves. It is an FCA-authorised intermediary (FRN 782061, company number 10414152, England and Wales) and a certified B Corp, selling contents, buildings and contents, students contents, tenants liability, landlord, home emergency and public liability cover through its own digital journey at myurbanjungle.com, and claiming over 100,000 customers. Its API posture is partner-gated and undocumented in public. Urban Jungle announced a partnership programme and quote API in 2018, positioned so lettings agents, PropTech firms, institutional landlords and eCommerce sites can serve Urban Jungle quotes inside their own apps without being directly FCA-regulated themselves, but there is no developer portal, no reference documentation, no machine- readable specification and no self-serve signup. The only route in is a partnerships email address on a marketing page. No ACORD, AL3 or NGDS reference appears anywhere on the company's site or in its front-end bundles.

providers.name: Valley National Bank
providers.description: Valley National Bank is a nationally chartered commercial bank (OCC-regulated) and the principal banking subsidiary of Valley National Bancorp (NASDAQ: VLY), a regional financial holding company founded in 1927 with roughly $64 billion in assets and more than 200 offices serving consumers, families, and businesses across New Jersey, New York, Florida, Alabama, California, and Illinois. Its business spans consumer banking, commercial banking, and treasury services. As of this profile Valley National Bank operates no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable API specifications; consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached only through third-party open-finance aggregators (Finicity by Mastercard is documented, alongside general Plaid/Tink connectivity) rather than a directly exposed FDX-conformant or first-party API.

providers.name: Vircle
providers.description: Vircle is a Malaysian family fintech platform, operated by Debit Circles Sdn Bhd, offering a parent app paired with a prepaid card for children so families can give pocket money, assign chores, and teach kids to earn, save, and spend responsibly. It issues a Visa Prepaid Card (Vircle Club) usable at Visa merchants worldwide and a School Card for cafeteria and campus e-store purchases, with real-time spend alerts and parental controls. Card issuance is provided in partnership with Fass Payment Solutions (Fasspay). Vircle is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As a consumer mobile app it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Voldex
providers.description: Voldex (Voldex Entertainment) is a game developer and publisher founded in 2015 that acquires, operates, and grows platform-leading games on Roblox, including Brookhaven, Driving Empire, and NFL Universe Football, collectively reaching over 140 million monthly players. Its stated mission is to "bring people together through fun," pursuing a focused strategy of selectively acquiring and stewarding enduring Roblox experiences rather than broad portfolio expansion. Voldex publishes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or API documentation surface — it is a consumer games studio whose products run inside the Roblox platform. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; it was reviewed by the enrichment pipeline and confirmed to have no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Vytalize Health
providers.description: Vytalize Health is a Hoboken, New Jersey based value-based care company that operates as a Medicare Accountable Care Organization (ACO), partnering with independent primary care practices, group practices, community health centers and existing ACOs to move them into risk-bearing Medicare programs. The company pairs shared-savings economics with a technology and clinical services stack: Vytal Insights, a physician-built clinical decision support product that analyzes claims data, clinical notes, hospital admission-discharge-transfer feeds and social determinants of health to surface point-of-care recommendations; Vytal Care, a suite of remote and in-home programs (transitions of care, chronic disease management, home health review) delivered by an interdisciplinary team of RN care managers, health coaches, pharmacists and licensed clinical social workers; and Vytal Network, its specialist, hospital and ancillary provider network layer. Vytalize supports tens of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries across multiple states. Its software reaches practice partners through an authenticated web portal at app.vytalizehealth.com rather than through a public developer platform.

providers.name: Wevat
providers.description: Wevat is a Seedcamp-backed fintech and travel-tech company operating a mobile app that digitizes VAT (Value Added Tax) refunds for international travellers shopping in France. Instead of paper tax-free forms, shoppers photograph their invoices in the Wevat app, which consolidates purchases across stores into a single digital tax-refund form, validates it at the departure point, and pays out the refund (up to around 13% of spend) in the traveller's chosen currency via credit card, bank transfer, Alipay, or WeChat Pay. Wevat is a consumer mobile-app product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its public web and business identity.

providers.name: Whitespace
providers.description: Whitespace is an AI operating system for wholesale distributors, based in London and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch. The platform connects to a distributor's existing business systems (ERPs such as SAP, NetSuite, Epicor, Infor, Microsoft Dynamics and Sage, plus Salesforce, HubSpot, QuickBooks, Gmail and Outlook) to build a model of operations, then deploys self-improving AI agents that automate demand forecasting, inventory replenishment, order entry, quote generation, customer query responses, and accounts payable and receivable. It targets sectors including industrial supplies, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, building materials, foodservice, consumer goods and textiles. Founded by Alex Tung and Leon Yao. As an early-stage company it currently ships a product but publishes no public API, developer documentation or SDK.

providers.name: Yonder
providers.description: Yonder is a UK-based financial technology company offering rewards credit and debit cards — a "financial membership" that earns points on everyday spending, redeemable across 300+ dining, travel, shopping, entertainment and wellness partners. Cards run on the Mastercard network with no foreign-exchange fees, and Yonder is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) with FSCS-protected accounts held via partner banks. Yonder ships a consumer mobile app and a help centre but does not expose a public developer API or portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (backers include Northzone, Seedcamp and Techstars).

providers.name: 21 Market
providers.description: 21 Market is the API Evangelist network profile for 주식회사 21세기전파상 (21st Century Electronics Shop Co., Ltd.), a South Korean consumer-electronics resale company that operates the Repercent (리퍼센트) service at repercent.com. Repercent buys used smartphones and mobile devices — iPhone, Galaxy, tablets, and laptops — from individual sellers, providing instant online price quotes, fast payment, and a simple pickup/logistics flow for secondhand device trade-in. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company and was surfaced into the network as a venture portfolio lead. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface; this profile captures verified company identity, its live web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: 247Solar
providers.description: 247Solar, Inc. is a zero-carbon energy technology company with MIT origins that designs and builds modular third-generation concentrated solar power (CSP) systems delivering round-the-clock clean electricity and industrial-grade heat. Its 247Solar Plant couples a high-temperature solar receiver (~970C) with the Heat2Power turbine and HeatStore thermal storage, holding energy in ceramic pellets or ordinary sand for 20+ hours without batteries or molten salts. The company targets mining, microgrids, off-grid and rural electrification, industrial heat, economic development zones, grid support, data centers and green hydrogen, and sells through power purchase agreements as well as equipment. Headquartered in Great Falls, Virginia, 247Solar is a hardware and project-development business; it publishes no public API, developer program or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: 3D Glass Solutions
providers.description: 3D Glass Solutions (3DGS) is a US-based pure-play glass foundry in Albuquerque, New Mexico that manufactures photo-definable glass-ceramic substrates for advanced semiconductor packaging. Its patented APEX Glass material supports through-glass vias (TGV), high-density interconnect, integrated passive devices, RF substrates, micro-cavities and 3D heterogeneous integration for wireless communications, aerospace and defense, photonics, HPC/AI and sensor markets. The company sells wafer processing, custom fabrication and design-enablement services — including process design kits (PDKs) delivered through EDA partners such as the AWR software group — rather than software, and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: 42Maru
providers.description: 42Maru is a South Korean AI deep-tech company building a Deep Semantic TA (Text Analytics) and QA (Question Answering) platform that understands the true intent behind a user's question and returns a single answer drawn from large sets of unstructured documents. Its cognitive-search stack pairs document retrieval with Machine Reading Comprehension (MRC) and is delivered as enterprise chatbots (CHAT42), question-answering engines (QA42), natural-language processing (NL42), and the Platform42 SaaS. 42Maru ranked #1 on Stanford's SQuAD 2.0 machine-reading benchmark, won an AWS AI Challenge award, and is a Techstars London alumnus. It was added to the API Evangelist network from the Techstars portfolio and enriched from its public marketing site, GitHub organizations, and gitbook documentation; no public REST API, OpenAPI, first-party SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface was found — Platform42 API access appears to be provisioned per enterprise customer.

providers.name: 4D Lifetec
providers.description: 4D Lifetec AG is a Swiss in-vitro diagnostics company headquartered at Gewerbestrasse 8, 6330 Cham, Switzerland, developing the 4D Lifetest — a non-invasive, immuno-oncological blood test for the early detection of cancer. The test reads a proprietary DNA Damage Sensitivity (DDS) biomarker from a liquid biopsy using single-cell gel electrophoresis (the comet assay), run on the company's own 4D Lifechamber instrument for a fully automated and standardized procedure and scored by 4D LifeAI, its trained image analysis software. The flagship product is 4D Lifetest Lung Dx, with 4D Lifetest Breast Dx, Prostate Dx and Colon Dx as further assays in the same platform, and the company holds patent protection across the US, Europe, China and other territories. 4D Lifetec is a diagnostics manufacturer and laboratory-services company, not a software vendor. Its public web presence is an eight-page SilverStripe marketing and investor-relations site with no developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs, no public GitHub organization and no machine-readable specification of any kind; probing every documented contract location on 4dlifetec.com — /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs, /graphql, /llms.txt and the full /.well-known/ path list — returned the site's SilverStripe 404 page in every case, and no api, docs, developer, portal or app subdomain resolves in DNS. The only software the company describes, 4D LifeAI, is embedded in the instrument rather than exposed as a service.

providers.name: 8fig
providers.description: 8fig is an eCommerce growth platform and direct lender that provides continuous, revenue-based funding and cash-flow planning technology to online sellers on Amazon, Shopify, and other marketplaces. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Miami, Florida (with R&D in Tel Aviv), 8fig offers funding of up to $10 million through its Growth Plan product, using proprietary AI-driven cash-flow modeling to align capital disbursements to a seller's supply-chain costs. 8fig also exposes an integration/partnership program that lets platforms embed its funding tools, though it does not publish a public developer portal or API reference.

providers.name: Accent Therapeutics
providers.description: Accent Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering a new class of small-molecule precision cancer therapies that target critical intracellular dependencies spanning multiple types of cancer. Its pipeline is led by ATX-295, a novel KIF18A inhibitor in clinical development, with data presented at AACR and ASCO. Backed by GV, Accent focuses on precision oncology drug discovery and development. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its corporate and web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Accord
providers.description: A UK-based financial services company operating within the Allianz group, providing insurance and financial products to retail and business customers across the United Kingdom.

providers.name: Achates Power
providers.description: Achates Power is a San Diego, California engine technology company founded in 2004 by Dr. James Lemke and John Walton that develops opposed-piston, two-stroke compression-ignition engine architecture and licenses the resulting engine designs, development tools, simulation software and patents to engine manufacturers and OEMs. Its engines target passenger vehicles, medium and heavy-duty commercial trucks, military vehicles, and off-road and power-generation applications, and the company has claimed fuel-efficiency improvements of as much as 30 percent over conventional engines at comparable or better emissions. Achates Power has received U.S. Army TARDEC, Department of Energy and ARPA-E funding and partners with engine manufacturers such as Fairbanks Morse. It is a privately held hardware and engineering licensing business and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Aerska
providers.description: Aerska is a biotechnology company developing RNA interference (RNAi) medicines to treat, delay, and prevent diseases of the brain and central nervous system. The company pairs next-generation RNAi therapeutics with receptor-mediated "brain shuttle" delivery technology engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier and silence disease-causing genes in the CNS. Founded in 2025 by Jack O'Meara, Stuart Milstein, and Dave Hardwicke, Aerska is headquartered in Dublin, Ireland with research operations in London. It emerged from stealth in 2026 having raised a Series A round led by the EQT Dementia Fund and age1, with additional backing from Speedinvest and Backed. Aerska is a pre-clinical drug-discovery company and does not currently publish a public developer API or platform.

providers.name: Aestheticpartners
providers.description: Aesthetic Partners is a clinical-aesthetics practice-management company that partners with physician-led medical aesthetics, cosmetic dermatology, and plastic surgery clinics to help them grow through expansion rather than consolidation. It provides partner practices with capital, marketing, HR, recruiting, IT, accounting, and legal support, plus professional development and new-clinic launch help. Incubated at Harvard and distinguished as female- and minority-owned, the company operates a network of practices across California, Florida, North Carolina, and Virginia, is headquartered in Miami, FL, and is backed by a strategic investment from Norwest Venture Partners. Aesthetic Partners is a non-technical healthcare-services business and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: AFi
providers.description: AFi provides a platform for sending and receiving commercial payments across Africa. Targeting unbanked and underbanked small businesses, AFi enables B2B transactions via mobile phones, supporting mobile money and bank accounts. Currently operating in Ghana and Togo, with plans to expand to WAEMU, Nigeria, and the US, the service offers secure, swift, and affordable cross‑border payments, along with tools for document submission and capital management.

providers.name: AgadoLive
providers.description: Agado Live is an AI-powered telerehabilitation platform built for physical therapy clinics, letting one therapist supervise many patients at once while capturing measurable outcomes. Its computer-vision engine extracts joint kinematics in real time from a single smartphone or webcam, with no wearables, markers, or proprietary hardware, then flags form issues live and directs the therapist's attention where it is needed most. The platform delivers Live Group Care, AI movement assessment, auto-generated SOAP notes, and specialized orthopedic, neurological, and geriatric protocols. Founded by Tzach Goren, Gili Yaron, Gil Shamai, and Vittaly Tavor, Agado Live operates from Tel Aviv and Boston and is backed by Techstars. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the company publishes a marketing and clinical site but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Age of Learning
providers.description: Age of Learning, Inc. is a Glendale, California educational technology company founded in 2007, best known for ABCmouse.com Early Learning Academy, a subscription digital curriculum for children ages 2-8, along with Adventure Academy (ages 8-13) and Mastery-branded school programs. It builds direct-to-consumer and school-facing learning products delivered through web and mobile apps (iOS and Android). Age of Learning does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a consumer edtech provider surfaced from the ICONIQ Capital portfolio, enriched with the public link surface (privacy, terms, support, press, careers) and a domain-security posture probed from public DNS/TLS records.

providers.name: Airis Labs
providers.description: Airis Labs (AI RIS Labs Ltd.) is a defense and public-safety AI company, founded in 2023 and based in Washington, D.C. and Tel Aviv, whose User-Generated Field Intelligence (UGFI) platform turns unstructured user-generated video and other visual sources - smartphones, social media, digital forensics, CCTV, body cams, drones and FMV - into structured, searchable intelligence for government, homeland security, law enforcement and military analysts, with agentic analyst workflows and self-hosted or sovereign-cloud deployment. The company markets a demo-led, customer-controlled product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: AIRNA
providers.description: AIRNA Corporation is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing precision RNA editing therapeutics based on ADAR (adenosine deaminase acting on RNA), a naturally occurring human protein the company redirects to convert adenosine to inosine at a targeted RNA site — changing protein function without permanently altering DNA. Its oligonucleotide medicines are designed for durable, reversible and repeatable dosing. The lead program, AIR-001, targets alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD), alongside cardiometabolic RNA editing programs spanning rare genetic disorders and common conditions. Founded by scientific pioneers of ADAR editing, AIRNA operates from Cambridge, Massachusetts and Tübingen, Germany (AIRNA Bio Germany GmbH). AIRNA publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; therapeutics, not software, are the product.

providers.name: Aizome
providers.description: Aizome is an enterprise AI agent security and governance platform that makes autonomous AI agents accountable through identity-led access control and intent validation. Its platform follows a three-step model: Discover (map every AI agent in the enterprise, including undocumented ones), Assess Risk (score agents by data access, functionality, and behavior), and Control and Govern (enforce policy through identity-led governance and intent interception before execution). Aizome inherits agent identity from users scoped to specific tasks and integrates with existing enterprise identity systems such as Okta, Microsoft Entra, and SailPoint rather than replacing them. It targets enterprise workflow automation use cases including billing, talent reviews, contract monitoring, and customer service. Aizome is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Alliance DAO
providers.description: Alliance (Alliance DAO) is a leading crypto, fintech, and AI startup accelerator. Its cohort-based program pairs two weeks of in-person onboarding in New York City with eight weeks of remote acceleration, offering mentorship, lectures, weekly check-ins, and a Demo Day pitch event. Alliance invests $500,000 per startup and runs three cohorts per year. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital, Alliance publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Altius Labs
providers.description: Altius Labs builds customized, high-performance blockchain infrastructure for high-frequency onchain markets and trading applications. Founded by former Hudson River Trading engineers, Altius offers a VM-agnostic modular execution stack that decouples execution from consensus and storage to deliver parallel transaction processing, targeting 10,000+ TPS and sub-millisecond latency while remaining EVM-compatible through a hybrid architecture (Altius L1 for settlement plus a high-performance execution coprocessor). Applications retain gas fees, sequencing revenue, and governance rather than ceding them to a base layer. The stack integrates with existing L1, L2, and app chains and supports multiple virtual machines (EVM, MoveVM, CosmWasm, SolanaVM). Altius Labs is backed by Founders Fund, Pantera Capital, Archetype, and others, and positions itself as institutional-grade dedicated chain infrastructure deployable in weeks rather than years.

providers.name: Ambyint
providers.description: Ambyint provides AI‑powered production optimization solutions for the oil and gas industry. Their platform uses machine learning to continuously improve well performance, offering tools such as rod‑lift, plunger‑lift, and gas‑lift optimization, as well as ESP management. The company aims to maximize output while reducing operational costs through autonomous set‑point management and predictive maintenance.

providers.name: Amicus Therapeutics
providers.description: Amicus Therapeutics is a global rare disease biotechnology company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing medicines for people living with genetically defined conditions. Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey, Amicus markets two approved therapies: Galafold (migalastat) — the first and only oral therapy for adults with Fabry disease who have an amenable GLA variant, approved by the European Commission in May 2016 — and the two-component Pombiliti (cipaglucosidase alfa-atga) + Opfolda (miglustat) enzyme replacement / stabilizer combination for adults with late-onset Pompe disease. Amicus operates wholly owned subsidiaries in Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc. agreed to acquire Amicus in December 2025 for $4.8 billion; the acquisition completed on April 27, 2026 and Amicus now operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of BioMarin, having previously traded on NASDAQ under the ticker FOLD. The company maintains no publicly documented commercial developer APIs, SDKs, or GitHub organization; its digital surface is composed of corporate, product, patient-support, and clinical-trial websites.

providers.name: AminoChain
providers.description: AminoChain operates a transparent, decentralized research ecosystem for patient-centric biomedical research. Its Specimen Center helps researchers discover and access legacy biospecimens through decentralized specimen discovery and collaboration, while its Donor Platform enables prospective participant registries and manages participant involvement in studies. The platform emphasizes privacy-preserving re-engagement, cryptographic tracking of biospecimens, auditable consent, and benefit-sharing models that return value to patients and donors. Backed by a16z. AminoChain currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Anaqua
providers.description: Anaqua provides intellectual property management (IPMS) software and services for corporations and law firms, unifying patent, trademark, and broader IP portfolio operations through process automation, business intelligence, and analytics. Its AQX platform (AQX Corporate, AQX Law Firm, AQX Pharma) is complemented by PATTSY WAVE portfolio analytics, AcclaimIP patent search, ideaPoint innovation management, and IP services such as annuity, renewal, foreign filing, and docketing. Clients include Adidas, ARM, TSMC, and GSK. Backed by Insight Partners and Bessemer Venture Partners, Anaqua does not currently publish a public developer API or portal; integration is handled via its SeeUnity application-integration technology.

providers.name: Anipen
providers.description: Anipen (애니펜) is a South Korean technology company focused on immersive XR, AR, and AI-driven content platforms. It develops metaverse infrastructure, AR kiosks, AI-powered avatar engines, and digital twin solutions for various industries. Since 2013, Anipen has delivered over 19 million global app downloads, 7.5 million AR video views, and operates services such as AR live streaming, XR commerce, and AI character platforms, positioning itself as a key player in the Korean and global metaverse ecosystem.

providers.name: Answers.com
providers.description: Answers.com is a consumer question-and-answer and reference website where visitors ask questions and get instant answers across trivia, science, history, and everyday topics, increasingly blended with AI-personality chat, flashcard makers, study guides, and a math solver. It operates as a content and reference destination rather than a developer platform, and the enrichment pipeline found no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile is retained as a company record in the API Evangelist network; the only machine-verifiable artifact is a live domain-security probe of the answers.com host.

providers.name: Antares
providers.description: Antares is a technology company that provides advanced data analytics and cloud-based solutions for financial services. The company focuses on delivering scalable platforms that enable real-time data processing, risk assessment, and market insights for institutional investors and traders. Antares aims to empower clients with customizable tools and APIs that integrate seamlessly into existing workflows, enhancing decision-making and operational efficiency.

providers.name: antengene
providers.description: Antengene Corporation is a commercial-stage, R&D-driven global biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing first-in-class and best-in-class therapies for the treatment of hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. Headquartered in Shanghai with a global footprint across the Asia Pacific region and beyond, Antengene's marketed product XPOVIO (selinexor) and a pipeline of oncology assets such as the Claudin 18.2 antibody-drug conjugate ATG-022 and the CD73 inhibitor ATG-037 target unmet needs in cancer care. Antengene operates in the life sciences sector and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and captured in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence and enrichment.

providers.name: Asher Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Asher Biotherapeutics (Asher Bio) is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2019 and headquartered at 650 Gateway Blvd. in South San Francisco, California. The company develops cis-targeted immunotherapies — engineered biologics that simultaneously engage an immunomodulatory receptor and a cell-type-specific target on the same immune cell, so a cytokine is only activated on the intended cell population rather than acting indiscriminately across immune subsets. Its lead candidate, etakafusp alfa (AB248), is a cis-targeted IL-2 directed at CD8+ effector T cells and is in Phase 1a/1b clinical development in cancer, alongside earlier-stage programs AB821 and AB359 and a cis-targeted cytokine augmentation program for cell therapies. Asher Bio is a therapeutics developer, not a software or platform company: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: ATI
providers.description: Allegheny Technologies Incorporated, which trades and brands itself as ATI Inc., is an American producer of specialty materials and components headquartered in Dallas, Texas and listed on the NYSE under the ticker ATI. ATI melts, forges, rolls, machines and additively manufactures titanium and titanium alloys, nickel-based alloys and superalloys, stainless and specialty steels, zirconium, hafnium, niobium and tungsten materials, plus forgings and castings. It serves aerospace and defense — over half of sales — along with oil and gas, chemical and hydrocarbon processing, power generation, medical and electronics markets, on roughly $4.6 billion in annual revenue. ATI is a materials manufacturer rather than a software company and publishes no public API: as of 2026-09-01 probing found no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or WSDL contract, no SDK on any public package registry and no GitHub organization. The only credentialed digital surfaces are My ATI, a customer and supplier extranet behind a logon form, and a third-party sourcing platform linked from the supplier self-service page; customer onboarding itself is documented as PDF forms emailed to a sales contact.

providers.name: Auron Therapeutics
providers.description: Auron Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts, developing therapies that target cell-state plasticity to address the underlying causes of disease across oncology and inflammatory disease indications. The company built the AURIGIN platform, which integrates multi-omic profiling and computational biology to map how cells change states and identify those states that can be therapeutically targeted. Auron was founded by Dr. Katharine Yen with co-founders Dr. Ross Levine, Dr. Eytan Stein, and Dr. Matthew Vander Heiden, a team drawing on experience from Agios Pharmaceuticals and its FDA-approved IDH inhibitor programs. It is backed by investors including Apollo, Arkin Bio, Casdin Capital, and DCVC Bio. As a therapeutics company Auron publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate and legal web presence only.

providers.name: AutoLotto
providers.description: AutoLotto, Inc. operates Lottery.com, a mobile platform that lets users in participating US states play official draw lottery games such as Powerball and Mega Millions from their phones, track tickets, view winning numbers, jackpot sizes and draw times, and collect winnings to a linked bank account. Beyond the consumer app, AutoLotto runs a business data-licensing offering that syndicates results and draw data for hundreds of lottery games worldwide to partner digital properties. AutoLotto is venture-backed (500 Global, Pantera Capital) and its parent trades publicly. As of this enrichment pass Lottery.com exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; data access is arranged through a manual "license our data" inquiry form rather than a programmatic surface.

providers.name: Barnana
providers.description: Barnana is a snack food company that creates plant‑based, organic banana, plantain, and cassava chips and bites. Founded with a mission to reduce food waste, the brand sources imperfect bananas and turns them into tasty, sustainably‑packaged snacks. Their product line includes organic plantain chips, cassava chips, banana bites, and seasonal flavors, sold online and in retail stores across the United States.

providers.name: Basking Biosciences
providers.description: Basking Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Research Triangle, North Carolina (with operations in Mitchelton, Queensland, Australia) developing novel therapies for life-threatening blood clots. Its lead program BB-031 is an investigational RNA aptamer that targets von Willebrand Factor (vWF) to deliver a rapid-onset, targeted, and reversible thrombolytic for acute ischemic stroke, paired with BB-025, a direct-acting reversal agent designed to rapidly neutralize BB-031. The company is running the RAISE Phase 2 clinical trial and is backed by Insight Partners. Surfaced as a VC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Beatdapp
providers.description: Beatdapp is a trust and safety operating system for digital platforms, providing AI-driven fraud detection and content integrity. Originally built to detect streaming fraud in the music industry, its platform now spans anomaly detection, customer due diligence, AI-generated music detection, account takeover detection, and recommendation systems across streaming, gaming, media, and marketplaces. The company reports analyzing 6T+ streams and 65T+ data points, with clients including Universal Music Group, iHeartRadio, Beatport, and SoundExchange. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published at this time.

providers.name: Beijingaccbbiotechltd
providers.description: ACC Biotech Limited (北京雅康博生物科技有限公司) is a Hong‑Kong based professional health‑supplement OEM/ODM manufacturer. It offers end‑to‑end services from formulation design, global ingredient sourcing, production, packaging and regulatory compliance, serving clients worldwide. The company also provides patented ingredient development and a range of supplement dosage forms.

providers.name: Bespo
providers.description: Bespo is an online retailer that offers bespoke, customizable products across fashion, home décor, and gifts. Customers can personalize items such as clothing, wall art, accessories, and homeware, creating unique, made‑to‑order pieces. The platform emphasizes design flexibility, high‑quality materials, a seamless shopping experience, and worldwide shipping, catering to both individual consumers and wholesale buyers seeking personalized merchandise.

providers.name: Better Origin
providers.description: Better Origin is a UK-based agritech company decarbonizing the food chain by converting food waste into sustainable, locally produced animal feed. Its core technology is a fully automated, AI-controlled containerized insect farm that breeds black soldier fly larvae to consume food waste and produce nutrient-rich insect-based ingredients for pet food, poultry feed, and aquaculture. The systems are remotely monitored and controlled by software and require no specialist knowledge from operators. Better Origin is a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Beyond Meat
providers.description: Beyond Meat, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based producer of plant-based meat substitutes founded in 2009 and publicly traded on Nasdaq (BYND). The company makes plant-protein versions of beef, pork, and poultry products, including the Beyond Burger, Beyond Sausage, Beyond Beef, and Beyond Chicken, distributed across grocery retail and foodservice channels worldwide. Beyond Meat operates as a consumer packaged-goods brand rather than a technology or developer-platform company; it publishes a marketing and e-commerce website, product and recipe catalogs, a newsroom, and an investor-relations presence, but does not offer a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: BiomEdit
providers.description: BiomEdit is an innovation company that discovers, designs, and develops novel microbiome‑derived products to address unmet needs in animal health. Leveraging the animal’s own microbial ecosystem, BiomEdit creates solutions where none exist, focusing on improving animal health through microbiome science and advanced product development pipelines.

providers.name: Bitterroot Bio
providers.description: Bitterroot Bio is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Palo Alto, California, pioneering the emerging field of cardio-immunology — the interplay between the immune system and cardiovascular disease. Its lead program, BRB-002, is a novel investigational immunomodulating protein therapy that targets CD47 to treat atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) by acting on atherosclerotic plaque through the immunomodulation of macrophages, an approach distinct from current standards of care. Founded in 2021, the company is advancing BRB-002 through its MATADOR Phase 2a proof-of-concept study. Bitterroot Bio is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer API or programmatic surface; this profile captures its public web identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Blink Charging
providers.description: Blink Charging Co. (Nasdaq BLNK) operates the Blink Network of Level 2 and DC Fast electric vehicle chargers across North America and Europe, alongside brands acquired via SemaConnect, Blue Corner, BlueLA, and Envoy. Blink's charger hardware (Series 7/8/9) is OCPP 2.0.1 certified for CSMS interoperability, and in 2025 Blink joined Hubject's Intercharge eRoaming platform as a charge point operator using the OCPI protocol so third-party e-mobility service providers can route drivers and billing to Blink stations. Blink also runs a gated BlinkMap API developer program (station locations, hours, and live network status) and a Blink Fleet platform that partners such as Presto and BetterFleet integrate with via API for fleet charging, sessions, and billing. None of these programs currently publish a full public self-serve API reference; access requires signing up directly with Blink.

providers.name: Blox
providers.description: BLOX is a Bessemer, Alabama design-manufacture-construct (DMC) company that describes itself as the largest manufacturer of healthcare buildings in the United States. Founded in 2010-2011 as a spinoff of Giattina Aycock Architecture Studio by Chris Giattina, BLOX designs, prefabricates and installs modular medical buildings and building components — freestanding emergency departments, acute-care patient-room modules, primary-care clinics and full hospitals — from a former Pullman Standard railcar plant in the Interstate Industrial Park. Customers include HCA Healthcare, Encompass Health, Universal Health Services and Walmart Health. The company is privately held and its shares appear on secondary-market venues such as Forge Global. BLOX publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable specification; its software work is internal tooling for the DMC delivery system rather than a product.

providers.name: blueflite
providers.description: blueflite is a Techstars-backed unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) company that designs and manufactures autonomous cargo and delivery drones built on its SLATE platform for all-weather, time-sensitive logistics. Its aircraft target last-mile shipping and medical or life-saving delivery (such as defibrillators and emergency supplies), and the company complements the hardware with blueDelivery (a consumer ordering app), blueDigital (a cloud productivity tool), and blueControl, alongside drone consulting, engineering, and project services. blueflite is on the FAA Section 44807 approved UAS list and holds FCC conditional approval, and was founded by Frank Noppel and James McClearen. No public developer or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Bongobd
providers.description: Bongobd, operating as Bongo, is Bangladesh’s leading OTT and VOD platform since 2013, offering a vast catalog of Bangla movies, natok, web series, live TV channels, and originals. It streams content in HD, provides subtitles and dubbing in multiple languages, and supports offline downloads via its app. With over 500 YouTube channels, 83+ million subscribers, and a reach of 210 million unique viewers monthly, Bongo serves a South Asian audience across multiple countries, delivering entertainment through state‑of‑the‑art video delivery technology.

providers.name: Brainscopecompany
providers.description: BrainScope is a leading neurotechnology company with over 15 years of experience advancing brain health by transforming EEG data into objective diagnostic insights. It offers FDA‑cleared AI‑driven platforms for rapid, radiation‑free assessment of head injuries, and is developing novel biomarkers for broader clinical use.

providers.name: Brunswick
providers.description: Brunswick Corporation is a global leader in marine recreation and technology, headquartered in Mettawa, Illinois (NYSE: BC). Brunswick owns over 60 brands across marine propulsion (Mercury Marine, Mercury Racing, MerCruiser, Fliteboard), boat manufacturing (Boston Whaler, Sea Ray, Bayliner, Lund, Crestliner, Harris, Lowe, heyday), and marine parts and accessories (Navico Group: B&G, C-Map, Lowrance, Simrad). The company's ACES innovation strategy centers on Autonomy/Assistance, Connectivity, Electrification, and Shared Access.

providers.name: Business Insider
providers.description: Business Insider is a global business and financial news media company founded in 2007 and headquartered in New York City, operating as part of Axel Springer. It publishes fast-paced coverage of markets, technology, finance, the economy, retail, media, and careers across its flagship Business Insider brand and verticals such as Markets Insider. The organization was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm IVP. It operates consumer news properties and content syndication feeds rather than a public developer API program, so this profile tracks its public web presence and domain security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Cabana
providers.description: Cabana Pools is a California pool-service company providing recurring maintenance, repair, and equipment installation for residential swimming pools across San Diego, Los Angeles, Orange County, and Sacramento. Services include weekly cleaning, filter maintenance, chemical balancing, algae removal, and repair of pumps, heaters, filters, and automation systems, delivered by CPO-certified technicians with photo documentation and chemical reports after each visit. The company offers an instant online pricing quote tool. No public API or developer surface is currently published; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead.

providers.name: Calystaenergy
providers.description: Calysta is a world‑leader in sustainable protein solutions, using patented cellular agriculture fermentation to produce FeedKind ingredients for feed and food without arable land or animal inputs. The company focuses on reducing environmental impact while meeting growing global demand for nutritious protein across livestock, pets, and human food markets.

providers.name: Careforce
providers.description: Careforce (Helpcare AI, Inc., d/b/a Careforce) provides an autonomous AI workforce platform for healthcare operations. Its AI agents — Angelica, a care coordinator handling preventive-care outreach, appointment scheduling, reminders, and referral management, and David, a data analyst that pulls and analyzes patient data across EHR and portal systems — integrate with 30+ healthcare platforms including Epic, Cerner, Athenahealth, and NextGen to close care gaps and reduce staff workload. Backed by CRV. Careforce consumes third-party healthcare APIs rather than publishing a public developer API; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: CarSwitch
providers.description: CarSwitch is a tech-enabled used-car marketplace founded in Dubai in 2016 that facilitates buying and selling of pre-owned vehicles across the United Arab Emirates (Dubai, Abu Dhabi and nationwide) and Saudi Arabia. Rather than a traditional classifieds site, CarSwitch operates as a fully managed service: every car undergoes a 200-point inspection before listing, sellers get an end-to-end managed selling service (professional photography, listing, negotiation and RTA transfer handling), and buyers get price transparency, a free online car-valuation tool and installment financing through banking partners such as Emirates NBD, FAB, ADCB, ADIB, DIB and Emirates Islamic. The company has inspected 130,000+ vehicles and facilitated over $500 million in sales. CarSwitch was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a consumer marketplace with no public developer API program.

providers.name: CarWale
providers.description: CarWale is an Indian automotive marketplace and part of CarTrade Tech Limited, connecting car buyers with new-car dealers and used-car sellers across 1,500+ cities in India. The consumer platform offers new and used vehicle listings, accurate on-road pricing sourced directly from dealers, car valuation and sell-car tools, side-by-side comparisons, expert reviews and first-drive reports, and automotive news and video content. CarWale reports over 34 million monthly unique visitors and operates alongside sister brands including BikeWale, CarTrade, CarWale abSure, Mobility Outlook, and Adroit Auto. CarWale does not currently publish a public developer portal or API; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Castelion
providers.description: Castelion is a vertically integrated defense technology company that designs, tests, and manufactures next-generation military systems, with a focus on affordable, mass-producible hypersonic strike weapons such as its Blackbeard system, built rapidly and at scale to deter future conflict. Founded by former SpaceX and defense-industry engineers, it operates manufacturing and test facilities in Torrance, CA; Rio Rancho, NM; Midland, TX; and Allen, TX. Castelion is privately held and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

providers.name: Cedar
providers.description: Cedar is a healthcare financial technology company whose patient financial experience platform unifies billing, payments, insurance coverage, and support for health systems, hospitals, and clinician-services groups. Its products include Cedar Pay (pre-visit, post-visit, and financing patient payments), Cedar Cover (benefits and financial assistance, including Medicaid enrollment), Cedar Support (AI-powered patient support and call-center automation via Kora AI), and Cedar Intelligence (a proprietary AI system for personalized patient engagement). Cedar reports having served over 50 million patients and processed billions of dollars in patient payments. The company is backed by a16z, Founders Fund, QED Investors, and SV Angel. Cedar publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or GitHub organization; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security-posture surface.

providers.name: Cellares
providers.description: Cellares is an Integrated Development and Manufacturing Organization (IDMO) for cell therapies, operating a global network of automated "Smart Factories." Its FDA-recognized Cell Shuttle platform delivers high-throughput, end-to-end, cGMP industrial-scale cell therapy manufacturing, and its Cell Q platform automates quality-control testing of cell therapy products. Smart Factories operate in South San Francisco (CA), Bridgewater (NJ), Leiden (Netherlands), and Kashiwa (Japan). Cellares was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as a cell therapy manufacturing organization it publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cheddar
providers.description: Cheddar is a business and technology news media company producing live and on-demand video, articles, and newsletters covering financial markets, technology, innovation, entrepreneurship, and culture for a modern digital audience. Founded as a millennial-focused financial news network and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Ribbit Capital, Comcast Ventures, and Altice USA, Cheddar streams programming such as Opening Bell, Big Business This Week, and NYSE TV Live across its website, connected-TV apps, and social platforms. It operates as a digital media and content publisher rather than an API or developer-platform company; this profile tracks Cheddar within the API Evangelist network and carries no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Circular Genomics
providers.description: Circular Genomics is a San Diego, California precision-neurology diagnostics company that uses brain-derived circular RNA (circRNA) as a class of stable, blood-based biomarkers for psychiatric and neurological disease. Spun out of the University of New Mexico in 2021 and now resident at Lilly Gateway Labs in San Diego, the company builds CircPath, a proprietary molecular-intelligence platform that discovers, validates and translates circRNA signals into biological insight, and productizes it as research and clinical assays: Discover 1600+ (whole-transcriptome circRNA sequencing across 1,600+ brain-derived circRNAs with pathway-level analysis), AD Predict and AD Detect for Alzheimer's disease, and MindLight, an SSRI antidepressant response test for major depressive disorder. Test ordering and results delivery for licensed healthcare providers run through a login-gated provider portal at mindlight.circulargenomics.com, which is a white-labeled CrelioHealth laboratory information system rather than a first-party developer surface. Circular Genomics publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer documentation of any kind.

providers.name: Clarium
providers.description: Clarium is a healthcare supply chain resiliency company founded in early 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic and headquartered in New York City. Its AI-powered platform, Astra OS, unifies real-time data from hospitals and their suppliers across systems of record, then layers data-enabled workflow apps on top: Disruption Monitoring to detect and resolve supply chain disruptions faster, Substitute Management to automate product approvals, and Procedure Card Optimization to standardize and cut cost. Clarium has raised $43M+ (including a $27M Series A led by General Catalyst, with Northzone among its backers) and works with leading health systems such as Mount Sinai, Ochsner Health, Allina Health, and Yale New Haven.

providers.name: Columbia Bank
providers.description: Columbia Bank is an Oregon state-chartered commercial bank and the principal banking subsidiary of Columbia Banking System, Inc. (NASDAQ: COLB), a West Coast regional bank holding company headquartered in Tacoma, Washington with more than $50 billion in assets. The bank took the legal name "Columbia Bank" effective July 1, 2025, having previously operated as Umpqua Bank following the 2023 merger of Columbia Banking System and Umpqua Holdings Corporation. On the open-finance front, Columbia is one of the relatively few US regional banks to run a first-party developer surface: Columbia API Banking, a commercial and treasury-management integration product exposing capabilities such as book transfers, ACH file imports, positive pay, stop-payment and NSF management, lockbox management, transaction and statement search, check images, and real-time account balances in JSON and XML, backed by a production-ready SDK and the gated Columbia API Portal. That surface is commercial/ERP-oriented rather than a self-serve public developer portal, and consumer-permissioned data access is instead delivered through the Plaid aggregator. No documented FDX participation or published CFPB Section 1033 posture was found.

providers.name: Comento
providers.description: Comento is a South Korean career development and mentoring platform based in Seoul that connects job seekers with working professionals. The service offers a Q&A community and timeline for career discussions, free unlimited mentoring questions answered by industry practitioners, resume and cover letter (자기소개서) review, an AI resume analyzer, interview preparation, and job-focused educational programs including bootcamps (직무부트캠프) and classes for the Korean job market. It also runs corporate training and university affiliation partnerships. Comento operates as a consumer-facing web platform and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched with the domain and identity signals that are publicly observable.

providers.name: Conbini
