It simplifies the development of web UIs through a component-driven approach with managed beans, an event-driven programming model, page navigation, state management, input validation, and built-in support for internationalization and accessibility. Jakarta Faces 4.1 is the current stable release with Jakarta EE 11, with 5.0 in development for Jakarta EE 12.

providers.name: JSON Binding
providers.description: Jakarta JSON Binding (JSON-B) defines a standard binding layer for converting Java objects to and from JSON documents. It specifies a default mapping algorithm for serializing and deserializing existing Java classes to and from JSON, while enabling developers to customize the mapping process through a Java API. JSON-B 3.0 is the stable release shipped with Jakarta EE 10, with version 3.1 under development for Jakarta EE 12.

providers.name: Jump
providers.description: Jump is a unified fan experience and ticketing platform built exclusively for professional sports teams. It combines primary and resale ticketing, team-branded mobile apps and websites, marketing and messaging, loyalty, fan identity and wallet, point-of-sale and scanning, dynamic pricing, and a unified fan-data foundation into a single system that teams own and control. Jump also embeds agentic AI agents to automate pricing, inventory, and revenue operations. It serves teams across the NBA, MLB, WNBA, NWSL, USL, and NCAA and is backed by Battery Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, Index Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. Jump connects to the tools teams already use through integration APIs, but publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or self-serve API documentation.

providers.name: Khatabook
providers.description: Khatabook is a Bengaluru, India-based fintech company building a mobile-first digital ledger ("bahi khata") and business management platform for India's 6.3 crore-strong MSME sector. Founded in 2018 by Ravish Naresh, Vaibhav Kalpe, Dhanesh Kumar, and Jaideep Poonia, its flagship Khatabook Android app lets shopkeepers and small merchants record credit transactions ("udhaar"), send free WhatsApp/SMS payment reminders, collect payments via UPI and QR codes, and generate ledger statements — replacing the paper notebook ("khata") historically used across Indian retail. The app has been downloaded over 50 million times and is offered in 13+ Indian languages. Khatabook's portfolio also includes Cashbook (cash-in/cash-out tracking), Pagarkhata/Pagarbook (staff attendance and salary management), Biz Analyst (Tally mobility for accountants, acquired in 2021 for ~$10M), and a suite of GST, EMI, income tax, payroll, and loan calculators. The company has raised roughly $190M across seed through Series C from Sequoia Capital, Tencent, DST Global, GGV Capital, Y Combinator, B Capital, Moore Strategic Ventures, and angels including MS Dhoni, valuing it around $600M. Khatabook monetizes via SMB lending tie-ups, premium business tools, and adjacent fintech distribution. The Khatabook GitHub organization (verified, owns khatabook.com) exists but has no public repositories, and the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or partner program — its surface is a consumer/SMB mobile app rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Kickpay
providers.description: Kickpay is an intelligent finance platform for e-commerce and hardware brands that unlocks capital tied up in inventory. It plugs into a company's data sources — fulfillment centers, e-commerce sales channels, and bank accounts — to see historic sales, then finances the manufacturing cost of each SKU it estimates will sell within a reasonable window (typically around 16 weeks). Kickpay can fund the brand directly or pay the manufacturer to purchase more inventory, and the brand only pays Kickpay back as units ship: when a unit ships from the fulfillment center, Kickpay activates an ACH payment for the manufacturing price plus a fixed fee. It provides smart daily servicing and reporting, distinguishes customer shipments from internal stock movements, and uses prediction tooling to forecast future sales and cash flow so it can underwrite startups with as little as three months of sales history. Kickpay was backed by Canaan Partners and DCVC. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Kickpay publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs, and the enrichment pipeline found no machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: LJ Hooker
providers.description: LJ Hooker is one of the largest residential and commercial real estate brokerage and property management networks in Australia and New Zealand. Founded in Maroubra, Sydney in 1928, the franchise network reports 390 businesses and around 4,000 sales professionals, property managers and support staff, facilitated more than AUD$20 billion in property transactions during 2024, and manages roughly 100,000 properties valued at about AUD$82 billion on behalf of investors. It operates across residential sales and rentals (ljhooker.com.au), commercial (ljhcommercial.com.au), rural (ljhrural.com.au), land and projects (ljhland.com.au) and New Zealand (ljhooker.co.nz). LJ Hooker sits at the agency layer of the Australian property value chain — below the REA Group / Domain portal duopoly that distributes its listings, and upstream of PEXA electronic conveyancing and the PropTrack / CoreLogic valuation data concentration. Its API posture is honestly stated as none-published: there is no developer portal, no published API documentation, no API terms of use and no partner or data-feed programme on any LJ Hooker domain. The only programmatic surface located is an undocumented, vendor-operated website backend at api01.ljx.com.au, generated by OpenAPI Generator and consumed by the Agentpoint-built property search front end; that OpenAPI definition is not published. RESO — the Real Estate Standards Organization Web API and Data Dictionary — is a North American, NAR-driven regime with no Australian footprint, and LJ Hooker appears nowhere in the RESO certificates directory.

providers.name: Made In Cookware
providers.description: Made In Cookware designs and sells professional-quality cookware, non-stick, carbon steel, and knives. The company offers a range of kitchen sets, individual pieces, and accessories, focusing on durability and performance. Their products are sold directly to consumers through their online store and are marketed as premium kitchen tools for home chefs.

providers.name: Magicpin
providers.description: Magicpin (operated by Samast Technologies Private Limited) is India's hyperlocal savings and discovery platform, connecting consumers with deals, cashback, and vouchers across restaurants, food delivery, fashion, grocery, beauty, fitness, and electronics merchants in cities throughout India. The company operates a consumer savings app alongside a merchant/brands portal and corporate voucher solutions. As of this enrichment pass Magicpin publishes a consumer web and mobile experience plus partner and brand onboarding portals, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer documentation.

providers.name: MathWallet
providers.description: MathWallet is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto-web3. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: MaxRewards
providers.description: MaxRewards is a consumer credit-card rewards app for iOS and Android that helps people manage their credit cards and maximize the rewards they earn on everyday spending. It links a user's cards, tracks spending, automatically activates card-linked offers, surfaces personalized card recommendations, compares credit cards by rewards rate and welcome offer, and monitors credit scores — all in one place — so cardholders earn more cash back and points with less manual effort. MaxRewards is an Atlanta-based fintech backed by Techstars. It is a consumer product company: it publishes a public marketing site and an internal app API, but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic
providers.description: Mayo Clinic provides a developer API portal with access to clinical and healthcare APIs hosted on an Apigee API catalog. Developers can review, test, and integrate with available APIs for healthcare data and services.

providers.name: MightyHive
providers.description: MightyHive was a data and digital media consultancy that helped brands take control of their programmatic advertising, media buying, data strategy, and marketing technology. Founded as an independent programmatic trading and media consultancy, it was acquired by S4 Capital and rebranded to Media.Monks in August 2021; the S4 Capital operating company has since consolidated under the single "Monks" brand (monks.com). Its offerings spanned digital media transformation, campaign launch and measurement, customer data platform (CDP) work, Amazon eCommerce solutions, and marketing/AI transformation services for enterprise brands. It is a professional-services / consulting business, not an API product company: it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, machine-readable specification, or client SDK on any package registry. It does keep a public GitHub organization (github.com/MightyHive, named "Media.Monks (formerly MightyHive)") of internal tooling, Looker blocks and ML notebooks, but nothing there is a released API or client library. The legacy mightyhive.com domain still resolves and serves a frozen archive of pre-2021 press and case studies. Added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z-portfolio lead; repeated enrichment confirms no API surface exists.

providers.name: mojiworks
providers.description: Mojiworks is a UK-based social games studio, backed by Balderton Capital, that is pioneering a game genre it calls MuGC (Multi-User Generative Creation) — living, collaborative worlds that communities and AI systems build together. Its released titles include Ready Chef Go, Trivia Party, Chef Showdown and Hatch Cats, and it is building its first MuGC world as a persistent, community-shaped city. The company publishes a public AI Ethics Policy committing to licensed training data, environmental accountability, human oversight and content-safety controls. Mojiworks does not currently expose a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Nagish
providers.description: Nagish (now operating as Rylo, following an $85M raise and rebrand) is a free phone-call captioning and live-transcription service for people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability. Originally launched as the Nagish app (talknagish.com), the FCC-certified service delivers real-time captions on incoming and outgoing calls, in-person Live Transcribe, voicemail captioning, 50+ language support, and AI-powered quick replies, with transcripts kept private on-device. It is a consumer mobile/telecom product and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by Canaan Partners and Techstars; profiled in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: National Endowment for the Humanities
providers.description: The National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) is the nation's largest public funder of the humanities, which include history, philosophy, literature, language, ethics, law, archaeology, political theory, comparative religion, anthropology, sociology, and media and cultural studies. NEH does not publish a fully documented public REST API, but it offers a Funded Project Query Form API and bulk XML datasets covering all grants awarded since 1965, plus evaluator and panelist information from 1988 onward.

providers.name: Netflix
providers.description: Netflix is a streaming entertainment service operating one of the world's largest content delivery networks. While Netflix does not publish a general public consumer API, it operates partner programs including Open Connect for ISP CDN integration and device certification programs for manufacturers embedding the Netflix application.

providers.name: Netreveal
providers.description: Netreveal is BAE Systems Applied Intelligence's financial crime detection and prevention platform, providing analytics for anti-money laundering, fraud detection, sanctions screening, and regulatory compliance for banks and financial institutions. Netreveal does not currently publish public developer-facing APIs; integrations are typically delivered through customer engagements.

providers.name: Norgate Data
providers.description: Norgate Data provides high-quality, survivorship-bias-free end-of-day (EOD) historical market data for US, Australian and Canadian stocks, around 100 worldwide futures markets, and foreign exchange. Data is not delivered as a hosted REST API. Instead, subscribers install the Norgate Data Updater (NDU), a Windows desktop application that downloads and maintains a complete local database and runs a local data service. Programmatic access is through the norgatedata Python package (on PyPI), which talks to that local NDU service and returns price/volume history, corporate actions, index constituent history, security metadata, fundamentals, and watchlists as Pandas DataFrames or NumPy arrays. Norgate also ships plugins for platforms such as Amibroker and is widely used with Python backtesting frameworks (Zipline, Backtrader). This entry honestly models the norgatedata library's logical operations as capability areas; it is a client library over a local service, not a public HTTP/REST API.

providers.name: OneConnect
providers.description: OneConnect Financial Technology (NYSE: OCFT; HKEX: 6638) is a technology-as-a-service platform for financial institutions, incorporated in 2015 as an associate of China's Ping An Group to externalize its banking and insurance technology. Its cloud-native, microservices platform spans digital banking, digital insurance, and the Gamma platform (AI voice, computer vision, blockchain and big-data analytics), serving hundreds of banks and insurers across China and Southeast Asia with ready-to-integrate financial technology components exposed through Open APIs. OneConnect raised a US$650M Series A in 2018 from investors including the SoftBank Vision Fund and SBI Group. Its APIs are delivered as enterprise B2B integrations rather than a public self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: OpenSpace
providers.description: OpenSpace is a visual intelligence platform for the construction industry, headquartered at 333 Kearny Street, San Francisco, California. The company pairs an off-the-shelf 360-degree camera worn on a hardhat with computer-vision software that automatically maps captured imagery to construction floor plans and BIM models, producing a navigable, time-indexed visual record of every jobsite walk. The platform is built around five products: Capture (complete visual record), Field (image-based task management with AI Autolocation), Track (AI-driven progress tracking against schedule), Air (drone imagery management), and BIM+ (3D field tools). OpenSpace reports more than 69 billion square feet captured across projects in 131 countries, with regional presence in Australia, Canada, EU, Japan, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, and the United Kingdom. The company is led by CEO and co-founder Jeevan Kalanithi. OpenSpace integrates with the major construction software stacks, including Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud / Autodesk Build, Revizto, PlanGrid, and Bluebeam. A REST API exists for partner and enterprise integration but is not publicly self-serve; integration access is obtained via OpenSpace's support and partner channels.

providers.name: Pano
providers.description: Pano AI provides enterprise-grade, AI-powered wildfire and bushfire detection. The platform combines ultra-high-definition 360-degree mountaintop cameras, satellite feeds, field sensor data, and machine learning to detect ignitions early, confirm and triangulate their location, and deliver real-time visual situational intelligence to utilities, fire agencies, first responders, and landowners. Operators access the Pano 360 platform at 360.pano.ai to monitor camera networks, review AI detections, and coordinate incident response. Backed by DCVC and Initialized Capital, Pano was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Pellego
providers.description: Pellego is a real estate technology and brokerage platform serving real estate professionals including agents, contractors, flippers, landlords, lenders, and wholesalers. It offers property analysis software (comparable sales analysis, rehab calculators, and investment filtering), a 100% commission brokerage for agents who hang their license, an agent marketplace connecting investors with experienced agents, and deal discovery for flips, rentals, and assumable loans. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Plumerai
providers.description: Plumerai builds AI software for intelligent cameras that pairs tiny on-device edge AI models with cloud Vision Language Models (VLMs). Its Video Intelligence products cover detection of people, vehicles, animals and packages, Familiar Face Identification, cross-camera Re-Identification, noise-robust motion detection, VLM-based video search, and custom AI notifications. The Plumerai Inference Engine is a deep-learning model compiler and runtime optimized for CPU inference on Arm Cortex-M / Cortex-A, RISC-V and x86_64. Plumerai integrates via SDKs (C++, C, Python, Rust, Java) rather than a hosted REST API, with the same unified API running from microcontrollers to servers. Plumerai also maintains the open-source Larq ecosystem for training and running Binarized Neural Networks.

providers.name: Postfix
providers.description: Postfix is a free, open source mail transfer agent (MTA) originally written by Wietse Venema at IBM Research as a fast, secure, and easy-to-administer alternative to Sendmail. It runs on UNIX-like systems including Linux, BSD, and macOS, routing and delivering email over SMTP with extensive support for TLS, SASL, DKIM/SPF/DMARC integration, content filtering, and policy delegation. Postfix is administered via configuration files (main.cf, master.cf) and command-line tools rather than a public HTTP API, and is one of the most widely deployed mail servers on the internet.

providers.name: Profitero
providers.description: Profitero+ is an eCommerce data, technology and services platform that helps consumer brands measure and grow their digital shelf presence across major retailers including Amazon, Walmart, Tesco and Target. It combines digital shelf analytics, Amazon sales and share measurement, content optimisation, retail media activation (Shelf Intelligent Media) and managed services, monitoring more than 1,400 retailer sites in 70+ countries for over 9,000 global brands. Founded in Dublin in 2010 and acquired by Publicis Groupe in March 2022, it now operates inside Publicis Commerce. Profitero was surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network. A partner API does exist — Profitero's own CEO wrote in 2020 that technology partners such as Kenshoo and Pacvue "integrate directly with Profitero via API" — but the company publishes no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or AsyncAPI definition, GraphQL endpoint, Postman collection, MCP server, agent card or SDK on any public host, and no pricing. Access runs through the Open Commerce Ecosystem partner programme and a sales demo request.

providers.name: RACE Protocol
providers.description: RACE Protocol is a multi-chain, on-chain infrastructure for developing and deploying secure and fair web3 games. It is delivered primarily through a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK (sdk-core, sdk-solana, sdk-sui, sdk-facade) and a command-line tool (race-cli) for game bundle publishing, account management, and payment claims, rather than as a traditional REST API. Smart contracts run on Solana and Sui.

providers.name: SATIM
providers.description: SATIM provides AI-powered analysis of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) operations. Its OREC analytics engine performs automated object detection and classification on satellite and airborne SAR data (accuracy up to 95%), deployable in cloud, edge, or air-gapped environments and integrable into C2 and C4ISR workflows. OREC-Intelligence adds persistent monitoring with real-time area-of-interest change alerts and activity pattern analysis. Headquartered in Krakow, Poland, with offices in Dover, Delaware and London. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API surface, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation are published at this time.

providers.name: Savills
providers.description: Savills plc is a London-headquartered global real estate advisor, established in 1855, listed on the London Stock Exchange, with more than 42,000 people in over 70 countries. It sits on the advisory side of the property value chain rather than the data-platform side: commercial and prime residential agency, transaction advisory and capital markets, valuation and professional services, building and project consultancy, property and facilities management, rural and agricultural advisory, occupier services, the Savills Research publication programme, and a separate fund manager in Savills Investment Management. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where there is no MLS and no cooperative listing standard — residential stock reaches consumers through the Rightmove and Zoopla duopoly by way of agency CRM software (Reapit, Alto, Street, Apex27) rather than a shared cooperative pool. Savills is a supplier into that pipe, not an operator of it. Its API posture is the honest null case for this sector. Savills publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK, no Postman collection and no machine-readable contract of any kind: developer., developers., docs. and apis.savills.com do not resolve, /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs on savills.com, savills.co.uk and savills.us all return 404, and no OpenID Connect discovery document is served. Undocumented internal service hosts do exist behind the consumer property search — livev6-searchapi, livev6-authentication and livev6-profile.savills.com, named in the search application's own endpoints.js — but every one of them returns 404 to an anonymous client and none is described anywhere public. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the Savills estate; RESO is a North American NAR/MLS construct and the UK has nothing to certify against. Savills publishes no open data either — its research output is PDF and web narrative, and the genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector (HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey), not to the brokerage. For a developer there is no gate to pass, because there is no door: the only published route is the corporate contact form.

providers.name: SchoolCare
providers.description: SchoolCare provides a unified Student Health Record Platform for K‑12 schools, parents, and healthcare providers. It enables secure digital charting of student health information, immunizations, medications, and care coordination, complying with HIPAA and FERPA. The solution connects families and school staff to streamline health data management and improve student wellbeing across districts.

providers.name: Sensefinity
providers.description: Sensefinity is a supply-chain IoT company ("The IoT Transformation Company") delivering real-time tracking, monitoring, and analytics for global cargo and logistics operations. Its platform combines GPS/NB-IoT tracking devices for maritime containers, pallets, and vehicles with temperature and condition (cold-chain) sensors, indoor location tracking, a cloud analytics and machine learning layer, and digital product passport / blockchain integrations. The operational platform is delivered as a hosted web application (uiadmin.sensefinity.com) and mobile asset-management apps, serving enterprise customers across food, pharma, automotive, and manufacturing supply chains. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published as of this profile; a private API host (api.sensefinity.com) backs the platform.

providers.name: Sequen AI
providers.description: Sequen AI operates a Behavior Design Engine — an AI-powered ranking and real-time, in-session personalization platform for consumer applications. Its proprietary Large Event Models (LEMs) generalize user behavior from sparse event data (clicks, scrolls, hovers, purchases) to dynamically rank and re-rank product discovery, search, recommendations, and advertising with sub-20ms latency. Products include Sequen IQ (LEM-based ranking on purpose-built Sequen Ranking Clusters), Sequen Ranktune (model building and experimentation), and Sequen Rumi (analytics and behavioral-insight dashboard). The platform integrates via API with existing stacks. Sequen AI is backed by Threshold Ventures. No public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition are published at this time.

providers.name: Simplywise
providers.description: SimplyWise is an AI-powered admin-automation platform for contractors, tradespeople, and small business owners. Its consumer mobile and web apps bundle a receipt scanner and expense organizer, an automatic mileage tracker for tax deductions, an AI-powered job/cost estimator, and an AI receptionist that answers inbound calls and messages. The company reports serving more than 1.2 million business owners. SimplyWise is a fintech-adjacent SMB productivity product backed by QED Investors; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, webhooks, or developer portal — the apps are consumer-facing only.

providers.name: SlashNext
providers.description: SlashNext is an AI-native phishing and social-engineering threat detection company founded by Atif Mushtaq (an architect of FireEye's core malware sandbox). Its Real-Time Phishing Threat Intelligence is delivered through the SlashNext On-demand Threat Intelligence (OTI) REST API at oti.slashnext.cloud, which offers URL and host reputation lookups, real-time cloud SEER-engine URL scanning in both asynchronous and blocking modes, and forensic downloads (screenshot, HTML, and rendered text) keyed by scan id, plus per-tenant API quota status. Responses are available as JSON, CSV, or plaintext and every request authenticates with a per-tenant API key passed as the authkey parameter. SlashNext was acquired by Varonis Systems in August 2025 and its detection capabilities are being integrated into the Varonis Email Security and MDDR platform.

providers.name: Slingshot AI
providers.description: Slingshot AI is a mental-health AI research lab building a foundation model for psychology. Its consumer product, Ash, is a voice- and text-based AI companion for mental health support, trained on behavioral-health approaches including CBT, DBT, ACT, psychodynamic therapy, and motivational interviewing, and shipped as a free iOS and Android app. Founded by Neil Parikh (co-founder of Casper) and Daniel Reid Cahn, the company has raised roughly $93M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Forerunner Ventures, Menlo Ventures, and Radical Ventures. As of this pass Slingshot AI publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; Ash is a consumer-facing application at talktoash.com.

providers.name: Solomon
providers.description: Solomon (Solomon AI, solomontax.ai) is an agentic AI platform for tax preparation aimed at accounting firms, automating the preparation of review-ready individual 1040 returns for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients. The system interprets K-1/K-3 footnotes, applies multi-state SALT rules to K-1s, reconciles rental and real estate investments, analyzes brokerage statements for foreign income, and produces workpapers and audit trails, positioning itself to replace legacy tools such as SurePrep and K1x. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: Springcoin
providers.description: Springcoin (operating as Spring Labs) is an AI-native compliance and customer-experience platform for financial services. It builds autonomous AI agents for contact centers, quality assurance, complaint handling, and dispute resolution, alongside SummerGRC, a governance, risk, and compliance product with entity intelligence and an agent builder. The platform integrates with 50+ contact-center and CRM systems and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or open documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SUSE
providers.description: SUSE is a global provider of open source enterprise solutions including SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES), SUSE Rancher Prime for Kubernetes management, SUSE Manager (SUMA) for Linux systems management, and SUSE Edge and Security solutions. SUSE products expose REST and "A-REST" APIs for automation, configuration, and integration. The SUSE Manager API and Rancher API provide programmatic control over systems, clusters, and policies.

providers.name: Sweater
providers.description: Sweater (سويتر) is a Saudi Arabian on-demand mobile car-care company that brings waterless vehicle washing, interior cleaning, detailing, and fragrance services to customers wherever their car is parked. Its app-based platform uses smart scheduling to dispatch field teams by location and uses roughly 7 liters of water per wash versus about 120 liters for traditional methods. The company reports 2M+ washes, 750K+ users, 500+ corporate partnerships, and operations across 8 Saudi cities (Riyadh, Dammam, Khobar, Jeddah, Jubail, Medina, Al-Hassa, and Mecca). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer/B2B services business with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Telewerken
providers.description: Telewerken.be is a Belgian information platform dedicated to remote work (telewerken), operated jointly by Vias Institute and the FOD Mobiliteit en Vervoer (Federal Public Service for Mobility and Transport). The platform provides comprehensive resources on Belgian telework legislation, regulations, employer obligations, employee rights, and telework statistics. Belgium's remote work framework is governed by Collective Bargaining Agreement No. 85 (CBA 85) and the Law of 5 March 2017 on feasible and workable work. The platform serves both employers and employees navigating Belgium's structured telework policy landscape.

providers.name: Turo
providers.description: Turo is a San Francisco-headquartered peer-to-peer car sharing marketplace operating in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, and Australia. The platform lets vehicle owners (hosts) list their cars for rent and lets travelers (guests) book those vehicles directly through the Turo app or website, with Turo handling identity verification, insurance, protection plans, payments, and trust and safety on top of the host's inventory. The marketplace covers economy cars, SUVs, trucks, vans, exotic and classic vehicles, and EVs across more than 14,000 cities, and offers contactless Turo Go vehicles where supported. Turo's revenue model is a marketplace take-rate against each trip plus protection plan and ancillary fees, supported by an integrated host operations stack (calendar, pricing, messaging, and earnings) and a guest mobile and web booking experience. Turo does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or partner developer portal. The only third-party-facing surface was a now-deprecated ChatGPT plugin (chatgpt.turo.com) launched in 2023 and sunset alongside OpenAI's plugins program in 2024. Integrations with connected-car platforms such as Smartcar are negotiated directly rather than through self-serve developer onboarding, and Turo's public GitHub presence (github.com/turo, github.com/open-turo) is limited to internal engineering tooling, GitHub Actions, ESLint configs, and language-specific libraries rather than a public marketplace API.

providers.name: Vanu
providers.description: Vanu, Inc. builds wireless network solutions that extend cellular coverage to areas that cannot be profitably served with conventional technology - rural regions, buildings, tunnels, and maritime environments. Founded in 1998 out of MIT software-radio research and headquartered in Lexington, MA (with offices in Gurgaon, Bangalore, and Kigali), Vanu ships the Anywave dual-mode GSM/LTE base station (the first FCC-certified software-defined radio), Community Connect village systems, portable LTE networks, VanuMaps coverage mapping, and coverage-as-a-service for mobile carriers, with deployments across rural India, Rwanda, and post-hurricane Puerto Rico and partnerships with Amazon Leo / Project Kuiper. Vanu publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: VaultDragon
providers.description: VaultDragon (Vault Dragon Pte Ltd) is a Singapore-based digital healthcare company building end-to-end practice-management software for clinics and medical providers across Southeast Asia and China. Its product suite includes DragonHub, an end-to-end clinic-management platform covering appointment scheduling, patient tracking, electronic health records, inventory and invoicing; DragonCare, a patient-facing web app for self-booking, reminders and access to medical history; DragonInsights, an on-demand business- intelligence and analytics layer; and DragonLab, a laboratory information system automating the workflow from sample receipt to report delivery. VaultDragon serves 650+ healthcare providers across Singapore, China, Indonesia, Thailand and Cambodia. The platform is delivered as a hosted SaaS (hub.vaultdragon.com) backed by a private, authenticated internal API; the company currently publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or client SDKs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: vAuto
providers.description: vAuto is a Cox Automotive brand providing new and used vehicle inventory management, appraisal, pricing, and merchandising software for automotive dealers (ProfitTime GPS, Provision, Conquest, Stockwave). vAuto exposes partner-gated APIs through the Cox Automotive Integration Platform (developer.coxautoinc.com) - notably the vAuto Inventory API and the vAuto Appraisal API - that let authorized integrators programmatically read vehicle inventory, update list price, and create and access appraisals in the vAuto ecosystem. Access is not open self-service; integrators must be approved partners, authenticate via Cox Automotive Bridge ID / OAuth with an issued API key, and endpoint-level reference documentation is behind the partner developer portal login. Per-path endpoints below are modeled from the published product summaries, not copied from public reference docs.

providers.name: Viva Translate
providers.description: Viva Translate is an AI-powered real-time translation platform that acts as a personal meeting analyst, delivering live translation, transcription, automatic summaries, and action items across Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom. Reported usage spans 1M+ minutes translated, 20+ countries, and 1.8k+ companies. The company ships a consumer/B2B product (no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time) and has open-sourced its browser-based translation tooling as a Chrome extension that consumes third-party DeepL, Gladia, and OpenAI APIs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of general-catalyst and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Volter
providers.description: Volter (Get Volter Ltd) is a London-based energy platform that connects UK businesses with renewable generators to procure cheaper, greener electricity, and helps commercial real estate owners and generators deploy, optimize, and monetize rooftop solar and other onsite renewable assets. The platform spans renewable energy matching, solar optimization, and a forthcoming energy management suite with analytics, anomaly detection, flexible asset control, and battery storage. Backed by Transition and Seedcamp with a $3.2M pre-seed round in 2024. Volter does not currently publish a public API or developer documentation.

providers.name: WithAI
providers.description: WithAI is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company building Multiplier, a secure AI platform for institutional investors and independent equity hedge funds. Multiplier unifies structured data, unstructured data, AI agents, human work, and firm knowledge so investment teams can research stocks and manage portfolios more efficiently, with an integration ecosystem spanning Bloomberg, FactSet, Enfusion, Snowflake, and other market data and infrastructure platforms. WithAI does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Xfactor.io
providers.description: Xfactor.io is an AI-powered revenue operations platform founded by Mike Carpenter and backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its Growth AI engine, together with the Xfactor Central, OpenInsights, and Simulation products, builds a live digital twin of a company's go-to-market operations — connecting CRM, pipeline, usage, and financial data so revenue teams can test decisions through simulation before rolling them out. The platform is delivered as a closed B2B SaaS application (app.xfactor.io) and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or client SDKs; security posture is documented on a Secureframe trust center with a SOC 2 Type II attestation.

providers.name: XTIUM
providers.description: XTIUM provides managed IT solutions, AI services, and cloud infrastructure for enterprises. Their offerings include AI readiness assessments, managed detection and response, desktop-as-a-service, and secure networking. The company emphasizes secure, scalable solutions across healthcare, finance, retail, and education sectors, positioning itself as a trusted partner for digital transformation.

providers.name: Agility Robotics
providers.description: Agility Robotics is a Salem, Oregon humanoid robotics company building industrial bipedal robots for warehouse and factory automation. Founded in 2015 as a spin-out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Laboratory, its flagship product is Digit — described as the first humanoid robot in commercial production deployment — and Arc, the cloud-based automation platform that operates Digit fleets, provides real-time visibility, manages task assignments, and connects Digit to existing warehouse automation including AMRs, WMS, and WES systems. Digit has commercial deployments and pilots with Amazon, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre, with an expanded NVIDIA partnership for foundation-model and simulation tooling. Agility operates RoboFab, a humanoid robot factory in Salem, OR with capacity to produce 10,000 robots annually. Digit has surpassed 100,000 totes moved in commercial deployment at a single Georgia facility. Agility Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Digit or Arc; integration is performed by Agility's solutions team and partners through a gated low-level JSON-over-WebSocket API and pysdk delivered with the robot. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (JFrog, Bazel, Fluent Bit, Kubernetes Cluster API) plus an archived documentation repo for the earlier Cassie research platform.

providers.name: Airvet
providers.description: Airvet is a Los Angeles-based pet telehealth company, founded in 2018, that connects pet parents with licensed veterinarians 24/7 by video and chat through its Airvet for Pet Parents app (iOS/Android) and a companion Airvet Doctor app for its nationwide network of vets. It sells the service two ways - as "Vetcare as a Benefit", an employer-sponsored benefit adopted by companies such as Adobe, Activision, Synchrony and PepsiCo that covers every pet in an employee's household, and as a direct annual consumer membership - and layers on partner offers such as Pumpkin wellness plans and Healthy Paws insurance. Airvet is a consumer/B2B2C telehealth product, not an API platform - as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, webhooks or machine-readable API contract, and its GitHub organization has no public repositories.

providers.name: AIS Group
providers.description: AIS Group — trading as AIS Capital Management, L.P., where AIS stands for "Applied Intelligence Strategies" — is an investment management firm running absolute-return, global macro programs for financial advisors and individual investors. It combines discretionary macroeconomic and intermarket research (the Multi-Asset Allocation Portfolio family) with systematic, shorter-horizon models (the Frontera programs), trading only liquid instruments listed on major exchanges and describing its methodology as transparent rather than black-box. The firm is an investment manager rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public API, no developer program and no machine-readable contract, and its client portal is a licensed third-party workspace rather than software it operates.

providers.name: AIxMed
providers.description: AIxMed, Inc. provides AI-driven digital cytology solutions that enhance pathology workflows and improve patient care outcomes. Their platform offers quantitative and qualitative data insights, supporting cancer detection and diagnosis through advanced computational tools. The company focuses on delivering efficient, data‑driven pathology solutions across various medical settings, aiming to streamline processes and elevate diagnostic accuracy.

providers.name: Alberta
providers.description: Alberta is a open data portal open-data portal for Canada running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 33,436 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Alogent
providers.description: Alogent is a banking and financial technology provider that delivers cloud-native software to banks and credit unions across three product families: payments and deposit automation (Unify omni-channel check capture across branch, mobile, and ATM/ITM), intelligent check fraud detection and mitigation (Alogent Shield and Shield+), and enterprise content and loan document management (FASTdocs, AccuAccount, and the Alogent Document Portal). The platform emphasizes workflow automation, compliance controls, real-time transaction processing, and AI-assisted fraud prevention for financial institutions of all sizes. Alogent is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. No public developer portal or API documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Alto Neuroscience
providers.description: Alto Neuroscience develops precision psychiatry solutions, leveraging neurotechnology and data-driven approaches to improve diagnosis and treatment of mental health disorders. The company offers a platform integrating brain imaging, biomarkers, and AI analytics to support clinicians and researchers in delivering personalized care.

providers.name: AmeriGEOSS Community Platform
providers.description: AmeriGEOSS Community Platform is a organization open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 645,296 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Amex Bank of Canada
providers.description: Amex Bank of Canada is the Canadian banking subsidiary of the American Express Company (United States), incorporated in 1990 and headquartered in the Toronto area (Markham, Ontario). It is a Schedule II bank under Canada's Bank Act — a foreign-bank subsidiary regulated by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and treated as a Category II small-and-medium-sized deposit-taking institution — and it issues American Express charge and credit cards to Canadian consumers and businesses. As a card-centric Schedule II bank, Amex Bank of Canada runs no first-party developer portal of its own; the global American Express developer platform at developer.americanexpress.com is operated by the U.S. parent (a separate profile), not by this Canadian entity. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer, is not yet operational, so consumer data access to Amex-Canada accounts today is voluntary and largely aggregator-based rather than served by a public first-party API. This is an identity/provider record; no public Canadian API surface is documented.

providers.name: Anto Biosciences
providers.description: Anto Biosciences is a frontier biology AI lab making the gut microbiome computable for the first time. It builds foundation models for microbial communities and quality-aware, goal-directed sparsification algorithms that filter noise from microbiome data to predict how the gut microbiome affects drug efficacy, toxicity, and safety across diverse populations (by geography, age, and diet). Applications include population-specific drug response prediction, identifying failure mechanisms at the microbial metabolic-pathway level, and molecule optimization for broader effectiveness. Backed by Y Combinator, the company is early stage and research-focused; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or a GitHub organization. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and enriched with verified identity links only (no API artifacts, none published).

providers.name: Aragón Open Data
providers.description: Aragón Open Data is a open data portal open-data portal for Spain running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 2,429 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Astranis
providers.description: Astranis designs, manufactures, and operates small, dedicated geostationary communications satellites known as MicroGEO. Each spacecraft uses radiation-hardened digital payload technology to deliver dedicated broadband capacity to specific countries, telecom operators, enterprise users, and the U.S. government. Astranis is a satellite operator and manufacturer rather than an API provider; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Atlasmagnetics
providers.description: Atlas Magnetics is a Southern California based manufacturer of custom solenoids, magnetic components, μASICs, DC/DC converters and load switches. It serves aerospace, defense and industrial customers, offering standard components with full datasheets and evaluation boards available in‑stock through distribution partners. The company provides engineering resources, design services and rapid prototyping to accelerate product development.

providers.name: Atmo AI
providers.description: Atmo AI provides ultra‑precise AI‑driven weather forecasting for micro‑climates, leveraging real‑time satellite, radar, buoy and ground‑station data. Its deep‑learning models deliver forecasts up to 40,000× faster than traditional methods, achieving up to 50% higher accuracy across nowcasting to 14‑day horizons. Trusted by governments, militaries and industries worldwide, Atmo AI serves sectors such as aerospace, defense, agriculture and disaster response.

providers.name: Autoflight
providers.description: Autoflight builds the future of mass individual aerial transport, offering high‑reliability, all‑weather capable drone solutions for personal and commercial flight. The company focuses on innovative aviation technology, safety, and sustainability, aiming to democratize air mobility for everyday users and businesses alike.

providers.name: Avationmedical
providers.description: Avation Medical manufactures the Vivally System, the only FDA‑cleared wearable closed‑loop neuromodulation device for overactive bladder. The company provides at‑home treatment using transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, offering patients a non‑invasive solution for urge urinary incontinence. Avation focuses on digital health and neuromodulation, delivering clinical evidence, patient resources, and a leadership team dedicated to advancing medical technology.

providers.name: Avoindata.fi
providers.description: Avoindata.fi is a national government open-data portal for Finland running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 2,521 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. providers.name: Axend

providers.name: First Nations Bank of Canada
providers.description: First Nations Bank of Canada (FNBC) is a Schedule I federally regulated chartered bank under the Bank Act, chartered on 19 November 1996 and headquartered in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan. It is the first Canadian chartered bank to be independently controlled by Indigenous shareholders — roughly 88% Indigenous owned and controlled by 78 Indigenous shareholder groups from Nunavut, Northwest Territories, Yukon, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Alberta and Quebec — and focuses on serving the Indigenous marketplace, with over 90% of its loans going directly to Indigenous communities, many of its branches on reserve, and CDIC-insured deposits. On the open-finance and API front, FNBC runs no first-party developer portal and publishes no public API: probes of developer.fnbc.ca, api.fnbc.ca and developers.fnbc.ca all fail to resolve, and the fnbc.ca site exposes only retail online-banking and a mobile app, not a documented API surface. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated via Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, with FCAC as overseer) is not yet operational, so third-party access to FNBC account data today is voluntary and effectively aggregator-mediated (Flinks, Plaid and similar), not a first-party open-banking API.

providers.name: FloatMe
providers.description: FloatMe is a US fintech app offering interest-free cash advances ("Floats") to help members bridge income gaps between paychecks — new eligible members can request up to $50 and existing members up to $100, with no credit check and no reporting to credit bureaus. Beyond advances, FloatMe provides spending tracking and insights, low-balance alerts to help avoid overdraft fees, income and cash-flow forecasting, and an exclusive marketplace of deals on everyday essentials. The service runs on a $4.99/month membership, with optional instant-transfer fees. FloatMe operates a consumer mobile app and website; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Generally Intelligent
providers.description: Generally Intelligent is the former name of Imbue, the San Francisco AI research lab founded in 2021 by Kanjun Qiu and Josh Albrecht to build agentic reasoning models and the tooling around them. The company rebranded to Imbue in 2023; its original domain generallyintelligent.com now redirects permanently to imbue.com, and every product, research release and open-source repository that began under the Generally Intelligent name (the Avalon RL benchmark, CARBS hyperparameter tuning, jupyter_ascending) is published today under the Imbue brand and the github.com/imbue-ai organization. Neither name has ever shipped a public, credentialed developer API: there is no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, A2A agent card or llms.txt on any host the company controls, and integration happens through open-source repositories, model artifacts on Hugging Face and research releases. The living profile for this company is all/imbue.

providers.name: Honorlock
providers.description: Honorlock is an online exam proctoring and academic integrity platform for higher education and professional certification. Its primary integration path is LTI 1.3, installed natively into LMS platforms - Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, D2L Brightspace, Open LMS, Docebo, and Intellum - plus publisher platforms such as Pearson, McGraw Hill, and ALEKS via LMS workflows. providers.name: HotSpot Therapeutics
providers.description: HotSpot Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, pioneering allosteric drug discovery by targeting "natural hotspots" — the regulatory on/off switches on proteins. Its Smart Allostery platform combines AI-driven mining of large, diverse structural and biological data sets with a tailored pharmacology toolkit and bespoke medicinal chemistry to design first-in-class oral small molecules, and has been applied across E3 ligases, kinases and transcription factors. The company has raised roughly $190M across Series A, B and C financings and advanced its lead candidate HST-1011, an oral allosteric CBL-B inhibitor, into first-in-human dosing for cancer, alongside programs in autoimmune disease. HotSpot sells medicines and research collaborations, not software: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

Intella raised a $12.5M Series A led by Prosus and is backed by 500 Global, Hala Ventures, and Hearst, with partnerships including Visa and Jumia Egypt. providers.name: Klaim

Products span Klaim Health (insurance claim advances plus AI denial prediction), Klaim Flow (SME receivables purchasing with an escrow model), Klaim Estate (real estate commission advances) and Klaim Eligible (insurance eligibility verification). Founded in December 2019 by Karim Dakki and Ahmad Ghafour, backed by Techstars, and operating across the GCC, North Africa and Turkey. providers.name: RethinkDB

ITC exposes a web service-based rating API (a service-oriented version of TurboRater it first offered to third parties in 2010, extended with a homeowner rating API in 2016) that returns real-time rates from hundreds of carriers and can pull quote data as XML or ITC's proprietary Turbo Tags (TT2) format, plus a real-time bridge that hands a completed quote into an agency point-of-sale or management system. The company advances the equity trapped in a client's existing home so the client can make a non-contingent — effectively all-cash — offer on a new home, move once, and sell the old home afterward, with UpEquity making a backup offer on the departing residence. It also runs UpEquity Title and originates mortgages directly under NMLS #2101265, licensed across roughly twenty US states. The company converts that discovery platform into physical products rather than software: the RapidPrint series of reinforced nylon 3D printing filaments and the Ultra series of carbon fiber-loaded filaments for aerospace and defense additive manufacturing, with aluminum-replacing super materials and AI-designed proteins for selective extraction of lithium, nickel and rare earth elements from low-concentration brines in development. providers.name: Amentum
providers.description: Amentum Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: AMTM) is a global advanced engineering and technology solutions company serving U.S. federal customers across defense, intelligence, energy, space, and civilian missions, with allied work in the United Kingdom and Australia. The company was created from the spin-off of AECOM's Management Services business in 2020, and on September 27, 2024 completed a Reverse Morris Trust transaction with Jacobs Solutions to merge Jacobs' Critical Mission Solutions (CMS) and Cyber & Intelligence (C&I) businesses into Amentum. Post-merger Amentum reports approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal year 2025 revenue, a $47.1 billion backlog, ~53,000 employees in 80 countries, and is headquartered in Chantilly, Virginia. It provides tools for framing, matting, and shipping worldwide, and includes features such as AI‑powered search, curated collections, and a marketplace for artists. providers.name: ARTBIO
providers.description: ARTBIO is a clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company developing a new class of targeted Alpha Radioligand Therapies (ARTs) built on the lead-212 (212Pb) isotope. Founded in 2021 out of research at the University of Oslo and Norway's Radium Hospital by Roy Larsen and Oyvind Bruland - the scientific co-founders behind Xofigo - the company pairs a differentiated oncology pipeline with its proprietary AlphaDirect isotope-production technology, a first-of-its-kind 212Pb isolation method intended to enable distributed manufacturing and reliable supply of alpha radioligand therapies. Its lead program AB001 (212Pb-NG001) is in first-in-human Phase 1 trials in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, with additional preclinical and discovery programs across breast, head and neck, lung, pancreatic and other solid tumors. ARTBIO operates from Cambridge, Massachusetts and Oslo, is backed by F-Prime Capital, Third Rock Ventures, Omega Funds, Sofinnova Partners, B Capital, ARE and QIA, and is privately held. providers.name: Arteria AI
providers.description: Arteria AI is an enterprise AI company for financial services that positions itself as the agentic backbone of financial services operations. Its platform automates document-intensive workflows across the institutional client lifecycle for tier-one global financial institutions: OTC derivatives and ISDA onboarding, prime brokerage, securities services and custody, corporate and commercial lending, trade confirmations, securities lending and repo, regulatory reporting, and post-transaction loan compliance. The platform spans four layers (data, component, agentic, and workflow), combining no-code configuration, automated document generation, intelligent extraction with zero-shot models, clause comparison and decisioning, and controlled agentic orchestration. Arteria AI is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. It does not publish a public API or developer portal; this profile captures the company identity, domain-security posture, and published compliance certifications.

providers.name: Asherbio
providers.description: Asherbio is a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing cis‑targeted immunotherapies that selectively activate immune cells to treat cancer and other diseases. Their platform aims to improve efficacy and reduce side effects by precisely targeting the immune response. Asher Bio’s pipeline includes candidates such as Etakafusp alfa, AB821, and AB359, with ongoing clinical collaborations and presentations at major oncology meetings. The company emphasizes innovative approaches to immune cell targeting, aiming to restore hope, health, and happiness for patients.

providers.name: AST SpaceMobile
providers.description: AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ, ASTS) is a United States satellite operator building the SpaceMobile Network, a space-based cellular broadband constellation of BlueBird satellites carrying the largest commercial phased-array antennas in low Earth orbit, designed to deliver 4G and 5G directly to standard, unmodified smartphones. It sits upstream of the retail telecom market as a wholesale coverage layer, not a consumer brand, not a CPaaS: signals from a handset are relayed by satellite to a small number of in-country ground gateways, which compensate for Doppler and delay and then hand the traffic into a mobile network operator's core, where the operator completes the call and bills the subscriber. Distribution runs entirely through partner carriers, with agreements covering nearly 60 mobile network operators serving over 3 billion subscribers, including AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten, Bell, TELUS and stc, plus strategic investment from Google and American Tower. Its API posture is that of a satellite infrastructure company rather than a network-API publisher, honestly assessed as none: as of July 2026 AST SpaceMobile publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs and no public network-API surface. Probes of developer, developers, docs, api and opengateway subdomains and the corresponding site paths all fail to resolve or return 404, and no CAMARA, GSMA Open Gateway, TM Forum or 3GPP NEF exposure claim appears anywhere on ast-science.com or in its press releases. Any programmable access to SpaceMobile capacity reaches developers only indirectly, through the partner carrier that owns the subscriber relationship and the network APIs.

Related products include Azara Cost & Utilization, Azara Patient Outreach, Azara Care Connect, and value-based care reporting. Azara is backed by Insight Partners and serves the safety-net and federally qualified health center (FQHC) market. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; the provider publishes no public developer portal or API at this time.

Readings stream to Biobeat's HIPAA- and GDPR-compliant, cloud-based patient management platform, where clinicians view real-time data, trends, and configurable alerts. Biobeat offers programmatic data access and EMR/EHR integration as a paid add-on for hospitals, health systems, and research partners; there is no publicly documented self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Bondbloxx Investment
providers.description: Bondbloxx Investment is a provider of specialized fixed‑income exchange‑traded funds (ETFs) focused on U.S. Treasuries, corporate bonds, private credit, and tax‑aware strategies. The firm offers a suite of ETFs designed for precise income generation, capital preservation, and diversified exposure to various credit markets, serving institutional and retail investors seeking tailored bond market solutions.

providers.name: Bondevalue
providers.description: Bondevalue provides a digital platform for tracking and trading bonds, offering curated bond portfolios, market data, and trading tools to investors. The service is regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Recognised Market Operator, delivering transparent bond pricing and portfolio management through its BondbloX platform.

providers.name: Brightree
providers.description: Brightree is a ResMed company providing cloud-based business management software for post-acute care providers, including home medical equipment (HME), durable medical equipment (DME), home infusion and specialty pharmacy, orthotics and prosthetics, and home health and hospice organizations. Its platform automates the end-to-end operational workflow from intake, documentation and inventory through billing, delivery, resupply, and patient engagement. Brightree does not publish a public, self-service developer API; integrations are delivered through a partner-gated Integrated Vendor program, so this profile is limited to the company's public web presence rather than a developer portal or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Bustle Digital Group
providers.description: Bustle Digital Group is a digital media company that operates a portfolio of online brands, including Bustle, Elite Daily, Mic, and others. It creates content across lifestyle, news, entertainment, and culture, reaching millions of readers worldwide. The company leverages data-driven storytelling and social media distribution to engage audiences and offers advertising solutions for brands.

providers.name: Carbon Capture
providers.description: Carbon Capture Inc. provides direct air capture (DAC) technology to remove CO₂ from the atmosphere and store it underground. Founded in 2022, the company offers modular, scalable DAC systems, sells carbon removal credits, and operates large‑scale projects such as the multi‑megaton Project Bison in Wyoming. It aims to accelerate the transition to net‑zero by delivering cost‑effective carbon removal solutions for industrial and corporate customers.

providers.name: Cardiofocus
providers.description: Cardiofocus is a medical technology company specializing in pulsed field ablation (PFA) solutions for cardiac arrhythmia treatment. The firm develops integrated catheter and waveform generator systems, including the Centauri, QuickShot, OptiShot, and CardioWave platforms, to provide electrophysiologists with precise, controlled therapy. CardioFocus advances its technology through extensive research, clinical trials, and regulatory approvals, serving physicians and patients worldwide.

providers.name: Careport Health
providers.description: CarePort Health, powered by WellSky, is a healthcare technology company providing care coordination and patient transition management across the entire care continuum. Its platform connects hospitals, health systems, ACOs, physician groups, payers, and post-acute providers to manage discharge planning, referrals, transitions of care, emergency department optimization, utilization and authorization management, and value-based programs. Products include Guide, Connect, Insight, Care Management, Transition, Referral Management, Intake, and Discharge, with EHR integrations for Epic and Cerner. CarePort reports covering 14M lives across roughly 2,000 hospitals in 43 U.S. states. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead (500 Global, Techstars); no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Cecelia Health
providers.description: Cecelia Health provides virtual, human-centered care solutions focused on integrated cardiometabolic management, GLP‑1 clinical support, and lifestyle‑driven weight management for employers. Their platform offers patient support services for pharma partners and delivers insights for individuals, combining technology with personalized care to improve health outcomes across populations.

providers.name: Cellcentric
providers.description: Cellcentric is a joint venture between Daimler Truck AG and Volvo Group, founded in 2021 to develop, produce, and commercialize hydrogen fuel cell systems for heavy‑duty vehicles. The company supplies Tier‑1 fuel cell modules, aiming for climate‑neutral transport by 2050, and operates globally with sites in Germany, Canada, and beyond. It offers advanced fuel cell products such as the BZA375, supports OEMs and fleet operators, and maintains a strong portfolio of patents and partnerships across the hydrogen ecosystem.

providers.name: CellFE
providers.description: CellFE is a biotech company focused on transforming cell therapy manufacturing through microfluidics technology, aiming to make advanced treatments affordable and accessible for patients worldwide. The company provides platforms and services that streamline production, reduce costs, and accelerate the delivery of cell-based medicines.

providers.name: Chestnutcarbon
providers.description: Chestnutcarbon is a U.S.-based nature‑based carbon removal company that develops, finances, and operates forest‑based carbon offset projects. It focuses on afforestation, improved forest management, and nature‑works initiatives, delivering high‑quality carbon credits to corporate clients and investors. The firm emphasizes transparency, community benefits, and biodiversity, managing over 90,000 acres of land and supporting sustainable land restoration across the United States.

providers.name: Clariter
providers.description: Clariter is a global cleantech company producing sustainable petrochemicals upcycled from plastic waste. It offers high‑quality alternatives to fossil‑based products for thousands of industrial and consumer applications, helping create circularity and reduce carbon waste. The company’s proprietary technology turns plastic waste into profitable, sustainable solutions, addressing the global plastic waste epidemic.

providers.name: Clariterrecyclingandrefiningcenter
providers.description: Clariter is a global cleantech company producing sustainable petrochemicals upcycled from plastic waste. It pioneers chemical recycling technology, offering high‑quality, food‑grade and industrial‑grade products, and operates worldwide with plants and partnerships to create circular economies.

providers.name: Coco Robotics
providers.description: Coco Robotics builds the world’s largest fleet of autonomous delivery vehicles, offering self‑driving delivery services across major cities. Their platform enables affordable, reliable, clean, and fast last‑mile logistics for advertisers, merchants, and communities, aiming to transform urban delivery with AI‑powered robotics.

providers.name: Conagen
providers.description: Conagen, Inc. is a synthetic biology and biomanufacturing company that engineers microbes to produce natural products with precision. They develop strain and organism platforms, scale microbial fermentation, and create ingredients for food, flavors, cosmetics, nutraceuticals, and pharmaceuticals. Their mission is to advance sustainable manufacturing of high‑value chemicals using engineered biology.

providers.name: Constanellisaerospace
providers.description: Constanellis Aerospace is a cislunar infrastructure company developing manufacturing, qualification, cislunar awareness, and power provision and measurement. It provides systems, services, and commercial solutions for space missions, focusing on power, control, and production for demanding lunar and orbital operations.

providers.name: CoRegen
providers.description: CoRegen, Inc. (CoRegen Science) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Houston, Texas developing adoptive cell therapies for aggressive solid tumors. Its platform, licensed exclusively from the O'Malley Lab at Baylor College of Medicine, uses CRISPR gene editing to knock out the SRC-3 steroid receptor coactivator gene in regulatory T (Treg) cells, reprogramming them from immunosuppressors into tumor-killing effectors. The lead program, CRG-150, received FDA IND clearance for a first-in-human Phase 1/2a trial in advanced solid tumors, and the underlying science won the 2023 Cozzarelli Prize. CoRegen is a therapeutics organization, not a software company: it publishes a nine-page marketing and science site (about, the science, preclinical studies, pipeline, publications, leadership, news, careers, contact) and no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Creekstoneenergy
providers.description: Creekstone Energy develops purpose‑built, behind‑the‑meter power generation for hyperscale AI data centers. Combining natural gas, solar, and storage, the company delivers multi‑source, high‑density, reliable electricity directly at AI campuses. Their flagship Delta Gigasite in Utah showcases over 10 GW in development, 100 % behind‑the‑meter generation, and 60+ kW per rack density, positioning Creekstone as a critical infrastructure provider for AI workloads.

providers.name: CrossAmerica Partners
providers.description: CrossAmerica Partners LP (NYSE: CAPL) is a U.S. wholesale distributor of motor fuels, operator of convenience stores, and owner and lessee of real estate used in the retail distribution of motor fuels. Headquartered in Allentown, Pennsylvania and formed in 2012, it distributes branded (Exxon, Mobil, BP, Shell, Valero, Citgo, Marathon, Phillips 66) and unbranded petroleum to approximately 1,600 locations across 34 states, owns or leases about 900 sites, and runs seven convenience-store brands at 340 locations in 17 states. CrossAmerica publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable contract; its only integration surface is a credential-gated Dealer Portal (account balance, pricing notifications, fuel and real-estate invoices, EFTs) hosted on a third-party platform, with logins issued by a Territory Manager under a dealer agreement.

providers.name: Cryotherapeutics
providers.description: Cryotherapeutics develops implant‑free cryotherapy technology aimed at stabilising vulnerable atherosclerotic plaques to reduce heart attack risk. Their patented system combines a console and an intracoronary balloon catheter that delivers controlled cooling to the plaque, offering a novel interventional treatment for cardiovascular disease.

providers.name: Curb
providers.description: Curb is a music entertainment company under Word Entertainment, operating record labels, artist management, and related media services. The public website provides information about its catalog, artists, and merchandise, but no public API documentation or developer portal is evident.

providers.name: Emidat
providers.description: Emidat GmbH is a Munich-based climate technology company building product intelligence infrastructure for the construction industry. Its SaaS platform lets construction material manufacturers create verified Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), run Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs), and produce Digital Product Passports (DPPs) at scale. Emidat ingests plant, ERP, and energy-management data through integrations, performs intelligent data matching, and generates ISO-compliant, verified EPDs in as little as a day rather than the typical six to twelve months. The platform also surfaces environmental-impact hotspots so manufacturers can find emission-reduction opportunities and turn sustainability data into business value. Related tools include the public EPD Database and Emidat Atlas.

providers.name: Farmwise
providers.description: FarmWise Labs is an agricultural technology company building AI-powered robotics for specialty crop farming. Its flagship product, Vulcan, is an intra-row weeder and precision cultivator that uses computer vision and machine learning to identify and mechanically remove weeds without herbicides, covering up to three acres per hour and saving growers an estimated $250+ per acre. The self-calibrating machine operates in all field conditions and receives over-the-air software updates. Founded in San Francisco and backed by GV (Google Ventures), FarmWise is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification surface.

providers.name: Feetme
providers.description: FeetMe is a Paris-based medical device company, founded in 2013, that develops smart connected insoles and digital health software for real-time gait analysis and mobility care. Its CE-marked, ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certified wearables embed plantar pressure sensors and a 6-axis inertial measurement unit to capture more than twenty gait and balance metrics per step, streaming them over Bluetooth Low Energy to the FeetMe Mobility dashboard used by clinicians for neurological, orthopedic and rehabilitation assessment. Product lines include FeetMe Evaluation, FeetMe Rehabilitation, FeetMe Monitor and FeetMe Stimulate. The company is backed by Partech. FeetMe does not currently expose a public developer API or OpenAPI-described web API; a partner SDK for raw-data integration is referenced in product materials but is not publicly documented.

providers.name: Fundly
providers.description: Fundly is a Mumbai-based fintech platform purpose-built for India's pharmaceutical retail supply chain, offering embedded credit, B2B commerce, and payment solutions to pharma retailers and distributors. Its lending product provides unsecured working capital with interest charged only for the period funds are actually drawn, alongside B2B commerce tooling and payment rails tailored to the cash-flow cycles of the pharma industry. Backed by Accel, Fundly distributes primarily through native iOS and Android apps and works with RBI-regulated lending partners. No public API, developer portal, or technical documentation is currently published; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: HistoSonics
providers.description: HistoSonics is a medical device company commercializing histotripsy, a non-invasive, non-thermal and non-ionizing sonic beam therapy that uses focused ultrasound to form a controlled bubble cloud which mechanically destroys and liquefies targeted tissue at a sub-cellular level. Its robotically assisted Edison Histotripsy System received U.S. FDA marketing authorization through the De Novo Classification Request process in October 2023 for the non-invasive destruction of liver tumors, making it the first histotripsy platform authorized anywhere in the world, and has since added CE Mark authorization in Europe and an FDA submission covering kidney tumors. The underlying science originated with researchers at the University of Michigan, and the company maintains clinical partnerships with the University of Michigan and the University of Wisconsin. HistoSonics publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API specification; its public web surface is a marketing, clinical-evidence, physician-education and eIFU site rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Jane (iHeartJane)
providers.description: Jane Technologies (iHeartJane) is a cannabis ecommerce and marketplace platform that powers real-time online menus, point-of-sale and kiosk checkout, order and reservation flows, and the Jane Universal Product Catalog for 2,500+ dispensaries and brands across the United States and Canada. Jane exposes a documented HTTP API (the Jane API, published as Swagger at api.iheartjane.com/jane-api-docs) for retrieving live store menu products and generating access tokens, and a partner Digital Merchandising SDK (Jane DM SDK) for embedding MyHigh-powered personalization and sponsored-product widgets into a retailer's own menu. Both surfaces are partner-gated - access requires approval and credentials from a Jane account representative - so the endpoints listed here are modeled from Jane's public documentation rather than exercised against a live, open, unauthenticated API.

providers.name: Kindred Healthcare
providers.description: Kindred Healthcare operated a nationwide network of long-term acute care hospitals and inpatient rehabilitation facilities. The Kindred name was retired after the 2021 merger with LifePoint Health, with the acute care facilities operating under the ScionHealth brand and rehabilitation facilities continuing as Kindred Hospital Rehabilitation Services. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified for the legacy Kindred Healthcare or its successor entities.

providers.name: Knoetic
providers.description: Knoetic is an HR technology company that operates CPOHQ, a platform built for Chief People Officers and senior people-function executives.
