The defer.run service has since transitioned and the defer.run domain currently redirects to digger.tools; this entry preserves the historical profile and links to the surviving documentation, GitHub organization, and references.

providers.name: Drug Enforcement Administration
providers.description: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Registration File API for Web Developers (on the Internet) (25,000 Inquiries). DEA25000. Publication Date: 2006: Page Count: 0: Abstract: The DEA API (Application Program Interface) enables a programmer to develop a program for a specific platform and integrate the DEA data into their verification system ...

providers.name: eduGAIN
providers.description: eduGAIN provides a federated identity service that enables simple, secure single‑sign‑on access to thousands of educational services worldwide. It connects over 80 participant federations and more than 10,000 identity and service providers, allowing students, researchers, staff, and institutions to access online resources with reduced account management complexity.

providers.name: Envelop Risk
providers.description: Envelop Risk is a technology-led reinsurance underwriting and analytics firm specializing in cyber and other complex, emerging risks. The company combines actuarial science, machine learning, and cyber threat intelligence to model, price, and underwrite cyber (re)insurance for insurers, MGAs, and capital-market partners. Its platforms include CyberTooth (cyber risk modeling and augmented underwriting), Cyber Threat Intelligence, Envelop Capital Markets, and Envelop Risk Solutions (product development, analytics, modeling support). Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Envelop Risk surpassed a $1bn gross-written-premium milestone. This API Evangelist profile was created as a portfolio-company lead; the company does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Farm Service Agency
providers.description: As directed by the OPEN (Open, Public, Electronic, and Necessary) Government Data Act and through its commitment to United States agriculturalists and interested public, FSA provides numerous data resources through reports, visualizations, and other formats.

providers.name: Finres
providers.description: Finres (finres SAS) is a French climate-risk analytics company building a decision platform for agriculture. It translates climate hazards into economic consequences for farms, agricultural value chains and territories, combining agronomic, pedological, climate and market data with AI models that are peer-reviewed and validated against published research. Two productized offerings sit on top of the platform - a farm-level economic and climate viability diagnostic (DPEC, currently in beta, seeded from a grower's TelePAC parcel file and reference datasets such as Agreste, IPPAP and RICA) and bespoke territorial or sector studies. Finres was founded by Florent Baarsch, previously with the World Bank, the United Nations and climate research institutes, and its customers include the French government, the World Bank, the Green Climate Fund, IFAD and the FAO. The company markets high-resolution data delivery into customer decision systems, but as of this enrichment pass publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification or SDK - access is arranged through a sales demo.

providers.name: Flank
providers.description: Flank builds AI agents for enterprise legal teams that handle high-volume, routine legal work autonomously. Its supervised agents operate like paralegals, taking in requests via email or portals, executing contracting tasks against an organization's own templates and playbooks, and returning completed work for lawyer review. The platform covers drafting, contract review, negotiation, and triage, letting legal departments insource repetitive work while lawyers supervise finished output and high-risk items. Flank is backed by HV Capital, Insight Partners, and Speedinvest, and is SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 42001, GDPR, and CCPA compliant.

providers.name: Glimmer (formerly Storyhunter)
providers.description: Glimmer, formerly known as Storyhunter, is an all-in-one creator management platform and global marketplace connecting brands and media companies with a vetted network of 50,000+ freelance content creators, video producers, and journalists across 170+ countries. Founded in 2012 by Jaron Gilinsky in Brooklyn, New York, and rebranded from Storyhunter to Glimmer in November 2023, the platform organizes creator teams, messaging, project management, online contracts, and global payments in one central dashboard, and offers Glimmer Select as a full-service managed production studio. Clients have included CNN, The New York Times, National Geographic, MSNBC, and Starbucks. The company was backed in part by 500 Global and is surfaced here as an API Evangelist network company profile; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Green Software Foundation
providers.description: The Green Software Foundation is a Linux Foundation project founded by Accenture, GitHub, Microsoft, and ThoughtWorks to build standards, tools, and best practices for reducing the carbon emissions of software. It developed the Software Carbon Intensity specification and provides patterns for building green software.

providers.name: Gut Wellness Club
providers.description: Gut Wellness Club is an India-based consumer wellness brand offering a "Gut Reset" program that promises to resolve digestive issues in 15-20 days using natural traditional foods, yoga, Ayurveda, and Naturopathy as an alternative to medication. The site is Wix-hosted and, notably for a consumer brand, exposes agent-native surfaces: a published /llms.txt and a live, hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint that lets AI agents retrieve business details, search the site, and access Wix REST APIs without scraping. It has no first-party developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs. Surfaced via Accel portfolio mining and enriched from its real public agent surfaces.

providers.name: Humanitarian Data Exchange
providers.description: Humanitarian Data Exchange is a organization open-data portal running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 27,880 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Hydrow
providers.description: Hydrow (legally True Rowing, Inc., Boston, Massachusetts) is a connected-fitness hardware company that makes the Hydrow indoor rowing machine and the LYQUID strength-training platform, sold with a subscription to a library of live and on-demand athlete-led workouts filmed on real water. Members interact with Hydrow through its rower touchscreens and the Hydrow iOS/Android companion apps, which sync workout summaries outward to Strava and Apple Health. Hydrow operates a real production backend for those apps, but publishes no public developer program, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no first-party SDK in any package registry; its developer-facing subdomains do not resolve to a service. Its public machine-readable surface is limited to an Atlassian Statuspage.

providers.name: ICPSR
providers.description: The Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR) at the University of Michigan provides a curated archive of social science data, offering tools for data discovery, access, and management. It supports researchers, educators, and policymakers with datasets spanning health, politics, economics, and more, and provides documentation, help guides, and membership resources.

providers.name: JD.com (Jingdong)
providers.description: JD.com (Jingdong) is one of China's largest direct-sales e-commerce platforms, operating a vast first-party retail business and a third-party (POP) marketplace alongside JD Logistics (one of China's largest integrated logistics networks), JD Health, JD Industrials, JD Property, and JD Cloud. JD exposes two distinct developer platforms: JD Open Platform (open.jd.com) — also known as JOS (Jingdong Open Service) — which hosts the partner / ISV REST API for sellers and ERP / OMS vendors covering ware (product), order, promotion, after-sale, warehouse, finance, customer service, message, JD logistics, and B2B; and JD Cloud (jdcloud.com) — JD's public cloud with compute (Cloud Virtual Machine, GPU, bare metal, function compute), storage (object, block, file), network (VPC, CDN, load balancer), database (MySQL, TiDB, StarDB, Redis, MongoDB, ClickHouse), AI (JoyBuilder, JoyAgent, JoyCode, OCR, speech), and security services.

providers.name: Juna.ai
providers.description: Juna.ai is a Berlin-based industrial AI company building an Agentic Factory OS — a platform of autonomous AI agents that plan, steer, and continuously improve complex industrial production processes. Its agents ingest live plant data through integrations with existing IT/OT systems (SAP, Siemens, AVEVA, PI Server, Snowflake), model assets and processes into a Factory Graph and Knowledge Graph, detect anomalies, run root-cause analysis, generate reports, and recommend or execute control actions 24/7 with human-in-the-loop oversight and full traceability. Juna targets heavy and process industries including chemicals, cement, pulp & paper, glass, food & beverage, pharma, consumer goods, and industrial manufacturing, focused on maximizing output, quality, energy efficiency, and sustainability. The company is backed by Kleiner Perkins, Norrsken VC, and John Doerr. Juna delivers integration through enterprise engagements and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Kenbi
providers.description: Kenbi is a German healthcare organization focused on nursing education and workforce development, operating through two divisions. Kenbi Academy delivers continuing professional development for care workers with 100+ ZFU-certified courses recognized by all German health insurers and available nationwide, spanning nursing service management, quality assurance, wound care, and instructor training. Kenbi Campus runs vocational nursing programs in Berlin and Hamburg, including a three-year registered nurse generalist program and an 18-month nursing assistant curriculum. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Layer3
providers.description: Layer3 is a consumer crypto platform that bills itself as a gateway to the onchain economy, combining a gasless smart wallet with curated protocol "Activations" where users complete onchain tasks to earn CUBE rewards and the L3 token. It spans 40+ chains and 500+ applications, adds trading, staking, competitions, perks, and social features, and offers a Builder product that lets protocols launch incentivized activations, set up a Space, and distribute token rewards. It is backed by Electric Capital. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface was found during enrichment; the docs at docs.layer3.xyz cover the end-user Platform and no-code Builder products only.

providers.name: LF Networking
providers.description: LF Networking is an umbrella organization under the Linux Foundation that provides the largest set of open source networking projects including ONAP, FD.io, and OPNFV. It fosters collaboration across a broad industry coalition to build an open networking stack.

providers.name: Medtronic
providers.description: Medtronic is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Medtronic API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Miuros
providers.description: Miuros is a performance platform for customer service that provides AI-powered analytics, quality assurance (Review & Insights), and agent-assist automation (Assist) for international and scaling customer support teams. Founded as a standalone startup and backed by Techstars, Miuros was acquired by Dixa and is now offered as Miuros by Dixa. The Miuros product surface — Data sync, Review & Insights, Assist, and Miuros APIs — remains operational and is tracked on a dedicated Miuros status page, while platform developer documentation is served through the Dixa developer hub.

providers.name: Morpheus Space
providers.description: Morpheus Space is an in-space mobility company building electric propulsion systems and mission-design software for the New Space economy. Founded in 2018 out of the Technical University of Dresden, its second-generation GO-2 system uses FEEP (Field Emission Electric Propulsion) technology to deliver continuous, chemical-free thrust for satellite constellation deployment, station keeping, collision avoidance, repositioning, and deorbiting. The company also offers Journey, a mission simulation and design platform that matches simulated requirements to available satellite subsystems. Morpheus Space markets ITAR-free solutions and is backed by investors including Techstars, Alpine Space Ventures, Airbus Ventures, Lavrock Ventures, and In-Q-Tel. The company publishes no public developer API; its only machine-facing surface is a platform-hosted (Wix) site MCP endpoint and an auto-generated llms.txt for agent access to public marketing content.

providers.name: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS)
providers.description: The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) is part of the U.S. National Institutes of Health and supports research into the causes, treatment, and prevention of arthritis and musculoskeletal and skin diseases. NIAMS publishes health information, research resources, and grant data via its website.

providers.name: National Invasive Species Information Center
providers.description: National Invasive Species Information Center (NISIC) is the gateway to invasive species information covering federal, state, local, and international sources. Invasive species are plants, animals, or pathogens that are non-native to the ecosystem under consideration, and whose introduction causes or is likely to cause harm.

providers.name: National Pesticide Information Center
providers.description: The National Pesticide Information Center (NPIC) provides objective, science-based information about pesticides and their potential health and environmental effects. NPIC is a cooperative agreement between Oregon State University and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, serving the general public, health professionals, and pesticide manufacturers.

providers.name: Noox
providers.description: Noox is a Web3 platform for creating and collecting achievement badges as soulbound NFTs, letting people build verifiable on-chain reputation. Users discover community-curated Web3 achievements, check eligibility, and mint them as identity-bound (non-transferable) NFTs, while creators build custom on-chain achievements from live blockchain data with a no-code, template-based designer. The protocol is deployed on Ethereum mainnet (badge, badgeMinter and feeCollector smart contracts) and is powered by Alchemy Web3 infrastructure. Noox is a portfolio company of Electric Capital in the crypto sector. Note: Noox exposes no public REST/HTTP developer API, OpenAPI, GraphQL/subgraph, or SDK; its developer surface is the on-chain smart contracts.

providers.name: Nutrition & Exercise API
providers.description: The Dietagram Nutrition API is designed to simplify the integration of your application with Dietagram's extensive food database and nutritional standards. Rather than developing and maintaining your own nutrient database, you can rely on Dietagram for high-quality source data.

providers.name: Office of Child Support Services
providers.description: The Office of Child Support Services is a government agency that works to ensure that children receive the financial support they need from their non-custodial parent. This office helps establish legal paternity, locate absent parents, and establish and enforce child support orders. They work with both custodial and non-custodial parents to facilitate the collection and distribution of child support payments, ensuring that children have the resources they need to thrive.

providers.name: OSIsoft
providers.description: OSIsoft was the enterprise software company behind the PI System, the operational data infrastructure used across manufacturing, energy, utilities, oil and gas, and other industrial sectors to collect, historize, contextualize, and visualize high-volume real-time sensor and control-system time-series data. Its developer surface centered on the PI Web API (a RESTful interface to the PI Data Archive and Asset Framework), AF SDK, and the PI Square developer community. OSIsoft was acquired by AVEVA in 2021; all osisoft.com and docs.osisoft.com properties now redirect to AVEVA, where the product ships as the AVEVA PI System. This profile is maintained as a historical/acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network, with developer resources pointing at the live AVEVA successor pages.

providers.name: Outsmart College
providers.description: Outsmart (Outsmart Education, Inc.) is an education-technology company rebuilding higher education for the AI era, aiming to make learning smarter, faster, and more engaging than traditional lectures and student debt. The company is currently pre-launch, operating a public waitlist at joinoutsmart.com, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this profile the company publishes only a marketing site with a legal Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions and does not expose a public developer or API surface. This record was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for ongoing enrichment as any API surface appears.

providers.name: Porters
providers.description: Porters is an AI-native outsourcing partner for European banking operations. Its platform uses AI agents with human oversight to automate high-volume back-office banking processes — account seizure processing (private and public account seizures), insolvency case management from intake to resolution, and chargeback dispute data collection, triage, and resolution. Documents are ingested, extracted, and classified; decisions are made with a human in the loop; and banking actions plus audit reports are generated automatically. Porters hosts data in the EU in line with GDPR, maintains 24/7 audit trails, and does not use customer data for model training. It was founded by veterans of McKinsey, Qonto, Upvest, Solaris, and Roland Berger, and is backed by Earlybird and Seedcamp. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Reface
providers.description: Reface (NeoCortext, Inc.) is an AI-native consumer app studio best known for its flagship Reface face-swap and AI-avatar application, alongside a portfolio of generative media apps including Revive (photo animation), Restyle (AI photo and video filters), Ink AI (virtual tattoo try-on), BitePal (AI calorie tracking), Lightly (AI journaling), Letsy (virtual clothing try-on), and Memomet. Backed by a16z, Reface builds and distributes mobile-first generative AI experiences directly to consumers via the App Store and Google Play. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its surface is consumer applications rather than a programmable platform. This APIs.json profile is a company lead in the API Evangelist network awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: Reliance Steel & Aluminum
providers.description: Reliance Steel & Aluminum Co. is the largest metals service center in North America, providing value-added metals processing services and distributing a full line of metal products including aluminum, brass, bronze, carbon and alloy steel, copper, titanium, and stainless steel. Operating over 300 service center locations across 40 US states and 13 countries, Reliance serves more than 130,000 customers across aerospace, automotive, defense, energy, electronics, construction, and semiconductor end markets.

providers.name: San Diego Gas & Electric
providers.description: San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E) is a regulated electric and natural gas utility serving San Diego and southern Orange County, a subsidiary of Sempra. Under CPUC rules it offers Green Button Download My Data and Green Button Connect My Data, letting customers authorize registered third parties to receive their energy usage data via the SDG&E My Account portal. No public developer portal or machine-readable API contract was found.

providers.name: Snapsheet
providers.description: Snapsheet is a cloud-based property & casualty (P&C) claims management platform for insurance carriers, MGAs, and TPAs. It runs the full claims lifecycle with no-code workflow configuration, intelligent automation, document management, virtual vehicle appraisals, total-loss settlement, integrated claims payments, and analytics. Snapsheet reports serving 170+ customers, including 16 of the top 20 P&C carriers, and processing more than 400 million API calls per month. It exposes open APIs and webhooks to customers and partners for connecting policy, billing, underwriting, and vendor systems, though API access is arranged through its sales and partner channel rather than a public self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: SoftBank
providers.description: SoftBank Corp. is a multinational conglomerate headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, operating across telecommunications, internet services, AI, robotics, and investment. The company provides a wide range of consumer and enterprise services, including mobile communications, broadband, energy solutions, and a portfolio of technology investments. Its public website offers information on corporate philosophy, sustainability initiatives, news, and support resources, reflecting its role as a major player in the global technology and finance sectors.

providers.name: Steel Dynamics
providers.description: Steel Dynamics, Inc. is one of the largest domestic steel producers and metals recyclers in the United States, with operations spanning steel manufacturing, steel processing, and metals recycling. Founded in 1993 and headquartered in Fort Wayne, Indiana, the company operates steel mills, fabrication operations, and metals recycling facilities. Steel Dynamics is a Fortune 500 company listed on NASDAQ (STLD) and does not offer public developer APIs; data access is available through financial data providers and investor relations communications.

providers.name: Terawatt Infrastructure
providers.description: Terawatt Infrastructure is a US infrastructure company that acquires, develops, owns, and operates purpose-built electric-vehicle charging centers for commercial fleets — medium- and heavy-duty trucking, drayage, autonomous vehicle and rideshare operators. The company sells charging-as-a-service rather than software: it holds real estate and grid interconnection, builds high-power charging sites (including the I-10 electrified corridor and sites near the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach), and runs them with its own proprietary Charge Management Software, operations and maintenance program, and a customer reservations portal. Terawatt states publicly that it has implemented the Open Charge Point Interface (OCPI) with custom extensions so fleet customers get visibility into its charging facilities, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract for that surface.

providers.name: The GEO Group
providers.description: The GEO Group, Inc. (NYSE: GEO) is a publicly traded private corrections and community supervision company headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida. Founded in 1984 as Wackenhut Corrections Corporation and rebranded in 2004, it is the largest private prison operator in the United States and a primary contractor to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the U.S. Marshals Service, the Federal Bureau of Prisons, and numerous state departments of corrections. As of 2024 the company owned or managed approximately 80,000 beds across roughly 99 facilities and reported $2.424 billion in revenue. Its wholly owned subsidiary BI Incorporated operates the federal Intensive Supervision Appearance Program (ISAP) and builds the ankle monitors, GPS trackers, voice-verification systems and SmartLINK smartphone app used to monitor people in immigration proceedings and community supervision. GEO Group publishes no public developer API and has no GitHub presence; the only "platform" surfaces it exposes are customer-facing operational systems (BI TotalAccess for officers, BI SmartLINK for supervised individuals) used inside its own contracts. This repository documents the corporate footprint, the technology subsidiary, and the public-record controversies surrounding the firm under the second Trump administration's 2025+ ICE detention expansion, for purposes of the API Evangelist network's coverage of API absence in sensitive sectors.

providers.name: Tomo
providers.description: Tomo is a consumer "personal AI" application that lives in your text messages: users tell Tomo about their life, goals, problems, and aspirations over SMS, and the AI assistant learns those goals and guides them toward achieving them through ongoing text-based conversation. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Ribbit Capital, Tomo operates in the AI-apps sector as a mobile-first consumer product rather than a developer platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site (tomo.ai) with About, Careers, Privacy, Terms, and Login pages but no public developer program: no API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, MCP server, llms.txt, or .well-known discovery endpoints were found. This profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness.

providers.name: Ventas
providers.description: Ventas, Inc. is an S&P 500 healthcare real estate investment trust (REIT) and one of the largest owners of senior housing communities, medical office buildings, life science research facilities, and health system facilities in the United States, Canada, and United Kingdom. Ventas operates the Ventas OI proprietary data platform for operational intelligence across its portfolio of approximately 1,400 properties. Ventas does not offer a public developer API; data access is available through financial data providers and SEC EDGAR filings.

providers.name: Vridhi Home Finance
providers.description: Vridhi Home Finance (Vridhi Finserv Home Finance Limited) is an affordable housing finance company (HFC) headquartered in Bengaluru, India, founded in 2022. Operating as a tech-enabled brick-and-mortar lender across tier-2 and tier-3 cities, it provides home purchase loans, home construction loans, plot-and-construction loans, balance-transfer and top-up loans, and loans against property to salaried and self-employed customers. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Elevation Capital. It operates a public marketing website, a customer service portal, a refer-and-earn portal, and an Android mobile app, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Zurich Insurance
providers.description: A Swiss multinational insurance company and one of the world's largest insurers providing property, casualty, life, and specialty insurance products. Zurich operates a public API platform at exchange.zurich.com (Zurich Exchange / ConnectZ / Zurich Edge) that exposes 30+ internal and external APIs across policy, claims, quoting, partner analytics, procurement, and operations.

providers.name: 3D Medivision
providers.description: 3D Medivision (쓰리디메디비젼) is a Seoul, South Korea medical imaging and medical-education company founded around 3D surgical video capture. It builds 3D/2D camera systems, recorders and monitors that mount to surgical microscopes and endoscopes so a procedure can be recorded stereoscopically and streamed to surgeons in another room, hospital or country. On top of that hardware it operates a set of end-user education products: Veterflix and Global Veterflix (video-on-demand veterinary courses, webinars and 3D canine anatomy), VGTC (live 3D surgery streaming plus hands-on courses in Incheon), VET-TV (a 3D anatomy lecture system for large-group teaching), Veter VR (VR-based veterinary training) and Surgflix for human surgery. The company sells hardware, subscriptions and training — it does not operate a public developer program, and no public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable API contract was found on any host it controls.

providers.name: @Stake
providers.description: Stake (Stake Technologies, Inc., NMLS #2535498) operates the "Return on Rent" cash-back network for renters. Renters earn cash back on their rent payments, build credit history through on-time payments, unlock exclusive local deals, and access banking services including an FDIC-insured checking account and debit card provided through banking partner Midland States Bank. Co-founded by Rowland Hobbs and Jimmy Jacobson, the platform reports more than 550,000 homes in its network and over $50M in cash back earned by renters, averaging roughly $350 per renter annually. Stake is a consumer-facing fintech product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (surfaced under Battery Ventures).

providers.name: Alt
providers.description: Alt (alt.xyz) is an alternative-asset platform for high-value graded trading cards, founded by Leore Avidar, who previously co-founded the address and print API company Lob. Alt lets collectors and investors research, value, buy, sell, vault, and borrow against slabbed cards in one place, spanning baseball, basketball, football, hockey, soccer, golf, tennis, racing and combat-sports cards as well as Pokemon and other trading-card games. The platform combines a fixed-price marketplace, timed and "Liquid" auctions, an Instant Pricer, market-trend and research views, a physical vault in Delaware that removes sales tax from transactions, and card-backed lending. Its pricing engine, Alt Value, is a machine-learning model tuned by card-pricing specialists that produces a real-time value for every BGS, PSA and SGC card vaulted with Alt, and that value underwrites every trade, loan and product on the platform. Alt raised a $75M Series B in November 2021 led by Spearhead with Seven Seven Six and a group of professional athletes. Alt publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, CLI, sandbox or self-service API signup. Its programmatic surface is the private backend behind the alt.xyz web and mobile applications (a FastAPI/GraphQL platform service, with the engineering organisation on GitHub as github.com/onlyalt), which integrates payment, identity-verification, authentication, lending-servicing and shipping vendors but is neither documented nor offered to third parties.

providers.name: Apparta
providers.description: Apparta is a Colombian hospitality technology company providing a reservation-management and guest-engagement platform for restaurants, bars, and dining venues across Latin America (Bogota, Medellin, Cali, Barranquilla). The SaaS product covers AI-assisted table assignment and floor-plan zoning, no-show prevention with prepayments and cancellation policies, a WhatsApp AI chatbot for automated bookings, CRM campaigns over SMS/email/WhatsApp, POS integration, branded booking pages and digital menus, and marketing connectors to Google, Google Maps, Instagram, TripAdvisor, and Facebook. Apparta is offered in tiered monthly plans (Basico, Standard, Plus) and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profiling; higher tiers expose a WhatsApp Business API integration on behalf of venues rather than a first-party Apparta API.

providers.name: Auraaero
providers.description: Auraaero is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Aurealistherapeutics
providers.description: Aurealis Therapeutics is a biotechnology company focused on developing multi-target therapies for chronic wounds, diabetic foot ulcers, and cancer. The firm conducts clinical trials, publishes scientific research, and partners with healthcare organizations to bring innovative treatments to market. Their platform integrates advanced drug discovery with rigorous clinical validation to address unmet medical needs.

providers.name: Avant-Garde Health
providers.description: Avant-Garde Health is a healthcare data analytics company that helps hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs), and physicians identify cost-reduction and quality-improvement opportunities in surgical care. Its CareMeasurement platform ingests electronic medical record (EMR), financial, and patient-reported outcomes data, combines it with claims data and proprietary algorithms, and applies time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) so care teams can drill into clinical, financial, and operational detail, benchmark performance across departments and institutions, and drive value-based improvement. Products span surgical cost management, surgical coding optimization, surgical quality and outcomes optimization (ERAS), PACU and OR throughput, and CMS TEAM support. Surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Bethesdasoftworks
providers.description: Bethesda Softworks is an American video game publisher based in Rockville, Maryland, known for popular franchises such as The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and Doom. Founded in 1986, the company develops and publishes games across multiple platforms, operating a digital storefront at bethesda.net and supporting a vibrant community of players worldwide.

providers.name: bith.tv
providers.description: Bith.ai (bith.tv) is an all-in-one, AI-powered video editing and content creation platform for creators, letting users record, edit, resize, caption, and publish short-form video reformatted for the major social platforms from a single browser-based dashboard. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Amman, Jordan, the company is backed by 500 Global, BeyondCapital, Propeller, and Oasis500. Bith does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with what the company publicly publishes (website, marketing tool pages, pricing, sign-up, and probed domain security posture).

providers.name: BoardEffect
providers.description: BoardEffect is a board management (board portal) platform for meetings, agendas, board books, document libraries, committees, workrooms, surveys, and voting, purpose-built for mission-driven organizations such as nonprofits, healthcare systems, higher education institutions, foundations, and credit unions. BoardEffect is owned by Diligent and is delivered as part of the Diligent One Platform. It does not publish a self-serve public developer API - integrations are handled through a customer-facing Integration Panel (SSO plus documented web services) provisioned per tenant, and the separate Diligent Developer Portal (developer.diligent.com) exposes APIs for the Diligent One GRC platform rather than for BoardEffect's board-management data. Pricing is contact-sales only (annual subscription, tiered by users).

providers.name: Bodyfriend
providers.description: Bodyfriend is a digital technology healthcare company specializing in premium 4D full-body massage chairs and wellness products. Their patented ROVO bipedal technology offers therapeutic stretching, mobility support, and relaxation, aiming to extend users’ lives by ten years through healthy living practices. The brand combines advanced engineering, medical expertise, and elegant design to deliver home wellness solutions.

providers.name: Bright
providers.description: Bright is Mexico's leading residential and commercial solar energy provider, founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) by Jonah Greenberger. Often described as "Sunrun for the developing world," Bright combines financing and software to let homeowners and businesses adopt rooftop solar and battery energy storage (BESS) at no upfront cost. The company operates a marketplace connecting a network of local installers, distributors, and retail promoters with customers, and offers financing models such as solar PPAs and leasing schemes. Bright's public web presence is a Wix-hosted marketing site (thinkbright.mx) covering its industrial, commercial, and home solutions, success cases, and 24/7 energy monitoring technology. It exposes an agent-facing surface via an llms.txt and a hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint, but publishes no first-party developer/REST API.

providers.name: Chipper Cash
providers.description: Chipper Cash is a pan-African fintech (legal entities Critical Ideas, Inc. and Voyse Technologies US, Inc.) operating a mobile-first cross-border money transfer, digital payments, crypto, and investing platform across Africa and the diaspora. Founded in 2018 by Ham Serunjogi (Uganda) and Maijid Moujaled (Ghana) after they met at Grinnell College in Iowa, Chipper became one of Africa's fintech unicorns in 2021 and has raised over $340M to date. The consumer app — available on iOS, Android, and web — supports peer-to-peer and cross-border transfers across 21+ African countries, virtual Visa cards (Chipper Card), bill pay and airtime top-ups, fractional US-stock investing (Chipper Stocks, 6,000+ public companies, from $1), and historically crypto trading (BTC/ETH). Reported scale includes 5M+ registered users, 1M+ Visa cards issued, and 250,000+ daily transactions. Direct consumer markets include Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda, the UK, and the US. On the developer side, Chipper exposes the Chipper Network API ("Pay With Chipper") — a merchant-facing API that lets authorized businesses accept cross-border payments across 9 currencies, initiate payouts, issue refunds, and look up Chipper user accounts, authenticated with a Chipper User ID + Network API Key. Documentation is published as a Postman collection and access is gated by merchant onboarding; no public OpenAPI or open-source SDK is currently published. Adjacent products include Chipper ID (AI-led identity verification), Chipper Enterprise (bulk payments and collections), Business Accounts, and Zoona (agent-network remittances), plus an integration with TBD's tbDEX protocol for decentralized cross-border payments.

providers.name: Congruencetherapeutics
providers.description: Congruencetherapeutics, operating as Congruence Therapeutics, is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company focused on discovering and developing small‑molecule correctors and allosteric modulators. Leveraging AI‑enabled protein structural data, biology, and chemistry, the firm aims to treat diseases at the molecular level by correcting protein misfolding and signaling. Their pipeline targets metabolic, neurological, immunological, oncology and rare disease indications.

providers.name: Core10
providers.description: Core10, Inc. is a U.S.-based fintech software development and API integration firm founded in 2016 by Lee Farabaugh and Jeff Martin, headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee with delivery centers in Martin, Tennessee and Huntington, West Virginia, built on a domestic-outsourcing model it trademarked as Hereshore(R). Core10 wrote custom software, core-banking integrations and API layers for community banks, credit unions and fintechs, and acquired Accrue Technologies in 2021 to add a Salesforce-based digital lending, account opening and treasury onboarding platform. In January 2024 it spun its implementation practice out as Monarch, and the Core10 brand has since been retired: core10.io now 301-redirects to monarchfts.com, where Monarch operates as an Intapp DealCloud implementation, configuration and managed-services consultancy for private capital firms, while the Accrue platform trades independently at getaccrue.com under its own leadership. Core10 built API integrations for other companies for nearly a decade but never published a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract of its own, and as of 2026-08-11 neither successor brand does either.

providers.name: Corractions
providers.description: CorrActions develops AI-based neuromonitoring technology that measures drivers' cognitive states such as alcohol level, fatigue, distraction and other impairments using existing in-cabin sensors. The software-only solution integrates via OTA updates, aims to improve road safety, and is marketed to automotive OEMs and safety regulators. CorrActions is active in Euro NCAP and NHTSA committees and partners with industry leaders to bring real-time driver monitoring to market.

providers.name: Craftable
providers.description: Craftable is hospitality's back-office software platform for restaurants, bars, hotels, and resorts, originally known for its Bevager and Foodager products, that connects purchasing, inventory, recipes, and accounts payable with accounting and sales data. Its suite spans Intelligent Ordering (eProcurement), AP Automation with Invoice AI, Inventory and Recipe Management, and Daily Actionable Insights, plus AI features such as Operator AI and the Crafty in-app assistant. Craftable is SOC 2 compliant and SSO-capable, with more than 1,000 POS, EDI, and vendor/API integrations spanning systems such as Toast, Square, Lightspeed, Clover, SpotOn, TouchBistro, Aloha by NCR Voyix, Restaurant365, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite, Acumatica, QuickBooks, and Xero. Craftable does not publish a public self-service developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; integrations are delivered through its implementation team during onboarding, and API access to a connected platform is provisioned by requesting a scoped API key from that platform's support team.

providers.name: CREW Carbon
providers.description: CREW Carbon supplies a calcium‑based alkalinity enhancement product for wastewater treatment facilities. The product is dosed into existing biological treatment processes to improve nutrient removal, settleability, and operational cost while permanently removing greenhouse gases. It is marketed to plant owners, operators, and affiliates seeking process intensification and carbon removal solutions.

providers.name: Digital Room
providers.description: Digital Room is an e-commerce and manufacturing company that for nearly three decades has helped small and medium-sized businesses reach customers, promote products, and build their brands. It sells customized marketing products through ten uniquely branded storefronts — UPrinting, Signs.com, NextDayFlyers, PrintPlace, PrintRunner, eSigns, 48HourPrint, LogoSportswear, Packlane and Packola — backed by purpose-built ordering and design software and a coast-to-coast production network of nine U.S. facilities plus two in the Philippines, covering print, signage, packaging, apparel and promotional products. Sycamore Partners acquired the company from H.I.G. Capital in December 2021; Insight Partners is also an investor, which is how it entered the API Evangelist network. Digital Room publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, MCP server or agent card. Its one machine-readable agent surface is llms.txt — all ten brand storefronts serve a substantive, hand-authored file, several with explicit "For AI Agents" routing instructions, while the corporate host serves none.

providers.name: Dusk
providers.description: Dusk (dusk.app), tagline "Make the night," is a consumer mobile app backed by 500 Global. It publishes product documentation on a Notion-hosted docs site (docs.dusk.app) and maintains an RFC 9116 security.txt pointing to a public Responsible Disclosure Policy. Dusk was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time, so this profile captures its verifiable web, documentation, and security posture.

providers.name: Emma
providers.description: Emma (by EDAILABS) is an AI-powered English language learning application built around a 3D interactive avatar tutor that offers real-time spoken conversation practice, instant pronunciation and grammar corrections, and personalized, adaptive learning paths. Positioned as "more than just a chatbot," the app models native accents and speech patterns for judgment-free practice available 24/7, and reports more than 500,000 users. It is a consumer iOS mobile application backed by Seedcamp; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Fiber
providers.description: Fiber is an Express-inspired web framework for Go built on Fasthttp for building fast and scalable microservices and APIs.

providers.name: Home Trust
providers.description: Home Trust Company is a federally regulated Canadian trust company founded in 1977 and headquartered in Toronto, and the principal operating subsidiary of Home Capital Group. Home Capital was taken private by Smith Financial Corporation (Stephen Smith) in 2023, and the group now spans Home Trust, Home Bank (a Schedule I bank), Fairstone Bank, and the Oaken Financial deposit brand, positioning itself as one of Canada's leading alternative (non-prime) lenders. Its products include residential and commercial mortgages, reverse mortgages, Equityline, Preferred and Secured Visa credit cards, and Oaken GIC and high-interest savings deposits. Home Trust operates no public developer portal or first-party API: developer.hometrust.ca and api.hometrust.ca do not resolve (DNS NXDOMAIN), no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger is published, and no Interac e-Transfer or Payments Canada Real-Time Rail (RTR) API surface is documented. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, FCAC as overseer) but not yet operational, and Home Trust publishes no stated CDB or FDX position; any consumer data access today would be via screen-scraping aggregators such as Flinks or Plaid rather than a first-party API. This is an identity-only record: no public API exists as of July 2026.

providers.name: Howdy
providers.description: Howdy is a nearshore talent platform that connects US companies with senior software engineers, data, DevOps, design, and product professionals across Latin America. Operating as an employer of record (EOR), Howdy handles recruiting, vetting, payroll, benefits, equipment, compliance, and team performance coaching through physical "Howdy Houses" in cities across the region. Founded in 2018 in Austin, Texas by Jacqueline Samira and Frank Licea, the company went through Y Combinator (W21) and acquired the Brazilian recruiting platform GeekHunter in 2023. It is a services/staffing business with no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, agent-facing, and legal surface.

providers.name: Identiq
providers.description: Identiq operates a privacy-preserving, peer-to-peer identity validation network that lets member companies confirm a customer is already known and trusted by other members without any party sharing, exposing, or centralizing personal data. Its patented anonymized protocol keeps identity data encrypted inside each member's own environment while answering cross-network trust queries in real time. Products include customer identification, sign-up validation, risk-based onboarding, payment optimization, and trust & safety, serving travel, e-commerce, ticketing, fintech, telco, and marketplace verticals. Identiq is a cybersecurity company backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it publishes a public trust center but no public developer API.

providers.name: Infermedica
providers.description: NLP based symptom checker and patient triage API for health diagnosis from text

providers.name: Jefferies Financial Group
providers.description: Jefferies Financial Group is a leading global, full-service investment banking and capital markets firm providing advisory, capital raising, sales, trading, research, wealth management, and alternative asset management services to clients across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific.

providers.name: Kaiber
providers.description: Kaiber (Kyber Corp., dba Kaiber) is an AI creative studio for generative video and audio. Its web and mobile apps let creators turn text prompts, images, and music into stylized videos through features such as Canvas, Beat Sync, Auto-Clip, and an Editor timeline, sold via credit-based monthly subscription plans (Starter, Creator, Pro, Visionary) plus day passes and one-time credit packs. Kaiber does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company's identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network, surfaced originally as a portfolio company of eqt-ventures.

providers.name: Lantmäteriet
providers.description: Lantmäteriet is Sweden’s national land authority, providing geospatial data, cadastral information, and mapping services. It maintains the official register of property ownership, offers free and paid datasets, and supports developers through APIs for address lookup, map tiles, and geographic data downloads. The agency aims to increase transparency and accessibility of land information for public, businesses, and municipalities.

providers.name: Laureate Education
providers.description: Laureate Education, Inc. is a for-profit higher-education network founded in 1989 as Sylvan Learning Systems and renamed Laureate Education in May 2004. At its 2017 IPO peak the company operated more than 200 campuses across 28 countries serving over one million students; it became only the third B Corporation to go public when it listed on NASDAQ (ticker: LAUR) on 1 February 2017. Between 2018 and 2021 Laureate executed one of the largest sector-wide divestiture programs in the history of higher education, exiting Brazil (sold to Ânima Holding for ~$765M), the United States (Walden University sold to Adtalem for $1.48B), Australia / New Zealand (sold to Strategic Education), Chile (Universidad Andrés Bello transferred to Fundación Educación y Cultura in September 2020), Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, Malaysia, China, Italy, Cyprus and the United Kingdom — returning $1.29B to shareholders in October 2021. After the divestiture cycle Laureate continued as a pure-play Mexico / Peru operator with five remaining institutions and approximately 460,000 students. In May 2024 the company was acquired by an investor group led by the International Finance Corporation (IFC, a member of the World Bank Group) and Sterling Capital, taking Laureate Education private and delisting it from NASDAQ. The company is headquartered at 1000 Brickell Avenue, Suite 715, Miami, FL. Laureate does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, webhook surface, or status page. There is no Laureate Education GitHub organization. This profile therefore captures the corporate surface — institutions, divestiture history, leadership, investor status, news — rather than a programmable interface. The five remaining campus-network institutions each publish their own consumer-facing websites (UVM, UNITEC in Mexico; UPC, UPN, Cibertec in Peru) but none expose machine-readable APIs documented from the parent.

providers.name: Lean Six Sigma
providers.description: Lean Six Sigma is a methodology that combines Lean manufacturing principles and Six Sigma quality management techniques to improve business processes by eliminating waste and reducing variation, focusing on data-driven decision making and continuous improvement.

providers.name: LocateAI
providers.description: LocateAI (Locate) is an AI-integrated commercial real estate brokerage focused on retail site selection for multi-unit and franchise brands. Its platform pairs proprietary AI models with full-service advisory to help brands choose markets, source and score sites, forecast Year-1 revenue and cannibalization risk, right-size franchise territories, and negotiate leases — from the first market through the signed lease. The models analyze 200M+ mobile devices and 1,100+ variables for device-level trade-area, fair-share, and time-weighted revenue analysis. Locate is delivered as a managed service; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company.

providers.name: LyGenesis
providers.description: LyGenesis is a Pittsburgh-based clinical-stage cell therapy company developing allogeneic regenerative therapies that use a patient's own lymph nodes as bioreactors to grow functioning ectopic organs. Its lead program transplants donor hepatocytes into upper-abdominal lymph nodes via endoscopic ultrasound to treat end-stage liver disease and is in a Phase 2a clinical trial; preclinical proof-of-concept programs target thymus (aging), kidney (end-stage renal disease) and pancreas (Type 1 diabetes). LyGenesis is a laboratory and clinical-research organization, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and this profile records that absence rather than any API surface.

providers.name: Nomagic
providers.description: Nomagic builds Physical AI for end-to-end warehouse automation, using AI-powered robotic arms and computer vision to automate picking, packing, sorting and other fulfillment tasks across e-commerce, fashion, pharmaceutical and third-party logistics warehouses. Nomagic exposes a standard Station API for systems integrators, WCS/WMS providers and customers to control its robots, and a Grip AI API that adds an intelligence layer to third-party robot hardware; all robot actions are recorded to the Nomagic Cloud to continually improve its models. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures. Public developer documentation for these APIs is not published; integration is arranged directly with Nomagic.

providers.name: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts (PAFA)
providers.description: The Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts (PAFA) is the United States' first museum and school of fine arts, founded in 1805 in Philadelphia by painter and scientist Charles Willson Peale, sculptor William Rush, and other artists and business leaders. PAFA operates as a 501(c)(3) cultural nonprofit at 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102 and occupies two connected historic buildings — the Frank Furness and George Hewitt-designed Furness-Hewitt Building (1876, designated a National Historic Landmark in 1975) and the Samuel M. V. Hamilton Building — joined by Lenfest Plaza. PAFA's permanent collection focuses on 19th- and 20th-century American art and includes works tied to alumni and faculty such as Mary Cassatt, Thomas Eakins, Henry Ossawa Tanner, William Glackens, Barkley L. Hendricks, Violet Oakley, Cecilia Beaux, Louis Kahn, David Lynch, and Njideka Akunyili Crosby, alongside the Linda Lee Alter Collection of Art by Women. Following a March 2025 announcement of a financial crisis driven by a reported roughly $3 million annual deficit and a sharp decline in enrollment, PAFA stopped granting its own BFA and MFA degrees beginning with the 2024-2025 academic year. As of 2026 the school's active educational pathways are the three-year Fine Arts Certificate Program ("designed to prepare students for entry-level professional roles within the visual arts and related creative industries"), Continuing Education classes ("an inclusive studio arts offering for artists of all ages and skill levels, from beginners to advanced creatives") delivered in-person and online, Youth & Teen programs including Summer Art Camp and Summer Academy, and PAFA Shop Memberships providing self-guided access to professional-grade printmaking, papermaking, and sculpture studios. The museum continues to operate, with admission $25 adults / $23 seniors / $10 students / $5 youth / free for children 12 and under and members, and is presenting the once-in-a-generation exhibition "A Nation of Artists" (April 2026 - September 2027) in partnership with the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Middleton Family Collection. PAFA is a cultural nonprofit, not a technology company. It publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI specifications, no SDKs, no public REST or GraphQL APIs, no webhooks, no status page, and no engineering blog. There is no `github.com/pafa` institutional organization — the user account `github.com/pafa` is an unrelated personal account focused on ERP and WeChat tooling. The institution's only programmatic third-party surface is its participation in the Bloomberg Connects free digital museum guide app, which presents PAFA's collection and tours through Bloomberg Philanthropies' shared mobile platform. Donations are routed through the third-party platform community.pafa.org/give and ticketing through standard museum e-commerce.

providers.name: Polycom
providers.description: Polycom, Inc. was a pioneer of unified communications and video conferencing, known for its RealPresence video collaboration platform, SoundStation conference phones, and Group Series and HDX room video endpoints. Polycom merged with Plantronics in 2018 to form Poly, which HP acquired in 2022; the polycom.com domain now redirects to HP's Poly product line. For developers, Polycom exposed the RealPresence Platform REST API (via the RealPresence Resource Manager and Distributed Media Application, later branded Clariti) along with device REST APIs on its VideoOS endpoints, enabling programmatic conference control, scheduling, provisioning, resource monitoring, and billing integration. Developer resources are now consolidated under HP's Poly developer portal.

providers.name: Praxis Labs
providers.description: Praxis Labs is an AI-powered leadership and human-skills learning platform, surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and acquired by Torch. Its flagship product, Pivotal Practice, uses immersive simulations, personalized AI coaching, and role-play scenarios to build critical management capabilities such as difficult conversations and performance discussions, with behavior-change tracking and ROI analytics. The learning application runs at practice.praxislabs.co behind login and integrates with HR/L&D systems including Workday, Docebo, and Degreed. Praxis Labs is SOC 2 Type 2 certified. No public API, developer portal, or SDK was found during enrichment; this remains a company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Rakuten Medical
providers.description: Rakuten Medical, Inc. is a global biotechnology company headquartered in San Diego, California, developing precision, cell-targeting investigational cancer therapies on its proprietary Alluminox platform — a drug-device combination pairing an IRDye 700DX light-activated dye conjugated to a cell-targeting antibody with local illumination by 690nm red light. Founded in 2010 as Aspyrian Therapeutics and renamed following investment from Rakuten Group, the company operates in the United States, Japan, Taiwan, Switzerland and India. Its lead asset ASP-1929, an EGFR-targeting antibody-dye conjugate, received marketing approval in Japan in 2021 as Akalux for unresectable locally advanced or recurrent head and neck cancer and is in global Phase 3 development alone and in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy; RM-1995 and RM-0256 follow in earlier-stage programs. As a clinical-stage therapeutics and drug-device company, Rakuten Medical publishes no public developer API, SDK, webhook, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures its corporate identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sentient
providers.description: Sentient (Sentient Labs / Sentient Foundation) is an open-source AI research lab and crypto protocol building Open, Monetizable, and Loyal (OML) artificial general intelligence. Its work spans agent frameworks (ROMA recursive meta-agent, Open Deep Search, EvoSkill agent-skill synthesis), the OML 1.0 model-fingerprinting system for verifiable model ownership and monetization, and the GRID protocol with Sentient Chat as a universal interface for discovering, composing, and coordinating AI artifacts. Backed by Pantera Capital, Sentient publishes peer-reviewed research (NeurIPS, ICML, COLM) and ships its tooling as open-source repositories on GitHub and models on Hugging Face rather than as a hosted commercial REST API.

providers.name: Skylo
providers.description: Skylo Technologies is a satellite communications company based in Mountain View, California, operating a global Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) that lets standard smartphones and IoT cellular devices connect directly to satellites over 3GPP Release 17 direct-to-device (D2D) standards for SMS, sensor telemetry, and other low-bandwidth messaging. Founded in 2017 and backed by DCM, SoftBank, Intel Capital, Innovation Endeavors, BMW i Ventures, Samsung Catalyst, Next47, Seraphim Space, and NGP Capital, Skylo has commercial service across the US, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, and Europe. Skylo does not publish a public REST/HTTP API; developer integration is device-level (certified modules such as Quectel, Murata, Blues Notecard and Particle) with detailed procedures gated behind a partner Knowledge Base. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company and its developer surface.

providers.name: Socialstyrelsen (National Board of Health and Welfare)
providers.description: Socialstyrelsen, the National Board of Health and Welfare of Sweden, is a governmental authority responsible for developing and supervising health and social care policies, regulations, and guidelines. It provides extensive public information, statistical data, and professional resources across areas such as child and youth health, cancer, mental health, elder care, and medical education. The agency also publishes standards, recommendations, and support tools for healthcare professionals and the public.

providers.name: Solv Health
providers.description: Solv Health operates a consumer marketplace (solvhealth.com and the Solv app) for booking same-day urgent care, primary care, and lab appointments, plus a provider-facing platform (scheduling, intake, patient acquisition, reputation management, messaging, payments) sold to clinics and health systems. There is no self-serve public developer API or published API reference on solvhealth.com; API access is gated behind a sales-led partnership. Solv states it exposes "interoperable APIs" that power custom booking experiences on partner websites and apps, a "Final Mile" API/network that lets digital-first and virtual-care partners (e.g. Included Health) hand patients off to real-time same-day appointment availability at Solv's national network of urgent care clinics, and bidirectional EHR interoperability (APIs, HL7, FHIR, and RPA) that syncs patient demographics, appointment status, and documents with systems like Epic, Athena, Cerner, Allscripts, DrChrono, eClinicalWorks, Experity, and NextGen. None of these capabilities have a published base URL, endpoint reference, or self-serve API key signup; access is provisioned per partner/clinic inside a commercial contract.

providers.name: Sona
providers.description: Sona is an AI-powered workforce management platform for large, multi-site organizations in hospitality, hotels, care, retail, and logistics. It unifies labor demand forecasting, autonomous staff scheduling, core HR (onboarding, absence, training), and payroll automation, with a Raffy AI assistant that guides manager decisions plus real-time analytics across locations. Sona ships 95+ pre-built integrations (ATS, POS, LMS, tipping, earned-wage-access, and care-planning systems) and advertises a private API for building bespoke integrations, though it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (Northzone, Polychain, Speedinvest) and enriched via the local pipeline.

providers.name: Syncloop
providers.description: Syncloop is an advanced API development and management platform that enables organizations to design, deploy, and manage APIs efficiently. The platform provides a low-code/no-code API builder with support for REST, SOAP, and third-party integrations, running on cloud or on-premise infrastructure. Syncloop offers built-in authentication, rate limiting, monitoring, analytics, and a developer portal for API discovery and documentation.

providers.name: TBO.com
providers.description: TBO.com is a leading global travel distribution platform that simplifies travel business operations for agents, enterprises, and travel providers. Offering a comprehensive suite of products including hotels, packages, transfers, rail, cargo, marine, and more, TBO.com provides robust APIs that enable partners to integrate travel services, manage bookings, and expand their offerings worldwide.

providers.name: Tengo
providers.description: Tengo is an AI-powered public procurement platform that helps companies find, evaluate, and respond to public tenders in one place. Founded in 2023 in France by Hugues Renou and Yoann Gauthier, Tengo covers the full tender lifecycle — sourcing and targeting relevant opportunities, drafting and writing proposals with AI, and managing responses and performance analytics — serving SMEs, mid-sized companies, and large corporations. Tengo raised a €3M round led by Point Nine in 2024. It operates a business-user SaaS with a request-a-demo onboarding and no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Time Warner
providers.description: Time Warner was a Fortune 500 American multinational mass media and entertainment conglomerate, one of the largest media companies in the world until its acquisition by AT&T in 2018. It operated major brands including HBO, CNN, Turner Broadcasting, Warner Bros., and DC Comics. After the AT&T acquisition it was rebranded as WarnerMedia. In 2022, WarnerMedia merged with Discovery Inc. to form Warner Bros. Discovery. Time Warner did not offer a public developer API platform.

providers.name: Ukio
providers.description: Ukio is a Barcelona-founded proptech company offering monthly furnished apartment rentals across Europe, with apartments in Barcelona, Madrid, Berlin, Lisbon, Milan, and Paris. It serves individuals relocating for work or lifestyle, provides corporate housing for companies, and partners with property owners through a real-estate property-management program. Backed by Partech. Ukio publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Verso Corporation
providers.description: Verso Corporation (NYSE: VRS) was a North American producer of coated papers including coated groundwood, coated freesheet, and specialty products used in magazines, catalogs, commercial print, books, and packaging. Headquartered in Miamisburg, Ohio, Verso operated mills in Wisconsin Rapids (Wisconsin), Escanaba (Michigan), Duluth (Minnesota), and historically Luke (Maryland). In March 2022, Swedish pulp and paper group BillerudKorsnäs (now Billerud) completed its acquisition of Verso for $825 million in cash, taking the company private and rebranding it as Billerud Americas Corporation. The Verso standalone brand, ticker, and corporate web presence have been retired; ongoing North American operations, paper grades, and customer relationships now sit inside Billerud's global business.

providers.name: Watershed
providers.description: Watershed is an enterprise sustainability platform used by large companies to measure their carbon footprint, report against regulatory and voluntary frameworks, and act on decarbonization opportunities. The platform combines a library of 500,000+ emissions factors, pre-verified methodologies, and AI agents for data cleaning, analysis, and report drafting. Watershed exposes an API for automated data ingestion and reporting, alongside guided uploads, and publishes integrations for common enterprise data sources. API keys are provisioned to customers via the Watershed dashboard at dashboard.watershedclimate.com. Public developer documentation is limited; most API access is delivered through customer onboarding and partner enablement.

providers.name: Wumbo
providers.description: Wumbo is a technology startup focused on delivering innovative data integration solutions for modern enterprises. Founded in 2023 and backed by Starting Line VC, the company builds a platform that simplifies the connection, transformation, and orchestration of APIs across diverse services. Wumbo aims to reduce integration complexity, accelerate time‑to‑market, and enable businesses to create flexible, scalable data pipelines without extensive custom code.

providers.name: 1ST Biotherapeutics
providers.description: 1ST Biotherapeutics (1STBIO) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Gyeonggi-do, South Korea. It discovers and develops novel small-molecule therapeutics for areas of significant unmet medical need, with programs spanning neurodegenerative disease, immuno-oncology, metabolic disease and rare/orphan disease, supported by a genomics-based target discovery capability and an R&D network of academic, hospital, CRO and investor partners. The company sells no software product and operates no developer program: its public web presence is an eight-page corporate and investor site with no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Academic Partnerships
providers.description: Academic Partnerships (rebranded as Risepoint in 2024) is an education technology and online program management (OPM) company that partners with more than 100 regional public universities to launch, market, and scale affordable, workforce-focused online degree programs. The company provides operational support services including digital marketing, student enrollment and retention coaching, faculty support, and technology implementation, while curriculum, instruction, and degree conferral remain under university control. Its programs concentrate in high-ROI fields such as nursing, teaching, business, and public service. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Aion Digital
providers.description: Aion Digital is a Bahrain-headquartered digital banking platform vendor, operated by Waqfe W.L.L and founded in 2017, that sells bank-in-a-box software to financial institutions across the GCC and Pakistan. Its product lines are eKYC and digital onboarding, retail digital banking, corporate digital banking, an AI layer (Aion Hikmah) and the Aion Rubix platform, whose marketed components include an API gateway, an API management and analytics platform, and modular middleware with pre-integrations. Aion Digital markets an API platform and, through a 2019 Open Bank Project partnership, an API catalogue and sandbox delivered to its bank customers, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract of its own: every developer-facing call to action on aiondigital.com and ekyc.aiondigital.com is "Request a demo". The one public first-party code it does ship is a small set of internal platform libraries on npm and an iOS analytics framework on GitHub.

providers.name: Angeleffect
providers.description: Angeleffect is an angel investing platform that connects entrepreneurs with value‑creating investors, partners, and mentors worldwide. The site describes a global network offering access to high‑impact startup opportunities, with features such as a portfolio of over 2,200 startups across 112 countries, mentorship, and a minimum ticket size of $5,000. It provides information on its AE Network, fund structure, FAQs, and contact options, positioning itself as a bridge between capital and innovative ventures.

providers.name: Api2Convert
providers.description: Online File Conversion API

providers.name: Aptabiotherapeutics
providers.description: Aptabi therapeutics is a biotechnology company focused on developing innovative antibody‑based therapeutics. The firm aims to address unmet medical needs by leveraging advanced protein engineering and platform technologies to create novel treatments for serious diseases. While detailed product pipelines are not publicly disclosed, the company positions itself within the emerging bio‑pharma sector, seeking collaborations and investment to advance its research programs.

providers.name: Arro
providers.description: Arro is a consumer fintech company that helps people build or rebuild credit without traditional barriers. Its flagship product is the Arro Card, a Mastercard with no deposit and no hard credit check that starts at up to $300 and grows to $2,500, issued by Community Federal Savings Bank (member FDIC). The Arro app pairs the card with financial-education lessons, credit tracking, personalized guidance, and Artie, an AI money coach. Arro is a mobile-first consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Arsagapartners
providers.description: Arsagapartners, operating as アルサーガパートナーズ株式会社, is a Japan‑based consulting and technology firm delivering end‑to‑end digital transformation (DX) solutions. It offers consulting, system development, AI services, and a suite of AI‑powered tools such as ARSAGA VIDEO CREATE and Chatty. The company combines a team of 100 consultants and 300 engineers to support clients across various industries, focusing on AI, web marketing, and custom software development.

providers.name: Atomo Coffee
providers.description: Atomo Coffee is a Seattle-based food-tech company that makes beanless "molecular" coffee: it reverse-engineers the coffee bean and reconstructs the taste, aroma, and caffeine of coffee from upcycled, naturally derived plant ingredients, producing cold brew, ground, and canned products with a lower carbon and water footprint than conventional bean-grown coffee. Backed by bessemer-venture-partners and other investors, it sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at atomocoffee.com. Atomo is a consumer packaged-goods brand and publishes no first-party developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record. Sector: deep-tech / food-tech.

providers.name: Autonomous Cyber
providers.description: Autonomous Cyber is the maker of FUZZ-E, an AI-powered platform for offensive cybersecurity marketed as "The AI Platform for Hacking." It equips commercial and government red teams with deep reconnaissance to uncover hard-to-find bugs and compromise networks, adaptive tooling that responds to AI-enabled defenses by building custom capabilities per engagement, and integrated intelligence workflows that consolidate data and toolkits inside the platform. The company states it operates strictly in the American national interest. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; no public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: Bayesian Health
providers.description: Bayesian Health is a real-time clinical intelligence company whose adaptive AI platform monitors hospitalized patients continuously inside the electronic health record, surfacing only the patients who need attention and giving clinicians evidence-based guidance to act. Its flagship Targeted Real-Time Early Warning System (TREWS) reads full patient charts — labs, vitals, and clinical notes — to detect sepsis and other deterioration hours earlier while cutting alert volume, and in May 2026 became the first-ever FDA-cleared continuous AI sepsis monitor. Founded by Johns Hopkins professor Suchi Saria, the company deploys through direct EHR partnerships with Epic and Cerner rather than a public developer API, and is backed by a16z.

providers.name: Bobyard
providers.description: Bobyard is an AI takeoff and estimating software company for the construction industry. Its platform reads construction drawings and blueprints to automatically extract quantities and organize takeoffs, cutting manual estimation work by 50-90% for trade contractors in landscaping, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and finishes. Trained on millions of drawings, Bobyard automates AI takeoff, manual takeoff, OC conversions, and estimate generation so contractors can increase bid capacity without expanding estimating staff. Bobyard was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes product documentation and a live status page (including an Inference API component) but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Bounce Imaging
providers.description: Bounce Imaging provides advanced imaging solutions for law enforcement, public safety, and defense sectors. Their product line includes rugged thermal cameras, K‑9 mounted systems, and remote sensing platforms designed for tactical operations, rescue missions, and border security. The company emphasizes real‑time video analytics, durability in harsh environments, and integration with command‑and‑control systems.

providers.name: Buildium
providers.description: Buildium, part of RealPage, is a cloud property-management platform aimed at small and mid-sized residential, association, and community-association property managers. The platform covers accounting, leasing, applicant and tenant management, rent collection, maintenance, communications, owner and resident portals, and association management. Buildium publishes a Public API used by certified partners and customers for property, lease, tenant, owner, vendor, rental application, financial, and webhook integration with the Buildium platform.

providers.name: Burger King
providers.description: Burger King is one of the world's largest fast-food hamburger chains operating over 18,000 locations in more than 100 countries. Known for the flame-grilled Whopper, Burger King is a subsidiary of Restaurant Brands International (RBI) and operates the BK mobile app, Royal Perks loyalty program, and delivery partnerships with DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub.

providers.name: Burlington Stores
providers.description: Burlington Stores, Inc. (NYSE: BURL) is a US national off-price department store retailer offering brand-name clothing, footwear, accessories, baby products and home decor at everyday low prices across more than 1,200 stores. Burlington operates no public developer program: no OpenAPI, GraphQL, gRPC, SOAP or event contract is served on any host it controls. Its one documented machine-to-machine surface is ASC X12 version 4010 EDI for merchandise vendors and freight carriers, and unusually for a retailer of this size the implementation guides are fully public — seventeen transaction-set PDFs plus a GS1-128 shipping label companion report, readable without a login at burlington.com/vendors/edi.
