Backed by DCVC, Sensemesh was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single marketing site (sensemesh.ai) with no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or well-known metadata.

providers.name: SevOne (Turbonomic)
providers.description: SevOne and Turbonomic are enterprise IT operations products now part of IBM's AIOps portfolio. IBM SevOne Network Performance Management (NPM) delivers real-time, multi-vendor network monitoring, flow analytics, and capacity planning across hybrid and enterprise networks. IBM Turbonomic is an application resource management (ARM) platform that continuously analyzes application demand and automates resourcing, scaling, and placement decisions across on-premises, cloud, and Kubernetes environments to assure performance while reducing cost. Both products expose REST APIs, but those APIs are hosted on the customer's own appliance / deployment rather than on a public developer portal, so there is no public base URL or published OpenAPI to catalog: the Turbonomic REST API is served from the appliance (for example the /vmturbo/rest path with its bundled Swagger UI), and SevOne exposes the SevOne NMS API and SevOne Data Insight API from the deployed instance. Product and API reference documentation is published by IBM.

providers.name: SilverRail
providers.description: SilverRail Technologies is a rail technology company that powers global rail ecommerce and distribution. Its platform spans journey planning, ticketing, and onboard information, aiming to transform the rail experience for travelers while making rail retail easier and more profitable for operators, travel agencies, and distributors. SilverRail connects rail carriers and sellers so rail inventory can be searched, booked, and ticketed across markets. The company was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel and Canaan Partners. As of this enrichment pass SilverRail runs a corporate marketing site (Next.js) but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery documents; its API and distribution capabilities appear to be delivered through partner/enterprise integration rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Sixfold
providers.description: Sixfold is a New York City-headquartered AI company building purpose-built artificial intelligence for insurance underwriting across Property & Casualty and Life & Health lines. Founded by Alex Schmelkin (CEO, previously co-founder of Unqork), Jane Tran (COO), and Brian Moseley (CTO, previously Head of Developer Experience at American Express), Sixfold processes unstructured submissions, automates risk research, produces appetite fit scores, generates cited case narratives, and applies underwriting guidelines consistently across submissions. The platform classifies risk using industry standards (SIC, NAICS, ISO), supports 40+ P&C and Life & Health business lines, and deploys either standalone or via a flexible API into existing underwriting workbench, CRM, and policy administration systems. Customers include Zurich North America, Guardian, Generali GC&C, Skyward Specialty, AXIS, and Mosaic Insurance, collectively representing roughly $265B in gross written premium. The company raised a $30M Series B in January 2026 and operates from offices in New York City and Lloyd's of London. Sixfold is the named provider behind these capabilities and is distinct from Cytora, a separate UK-based insurance AI provider. The platform is sold as enterprise SaaS to insurance carriers; there is no public self-serve developer portal, public API reference, SDKs, or open-source release — API integration is delivered under enterprise engagement.

providers.name: Stampli
providers.description: Stampli is an AI-driven accounts payable and procure-to-pay automation platform (invoice capture, coding, approvals, vendor management, payments, and corporate cards) that stays aligned to a company's ERP as the system of record. Stampli does NOT publish a public, self-serve developer API or developer portal. What Stampli markets as its "API" is a set of pre-built, in-house cloud-to-cloud ERP integrations (plus on-premises "Bridge" connectors and file-based sync) that Stampli operates on the customer's behalf to sync master data - invoices, vendors, purchase orders, GL accounts, locations/entities, and approvals - between Stampli and 70+ ERPs such as NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics, SAP, Oracle, and Acumatica. Access is gated behind a sales/onboarding relationship; there is no documented public REST/GraphQL/WebSocket surface, no self-service authentication, no OpenAPI reference, and no published developer documentation as of this catalog entry. Integrations are configured by Stampli during onboarding rather than by third-party developers against an open API.

providers.name: Swing Education
providers.description: Swing Education is a technology-driven substitute teacher staffing marketplace for K-12 schools and districts across the United States. Its vetted platform connects schools and districts with qualified, background-checked substitute teachers and classified staff to cover daily absences, long-term leaves, special education classrooms, and paraprofessional roles. Schools request coverage through an online admin console while substitutes browse and claim assignments through a dedicated app. The company reports a 94% fill rate, an average five-minute fill time, and coverage of more than 6,000 schools. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; the public site exposes no developer/API surface, so this record carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Telenor
providers.description: Telenor Group is a leading telecommunications operator headquartered in Norway, providing mobile, broadband, and TV services across Scandinavia, Eastern Europe, and Asia. The company focuses on digital transformation, connectivity, and sustainable business practices, serving millions of customers worldwide. It offers a range of consumer and enterprise solutions, including IoT platforms, cloud services, and digital payment options, reflecting its commitment to innovation and responsible growth.

providers.name: Thirdwave
providers.description: Thirdwave (Third Wave Automation) builds autonomous material-handling systems for warehouses and distribution centers, led by its shared-autonomy forklift platform where one human operator can supervise a fleet of self-driving forklifts that operate independently and hand control back to a person when needed. Its ArmadaFMS (Armada Fleet Management System) software coordinates the robotic fleet across facilities. The company is a venture-backed logistics-robotics provider (backed by Homebrew and Norwest Venture Partners). As of this enrichment pass Third Wave publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Tiyaro
providers.description: Tiyaro is an enterprise AI company whose product, DeepQuery, replicates complete business processes as AI agents that can be described in plain English. Rather than rules engines or brittle integration workflows, DeepQuery uses LLMs combined with enterprise-specific product and customer data to identify a solution strategy and execute it across multiple steps using built-in tools. Its flagship application targets customer support and IT service desks - an "IT SuperAgent" trained on hundreds of third-party product procedures that recommends and executes resolution steps for incoming tickets - alongside revenue-operations and sales/marketing automation use cases. The company was founded by a team that previously built an edge software stack for hosting AI applications, and is backed by General Catalyst. Tiyaro goes to market as an enterprise product engaged through a book-a-demo motion rather than a self-serve developer API.

providers.name: TokyoOtakuMode
providers.description: Tokyo Otaku Mode (TOM) is a Japan-based e-commerce company and online destination for fans of Japanese pop culture, selling official anime figures, manga merchandise, apparel, and collectibles worldwide through its otakumode.com shop. Grown out of a large social-media following, TOM curates and ships Japanese otaku goods internationally. It runs a private, API-key-gated backend (api.otakumode.com) that powers its storefront, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications, or first-party client SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from live public probes.

providers.name: turntable
providers.description: turntable (Turntable Labs) is a consumer social-music company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and union-square-ventures. The original Turntable.fm social listening service shut down in 2013 and its domain no longer resolves. The lineage lives on at Turntable Labs, which operates two consumer music products - Hangout (a social music-streaming and group-chat app at hangout.fm / hang.fm) and Turntable (a create-share-and-vibe GenAI music experience). No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation are published for any of these products - this is a consumer application, not an API provider. Enrichment probes (DNS, HTTP, site fetch) confirmed no developer surface as of 2026-07-21.

providers.name: Ulta Salon, Cosmetics & Fragrance
providers.description: Ulta Salon, Cosmetics & Fragrance (now operating as Ulta Beauty) is the largest beauty retailer in the United States, offering cosmetics, fragrance, skin care products, hair care products, and salon services through retail stores and online. This entry tracks the legacy brand identity prior to the Ulta Beauty rebranding. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Vixtra
providers.description: Vixtra (VIXTRA Tecnologia e Serviços Financeiros LTDA., CNPJ 43.443.444/0001-04) is a Brazilian trade-finance fintech founded in July 2021 and headquartered in São Paulo, positioning itself as "the Trade Banking of the Brazilian importer." It pioneers financing for importers using in-transit maritime cargo as collateral, and delivers credit, foreign exchange, guarantees, and cash-flow management for foreign trade from a single digital platform. Its products include Crédito Flex (revolving working-capital credit), Crédito Pré (pre-shipment import financing), Câmbio Fácil (100% digital commercial FX), Trade Banking (the unified operations platform), and a Vixtra stablecoin for cross-border payments. Vixtra operates as a banking correspondent of BMP Money Plus SCD and an FX correspondent of Ebury Banco de Câmbio, has raised roughly US$36M (US$30M debt + US$6M seed extension) led by QED Investors with Valor Capital Group, Endeavor Promessas, NXTP Ventures, Actyus, and BluStone, and processes data in compliance with Brazil's LGPD. No public developer portal or API is currently published; the api.vixtra.com host backs the customer application and returns 403 to anonymous callers.

providers.name: W. W. Grainger
providers.description: W. W. Grainger, Inc. (NYSE: GWW) is a Fortune 500 broad-line distributor of maintenance, repair and operating (MRO) products serving businesses and institutions across North America, Japan and the United Kingdom through roughly 331 branches, 34 distribution centers and its digital channels. Its system-to-system commerce runs through eProcurement rather than a public developer program: PunchOut catalogs into Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer, SAP, Oracle and GHX, ANSI ASC X12 4010 EDI for purchase orders, acknowledgments, ship notices and invoices, and the KeepStock inventory-management program. Grainger operates an API gateway at api.grainger.com, but its Swagger surface answers anonymous callers with an ACCESS DENIED page requiring the Grainger corporate network, and integration credentials are issued only by a Grainger account representative, so no public API contract or reference is available to evaluate.

providers.name: Westar Energy
providers.description: Westar Energy was the largest electric utility in Kansas, providing electric service to homes, businesses, and industries throughout Kansas before merging with Great Plains Energy in 2018 to form Evergy, Inc. As Evergy, the company continues to serve approximately 1.6 million customers in Kansas and Missouri with a focus on grid modernization, smart metering (AMI) through its Gridstream Connect IoT platform, and clean energy transformation including wind power and demand response programs.

providers.name: Woowa Brothers
providers.description: Woowa Brothers is the Seoul-based technology company behind Baedal Minjok (Baemin), South Korea's leading food delivery platform, alongside B-Mart quick commerce, Baemin Connect rider services, and robotics initiatives for serving and delivery robots. A subsidiary of Delivery Hero since 2021, the company runs a strong engineering culture through its Woowahan tech blog and first-party open-source libraries on GitHub (NestJS libraries, WoowahanJS, Redis tooling), but it does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Zapia
providers.description: Zapia is a personal AI assistant built for Latin America by BrainLogic AI (a Uruguay/Silicon Valley startup), delivered inside WhatsApp and as native Android and iOS apps plus a Flutter web app at app.zapia.com. It engages consumers in hyper-localized, natural-language conversations to compare prices, reply to and transcribe WhatsApp messages and voice notes, organize calendars (with Google Calendar sync), make reservations, and discover nearby businesses using BrainLogic's database of millions of Latin American business WhatsApp numbers. Zapia runs on Claude via Google Cloud Vertex AI and has surpassed 5.5 million users across the region, backed by seed funding led by Prosus Ventures. It is a consumer (B2C) product: as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal — this profile captures its public identity and consumer-facing surfaces.

providers.name: 3721zh.com
providers.description: 3721zh.com is the public domain of 转换商城 (Zhuanhuan Mall / "Conversion Mall"), the local-life private-domain e-commerce platform operated by 转换空间（上海）电子商务有限公司 (Zhuanhuan Space (Shanghai) E-Commerce Co., Ltd.), founded in 2018 and headquartered in Shanghai, China. It bundles a free-to-merchant SaaS with a branded-goods supply chain, fulfilment, and private-domain traffic build-out and agency operation, so catering, property-management, beauty, hotel, foot-bath, tea-house, education and retail-chain merchants can turn in-store spend into equivalent-value goods, vouchers, coupons and memberships. Company materials list WeCom, WeCom communities, WeChat mini programs, API interfaces and private deployment as the delivery modes of that service system. As of the 2026-09-05 probe the company publishes no developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract; integration is arranged through its onboarding forms and a sales conversation.

providers.name: ACTIVON Co., Ltd.
providers.description: ACTIVON Co., Ltd. (엑티브온) is a South Korean green-biotechnology materials company founded in 2009 and headquartered in Suwon, Gyeonggi-do, that develops and manufactures cosmetic ingredients and micro-encapsulation technology — skin-safe preservative alternatives, multifunctional actives, emollients, humectants and bio-converted ingredients — alongside functional pigment lines (EnergiON heat-storage, Thermon thermochromic, Photon, Fragron, Memorion, MultiON) sold into textiles, coatings, plastics and cosmetics. It is a specialty-materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract. Its only machine-readable agent surface is the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint and llms.txt served on its corporate site, both probed live by API Evangelist.

providers.name: Adarga
providers.description: Adarga is a British artificial-intelligence software company, founded in London in 2016 by Rob Bassett Cross, that builds information-intelligence and decision-advantage software for Defence, National Security and Resilience customers. Its products include Adarga Vantage, an AI analysis platform that extracts, contextualises and connects information from millions of internal and external sources in more than 75 languages; Adarga Augur, an alerting and intelligence tool; and Catalyst, a multidomain data-fusion and developer platform that the company markets as a Sovereign AI Stack. Adarga sells to the UK Ministry of Defence and Strategic Command and to US federal customers, and partners with Oracle to run Vantage on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Adarga publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its product documentation sits behind a customer support portal.

providers.name: Agrapp
providers.description: Agrapp is a Chilean agricultural technology (AgTech) company offering "el cuaderno de campo inteligente" (the intelligent field notebook) — a mobile and web SaaS platform that helps small and medium farmers record, track, and manage their field operations without complex spreadsheets. Founded in 2016 in Santiago and backed by 500 Global, Start-Up Chile, OpenBeauchef, and ChileGlobal Ventures, the platform provides labor and task tracking with per-task cost analysis, inventory and supply (bodega) control, a work calendar, worker attendance and performance monitoring, WhatsApp and email alerts, and agricultural plus financial reporting to support data-driven decisions. It runs on iOS and Android with an offline mode that syncs when connectivity returns. Agrapp does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public web surface, commercial links, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Airbase
providers.description: Airbase is a modern spend management platform for finance teams that combines accounts-payable (AP) automation and bill pay, guided procurement and purchase orders, corporate cards, and expense reimbursements on a single system with real-time general-ledger sync. Airbase Inc. was acquired by Paylocity in a ~$325M deal announced September 4, 2024 and completed October 1, 2024, and now operates as "Airbase by Paylocity," extending Paylocity's HCM suite into the office of the CFO. Airbase exposes a developer platform at developer.airbase.io (REST API reference, OpenAPI/Swagger, Postman and Insomnia collections, a webhooks management API, an OAuth playground, and a sandbox) used to build custom connections for systems not covered by the pre-built integrations. API access is account-gated - credentials are generated inside the customer's Airbase/Paylocity tenant rather than through open self-serve signup - so the logical APIs below are honestly modeled from the documented product surface and developer portal, and the exact endpoint paths and base URL are not publicly reproduced here (endpointsModeled).

providers.name: Alicecom
providers.description: Alicecom is a stub entry in the API Evangelist catalog, representing a company identified from secondary-market sources. The entry is intended for full profiling through the enrichment pipeline, which will gather detailed information about its APIs, documentation, and operational characteristics. This placeholder description will be expanded as real data is collected and verified.

providers.name: Alltrna
providers.description: Alltrna develops engineered transfer RNA (tRNA) medicines that correct premature termination (stop) codons and restore full‑length protein production. The company applies its tRNA platform to create universal genetic medicines for thousands of diseases caused by shared genetic mutations, focusing on rare and genetic disorders. It targets patients with nonsense mutations and other genetic diseases requiring protein restoration.

providers.name: Alpharank
providers.description: Alpharank is a no-code sales guidance and digital-origination analytics platform for banks and credit unions. It analyzes funded loan and deposit applications to reveal which marketing tactics, channels, and campaigns actually drive funded dollars, then guides institutions to optimize their online branch, curb funnel abandonment, and turn ad spend into higher-quality leads. Its products include Optimizer, AdSync, and CRMSync, and it serves roughly 200 financial institutions nationwide. Originally recognized for turning payment transaction data into customer influence graphs, Alpharank is a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Alpharank publishes a marketing and client-login presence but no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Ampleforth
providers.description: Ampleforth is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol behind AMPL, a price-stable but supply-elastic cryptocurrency that targets the CPI-adjusted 2019 US dollar by algorithmically adjusting token supply (rebasing) across all holders rather than moving price. The ecosystem spans the AMPL rebasing token, Wrapped AMPL (WAMPL), the FORTH governance token and DAO, and the SPOT inflation-resistant store-of-value protocol built on tranched AMPL collateral. Ampleforth is open-source (smart contracts under the fragmentsorg GitHub organization, working name uFragments), audited, and deployed on Ethereum with cross-chain support. Surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and enriched in the API Evangelist network from its public docs, GitHub org, blog, and community channels; it publishes protocol documentation and an llms.txt but no REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Arcol
providers.description: Arcol is a browser-based, real-time collaborative building design and documentation platform for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, often described as a "Figma for BIM." Founded in 2021 by Paul O'Carroll and based in New York City, Arcol keeps massing, floorplans, metrics, estimating, and construction documentation connected in a single cloud-native workspace so early design decisions stay constructible. It supports multiplayer editing (built on Liveblocks), IFC and Excel import/export, a Rhino integration, and AI-assisted modeling. Arcol is backed by Cowboy Ventures and Craft Ventures. A public plugin API and developer SDK are described on the roadmap but are not yet published, so this profile currently exposes no programmatic API surface.

providers.name: Aspyriantherapeutics
providers.description: Aspyriantherapeutics, now operating as Rakuten Medical, is a privately funded clinical‑stage biotechnology company based in San Diego, United States. Founded in 2010, it develops precision, cell‑targeting photoimmunotherapy based on its proprietary Alluminox® platform to treat solid tumours, particularly head and neck cancers. The company has raised significant funding and is advancing its pipeline through clinical trials and expanded access programs.

providers.name: Autositu
providers.description: Autositu (AutoSitu) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) PropTech startup building an AI-native intelligence layer for real estate development plan review. Its multi-agent platform automatically analyzes site plans, building plans, and AEC drawings against municipal zoning and building codes to flag compliance issues before submission, cutting city comments and resubmittals so approvals move faster. The product serves cities, architecture and engineering firms, and real estate developers with human-in-the-loop review workflows. Autositu is an early-stage SaaS company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Avantifinance
providers.description: Avantifinance is a financial technology company that aims to provide innovative lending solutions for underserved markets. The company focuses on leveraging data-driven underwriting and digital platforms to streamline loan applications, approvals, and servicing. As a relatively new entrant, Avantifinance is building its API ecosystem to enable partners and developers to integrate financing options into their services, though public API documentation is not yet available. The firm targets small and medium enterprises in emerging economies, offering flexible credit terms and real-time decisioning powered by machine learning models. Its platform includes APIs for loan origination, repayment tracking, and compliance reporting, positioning Avantifinance as a modern fintech bridge between lenders and borrowers.

providers.name: Avenue3
providers.description: Avenue3 Limited is a UK open data and openEHR technology consultancy headquartered at Platform, New Station Street, Leeds. Founded in November 2020 (Companies House 13040131), the firm positions itself as a trusted public sector partner delivering strategy, discovery, architecture and full-stack engineering services that separate clinical data from the applications that write it. Its practice is built around openEHR — the vendor-neutral health record standard used by NHS organisations across England, Scotland and Wales and by national programmes in Norway, Germany, Slovenia and Australia — and it is a listed openEHR Industry Partner. Avenue3 sells consulting engagements rather than a software product: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable contract of its own, and the APIs it builds are operated by its clients. Its only public technical surface is the Avenue3-dev GitHub organisation, which ships a small set of general-purpose open-source developer libraries to npm and NuGet. Avenue3 is also listed on the UK Digital Marketplace as a G-Cloud 14 supplier.

providers.name: Avidbots
providers.description: Avidbots is a robotics company that designs and manufactures fully autonomous commercial floor-cleaning robots, including the Neo, Neo 2W, and Kas scrubbers, powered by its proprietary Avidbots Autonomy AI, lidar, and 3D sensing for real-time mapping, dynamic route planning, and intervention-free cleaning. Its robots serve airports, warehouses, retail, manufacturing, education, and healthcare facilities, and are managed through the web-based Avidbots Command Center. Avidbots was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Babbel
providers.description: Babbel is a Berlin, Germany-based language learning company founded in 2007 by Thomas Holl, Markus Witte, Lorenz Heine, and Toine Diepstraten. It operates one of the world's first online language-learning platforms, offering structured, conversation-focused courses in 14 languages including Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Polish, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Dutch, Turkish, Indonesian, and English. The Babbel product suite includes the core subscription Babbel App with interactive bite-sized lessons, speech recognition, and AI conversation partners; Babbel Live for online classes with certified teachers; Babbel for Business for enterprise language training; Babbel Podcasts and Babbel Magazine for supplemental content; and Babbel Videos on YouTube. The company has sold over 25 million subscriptions and reports that 92% of users improved their proficiency in two months, with effectiveness studies conducted by Michigan State University, Yale University, and CUNY. Babbel maintains an additional office in New York City and is privately held. Babbel's revenue model is direct-to-consumer subscriptions (monthly, annual, lifetime tiers) plus enterprise B2B licensing through Babbel for Business; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source learner content. The Babbel GitHub organization publishes internal infrastructure tooling (Terraform AWS modules, Puma plugins, OkHttp AWS signing, GitHub Actions) but no consumer-facing API.

providers.name: Blueprint Title
providers.description: Blueprint Title operates as a platform within the Nasdaq Private Market ecosystem, offering liquidity solutions, investment opportunities, and data intelligence for private companies and accredited investors. It facilitates buying and selling of pre-IPO stock, structured tender offers, and provides patented settlement technology, while also delivering market analytics and capital solutions to support growth and liquidity for private firms.

providers.name: Bold Metrics
providers.description: Bold Metrics is an AI body data platform for the apparel and fashion industry that uses digital-twin technology to power apparel fit and sizing. From just 4-6 simple body-data inputs it predicts 50+ individual body measurements with tailor-level accuracy, without photos, scanning, or measuring tapes. Its products - Smart Size Chart, Virtual Sizer, Virtual Tailor, Apparel Insights, and the Agentic Sizing Protocol - help brands reduce returns, lift conversion, and increase average order value with personalized size recommendations. The Agentic Sizing Protocol exposes this capability to AI shopping agents while keeping retailer API credentials off the agent and out of any LLM. Bold Metrics has processed 250M+ digital twins and 12B+ body-data points. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Techstars. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Bold Metrics publishes no public API documentation - integration is gated behind a demo/partner engagement.

providers.name: Borderxlab
providers.description: Borderxlab is a Silicon Valley‑based AI‑driven cross‑border e‑commerce platform. Founded in 2014 by three former Google PhDs, it offers products such as CloudStore AI, BeyondStyle, and BieYang app to enable brands and merchants to sell globally. The company reports over 5 million successful orders, 20 million SKUs and $1 billion GMV, positioning itself as a leader in agentic commerce.

providers.name: Bostonbiomotion
providers.description: Bostonbiomotion, now operating under the brand Proteus, provides advanced biomechanical measurement solutions for strength and power assessment. Their platform combines hardware sensors with cloud analytics to deliver real‑time performance insights for athletes, clinicians, and fitness facilities. The company focuses on sports performance, physical therapy, and training environments, offering products that capture motion data and translate it into actionable metrics for improving training outcomes.

providers.name: Branchtechnology
providers.description: Branchtechnology is a 3D printing construction technology company founded in 2014, specializing in freeform large‑scale additive manufacturing for building facades and off‑world structures. It combines industrial robotics, digital design, and patented processes to create sustainable, efficient construction solutions, offering products, approach, portfolio, and services for architects, developers, and space‑industry partners.

providers.name: Brightwheel
providers.description: Brightwheel (mybrightwheel.com) is an all-in-one childcare and early education management platform used by childcare centers, preschools, and early-learning programs to run daily operations - attendance and check-in, digital daily sheets, tuition billing and payments, enrollment and admissions, staff/timecards, classroom (room) management, learning assessments, and real-time parent messaging and photo/video sharing. As of this catalog entry, Brightwheel does NOT publish a documented, self-serve public or partner developer API. There is no developer portal, API reference, API key signup, OpenAPI specification, or webhook documentation. The only Brightwheel API activity that is publicly acknowledged is bespoke, contract-scoped work built for individual government partners - for example a private API implemented to submit attendance and subsidy data to Iowa's childcare subsidy data system - and inbound integrations where Brightwheel pushes data into third-party products (e.g. staff timecards to Gusto for payroll). None of these expose a documented API surface that outside developers can build against. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the provider and its access model; no API definitions are asserted because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Cambrian Bio
providers.description: Cambrian Bio (Cambrian BioPharma, Inc.) is a New York-headquartered clinical-stage drug development company working on the biology of aging. It runs a distributed "PipeCo" model — sourcing promising academic and early-stage science, then capitalizing and staffing each program as a separate subsidiary company under a shared development engine — to advance therapeutics that target the metabolic pathways that decline with age, first as treatments for chronic metabolic disease and ultimately as preventive medicines that extend healthspan. Its lead program, ATX-304, is an AMPK network activator with reported positive human translational data. Cambrian Bio is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate website, a science and pipeline overview, news and publications, and a blog, but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Code Metal
providers.description: Code Metal is a Boston-based AI company building a verifiable code translation and optimization platform for mission-critical, edge, and regulated industries including defense, automotive, semiconductor, robotics, and aerospace. The platform ingests high-level research and prototype code (Python, MATLAB, Julia) and produces optimized, edge-ready low-level code across C/C++, Rust, VHDL, Verilog, CUDA, HIP, and ONNX, using a divide-and-conquer pipeline that instruments and tests, translates and verifies functional equivalence, then optimizes and benchmarks against target CPU/GPU/FPGA runtimes. Code Metal was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or specification surface; this profile carries verified company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Colubrismx
providers.description: Colubrismx is a stub entry originating from the API Evangelist secondary‑market harvest. The company currently lacks a publicly verified corporate website, and no official API documentation or developer portal has been identified. This placeholder record will be enriched as further information becomes available, including a proper description, branding image, and link‑property pointers when they can be verified.

providers.name: Concert Health
providers.description: Concert Health is a behavioral health medical group that partners with medical groups, health systems, and health plans to integrate collaborative care into primary care. They provide a turnkey solution that improves patient outcomes, with over 70,000 lives cared for nationwide. The company offers resources, research, pathways, and a blog to support partners and patients.

providers.name: Corvus Insurance
providers.description: Corvus Insurance — now operating as Corvus by Travelers — is a cyber-insurance managing general agency and insurtech company that pairs property and casualty underwriting with security-focused data science. It offers Smart Cyber Insurance and Smart Tech Errors & Omissions coverage, a Cyber Risk Dashboard that continuously scans policyholders' external attack surface for vulnerabilities and delivers threat intelligence and remediation guidance, 24/7 incident response and claims support, and broker tooling for collaborative quoting and renewal management. Founded in 2017 and backed by Insight Partners and Obvious Ventures, Corvus was acquired by Travelers in 2024 and now operates as a Travelers company. The public site exposes marketing, broker resources, and a broker portal, but no public developer API program.

providers.name: Divebell
providers.description: Divebell is a cloud-native data privacy and security compliance platform that helps organizations discover, classify, and protect sensitive data and personally identifiable information (PII) across their data sources. The platform pairs continuous, intelligent data scanning with "Deep Automation" to deliver four capability areas: Data Discovery (data classification, data mapping, and access management), Compliance Automation (risk assessment, data retention, and regulatory compliance), DSR Fulfillment (data subject request workflows, subject mapping, and automated retrieval), and Risk Protection (a policy engine, "Risk Sonar," and remediation actions). Delivered as a lightweight modern SaaS with private data processing, Divebell protects customer data across sources such as Snowflake and AWS. Divebell was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and is now part of the Exterro family, operating as Exterro Data Discovery.

providers.name: Donkey
providers.description: Donkey is an AI-native trading company (Y Combinator, Summer 2026) that buys directly from Chinese factories and sells delivered duty-paid to US importers. Donkey mines public US customs records to identify the factory that actually makes a product, returns a landed DDP quote within 72 hours, runs its own on-the-floor quality inspections before the factory is paid, clears customs, moves the money, and offers credit-insured net-45 terms to qualified buyers. Founded by Benjamin Martindale (CEO) and Minghao Tan (CTO), the company runs small teams in San Francisco and China. Donkey publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform today; this profile tracks its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Effectiv
providers.description: Effectiv is a real-time fraud and risk decisioning platform for banks and fintechs, founded in 2021 and acquired by Socure in 2024 for approximately $136M. Its AI-driven decisioning engine and orchestration layer let risk teams automate decisions across the customer lifecycle, integrating 50+ third-party data and solution providers behind one developer-friendly API. The platform spans identity verification (KYC and Know-Your-Business KYB), payment and identity fraud controls across card, ACH, wire, check, and real-time payment rails, AML transaction monitoring, and credit underwriting, backed by a unified case-management workspace and client-side Device Intelligence SDKs for iOS and React Native.

providers.name: Eikon
providers.description: Eikon Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company that integrates Nobel Prize-winning super-resolution single-molecule tracking (SMT) microscopy, advanced engineering, automation, and high-performance computing to visualize and measure the real-time movement of individual proteins in living cells. This proprietary live-cell imaging platform screens protein-ligand interactions across millions of cells per day, generating large, high-dimensional datasets that power the discovery and development of novel small-molecule medicines. Eikon advances a clinical- and preclinical-stage oncology and immunology pipeline, including EIK1001 (a TLR7/8 agonist) and IMP1734 (a selective PARP1 inhibitor). Backed by General Catalyst, the company is headquartered in Millbrae, California with offices in New York and Jersey City.

providers.name: Enko Chem
providers.description: Enko Chem, Inc. (Enko) is an agricultural life sciences company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Mystic, Connecticut, where it operates an 89,000 sq ft research lab and greenhouse campus. Enko discovers and develops next-generation crop protection chemistry — weed, disease, insect and soil-pest control — using its proprietary ENKOMPASS platform, which combines DNA-encoded library screening, structure-based design, artificial intelligence and machine learning to identify new modes of action and lead molecules faster and at lower cost than conventional agrochemical R&D. Enko works through partnerships with Syngenta, Bayer, Nufarm and the Gates Foundation Strategic Investment Fund rather than selling software, and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Equinox Holdings
providers.description: Equinox Holdings is a privately held luxury lifestyle and fitness company majority-owned by Related Companies. Its portfolio spans high-end fitness clubs (Equinox), boutique indoor cycling (SoulCycle), yoga (Pure Yoga), value-tier gyms (Blink Fitness), luxury hospitality (Equinox Hotels), and a consumer streaming fitness app (Equinox+). The group operates more than 300 club facilities across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom and is positioned around the tagline "It's not fitness. It's life." Equinox Holdings does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a GitHub organization; all consumer experiences are delivered through its native iOS/Android apps and websites, with no documented partner or open API surface.

providers.name: Eyva
providers.description: Eyva (operated by datazeit GmbH of Cologne, Germany) is an AI-powered portfolio-intelligence platform for the beauty and personal-care industry. It unifies consumer, market, and product data so product, marketing, and R&D teams can detect emerging consumer trends across Google search, TikTok, Instagram, and product reviews, benchmark their portfolio, run gap and competitive analysis, track ingredients and claims, and develop AI-assisted product concepts. The platform bundles an AI research assistant, automated AI reporting, and data-backed product recommendations, and is used by 700+ teams at brands including Beiersdorf, Nivea, dm, BASF, Babor, and Lavera. Eyva is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. It is a B2B SaaS delivered through a demo-led sales motion and an authenticated web application; no public developer API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Fidelity Investments
providers.description: One of the largest financial services companies in the world providing investment management, retirement planning, brokerage, and wealth management services. Manages trillions of dollars in assets and serves tens of millions of individual investors and institutions. Fidelity does not run a public developer portal; partner integrations are delivered through curated marketplace relationships and through Fidelity Institutional / Wealthscape for advisors.

providers.name: Finaccess
providers.description: Finaccess Mexico, S.A. de C.V., Sociedad Operadora de Fondos de Inversion, is an independent Mexican investment-fund operator (asset manager) authorized by the CNBV and the SHCP and regulated by Banco de Mexico. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Mexico City, it is part of Grupo Finaccess and operates under the tagline "Acceso financiero para todos" (financial access for everyone). Finaccess manages the AXES family of mutual funds spanning short/medium/long-term local debt (AXES CP, MP, LP), domestic and international equity (AXES BMV, GLO, GSP, USA), dollar-denominated debt (AXES COB), and ESG equity (AXES ESG), and it distributes third-party funds from Franklin Templeton, Santander, and Scotiabank. It provides model portfolios, published rate-of-return tracking, and Morningstar-rated fund evaluation for retail and institutional clients. Finaccess publishes no public developer API; this profile carries company identity and domain-security enrichment only.

providers.name: Formation Bio
providers.description: Formation Bio (formerly TrialSpark, founded 2016 in New York City) is a tech-driven, AI-native pharmaceutical company that aims to bring new treatments to patients faster and more efficiently. Rather than discovering drugs, Formation Bio in-licenses and acquires clinical-stage drug assets from pharma companies, universities, and biotech firms, then develops them using proprietary technology platforms, process automation, and large language models applied across the drug development lifecycle — patient recruitment, e-consent, data management, monitoring, and biostatistics. The company rebranded from TrialSpark to Formation Bio in 2023 as it moved from a pure clinical-trial software platform to combined platform-plus-asset ownership. It raised a $372M Series D in 2024 and announced a first-in-class AI collaboration with Sanofi and OpenAI. Formation Bio operates hybrid teams across New York City, Boston, the San Francisco Bay Area, and North Carolina's Research Triangle. It is a private company with no public developer API program; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Forward Platform
providers.description: FORWARD Platform is a govtech SaaS company (a Techstars portfolio company) offering one secure platform for administering public-benefit programs. It serves governments, nonprofits, and foundations with tooling for program management, online form building, eligibility determination, case management, client communication, referrals, payment disbursement, reporting and analytics, and fraud prevention. FORWARD supports service-delivery programs such as guaranteed basic income, housing assistance, and emergency management, and is packaged in Direct, Pro, Enterprise, and Ally tiers. Enrichment found no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer portal — this is a product/marketing web presence only.

providers.name: Gangkhar
providers.description: Gangkhar is an AI-native embedded protection infrastructure platform that lets digital platforms, insurers, MGAs, and brokers configure, launch, and continuously optimize embedded insurance products globally through a single infrastructure layer and API. Its Sherpa+ engine provides full-stack embedded protection rails covering onboarding, pricing, underwriting, and claims across multiple carriers and markets, while Sherpa+Lens applies real-time AI optimization to pricing, messaging, and product versions. The platform enables sectors like mobility, delivery, fintech, e-commerce, travel, health, and vertical SaaS to embed compliant protection directly into their customer experiences without becoming insurers themselves. Founded in 2025 and led by former Chubb executive Federico Spagnoli, Gangkhar closed a $4.25M seed round in March 2026 led by Anthemis. Surfaced as an Anthemis portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gerrit Code Review
providers.description: Gerrit Code Review is an open‑source, web‑based code review system built for Git repositories. It enables teams to collaborate on patch‑set based reviews with fine‑grained permissions, extensive plugin architecture, and REST API integration. The platform scales to thousands of developers, supports enterprise‑grade security, and offers extensive documentation, roadmaps, and community resources.

providers.name: Glint
providers.description: Glint is an employee-engagement and organizational-health platform built on people-science pulse surveys, manager dashboards, and action-planning analytics. Founded in 2013 and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Shasta Ventures, Glint was acquired by LinkedIn in 2018 and subsequently folded into Microsoft, where it now ships as Microsoft Viva Glint within the Microsoft Viva employee-experience suite. The original glintinc.com domain now redirects to Microsoft, and the product is administered through the Microsoft 365 tenant and Microsoft Entra ID rather than a standalone public developer API; Glint does not publish an independent OpenAPI, REST API reference, or developer portal.

providers.name: Gravel AI
providers.description: Gravel AI is a beauty and personal care market intelligence platform that turns alternative data into early trend, ingredient, brand, and product signals for the global cosmetics industry. It offers a suite of analysis tools — application and ingredient trends, brand and market deep dives, consumer review analysis, new brand and product launch monitoring, ingredient supplier and OEM mapping, and product analyzers — alongside curated datasets, market reports, and an enterprise data/API service that delivers licensed beauty data into customer pipelines (API, Snowflake, S3). Backed by Techstars, Gravel AI serves beauty brands, ingredient and contract manufacturers, and enterprise insights, R&D, procurement, and data teams. Its flagship Gravel Early Trends product positions against incumbents such as Euromonitor, Mintel, NielsenIQ, Circana, WGSN, and Spate.

providers.name: Grubmarket
providers.description: GrubMarket is a food technology company founded in 2014 that digitally transforms the American food supply chain across the U.S. and Canada. It operates a B2B wholesale eCommerce marketplace connecting buyers to thousands of food products, an AI-powered ERP and warehouse-management software suite (WholesaleWare) for food distributors and growers, and a direct-to-consumer farm-fresh food delivery service. Backed by Battery Ventures, GGV Capital, and Y Combinator, GrubMarket was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass GrubMarket publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security posture.

providers.name: iControl
providers.description: iControl is a Swedish construction-technology company whose mobile application digitalizes documentation on construction sites, replacing paper-based protocols and inspection records with real-time digital capture. Field personnel create, share, and manage project documentation from the job site, with offline capture that syncs when connectivity returns, drawing and blueprint uploads, and team collaboration. Marketed under the promise "Skriv aldrig ett protokoll igen" (never write a protocol again), iControl is used by leading Nordic contractors including NCC, JM, Veidekke, ARCONA, and In3prenor across infrastructure, residential, commercial, and public-facility projects. The company is headquartered in Stockholm and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. iControl exposes a consumer-facing web and mobile application; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK was found during enrichment.

providers.name: IntelliMatch
providers.description: IntelliMatch is a transaction and account reconciliation platform originally developed by SunGard, now offered by FIS, and since renamed FIS Data Integrity Manager. It performs account-level balance and transaction proofing at high volume and drives review, approval, exception management and escalation through an integrated workflow engine, so financial institutions and corporates can reconcile cash, securities and intercompany activity and track data integrity centrally. The product is SWIFT-accredited, embeds machine learning through an AI Virtual Reconciler, and is sold either customer-hosted or as the FIS Optimized Reconciliation Service (formerly Managed Reconciliation Service). FIS publishes no developer program, documentation, OpenAPI or any other machine-readable contract for it; integration is arranged commercially. FIS's public API marketplace, Code Connect, carries a different product line and is profiled separately.

providers.name: Intrinsic
providers.description: Intrinsic is a unified Trust & Safety platform that gives safety teams a single API and dashboard to detect, investigate, and enforce against abuse across user- and AI-generated content, fraud, and marketplace abuse. The platform surfaces machine-learning classifiers (for example text toxicity and IP trust scoring), account graph lineage for linkage analysis, geo enrichers, and global intelligence signals through a synchronous API, and lets teams author, version, deploy, and monitor real-time anti-abuse rules from a hosted dashboard. Founded in 2022 in San Francisco by Karine Mellata and Michael Lin (previously on Trust & Safety ML and data-engineering infrastructure at Apple and Discord), Intrinsic has since rebranded to Variance (variance.co); the Intrinsic-branded developer surfaces at docs.intrinsicapi.com and api.intrinsicapi.com remain in service.

providers.name: Irreverent Labs
providers.description: Irreverent Labs is a Bellevue, Washington startup founded in 2021 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Samsung Next, and Michael Ovitz. The company began by building MechaFightClub, a web3 gaming property, then pivoted to generative AI, developing video foundation models intended to let creators, game studios, and developers produce short-form video from natural-language prompts. Its current public product is Supermodel (supermodel.ai), an autonomous on-chain trading agent that watches top Hyperliquid wallets, scores their track records, and fuses crowd, technical, and prediction-market signals into trades. The company has publicly signaled intent to ship a developer API for its video generation models, but no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK has been released as of this profile.

providers.name: Jade Autism
providers.description: Jade (Jade ND) is a Brazil-, UAE-, and UK-based education technology company building inclusive digital solutions for neurodivergent children, including those on the autism spectrum (ASD). Its product family includes Jade Edu (personalized-learning software for schools and educators), the Jade App (cognitive-development games for children, with 185,000+ downloads across 179 countries), Jade Astea (eye-tracking technology that assists professionals in evaluating autism-spectrum diagnosis), and Jade Academy (professional-development courses on inclusive and diverse education). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Jive
providers.description: Jive (marketed today as "Jive AI" and owned by IgniteTech, an ESW Capital company based in Austin, Texas) is an enterprise collaboration and communication platform — a digital workplace that unifies people, knowledge, and content across departments and locations for large, often regulated organizations. Capabilities include collaboration spaces and group discussions, knowledge management with search and co-editing, personalized role-based news feeds, mobile and desktop apps, and engagement analytics. Jive originated as a venture-backed (Kleiner Perkins) enterprise-social vendor that IPO'd in 2011 and shipped a REST API plus an official Node.js add-on SDK. It was later acquired into the Aurea / ESW Capital / IgniteTech family.

providers.name: Klaimee
providers.description: Klaimee is a Y Combinator (Spring/P26 batch) startup building certification, financial guarantee, and liability insurance for AI agents running in production. The company evaluates an autonomous agent across risk dimensions such as scope, data exfiltration, unauthorized action, output integrity, adversarial manipulation, behavioral stability, model drift, and operational control, then issues a letter-graded certification report with remediation guidance and a Klaimee-Verified badge that AI vendors use to clear enterprise procurement. Certified agents are backed by a financial guarantee and by AI liability insurance priced against the certification score, covering the gap that traditional errors-and-omissions and cyber policies explicitly exclude — hallucinated outputs, unauthorized actions, data exposure, prompt injection, and wrongful commitments. Klaimee also runs a public adversarial-testing playground where teams can stress-test an agent with probes for prompt injection, jailbreak, decision drift, data leakage, and biased outputs. Klaimee currently sells a human-delivered certification and underwriting service; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation as of this enrichment pass. Founded in 2026 by Ines Boutemadja (CEO) and Julien Catonnet (CTO), based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Kodiak Networks
providers.description: Kodiak Networks built a carrier-grade Push-to-Talk over Cellular (PoC) platform that wireless operators deployed as their own branded push-to-talk service, competing with legacy land mobile radio for dispatch, field-service and public-safety workforces. Motorola Solutions acquired the company in 2017 and the technology now ships as Motorola Solutions' "Kodiak" mission-critical push-to-talk (MCPTT) offering for carriers, aligned to the 3GPP SA WG6 MCPTT specifications (TS 23.379, TS 24.382, TS 24.482, TS 22.582) and interoperable with land mobile radio through Critical Connect. Kodiak Networks no longer operates independently: its legacy domain serves only a static "Site under maintenance" placeholder over plain HTTP, and it publishes no OpenAPI, developer documentation, SDKs or public API surface of its own. Broadband push-to-talk APIs for third-party integration do exist, but access is gated behind the Motorola Solutions Application Developer Program.

providers.name: Koska
providers.description: KOSKA Corporation (株式会社KOSKA) is a Tokyo-based manufacturing technology company, founded in October 2018, that applies cost accounting and IoT to the Japanese factory floor. Its flagship product GenKan (原価管理自動化サービス) automates cost management for high-mix low-volume manufacturers: RFID and power sensors installed on existing equipment capture work progress and consumption without changing operator behavior, then make processing cost, material cost, and electricity cost visible line by line, feeding real actual-cost figures and KPI setting back to the shop floor and management. A second product, ながら記録 (Nagara Kiroku / "vScribe"), is an AI record-keeping app for manufacturing, construction, and logistics sites — photograph a paper form and AI generates the input form, then operators record hands-free by speaking, with the AI parsing natural speech into structured records, inspections, and reports. KOSKA is led by CEO Kenichiro Sone (Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2021) and advised by Hiroshi Obata, former chair of the Japan Cost Accounting Association. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a sensor-and-SaaS product company, not an API provider.

providers.name: LHC Group
providers.description: LHC Group is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The LHC Group API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: LYST
providers.description: Lyst is a global fashion aggregation and shopping platform that consolidates products from more than 27,000 brands and retailers, connecting roughly 160 million annual shoppers with clothing, shoes, bags, accessories and jewelry across a single personalized, AI-driven catalog. Rather than a public developer API, Lyst exposes a partner surface: brands and retailers integrate via product-feed synchronization and a Stripe-powered "Lyst Shop" checkout, with API access granted privately during a two-week partner onboarding. Backed by Accel and Balderton Capital, Lyst also runs an engineering organization (making.lyst.com, github.com/lyst) best known for the open-source LightFM recommendation library.

providers.name: Maximus
providers.description: Maximus is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Maximus API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Oxia
providers.description: Oxia is a scalable metadata store and coordination service designed for distributed systems, providing strong consistency guarantees and high availability. It is developed by StreamNative as an alternative to ZooKeeper.

providers.name: Paxton AI
providers.description: Paxton AI is a legal AI assistant built for attorneys and law firms, delivering rapid case-law and regulatory research, AI-assisted document drafting, file analysis, deposition and discovery summarization, and specialized workflows for medical chronologies and billing summaries. Founded by Tanguy Chau (CEO) and Michael Ulin and headquartered in Bend, Oregon, the company has raised roughly $28M across a $6M seed round led by WVV Capital and a $22M Series A led by Unusual Ventures, with participation from Kyber Knight and 25Madison. Paxton's platform covers US federal regulations, state laws, and case law across all fifty states, surfaces precise authority-linked citations, and runs in a closed model environment that is SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliant with data never used for model training. The product is delivered as a web SaaS targeted at solo practitioners, small and mid-size firms, and enterprise legal teams across personal injury, family, employment, criminal, and corporate practice areas; commercial access is sold via per-seat Individual plans ($499/month or $2,999/year) and a volume-priced Enterprise plan, with a 7-day free trial. Paxton publishes a small public GitHub presence with citator and legal-hallucination benchmark datasets but does not offer a public developer API, SDK, or open-source platform.

providers.name: Pickle Robot Company
providers.description: Pickle Robot Company builds Physical AI robots for supply chain automation, focused on autonomously unloading non-palletized goods (floor-loaded boxes and parcels) from trucks and shipping containers at warehouse speed. Its Dill Autonomy Engine (DAE) combines classical optimal control with generative AI and machine vision so fleets improve continuously across deployments, with operational dashboards reporting picks-per-hour, unload times, and package-mix analysis. Customers include UPS and Cintas. Headquartered in the Boston, Massachusetts area, Pickle Robot is a DCVC portfolio company backed by investors including Teradyne Robotics Ventures, Toyota Ventures, Catapult Ventures, Hyperplane, and VersionOne. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK; its GitHub organization hosts robotics tooling (mostly ROS/SLAM forks) rather than API client libraries.

providers.name: Principly
providers.description: Principly, Inc. is an SEC-registered investment adviser that operates the consumer fintech product Backer (backer.com), a mobile-first platform for opening and managing 529 education savings plans. Backer lets parents open a 529 plan in minutes, automate contributions, and share custom gifting links so family and friends can contribute to a child's college fund. The service helps families choose among more than 100 U.S. 529 plans, reporting 250K+ users and $70M+ saved. It is a consumer-facing mobile and web application and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. Principly is backed by 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: QuidelOrtho
providers.description: QuidelOrtho is a diagnostics company that transforms diagnostic data into action across the entire healthcare spectrum, from home testing to hospital laboratories. The company offers over 550 assays in more than 140 countries and territories. QuidelOrtho maintains technical documentation libraries, customer portals (MyQuidel and Ortho Plus), and a comprehensive Instructions for Use library for healthcare professionals.

providers.name: Randolph-Brooks FCU
providers.description: Randolph-Brooks Federal Credit Union (RBFCU) is a member-owned, not-for-profit federal credit union headquartered in Live Oak, Texas, federally insured by the NCUA and serving more than one million members across Texas and beyond. Chartered as a federal credit union rather than a state or national bank, RBFCU is one of the largest credit unions in the United States by membership and assets, offering retail banking, mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and deposit products through branches and digital channels. As a member-focused retail institution, RBFCU publishes no first-party public developer program, API documentation, or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reached through third-party aggregators (such as Plaid, MX, Finicity, or Akoya) rather than a directly documented open-finance API, and it publishes no stated CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture or documented FDX participation.

providers.name: RealPact
providers.description: RealPact is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-native operating system for real estate brokerages. Its voice-enabled AI agents automate the operational work behind every deal: the Deed Agent retrieves county deed records and flags encumbrances, the Tax & Vision Agent uses computer vision to extract tax assessments and property details, the Property Agent consolidates ownership and property information, and the Transaction Agent auto-fills contracts, manages disclosures, coordinates signatures, and tracks compliance deadlines. The company aims to compress transaction workflows from hours to minutes for brokerages, with early customers including Four Seasons Sotheby's International Realty and Black House Real Estate. Backed by Y Combinator and the LeapYear Fund, RealPact currently operates a customer-facing application and marketing site but publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program as of this profiling.

providers.name: Rebrandly
providers.description: Custom URL shortener for sharing branded links

providers.name: Red Ventures
providers.description: Red Ventures is a privately held digital marketing and media holding company headquartered in Fort Mill, South Carolina, operating a portfolio of high-growth consumer comparison, commerce, education, and content businesses including Bankrate, The Points Guy, Lonely Planet, Allconnect, Sage Home Loans, RV Education, and RV Home Client Services. The company combines proprietary technology, data science, and performance marketing to acquire customers on behalf of its brands and partners. It maintains a public GitHub organization of 77 largely-forked internal engineering repositories and a company blog, but publishes no public developer API program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, first-party SDK, or served /.well-known/ discovery document on any Red Ventures-controlled host.

providers.name: Republic
providers.description: Republic is a New York-based fintech and private investing platform (republic.com) that lets retail and accredited investors access early-stage startups, private companies, real estate, crypto, and other alternative assets through regulated investment crowdfunding offerings. Backed by prosus-ventures, Republic operates a consumer investing marketplace rather than a public developer platform: it publishes a security and compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001) at republic.com/security but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface at the time of this enrichment pass. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the provider-security signals that could be probed directly.

providers.name: Roboflow Universe
providers.description: Pre-trained computer vision models

providers.name: Sereact
providers.description: Sereact GmbH is a Stuttgart, Germany based physical-AI company building intelligent robotic systems for warehouse and fulfillment automation. Its "Cortex" platform pairs a Vision Language Action Model (VLAM) with robot control so robots can pick, place, sort, induct, and inspect diverse items in production without task-specific retraining, running across 50+ deployments in Europe and the US. Products include Pick-and-Place, Putwall, Induction, Bin Handling, Returns Handling, and the Lens perception system. Backed by Creandum and Point Nine; announced a $110M Series B. Sereact does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — an internal api.sereact.ai host exists but is a placeholder. This profile captures the company identity and public web/GitHub surface.

providers.name: Solace
providers.description: Solace Health is a US healthcare navigation company that connects patients with human patient advocates and care coordinators whose services are covered by insurance, including Medicare. Through solace.health and the app.solace.health member portal, patients are matched with an advocate who helps them understand diagnoses, prepare for appointments, coordinate care, manage bills, and navigate the healthcare system. Solace is a consumer-facing healthcare service company; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer program, API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Sourceful
providers.description: Sourceful is a Manchester, United Kingdom packaging technology company that began as a sustainable packaging marketplace connecting brands with vetted manufacturers and offering data-driven carbon footprint, life-cycle, and recyclability metrics for every packaging design. Founded in 2020 by Wing Chan and Charlie Bradshaw, the company raised roughly $32M from investors including Index Ventures, Coatue, and Eka Ventures, and grew to over 100 employees serving climate-conscious consumer brands. Since 2024–2025 Sourceful has pivoted toward AI-powered visual design for packaging, releasing Sourceful 3.0 and Riverflow 1, a proprietary image-editing foundation model marketed as state-of-the-art for design-grade, print-ready packaging artwork. The current product line covers AI logo design, packaging design, AI product photography, image editing, packaging ranges, flavor/variant ranges, brand moodboards, and (announced) product mockups and social ads. Sourceful is ISO 42001 certified for AI management. As of this profile the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source GitHub organization for the packaging/design platform, and the original sustainable-packaging marketplace surface and supplier-facing carbon footprint API have been superseded by the AI design product; there is no Sourceful developer portal at this time. The unrelated github.com/sourceful organization belongs to Pony Foo, not this company, and sourceful.energy is a separate distributed-energy-resource platform unrelated to Sourceful Ltd.

providers.name: Strand Therapeutics
providers.description: Strand Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, founded by biological engineers out of MIT — including Jacob Becraft (CEO), Tasuku Kitada (President, Head of R&D), Ron Weiss and Darrell J. Irvine — around what the company describes as the first mRNA programming language. Strand engineers programmable genetic medicines across three named platforms: SignalPath LNPs for tissue-selective delivery of mRNA payloads, SignalLock RNA which restricts expression to target tissues and deactivates it elsewhere, and SignalScript RNA for self-replicating and circular RNA constructs. Its clinical pipeline includes STX-001, STX-003 (systemic tumor delivery, entering the clinic in 2026) and STX-005 (in vivo CAR T), targeting solid tumors, blood cancers and autoimmune disease. Strand operates no developer program and publishes no API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable specification of any kind; its corporate site is a static Webflow property behind Cloudflare with no content API, no feed and no sitemap. It is catalogued here because it appears in the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest backlog, and this profile records the honest zero.

providers.name: Sturdy
providers.description: Sturdy is a decentralized liquid money market protocol for on-chain lending and borrowing. Sturdy V2 uses a two-tier architecture: a base layer of risk-isolated lending pairs, where each siloed market consists of a single lending asset and a single collateral asset, and an aggregation layer on top that lets lenders choose acceptable collateral types while avoiding liquidity fragmentation. The protocol is oracle-agnostic (using RedStone, API3, and eOracle feeds depending on the market), is governed by the $STRDY token and the Sturdy DAO, and has been audited by Zellic, ChainSecurity, Spearbit, Certik, Code4rena, and Quantstamp. Sturdy is an on-chain smart-contract protocol rather than a hosted REST API: its developer surface is the published smart contracts, oracle integrations, and the Sturdy Subnet, with no first-party web API, SDK, or OpenAPI. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital.

providers.name: SwingVision
providers.description: SwingVision is an AI-powered tennis and pickleball platform built by a team of A.I. experts from Tesla and Apple, venture-backed by Tennis Australia, Sony, and Techstars. Its mobile app processes video on-device with computer vision to deliver automated line calling, scoring, match stats, and highlight reels from a single phone or tablet camera. SwingVision is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API; its api.swing.vision backend is private and undocumented, with data export offered through the app as video and spreadsheet files.

providers.name: TimeTrace Labs
providers.description: TimeTrace Labs is a London-based mathematics and artificial intelligence company building the measurement layer for healthcare, spun out of a decade of research at the University of Oxford and backed by Seedcamp and Fly Ventures. Its quantitative measurement platform separates signal from noise in multimodal physiological time-series (kinematics, EEG, ECG, actigraphy, glucose, voice), powering analytics for drug development, clinical trials, and public health that the company delivers to partners through secure APIs and a compliant analytics dashboard — though it publishes no public developer portal or API documentation yet.

providers.name: Vaas
providers.description: Vaas is a Colombian fintech building debt infrastructure for Latin America, operating a platform that automates asset-backed debt facilities for originators, asset managers, and debt providers across industries. Vaas autonomously verifies asset documentation, reconciles cash flows end to end, and enforces collateral ownership in real time so assets cannot be pledged twice, bringing liquidity and transparency to private credit. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). Vaas does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Voidly
providers.description: Internet censorship measurements, incidents, and ISP-level blocking data across 126 countries

providers.name: Voya Financial
providers.description: Voya Financial (NYSE: VOYA) is a leading health, wealth, and investment company serving approximately 14.7 million individual, workplace, and institutional clients. Voya specializes in retirement plans, group employee benefits, health savings accounts (HSAs), and investment management. Their myVoyage platform integrates financial wellness tools to help participants plan, invest, and protect their financial futures. Voya does not offer a public developer API but provides account connectivity through open banking aggregators such as Plaid.

providers.name: 21gram
providers.description: 21gram (21그램) is a South Korean pet end-of-life care company that operates pet funeral homes and an online booking and consultation platform for pet funerals. Founded in Seoul and led by Kwon Shin-gu, it began as an online brokerage letting owners find licensed pet funeral homes nationwide and book a service with 24-hour consultation, reservation and payment, then moved into operating its own facilities — acquiring Korea's first pet funeral hall, Arongi Cheonguk, in Gwangju, Gyeonggi Province — and now runs branches including Gwangju, Namyangju and Cheonan plus a large charnel house. Its consumer surface covers funeral procedures and pricing, cremation, memorial jewelry, hearse and non-attending funeral options, urns, flowers, temporary storage and scattering, and grief-support classes. It is venture-backed and trades on secondary markets. It publishes no developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its website runs on the hosted imweb site builder.

providers.name: Abgenomics
providers.description: AbGenomics (AbGenomics International, Inc.) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2000 with offices in the San Francisco Bay Area, California and an R&D center in Taipei, Taiwan. It develops targeted antibody therapeutics for immune-mediated inflammatory disease and cancer, built on a PSGL-1 T-cell checkpoint regulator platform, with clinical candidates including neihulizumab (AbGn-168H / ALTB-168) and the antibody-drug conjugate AbGn-107. The company rebranded as AltruBio, Inc. in 2020 and now operates at altrubio.com; the original abgenomics.com domain is a parked for-sale listing. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable API description of any kind.

providers.name: Acera Surgical
providers.description: Acera Surgical Inc. is a St. Louis, Missouri bioscience company founded in 2013 that develops and commercializes fully engineered, 100% synthetic materials for regenerative wound care and soft tissue repair, built on a proprietary electrospun nanofiber technology platform. Its Restrata product family — Restrata Sheet, Restrata Meshed and Restrata MiniMatrix — is a fully resorbable synthetic matrix used to treat hard-to-heal and complex wounds in acute care settings, and its Cerafix implant addresses dural repair and cerebrospinal fluid leakage. Acera was acquired by Solventum Corporation on December 23, 2025 for $725 million in cash plus up to $125 million in milestone payments, and now sits inside Solventum's Medical segment MedSurg portfolio. Acera is a medical device manufacturer, not a software company: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: ACROVE
providers.description: ACROVE, Inc. (株式会社ACROVE) is a Tokyo e-commerce platform and brand roll-up company, founded 15 November 2018 as Anoma, Inc. and renamed ACROVE in October 2020, led by representative director Shunsuke Arai and headquartered in Nishi-Shinjuku. It runs two businesses: a Commerce Transformation practice that grows client brand sales on Amazon, Rakuten, Qoo10 and other Japanese marketplaces using its proprietary EC analytics engine ACROVE FORCE (now presented as ACROVE INSIGHT), and an EC roll-up business that acquires and operates consumer brands. It reports support for 170+ client companies and raised a Series C in September 2024. Its commerce arm — the former Digital-Free K.K., now 株式会社Acrove at commerce.acrove.co.jp — is a Magento / Adobe Commerce implementation specialist. ACROVE FORCE, ACROVE MDM and the ACROVE Knowledge Base are login-gated applications; the company publishes no public API, SDK, webhook surface, machine-readable contract or developer portal on any host it operates.

providers.name: AdjuCor
providers.description: AdjuCor GmbH is a Munich, Germany medical device company, founded in 2012, that develops reBEAT — an implantable, patient-specific cardiac support system for advanced heart failure. reBEAT is an epicardial device that conforms to the outside of the heart and delivers uni- or biventricular mechanical circulatory support without ever contacting blood, which is intended to avoid the thrombosis, stroke and haemolysis risks that constrain conventional blood-pumping ventricular assist devices.
