providers.name: PenFed Credit Union
providers.description: PenFed Credit Union (Pentagon Federal Credit Union), founded in 1935 and headquartered in McLean, Virginia, is a federally chartered credit union regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) and one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly 2.9 million members and tens of billions of dollars in assets. It is a not-for-profit, member-owned financial cooperative that originally served the U.S. military and defense community and now offers open membership, providing mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, personal loans, and deposit accounts. On the open-finance front, PenFed runs an internal API-management practice — MuleSoft/Anypoint is the backbone of its digital-banking platform and an Apigee-backed developer portal host exists at developer.penfed.org (with an api.penfed.org gateway) — but neither surface is publicly documented or openly reachable: there is no public developer program, no published OpenAPI, and consumer account data is made available to members through permissioned third-party aggregators such as Plaid rather than a directly documented FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API.

providers.name: Pinscreen
providers.description: Pinscreen is an American AI and VFX production company founded in 2015 by Hao Li (MIT TR35 winner and professor of computer vision at MBZUAI), headquartered in Los Angeles with a branch in Abu Dhabi (UAE). It builds advanced generative AI for film production and interactive experiences, including AI lip sync, face reenactment, face swaps, de-aging, voice cloning, and photoreal 3D avatar digitization, and is known for developing the world's first real-time deepfake technology. Its Avatar Neo product generates a photoreal, riggable 3D avatar from a single photo (exportable as GLB/FBX with animation rigs) and is offered to developers as the Avatar Neo SDK: Unreal and Unity engine plugins backed by an avatar-generation API that can be deployed anywhere. Customers include Netflix, Amazon Studios, Warner Bros, Miramax, Apple, Google, Adobe, and DARPA. Backed by Lux Capital and Middle East investors.

providers.name: Prospera Credit Union
providers.description: Prospera Credit Union is a member-owned cooperative financial institution headquartered in British Columbia, Canada, formed on January 1, 2020 through the merger of the original Prospera Credit Union and Westminster Savings Credit Union — the largest credit-union merger in Canadian history. With roughly CA$9 billion in assets under management, about 120,000 members, and some 900 employees across branches in Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley, and the Okanagan, it is the third largest credit union in British Columbia and among the six largest in Canada. As a provincially regulated cooperative (credit unions in BC are overseen by BC Financial Services Authority and deposits are protected by the Credit Union Deposit Insurance Corporation of BC), Prospera serves personal and business members with chequing and savings accounts, credit cards, mortgages, loans, and Interac e-Transfer. On the open-finance side, Prospera runs NO public first-party developer portal or documented API — none of developer/api/developers.prospera.ca resolve — and Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and overseen by the FCAC, is not yet operational. Like most Canadian credit unions, Prospera reaches national payment rails and consumer data-sharing through shared credit-union-system infrastructure rather than a proprietary API, and third-party data access today is aggregator/screen-scraping based (e.g. Flinks, Plaid). This is an honest identity-only profile with no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Reframe
providers.description: Reframe (usereframe.ai) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, founded in 2025 by Bryan Zin (previously a Product Design Engineer on the iPhone team at Apple) and Eric Wiener, building an AI-native hardware procurement platform. Reframe automates the manual procurement process in hardware supply chains: instead of emails and spreadsheets, AI agents handle purchase orders, supplier follow-ups, and part tracking for both COTS and custom-manufactured components, with Slack and Gmail integrations for team workflows. This API Evangelist profile tracks Reframe as a company in the network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Roam
providers.description: Roam (withroam.com) is a nationwide assumable-mortgage marketplace that helps homebuyers and sellers transact on homes carrying low-rate, legally assumable FHA and VA loans. A qualified buyer can take over a seller's existing mortgage, inheriting the original interest rate, remaining balance, and terms, which in a 6%+ market against sellers' 2-3% loans can save buyers hundreds of thousands in interest. Roam manages the end-to-end assumption process from buyer qualification and lender coordination through paperwork and a 45-day close, and offers proprietary secondary financing so buyers can put as little as 5% down. It is a proptech company backed by Fifth Wall and IVP. Roam publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and llms.txt surface.

providers.name: Schaeffler
providers.description: Schaeffler Group is a German global Tier 1 automotive and industrial supplier headquartered in Herzogenaurach. Schaeffler designs and manufactures precision bearings, powertrain components, chassis applications, and e-mobility systems for the automotive and industrial sectors.

providers.description: Scouter is a Mexican online marketplace, founded in 2021 in Guadalajara, for discovering and booking unique locations — houses, mansions, studios, terraces, haciendas, rooftops and more — for audiovisual productions, events, photo shoots and workshops across Mexico. It connects brands, agencies and production companies with the owners of over 1,500 spaces, handling quotes and reservations directly via WhatsApp (no public list prices, 8-hour minimum booking). Clients have included Netflix, HBO, Puma, Nike and Grupo Modelo. Backed by 500 Global (500 LatAm "Somos Lucha" Batch 16). The public product is a consumer/host web app at wearescouter.com; it exposes no public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched.

providers.name: Seafair
providers.description: Seafair is an AI-native ERP platform for maritime operations, unifying crew management, HSQE and regulatory compliance, technical maintenance (planned maintenance systems and defect tracking), and accounting into a single system for shipping companies and ship managers. Its AI compliance engine performs document search and framework reviews (such as DryBMS and TMSA) and embeds AI assistance directly into operational workflows. Seafair markets itself as API-first with fast ERP integrations, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition. Seafair is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and is tracked in the API Evangelist network.

The agency aims to simplify tax processes through digital services and transparent communication with the public.

providers.name: Sonus
providers.description: Sonus is the API Evangelist network profile for the company that began as Sonus Networks, an early pioneer of VoIP softswitches and session border controllers (SBCs), and which today operates as Ribbon Communications (NASDAQ: RBBN) following its 2017 merger with GENBAND. Ribbon builds real-time communications, IP optical networking, session border control, cloud and edge, and network security and analytics software for service providers and enterprises. This profile originated as a Matrix Partners portfolio lead. Ribbon publishes enterprise product, support, and responsible-disclosure resources but no public developer API or open API specification was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Specific Labs
providers.description: Specific Labs is a Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) applied AI research lab based in San Francisco and operated by Bear AI Inc. The company builds datasets and benchmarks derived from real enterprise workflows, capturing authentic business decision-making patterns and audio and enterprise data that are otherwise hard to access, and turns them into training data and evaluation benchmarks for building reliable, domain-grounded AI agents. It works with frontier AI labs seeking datasets from real enterprises and with enterprises building dependable agents. Founded by Janak Sunil (CEO, formerly Coinbase) and Siddhant Paliwal (CTO). As of this profile Specific Labs publishes a marketing site with a benchmarks page and company information, and does not yet expose a public API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Sunrise
providers.description: Sunrise Robotics builds intelligent, two-armed autonomous robotic cells for manufacturing. The AI-driven system combines built-in perception and environmental awareness with autonomous execution to transform existing production processes, increase capacity, and free human workers for higher-value tasks. Cells deploy quickly (needing only a three-phase outlet), are flexible across manufacturing applications, and are built to ISO 10218 / TS 15066 safety standards. The company is backed by Seedcamp and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Surf AI
providers.description: Surf AI is an agentic security-operations platform that helps CISOs and modern security teams operationalize their entire program with specialized AI agents. It connects across identity, cloud, SaaS, and data systems to continuously monitor assets, surface exposures, trace issues to their owners, and drive automated remediation so teams can shrink the attack surface before it is exploited. The company integrates with 60+ security, identity, cloud, SIEM, and business tools, and is backed by Accel, Cyberstarts, and Boldstart Ventures. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from public sources; Surf AI markets an enterprise platform and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Thermondo
providers.description: Thermondo is Germany's largest residential heating installer, focused on heat pumps, photovoltaic (solar) systems, home energy management (thermondo smart), dynamic electricity tariffs, financing and subsidy assistance, and maintenance and repair services for homeowners. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Berlin, the company employs over 1,200 staff and has completed installations for more than 55,000 customers. Thermondo is a consumer-facing climate-energy provider and a portfolio company of HV Capital. It publishes no public developer API or documentation surface; it does operate a security.txt vulnerability-disclosure program and a GitHub organization. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from HV Capital's portfolio and enriched with the public security surface that could be verified.

providers.name: Tillpoint
providers.description: Tillpoint is a modular, cloud-based EPOS (electronic point of sale) and business management platform for retail, hospitality, and services. A single subscription bundles 25+ modules - Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers/CRM, Staff, Accounting, Purchase Orders, Reporting, and more - across one terminal or thousands of locations. As of this review Tillpoint does not publish a documented public or partner developer API - there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no OpenAPI. Connectivity is delivered through pre-built integrations (QuickBooks Online, Xero, WooCommerce, PayPal, Worldpay, Mailchimp). The API surfaces catalogued here (Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers, Accounting) are logical capability areas of the platform and are honestly marked as endpointsModeled - no endpoints are fabricated. Direct/programmatic access requires contacting Tillpoint.

providers.name: Tongdun
providers.description: Tongdun (同盾科技 / Tongdun Technology) is a Hangzhou-based intelligent risk-control and anti-fraud analytics company whose public product presence now operates under the 小盾未来 (Xiaodun Future) brand at xiaodun.com. It uses AI and intelligent-analysis techniques to predict and score fraud and credit risk across consumer lending, banking, insurance, and e-commerce, delivering decisioning, anti-fraud, and risk-management capabilities to financial institutions, small-loan and consumer-finance lenders, auto finance, and internet businesses. Its risk-control services are consumed as enterprise interfaces (风控接口) provisioned behind account registration and sales onboarding; there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK registry surface exposed at this time. This record was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and enriched from the company's live public web presence.

providers.name: Transbnk
providers.description: TransBnk — rebranded as TBX — is an Indian open-finance and transaction-banking infrastructure company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Mumbai. It gives banks, enterprises, fintechs, corporates, and NBFCs the platforms, APIs, and connected workflows behind corporate banking: mandate management, escrow flows, virtual accounts, reconciliation, lending acceleration, and cash and treasury management. TransBnk reports partnerships with 25+ banks, 200+ APIs extended, 100+ BFSI clients, and 50M+ transactions processed. Products include TxB Hub (transaction banking), TrustHub (core banking and escrow), and the API Hub integration surface. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, 8i Ventures, and Accion Venture Lab.

providers.name: Waymo
providers.description: Waymo is the autonomous driving subsidiary of Alphabet, originally spun out of the Google Self-Driving Car Project. The company develops the Waymo Driver, a full Level 4 autonomous driving stack combining custom lidar, radar, and camera sensors with proprietary perception, prediction, and planning models. Waymo One operates a commercial robotaxi service in Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Austin, and other expanding US markets, with announced launches in Tokyo and London. The company has logged tens of millions of rider-only miles and reports significantly fewer serious-injury crashes than human-driven benchmarks. Waymo does not publish a traditional public developer API. Its primary developer-facing artifacts are the Waymo Open Dataset, the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, the Waymax JAX-based driving simulator, and a robust research publication catalogue spanning perception, behaviour prediction, planning, simulation, and end-to-end driving. Consumer access is through the Waymo One mobile app.

providers.name: Yandex.Maps Geocoder
providers.description: Use geocoding to get an object's coordinates from its address

providers.name: Yandex.Weather
providers.description: Assesses weather condition in specific locations

providers.name: ABABA
providers.description: ABABA (株式会社ABABA) is a Tokyo-based Japanese HR technology company operating a new-graduate direct-recruiting platform built on an unusual premise: only students who have already reached the FINAL interview stage at another company may register, and each submits evidence of that selection history, so every candidate in the database arrives pre-qualified by someone else's hiring bar. Employers then scout those near-miss finalists into abbreviated selection flows — the company reports that 94% of adopting employers waive the entry sheet or the first interview for an ABABA candidate. A second product, REALME, runs AI mock interviews and matching. Founded 19 October 2020 and led by co-representatives Shunki Kubo (CEO) and Tatsuya Nakai, ABABA raised a 1.25 billion yen Series B in March 2025 led by DBJ Capital (1.82 billion yen total to date) and reported passing 3,000 cumulative adopting companies in November 2025. The product ships purely as an end-user web application: ABABA publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Aether Fuels
providers.description: Aether Fuels is a sustainable-fuels technology company founded in April 2022 by Conor Madigan with Xora Innovation, headquartered at Republic Plaza in Singapore with a U.S. R&D center on the GTI Energy campus in the Chicago area. Its Aether Aurora process is a radically simplified gas-to-liquid route that converts waste carbon — CO2, CO, methane and other hydrocarbons from gasified biomass, municipal solid waste, biogas and industrial off-gases — into drop-in sustainable liquid fuels for aviation and ocean shipping, combining an electrified thermochemical syngas reactor, three proprietary catalysts and by-product recycling to cut capital cost and raise carbon conversion efficiency at medium plant scale. The company runs a 1.5 gallon-per-day integrated pilot line with strategic partner GTI Energy, whose technology it licenses, and is building a 1+ barrel-per-day demonstration plant; it has signed MOUs with JetBlue and FlyORO and is partnered with Aster on a first commercial SAF plant in Singapore. Aether Fuels sells fuel and process technology, not software: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Animab
providers.description: Animab is a biotechnology company that develops oral antibody technologies to improve gut health in livestock, particularly piglets during the post‑weaning stage. By mimicking secretory IgA, its products aim to reduce infections, lower antimicrobial use, and enhance animal performance, supporting sustainable agriculture and better feed conversion.

providers.name: API Setu
providers.description: An Indian Government platform that provides a lot of APIS for KYC, business, education & employment

providers.name: Asignio
providers.description: Asignio provides biometric authentication solutions that replace passwords with user‑drawn signatures, facial and voice biometrics. Their platform combats phishing, ransomware and deep‑fake attacks by verifying identity through AI‑driven behavioral markers, live selfie checks and multi‑modal biometrics, offering a password‑less, fraud‑resistant sign‑in experience for web and mobile applications.

providers.name: Augmodo
providers.description: Augmodo provides Spatial AI solutions to augment retail workforces, enabling real‑time inventory tracking across stores. Their platform offers a visual dashboard that helps retailers stay stocked, leveraging computer‑vision and AI to monitor product placement and availability instantly. Clients include major brands such as Amazon, Grammarly, Wyze, Oculus, and others, showcasing broad applicability across e‑commerce and physical retail environments.

providers.name: Aurorin CAD
providers.description: Aurorin CAD is a San Francisco company building a modern mechanical CAD application for engineers and hardware teams, founded in 2026 by Michael Baron and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Rather than layering on top of the geometry kernels that underpin incumbent tools such as SolidWorks, NX, Creo, CATIA, Fusion 360 and Onshape, Aurorin has written its own parametric, B-Rep driven CAD kernel designed to exploit modern multi-core CPUs and GPUs and to be AI-native from the foundation rather than as a bolted-on assistant. The product ships as a native desktop application for macOS and Windows, pairing conventional direct and parametric editing with an integrated AI agent driven through a chat interface, with the stated goal of collapsing modeling work that traditionally takes twenty minutes into seconds and avoiding the slow rebuilds and cascading feature breakage common to older parametric systems. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or API documentation; its public surface is a marketing site, a blog, an about/contact page, and careers listings.

providers.name: Automed
providers.description: Automed provides an AI‑powered medication safety platform that combines smart dispensing, connected monitoring, and predictive insights to ensure patients take the right medication at the right time across home, hospital, and pharmacy settings. The solution offers closed‑loop verification, adherence visibility for care teams, and predictive analytics to close the gap between prescribed and actually taken medication.

providers.name: Autonomize AI
providers.description: Autonomize AI provides an AI-native platform that enables healthcare enterprises to achieve autonomous operations. By embedding artificial intelligence directly into clinical workflows, the platform automates prior authorizations, appeals, and case preparation, dramatically reducing processing times and improving audit traceability. Recognized as a 2026 Technology Pioneer by the World Economic Forum, Autonomize AI delivers trusted, context-aware decision support, empowering providers to deliver faster, more accurate patient care while maintaining compliance and operational efficiency.

providers.name: Benewake
providers.description: Benewake develops high‑performance LiDAR sensors for autonomous driving, robotics, UAVs, and smart transportation. Based in Beijing, the company offers a wide range of short‑, medium‑, long‑distance and underwater LiDAR modules, serving global markets with over 300 patents and partnerships in more than 90 countries.

providers.name: BentoBox
providers.description: BentoBox is a restaurant marketing and commerce platform, part of Fiserv, that powers restaurant websites, online ordering, takeout and delivery, events, reservations, and digital presence for thousands of hospitality brands. While BentoBox runs a Technology Partners program and connects to 50+ third-party services across POS, reservations, delivery, payments, marketing, and shipping, it does not publish a public self-service developer API or API reference. Integrations are built through partnership rather than open documentation, and prospective technology partners are directed to contact the BentoBox partnerships team to integrate with the platform. As a Fiserv company, payments and commerce flows connect through Clover and Fiserv rails.

providers.name: Bio-Rad Laboratories
providers.description: Bio-Rad Laboratories is a global leader in developing and manufacturing a wide range of products for the life science research and clinical diagnostic markets, including instruments, reagents, consumables, software, and services. Founded in 1952, Bio-Rad serves scientists in genomics, proteomics, cell biology, quality control, and clinical diagnostics with products like real-time PCR systems, western blotting instruments, flow cytometers, and digital PCR.

providers.name: Blazebioscience
providers.description: Blaze Bioscience develops imaging agents and imaging systems for precision tumor imaging, enabling surgeons to visualize cancer tissue intraoperatively. The company focuses on fluorescence-guided surgery, offering tumor paint technology and clinical programs across multiple cancer types, with FDA Fast Track designation for tozuleristide.

providers.name: Brainbuddy
providers.description: Brainbuddy offers a mobile app focused on helping individuals overcome porn addiction through science-based behavioral therapy, tracking, and community support. The app provides personalized quizzes, progress metrics, and tools to rewire dopamine pathways, aiming to improve users' wellbeing, relationships, and motivation.

providers.name: Brazilian Chamber of Deputies Open Data
providers.description: Provides legislative information in Apis XML and JSON, as well as files in various formats

providers.name: Bug Labs
providers.description: Bug Labs is a New York City enterprise software company founded in 2006, first as one of the earliest open-source modular hardware makers and later as an enterprise IoT platform provider serving Fortune 500 customers including Verizon, Comcast, VMware, Ford, Charter and Orange. Its current flagship product, Signalpattern, targets workflow fragmentation by mapping and connecting dispersed enterprise systems, automating cross-system tasks, and letting users interact with APIs directly without writing code. Bug Labs previously operated the well-known public IoT APIs dweet.io, dweetpro.io and freeboard.io; all three are decommissioned and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation or public API today. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital and Court Square Ventures.

providers.name: BuyBuddy
providers.description: BuyBuddy is an AI-powered retail merchandising platform positioned as an "AI Merchandiser that tracks, thinks & acts for you." It automates in-store operations for retailers and brands, including planogram compliance and shelf monitoring via computer vision, stockout prevention, product placement optimization, dynamic pricing and promotions, demand forecasting, store transfers, and shopper-behavior analysis through smart tags. BuyBuddy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; at time of enrichment BuyBuddy publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or specification surface, so this remains a company-level profile.

providers.name: Canoesoftware
providers.description: Canoesoftware is a technology company that provides software solutions for managing and optimizing canoe rental operations. The company focuses on delivering APIs that enable integration with booking systems, inventory management, and customer relationship tools. While detailed public information is limited, Canoesoftware aims to streamline the workflow for businesses in the recreational watercraft industry, offering developers programmatic access to core functionalities such as reservation handling, pricing, and reporting. The organization appears to be associated with Canoe Intelligence, as the domain canoeesoftware.com redirects to canoeintelligence.com, suggesting a possible rebranding or acquisition, though the exact relationship remains unclear.

providers.name: Carbon Direct
providers.description: Carbon Direct is a science-first carbon management company that pairs an enterprise carbon management platform with a team of 70+ scientists. The platform helps organizations measure emissions, set science-based targets, reduce, and procure high-quality carbon dioxide removal (CDR), with monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) capabilities expanded through its 2025 acquisition of Pachama. Carbon Direct is an enterprise SaaS and advisory offering and does not publish a public developer API as of this profile.

providers.name: Ccmtechnologies
providers.description: CCm Technologies is an award‑winning cleantech company that optimises resource use through Carbon Capture and Utilisation (CCU) solutions. It converts captured CO₂ and other waste streams into stable, low‑carbon fertiliser and material products for agriculture, food manufacturing, bio‑char and water treatment sectors, aligning with UN Sustainable Development Goals and delivering commercial value while reducing scope 1‑3 emissions.

providers.name: CelesTrak
providers.description: CelesTrak is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: space) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: CellPhire Therapeutics
providers.description: CellPhire Therapeutics develops platelet‑based therapeutics to treat acute hemorrhage and promote vascular repair. Their platform includes CLPH‑511, a frozen activated platelet product, and the FPH platform targeting hemostasis and vascular permeability. The company aims to save lives in trauma, surgery, and critical care by providing innovative biologics that address platelet availability challenges.

providers.name: Cencorpautomation
providers.description: Cencorpautomation, operating under the brand Cencorp Automation, specializes in back-end automation solutions for the electronics industry. It offers advanced production automation, depaneling, odd-form placement, test handling, and laser processing technologies. The company serves leading automotive, telecom, consumer, and industrial manufacturers, focusing on improving productivity, quality, and traceability across complex manufacturing workflows.

providers.name: Chain Bridge Bank
providers.description: Chain Bridge Bank, N.A., is a nationally chartered bank headquartered in McLean, Virginia, offering commercial, personal, and trust banking services. Founded in 2007, it serves political campaigns, lobbying firms, and other clients, providing deposit accounts, loans, treasury management, and wealth management nationwide.

providers.name: City, Toronto Open Data
providers.description: Toronto (CA) City Open Data

providers.name: Coinhouse
providers.description: Coinhouse is a French cryptocurrency brokerage and investment platform offering buying, selling, and staking of major digital assets such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana. Founded in 2014, it provides services for private individuals, corporate clients, and wealth advisors, featuring automated recurring purchases (DCA), crypto staking rewards, and a dedicated app. The company emphasizes security, regulatory compliance, and educational resources through its Academy and blog, positioning itself as a trusted gateway to the crypto market for European customers.

providers.name: Collectivex
providers.description: CollectiveX is an AI‑powered healthcare platform that combines global medical expertise with advanced artificial intelligence to enhance diagnostic accuracy, improve patient outcomes, and accelerate medical research and education. The platform offers diagnosis support, treatment planning, and collaborative research tools for clinicians and researchers worldwide.

providers.name: ConocoPhillips
providers.description: ConocoPhillips is a leading global exploration and production company, headquartered in Houston, Texas, that is uniquely equipped to deliver reliable, responsibly produced oil and natural gas. The company operates in more than a dozen countries with conventional and unconventional crude oil, natural gas, LNG, and natural gas liquids assets. ConocoPhillips does not publish public developer APIs; its external digital surface is organized around an investor relations portal, a vendor relations portal (powered by third-party platforms such as GEP and Taulia), an LNG technology and licensing program, and a custom sustainability report builder.

providers.name: Contractor Foreman
providers.description: Contractor Foreman is all-in-one construction management software for contractors - estimates, invoicing, scheduling, time cards, daily logs, change orders, and job costing - used by contractors in more than 75 countries. There is no self-serve public developer API or public API reference; the company's dedicated API subdomain (api.contractorforeman.net) displays only a "Coming soon" placeholder as of this review. The one confirmed API capability is a private, account-scoped API key (generated under Settings > Integration > Zapier) that powers Contractor Foreman's official Zapier app, exposing Customer and Lead create/archive/delete triggers and actions plus a File Uploaded trigger. That key and its underlying endpoints are not documented or published for direct third-party use outside the Zapier integration; broader third-party connectivity otherwise runs through native integrations (QuickBooks, Gusto, Google Calendar/Outlook, Stripe, Angi Leads, CompanyCam, MS Project, SweetPay) and Zapier/webhook automation rather than an open API.

providers.name: Convene
providers.description: Convene provides hospitality-driven meeting, event, and flexible office space solutions for businesses and organizations. Their platform offers venues, technology, and services to host conferences, corporate events, and collaborative workspaces across major cities worldwide, emphasizing seamless experiences and flexible arrangements.

providers.name: Deepcode
providers.description: AI for code review

providers.name: DermBiont
providers.description: DermBiont, Inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts clinical-stage dermatology therapeutics company founded in 2017 that develops targeted topical treatments addressing the root cause of skin disease rather than its symptoms. Its lead program SM-030 is a first-in-class topical PKC-beta inhibitor in development for melasma and other hyperpigmentation disorders of the skin, targeting excess melanin production; earlier programs included SM-020 for seborrheic keratosis and the live-bacterial DBI-001 and DBI-002 candidates for atopic dermatitis, tinea pedis and onychomycosis. The company describes an in-house discovery platform for microbiome-based therapeutics built on terabytes of DNA sequencing data from human skin samples across healthy individuals and patients, paired with a proprietary computational biology platform that identifies functions gained and lost by the skin microbiome. That computational platform is internal research tooling, not a product: DermBiont sells drug candidates and partnering opportunities, publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and its website is a Squarespace-hosted corporate site.

providers.name: Django
providers.description: A high-level Python web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design. Django follows the model-template-views architectural pattern and includes an ORM, automatic admin interface, robust template system, and quick internationalization support. The current release line is Django 6.0, supported by the non-profit Django Software Foundation, and it powers some of the busiest websites globally.

providers.name: DraftKings
providers.description: DraftKings is a digital sports entertainment and gaming company that operates a leading daily fantasy sports platform, an online sportsbook, and an iGaming casino across regulated jurisdictions in North America. The company also runs DraftKings Marketplace for digital collectibles and offers business-to-business gaming technology. No publicly documented developer API or developer portal is currently exposed at draftkings.com; integrations are typically handled through licensed partner agreements rather than self-serve developer access.

providers.name: Estately
providers.description: Estately is a Seattle-based, MLS-based residential real estate search platform for browsing homes for sale, recently sold homes, home values, and neighborhood information, and for connecting buyers and sellers with agents. Estately does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its notable developer-facing surface is the open-source `rets` Ruby library it maintains for fetching data from RETS (Real Estate Transaction Standard) servers, distributed on RubyGems with a bundled command-line client. This profile was surfaced from VC-portfolio signals (500 Global, Uncork Capital) and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Fourier Intelligence
providers.description: Fourier (Fourier Intelligence, founded 2015 and headquartered in Shanghai, China) is a full-stack robotics company that develops core robot technology and finished robot products. It began in rehabilitation robotics — exoskeletons and upper/lower-limb rehab devices such as the ArmMotus and ExoMotus lines and the RehabHub intelligent rehabilitation ecosystem — and has expanded into general-purpose humanoid robots (the GRx series, including GR-1 and GR-2), smart actuators (FSA), and dexterous hands. Fourier publishes first-party developer SDKs for robot control through its FFTAI GitHub organization: the RoCS (Robot Control System / General Robotics OS) client libraries for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, and the fourier-grx control stack for the GRx humanoid series. Fourier is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. These are device/robot-control developer libraries rather than a hosted web API; the company publishes no public REST/OpenAPI surface.

providers.description: UK official public record API

providers.name: Gilgamesh Pharma
providers.description: Gilgamesh Pharma (Gilgamesh Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) is a New York based clinical-stage neuroscience company founded in 2019 that develops rapid-acting, next-generation therapeutics for psychiatric and substance use disorders. Its discovery and translational platform combines medicinal chemistry, neurocircuitry science, electrophysiology and machine learning to identify new chemical entities, and its pipeline spans short-acting 5-HT2A receptor agonists, NMDA receptor antagonists, non-hallucinogenic neuroplastogens, cardiac-safe ibogaine analogs and M1/M4 muscarinic programs. Lead assets include bretisilocin (GM-2505), acquired by AbbVie in August 2025, and blixeprodil (GM-1020), an orally bioavailable NMDAR antagonist in Phase 2 for major depressive disorder. Gilgamesh is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: InAuth (American Express)
providers.description: InAuth is a mobile-first digital device intelligence and authentication company acquired by American Express in 2018 and now operated within American Express's fraud-management portfolio; its technology also powers Accertify Device Intelligence. The InAuth Security Platform provides persistent device identification (device fingerprinting), malware and criminal-tool detection, rooted/jailbroken-device detection, location and behavioral risk analysis, and transaction risk scoring, delivered primarily through native iOS and Android SDKs embedded in merchant and financial-institution apps. Access is enterprise-gated through the Amex for Developers portal; there is no public self-serve REST API, OpenAPI specification, public package-registry distribution, or InAuth-specific public code repository for the product line.

providers.name: Infosys
providers.description: Infosys is a global IT services, consulting, and outsourcing company headquartered in Bengaluru, India, providing digital transformation, cloud, AI, and business process services. Through its Finacle banking software product and Banking API Platform, Infosys exposes open banking APIs for deposits, loans, payments, trade finance, and data privacy, along with a configurable developer portal, API composer, and consent management. A public Finacle Open Bank Project sandbox is also available for developers to explore banking APIs.

providers.name: Kaggle
providers.description: Create and interact with Datasets, Notebooks, and connect with Kaggle

providers.name: Kraftful
providers.description: Kraftful is a startup focused on providing a platform for managing smart home devices and IoT integrations. The company offers APIs that enable developers to connect, control, and monitor a variety of connected products, aiming to simplify the creation of unified smart home experiences. Backed by leadout-capital, Kraftful targets both consumer and enterprise markets, delivering tools for device onboarding, state synchronization, and automation workflows.

providers.name: LendingClub
providers.description: LendingClub is a US consumer-finance company and national bank, founded in 2006 as a peer-to-peer marketplace lender and now a Fortune 1000 digital bank following its 2021 acquisition of Radius Bancorp. In 2026 it rebranded as Happen Bank, N.A. and moved its web presence from lendingclub.com to happen.com. It no longer operates a public developer program: the /developers tree and the LCX Primary and Secondary Market API technical documentation were withdrawn during the rebrand and now return HTTP 404, while the legacy investor host api.lendingclub.com remains live but gated and undocumented. The API the company still markets - "API-driven purchasing" inside Marketplace Connect for institutional loan buyers - is reachable only through an institutional contact-sales form, with no published reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Länsförsäkringar
providers.description: Länsförsäkringar is a Swedish financial services group offering banking, insurance, loans, savings and pension products. It operates regionally across Sweden, providing digital and physical services to private customers and businesses. The company’s website presents extensive information about its offerings, corporate governance, sustainability initiatives, and customer support.

providers.name: Medigram
providers.description: Medigram, Inc. is a healthcare AI governance company founded by Sherri Douville that builds Darwin, a governed decision platform for high-stakes clinical and performance AI. Darwin implements the sociotechnical data-governance architecture defined in IEEE UL 2933 (the six-dimension TIPPSS framework: Trust, Identity, Privacy, Protection, Safety, Security) and ANSI/HSI 2800:2025, scoring AI systems against a five-level maturity model and crosswalking them to ten governance frameworks (IEEE UL 2933, ANSI/HSI 2800:2025, ISO 42001, OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, NIST AI RMF, FDA, EU AI Act, and the HSCC guides). Applications include medtech AI governance, health-system IT review, and professional-sports player-health governance. Historically Medigram provided a secure, cloud-based mobile communication platform for healthcare professionals. Medigram is a portfolio company surfaced from the a16z network; it publishes marketing and standards content but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: MessengerX.io
providers.description: A FREE API for developers to build and monetize personalized ML based chat apps

providers.name: NachoNacho
providers.description: NachoNacho is a SaaS procurement and subscription management marketplace helping businesses discover, buy, and manage software subscriptions.

providers.name: Nitricity
providers.description: Nitricity is a climate-tech and agricultural-technology company that produces nitrogen fertilizer on-farm from only air, water, and renewable electricity. Founded in 2018 by Stanford graduate researchers Nicolas Pinkowski and Joshua McEnaney, the company uses a solar-powered plasma / electrochemical process to fix atmospheric nitrogen and produce nitric acid and calcium nitrate fertilizers on-site and on-demand, eliminating the fossil-fuel-intensive Haber-Bosch process and long-distance transportation that make conventional fertilizer responsible for roughly 5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Fine Structure Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, and strategic investor Chipotle, Nitricity is a hardware and physical-product company; it publishes a corporate website, blog, and field-trial program but exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Pivot Bio
providers.description: Pivot Bio is an agricultural biotechnology company headquartered in Berkeley, California with additional operations in St. Louis, Missouri. The company engineers naturally occurring soil microbes to fix atmospheric nitrogen on crop root systems, providing a biological alternative to synthetic nitrogen fertilizer that reduces nitrous-oxide emissions, nitrate runoff, and exposure to volatile fertilizer prices. Pivot Bio's product line includes PROVEN 40 and PROVEN G3 (corn and corn silage), RETURN (wheat and small grains), CERT-N (cotton), and RETAIN (sorghum). The company also operates N-OVATOR, an outcomes-based program that pays farmers for verified emissions reductions; the program reports having paid out more than $6M to growers since 2022 and contributing to over 1,050,000 metric tons of CO2e avoided. Pivot Bio was founded by Karsten Temme (CEO) and Alvin Tamsir. Investors include Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Temasek, DCVC, Generation Investment Management, Pavilion Capital, G2 Venture Partners, Bond, and others. Pivot Bio's product is the microbe, not an API; the company operates a farmer-facing Salesforce-based portal but does not publish a public developer API or SDK.

providers.description: Find Canadian Government Representatives

providers.name: Revagenix
providers.description: Revagenix, Inc. is a private clinical-stage precision-therapeutics company headquartered in San Francisco, California, founded in 2019 by antibacterial-discovery veterans from Achaogen. The company takes a first-principles approach to drug design for serious chronic disease, engineering each candidate around target biology, route of delivery and tolerability. Its lead program, Rev-56, is a first-in-class inhaled precision therapy with a novel mechanism of action targeting chronic Pseudomonas infection in non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB), a progressive respiratory disease affecting an estimated 350,000 to 500,000 adults in the United States; Rev-56 is entering Phase 1 clinical development in 2026, with a dry-powder formulation approaching candidate selection. Revagenix is backed by Novo Holdings, Tenmile, the REPAIR Impact Fund and the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID contract 75N93022C00061). Revagenix is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Reven Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Reven Pharmaceuticals is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado. Reven develops medicines from its proprietary RJX Technology platform - a patented, first-in-class intravenous composition of anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory ingredients - and is advancing candidates for sepsis, multi-system inflammation, cytokine release syndrome, ARDS and vascular, oncology, CNS and ocular indications. Its lead candidate, Rejuveinix (RJX), completed a double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 dose-escalation study in healthy volunteers and received FDA clearance of an Investigational New Drug application for the treatment of COVID-19. Reven publishes a corporate and investor website at reven.com covering its pipeline, modalities, clinical trials, expanded-access program and news, but operates no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: Ritual
providers.description: Ritual is a Toronto-based restaurant order-ahead and "social ordering" platform (ritual.co, founded 2014) that lets consumers pre-order, pay, and skip the line at local restaurants and coffee shops, and lets colleagues pile onto a shared order for group pickup. For restaurants it offers Ritual ONE (online ordering, company/building perk programs, and Ritual for Coffee). Ritual does NOT publish a public or self-serve developer API - there is no developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or authentication documentation. Restaurant order injection into point-of-sale systems is handled through partner/POS integrations (documented on partnersupport.ritual.co) and third-party ordering aggregators such as Deliverect, not through a Ritual-published API. Operating status - Ritual continues to operate the consumer app and online-ordering platform, but the business is distressed and in transition - revenue fell from ~US$11M (2021) to ~US$3.9M (H1 2024) with repeated layoffs, and in January 2025 Shopify "acqui-hired" the co-founders (CEO Ray Reddy became Shopify's VP of Retail/POS) and much of the R&D team while a separate process to sell the standalone Ritual business was underway. This entry is a documentation stub with no APIs modeled because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Sajilni
providers.description: Sajilni is a Middle East / MENA event ticketing and event-management platform built for organizers who care about data and branding. Organizers use it to create events, design branded registration pages, sell and scan tickets, manage seating and booths, run promo/discount codes, collect payments, and analyze attendee data. The consumer-facing site is sajilni.com with an organizer/business portal at business.sajilni.com; the platform is a Java/Spring web application with an internal authentication service at auth.sajilni.com. As of this enrichment pass Sajilni publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or webhook surface, so this profile captures the company identity, commercial pages, and a live domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Scalable Capital
providers.description: Scalable Capital is a Munich-based digital investment platform and licensed bank operating across Germany, Austria, Italy, France, Spain and the Netherlands. It offers a self-directed neobroker for trading stocks, ETFs, bonds, funds, crypto and derivatives, automated Wealth (robo-advisory) portfolio management, ETF and stock savings plans, an interest-bearing overnight cash account, and credit services. Backed by Balderton Capital and HV Capital, Scalable Capital serves retail investors through consumer web and mobile applications; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched via public-surface probes.

providers.name: Sec3
providers.description: Sec3 (formerly Soteria) is a Solana-native security firm, founded in 2021, providing smart-contract security audits, formal verification, and post-deployment on-chain monitoring for high-stakes protocols and institutions building on Solana. The team combines manual security review by experienced researchers with automated tooling and formal methods, and maintains open-source tools including the X-Ray static analysis scanner and IDL Guesser. Sec3 has secured protocols such as the Solana Foundation, Wormhole, Kamino Finance, Helium Network, Jupiter, Orca, Metaplex, and Solana Mobile, publishes an annual Solana Security Ecosystem Report, and offers free nonce and multisig monitoring tooling. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched from Sec3's public surface; it is a security-services firm with no self-serve public API.

providers.name: Stellation Care
providers.description: Stellation Care provides AI‑augmented provider intelligence and engagement platforms for health plans and provider groups. Their platform combines advanced algorithms with nationwide Medicare and Medicaid claims data to identify high‑performing providers, optimize network strategies, and improve patient outcomes. Acquired by Skylight Health, they offer solutions for provider performance, network tiering, anomaly detection, and workflow automation.

providers.name: Synchronoss
providers.description: Synchronoss Technologies is a global provider of white-label, operator-branded Personal Cloud and messaging solutions for telecommunications carriers and service providers. Its platform lets subscribers back up, store, manage, and share photos, videos, documents, contacts, messages, and call logs, delivered as a branded cloud experience for operators such as Verizon, AT&T, SoftBank, and BT. Product lines include Personal Cloud, Cloud Insurance, the engageX engagement suite, Advanced Messaging (RCS), and ExpenseNX financial analytics. Synchronoss exposes an API and SDK framework to carrier partners rather than a public self-serve developer portal, so this profile captures the company's public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Tingsn
providers.description: Jiangsu Tingsn Technology (霆升科技) is a Nanjing, China medical-device company focused on ultrasound for cardiac electrophysiology and structural heart disease. It develops intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) products, including the TINGSN Sonic Eyes line of disposable 2D ICE diagnostic catheters — among the first domestically developed ICE catheters approved by China's NMPA (registration 2023) — and TINGSN FINDERS portable color ultrasound systems, with 4D ICE, ultrasound 3D mapping, and ultrasound ablation platforms in development. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners with R&D centers in Nanjing and Massachusetts, Tingsn is a clinical hardware company and publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Tracelytics
providers.description: Tracelytics was a Boston/Providence application-tracing (APM) startup, backed by investors including Google Ventures, that built full-stack distributed tracing for web applications. AppNeta acquired Tracelytics in 2012 and the product became AppNeta TraceView; SolarWinds acquired TraceView in 2016, and AppNeta itself was acquired by Broadcom in 2021. The company no longer operates independently — the tracelytics.com domain no longer resolves and its TraceView Data API (api.tracelytics.com) is defunct — but its verified GitHub organization and first-party TraceView instrumentation packages remain published on RubyGems and npm.

providers.name: Transform
providers.description: Transform (Transform Data) was a metrics-store and semantic-layer company backed by Redpoint Ventures that offered a metrics framework, a metrics catalog, and the MQL (Metrics Query Language) API, and open-sourced the MetricFlow metrics framework. Transform was acquired by dbt Labs (announced February 2023), and its technology lives on as MetricFlow and the dbt Semantic Layer. transform.co now returns a 308 Permanent Redirect to getdbt.com on every path, and the company no longer operates an independent API or developer surface — see the dbt provider profile in this network for the successor APIs.

providers.name: Trygg-Hansa
providers.description: Trygg-Hansa is a Swedish insurance company offering a wide range of insurance products for individuals and businesses, including car, home, travel, health, and life insurance. The company focuses on providing reliable coverage and customer service, leveraging digital channels for policy management and claims handling. As part of the API Evangelist network, its digital presence includes a public website and customer portals, though detailed API specifications are not publicly documented at this time.

providers.name: UK Companies House
providers.description: UK Companies House Data from the UK government

providers.name: Urban Machine
providers.description: Urban Machine is a GV-backed robotics company building AI and computer-vision powered machines that remove metal fasteners (nails, staples, and screws) from construction and demolition lumber waste, reclaiming it for premium wood products and circular-economy reuse. The company publishes no public API, but maintains an open-source ROS/Python robotics tooling footprint on GitHub, including the colcon-poetry-ros package on PyPI.

providers.name: Vertical Semiconductor
providers.description: Vertical Semiconductor is an MIT spinout developing next-generation vertical Gallium Nitride (GaN) power devices for AI data centers and grid infrastructure. Built on a decade of research from MIT's Palacios Group, its vertical GaN transistors push energy conversion closer to the chip with less power loss and heat, targeting high-voltage applications from 100V to over 2kV. The company claims up to 30% higher efficiency, a 50% smaller power footprint, and 10% lower total cost of ownership versus silicon, and has demonstrated its platform on 8-inch wafers using standard silicon CMOS manufacturing. It is a hardware/deep-tech power-electronics company with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface. Backed by Playground Global.

providers.name: Voxeet
providers.description: Voxeet was a San Francisco-based startup that built spatial-audio voice and video conferencing APIs and SDKs for web and mobile applications, backed by 500 Global. Dolby Laboratories acquired Voxeet in 2019 and rebranded its technology as the Dolby.io Communications APIs and SDKs. That surface has since been retired -- the voxeet GitHub org archived all 88 repositories on 2024-08-30 and the Dolby.io Communications documentation now redirects to Dolby OptiView. This profile preserves the historical record; see the dolby and dolby-io profiles for the successor platform.

providers.name: wefox
providers.description: wefox is a Berlin-headquartered digital insurance distribution platform that connects insurance carriers, brokers, and end customers through a single technology stack. Founded in 2014 and originally known as FinanceFox, the company operates across Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, and France, selling personal-lines products such as motor, home, liability, life, and commercial insurance via its in-house carrier (wefox Insurance) and a network of independent brokers. wefox positions itself as an "indirect" insurtech — meaning it distributes through human advisors augmented by software rather than selling direct-to-consumer — and has historically been one of Europe's most highly funded insurtech companies, with backing from Mubadala, Target Global, Salesforce Ventures, OMERS Ventures, Eurazeo, Mountain Partners, and others. The platform itself is a multi-tenant SaaS used by brokers and agents to manage customer relationships, quote and bind policies across multiple carriers, handle claims, and trigger commissions. wefox does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a github.com/wefox organization; integration with the wefox platform is carrier-, broker-, and partner-mediated rather than self-service, and there is no Tier-1 developer surface to document. This repo profiles wefox as an insurance distribution business and tracks any future move toward a public API program.

providers.name: AcreLens
providers.description: Land suitability scoring API for any US property: off-grid, rural, recreational, investment

providers.name: Alan
providers.description: Alan is a Paris-based digital health insurance and wellness company founded in 2016 by Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve and Charles Gorintin. It was the first independent health insurance provider licensed in France in over fifty years and offers an integrated product combining complementary health insurance ("mutuelle"), prevention, and care delivery through a single mobile and web experience. Alan's product surface includes group and individual health plans (Alan Santé), retirement plans (Alan Dolce Vita), public-sector and self-employed offerings, an HR/benefits admin dashboard for employers, an in-house telehealth and chat-care service (Clinique Alan) staffed by salaried clinicians, a gamified prevention and step-tracking program (Alan Play / Alan Mind), and vision/optical benefits with zero out-of-pocket pricing. The company reports over one million members and roughly 33,000 client businesses, operates in France, Belgium, and Spain, and reached a reported €5B valuation in its 2026 Series F round. Engineering and product practice is documented publicly on the Alan Product and Technical Blog at medium.com/alan, and a small portfolio of internal-tools and design assets (most notably react-native-fast-shadow and the Alan Sans typeface) is open-sourced on github.com/alan-eu. Alan does not publish a public-facing developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; all member and employer interactions happen through Alan's first-party apps and the HR/benefits dashboard.

providers.name: Apis Point Energy
providers.description: Apis Point Energy is a physical commodity trading house specializing in distillate in the Northeast United States. It provides risk management solutions, hedging products priced off local terminal prices, and over‑the‑counter swaps and options on a principal‑to‑principal basis. The company serves fuel providers across the country, offering locally‑protected fuel contracts and focusing on Northeast Distillate markets.

providers.name: Arcturusstudio
providers.description: Arcturusstudio, operating as Arcturus Studio, delivers real‑time 3D volumetric video of sports events using computer vision and AI. Their platform enables broadcasters, teams, leagues, and venues to provide immersive, interactive experiences across 2D broadcast, social media, and AR/VR devices. The company also offers data products derived from player and game analytics, supporting coaches and analysts with actionable insights.

providers.name: Autograb
providers.description: AutoGrab provides automotive intelligence platforms across multiple regions, offering real-time vehicle data, market insights, and tools for sourcing, pricing, valuation, and inventory analysis. Their solutions serve dealerships, finance and insurance companies, enhancing decision‑making and operational efficiency through AI‑driven analytics and scalable infrastructure.

providers.name: Avea Robotics
providers.description: Avea Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics software company (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building teleoperation software that lets operators control robots from anywhere in the world with ultra-low latency. Its product, Sentinel, provides real-time remote control, immersive viewing, haptic feedback, and multi-stream video so operators can remotely intervene and keep robots running continuously. The platform supports industrial robotic arms, humanoid robots, and custom systems, and targets use cases such as data collection for Physical AI training, remote real-world robot deployment, and supervised autonomy with human oversight. Integration is handled during onboarding by sharing a robot's URDF and joint control API rather than through a public developer API. As an early-stage startup, Avea Robotics publishes a website, Notion-hosted documentation, and a Substack blog, but does not yet expose a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a self-serve developer platform.

providers.name: Ayannah
providers.description: Ayannah (Ayannah Information Systems, Inc.) is a Philippines-based fintech company providing digital finance and digital commerce services to the emerging middle class across emerging markets, many of whom are migrants and/or unbanked. It operates a market-proven stack of digital financial services spanning payments, commerce, and analytics, reporting 10K+ touchpoints and 50M+ transactions processed. Marquee products include Sendah Direct (a B2B SaaS payment platform for retailers offering mobile top-ups, game credits, and domestic remittance, adopted in 7,000+ outlets), Sendah Remit (bank-grade interoperable international and domestic remittance), Sendah (a B2C gift-remittance service for Overseas Filipinos), and Asira (Indonesian B2B2C/B2C lending, insurance, and investment apps). Ayannah is backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Balance Re
providers.description: Balance Re is a fully licensed German life reinsurance company headquartered in Cologne, with an office in London, offering asset-liability management (ALM) reinsurance solutions to life insurers and pension funds. Its proprietary technology delivers real-time analytics that help clients manage capital and liquidity, price and transfer longevity, savings and retirement risk, and improve competitiveness through quantitative asset-liability management. Balance Re raised a $10M Series A in 2021 led by Anthemis Group, with participation from Global Brain, Roland Berger Industries and Talabot Finance. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the company publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer API, documentation, or machine-readable specifications as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Bedrock Energy
providers.description: Bedrock Energy provides innovative geothermal heating and cooling solutions for residential and commercial properties. Leveraging proprietary drilling technology and advanced data algorithms, the company enables fast, cost-effective borehole installations that deliver high-efficiency, resilient energy performance. Their mission is to make geothermal energy affordable and accessible, reducing energy costs and environmental impact for building owners across the United States.

providers.name: Berlin Brands Group
providers.description: Berlin Brands Group (BBG) is a Berlin‑based holding company that creates, builds, buys and scales consumer brands globally. Founded in 2005, it operates multiple e‑commerce brands across home appliances, audio, lighting and lifestyle, employing thousands and serving European markets.

providers.name: Blacksmith Medicines
providers.description: Blacksmith Medicines is a biotech company focused on developing human metalloenzyme‑targeted medicines. Based in San Diego, the firm leverages a purpose‑built platform to discover and advance novel therapeutics for a range of diseases. Their pipeline includes innovative candidates addressing unmet medical needs, supported by a team of experts in chemistry, biology, and drug development. The company aims to translate cutting‑edge science into safe and effective treatments for patients worldwide.

providers.name: Blink Identity
providers.description: Blink Identity is an Austin, Texas company building a privacy-first facial-recognition identity platform for live entertainment venues, stadiums, and public spaces. Its "identify-in-motion" machine-vision system lets patrons enroll with a smartphone photo, then walk through touchless entry, pay-with-your-face concessions, and automatic loyalty recognition without stopping to scan a ticket. Facial images are converted into encrypted templates rather than stored as photos, and the company is a Techstars Music alumnus that has partnered with Live Nation / Ticketmaster on facial-recognition ticketing. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website; Blink Identity does not currently publish a developer-facing API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Brami
providers.description: Brami is an Italian community-driven nonprofit organization focused on revitalizing local cultural spaces and promoting civic engagement. It operates a platform that connects volunteers, donors, and local authorities to support events, educational programs, and community projects. Through its online portal, Brami facilitates contributions, volunteer sign‑ups, and information sharing, aiming to strengthen neighborhood ties and preserve cultural heritage across Italy.

providers.name: bttn
providers.description: bttn (bttn Inc., trading online as bttnusa.com) is a Seattle, Washington based business-to-business e-commerce marketplace and wholesale distributor of medical supplies, lab equipment and pharmaceuticals, selling name-brand consumables to clinics, dental, veterinary and physical-therapy practices, clinical laboratories, home-healthcare providers and other healthcare buyers across the United States. Founded in 2021 by JT Garwood and Jack Miller and backed by Tiger Global, the company operates a self-serve online storefront carrying 60,000+ catalog products with bulk and volume pricing, same- or next-business-day shipping, quote requests, purchase-order and invoice payment, shopping lists, quick-order pads and recurring reorder tooling. The storefront is a BigCommerce commerce back end fronted by a Catalyst/Next.js application. bttn publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract; its e-commerce surface is buyer-facing only.

providers.name: CarbonBuilt
providers.description: CarbonBuilt produces ultra‑low‑carbon concrete masonry products, replacing up to 50% of cement with its proprietary Reversa® binder. The company offers sustainable building materials that reduce carbon footprints by up to 70% while maintaining price and performance, targeting construction, hardscape and masonry markets worldwide.

providers.name: Cellbri
providers.description: CellBri Bio Innovation Technology Ltd provides automated cell therapy manufacturing platforms. Their modular and all‑in‑one solutions enable biotech and CDMO customers to accelerate development, improve batch success, and ensure GMP‑aligned traceability. With multiple manufacturing centers worldwide, CellBri offers flexible, scalable systems for CAR‑T, TCR, MSC and iPSC therapies, backed by extensive IP and technical expertise.

providers.name: Cellino Biotech
providers.description: Cellino Biotech is a regenerative medicine company focused on personalized cell therapies using advanced iPSC technology. It offers a platform for patient-specific tissue and organ replacement, leveraging AI-driven bioprocessing to scale autologous treatments for a range of degenerative diseases.

providers.name: Clovertherapeutics
providers.description: Clovertherapeutics is developing innovative medicines for diseases of aging. Partnering with patients, providers, payers, and researchers, they integrate genetics with longitudinal clinical records to advance understanding and treatment of age‑related diseases. Their approach focuses on high‑unmet‑need conditions, aiming to accelerate targeted drug development through collaborative research.

providers.name: Cowin
providers.description: Cowin & Company, Inc. is a Birmingham‑based mining construction firm founded in 1924, offering a wide range of underground and surface mining services such as highwall stabilization, aggregate mining, tunnel construction, and shotcrete. With over a century of experience, the company emphasizes safety, skilled personnel, and custom engineering solutions for clients across the United States.

providers.name: Cssmart
providers.description: CS‑Smart is a consulting and analytics firm that helps organizations across sectors—including finance, energy, public‑sector, and telecommunications—make data‑driven decisions. Their services cover market intelligence, behavioral change, crisis management, and digital tracking, delivering strategic insights to improve performance and innovation. The company’s website (cs‑smart.com) provides detailed information about expertise, solutions, and contact options.

providers.name: Dupe
providers.description: Dupe.com is a free AI-powered visual search engine and product-comparison platform that finds near-identical, lower-priced alternatives ("dupes") to designer and higher-priced products. Users paste any product URL, upload an image, or type a description, and Dupe's visual matching surfaces similar items from thousands of online retailers at up to 90% less — spanning furniture, home decor, fashion, footwear, beauty, and more. The service also offers AI research reports, room/outfit restyling, a Chrome extension, an iOS app, and a $DUPE rewards program, and it earns revenue through affiliate commissions at no extra cost to users. Dupe additionally operates a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI assistants can search its catalog programmatically. Backed by Kindred Ventures.

providers.name: Edge Markets
providers.description: EDGE Markets builds financial infrastructure for high-throughput gaming and trading environments, positioning itself as the "financial backbone for a new asset class." Its product line spans EDGE Boost, a high-limit debit platform (up to a $1,000,000 daily limit) with built-in responsible-gaming controls and activity tracking; EDGE Connect, a private payment rail and closed-loop settlement layer that replaces traditional consumer card networks to cut transaction costs and chargebacks; and EDGE Pro, a banking platform (in development) for market makers and institutional investors. The company has raised a $29.2M Series A and partners with gaming and betting operators. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing and newsroom presence only — no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface has been found.

providers.name: Firefly Aerospace
providers.description: Firefly Aerospace is an end-to-end space transportation company building the Alpha small-lift rocket, the Eclipse (formerly MLV) medium-lift vehicle, the Blue Ghost lunar lander, and the Elytra orbital vehicle (with the Ocula lunar imaging service). Firefly sells launch, lunar delivery, and on-orbit services through sales and payload-user-guide channels; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Georgia Power
providers.description: Georgia Power is the largest electric utility in Georgia and a subsidiary of Southern Company. It publishes no public developer API: no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, or developer portal was found, and it offers no Green Button Connect My Data program. Customers can export usage data through My Power Usage and EnergyDirect.

providers.name: GitOps
providers.description: A operational framework that takes DevOps best practices used for application development such as version control, collaboration, compliance, and CI/CD, and applies them to infrastructure automation. GitOps uses Git as a single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications.

providers.name: Govenda
providers.description: Govenda (formerly BoardBookit, acquired by OnBoard in 2024) is board management and governance software - a secure board portal for scheduling and running board and committee meetings, distributing board books and documents, managing directors and members, capturing votes and minutes, and reporting to administrators. Access is delivered through web and mobile applications for board professionals, administrators, directors, and executives. As of this cataloging, Govenda does NOT publish a public or partner developer API, an API reference, or developer documentation. Integration is limited to identity and productivity connectors - single sign-on (for example Okta), Microsoft 365 in-browser collaboration, calendar connectivity, two-factor authentication, and biometric login. Any programmatic or SCIM/provisioning access would need to be arranged directly with Govenda/OnBoard sales; there is no self-serve, documented API surface to model. This entry is therefore a stub - no API endpoints are claimed or modeled.

providers.name: Hims
providers.description: Hims is the men's brand of Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (NYSE: HIMS), a U.S.-based direct-to-consumer telehealth platform. Through forhims.com it connects patients with licensed medical providers and affiliated pharmacies to offer treatment for sexual health, hair loss, dermatology and skincare, mental health, and weight loss, including provider consultations, personalized prescriptions, and recurring subscription fulfillment shipped to the customer. Hims & Hers operates the sibling Hers brand for women and runs its own pharmacy and fulfillment operations. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, security, and trust surface; Hims does not currently publish a public developer API, so this record is identity- and security-focused rather than spec-bearing.

providers.name: Hotelogix
providers.description: Hotelogix is a cloud-based hotel property management system (PMS) headquartered in Noida, India, serving more than 12,000 independent hotels, groups, chains, and resorts across 100+ countries since 2008. The platform provides front desk management, reservations, point-of-sale, housekeeping, revenue management, multi-property and group management, a web booking engine, a guest service mobile app, and an integrated channel manager that distributes inventory to OTAs and GDS. Hotelogix exposes a partner Web API (HAPI) at developer.hotelogix.net that uses XML POST over HTTP rather than REST/JSON, enabling channel managers, payment gateways, accounting systems, CRMs, loyalty programs, door locks, ID scanners, and in-room devices to integrate with the PMS. Documentation is split into Web (booking engine), Admin, and Frontdesk surfaces. There is no public OpenAPI specification, no public SDK, and no public GitHub org content; partner access and credentials are granted on request through the Hotelogix support and partnership teams. Revenue model is SaaS subscriptions per hotel/room along with an integration marketplace ecosystem.

providers.name: Jawbone
providers.description: Jawbone was a consumer electronics company known for its wearable fitness trackers and Bluetooth headsets. Founded in 1999, the company focused on integrating health and activity monitoring into everyday accessories, offering products like the Jawbone UP series and the Jambox speaker. Although it ceased operations in 2017, its legacy includes pioneering the use of motion sensors and cloud-based data analytics in personal health devices, influencing the modern wearable market.

providers.name: Karpatia Benefits
providers.description: Karpatia Benefits is an all-in-one corporate employee-benefits management platform used by 100+ companies to administer insurance, sports and education allowances, and mental-health support for distributed teams. It combines a benefits marketplace of 40+ partner vendors offering corporate discounts, reimbursement processing, and HR analytics dashboards, and says it removes roughly 95% of the administrative work of running a benefits program. The company primarily serves Ukrainian companies with multi-country localization. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer API is published at this time.

providers.name: Kindbody
providers.description: Kindbody is a national fertility and family-building clinic network and employer benefit provider. Services include IVF, egg freezing, embryo banking, male fertility care, LGBTQ+ family building, oncofertility, gestational surrogacy, and egg donation, plus a wellness layer (Kindbody360) and lab testing (Kindlabs). Kindbody operates a direct-to-employer fertility benefit and partners with payers; clinical workflows are exposed through a Patient Portal, an online scheduling system, and a Referring Provider Portal. No public developer or partner API has been identified - integration appears to be handled through gated employer and payer onboarding. This entry catalogs the company surface for the API Evangelist index.

providers.name: Lakemedelsverket (Swedish Medical Products Agency)
providers.description: Lakemedelsverket (Swedish Medical Products Agency) is a Swedish governmental authority responsible for promoting public and animal health concerning medicines, medical devices, and cosmetics. It oversees the regulation, approval, and monitoring of pharmaceuticals and related products to ensure safety and efficacy for the Swedish population.

providers.name: Limbo
providers.description: Limbo is a direct-to-consumer digital weight-loss and metabolic-health program operated by Vitals in View, Inc., with subsidiaries in the UK (company no. 15047668) and Ireland (company no. 725671). Members wear a body-worn "energy sensor" that reads metabolic signals, and a companion app turns those readings into personalized, nudge-based guidance intended to change eating habits without calorie counting. The company is Seedcamp-backed, raised a seed round in September 2022, and is mid-rebrand from Limbo (limborevolution.com) to Viv (viv.co), with the marketing site now served from content.viv.co. Limbo publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and probed security posture only.

providers.name: Matchday
providers.description: Matchday is a consumer mobile platform for collecting officially licensed digital football (soccer) player cards and building a squad, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The product is a business-to-consumer collecting and squad-building experience delivered through its mobile apps and website at matchday.com.
