providers.name: AgZen
providers.description: AgZen is an MIT spinout building RealCoverage, a sensor- and AI-based system that measures and controls how many droplets of crop-protection product land on every leaf during agricultural spraying. A boom-mounted computer-vision sensor analyzes spray coverage and droplet quality in real time and displays actionable data on an in-cab tablet, automatically optimizing foliar sprays on any sprayer as the operator drives. Growers use RealCoverage to cut chemical and water use by up to 50% while maintaining or improving efficacy and yield, with a typical payback in under a year. RealCoverage retrofits onto any generation of sprayer and won Crop Protection Solution of the Year in 2025. AgZen is headquartered at Greentown Labs in Somerville, Massachusetts and is backed by DCVC Bio, Material Impact, Astanor Ventures, and Syngenta Group Ventures.

providers.name: Aijia Home Furnishing Products
providers.description: Aijia Home Furnishing Products (艾佳生活, operated by 江苏艾佳家居用品有限公司 / Jiangsu Aijia Home Furnishing Products Co., Ltd.) is a Nanjing-based Chinese internet home-furnishing and home-improvement platform, founded in 2015 as a joint venture of Jiangsu Yide Group and Central China (Jianye) Group. It sells a one-stop packaged fit-out for newly delivered apartments — design, hard decoration, soft furnishing, construction, acceptance, delivery and after-sales — plus its 全品家 furniture suites, distributed through property-developer partnerships across 25 Chinese provinces and 500-plus residential projects. It raised a RMB 1 billion Series B led by Tiantu Capital in 2018 at a valuation above USD 1 billion and launched Dramatic Reality (DR), an AI design platform, in 2019. Its public surface is a Chinese-language consumer website, a mobile site, a consumer app and a login-only merchant console; it publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Aikenong
providers.description: Aikenong (爱科农 / Beijing Aikenong Technology Co., Ltd., also trading internationally as ICAN) is a Chinese smart-agriculture company founded in 2016 in Chaoyang District, Beijing. It builds a proprietary plant-soil-atmosphere crop growth model and a data-driven agronomy platform (ICAN) that combines satellite and UAV remote sensing, weather and soil telemetry, and AI prediction into whole-season planting decision guidance for growers. Its product line spans the Aigengyun (爱耕耘) grower app and WeChat mini program, Aigengyun Enterprise and Business editions for farming enterprises and agri-input dealers, the AIGROW breeding information management system, a high-yield irrigation control system, and a catalogue of field hardware (weather stations, soil moisture stations, smart valves, fertigation controllers, greenhouse controllers, phenotyping cameras and inspection robots). The company reports service across roughly ten Chinese provinces and 30,000+ growers, and raised more than CNY 100 million in Series A/A+ rounds led by Source Code Capital, IDG Capital and GL Ventures. It is a SaaS and hardware vendor rather than an API vendor: no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract is published anywhere on its own domains as of this profile.

providers.name: Alexion Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Alexion Pharmaceuticals was a global biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, focused on developing life-transforming therapies for rare diseases. Founded in 1992, the company pioneered complement inhibition therapy and developed leading treatments for rare hematological and neurological conditions including Soliris (eculizumab) and Ultomiris (ravulizumab). AstraZeneca acquired Alexion in July 2021 for $39 billion, and the company now operates as Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease. The combined entity maintains research programs in complement biology, hematology, nephrology, neurology, metabolic disorders, cardiology, and ophthalmology. Alexion's GitHub organization (alxndgb) hosts research tools including genomic data analysis platforms, precision medicine knowledge graphs, and rare disease target discovery systems.

providers.name: AnySignal
providers.description: AnySignal delivers an end‑to‑end RF platform that provides spectrum supremacy for mission‑critical environments across space, land, air, and sea. Their solutions combine hardware, software, and orchestration tools to enable reliable, low‑latency communications for aerospace, defense, and national security customers. The platform includes capabilities such as communications, electronic warfare, autonomous systems, radar, and a resilient network, supporting both commercial and government missions.

providers.name: Aoquan
providers.description: Auquan (formerly Aoquan) provides agentic AI solutions for institutional finance, automating data collection, analysis, and reporting workflows. Their platform enables finance professionals to reduce manual effort, accelerate decision‑making, and focus on strategic insights across credit, sustainability, and investor relations. The company offers a suite of AI‑driven tools, a sandbox environment, and integrations that streamline complex financial processes.

providers.name: Arzeda
providers.description: Arzeda Corp is a Seattle, Washington protein design company — "The Protein Design Company" — founded in 2008 by David Baker (2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry), Alexandre Zanghellini and colleagues out of the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design. Its Intelligent Protein Design Technology combines physics-based computational protein design, generative AI and an agentic design-build-test-learn loop over fifteen years of proprietary in-house experimental data to create designer enzymes and proteins that do not exist in nature, then scale them to commercial production. Commercial programs span food and beverage (ViaLeaf Reb M / ProSweet Reb M stevia sweeteners with MANE), home and personal care enzymes (Unilever), advanced materials (W. L. Gore & Associates) and pharmaceutical biologics (Takeda), alongside DARPA and NSF funded work on AI-driven protein design and cell-free biomanufacturing. Arzeda co-founded the OpenFold consortium for open-source protein structure prediction. It sells designed molecules and joint development programs, not software, and publishes no public developer program, API or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Basis Set Ventures
providers.description: Basis Set Ventures is an AI-native, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2017 by Dr. Lan Xuezhao and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. The firm invests at the seed and early stages in founders building artificial intelligence across AI infrastructure, autonomous systems, molecular and materials discovery, agentic development tooling, intelligent collaboration, and automated workflows. Basis Set announced a $250M Fund IV and describes itself as "the first capital when it's just you and your vision," pairing capital with an operator-led founder concierge team. Portfolio companies include Path Robotics, Quince, Sakana AI, Tigris Data, Mem0, OpenArt, Cusp, Simular, Vizcom, and Entire. This is an API Evangelist network profile of the firm; Basis Set Ventures does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so this record captures firm identity, web properties, and derived security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Baya Systems
providers.description: Baya Systems is a semiconductor IP company accelerating intelligent compute with chiplets. Backed by Matrix Partners and Intel Capital and based in Santa Clara, California (with offices in Austin, Texas and Bengaluru, India), Baya provides the WeaverPro software platform and the WeaveIP unified fabric and cache IP portfolio. Together they let system architects analyze, design and post-silicon tune optimal single-die or multi-die, chiplet-ready Network-on-Chip (NoC) interconnect systems, with multi-level coherency and multicast for AI acceleration scaling into petabytes per second across hyperscale, enterprise, AI, automotive, GPU and IoT markets. Baya Systems does not publish a public developer API, portal or SDK at this time; this API Evangelist network profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Beijinginstituteoftechnologygenshutechnology
providers.description: Beijing Institute of Technology Genshu Technology Co., Ltd. (北京理工亘舒科技有限公司) was founded in December 2016. It focuses on the commercialization of aerospace biomedical technology, offering high-end cold chain equipment, space microfluidic medical testing, smart traditional Chinese medicine platforms, space payload services, and STEAM education. Backed by Beijing Institute of Technology and collaborations with aerospace academies, it operates as a specialized high‑tech enterprise.

providers.name: Bestselfco
providers.description: Bestselfco creates personal development tools, planners, journals, and decks aimed at improving productivity, relationships, and personal growth. Their product line includes the BestSelf Planner, Self Journal, Intimacy Deck, and various digital downloads, marketed through their e‑commerce site bestself.co.

providers.name: Blank Rome
providers.description: Blank Rome LLP is an Am Law 100 U.S. law firm founded in 1946 and headquartered in Philadelphia, with approximately 600+ attorneys across roughly 14 U.S. offices plus an international presence (Shanghai). The firm provides comprehensive legal and government-advocacy services across commercial and corporate litigation, corporate / M&A and finance, restructuring and bankruptcy, government contracts, intellectual property, labor and employment, real estate, tax, white-collar defense, matrimonial and family law, and a nationally recognized maritime and international trade practice. Blank Rome Government Relations LLC, the firm's affiliated lobbying arm, operates from Washington, D.C. The firm publishes practice-area client alerts, the Mainbrace maritime newsletter, and industry insights through its website's News & Events and Publications sections. Blank Rome does not operate a public developer program, REST/GraphQL API, SDK ecosystem, or GitHub organization; this profile catalogs the firm's public-facing knowledge surface (practice pages, newsletters, alerts) rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Bota Biosciences
providers.description: Bota Biosciences (Bota Bio, 恩和科技) is an industrial and synthetic biology company that applies AI-driven computation and laboratory automation to bio-manufacturing. Its in-house Bota Biofoundry and Cell2Cloud platforms combine computational algorithms, non-model industrial strain engineering, rapid iterative enzyme engineering and performance protein design to shorten design-build-test-learn cycles, and in March 2026 it launched SAION AI, a three-layer "Physical AI" platform (cognition, orchestration, execution) that drives laboratory hardware through a proprietary Biological Protocol Language. Bota commercializes this work as physical ingredients rather than software: Purtect bio-preservatives (nisin, natamycin, ε-poly-lysine, lysozyme), Prorylia biomimetic proteins and Re² Coffea Arabica peptides, sold through its HeliaGenesis food and nutrition brand and its YuccaElements personal care brand, with partnerships including BASF, Proya, Syensqo and Puratos. Founded in 2019 with operations in Hangzhou, China and the San Francisco Bay Area, Bota publishes no developer portal, no public API documentation, no SDKs and no machine-readable specification; its computational software is internal laboratory tooling and its SAION AI application is reachable only through a login with an administrator-managed account whitelist.

providers.name: Bowery Capital
providers.description: Bowery Capital is a B2B-focused venture capital firm that leads Pre-Seed and Seed rounds in founders "modernizing business through technology." It concentrates on SaaS and marketplace companies, with particular interest in vertical AI and back-office software, and takes lead-investor positions that it supports hands-on through four pillars: Growth (go-to-market and sales enablement), Talent (hiring, culture, and benefits), Business Development (pipeline and customer introductions), and a Revenue Council advisory network of operators. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Foundry Group. Bowery Capital is an investor rather than an API provider and publishes no developer API surface.

providers.name: Bridgewire
providers.description: Bridgewire connects Telegram and WhatsApp so your messages, photos, and videos flow between them automatically — no manual forwarding, nothing missed. It provides real‑time bi‑directional messaging, enabling seamless communication across platforms for individuals and businesses.

providers.name: Brik
providers.description: Brik ("[Re]Constructing Construction") is an Indonesian construction-materials company, backed by Accel, that operates concrete batching plants and supplies ready-mix concrete for building and infrastructure projects across the Greater Jakarta region, including Bekasi, Bogor, Karawang, and Bandung. Its product line spans standard ready-mix batches and higher-performance "Super Concrete" variants used for mass-concrete pours. At the time of enrichment Brik publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Buildcon
providers.description: Buildcon is a Belgrade-based construction and logistics digitalisation company that builds Buildx, a proprietary construction project management platform covering project scheduling, cost tracking, daily logs, installed-quantities tracking, and reporting, alongside Buildx Warehouse for warehouse management and Buildx Tracking for real-time asset tracking. The team pairs deep construction and logistics domain knowledge with a modern web stack (React, Angular, Node.js, PostgreSQL on AWS/DigitalOcean) to help builders and logistics operators move off spreadsheets and onto connected operational software. Buildcon is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Businesscanvas
providers.description: Business Canvas is a business development and client acquisition advisory firm helping established B2B service businesses strengthen market positioning, attract better-fit clients, and develop more effective acquisition approaches around buyer behavior. It offers a 4‑Pillar Accelerator Program and strategic consulting to improve revenue growth and client quality for service firms.

providers.name: Buymed
providers.description: Buymed leverages technology, innovation, and data to build a seamless, intelligent pharmaceutical supply chain that connects manufacturers, distributors, hospitals, pharmacies and patients across Vietnam, Cambodia, and Thailand. Founded in 2018, it aims to provide faster, fairer, and more efficient access to healthcare, empowering better outcomes for millions.

providers.name: Byanat
providers.description: Byanat is an Oman-based, award-winning AI company offering a unified platform for optimizing digital infrastructure across telecommunications networks and data centers. The platform pairs system-wide visibility with custom-tailored automation to scale operations, ensure compliance, and promote sustainability, an approach the company frames as "Infrastructure 4.0." Its product families span mobile network solutions (site management, degradation detection, auto-discovery, performance analytics), data centre solutions (predictive analytics, capacity forecasting, energy management, infrastructure monitoring), and an API and integration layer for cross-platform connectivity and AI-powered workflow automation. Byanat is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference; its API and integration capability is delivered as a managed product.

providers.name: Calidi Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Calidi Biotherapeutics is a biotechnology company focused on developing genetically engineered cell therapies for cancer and other complex diseases. Based in the United States, Calidi leverages its proprietary platform to deliver precise genetic medicines to disease sites, advancing pipelines in oncology and beyond. The company provides detailed scientific information, pipeline updates, and investor relations through its corporate website.

providers.name: Carbon America
providers.description: Carbon America is a carbon capture and storage (CCS) developer focused on delivering the full CO₂ capture‑transport‑storage value chain. The company designs, builds, and operates large‑scale CCS projects, partnering with emitters, communities, and investors to reduce industrial emissions and combat climate change. With a mission to make climate change history, Carbon America leverages its proprietary technology and expertise to create secure geological storage solutions worldwide.

providers.name: Cellworks
providers.description: Cellworks provides actionable AI for individualized precision medicine, integrating mechanistic biology, clinical guidelines, and over 300 million patient records to predict individual drug responses. Their platform serves bio‑pharma companies, physicians, and health systems with tools for case analysis, evidence generation, and therapeutic decision support.

providers.name: CH2M Hill
providers.description: CH2M Hill was a global engineering, consulting, design, construction and operations firm providing services for corporations and federal, state, and local governments. Headquartered in Englewood, Colorado, the firm delivered work in water, transportation, environment, energy, industrial, and facilities markets. In December 2017 CH2M was acquired by Jacobs Engineering (now Jacobs Solutions) and its operations have been integrated into Jacobs. As of the acquisition, CH2M Hill no longer publishes a standalone public API program; relevant digital engineering, project delivery, and data services are now offered under the Jacobs brand.

providers.name: Cloudmosa
providers.description: CloudMosa, Inc. is a cloud technology innovator founded in 2009, known for its Puffin browser and Cloud Phone solutions that offload web rendering to the cloud. The company focuses on security‑first remote browser isolation, improving performance for low‑end devices and enhancing user privacy. Over a decade, CloudMosa has expanded its offerings to include cloud‑based browsing, enterprise solutions, and developer tools, serving millions of devices worldwide.

providers.name: Cogent Security
providers.description: Cogent Security LLC, founded in 2010, provides security services for U.S. government and defense sectors. Offering risk management, intelligence, counterintelligence, security engineering, and technical surveillance, the company supports the National Nuclear Security Administration and other federal agencies. In 2022 Cogent expanded by acquiring Innovative Technology Partnerships, broadening its capabilities across program management, cloud services, and advanced security programs. The firm emphasizes independent, interdisciplinary expertise to deliver comprehensive security solutions.

providers.name: Conundrum
providers.description: Conundrum (Conundrum Industrial Ltd, Cambridge, UK) is an industrial AI company building AI-driven, closed-loop advanced process control (APC) and model predictive control (MPC) software for the metals, mining, and cement industries. Its platform combines physics-informed and machine-learning models with real-time controllers, optimizers, data-quality tooling, interactive process-flow diagrams, drag-and-drop dashboards, and a Python SDK for building configurable runtime applications. Conundrum optimizes crushing, grinding, flotation, and cement processes to raise throughput and metal recovery while reducing energy consumption, deployed on-premises or in the cloud across plants running 24/7. The company is backed by Speedinvest and reports deployments across multiple plants in several countries.

providers.name: ConXtech
providers.description: ConXtech is a Pleasanton, California structural steel subcontractor that designs, fabricates, delivers and erects prefabricated steel building frames for commercial construction. Its ConX Systems product line — the XL-400 and XR-200 chassis — uses patented collar-and-column connection technology and AISC 358 seismic prequalification to erect frames the company reports are three to five times faster than traditional steel erection, across healthcare, data center, retail, office, education, high-density residential, hospitality, industrial and government projects totalling more than 20 million square feet. ConXtech is a private company; its equity trades on secondary markets. It sells a physical building system, not software, and publishes no public developer program, API or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Cova
providers.description: Cova is an AI-native home care agency licensed in Michigan and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026). The company serves Medicaid, long-term care insurance (LTCI), and private-pay patients, pays caregivers the highest base rate in the state, and helps unpaid family caregivers get paid through programs they may not know they qualify for. Cova operates a home care platform that connects caregivers with families needing in-home assistance, using an AI-driven operational model to reduce traditional agency overhead while maximizing caregiver compensation. Founded in 2026 by Jordan Ibe and Ansh Tandon, the team is based in Detroit, Michigan. Cova also runs MichiganHomeHelp.com as a Medicaid Home Help information resource. As a consumer home-care service, Cova does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Cozen O'Connor
providers.description: Cozen O'Connor is a full-service U.S. law firm founded in 1970 and headquartered in Philadelphia, with more than 1,000 attorneys across 33+ offices in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The firm is ranked among the top 100 law firms in America and is best known for its nationally recognized subrogation, insurance, labor and employment, global corporate, intellectual property, and government relations practices. Cozen O'Connor Public Strategies, the firm's bipartisan federal, state, and local government affairs and lobbying arm, operates from Washington, D.C. and major state capitals. The firm operates an unusually broad thought-leadership network of LexBlog/WordPress-powered blogs and podcasts (subrogation, cyber law, health law, state AGs, transformative AI, OSHA, employment law, family law, property insurance, casualty coverage, real estate / land use, professional responsibility, and a Public Strategies feed), each of which exposes a standard `/feed/` RSS endpoint. Cozen O'Connor does not operate a public developer program, REST/GraphQL API, SDK ecosystem, or GitHub organization. This profile catalogs the firm's public-facing knowledge surface — practice and industry pages, attorney directory, ancillary businesses, lobbying arm, and the blog/podcast RSS network — rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: DIVE studios
providers.description: DIVE Studios is a global K-entertainment media platform that produces original shows, podcasts, and short-form social content, reaching over 135M Gen Z and Millennial fans and 5B+ lifetime views. The company operates two commercial arms: DIVE Media, which sells advertising and branded content across its podcast, video, and social network, and DIVE Agency (DIVE X), which builds creator, influencer, and celebrity marketing campaigns for global brands connecting with K-culture audiences. It publishes an llms.txt describing its pages but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or portal. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Doos
providers.description: Doos is a Saudi-based quick-commerce (q-commerce) platform and mobile app that delivers groceries, fresh produce, beauty, gifting, pharmacy, and lifestyle products in minutes across Saudi Arabia. Founded in 2023 by Tala Al Sahsah, it operates cloud/dark stores in Jeddah and Riyadh with localised assortments, prices, and promotions by city and delivery zone, offering a bilingual (Arabic/English) shopping experience. Doos is backed by 500 Global and received a strategic investment from Jahez to accelerate its expansion in the Kingdom's growing quick-commerce sector. This is a consumer-facing storefront; no public developer program or API has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Drexel University
providers.description: Drexel University is a private research university in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with roughly 24,000 students and a Carnegie R1 (very high research activity) classification. Drexel is internationally known for its cooperative education (co-op) program, which embeds full-time professional work experience into undergraduate degrees. Core enterprise systems run on Ellucian Banner, surfaced to students and staff through the DrexelOne portal. Drexel does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open data portal; the organization's GitHub org (drexel-university) currently lists no public repositories, and library, catalog, and IT service pages do not expose documented integration endpoints. This profile is maintained as a tier-3 no-public-API index entry.

providers.name: Drivemate
providers.description: Drivemate is a peer-to-peer car-sharing and car-rental marketplace based in Bangkok, Thailand, founded in 2016. The platform lets vehicle owners list their cars and lets travelers and residents rent directly from those owners through the Drivemate mobile app and website, handling booking, verification, insurance and payments end to end. Drivemate operates one of the largest car-rental selections in Thailand with more than 3,000 vehicles across 35 provinces and a community of over 100,000 users, and has raised Series A funding from investors including 500 Global (500 Startups), NetSol, Isuzu UNT and Colopl Next. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public digital and developer surface; Drivemate is a consumer mobility marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API program, so this record captures identity, distribution and domain-security signals rather than API specifications.

providers.name: Ducks Unlimited
providers.description: API explorer that gives a query URL with a JSON response of locations and cities

providers.name: Easel AI
providers.description: Easel AI is a Los Angeles based generative AI company building a consumer app and a partner-facing image generation platform. Its models turn a single selfie into photorealistic single and multiplayer avatars without any per-user AI training, and the same technology is packaged for commercial use as Fashion Photoshoot (AI models of any race or body type wearing any outfit), Fashion Try-On (shoppers upload a picture and see themselves in an outfit instantly), Ad Creator (personalized ad creative from one selfie plus a context image), and Product Photoshoot (products placed in any scenario). Easel ships a consumer iOS app and markets a Try-On API and ad-generation API to fashion brands, ad platforms, messaging apps, dating and social apps, and talent agencies monetizing digital IP. As of this pass the API surface is partner-gated and contact-sales only - there is no public developer portal, documentation, API reference, machine-readable specification, or self-serve signup published on the website. Easel appears on the a16z investment list.

providers.name: eBPF Foundation
providers.description: The eBPF Foundation is a Linux Foundation project that advances eBPF technology by guiding upstream development, promoting its benefits, and enhancing its security and reliability. eBPF enables programmable kernel functionality for networking, observability, tracing, and security without changing kernel source code. The Foundation itself does not operate a public API; it stewards the technology and community.

providers.name: EnerVenue
providers.description: EnerVenue is a Fremont, California-based energy infrastructure company building long-duration stationary energy storage using a metal-hydrogen (nickel-hydrogen) battery chemistry derived from NASA-heritage technology that has powered the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station since the 1980s. Co-founded by Stanford materials scientist Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue refined the orbital nickel-hydrogen cell into a grid-scale "Energy Storage Vessel" (ESV) targeting a 30-year, 30,000+ cycle service life with 100% usable depth of discharge, ~90% round-trip efficiency, an operating range of -20 C to +60 C, no thermal runaway risk, and no active thermal management. The ESV's aqueous metal cell (AMC) uses a nickel hydroxide cathode, a nickel-alloy anode, an alkaline electrolyte, and hermetically sealed hydrogen gas storage built from steel, nickel, fiberglass, resin, and water — no lithium, cobalt, or rare earths. EnerVenue is scaling manufacturing through a one-million- square-foot gigafactory in Shelby County, Kentucky (1 GWh phase one, scaling toward 20 GWh per year with ~$1B of follow-on investment) plus a high-volume line in Changzhou, China (250 MWh by Q3 2026, 1 GWh in 2027). Customer commitments exceed 7 GWh and include Pine Gate Renewables (2.4 GWh, multi-year), Green Energy Renewable Solutions (Nicon Industries), Sonnell Power Solutions, and VedantaESS. The company closed a $300M Series B in 2026 to fund the gigafactory build-out. EnerVenue sells hardware, EPC-integrated storage systems, and long-duration service warranties — it does not publish a developer API, SDK, public OpenAPI specification, or open-source repository.

providers.name: eSpark
providers.description: eSpark is a K-5 adaptive learning platform that extends a district's core reading and math programs with differentiated, standards-aligned practice in reading, math, and writing. The platform uses adaptive lesson sequencing that adjusts difficulty to each student's performance, interest-based content, and real-time feedback to deliver personalized instruction, and it reports back to teachers and administrators on student progress. eSpark serves 10,000+ schools and districts nationwide and rosters students through Clever, ClassLink, Google Classroom, and QR-code sign-in. eSpark was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile captures company identity, its public web properties, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Essential AI
providers.description: Essential AI is a San Francisco artificial-intelligence research company founded in 2023 by Ashish Vaswani and Niki Parmar, two co-authors of the 2017 "Attention Is All You Need" transformer paper. The company builds open-source models, datasets, and training infrastructure to keep frontier AI capability in the open rather than behind closed platforms. Its flagship release is the Rnj-1 family — 8B-parameter dense base and instruction-tuned models with a 32K context window, trained from scratch and tuned for code generation, STEM and mathematical reasoning, and agentic tool use, published under Apache 2.0. Essential AI also publishes Essential-Web v1.0, a large document-level web dataset organized by a twelve-category taxonomy, the EAI taxonomy classifier models and domain-filtered corpora, and research on the Muon optimizer, grokking, reflection, long-context perplexity, and large-scale training infrastructure. Distribution is through Hugging Face, GitHub, a Homebrew cask for the RNJ macOS desktop app, and third-party inference platforms (Together AI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio). As of this profile Essential AI operates no first-party public HTTP API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract — its public interface is open model weights, datasets, and research code.

providers.name: Essity
providers.description: Essity is a Swedish-headquartered global hygiene and health company operating across four business areas: Health & Medical, Personal Care, Consumer Tissue, and Professional Hygiene. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ESSITY) and owns roughly 40 brands including TENA (incontinence care), Tork (professional hygiene), Libero (baby diapers), Libresse / Bodyform / Nana / Saba / Nuvenia / Libra (feminine care), Modibodi and Knix (period underwear), JOBST (compression hosiery), Leukoplast (adhesive bandages), Cutimed, Sorbact, Hydrofera and Actimove (wound care, sports medicine, orthopedic supports), Delta-Cast (casting), and consumer tissue brands Lotus, Zewa, Tempo, Cushelle, Plenty, Velvet, Regio, Sorbent and Purex. No public developer-facing APIs or developer portal have been identified for Essity; this repository tracks corporate, brand, sustainability, investor, and integration surfaces for ongoing API discovery. The company's Tork brand ships a connected washroom data platform — Tork Vision Cleaning — which is the closest thing to a public data surface in the portfolio.

providers.name: Ethonai
providers.description: EthonAI AG is an ETH Zurich spin-off (founded 2021, Zurich, Switzerland) that builds an Industrial AI Platform — the Manufacturing Analytics System (MAS). It applies Causal AI through a no-code platform so manufacturing engineers can move from reactive dashboards to prescriptive quality and process analytics, deploying models to production in hours. The platform ships as Analyst, Inspector, and Operator modules, is cloud-agnostic (AWS, GCP, Azure), and is API-first: data flows in and out via a REST API, MQTT streaming, and a Python SDK for notebooks and custom applications. EthonAI is used by manufacturers including Siemens, Bosch, Roche, and Lindt & Sprüngli, is part of the Siemens Xcelerator ecosystem, and is backed by Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Earlybird, and Founderful. It does not publish a public API reference or developer portal; its API and SDK are documented inside the authenticated product.

providers.name: Ezy
providers.description: ezy is a graphical gRPC and gRPC-Web client for testing and debugging gRPC services with an intuitive desktop interface.

providers.name: Fantasmo
providers.description: Fantasmo builds CPS (Camera Positioning System), a computer-vision positioning technology it positions as a "camera-powered GPS replacement" delivering hyper-accurate localization that works indoors and in dense urban environments where satellite GPS degrades, using only a device camera and a data connection rather than additional infrastructure. Its target applications span micromobility (scooter/bike tracking and theft prevention), robotics navigation, mobile augmented-reality experiences, and automotive lane-level positioning. Fantasmo was a Techstars-backed startup and was acquired by Niantic in 2022; the public fantasmo.io site remains online but exposes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI surface at this time. This profile was enriched from the provider's public web presence and live DNS/TLS/HTTP probes.

providers.name: Flapico
providers.description: Flapico is a technology company specializing in AI and infrastructure, operating like a lab that builds products and services for the next generation of web users. The company focuses on rebuilding the web for agents and humans, offering AI-driven solutions, fast iteration, and a philosophy of loud, clear error handling. Flapico ships its own products, runs them first, and emphasizes rapid development and innovation across its portfolio.

providers.name: Hawk-Eye Innovations
providers.description: Hawk-Eye Innovations is a Basingstoke, UK-headquartered sports technology company and part of the Sony Group, specializing in precision optical tracking, electronic officiating, video replay, and performance analytics across 25+ professional sports in 100+ countries. Founded in 2001 by Paul Hawkins and acquired by Sony in 2011, Hawk-Eye operates alongside Pulselive and Beyond Sports within Sony's sports division. The company is the standard for ball-tracking in tennis (Electronic Line Calling, now used in place of human line judges at the major tours), goal-line technology and semi-automated offside in football (Premier League, FIFA), video replay in cricket (DRS), NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, rugby, and PGA Tour shot-tracking. Core product platforms include SMART Replay, SMART Track, SMART Insight, HawkAR, iHawk, HawkREPLAY, HawkNEST, HawkVISION, SkeleTRACK, Electronic Line Calling, Goal Line Technology, Semi-Automated Offside Technology, and VAR systems. Revenue comes from long-term contracts with leagues, federations, and broadcasters; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hawk-Eye products. All integrations are bespoke and delivered through Sony Sports Business / Hawk-Eye operations teams.

providers.name: Home24
providers.description: Home24 is a leading pure-play home & living e-commerce retailer in Continental Europe, founded in Berlin in 2009. It operates across Germany, France, Austria, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Belgium and Italy, selling furniture and home accessories through home24.de and its sister storefronts with a catalog of more than 250,000 products, alongside its own private labels and logistics network. Since April 2023 Home24 SE has been part of the Austrian XXXLutz Group, and it was delisted from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in September 2023. Home24 publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI definition; its programmatic surfaces are a partner/affiliate marketing program and marketplace seller integrations used to syndicate product-data feeds, plus a public engineering blog. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the API-artifact facets are not applicable because there is no public API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Host Hotels & Resorts
providers.description: Host Hotels & Resorts is a leading lodging real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns luxury and upper-upscale hotels operating under premium brands in major U.S. and international markets. No public APIs are offered.

providers.name: Ideal Power Converters
providers.description: Ideal Power Inc. (NASDAQ: IPWR), formerly Ideal Power Converters, is an Austin, Texas power semiconductor company developing bidirectional bipolar junction transistor (B-TRAN) technology for ultra-low conduction losses, bidirectional current flow, and fast fault protection and switching. Its product portfolio includes B-TRAN power switches, SymCool power modules, and B-TRAN Known Good Die, targeting data centers, energy storage systems, power grids, solid-state circuit breakers, and EV charging infrastructure. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the company publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: imyup
providers.description: imyup (imyup.com) is a WordPress-powered content website publishing how-to guides, reviews, and download articles focused on mobile gaming (PUBG Mobile, GTA, FIFA, racing and bike games) alongside jobs and general-information posts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass the public site exposes no API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; the only machine-readable artifacts discovered are an auto-generated llms.txt and a public XML sitemap. This profile remains a content publication rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Incandor
providers.description: Incandor is a San Francisco based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building behavioral intelligence infrastructure for fraud and abuse detection. Rather than relying on identity verification at account creation, Incandor constructs a behavioral map of every user on a platform from how they physically interact with an app or website — mouse dynamics, keystroke timing, scroll patterns, and on mobile how a device is held. It requires no fraud labels and no enrollment period, working from the first session. At the individual level it identifies account takeovers with greater than 99 percent accuracy; at the population level it separates out coordinated fraud rings, mule operators, shared operators, bots and agents, and coerced or duress sessions. Incandor is delivered as a programmable API and a client-side telemetry SDK rather than a black-box risk score, letting fraud teams combine behavioral signals with their own transaction history, customer records, and business rules. It collects only behavioral signals — not what users type, read, or view — keeping user data private by design. The company was founded by Matthew Yekell (CEO) and Luc Rosenzweig (CTO), both Stanford CS graduates. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; the developer platform is currently early access.

providers.name: Insilico Medicine
providers.description: Insilico Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company applying generative AI and robotic automation to drug discovery and development. Its Pharma.AI software suite includes PandaOmics (target discovery from multi-omics data), Chemistry42 (generative chemistry with retrosynthesis, property prediction, and ADMET), Generative Biologics, inClinico (clinical trial outcome prediction), Science42 DORA (research assistant), Nach01, and PreciousGPT-family models for life sciences. The company runs its own therapeutic pipeline spanning oncology, fibrosis, and inflammation, with programs targeting TNIK, USP1, QPCTL, PHD, MAT2A, TEAD, ENPP1, KAT6 and others through Phase II. Insilico monetizes through Pharma.AI software licensing, partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies, and progression of its in-house assets. Pharma.AI tools are commercial SaaS products accessed via web UI; the company publishes open-source research code on GitHub (GENTRL, fcd_torch, BiAAE, DD-VAE, DORA) but does not expose a public commercial API.

providers.name: Isomorphic Labs
providers.description: Isomorphic Labs is a London-based AI-first drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind in 2021 and operating as an Alphabet subsidiary. Founded and led by Sir Demis Hassabis, the company applies frontier AI — including derivatives of the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system and its proprietary Unified Drug Design Engine — to accelerate the design of small-molecule and biologic therapeutics across oncology, immunology, and other therapeutic areas. The Drug Design Engine is positioned as a target- and disease-agnostic, multi-modality platform that combines predictive and generative models with a curated proprietary life-science "Dataverse" and large-scale GPU infrastructure. Isomorphic Labs monetises through strategic pharmaceutical research collaborations — disclosed deals include Novartis (January 2024, expanded February 2025), Eli Lilly, and Johnson & Johnson (January 2026) — and through its own internal therapeutic pipeline. The company closed a $600M external Series B investment round in March 2025. Isomorphic Labs does not operate a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of its Drug Design Engine; external researcher access to AlphaFold-family models is provided separately by Google DeepMind via the free AlphaFold Server (alphafoldserver.com) for non-commercial use, and via the open-source AlphaFold 3 inference code released by DeepMind. The Isomorphic Labs GitHub organisation hosts only a small number of forks of internal Kubernetes and configuration-management tooling.

providers.name: K9 Ventures
providers.description: K9 Ventures is a technology-focused Pre-Seed venture capital fund based in Palo Alto, California, founded by Manu Kumar (its "Chief Firestarter"). The firm provides the first institutional capital to companies at "frighteningly early" stages, backing new core technologies, technology platforms, and new markets rather than following a fixed sector thesis. K9 makes only a handful of concentrated investments each year, favoring teams building something genuinely new. Notable past portfolio companies include Twilio, Lytro, CrowdFlower, and DNAnexus. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Foundry Group and added to the API Evangelist network; K9 Ventures does not publish a public API surface.

providers.name: Krosslinker
providers.description: Krosslinker (KrossLinker) is a Singapore-based deep-tech advanced-materials company that designs and manufactures silica aerogels — among the most insulating solids known — using a proprietary, water-based and scalable chemistry and manufacturing platform the company calls Aspire. Its product line spans Cryar super-insulating aerogel composite board, QuintAero ultra-light silica aerogel powder, KrossShield SR Pro aerogel-powered cooling paint, and a flexible aerogel blanket in development, serving cold-chain pharma and food packaging, building and construction passive cooling, and industrial insulation. Krosslinker operates from CleanTech III in Singapore and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a physical-materials manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web, product, and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Leggett and Platt
providers.description: Leggett and Platt is a diversified manufacturer that designs and produces engineered components and products found in many homes, offices, vehicles, and aircraft, including bedding components, automotive seating, hydraulic cylinders, and aerospace tube assemblies. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: LetGo
providers.description: letgo is a mobile-first classifieds and secondhand marketplace where individuals list, browse, and negotiate on used goods — vehicles, electronics, furniture, and household items — with chat-based buyer/seller messaging and location-based discovery. Launched in 2015 and backed by Naspers/OLX, letgo grew into one of the largest peer-to-peer resale apps in the United States before combining its US operation with OfferUp in 2020. The letgo brand and letgo.com continue to operate as a regional classifieds marketplace; the live site currently serves a Turkish-language catalog (category browsing, search, and an otoplus vehicles section per its robots.txt). letgo publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs. The application-internal API under /api/ is explicitly disallowed in robots.txt, and the entire site sits behind an Akamai bot-mitigation challenge, so no developer surface could be verified.

providers.name: Magic
providers.description: Magic (magic.dev) is a San Francisco frontier AI research lab building frontier-scale code models - an "AI coworker" for software engineering, and ultimately a path to safe AGI - rather than a shipping developer product. It has raised roughly $515M from Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, CapitalG, Elad Gil, Sequoia, Jane Street, and Eric Schmidt, and has published research on ultra-long-context models (LTM-1 at a 5M token context window, and the unreleased LTM-2-mini research prototype claimed to handle up to 100M tokens). As of this review Magic does not publish a public, self-serve developer API, API reference, SDK, or waitlist; its website and careers pages describe mission, research, and open roles only, with no product access model, pricing, or documented endpoints. Its GitHub organization (magicproduct) hosts research tooling (e.g. hash-hop, a long-context evaluation harness) and infrastructure forks, not an API client or SDK.

providers.name: Mendel AI
providers.description: Mendel AI is a San Jose, California clinical AI company founded in 2017 by Dr. Karim Galil to streamline oncology research by organizing real-world data and accelerating clinical-trial workflows. Its flagship platform, Mendel Hypercube, pairs large language models with a clinician-built clinical knowledge hypergraph to add physician-like reasoning to LLMs operating over electronic health records, pathology reports, genomic data, clinician notes, claims, diagnostic data, and EDC submissions. Hypercube is offered as three productized experiences — Hypercube Cohort for patient cohort discovery (with funnel-style criteria analysis and direct integration to clinicaltrials.gov), Hypercube Analyst for AI-driven analysis of structured and unstructured real-world data, and Build Your Own Hypercube for custom clinical-data queries. The platform integrates with enterprise data warehouses (Databricks, Snowflake) and BI tools (Tableau, Qlik), and is available through the AWS Marketplace, Microsoft Azure Marketplace, and natively on the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. Mendel serves pharma, providers, payers, and research organizations including Quest Diagnostics, Boston Scientific, Gatehouse Bio, and the University of Pennsylvania, with published evidence in oncology trial prescreening. Mendel has no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source GitHub repositories; integration is delivered through enterprise contracts and cloud-marketplace deployments.

providers.name: OkHttp
providers.description: OkHttp is an efficient HTTP and HTTP/2 client for Android and Java applications with connection pooling and transparent GZIP.

providers.name: op.ai
providers.description: audioMCP (op.ai) provides a Managed Conversational Platform (MCP) that enables AI agents to build, configure, and deploy production voice agents. Users can describe a voice agent and launch it within seconds, integrating with telephony, speech-to-text, and text-to-speech services. The platform offers tools for scaling, monitoring, and customizing voice interactions for enterprise AI deployments.

providers.name: Orbio
providers.description: Orbio Earth is a climate-tech company (founded 2021; Dover, Delaware, USA and Cologne, Germany) that turns open satellite data into industrial methane intelligence for the energy sector. Its platform detects, quantifies, and tracks methane emissions from oil-and-gas infrastructure globally at asset level with a roughly 5-day revisit rate, using multispectral imagery (Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, EMIT) and machine learning, plus Bayesian uncertainty estimation. Customers — oil-and-gas operators and private-equity firms — use it for super-emitter identification, historical trend and root-cause analysis, and compliance with emerging methane regulation. Platform access is offered via the web application or a sales-gated data API integration; there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK. Orbio also publishes the open-source Project Eucalyptus methane-detection pipelines on GitHub for research use.

providers.name: Orchard Robotics
providers.description: Orchard Robotics (Orchard AI, "The AI Farming Company") is an agricultural technology startup founded in 2022 that builds AI-powered camera systems and farm-management software for precision fruit and vine growing. Its FruitScope platform mounts AI-enabled cameras on any farm vehicle to collect precise per-tree and per-vine data — fruit count, size, color, and growth rate — which is stored in FruitScope Vault and surfaced through FruitScope OS for crop decision-making, with a Vineyard Robotics division serving grape growers. Backed by General Catalyst, the company has raised roughly $22M. As of this profile Orchard Robotics publishes a marketing and careers website but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Owens-Illinois (O-I Glass)
providers.description: Owens-Illinois (now O-I Glass) is one of the world's leading manufacturers of glass containers, supplying glass packaging to the food, beverage, beer, wine, spirits, and pharmaceutical industries. No public APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Panacea
providers.description: Panacea is an AI-native FDA regulatory services firm (Y Combinator Spring 2026, operating as withpanacea.com) that pairs experienced ex-FDA regulatory consultants with a proprietary AI platform to accelerate medical device and pharmaceutical companies through FDA approval. Panacea supports the full range of U.S. regulatory pathways - 510(k), De Novo, PMA, IDE, IND, NDA, BLA, ODD, Pre-Subs, and BDD - handling regulatory strategy, pre-FDA meetings, and submission authoring through to clearance and approval. The company differentiates on milestone-based, outcome-aligned pricing rather than hourly billing, claiming results roughly 60% faster than traditional firms while keeping 100% expert oversight. Panacea is a professional services / consulting company; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Perfectbit
providers.description: PerfectBit, Inc. is a Y Combinator-backed company that produces high-quality, verifier-grounded training data for frontier AI models. Rather than relying on human annotators alone, PerfectBit generates and verifies data against external ground-truth sources - formal proof systems, physics and scientific simulators, executable tests, and oracle databases - across text, code, image, audio, and video. Its stated goal is to let AI labs "train on reality, not noise." The company operates as a B2B data provider engaged in pilot work with frontier AI labs, and does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Picasso
providers.description: Picasso is an image downloading and caching library for Android, focused on simplicity and minimal disk space usage. It is an open-source project by Square. Picasso is a client-side library, not a hosted HTTP API.

providers.name: Prevenotics
providers.description: Prevenotics, Inc. is an AI-powered preventive healthcare and diagnostics company working toward "a zero cancer world powered by AI." Its flagship solution provides real-time identification of pre-cancerous risks during gastroscopy, helping physicians move beyond diagnosis to effective prognosis management and stomach cancer prevention. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global and cites partnerships with NVIDIA, LG Electronics, Kakao, and Korean research and government institutions (NIPA, NIA, Seoul AI Hub). No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation was found during enrichment; this profile currently tracks the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Profility
providers.description: Profility, Inc. is a Boston-based healthcare technology company whose AI-powered platform supports collaboration and decision-making across the post-acute care continuum. Its cloud platform combines large historical patient datasets with predictive analytics to build personalized care-planning profiles, predict rehabilitation success and readmission risk across post-acute settings, and guide placement and referral decisions between hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, home health, behavioral health and dialysis providers. Its PReP Authorize product automates prior authorization and concurrent review for managed-care patients, covering managed-care contract intelligence, denial reduction and audit preparedness. Profility markets analytical reporting that scores post-acute providers and maps local market position for referral-pattern optimization. The company reports deployment across 500+ facilities. Profility ships its platform as an end-user web application; it publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Quantum Space
providers.description: Quantum Space is a space defense and orbital mobility company headquartered in Rockville, Maryland, building Ranger — a maneuverable spacecraft designed to operate across LEO, MEO, GEO and cislunar orbits. Per the company's own published material, Ranger carries up to 4,000 kg of storable propellant, uses multi-mode chemical and electric propulsion for up to 12 km/s of delta-V, is designed for a 15-year on-station operational life, supports on-orbit refueling in both directions, and exposes a modular five-port payload architecture. The company sells space domain awareness, satellite servicing, satellite life extension and on-orbit refueling to national security, civil and commercial customers, with engineering in Rockville, propulsion and integration in Hawthorne, California and Huntsville, Alabama, and spacecraft production in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Leadership includes CEO Jim Bridenstine (former NASA Administrator), Executive Chairman Kam Ghaffarian and President Kerry Wisnosky. Quantum Space publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; the only machine-readable artifact served from its own hosts is an llms.txt at the website root.

providers.name: Relay Therapeutics
providers.description: Relay Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision-medicine company in Cambridge, Massachusetts that discovers and develops small-molecule therapeutics for cancer and genetic disease. Its proprietary Dynamo platform combines computational and experimental approaches — motion-based drug discovery, protein-motion simulation, structural biology, and biophysics — to drug targets that have historically been difficult to reach. The company advances a pipeline of oncology and precision-medicine candidates. Relay Therapeutics was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As a biotechnology / drug-discovery company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and web properties.

providers.name: Sallie Mae Bank
providers.description: Sallie Mae Bank is a Utah state-chartered industrial bank (industrial loan company) founded on November 28, 2005 and headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, operating as the FDIC-insured banking subsidiary (FDIC cert #58177) of SLM Corporation (NASDAQ SLM), the publicly traded, S&P 400 consumer-finance company best known as the largest originator of private student loans in the United States. Beyond student and education lending, the bank offers retail deposit products including high-yield savings accounts, money market accounts, and certificates of deposit through salliemae.com. Sallie Mae Bank does not operate a first-party public developer program - there is no developer.salliemae.com portal, no api.salliemae.com host, and no published OpenAPI/Swagger definitions. Consumer account and transaction data is reachable only on a permissioned basis through third-party data aggregators (historically Plaid), and no first-party FDX data-access API or published CFPB Section 1033 data-rights posture could be confirmed. This is an identity-only, aggregator-access record reflecting the honest reality that this institution exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: Shibe.Online
providers.description: Random pictures of Shiba Inu, cats or birds

providers.name: Shipium
providers.description: Shipium is a shipping platform for high-volume e-commerce, optimizing carrier selection, multi-warehouse delivery promises, and parcel routing.

providers.name: Simigo by Telmobil Inc
providers.description: Simigo by Telmobil Inc provides a vendor API platform for resellers to integrate telecom services. The platform offers endpoints under /v1/reseller/* for operations such as checking reseller balances, managing customers, and provisioning services. Hosted at api.simigo.ai with Swagger UI documentation, the service targets partners and developers needing programmatic access to Telmobil’s telecom offerings. The company is part of Telmobil Inc and focuses on enabling automated telecom workflows via RESTful APIs.

providers.name: Sokowatch / Wasoko
providers.description: Sokowatch — rebranded as Wasoko in 2022 — is a pan-African B2B e-commerce and distribution platform serving informal retailers (the mom-and-pop dukas, kiosks, and neighborhood shops that move the majority of fast-moving consumer goods across the continent). Founded in 2016 in Nairobi, Kenya by Daniel Yu, the platform lets small shopkeepers order FMCG inventory via a mobile app or SMS, with free same-day delivery to the shop door, eliminating costly trips to wholesalers. Wasoko layers embedded fintech on top of commerce: buy-now-pay-later inventory credit, working-capital loans for shopkeepers who often lack access to traditional banking, and digital payments. At peak the company operated across Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In December 2023, Wasoko announced a merger with Egyptian B2B peer MaxAB, which closed in August 2024 to form MaxAB-Wasoko, Africa's largest B2B informal-retail network with more than 450,000 merchants across eight countries (combining MaxAB's North African footprint in Egypt and Morocco with Wasoko's Sub-Saharan reach) and roughly 4,000 employees, co-led by Daniel Yu and MaxAB founder Belal El-Megharbel. Post-merger the group exited underperforming markets (Zambia, Uganda, Senegal) and pivoted harder into fintech, where margins exceed core distribution. Wasoko's revenue model is wholesale-to-retail product sales plus fintech (credit, payments) and logistics fees. The platform is operated as a closed retailer-facing app; there is no public developer API, SDK, partner integration program, or open-source release for the commerce, logistics, or fintech surface. The legacy Sokowatch GitHub organization exists but contains only forks of third-party tools (Apache Superset, Fineract CN, Botpress, Kutt, Portainer) used internally, with no first-party libraries or specifications.

providers.name: SolveAI
providers.description: SolveAI is an enterprise AI platform that helps organizations turn complex business problems into custom AI applications, providing tooling to align stakeholders and then build, deploy, and maintain AI solutions across the enterprise. The company is backed by Accel, GV, and Northzone. As of this profile SolveAI publishes a marketing website at solve.ai (a static single-page app on S3/CloudFront) with no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, webhook surface, or MCP server; this entry captures the verifiable identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: SUPA
providers.description: SUPA is an AI data infrastructure company that helps machine learning teams build high-quality training datasets through a blend of technology and expert human annotation. It delivers data labeling and curation services spanning RLHF, LLM training, semantic segmentation, image classification, and medical imaging annotation, drawing on domain-expert networks across healthcare, manufacturing, robotics, agriculture, design, and industrial sectors. SUPA claims annotation accuracy above 95% and delivery of over one million data points per week. It publishes datasets on Hugging Face and is backed by 500 Global. As of enrichment, SUPA exposes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or /.well-known/ discovery surface — engagement is through its sales/contact channels.

providers.name: Transport for Norway
providers.description: Transport APIs and dataset for Norway

providers.name: Unmannd
providers.description: Unmannd (Unmannd Autonomy Pvt Ltd) is an India-based defense technology company backed by Accel and Speciale Invest, engineering autonomous drones under the banner of aerial dominance. Its TITAN 30 is an autonomous defense-logistics drone with a 30 kg max payload, 60 km/h cruise speed, 20,000 ft operational ceiling, and 30 km max range; its FURY counter-UAS interceptor was announced as launching in Q1 2026. Unmannd is a hardware/defense company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Unshackled Ventures I
providers.description: Unshackled Ventures is an inception-stage venture capital firm that writes the first check for founders before they have products, traction, or revenue, with a focus on immigrant and international founders. Beyond capital the firm provides an immigration platform that handles founder visas at no cost, a mentorship network of founders and operators, and a fundraising engine for follow-on rounds. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio entry of 500 Global; it is a venture firm and publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: User1st
providers.description: User1st is a web and mobile digital accessibility company whose U1 Suite gives organizations an efficient path to WCAG, ADA, and European Accessibility Act (EAA) compliance. It provides accessibility toolkits and remediation across web frameworks (JavaScript/TypeScript, React, Angular, Vue, WordPress, Shopify) and mobile platforms (iOS Native, Android Native, React Native, Flutter), plus a free accessibility scanner and GenAI-assisted code-fixing and image-description tooling. Trusted by organizations including Amtrak, Fannie Mae, IKEA, iRobot, T-Mobile, Santander, Mount Sinai, and the City of New York. Backed by 500 Global. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the product backend is an internal SaaS API with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Vaire Computing
providers.description: Vaire Computing is a deep-tech semiconductor startup building reversible computing chips for near-zero energy computing. Its reversible logic gates recover and recycle the energy of computation instead of dissipating it as heat, aiming to decouple energy consumption from growth in computing power. The company was co-founded by Rodolfo Rosini (CEO) and Dr Hannah Earley (CTO), is backed by Seedcamp, 7percent Ventures, and Lifeline Ventures, and publishes technology and software whitepapers. Vaire currently publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Valar Atomics
providers.description: Valar Atomics is a nuclear energy company developing high-temperature gas reactors (HTGR) with TRISO fuel, graphite moderators, and helium coolant, deployed as grid-independent gigasites of many small reactors that power heavy industry - hydrogen production via the sulfur-iodine cycle, AI data center power, industrial process heat, and clean synthetic hydrocarbon fuels via Fischer-Tropsch synthesis with captured CO2. Its Ward 250 test reactor is a partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy, the San Rafael Energy Research Center, and the State of Utah. Founded by Isaiah Taylor and backed by Initialized Capital, the company publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: VeeR VR
providers.description: VeeR VR is a virtual reality content community founded in June 2016 that lets creators produce, edit, and share 360-degree videos and photos through its VeeR VR and VeeR Editor mobile apps, and is a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public API surface, and its primary domain veer.tv redirects to veervr.com, which no longer resolves.

providers.name: Veritiv
providers.description: Veritiv is a North American business-to-business distributor of packaging, facility solutions, print, and publishing products. Formed in July 2014 through the merger of International Paper's xpedx division with Unisource Worldwide, Veritiv operated as a publicly traded company on the New York Stock Exchange until it was acquired and taken private by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) in November 2023 in a transaction valued at approximately $2.3 billion. The company is headquartered in Sandy Springs, Georgia, and operates roughly 125 distribution centers across the United States and Mexico. Veritiv does not publish any public developer APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal — its commercial surface is built around sales reps, account managers, and large-account customer portals rather than a programmable API.

providers.name: Xona Space Systems
providers.description: Xona Space Systems builds Pulsar, a commercial low-Earth-orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) satellite service designed to complement and harden GPS with centimeter-level accuracy and encrypted, jam-resistant signals usable by existing GNSS devices via software updates. The planned constellation is 258 small satellites at roughly 1,080 km altitude, with the Pulsar Verified ecosystem (receivers, simulators, test platforms) delivered through partners including Trimble, Septentrio, Topcon, Furuno, and Murata. A Craft Ventures portfolio company serving defense, agriculture, telecom, transportation, maritime, aviation, and autonomous systems. No public developer API surface was found as of July 2026.

providers.name: Yassir
providers.description: Yassir is an Algerian-founded super app providing on-demand and financial services across the Maghreb, sub-Saharan Africa, Canada, and France. Founded in 2017 by Noureddine Tayebi and headquartered in Palo Alto, California with operations centered in Algiers, the company bundles ride-hailing (Yassir Ride), food delivery (Yassir Food), grocery delivery (Yassir Market), and digital financial services (Yassir Cash) into a single consumer mobile app, alongside a Yassir B2B suite covering corporate mobility, meal benefits, procurement, parcel delivery, and digital gift cards. Yassir reports more than six million users, 130,000+ driver and merchant partners, and 4,500 employees operating across cities in Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, South Africa, Senegal, Canada, and France. The company has raised roughly $193M to date, including a $150M Series B led by BOND with participation from Y Combinator and DN Capital, and a global sponsorship partnership with Paris Saint-Germain. Yassir is a consumer and merchant-facing super app: it operates iOS and Android apps and a business portal (go-business.yassir.com) but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source project. Driver, courier, restaurant, and store onboarding flow through partner sign-up forms rather than a developer program, and the yassir-tech GitHub organization currently has no public repositories.

providers.name: Zunum Aero
providers.description: Zunum Aero is an American aerospace company founded in 2013 and based in the Seattle area (Kirkland / Bothell, Washington) that set out to build hybrid-to-electric regional aircraft. Its ZA10 program targeted a six-to-twelve-seat hybrid-electric airplane with a 700-nautical-mile range, aimed at reviving short-haul point-to-point air travel from secondary airports, and it was backed by Boeing HorizonX and JetBlue Technology Ventures. The company laid off nearly all of its staff in late 2018 and paused operations, and it later pursued trade-secret litigation against Boeing. Zunum Aero is an aircraft manufacturer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a marketing and press site with no developer program, no developer portal, no documentation, and no published machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: ABM Therapeutics
providers.description: ABM Therapeutics (ABM) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2015, operating from San Diego, California and Zhangjiang, Pudong, Shanghai. It discovers and develops small-molecule targeted therapies for primary brain cancers including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) and for brain metastases arising from melanoma, lung cancer and breast cancer. Its lead program, ABM-1310, is a brain-penetrant, selective BRAF V600 inhibitor that received US IND clearance in November 2019 and is in Phase 1 clinical study. ABM publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification; its only public surface is a corporate, investor and clinical-news website. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist harvest backlog from a secondary-market listing under the ticker-style slug "abmtx".

providers.name: AbTis
providers.description: AbTis Co., Ltd. (앱티스) is a South Korean biotechnology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do, inside the Dong-A Socio Holdings R&D Center. It develops AbClick, a third-generation site-selective antibody conjugation platform that attaches payloads to the Fc Lys248 residue of native IgG antibodies with no enzyme and no Fc engineering, giving a controlled drug-to-antibody ratio and batch-to-batch consistency across ADC, DAC, AOC, ARC, ISAC and dual-payload designs. AbTis licenses the platform, runs collaborative research and fee-for-service ADC development, and advances its own pipeline led by AT-211, a Claudin 18.2-targeting MMAE ADC. Acquired by Dong-A ST in 2023, it now operates as that company's ADC-specialised subsidiary. Its product is licensed chemistry and drug intellectual property, not software: it runs no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Acelot
providers.description: Acelot, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, developing first-in-class small-molecule therapies for neurodegenerative diseases with high unmet need. Its lead candidate, ACE-2223, is designed to target misfolded and aggregated TDP-43 and restore the protein's healthy form and function, addressing pathology central to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Acelot's discovery work is powered by Resolute, an internal integrated drug-discovery platform combining AI-driven computational chemistry with structural and biological insight to drug historically intractable protein targets. Acelot publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification; its four public GitHub repositories are forks of third-party cheminformatics tooling.

providers.name: AEOL
providers.description: AEOL (AEOL KOREA Co., Ltd. / 주식회사 에이올코리아) is a South Korean advanced-materials and climate-technology manufacturer founded in February 2018 out of the Korea University Campus Town programme and headquartered in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. The company holds a twenty-year exclusive licence from the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology to manufacture and sell Metal-Organic Framework (MOF) materials, and was the first Korean firm to commercialise MOF production at scale. It turns that porous-adsorbent chemistry into physical equipment: MOF desiccant rotors and hybrid dehumidifiers that regenerate at low temperature instead of using refrigerant compression, all-in-one units combining heat-recovery ventilation with UV-LED and HEPA air purification and auxiliary cooling, harmful-gas and odour adsorption products such as the Red Dot-awarded Mofresh Mini, and the CarbonSorV rotary wheel for continuous CO2 capture shown at CES 2025. AEOL won a CES 2024 Innovation Award and the FIX 2024 Grand Innovation Award, has raised roughly USD 10-23 million from investors including KU Startup, BlissVine Ventures, JCGI, KNET Investment Partners and NH Venture Investment, and sells through appliance-maker R&D partnerships and distribution agreements in North America and New Zealand. AEOL sells hardware and materials, not software: it operates a single Korean-language Cafe24-hosted corporate site with no developer section, publishes no API documentation, SDK, webhook or machine-readable API contract of any kind, and maintains no public code repositories or package-registry releases.

providers.name: Aerospace Kate
providers.description: Aerospace Kate (航天凯特) is the trading name of Chengdu Aerospace Kate Mechanical & Electrical Technology Co., Ltd. (成都航天凯特机电科技有限公司), a Chinese high-precision servo drive manufacturer founded in 2017 in Pidu District, Chengdu, Sichuan. A national high-tech and state-designated "little giant" specialized-and-innovative enterprise with roughly 200 staff (over half in R&D) and 210+ registered IP rights, it builds fully domestically-sourced servo drivers spanning 15V to 800V (KTSD, 蜀芯, 蓉驭 and 锦驱 series), KTMT hollow-cup motors, underwater thrusters and electric actuators, phased-array antenna steering gear, and the 灵捷 (Lingjie) line of robot joint modules, collaborative arms, quadruped robots and humanoid platforms. A second line covers optoelectronic detection — panoramic detectors, maritime search lights and airport runway FOD detection. The product is physical hardware; Aerospace Kate publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: AID:Tech
providers.description: AID:Tech is a Dublin-based payments and digital-identity infrastructure company that bridges Web2 and Web3, delivering self-sovereign decentralized identity (DID), KYC/AML verification, digital wallets with virtual cards, and secure payouts for benefits distribution, disaster relief, and financial inclusion. Its products include Kare (benefits and disaster-relief distribution) and Klimify, and its engineering is rooted in blockchain and distributed-ledger technology (Hyperledger Fabric, Openchain, and the bryk/algo DID methods). AID:Tech does not publish a first-party public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; its public technical surface is its GitHub organization (DID-method reference implementations, a Circle API SDK, and Kubernetes/Hyperledger tooling) and its Medium engineering blog.

providers.name: Aliro Quantum
providers.description: Aliro Quantum (branded "Aliro, The Quantum Networking Company") is a Boston-based, Harvard spin-out building full-stack software for entanglement-based quantum networks. Its platform unifies three core products: the Aliro Simulator for physically accurate, optical-level modeling and validation of heterogeneous quantum networks before any hardware is deployed; AlirOS, a vendor-agnostic control-plane operating system that runs on quantum end-nodes and quantum repeaters across multiple hardware modalities; and the Aliro Orchestrator, a centralized single-pane-of-glass management system that configures, monitors, and operates quantum nodes and services through the full network lifecycle. These are packaged commercially as AliroNet — described by Aliro as the world's first end-to-end entanglement-based quantum network solution — delivered in three modes (Emulate, Pilot, and Deployment) and also available as AliroNet Quickstart, a bundled hardware-plus-software starter package that pairs third-party photon sources, detectors, memories, repeaters, and routers with Aliro's orchestration, control, and data operations software. The company markets Quantum-Powered Security as its anchor use case (Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later mitigation for telcos, utilities, financial services, and defense), alongside quantum-computing interconnects (clustered and blind quantum compute for cloud providers), networked quantum sensors for positioning/navigation/timing, and quantum position verification. Customers and design partners disclosed publicly include EPB of Chattanooga, Boeing, Cisco, the US Air Force, Brookhaven National Laboratory, Stony Brook University, and Noblis.
