providers.name: Dream11
providers.description: Dream11 is India's largest fantasy sports platform, operated by Sporta Technologies Private Limited and part of the Dream Sports group founded in 2008 by Harsh Jain and Bhavit Sheth and headquartered in Mumbai. Launched as a freemium fantasy game in 2012, it lets 140 million-plus users draft virtual teams and compete in free and paid contests across cricket, football, kabaddi, basketball and hockey, scoring on the real-world performance of the athletes they pick. Dream11 is a consumer, mobile-first product with no public consumer API program; its engineering organization does maintain public open-source infrastructure (Kong rate-limiter and circuit-breaker plugins, the Odin deployment tool) on GitHub and publishes an engineering blog.

providers.name: Enel X
providers.description: Enel X is the advanced-energy-services business line of the Enel Group, an Italian multinational utility headquartered in Rome. Enel X delivers smart energy products and services across electrification, e-mobility, demand response, virtual power plants, and distributed energy resource (DER) management for residential, commercial, industrial, public-sector, and utility customers. Its principal offerings include the Enel X Way app and network for electric-vehicle charging (the consolidated successor to JuicePass and JuiceNet), the JuiceBox and JuicePedestal hardware lines, the JuiceNet Utility Edition managed-charging platform, the DER.OS / DER optimization software (now run as Calibrant Energy in North America after Enel's 2023 divestiture of its North American demand-response business), Enel X Flex flexibility management software, and VPP Connect, a set of API endpoints that lets third-party DER operators — OEMs, automation providers, and equipment manufacturers — aggregate EV chargers, batteries, HVAC systems, heat pumps, and other controllable assets into Enel's virtual power plant and earn revenue from demand-response and grid-services programs via either the open Automated Demand Response (oADR) protocol or a custom Enel API. Enel X exposes additional non-public surfaces — including the emobility.enelx.com OAuth/charging endpoints used by the Enel X Way mobile apps — but does not publish OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal; VPP Connect documentation is delivered under partnership agreement after a guided onboarding process. The official Enelx GitHub organization has effectively no public engineering presence, and the legacy JuiceNet public API has been deprecated as part of the platform migration to Enel X Way.

providers.name: EnergyBank
providers.description: EnergyBank is a New Zealand deep-tech energy company developing next-generation energy storage for the offshore wind market. Its core approach firms floating offshore wind generation at the turbine so that compute modules can be co-located with the generation itself — taking "data to the power rather than electricity to the data" — which removes the need for a grid connection, enables consentless high-seas deployment, and allows direct ocean cooling of the co-located compute. The company was founded by CEO Tim Hawkey and CTO Alex Szczepaniak, and its team combines applied mathematicians, electronics engineers, and business development staff with advisors drawn from subsea turbomachinery. EnergyBank is venture backed by Version One Ventures, Blackbird, Icehouse Ventures, Outset Ventures, Promus Ventures, Nuance Capital, and Boost VC. As of this enrichment pass EnergyBank publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification — it is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Etched
providers.description: Etched is an AI hardware company building Sohu, a transformer-only ASIC designed to accelerate inference for large language models by hard-wiring the transformer architecture directly into silicon. Etched markets Sohu as an alternative to general-purpose GPUs for transformer inference, claiming order-of-magnitude throughput improvements on models such as Llama 70B when deployed in eight-chip server configurations. The chip is fabricated on TSMC's 4nm process with 144 GB of HBM3E per package. As of mid-2026 Etched has raised more than 625 million dollars at a 5 billion dollar valuation but has not yet shipped Sohu to customers in volume, and there is no public Etched API or developer surface. This profile is company-and-product-only and intentionally has an empty apis list.

providers.name: Eyewa
providers.description: Eyewa is an online-first eyewear retailer serving the Middle East, selling prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, clear and colored contact lenses, eyewear accessories, and eye-health vitamins through its e-commerce storefront and a network of 260+ physical stores with click-and-collect. Headquartered in Dubai, UAE, Eyewa operates across the GCC and offers regional payment options such as Tabby, Tamara, and Apple Pay. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. Eyewa publishes a consumer storefront, an educational vision-and-eyewear blog, and standard commercial policy pages, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documented API surface.

providers.name: File Format
providers.description: File formats define how information is encoded for storage in a computer file, spanning images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF), audio (WAV, MP3, OGG, FLAC), video (MP4, MOV, MKV), documents (PDF, HTML, DOCX, ODT), data serialization (JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, Parquet, Avro), archives (ZIP, TAR, GZIP), and executables. File formats are central to API and data interoperability, identified via filename extensions, magic numbers, MIME types, and IANA media-type registrations.

providers.name: Filmgrail
providers.description: Filmgrail is an Oslo, Norway based software company offering an AI-powered digital platform for cinema operators. Its product suite bundles a cinema content management system (CMS), native iOS and Android mobile apps, branded cinema websites, and marketing and analytics tooling into a single managed offering, with a loyalty system, festival platform, push notifications, and a planning tool layered on top. Filmgrail markets these capabilities as a way to automate cinema operations and grow digital ticket sales and moviegoer engagement, and describes API-based integration between its platform and cinema point-of-sale systems, websites, and mobile apps. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from Oslo, Norway and Delaware, USA. Filmgrail does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Floobits
providers.description: Floobits was a real-time collaborative code editing service — "remote collaboration tools for dev teams, work together, apart." It shipped editor plugins for Sublime Text, Vim, Neovim, Emacs, Atom, and the IntelliJ family of IDEs, plus flootty, a shared-terminal tool for pair terminal sessions. Plugins connected editors to shared Floobits workspaces where multiple developers edited the same files and terminals in real time over a synchronizing backend (built on a diff-match-patch model). Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of 2026-07-19 the hosted service at floobits.com no longer resolves in DNS and the GitHub org has had no activity since December 2022; the open-source editor plugins and the flootty PyPI package remain the durable public surface.

providers.name: Givemetap
providers.description: GiveMeTap is a UK-based social-enterprise consumer brand that designs and sells reusable, BPA-free stainless-steel and insulated water bottles (500ml and 700ml, plus custom co-branded bottles for businesses). For every bottle sold, GiveMeTap funds five years of clean drinking water for a person in Ghana, giving 20% of its revenue to water projects in Africa; the company reports 116,391 people reached with clean water for life. It operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront on the Shopify platform. GiveMeTap is a physical-products company with no first-party developer API, developer portal, or public API documentation; it was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub.

providers.name: Headgum
providers.description: Headgum is an American comedy podcast network founded in 2015 by Marty Michael, Amir Blumenfeld, and Jake Hurwitz, with studios in Los Angeles and New York. It produces and distributes premium comedy and entertainment podcasts including Doughboys, Not Another D&D Podcast, Dead Eyes, Hey Riddle Riddle, and Why Won't You Date Me?, and operates Gumball, a host-read podcast and YouTube advertising marketplace that lets brands buy ads directly from creators. Headgum is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Headgum publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: HelloFresh
providers.description: HelloFresh SE is a publicly listed (Frankfurt Stock Exchange: HFG), Berlin-headquartered global meal-kit and food-solutions company that ships recipes and pre-portioned ingredients to households across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. Its brand portfolio includes HelloFresh, Factor, Green Chef, EveryPlate, Chefs Plate, Youfoodz, and Good Chop. HelloFresh does not publish a public consumer developer API; its engineering organization is active in open source on GitHub, maintaining widely used infrastructure tooling such as the Janus API gateway, the health-go healthcheck library, and the goengine event-sourcing framework. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Insight Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Henkel
providers.description: A German multinational company operating in adhesives, beauty care, and laundry and home care markets. Produces well-known consumer brands alongside industrial adhesive technologies used worldwide. No public developer API or developer portal was located; Henkel operates a Safety Data Sheets product portal at mysds.henkel.com but does not publish open developer APIs.

providers.name: Hexing Electrical
providers.description: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd. (海兴电力 / Hexing) is a Chinese energy-technology company focused on smart power distribution and utilization, new energy, smart water and gas, water treatment and clean water, and marine electrification. Beyond hardware, Hexing delivers integrated solutions and project delivery spanning metering devices, communication networks (RF, PLC, cellular, NB-IoT), MDC / MDM / AMI platforms, billing systems, distribution automation, energy storage (BESS), EV charging, water metering, seawater desalination and electric marine propulsion. The company reports 34 years of industry experience, operations across 110+ countries and 17 global manufacturing hubs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; Hexing publishes no public developer/API surface today, so this profile captures corporate identity plus the AI knowledge file (llms.txt) the company publishes for AI search / RAG.

providers.name: HTTP/2
providers.description: HTTP/2 is the second major version of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol, defined by the IETF in RFC 7540 and standardized in 2015. It optimizes use of network resources and reduces perceived latency by introducing a binary framing layer over a single TCP connection, with full request and response multiplexing across independent bidirectional streams. HTTP/2 uses HPACK header compression to eliminate redundant header data, credit-based flow control via WINDOW_UPDATE frames, stream prioritization through dependencies and weights, and server push via PUSH_PROMISE frames to proactively deliver anticipated resources. Core frame types include DATA, HEADERS, PRIORITY, RST_STREAM, SETTINGS, PUSH_PROMISE, PING, and GOAWAY, with the protocol preserving the existing HTTP semantics of methods, status codes, and headers while transforming how they are transported on the wire.

providers.name: Ilumno
providers.description: Ilumno is a Latin American education technology company that helps higher education institutions grow and modernize through digital transformation. Its services span student acquisition and retention (Growth), online and virtual learning platforms (Virtuality), and real-time analytics and student-data management tools, all delivered on its Growth Engine technology platform. Ilumno reports supporting more than 220,000 students across the region, with offices in Bogota (Colombia), Dallas (USA) and Amsterdam (Netherlands). The company is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Inkitt
providers.description: Inkitt is a data-driven storytelling and self-publishing technology company that runs a reading and writing community (inkitt.com) and the paid serialized-fiction reading app Galatea. It uses reader-engagement analytics and algorithms to discover promising manuscripts from independent authors and develop the most popular into commercial fiction and adaptations across its Inkitt and Galatea platforms. Founded in 2013 and backed by Earlybird, HV Capital, Khosla Ventures, Kleiner Perkins and Speedinvest, Inkitt operates consumer mobile and web reading products rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, domain-security, and GitHub surface.

providers.name: InRisk
providers.description: InRisk Labs is a climate insurtech company building parametric insurance products for climate and disaster risk financing. Its platform pairs an AI-driven pricing engine, real-time geospatial and weather monitoring, and blockchain smart contracts to deliver rapid, data-triggered payouts across 15+ parametric products spanning agriculture (crop, livestock, agri-input), renewable energy (solar, wind), logistics, tourism, energy demand, infrastructure protection, and wage and business-interruption cover. Risk models incorporate global climate drivers such as ENSO and IOD and range from India to global coverage. InRisk exposes an "API on-demand" so insurance partners can integrate customized products, dynamic pricing, and real-time analytics into their own infrastructure. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Ion Mobility
providers.description: ION Mobility is a Singapore-headquartered technology and automotive company that designs and builds affordable, zero-emission smart electric motorcycles for riders across Southeast Asia, with its flagship M1-S model and a companion rider mobile app. The company combines advanced hardware and software with human-centred design, spanning electric two-wheelers and energy charging and storage solutions, with additional offices in Jakarta and Shenzhen and backing from investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and identity surface; ION Mobility currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification, operating a consumer waitlist/test-ride site and an internal open-source tooling estate on GitHub.

providers.name: Iris.ai
providers.description: Iris.ai is a Norwegian AI company providing an AI knowledge foundation for regulated enterprises, turning complex enterprise and scientific data into trustworthy, compliant AI. Its platform spans three products — Axion (data organization for AI-ready intelligence), Neuralith (enterprise knowledge integration into AI engines), and RSpace, the Researcher Workspace that lets R&D teams, librarians, and academics search, filter, analyze, extract, summarize, and report across scientific literature. Iris.ai is backed by 500 Global. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: J.C. Penney
providers.description: J.C. Penney Company, Inc. (JCPenney) is an American department store chain offering apparel, accessories, beauty, jewelry, footwear, and home goods. The company emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in late 2020 and continues to operate hundreds of department stores across the United States and Puerto Rico.

providers.name: Jetapult
providers.description: Jetapult is a capital and support firm focused on scaling mobile game studios, combining operator-first funding with hands-on systems for monetization, user acquisition, market expansion, and operational efficiency. Its GamePac AI toolset helps indie studios create, grow, and monetize their games. Jetapult is backed by Accel and operates as a partner-and-capital platform for gaming studios such as Holy Cow Studio and UMX Studio. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Jetapult does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Kano Computing
providers.description: Kano Computing is a London-based technology company founded in 2013 by Alex Klein, Saul Klein and Yonatan Raz-Fridman that began by shipping build-it-yourself computer and coding kits designed to teach STEM and creative computing to children on top of Raspberry Pi hardware. Its catalog spanned the Kano Computer Kit, motion-sensor and Harry Potter / Star Wars coding wands, the Windows-based Kano PC built with Microsoft, and the Stem Player and Stem Video Projector consumer devices. Kano paired the hardware with Kano Code, a block-to-text creative-coding platform, and Kano World, an online making and sharing community. The company entered administration in 2023 and its assets now trade under the Stem brand; its developer footprint survives as open-source tooling in the KanoComputing GitHub organization and the npm @kano scope rather than a hosted API.

providers.name: Kira Systems
providers.description: Kira Systems is a machine-learning contract analysis and review platform for law firms and corporate legal teams, automatically extracting clauses, concepts, and data points from contracts during M&A due diligence, real estate, banking, and other transactional work. Founded in Toronto and backed by Insight Partners, Kira was acquired by Litera in 2021 and is now offered as Litera Kira. It integrates with HighQ and Intralinks data rooms and Litera Transact, and exposes an Open API for additional customer integration needs; no public developer portal or OpenAPI specification is currently published.

providers.name: Kyndryl
providers.description: Kyndryl is a Fortune 500 IT infrastructure services company spun off from IBM in 2021. The company designs, builds, manages, and modernizes mission-critical technology systems across cloud, mainframe, networking, digital workplace, security, applications, data, and AI. Kyndryl operates the Kyndryl Bridge integration and observability platform, runs the Kyndryl Vital design studios, and partners with hyperscalers including AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and SAP. No public developer API has been documented.

providers.name: Kyten Technologies
providers.description: Kyten Technologies is a Seattle, Washington hardware manufacturing startup building a factory to produce custom aerospace-grade battery packs. The founders spent six years at Starlink, where they put more than 5,000 battery packs into space, and are now bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the wider industry. The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. Kyten Technologies is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, classified under Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics, and was an early-stage two-person team at the time of profiling. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: L-3 Communications
providers.description: L-3 Communications was a U.S. defense prime contractor specializing in command, control, communications, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C3ISR) systems, aircraft modernization and maintenance, and government services. In 2019 L-3 merged with Harris Corporation to form L3Harris Technologies, which continues the legacy product lines and is now ranked among the top U.S. defense contractors. No public developer API has been documented.

providers.name: Leidos
providers.description: Leidos, a Fortune 500 digital and mission innovator, delivers solutions at the intersection of national security, health, and critical infrastructure. With a global workforce of approximately 47,000, the company is executing its NorthStar 2030 strategy focused on five growth engines: space and maritime, energy infrastructure, digital modernization and cyber, mission software, and managed health. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified.

providers.name: Life Time Group Holdings
providers.description: Life Time Group Holdings is an American health and wellness company operating large-format athletic resort destinations across the United States and Canada. The company offers fitness facilities, personal training, group classes, aquatics, indoor and outdoor sports, spa services, and healthy living programs in premium resort-style facilities, plus the Life Time app for members. Life Time does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Light Chaser Animation Studios
providers.description: Light Chaser Animation Studios (追光动画) is a Chinese computer-animation film studio founded in March 2013 by Gary Wang (王微), founder and former CEO of the video platform Tudou, and headquartered in Beijing. The studio produces original CG animated feature films for the Chinese domestic market, drawing on Chinese mythology, literature and history. Its released titles include Little Door Gods (小门神), Tea Pets (阿唐奇遇), Cats and Peachtopia (猫与桃花源), White Snake (白蛇：缘起), New Gods: Nezha Reborn (新神榜：哪吒重生), White Snake 2: Green Snake (白蛇2：青蛇劫起), New Gods: Yang Jian (新神榜：杨戬) and Chang An (长安三万里). Light Chaser is a film-production company rather than a technology vendor: its public web presence is a bilingual WordPress marketing and recruiting site at zhuiguang.com, and as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind.

providers.name: LiquidStack
providers.description: LiquidStack is a data center liquid cooling company that designs, manufactures and services direct-to-chip and immersion cooling systems for AI, hyperscale, high performance computing, edge/5G and cryptocurrency workloads. Its product line spans direct-to-chip coolant distribution units — the CDU-1MW at up to 1,350kW of cooling at N+1 and the modular GigaModular CDU-10MW platform — alongside single-phase and two-phase immersion DataTank systems rated to 252kW, plus full lifecycle services covering consulting, installation, training and maintenance. The company spun out of Bitfury in 2021, raised $20 million from Tiger Global, is headquartered in Carrollton, Texas with engineering, R&D and manufacturing operations in Texas and Hong Kong, and was acquired by Trane Technologies in a deal completed in March 2026. LiquidStack sells capital equipment and services rather than software: it operates no developer program and publishes no public API, specification, SDK or developer portal. The only machine interface it documents is embedded in the hardware — its CDUs ship with native MODBUS TCP/IP or a RESTful API, plus BACnet/IP and SNMP, for remote management from a customer's own building or data center management system.

providers.name: lovecrafts
providers.description: LoveCrafts (LoveCrafts Group Limited) is a UK-based crafting commerce and community platform — "your home to shop, share and dream in crafts" — selling yarns and fibers, knitting, crochet, sewing, quilting and embroidery patterns, supplies, tools, kits and fabrics, alongside free and paid patterns, tutorials and inspiration content. It operates localized storefronts for North America, the UK, Germany, Australia and France on a Nuxt-based e-commerce stack. LoveCrafts was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. It exposes no public developer portal or API surface; the only machine-discoverable public artifact is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a responsible- disclosure policy (no bug bounty programme).

providers.name: Manufactured
providers.description: Manufactured is a supply-chain and production platform for hardware and consumer-product brands, backed by Bullpen Capital. Its web application (app.manufactured.com) helps teams run overseas production end to end — issuing sourcing requests to vendors, managing supplier and vendor profiles, negotiating order estimates and contracts under master procurement agreements, tracking production timelines and calendars, and financing purchase orders through production and repayment terms. The product also embeds an AI assistant built on LangChain. At the time of enrichment the public marketing site and the api/docs/developer subdomains were unreachable, and the GraphQL, Lambda and bot backends are private and authentication-gated (introspection blocked), so no public API specification, developer portal, or documentation could be harvested. This profile captures the real, observable surface only.

providers.name: Miruvor AI
providers.description: Miruvor AI Inc. is an early-stage deep-tech AI research lab building brain-inspired continual learning models. Rather than scaling frozen, pre-trained models, Miruvor uses spiking neural networks as its representational substrate together with local learning rules to build systems that learn from experience in real time, with persistent memory and low-energy, neuromorphic efficiency. Founded out of The Residency and backed by 500 Global, the company is pre-product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.description: Current and historical MLB statistics

providers.name: Modern Electron
providers.description: Modern Electron is a Bothell, Washington energy-hardware company founded in 2015 by Tony Pan (CEO) and Max Mankin (CTO) as a spin-out of Intellectual Ventures. It was built to commercialize advanced thermionic energy converters — solid-state, direct heat-to-electricity devices intended to add on-site generation to combustion and thermal equipment. The company now operates publicly as Modern Hydrogen, applying methane pyrolysis behind the meter to crack natural gas into hydrogen and solid carbon before combustion, for industrial heat and steam, on-site power, data-center energy, asphalt products and heavy-duty fleet fueling. The product is physical equipment installed at customer sites; Modern Electron / Modern Hydrogen operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and its public GitHub organization holds only forks of open-source scientific-computing projects (WarpX, AMReX, PICMI, GPy) used in its own R&D.

providers.name: Monto
providers.description: Monto is a B2B payments platform that automates supplier-side billing and collection across customer accounts-payable (AP) portals. It connects suppliers to 500+ AP platforms, using AI to deliver and format invoices per portal, verify data, match invoices to purchase orders, track invoice and payment status in real time, and retrieve remittance details end to end. Integrations include a NetSuite bundle (Send to Monto), generic ERP integration, and email or web upload. Monto reports $10B+ collected across 67 countries. The company is SOC 2 Type II audited. Monto is backed by Scale Venture Partners. This profile has no public developer API or documentation surface as of enrichment.

providers.name: Muon Space
providers.description: Muon Space is a Mountain View, California-based end-to-end space systems company that designs, builds, and operates mission-optimized satellite constellations to deliver Earth Intelligence and enable real-time compute and decision-making in space. Founded in 2021 by veterans of Skybox, NASA, and SpaceX, the company's core product is Muon Halo, an integrated technology stack composed of MuSim (constellation simulation and digital twin), MuOS (IP-based software-defined network middleware connecting space, ground, and cloud), MuCore (software-configurable instrument core), Condor (modular Condor-M and Condor-XL spacecraft platforms), and MuDash (cloud-based tasking, scheduling, and operations dashboard). Muon Space's flagship public mission is FireSat, a purpose-built wildfire detection and monitoring constellation developed with the Earth Fire Alliance, Google Research, and the Gordon & Betty Moore Foundation; FireSat carries a high-dynamic-range multispectral IR instrument capable of detecting 5x5 meter fires across a 1,500 km swath with a 50 m nadir ground sample distance, with revisit times targeted to twenty minutes once the full constellation is operational. The Protoflight satellite produced its first-light imagery in June 2025, with the first block of three additional satellites launching in 2026 and full operational capacity targeted for 2030. Other Muon Space missions support the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force for next-generation weather monitoring, Hydrosat for thermal geospatial intelligence in climate and agriculture, and global security applications including missile-defense architecture. Muon Space's revenue model is mission contracting, spacecraft and constellation delivery, and hosted data services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Halo platform or FireSat data feed.

providers.name: MUSINSA
providers.description: MUSINSA is South Korea's leading online fashion platform, founded in 2001 by Cho Man-ho as a streetwear community and now operating a marketplace that connects more than 10,000 brands with over 16 million members. The company reported roughly USD 3.3 billion in GMV and USD 907 million in revenue for 2024, returned to operating profit, and is pursuing a KOSPI IPO. MUSINSA runs domestic and global storefronts (musinsa.com, global.musinsa.com), a partner/seller program for K-fashion brands, and an engineering organization that publishes on the MUSINSA tech blog. It has raised funding from investors including KKR, Sequoia/Peak XV (formerly Sequoia Capital China / HongShan) and IMM Investment. No genuine public product/developer API or OpenAPI-backed developer portal was found during enrichment; a corporate CMS Swagger UI at dev-api.corp.musinsa.com is an internal tool (its public spec still points at the Swagger petstore demo), so this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Nestlé
providers.description: Nestlé S.A. is the world's largest food and beverage company by revenue, headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland. Its product portfolio spans coffee (Nescafé, Nespresso), water, pet food (Purina), baby and infant nutrition (Gerber, Cerelac), confectionery (KitKat), dairy, and health science. No public developer portal or external API offering has been identified for Nestlé; integrations with retailers and partners are handled through private B2B systems rather than a self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Neuron23
providers.description: Neuron23 is a clinical-stage precision-medicine biotechnology company developing genetically targeted small-molecule therapies for neurological and immunological diseases, with a lead precision-medicine program focused on Parkinson's disease. It combines machine-learning-driven genetic biomarker discovery with drug development to match patients to the therapies most likely to help them. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund, Neuron23 is a therapeutics company that publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Nlight
providers.description: nLIGHT, Inc. (NASDAQ: LASR) is a US-based designer and manufacturer of high-power semiconductor and fiber lasers, optical fibers, and beam-control systems. For more than 25 years the company has served mission-critical directed-energy and defense, sensing, and advanced-manufacturing markets (cutting, welding, additive, medical, and battery production) from a vertically integrated stack spanning semiconductor chips to complete laser systems, with a portfolio of over 450 patents and design and manufacturing based in Camas, Washington. nLIGHT is a hardware and photonics company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Nuro
providers.description: Nuro is a Mountain View-based autonomy company that has pivoted from its original autonomous-goods-delivery vehicle program (R1, R2, R3) to a licensable, vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving stack. The Nuro Driver is an AI-first Level 4 self-driving system, validated through 5+ years of driverless deployments and more than 1.7 million autonomous miles with zero at-fault incidents, paired with the Nuro Toolkit suite of supporting technology. Partners and customers include Uber and Lucid (premium robotaxi program with production-intent vehicles announced for CES 2026), Mercedes- Benz, Toyota, Kroger, Domino's, and Walmart, with NVIDIA participation in recent funding rounds. Nuro has offices in Mountain View, San Francisco, Santa Clara, Las Vegas, Houston, Toronto, Washington DC, Shenzhen, Tokyo, and an upcoming Munich expansion. Nuro does not publish a public developer API; the Driver and Toolkit are commercialized through B2B licensing rather than a self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: Nymbus
providers.description: Nymbus is a Jacksonville, Florida-based fintech software provider delivering cloud-based core banking, digital banking, and account onboarding technology to community banks and credit unions. Its Nymbus Connect product exposes a modern RESTful API layer alongside a client- and partner-facing developer portal, a secure sandbox environment, real-time Kafka event streaming (event-driven architecture), and an AWS-based data lake and Redshift data warehouse for reporting and analytics. Nymbus is backed by Insight Partners. The public developer portal and API reference are gated to authenticated clients and partners, so no public OpenAPI specification is available at this time.

providers.name: Ohalo Genetics
providers.description: Ohalo Genetics is an American agricultural biotechnology company founded in 2019 and led by CEO David Friedberg, developing plant-breeding platforms and proprietary crop varieties. Its flagship Boosted Breeding technology — marketed as "2x + 2x = 4x" — alters the reproductive circuitry of parent plants so each parent passes its entire genome to the next generation rather than a random half, producing polyploid offspring that carry the full genetic contribution of both parents and, in early field trials, substantially higher yields. Ohalo pairs this with an Agile Breeding service and a True Seed program that ships uniform, disease-free seedlings directly to growers, with active programs in potato, almond (the FruitionOne self-fertile Nonpareil variety), strawberry and corn, delivered through partnerships such as the Allied Potato partnership and a strawberry consortium. The company sells plant genetics and breeding services to agricultural partners; it is not a software vendor and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: One Robot
providers.description: One Robot is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building world-model-based simulation environments for robotics teams. Its core product learns physics and visual appearance directly from real robot data, producing simulation environments that are both visually and physically realistic so teams can train and evaluate robot manipulation policies without excessive reliance on physical robot time and real-world data collection. One Robot specializes in contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects (such as textile and box folding), and precise assembly tasks. As an early-stage two-person company it currently offers task-specific simulation collaboration rather than a public developer platform or API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network for future enrichment as any developer surface emerges.

providers.name: Otrafy
providers.description: Otrafy is an AI-powered supplier management platform that automates regulatory compliance, supplier data collection, and supply chain risk assessment for QA, R&D, Regulatory, and Procurement teams at enterprise clients. The platform uses natural language processing to automate supplier data collection (citing high supplier response rates), monitors suppliers in real time against regulatory standards such as FDA, EU MRLs, California Prop 65, and PFAS, and applies AI-driven risk scoring to suppliers and facilities to streamline buyer-supplier collaboration. Otrafy is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website and product/contact pages but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Peerby
providers.description: Peerby is a Dutch peer-to-peer sharing platform that lets neighbors borrow and rent everyday goods from one another instead of buying them new. Through its website and mobile apps, members request or list items such as tools, party and event equipment, electronics, bicycles, and household goods, then arrange local pickup and return. Positioned as an affordable, convenient, and more sustainable alternative to ownership, Peerby aims to reduce consumption and waste by unlocking the underused items already sitting in people's homes. Backed by Techstars, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Peerby operates a consumer single-page web application and native apps; it does not publish a public developer/API program, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or a .well-known discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Placester
providers.description: Placester is a real estate marketing and technology platform that provides IDX-enabled websites, CRM, lead generation, and marketing automation tools for real estate agents, teams, and brokerages. Historically Placester published a developer-facing Real Estate API (api.placester.com) for listings, contacts, and website content, but the developer portal (developer.placester.com) now redirects to a site-unavailable page, indicating the public developer program is discontinued or inaccessible. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no accessible public API surface, OpenAPI, or SDK was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Planqc
providers.description: planqc GmbH is a German quantum computing company building neutral-atom quantum computers, using individual atoms trapped in optical lattices as qubits on what it describes as the most promising path to fault-tolerant, scalable systems. Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, the company delivers full-stack quantum computing — hardware, control software, and applications — including its MAQCS (Multicore Atomic Quantum Computing System) line for enterprise and scientific customers across aerospace, automotive, energy, and financial services. planqc operates from Garching and Ulm in Germany and Innsbruck in Austria, and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic cloud-access surface; access is arranged directly through the company. This profile is a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network, enriched with verified public identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Plexus
providers.description: Plexus is a global manufacturing and product development company that helps customers in highly regulated industries (Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Industrial, and Semiconductor Capital Equipment) design, manufacture, and service their products. Plexus does not currently publish a public developer API; this index tracks customer/supplier portals and corporate web properties.

providers.name: Prose
providers.description: Prose is a New York City-based direct-to-consumer beauty company that makes truly custom haircare and skincare. Customers complete an online consultation covering hair type, scalp, lifestyle, diet, and local environment, and Prose then formulates personalized shampoo, conditioner, hair masks, supplements, and skincare made to order and sold primarily through a subscription model. Prose was surfaced as a portfolio company of forerunner-ventures and insight-partners. It operates no public developer API; its verified GitHub organization publishes internal tooling and third-party client libraries only, so this profile carries company identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Reniac
providers.description: rENIAC Inc. is a Santa Clara-based data acceleration company whose flagship product, the rENIAC Data Engine (rDE), is a drop-in accelerator for open source and NoSQL databases such as Apache Cassandra. Combining FPGAs with proprietary software, rDE speeds storage, network, and compute operations and can be deployed as a hardware-optimized cache, a transparent data-acceleration proxy, or a scalable storage engine on-prem, hybrid, or in the cloud (including early availability on AWS). rENIAC targets ultra-low-latency, real-time workloads — AI/ML, fraud prevention, payment processing, electronic trading, and recommendation engines — claiming up to 10x throughput, 13x lower latency, and significant TCO and CPU reductions. rENIAC ships an infrastructure/hardware acceleration product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: ScentBird
providers.description: Scentbird is a New York City-based monthly fragrance subscription service, founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator. Members receive a travel-size (8ml) designer fragrance each month for a flat subscription fee, selecting from a rotating catalog of hundreds of designer and niche perfume and cologne brands, and can also purchase full-size bottles, candles, and beauty products through the direct-to-consumer storefront. Scentbird operates as a consumer e-commerce and subscription brand; its public engineering presence is a GitHub organization of internal tooling and open-source forks (data-integration taps, shipping-API clients, Grails plugins), and it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Seeing Systems
providers.description: Seeing Systems is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) defense technology company building autonomous, modular strike drones and AI-powered swarm coordination software at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics. Its product line includes Bandit, a cost-effective FPV drone for training and expendable missions with 30+ km of range; Banshee, an autonomous modular platform built for contested, jamming-resistant environments with 40+ km of range; and Aerie AI, swarm coordination software for multi-platform operations that lowers operator cognitive load. The company works directly with military and defense partners — including UK Royal Marine Commandos and NATO forces — rather than publishing a public developer platform. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of the latest enrichment pass Seeing Systems exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Sellpy
providers.description: Sellpy is a Swedish online second‑hand marketplace that enables individuals and businesses to sell pre‑owned items such as clothing, electronics, and home goods. By providing a convenient platform for resale, Sellpy promotes circular consumption, reduces waste, and offers buyers quality‑checked products at lower prices. The service includes collection, inspection, photography, and shipping, making sustainable shopping easy and trustworthy for customers across Sweden and beyond.

providers.name: Service Properties Trust
providers.description: Service Properties Trust (NASDAQ: SVC) is a real estate investment trust (REIT) with approximately $9.9 billion invested across two asset categories: service-focused retail net lease properties and hotels. As of March 31, 2026 SVC owned 761 net lease properties (over 13.6 million sq ft) and 93 hotels (over 21,000 guest rooms) throughout the United States. The company is externally managed by The RMR Group (NASDAQ: RMR). SVC does not operate a public developer program and exposes no public APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or webhooks; investor-facing endpoints are limited to SEC filings, press releases, email alerts, and end-of-day stock quotes.

providers.name: Sirum
providers.description: SIRUM (Supporting Initiatives to Redistribute Unused Medicine) is a nonprofit and the country's largest redistributor of surplus prescription medication. It connects unused, in-date medicine from manufacturers, wholesalers, pharmacies, and nursing homes with patients who cannot afford their prescriptions, operating under drug-donation laws across the United States. SIRUM runs a logistics and matching platform that routes donated medication to community partners and individuals in need, aiming to close the gap for the tens of millions of Americans who skip prescribed medication because of cost. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sleek EV
providers.description: Sleek EV (SLEEK EV) is a Thai-Singaporean electric motorcycle company founded in 2022, headquartered in Singapore with primary operations in Thailand. Under the mission "Sustainability must be affordable," it builds accessible electric two-wheelers — the TYPE-S, TYPE-E and TYPE-X motorcycles and the SLEEK Play 1.0 urban scooter — powered by its S-DRIVE powertrain and IP67-rated lithium-ion batteries (via Ampace/CATL). It runs the S-Charge fast-charging network (100+ stations across Bangkok) and a SLEEK App for vehicle monitoring, route planning and station finding, sold through a nationwide dealer network. BOI-certified and backed by ORZON Ventures (OR + 500 TukTuks), January Capital, A2D Ventures and Krungsri Finnovate. This is a consumer product company with no public developer/API surface.

providers.name: SmartRent
providers.description: SmartRent, Inc. (NYSE: SMRT), founded in 2017 and headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a leading provider of smart home and smart property technology for the multifamily and single-family rental industries. Its platform pairs smart hardware — smart locks, thermostats, water/leak sensors, access control and hubs (Alloy, Fusion) — with cloud-based SaaS for property operators to manage connected devices at scale. Products span smart apartments, building and common-area access control, asset protection and leak monitoring, parking management, self-guided tours, Virtual Intercom (browser-based WebRTC entry), and community/resident WiFi. SmartRent exposes a partner-gated REST API and a Phoenix Sockets real-time API for integrations, but publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI; API credentials are provisioned on request via api@smartrent.com. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: The Nuclear Company
providers.description: The Nuclear Company (TNC) is a U.S.-based nuclear energy infrastructure firm deploying nuclear power at fleet scale with a "design once, build many" standardized construction approach. Through its Powerhouse Resources arm it provides maintenance, outage execution, turbine, electrical, and instrumentation services to nuclear plants nationwide, and its proprietary AI-driven Nuclear Operating System (NOS) manages deployment and operations across the nuclear lifecycle. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network company and portfolio company of True Ventures.

providers.name: Tradeway
providers.description: Tradeway is an AI-powered field assistant for residential trade contractors working in electrical, plumbing, and HVAC. Technicians use it to plan jobs step by step with the right materials and code requirements, to identify parts from a photo with nearby supplier pricing and sourcing, and to get hands-free answers to technical questions on the job site. For business owners it centralizes crew history and field activity into a single view, reducing callbacks and rework through built-in code checks and standardized, repeatable processes so new hires can bill like veterans. Tradeway is backed by Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Transphorm
providers.description: Transphorm was a GaN (gallium nitride) power-semiconductor company based in Goleta, California, known for its GaN-on-Si cascode FET technology used in power supplies, fast chargers, motor drives, solar inverters, and EV charging. It was acquired by Renesas Electronics in June 2024, and transphormusa.com now redirects to the Renesas GaN power-discretes product line. Transphorm publishes no public web API surface.

providers.name: TTM Technologies
providers.description: TTM Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTMI) is a leading global manufacturer of technology products, including mission systems, radio frequency components, RF microwave and microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced printed circuit boards (PCBs). TTM serves aerospace and defense, data center computing, medical, industrial and instrumentation, automotive, and networking and communications markets. The company reported approximately $2.9B in FY2025 revenue, operates 24 specialized facilities across North America and Asia Pacific, and employs more than 18,000 people. TTM expanded its defense electronics footprint with the 2022 acquisition of Telephonics from Griffon Corporation.

providers.name: Twenty-First Century Fox
providers.description: Twenty-First Century Fox was an American multinational mass media corporation that operated film, television, and cable assets before being largely acquired by The Walt Disney Company in 2019. Its remaining broadcasting and news assets continued under Fox Corporation. The company no longer exists as an independent entity and did not expose public developer APIs.

providers.name: Upollo
providers.description: Upollo is a startup founded by Cayden Meyer and backed by Index Ventures that helped subscription businesses find and convert repeat trialers, account sharers, and other high-intent users, with its detection surface reachable through integrations such as a Segment browser destination action and Pipedream API components. As of July 2026 its primary domain upollo.ai no longer resolves, its GitHub organization has no public repositories, and the only first-party package remaining in public registries is a 2022 Android SDK on Maven Central, so no live API surface is currently published to capture.

providers.name: Valor Water Analytics
providers.description: Valor Water Analytics was a San Francisco-based water analytics company that built financial data and dashboard tools for water utilities, including leak and revenue-loss detection. A Y Combinator, Imagine H2O, and 500 Global portfolio company, it was acquired by Xylem Inc. (completed February 2, 2018) and folded into Xylem's digital portfolio, now represented by the Xylem Vue platform. valorwater.com redirects to Xylem Vue, and no independent API surface remains published.

providers.name: VICTUS Technologies
providers.description: VICTUS Technologies builds contested-autonomy software for autonomous systems operating in GPS-denied and jamming-heavy environments. Its PhantomNAV platform delivers precise state estimation from the gravity and inertial sensors already embedded in drones, aircraft, submarines, satellites, and ships - no new hardware required - and integrates with Palantir Foundry's AIP infrastructure. VICTUS is backed by Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a marketing and platform site but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Voxel Energy
providers.description: Voxel Energy is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company building energy-independent, off-grid data centers powered by on-site solar generation and second-life EV batteries over a DC microgrid architecture. Founded in 2025 by ex-Tesla engineers Casey Spencer, Max Pfeiffer, and Evan Schmidt, the San Francisco company delivers modular, prefabricated data center power systems that bypass multi-year utility interconnection queues, taking facilities from site selection to commissioning in months. Voxel Energy is an infrastructure hardware company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Waltz Health
providers.description: Waltz Health is a Chicago-based digital health company founded in 2021 by Mark Thierer (former CEO of OptumRx and Catamaran) and Jonathon Thierer, building AI-driven prescription drug pricing marketplaces that help consumers, payers, pharmacy benefit managers, pharmacies, and self-insured employers make better-informed, lower-cost decisions on prescription care. Its Marketplace Search product is a multi-card search engine that compares medication prices across every major discount and savings program, and Waltz Connect is an end-to-end solution that lowers the cost of specialty medications through a network of national and regional specialty pharmacies that compete on price and clinical outcomes. The company raised a $35M Series A led by GV and, in August 2025, merged with EVERSANA to form a combined pharmaceutical commercialization and drug-access platform, with Mark Thierer appointed CEO of EVERSANA. Waltz Health has no public developer API program; this profile captures company identity and live domain-security posture.

providers.name: Wheels Up
providers.description: Wheels Up Experience Inc. (NYSE: UP) is a leading on-demand private aviation provider in the U.S., offering charter and membership programs, commercial travel benefits through a strategic partnership with Delta Air Lines, and cargo services. Founded in 2013 by Kenny Dichter, Wheels Up was rescued from potential bankruptcy in September 2023 when a Delta Air Lines-led consortium (Delta, Certares, Knighthead, Cox) closed a $500M financing package and took a ~95% controlling equity stake. In November 2024 the company acquired the Embraer Phenom 300/300E fleet of GrandView Aviation ($105M) and secured $332M in equipment financing from Bank of America as part of a multi-year fleet modernization toward two core aircraft types (Phenom 300 series and Challenger 300/350). In 2025 it launched a new Signature membership portfolio and an industry-first integrated self-booking of Delta commercial flights inside the Wheels Up members app. Wheels Up does not publish a public developer API — its booking surface is a members-only mobile app and members.wheelsup.com web portal, with B2B operator connectivity historically routed through its acquired Avianis platform (2019).

providers.name: YOOX NET-A-PORTER (YNAP)
providers.description: YOOX NET-A-PORTER (YNAP) is a leading digital multi-brand luxury fashion group operating the online stores NET-A-PORTER, MR PORTER, YOOX, and THE OUTNET. Following the 2025 acquisition by Mytheresa, the group operates under the parent LuxExperience B.V. (NYSE ticker "LUXE"), pairing full-price curated luxury with off-price destinations. YNAP was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The group runs an engineering organization (YNAP Tech) and maintains public GitHub open-source tooling, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or partner developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Zomato
providers.description: Zomato is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of d1-capital, softbank-vision-fund and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: food. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: 21Vianet
providers.description: 21Vianet (VNET Group, Inc.) is the largest carrier-neutral internet and data center services provider in China, operating more than 50 data centers across over 20 cities with tens of thousands of cabinets and multi-terabit network port capacity. The company delivers hosting, managed hosting, interconnectivity, cloud, and hybrid IT infrastructure services to enterprise customers, and is the exclusive operator of Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform in mainland China through its Blue Cloud subsidiary. 21Vianet trades on Nasdaq under the ticker VNET. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; 21Vianet does not publish a public first-party developer API program, so most API artifacts are legitimately not applicable.

providers.name: 4C Medical Technologies
providers.description: 4C Medical Technologies, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage medical device company headquartered at 6655 Wedgwood Road North, Suite 160, Maple Grove, Minnesota, developing minimally invasive therapies for structural heart disease. Its lead product is the AltaValve System, a supra-annular transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) device delivered by transseptal or transapical catheter and designed to expand the treatable severe mitral regurgitation patient population, streamline the procedure and preserve the native mitral valve; the device is fully recapturable until released from the delivery catheter. AltaValve holds FDA Breakthrough Device designation and is enrolling the ATLAS global pivotal trial (NCT06465745) in the United States and Europe. The company closed a $175M Series D financing led by Boston Scientific in March 2025. It is a physical medical device manufacturer and publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Accutar Biotechnology
providers.description: Accutar Biotechnology Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Cranbury, New Jersey, founded in 2015 and previously based in Brooklyn, New York, with operations in Shanghai. It applies deep learning to small-molecule drug discovery and runs its own oncology pipeline, including the AC0682 and AC0176 protein degraders in Phase 1 trials. Its computational platform is a set of in-house AI products used in its own preclinical workflow and offered to partners: ChemiRise (retrosynthesis), Orbital (neural-network docking), Virtual Screen, Intelligent-SAR, Chemi-Net (ADME prediction) and the PatentOne AI suite (InsightOne, GenusOne). Accutar publishes no developer program: no public API, developer portal, reference documentation, machine-readable specification or SDK exists on any host it operates. Access to the AI products is arranged by email enquiry for a trial or demo.

providers.name: Again
providers.description: Again is a Copenhagen-based carbon-utilization biotech spun out of research from the Danish Technical University, Stanford, and MIT. Rather than storing captured carbon, Again feeds industrial CO2 waste and hydrogen into bioreactors where AI-designed biocatalysts ferment the gas — much like brewing — into commercial-grade acetate and other green chemicals used in adhesives, solvents, plastics, textiles, cosmetics, aromas and flavors, industrial enzymes, proteins, and fertilizers. The company runs carbon-utilization facilities in Copenhagen (CPH-1), Texas City (TXS-1, with Dow and HELM AG), and Porsgrunn, Norway (NOR-1). Again raised a $43M Series A co-led by GV (Google Ventures) and HV Capital in 2024. No public developer API surface was found during API Evangelist enrichment.

providers.name: Ainos Technology
providers.description: Ainos Technology (北京爱诺斯科技有限公司, brand eYenurse) is a Beijing health-informatization company founded in 2016 that applies artificial intelligence to children's eye health and school health administration in China, selling to government and institutional buyers rather than to developers. Its products are a national vision and common-disease monitoring, early-warning and intervention system for education bureaus and schools, a student infectious-disease early-warning system, a 0-6 eye-health screening platform for maternal and child health institutions, AI screening hardware (smart visual-acuity charts and a module linking 130+ third-party ophthalmic instruments), and the eYenurse smart ophthalmology cloud platform. It reports deployments in all 31 provinces across 1,700+ institutions and is backed by Donghua Software (002065). It publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Akston Biosciences
providers.description: Akston Biosciences Corporation is a privately held biotechnology company headquartered in Beverly, Massachusetts, founded in 2011 by the team from SmartCells, Inc. and led by CEO Todd Zion, Ph.D. Akston designs, develops and manufactures protein therapeutics built on its proprietary Ambifect Fc-fusion protein platform, with a pipeline focused on companion-animal (veterinary) medicine: PD-L1 monoclonal antibody oncology candidates (AKS-701d, AKS-619d), a long-acting GLP-1 for feline weight management (AKS-562c), an IL-31 targeting therapy for canine pruritus (AKS-699), and NGF-targeting candidates for osteoarthritis pain. Its veterinary insulin program was sold to Dechra in 2024, and human programs continue through the Vakston and Diamune Therapeutics subsidiaries. The company announced a manufacturing expansion in Shreveport, Louisiana. Akston is a therapeutics developer and manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate marketing site and no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Aleris
providers.description: Aleris was a global producer of rolled aluminum products serving the aerospace, automotive, building and construction, and other industrial end-use markets. Founded as IMCO Recycling and later renamed Aleris International, the company operated manufacturing plants across North America, Europe, and Asia. Aleris was acquired by Novelis Inc. (a subsidiary of Hindalco Industries) on April 14, 2020 for approximately $2.8 billion. The company's primary product lines included aluminum sheet, plate, and engineered products for demanding applications such as aerospace structures and automotive body panels. As a manufacturing-focused business, Aleris did not maintain a public developer API program, but engaged in B2B EDI integrations with major customers and suppliers across its supply chain. The Aleris brand has since been absorbed into Novelis and aleris.com no longer serves a website.

providers.name: Altru
providers.description: Altru (Altru Labs, Inc.) was a mobile-first, employee-generated video storytelling platform for recruitment marketing and talent acquisition, enabling organizations to capture, edit, brand, approve, and distribute authentic employee video content across career sites, social media, and email/text campaigns, with video transcription in 14+ languages. Founded in 2017 and based in Brooklyn, New York, and backed by Techstars, Altru served brands including Target, PwC, Intuit, L'Oreal, and Box before being acquired by iCIMS on December 14, 2020 and folded into the iCIMS Talent Cloud. Altru no longer operates as an independent provider — altrulabs.com now redirects to icims.com and there is no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Alume Biosciences
providers.description: Alume Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in La Jolla, California, developing nerve-targeted fluorescent agents for precision surgery. Its lead candidate, bevonescein (ALM-488) — a peptide-dye conjugate co-invented by the late Nobel Laureate Dr. Roger Tsien and surgeon Dr. Quyen Nguyen — is administered intravenously roughly an hour before an operation so surgeons can see nerves illuminated in the surgical field and avoid inadvertent nerve injury. The compound has FDA Fast Track designation, is in Phase 3 pivotal trials in head-and-neck surgery, and the company has stated it plans a New Drug Application submission in 2026. Alume is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

Its lead candidate, ABI-2280, is a topical antiviral in Phase 1b/2 clinical development for high-risk cervical HPV infection, and the company frames its work in support of the World Health Organization's global Cervical Cancer Elimination Initiative. Antiva is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and GV, and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile awaiting further enrichment.

Its pipeline includes AK0529 (ziresovir) for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, AK0901 for ADHD, AK3280 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, AK0610 for RSV prevention, and AK0705 for COPD. The company is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Armada Lintas Samudra, operating as Armada Logistics, is a professional freight forwarding and logistics company headquartered in Batam, Indonesia, with branches in Jakarta and Semarang. Founded in 2013, it offers domestic and international transportation services including ocean and air freight, chartering, land trucking, customs clearance, stevedoring, warehousing, and towing, emphasizing professionalism, speed, accuracy, safety, and integrity.

providers.name: Arpelos Biosciences
providers.description: Arpelos Biosciences is a seed-stage biotechnology company based in Kendall Square, Cambridge, developing multivalent medicines — therapeutics engineered for high potency and selectivity by engaging multiple targets or sites simultaneously. The founding team comprises scientists from UCSF, Penn, Stanford, and MIT spanning computational biology, immunology, and protein engineering, and the company is backed by prominent biotech investors including Wing Venture Capital. Arpelos currently operates as a stealth-stage research company with a single-page web presence and does not publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: ArsenalBio
providers.description: ArsenalBio is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company in South San Francisco developing programmable, integrated cell therapies for solid tumors. Its platform engineers autonomous CAR-T cells using large-scale genome engineering and computational biology to create multi-functional therapies. Backed by Kleiner Perkins and SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates in the healthcare and biotechnology sector. It publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record.

providers.name: Atara Bio

The company operates through subsidiaries such as AIG Aerospace and offers services in fabrication, manufacturing engineering, logistics technology, industrial chemicals, and scientific innovation.

providers.name: Atom Computing
providers.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

providers.name: Baan
providers.description: Baan (Baan Company N.V., originally The Baan Corporation) was a Dutch enterprise resource planning software vendor founded in 1978 in Barneveld, Netherlands by Jan Baan and later joined by his brother Paul Baan. Baan built one of the first genuinely component-based ERP suites, known for its Dynamic Enterprise Modeler (DEM), its Baan Tools 4GL development environment, and deep manufacturing and project-industry functionality. At its late-1990s peak Baan served roughly 3,000 customers and posted close to $700 million in revenue, making it one of the leading global ERP providers alongside SAP, Oracle and PeopleSoft. Following accounting controversy and a collapse in its share price, Baan was acquired by the British engineering group Invensys in 2000, sold on to SSA Global Technologies in 2003, and absorbed into Infor Global Solutions when Infor acquired SSA in 2006. Baan no longer exists as an operating company or an independent brand: the product line lives on as Infor LN, and the baan.com and baan.nl domains now permanently redirect to the Infor LN product page. Consequently this profile carries no first-party API surface of its own — any modern programmatic access to the Baan lineage is delivered through Infor LN REST APIs and the Infor ION API gateway on Infor's developer platform. Baan Company is listed by Battery Ventures as an exited investment.

Bambee also offers guided payroll and staff training, positioning itself as an all-in-one HR compliance solution that starts at a low monthly membership. providers.name: Citymapper
providers.description: Citymapper is a London-based urban transit and journey-planning company, founded in 2011, that operates a consumer mobile app for iOS and Android covering more than 80 cities worldwide. The app combines public transit (bus, rail, metro, tram, ferry), micromobility (bike share, scooter, e-bike), ride-hail, walking, and driving into multi-modal routes with real-time arrivals, disruption alerts, step-by-step navigation, fare comparisons, and journey-saving features such as Get Me Somewhere, Go, and Citymapper CLUB (its paid premium subscription). In March 2023 Citymapper was acquired by Via Transportation, the New York-based TransitTech company that supplies on-demand transit, paratransit, and network-planning software to cities and transit agencies; Via integrates Citymapper as the rider-facing layer of its end-to-end transit platform alongside Remix (network planning) and Via's own on-demand operations software. Citymapper additionally offers a B2B advertising platform (ads.citymapper.com) targeting urban commuters. Citymapper previously published a self-service Directions API, a Navigation SDK (iOS, Android, Web), and Travel Time / Routing endpoints, but discontinued all self-serve developer products on 23 June 2023; remaining transit-data and routing integrations are now delivered under enterprise contracts through Via Transportation rather than via a public developer portal. providers.description: Gate Bioscience is a preclinical biotechnology company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Brisbane, California, creating a new class of small-molecule medicines called Molecular Gates. Molecular Gates selectively eliminate disease-causing extracellular proteins at their origin inside the cell by binding the secretory translocon, the channel through which proteins exit the cell, so targeted proteins are degraded rather than secreted. The company's proprietary Molecular Gate Discovery Platform pairs a privileged library of molecules with bespoke secretion-focused assays and deep secretory-pathway biology to pursue more than 1,000 diseases linked to extracellular proteins. Gate Bioscience is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Bio + Health, GV, Versant Ventures, ARCH Venture Partners, Forbion and Eli Lilly, and has raised roughly $134M across Series A and an oversubscribed $65M Series B. Backed by DCVC since 2017, the company has developed techniques to improve the effectiveness and specificity of mRNA vaccines, including a next-generation COVID-19 vaccine engineered to resist viral mutation. HelixNano is now pursuing a broader vision of self-designing, adaptive therapeutics — drugs that could improve with every patient and, ideally, require only a single dose. The company operates out of 5 Channel Center Street in Boston, Massachusetts, and remains at an early, largely stealth stage with no public developer program or API surface at this time.

Its managed services span human resources, accounting and legal, payroll, payor negotiations and credentialing, marketing, recruiting, revenue cycle management, IT and cybersecurity, procurement, insurance and risk management, and tax preparation. The company is a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company. It operates as a healthcare business-services provider and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK.

providers.name: Holtec International
providers.description: Holtec International is a privately held American supplier of equipment and systems for the nuclear, solar, geothermal, and fossil power-generation industries. The company is best known for its spent-fuel storage and transport casks (HI-STAR, HI-STORM, HI-STORE CISF), decommissioning services through Holtec Decommissioning International (HDI), and its in-development SMR-300 small modular reactor — a roughly 320 MWe two-loop pressurized water reactor with an 80-year design life. Holtec is currently pursuing the first-ever restart of a permanently shut-down U.S. commercial nuclear power plant at Palisades in Michigan, which is also designated as the first deployment site for the SMR-300. The company runs manufacturing facilities in Camden, NJ, Pittsburgh, PA, and Orrville, OH, and partners with Hyundai Engineering & Construction (HDEC) on SMR-300 detailed design and full-scope plant construction.

providers.name: Honor

In August 2021 Honor acquired Home Instead, the world's largest senior home care franchise network, which now operates as a subsidiary of Honor; the Honor Care Platform powers both the Honor Care Network and Home Instead franchise offices. Honor exposes its platform to internal staff and to caregivers and families through the Honor Care Pro and Honor Family mobile apps and a client web portal. As of this writing Honor publishes NO public or partner developer API, developer portal, or API reference documentation - the platform is a closed, first-party care-delivery operations system rather than an API product. This entry is therefore a documentation stub kept for catalog completeness; it will be updated if Honor ever ships a documented public or partner API.

The founding team has led work in reasoning, behavioral training, agents, and alignment across frontier industry and academic labs including xAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, Reflection, AI2, Stanford, and MIT. providers.name: Kuva Space
providers.description: Kuva Space is a Finnish space-data company headquartered in Espoo that operates a fleet of hyperspectral Earth observation microsatellites and delivers AI-driven planetary intelligence through its Kuva Sense platform. Founded in 2016 (originally as Reaktor Space Lab) by Tuomas Tikka and Janne Kuhno in collaboration with Reaktor, the company designs, builds, and operates its own 6U CubeSat-class spacecraft carrying a patented in-orbit tunable Fabry-Perot 2D snapshot hyperspectral imager. Its operational Hyperfield-1A (launched August 2024 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg) and Hyperfield-1B (launched June 2025) cover the 475–950 nm VNIR range with up to 160 tunable spectral bands at 25 m spatial resolution and a 50 km swath from a 500 km polar sun-synchronous orbit. The larger 70 kg Hyperfield-2 microsatellite, scheduled for H2 2026, expands coverage to 450–1,650 nm at 15 m resolution with an additional 3.6 m GSD RGB camera. By 2030 Kuva Space plans to grow the constellation to roughly 100 satellites to enable sub-daily revisit anywhere on Earth. Onboard AI handles cloud filtering, spectral band alignment, and compression so that downlinked products feed directly into Kuva Sense, where automated analytics generate insights-as-a-service for agriculture (crop identification, yield forecasting, harvest timing), aquaculture (water quality, algal bloom detection, biomass), environment and carbon (sequestration monitoring, deforestation, pollution tracking), and safety and security (vessel detection and tracking, illegal activity warning, rapid change detection). Kuva Space is part of the European Space Agency InCubed-co-funded HYPERFIELD program, was awarded a €1.8M ESA Civil Security from Space contract within the SMART-CONNECT consortium to demonstrate rapid hyperspectral insights for crisis response, and in 2026 signed a Letter of Intent with SSC Space to strengthen Nordic space capabilities. The commercial model is subscription-based insights-as-a-service rather than pay-per-pixel imagery sales, with current access offered through the Kuva Sense Early Adopter Program; the company markets "robust APIs and customizable data formats" for system integration but does not currently publish open public API reference documentation, an OpenAPI specification, or a self-service developer portal. The only public engineering surface is the open-source kuva-data-processing Python toolkit (kuva-metadata, kuva-reader, kuva-geometry) on GitHub and PyPI, which reads Kuva GeoTIFF-based L0/L1AB/L1C/L2A data products and their metadata sidecars.
