Its services span executive advisory (fractional AI and HR leadership, AI adoption and change management, AI agent buildout), executive training (signature programs from "AI Readiness for Enterprise" through "Organizational Leadership," delivered on-demand or live), and executive search (C-suite, board, and professional placements with succession planning). Mogul reports having educated 1MM+ leaders and counts Amazon, Google, Disney, Microsoft, and Nike among its clients. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Mogul publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation; it operates as a B2B services and training business.

Each listing surfaces agency details including location, budget ranges and service descriptions, and agencies can submit or claim their own profiles. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass the live site publishes no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface.

Headquartered in Redwood City, California with an office in Basel, Switzerland, the company is pursuing a pharmacological alternative to mechanical CPAP devices by reactivating the upper-airway muscles that keep the airway open during sleep. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners, Mosanna operates a corporate marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

The platform applies domain-adapted large language models, image models, agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, and document/plan parsing (OCR and computer vision) to automate bid comparison, estimation, bill-of-materials, and budget updates for teams that still run on spreadsheets. Muro is backed by Techstars and integrates with industry tools such as Procore. As of this profiling the company publishes a marketing site, a blog, and careers pages, but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so this record captures identity and a domain-security probe rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Novocall
providers.description: Novocall was a Singapore-based callback and lead-conversion SaaS (a click-to-call and callback-scheduling widget that turned website visitors into inbound phone calls and booked meetings), surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. It was acquired by Malaysian commerce platform EasyStore in March 2023, alongside sibling product NovoChat, and has been marketed since as "Novocall, an EasyStore company". As of the August 2026 enrichment pass every Novocall host is dead: the apex novocall.co keeps live email DNS (Google Workspace MX, SPF, DMARC quarantine, CAA) but has no A record at all, www.novocall.co, app.novocall.co and call.novocall.co — the widget/dashboard host hardcoded in Novocall's own WordPress plugin — all return a Cloudflare 530 (edge up, origin gone), help.novocall.co returns 429 with Cloudflare error 1027 (account daily request limit reached), getnovocall.com times out, and novocall.com is now an Afternic parked domain whose catch-all answers 200 with an HTML lander for every path including /openapi.json and /.well-known/agent-card.json. No API, specification, developer portal, .well-known document or documentation surface exists on any reachable host. The only first-party artifact Novocall ever published that survives is a WordPress callback-widget plugin, stuck at version 1.0.0 since 2019-04-08.

Novotech reports 4,450+ trials conducted across 7,260+ trial sites in 50+ countries, supporting 60+ drugs to market. Added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company of Hongshan; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: NuScale Power
providers.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

providers.name: NVision Imaging Technologies
providers.description: NVision Imaging Technologies (now operating as NVision Quantum Technologies) is a deep-tech healthcare company that engineers quantum technology at the molecular level. Its flagship POLARIS platform delivers quantum-enhanced MRI, boosting the magnetic signal of engineered sugar molecules by over 10,000x to image disease metabolism in real time, and its PIQC platform is a quantum-computing architecture built on molecular quantum nodes native to photonic chips. The company is backed by Playground Global. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface; this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Orbital Insight
providers.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program). The company applied computer vision and machine learning to satellite imagery, aerial photography, AIS vessel signals, and IoT/mobile location data to produce intelligence on supply chains, global commodities (notably oil storage via its Global Geospatial Crude Index), geopolitical events, demographics, retail foot traffic, disaster damage, and national-security questions. Its flagship product was the GO platform (later rebranded TerraScope), a self-service geospatial intelligence platform layering proprietary models over commercial satellite imagery from partners including DigitalGlobe, Airbus, Planet Labs, and e-GEOS. Orbital Insight raised funding from In-Q-Tel, GV (Google Ventures), Sequoia Capital, CME Ventures, and others, and acquired Boston-based FeatureX in 2018. After a period of financial distress in 2023, Orbital Insight was acquired by Privateer (co-founded by Apple's Steve Wozniak and Alex Fielding) on May 6, 2024. Following the acquisition, the standalone orbitalinsight.com brand was wound down and the TerraScope platform is now offered by Privateer alongside its Wayfinder space-domain-awareness data engine, fused into Privateer's "Elements" all-domain data platform. As of 2026 there is no public self-service Orbital Insight developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the orbitalinsight GitHub organization has only two archived repositories (a region-aggregation reference and a fork of tileserver-gl) and no current developer portal.

providers.name: Orna Therapeutics
providers.description: Orna Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company, founded in 2019 on research from MIT and built by MPM Capital, that engineers circular RNA (oRNA) paired with lipid nanoparticle delivery so a patient's own body generates cell therapies — its lead program ORN-252 is a CD19-targeting in vivo CAR-T designed for B-cell-driven autoimmune disease. Orna acquired ReNAgade Therapeutics in 2024, combining its circular RNA platform with ReNAgade's LNP delivery and RNA editing capabilities, and Eli Lilly announced a definitive agreement to acquire Orna on 2026-02-09 for up to $2.4B. Orna is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract, and as of this profile its own domain ornatx.com redirects in whole to Eli Lilly's subsidiaries page.

providers.name: Ouro Medicines
providers.description: Ouro Medicines is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, California, defining the future of treatment for people with immune-mediated diseases. Its pipeline centers on T cell engager programs for autoimmune conditions, including the lead candidate OM336 (evaluated in the AIC-1001 clinical trial), alongside an expanded access policy. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As a therapeutics developer, Ouro Medicines publishes a corporate and scientific website but no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface. Recent company news includes a definitive agreement for Gilead Sciences to acquire Ouro Medicines to advance its first-in-class T cell engager program for autoimmune diseases.

providers.name: Pachama
providers.description: Pachama is a San Francisco–based climate technology company founded in 2018 that built a satellite- and machine-learning-powered platform for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of nature-based carbon projects — including forest conservation, reforestation, afforestation, and improved forest management. Pachama combined satellite imagery, LiDAR, remote sensing, and deep-learning models to measure aboveground biomass, detect deforestation, and track project performance against verified baselines, surfacing that intelligence through an online marketplace where corporate buyers (including Microsoft, Shopify, Salesforce, Flexport.org, Mercado Libre, Boom Supersonic, and Nespresso) could discover and purchase high-integrity carbon credits. In November 2025, Pachama was acquired by Carbon Direct, and its proprietary digital MRV platform and forest-carbon science team were folded into Carbon Direct's science-backed carbon management offering; pachama.com now redirects to carbon-direct.com. Throughout its life as an independent company Pachama operated a buyer marketplace and discussed plans for a partner API to embed project selection and retirement data into third-party products, but never shipped a public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification — its GitHub organization contains only forks and archived internal tooling.

providers.name: Petcube
providers.description: Petcube is a pet-technology company (a Y Combinator alum) that makes interactive Wi-Fi pet cameras and a companion mobile app for remote pet care. Its consumer hardware line includes the Petcube Cam, Bites treat-dispensing camera, and Play laser camera, offering HD video, night vision, two-way audio, motion and sound alerts, and app-controlled treat tossing and play. Petcube also sells the Care subscription (cloud video history, extended alerts) and Online Vet / Emergency Fund telehealth services. As of this enrichment pass Petcube exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented integration surface — the primary interface is the consumer iOS/Android app tied to its private cloud backend. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Pharmazz
providers.description: Pharmazz, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Willowbrook, Illinois, founded and led by pharmacologist Dr. Anil Gulati. The company discovers, develops and commercializes first-in-class therapeutics for critical care and neurovascular medicine, built around two lead small-molecule candidates: centhaquine (Lyfaquin), a resuscitative agent for hypovolemic shock that holds marketing authorization from the Drugs Controller General of India and is licensed to Dr. Reddy's Laboratories for the Indian market, and sovateltide (Tycamzzi), an endothelin-B receptor agonist for cerebral ischemic stroke. Additional pipeline programs target septic shock, acute kidney injury, cardiac arrest, acute spinal cord injury, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and Alzheimer's disease. Pharmazz is a drug-development company, not a software vendor; its public web presence is a corporate and investor brochure site and it operates no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: PillPack
providers.description: PillPack is a full-service mail-order pharmacy that sorts each customer's medications by date and time, packages them into clearly labeled dose packets, and delivers them monthly with automatic refill management. The service coordinates directly with prescribing doctors and insurance providers, charges no service fee (customers pay only for their medications), and holds URAC Mail Service Pharmacy accreditation with NCPDP E-Scribe capabilities out of Manchester, NH. Founded in 2013 and acquired by Amazon in 2018, PillPack is now operated by the same team of licensed pharmacists behind Amazon Pharmacy, which the site increasingly directs customers toward for same-day delivery and additional savings. PillPack is a consumer-facing pharmacy service with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: PsiQuantum
providers.description: PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California photonic quantum computing company founded in 2016 by Jeremy O'Brien, Terry Rudolph, Pete Shadbolt, and Mark Thompson, building utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers based on single-photon qubits at telecom wavelength. Its Omega chipset — a silicon photonic system integrating on-chip single-photon sources, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, barium-titanate optical switches, and low-loss fiber couplers — is manufactured on 300mm wafers at GlobalFoundries' flagship fab in Malta, NY, leveraging mature semiconductor processes rather than exotic cryogenic fabrication. The company is constructing two utility- scale, million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum computing sites: one at Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia (in partnership with the Australian and Queensland governments) and one at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago, Illinois (with additional R&D at PsiLabs in Daresbury, UK and assembly at PsiFactory in Milpitas, CA). PsiQuantum exposes a developer surface aimed at fault-tolerant quantum algorithm researchers: Construct, an enterprise platform for FTQC algorithm development, resource analysis, and training; Circuit Designer, a free web tool for prototyping and visualizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits; Circuit Hub, a shared library of `.circuit` files; and two open-source Python projects on GitHub — Bartiq, a symbolic quantum resource estimator that compiles subroutine-level costs to global T-gate, Toffoli, qubit, and circuit-volume estimates, and QREF, an open JSON-Schema-based format for representing quantum algorithms as hierarchical DAGs with a Pydantic validation library and a `qref-render` visualization tool. NVIDIA's CUDA-Q is integrated into Construct for accelerated simulation. PsiQuantum does not currently publish a commercial cloud-access REST API, OpenAPI specification, or a general-purpose quantum-execution SDK comparable to those of gate-model quantum cloud providers — its public developer artifacts are confined to FTQC resource-estimation tooling and algorithm-design surfaces — and there is no public pricing or self-serve tier for the underlying quantum hardware.

Its CAPAC (Click Activated Protodrugs Against Cancer) platform uses a pre-targeting approach that captures therapeutic payloads at the tumor via in-vivo click chemistry, separating tumor-targeting molecules from their drug payloads and reuniting them at the cancer site to maximize drug delivery while reducing systemic toxicity. providers.name: Shopzilla
providers.description: Shopzilla is a comparison-shopping brand that lets consumers search across thousands of merchants to compare products, prices, and merchant ratings. Originally launched as BizRate and later Shopzilla, Inc., the business rebranded its corporate entity to Connexity in 2014 and is today operated by Connexity, a Taboola company, alongside sibling properties such as Bizrate, Beso, and PriceGrabber. Shopzilla itself publishes no API: no Shopzilla-branded developer host resolves in DNS (developer.shopzilla.com, api.shopzilla.com and docs.shopzilla.com are all NXDOMAIN), and www.shopzilla.com sits behind an AWS CloudFront WAF that bot-challenges the root and returns HTTP 403 on every other path, including all /.well-known/ locations. The publisher/affiliate API program that was historically marketed as the Shopzilla Publisher Program is today published under the CONNEXITY brand, on Connexity-owned hosts, and is deliberately not catalogued here: the docs are titled "Connexity Monetization API", list info@connexity.com as the contact, and are served from api.cnnx.link and publisher-api.connexity.com. The legacy Catalog API host catalog.bizrate.com does still answer, but returns bare Tomcat errors and publishes no specification. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners; the 2026-08-13 enrichment pass probed 18 paths across three hosts, swept five package registries, and found no Shopzilla developer surface of any kind.

providers.name: Singular Medical
providers.description: Singular Medical (Suzhou Singular Medical Equipment Co., Ltd. / 苏州无双医疗设备有限公司) is a Chinese medical-device company pioneering the domestic research, development, and manufacturing of cardiac rhythm management (CRM) products. It builds China's own implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICD) and implantable cardiac monitors (ICM) — devices that automatically identify malignant arrhythmias, deliver anti-tachycardia pacing and defibrillation to prevent sudden cardiac death, and provide long-term subcutaneous ECG monitoring for the diagnosis of unexplained syncope, atrial fibrillation, and cryptogenic stroke, with cloud-based event transmission for remote clinical review. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. This is a medical-device hardware manufacturer with a corporate marketing web presence and no public developer, API, or documentation program at this time.

providers.name: Sino Biological
providers.description: Sino Biological is a global life-science reagent supplier and contract research organization founded in 2007, headquartered in Beijing, China, with a US subsidiary in Wayne, Pennsylvania and offices across Europe. The company manufactures and sells recombinant proteins, antibodies, ELISA kits, cDNA clones, and other research reagents in-house, and provides contract biologics services (protein production, antibody development, gene synthesis) for academic, biopharmaceutical, and diagnostic customers worldwide. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company stub of Qiming Venture Partners, this profile was run through the enrichment pipeline; no public developer API, developer portal, or programmatic-access surface was discoverable (the corporate site is bot-protected and returns HTTP 403 to automated clients).

providers.name: Slice Labs
providers.description: Slice Labs is a New York-based insurtech company that operates as an insurance-as-a-service cloud platform provider. Founded in 2015 and publicly launched in 2016, Slice originally offered on-demand insurance products for the sharing economy (homeshare, rideshare, cyber) and then pivoted to offering its underlying digital insurer stack — branded Insurance Cloud Services (ICS) — to other carriers, MGAs, and brands. The ICS platform packages pricing, rating, licensing, real-time and automated underwriting, policy servicing, claims, and capacity into a cloud-hosted, API-embeddable subscription. The company's modern product surface focuses on 100% digital small-business insurance distributed through agents and partners (currently Contractors General Liability, with Commercial Real Estate and Excess Casualty announced as coming soon) on top of Slice Mind, an AI/ML, behavioral-science, and LLM-driven intelligence layer. Slice Labs publicly markets its platform as "fully embeddable via API," but the developer portal, OpenAPI specs, SDKs, and endpoint reference are not exposed on the open web — integration is gated behind a B2B carrier/partner relationship. The official GitHub organization (github.com/slicelabs) exists but is archived with zero public repositories, and there is no public developer.slice domain serving documentation. As a result this profile captures the company, product, and platform surface only; no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, Naftiko capability, plan, rate-limit, or FinOps artifact is generated here because none of the underlying contracts are publicly observable.

providers.name: Spokn
providers.description: Spokn is an AI-powered short-form video creation platform built for internal communications, HR, and learning & development teams. It lets organizations collect selfie, full-screen, or screen-share clips from employees across desktop and mobile, then stitch, trim, caption, translate (15 languages), and brand them into polished employee videos in under 30 minutes without video-editing expertise. Finished videos distribute via intranet, LMS, Microsoft Teams, Slack, email, or MP4 export. Spokn integrates with common HRIS (BambooHR, Workday, Zenefits, ADP, Rippling), SSO (Okta, OneLogin, G Suite), and Slack, but does not currently publish a public developer API, API reference, or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Stats Perform
providers.description: Stats Perform is a global sports data, AI, and technology company formed by the 2019 merger of Stats LLC and the Perform Group. The company owns and operates the Opta brand, the de facto standard for granular football (soccer) event data, and supplies live data, advanced metrics, predictive models, video, graphics, and AI-powered content to media broadcasters, sportsbooks, fantasy operators, professional clubs, leagues, governing bodies, and brands. Its product portfolio is organised around three customer segments — Media & Tech, Betting & Fantasy, and Team Performance — and exposes data and AI capabilities through a family of Opta-branded products including Opta Feeds (XML/JSON sports data feeds), Opta Live (live event data), Opta Stream (low-latency push), Opta Vision (computer-vision tracking), Opta Predictions (probability models), Opta Points (player ratings), Opta Pulse (event commentary), Opta Stories (auto-generated narratives), Opta Search (natural-language sports search), Opta Graphics (broadcast graphics), and OptaAI Studio (AI content tooling). Access to Opta data and APIs is partner-gated: prospective customers must contract through Stats Perform sales, and developer documentation, schemas, and reference material are delivered through a private customer portal rather than a public developer area. Stats Perform also operates StatsBomb's competitors The Analyst as a public-facing editorial property, and runs the annual Opta Forum for customers and analysts.

providers.name: Stickies
providers.description: Stickies (stickies.wtf) was a Los Angeles-based consumer web3 company, built by BYO Labs, that made "dumb stickers and GIFs starring your favorite NFTs" — users connected a crypto wallet holding their NFTs and generated custom stickers and GIFs of those avatars for use in messaging and social apps. Founded around 2022 by Tom Wright (CEO) and Sterling Barnett (COO), it raised roughly $5.5M with backing from Lightspeed Venture Partners (Jeremy Liew). The product was a closed consumer web app with no public developer API, documentation, or SDK. The company appears defunct: the stickies.wtf site was last captured live in 2023, returned 403s by mid-2024, and the domain no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN) as of July 2026; co-founder Sterling Barnett has since moved on to other ventures.

providers.name: The Lowdown

It enables people to review and research their health conditions, symptoms and medications so they can make more informed decisions, starting with contraception and expanding into menopause, fertility, PCOS, endometriosis, periods and weight care. The platform combines scientific information with a unique dataset of thousands of community reviews and hundreds of thousands of data points on lived experience across dozens of contraceptive methods and brands, alongside medical advice and online prescriptions. It is free to use, monetising through partnerships with the NHS, women's health innovators and clinical trial recruitment. The Lowdown was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it is a consumer web platform and currently exposes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Traverse
providers.description: Traverse is a San Francisco data research lab, founded in 2025 by Lance Yan and backed by Y Combinator (W26) along with angel investors from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and Meta. Traverse partners with frontier AI labs to solve "non-verifiable" work: the ambiguous, taste-dependent, long-horizon tasks in domains like law, healthcare, sales, and writing where reinforcement learning lacks the clean deterministic feedback loops it has in math and coding. The lab captures real human expert behavior in highly controlled settings and turns judgment, taste, and reasoning into high-fidelity training environments for frontier models. As of mid-2026 Traverse is an early-stage research lab with no public API, developer platform, SDKs, or product documentation — its public surface is a manifesto-style website, a blog, careers pages, and a contact CTA for prospective lab partners.

Tripoto was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. At the time of this profile no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal was discoverable; an api.tripoto.com host exists but serves the consumer application backend.

providers.name: Trishula Therapeutics
providers.description: Trishula Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing cancer immunotherapies that target immune-evasion mechanisms in the tumor microenvironment. Its lead candidate, TTX-030, is a first-in-class monoclonal antibody that inhibits CD39, an enzyme in the adenosine pathway that tumors exploit to suppress anti-tumor immunity; TTX-030 has advanced into Phase 2 clinical trials, including studies in metastatic pancreatic cancer. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a therapeutics company with a corporate web presence and no public API, developer, or software product surface.

providers.name: TTAGG
providers.description: TTAGG was a social media analytics startup founded in October 2011 in Fayetteville, Arkansas, and backed by 500 Global. It rebranded as DataRank in 2013, providing brand managers with tools to monitor and rank conversations about their brands and competitors across social media, blogs, forums, and e-commerce sites. DataRank was acquired by Simply Measured in 2015, which was in turn acquired by Sprout Social in 2017. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API; datarank.com redirects to sproutsocial.com and ttagg.com is parked.

providers.name: Tulipshare
providers.description: Tulipshare is a London-based impact investor and shareholder advocacy group that uses activist investing to push for ethical and sustainable change at the world's largest companies. It leverages shareholder proposals, direct board and ESG-team engagement, and other shareholder rights on behalf of foundations, asset managers, universities, and pension funds. Backed by Speedinvest. Its consumer website (tulipshare.com) went offline in 2026 and the company publishes no public API surface.

providers.name: Tupperware Brands
providers.description: Tupperware Brands Corporation was an American multinational consumer goods company that manufactured and marketed premium kitchen storage, preparation, and serving products under the Tupperware brand, as well as related home product lines. The company distributed products to approximately 70 countries through independent sales force members. Tupperware Brands filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2024 and underwent liquidation in 2025. The Tupperware brand name was subsequently acquired by Party Products LLC. No public developer API program was available during the company's operation.

providers.name: Twenty20
providers.description: Twenty20 was a crowdsourced stock photography marketplace that sourced authentic, mobile-first imagery from a community of smartphone photographers, backed by Bullpen Capital, Canaan Partners, and Version One Ventures. The company was acquired by Envato in 2021 and no longer operates a standalone product - twenty20.com now permanently redirects to Envato Elements, and no public API, developer portal, or first-party SDKs remain (probed 2026-07-21).

providers.name: UberSense
providers.description: UberSense was a Boston, Massachusetts sports-technology startup whose mobile app provided slow-motion video capture and analysis for coaching athletes, from recreational to Olympic and professional levels. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), UberSense was acquired by Hudl in September 2014 and its technology folded into Hudl's sports video analysis products. The ubersense.com website is now defunct (a decommissioned Heroku app) and the company publishes no public API surface.

providers.name: Umbala
providers.description: Umbala (Umbala Labs, formerly Umbala Technologies / UmbalaTv) is a Vietnamese consumer video and camera technology startup backed by 500 Global. It built the UmbalaTv short-video and livestream mobile app and later the Umbala Network blockchain platform, including StreamX decentralized live video streaming and the CameraX camera AI/AR engine. The company currently maintains a minimal site at umbala.io and publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its historical umbala.tv domain now redirects to unrelated third-party content.

providers.name: United Dwelling
providers.description: United Dwelling was a Los Angeles-based real estate development company founded in 2018 by venture capitalist Steven Dietz to address the affordable housing shortage by converting underused garages and backyards into accessory dwelling units (ADUs). The company offered studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom zero-net-carbon units ranging from 328 to 647 square feet and handled permitting, construction, financing, and property management end to end. It raised a $10 million Series B in May 2020 led by Alpha Edison with participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners. The business appears to have wound down - its website has lapsed (Squarespace account expired) and its Los Angeles location is marked closed as of mid-2026 - and it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Venova Medical
providers.description: Venova Medical, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage medical device company in Los Gatos, California, developing minimally invasive vascular access technology for patients on hemodialysis. Its Velocity Percutaneous AVF System is a next-generation percutaneous arteriovenous fistula (pAVF) device intended to create a functional dialysis access with fewer reinterventions and faster maturation than a surgically created fistula, targeting the stenosis at the artery-vein junction that is the most common barrier to AVF success. The company is running the VENOS clinical program (VENOS-2 early feasibility, VENOS-3 IDE pivotal) toward FDA approval; the Velocity System remains investigational and is not FDA cleared or approved. Venova is backed by ShangBay Capital, Banyan Pacific, Aphelion Capital, Cardeation, Kofa Healthcare, Catalyst Health Ventures, Cadence Growth Capital and Mirae Asset Capital Life Science. Venova publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification: it is a physical medical device manufacturer, not a software provider.

Backed by General Catalyst, SignalFire, Sapphire Ventures, Abstract Ventures, and Y Combinator. providers.name: VideaHealth
providers.description: VideaHealth (VideaAI) is an FDA-cleared dental artificial intelligence platform that analyzes dental radiographs to detect clinical findings such as caries, bone loss, calculus, and periapical lesions, and to surface aligner and implant treatment opportunities. VideaAI runs as ambient, chairside AI embedded directly inside dental practice-management and imaging systems (Dentrix, Denticon, Open Dental, Eaglesoft, Carestream, Dexis, Apteryx XVWeb, and others) - as soon as an X-ray is captured, the platform analyzes it and returns findings in the tools clinicians already use. Its detection, findings, study, and integration capabilities are delivered through partner-gated, embedded integrations rather than a public, self-serve developer API; there is no publicly documented REST API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI definition as of this writing.

Virtuoso is a venture-backed portfolio company of Canaan Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: X-energy
providers.description: X-energy is an advanced nuclear reactor and fuel company headquartered in Rockville, Maryland, founded in 2009 by Dr. Kam Ghaffarian. The company's flagship product is the Xe-100, an 80 MWe (320 MWe four-pack) high-temperature gas-cooled small modular reactor (SMR) using helium coolant and TRISO-X pebble fuel, designed to deliver both electricity and high-temperature process steam to industrial customers. X-energy's fuel subsidiary, TRISO-X, is building a commercial TRISO fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. Project pipeline includes a four-unit Xe-100 plant for Dow Chemical at Seadrift, Texas (NRC environmental assessment completed May 2026, the first US advanced reactor environmental review to be completed), a 12-unit Xe-100 deployment with Energy Northwest at the Tri-Cities, Washington site, a collaboration with Amazon Web Services for data-center power, a feasibility study with LG&E and KU in Kentucky, work with Ontario Power Generation in Canada, and selection under the US Department of Energy's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP). X-energy is led by CEO J. Clay Sell and Chairman/founder Dr. Kam Ghaffarian. Investors include Amazon (Climate Pledge Fund), Ares Management, Citadel, Segra Capital Management, Jane Street, Ken Griffin, the University of Michigan, and others. X-energy completed an upsized IPO on Nasdaq in April 2026. The company does not publish a public developer API or SDK.

Its platforms — 订餐小秘书, 宴位 (Yanwei, an AI-driven dynamic-pricing product for restaurant private rooms), and 高能店长 — let diners book tables and discounted private-room packages at Shanghai restaurants through web, WAP (m.xiaomishu.com / m.57.cn), phone, and WeChat mini-program channels. providers.name: Zivtech
providers.description: Zivtech is a Philadelphia-based digital design and development agency founded in 2008, specializing in open-source web platforms (Drupal and WordPress) for mission-driven organizations including universities, hospitals, museums, and foundations. Founder and CEO Alex Urevick-Ackelsberg leads a small team (~10 staff) serving clients such as Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, Rutgers University, Temple University, Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, the Institute for Advanced Study, the Science History Institute, and the John Templeton Foundation. Their tagline: "We design and build technology that helps progressive organizations meet ambitious goals." Zivtech is a services firm — not an API provider. They build custom Drupal and WordPress sites, mobile applications, and digital experiences for clients, but they do not publish or operate any public APIs, SDKs, developer portals, pricing, status pages, or OpenAPI artifacts of their own. Their value lies in professional services and long-term client partnerships rather than a product or platform with a programmable surface area. For API Evangelist purposes this repo serves only as a registry placeholder confirming the agency's existence, scope, and status.

providers.name: 1yongcloud
providers.description: Beijing Yiyong Technology Co., Ltd. (北京壹永科技有限公司 / 1yongcloud), founded in October 2017, is a Chinese oncology big-data and artificial-intelligence company. It builds medical-data collection, quality-control and governance capabilities and healthcare information products for hospitals and government health programs. Its product lines include a tumor diagnosis-and-treatment standardization and cost-rationalization platform, a hospital cancer opportunistic-screening platform, an integrated clinical-research platform, and a smart-hospital comprehensive operations decision platform. The company is backed by investors including Qiming Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital China, and Cathay Capital. It operates no public developer portal, API, or SDK; this profile tracks 1yongcloud as a company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AA Audience
providers.description: AA Audience is an adtech and data company that estimates a mobile user's credit score from their online activity using proprietary machine learning models. It collects data from partner mobile apps and ad networks, analyzes it, and connects with popular DSPs and DMPs so its clients - banks, credit card companies, and financial services firms - can target audiences interested in credit cards, loans, and financial services with guaranteed ROI. Publishers integrate a JavaScript header-bidding tag to enrich their bid stream; advertisers buy segments into their own DMP or as a DealID for their DSP, from a stated floor of $1 CPM. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, documentation, specification, SDK, or public repository was found during enrichment - the site is five static HTML pages served from an S3 bucket whose homepage has not changed since March 2018, and the Login link in the navigation is a dead button on a page with no form.

providers.name: abcMob
providers.description: abcMob is a mobile business application company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Westminster, California. It builds and sells ready-made and custom native business applications for banking, airlines, HRIS, insurance, restaurants, hotels, tourism, universities, gyms, music, sport clubs, brokerage, oil and gas, real estate, retail, agriculture, survey, TV and places of worship. Its stated approach is to write one codebase that is translated to native code per platform (Objective-C on iOS, Java on Android, C on Windows and Linux) and compiled into full native applications, with an HTML5 web view of the same service, so the look, feel and update cadence stay consistent across devices. The company sells finished client/server applications and cloud hosting to businesses; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Absology
providers.description: Absology Co., Ltd. is a South Korean in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Anyang, Gyeonggi-do. It designs and manufactures point-of-care immunoassay analyzers and the reagent cartridges that run on them, built on microfluidic immunoassay and photo-oxidation-induced fluorescence amplification chemistry. Its Absol analyzer line runs rapid and ultra-sensitive quantitative blood tests — testosterone, vitamin D, PSA, TSH, free T4, PCT, cortisol and cardiac markers — for human and companion-animal use, with stated research programs in anti-cancer therapy monitoring, cardiovascular disease and neurodegenerative disease. Absology is a hardware and consumables manufacturer rather than a software vendor, and no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract has been found on its corporate site or in any public package registry or code host.

providers.name: ACE Green Recycling
providers.description: ACE Green Recycling, Inc. is a US-headquartered battery recycling technology company that develops and licenses electrified, hydrometallurgical processes for recovering critical materials from end-of-life lead-acid and lithium-ion batteries. Its proprietary GREENLEAD process produces battery-grade lead, and its LithiumFirst process recovers lithium carbonate, graphite, NMC and MHP precursors, cobalt, nickel and copper salts from LFP, NMC and LTO chemistries, all at zero Scope 1 emissions. ACE operates commercial lead and lithium plants in India and Taiwan, licenses its technology to existing recyclers internationally, and is building its own advanced recycling operations in the United States. The company announced a NASDAQ listing and $32M in PIPE funding in 2026. ACE is an industrial process and materials technology company; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: ACT-ion
providers.description: ACT-ion Battery Technologies, Inc. is an advanced battery materials company founded in Dallas, Texas and spun out of Hunt Energy Enterprises, now running an advanced cathode pilot plant in Carrollton, Texas. It manufactures surface-engineered single-crystal cathode active materials (CAM) for lithium-ion batteries across LFP, LMFP, NMC and lithium-manganese-rich chemistries, marketed as ACT-ion LXP+, using a chemistry-agnostic high-throughput continuous synthesis process that deposits a protective, conductive shell during particle growth to cut CAM cost and plant footprint. It raised a $7.5M pre-Series A led by BASF Venture Capital, extended to $11.5M, won a 2024 R&D 100 Award, and named Mark McGough CEO in August 2026. ACT-ion is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: AeroShield
providers.description: AeroShield (AeroShield Materials, Inc.) is a Waltham, Massachusetts materials science company spun out of MIT in 2019 that has developed and scaled the world's most transparent silica aerogel. Its ultra-clear aerogel sheets are laminated into insulated glass units so that a standard double-pane window or door can outperform a triple pane while remaining thinner and lighter, boosting thermal efficiency by up to 65%. The company sells business-to-business to window, door and skylight manufacturers rather than to consumers, operates a pilot manufacturing facility in Waltham, and was selected for a $14.5M ARPA-E award. It publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts; this profile records that absence.

providers.name: AESOP
providers.description: AESOP Technology is a clinical AI company building a Clinical Deep Reasoning engine that reconstructs, models, and analyzes how clinicians make decisions across diagnosis, treatment, medication management, and medical coding. A 2019 spinoff from Taipei Medical University now headquartered in San Francisco, AESOP trains on more than 3.2 billion real-world medical records and 5 million clinical decision pathways to make clinical reasoning explicit, traceable, and actionable. Its products DxPrime (diagnostic integrity and automated code translation, a qualified solution on Mayo Clinic Platform) and Medigator integrate with EHR systems to improve patient safety, coding accuracy, and medication management. AESOP is backed by 500 Global, Taiwania Capital, BE Capital, and Colopl Next.

providers.name: Aktoria Robotics
providers.description: Aktoria Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics company (Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch) building a teleoperation and remote-operation layer for robots under the banner "Human as API for Robots." Its platform lets operators run any robot anywhere in the world, remotely collecting operational data from robot fleets 24 hours a day, monitoring and intervening in deployed fleets, and moving hardware through a train-to-deploy-to-monitor lifecycle. Founded in 2026 by Shreenabh Agrawal (robotics, Carnegie Mellon University) and Jaskaran Singh Walia (previously a researcher at Microsoft, MIT, CMU, Cambridge, and NUS), the company is at the pre-product-launch stage and does not yet publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Alabama Power
providers.description: Alabama Power is an investor-owned electric utility serving Alabama and a subsidiary of Southern Company. No public developer portal, API, or Green Button Connect My Data program was found.

providers.name: Alpha Technologies
providers.description: Alpha Technologies is a power-systems manufacturer providing AC, DC, and renewable powering solutions for the telecom, cable-broadband, traffic, security, industrial, and alternative-energy industries. Its product line spans uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), standby and non-standby power systems, batteries, enclosures, network/fiber powering gear, and renewable-energy products. Founded in the 1980s and now part of EnerSys, Alpha operates as a hardware and stored-energy solutions provider rather than a public API platform; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel-associated portfolio lead and carries no public developer or API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Alsym Energy
providers.description: Alsym Energy is a Malden, Massachusetts battery technology company founded in 2015 by Mukesh Chatter, Rahul Mukherjee, and Kripa Varanasi to develop low-cost, high-performance rechargeable batteries that are free of lithium and cobalt. Its Na-Series is a line of non-flammable, non-toxic sodium-ion batteries aimed at grid and utility-scale energy storage, data-center backup, and industrial applications where safety and supply-chain resilience matter. The company uses a proprietary AI/computational-materials platform to accelerate battery chemistry development, and has raised roughly $111M+ including a $78M round in 2024 led by Tata Limited and General Catalyst. Alsym is a hardware/energy-infrastructure manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AMP Fund
providers.description: AMP (AMP PBC) is a public benefit corporation founded in 2025 by Anjney Midha, a former Andreessen Horowitz general partner, to build an independent "AI grid" — a pooled compute utility for frontier AI research teams. Rather than operating as a cloud provider or a conventional venture firm, AMP acts as an independent system operator: data center operators and labs contribute underutilized GPU capacity to a shared network, and member research teams draw base-load and burst compute from that pool at rates intended to sit below the volatile spot market. AMP pairs capital with compute, having raised roughly $1.3 billion for its first fund, and its PBC charter is structured so leadership can supply compute at cost without shareholder challenge. It has also committed a Public Wealth Fund of up to $500 million through 2030 toward education, workforce readiness, healthcare access, and economic resilience in communities affected by the AI transition. AMP publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Aneira Pharma
providers.description: Aneira Pharma is a biotechnology company focused on innovative hair growth therapies. Their flagship product ANR-001 combines minoxidil and latanoprost to stimulate thicker, longer, darker hair. The company seeks foreign clinical and commercial partners, holds patents in 58 countries, and is advancing clinical development with FDA‑approved imaging validation. Founded by pharma veterans, Aneira aims to bring dual‑action hair growth solutions to global markets.

providers.name: Ariceumtherapeutics
providers.description: Ariceumtherapeutics is a biotech company focused on developing innovative radiopharmaceutical therapies for rare cancers. The firm aims to leverage cutting‑edge molecular targeting and imaging technologies to create precision treatments that improve patient outcomes while minimizing side effects. As a relatively new entrant in the oncology space, Ariceumtherapeutics is building its pipeline through collaborations with academic institutions and seeks to expand its clinical trial portfolio in the coming years.

providers.name: Atlas Discovery
providers.description: Atlas Discovery is an AI-powered biotechnology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building foundation models of human patient biology to predict how people will respond to drugs in clinical trials. Nine of ten drugs fail in trials because no animal model or cell in a dish reliably predicts a human response; Atlas Discovery trains models on preclinical and clinical data to improve trial design and rescue stalled drug programs. Its research spans single-cell representation learning (ExpressionVAE) and clinical response prediction, with work presented at ICLR '26, ICML '26, and CSHL '26. The company is an early-stage research lab with no public API, developer program, or product surface yet; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting a public developer offering.

providers.name: Ayima
providers.description: Ayima is an enterprise SEO consultancy founded in 2007, offering technical SEO, AI-driven insights, migrations, link building, and performance optimization services. Their AI Co-Pilot provides diagnostics, recommendations, and strategies to improve site speed, crawl errors, and backlink profiles, serving major global brands.

providers.name: Azuria
providers.description: The website wired to this profile (azuria.com) resolves to Azuria Water Solutions, an infrastructure-rehabilitation company that has operated for over 50 years in the water, wastewater, and stormwater sector. It renews aging pipeline infrastructure through cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) technology, water main renewal, cathodic protection, and spray-on lining, operating through brands including Insituform, Underground Solutions, MTC, and Corrpro. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface: it is not an API provider. NOTE: this stub was surfaced as a norwest-venture-partners portfolio lead, but that linkage is unverified — Norwest's public portfolio does not list an "Azuria", and this water-infrastructure company may be a different entity than the intended Norwest-backed one.

providers.name: BBN Technologies
providers.description: BBN Technologies is a research and development organization founded in 1948 (originally Bolt Beranek and Newman) and now operating as RTX BBN Technologies, a division of RTX (Raytheon). BBN is historically notable for pioneering the ARPANET, early network email, and packet-switched networking, and today conducts advanced defense and intelligence R&D across AI/machine learning, command and control, cyber operations, signal processing and spectrum, networking, quantum and photonics, and voice and language technologies. BBN serves government and defense customers and does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface; this profile is maintained for network identity and discovery only.

providers.name: BDG
providers.description: BDG is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling. It currently exists as a placeholder entry with minimal public information, and its primary listed website points to the Nasdaq Private Market portal. No specific API endpoints or documentation have been identified, and the entry serves as a starting point for future enrichment as more data becomes available.

providers.name: Be Biopharma
providers.description: Be Biopharma (Be Bio) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in October 2020 by Longwood Fund together with B cell engineering researchers David Rawlings, M.D. and Richard James, Ph.D. of Seattle Children's Research Institute. The company develops engineered B Cell Medicines (BCMs) — a patient's own B cells engineered to produce a therapeutic protein — for genetic disease, cancer and other serious conditions. Its lead candidate, BE-101, inserted a functional Factor IX gene into primary human B cells for hemophilia B and held FDA Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations; a second program, BE-102, targeted hypophosphatasia. The company raised $82M in October 2024 and $92M in a January 2025 Series C, dosed the first participant in the Phase 1/2 BeCoMe-9 trial in July 2025, and terminated that trial in June 2026 for stated strategic business reasons. Be Biopharma is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it has never published a developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Benga
providers.description: Benga International GmbH is a diversified provider of specialized products and services, including medical supplies, military and police equipment, travel accessories, and custom branding solutions. Operating out of Cyprus with a global client base across Germany, Japan, and the USA, Benga leverages over 25 years of experience to deliver high‑quality, durable products tailored to government tenders and private sector needs. The company emphasizes innovative research, comprehensive engineering, and customer service, positioning itself as a world‑class supplier for discerning clients seeking reliable, customizable solutions.

providers.name: Bestviewlaser
providers.description: Bestviewlaser, also known as BV Laser, is a global manufacturer of medical aesthetic laser equipment offering ODM and OEM services. The company provides advanced diode, CO2, picosecond, and other laser technologies for dermatology, dentistry, surgery, and aesthetic clinics worldwide. With a comprehensive R&D center, extensive certification (FDA, CE), and a sales network covering over 70 countries, BV Laser delivers innovative, safe, and effective laser solutions for professional practitioners.

providers.name: Betterskillsinc
providers.description: Betterskillsinc provides ITIL, COBIT, ISO and other professional certification training courses in Portugal. It offers a range of certification programs, including ITIL 4 Foundation, Managing Professional, Strategic Leader, and various ISO standards, targeting individuals and organizations seeking to improve their IT service management and governance capabilities.

providers.name: Beyond Reach Labs
providers.description: Beyond Reach Labs is a Brooklyn, New York aerospace company building deployable solar arrays and thermal radiators for spacecraft that expand from compact launch sizes to enormous structures in orbit. Its patented geometry-changing panels grow from the size of a dining table to a football field once deployed, giving satellites, orbital data centers, commercial space stations, and lunar outposts up to 10x more usable power without adding launch mass or volume. Founded by two aerospace engineers, the company is targeting its first in-space demonstration in Q2 2027 and is a Y Combinator portfolio company. Beyond Reach Labs is a hardware manufacturer and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.description: Open Source Shrimad Bhagavad Gita API including 21+ authors translation in Sanskrit/English/Hindi

providers.name: Big Shot Pictures
providers.description: Big Shot Pictures is a next‑generation entertainment studio focused on building global franchises. It creates original worlds designed to scale across platforms, audiences, and formats, combining proven storytelling expertise with cutting‑edge technology. The company aims to develop properties that resonate worldwide, leveraging decades of experience in film, TV, and digital media to reach billions of viewers.

providers.name: BioInno
providers.description: BioInno is a biotechnology-focused company identified in the API Evangelist harvest backlog. Public information is limited; the primary website https://bioinno.com responds with a JavaScript-rendered page, and no detailed corporate description or product information is readily available. The company appears to operate in the life sciences sector, but further specifics require direct inquiry or access to proprietary sources.

providers.name: Bitglass
providers.description: Bitglass is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: BlackSky
providers.description: BlackSky Technology (NYSE: BKSY) is a Herndon, Virginia headquartered real-time space-based intelligence company that operates a high-revisit Earth observation constellation and delivers AI-enhanced tactical ISR (intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance) imagery and analytics to defense, intelligence, and global security customers. BlackSky's flagship product is the Spectra platform — a cloud-based intelligence hub that provides on-demand satellite tasking, sub-90-minute imagery delivery, automated AI-driven object detection and change monitoring, archived imagery access, and a secure tasking and delivery API. The company operates Gen-2 satellites at 83 cm resolution and a newer Gen-3 constellation delivering 35 cm class very-high-resolution imagery with infrared sensors, inter-satellite links, and on-board AI processing, manufactured at BlackSky's facility in Tukwila, Washington. Commercial offerings include BlackSky ON-DEMAND (flexible global tasking) and BlackSky ASSURED (dedicated, contracted persistent monitoring capacity). BlackSky's Spectra tasking and imagery API is integrated into partner platforms including Esri ArcGIS, UP42, and the STAT (Satellite Tasking API) community spec, however the API is access-controlled for vetted defense, intelligence, and enterprise customers and is not exposed as a public self-service developer portal — there is no public Spectra developer documentation site, OpenAPI specification, or open SDKs at the time of this entry. The customer revenue model is subscription-based Spectra ON-DEMAND and ASSURED contracts, Mission Solutions custom engagements, and through marketplace partners.

providers.name: Blue Current
providers.description: Blue Current is a stub entry created by the API Evangelist harvest process, representing a company identified in secondary-market data sources. The entry serves as a placeholder for future enrichment, awaiting verification of its official website, detailed description, and associated API documentation. This placeholder enables the profiling pipeline to track and eventually incorporate comprehensive information about the company’s services, products, and technical interfaces as they become available.

providers.name: Blue Planet
providers.description: Blue Planet is a stub entry in the API Evangelist catalog, representing a company for which detailed API information has not yet been discovered. The entry serves as a placeholder pending further investigation to identify the company's official website, API offerings, and related documentation. This placeholder will be enriched as more data becomes available through subsequent profiling steps.

providers.name: Bluebook
providers.description: Bluebook is a Stockholm, Sweden based software company building AI agents for accounting firms, accountants, and CFOs. The platform automates accounting workflows — reconciliations, accruals, accounts payable and receivable, month-end close, reporting, and accounting research — with the stated goal of a "zero-day close", and integrates with the general ledgers firms already run on, notably QuickBooks and NetSuite. The product surface is organized around Background Agents, Checklists (tasks, delegation, human-in-the-loop approvals, month-end close), and an Assistant covering FP&A, flux analysis, and accounting research. Founded in 2024 by Philip Andersson (CEO), Jonathan Andersson (COO), and Filip Stål (CTO), Bluebook went through Y Combinator (Winter 2025) and raised a $3M pre-seed led by EQT Ventures with participation from Y Combinator and angel investors from Affirm, OpenAI, and ElevenLabs. Bluebook is a product company, not an API provider: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: BSOS
providers.description: BSOS is a Web3 infrastructure company building compliant financial rails across emerging markets and institutional finance. It operates two core lines of business - compliant stablecoin payment networks for cross-border USD settlement in emerging markets (starting with Latin America), and institutional-grade real-world asset (RWA) tokenization systems for leading financial institutions in Asia. Its products include Velaro for cross-border USD payments, RWA SuiteX for asset tokenization, and SUPLEX for supply chain finance. BSOS is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Calpine
providers.description: Calpine Corporation was a major U.S. energy company headquartered in Houston, Texas, and was the largest generator of electricity from natural gas and geothermal energy in the United States. It operated 80 power plants with approximately 26,035 megawatts of generation capacity, including The Geysers, the world's largest geothermal complex. Calpine also operated the Champion Energy retail electricity subsidiary serving deregulated markets. As of January 2026, Constellation Energy completed its acquisition of Calpine for $16.4 billion, making it a business unit of Constellation. Calpine does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Cameo3
providers.description: Cameo3 is a marketplace that connects fans with their favorite celebrities, allowing personalized video shoutouts and other fan experiences. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, Cameo has grown into a platform hosting thousands of talent across entertainment, sports, and business, offering a range of services for both consumers and creators.

providers.name: Ciitizen
providers.description: Ciitizen is a digital health company that helps patients collect, organize, and control their own medical records. Founded by Anil Sethi and backed by a16z, Ciitizen built patient-directed tools for aggregating records across providers under HIPAA right-of-access, originally with a focus on cancer patients. The team and technology now operate as Citizen Health (citizen.health), which turns a patient's medical records into instant answers through an AI Advocate built for rare disease patients and caregivers and used by 100+ patient advocacy groups. Ciitizen exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time; this profile captures the company identity and its live web presence.

providers.name: Collaborative Robotics
providers.description: Collaborative Robotics (Cobot) is a Physical AI company founded by Brad Porter building AI-powered collaborative robots that work safely alongside people. Its flagship robot, Proxie, is a human-capable mobile manipulator designed to address labor shortages across warehousing, manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare. The company uses ScoutMap to analyze facility operations and identify automation opportunities, then deploys robots that learn real-world workflow patterns. Backed by General Catalyst, Collaborative Robotics is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it is a hardware / Physical AI provider with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Convertinsights
providers.description: Conversion Insights is a strategic AI advisory firm that helps businesses accelerate growth through digital customer acquisition and real‑time intelligence. Their platform combines AI‑driven paid media, conversion optimization, data integration, CRM, and content strategies to fill marketing pipelines, while offering dashboards, anomaly detection, and actionable alerts that turn data into immediate business decisions.

providers.name: Coolso
providers.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: CopilotKit
providers.description: CopilotKit builds AI‑powered developer tools that streamline the creation, testing, and deployment of AI agents. Their platform offers a suite of components—including a VS Code extension, mock infrastructure, oversight dashboards, knowledge‑base search, and intelligent support outpost—to help developers integrate large language models into applications with reliable tooling, observability, and rapid iteration.

providers.name: Core & Main
providers.description: Core & Main is a leading specialty distributor of water, wastewater, storm drainage, and fire protection products and related services to municipalities, contractors, and engineers across the United States. As a Fortune 500 company, Core & Main operates more than 320 branch locations and provides products and services for water infrastructure, geosynthetics, fusible HDPE pipe, smart metering, fire protection, and erosion control.

providers.name: Coremedic
providers.description: Coremedic GmbH is a privately held medical device company headquartered in Radolfzell, Germany, with a subsidiary in Biel, Switzerland. Founded in 2012 as a spin‑out from the University of Bern, Coremedic develops minimally invasive treatments for mitral valve regurgitation, notably the ChordArt TMVr system. The company focuses on innovative cardiology solutions, holds EN ISO 13485 certification, and operates within the European medical technology market, offering detailed product information, clinical data, and contact resources through its website.

providers.name: Coreshell
providers.description: Coreshell (Coreshell Technologies, Inc.) is a San Leandro, California battery technology company founded in 2017 that develops silicon-anode lithium-ion battery cells built on low-cost, domestically sourced metallurgical-grade silicon instead of graphite or refined polysilicon. A proprietary nanolayer surface coating stabilizes the silicon anode, and the company has unveiled commercial-scale 60 Ah cells aimed at electric vehicles, defense platforms and stationary energy storage. Coreshell is a materials and cell manufacturer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a Webflow marketing site with no developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, SDK, or public code repository.

providers.name: Cornershop by Uber
providers.description: Cornershop is an on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service founded in 2015 in Chile by Oskar Hjertonsson, Daniel Undurraga, and Juan Pablo Cuevas, simultaneously launching in Santiago, Chile and Mexico City, Mexico. The platform connects consumers with personal shoppers who pick and deliver groceries, pharmacy items, and other goods from local supermarkets, specialty stores, and big-box retailers. After a 2018 acquisition attempt by Walmart was blocked by Mexican regulators, Uber agreed in October 2019 to acquire majority ownership, completing full acquisition in July 2021 at a reported valuation north of US$3 billion — Chile's first unicorn exit. At its peak Cornershop operated in eight countries across the Americas: Chile, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Peru, Canada, and the United States. Beginning in 2021 Uber merged the Cornershop brand into Uber Eats, migrating the grocery vertical ("Uber Eats Grocery") into its main consumer app and progressively shutting down the standalone Cornershop apps and websites. As of 2026 cornershopapp.com and cornershop.io redirect to ubereats.com, the Cornershop LLC GitHub organization (archived October 2024) has zero public repositories, and there is no public developer API, SDK, partner program, or technical documentation under the Cornershop brand — Cornershop survives only as engineering history and as the LatAm backbone of Uber Eats Grocery. Community-built unofficial Python wrappers exist on GitHub but reverse-engineer the consumer mobile app and are not sanctioned by Uber.

providers.name: Cosemitech
providers.description: Cosemitech (意瑞半导体（上海）有限公司) is a high‑tech semiconductor solutions provider founded in 2014, designing and producing sensing and control ICs such as Hall switches, current sensors, linear Hall and speed sensor ICs for automotive, industrial, energy and consumer electronics markets. The company has shipped over 700 million units to more than 300 global customers, offering high‑performance, reliable and functional‑safety‑focused products.

providers.name: CubeSmart
providers.description: CubeSmart (NYSE CUBE) is a self-administered and self-managed real estate investment trust (REIT) and the third-largest owner and operator of self-storage properties in the United States. As of December 31, 2024 the company owns 631 self-storage properties across 25 states and Washington DC, containing approximately 45.8 million rentable square feet, and operates a third-party management platform that pushes the total managed network well past 1,300 properties. Headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, CubeSmart originated as U-Store-It Trust (founded July 2004, IPO October 2004) and rebranded to CubeSmart on September 14, 2011. The company is a component of the S&P 400. CubeSmart does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal — its public technology footprint is limited to the consumer cubesmart.com booking/account site and the CubeSmart mobile apps for iOS and Android.

providers.name: Darling Ingredients
providers.description: Darling Ingredients is a global developer and producer of sustainable natural ingredients from edible and inedible bio-nutrients, creating products for the food, pet food, feed, fuel, bioenergy, and fertilizer industries. Darling operates Diamond Green Diesel as a renewable diesel joint venture with Valero, and brands such as Rousselot (gelatin and collagen), Sonac, CTH, and EnviroFlight. Darling does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: DeepWay 深向
providers.description: DeepWay (深向科技 / Shenxiang Technology) is a Chinese intelligent new-energy heavy-truck company, backed by Baidu and Qiming Venture Partners, that designs and manufactures electric autonomous freight trucks it calls RoboTrucks. Its vehicle line includes the Xingchen II (深向星辰 II) and Xingtu (深向星途) electric heavy trucks paired with the Tianji (天玑) driver-assistance and autonomous driving stack, an AI-based fleet management platform, and a vehicle-owner mobile app. DeepWay reports 7,500+ activated L2 vehicles, a 30%+ subscription rate, and 300M+ km of assisted-driving operation, and follows a roadmap from L2 assistance (2023) to L4 platooning (2025) to single-vehicle L4 autonomy (2028). Its business model progresses from vehicle sales to subscription services to large-scale autonomous logistics capacity. As of this enrichment pass DeepWay publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification — this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Doczen
providers.description: Doczen is an enterprise AI transformation platform that connects business signals to actionable outcomes, helping large organizations adopt AI in days rather than months. The product uses AI agents to interview employees and aggregate signals from communication and productivity tools to surface operational issues, then ranks the resulting opportunities by financial impact, ROI, feasibility, and urgency. It guides implementation through buy-vs-build decisions and vendor recommendations, and runs a continuous monitoring loop that tracks progress and measures business impact. Doczen targets enterprises across financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, energy, technology, and transportation and logistics, and integrates with hundreds of tools. It advertises an enterprise security and compliance posture (ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, EU AI Act) via a Vanta-hosted trust center. Doczen is backed by Seedcamp and was added to the API Evangelist network from the Seedcamp portfolio; it currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Echo AI (fka Pathlight)
providers.description: Echo AI (formerly Pathlight) was an AI-driven customer conversation intelligence platform used by customer-experience and support teams to analyze support conversations, surface hidden insights, and coach agents. Founded as Pathlight and backed by Kleiner Perkins, Insight Partners and Quiet Capital, it rebranded to Echo AI in January 2024 and was acquired by contact-center workforce-engagement vendor Calabrio on 2024-12-11; the technology now ships inside Calabrio ONE, and calabrio.com itself now redirects to verint.com. The company publishes no discoverable public developer surface of its own — no API documentation, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP server, agent card or first-party SDK — and both brand domains are dark — pathlight.com no longer resolves and echoai.com returns a removed Framer site (HTTP 404). The Wayback index for both domains contains no /api, /docs/api or /developer path at any point in their history, only legal pages. The only verified live public asset is the Pathlight GitHub organization, whose 62 public repositories are third-party forks plus first-party Singer.io taps that INGEST other vendors' APIs (Zendesk, Gorgias, Gladly, Dialpad, Five9, Kustomer) rather than any first-party client library. This profile is retained as an identity record; no fabricated API artifacts were added, and the npm/PyPI packages that share the Pathlight and Echo AI names were verified to belong to unrelated publishers.

providers.name: Electio
providers.description: Electio (Electio Technologies) is a San Francisco-based, General Catalyst-backed software company building modern control-system software for energy production and transportation infrastructure. The company modernizes the legacy industrial control layers behind power generation, oil and gas, and transportation networks with next-generation software for monitoring, automation, and operational reliability. Electio is an early-stage, largely stealth company: it publishes a company website, a careers page, a contact page, and a privacy policy, but has not released a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile. This entry was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and enriched as an identity-only lead.

providers.name: Elektrik App
providers.description: Elektrik is a medium voltage (MV) equipment procurement platform for electrical distributors, contractors, and Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms. Founded in 2020 by Mario Dealba out of the Techstars Alabama EnergyTech Accelerator, the company streamlines sourcing of medium- to high-voltage supplies (roughly 5kV-35kV / 600V-69kV) including MV cable, terminations, splices, deadbreak and loadbreak connectors, and transformers. Buyers build part lists and specifications in the web app and Elektrik surfaces matching products across leading manufacturers such as TE Connectivity, BURNDY, Richards Manufacturing, and PFISTERER, compressing a traditionally slow, quote-driven procurement cycle. Backed by Techstars and growth capital, Elektrik is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Elion Therapeutics
providers.description: Elion Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for life-threatening invasive fungal infections (IFIs). Formerly known as Sfunga Therapeutics, the company was founded on the belief that mechanistic insight into natural products enables targeted optimization of them. Its lead candidate, SF001, is a next-generation polyene antifungal — a rationally designed analog of amphotericin B intended to retain broad fungicidal activity while mitigating the systemic toxicity that limits the parent molecule. SF001 received FDA Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) and Fast Track designations in 2023 and has advanced from a first-in-human single-ascending-dose study into multiple-ascending-dose evaluation.
