providers.name: Uniform Teeth
providers.description: Uniform Teeth was a San Francisco clear-aligner orthodontics startup founded by Meghan Jewitt and orthodontist Dr. Kjeld Aamodt, launched in 2018, pairing licensed in-clinic orthodontists with a patient app — positioned between traditional orthodontics and direct-to-consumer aligners. Canaan Partners led its $10M Series A. On August 5, 2022 it was acquired by (merged with) Barcelona-based Impress (smile2impress.com) to build a worldwide network of invisible-orthodontic clinics. The company published no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, and uniformteeth.com no longer serves a site (stale Netlify deployment returning 404); this API Evangelist profile records its identity and domain posture.

providers.name: Variant
providers.description: Variant is an AI-powered design tool at variant.com (formerly variant.ai) built around the promise of endless designs for your ideas - enter an idea for an app or site and see endless design options just by scrolling. A Kindred Ventures portfolio company, Variant currently keeps its product and site pages behind authentication and publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: venusmedtech
providers.description: Venus Medtech (Hangzhou) Inc. is a China-based innovator in transcatheter structural heart valve therapies, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Hangzhou. Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (2500.HK), it pioneered first-in-China TAVR and TPVR solutions and covers TAVR, TPVR, TMVR and TTVR heart valve intervention devices, including the commercialized VenusA-Valve, VenusA-Plus, VenusA-Pro, VenusA-Deluxe and the VenusP-Valve TPVR system. It is a physical medical-device manufacturer that publishes a corporate/product marketing site and an eIFU (electronic Instructions for Use) portal, and has no public developer API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Vertosmed
providers.description: Vertos Medical (vertosmed.com) is a medical device company founded in 2005 and based in Aliso Viejo, California, focused on minimally invasive treatments for lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS). Its proprietary Mild (Minimally Invasive Lumbar Decompression) procedure is an image-guided outpatient treatment that removes a major root cause of LSS through an incision smaller than a baby aspirin, without implants, general anesthesia, or stitches. Vertos Medical was acquired by Stryker Corporation in 2024 and is now part of Stryker's Interventional Spine business; vertosmed.com now redirects to stryker.com. As a clinical medical-device manufacturer, Vertos Medical publishes no public developer, API, SDK, or integration surface.

providers.name: Verve Therapeutics
providers.description: Verve Therapeutics is a Boston-based clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of in vivo gene editing medicines designed to treat cardiovascular disease with a single, one-time treatment. Its programs use base editing and CRISPR technology to durably switch off disease-driving genes, led by VERVE-102 (targeting PCSK9 to lower LDL cholesterol), alongside VERVE-201 (ANGPTL3) and VERVE-301 (LPA). Verve was acquired by Eli Lilly in July 2025 in a deal worth up to $1.3 billion. As a therapeutics/research company it publishes no public developer API; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: Vicinitas Therapeutics
providers.description: Vicinitas Therapeutics is a biotechnology company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. It operates in the therapeutics and drug-discovery space (vicinitastx.com) and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface. providers.description: Zap Energy is a Seattle, Washington fusion energy company pursuing commercial fusion power via the sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch — a compact, magnet-free pulsed-power approach in which a flowing column of deuterium plasma is compressed (pinched) to fusion conditions inside a roughly two-meter metal tube, with shear in the axial flow stabilizing the pinch in place of the heavy superconducting magnets used by tokamak and stellarator designs. Founded in 2017 by Benj Conway, Brian A. Nelson, and Uri Shumlak as a spinout of University of Washington and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory research, the company has developed a lineage of devices — ZaP, ZaP-HD, FuZE, FuZE-Q, and FuZE-3 — culminating in 2024 with Century, a 100-kW-scale repetitive pulsed-power test platform with liquid-metal walls intended to demonstrate plant-relevant technologies. In November 2025 FuZE-3 reported plasma electron pressures of 830 MPa (1.6 GPa total), the highest pressure measured in any sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch and a marker on the path to scientific energy gain (Q>1). Zap Energy was selected for the U.S. Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program in May 2023 and received DOE approval of the preconceptual design of its Fusion Pilot Plant. The company has raised over $325 million across Series A–D from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, Energy Impact Partners, Chevron Technology Ventures, Shell Ventures, DCVC, Valor Equity Partners, and Addition. As of April 2026, Zabrina Johal serves as CEO with Conway as President, and the company has expanded its mandate to also pursue small modular fission alongside its fusion roadmap. Zap Energy has no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release; the technical surface is published as peer-reviewed papers and DOE milestone reports.

The company raised a $10M seed round in October 2025 led by Union Square Ventures with Voyager Ventures, Fifty Years, and Harpoon Ventures, and counts Breakthrough Energy among its backers. providers.name: Tractable
providers.description: Tractable is a London-headquartered artificial intelligence company founded in 2014 by Alexandre Dalyac, Razvan Ranca, and Adrien Cohen that applies computer vision and deep learning to automate visual damage assessment for auto and property insurance claims. The platform analyzes photos of vehicles and buildings down to the pixel to produce accident first-notice- of-loss (FNOL) triage decisions, AI-generated preliminary repair estimates, automated claim review for fraud and consistency, subrogation packet analysis, and property repair-cost estimation and underwriting condition assessment. Tractable's flagship offerings include Auto Estimator, Auto Damage Appraiser, Auto Salvage, Property Estimator, Property Underwriter, and the LumaScanner fixed-operations vehicle scanning product. The company serves insurers, dealerships, repair networks, recyclers, and fleet and rental operators including GEICO, Aviva, Mitchell, Tokio Marine, Admiral, Sompo, Aioi Nissay Dowa, and LKQ. Tractable reached unicorn status in June 2021 and secured a $65M investment from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 in July 2023, scaling to over 300 employees across offices in London, Warsaw, Paris, Milan, Spain, Romania, New York, Toronto, Tokyo, and Bangkok. The product is delivered through flexible desktop and API integrations with FNOL, estimatics, and claim review systems, but the developer surface is gated to enterprise partners — there is no public developer portal, self-service API key, OpenAPI specification, SDK release, or open-source repository, and no publicly published authentication, endpoint, pricing, or rate-limit documentation.

The company designs, synthesizes and characterizes novel organic semiconductor molecules, evaluates transparent photovoltaic devices against industry test protocols, and sells technical consultation, R&D, design and engineering services to glass and glass-coating manufacturers. The company uses a single-step fermentation process that produces and biodegradably encapsulates biological actives all at once, giving added stability and a tunable release profile for targeted, non-toxic pest and disease control intended to be safe for pollinators, people and soil. Its first commercial product, the broad-spectrum biofungicide FUN-THYME, is marketed through an exclusive partnership with Wilbur-Ellis and was approved in California in 2026. providers.description: AllTrails is an outdoor recreation platform for discovering, mapping, and navigating hiking, trail running, mountain biking, and backpacking routes. It offers a searchable database of hundreds of thousands of trails worldwide with maps, elevation profiles, community reviews, photos, and conditions, plus GPS turn-by-turn navigation, offline downloadable maps, and route planning through its AllTrails+ subscription. AllTrails is a consumer mobile and web application; it does not publish a public developer API program, and its web surface is served behind a Cloudflare WAF that blocks automated discovery. providers.name: Alphina Therapeutics
providers.description: Alphina Therapeutics is a New Haven, Connecticut precision-oncology biotechnology company founded by experts in DNA repair and metabolic lethality. It develops next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) that deliver potent NAMPT inhibitor payloads directly to tumors, designed to kill both dividing and non-dividing cancer cells, and pairs them with a proprietary companion diagnostic that identifies the patients most likely to respond. The company is venture-backed by Canaan Partners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation, so no API artifacts apply at this time.

providers.name: Amber Bio
providers.description: Amber Bio is a San Francisco biotechnology company developing an RNA-based gene-editing platform capable of making multi-kilobase edits — rewriting thousands of bases on a single RNA strand in one step — to reach previously undruggable patient populations. Because edited RNA eventually degrades in the body, the approach is designed to be safer and reversible compared with permanent DNA editing. The platform pairs multi-kilobase RNA writing with AI foundation models to target diverse pathogenic variants across patients with a single product, initially focused on ophthalmology and central nervous system diseases. Founded by CRISPR-field researchers from the Broad Institute and UC Berkeley (co-founder and CTO Basem Al-Shayeb, advised by Nobel Laureate Jennifer Doudna), Amber Bio launched in 2023 with a $26M seed round co-led by Playground Global and Andreessen Horowitz. It has no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: AnalytiChem

The company operates under ISO 17034, ISO 17025 and ISO 9001 quality accreditations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. providers.name: Applied Biosystems

Its software surface is delivered through Thermo Fisher Connect, a cloud platform for storing, analyzing, and sharing instrument data with Applied Biosystems qPCR and Sanger secondary-analysis modules, the Cloud Connect Utility for uploading data from non-cloud-enabled instruments, and the Instrument Connect remote-monitoring app. Applied Biosystems does not publish a standalone public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program; its programmatic footprint is instrument-connectivity and cloud analysis rather than a hosted web API. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with verified company identity only.

providers.name: Aurora Therapeutics
providers.description: Aurora Therapeutics is a CRISPR gene-editing biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing scalable, personalized genetic medicines for rare diseases. Founded by gene-editing pioneers including Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Fyodor Urnov and led by CEO Edward M. Kaye, the company uses an "umbrella" approach that bundles multiple rare disease-causing mutations under a single regulatory pathway, combining guide RNA design, AI-engineered editors, and delivery systems to correct mutations at scale. Backed by Menlo Ventures, Aurora is profiled in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass it publishes a corporate website and news surface but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other technical/developer surface.

The physical REAL Series card holds the keys; a companion mobile app, Ballet Crypto, lets holders check balances and market value and add assets. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Ballet is a hardware/consumer product rather than a developer platform, so it publishes no public API — this profile captures its identity, security posture, and open-source footprint.

It aims to streamline legal workflows with advanced search, AI-driven insights, and collaboration features, positioning itself as a leading solution in the legal technology market.

providers.name: Bloomin' Brands

It owns and operates four restaurant concepts — Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill, and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar — across the United States and internationally (Brazil, South Korea, Hong Kong, and China). The company's consumer technology centers on the Web-based Dine Rewards loyalty program, per-brand mobile apps (iOS/Android) for online ordering, curbside takeaway, delivery, table payment, reservations, and waitlist, and corporate supplier portals (BBI Connect). providers.name: Brightloom

The product unifies point-of-sale, loyalty, ecommerce and marketing data into a single customer view, reports on data health, runs AI-driven hyper-segmentation and anomaly detection over that data, and recommends the next campaign and audience a brand should target. Brightloom was sold as an end-user SaaS with prebuilt connectors to common POS, loyalty and marketing platforms rather than as a developer platform, and it published no public API reference, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification. The company now appears defunct: the last dated item on its own press page is December 2022, the entire operating estate it once held TLS certificates for is gone from DNS — api.brightloom.com, api-prd/api-dev, the cgp.brightloom.com application, its auth0-cgp Auth0 tenant, and the status, support and knowledgebase hosts all NXDOMAIN — brightloom.com publishes no MX record, and only the frozen marketing site remains, with its /about/ page defaced by injected search-spam.

providers.description: Forge Robotics is a Galway, Ireland and San Francisco based robotics company building modular autonomous factories for metal fabrication. Its shipping container sized, software configurable units combine a vision system, sub millimeter 3D scanning, and robotic intelligence to autonomously handle, position, weld, laser engrave, and finish metal assemblies, turning conventional human programmed industrial welding robot arms into autonomous members of the workforce. The company targets the skilled welder shortage in US manufacturing with continuously operating, snap together production modules. Forge Robotics was co founded by Eoin Cobbe (CEO) and Robert Cormican (CTO) and is a Y Combinator backed pre seed startup. Grove has demonstrated proof-of-concept against targets including AR/AR-V7, SHOC2, MYC, TAU, and KEAP1/NRF2. providers.name: Iridium
providers.description: Iridium Communications Inc. (NASDAQ: IRDM) is a McLean, Virginia satellite communications company operating a constellation of 66 cross-linked Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that deliver truly global L-band voice, data, IoT, and positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) services across every region of the Earth, including the polar oceans. Iridium sells satellite phones (Iridium Extreme), satellite messengers, satellite IoT modules and modems (Iridium 9602/9603, Iridium Certus 9770/9810/9704, Iridium Edge, Iridium Edge Pro, Iridium Edge Solar), Short Burst Data (SBD) messaging, broadband Certus terminals, and next-generation Iridium NTN Direct 5G Non-Terrestrial Network services built on 3GPP NB-IoT for direct-to-device smartphone and IoT connectivity. Iridium CloudConnect — co-developed with Amazon Web Services — pipes satellite IoT data as JSON into customer-owned Amazon SQS queues inside their own AWS VPC over a dedicated private Iridium-AWS interconnect, making Iridium the first global cloud-native satellite IoT backhaul. The company serves aviation, maritime, government/defense, land-mobile, autonomous systems, and IoT markets through a partner ecosystem of more than 500 service providers, value-added resellers, and hardware OEMs, and in May 2026 announced a planned acquisition of Aireon, operator of the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance network. Iridium's business model is airtime/subscription revenue plus hardware module licensing and engineering services; there is no public, self-service developer API or OpenAPI — network access is mediated through Iridium-authorized service providers, the Iridium CloudConnect AWS integration, and hardware-level AT-command and SBD interfaces on Iridium modems.

providers.name: Medikine

PEPTIKINES emulate the beneficial activities of natural cytokines while being much smaller in molecular weight and structurally unrelated in sequence, making them amenable to enhanced pharmacokinetics, cell targeting, and conditional activation without generating neutralizing antibodies to native cytokines. The company's lead candidate, MDK-703, is an Fc-fusion protein containing an IL-7 PEPTIKINE that mimics the T-cell-supporting properties of IL-7, with a pipeline spanning oncology, autoimmune, and infectious-disease therapeutics. Medikine is a private, venture-backed drug-discovery company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or technical developer surface.

Mount secures the agent workflow, quantifies the residual operational risk, helps fix vulnerabilities, and transfers the remaining risk through insurance, advertising fast activation and dynamic, usage-based pricing. Founded in 2026 by Fabian Amherd and John Bachmann and based in San Francisco, Mount aims to rebuild the commercial-insurance carrier stack from the ground up with AI at its core.
