Robinhood acquired X1 in 2023 and folded the product into what is now the Robinhood Gold Card; x1creditcard.com and api.x1creditcard.com redirect to robinhood.com (probed 2026-07-21). X1 never published a public developer API, ships no SDK packages, and has no GitHub organization, so this profile records the acquisition and the domain-security posture of the remaining domain and points to the Robinhood profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Yards Brewing
providers.description: Yards Brewing Company is an independent craft brewery founded in 1995 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Yards operates a brewery and taproom at 500 Spring Garden Street and distributes its classic and seasonal beers across the Mid-Atlantic. The company emphasizes local craftsmanship, community, and Philadelphia identity, summed up in their tagline that things are not made in Philadelphia but made BY Philadelphia.

providers.name: Yodle
providers.description: Yodle was a New York-based local online marketing and lead-generation company for small and medium-sized businesses, offering all-in-one advertising, web presence, and business-automation products such as Marketing Essentials, Yodle Ads, and Lighthouse 360. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, it was acquired by Web.com in February 2016 for roughly $342 million and no longer operates as a standalone brand — its technology was folded into Web.com, now part of Newfold Digital. Yodle exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; api.yodle.com is an internal, auth-gated endpoint (HTTP 401) and the legacy www.yodle.com site is effectively defunct.

providers.name: Yoom (fka Tetavi)
providers.description: Yoom (formerly Tetavi) is an Israeli deep-tech company founded in 2016 that develops volumetric video and markerless performance-capture technology using proprietary AI and neural networks. Its products include YoomTrack, a studio-grade markerless motion-capture system that captures full-body, hand, and facial motion simultaneously, and the YOOM Volumetric plugin for Unreal Engine (distributed via Epic Games' Fab marketplace) that plays back volumetric capture content in real time. Yoom serves gaming, film, TV, VFX, and immersive-media studios and is backed by Insight Partners. The company distributes its technology as game-engine plugins (Unreal Engine, Unity, Autodesk Maya, MotionBuilder) rather than as a public web API; as of this pass it publishes no REST/GraphQL API, developer portal, SDK on a public package registry, or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: ypxfood
providers.description: ypxfood (YPX Cayman) is a Taiwanese quick-service restaurant company specializing in Taiwanese food and snacks, backed by Qiming Venture Partners, LionRock Capital, and Ignition Capital. It is a consumer restaurant and food business with no public developer or API surface; enrichment probes found the corporate website (Cloudflare-fronted, returning 403 to automated clients) and no documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or well-known discovery endpoints. This profile is retained as a network company record.

providers.name: Yunji
providers.description: Yunji (云集) is a leading membership-based social e-commerce platform in China, founded in Hangzhou in May 2015. Yunji curates a wide range of consumer products across health food, beauty, personal care, digital devices, and apparel, and uses a member-driven model in which members earn rewards by sharing products with their social contacts. The company applies big data and artificial intelligence to optimize the shopping experience and incentivize social promotion. Yunji listed on the Nasdaq Stock Exchange (ticker YJ) in May 2019 as the first membership-based Chinese e-commerce firm to do so. Yunji was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, Yunji operates as a consumer mobile-app commerce platform and publishes no public developer or open API program.

providers.name: Zapp
providers.description: Zapp is a London-based premium quick-commerce (q-commerce) business that delivers daily essentials such as snacks, drinks, groceries, household items and pharmacy needs across central London in minutes, 24/7. Founded in 2020 by Navid Hadzaad and Joe Falter, the company operates a network of micro-fulfilment "dark stores" and a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) rather than a public developer platform. Zapp is a venture-backed company whose investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this profile, Zapp exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; it is a business-to-consumer delivery brand surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Zebrium
providers.description: Zebrium was an AIOps startup that used unsupervised machine learning to automatically detect anomalies and surface root cause from log data, correlating logs and metrics into plain-language incident summaries without manual rules or training. Backed by Accel, the company was acquired by ScienceLogic in 2022 and its technology folded into the ScienceLogic AIOps / SL1 platform (now surfaced as Skylar). The independent zebrium.com developer/API surface has been retired: the domain 301-redirects to sciencelogic.com and no standalone Zebrium API, documentation, or specification remains publicly discoverable. This profile is retained as a network lead recording the acquisition and the residual domain footprint.

providers.name: Zed.run
providers.description: Zed.run is a digital horse racing platform where players buy, breed, and race NFT racehorses, originally built on the Ethereum and Polygon blockchains and developed by Virtually Human Studio. Players collect uniquely bred digital racehorses as non-fungible tokens, enter them into skill- and bloodline-based races, and trade them on a secondary marketplace. providers.description: MNT-Halan is a Cairo, Egypt-headquartered fintech holding company and Egypt's first private fintech unicorn, founded in 2017 by Mounir Nakhla (CEO) and Ahmed Mohsen (CTO). MNT-Halan operates a financial super app ("Halan") and a vertically integrated digital ecosystem covering micro-finance and SME lending, consumer credit, e-payments and money transfers, an e-wallet, prepaid and installment cards, payroll advances, investment and gold-installment products, and e-commerce (electronics, appliances, FMCG, e-grocer). Lending products span nano loans up to EGP 2,000, microloans, consumer loans up to EGP 500,000 over 36 installments, SME loans from EGP 200,000 up to EGP 15 million, education and home financing up to EGP 4 million, light-vehicle financing, and buy-now-pay-later. The Halan app and its supporting agent network reportedly serve 5–7 million customers, have disbursed in excess of USD 4 billion in loans across 3 million borrowers, and process 100+ million USD in monthly payments and 50+ million USD in monthly e-commerce sales. After raising USD 400 million in 2023 to cross unicorn status and an additional USD 157.5 million in 2024 (including an IFC investment), MNT-Halan expanded beyond Egypt into Turkey (via the August 2024 acquisition of Tam Finans), the UAE (December 2024 launch), and Pakistan. MNT-Halan's revenue model is interest and fees on lending, merchant and payment fees, e-commerce gross margin, and card interchange; the company markets directly to consumers and SMEs through its Halan app and physical outlets, and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, partner sandbox, or open-source code repository.

Two products are already deployed with major market players: IRIS, a wheeled autonomous robot that captures large-scale site data, and BOX, which provides a reliable home base and on-site infrastructure for entirely self-sufficient robots. Two more robots are joining the fleet: MULE for onsite material handling and SCRUBBLES for site cleanup. The company is vertically integrated from developing its own AI to 3D printing its robots, owning the full hardware and software stack. Founded by CEO Scott Fairley and based in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, Optimotive raised a 2M USD seed round led by Version One Ventures in September 2024, with participation from Garage and NewLab. As a physical robotics hardware business, Optimotive publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: 1366 Technologies
providers.description: 1366 Technologies was a Bedford, Massachusetts solar manufacturing company founded in 2008 out of MIT, best known for its patented Direct Wafer process — a kerfless method that casts multicrystalline silicon photovoltaic wafers directly from molten silicon in a mold, skipping the ingot-growing and wire-sawing steps that waste roughly half the silicon in conventional wafer production. The company raised venture funding from North Bridge Venture Partners, Polaris Partners, Hanwha, Tokuyama and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and operated a demonstration line in Bedford. In June 2021 it merged with Dallas-based Hunt Perovskite Technologies to form CubicPV, combining Direct Wafer silicon with printed perovskite to pursue tandem modules; CubicPV cancelled its planned 10 GW US wafer factory in February 2024 and refocused on perovskite tandem development. 1366 Technologies is a materials and equipment manufacturer, not a software vendor: it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and its own domain 1366tech.com has served an expired TLS certificate since May 2024.

providers.name: AdBm Technologies
providers.description: AdBm Technologies is an Austin, Texas acoustical engineering company that designs and manufactures near-pile underwater noise mitigation systems for offshore wind construction. Its injection-molded HDPE Helmholtz resonators, mounted on an expandable steel framework and paired with an integrated bubble curtain, absorb and disperse the low-frequency sound energy generated during pile driving so contractors can meet underwater noise regulations while protecting marine life. The technology grew out of more than a decade of research at the University of Texas at Austin Applied Research Laboratories and has been deployed on offshore wind projects from the North Sea to the Atlantic coast of the United States. The company sells and leases hardware and project services; it publishes no public API, developer program, or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Advanced Ionics

Founded in 2017 and relocated to Milwaukee in 2018, the company targets decarbonization of heavy industry — steel, ammonia, refining and other hydrogen-intensive sectors — and has run pilot and demonstration projects with Shell through its GameChanger program and with the Entrepreneurs Fund of the Repsol Foundation, and signed a collaboration MOU with ACWA Power. Advanced Ionics manufactures electrolyzer hardware; it does not operate a public developer program, and no public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification was found.

Its developer and API hostnames do not resolve, and the entire cwbank.com domain now 301-redirects to National Bank of Canada (nbc.ca). Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached only indirectly through third-party data aggregators (Plaid is confirmed via aggregator coverage directories). providers.description: Chanjeenergy is a startup focused on providing innovative energy solutions and financing options to accelerate the transition to renewable energy. The company aims to bridge the gap between investors and clean energy projects, offering flexible financing structures and leveraging technology to streamline project development and management. Through its platform, Chanjeenergy connects developers, investors, and stakeholders to facilitate the growth of sustainable energy infrastructure worldwide.

providers.name: Chargelab
providers.description: Chargelab is a fintech startup focused on providing innovative charging solutions for electric vehicles. The company aims to simplify the EV charging experience through a robust API platform that enables developers to integrate charging station data, availability, pricing, and transaction processing into their applications. Chargelab’s services include real‑time station status, reservation management, billing integration, and analytics, targeting fleet operators, mobility providers, and consumer apps. While still early in its public rollout, the company positions itself as a bridge between EV infrastructure and digital services, emphasizing scalability, security, and developer-friendly documentation.

providers.name: Chargexmunichgermany
providers.description: Chargexmunichgermany is currently listed as a stub company in the API Evangelist catalog, originating from a secondary-market harvest. No public website or detailed corporate information has been identified. The entry exists to enable future profiling and enrichment as more data becomes available.

providers.name: Chengrui
providers.description: Chengrui Power Technology (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. is a Chinese company specializing in port and maritime electrification solutions, energy storage, and smart shipboard power systems. The firm offers a range of products including shore power systems for ports, energy-saving and intelligent solutions for maritime operations, storage systems, and shipboard power equipment. Their mission is to become a leading domestic and world-class provider of new energy and electrical automation technologies for the maritime industry, delivering innovative, reliable, and efficient power solutions to support sustainable port and shipping operations.

providers.name: Chesapeake Green Fuels
providers.description: Chesapeake Green Fuels is a nascent clean‑energy company focused on producing low‑carbon renewable fuels from sustainable feedstocks. The firm aims to reduce greenhouse‑gas emissions by developing advanced bio‑fuel technologies and partnering with regional distributors. While still early‑stage, Chesapeake Green Fuels is positioned to contribute to the transition toward greener transportation fuels and supports environmental sustainability initiatives across the energy sector.

providers.name: Churuiintelligent
providers.description: Churui Intelligent Technology provides integrated software and hardware solutions focused on high‑end special energy storage, new energy, and semiconductor tracks. Founded in 2016, it develops battery cells, BMS, and AI‑driven data analytics for advanced energy storage applications.

providers.name: CIT Group
providers.description: CIT Group was a US financial holding company providing commercial financing, equipment leasing, factoring, and middle-market banking services. CIT was acquired by First Citizens BancShares in January 2022 and has been integrated into First Citizens Bank as the Commercial Banking division. CIT Group does not maintain a public developer portal and never published general-purpose REST APIs; legacy customer integrations were delivered through file-based ACH/wire feeds, the OneWest online banking platform, and partner-mediated treasury connectivity. New API-based integrations for the combined institution are now exposed through First Citizens Bank.

providers.name: Cleanenergyconnect
providers.description: Cleanenergyconnect is a clean energy marketplace platform that connects renewable energy producers with buyers, facilitating transparent transactions, data sharing, and integration of sustainable energy assets. The company aims to accelerate the adoption of clean energy by providing tools for project financing, carbon accounting, and market analytics, supporting a greener energy future.

providers.name: Cleanwatts
providers.description: Cleanwatts accelerates the energy transition by developing, financing, and operating distributed solar energy projects and energy communities for commercial and industrial clients. The company enables organizations to consume renewable energy with zero upfront investment, offering predictable, competitive energy costs while reducing carbon footprints. Cleanwatts focuses on local solutions, leveraging solar installations at client facilities to drive sustainable power generation and support the broader shift toward clean energy.

providers.name: CNCITY Energy
providers.description: CNCITY Energy Co., Ltd. is a South Korean integrated energy utility provider, delivering city gas, electricity, heat, and steam services to residential, commercial, and industrial customers in Daejeon and Gyeryong. Established in 1985, the company operates a 113 MW cogeneration plant and a district energy system, offering reliable and secure energy solutions across its service area.

providers.name: ComEd
providers.description: ComEd (Commonwealth Edison) is the Exelon-owned electric utility serving northern Illinois, including Chicago. It publishes no public developer portal or API contract; customer energy-usage data sharing runs through the Green Button program, with third-party Green Button Connect My Data access arranged through a utility registration process referenced in Illinois Commerce Commission filings.

providers.name: Coolenergy
providers.description: Coolenergy is a Boulder‑based clean‑energy technology company that develops and commercializes the ThermoHeart Engine™, a low‑temperature Stirling‑cycle engine that converts waste heat into electricity. Founded in 2006, the firm targets industrial exhaust, stationary power generation, and pollution control applications, offering solutions that improve energy efficiency and reduce emissions. Coolenergy provides engineering services, licensing, and turnkey installations for customers in the United States and Europe, aiming to accelerate the adoption of sustainable power conversion technologies.

providers.name: Curasen
providers.description: Curasen is currently listed as a stub company in the API Evangelist harvest backlog, with limited publicly available information. No official website or detailed corporate profile could be located through standard web searches, suggesting the company may be inactive, very new, or otherwise not maintaining a public-facing web presence. Further investigation may be required to confirm its operational status and any associated API offerings.

providers.name: DCU (Digital Federal Credit Union)
providers.description: Digital Federal Credit Union (DCU) is a not-for-profit, member-owned federal credit union headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts and regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), with roughly 1.18 million members, 23 branches across Massachusetts and New Hampshire, and nationwide access via the Co-Op shared-branch and surcharge-free ATM networks. It offers consumer and business banking, lending, mortgages, credit cards, and investment services, and has recently merged with First Technology Federal Credit Union. Like most US credit unions, DCU publishes NO public first-party developer API, developer portal, or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reached only indirectly through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) and its core banking provider, and there is no publicly documented FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access program. This is an honest identity-only record: no public API surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: Entegris
providers.description: Entegris is a global supplier of advanced materials and process solutions for the semiconductor and other high-technology industries. The company develops and manufactures specialty chemicals, gases, filtration and purification systems, advanced materials handling, and process control products. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified at the corporate level; technical integration is typically supported through sales engineering, the supplier portal, and product documentation.

providers.name: EXUDE-API
providers.description: Used for the primary ways for filtering the stopping, stemming words from the text data

providers.name: FairMoney
providers.description: FairMoney is a credit-led digital bank for emerging markets, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Paris, France, with operating subsidiaries in Nigeria and India. The company began life as a France-incubated micro- lending app and pivoted to focus on Africa, becoming one of the largest digital lenders in Nigeria after the Central Bank of Nigeria granted its subsidiary a Microfinance Bank (MfB) license. FairMoney's consumer mobile app offers near-instant collateral-free personal loans, FlexiCredit, asset finance, savings products (FairLock, FairSave, FairTarget, FairDollar), a current account, debit cards, bill payments, and peer-to-peer transfers. Its Business Banking arm extends current accounts, payments, and credit to Nigerian SMEs. In India, FairMoney operates as a digital lender disbursing small-ticket personal loans through its mobile app. FairMoney does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a third-party developer portal; integration is internal and partner- driven, and the company's only public technical surface is its engineering GitHub organization, which mirrors infrastructure-as-code and open-source tooling forks (Terraform AWS modules, GitHub Actions, rubocop, puma plugins, salesforce_bulk_api) rather than a product API.

providers.name: Finiata
providers.description: Finiata was a Berlin-founded fintech providing working-capital and invoice financing to small businesses, freelancers and micro-enterprises, operating principally in Germany and Poland and backed by investors including Point Nine. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass Finiata has no live public surface: finiata.com is registered but fully undelegated (no NS, SOA, A, MX or TXT records) and does not resolve; the former developer portal developer.finiata.com, archived as live in 2019, no longer resolves; and finiata.de has been taken over by unrelated third-party gambling-affiliate content. The only live first-party assets found are the company's GitHub organization (github.com/debitech) and one unmaintained internal npm tooling package. No API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, documentation, or well-known surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: Fintesa
providers.description: Fintesa Inc. is a financial technology company providing comprehensive financial solutions for merchants and businesses, positioning itself as a trusted financial partner. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. At the time of enrichment no public API program, developer portal, or API documentation was reachable — the site sits behind a bot-protection challenge and exposes no developer subdomains — so this profile remains an identity-and-domain-security stub awaiting a discoverable API surface.

providers.name: First West Credit Union
providers.description: First West Credit Union — rebranded Tru Cooperative Bank in 2026 — is a member-owned Canadian cooperative financial institution headquartered in Langley, British Columbia. Formed in 2010 by the merger of Envision Credit Union and Valley First, and later joined by Island Savings and Enderby & District Financial, it operates those four regional brands over a shared branch network with roughly 291,000 members, about $20.8 billion in total assets, 45 branches, and around 1,300 employees. After members voted in 2021 for federal continuance, it received a federal charter under Canada's Bank Act and became a federal credit union / cooperative bank (CDIC-insured) as of April 1, 2026. On the open-finance front First West / Tru runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or partner API; both developer.firstwestcu.ca and developer.trucooperativebank.ca resolve to nothing (NXDOMAIN). Third-party access to member account data today is aggregator-based (screen-scraping via providers such as Plaid and Flinks), the fragmented and voluntary Canadian norm while the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, overseen by the FCAC) remains legislated but not yet operational.

providers.name: Florin
providers.description: Florin is a San Francisco fintech startup building an integrated financial operating system for venture-backed companies. Rather than reselling another bank's infrastructure, Florin is building the underlying money-movement rails end to end so that funds settle in real time on a single ledger the company owns. The product combines business accounts, cards, payments, and treasury management into one invite-only membership aimed at startup founders who would otherwise stitch together half a dozen separate tools to hold, move, and grow their capital. Florin was founded in 2026 by Shaurya Aggarwal (CEO), Amol Pant (CTO), and Aydin Sorensen, and is a member of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch. At the time of this profile Florin operates a single marketing landing page with a waitlist and publishes no public API, developer documentation, or other developer-facing surface yet; this entry captures the company's identity and awaits a public API to enrich further.

providers.name: Janney Montgomery Scott
providers.description: Janney Montgomery Scott LLC is a full-service wealth management, financial services, and investment banking firm headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and continuously operating since 1832. A wholly owned subsidiary of The Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company, Janney serves individual investors, corporations, and municipalities through more than 100 branch offices across the United States, with over 900 financial advisors managing in excess of $167 billion in client assets under advisement. The firm provides client account access through the MyJanney online portal and iOS/Android mobile apps, but does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or external developer portal.

providers.name: Khazna
providers.description: Khazna is Egypt's leading financial super app, a Cairo-based fintech building inclusive financial services for the country's underbanked payroll workers and their families. Through its consumer mobile app it offers earned-wage access and salary advances, bill and utility payments, savings, and everyday consumer lending, with the goal of extending affordable, digital financial services to people traditionally excluded from the formal banking system. Khazna is backed by Speedinvest and operates as a business-to-consumer application; it does not publish a public developer portal or open API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with verified public identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Kobo360
providers.description: Kobo360 is a Nigerian-founded, pan-African B2B digital freight marketplace and logistics technology platform headquartered in Lagos, with operations across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Togo, Uganda, and other African countries. Founded in 2017 by Obi Ozor and Ife Oyedele II, Kobo360 operates an "Uber for trucks" long-haul logistics model that matches cargo owners and enterprise shippers with truck owners and drivers through a single digital ecosystem. The company runs the Global Logistics Operating System (G-LOS), an enterprise-grade logistics SaaS / digital freight forwarding platform that provides shipper dashboards, end-to-end shipment visibility, driver and truck ratings, embedded credit and working-capital products for carriers, and route and load optimization across the Kobo network of registered drivers and trucks. Kobo360 serves large FMCG, manufacturing, and commodities customers including Dangote, DHL, Honeywell, Olam, and Unilever, and has raised funding from investors such as Goldman Sachs, IFC, TLcom Capital, and Western Asset. Kobo360 does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open developer portal; integrations with shippers and partners are delivered through enterprise onboarding rather than a self-service API program.

providers.name: littlefish
providers.description: littlefish is a next generation merchant services platform positioned as a full-stack enterprise payments platform that extends a business's existing infrastructure instead of replacing it. Backed by Partech and operating in the Financial Services sector, littlefish covers merchant services, payments, finance, commerce, onboarding, operations, intelligence, and customer engagement, with a stated focus on financial inclusion. As of enrichment the company publishes a marketing site only (littlefishapp.com) with no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface discovered; this profile captures verified identity, legal, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: LotusFlare
providers.description: LotusFlare is a cloud-native digital commerce and monetization platform for telecommunications operators. Its Digital Network Operator (DNO) Cloud provides charging, product catalog, ordering, and digital customer-experience (BSS) capabilities as a managed SaaS to mobile carriers, and powers eSIM and travel-connectivity brands. The platform is delivered to enterprise telecom customers rather than through a public self-serve developer API; no public developer portal or API definition was discoverable at profile time. Backed by GV and Social Capital.

providers.name: Machinetutors
providers.description: AI Solutions: Video/Image Classification & Tagging, NSFW, Icon/Image/Audio Search, NLP

providers.name: MasTec
providers.description: MasTec is a Fortune 500 infrastructure construction company operating across clean energy, data centers, EV infrastructure, pipelines, power generation and delivery, civil infrastructure, technology deployment, water and wastewater, and communications. No public developer portal or APIs have been identified.

providers.name: Meridian Credit Union
providers.description: Meridian Credit Union is Ontario's largest credit union and one of the largest in Canada — a member-owned financial cooperative headquartered in St. Catharines and Toronto, serving more than 365,000 members with roughly CAD $31 billion in assets under management, over 2,200 employees, and more than 75 years of history. Formed in 2005 through the merger of Niagara Credit Union and HEPCOE Credit Union, Meridian offers personal, business, and wealth banking and owns Meridian OneCap Credit Corp. (commercial equipment leasing and financing); it previously operated the federally chartered digital bank motusbank, which was wound down in 2023. As a provincially regulated Ontario credit union — overseen by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA), with member deposits insured under Ontario's credit-union deposit-insurance scheme — Meridian is a cooperative, not a Schedule I or Schedule II bank. It publishes no first-party public developer API and no downloadable OpenAPI specification. Consumer-permissioned account-data access today is aggregator-mediated rather than first-party: Plaid maintains a Meridian institution connector, and the Central 1 / Flinks Outbound seam provides API-based data sharing for member credit unions. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated in 2024 with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada / FCAC as overseer) is not yet operational, so Meridian's open-finance participation remains voluntary and aggregator-based.

providers.name: Mintifi
providers.description: Mintifi is an Indian supply-chain financing platform that provides inventory and working-capital financing to SMEs, distributors, and dealers across manufacturer distribution networks. Its products include checkout and inventory financing, an Electronic Invoice Presentment and Payment (EIPP) solution for ERP-integrated invoice settlement and reconciliation, WhatsApp-based inventory financing, and Mintifi Collect for payment collection with Tally integration. The company exposes ERP-integration APIs to partners and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or self-serve API documentation is currently published; the docs host is access-gated.

providers.name: NAKAD
providers.description: NAKAD is India's leading Reconciliation-as-a-Service platform, a fintech delivering cash-flow and working-capital solutions to small businesses and MSMEs. Its proprietary MicroBill technology enables lending and loans through invoice discounting, invoice factoring and reverse factoring so suppliers receive early payment, with built-in reconciliation for accounts receivable, accounts payable, payments, debit notes, credit notes and banking. Backed by Accel. No public developer API surface, documentation, SDKs, or well-known discovery documents were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Nanogrid
providers.description: Nanogrid was an Oakland, California software startup founded in 2017 by Patrick Sheehan (CEO), Jon McKay (Co-Founder & CPO), and Dan Lopuch (Co-Founder & CTO) that built software to determine the value of residential solar, battery storage, and electric vehicles for homeowners. Its platform simulated, estimated, and optimized these distributed energy resources and captured the operational synergies between the devices. A 500 Startups (500 Global) Batch 25 company, Nanogrid raised roughly $150K from 500 Global and Plug and Play Tech Center before being acquired by clean-energy company Arcadia on April 22, 2021. The company no longer operates independently and its nanogrid.tech domain no longer resolves; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record. (Not to be confused with the separate nanoGrid energy-data platform at nanogrid.com.)

providers.name: Navy
providers.description: The U.S. Navy plays a crucial role in defending national security and protecting the country's interests at sea. It operates a fleet of ships and submarines, as well as aircraft and personnel, to conduct a range of missions, including maritime patrol, reconnaissance, and combat operations. The Navy also performs humanitarian missions, such as disaster relief and search and rescue efforts. No public APIs have been identified at this time. The previously listed CNATRA "API" reference is an Aviation Preflight Indoctrination training video library, not a programmatic API.

providers.name: Nowpay
providers.description: NowPay is an employer-integrated financial wellness platform whose core product lets employees access their earned salary early and repay it in installments, positioned as a workplace benefit rather than a consumer lender. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass NowPay publishes only a client-rendered marketing site (nowpay.cash, which redirects to nowpay.com) with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface; every probed path returns the single-page-app shell. This profile therefore carries identity and a live domain-security probe only.

providers.name: NRG Energy
providers.description: NRG Energy is a Fortune 500 American energy company. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for NRG Energy. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: NVE
providers.description: NVE Corporation (nve.com, NASDAQ: NVEC) is a leader in the practical commercialization of spintronics, a nanotechnology that relies on electron spin rather than electron charge to acquire, store, and transmit information. NVE designs and manufactures spintronic GMR and TMR magnetic sensors (analog, angle/rotation, current, gear-tooth, and medical sensors), digital signal isolators (CAN, RS-422/485, PLC, battery-management, and power interfaces), and power-management ICs. Its developer surface is hardware-oriented: PDF datasheets, application notes, reference designs, magnetic-field calculators/web apps, a YouTube channel, and Arduino/embedded sample code on GitHub. NVE publishes no software/web API, OpenAPI or AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or developer API platform.

providers.name: Okcredit
providers.description: OkCredit is a mobile digital ledger (bahi khata) application for small business owners and merchants across India, letting shopkeepers record credit and payment transactions digitally, send automated collection reminders over SMS and WhatsApp, and share account statements with customers. The consumer-facing Android and iOS apps replace the traditional paper udhaar ledger; the company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Ovintiv
providers.description: Ovintiv is a Fortune 500 oil and natural gas exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado. The company operates across North America with a focus on multi-basin development. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Ovintiv.

providers.name: payflows
providers.description: Payflows is an AI-native financial operations platform that unifies procurement, treasury, and accounting into one agentic workspace for finance teams. Its product suites span Apollo (procurement from purchase request to receipt), Vera (vendor and contract management), Athena (accounting and AP automation from AP to tax reporting), and Metis (treasury from payment to bank reconciliation), with spend analytics, cashflow forecasting, global payments, and risk management. Payflows integrates with major ERP, banking, payment, and expense systems. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Peabody Energy
providers.description: Peabody Energy is the world's largest private-sector coal company, mining and supplying coal to electricity generators and steel producers in the United States and around the world. No public developer APIs are currently documented for this organization.

providers.name: Pocket Menu
providers.description: Pocket Menu (Pocket Concierge / ポケットコンシェルジュ) is a Japanese fine-dining restaurant reservation and payment service that curates high-quality restaurants and lets diners book and pay for reservations online. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The public surface is a consumer web application (Ruby on Rails / React on Rails) at pocket-concierge.jp with no published developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or .well-known discovery documents detected during enrichment.

providers.name: Qashio
providers.description: Qashio is a United Arab Emirates-based financial technology company providing corporate spend management for businesses. Its platform offers unlimited smart corporate cards with advanced spending controls, rewards and cashback on transactions, and automated expense management, and it integrates with major ERP and accounting systems including Microsoft Dynamics 365, Oracle NetSuite, SAP, Xero, and Zoho. As of this enrichment pass Qashio publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and remains a company-level record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Remilk
providers.description: Remilk is a food-technology company, founded in 2019 by Aviv Wolff and Ori Cohavi and headquartered in Rehovot, Israel, that produces animal-free dairy proteins by precision fermentation. The company inserts the gene that codes for a cow milk protein into a yeast strain from the same family used in brewing and baking, ferments it at scale, and harvests a milk protein it describes as identical to the bovine original but free of lactose, cholesterol, hormones and antibiotics; the protein is then formulated with non-animal fat and sugar, vitamins and minerals into finished dairy products. Remilk has raised more than $150M, and was the first company to win regulatory clearance for a precision-fermented dairy protein in Israel, with subsequent clearances in Singapore, the United States (GRAS) and Canada. In November 2025 it commercialised the ingredient with Gad Dairies, Israel's fourth-largest dairy company, launching "The New Milk" barista and retail line, and it has publicly paused its plan to build what would have been the world's largest precision fermentation facility in Denmark. Remilk sells a food ingredient and consumer dairy products, not software: it operates no developer program, publishes no API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and maintains no public source-code organization.

providers.name: Returnly
providers.description: Returnly was a fintech-flavored e-commerce returns and exchanges platform (Returnly Green Returns, instant store credit, and return-shipping insurance) surfaced as a craft-ventures portfolio company. It was acquired by Affirm in 2021, and its returnly.com domain now permanently redirects to Loop Returns (www.loopreturns.com/returnly/); no independent Returnly developer portal, API reference, or API host resolves. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no surviving public API surface; only a live domain-security probe of the redirecting returnly.com domain was captured.

providers.name: SODA
providers.description: SODA Inc. (株式会社SODA) is a Japanese consumer-technology company that operates SNKRDUNK (スニーカーダンク / スニダン), one of Japan's largest consumer-to-consumer marketplaces for sneakers, trading cards ("トレカ"), apparel, and accessories. The SNKRDUNK app lets users buy and sell collectible and secondary-market goods with professional in-house authentication (真贋鑑定 by プロ鑑定士) and a full purchase-protection / compensation guarantee, alongside a buyback service. SODA is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. As a consumer marketplace app, SODA publishes no public developer program or API at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Swoop
providers.description: Swoop (formerly Thumo) is an African super-app building toward a single consumer platform for everyday commerce, starting with same-day food delivery and online shopping in Lagos, Nigeria (Yaba, Surulere, Gbagada and surrounding areas) and Eswatini, where it launched in 2025 and became the country's largest ecommerce platform. The app offers real-time order tracking, transparent upfront pricing, in-app support, and payments via card, bank transfer and OPay, with plans to add a payments app and further services on the road to a pan-African super-app. Founded by Thiel Fellow Aubrey Niederhoffer and Edwin Ruiz, Swoop raised a $7.3M seed round in 2026 with participation from Version One Ventures, Long Journey, Variant, Soma Capital and Dune. Swoop is a consumer-facing mobile and web platform; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation. This profile was surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio company and enriched as an identity-only lead.

providers.name: Targa Resources
providers.description: Targa Resources Corp. is a Fortune 500 and S&P 500 midstream energy infrastructure company and one of the largest independent midstream companies in North America. The company provides midstream services including gathering, compression, treating, processing, and selling of natural gas; fractionating, treating, transporting, and selling of natural gas liquids (NGLs); gathering, storing, terminaling and selling crude oil; and storing and selling refined petroleum products. Targa operates primarily in the Permian Basin, Anadarko Basin, and South Texas production areas, and owns the Grand Prix NGL Pipeline.

providers.name: Tripplus
providers.description: TripPlus (點數旅遊) is a Taiwan-based travel-rewards and loyalty-points platform. It provides airline mileage award-ticket search and redemption tools, curated recommendations and comparisons of US travel credit cards, and a marketplace for buying and selling airline miles and reward points. The consumer-facing site (tripplus.cc) is fronted by Cloudflare and, as of this enrichment pass, exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documented well-known endpoints. Backed by 500 Global; tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Trustid
providers.description: TRUSTID was a Portland, Oregon telephone caller-authentication and call-center anti-fraud company led by CEO Patrick Cox, authenticating inbound callers pre-answer without knowledge-based interrogation of the caller. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures, TRUSTID was acquired by Neustar (closed January 2019), and Neustar was itself acquired by TransUnion in December 2021, where the caller-authentication capability lives on in Trusted Call Solutions. TRUSTID no longer operates independently and publishes no public API surface — trustid.com is unresponsive and www.trustid.com returns HTTP 503 from Neustar redirect infrastructure.

providers.name: TurboFlow
providers.description: TurboFlow is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Ubiquisys
providers.description: Ubiquisys was a UK-based developer of intelligent 3G/LTE/Wi-Fi small cells and femtocells for mobile operators, with products like ActiveRadio, ActiveSON, CloudBase, and EdgeCloud deployed by carriers such as SFR and SoftBank, and was ranked #1 in ABI Research's Small Cell Vendor Matrix. Backed by Accel, Cisco announced its intent to acquire Ubiquisys on April 3, 2013, and the company was absorbed into Cisco's small cell portfolio; ubiquisys.com is now Cisco-owned and redirects to Cisco's acquisitions page. Ubiquisys published no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Unilever
providers.description: A British-Dutch multinational consumer goods company with a portfolio spanning food, personal care, and household brands. Owns over 400 brands including Dove, Ben & Jerry's, Hellmann's, and Vaseline sold in 190 countries.

providers.name: USA TODAY
providers.description: A major American daily national newspaper and digital news platform owned by Gannett. One of the most widely circulated newspapers in the United States covering news, sports, entertainment, and lifestyle topics.

providers.name: Veolia
providers.description: A French multinational corporation and the global leader in environmental services including water management, waste management, and energy services. Operates in nearly 50 countries providing solutions for water treatment, waste recycling, and pollution remediation.

providers.name: VyStar Credit Union
providers.description: VyStar Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida. Founded in 1952 as Jax Navy Federal Credit Union to serve military members at Naval Air Station Jacksonville and renamed VyStar in 2002, it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly $14 billion in assets, more than 950,000 members, and approximately 80 branches across Florida and Georgia. It is state-chartered and federally insured by the NCUA. Like most US credit unions, VyStar publishes no public, first-party developer API program: there is no live developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definition, and no documented first-party data-access API. Consumer-permissioned account data is shared with third parties through financial-data aggregators rather than a documented open API, and the United States has no single mandated open-banking contract. VyStar's open-finance posture is therefore aggregator-mediated, with the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule as the relevant regulatory horizon.

It runs an "urban renewal and spatial reconstruction" model that blends co-working, co-living, food and beverage, retail, fitness and cultural programming into single mixed-use compounds — the name stands for livable, linked, liberal, lively and landscape. Its Dongsi compound in Beijing pairs a basement co-working floor with a cafe and bakery, a gym, the Hatchery food incubator, the Unread bookstore, a 24-hour convenience store, residential units and a rooftop garden. The company raised roughly RMB 400 million in October 2016 and a USD 14.55 million Series B in early 2017 led by GIC, Singapore's sovereign wealth fund, alongside Kaifeng Culture Tourism Investment Group, and is valued in the secondary market rather than publicly listed. 5Lmeet is a real-estate and hospitality operator, not a software vendor: the only software it has published is an end-user iPad visitor-management app for its own front desks, and it operates no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Absci
providers.description: Absci is a Vancouver, Washington-based generative AI drug creation company (NASDAQ: ABSI) using AI and synthetic biology to design de novo antibodies in silico against specified epitopes. Its Integrated Drug Creation platform couples generative AI models — including the Origin-1 antibody foundation model — with a 77,000+ sq ft wet lab running proprietary SoluPro and ACE Assay technologies, screening millions of antibody sequence variants per cycle. The data flywheel between in silico design and high-throughput wet lab validation completes in as little as six weeks and can advance from target identification to development candidate in roughly 14 months. Absci's internal pipeline includes ABS-101, an anti-TL1A antibody for inflammatory bowel disease now in Phase 1; ABS-201, a novel anti-PRLR antibody for androgenetic alopecia in the Phase 1/2a HEADLINE trial; and ABS-301, a first-in-class AI-discovered oncology antibody. Strategic partnerships span AstraZeneca, Merck, Almirall, Twist Bioscience, NVIDIA, Owkin, Caltech, and the Gates Foundation. Absci's commercial model is therapeutic development (internal pipeline plus partnered programs and royalties); there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Origin-1 model or its drug creation platform.
