It was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of Accel. As of this enrichment pass Wiom operates a consumer marketing website (a React single-page application) but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface, so this profile carries verified identity and a live domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Your Super
providers.description: Your Super (Your Superfoods, Inc.) is a direct-to-consumer plant-based superfoods brand founded in 2015 in Venice, California by Michael Kuech and Kristel de Groot. It sells functional superfood and protein mixes and bars made from five to six nutrient-dense whole-food ingredients that are certified organic, Non-GMO, glyphosate-free, and gluten-free, sold through Shopify storefronts in the US and Europe and via Amazon. The company raised roughly $22.5M across five rounds from investors including 500 Global and PowerPlant Ventures, and was acquired by The Healing Company in October 2022. It is a consumer e-commerce brand and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: YouStake
providers.description: YouStake is a peer-to-peer sports staking and sponsorship marketplace, founded in 2013, that lets fans invest in skilled poker and esports players in exchange for a share of their tournament winnings. Players list their buy-ins and backers can stake them for as little as $20, structured as a person-to-person sponsorship agreement rather than gambling. The consumer platform has since rebranded and now operates as StakeKings (youstake.com redirects to stakekings.com), which also offers white-label staking-marketplace software to partners. It is a business-to-consumer web application with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or published API documentation.

providers.name: Zhuhai DL Biotech (medicaldl)
providers.description: Zhuhai DL Biotech Co., Ltd. (Zhuhai Deer Bioengineering Co., Ltd., brand "DL" / 迪尔), founded in 2003 and based in Zhuhai, China, is a high-tech in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) enterprise specializing in the R&D, manufacturing, and service of microbial diagnostic instruments and reagents. Its product lines cover automated blood culture systems, automated bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (ID/AST), MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry microbial identification, automated staining, fluorescence immunoassay, and molecular diagnostics, serving over 5,000 clinical healthcare institutions across more than 50 countries. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. Enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or software integration surface — this is a diagnostic-hardware and reagent business, not a software/API provider.

providers.name: Zimperium
providers.description: Zimperium is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of sierra-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: security. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Zingroll
providers.description: Zingroll is a consumer AI entertainment platform that generates personalized episodic video shows starring the user. A person uploads a single selfie and Zingroll casts them as the lead in an AI-generated series spanning up to 200 episodes across genres including action, romance, horror, and comedy, which can then be watched and shared. Backed by Accel, Zingroll operates in the AI media and generative-video space. The company runs a public consumer web application at zingroll.com but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile tracks it in the API Evangelist network as an AI-sector lead.

providers.name: Zolar
providers.description: Zolar is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of partech and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: Climate. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Zwitterco
providers.description: ZwitterCo is an advanced water treatment company that manufactures filtration membranes based on zwitterionic chemistry, a surface science that makes membranes attract water rather than organic compounds and thereby resist the organic fouling that limits conventional membranes. Its product families target food and dairy processing (Evolution membranes for whey and milk concentration), industrial and municipal wastewater (Elevation membranes for landfill leachate, refinery streams, and produced water), and extreme high-fouling waste streams (Expedition superfiltration). ZwitterCo is a DCVC portfolio company. It sells physical membrane hardware and treatment systems through direct sales and does not currently publish any public developer portal, API, SDKs, or machine-readable interface; this profile is a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API producer.

providers.name: 61draw
providers.description: 61draw (广东省六一线上非学科培训学校有限公司, Guangdong Liuyi Online Non-Academic Training School Co., Ltd.) is a China-based online children's art and non-academic education platform delivering live-broadcast art lessons to children roughly aged five to nine. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and Matrix Partners China, which co-led its Series B round, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. The company runs a consumer web and mobile presence at 61draw.com; no public developer, API, or documentation surface has been found during enrichment.

providers.name: Academy Sports and Outdoors
providers.description: Academy Sports + Outdoors is a Fortune 500 sporting goods and outdoor recreation retailer headquartered in Katy, Texas. The company operates retail stores across the United States and an e-commerce platform offering sporting equipment, apparel, footwear, hunting and fishing gear, camping supplies, and outdoor recreation products. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Academy Sports + Outdoors. No public developer APIs or documentation portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Achieve3000
providers.description: Achieve3000 is a supplemental digital literacy solution for grades 3-12 that uses adaptive technology to personalize reading instruction, delivering differentiated nonfiction texts matched to each student's Lexile reading level to build vocabulary and comprehension. Originally an independent education-technology company backed by Insight Partners, Achieve3000 was acquired by McGraw Hill and is now offered as "Achieve3000 Literacy" within McGraw Hill's PreK-12 portfolio. Students and educators access the platform through their district's approved single sign-on (SSO); the product publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and demand tracking.

providers.name: Ally
providers.description: Ally.io was an OKR and goal-management SaaS platform for people and performance teams, helping organizations set, align, and track objectives and key results across the workforce. Backed by Accel, Greylock, Tiger Global and Addition, the company was acquired by Microsoft in October 2021 and its product was folded into Microsoft Viva Goals. The ally.io domain remains actively hosted but no longer exposes a public developer/API surface; developer, docs and API subdomains do not resolve. This API Evangelist profile is retained as an hr-tech portfolio lead with a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: AllyO
providers.description: AllyO is an HR-tech company, founded in 2016 in Palo Alto, California, that built a conversation-first, AI recruiting chatbot and automation platform for high-volume hiring. Its chatbot let candidates apply to jobs, answer common questions, get screened, and schedule interviews via text and web chat 24/7, with integrations into applicant tracking systems, job boards, and background-check providers. AllyO raised roughly $64M in venture funding (including a $45M round in 2019 backed by investors such as Sapphire Ventures) before being acquired by HireVue in October 2020. The AllyO product now lives inside HireVue as its Conversational AI and Automation offering; www.allyo.com 301-redirects to HireVue and AllyO no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Altera
providers.description: Altera is an applied AI research company founded in December 2023 by former MIT computational neuroscientist Robert Yang, building "digital human beings" — autonomous, collaborative, and socially intelligent AI agents. Its research began with multi-agent experiments in games such as Minecraft and Roblox (agents that can play alongside a person like a friend), and produced Project Sid, a large-scale AI-agent civilization powered by its PIANO architecture. The team is drawn from MIT EECS, the Stanford NLP Group, Google X, and Citadel. Altera raised a $2M pre-seed and a $9M seed (backers include a16z SPEEDRUN, Patron, First Spark Ventures, and Eric Schmidt) and has since rebranded to Fundamental Research Labs following a $33M Series A led by Prosus. Altera is a research organization and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; its only public developer surface is the altera-al GitHub organization (the project-sid research codebase).

providers.name: APi Group
providers.description: APi Group Corporation is a Fortune 500 global, market-leading business services provider of safety, specialty, and industrial services. The company delivers life safety, security, specialty trades, and industrial contracting services through a network of operating companies across North America, Europe, the Asia-Pacific region, and beyond. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with APi Group. No public developer APIs or documentation portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Applica
providers.description: Applica was an AI-based document understanding and text automation company founded in Warsaw, Poland, built on deep-learning research in natural language processing for unstructured documents. Its platform read, interpreted, and extracted information from documents such as invoices, contracts, insurance claims, legal documents, and financial filings across the finance, insurance, legal, and media industries. Applica went through the Barclays Accelerator powered by Techstars and raised a Series A led by Cogito Capital Partners in 2020. Snowflake announced its intent to acquire Applica in August 2022 and absorbed the technology into the Snowflake platform. Applica no longer operates as an independent product or API provider, and applica.ai is no longer a live developer surface; this profile is retained for historical/network provenance.

providers.name: Archax
providers.description: Archax builds regulated infrastructure for tokenising, trading, and safekeeping real-world assets. Authorized across the UK and EU, Archax provides a secure, compliant platform for digital asset markets, offering institutional-grade solutions for asset tokenisation, secondary market trading, and custodial services, enabling investors to access tokenised real-world assets with confidence and regulatory oversight.

providers.name: ASOS
providers.description: ASOS plc is a global online fashion retailer offering a wide range of clothing, accessories and beauty products for men and women. Founded in 2000, the company operates primarily through its e‑commerce platform, serving customers in over 200 markets. ASOS provides APIs for product catalog, inventory, order management and user personalization, enabling developers to integrate its services into third‑party applications and services.

providers.name: ASPACE International Holdings
providers.description: ASPACE International Holdings is a commercial space company founded in 2015 with offices listed in Dubai, United Arab Emirates and Hong Kong, China. It positions itself as an aerospace manufacturing conglomerate centred on the Abu Dhabi Space Eco City — a three-million-square-metre industrial cluster it says will bring together more than 3,000 partner companies across satellite manufacturing, space trade and aerospace technology innovation. The ASPACE brand is shared with Hong Kong-listed USPACE Technology Group, whose satellite-manufacturing subsidiary was renamed Aspace Satellite Technology Limited in 2023. ASPACE International Holdings has taken investment from Alpha MBM Investments and makes minority investments of its own, including a stake in the private-equity trading platform Cubin LLC announced in 2023. It is a hardware, industrial-development and investment holding business rather than a software vendor: no first-party corporate domain for the company resolves, its only verified public surfaces are a LinkedIn company page, a Hiive secondary-market listing and third-party investor databases, and it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Atkore
providers.description: Atkore is a manufacturer of electrical conduit, cable management systems, metal framing, and other safety and infrastructure products used in commercial, industrial, and residential construction. The company offers several end-user technical tools, including the Atkore BIM Toolbar (a Revit plugin), Atkore Virtual 3D, and an online Hanger Configurator, but does not expose a public REST API or self-service developer portal at this time.

providers.name: B2B Bank
providers.description: B2B Bank is a Schedule I Canadian bank, headquartered in Toronto and wholly owned by Laurentian Bank of Canada (Laurentian Bank Financial Group). It operates a business-to-business, intermediary-only model: rather than serving retail consumers directly, it manufactures and distributes banking products through a network of roughly 27,000 financial professionals — financial advisors and their dealerships, deposit and mortgage brokers and their firms, mutual fund and insurance manufacturers, and CIRO (formerly MFDA/IIROC) members. Its product lines include investment loans, RSP and TFSA loans, broker deposits (GICs and high-interest savings/investment accounts), broker mortgages, and investment and banking accounts. The bank became a Schedule I bank and adopted the B2B Bank name in 2012, consolidating predecessor trust businesses (North American Trust, Sun Life Trust), and its deposits are CDIC insured. On open finance, B2B Bank publishes no first-party developer portal or public API: developer.b2bbank.com and api.b2bbank.com do not resolve, and the public site exposes only gated advisor/broker applications (Advisor Access, EASE online loans, Group Access, Investor Access, online banking). Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework is legislated but not yet operational, and the bank documents no FDX participation, Interac data-sharing API, or aggregator program of its own — consistent with an intermediary bank whose digital surface is partner-gated rather than developer-facing.

providers.name: Ballard Spahr
providers.description: Ballard Spahr LLP is a national U.S. law firm founded in 1885 and headquartered in Philadelphia. Following its January 1, 2025 combination with Seattle-based Lane Powell, the firm operates as a "nationally recognized firm of more than 750 lawyers across 18 U.S. offices" with departments in Business and Transactions, Finance, Intellectual Property, Litigation, and Real Estate. The firm has historic depth in consumer financial services, real estate, public finance, and IP, and runs widely read thought-leadership properties including the Consumer Finance Monitor blog (with public RSS feed) and the Business Better podcast. Ballard Spahr does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is the Consumer Finance Monitor RSS feed.

providers.name: Bhubai
providers.description: Bhubai is a company listed in the API Evangelist harvest backlog, identified from secondary-market sources. At this time, public information about its products, services, or API offerings is limited. The entry serves as a placeholder for future enrichment as more data becomes available.

providers.name: Bittrexllc
providers.description: Bittrex LLC is a leading cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2014, offering a secure platform for buying, selling, and trading a wide variety of digital assets. The exchange provides advanced trading features, robust security measures, and a comprehensive API suite that enables developers to integrate market data, order execution, and account management into their applications. Bittrex serves retail and institutional clients worldwide, emphasizing compliance, liquidity, and a user-friendly experience across web, mobile, and API interfaces.

providers.name: Blinkist
providers.description: Blinkist is a Berlin-founded subscription learning app that condenses the key ideas of thousands of nonfiction books and podcasts into roughly 15-minute text and audio summaries called "Blinks." Launched in 2012, it is used by millions of readers to learn on the go across categories such as productivity, business, psychology, personal growth, and science, and it also offers Blinkist for Business for teams and organizations. The consumer product is delivered through the web and iOS/Android apps backed by a private mobile backend at api.blinkist.com; Blinkist does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. Blinkist was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by Insight Partners) and enriched with the provider signals that could be verified from its public surface.

providers.name: Blue Studios
providers.description: Blue Studios Labs is a family-focused technology company operating under the tagline "Where Families Flourish." It builds consumer digital products that help couples and families explore, learn, and grow together. Its portfolio includes Wallio, a shared financial-management app for couples and families; Blue Studios EDU, an entertainment-based educational streaming service; and Blue Studios Entertainment, a media-production studio creating family-oriented narratives and content. The company reports more than 400 million digital views, 350,000 game plays, and 4,000+ classes delivered. Blue Studios is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Bolsterinc
providers.description: Bolsterinc is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Boomerangmedical
providers.description: Boomerangmedical is a healthcare technology startup identified through the API Evangelist secondary‑market harvest. No public website or documentation could be located despite web searches, indicating the company may be early‑stage, operating privately, or its online presence is not publicly indexed. This entry serves as a placeholder for future enrichment when verifiable resources become available.

providers.name: Boss
providers.description: Boss (BOSS Zhipin / BOSS直聘) is the largest online recruitment platform in China by average monthly active users, operated by Kanzhun Limited (NASDAQ: BZ, HKEX: 2076) and founded in 2014 in Beijing. It pioneered the "Direct Recruitment" model, a mobile-native experience that connects employers (bosses) and job seekers through instant direct chat rather than static resume exchange, with candidate and job matching powered by proprietary AI algorithms and big-data insights. The consumer job-search product at zhipin.com does not publish a public developer/job-data API; an authorized enterprise developer surface (BossHi mini-program open platform) exists for partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: BrightBytes
providers.description: BrightBytes was a San Francisco-based K-12 education data and analytics company founded in 2012 by Rob Mancabelli, best known for Clarity, a decision-support and analytics platform used by schools and districts to connect technology spending and classroom use to student learning outcomes, and for DataSense, a data-integration platform that captured, cleaned, and synced student data between disparate school systems. The company sold DataSense and its team to Microsoft in February 2019 and was itself acquired by Google in 2022. BrightBytes no longer operates independently: as of July 2026 www.brightbytes.net returns an expired-site placeholder and no developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or status surface remains. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Brine (Tanx)
providers.description: Brine — now rebranded as tanX — is a cross-chain, self-custodial orderbook decentralized exchange (DEX) built on StarkWare's StarkEx Layer-2 scaling engine. It combines the trustless, non-custodial security of a DEX with the speed and low fees of a centralized exchange: gasless trading, rapid off-chain order execution with on-chain settlement, cross-chain deposits and withdrawals, and simple APIs for programmatic trading. The company is backed by Pantera Capital and is repositioning around "a secure and compliant future for crypto." This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Pantera Capital's portfolio and enriched by the pipeline; as of this pass the public REST API host is no longer reachable and the developer surface is limited to the GitBook documentation.

providers.name: Cal-Maine Foods
providers.description: Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. is the largest producer and distributor of fresh shell eggs in the United States. The company sells most of its shell eggs to grocery store chains, club stores, foodservice distributors, and egg product consumers across the country and produces specialty eggs including organic, cage-free, free-range, and nutritionally enhanced varieties. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: Caliberid
providers.description: Caliber I.D. (Imaging & Diagnostics, Inc.) provides advanced confocal imaging devices and software for cellular‑level diagnostics in dermatology, pathology and research. Their products such as VivaScope, VivaCam and VivaScan enable in‑vivo laser imaging, delivering high‑resolution, real‑time visualisation of tissue for cancer detection and other medical applications. The company emphasizes innovation in microscopy, offering both hardware and cloud‑based analysis tools for clinicians and scientists.

providers.name: Cambridge Blockchain
providers.description: Cambridge Blockchain, Inc. was a blockchain-based digital identity and compliance software company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Cambridge / Boston, Massachusetts. Its enterprise platform let financial institutions deliver strong digital identities to end users while meeting KYC/AML and data privacy obligations (including European GDPR), giving individuals control over their own personal identity data shared across institutions. The company was backed by investors including Partech and PayPal, and was acquired by Blockchains, Inc. in December 2020, after which its team and identity technology were folded into Blockchains' digital identity product. The former company website (cambridge-blockchain.com) is no longer served; the surviving public developer surface is its GitHub organization and two first-party npm cryptographic libraries. No public HTTP API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or hosted documentation was ever published.

providers.name: Caparoom
providers.description: Caparoom Inc. provides business consulting services focused on accelerating the growth of digital businesses. It offers strategic investments for digital transformation and innovation, leveraging digital and algorithmic solutions to help companies expand globally, especially across the Pacific region. Services include strategic business development, market insights, investment assistance, and growth hacking to enhance customer acquisition and retention.

providers.name: Capsule8
providers.description: Capsule8 was a New York-based cybersecurity company (founded 2016) that built high-performance runtime visibility, detection, and response for Linux production servers and containers across on-premises and cloud workloads. Its open-source sensor exposed a gRPC (v0) telemetry API for subscribing to security events. Sophos acquired Capsule8 in July 2021 and absorbed the technology into its Adaptive Cybersecurity Ecosystem (Intercept X server protection, XDR, and Managed Threat Response). The capsule8.com domain now redirects to Sophos, the flagship open-source sensor/API repository has been removed, and no independent Capsule8 developer API, portal, or documentation remains live. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company and is retained as an acquired-company record.

providers.name: Chalkable
providers.description: Chalkable was a K-12 education technology company that provided a cloud-based student information system (SIS), learning management, and an education "app store" letting schools run third-party classroom apps on top of shared student data. Its developer platform exposed a RESTful API (OAuth 2.0) over school data points such as student and teacher scheduling, real-time attendance, grading and discipline records, announcements, messaging, and notifications, with partner apps rendered inside an iframe within the Chalkable classroom. Chalkable was acquired by PowerSchool on October 12, 2016, and the product line was absorbed into PowerSchool; the original developer surface (dev.chalkable.com and classroom.chalkable.com/Developer) is no longer operational. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Chenxinsemiconductor
providers.description: Chenxinsemiconductor, also known as Changsha Chixin Semiconductor Technology Co., Ltd., was founded in June 2020 and is headquartered in Xiangjiang New District, Hunan Province, China, with a Shanghai subsidiary. The company focuses on research, development, and sales of ultra-wide-band (UWB) chip products, aiming to become a leading global supplier of UWB solutions. It offers products such as the CX310 and CX500 series and provides solutions for various industries.

providers.name: Clutch Learning
providers.description: Clutch Learning (Clutch Prep) was a Miami-based education-technology startup founded in 2011 that helped more than two million college students learn through thousands of short-form, topic-based video tutorials and practice problems across subjects such as chemistry, physics, biology, accounting, and calculus. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), the company was acquired by Pearson in 2022 and folded into the Pearson+ study platform, where the offering now lives as Pearson Channels. The standalone clutchprep.com product is no longer independently operated. The domain 301-redirects to pearson.com/channels, and the company exposes no independent developer portal, public API, SDKs, or event surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record.

providers.name: Cohesion
providers.description: Cohesion is a New York City-based financial intelligence company (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building AI agents that automate investment research for hedge funds and institutional investors. The platform continuously monitors public companies across earnings reports, news, podcasts, and social media such as X/Twitter to surface differentiated investing signals that fundamental equity analysts would otherwise spend hours a week tracking manually. Founded by Devon Krapcho (CEO), Matthew McBrien, and Matt Munns, its agents are used by 10+ long/short and long-only equity funds managing over $10 billion in assets. Marketed as "Modern Intelligence for Finance," Cohesion currently ships only a single-page marketing site with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its verified company identity as an API Evangelist network lead.

providers.name: Coinflipsolutions
providers.description: Coinflipsolutions is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Collegeconsortium
providers.description: Collegeconsortium is an independent educational consulting firm founded in 2007 that helps students and families navigate the college admissions process. It offers personalized guidance from exploration through application, leveraging expertise from its founder Marilyn O’Toole, CEP, and affiliations with IECA, NACAC, and the Character Collaborative. The organization provides resources, counseling, and support to ensure informed, ethical, and successful college decisions for diverse applicants.

providers.name: CoreOS
providers.description: CoreOS was a San Francisco-based container infrastructure company founded in 2013 that built a lightweight, automatically-updating Linux distribution (Container Linux, originally CoreOS Linux) and a family of now-foundational cloud-native open source projects: etcd (the distributed key-value store at the heart of Kubernetes), the Quay container registry, the Tectonic enterprise Kubernetes platform, the rkt container engine, flannel networking, Clair image-vulnerability scanning, and Ignition provisioning. Red Hat acquired CoreOS in January 2018 for approximately $250 million. Its technologies were folded into Red Hat's portfolio — Container Linux became Red Hat CoreOS and the community Fedora CoreOS, Tectonic merged into OpenShift, Quay continues as Red Hat Quay, and etcd and rkt were donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. The company no longer operates independently; coreos.com redirects to Red Hat OpenShift. The github.com/coreos organization remains active as the upstream home for Fedora CoreOS components such as Ignition, Butane, and fleetlock.

providers.name: Crew32
providers.description: Crew32 was a stealth-stage technology startup based in Santa Monica, California, working in the human resources, employment, and workplace-culture space. It was founded by Jason Nazar (previously co-founder and CEO of Docstoc), George Ishii (co-founder of Betterworks, Geni, and Yammer), and Yadid Ramot, and raised roughly $5.8 million in early funding around 2016. The company is publicly associated with the comparably.com workplace-culture and compensation review platform. Crew32 was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; no public API, developer portal, or SDK has been identified for this company.

providers.name: CTRL-labs *
providers.description: CTRL-labs was a neurotechnology company founded in 2015 in New York City (originally Cognescent) by Thomas Reardon, Patrick Kaifosh, and Tim Machado, building a non-invasive neural interface: a wrist-worn band that reads surface electromyography (sEMG) signals from motor neurons to decode intended hand and finger movements for human-computer interaction. Its developer hardware was the CTRL-kit, and it acquired the Myo armband patents from North. In fall 2019 CTRL-labs was acquired by Facebook and folded into Facebook (now Meta) Reality Labs, where the technology became the basis of Meta's neuromotor wristband for AR glasses (detailed in a July 2025 Nature paper). The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this record is retained as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Cypress
providers.description: Cypress Semiconductor Corporation was a San Jose, California semiconductor company founded in 1982, and an early Mayfield venture investment. It designed and manufactured mixed-signal, embedded, and connectivity silicon — most notably the PSoC programmable system-on-chip microcontrollers, WICED Wi-Fi and Bluetooth wireless combos, USB controllers (EZ-USB), NOR flash and SRAM memory, and automotive Traveo microcontrollers — supported by the ModusToolbox and PSoC Creator developer tooling and the Cypress Developer Community. Infineon Technologies AG acquired Cypress in April 2020 for approximately 9.4 billion dollars; the business, its developer community, and its GitHub repositories have since been folded into Infineon. cypress.com now redirects to infineon.com and the developer resources live at community.infineon.com. Cypress shipped hardware SDKs and embedded toolchains rather than a public web/REST API, so there is no independent HTTP API surface to catalog for this entity — this profile documents it as a historical, acquired provider.

providers.name: dejavu
providers.description: dejavu is a spatial-computing and 3D graphics startup founded by XR entrepreneur Matt Miesnieks (previously Layar and 6D.ai) that launched at GDC 2024 out of the a16z Speedrun accelerator. Its rendering engine takes high-quality photorealistic 3D scenes and makes them run at full resolution on any device, including the Apple Vision Pro, in a fraction of the time and cost of a traditional visual-effects pipeline, bridging the gap between reality-capture tools like Matterport and full VFX studios. As of this profiling the company appears dormant as a developer surface, its djv.ai website is an expired Squarespace account and it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or well-known metadata. Its GitHub organization exists but is empty.

providers.name: docin
providers.description: docin (豆丁网, docin.com) is a Chinese C2C document-sharing platform operated by Beijing Docin Century Network Technology (北京豆丁世纪网络技术有限公司) that faces the global market. The platform hosts over 1.3 billion documents, books, magazines, and publications spanning education, architecture and construction, business and contracts, medical and psychological materials, industry reports, and legal documents, supporting both learning and practical application. It offers a "豆丁书房" (Docin Reading Room) mobile reading app and VIP membership tiers. docin was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Probing found no public developer or API platform: open.docin.com 301-redirects to the homepage, /app/api returns 404, and no /.well-known discovery documents are published.

providers.name: EduPristine
providers.description: EduPristine is a Mumbai-based finance, accounting, and analytics training institute founded in 2008, offering classroom and online certification-prep and professional up-skilling programs. Its catalog spans financial modeling, CFA, FRM, ACCA, US CPA and US CMA, business analytics and data science, digital marketing, financial accounting (Big 4 aligned), and healthcare/medical coding. EduPristine runs training centers across India alongside self-paced and instructor-led online courses, and is part of Adtalem Global Education. Sector: edtech. No public developer API or documented API surface was found during enrichment; the corporate website sits behind a WAF that blocks automated discovery of a well-known or developer surface.

providers.name: Elite Business Ventures
providers.description: Elite Business Ventures, LLC (EBV, ebvinc.com) is a San Diego-based workplace compliance company founded in 2005 that has helped over one million businesses stay compliant with federal and state labor laws and workplace safety regulations. It operates through two primary brands: PosterElite, a white-label labor-law-poster compliance platform embedded by HR, payroll, HCM, PEO, and workforce-management providers under their own brand; and Osha4Less.com, an ecommerce store of affordable OSHA and labor-law compliance products for small businesses. EBV is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. The company exposes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or documentation surface — partner integration is handled through direct white-label / reseller arrangements rather than a self-service developer program.

providers.name: Envision Healthcare Holdings
providers.description: Envision Healthcare is a leading provider of physician-led services and ambulatory surgery services in the United States, supporting healthcare professionals across emergency, anesthesiology, radiology, women's and children's, and surgery. No public developer APIs have been identified for Envision Healthcare Holdings at this time.

providers.name: FirstCash Holdings
providers.description: FirstCash Holdings is a leading international operator of pawn stores and a major provider of retail point-of-sale payment solutions. The company operates pawn store locations across the United States and Latin America, offering pawn loans, retail merchandise sales, and lease-to-own financing through its American First Finance subsidiary. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: Folhamatic
providers.description: Folhamatic (IOB Folhamatic Group) is a Brazilian developer of integrated accounting, payroll, and fiscal/tax software for accounting firms and businesses, founded in 1990 and headquartered in Americana, Sao Paulo. Its product line includes Folhamatic Payroll for personnel management and electronic files, Electronic Point Control for time-clock management, the Folhamatic Accounting system for management reporting, and Folhamatic Written Tax for tax departments. At acquisition it served more than 11,000 companies with 500-plus employees. Folhamatic was acquired by the UK's Sage Group in June 2012 and now operates as part of Sage in Brazil. The company publishes no first-party public developer API, and the historic folhamatic.com.br domain no longer serves a live site.

providers.name: Gaming and Leisure Properties
providers.description: Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc. (NASDAQ: GLPI) is "the nation's first real estate investment trust focused on acquiring real property assets leased to gaming operators." Headquartered in Wyomissing, Pennsylvania, GLPI's portfolio comprises 71 premier gaming and related facilities across 21 states, totaling more than 29.3 million square feet and over 15,100 hotel rooms, leased on a triple-net basis to operators including Penn Entertainment, Caesars Entertainment, Bally's Corporation, Boyd Gaming, the Cordish Companies, and Hard Rock. No public developer API, data feed, or GitHub organization has been identified; GLPI engages investors, tenants, and partners through corporate and investor relations channels only.

providers.name: GGFolks
providers.description: GGFolks (Good Game Folks) is a small, experimental independent game-development group that publishes its work as open source on GitHub under the ggfolks organization, with the tagline "We make good feels." Its repositories are early-stage games and supporting tooling rather than a commercial API product: platform is a TypeScript social-multiplayer web game framework (the `tfw` package, MIT-licensed), moncher is a monster-ranching social game, spaced is a web-based space editor, chatapp is a Dart messaging experiment, and ggdobj/esl provide shared C#/Unity client-server and simulation code. GGFolks does not publish a public developer portal, hosted API, OpenAPI definition, or released client SDK, so it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Glintinc
providers.description: Glint (Glint Inc), founded in 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, built a people-success and employee-engagement platform centered on frequent pulse surveys, engagement analytics, and manager action-planning to help organizations measure and improve employee experience. LinkedIn acquired Glint in November 2018, and the product was subsequently folded into Microsoft Viva as Viva Glint. There is no standalone Glint developer portal or public API: the former glintinc.com domain now 302-redirects to Microsoft's Viva Glint community, and the offering is delivered and documented through Microsoft Viva. This profile is retained for network lineage as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company that was acquired rather than an independently operating API provider.

providers.name: Glints
providers.description: Glints is a talent recruitment and career development platform headquartered in Singapore and operating across Southeast Asia, including Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Taiwan and the Philippines. Founded in 2013, it runs an online job marketplace connecting job seekers with employers, a curated headhunting service (TalentHunt), and a cross-border managed-talent / remote-hiring offering that lets companies build and employ distributed teams across the region. Glints also publishes career resources and expert classes. It is one of the largest talent ecosystems in Southeast Asia and is backed by investors including DCM Ventures, Monk's Hill Ventures and PERSOL. This API Evangelist profile was added as a portfolio-company lead; Glints exposes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Hyphen
providers.description: Hyphen was a mobile-first employee engagement and pulse-survey platform that let organizations collect anonymous employee feedback, run continuous sentiment surveys, and give managers analytics on engagement and culture. Founded as a 500 Global-backed startup, Hyphen was acquired by Betterworks and folded into the Betterworks Engage product line. Its original domain, gethyphen.com, now 301-redirects to betterworks.com/product/engage-overview/, and the company no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network; the live successor product is Betterworks Engage.

providers.name: In Focus Systems
providers.description: In Focus Systems, Inc. (later InFocus Corporation, and today marketed as InFocus) is an audiovisual technology company founded in 1986 in Oregon by Steve Hix and Paul Gulick, both formerly of Tektronix. The company pioneered LCD projection panels and is credited with inventing the digital projector, going public on NASDAQ (ticker INFS) in December 1990. It grew into a leading maker of DLP and LCD projectors, interactive flat-panel displays, DVLED video walls, and collaboration hardware for business, education, installation, and home markets. In Focus Systems was an early Battery Ventures investment (since exited). The InFocus business was acquired by Image Holdings Corp. in 2009 and operates today as a privately held subsidiary headquartered in the Portland, Oregon area. It is a hardware and audiovisual solutions company and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: INTL FCStone
providers.description: INTL FCStone Inc. (rebranded as StoneX Group in 2020) is a Fortune 100 financial services organization providing execution, risk management, advisory services, market intelligence, and post-trade services across asset classes and global markets including commodities, equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, and securities.

providers.name: Jabil Circuit
providers.description: Jabil (formerly Jabil Circuit) is a global manufacturing services and solutions company providing comprehensive electronics design, production, and product management services to electronics and technology companies in a broad range of industries.

providers.name: Kelly Services
providers.description: Kelly Services is a global leader in providing workforce solutions, connecting talented people to companies in need of their skills across a variety of industries including staffing, talent management, and outsourcing.

providers.name: Kings
providers.description: Kings International Olympiads (kings.lt) is an international educational olympiads organization that runs academic competitions for students, operating a multi-language web platform served from kingsolympiad.com. It was surfaced through the 500 Global venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the organization publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery artifacts (/.well-known/*, llms.txt all resolve to the SPA shell, i.e. soft 404s).

providers.name: Kumu Networks
providers.description: Kumu Networks, Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California semiconductor and RF technology company founded in 2011 to commercialize Stanford University research into full-duplex wireless and self-interference cancellation (SIC). Its silicon and module products — RF integrated circuits, cancellers such as the K8 canceller prototype, and self-interference-cancelling smart repeaters — let a radio transmit and receive on the same or an adjacent channel at the same time, across roughly 200 MHz to 60 GHz, targeting 4G/5G/6G infrastructure, Wi-Fi, IoT, satellite, and defense and aerospace programs including US Army demonstrations and Department of Defense dynamic spectrum-sharing work. The company raised roughly $45M from investors including Khosla Ventures, New Enterprise Associates, Cisco Investments, Deutsche Telekom, Verizon Ventures, Swisscom, Singtel Innov8 and Third Point, and its shares trade on secondary marketplaces. Kumu Networks licenses hardware IP and sells modules to wireless equipment manufacturers rather than operating a public developer platform: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI or public code repositories, and its own website at kumunetworks.com returns HTTP 404 from its WP Engine host (last successful Internet Archive capture 2024-08-10).

providers.name: Laurentian Bank of Canada
providers.description: Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada) is a Montreal-headquartered Schedule I chartered bank, founded in 1846 as the Montreal City and District Savings Bank and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange as LB. With roughly CA$47 billion in assets, about 3,000 employees, and approximately 1.5 million clients, it serves personal, commercial, and capital-markets customers - concentrated in Quebec with commercial offices across Canada - through subsidiaries including B2B Bank, Laurentian Bank Securities, and LBC Capital. The bank operates no public developer portal and exposes no first-party or FDX-style data-access API; consumer data access is aggregator-mediated today (screen-scraping via providers such as Flinks and Plaid), and Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework remains legislated but not yet operational, so participation is voluntary. In December 2025 the bank announced a proposed sale to Fairstone Bank of Canada, with National Bank of Canada acquiring its retail operations.

providers.name: Leucadia National
providers.description: Leucadia National Corporation was a diversified holding company engaged in a variety of businesses, including investment banking, beef processing, manufacturing, telecommunications, and real estate. In 2018 it was renamed Jefferies Financial Group following the merger with Jefferies Group LLC. No public API program is documented under the legacy Leucadia National brand.

providers.name: liangzizhige
providers.description: liangzizhige.com is the corporate domain of QuantaSing Group Limited (NASDAQ QSG), a China-based online learning company listed by Qiming Venture Partners in its technology portfolio as a provider of personal finance online courses. As of this enrichment pass the liangzizhige.com domain is registered through Alibaba Cloud but publishes no A record and serves no website; the only live company surface found is the investor-relations site, which redirects to ir.quantasing.com. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, public GitHub organization, or published client libraries were found for this company.

providers.name: Likeplum
providers.description: Likeplum (likeplum.com) was an online expert-knowledge and task marketplace that billed itself as "expert knowledge and skills at your fingertips" and invited users to "ask experts to answer your questions and hire skilled engineers, programmers, designers, writers, marketers and more on the world's largest information trading marketplace." Members posted either a free-to-ask question or a paid task, received answers and completed work from the site's expert pool, and paid only after approving the result under a post-pay model, with optional fully private posts and card or PayPal settlement. Its busiest categories were writing, programming, graphic design, and marketing and SEO. By late 2014 the company had folded the brand into the "Createpool" network, splitting its four most popular categories into dedicated sites — hackerpool.com for programming tasks, studypool.com for academic and homework Q&A, mechanicpool.com for auto repair, and counselpool.com for legal questions — and migrated every likeplum account, question, answer, and profile across. Only the academic property survives today: likeplum.com now 301-redirects to www.studypool.com, while createpool.com fails TLS negotiation and hackerpool.com, mechanicpool.com, and counselpool.com no longer resolve. The Likeplum brand exposes no developer portal, documentation, SDK, package, or public API, so this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record for a rebranded 500 Global portfolio company rather than as an API provider.

providers.name: Macy's
providers.description: Macy's, Inc. is one of the nation's premier omnichannel retailers, operating department stores, websites, and apps under the Macy's, Bloomingdale's, and Bluemercury brands. This repository tracks any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts that are made publicly available by Macy's.

providers.name: MakeMyTrip
providers.description: MakeMyTrip is a leading Indian online travel company that provides a comprehensive platform for booking flights, hotels, holiday packages, and rail tickets. Founded in 2000, it offers a user-friendly interface and mobile apps, serving millions of customers across India and abroad. The company exposes APIs for partners to integrate travel search, pricing, and booking functionalities, enabling developers to build travel solutions and services. This profile expands the stub with a detailed description for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Metis Labs
providers.description: Metis Labs Limited is a London-based industrial AI company founded in 2017 by Alex Appelbe and Bashir Beikzadeh (an Entrepreneur First EF8 alumnus and a Speedinvest portfolio company). Its product, Kelvin Analytics, is an intelligent factory-optimization platform that applies reinforcement machine-learning to real-time monitoring and predictive analysis, helping process manufacturers in consumer-packaged chemicals, food and beverage, and construction materials cut production-line waste, raise product quality, and improve throughput. Metis Labs was acquired by Ascalia in September 2024. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Mschf Product Studio
providers.description: MSCHF Product Studio, Inc. (pronounced "mischief") is a Brooklyn, New York-based art collective and product studio founded in 2016 by Gabriel Whaley. It is known for viral, limited-edition "drops" released roughly every two weeks — from the Big Red Boots to Satan Shoes, The Persistence of Chaos, and Tax Heaven 3000 — and operates primarily through its own website and brand partnerships. In 2025 it launched Applied MSCHF, an advertising agency. MSCHF is a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment; this remains a company/identity profile.

providers.name: Mujer Financiera
providers.description: Mujer Financiera is a Latin American financial-education platform founded in 2018 in Buenos Aires, Argentina by Sabrina Castelli, focused on closing the gender gap in financial inclusion. It delivers courses, packs, and multi-month programs (MF Platinum) on budgeting, saving, and investing, alongside a mobile app for tracking personal finances, a supportive community, a newsletter, and corporate financial-education services for companies. The platform reports hundreds of thousands of women served across 12+ countries and is backed by 500 Global. It is a business-to-consumer fintech/edtech offering and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Narrator
providers.description: Narrator was a New York data-intelligence company (Y Combinator S2019) that built an end-to-end analytics platform on top of the Activity Schema — a single time-series modeling approach it published as an alternative to star-schema warehouse modeling — covering warehouse transformations, dataset and narrative building, customer-journey analysis and scheduled materializations. The company raised roughly $7.6M and is listed by Y Combinator as Inactive; its narrator.ai domain now 301-redirects to an unrelated WordPress site, and its API, app and documentation hosts no longer resolve or serve. The only surviving first-party surface is the narratorai GitHub organization, where the full platform source (Hasura graph, the Mavis Python service, and the Next.js portal) was published under an MIT license in February 2025.

providers.name: Neiman Marcus Group
providers.description: Neiman Marcus Group is an American chain of luxury department stores selling designer apparel, accessories, jewelry, beauty, home, and gifts under the Neiman Marcus, Bergdorf Goodman, and Last Call banners.

providers.name: Newell Brands
providers.description: Newell Brands is a Fortune 500 global consumer goods company with a strong portfolio of well-known brands including Rubbermaid, Sharpie, Graco, Coleman, Yankee Candle, Paper Mate, Parker, Elmer's, Oster, NUK, and Mr. Coffee.

providers.name: Newell Rubbermaid
providers.description: Newell Rubbermaid was a global marketer of consumer and commercial products with brands including Sharpie, Paper Mate, Rubbermaid, and Calphalon before merging with Jarden in 2016 to form Newell Brands.

providers.name: Noonswoon
providers.description: Noonswoon is an early-stage consumer mobile startup surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/noonswoon) hosts a set of older mobile and social application projects (iOS/Android growth apps, a social-TV effort, and a web forum) dating from roughly 2012-2015. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs, and its primary web property (noonswoonapp.com) returns a 502 backend error, indicating the consumer product is no longer actively operating. No public API surface was found to catalog; this profile captures the identity, domain-security posture, and source-code footprint that remain discoverable.

providers.name: NorthOne
providers.description: NorthOne was a mobile-first, API-enabled business banking platform for small businesses, freelancers, and startups, founded in 2016 by Eytan Bensoussan and Justin Adler with banking services provided by The Bancorp Bank, N.A. It offered the Connected Bank Account (a digital business checking account) with envelope budgeting, savings goals, bookkeeping and accounting integrations, cash deposits, and small-business lending, serving 320,000+ businesses and backed by Battery Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, and Tencent. As of 2026 the northone.com domain redirects to Relay (relayfi.com); NorthOne publishes no public developer API, developer portal, documentation, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Omni Creator Products
providers.description: Omni Creator Products (OCP) is a game development platform company founded in 2021 and based in Raleigh, North Carolina, operating fully remote. Its mission is to "empower every player to become a creator" by making game creation and modding accessible, intuitive, and magical. OCP's products include Muse, a game designed as a scaffold for user-generated content (UGC), and Creator Lab, a toolset that lets players remix and build upon existing games. The company raised a $16.25M Series A in 2022 with investors including a16z (Andreessen Horowitz). As of this enrichment pass OCP publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or OpenAPI surface, and its GitHub organization (ocpgg) has no public repositories.

providers.name: openCypher
providers.description: openCypher is an open-source project that provides a standardized graph query language originally developed by Neo4j for querying property graphs. It enables developers to write expressive pattern-matching queries against graph databases, and its specification has been adopted by multiple graph database vendors.

providers.name: Optimyze
providers.description: Optimyze (Optimyze.cloud Inc.) was a Zurich, Switzerland based continuous-profiling startup, seeded by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) in 2020, and the maker of Prodfiler — a whole-system, eBPF-based continuous profiler that observed CPU and memory usage down to the individual line of code across C/C++, Rust, Go, PHP, Python, Java, Scala, Ruby and Perl, with roughly 1% CPU overhead and no source-code changes or on-host debug symbols. Optimyze was acquired by Elastic N.V. in October 2021 and its Prodfiler technology was folded into Elastic Observability as Elastic Universal Profiling. The independent company no longer operates: the optimyze.cloud domain no longer resolves, the GitHub organization was archived in 2024, and the Prodfiler developer sub-sites (documentation, app, community) are offline. No independent public Optimyze API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal exists to enrich; this profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Orby AI
providers.description: Orby AI is an enterprise generative process automation company that uses Large Action Models, neuro-symbolic reasoning, and agentic process discovery to observe how people work and then automate repetitive back-office and desktop workflows across applications. Founded by former DeepMind and Google researchers, Orby was backed by Wing Venture Capital and NEA before being acquired by Uniphore in August 2025, where its technology now powers the Uniphore Business AI Cloud. Orby publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; its capabilities are delivered as an enterprise platform accessed via demo and sales engagement.

providers.name: Parker Hannifin
providers.description: Parker Hannifin is a global leader in motion and control technologies, providing precision-engineered solutions for a wide variety of mobile, industrial, and aerospace markets. No public developer API has been documented at this time.

providers.name: Petuum
providers.description: Petuum is an AI/ML infrastructure company (backed by SoftBank Vision Fund) known for its CASL (Composable, Automatic, Scalable Learning) open-source initiative — distributed deep-learning and AutoML tooling such as AdaptDL, AutoDist, and Tuun published on GitHub. It was added to the API Evangelist network from the SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio. As of the latest enrichment pass the public website (petuum.com) returns HTTP 530 (origin unreachable) and no public API, developer docs, or machine-readable API description surface could be discovered; the only live public property is the GitHub organization.

providers.name: Playcurio
providers.description: PlayCurio is a Seoul-based educational technology company that builds AR (augmented reality) play-learning products for children, pairing physical educational tools with digital content. Its catalog includes AR titles such as Curio Safari, Phonics Pop, Dictionary Pop, and Math Mates, alongside a content-IP business spanning characters like Detective Pete, Dino Tales, and 100+ Curio Safari animals, plus B2B production services (character development, 2D/3D animation, UI/UX, and live-action video). PlayCurio is consumer- and partnership-facing and publishes no developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation. Surfaced via the 500 Global portfolio and enriched here; a domain-security probe of play-curio.com is the only technical artifact this pass produced.

providers.name: Popular
providers.description: Popular Inc. is a financial holding company offering retail, mortgage, and commercial banking services through its principal subsidiaries Banco Popular de Puerto Rico and Popular Bank in the continental United States.

providers.name: Powerplay
providers.description: Powerplay is a construction project management platform built by Coffer Internet Services Pvt. Ltd. (Bengaluru, India) that gives builders, general contractors, subcontractors, project managers, and site engineers mobile and desktop tools to run construction projects end to end: real-time work and progress tracking, material procurement and inventory management, labor attendance and payroll, issue tracking, petty-cash and expense management, and reporting dashboards. The product is delivered primarily through iOS and Android field apps with a desktop companion. Powerplay does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation, so this profile captures its identity and web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Privacy by Design
providers.description: Privacy By Design is a framework and approach that embeds privacy protections into the design and operation of IT systems, networked infrastructure, and business practices from the ground up, rather than as an afterthought.

providers.name: Qapa
providers.description: Qapa (qapa.fr) is a Paris-based French online recruitment and temporary-work (interim) marketplace that matched companies with job seekers for permanent and temp placements. Backed by Index Ventures and Partech, it was majority-acquired by the Adecco Group. The qapa.fr web property is now gated behind an Azure Application Gateway (HTTP 403) and exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface; this profile is retained as an API Evangelist network record.

providers.name: Qerja
providers.description: PT Qerja Manfaat Bangsa (Qerja) is an Indonesian human-resources company operating an end-to-end HR product ecosystem for employers, established in 2007 and later part of the PT M Cash Integrasi Tbk technology group. In 2019 it acquired Karir.com, Indonesia's first job portal (since 1998), and reports serving over 50,000 clients and 8 million member users across the country. The public presence is a corporate marketing site (qerjagroup.com) covering its HR services, clients, and user demographics; no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: QVC
providers.description: QVC is a multinational corporation specializing in televised home shopping owned by Qurate Retail Group, broadcasting to millions of households worldwide and offering products through television, mobile apps, and websites.

providers.name: Renewable Energy Group
providers.description: Renewable Energy Group (REG) is a North American producer of biodiesel and renewable diesel, founded with biodiesel operations dating to 1996 and formally established as a separate company in 2006, with headquarters in Ames, Iowa. REG operated as a publicly traded company on Nasdaq under the ticker REGI until February 28, 2022, when Chevron Corporation announced the acquisition of REG for approximately $3.15 billion; the deal closed on June 13, 2022, and REG now operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Chevron under the Chevron Renewable Energy Group brand at chevron-reg.com. REG operates a fleet of biorefineries across the United States and Europe, producing biodiesel, renewable diesel, and related lower-carbon fuel products from a diversified mix of feedstocks including used cooking oil, inedible animal fats, distillers corn oil, and vegetable oils. As of this profile, neither REG nor the Chevron Renewable Energy Group subsidiary publishes a public consumer-facing developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or GitHub organization; customer, supplier, distributor, and feedstock-partner integrations are handled through Chevron Renewable Energy Group sales, supply, and supplier-relations channels.

providers.name: ResearchGate
providers.description: ResearchGate is a professional network and social platform for scientists and researchers, founded in 2008 in Berlin, Germany. Members use it to share and discover research publications, connect and collaborate with colleagues, ask and answer questions, and track the reach and citations of their work. The platform hosts tens of millions of researcher profiles and a large corpus of full-text papers, and is operated by ResearchGate GmbH. It exposes no publicly documented developer API surface; this profile was surfaced via the dragoneer portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Salduu (Profe Social)
providers.description: Salduu, operating as Profe Social at profe.social, is a 500 Global-backed social networking platform. The live host serves Mastodon's default robots.txt (Disallow /search, sitemap.xml.gz) and a Ruby on Rails error stack, indicating the platform runs on Mastodon / ActivityPub fediverse technology, so it exposes the standard Mastodon client REST API and ActivityPub federation endpoints under /api. Both the site and its API surface sit behind a Cloudflare managed challenge, so the instance's own instance metadata, OpenAPI, and developer pages could not be retrieved by a non-browser client during enrichment. This profile records what was directly observed via DNS/TLS/HTTP and well-known probes; the API contract itself remains to be captured once the challenge is cleared or the provider publishes a spec.

providers.name: Saris
providers.description: Saris (saris.ai) is an enterprise AI company building AI workflow agents for banks and credit unions. Its platform automates multi-step back-office processes across lending, compliance, and operations — document processing, data validation, core-system updates, and compliance tracking — while keeping humans in control with full audit trails. Saris integrates with financial-technology platforms such as Fiserv and with model providers including OpenAI and Anthropic, and is a recommended CCUA partner for Northeast credit unions. The company raised a $28.8M Series A and is backed by 8vc. As of this enrichment pass Saris exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Screenhero
providers.description: Screenhero was a Y Combinator (W13) startup that built interactive screen sharing with voice and video, letting remote users share and control any application together. It was acquired by Slack in January 2015; the six-person team joined Slack and the standalone Screenhero product was discontinued, with its screen-sharing, voice, and video capabilities folded into Slack (today surfaced as Slack Huddles). The screenhero.com domain now 301-redirects to slack.com/features/huddles. No independent Screenhero developer portal, API, or SDK exists; this record is retained as a historical a16z portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Simplifai Labs
providers.description: Simplifai Labs is a Dubai-based artificial intelligence and marketing-technology company founded in 2018 by Sachin Rathnaraj Jain. Its deep-learning platform combines image recognition, computer vision, sentiment and emotion analysis, and natural language processing to place brand advertising alongside highly relevant, brand-safe content in real time, without relying on stored user cookie data. Simplifai Labs completed the 500 Global (Misk 500 MENA) accelerator in Riyadh and is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs. Its simplifailabs.com domain lapsed and was re-registered on 2025-08-18, and now serves a Cyberfuel hosting placeholder rather than any Simplifai Labs content; no API, docs, or developer subdomain resolves, and the simplifailabs GitHub organization holds a single forked UI repository and no first-party libraries. The founder's subsequent venture, Smartifai (Dubai, 2022), is a separate company and is not profiled here. No API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Simply
providers.description: Simply (hellosimply.com) is a consumer creative-learning company that makes AI-powered mobile apps for teaching music and art to beginners, with the stated mission of making the pursuit of creative hobbies simple and fun for all. Its product suite spans Simply Piano, Simply Guitar, Simply Sing, and the free Simply Tune tuner for music, plus Simply Draw for art, and a set of emerging extended-reality experiences including Simply Piano XR, Simply Piano for Apple Vision Pro and Google Android XR, and Simply Draw for Meta AI Glasses. Backed by GV, Simply is a direct-to-consumer subscription business and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; press inquiries are handled at press@hellosimply.com.

providers.name: Socra AI
providers.description: Socra AI operates Socra Tutor (소크라 튜터), a Korean-market, AI-powered education service that describes itself as an intelligent AI answer-comparison service — students submit problems and Socra compares and evaluates candidate answers using AI to help them learn. It is a consumer-facing edtech mobile/web application rather than a developer platform; as of this profile no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation could be found. Socra AI was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Socratic
providers.description: Socratic is an AI-powered homework help and learning app that lets students photograph or type a question and receive curated explanations, videos, and step-by-step resources across math, science, literature, and social studies. Founded in 2013 and backed at the early stage by investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Socratic was acquired by Google in 2018 and now operates as "Socratic by Google," a free consumer mobile app whose homework-help capabilities have largely been folded into Google Lens. Socratic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documented developer surface; this profile records it as an acquired consumer product with no independent API footprint.

providers.name: SpringRole
providers.description: SpringRole was a blockchain-based professional reputation and attestation platform — an endorsement and verified-resume network that let people attest to each other's skills and work history on-chain — and was a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Its primary domain, springrole.com, now issues a 301 redirect to Springworks (springworks.in), an HR-technology company whose products include SpringVerify (background verification), Goodfit (AI-native recruitment), and EngageWith (employee engagement). An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, developer portal, SDK/package, MCP server, llms.txt, or /.well-known discovery documents for SpringRole (the well-known paths return the Webflow marketing SPA, not real artifacts), and no separate developer or docs subdomain resolves.

providers.name: StayNTouch
providers.description: StayNTouch provides cloud‑based property management software designed for hotels and hospitality businesses. Their platform enables seamless guest check‑in, mobile key access, housekeeping coordination, and real‑time analytics to improve operational efficiency and guest experience. Founded in 2015, StayNTouch serves thousands of properties worldwide, integrating with major PMS systems and offering APIs for developers to build custom integrations and extensions.

providers.name: Stori
providers.description: Stori is a Mexico City–headquartered fintech (operating as a regulated Sociedad Financiera Popular under CNBV and CONDUSEF oversight) on a mission to democratize credit access for the roughly 400 million underbanked consumers in Latin America. Founded in 2019, the company achieved unicorn status in 2022 and has raised over $400M from investors including GGV Capital, General Catalyst, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Goodwater Capital, Source Code Capital, Vision Plus Capital, BAI Capital, Tresalia, and GIC. Stori's flagship product is the Stori Card, an inclusive Visa credit card marketed to first-time borrowers with little or no formal credit history, alongside Stori Black (premium tier), co-branded cards (SHEIN, Farmacias Similares, sports teams), Cuenta+ (a commission-free deposit account advertising up to 15% annual returns), personal loans up to roughly $3,000 MXN-equivalent, and payment services covering bill pay, mobile recharges, and phone-based merchant collection. The platform is delivered exclusively through its iOS and Android mobile apps and serves more than five million Mexican users. Stori has no public developer API, SDK, CLI, webhook surface, or open-source release; its revenue model is interest, interchange, and fee income from consumer credit and deposit products, with operations in Mexico, Colombia, and a U.S. corporate presence in Arlington, Virginia.

providers.name: StudentFinance
providers.description: StudentFinance is a European fintech company, backed by Seedcamp, focused on financing access to education and career development (income-share and deferred-payment models for students and upskilling programs). Surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, its public presence is currently a minimal Webflow marketing site; an enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: StudySoup
providers.description: StudySoup is a consumer education-technology platform that provides college and university students with study tools for better grades. It offers custom study guides written by student notetakers, step-by-step textbook solutions (AnswerED videos), video overviews of core curriculum (PreparED), and community features including a Discord channel and YouTube livestreams, alongside a notetaker monetization program that pays students to share their notes. StudySoup was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass the live site (studysoup.com) is an active B2C study-resources product with no publicly documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or integration surface.

providers.name: Sun Communities
providers.description: Sun Communities, Inc. is a real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns, operates, and develops manufactured home communities, recreational vehicle resorts, and marinas across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The company is one of the largest operators in its sector and is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: Supercritical
providers.description: Supercritical is a London-based carbon removal marketplace founded in 2021 by Michelle You and Aaron Randall, the team behind Songkick. The company builds the market infrastructure that turns carbon dioxide removal (CDR) commitments into delivered tonnes, connecting corporate buyers with vetted suppliers of durable, engineered, and nature-engineered carbon removal. Supercritical's marketplace covers the major durable CDR pathways — biochar, BECCS, enhanced weathering, direct air capture (DAC), DAC with ocean storage, woody biomass sinking, and bio-oil — with published per-tonne pricing and live availability data. The platform layers a proprietary 118-point vetting protocol on top of supplier listings, spanning climate science, environmental impact, delivery risk, and social benefits, and reports that 84% of assessed projects fail to meet its standards. Supercritical also provides supply sourcing and creation services to originate new CDR projects, buffer-pool-based delivery-risk mitigation, and policy and science advisory work (its team advises SBTi on CDR guidance). Customers include Virgin Atlantic, The Economist Group, Rothschild & Co, XTX Markets, and Tide, with reported coverage of roughly 80% of the global durable CDR market and 1.3M tonnes contracted across 200+ corporate buyers and 600+ tracked suppliers. The business is funded by Lightspeed Venture Partners, MMC Ventures, and GreenCode Ventures. Supercritical does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository; transactions, supplier discovery, and pricing data are delivered through its hosted marketplace, advisor relationships, and contracted buyer accounts.

providers.name: Tabular
providers.description: Tabular was an independent, managed cloud data platform and storage engine built on Apache Iceberg, founded in 2021 by Ryan Blue, Daniel Weeks, and Jason Reid — two of the original creators of Apache Iceberg and a former head of Data Engineering at Netflix. Its central product was a managed Iceberg catalog exposed over the open Apache Iceberg REST Catalog protocol (an OpenAPI-defined common API), giving any compute engine vendor-neutral access to a single copy of data. Databricks agreed to acquire Tabular in June 2024 and closed the deal that month; the founders joined Databricks and the standalone product was wound down. As of this enrichment pass the tabular.io domain no longer resolves and the tabular-io GitHub organization has no public repositories, so there is no live first-party API surface to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: The Athletic
providers.description: The Athletic is a subscription-based digital sports media company founded in 2016 by Alex Mather and Adam Hansmann, offering in-depth, ad-light coverage of national and local professional and college sports through a large staff of beat writers and columnists. Acquired by The New York Times Company in 2022, The Athletic delivers written articles, newsletters, podcasts, and live coverage across its website and mobile apps. As of this enrichment pass The Athletic does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; its GitHub organization contains only forks of open-source engineering tooling rather than any public API product.

providers.name: Tuza
providers.description: Tuza is a banking automation platform that orchestrates AI agents, customers and workflows to eliminate the manual processes that slow banks down. Originally launched in the UK at tuza.co.uk as a card-payment fee comparison and switching service for merchants, the company has repositioned as Tuza AI, delivering agentic automation for banks. It is an early-stage, venture-backed fintech (backed by Northzone) building a product that connects AI agents with core banking operations and customer-facing workflows.
