As of this profile Tuza publishes a marketing and careers site only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface has been released yet, so this record captures verified company identity plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: VIPThink
providers.description: VIPThink (豌豆思维) is a Chinese online education company operated by Guangdong Happy Seeds Technology Co., Ltd. (广东快乐种子科技有限公司), delivering small-class live-streaming courses in mathematical thinking and logic for young children (roughly ages 3-8). It is part of a family of consumer education brands that also includes Hualala drawing classes (画啦啦), Wandou speech training (豌豆口才), Gubi early-learning (咕比启蒙), and Little Lighthouse (小灯塔). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, VIPThink operates only consumer-facing web and mobile learning products and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: VNDLY
providers.description: VNDLY is a cloud-based vendor management system (VMS) for managing contingent workforce, external labor, statements of work (SOW), and services procurement. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Mason, Ohio, VNDLY was acquired by Workday in 2021 and is now offered as Workday VNDLY, pairing with Workday Human Capital Management (HCM) for total workforce optimization. The company no longer operates an independent public developer portal or API surface; integration is delivered through the Workday platform. This profile originated as a portfolio-company lead (Battery Ventures, Insight Partners) surfaced into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: WePlayed
providers.description: WePlayed builds AI-powered short-form video for college athletics, automatically turning full game and event footage into shareable highlight clips that athletic departments, sponsors, and fans use to engage audiences and power sponsorship deals. A Techstars Sports Accelerator company that raised a $2 million seed round, WePlayed partners with SIDEARM Sports to distribute highlights across collegiate athletics websites. As of this profile WePlayed does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Xenesis
providers.description: Xenesis, Inc. is an optical satellite communications company founded in 2017 by Mark LaPenna and headquartered in Lisle, Illinois. It builds the Xen-Hub, a free-space optical (laser) communications terminal enabled by a technology transfer from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and rated at greater than 10 Gbps, and plans Intercessor, a space-to-ground optical mesh network intended to backhaul high-bandwidth data with lower latency and higher capacity than radio-frequency or terrestrial fiber links. The company has taken Space Development Agency optical-terminal awards (Phase 1 in August 2022, a Phase 2 follow-on in December 2023) built to the SDA OCT v3.1 and v4.0 standards, signed a payload agreement with Airbus for a Bartolomeo demonstration slot on the International Space Station, and holds a $1.2M agreement with Georgia Tech for satellite optical communications work. Xenesis is a space hardware and telecommunications-infrastructure company, not a software vendor: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and its own website is currently returning an HTTP 401 site-wide password lock.

providers.name: Zuoyebang
providers.description: Zuoyebang (作业帮) is a Chinese educational technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Beijing, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It operates a "technology + education" online learning platform whose flagship homework-help app lets K-12 students photograph a problem to get step-by-step answers, on-demand tutoring, and self-study tools across all subjects, alongside math tutoring products aimed at elementary-school parents and teachers. It is a consumer mobile/web product with no public developer program, open platform, or documented API surface at the time of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Zylon
providers.description: Zylon is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of felicis and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Amber Wave
providers.description: AmberWave, Inc. (formerly AmberWave Systems Corporation) is a Lowell, Massachusetts deep-technology company that researches, develops, and licenses semiconductor and photovoltaic materials technology. It originated strained-silicon and aspect-ratio-trapping techniques from MIT and Bell Labs research, and today develops Ultra-Thin Silicon (UTSi) flexible solar cells and modules that weigh roughly 90% less than conventional panels, targeting lightweight commercial rooftops, off-grid power, building integration, vehicle, and aerospace applications. AmberWave is a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It publishes a corporate website but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface, so there are no machine-readable API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Arkuda Therapeutics
providers.description: Arkuda Therapeutics, Inc. was a privately held, preclinical-stage biotechnology company based in Watertown, Massachusetts, founded in 2018 by Gerhard Koenig, Ph.D. and Duane Burnett to develop small-molecule enhancers of lysosomal function for neurodegenerative disease. Its lead biology targeted progranulin (GRN) and lysosomal dysfunction in frontotemporal dementia (FTD-GRN), Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. Arkuda closed a $44M Series A in November 2019 and a $64M Series B in February 2022, backed by Atlas Venture, Cormorant Asset Management, Pfizer Ventures, abrdn plc, Mission BioCapital and Eli Lilly and Company. On 27 February 2024 it entered an option and asset purchase agreement with Johnson & Johnson, and on 9 January 2025 Johnson & Johnson (through Janssen Pharmaceuticals) exercised that option and acquired the entire portfolio of lysosomal function enhancers. Independent operations concluded thereafter; founder and CEO Gerhard Koenig became CEO of Augustine Therapeutics in January 2025. Arkuda was a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and both of its former domains have since lapsed.

providers.name: Atomic Alchemy
providers.description: Atomic Alchemy is a deep-tech nuclear company that designs, builds, and operates non-power research reactors to manufacture high-value radioisotopes for medical, research, industrial, defense, and space applications. Its proprietary Versatile Isotope Production Reactor (VIPR) technology and Meitner-1 facility are intended to create a scalable, onshore supply of isotopes such as molybdenum-99 (for cancer diagnostics and treatment), strontium-90, and americium-241, reducing US dependence on foreign isotope production. Founded by CEO Thomas Eiden and headquartered in Idaho Falls, Idaho, the company was backed by DCVC and Y Combinator and was acquired by advanced-fission company Oklo (NYSE: OKLO) in early 2025, operating as a wholly owned subsidiary. In 2026 the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission granted Atomic Alchemy a materials license to handle, process, and distribute isotopes. As a physical radioisotope manufacturer, Atomic Alchemy publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Banco de Mexico
providers.description: Banco de México, also known as Banxico, is the central bank of Mexico. It oversees monetary policy, financial stability, and the national payment systems. The institution provides economic indicators, statistical data, and regulatory information through its public portals, supporting transparency and research for businesses, analysts, and the public.

providers.name: Blinker
providers.description: Blinker provides a platform for auto warranty call centers to quote, fulfill, bill, and retain protection‑plan customers. It offers a connected workflow that includes quoting protection plans, collecting down payments, setting up recurring billing, capturing e‑signatures, delivering agreements in real time, and tracking customers from prospect through retention. The solution aims to streamline revenue capture and improve customer experience for D2C auto warranty businesses.

providers.name: cdhot (Hot New Energy Technology)
providers.description: cdhot (Hot New Energy Technology) is a Chinese industrial energy-efficiency company listed in the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio. Qiming describes the company as providing EPC (engineering, procurement and construction) and EMC (energy management contracting) services to industrial customers to achieve waste heat recovery — capturing surplus process heat from industrial operations and converting it into reusable energy. The company is an engineering and energy-services business rather than a software or API provider. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass its published website at cdhot.cc did not resolve over HTTPS, redirected to www.cdhot.cc over HTTP and returned an empty HTTP 404, and no developer portal, documentation, specification, or API surface of any kind could be found.

providers.name: Clearmindbiomedical
providers.description: Clearmindbiomedical is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: colandpharma
providers.description: colandpharma was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no public surface to profile: colandpharma.com is registered (created 2007-09-21, renewed through 2027-09-21, Gname.com registrar) and delegates to share-dns nameservers, but the zone publishes no A/AAAA, MX, TXT, SPF, DMARC or CAA records. The apex and the www, api, docs and developer subdomains do not resolve, and the authoritative nameserver itself returns no host records, confirming a dormant or parked domain rather than a transient outage. There is consequently no website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog. This record is retained as a lead; re-run enrichment if the domain is ever brought online.

providers.name: ConverzAI
providers.description: ConverzAI is a Seattle-based artificial intelligence company (founded 2019) that builds an agentic, voice-first AI platform for the recruitment and staffing industry. Its flagship Virtual Recruiter deploys autonomous AI agents that source, engage, screen, and match candidates through natural conversations over voice, text, and email, then update the customer's applicant tracking system automatically. The platform integrates with major ATS products used by staffing firms (Avionte, Bullhorn, Ceipal, JobDiva, Salesforce, TempWorks and others) and lets a single recruiter engage hundreds of thousands of candidates in parallel. ConverzAI raised a $16M Series A led by Menlo Ventures in February 2025 and reports processing over 100,000 jobs while engaging millions of candidates. This is a product/application company profile; ConverzAI does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Downstream Energy
providers.description: Downstream Energy is a software company that provides business-to-business electronic commerce solutions for the refined petrochemical and downstream petroleum industry, supporting the buying and selling of refined products such as gasoline, distillate, propane, and jet fuel. It is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification has been located for this provider during enrichment, so the profile remains a lightly enriched identity stub pending discovery of a public API surface.

providers.name: Energy Future Holdings
providers.description: Energy Future Holdings was a Dallas-based privately held energy company involved in electricity generation, mining, wholesale energy trading, transmission and distribution, and retail electricity through subsidiaries Luminant, Oncor, and TXU Energy. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2014 and was succeeded by Vistra Corp (which absorbed Luminant and TXU Energy generation/retail operations) and Sempra Texas Utilities (which acquired Oncor). No active developer APIs are offered under the Energy Future Holdings name.

providers.name: Enpirion
providers.description: Enpirion was a fabless semiconductor company specializing in high-frequency power-management integrated circuits, best known for its PowerSoC family of integrated DC-DC converters that combined the controller, MOSFETs, and inductor in a single package for point-of-load power conversion in networking, computing, and industrial systems. The company was acquired by Altera in 2013 and subsequently absorbed into Intel with Altera in 2015; the Enpirion brand and its enpirion.com developer/product site are now defunct. It never operated a public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK program, so this record is retained as a company identity stub rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Estes Energy
providers.description: Estes Energy is a US-based manufacturer of advanced battery packs for heavy-duty transport. Its magnesium-alloy Magnus platform (proprietary MgCarbonit thermo-structural body) delivers roughly 225 Wh/kg for rail, marine, aviation and off-highway applications, with chemistry-agnostic (sodium, LFP, nickel) packs manufactured entirely in the United States. Backed by DCVC, Fortescue Ventures, BMW and New System Ventures. A hardware/manufacturing company with no public API, developer portal, SDK or software product surface at this time.

providers.name: Exact Sciences
providers.description: Exact Sciences is a molecular diagnostics company and a Fortune 1000 firm best known for the Cologuard colorectal cancer screening test and the Oncotype DX family of cancer tests. The company develops, manufactures, and markets laboratory-based screening and precision oncology tests delivered to patients and providers through its Exact Labs operations. Exact Sciences does not publish a public developer portal or external API.

providers.name: Fervo Energy
providers.description: Fervo Energy is a next-generation geothermal power company headquartered in Houston, Texas, that generates carbon-free, always-on electricity through enhanced geothermal systems (EGS). Founded in 2017 by Tim Latimer and Jack Norbeck, Fervo adapts horizontal drilling, distributed fiber-optic sensing, and advanced subsurface data analytics from the oil and gas industry to make geothermal energy viable in previously uneconomic locations. Its projects include the Project Red pilot in Nevada and the flagship 500 MW Cape Station development in Beaver County, Utah. Fervo trades on Nasdaq under the ticker FRVO and is backed by investors including DCVC. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network surfaced from the DCVC portfolio; Fervo Energy is a physical energy-infrastructure company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: FirstFuel Software
providers.description: FirstFuel Software was a business-focused energy analytics SaaS company that used utility meter and building data to profile commercial and industrial customers, helping utilities target energy-efficiency and customer-engagement programs. The company was acquired by Uplight, and the firstfuel.com domain now redirects to uplight.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. The enrichment pipeline found no active first-party developer surface (no developer, api, or docs subdomains resolve, and no OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP artifacts are published), so this profile remains an identity-only record for a company that no longer operates a standalone API program.

providers.name: GoDays
providers.description: GoDays is an AI-powered workforce analytics platform for enterprises that predicts and helps prevent employee burnout. It analyzes internal company data — keyboard usage behaviors, employee sentiment, interactions, performance, and feedback — to measure and forecast burnout risk, then surfaces recommendations to improve workflow, productivity, and employee wellbeing. Founded in 2021 and based in Seoul (Gangnam), South Korea, the company was co-founded by CEO Yelnur Kai and Adiar Bopov, and raised a seed round in 2024 with participation from 500 Global and Domino VC. GoDays was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site only, with no public API, developer portal, or specification surface.

providers.name: Govlist
providers.description: Govlist, Inc. (which operated as ProcureNow) was a San Francisco-based govtech startup providing a multi-tenant SaaS platform for government procurement and contract management. Its Government Procurement Automation Cloud helped local and state agencies build, source, and evaluate RFPs and bids, and helped suppliers read, understand, and respond to complex public solicitations. The company, backed by 500 Global and Civstart, was acquired by OpenGov in 2021 (announced June 2021), where the product now lives as OpenGov Procurement. Govlist has no independent developer surface, API, or portal; its original domain (thegovlist.com) no longer resolves. This profile is preserved as a historical lead surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio.

providers.name: Graviti
providers.description: Graviti is a Mexico City-based consumer fintech founded in 2020 that unlocks affordable access to essential home utilities for unbanked and underserved Mexican families, starting with solar water heaters financed through a pay-as-you-go (PayGo / BNPL) model of small recurring payments. Backed by 500 Global, Clocktower Technology Ventures, Mucker Capital, Active Capital, and BFA Global's Catalyst Fund, the company combines hardware installation with embedded consumer lending. Graviti is a consumer-facing product company and does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with an honest no-API-surface result.

providers.name: GridBank
providers.description: GridBank is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: energy. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Health Co (Stealth)
providers.description: Health Co (Stealth) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Hospira
providers.description: Hospira was a global specialty pharmaceutical and medication delivery company providing injectable drugs and infusion technologies before being acquired by Pfizer in 2015. No public APIs are offered under the Hospira brand.

providers.name: i2c
providers.description: Outpace legacy and unproven modern platforms with i2c’s next generation platform and composable solutions built for speed, reliability and scale. i2c Inc. provides a comprehensive suite of banking and payments APIs, enabling fintechs and enterprises to integrate core financial services quickly and securely.

providers.name: IASIS Healthcare
providers.description: IASIS Healthcare was a leading owner and operator of acute care hospitals in growing urban markets in the United States before being acquired by Steward Health Care in 2017. Operations and any legacy developer resources have since been consolidated under Steward Health Care.

providers.name: In Charge One
providers.description: In Charge One, Inc. is a hardware startup behind "Socket to Pocket," a paid charging system for electronic devices in public spaces. The device lets visitors charge smartphones, laptops, drones, e-bikes, and scooters at cafes, shops, clinics, stadiums, airports, and other venues by tapping a card and paying for access, while venue owners monetize the outlet and earn a commission per plugged socket. It ships in wall-mounted, extension-cord, and anti-vandal street versions. Founded in 2023 by Danylo (Daniel) Tonkopii, co-founder of Delfast electric bikes, and Andriy Zinchuk, the company is based in Los Angeles, California and was developed by Ukrainian engineers. It is a consumer/commercial hardware and payments business, not an API provider: no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface has been published, and its incharge.one domain is currently non-resolving and in registrar redemption/pending-delete status. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is retained as an identity record.

providers.name: Istra Research
providers.description: Istra Research (Istra LLC) is a quantitative proprietary trading firm that develops data-centric algorithms and low-latency technology to participate in global financial markets. The firm employs researchers and engineers who build automated trading strategies grounded in advanced mathematics, statistics, and large-scale data analysis, spanning quantitative research, algorithm development, and custom hardware/VLSI and software engineering. Istra is a proprietary trading operation rather than an API-first technology vendor: it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or developer documentation, and its technology is used internally. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Justinian
providers.description: Justinian is an applied AI company, backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026), building what it calls the first AI-native government affairs firm. Founded by Parth Badhwar (previously Clipbook, The White House, Deloitte's policy team, and the Harris campaign), Justinian helps early-stage companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts. The firm operates from San Francisco and Washington, DC, pairing staff drawn from the White House and top lobbying firms with engineering, and frames its mission as rebuilding public-private partnerships in America. Justinian currently presents as a services and product company with a demo-request/contact flow; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Madrone
providers.description: Madrone is a data center cooling technology company (Y Combinator Spring 2026, NVIDIA Inception) building modular thermodynamic cooling systems that sit outside the data center and chill water to the dew point, eliminating the need for mechanical chillers and cooling towers. The company claims roughly 30% less power and water than a conventional chiller-plus-cooling-tower setup in Texas installations, freeing that power and capital for additional GPU compute. It is an early-stage hardware and infrastructure company with a sales-and-partnerships motion; as of this profiling it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, documentation, or other machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Marvel Tech (Mufan Power)
providers.description: Marvel Tech (Mufan Power, 慕帆动力) is a Chinese industrial power-equipment manufacturer developing next-generation zero-carbon clean power-generation technology and products. Its portfolio centers on hydrogen-fuelled gas turbine generating sets, high-speed multi-stage cantilever turbines, special-gas and TRT flow-path (通流) turbines, dry low-NOx combustors, and industrial waste-heat and waste-pressure recovery equipment. The company runs a corporate brochure website in Chinese and English (ICP 沪ICP备17001438号) and publishes no public developer, API, or SDK surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mayflower
providers.description: Mayflower is an early-stage (Y Combinator, Fall 2025) startup building an AI-powered HR plug-in that automates immigration screening, visa eligibility assessment, and compliance for international hiring. The platform parses candidate documents, classifies visa pathways, and generates attorney-ready forms, integrating directly with existing HR systems so companies can surface only compliant candidates and reduce legal risk. Founded in 2025 by Naren Chittem and Aryan Gulati and based in San Francisco, the company currently operates a marketing landing page with a book-a-call motion and publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or GitHub organization. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; the enrichment pipeline found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Modular Wind Energy
providers.description: Modular Wind Energy is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Moveha
providers.description: Moveha is a student-housing and long-term rental platform for the United States, built to help college students and relocating professionals find, reserve, and secure off-campus housing before they arrive in the country. Founded by former international students and backed by 500 Global, Moveha positions itself as an "Airbnb for long-term rentals" — a faster, more transparent way to browse verified properties, reserve remotely, share rooms, or list a property for lease, with identity-verified users. As of this enrichment pass Moveha publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: National Institute of Corrections
providers.description: The National Institute of Corrections (NIC) is an agency within the U.S. Department of Justice that provides training, technical assistance, and information to federal, state, and local corrections agencies. NIC publishes guidance, library resources, and corrections-related data through its website but does not currently expose a public web API.

providers.name: Norstel
providers.description: Norstel AB was a Swedish semiconductor materials company that produced silicon carbide (SiC) wafers for power electronics, high-frequency and high-temperature electronics, and sensors, using its patented High Temperature Chemical Vapor Deposition (HTCVD) crystal-growth technology. Backed by Creandum among other investors, Norstel was acquired by STMicroelectronics in December 2019 and folded into ST's silicon carbide operations; it no longer operates as an independent company. As a hardware and materials manufacturer, Norstel published no developer platform, API, or SDK, so this API Evangelist record is an identity-only profile with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
providers.description: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is a US federal agency that sets and enforces standards for safe and healthful working conditions. OSHA provides data APIs for accessing workplace injury and illness data, establishment inspection records, and compliance information.

providers.name: Office of Government Ethics
providers.description: The Office of Government Ethics (OGE) is an independent agency within the federal government that oversees the behavior and ethics of executive branch employees. The OGE provides guidance and advice on ethics laws and regulations to government officials, conducts ethics training programs, and reviews financial disclosure reports to ensure compliance with ethical standards. The office also works to prevent conflicts of interest and promote transparency and accountability in government operations.

providers.name: Office of Inspector General
providers.description: The Office of Inspector General (OIG) conducts audits, investigations, inspections, and other reviews to promote economy and efficiency in government programs and operations, and to prevent and detect fraud, waste, and abuse.

providers.name: Olea
providers.description: Olea is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: government. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Omnicare
providers.description: Omnicare is a long-term care pharmacy services company providing pharmacy services to long-term care facilities, senior living communities, and other healthcare providers. Customer-facing portals (Omniview, MyOmniview) exist for clients but no public developer APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: OptoAtmospherics
providers.description: OptoAtmospherics, Inc. is an Ann Arbor, Michigan company (founded 2009, spun out of Michigan Aerospace Corporation) that develops UV-based Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR) systems for the wind energy industry. Its laser-based atmospheric measurement products deliver continuous wind speed, direction, temperature, and density reporting from turbine-mounted or ground-based platforms, with real-time detection of wind gusts, shear, and turbulence to improve site assessment, increase energy output, and protect turbine equipment. The business is a hardware and atmospheric-sensing venture; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or software platform. Its former domain (optoatmospherics.com) is now parked/for-sale and the product line lives on under michiganaerospace.com/optoatmospherics/.

providers.name: Proterra
providers.description: Proterra is a US-based manufacturer of high-energy lithium-ion battery systems for electric vehicles and commercial equipment, including transit buses, trucks, and off-highway EVs, with charging and fleet solutions. Originally an electric transit bus and powertrain manufacturer founded in 2004, the battery-systems business (Powered by Proterra) continues under the proterra.com domain following the 2023 restructuring. It is a physical hardware and energy-storage company backed by Obvious Ventures under its planetary-health thesis, and publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Raised
providers.description: Raised (joinraised.com) is an AI-powered recruiting platform founded in 2022 and backed by 500 Global. It delivers vetted candidates to venture-backed startups — particularly in AI, deep tech, and Web3 — at a fraction of the cost and time of traditional recruitment agencies, using proprietary AI to match candidates to roles. The company is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, and operates as a software-enabled alternative to traditional staffing firms. Raised publishes a marketing website only; no public developer API, documentation, or developer platform surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Rens Energy
providers.description: Rens Energy is a Shanghai-based distributed energy-storage and energy-management company founded in 2017. It builds distributed energy-storage systems and energy-management software that let customers deliver power and energy-balance scheduling, energy-usage analysis, and energy optimization for efficient operation and asset appreciation of their power assets. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment probing found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Safire
providers.description: Safire (Safire Technology Group, Inc.) is a Canaan Partners portfolio company operating in battery and energy-materials deep tech. It develops impact-resistant, safety-focused electrolyte technology aimed at making lithium-ion batteries more resistant to fire and physical damage. Added to the API Evangelist network as a stub from Canaan's portfolio, it is a hardware and materials-science business rather than a software vendor; an enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 probed the company's likely domains and found no public developer portal, API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Smalt
providers.description: Smalt is a Berlin-based training academy and technology platform for the green-energy installation trades. It combines a B2B installation services business (solar and, increasingly, heat pumps and other climate-trade work) with an education platform that upskills and certifies installers, plus a franchise model that lets trained installers run their own training businesses on Smalt's learning materials and tooling. Founded in 2023 and backed by General Catalyst, noa, Owl Ventures, Heartfelt, La Famiglia and Loric Ventures, Smalt is a workforce/services company rather than an API provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface to catalog.

providers.name: Solar City
providers.description: SolarCity was a San Mateo, California based provider of residential and commercial solar energy systems, founded in 2006 by brothers Peter and Lyndon Rive with backing and board chairmanship from their cousin Elon Musk. The company designed, financed, installed, and monitored rooftop solar and energy-storage systems, and became the largest residential solar installer in the United States before its 2012 IPO (NASDAQ: SCTY). In November 2016 SolarCity was acquired by Tesla, Inc. in an all-stock deal valued at roughly 2.6 billion US dollars and was absorbed into Tesla's energy-generation and storage business; the SolarCity brand was subsequently retired and its products relaunched under Tesla (Solar Roof, Solar Panels, Powerwall). SolarCity no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone developer portal, public API, or OpenAPI surface. The solarcity.com domain remains registered under Tesla's DNS infrastructure but no longer serves a live website.

providers.name: Terra AI
providers.description: Terra AI is a geoscience frontier company building specialized artificial intelligence for the natural resources sector, focused on subsurface characterization and exploration optimization for mining and reservoir operators. Its platform integrates exploration data to generate large populations of geological models, helping teams decide where to drill, characterize deposits, and assess project economics earlier — the company cites 50-60% fewer drilling meters and 2-3x more precise resource estimates versus conventional methods. Terra AI raised a $20M Series A led by Khosla Ventures with BHP Ventures in June 2026 and serves copper, gold, rare-earth (REE), and reservoir projects. The company operates on a B2B model and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Toyota
providers.description: The world's largest automobile manufacturer by production volume, producing a wide range of vehicles from sedans and SUVs to hybrids and hydrogen fuel cell cars. Pioneer of lean manufacturing and hybrid technology through the iconic Prius.

providers.name: Vaccitech *
providers.description: Vaccitech * is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: life-sciences. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: viaPhoton
providers.description: viaPhoton is a Naperville, Illinois fiber optic connectivity manufacturer, founded in 2020, that designs and builds high-density fiber solutions for hyperscale and enterprise data centers, 5G and broadband access networks, and AI network fabrics. Its catalog spans inside-plant products (fiber trunks, fiber arrays, patch cords, MPO/MTP connectivity, structured cabling) and outside-plant products (outdoor fiber jumpers, fiber drop cables, outdoor trunks), produced in a domestic "micro-factory" model intended to shorten lead times against an industry that sources roughly 90% of fiber optic material offshore. viaPhoton sells through a configure-price-quote product configurator rather than a developer program; it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: VLTA
providers.description: VLTA (Volta Charging) is an electric-vehicle charging network that pairs public EV chargers with digital out-of-home advertising displays at retail, grocery, and shopping destinations. The Volta business was acquired by Shell in 2023; its voltacharging.com domain now redirects to Shell's mobility/EV-charging pages, and consumer charging operations are presented under the JOLT brand (joltcharge.com) offering a mobile app to locate chargers, start/stop sessions, and view pricing. No public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or GitHub organization was found during enrichment; this remains an identity/company profile with no API surface.

providers.name: Zephyr Fusion
providers.description: Zephyr Fusion is a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) company building the first in-orbit fusion power source: a compact, megawatt-class magnetic-confinement fusion reactor designed to enable large-scale industry in space at a fraction of the cost of equivalent solar. Founded by former Lawrence Livermore and Oak Ridge National Laboratory physicists, the company targets microgravity manufacturing, orbital data centers, defense, propulsion, and human habitation in space, exploiting the vacuum of space to accommodate larger plasma regions than Earth-based reactors. As an early-stage deep-tech hardware company, Zephyr Fusion currently publishes no public API, developer platform, SDK, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures its identity in the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 confirmed no API surface exists (no api./docs./developer. hosts resolve; no /developers, /docs, or /.well-known discovery surface is published).

providers.name: Zumutor
providers.description: Zumutor is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Aizenglobal
providers.description: Aizenglobal is a fintech company based in Asia that leverages artificial intelligence to provide innovative digital banking, credit financing, and ESG‑focused financial services. Their platform offers AI‑driven credit assessment, multi‑modeling tools, and embedded banking solutions for enterprises and consumers, aiming to drive sustainable finance and data‑centric innovation across the region.

providers.name: Alphion
providers.description: Alphion Corporation is a broadband access equipment manufacturer that develops fiber-optic and wireless networking solutions for network operators, enterprises, and community networks. Founded in 2000 and based in Princeton Junction, New Jersey, the company builds GPON-based fiber-to-the-x (FTTx/FTTH) access systems, optical network terminals (AONT/ONT), and secure GigaWi-Fi broadband access products that deliver voice, data, video, and wireless services over passive optical networks. Alphion is a photonics and telecommunications hardware provider; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It does not currently publish a developer portal, public API, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Ambersolutionsinc
providers.description: Amber Solutions provides tailored cybersecurity services, including agile pentesting, social engineering simulations, technical audits, infrastructure analysis, and DoS/DDoS protection. The company emphasizes personalized, agile approaches to protect data and digital assets, targeting enterprises seeking flexible security solutions.

providers.name: Arcot Systems
providers.description: Arcot Systems is a payment security and advanced authentication company founded in 1997 that co-invented the 3-D Secure protocol with Visa. Its TransFort and ArcotID products delivered card-not-present fraud prevention, risk-based authentication, and cardholder authentication for online card payments. Accel was an early venture investor. CA Technologies acquired Arcot in 2010 in a $200 million all-cash transaction, and the technology now ships as the "Arcot by Broadcom" payment security and fraud prevention product line at arcot.broadcom.com. It is no longer an independent company and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Asula
providers.description: Asula is a Bitcoin company building the next generation of financial products at the intersection of bitcoin, blockchain infrastructure, and finance. The company is developing a mobile app that lets people buy, sell, and borrow against their Bitcoin, spanning a mobile wallet with seamless onboarding, cross-chain swaps, and a lending protocol. Asula has raised roughly $6.7M from Electric Capital, Framework Ventures, and Figment Capital, and ships two products, Bedlam and Dawn. As of July 2026 Asula publishes a minimal landing page and careers portal only, with no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Babelflex
providers.description: Babelflex (建木 BABELFLEX) is a Chinese‑based physical AI robotics company that builds flexible sensor hardware, data acquisition devices and domain‑specific AI models to create digital twins of real‑world environments. Their solutions target logistics, manufacturing, aerospace and energy sectors, offering hardware‑as‑a‑service platforms for real‑time monitoring, predictive maintenance and adaptive control.

providers.name: C14
providers.description: C14 is a fintech company operating at c14.money that provides fiat-to-crypto on-ramp and payment infrastructure, letting applications and platforms embed a compliant flow for users to buy digital assets with cards and other payment methods. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. This enrichment pass could not reach C14's developer surface (the public hosts reset TLS connections to automated clients), so no OpenAPI, docs, or SDK artifacts could be harvested this round; the profile carries confirmed domain-security signals probed from DNS and remains a lead awaiting a reachable developer surface.

providers.name: Caper
providers.description: Caper (caper.ai) is a New York-founded computer-vision company that builds AI-powered smart shopping carts and cashierless checkout technology for grocery and retail. Its Caper Cart uses a set of onboard cameras and deep-learning object recognition, running on NVIDIA Jetson edge AI, to auto-detect items as shoppers add them and let customers skip the checkout line. Founded in 2016 (Y Combinator) by Lindon Gao and team, Caper was acquired by Instacart in 2021 for roughly $350M and now operates as part of the Instacart Enterprise Platform (Connected Stores), deployed with retailers including ALDI and Coles. Caper ships retail hardware and an internal edge/vision platform; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Community Broadcasters
providers.description: Community Broadcasters is a U.S.-based radio broadcasting group that owns and operates over 100 radio stations across multiple markets. Founded in 2006, the company combines traditional broadcasting with an in‑house full‑service advertising agency, MITTCOM, to offer omnichannel marketing solutions. Their portfolio includes stations in New York, South Carolina, and other regions, focusing on local community engagement and brand partnerships.

providers.name: Concerto
providers.description: Concerto is a consumer fintech in the credit-card space, surfaced as a Matrix Partners portfolio company and tracked in the API Evangelist network. It operates a co-branded / consumer card program: cardholders are served through an account portal at app.concertocard.com that redirects to a Servicing Solutions cardholder-servicing platform (cardservices.servicingsolutions.com). The concertocard.com apex is used for corporate email (Microsoft 365) and domain verification (Atlassian, Facebook, GlobalSign) but does not currently serve a public marketing site, and an enrichment probe of July 2026 found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or other machine API surface. This profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: CrowdRise
providers.description: CrowdRise was an online fundraising platform for charities, nonprofits, and personal causes, founded around 2010 by Edward Norton and Robert Wolfe. It let individuals, event participants, and organizations create fundraising pages, run peer-to-peer campaigns, and collect donations for good. CrowdRise was acquired by GoFundMe in 2017 and subsequently merged into the GoFundMe platform; the crowdrise.com domain now 301-redirects to gofundme.com/c/crowdrise. This profile originated as a Union Square Ventures portfolio lead; no independent developer portal, documented API, SDKs, or discovery surface remains, so the record is retained for provenance only.

providers.name: Cureverse
providers.description: Cureverse (큐어버스) is a Korean biotechnology and research organization focused on developing innovative solutions in the fields of neuroscience, drug discovery, and clinical pipelines. The website offers sections such as About Us, R&D, Core Technologies, Research Areas, Pipeline, Investor Relations, News, Articles, Videos, Careers, and Contact. It provides information on collaborations, funded projects, and publications, reflecting a broad engagement with academic and industry partners.

providers.name: Deserve
providers.description: Deserve was a mobile-first, cloud-native credit card platform and issuer processor that let regional banks, credit unions, and B2B companies launch and embed consumer, small-business, and commercial co-branded credit and charge cards via APIs and SDKs, with configurable modules for origination, underwriting, rewards, credit policy, and fraud. Founded as SelfScore and backed by Accel, Goldman Sachs, Mastercard, and Visa, the company was acquired by Intuit in April 2025, which took its core technology assets and select team members. As of 2026 the public deserve.com site serves only a "Launching Soon" placeholder and Deserve publishes no live developer portal, API reference, or documentation. This profile captures the residual public surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dora
providers.description: Dora (Hola Dora) is a Colombian proptech and fintech startup, founded in 2023 and headquartered in Bogota, that acts as a rental guarantee for the residential real-estate market. It underwrites tenants in roughly five minutes over WhatsApp with no guarantor or co-signer, generates a digitally signed lease, and then guarantees the rent to landlords and property managers by paying the monthly amount on a fixed day whether or not the tenant has paid. Its InvestigaDora, ContrataDora and GarantizaDora flows cover tenant screening, electronic contracting, and guaranteed collection, reconciliation and payout for real-estate operators.

providers.name: Earn
providers.description: Earn.com (formerly 21 Inc / 21.co) was a cryptocurrency startup that let people earn Bitcoin by replying to paid messages and completing microtasks, effectively a paid-email and paid-task marketplace settled in crypto. Founded by Balaji Srinivasan and backed by DCVC among others, the company was acquired by Coinbase in April 2018 (Coinbase, ticker COIN) and folded into the Coinbase Earn product. The independent earn.com property no longer operates a standalone product or developer surface: earn.com now issues a 301 redirect to coinbase.com/earn, and earlier hosts such as 21.co and api.earn.com no longer resolve. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record; there is no independent, first-party API, developer portal, or OpenAPI to enrich.

providers.name: Education Management Corporation
providers.description: Education Management Corporation was one of the largest providers of post-secondary education in North America, operating The Art Institutes, Argosy University, Brown Mackie College, and South University.

providers.name: Energysquare
providers.description: Energysquare is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of partech and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: Industrial, Energy & IoT. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Eversource Energy
providers.description: Eversource Energy is the largest energy delivery company in New England, providing electric, natural gas, and water service to millions of customers in Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire.

providers.name: FirstEnergy
providers.description: FirstEnergy is one of the largest investor-owned electric systems in the United States, with utilities serving customers in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, West Virginia, Maryland, and New York. FirstEnergy does not publish a public developer portal or open API catalog. Customer energy data is shared with authorized Curtailment Service Providers and Conservation Service Providers under its Third-Party Data Access program in Pennsylvania, and bulk utility data is exchanged with state regulators and grid operators through Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) and other industry-standard interfaces.

providers.name: Flex
providers.description: Flex is a consumer financial technology company that lets renters pay their monthly rent in smaller installments spread across the month, instead of a single lump sum on the due date, so payments better fit each person's pay schedule and cash flow. The company pays the landlord or property manager in full on the due date and collects from the renter over the month, positioning itself as a flexible-payments layer on top of the largest recurring expense most households carry. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York City, Flex operates a consumer mobile app and partners with property-management platforms; it is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and surfaced in the 500 Global portfolio. Flex publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or discovery surface today - this profile is a network lead.

providers.name: Fortu
providers.description: Fortu (Fortu Wealth Ltd) is a London-based fintech, founded in 2019, offering digital private banking for high-net-worth individuals and their businesses, including borderless multi-currency accounts, payments, and a curated selection of investment opportunities across fintech and real-estate-driven debt strategies. Fortu also operates a business-to-business Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that lets private banks, wealth managers, and multi-family offices roll out their own branded investment and payments products, with automated payment processing and an API-driven compliance-monitoring tool. Co-founded by co-CEOs Firdavs Shakhidi and Azmat Sultanov, the company was selected for the 500 Global startup accelerator and raised an oversubscribed crowdfunding round (~GBP 500k) on Seedrs. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Fortu does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI, and its primary web deployment was offline (HTTP 402, disabled deployment) at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Frazer Consultants
providers.description: Frazer Consultants is a funeral-home technology company providing all-in-one death-care software - responsive funeral home websites, the FrazerGO funeral home management system, Tribute Pay payments, the Tribute Store (flowers, gifts, trees), and the Tribute Center (tribute videos, personalized stationery, and live or delayed webcasting). Frazer is now part of Tribute Technology, and its products connect into the Tribute Technology full-stack platform. Frazer markets an "open-source API" that lets its websites integrate with third-party data management, call forwarding, and webcasting software, and Tribute Technology connects Premier Partners to its Platform Services through proprietary APIs. However, as of this writing there is NO public developer portal, no published API reference, and no self-serve OpenAPI - API/integration access is partner-gated and arranged directly with Frazer / Tribute Technology. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the access model rather than a documented public API.

providers.name: Gas POS
providers.description: Gas Pos is a North Little Rock, Arkansas technology company (founded 2015) that builds cloud-based point-of-sale systems and EMV-certified fuel dispensers for gas stations and truck stops across the United States. Delivered as equipment-as-a-service with no upfront hardware cost, the platform pairs touchscreen POS terminals, barcode scanners, and back-office inventory and pricing tools with PCI-compliant, EMV-certified payment processing at both the register and the pump. It accepts major fleet cards including Comdata, Comchek, EFS, T-Chek, Voyager, and Fleetone, and lets operators manage item pricing and inventory remotely from a phone. Backed by 500 Global and Pioneer Fund. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface has been located to date.

providers.name: Genworth Financial
providers.description: Genworth Financial is a Fortune 500 insurance holding company providing long-term care insurance, life insurance, annuities, and mortgage insurance products primarily in the United States.

providers.name: Green Plains
providers.description: Green Plains is a vertically integrated ethanol producer that operates ethanol plants, grain handling and storage facilities, and a cattle-feeding operation. No public APIs are documented.

providers.name: Groupalia
providers.description: Groupalia was a Spanish group-buying / daily-deals company (a Groupon-style local commerce marketplace) founded in 2010 and backed by investors including Insight Partners, operating across Spain, Italy and parts of Latin America before consolidating in the group-buying downturn. The brand's only active surface today is the Italian domain groupalia.it, a gift-card storefront whose checkout is operated by EPIPOLI S.p.A. (mygiftcard.it); the original www.groupalia.com domain no longer resolves. No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or agent-facing surface is published, so this profile remains a consumer-company identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Integrys Energy Group
providers.description: Integrys Energy Group was a holding company with regulated natural gas and electric utility operations and a non-regulated retail energy business before being acquired by Wisconsin Energy Corporation in 2015 to form WEC Energy Group. There is no public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: ITT
providers.description: ITT Inc. is a diversified leading manufacturer of highly engineered critical components and customized technology solutions for the transportation, industrial, and oil and gas markets.

providers.name: Kezaihui
providers.description: Kezaihui (再惠 / Zaihuihui (Shanghai) Network Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Shanghai-based Chinese SaaS platform for local-life-service commerce, providing offline merchants — primarily mid-tier restaurants plus entertainment, beauty, and hospitality businesses — with one-stop store-opening and digital-operations tooling. Founded around 2012, the company offers private-domain member and community management, trading-platform shop diagnostics and automated strategy recommendations, content-creator (influencer) marketing, multi-channel precision ad delivery, and the Hui Shenghuo (惠生活) rights-aggregation platform, helping merchants operate across Meituan, Douyin, Xiaohongshu, and Taobao. It reports serving hundreds of thousands of merchants across dozens of Chinese cities with more than 1,000 employees. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer program or API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Konfio
providers.description: Konfio is a leading Mexican fintech serving small and medium businesses (SMBs) with an all-in-one platform: working-capital and term loans (Konfio Creditos), a business credit card (Konfio Tarjeta), payment terminals and acceptance (Konfio Pagos / Sirvis), and SMB management tools. Underwriting is powered by a proprietary algorithm that combines alternative data and ML to score creditworthiness in minutes. Konfio's product surface is overwhelmingly direct-to-SMB and the company does not publish a self-service public developer portal. Partner integrations (e.g. PayPal Working Capital, Goldman Sachs / Gramercy capital facilities, marketplace lending) are negotiated bilaterally.

providers.name: LightCyber
providers.description: LightCyber was an Israeli-American cybersecurity company that pioneered a category it called Behavioral Attack Detection — using behavior-based profiling of network traffic and endpoint activity, rather than malware signatures or technical artifacts, to detect attackers already operating inside an enterprise network. Its LightCyber Magna platform shipped as a set of appliances and services (Magna Detector, Magna Probe, Magna Master, Magna Pathfinder, and the Magna Cloud Expert System) and was positioned for user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), network traffic analysis, security visibility, and PCI compliance. The company was backed by Battery Ventures, Glilot Capital Partners, Amplify Partners, and angel investor Shlomo Kramer. Palo Alto Networks announced the completed acquisition of LightCyber for $105 million in cash on February 28, 2017, and engineered its automated behavioral analytics into the Palo Alto Networks security platform. The independent LightCyber brand, product line, and web presence no longer exist; the lightcyber.com domain has since lapsed from Palo Alto Networks' control and now resolves to an unrelated third-party site. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company lead and carries no live API artifacts.

providers.name: Marvin
providers.description: Marvin (Marvin Tecnologia Ltda., CNPJ 41.240.161/0001-30) is a São Paulo, Brazil based B2B fintech and tech-native collateral agent that transforms credit-card and duplicata receivables into registered financial guarantees. Born out of Brazilian Central Bank Resolution 264 — which legalized the negotiation of credit-card receivables as financial assets — Marvin operates a "registration-as-a-service" platform that lets retailers, banks and suppliers register, manage and settle receivables-backed collateral, unlocking working capital for merchants. The company is backed by a US$15M Series A led by Canaan Partners (with Canary and Maúa Capital) and works with partners including B3, C6 Bank, Casas Bahia, Electrolux, Pernambucanas and AVLA. Marvin runs a private backend (app.marvin.com.br) for its customers; it does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Medical Mutual of Ohio
providers.description: Medical Mutual of Ohio is the oldest and one of the largest health insurance companies based in Ohio, providing health insurance plans to individuals, families, and employer groups. No public developer portal or API specifications are currently documented; CMS-mandated Patient Access and Provider Directory FHIR endpoints, where they exist, are typically reached via member or provider account workflows rather than an open developer site.

providers.name: Mouser Electronics
providers.description: Mouser Electronics is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: tag-qc) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: National Fuel Gas Company
providers.description: National Fuel Gas Company is a diversified energy company engaged in natural gas distribution, gas pipeline and storage, gas exploration and production, and energy marketing across the northeastern United States. National Fuel Gas does not currently publish a documented public REST API or developer portal; customer information and operational disclosures are made available through its corporate website, investor relations channels, and FERC regulatory filings.

providers.name: Noon
providers.description: Noon is a Dubai-headquartered e-commerce marketplace and digital ecosystem launched in 2017 as a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Emirati businessman Mohamed Alabbar. Frequently described as the Amazon of the MENA region, Noon operates as the leading online shopping destination across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Egypt, offering electronics, mobiles, fashion, beauty, home, appliances, baby, and grocery categories through a hybrid first-party and third-party seller marketplace. Beyond the core marketplace, Noon has expanded into a lifestyle super-app spanning Noon Food (quick-service restaurant delivery competing with Talabat and Deliveroo), Noon Daily (next-day grocery delivery), Noon Minutes (15-minute instant grocery and essentials delivery), Noon Pay and the Noon mobile wallet (QR payments, bill pay, and a co-branded credit card), Noon VIP (loyalty/subscription), NowNow (on-demand delivery in KSA), and SIVVI (acquired regional fashion brand). Noon operates its own last-mile logistics arm and warehouses across the region, and provides a Fulfilled by Partner Integration (FBPI) program with commercial APIs that allow third-party sellers and channel-integration partners (ChannelEngine, Unicommerce, Vinculum, Ecom Energize and others) to programmatically publish catalog, sync inventory, and manage shipments. These APIs are gated to onboarded sellers and certified integrators inside the noon.partners environment — there is no general public developer portal, no published OpenAPI specification, and no Noon-maintained SDKs, CLIs, or open-source repositories.

providers.name: Office Depot
providers.description: Office Depot is a leading provider of business products and services delivering workplace solutions through retail stores, e-commerce sites, and a dedicated business-to-business sales organization.

providers.name: Omnidock
providers.description: Omnidock is a merchant-of-record platform that streamlines multi-marketplace expansion for online sellers. The service lets merchants launch and sell products across multiple online marketplaces using pre-vetted seller accounts, while Omnidock acts as the merchant of record and handles the underlying transaction processing, payments, and compliance. The stated goal is to remove the operational complexity of expanding onto many marketplaces at once and make multi-marketplace selling effortless. Omnidock was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes only a marketing landing page and exposes no public API, developer documentation, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: ONEOK
providers.description: ONEOK is a Fortune 500 energy company providing midstream services to natural gas and natural gas liquids producers, processors, and customers. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with ONEOK.

providers.name: Parallax
providers.description: Parallax is a stablecoin-powered cross-border and B2B payments platform founded by Mika Reyes (CEO) and Alex Kuang (CTO) to remove the friction, delays, and opaque fees from international money movement across the roughly $21 trillion cross-border payments market. Serving freelancers, remote workers, and businesses in 150+ countries, Parallax let recipients get paid near-instantly in USDC, hold balances in a self-custodied wallet, and withdraw to local currency, while its first B2B product streamlined web3 companies' payables and receivables from vendor onboarding and approvals through payout and accounting. The company raised a $4.5M seed round backed by General Catalyst, Dragonfly, Circle, and gumi Cryptos Capital. Parallax was acquired by crypto wallet company Phantom, and the standalone Parallax app wound down on September 18, 2025.

providers.name: Paytm Payments Bank
providers.description: Paytm Payments Bank Limited is an Indian payments bank headquartered in Noida, offering digital savings and current accounts, the Paytm Wallet, FASTag, debit cards, UPI and other retail banking services to consumers and merchants. It operates as a distinct entity from Paytm's merchant payment-gateway developer platform (One97 Communications), and does not publish its own public developer API surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Pravica
providers.description: Pravica is a financial-technology company providing institutional-grade infrastructure for programmable money. It enables banks, fintechs, and enterprises to launch secure, compliant digital payment systems spanning online and offline payments, remittances, and global settlement. The Pravica suite includes consumer-facing products such as Walletify and s3.money. Backed by 500 Global, Pravica was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. As of this enrichment pass the public site is marketing-only with no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface found, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal but no API artifacts.

providers.name: Prompto
providers.description: Prompto is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: g2-catalog) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Puget Energy
providers.description: Puget Energy is the parent company of Puget Sound Energy (PSE), a regulated electric and natural gas utility serving customers across Washington state. Headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, the company provides electricity and natural gas service, energy efficiency programs, outage management, and customer billing services. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Qubit Smart Tickets
providers.description: Qubit Smart Tickets (Boletos Qubit) is a Colombian event-ticketing platform operating at boletosqubit.co, a Spanish-language consumer web application for buying and validating tickets to concerts, sports, and live events, with local payment methods including Nequi. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no publicly documented API, developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, SDKs, changelog, or /.well-known discovery endpoints; the only server-side surface reachable is an internal PHP backend not intended for public integration, so no API artifacts were generated.

providers.name: Sanad Cash
providers.description: Sanad Cash was a Saudi Arabia-based fintech startup that operated an on-demand payment platform, giving employees early access to earned wages and providing employers with tools to manage on-demand pay. The company raised a $1.6M seed round in January 2022 with participation from Impact46 and was backed by 500 Global. Sanad Cash was acquired by HyperPay in July 2023, and the Sanad Cash business was subsequently acquired by Qashio in October 2025. The independent sanadcash.com property is no longer reachable (no live HTTPS service), so this profile documents the company's identity and residual domain footprint rather than a live developer/API surface.

providers.name: Scrum
providers.description: Scrum is an agile project management framework that organizes work into fixed-length iterations called sprints, typically lasting two to four weeks. It defines clear roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Developers) and ceremonies (sprint planning, daily standups, retrospectives) to enable teams to deliver value incrementally and continuously improve.

providers.name: Secure Software Development Life Cycle
providers.description: A framework that integrates security practices and considerations into every phase of the software development process, from initial design through deployment and maintenance, to minimize vulnerabilities and ensure secure applications. It is used across a range of industries and technical contexts to improve efficiency and outcomes.

providers.name: Secure-By-Default
providers.description: A security design principle where systems and software are configured with the most secure settings from the initial deployment, requiring users to explicitly opt-in to less secure options rather than having to manually enable security features. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture.

providers.name: SNCF
providers.description: SNCF is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: travel) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Stoke Talent
providers.description: Stoke Talent is a Freelance Management System (FMS) that lets enterprises source, onboard, manage, and pay external freelancers and contractors in one place while handling worker classification, contracts, tax, legal, and compliance. Founded in Israel and backed by Battery Ventures, Stoke was acquired by Fiverr in November 2021 for roughly $95M and subsequently rebranded as Fiverr Enterprise, now offered under the Fiverr Pro / Fiverr Enterprise product line. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or webhook documentation; this profile is maintained for network completeness.

providers.name: Tamatem
providers.description: Tamatem is a Jordan-based mobile games publisher and platform focused on the Arabic-speaking MENA market. It localizes and publishes mobile games for Arab gamers and operates Tamatem Plus (tamatemplus.com), a consumer store for game vouchers, in-game items, and top-ups with a range of local payment options. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Tamatem publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface — it is a consumer-facing gaming and digital-goods business, so this profile carries identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Texaco
providers.description: An American petroleum brand owned by Chevron marketing fuels, lubricants, and petrochemical products. Operates a network of service stations across the United States and internationally with a long history in the oil industry.

providers.name: Utopia Labs
providers.description: Utopia Labs was a stablecoin payments and finance-operations platform for crypto-native teams and DAOs, covering payments, payroll, invoicing, and approval workflows, backed by Paradigm. Coinbase acquired Utopia Labs Corp. on November 13, 2024, and the team joined Base to build onchain payments into Coinbase Wallet. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API surface — utopialabs.com returns 404 and its former docs, api, and app subdomains no longer resolve.

providers.name: WayPay
providers.description: WayPay was a cloud-based B2B payments and accounts-payable-automation fintech headquartered in Burlington, Ontario, Canada. Its platform let businesses pay any supplier by any method (EFT, cheque, credit card, wire) from a single dashboard, reconciling against accounting and ERP software to automate the accounts-payable workflow. Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) announced its acquisition of WayPay in July 2019, after which the independent brand was retired. As of this enrichment pass the domain waypay.ca resolves via DNS (behind Akamai, enterprise mail) but serves no public site (HTTP 503), and there is no reachable public developer portal, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: 1 Mainstream
providers.description: 1 Mainstream was a cloud-based OTT (over-the-top) video streaming platform for content owners and distributors, enabling operators to launch live and on-demand video services across connected devices including iOS, Android, Roku, Amazon Fire TV, Chromecast, game consoles, smart TVs, and Apple TV, with DRM (Widevine, PlayReady), multi-CDN control, subscriber management, entitlements, and a CMS-based analytics engine. Backed by Sky and DCM Ventures, the company was acquired by Cisco in October 2015 and folded into Cisco's Infinite Video suite of cloud-powered video entertainment solutions. The standalone 1mainstream.com domain no longer resolves; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: 1-Automotive
providers.description: 1-Automotive is a catalog entry for which no operating company, developer program, or live web presence could be verified. The only host this profile ever recorded, www.1-automotive.com, is not a registered domain — Verisign WHOIS returns "No match for domain 1-AUTOMOTIVE.COM" and DNS answers NXDOMAIN for both the apex and the www label (probed 2026-08-29) — so the Website pointer that stood here asserted a page that has never existed and has been removed. Public web search returns no organization trading under this exact name; the nearest real match, and the likely origin of this slug, is Group 1 Automotive (NYSE: GPI), the Fortune 500 automotive retailer that API Evangelist profiles separately under the group-1-automotive slug, where its live llms.txt vehicle-inventory surface is already captured. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP server, A2A agent card, SDK, package or developer portal exists for this entry, and none has been authored on its behalf.

providers.name: 10 Percent
providers.description: 10 Percent is a two-sided agricultural marketplace with embedded financial services, a Speedinvest portfolio company (invested ~2020) operating in the agri-fintech and marketplaces space. Public sources describe it combining agricultural supply-chain e-commerce, grain procurement, and business-intelligence services with embedded financing such as factoring and credit offered inside transactions to help agricultural partners manage cash flow and access capital. It was surfaced as a Speedinvest portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment searched the public web and found no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested. This profile remains an identity-only lead pending a discoverable API.

providers.name: 18F
providers.description: Unofficial US Federal Government API Development

providers.name: 3D Cell Bioprinting Consortium
providers.description: The 3D Cell Bioprinting Consortium (traded on the EquityZen secondary marketplace under the symbol TDCC) is an alliance of laboratory-instrument and biomaterials companies formed in 2016 and publicly launched in February 2017, headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts. It describes itself as "a group of companies focused on offering the complete solution for tissue engineering" — coordinating bioprinter hardware, bioinks and hydrogels, cell lines and culture reagents into a single workflow for pre-clinical drug discovery, regenerative medicine and diagnostics. It was founded by Sid Braginsky, CEO and Chairman of Digilab Corp., and its named members include Digilab, Inc. (maker of the CellJet cell printer, represented by President and COO John Moore) and 3-D Matrix, Inc. (self-assembling peptide hydrogels, represented by Managing Director Marc Rioult). The consortium is a coordinating body for physical laboratory products, not a software vendor: it publishes no first-party website, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API specification, and no domain matching its name resolves in DNS. This profile is an independent third-party record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Accelerator Sciences
providers.description: Accelerator Sciences is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Accion Systems
providers.description: Accion Systems is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of shasta-ventures, slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: aerospace. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Acompli
providers.description: Acompli was a mobile email application for iOS and Android, first released in April 2014, that unified email, calendar, contacts, and file management across Microsoft Exchange, Office 365, Google Apps, Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo, and Outlook.com/Hotmail accounts. The San Francisco startup was backed by Redpoint Ventures and acquired by Microsoft on December 1, 2014 for a reported $200M+, after which its 21-person team and product were rebranded as Microsoft Outlook for iOS and Android. Acompli no longer operates as an independent company and never published a public developer API; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical, acquired-company lead.

providers.name: acorn systems
providers.description: Acorn is a Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing (TD-ABC) and profitability-management platform for multi-dimensional cost-to-serve analysis, precisely attributing direct and indirect costs against products, customers, regions, business units and facilities. It offers what-if scenario modeling, shared-services optimization, custom business-process modeling, and OLAP/analytics for pricing, supplier negotiation and supply-chain decisions. Originally Acorn Systems, the product is now owned and operated by IgniteTech (an ESW Capital enterprise-software company); the acornsys.com domain 301-redirects into IgniteTech's software library. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification is published for the product.

providers.name: Acre Homes
providers.description: Acre Homes is a North Carolina-based homeownership company whose mission is to "create the best way to experience homeownership." Acre enables individuals to buy quality homes in desirable neighborhoods while sharing in ownership appreciation and reducing costs, notably without requiring traditional debt financing. Positioned in the wealth and asset management corner of fintech and proptech, the company reframes owning a home as a less financially burdensome decision than the conventional mortgage path, letting residents build equity through a shared-appreciation model rather than a conventional debt-financed purchase. Acre Homes is an early-stage venture-backed company and a portfolio company of Anthemis Group. It operates a consumer-facing homeownership offering and does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or developer documentation; this profile captures verified company identity and public links.

providers.name: Actuate
providers.description: Actuate Corporation was an enterprise business intelligence and reporting software company founded in 1993 and backed by Accel (partner Arthur Patterson).
