It was the original developer of BIRT (Business Intelligence and Reporting Tools), building a developer community measured in millions of downloads, and traded on NASDAQ under the ticker BIRT. OpenText acquired Actuate in January 2015 and folded its analytics and reporting technology into OpenText Analytics Cloud. The standalone actuate.com site is no longer an active product presence (all paths return HTTP 404) and the company publishes no independent, live API or developer portal today. A separately named company at actuate.ai (AI video/threat detection) is unrelated to this Accel-portfolio entity and likewise exposes no public API.

providers.name: Adc
providers.description: Adc is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: unknown. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Addiction Campuses of America
providers.description: Addiction Campuses of America (EquityZen ticker ACOA) was founded in 2014 in Brentwood, Tennessee and owned, operated and managed residential behavioral-healthcare campuses across the United States, treating substance use disorder and co-occurring mental health conditions through detox, residential, partial-hospitalization and outpatient programs, several of them holding the Joint Commission Gold Seal of Approval. Summit Partners invested in the company in 2018, and on 2020-08-01 it renamed itself Vertava Health. The successor host vertavahealth.com is still a live WordPress installation but now 301-redirects its homepage to Connections Wellness Group, an unrelated behavioral-health provider, and the original addictioncampuses.com answers every request with a SiteGround proof-of-work bot interstitial. This is a clinical services operator, not a software vendor: a full contract-discovery pass across all three hosts, the package registries, GitHub and 4,000 archived URLs found no developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Adjoint
providers.description: Adjoint Inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts fintech (founded 2016) that built distributed-ledger and smart-contract software for corporate treasury and insurance. Its flagship platform, Uplink, let financial firms onboard assets onto a permissioned ledger, manage balances, and author self-executing agreements in Adjoint's Financial Core Language (FCL), with SDKs to bridge to traditional systems. The company raised roughly $10.4M and competed with Kyriba, Trovata, and Modern Treasury. As of this enrichment pass the company appears dormant: its adjoint.io domain now resolves to a parked/expired Namecheap page, its GitHub organization returns 404, and no first-party client SDKs are published to public registries. This profile is a VC-portfolio enrichment stub; see the data-quality note below regarding the originally-attached website.

providers.name: Adphorus
providers.description: Adphorus was an Istanbul- and Berlin-based travel marketing-science company and an official Facebook and Instagram Marketing Partner (certified since 2014) that specialized in automated, scalable Dynamic Ads for Travel, helping brands such as Expedia, Trivago, and Kayak scale full-funnel performance on Facebook and Instagram. The company was acquired by Sojern in November 2017 and subsequently absorbed; it operates no independent public website or developer API today, so this network profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record rather than an active API provider. The enrichment pipeline found no live domain, developer portal, or specification to harvest.

providers.name: Aelita Software
providers.description: Aelita Software Corporation was an enterprise systems-management software company founded in 1998 by Ratmir Timashev (who later co-founded Veeam Software). Headquartered in the Columbus, Ohio area (Dublin/Powell, OH), Aelita built Windows infrastructure management tooling for Microsoft Active Directory and Microsoft Exchange environments — including migration, directory management, auditing, reporting, security analysis, systems monitoring, and disaster recovery. Marquee products included Migration Manager for Active Directory, Migration Manager for Exchange, Secure Copy, Enterprise Reporter, Recovery Manager for Active Directory, ActiveRoles Server, and InTrust. Insight Partners was an early investor. Aelita was acquired by Quest Software in March 2004 for approximately $115 million and its technology was folded into Quest's Windows Management line (much of which is now part of One Identity). The company has had no independent operation since 2004; it exposed no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface, and there is no live web presence today (the aelita.com domain is parked/for sale). This profile is retained as a historical Insight Partners portfolio record — there is no active developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: afujingyou
providers.description: afujingyou (阿芙 / AFU) is a Chinese consumer essential-oil, aromatherapy and skincare brand founded in 2006, backed by Qiming Venture Partners (Series C, 2017). It sells single and blended essential oils, base/carrier oils, masks, emulsions and face creams through retail and e-commerce channels (Tmall/JD/Weibo storefronts). Enrichment finding (2026-07-17): this is a consumer packaged-goods brand, not an API provider — no public developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or other API artifacts exist to harvest, and the catalog domain afujingyou.net.cn does not resolve (NXDOMAIN). Retained as an identity-only record; no API artifacts are applicable.

providers.name: Agile Software
providers.description: Agile Software Corporation was an American product lifecycle management (PLM) software company founded in 1995 and headquartered in San Jose, California. Backed by Accel, it IPO'd on the NASDAQ in 1999 and built enterprise software that helped manufacturers manage product records, bills of materials, engineering change orders, quality, compliance, and supply-chain data across a product's development and production lifecycle. Oracle Corporation acquired Agile Software in July 2007 for approximately US$495 million; its products were rebranded as Oracle Agile PLM and folded into Oracle's supply-chain and applications suite. The company no longer operates independently: agilesoft.com now redirects to Oracle, and the only surviving developer surface is the legacy Oracle Agile PLM SDK (a Java API set) hosted on docs.oracle.com. This profile is retained as an acquired/historical record; there is no live, independent public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Ai-Blockchain
providers.description: Ai-Blockchain (also styled AI BlockChain, AIBC) is a Hoboken, New Jersey enterprise blockchain and artificial-intelligence software company founded in 2014 by Drew Hingorani and Stephen Reed. It builds a proprietary, patented private distributed ledger — US Patent 10,579,974, "Systems, methods, and program products for a distributed digital asset network with rapid transaction settlements" — that the company describes as gas-free, energy efficient and immutable, with artificial-intelligence agents managing the chain itself. Its marketed service lines are private blockchain with instant settlement, smart payment and transaction platforms, secure streaming and content distribution / digital rights management, AI-powered virtual assistants and customer-service chatbots, cloud cost optimization, a LIMS healthcare product, and custom AI + blockchain application development. It sells enterprise engagements and consulting rather than a self-serve developer product: as of September 2026 the company publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Aikito
providers.description: Aikito is a New York-based company (founded 2021) operating a commercial real-estate platform that helps business owners design, build, finance, and manage their commercial spaces. It pairs a suite of AI-driven tools with non-dilutive financing so tenants can build out a space and pay over time, covering the project lifecycle from lease execution through move-in. Aikito was founded by Amol Sarva and its investors include Bloomberg Beta, Gaingels, Calm Ventures, FJ Labs, and Northzone. As of this profile Aikito publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface, so it remains a company/identity record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

providers.name: AirWatch
providers.description: AirWatch was an enterprise mobility management (EMM) and mobile device management (MDM) company founded in 2003 in Atlanta, Georgia and backed by Accel. It provided cloud-based device, application, content, and email management for enterprise mobile fleets. VMware acquired AirWatch in February 2014 for roughly USD 1.5 billion, folding it into the VMware Workspace ONE Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform, and the brand was fully retired. In 2024 VMware End-User Computing (including Workspace ONE) was divested to Omnissa. As an independent brand AirWatch no longer operates a developer portal or public API: airwatch.com now redirects to the Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM product page, and the historical AirWatch REST API lives on as the per-tenant Workspace ONE UEM REST API served from customer *.awmdm.com consoles. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Alibaba Local Services
providers.description: Alibaba Local Services (阿里巴巴本地生活) is Alibaba Group's on-demand local-life services business, formed in 2018 by integrating the Ele.me food-delivery platform with the Koubei local-services and restaurant-discovery platform. It operates on-demand food and grocery delivery, local merchant services, reviews and reservations, and last-mile logistics across China, and received a major financing round led by the SoftBank Vision Fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the network as a lead; no distinct public developer API surface has been confirmed for the holding entity under this name (its consumer platforms Ele.me and Koubei operate their own separate open platforms).

providers.name: All Day Kitchens
providers.description: All Day Kitchens is a San Francisco-based cloud-kitchen (ghost kitchen) infrastructure company that operates a network of delivery-optimized commissary kitchens, letting restaurant brands expand into new markets and fulfill online delivery orders without building out their own physical locations. Often positioned as a "Kitchen as a Service" platform, it pairs shared kitchen capacity with software and operations for order routing, food preparation, and last-mile delivery hand-off. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it publishes only a marketing landing page at www.alldaykitchens.com with no public developer portal, API, documentation, or event surface.

providers.name: All Def Digital
providers.description: All Def (formerly All Def Digital) is a YouTube-focused digital content studio founded by Russell Simmons that produces unscripted original programming for Gen Z, Millennial, and multicultural audiences across comedy, food, hip-hop, and culture. Its owned-and-operated channels have amassed 15M+ fans and more than 2 billion video views, and it produces branded content for partners including Sprite, Snickers, Hyundai, Lexus, and McDonald's. All Def is a portfolio company of a16z, surfaced in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: AllTaster
providers.description: AllTaster Limited (trading as Taster) is a UK-registered, digital-first food-brand creator that imagines and operates virtual and physical restaurant concepts in collaboration with chefs, creators, and franchise partners, distributed largely through third-party delivery apps and its own consumer mobile apps. Its brand portfolio includes Pepe Chicken, Out Fry, La Vie Dirty Burgers, Sheesh!, and others. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, developer portal, or technical documentation, so no API artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived; this profile captures verified company identity only.

providers.name: Alwans
providers.description: Alwans is a Saudi technology investment and startup-development company based in Al Khubar, Saudi Arabia, and launched in January 2010. The firm is focused on enriching local Arabic technical content and competing globally by investing in and building startup ideas and technology projects, with an emphasis on e-commerce, online marketing, mobile applications, and mobile games. Alwans is a small team (2-10 employees) and is itself backed by 500 Global; its portfolio includes companies such as Foodics and Fnjalah. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs -- this profile is an identity record within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: amberjack
providers.description: Amberjack is a direct-to-consumer men's footwear brand based in Brooklyn, New York, that designs and manufactures dress shoes engineered with athletic-inspired technology such as heat-activated arch support and dual-density outsoles for all-day comfort in hybrid work settings. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify storefront and is backed by Slow Ventures. Enrichment found no public developer or API surface (no docs portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, OAuth, or /.well-known endpoints); it remains catalogued as a consumer-brand company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: American Financial
providers.description: American Financial is a financial-services profile in the API Evangelist catalog for which no operating company could be resolved on 2026-09-02. The only host ever recorded for it, american-financial.com, is not run by a business: it is a CNAME to traff-https.hugedomains.com and redirects to a HugeDomains "this domain is for sale" listing, so there is no website, no developer program, no documentation and no machine-readable API artifact behind this name. The Fortune 500 insurance and annuities holding company American Financial Group, Inc. (NYSE: AFG, Great American Insurance Group) is a different company and is profiled separately in this catalog as american-financial-group, where its Great American Carrier Services APIs belong.

providers.name: aminoapps

providers.name: Amixr.io
providers.description: Amixr was an incident-response and on-call management startup that provided alerting, escalation, and on-call scheduling for engineering and DevOps teams, integrating with monitoring stacks such as Grafana and Prometheus. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Grafana Labs in December 2021 and its product was folded into Grafana OnCall (now part of Grafana IRM). The standalone amixr.io product and developer surface have been retired; the domain no longer serves an active website, developer portal, or API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record following enrichment.

providers.name: Antic

providers.name: Anxiatechnology
providers.description: Anxiatechnology is a Shenzhen‑based technology company specializing in facial‑recognition attendance and access‑control solutions. Their product line includes turnstile gates, face‑recognition time‑attendance systems, and integrated access‑control devices that combine facial, ID‑card, and temperature monitoring technologies. The firm emphasizes high‑precision AI‑driven recognition, CE and ISO9000 certifications, and cost‑effective manufacturing for enterprise security deployments across various sectors.

providers.name: Aoshitechnology
providers.description: Aoshitechnology is a stub entry in the API Evangelist catalog, originating from a secondary‑market harvest. No public website, documentation, or API endpoints have been identified for this entity. The record exists solely to enable future profiling should the company publish machine‑readable resources. All attempts to locate an official domain or developer portal resulted in access denials or unrelated sites, confirming the current lack of publicly available information.

providers.name: API Fortress
providers.description: API Fortress was an API testing and monitoring platform that let engineering teams author, run, and continuously monitor functional and integration tests against REST and SOAP APIs, in the cloud or via an on-premise Docker-based agent. It was acquired by Sauce Labs in January 2020 and its capabilities were folded into the Sauce Labs API Testing product. The standalone apifortress.com developer surface has since been retired; as of this enrichment pass the domain no longer resolves (parked Route53 nameservers, no A records), the apifortress GitHub organization returns 404, and there is no live first-party API, docs, SDK, or well-known surface remaining to enrich.

providers.name: Apigy
providers.description: Apigy, Inc. is the company behind Lockitron, an early keyless smart-lock startup that let people lock, unlock, and share access to their doors from a smartphone. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and known for a large 2012 crowdfunding campaign, Apigy built connected door-lock hardware and companion mobile apps before the Lockitron product line was wound down. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; its public website (lockitron.com) is currently unreachable and no active developer or API surface could be located.

providers.name: Appionics
providers.description: Appionics Holdings Limited is a Hong Kong mobile applications and games company that operated under the consumer brand name "Animoca". Co-founded by Yat Siu and David Kim, and emerging out of the Outblaze group, Appionics developed and published cross-platform games and apps for iOS and Android, claiming more than 150 titles and over 40 million downloads during 2011. In 2014 the company spun off part of its app portfolio, along with a set of licensed intellectual-property game rights, into Animoca Brands Corporation Limited (ASX AB1), which listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in January 2015 and later pivoted to blockchain gaming and NFTs. Appionics itself never published a developer program, and today has no live web or API surface of its own.

providers.name: Apsalar
providers.description: Apsalar was a mobile marketing analytics and attribution company (founded 2010, headquartered in San Francisco, backed by Battery Ventures and 500 Startups/500 Global) that provided a mobile measurement platform (MMP) for app install attribution, campaign analytics, and marketing data unification. In 2017 Apsalar merged into Singular (singular.net); the Apsalar brand and its developer/API surface were retired as part of that acquisition. The apsalar.com apex domain no longer resolves to a live site and www.apsalar.com now redirects to Singular, so there is no active first-party API, OpenAPI, or developer portal to enrich. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead pointing to its successor, Singular.

providers.name: Arcellx
providers.description: Arcellx is a biotechnology company focused on developing innovative cellular analysis platforms. The company aims to provide researchers with advanced tools for high‑throughput single‑cell profiling, enabling deeper insights into cellular heterogeneity and function. While detailed public information is limited, Arcellx positions itself within the life‑science technology sector, offering solutions that integrate hardware and software for comprehensive cellular data acquisition and analysis.

providers.name: astaro
providers.description: astaro is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: cybersecurity. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: ATI
providers.description: ATI Inc. is a specialty materials and components manufacturer that produces high-performance alloys, titanium products, nickel-based superalloys, and engineered components. The company primarily serves the aerospace, defense, energy, electronics, and medical industries. ATI focuses on direct B2B customer relationships and does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: AtmoSec
providers.description: AtmoSec was an Israel-based SaaS security startup founded in January 2021 that built a platform for securing hyperconnected SaaS ecosystems. Its technology discovered authorized and shadow SaaS applications, controlled risky SaaS-to-SaaS and third-party OAuth app communication, detected and disconnected malicious apps, remediated SaaS misconfigurations, and governed non-human identities (API keys, OAuth apps, service accounts, and tokens) via native IAM APIs. Founded by former Armis and Google executives and backed by Battery Ventures and Glilot Capital, AtmoSec was acquired by Check Point Software Technologies in September 2023 and folded into the Check Point Infinity / SASE platform for continuous SaaS posture management. It no longer operates as a standalone company and publishes no public developer API; atmosec.com now redirects into checkpoint.com.

providers.name: Atomic Canyon
providers.description: Atomic Canyon provides a platform focused on data consent and privacy management, enabling users to control data sharing preferences across web services. The site offers tools for consent preferences, basic operations, content personalization, and site optimization, ensuring compliance with privacy regulations and enhancing user trust. Through its services, Atomic Canyon aims to secure data access while delivering personalized experiences.

providers.name: Avencell
providers.description: Avencell develops next‑generation immunotherapies, focusing on powerful, targeted, and safe CAR‑T cell platforms. Their proprietary switchable CAR technology enables precise control of T‑cell activity, improving therapeutic windows and reducing side effects. Avencell aims to overcome limitations of current cell therapies to treat hard‑to‑treat cancers worldwide.

providers.name: Axiometrix Solutions
providers.description: Axiometrix Solutions is a global test and measurement company serving technology-intensive industries through three specialist brands - GRAS Sound & Vibration (acoustic and vibration sensors for challenging environments), imc Test & Measurement (modular data acquisition, signal conditioning, and shock/vibration solutions), and Audio Precision (audio and RF analyzers for quality validation). Its integrated portfolio of sensors, data acquisition systems, control software, analysis software, and test fixtures supports advanced research, R&D, and production/manufacturing test across aerospace, defense, automotive, consumer electronics, audiology and medical technology, communications, semiconductor, and environmental monitoring markets. Backed by Battery Ventures. No public web API or developer program has been identified for this provider.

providers.name: B2B-Center
providers.description: B2B-Center is one of Russia's largest electronic trading platforms (ETP) for business-to-business procurement, operating at b2b-center.ru. The platform hosts electronic tenders, auctions, and competitive sourcing procedures that connect corporate and commercial buyers with a broad network of suppliers across many industries. It provides tools for organizing purchases, publishing procurement notices, qualifying and managing suppliers, and running the full electronic bidding lifecycle. B2B-Center is backed by Insight Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company awaiting deeper enrichment.

providers.name: Babycare
providers.description: Babycare is a Chinese mother-and-baby (母婴) consumer brand offering a broad range of maternity and infant-care products, including diapers, wipes, strollers, baby carriers, feeding bottles, toys, and maternal care goods. It operates primarily as a direct-to-consumer brand, selling through major Chinese e-commerce marketplaces (Tmall, JD.com, Douyin) alongside its own channels and offline retail, and is one of the leading new-generation mother-baby brands in China. Babycare is backed by venture investor Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). This profile is a consumer-brand entry in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been identified for this provider.

providers.name: BAMA TEA
providers.description: BAMA TEA (八马茶业), a brand of Fujian Bama Tea Industry Co., Ltd., is a large-scale Chinese tea enterprise founded in 1997 and headquartered in Anxi County, Quanzhou, Fujian Province. It integrates tea plantation cultivation, production and processing, branded retail-chain distribution, and export, and is best known for Tieguanyin oolong. The company operates a nationwide network of branded retail stores across China and sells oolong, black, green, white, and dark teas. It is a publicly listed company and a portfolio investment of IDG Capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector lead: BAMA TEA publishes a consumer e-commerce website but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so the API-artifact enrichment recipes do not apply.

providers.name: Bass Associates
providers.description: Bass Associates is an early- and growth-stage venture capital firm historically based at 435 Tasso Street, Palo Alto, California, and appears on the Battery Ventures "list of all companies" as an exited entry. Public investor databases record roughly 32 investments and 10 exits alongside co-investors such as Accel Partners, Kleiner Perkins and CRV, with its last recorded investment (Teloquent, growth equity) in January 2002 and its last recorded exit in December 2003. The 2026 enrichment pass found no operating website, no developer portal, no documentation and no API surface of any kind: the firm appears dormant and is not an API provider. It was surfaced into the API Evangelist network by the VC-portfolio crawl as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead, but the underlying entity is itself an investor rather than an operating software company.

providers.name: Bbb3
providers.description: Bbb3 is a placeholder company identified during the API Evangelist harvest process from secondary-market sources. It currently exists as a stub entry within the network, awaiting comprehensive profiling and enrichment. No public-facing website, documentation, or API endpoints have been discovered for Bbb3 at this time, and further investigation is required to determine its actual digital presence and offerings.

providers.name: Before Brands
providers.description: Before Brands, Inc. was a Menlo Park, California science-based food and nutrition company founded on Stanford allergy research by Dr. Kari Nadeau, best known for SpoonfulOne — a consumer early-allergen-introduction product line that blended sixteen commonly allergenic proteins into daily servings for infants and toddlers. Nestle Health Science took a minority stake plus ex-US licensing rights in 2019 and later absorbed the business outright. It was a consumer packaged goods company, not a software company: it never operated a developer program, published no API, SDK or webhook surface, and its own domain is now controlled by Nestle and no longer serves a site.

providers.name: Beimeipharmaceutical
providers.description: Beimeipharmaceutical, also known as Shenzhen Beimei Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., is a Chinese biopharmaceutical company focused on the development, manufacturing, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. Established in Shenzhen, the firm operates within the healthcare and biotech sectors, offering a range of medicines and health solutions. The company is listed on various business intelligence platforms and maintains a corporate presence on professional networks.

providers.name: Bempower
providers.description: Bempower is a nonprofit organization focused on empowering communities in East Africa through education, water, sanitation, health, climate-smart agriculture, and livelihood initiatives. It works to improve access to clean water, education, sustainable agriculture, and health services, while promoting climate resilience and human rights.

providers.name: Bev
providers.description: Bev is a female-focused beverage company disrupting the male-dominated alcohol industry with premium, low-sugar canned wines made from California grapes. Sold direct-to-consumer at drinkbev.com, its lineup spans Bubbly Rosé, Bubbly White, Rosé, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Grigio and Pinot Noir, each with less than 1g of sugar per serving. Founded on a mission to transform drinking culture and promote female empowerment in business, Bev is a seed-stage Canaan Partners portfolio company. This is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce brand with no public API, developer program, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Bgogo
providers.description: Bgogo is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Biomilq
providers.description: Biomilq is a women‑owned, science‑led biotechnology start‑up focused on mammary biotechnology. It leverages patented technology to produce functional cell‑cultured human milk components outside the body, aiming to bridge the gap between breast milk and infant formula. The company seeks to revolutionize early‑life nutrition by delivering the benefits of human milk through innovative, scalable biomanufacturing.

providers.name: Bitwise Industries
providers.description: Bitwise Industries was an American technology company focused on computer programming instruction, technology sales, and real estate operations. Founded in 2013 by Irma Olguin Jr. and Jake Soberal in Fresno, California, it grew to operate campuses and provide training, while also engaging in real estate development. The company ceased operations around 2024 following financial and legal challenges.

providers.name: black-unique
providers.description: Black Unique (全球购骑士特权, "Global Shopping Knight Privilege") is a membership-based consumer e-commerce and discounts platform founded in 2018 and headquartered in Guangzhou, China. Its core product is a privileges/membership card that aggregates discounts and special offers across a wide range of consumer categories: online shopping on major marketplaces such as Tmall, JD.com and Kaola, in-person shopping at international duty-free shops, outlets and supermarkets across 24-plus countries, plus dining, entertainment, travel and fuel. The company operates a consumer-facing app and website rather than a public developer program, and is backed by Qiming Venture Partners along with CCV, Eastern Bell Venture Capital and INCE Capital. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Qiming portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other developer surface.

providers.name: Blockfolio
providers.description: Blockfolio is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Bondit
providers.description: Bondit provides a free, social calendar app that helps users schedule group events, share calendars, and stay connected. It supports personal and club schedules, offers mobile apps for iOS and Android, and includes features like multiple calendars, event reminders, and a community-driven interface. The service targets students, families, and groups looking for simple, collaborative planning.

providers.name: Bonfire Studios
providers.description: Bonfire Studios is an independent video game development studio based in Irvine, California, focused on building original interactive entertainment, including its announced title Arkheron. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, Bonfire Studios does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other programmable developer surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich; this profile is maintained as a company record and an ongoing lead should a developer surface emerge.

providers.name: Bookpalkorea
providers.description: Bookpalkorea, operating under the brand Bookpal, is a Korean digital platform offering a wide range of novels and web novels. The service provides users with a library of romance, fantasy, BL, and other genres, along with features such as personal bookshelves, rankings, and community interaction. It includes business details like its Seoul address, registration number, and contact emails, indicating a formal corporate entity. The platform appears to target Korean readers seeking serialized fiction and related content.

providers.name: Boost Biomes
providers.description: Boost Biomes leverages the powerful social networks among microbes to provide novel, sustainable solutions that feed and heal people worldwide. Their technology focuses on a causal understanding of microbial interactions, enabling the rational design of functional consortia. Initial products aim to reduce agricultural waste caused by fungal pests, addressing significant needs in crop loss mitigation and post-harvest preservation.

providers.name: Breaker
providers.description: Breaker is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global, bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Bromium
providers.description: Bromium was an endpoint-security company founded in 2010 that pioneered application isolation through hardware-enforced micro-virtualization, running each untrusted task (a web page, email attachment, or downloaded file) inside its own disposable CPU-level micro-VM so malware could not escape to the host. Bromium was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Hewlett-Packard (HP Inc.) acquired Bromium in September 2019 and folded the micro-virtualization technology into HP Sure Click and the HP Wolf Security endpoint-protection line; bromium.com now permanently redirects to HP's endpoint-security pages. Bromium no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no standalone public developer API, so this profile carries company identity only rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: budcreate
providers.description: BUD (budcreate.xyz, app at joinbudapp.com) is an AI-powered 3D UGC (user-generated content) interactive content platform where millions of creators build, play, and share immersive experiences and games. It is a consumer mobile creation and social platform spanning avatars, 3D worlds, mini-games, and AI-assisted content generation. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass, BUD publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or discovery/.well-known surface — it is a consumer application, not an API provider.

providers.name: Bumped
providers.description: Bumped was a Portland, Oregon-based fintech that rewarded consumers with fractional shares of publicly traded stock in the brands and companies they shop with, turning everyday spending and loyalty into equity ownership. Backed by Canaan Partners, the company operated a consumer investing and rewards application before winding down its consumer product. It was surfaced through the Canaan Partners portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. During enrichment no live public developer surface, API, documentation, package, or well-known discovery endpoint could be located -- the primary domain (bumped.com) no longer resolves and related domains are parked -- so this remains an identity-only profile with no active API artifacts.

providers.name: Burt
providers.description: Burt builds AI teammates (AI coworkers) for logistics, aimed at freight brokers and forwarders. Its agents automate the repetitive, manual work of daily freight operations — track and trace, quoting, scheduling, carrier booking, document processing, proof-of-delivery chasing, and invoice and data entry — so human operators can focus on customer relationships and growing the business. Burt gives full visibility into every AI action with human oversight and approval workflows, rolls out autonomy gradually, and learns from operator corrections and exceptions to build institutional knowledge over time. Burt is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Burt does not currently publish a public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Byeaerospace
providers.description: Bye Aerospace, founded in 2007 in Colorado, pioneers electric aviation with the eFlyer series, aiming to certify the world’s first all‑electric Part 23 training aircraft. The company focuses on reducing emissions, lowering operating costs, and providing quieter, safer flight training solutions, advancing bold engineering at the intersection of electric propulsion, aircraft design, and FAA certification.

providers.name: Callin
providers.description: Callin was a social podcasting and live-streaming platform founded by David Sacks and Axel Ericsson, backed by Craft Ventures, that let creators stream live audio, take listener questions, then record, edit, publish and share the result as a podcast episode. The company was acquired by Rumble (NASDAQ: RUM) in May 2023 and the standalone consumer app was subsequently wound down. As of enrichment the callin.com domain returns only a Cloudflare-gated placeholder and the provider exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cap Hill Brands
providers.description: Cap Hill Brands was a Seattle-based e-commerce brand aggregator founded in 2020 by Kevin Saliba and Jason LeeKeenan (both former Zulily leaders). Operating as a "tech-first" Amazon aggregator, it acquired and operated digitally-native consumer/CPG brands sold on Amazon, Walmart, and Shopify, handling supply chain, marketing, and warehousing. It raised roughly $250M in debt and equity and acquired nearly 35 brands (including Butterfly Craze, merka, and LilGadgets). In March 2024 Cap Hill Brands merged with product developer Juvo+ to form Infinite Commerce, which has since been absorbed into Razor Group. Cap Hill Brands is a consumer operating company, not an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specs, SDKs, or partner integration surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Version One Ventures and retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record.

providers.name: Capacity Bio
providers.description: Capacity Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing mitophagy therapeutics to restore mitochondrial quality control in age- and disease-related conditions. Its platform advances small molecules, peptides, and nanoparticles that enhance identification and clearance of dysfunctional mitochondria. With operations in Los Angeles and Tokyo, the company closed a $35M financing round in 2023 and is backed by Insight Partners. As a drug-development firm, Capacity Bio publishes no public API, developer platform, or SDK surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: CapriCoast
providers.description: CapriCoast (CapriCoast Home Solutions Pvt Ltd) was a Bengaluru, India based online modular-furniture and modular-kitchen retailer, founded in 2014 and backed by Accel Partners and RB Investments. It offered an online 3D catalog of kitchens and wardrobes with designs pre-customized for project floor plans. The company was acquired by HomeLane in November 2017 and no longer operates independently; its domain (capricoast.com) is now parked/for-sale and it publishes no developer, API, or documentation surface. Sector: consumer. Retained in the network as an Accel portfolio record; no API artifacts are available to enrich.

providers.name: Capstan Therapeutics
providers.description: Capstan Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego, California, developing in vivo cell engineering medicines built on a proprietary targeted lipid nanoparticle (tLNP) platform that delivers mRNA and other RNA payloads to specific cell types inside the body. Its lead candidate CPTX2309 is an anti-CD19 in vivo CAR-T therapy in Phase 1 for B cell-mediated autoimmune disease, intended to achieve deep B cell depletion without lymphodepleting chemotherapy. AbbVie completed its acquisition of Capstan on 19 August 2025 for up to $2.1 billion. The company's own domain now redirects to AbbVie and its DNS is served by AbbVie nameservers; it operates no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Caretaker
providers.description: Caretaker is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of union-square-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Casai
providers.description: Casai was a technology-enabled short-term and furnished-apartment rental company operating across Latin America (notably Mexico and Brazil), surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The enrichment pass found no active developer surface for this entity. The casai.com domain now hosts an unrelated luxury villa rental business (Premium Holiday Rentals and Villas, curated by TravelAI), and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or public API is published under the original company. With no spec-bearing surface, no downstream enrichment artifacts (packages, well-known, MCP, scopes, errors, conformance, etc.) could be produced without fabrication, so this profile remains an identity-only lead.

providers.name: CipherCloud
providers.description: CipherCloud was a cloud security company, founded in 2010, that pioneered the cloud access security broker (CASB) category. Its platform provided encryption and tokenization, data loss prevention, cloud discovery and shadow IT visibility, threat protection, and compliance controls for SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Office 365, ServiceNow, and Box. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Index Ventures among others, CipherCloud was acquired by mobile and cloud security vendor Lookout in early 2021, and its CASB technology was folded into Lookout's Secure Cloud Access offering. The standalone ciphercloud.com developer and product surface has since been retired; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record. No live public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface could be located during enrichment (ciphercloud.com returns HTTP 404 and no developer/docs subdomains resolve).

Its published customer examples include the US Postal Service, JCPenney, and Best Buy, with claimed first-year savings of 10-20% of total Jan/San spend. It is one of the largest global producers of multi-wall carbon nanotubes for battery applications. Backed by IDG Capital. providers.name: Concentric Analgesics
providers.description: Concentric Analgesics, Inc. is a San Francisco based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing non-opioid pain therapeutics. Its lead candidate, vocacapsaicin (CA-008), is a first-in-class prodrug that converts to capsaicin, a TRPV1 agonist that selectively desensitizes pain-conducting nerve fibers without sensory numbness or motor weakness, given as a single local injection during surgery. The program holds FDA Fast Track designation (2017) and Breakthrough Therapy designation (2018), and has been evaluated in Phase 2 trials in bunionectomy, total knee arthroplasty and open ventral hernia repair. The company is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or other machine-readable surface, and as of this check its corporate website is an expired Squarespace account that returns HTTP 404 for every path.

providers.name: Coolplanetlabs
providers.description: Cool Planet Labs is a climate‑focused organization that leverages massive‑scale online collaboration to address climate change. Through educational initiatives, community‑building tools, and the EarthAtlas solution library, it inspires and mobilizes young people worldwide to share, discover, and implement innovative climate solutions. The nonprofit’s mission centers on fostering a sea change in environmental action via web‑based platforms and interactive applications.

providers.name: Core Labs
providers.description: Core Labs is an early-stage product studio based in New York City building the future of professional identity and connection for the digital economy. Founded by serial entrepreneur Ajay Rajani (previously Grovo and Tala), the company operates in rapid-experimentation mode, incubating and testing consumer and productivity products. Its portfolio includes Mural, a simple portfolio-building tool for product managers, marketers, and digital workers that turns shared URLs into rich embeds; Core, a peer-and-expert mentorship platform used in university entrepreneurship programs and fellowships; and Makeshop, an on-demand marketplace for creative services. Core Labs is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: Cortera
providers.description: Cortera was a business (trade) credit data provider that turned anonymized, contributed accounts-receivable and B2B payment data into forward-looking payment-risk insight, credit scores, and firmographics on private companies so credit teams could spot changes in a customer's financial health. Founded in Massachusetts, Cortera was acquired by Moody's (Moody's Analytics) in 2021 and its product line has since been folded into Moody's Company Reference Data / Trade Credit offering, marketed as "Moody's Pulse (formerly Cortera)". The standalone cortera.com domain now 301-redirects to Moody's; there is no independent Cortera developer portal or public self-serve API today — data is delivered through Moody's data-delivery APIs, CRM/ERP connectors, and file feeds. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and is retained as an acquired-company record.

providers.name: Court Buddy
providers.description: Court Buddy is a legal services marketplace that connected consumers and small businesses with independent attorneys for flat-fee, on-demand legal help, aiming to make legal representation more affordable and accessible. It operated under the LawChamps brand (lawchamps.com) and was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface was found during enrichment, and the primary web property is currently unreachable.

providers.name: Covestor
providers.description: Covestor was an online investment management and social investing platform, backed by Union Square Ventures, that let everyday investors mirror the portfolios of vetted model managers through managed brokerage accounts. Interactive Brokers acquired Covestor in 2015 and later rebranded it as Interactive Advisors; the covestor.com domain now 301-redirects to interactiveadvisors.com. No public Covestor developer or API surface exists, so this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub with only a live domain-security probe recorded.

providers.name: Crane
providers.description: Crane Co. (NYSE: CR) and its sister company Crane NXT (NYSE: CXT) are industrial manufacturing companies that resulted from the 2023 split of the legacy Crane Holdings, Co. Crane Co. is a diversified manufacturer of highly engineered industrial products serving aerospace and electronics, process flow technologies, and engineered materials markets. Crane NXT is a global leader in trusted technology solutions for payment, security, and authentication including currency, banknote, and authentication products. No public APIs or developer portals are published; integrations with industrial customers are arranged through enterprise channels.

providers.name: Creopop
providers.description: CreoPop is a consumer 3D-printing pen that lets you draw three-dimensional objects freehand. Unlike filament 3D pens it has no hot parts or melting plastic; instead it uses photopolymer "cool ink" cartridges that are solidified by built-in LEDs, and it is battery operated and charged over mini-USB. The product line includes specialty inks (elastic, magnetic, glow-in-the-dark, aromatic, temperature-sensitive, and electrically conductive). CreoPop is a hardware/consumer-electronics brand with a marketing and direct-to-consumer e-commerce website; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Crocodoc
providers.description: Crocodoc built an HTML5-based document viewing and annotation API that converted PDF, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files into HTML5 for plugin-free, in-browser viewing, embedding, and markup. A 500 Startups / Y Combinator-lineage company, Crocodoc was acquired by Box in 2013, and its document-rendering technology became the foundation of the Box View API (later Box Content Preview / UI Elements). The standalone Crocodoc API was subsequently deprecated and the crocodoc.com domain is no longer active. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Crocs
providers.description: Crocs, Inc. is a global designer, manufacturer, and retailer of casual footwear known for its iconic molded clog. The company sells through e-commerce, owned retail, and wholesale channels worldwide and also owns the HEYDUDE casual footwear brand. Crocs does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: Crowdamp
providers.description: Crowdamp is a privately held Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company co-founded by Ruben Mayer-Hirshfeld and Alexandra Botez. The company built SuperFan, a creator-economy messaging product that let fans text their favorite social media stars and receive a personalized reply, using natural language processing to help those creators respond efficiently at scale across their whole audience. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass Crowdamp publishes no developer surface of any kind: there is no developer portal, no documentation, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, no SDK packages in any public registry, and no working product website. The SuperFan domain superfanapp.com no longer resolves to the product and is listed for sale through a domain reseller, indicating the product is no longer operating. This profile is retained as a portfolio-graph record rather than as an API provider.

providers.name: Crown Castle
providers.description: Crown Castle is a leading United States provider of shared communications infrastructure including cell towers, small cells, and fiber. Crown Castle owns and operates more than 40,000 cell towers and approximately 90,000 route miles of fiber, supporting wireless carriers, enterprises, and government customers with managed connectivity, dark fiber, optical encryption, ultra-low-latency transport, and managed SD-WAN services. Crown Castle does not currently publish a public developer API program; technical integrations are handled through customer and channel partner agreements.

providers.name: Crystal
providers.description: Crystal (Crystal Semiconductor) was a hardtech company that designed audio and mixed-signal semiconductor chips. Kleiner Perkins partnered with the company in 1986 at the early stage, and Crystal was subsequently acquired by Cirrus Logic. The company was surfaced from the Kleiner Perkins portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. It operated as a fabless chip designer rather than a software or platform business, and no longer exists as an independent entity: it publishes no website, no developer portal, and no public API surface of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record and is not an API provider.

providers.name: Cult of the North
providers.description: Cult of the North (established November 2022 under the codename "Seidr") is a Stockholm, Sweden-based video game studio co-founded by former EA general manager Adam Schaub and former King SVP Marcus Jacobs, and backed by a seed investment from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The studio drew talent from King, Activision Blizzard, EA, Embark Studios, Resolution Games, and FunPlus, and set out to build large-scale, next-generation multiplayer PvP experiences for PC and console in Unreal Engine 5 — first the debut title codenamed "Project Gundalf" and later the free-to-play strategy war game "We Will Be Gods." As a consumer game studio it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile carries company identity only. Industry reporting in 2025 indicated the studio wound down operations.

providers.name: Cultivaet
providers.description: Cultivaet Technologies Holding Ltd. is an AI-driven agricultural technology ("AgriTech for Humanity") startup based in Egypt serving smallholder farmers across the Middle East. Its products include a Farmer AI Companion delivering personalized weather, crop-planning, pest-control and soil-health insights, a Knowledge Platform that collects/analyzes/distributes social and scientific agricultural data, and a Business SaaS connecting farmers with food-industry buyers for sustainable procurement and traceability. The company is backed by 500 Global and Sanabil and is part of the Google Cloud Startups Program (pre-seed, 2024). As of this enrichment pass Cultivaet publishes only a marketing site (cultivaet.ai) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or other developer surface, so no API artifacts were generated.

It develops, manufactures, and services intelligent automation and automated-test equipment for consumer electronics, semiconductor and integrated-circuit, automotive, medical, and new-energy industries. Once backed by Qiming Venture Partners, CYGIA became a subsidiary of publicly traded CYG (Changyuan Group, Shanghai Stock Exchange 600525.SH) in 2015. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface for CYGIA, which is a hardware/automation-equipment manufacturer rather than an API provider.

providers.description: Dabee (dabee.com.br) is a Brazilian consumer-technology review and comparison website that helps shoppers make informed purchasing decisions about electronics and gadgets. providers.name: Dascena

The algorithms were delivered as an embedded integration inside a customer hospital's EHR under a services and laboratory agreement rather than as a public developer API, so the company never operated a developer portal, published a machine-readable contract, or shipped client SDKs. CirrusDx acquired the Dascena Labs laboratory business effective 5 August 2022 and the company identity now trades as DBA CirrusDx; the dascena.com domain no longer resolves.

Data.ai was acquired by Sensor Tower in 2024 and now operates as a Sensor Tower company; its standalone site is a gated login and the former public API host serves a default page, so its independent API surface has been consolidated into Sensor Tower and effectively retired. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an ivp portfolio company.

The company was acquired by Roku in 2019 and its technology was absorbed into Roku's OneView advertising platform (now Roku Ads). DataXu no longer operates as an independent brand: its primary domain (dataxu.com) 301-redirects into Roku's advertising site, and there is no independent DataXu developer portal, public API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical / acquired-company record surfaced from the Menlo Ventures portfolio.

providers.name: Dealflo
providers.description: Dealflo was a UK-based financial-technology company that provided an automated agreement, identity-verification, and e-signature platform used by lenders and financial institutions to capture, verify, and legally bind financial agreements end to end. It was acquired by OneSpan (formerly VASCO Data Security) in September 2018 for roughly USD 55 million and folded into OneSpan's Digital Agreements / electronic-signature product line. The dealflo.com domain now 301-redirects to onespan.com and Dealflo no longer operates an independent developer program, public documentation, or API. Founded as a London-based startup, it was backed by Speedinvest and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network through VC-portfolio discovery. Deep Render publishes no independent developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface for enrichment at this time.

providers.name: Defense.net
providers.description: Defense.Net was a cloud DDoS-mitigation company founded in 2012 by Barrett Lyon (also the founder of Prolexic, the original DDoS-mitigation provider). It operated a global constellation of scrubbing/mitigation sites that filtered distributed-denial-of-service attacks against Internet-facing infrastructure in real time. Bessemer Venture Partners led a $9.5M Series A in 2012. In May 2014 the company was acquired by F5 Networks and folded into the F5 Silverline DDoS Protection managed service. Defense.Net no longer operates as an independent business: the defense.net domain now returns an HTTP 301 redirect to the F5 Silverline product page, and there is no independent developer portal, public API, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

Shopify acquired Deliverr in 2022 and folded it into Shopify Logistics / the Shopify Fulfillment Network; in 2023 Shopify sold that logistics business to Flexport. Deliverr no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone developer portal or API — its former domain (deliverr.com) now redirects to flexport.com, and its fulfillment capabilities live inside Flexport's platform. This profile is retained as a historical network stub; there is no live Deliverr API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Deployco
providers.description: Deployco (the OpenAI Deployment Company, DeployCo) is a ~$10B enterprise-AI joint venture launched by OpenAI in May 2026 to help organizations put frontier AI into production. It is an engineering-heavy consulting and deployment business: Forward Deployed Engineers and Deployment Specialists embed in client companies to connect OpenAI models to their data, tools, controls, and core workflows (RAG, fine-tuning/distillation, infrastructure, and safety/compliance). It is backed by a founding-investor group including Emergence Capital. DeployCo is a services/consulting entity and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs of its own; any API surface it uses is the OpenAI platform. No API artifacts are available to enrich at this time.

providers.name: DiDi Autonomous
providers.description: DiDi Autonomous Driving (滴滴自动驾驶) is the autonomous-driving subsidiary of Chinese mobility giant DiDi. Founded as an internal research unit in 2016 and spun out as an independent company in 2019, it develops Level 4 self-driving technology and operates robotaxi services integrated into the DiDi ride-hailing platform in Chinese cities including Shanghai and Guangzhou. In 2020 SoftBank Vision Fund led a roughly $500M funding round into the unit. As a hardware- and fleet-oriented autonomous mobility operator it does not currently publish a public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dover
providers.description: Dover Corporation is a diversified American industrial conglomerate headquartered in Downers Grove, Illinois. Dover operates across five segments - Engineered Products, Clean Energy and Fueling, Imaging and Identification, Pumps and Process Solutions, and Climate and Sustainability Technologies - through a portfolio of decentralized operating companies including Dover Fueling Solutions, OPW, Markem-Imaje, PSG, and Vehicle Service Group.

providers.name: Dream Voyage
providers.description: Dream Voyage Inc. is an AI-driven consumer studio founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz through its Speedrun accelerator alongside Soma Capital. Led by co-founder and CEO Coco Chen, a former TikTok founding product manager and Tinder PM, the studio builds viral AI-powered consumer applications spanning spiritual wellness, dream interpretation, gaming, and social payments. Its products include SINE Daily Manifest (an AI spiritual-health app offering daily affirmations, astrology, birth-chart analysis, and tarot readings that went viral on TikTok), Dreamore (AI-powered dream interpretation), Vdrop (turning social media into a payment network), and RPS (a Solana-based social game). Dream Voyage ships consumer mobile apps rather than a public developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documented API surface. This record is a network stub retained for discovery and future enrichment.

providers.name: Drishti
providers.description: Drishti was an AI and computer-vision company that turned manual assembly-line activity into continuous streams of process data for discrete manufacturers. Cameras securely streamed factory-floor video into proprietary neural networks that generated cycle-time data and detected the sequence of human actions within each cycle, giving plant teams system-wide visibility into variability, bottlenecks, and improvement opportunities. Founded in 2017 in Mountain View, California and backed by Emergence Capital, Drishti counted Ford, Honeywell, and Nissan among its customers before being acquired by Apple in September 2023. The company operated no public developer API, and all of its web and developer domains are now offline.
