No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time; this index captures DuPont's web presence for monitoring future developer activity.

providers.name: eCredit.com
providers.description: eCredit.com was an online trade-credit and credit-decisioning company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It no longer operates independently. The ecredit.com domain is delegated to Moody's nameservers and 301-redirects in full to Moody's trade-credit offering, where "Moody's eCredit" now exists as a platform within Moody's Trade Credit product line. Enrichment probes confirm no independent developer portal, documentation, API specification, or /.well-known surface remains on ecredit.com. Any live API capability for this product is delivered through Moody's, which is profiled separately in the network as the successor company.

providers.name: Efficient Frontier
providers.description: Efficient Frontier was a digital advertising optimization and search marketing company founded in 2002 that applied algorithmic, finance-inspired bid optimization to manage over $1 billion in annual marketing spend across search, display, and social (notably Facebook ad buying) for enterprise clients such as Discover, Travelodge, and Match.com. Adobe acquired the company in late 2011 (announced November 30, 2011; completed January 2012) and folded its multi-channel ad forecasting, execution, and optimization capabilities into the Adobe Digital Marketing / Advertising Cloud. The efrontier.com domain now redirects to adobe.com and the company has no independent website, developer portal, or public API.

providers.name: Eggrock
providers.description: Eggrock (Eggrock Modular Solutions; legally Innovative Modular Pre-Fabrication LLC) is a North American manufacturer of prefabricated "bathroom-in-a-box" pods — complete, custom, ready-to-install bathrooms built off-site using BIM-driven design and lean manufacturing for hotels, hospitals, dormitories, military barracks, and other multi-unit construction projects. Off-site fabrication compresses construction schedules and improves quality versus building bathrooms on site. In 2012 Eggrock licensed exclusive North American manufacturing and distribution to Oldcastle Precast. It is a construction / building-products manufacturer with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Eigentech
providers.description: Eigentech (eigentech.ai) is an artificial intelligence technology company, reported to have been founded around 2016 and headquartered in Hangzhou, China, that applies AI and machine learning to business and industrial domains. Its platform is positioned to help enterprises improve operational efficiency, optimize workflows, and strengthen data-driven decision-making by embedding AI into existing business processes. Eigentech is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for the enrichment pipeline. NOTE - as of the latest enrichment pass the company website (https://eigentech.ai) does not resolve and no public developer, documentation, or API surface could be reached, so no API artifacts could be harvested without fabrication.

providers.name: Elastifile
providers.description: Elastifile was an enterprise cloud file-storage company founded in 2013 in Tel Aviv, Israel. It built a software-defined, scale-out distributed file system (the Elastifile Cloud File System / ECFS) that delivered elastic, high-performance NFS-compatible shared storage for enterprise-grade applications running at scale in the public cloud, with the ability to scale capacity out or in on demand. Backed by Battery Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners (among others), Elastifile was acquired by Google Cloud in August 2019 (reported at roughly $200M) and its technology was folded into Google Cloud Filestore, powering the Filestore High Scale / Enterprise tiers. Elastifile no longer operates as an independent company or brand: elastifile.com redirects to Google Cloud Filestore, and there is no standalone Elastifile developer portal, API, or SDK surface to enrich.

providers.name: Element AI
providers.description: Element AI was a Montreal, Quebec-based artificial intelligence company founded in 2016 by Jean-Francois Gagne, Yoshua Bengio, Nicolas Chapados, Philippe Beaudoin, Anne Martel, and Jean-Sebastien Cournoyer. It operated as an AI systems integrator and professional-services firm with the mission of putting advanced AI capabilities - natural language processing, computer vision, document intelligence, and conversational AI - in reach of traditional enterprises. After raising roughly US$102M plus Canadian government funding and reaching an estimated US$600-700M valuation in 2019, the company ran short of runway and was acquired by ServiceNow (announced November 30, 2020; closed January 8, 2021 for approximately US$230M). Its research group became ServiceNow Research and its former domain now redirects there. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no standalone public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Elmawkaa
providers.description: Elmawkaa (الموقع) is an Egyptian B2B online marketplace that digitizes construction-materials procurement. Founded in Cairo in 2017 by Ebrahem Anwar, Mahmoud Habib, and Mohamed Thabet, the platform lets construction companies request and compare competitive supplier quotations for materials such as cement, steel, and gypsum board, using proprietary matching algorithms to replace slow, manual bidding with a documented, automated process. A 500 Startups (500 Global) accelerator graduate that raised a seed round led by Flat6Labs with Oqal and other regional backers, Elmawkaa was fully acquired by Saudi PropTech / real-estate-appraisal platform Ayen in a seven-figure deal in October 2024, with its marketplace folded into Ayen's services. Elmawkaa publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation, and its standalone domain (elmawkaa.com) no longer resolves following the acquisition.

providers.name: Energy Micro
providers.description: Energy Micro was a Norwegian fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2007 and headquartered in Oslo, best known for its EFM32 "Gecko" family of energy-friendly 32-bit ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers and the EFR radio products targeting low-power embedded and IoT applications. The company was acquired by Silicon Labs in 2013 and fully absorbed into that company's product lines; its former energymicro.com domain now redirects to silabs.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no independent, first-party API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface for Energy Micro as a standalone entity — the developer tooling for its EFM32 line lives under Silicon Labs today.

providers.name: ESPL
providers.description: ESPL (Esports Players League) is a Singapore-headquartered global esports tournament network and platform, founded in 2019, building an open, grassroots-focused ecosystem for amateur competitive gaming. It runs ESPL-branded online and on-ground tournaments across Asia, Europe, and the Americas with a mobile-first focus alongside PC and console titles, operated from its Singapore headquarters with regional offices in Cologne and Los Angeles. ESPL is a portfolio company of 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), which led its seed round in 2020. As of this enrichment pass ESPL publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface, and its espl.co domain did not resolve (DNS SERVFAIL) at probe time; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Facet
providers.description: Facet was a consumer AI image-editing and creative tool, backed by Accel and originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass, its domain facet.ai (HTTP) 301-redirects to www.vsco.co/features/canvas ("VSCO Canvas | AI Mood Board Maker for Photographers"), indicating the product has been acquired by / absorbed into VSCO. Facet exposes no independent developer platform, public API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface of its own; its HTTPS endpoint is unreachable.

providers.name: Factory Works
providers.description: Factory Works (Factory Berlin) is a Berlin-based venture-building and company-builder firm that partners with entrepreneurs, visual artists, and musicians to turn early ideas into scalable businesses. Positioning itself as a "neo company builder," Factory builds and scales ventures in exchange for equity while handling strategy, product, brand, marketing, legal, accounting, and operations, and it runs a physical Berlin venue with event, restaurant, and studio infrastructure alongside a mentor and investor network. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Factory publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Fan Controlled Football
providers.description: Fan Controlled Football (FCF) was a professional indoor American football league in which fans voted on play calls in real time through a mobile app, playing a fast, 7-on-7 format staged at Pullman Yards in Atlanta and streamed to social and live-video audiences. The league drew high-profile athlete and celebrity team owners and investors and positioned itself as a fan-interactive, tech-driven sports and entertainment property. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. FCF paused operations and its public web presence (fcf.io) no longer serves a live site, so it currently exposes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface.

providers.name: Fancy Technology
providers.description: Fancy Technology is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Fantiger
providers.description: Fantiger is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto-web3. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Fast Break Labs
providers.description: Fast Break Labs is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Fifth Door
providers.description: Fifth Door is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) AI-native gaming startup founded by Amir Ghazvinian and Daniel Kan that lets anyone create, share, and play games simply by describing what they imagine, with no coding required. Its generative-AI platform turns natural-language prompts into playable, customizable games, aiming to collapse the time, cost, and technical complexity of traditional game development for players, creators, and studios. Backed by Felicis, the company runs a consumer web app and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: Flowers Foods
providers.description: Flowers Foods is one of the largest producers and marketers of packaged bakery foods in the United States, with brands including Nature's Own, Wonder, Dave's Killer Bread, Tastykake, and Mrs. Freshley's. No public, developer-facing APIs have been identified for this company; partner and retailer integrations appear to be handled through internal EDI and account-managed channels.

providers.name: Fluidly
providers.description: Fluidly was a London-based intelligent cashflow forecasting fintech founded in 2016 by Caroline Plumb, providing SME cash-flow prediction, scenario planning, and working-capital tools used by roughly 1,300 UK accountancy firms. OakNorth Bank acquired Fluidly in December 2021 and folded the product into its Credit Intelligence Suite; the independent Fluidly brand has since been retired and fluidly.com now redirects to OakNorth's partnerships page. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record — no independent Fluidly developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface remains.

providers.name: Fortune Technology (China FIF)
providers.description: Fortune Technology, listed by Qiming Venture Partners as one of the largest commercial factoring companies in China, historically operating at china-fif.com. Commercial factoring is a trade-finance business: purchasing accounts receivable from suppliers at a discount to provide working capital. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe the company publishes no developer surface of any kind — no public API, no documentation portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents. The china-fif.com domain no longer serves the company: HTTPS is refused outright (port 443 closed) and plain HTTP returns an unrelated Chinese Premier League sports-streaming site running EmpireCMS. This record is retained as an honest negative result for the API Evangelist network rather than deleted.

providers.name: Foxconn Industrial Internet
providers.description: Foxconn Industrial Internet Co., Ltd. (FII, 工业富联) is a Shanghai Stock Exchange-listed subsidiary of Hon Hai Precision Industry (Foxconn), headquartered in Shenzhen, China. It is a smart-manufacturing and industrial-internet company producing cloud computing infrastructure and AI servers, communication and networking equipment, and precision tooling, and it offers factory-automation, lighthouse-factory, and industrial-internet platform services for global electronics OEMs. FII operates as a contract manufacturer and industrial platform rather than a public API provider: it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal. This profile tracks the company's corporate identity in the API Evangelist network; there is no API artifact surface to enrich.

providers.name: Framed *
providers.description: Framed (framed.io), formerly Framed Data, was a GV-backed predictive-analytics / customer churn-prediction machine-learning startup. As of 2026 the framed.io domain no longer hosts a product or developer surface: it serves a static Squarespace landing page titled "Framed + Square" that points visitors to Square Capital (squareup.com/capital), indicating the team/product moved to Square. No API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable artifact surface survives, so there is nothing to enrich against; this record is retained as a dormant/acquired lead.

providers.name: Fraugster
providers.description: Fraugster is a Berlin-based artificial intelligence company focused on payment fraud prevention and transaction risk scoring for online merchants, payment service providers, and acquirers. Its machine-learning platform was designed to analyze payments in real time to detect and block fraudulent transactions while reducing false declines and chargebacks. The company was surfaced through venture portfolio data (backed by Seedcamp) and added to the API Evangelist network. During this enrichment pass the company's public developer surface was not reachable to automated clients (the primary domain returns HTTP 403), so no API specifications, SDKs, or documentation could be harvested; only live infrastructure/domain-security signals were probed.

providers.name: Future Nostalgia Studios
providers.description: Future Nostalgia Studios, Inc. is a consumer software company that builds AI-powered mobile applications and companion experiences for iOS and Android. Its published apps include Kindred (AI stories and roleplay), Muze (AI fashion photography), Booboo (long-distance relationship tracker), Pocket Frens (self-care and habit tracker), and Minime (AI motivational buddy). Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, documentation, or /.well-known surface — it is a business-to-consumer app studio rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Gaspack
providers.description: Gaspack is a Web3 NFT launchpad that helps brands, creators, and artists turn their intellectual property into NFT projects and bridge them with their fans. The platform provides a full technology stack, community management, and creative consultancy that supports projects from ideation through minting, launching, scaling, and long-term maintenance as sustainable digital-collectible businesses. Gaspack operates a consumer application (app.gaspack.xyz) for collecting digital assets and has incubated branded NFT collections such as JPG People, Easy Demons Club, and Jukiverse, alongside Kometh, a Web3 comic publishing and discovery platform. Gaspack is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Gaspack publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its verified public identity only.

providers.name: Geekatoo
providers.description: Geekatoo was a Walnut Creek, California on-demand, in-home technology support marketplace that connected consumers to a nationwide network of vetted local technicians for computer repair, network troubleshooting, TV mounting, and home-theater/smart-home installation using a fixed-price and competitive-bid model positioned as an alternative to retail services like Geek Squad. Founded in 2013, it went through the 500 Startups accelerator (sixth batch) and raised roughly $2.2M from backers including 500 Startups, CRCM Venture Capital, DeNA, MicroVentures, and Wefunder. In May 2016 Geekatoo merged with Los Angeles-based HelloTech to form one of the largest on-demand in-home tech support networks in the US; the standalone Geekatoo brand and website (geekatoo.com) are no longer operational. This API Evangelist profile is a 500 Global portfolio lead retained for historical record; the enrichment pipeline found no live developer surface, API, or documentation to harvest.

providers.name: General Growth Properties
providers.description: General Growth Properties (GGP) was a major U.S.-based commercial real estate company and the second-largest shopping mall operator in the United States before being acquired by Brookfield Property Partners in 2018. The GGP portfolio is now operated under Brookfield Properties. No public developer APIs are documented for the legacy GGP entity.

providers.name: General Radar
providers.description: General Radar Corp. (GenRad) is a Belmont, California hardtech company founded in 2016 that designs and manufactures fully solid-state, high-resolution active electronically scanned array (AESA) phased-array radar systems built largely on commercial off-the-shelf hardware. Its products include the C-band GenRad GFC multi-mission AESA radar with a GaN front-end and digital beam-forming, and the Mark-IV 76-81GHz millimeter-wave 3D imaging radar producing LIDAR-like point clouds. The company serves aerospace and defense (U.S. Air Force, Navy, NORAD), counter-drone, airfield foreign-object-debris (FOD) detection, autonomy, wind energy, and weather markets, and has raised over $35M from investors including Kleiner Perkins and Octave Ventures. General Radar publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness.

providers.name: Generalastro
providers.description: General Astronautics (Generalastro) is a Y Combinator (W26) space-robotics company founded in 2025 by Bram Schork, based in San Francisco, building autonomous dexterous robotic arms that perform laboratory research and manufacturing tasks in microgravity without astronaut intervention. Its systems handle work like pipetting, sample prep, plate handling, and reagent mixing, targeting microgravity production of pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and fiber optics where crew time on orbital stations is the bottleneck (NASA estimates ISS crew time at ~$130K/hour). The company is pre-product hardware, backed by Y Combinator and Planet Ventures (~$7.1M raised), and currently exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Getable
providers.description: Getable is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Historically Getable operated a construction and equipment rental marketplace/software platform (getable.com). As of this enrichment pass the original company appears inactive; the getable.com domain resolves to a general home-services and equipment-rental lead-generation marketplace with no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or other public API surface. No OpenAPI, MCP, or agent-facing artifacts could be sourced, so this profile remains an identity stub rather than a scored API provider.

providers.name: Getaway
providers.description: Getaway was a consumer hospitality startup that operated a network of minimalist tiny cabins ("Outposts") in nature within a couple hours' drive of major US cities, letting people book short, disconnected nature escapes. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of cowboy-ventures (sector: consumer). The company was acquired by Marriott International and rebranded as "Postcard Cabins" under Marriott's Outdoor Collection; the getaway.house domain now 301-redirects entirely to the Marriott Postcard Cabins brand page. Getaway operates a consumer booking website only and publishes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface, so this profile carries identity metadata rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Glo Pharma
providers.description: GLO Pharma is a beauty and aesthetics company developing next-generation products for at-home use, best known for the subtopical skincare brand Ourself. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (Series A, 2020), the company operates as a direct-to-consumer beauty and personal-care business rather than a technology or API provider: it sells physical skincare and aesthetic products to end consumers and does not publish a developer platform, public API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed portfolio company profile; enrichment found no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Gnip
providers.description: Gnip was a social media data aggregation company founded in 2008 in Boulder, Colorado by Eric Marcoullier and Jud Valeski. It became the first authorized reseller of the Twitter "firehose" and delivered enterprise-grade access to real-time and historical social data from Twitter, Tumblr, WordPress, Disqus, StockTwits and many other sources through products such as PowerTrack, Historical PowerTrack, the Search API, the Audience API and the Engagement API. Twitter acquired Gnip in April 2014 and folded its technology into Twitter's enterprise data platform; the Gnip brand and standalone APIs were retired and gnip.com now 301-redirects to the Twitter/X enterprise developer documentation. This profile is preserved for historical/network completeness — Gnip is no longer an independent provider.

providers.name: Go Deed
providers.description: Go Deed (legally Deed Inc.) is a workplace-giving and corporate social responsibility platform founded in 2016 that helps enterprises engage employees around volunteering, charitable giving, donation matching, and everyday social-impact actions. With teams in New York, San Francisco, and Berlin, Deed served Fortune 500 and mid-market employers before being acquired into Bonterra, where it now ships as the "Deed" employee-engagement product. The joindeed.com domain 301-redirects to bonterratech.com/product/deed. Deed was surfaced as an Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company (investment 2021) and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no independent public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification for the standalone Go Deed / Deed brand.

providers.name: Goodme
providers.description: Goodme (brand "Good me", Chinese: 古茗; legal entity Guming Holdings Limited) is one of China's largest freshly-made tea-beverage franchise chains, founded in 2010 by Wang Yun'an and headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang. It sells fruit tea, milk tea, and coffee through a franchise model concentrated in China's lower-tier cities, and had grown to roughly 9,800 outlets nationwide by late 2024. The company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (SEHK: 1364) in February 2025, raising about US$233 million. It is a consumer-sector portfolio company of HongShan and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a food-and-beverage retail franchise, Goodme publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or agent-facing surface at this time.

providers.name: Gotiger
providers.description: GoTiger is a Berlin-based food company that operates multiple delivery-first food brands out of modern ghost kitchens, including Bok Bok Chicken, GoDumpling and Kyoo Chicken. Founded in 2022, the company began as GoTiger Asia Grocery Delivery, a same-day app-based service delivering Japanese, Korean and Chinese groceries and everyday essentials across Berlin and Potsdam on a Shopify Plus backend, before pivoting to a portfolio of virtual restaurant brands. GoTiger is a consumer product company backed by Speedinvest, Adjacent, Nucleus Capital and Shio Capital; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time.

providers.name: Graphiq
providers.description: Graphiq was a creative-technology startup founded in 2015 that set out to disrupt the traditional agency model by connecting companies with vetted graphic designers through a flexible design-subscription service. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Klingit in July 2024 and its brand folded into Klingit; the graphiq.design domain now redirects to klingit.com. Graphiq operated as a design-services marketplace and offered no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gridsnap
providers.description: Gridsnap is a Los Angeles-based gaming studio founded in 2024 and part of the a16z Speedrun Cohort 002. The studio builds interactive worlds for community, powered by user-generated content (UGC), primarily using Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN). Its work spans three areas - developing original IP, partnering with influencers to create community spaces inside Fortnite, and investing in emerging game developers by taking stakes in their projects while providing development support. Gridsnap publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation; this profile is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gxs
providers.description: Gxs is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: unknown. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Habitto
providers.description: Habitto is a Tokyo-based fintech company building a mobile financial wellness app for the Japanese market under the banner お金の新習慣 ("new money habits"). The app pairs a high-yield savings account and a cashback debit card with access to human financial advisors who help users save, grow, and protect their money. Habitto is backed by the fintech-focused venture investors Anthemis and QED Investors. This API Evangelist profile has been enriched with company identity, website link properties, and a domain-security probe; Habitto is a consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Hain Celestial Group
providers.description: The Hain Celestial Group is a leading organic and natural products company providing consumers with A Healthier Way of Life through a portfolio of natural, organic, and better-for-you brands. No public APIs or developer programs have been identified for Hain Celestial Group at this time.

providers.name: HauteLook
providers.description: HauteLook was a members-only, flash-sale e-commerce destination for fashion, beauty, and home goods, founded in 2007 in Los Angeles. It was acquired by Nordstrom in 2011 and operated as a standalone flash-sale brand before being folded into Nordstrom Rack; www.hautelook.com now redirects to the Nordstrom Rack Flash storefront. The provider publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, so no API artifacts could be enriched during the pipeline pass.

providers.name: Haven
providers.description: Haven, Inc. was an ocean freight technology company founded in 2014 that built software to automate quoting, booking, document management, and shipment management for commodity producers, traders, and freight forwarders moving international ocean cargo. Backed by DCVC, Haven was acquired by supply-chain visibility platform FourKites in April 2021, and its technology became the foundation of FourKites' Dynamic Ocean product for end-to-end international ocean shipment visibility. Haven no longer operates an independent public developer program or API; the Haven brand survives only as the "Haven Marketplace" login at app.haveninc.com, now operated as part of FourKites.

providers.name: Herbeast
providers.description: Herbeast is a sustainable skin care and lifestyle brand based in China, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The company explores the application of Chinese herbal essence to the skin, grounding its formulations in the concepts and technical principles of biomedicine. Founded and led by CEO Yisa He with Chief Scientist and co-founder Yanjing Bai, Herbeast operates as a consumer skin care and lifestyle products brand rather than an API-first technology provider. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; its only observed web property (herbeast.com) resolves to a deactivated Shopify storefront. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed portfolio identity record, not as an active API producer.

providers.name: Herman Miller
providers.description: Herman Miller is an American furniture company founded in 1905 and headquartered in Zeeland, Michigan, known for iconic office and residential designs including the Aeron chair and the Eames lounge chair. On July 19, 2021, Herman Miller closed its acquisition of Knoll Inc. in a $1.8 billion cash-and-stock deal and rebranded the combined company as MillerKnoll (NASDAQ: MLKN). Herman Miller continues as a consumer-facing brand within the MillerKnoll collective alongside Knoll, Design Within Reach, HAY, Muuto, Geiger, Holly Hunt, Maharam, Naughtone, DatesWeiser, Edelman Leather, and Colebrook Bosson Saunders. Herman Miller sells through retail, contract, and dealer channels and does not publish a public developer API portal — partner ordering, dealer pricing, and supply-chain integrations are private B2B channels run through MillerKnoll.

providers.name: Heroic Story
providers.description: Heroic Story was a Web3 gaming studio building a collaborative, community-owned tabletop role-playing game world — a Dungeons & Dragons-style on-chain MMORPG powered by smart contracts and NFTs on Polygon. Founded by Jay and Scott Rosenkrantz, it raised a $6M seed round in November 2022 led by Upfront Ventures with participation from Multicoin Capital and Polygon, bringing total financing to roughly $7.4M. As of this profiling the primary domain heroicstory.com resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander with no active product, documentation, developer, or API surface, indicating the project is dormant or defunct.

providers.name: hhgregg
providers.description: hhgregg is an electronics retailer offering products such as televisions, cameras, professional video equipment, laptops, headphones, drones, and more, with free shipping and installation services on many products.

providers.name: HYLA
providers.description: HYLA (HYLA Mobile) was a mobile device trade-in and reverse-supply-chain company that ran buyback, trade-in, and device-recommerce programs for carriers, retailers, and manufacturers, reselling and redistributing used smartphones into secondary markets. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, it was acquired and its business folded into Assurant: its site hylamobile.com now permanently redirects to Assurant's mobile/broadband unit. HYLA is not a public API provider — it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API, so this profile is an identity-only company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API catalog entry.

providers.name: IAC/InterActiveCorp
providers.description: IAC (InterActiveCorp) is a media and internet company comprising widely known consumer brands such as Vimeo, Dotdash Meredith (People Inc.), Angi, Care.com, Search (Ask Media Group, Investopedia), and Emerging brands including Vivian Health, The Daily Beast, Daily Burn, Apalon, Mosaic Group, and NurseFly. No consolidated public developer APIs are documented at the parent company level; subsidiaries may operate their own developer programs.

providers.name: IControl Networks
providers.description: IControl Networks was a smart-home and home-security platform company (OpenHome / Connect, Piper) backed by Kleiner Perkins. It was acquired by Comcast in 2017 (the platform underpinned Xfinity Home) with its residential SaaS business sold to Alarm.com; it no longer operates as an independent entity. Enrichment probe (2026-07-20): the icontrol.com domain no longer serves a website and is now delegated to Comcast nameservers (dns10x.comcast.net); icontrolnetworks.com, developer.icontrol.com, and api.icontrol.com do not resolve. No live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists to harvest. Sector: hardtech / IoT.

providers.name: Illusive Networks
providers.description: Illusive Networks was a cybersecurity company specializing in deception technology and identity threat detection and response (ITDR) — discovering and remediating identity vulnerabilities and detecting attacker lateral movement across on-premises and cloud environments using deceptive traps and agentless deception tactics. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Innovation Endeavors, TPG and others, the company was acquired by Proofpoint in December 2022. Its technology now ships as Proofpoint Identity Threat Defense (previously Illusive); the standalone illusive.com property redirects to Proofpoint and the company no longer operates an independent developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Impossible Aerospace
providers.description: Impossible Aerospace is a deep-tech aerospace hardware company founded in 2016 by Spencer Gore in Santa Clara, California. It builds the US-1, a long-range all-electric quadcopter whose lithium-ion cells form part of the airframe structure, giving it up to roughly two hours of flight time for aerial imaging, surveillance, and public-safety missions with law enforcement and first responders. The US-1 runs the third-party Auterion OS flight stack (built on the PX4 open autopilot). The company was later acquired and operates as a small team. providers.description: Kiva Software Corporation was a pioneer of the internet application server, founded in May 1994 by chairman and CEO Keng Lim and headquartered in Mountain View, California. The product line comprised the Kiva Enterprise Server (deployment and management runtime), the Kiva Application Builder (graphical development tool), and the Kiva SDK with Java and C++ foundation classes; the company also ran the Kiva Enterprise Alliance Program (KEAP) for end-to-end partner solutions. Customers included Bank of America, E-Trade, Travelocity, Internet Shopping Network, Hong Kong Telecom, and Pacific Bell Internet. Kiva raised roughly $13.9 million across two rounds from Weiss Peck & Greer, Greylock, Discovery Ventures, Sippl MacDonald Ventures, Norwest Venture Capital, and Trinity Ventures, and is listed in the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio as a 1996 early-stage investment. In December 1997 Netscape Communications acquired Kiva for approximately $180 million in stock (6.3 million Netscape shares), and the Kiva Enterprise Server became the Netscape Application Server — which went on to become the iPlanet Application Server under the AOL/Netscape–Sun Microsystems alliance, then Sun ONE Application Server and Sun Java System Application Server. Kiva has not operated independently since 1997, published no public developer API in the modern sense, and has no live web presence today (the historical www.kivasoft.com domain is now parked and listed for sale). This profile is retained as a historical Lightspeed and Trinity Ventures portfolio record — there is no active developer surface to enrich.

The company is backed by Y Combinator, NATO DIANA, the UK Defence and Security Accelerator, and the Royal Academy of Engineering. As of this enrichment pass Milliray publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — it is a hardware/defense provider without a programmable interface.

Its flagship product is Mylea, a mycelium-based leather-like material, alongside Biobo binder board, MYCL Composite for architecture and interior design, and Mylea Sea, a seaweed-based biopolymer. A certified B Corp and Good Design Award winner backed by 500 Global and the Unreasonable Group, MYCL sells physical materials and finished goods rather than software; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Myhero
providers.description: TradeHero (operated by My Manisku Pte Ltd, Singapore) is a gamified virtual stock-trading and social-investing mobile app. Users start with 100,000 virtual dollars to practice trading risk-free across 28 stock exchanges and 10 currency pairs, follow and copy validated top traders, learn through a short-tutorial investing academy, and compete on cash-prize leaderboards backed by real-time market data. Founded by former Wall Street trading-platform and Electronic Arts mobile-gaming veterans, and backed by venture firms including 500 Global, KPCB China, and IPV Capital. The public surface is a consumer mobile app and marketing site; no developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published.

providers.name: MyNewPlace

providers.description: MySale Group PLC is a former AIM-listed online retailer that operated flash-sale and outlet e-commerce marketplaces across Australia, New Zealand and Southeast Asia under brands including MySale, OzSale, BuyInvite and Cocosa. The group was delisted and its corporate operations wound down; the surviving consumer brand, OzSale (ozsale.com.au), now runs as a Shopify-hosted storefront. providers.name: Narrative Science
providers.description: Narrative Science was a Chicago-based artificial-intelligence company known for its Quill natural-language-generation (NLG) platform, which automatically turned structured data into written narratives and data stories. There is no independent public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface remaining to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical/acquisition record.

providers.name: Neolane
providers.description: Neolane was a marketing automation and cross-channel campaign management company, backed by Battery Ventures, that Adobe acquired in 2013 for roughly $600M and rebranded as Adobe Campaign. The former neolane.com domain now 301-redirects to Adobe's Campaign product page, and the company no longer operates an independent developer portal, API, or artifact surface of its own. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; its live API footprint, if any, belongs to Adobe Campaign rather than a standalone Neolane brand.

providers.name: Neon Wild
providers.description: Neon Wild is a personalized children's entertainment platform backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) through its SPEEDRUN games program. Founded in New York by Troy Kirwin, it uses AI to transform a child's likeness into the hero of interactive digital books and narrative experiences distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface, and its former neonwild.com Squarespace site has expired. This profile remains a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nextbite
providers.description: Nextbite is a virtual-restaurant / ghost-kitchen company that operates delivery-only food brands out of existing restaurant kitchens, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It reaches consumers through third-party delivery marketplaces rather than a public developer platform; its sister restaurant-ordering-aggregation product Ordermark has since merged into UrbanPiper (a DoorDash Preferred Integrations Partner). As of this enrichment pass Nextbite publishes only a thin marketing website (nextbite.com, "We Put Food on The Table") and exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Nicira Networks
providers.description: Nicira Networks was a software-defined networking (SDN) and network virtualization pioneer founded in 2007 out of research by Martin Casado, Nick McKeown, and Scott Shenker on OpenFlow. Its Network Virtualization Platform (NVP) decoupled virtual networks from underlying physical hardware. VMware acquired Nicira on August 24, 2012 for approximately $1.26 billion; the technology was folded into VMware vSwitch and relaunched as VMware NSX in 2013, and VMware was itself acquired by Broadcom in November 2023. Nicira no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no first-party developer portal or API. Its only historical API footprint is the third-party Nicira NVP plugin integrated into Apache CloudStack. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of a16z and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Nizthewiz
providers.description: NizTheWiz Technology Sdn Bhd is a Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia based logistics startup founded in 2015 that operates a crowd-sourced, on-demand same-day local courier and delivery platform. Its consumer mobile app connects senders with a crowd-sourced fleet of couriers and provides live GPS tracking and full last-mile transparency across the delivery lifecycle. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass NizTheWiz publishes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs — its product is a consumer-facing courier app rather than a developer platform, so there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: NOD Games
providers.description: NOD Games is a Seoul-based blockchain game studio founded in 2019 by CEO Chanki Lee, building entertaining game content and open, player-owned game platforms where gamers and communities own and trade in-game digital assets as NFTs. Its marquee titles are League of Kingdoms, a free-to-play 4X MMO strategy game with tradable Land NFTs and the LOKA token, and Crypto Sword & Magic, an RPG whose heroes, equipment, and pets are recorded on-chain with game logic running in smart contracts. The company is backed by a16z crypto. As of this enrichment pass NOD Games publishes no first-party developer program, public API, SDK, or GitHub organization; its official domain nodgames.com resolves to an unconfigured Wix parking page and the League of Kingdoms domain no longer resolves, so there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Noise & Vibration Technologies
providers.description: Noise & Vibration Technologies (NVT Group) is a Battery Ventures-backed platform of test-and-measurement companies that design, manufacture, and support equipment for measuring, simulating, and analyzing vibration, noise, shock, and other environmental variables. Its operating brands include Data Physics (SignalCalc dynamic signal analyzers and vibration controllers), Team Corporation (electrodynamic and hydraulic shakers), and Lansmont (package and product-testing systems), serving aerospace, defense, commercial space, automotive, and industrial customers worldwide. The company ships hardware and desktop analysis/control software rather than any public web API, REST service, SDK, or developer portal, so it has no programmable API surface for the API Evangelist network at this time.

It was a leader in premium marine GPS/chartplotter hardware and was acquired by Brunswick Corporation in December 2002 to form Brunswick New Technologies, and later sold to Navico in 2007. It is a defunct hardware company with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface; the enrichment pipeline found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: NovaSparks
providers.description: NovaSparks builds ultra-low-latency FPGA market data solutions for banks, trading firms, and electronic markets. Its NovaTick ticker plant, delivered as a hardware appliance or PCIe card, normalizes and distributes real-time feeds across global equities, options (OPRA), and other asset classes with deterministic nanosecond latency. Integration is via a proprietary ultra-low-latency C++ Software API and the NovaSparks Wire Format (NSWF), a normalized message protocol whose full specification is provided to banks and trading firms under NDA rather than published publicly. NovaSparks is now part of Exegy. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech.

providers.name: Novira Therapeutics
providers.description: Novira Therapeutics was a biopharmaceutical company developing direct-acting antivirals for chronic hepatitis B (HBV), notably HBV capsid assembly modulators. It was acquired by Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) in 2015 and no longer operates as an independent entity. Its domain (noviratherapeutics.com) is now run on Johnson & Johnson DNS and mail infrastructure with no public website, developer portal, or API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners; the enrichment pipeline confirms there is no API or developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: Nse-india
providers.description: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), operating at nseindia.com, is one of the world's largest stock exchanges by number of trades and derivatives contracts, headquartered in Mumbai. It runs electronic equity, derivatives, debt, and currency markets, publishes market data and corporate filings, and maintains the Nifty family of indices via NSE Indices. NSE exposes market data primarily through licensed data feeds and the undocumented endpoints powering nseindia.com rather than a published public developer API program; this profile was surfaced as an enrichment lead and has no documented public REST API surface at this time.

providers.name: Nu Skin Enterprises
providers.description: Nu Skin Enterprises is a global multilevel marketing company that develops and distributes personal care products and dietary supplements through a network of independent distributors. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: Nubis
providers.description: Nubis Communications is a co-packaged optics (CPO) and silicon-photonics semiconductor startup building high-density, low-power optical interconnects for AI, machine-learning, and hyperscale data-center systems. Its technology places optics directly next to switch and accelerator ASICs to move data at very high bandwidth with dramatically lower energy per bit than pluggable optics. The company (originally at nubis-inc.com) has been absorbed into Ciena, whose optics-for-co-packaged-applications product line now carries the work; the former Nubis domain redirects to Ciena. As a fabless hardware / photonics-IP company it exposes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so no API artifacts apply to this record.

providers.name: Numbersstation

providers.name: Numerify
providers.description: Numerify was an IT business analytics company that provided a cloud-based System of Intelligence for IT operations, applying AI and machine learning to data from ITSM, DevOps, and application-performance tools to predict change risk, reduce incidents, and improve software delivery. Numerify was acquired by Digital.ai in 2020, and its capabilities now live inside Digital.ai's Change Risk Prediction / Intelligence product line. The standalone numerify.com domain 301-redirects to digital.ai, and the company publishes no independent public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Nutcracker Therapeutics
providers.description: Nutcracker Therapeutics was an RNA therapeutics company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Emeryville, California, operating as a contract research, development and manufacturing organization (CRDMO) for RNA-based medicines. Its ACORN platform compressed RNA drug manufacturing onto single-use microfluidic biochips, and its NMU-Symphony system targeted on-demand, individualized production of personalized RNA therapeutics. The company raised more than $200 million across Series A through C rounds led by ARCH Venture Partners and others. Its business was laboratory instrumentation and GMP biomanufacturing services, not software, and it never published a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification. In December 2025 the company was acquired by Medici Therapeutics, the oncology platform formed by ARCH Venture Partners and the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy. Its corporate site at nutcrackerx.com went dark shortly afterwards and now returns a shared hosting placeholder.

Its proprietary nWayPlay engine powers fast-paced cross-platform multiplayer across mobile, PC, and console. nWay was surfaced as a portfolio lead of cowboy-ventures. providers.name: Octarine

Backed by Accel and Samsung NEXT, Octarine was acquired by VMware in May 2020 and its technology was folded into VMware Carbon Black Cloud and the Tanzu portfolio to deliver Kubernetes and container security. As an independent company Octarine no longer operates a public developer or API surface; its former domain octarinesec.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company / acquisition record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Oddup
providers.description: Oddup (now operating as Oddup Markets) is a Singapore-based platform founded in 2015 by James Giancotti. It began as a data-driven startup-rating and intelligence service — a 500 Global portfolio company scoring startups and crypto projects — and has since pivoted to prediction markets, letting users trade on real-world outcomes across crypto, FX, indices, and commodities using a distinctive Yes / No / Maybe outcome model. The current product is a client-side single-page web application hosted on Vercel at oddup.app (and oddup.com). As of this enrichment pass the live site is geo-restricted (HTTP 451, x-blocked-country: US) and exposes no public developer, API, documentation, or .well-known surface — no OpenAPI, no API subdomains, and no published packages were discoverable. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe only; it will be re-enriched if a public API surface appears.

providers.name: OGSystems
providers.description: OGSystems was a geospatial intelligence, data analytics, and advanced technology company based in Chantilly, Virginia, serving the United States intelligence community and Department of Defense with threat analytics, machine learning, and geospatial exploitation solutions. The company was acquired by Parsons Corporation in 2019 and folded into Parsons' national security and intelligence portfolio. Its former domain (ogsystems.com) now redirects to parsons.com, and it maintains no independent public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity/lead record surfaced from VC-portfolio data; there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.description: Old Town Media is a New York City media consulting and investment firm founded in 2017 by journalists Tom McGeveran and Josh Benson together with media operations executive Katherine Lehr. The firm helps launch and grow journalist-founded news organizations (The Colorado Sun, Block Club Chicago, Documented), consults with established media companies (Chalkbeat, The Marshall Project, Medium) on revenue and sustainability, brokers media-technology partnerships, and runs a venture fund for early-stage media investments. providers.name: Omen
providers.description: Omen (omen.ai) delivers real-time asset intelligence through continuous fluid analysis, monitoring the health of mission-critical machinery in data centers and heavy industry. Its two offerings are a non-invasive permanent sensor that attaches to equipment for continuous, automated fluid (oil, coolant, water) analysis and real-time health tracking, and a portable canister lab that performs on-site, off-site, and field spectroscopic testing. The platform detects wear, contamination, and degradation before failures occur, targeting the machines the world depends on. Backed by CRV. As of this enrichment pass Omen publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures company identity only.

OneASP delivered runtime application self-protection (RASP) for web applications, and was also marketed internationally under the OneRASP brand. As of enrichment (2026-07), no standalone OneASP developer portal, public API, or SDK surface resolves - the oneasp.com brand domain no longer resolves and OneASP appears to be a legacy/absorbed product line of the parent OneAPM platform.

providers.name: oneNav
providers.description: oneNav is a fabless GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) semiconductor company building the next generation of mobile positioning. Its L5-direct receiver acquires and tracks on the modern L5 satellite band without legacy L1 aiding, delivering higher location accuracy in urban canyons and far greater resilience to GPS jamming and spoofing, in half the RF size, power and cost of hybrid L1+L5 solutions. Founded in 2019 (Steve Poizner, Paul McBurney) with offices in Sunnyvale, CA and Tampere, Finland, oneNav targets smartphones, wearables, IoT trackers, defense and emergency services. It is backed by GV, Norwest Venture Partners and GSR Ventures. oneNav is a hardware/silicon company and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: opsmatic
providers.description: Opsmatic was a San Francisco-based infrastructure monitoring startup founded in 2013 that delivered a cloud service for real-time visibility into configuration changes and configuration "drift" across dynamic cloud infrastructure, alerting DevOps and operations teams so they could troubleshoot and reduce downtime. New Relic acquired Opsmatic in November 2015 to enter the infrastructure monitoring market, and the company no longer operates as an independent entity. The opsmatic.com domain now redirects to newrelic.com and there is no live independent developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. This record is retained as a historical VC-portfolio profile.

The company produced launch vehicles, satellites, missiles, ammunition, precision-guided munitions, rocket motors, and the Cygnus spacecraft for ISS resupply before being acquired by Northrop Grumman on June 6, 2018 and rebranded as Northrop Grumman Innovation Systems.

providers.description: Paragon Solutions Ltd is an Israeli cyber-intelligence and surveillance software vendor founded in 2019 in Tel Aviv by former Unit 8200 commander Ehud Schneorson together with Idan Nurick, Igor Bogudlov and Liad Avraham, with Ehud Barak among its backers. Its flagship product, Graphite, is mobile-device intelligence software marketed to government and law-enforcement agencies. Battery Ventures took an early-stage stake in the company; in 2024 Paragon was acquired by AE Industrial Partners and merged with the US cybersecurity firm RED Lattice. Surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead, Paragon operates no public developer platform: it publishes no API, SDKs, documentation, or self-service sign-up, and its domain (paragonsolutions.io) currently serves no website. providers.name: Parative
providers.description: Parative was an AI-powered customer intelligence / customer behavior platform (founded 2017, Boston, MA) that surfaced product-usage signals to define ICP fit, forecast net revenue retention, and predict churn, renewal, and expansion for go-to-market and customer success teams. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures (sector: ai-apps). One first-party artifact outlives the domain — the npm package @parative/library, the compiled front-end of the Parative app, last published 2024-08-07. providers.name: Parhelion Studio Co.

Founded by a team that met at the University of Michigan, the studio builds live-service anime mobile and PC games — including gacha titles and the tactical anime trading card game Echoes of Astra — publishing across Steam, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. Their mission is to make anime a global medium and to create long-lasting IP through games and technology. Parhelion Studio is a consumer entertainment company; a public, scan of its website (parhelion.gg), app-store listings, and the a16z Speedrun profile found no developer-facing API, SDK, MCP server, webhook, or other machine-readable API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead and enriched to confirm it has no public API program at this time.

It combines expertise in cell cultivation, bioprocessing, and culinary development to produce cultivated meat at scale, and in October 2025 became the first European company granted regulatory approval for cultivated protein. Its culinary brand, Gourmey, focuses on premium cultivated meats co-developed with Michelin-starred chefs. providers.name: Product Backlog
providers.description: A product backlog is a prioritized list of features, enhancements, and fixes that serves as the single source of requirements for product development. It is most commonly used in Agile and Scrum methodologies, where the product owner is responsible for ordering items based on business value, customer feedback, dependencies, and technical considerations. The backlog evolves continuously as new requirements emerge and priorities shift, providing development teams with a clear, ordered view of upcoming work.

providers.name: Product Backlog Items
providers.description: Product backlog items (PBIs) are the individual units of work that make up a product backlog, representing features, enhancements, bug fixes, and technical tasks in Agile and Scrum methodologies. Each PBI typically includes a description, acceptance criteria, priority, and an estimate of effort. PBIs are continuously refined through grooming and refinement sessions, and the highest-priority items are pulled into sprints by development teams to be implemented and delivered as increments of working software.

providers.name: Project Management Methodology
providers.description: A systematic approach or framework for planning, executing, and controlling projects to achieve specific goals within defined constraints of time, budget, and resources. It helps teams plan, execute, and deliver projects on time and within scope through structured methodologies.

providers.name: Pub/Sub
providers.description: A messaging pattern where publishers send messages to topics without knowledge of subscribers, and subscribers receive messages from topics they're interested in, enabling asynchronous and decoupled communication between services. Modern distributed architectures rely on it to coordinate workloads across multiple nodes and regions.
