providers.description: Skypunk is an independent game studio headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2021 to build new science-fiction multiplayer games. The studio is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and has raised approximately $750K in early funding. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Skypunk is a consumer game developer, not an API producer: its public presence is a studio marketing site and it publishes no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or any external API surface at this time.

providers.name: Smart Reno
providers.description: Smart Reno is a Montreal-based home-renovation marketplace, founded in 2012 by Andrei Uglar, that connects homeowners with qualified, available local contractors. Homeowners post a project and receive up to three competing quotes from vetted renovation professionals through a proprietary contractor-matching platform. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), Anges Quebec, and BDC, Smart Reno was acquired by RBC Ventures in 2019 and now operates its consumer marketplace under the soumissionrenovation.ca brand across Quebec, Ontario, and Alberta. The company exposes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or webhook surface; smartreno.com 301-redirects to the successor site and no /.well-known discovery documents were found.

providers.name: Soba
providers.description: Soba is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners, point-nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Socialee
providers.description: Socialee is a beauty shopping platform that blends social media with e-commerce, letting shoppers discover and buy products through shoppable videos, write reviews, and earn rewards as creators. Its catalog spans makeup, skincare, fragrance, haircare, and bath & body, with next-day delivery and 7-day returns. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; an enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public API, developer portal, or .well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Soha Systems
providers.description: Soha Systems was a cloud-delivered secure application access company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California. Its "Soha Cloud" service let enterprises grant users and third parties fast, secure, per-application access to internal apps without a traditional VPN, an early software-defined perimeter / zero-trust network access (ZTNA) approach. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Menlo Ventures, and Cervin Ventures, Soha Systems was acquired by Akamai Technologies in October 2016, and its technology became the basis for Akamai Enterprise Application Access (EAA). The company no longer operates independently and publishes no standalone developer portal, documentation, or public API; its former domain (soha.io) now resolves only to Akamai edge infrastructure and serves no content.

providers.name: Sonera
providers.description: Sonera is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of amplify-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ai-ml. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Spaceium
providers.description: Spaceium is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of initialized-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: unknown. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Speedlancer
providers.description: Speedlancer is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Spitab
providers.description: Spitab is a digital platform providing API-based services. Limited public documentation is available; this profile documents what is publicly known about the provider and will be updated as more information becomes available.

providers.name: Springpath
providers.description: Springpath Inc. was a Sunnyvale, California hyperconverged infrastructure startup, backed by Redpoint Ventures, whose distributed data-platform technology became the basis for Cisco HyperFlex Systems. Cisco moved to acquire the company (announced 2016) and folded its software into the HyperFlex product line. Cisco announced the discontinuation of HyperFlex infrastructure products in September 2023, and Springpath no longer operates as an independent company. The springpathinc.com domain is now served by Cisco nameservers and no longer hosts a live website, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an historical/acquired-company record; there is no independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Stabilitas
providers.description: Stabilitas was a Techstars-backed crisis and risk-intelligence startup whose stabilitas.io domain now issues a 301 redirect to crisis24.com/lp/onsolve. The company was absorbed into OnSolve, which is today part of Crisis24 (a GardaWorld company) providing critical event management, mass notification, travel risk, and security intelligence. Stabilitas no longer operates as an independent brand and exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal of its own. This profile is retained as an acquired/defunct portfolio lead; there is no standalone API surface left to enrich.

providers.name: Star Analytics
providers.description: Star Analytics is a business-intelligence software company described as a market leader in process automation and application integration across hybrid computing environments, with products built to address the automation and integration requirements of business intelligence software. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public developer platform, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; the primary domain (staranalytics.com) resolves to a parking IP and does not serve HTTPS, consistent with a legacy company that is no longer independently operating.

providers.name: Storemaven
providers.description: Storemaven was an app-store-optimization (ASO) and app-marketing platform founded in Tel Aviv in 2015 that pioneered App Store / Google Play A/B testing of icons, screenshots and videos using predictive, machine-learning-driven creative testing to lift install conversion rates for mobile app publishers. It was acquired by Zynga (Take-Two) in September 2022 and folded into the company's growth org, now operating as "mavens, a Zynga company." Storemaven shipped a login-gated SaaS dashboard and published no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal; the original storemaven.com domain has since lapsed and been repurposed into an unrelated third-party review site. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead with no independent API surface.

providers.name: Storia Originals
providers.description: Storia Originals, Inc. (doing business as Storiaverse) was a Los Angeles-based consumer mobile entertainment startup founded in 2023 by Agnes Kozera and David Kierzkowski. Its Storiaverse app pioneered a patent-pending "read-watch" format blending short-form reading, animation, and audio, connecting writers and animators to publish and monetize original stories across sci-fi, fantasy, horror, mystery, and comedy, including adaptations of HarperCollins titles. It raised a pre-seed round led by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; both its marketing site (storia.io) and its iOS/Android app store listings are no longer reachable (all HTTP 404), indicating the product is inactive or has been wound down.

providers.name: Stratim
providers.description: Stratim (originally incorporated as Zirx in 2014, rebranded to Stratim in 2017) was a San Francisco-based SaaS company that built an enterprise fleet-operations and logistics platform for transportation companies, autonomous-vehicle operators, and urban fleets. Its three product lines were the Stratim Platform (fleet operations software), the Stratim Exchange (on-the-ground vendor fulfillment), and the Stratim Marketplace (fleet-owner/vendor transactions), and it advertised API access, a workforce app, processing-engine integration, and SMS updates. Founded by Shmulik Fishman and Sean Behr and backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures ($36.4M raised), Stratim was acquired by ACV Auctions in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the stratim.com domain is held in custodial parking (CSC Corporate Domains) with no live website, developer portal, documentation, or reachable API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: StrikeAd
providers.description: StrikeAd was a mobile advertising technology company, founded in New York City in 2010 and backed by Uncork Capital, that built Fusion - one of the first demand-side platforms (DSPs) built specifically for mobile programmatic advertising. Sizmek Inc. completed its acquisition of StrikeAd for approximately $11.7 million in May 2015 and folded the platform into Sizmek MDX; Sizmek itself was subsequently broken up, with its ad server going to Amazon and its DSP and DMP to Zeta Global. The StrikeAd brand no longer operates. Its primary domain (strikead.com) is now a parked domain on GoDaddy nameservers that answers every request - homepage, /.well-known/ discovery paths, and common contract paths alike - with the same 114-byte HTML lander redirect to /lander, confirmed against a negative-control path. The api., docs. and developer. subdomains do not resolve, and the github.com/strikead organization is named "ex-StrikeAd" and has zero public repositories. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API surface exists.

providers.name: SwiftStack
providers.description: SwiftStack was a software-defined object and cloud storage company whose data platform managed unstructured data at scale across private data centers and public clouds using a distributed, shared-nothing architecture built on OpenStack Swift, targeting AI, deep learning, and large-dataset workloads. NVIDIA acquired SwiftStack in 2020; the data platform is no longer available for sale and only existing-customer support and portal resources remain. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed there is no active public API, developer portal, or SDK surface for the discontinued product.

providers.name: Symbio Robotics
providers.description: Symbio Robotics is an AI industrial-automation company founded in 2014 and based in Emeryville, California. Its flagship product, SymbioDCS, is a robot-agnostic middleware and Python programming framework that lets automation teams build, deploy, and continuously improve AI-driven assembly applications on existing factory robots. Symbio has publicly worked with automakers including Ford, Nissan, and Toyota to speed transmission and vehicle assembly. SymbioDCS is deployed on-premises inside manufacturing lines rather than offered as a public web API; as of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, SDK/package registry presence, MCP server, or API surface, and its former web domains (symb.io, symbiorobotics.com) now resolve to parked/for-sale landing pages.

providers.name: Synthetic Design Lab
providers.description: Synthetic Design Lab is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2022 developing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for cancer therapy. Its SYNTHBODY platform and SYNTHBODY Engine engineer multispecific biologics with layered BIO-LOGIC control mechanisms and targeted payload delivery reported at 10x or more versus conventional ADCs. The company emerged from stealth in April 2025 with a $20M seed round led by Playground Global and Godfrey Capital, and is led by CEO Daniel S. Chen (formerly Global Head of Cancer Immunotherapy Development at Genentech) and CSO Ramesh Baliga. This is a therapeutics research company with no public API, SDK, or developer surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Syrup
providers.description: Syrup (Syrup Tech) is an AI-powered inventory optimization and demand-forecasting platform for retail and apparel brands. Its machine-learning decision-support engine combines transactional, marketing, and inventory data with external signals such as social trends and weather to recommend how brands produce, buy, and allocate inventory across omnichannel commerce, reducing stockouts and overproduction. Founded in 2021 by James Theuerkauf and Ferdinand Stockmann, Syrup raised a $17.5M Series A led by Accel and was acquired by Anaplan in September 2025; syrup.tech now redirects to anaplan.com. Syrup exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: t4game
providers.description: t4game (呈天游 / Bstonegames) is the brand of Beijing Chengtian Network Technology Co., Ltd., a Chinese online-game developer and operator founded in 2008 and headquartered in Beijing. The company designs, publishes, and operates mobile, PC, and web-based games — including titles such as 醉江湖online (Drunk Rivers and Lakes Online) and 诛神传奇/诛神online (Zhushen Online) — spanning role-playing, real-time strategy, and shooting genres. Its public presence at t4game.com is a consumer-facing game portal (player login, registration, and recharge), company and culture pages, a product catalog, game/media news, and recruitment listings. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, MCP server, or other machine-readable API surface could be found.

providers.name: Taascom
providers.description: Taascom (branded "The As A Service Company", taascom.com) is a San Jose, California company founded in 2019 that provides an IoT-based servitization SaaS platform helping equipment makers shift from transactional capex sales to recurring subscription, pay-per-use, and outcome-based revenue models. Its packaged offerings include Device-as-a-Service, Auto-Replenishment-as-a-Service, and Uptime-as-a-Service. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found a marketing-stage web presence only — no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or OpenAPI surface at the time of this pass.

providers.name: Tagomi
providers.description: Tagomi was an institutional-grade cryptocurrency prime brokerage founded in 2018 in New York that offered smart order routing and cross-exchange best-execution across 14+ digital-asset venues, a library of advanced trading algorithms, post-trade reporting, and one-click settlement and custody for professional and institutional investors. Coinbase acquired Tagomi in May 2020 in an all-stock deal (reported at roughly $70-100M) and folded it in as the foundation of Coinbase Prime. The tagomi.com domain now 301-redirects to Coinbase Prime, and no independent Tagomi API, developer portal, or documentation surface remains.

providers.name: Talasim
providers.description: Talasim was a Jordanian user-generated-content website that curated photographs of funny signs on cars, stores, and roads, positioned as an online comedy and self-expression channel. Backed by Seedcamp, it was acquired by the regional reviews-and-listings community Jeeran (Amman, Jordan) in March 2010, with its engineering team absorbed into Jeeran's localisation efforts. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer, API, or documentation surface; the referenced jeeran.com domain no longer serves a live site (TLS handshake failure). This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio stub and has been enriched to reflect its acquired, no-API status.

providers.name: Talking Computers
providers.description: Talking Computers is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building Facility, described as "The Workplace for AI" and delivering autonomous organizations for enterprises. The company deploys fleets of AI Infrastructure Engineers that collaborate over week-long time horizons, run hundreds of experiments in parallel, and learn from them to optimize customers' training and inference infrastructure to their specific workloads. Talking Computers reports partnering with companies to speed up GPU kernels to 6x state-of-the-art and to cut the latency of voice models to roughly half that of competitors. As of enrichment, the company is an early-stage two-person team and publishes only a marketing presence at talkingcomputers.ai (a single-page application); it exposes no public API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from verified public sources.

providers.name: Tallan
providers.description: Tallan was a Hartford, Connecticut technology consultancy, founded in 1985, that built custom Microsoft- and Azure-powered solutions — application modernization, e-commerce and web development, user experience, mobile, cloud, data, and AI/ML — for clients in manufacturing, consumer packaged goods, pharma, healthcare, and state and local government. In February 2023 Tallan was acquired by EY US and folded into EY's Microsoft services group; the tallan.com domain now 301-redirects to EY's Microsoft alliance page. Tallan operated as a professional-services consultancy and never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or event surface, so there is no API to enrich.

providers.name: Tandem
providers.description: Tandem is a virtual office for remote and distributed teams, backed by Y Combinator and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), that recreates the presence and spontaneity of an in-person office online. It shows who is available and who is in a conversation, and lets teammates drop into low-friction voice and video rooms with screen sharing, plus integrations with tools like Notion, GitHub, and Trello. Surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network, Tandem is a consumer/team collaboration product with app integrations but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal at the time of enrichment (verified 2026-07-21 against https://tandem.chat).

providers.name: Tapastic
providers.description: Tapastic is the former brand of Tapas, a digital storytelling platform (Tapas Entertainment, a Kakao company) that hosts webcomics and web novels across romance, fantasy, action, drama, and other genres. Readers access serialized episodes through a free-with-premium model using an in-app "Ink" currency, and creators publish original and user-generated stories via the creators.tapas.io publishing portal. The original tapastic.com domain has been retired and now rebrands to tapas.io. As of this enrichment pass the platform exposes only a consumer web/mobile application and a content-creator publishing surface; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, developer portal, or documented webhook/event surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and remains a lead in the API Evangelist network with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Tapshots
providers.description: Tapshot, Inc. (marketed as Videokits) is a Cupertino, California company founded in 2012 that builds a mobile-first video capture and survey platform. Its Videokits Pro apps guide users through structured "kits" of survey questions and shot lists to capture video interviews and NPS/demographic survey responses in the field, then upload them to a web portal for storage, transcoding, streaming, and analysis. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the public website (videokits.com) does not respond and no developer/API surface (OpenAPI, SDK, developer portal, or GitHub organization) could be found; the iOS/iPad app was last updated June 2023, indicating a dormant product.

providers.name: taptrip.co
providers.description: TapTrip (taptrip.co) was a UK-based self-serve business travel and expense booking platform for SMEs, founded in 2018 in Manchester and part of the Barclays Accelerator powered by Techstars. It let smaller businesses book and manage flights, hotels, rail, and ground transportation without a travel management company. TapTrip was acquired by TripStax in July 2022 and folded into the TripStax platform as an SME online-booking module for travel management companies; the standalone brand was absorbed. As of this enrichment pass the taptrip.co domain no longer hosts an active product — it resolves to a ParkingCrew domain-parking service and the TLS endpoint does not respond. No public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface was found for the standalone company.

providers.name: Taskeer
providers.description: Taskeer Holdings Limited is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Technion Seed
providers.description: Technion Seed is an early-stage Israeli technology incubator and seed investment vehicle jointly owned by four venture capital funds — Vertex Ventures Israel, Battery Ventures, SCP-Vitalife and ProSeed — together with the Technion Research & Development Foundation. Through Technion Seed these funds invest up to roughly $1,000,000 in high-market-potential, early-stage technological ideas and ventures emerging from and around the Technion, helping entrepreneurs prove the viability of their idea at a stage of very high uncertainty. It is an investment firm and incubator rather than an API producer, and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: tempow
providers.description: Tempow was a Paris-based startup (founded 2016) building software to improve Bluetooth audio connectivity, including an operating system for true-wireless earbuds and multi-device audio streaming licensed to chipset makers and Android device manufacturers such as Motorola and TCL. Backed by Balderton Capital and C4 Ventures, Tempow was acquired by Google in 2021. The company operated as a B2B embedded-software and licensing business and never published a public developer API. Its website (www.tempow.com) no longer resolves. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirms there is no live API surface.

providers.name: Tenet Industries
providers.description: Tenet Industries is a Swedish defense-technology startup founded in 2026 by Hugo Frisk, Fabian Andersson, and Emil Falk (students from KTH Royal Institute of Technology and the Stockholm School of Economics) building low-cost, mass-producible defense systems. Applying design-for-manufacturing and first-principles engineering, the company starts with strike/attack drones — a kamikaze quadcopter that assembles in two minutes with roughly half the parts of comparable systems — and extends the same hardware/software platform to loitering munitions, jammers, radars, and missile systems. Backed by Y Combinator ($500K). As a defense hardware manufacturer, Tenet Industries currently publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: The Inside
providers.description: The Inside is a direct-to-consumer, made-to-order home furnishings brand founded in 2017 by Christiane Lemieux and Britt Bunn, offering customizable upholstered furniture — sofas, chairs, beds, headboards, and decor — in 100+ fabrics and patterns. Backed by Canaan Partners along with Corigin Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Forerunner Ventures, and BAM Ventures, it was acquired by Havenly in February 2022. Surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network; during enrichment no public developer API, OpenAPI, or well-known metadata surface was found — theinside.com serves an e-commerce storefront with no documented programmatic interface.

providers.name: The Rounds
providers.description: The Rounds was a membership-based sustainable grocery and household-goods delivery startup (backed by a16z and Redpoint Ventures) built around reusable packaging and reducing single-use waste. The company has since been wound down and folded into Misfits Market — as of this enrichment pass https://www.therounds.co/ returns an HTTP 301 redirect to a Misfits Market "welcome-new-rounds" landing page ("Same Mission, More Groceries"). No developer portal, API, documentation, or public API surface was found; api./docs./developer.therounds.co do not resolve. This profile is retained as a network lead with an acquired/defunct status.

providers.name: Thistle Technologies
providers.description: Thistle Technologies provides security tools, libraries, and services for the developers who build connected and embedded devices. Founded by security veteran Window Snyder and backed by DCVC, the company offers a turnkey embedded-device security platform whose two headline products are the Thistle Update Solution (end-to-end over-the-air firmware and software updates for Embedded Linux on ARM/ARM64 and x86-64 as well as Infineon PSoC 6 microcontrollers) and Thistle Secure Boot Enablement (tools and services for enabling secure/verified boot with managed key handling and firmware signing on hardware such as Espressif ESP32, Infineon OPTIGA Trust M secure elements, and U-Boot targets including the Raspberry Pi 4 and BeagleBone). Thistle helps device makers add mechanisms that keep IoT and edge/AI hardware updatable and resistant to compromise without building the security infrastructure themselves. The offering is delivered as SDKs, libraries, and managed services integrated into a customer's device firmware rather than as a public web API.

providers.name: thorough
providers.description: thorough (透彻未来 / Thorough Future) is a China-based company surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its site at thorough.ai serves a Chinese-language single-page web application over HTTP only (HTTPS is unreachable at the time of this pass) and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification surface. This profile remains a lead awaiting a public developer surface.

providers.name: Three Squirrels
providers.description: Three Squirrels (三只松鼠) is a Chinese consumer snack company founded in 2012 by Zhang Liaoyuan and headquartered in Wuhu, Anhui Province. Positioned as one of China's first internet-native food brands, it sells nuts, seeds, dried fruits, baked goods, and other leisure snacks primarily through e-commerce channels (Tmall, JD.com, and its own storefronts) alongside a growing offline retail footprint. The company is publicly listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange ChiNext board (stock code 300783). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; as a consumer packaged-goods retailer it does not publish a public developer API, open platform, or API documentation. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Three Wheels United
providers.description: Three Wheels United is a fintech-driven electric vehicle financing company in India, founded in 2017 by Cedrick Tandong, Kevin Wervenbos, and Apurv Mehra. It works to remove the financial barriers to clean mobility by providing loans for two- and three-wheeler electric vehicles — starting with auto-rickshaws — disbursed through its RBI-registered NBFC lending partner Shabri Investments Private Limited. The company pairs credit with a mobile app that helps drivers manage their loans and connect to services, and reports over 4,000 vehicles financed, 20,000+ customers served, and thousands of tonnes of CO2 reduced across Bangalore, Mumbai, and the Delhi NCR (Noida) region. It is backed by Techstars, Delta Corp Holdings, Asian Development Bank Ventures, Microsoft, and other global investors, having raised roughly $10 million in Series A funding. It is a consumer-facing lender with no public developer program, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Tome
providers.description: Tome is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global, lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Trader Joe's
providers.description: An American chain of specialty grocery stores known for its unique private-label products, affordable prices, and quirky branding. Operates over 500 stores nationwide with a cult following for its curated selection of food and beverages.

providers.name: TRED
providers.description: TRED is a Seattle-based peer-to-peer online marketplace for buying and selling used cars, founded in 2011 and backed by Techstars, Maveron, Lowercase Capital, and Founders' Co-op. The platform let private buyers and sellers list vehicles, ask questions, schedule concierge-delivered test drives, and complete financed purchases online, with concierges compensated on customer-service reviews rather than sales commission. The tred.com domain now resolves to Cox Automotive / Autotrader infrastructure, indicating TRED has been absorbed into Cox Automotive; it operates as a consumer web product with no public developer program, API, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Trusted Insight
providers.description: Trusted Insight is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global, dcvc and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: tuhu
providers.description: Tuhu (途虎养车) is a Chinese online-to-offline automotive services platform founded in 2011 and headquartered in Shanghai. Through its app, website, and network of franchised and self-operated workshops it sells tires and provides car maintenance, repair, and related aftermarket services to consumers across China. Tuhu is publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (9690) and counts Qiming Venture Partners among its investors. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; enrichment probes found no public developer API, open platform, or developer portal.

providers.name: Turnstyle
providers.description: Turnstyle (Turnstyle Analytics) was a WiFi-marketing and customer-analytics platform for brick-and-mortar businesses, capturing guest WiFi logins to build customer profiles, segments, and automated re-marketing campaigns. It was a 500 Global portfolio company and was acquired by Yelp, becoming Yelp WiFi. As of this enrichment pass the product no longer operates independently - its domain getturnstyle.com now permanently redirects through app.yelpwifi.com to business.yelp.com (Yelp for Business). No standalone Turnstyle developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs are published; there is no independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Unified Grocers
providers.description: Unified Grocers was a retailer-owned wholesale grocery cooperative that supplied independent supermarkets primarily in the western United States. Founded through the 1999 merger of Certified Grocers of California and Shurfine International subsidiaries, the cooperative served over 3,000 retail stores with annual sales exceeding $4 billion. In 2017, Unified Grocers was acquired by SuperValu (now UNFI — United Natural Foods Inc.), ending its existence as an independent entity. As a result, Unified Grocers does not maintain a public API developer portal or externally accessible APIs.

providers.name: Upteam
providers.description: Upteam is a 500 Global portfolio company whose public web presence now points at Luxclusif: upteamco.com returns an HTTP 302 redirect to luxclusif.com, the B2B luxury resale platform offering wholesale distribution of pre-owned luxury goods, stock acquisition, and resale-as-a-service programs. Enrichment probing found no developer portal, no API documentation, and no machine-readable API artifacts on either the Upteam domain or the Luxclusif site; /.well-known/ discovery paths on upteamco.com return 403 and site paths redirect to Luxclusif.

providers.name: Uroam
providers.description: uRoam, Inc. (1999-2003) was a Canaan Partners-backed security company that built FirePass, a clientless SSL-VPN appliance for "radically simplified remote access" to enterprise applications from any browser. After merging with Filanet, uRoam was acquired by F5 Networks in July 2003 for $25 million in cash, and FirePass became F5's SSL VPN product line. The company is defunct; uroam.com now redirects to f5.com, and uRoam publishes no APIs or developer surface of its own.

providers.name: Vantus
providers.description: Vantus is a stub surfaced from the Mayfield portfolio page whose permalink slug is "vantus" but whose actual company is Vantive Corporation, a historic Mayfield "Milestone" enterprise investment described by Mayfield as call center software leaders. Vantive provided customer relationship management (CRM) software and existed as an independent corporation until its merger with PeopleSoft in 1999; PeopleSoft was later acquired by Oracle and the Vantive brand no longer exists. There is no current company website or API surface to enrich. Unrelated live domains (vantus.com, Vantus Medical Systems; vantus.io, a Spanish AI automation consultancy) are different companies and are intentionally not linked here.

providers.name: Vascular Therapies
providers.description: Vascular Therapies, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Cresskill, New Jersey, developing Sirogen, a proprietary sirolimus formulation delivered from a bioabsorbable collagen implant placed perivascularly at the time of surgery. The product is aimed at reducing surgical stenosis and improving arteriovenous fistula maturation and patency in end-stage renal disease patients who need hemodialysis vascular access. Sirolimus for dialysis vascular access carries FDA Fast Track status and Orphan Drug designation in both the United States and the European Union. The company ran the Phase 3 ACCESS trial (243 ESRD patients across 20 US sites) and the multinational Phase 3 ACCESS 2 trial, whose topline results presented in April 2025 did not meet the primary clinical fistula maturation endpoint. Vascular Therapies is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it ships a drug-device combination product through clinical trials and regulatory review, and publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: VendorHawk

providers.name: Golden 1 Credit Union

Founded in 1933 and open to all Californians, it offers consumer checking, savings, credit cards, auto and home loans, and digital banking, and holds the naming rights to Golden 1 Center in Sacramento. The company manufactures through tier-1 foundry and OSAT partners including UMC and its compound semiconductor subsidiary Wavetek on 6-inch and 8-inch wafers, is ISO 9001:2015 certified as of September 2025, and raised an $80M Series C led by MediaTek with participation from UMC Capital, Jabil, Foxconn, EDBI, CDIB-TEN Capital and the Qatar Investment Authority, following a $37M Series B in September 2024. providers.name: Manulife Bank

Launched in 1993 as Canada's first branchless (direct) bank — and the first federally regulated bank opened by an insurance company in Canada — it operates entirely through online banking, a mobile app, and telephone banking, with no physical branches. It is best known for the Manulife One all-in-one account, the Advantage Account, GICs, mortgages, and lines of credit that connect everyday banking and borrowing with long-term financial planning. Manulife Bank publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; no developer.manulifebank.ca host resolves, and the public site is bot-protected. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework — legislated in Budget 2024 and the Fall Economic Statement 2024, with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer — is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer financial data access today is voluntary and occurs through financial-data aggregators (Plaid, Flinks, MX) rather than a first-party bank API. The 2026-07-19 enrichment pass could not establish a verifiable identity for this company. The URL captured alongside the name in the 500 Global portfolio scrape, price.com, resolves to Price Technologies Inc. (Los Angeles, CA), a consumer cash-back, coupon and price-comparison platform that is a different company and is tracked separately; that pointer has therefore been removed rather than misattributed to Klutter. No company named Klutter with a matching profile could be confirmed in the 500 Global portfolio through public sources. The klutter.com domain is parked (it serves only a JavaScript redirect to a registrar lander), and the other public uses of the name are unrelated third parties: the Klutter Flutter/Kotlin Multiplatform framework by buijs-dev, a Komga comic-server client app for iOS and Android by Mark Winckle, and a music project. None of these are venture-backed companies. There is no developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, package, or specification surface to harvest for this entity, so no artifacts were generated.

providers.name: nip.io / sslip.io
providers.description: nip.io and sslip.io are a single wildcard-DNS service that resolves any hostname containing an embedded IP address to that address — 93-184-216-34.nip.io and 93.184.216.34.sslip.io both return 93.184.216.34, with no signup, no configuration and no records to create. providers.name: 10i Commerce Services Pvt Ltd (ShopX)
providers.description: 10i Commerce Services Pvt Ltd, trading as ShopX, was a Bengaluru-based Indian B2B e-commerce enabler founded in 2015 by Amit Sharma and Apoorva Jois. It built an assisted-commerce network for kirana stores and small SME retailers, giving them sourcing, supply-chain, logistics and working-capital credit through a retailer-facing mobile app, and layering consumer digital services on top of the same counter — fast moving consumer goods, mobile phones and accessories, mobile and DTH recharge, bus and flight booking, and utility bill payment. At its peak the company reported a network of more than 170,000 retail partners across 440-plus towns in 24 Indian states, serving over eight million end customers, and it later pivoted toward a Shopify-style storefront platform and a consumer super-app for bulk and retail buying. It raised roughly $56-60 million from backers including Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, Fung Strategic Holdings, Rajesh Ranavat and Kewal Nohria. In August 2022 ShopX announced it had ceased operations and filed for insolvency under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, stating the business had become unviable at scale given the low margin profile of B2B retail distribution; a public announcement of the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process followed on the IBBI register on 14 June 2023 and the registered entity (CIN U72200KA2015PTC079186) remains under CIRP. ShopX never operated a public developer program, API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification — its retailer and consumer products were mobile apps — and shopx.in has since become a GoDaddy parked domain. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: 1sm
providers.description: 1sm was a New York City revenue-operations (RevOps) analytics startup founded in 2020 by James Weitzman, Chris Lonardo and Jordan Josloff. It raised a $375K pre-seed round announced in July 2020 while in the Techstars NYC 2020 accelerator class, and pitched itself as the first no-code RevOps analytics platform — integrating a company's existing sales and marketing tools into one unified view of buyer personas and ideal customer profiles, with forward-looking analytics predicting which messaging would drive clicks, meetings and closed deals. The product never advanced past a public beta waitlist and no public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer program was ever shipped. As of September 2026 the company's former domain, 1sm.io, is registered to a third party — Nocode ltd of Paphos, Cyprus, the entity behind the Latenode automation platform — which republishes the archived July 2020 marketing page with injected affiliate copy and a "Contact the Domain Owner" footer, so that host is deliberately NOT wired as this company's Website pointer.

providers.name: 24/7 Real Media
providers.description: 24/7 Real Media was a New York digital advertising technology and media company formed when 24/7 Media merged with Real Media in 2001, acquiring the Open AdStream publisher ad server. Venture-backed (Trinity Ventures, Zero Stage Capital) before its NASDAQ listing, it was acquired by WPP Group in July 2007 for approximately $649 million ($11.75 per share) and run inside WPP Digital. The business was renamed 24/7 Media, then merged into WPP's programmatic arm Xaxis in January 2014, retiring the 24/7 brand; Open AdStream was rebranded Xaxis for Publishers and sold to AppNexus later that year. Xaxis itself was sunset into GroupM Nexus in January 2024. The company is defunct: it operates no website, developer portal, or public API surface today.

providers.name: 2duche
providers.description: 2Duche was a Chinese used-car marketing and trading service platform, backed by Qiming Venture Partners and recognized on the Red Herring Asia 100 in 2009. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company appears defunct — the apex domain 2duche.com does not resolve and www.2duche.com is unreachable, with no discoverable developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or public code repositories. No API artifacts could be produced without fabrication.

providers.name: 2nd Address
providers.description: 2nd Address (formerly Homesuite) was a Palo Alto, California online marketplace for monthly furnished rentals and corporate housing aimed at business travelers, relocating professionals, and corporate clients. Founded in 2014 and launched in 2015 as Homesuite, it rebranded to 2nd Address in November 2017. Operating as a licensed real estate broker, it listed thousands of furnished homes for extended, month-to-month stays across major U.S. cities, positioning itself against vacation- rental platforms by focusing on longer corporate stays. It raised venture funding from Battery Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, Foundation Capital, and Google Ventures. The company never published a public API or developer program, and its website (2ndaddress.com) is no longer operational, so this profile is an identity record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: 3com
providers.description: 3Com Corporation was a networking-technology pioneer founded in 1979 by Robert Metcalfe, the co-inventor of Ethernet, and colleagues; its name derived from "Computer, Communication, and Compatibility." 3Com built Ethernet network interface cards, switches, routers, and enterprise networking and security hardware, and at one point owned the Palm handheld computing business. An early Mayfield Fund portfolio investment (seed participation in 1981, alongside NEA, Venrock, and Sequoia), 3Com later operated the 3Com, H3C, and TippingPoint brands before being acquired by Hewlett-Packard in 2010 for roughly $2.7 billion, after which the standalone brand was wound down. This record is a historical company profile; 3Com no longer operates an independent developer portal, public API, or live product surface (the 3com.com domain now serves a placeholder page).

providers.name: 4C
providers.description: 4C — legally 4C Insights, Inc. — was a Chicago-based marketing intelligence and advertising technology company founded in 2011 by Northwestern University professor Alok Choudhary, building on his research into large-scale data mining and social signal. Its Scope "closed ecosystems platform" let brands, agencies and media companies discover cross-channel audience insights, plan and execute paid campaigns inside walled-garden environments — Facebook, Instagram, X/Twitter, Snapchat, LinkedIn, Pinterest and connected TV — and measure the results in one self-service tool, with data delivery out to third-party systems by API, email, SFTP or web query. The company raised roughly $26 million through a Series C, grew to about 160 people and ran offices in Chicago, New York, Seattle and Singapore. Mediaocean announced its acquisition of 4C in July 2020 (reported at approximately $150 million) and folded the product into Flashtalking by Mediaocean; after Mediaocean's later combination with Innovid, the 4C social-advertising surface now lives inside Innovid's social ads management product. 4C never operated a public developer program: it consumed the advertising APIs of the closed ecosystems it served rather than publishing one of its own, and today the 4cinsights.com domain serves no HTTPS listener and blanket-301s every path to the acquirer's site. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no 4C API surface to enrich.

providers.name: 4Info
providers.description: 4INFO, Inc. was a San Mateo (originally Palo Alto) California advertising-technology company founded in 2004 by Pankaj Shah and Zaw Thet. It began as an SMS content and alerting service — Nielsen called it the largest business-to-consumer SMS content provider in North America in 2008 — then pivoted in 2010 into mobile display advertising with the AdHaven platform, a mobile ad server, audience data-management and analytics stack sold to publishers, aggregators and national advertisers. Its later product was an identity graph: patented technology ("Systems and methods for statistically associating mobile devices to households") that statistically resolved mobile devices, set-top boxes and connected TVs back to a single household so brands could target and measure across screens. mBlox bought the legacy SMS business in 2015, and Cadent acquired the remaining company in January 2020, folding the identity and cross-screen targeting technology into Cadent's advanced-TV platform. 4INFO no longer operates as an independent company: 4info.com is retained for email only and publishes no A or AAAA record, so there is no website, developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract of any kind on any 4Info host, live or archived.

providers.name: 6 Wunderkinder
providers.description: 6 Wunderkinder (6Wunderkinder GmbH) was a Berlin-based software startup founded in 2010 that built Wunderlist, a popular cross-platform to-do list and task management application. The company shipped a public REST API for Wunderlist in 2013, along with webhooks and integrations such as Slack and Sunrise, and rebuilt its backend into roughly 60 microservices behind a single unified API. Backed by Earlybird and Sequoia Capital, 6 Wunderkinder was acquired by Microsoft in June 2015 for a reported US$100-200M. Microsoft folded the product into Microsoft To Do and discontinued Wunderlist on 6 May 2020. This profile is retained as a historical record; the company is defunct and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: 60dB
providers.description: 60dB was a personalized short-form audio and podcast application built by Tiny Garage Labs, founded in 2016 by John Ciancutti, Steve Henn, and Steve McLendon. The app curated and recommended short radio-style audio stories tailored to a listener's habits, and was available on iOS, Android, and the web as well as through Alexa, Android Auto, and CarPlay. It was backed by Bloomberg Beta, Khosla Ventures, and Rivet Ventures. Google acqui-hired the founding team in October 2017 and the 60dB service was shut down on November 10, 2017. The company is defunct and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable interface today; the 60db.com domain now resolves to a parked placeholder page. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 8sec
providers.description: 8SEC was a hybrid-casual and hyper-casual mobile game studio based in Lyon, France, founded in 2015 and later opening a second office in Paris. Over a ten-year run it published more than 90 free-to-play mobile games for iOS and Android — Jump Race!, Turbo Taxi, Trivia.io, Untie! and Human Puzzle among them — collectively driving roughly 50 million downloads, and positioned itself as a full-stack studio spanning game design, development and publishing. UK publisher Kwalee invested EUR 1.5 million in January 2024 and took over publishing duties across the entire 8SEC catalogue. THE STUDIO IS NOW CLOSED — the shutdown was reported in October 2025, with all seven staff, including cofounders Louis Croquet and Louis Giraud, seeking new roles. The company's own site at 8sec.games is no longer deployed — the domain resolves to OVHcloud shared hosting serving a "Site not installed" 404 behind a certificate that does not cover the hostname — and the Teamtailor careers page returns 404. 8SEC was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead; it never published a public developer API, SDK, machine-readable specification or documentation surface, and it no longer exists to publish one.

providers.name: 8Tracks
providers.description: 8tracks was a San Francisco-based internet radio and social music-streaming service that let people create and share handcrafted playlists ("mixes") of at least eight tracks, discover mixes by mood, activity, genre, and tag, and play them back through the web, iOS, and Android apps. Founded in 2008, it grew to more than eight million monthly listeners by 2014 before declining. 8tracks published a public REST API (v2/v3) that exposed mix discovery, playback token sessions, track skip/report events, and user likes/favorites, but stopped issuing new API keys in February 2015. The company ceased operations on December 31, 2019, briefly relaunched under BackBeat Inc. in April 2020, and the service has been inactive since. This profile documents the historical API surface and web properties.

providers.name: 99degrees Custom
providers.description: 99Degrees (99Degrees Custom, Inc.) is a Lawrence, Massachusetts contract apparel manufacturer founded in 2013 by Brenna Nan Schneider, operating out of the historic Everett Mills. It produces performance activewear, workwear, uniforms and technology-integrated apparel for global and growth-stage brands, and runs an R&D operation focused on Design for Manufacturing, rapid prototyping and applied research — including integrating sensors, electronics, robotics and hardware into textiles for wearable medical and industrial safety products. During the COVID-19 pandemic it pivoted its Lawrence floor to medical gowns and PPE. The company raised roughly $2.35M across four rounds, won the MIT Inclusive Innovation Competition top prize and MassChallenge's $100k Diamond Prize, and entered a manufacturing partnership with Reliable Source Industrial. 99Degrees is a physical-goods manufacturer, not a software company: no source, live or archived, shows it ever published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification. Its canonical host 99degreescustom.com lapsed and was re-registered by a domain broker on 2026-05-24; it now serves a "for sale" parking lander and is deliberately not wired as a Website pointer. This profile is retained as a historical record — there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: 99Dresses
providers.description: 99Dresses was a fashion resale and clothing-swap marketplace ("infinite closet") founded by Nikki Durkin, which went through Y Combinator and operated from roughly 2011 to June 2014 before shutting down. It offered a consumer web and mobile app for trading second-hand designer clothing; it never exposed a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. As of 2026 the 99dresses.com domain resolves to a "Launching Soon" parked placeholder with no live product or developer content. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no real API artifacts exist to harvest because the company is defunct.

providers.name: @Home Network
providers.description: @Home Network (Excite@Home) was a pioneering residential broadband internet service provider founded in 1995, backed by venture firm Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and cable operator TCI. It delivered high-speed cable internet access to consumers and merged with the Excite web portal in 1999 to form Excite@Home. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on October 1, 2001 and ceased operations by February 2002; it is defunct and operates no website, developer portal, or API today. This record is retained as a historical portfolio-company profile and has no live surface to enrich.

providers.name: A. Schulman
providers.description: A. Schulman was a global supplier of high-performance plastic compounds, composites, and powders used by manufacturers across packaging, automotive, electronics, and consumer goods industries. The company was acquired by LyondellBasell in 2018 and now operates as the Advanced Polymer Solutions division, continuing to supply engineered plastics, masterbatches, compounds, and specialty powders to global manufacturers.

providers.name: Abibaa
providers.description: Abibaa was a global online B2B/B2C/C2C e-marketplace headquartered in North Brunswick, New Jersey, founded around 2011-2012 and led by Benjamin Koufie Akomeah, built to help small and medium-sized businesses trade across borders through a multi-language buyer-and-seller marketplace. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist harvest backlog from a secondary-market (EquityZen) pre-IPO listing. As of the 2026-09-06 enrichment pass the company has no live web presence: abibaa.com is registered to the domain reseller TurnCommerce/NameBright and serves a HugeDomains "this domain is for sale" page, the Internet Archive holds no capture of a working site after March 2022, and no alternate company domain resolves. No API, developer program, documentation or machine-readable contract of any kind was found.

providers.name: abillion
providers.description: abillion was a Singapore-based social platform and mobile app for discovering and reviewing vegan, sustainable, and cruelty-free products across food, beauty, and fashion, pairing a large consumer review community with a rewards model that converted member reviews into donations to non-profits and animal sanctuaries. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. NOTE: as of July 2026 the abillion platform has officially shut down ("abillion is closing its doors"); the public site serves only a farewell notice and states member data is archived for six months before permanent deletion. No public developer program, API, or discovery surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Able
providers.description: Able was a San Francisco artificial-intelligence company for commercial lending, founded in 2020 by Diego Represas and Andrew Hurst and operating at able.ai. Its platform used computer vision, robotic process automation and machine learning to collect, read and categorize borrower documentation for high-value commercial loan transactions, generating transaction-aware document checklists, sending automated follow-up reminders to the borrowing team, and giving lenders, borrowers and third parties such as appraisers, guarantors and insurers a single collaborative workspace with per-document access controls. It sold to banks and lenders rather than to borrowers, exited stealth in June 2022 with a $20M Series A led by Canapi Ventures with participation from Human Capital, demonstrated at FinovateFall 2022, and advertised SOC 2 compliance. Moody's acquired Able in March 2024 and absorbed it into its lending technology portfolio alongside Numerated Growth Technologies. The able.ai and ableai.com domains are still registered to Moody's registrant entity MIS Quality Management Corp. through CSC Corporate Domains, but the web surface is decommissioned: https://www.able.ai/ presents no TLS certificate and fails every handshake, while the plain-HTTP listener on that host 301-redirects to Moody's Commercial Lending Solutions page. Able never published a developer portal, public API, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification; the archived site, whose last HTTP 200 homepage snapshot is 2024-03-28, carried only marketing, company, security, careers and legal pages. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Abound
providers.description: Abound was a US tax-compliance API company for platforms, marketplaces and fintechs serving the 1099 economy. Its v4 REST API covered the full information-return lifecycle: collecting Form W-9, W-8BEN and W-8BEN-E from payees, running real-time TIN verification against the IRS, then generating, filing, correcting, voiding and physically mailing Form 1099-NEC, 1099-MISC, 1099-K and 1099-INT to federal and state tax authorities. It also shipped drop-in UI components for payee onboarding, a 44-event webhook surface, and an official TypeScript SDK. Abound was acquired (announced November 2024) and the service has since been retired: the withabound.com DNS zone is fully de-delegated, the API and docs hosts no longer resolve, and the GitHub organization has been removed. This profile preserves the API surface, recovered from the first-party Fern API Definition shipped inside the official npm package.

providers.name: Academi
providers.description: ACADEMI was the 2011-2014 name of the American private military, security and training company founded on 26 December 1996 in North Carolina by Erik Prince and Al Clark as Blackwater. It was renamed Blackwater Worldwide in October 2007 after the Nisour Square shooting in Baghdad, then Xe Services LLC in February 2009. In December 2010 the training business and its Moyock, North Carolina campus - the largest private training facility in the United States - were bought by USTC Holdings, an investor consortium led by Forte Capital Advisors and Manhattan Strategic Ventures, ending Erik Prince's involvement, and the company was rebranded ACADEMI in December 2011 under chairman Red McCombs. In June 2014 Academi Training Center, LLC was merged with Triple Canopy, Constellis Ltd., Strategic Social, Tidewater Global Services, National Strategic Protective Services and International Development Solutions to form Constellis Holdings, which Apollo Global Management acquired in September 2016 and which is headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. The ACADEMI brand was retired in the merger: Constellis states on its own site that "Academi remains part of historical, legal, and contractual records, but Constellis does not operate under the Academi name", and the Moyock campus now trades as the Constellis Training Center. The business sells physical services - firearms, driving, maritime, K-9, UAS/C-UAS and advanced security and military training, protective security details, and logistics and complex program management for United States government customers - not software. It never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable API specification, and academi.com no longer serves a website: the domain is retained by Constellis for email only. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Academic Capital Exchange
providers.description: Academic Capital Exchange (ACE) was a Chicago, Illinois online peer-to-peer student loan marketplace founded in 2008 by Shawn Bercuson, built to link students to the financial support and professional guidance needed to succeed in the classroom and beyond by matching student borrowers directly with individual lenders rather than routing them through a bank or a federal loan servicer. It followed CapAlly, an earlier peer-to-peer student lending marketplace and social network the same founder started in 2007 and sold before taking it to market. ACE was a consumer-facing lending marketplace, not a developer platform: it never operated a developer portal, never published a machine-readable API contract, and never shipped client SDKs, and no GitHub organization under the company name exists. The company is no longer operating. Its host academiccapitalexchange.com is not merely offline but entirely unregistered — whois returns "No match" and DNS returns NXDOMAIN for the .com, .net, .co and .io labels — and the Internet Archive holds a single snapshot of the site, from February 2008. The only surviving public record of the company is a secondary-market listing page on EquityZen, which is a trading venue and not the company's own web presence, so it is deliberately not wired as a Website pointer. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: AcceleDent
providers.description: AcceleDent was the flagship product of OrthoAccel Technologies, Inc., a privately held medical-device company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Bellaire, Texas, outside Houston. AcceleDent is an FDA-cleared Class II device built around the company's patented SoftPulse Technology: a hands-free mouthpiece and activator that a patient bit down on for about twenty minutes a day, delivering gentle micropulses intended to speed bone remodeling during orthodontic treatment and reduce the discomfort of braces and clear aligners. The line ran through three generations — the original AcceleDent, AcceleDent Aura in 2013, and AcceleDent Optima, cleared by the FDA in 2017 — sold to orthodontists and dentists rather than direct to consumers, with an e-commerce ordering site at shop.acceledent.com for practices. The company raised roughly $63.1M across sixteen rounds, the last a Series C in January 2017, and a later debt-and-equity financing led by S3 Ventures. It was a physical medical-device business, not a software business: OrthoAccel never operated a developer program, never published an API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind, and shipped no client libraries to any package registry. OrthoAccel is now reported defunct — orthoaccel.com no longer resolves, and acceledent.com was re-registered on 2022-08-30 and today sits on Afternic name servers as a GoDaddy aftermarket "for sale" listing whose parking system answers HTTP 200 with an identical 114-byte HTML stub on every path, including every /.well-known/ and spec path. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Accelus
providers.description: Accelus was a Palm Beach Gardens, Florida medical device company formed in 2021 by the combination of Integrity Implants and Fusion Robotics, built around an "Adaptive Geometry" expandable-implant platform for minimally invasive spine surgery. Its products were the FlareHawk and Toro expandable interbody fusion systems for transforaminal, posterior and lateral lumbar interbody fusion, the LineSider minimally invasive pedicle screw system, and the Remi Robotic Navigation System, a table-mounted intra-operative navigation and robotics platform that guided instrumentation from 2D fluoroscopic or 3D imaging. The company raised roughly $32M from investors including Concord Health Partners, Symbiotic Capital, Eastward Capital Partners and Trog Hawley Capital. It sold the Remi robotic navigation assets to Alphatec Holdings for $55M in April 2023 and its remaining implant products and intellectual property — FlareHawk, Toro and LineSider — to Highridge Medical on 2 September 2025. Accelus sold surgical hardware and single-use implants to hospitals and surgeons, never operated a developer program, and published no public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification. Its only host, the WordPress marketing site accelusinc.com, is now a suspended cPanel hosting account that returns an "Account Suspended" page on every path behind a TLS certificate that expired on 2026-05-13, and no accelusinc.com subdomain resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Accompany
providers.description: Accompany was a relationship-intelligence startup that built people-and-company intelligence for executives, backed by Cowboy Ventures and CRV. It was acquired by Cisco (announced May 2018) and folded into Cisco's collaboration products; www.accompany.com is now a static acquisition-announcement page. Enrichment pass 2026-07-17 verified there is no live product, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or any /.well-known/ or /llms.txt surface (the host is an nginx catch-all returning the same parked HTML for every path). No API artifacts exist to harvest; retained as a defunct/acquired VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: ActEvolve
providers.description: ActEvolve Inc. (株式会社ActEvolve) was a Tokyo virtual-reality entertainment company incorporated on 9 August 2017 by Takuya Kato, a former Capcom game developer, together with other ex-game-industry engineers. In November 2018 it launched VARK, a VR live platform on which VTuber and virtual-artist performances — most visibly the long-running "Cinderella switch" series with hololive — were staged as ticketed, seat-based concerts for Meta Quest, Android and iOS, paid for with in-app VARK Coin. The company took strategic investment from KLab Inc. in August 2019, renamed itself VARK Inc. (株式会社VARK) on 1 May 2020 alongside a roughly ¥200M round from ANRI, raised a further ¥600M in May 2021, and diversified into the VARK SHORTS 3D animation tool and the STAR BLOOM liver-management agency, producing metaverse events for ANYCOLOR, Avex, KADOKAWA, COVER, Dwango, Shochiku and Meta. VARK was a consumer entertainment app rather than a platform business: it never operated a developer program, and no public API, SDK, webhook catalogue or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP manifest, agent card) was published on any of its hosts at any point — 1,812 archived URLs across vark.co.jp and its subdomains contain no /api, /developers, /docs, /openapi or /graphql path of any kind. The VARK metaverse service shut down on 4 March 2024 with same-day notice, refunding unused VARK Coin until 5 May 2024 under Japan's Payment Services Act; the free tier of VARK SHORTS ended on 30 September 2024; and in March 2025 the entire company was sold in an all-share transaction whose acquirer and terms were kept confidential, with founder Takuya Kato stepping down as representative director. This profile is retained as a historical record — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Acureon Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Acureon Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was a private United States biopharmaceutical company founded in 2006 in the western suburbs of Philadelphia (Berwyn / Wayne, Pennsylvania), focused on specialty therapeutics intended to improve patient outcomes in the hospital areas of infectious disease, transplant and intensive care, by acquiring and commercializing novel and late-stage development drugs. It was backed by Domain Associates, New Enterprise Associates and Alta Partners. The company is defunct: it closed in 2008, filed nothing with the SEC after a single 2006 Form D (CIK 0001365869), and its former domain acureonpharma.com was re-registered by an unrelated party in November 2022 and now serves an unrelated medical-loan content site. Acureon published no API, developer program, SDK or machine-readable specification while it operated, and there is no first-party surface left to profile.

providers.name: Ad Infuse
providers.description: Ad Infuse was a San Francisco mobile advertising technology company, founded in 2005, that dynamically inserted targeted mobile ads at the moment of content delivery using carrier subscriber demographic and behavioral data, selling to operators and brands including Orange, France Telecom and Procter & Gamble. It raised roughly $18M in venture funding and was acquired by mobile marketing firm Velti in May 2009; Velti itself collapsed in 2013 and sold its US, UK and India mobile marketing businesses to affiliates of Blackstone's GSO Capital Partners. The company is recorded as closed, no successor developer program carries the Ad Infuse brand, and its adinfuse.com domain was re-registered by an unrelated party in 2020 and serves no content.

providers.name: Adap.tv
providers.description: Adap.tv was a global programmatic video advertising platform founded around 2007 and backed by Redpoint Ventures, offering brands, agencies, and publishers tools for planning, executing, and measuring video ad campaigns programmatically, including real-time bidding (RTB), audience targeting, campaign management, and analytics through its Pathway video-intelligence platform. AOL acquired Adap.tv in September 2013 for approximately $405 million and folded its technology into ONE by AOL; the business subsequently passed to Verizon Media and then Yahoo. Adap.tv no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, public API, or SDKs; the www.adap.tv domain now 301-redirects to yahooinc.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Additive Intelligence
providers.description: Additive Intelligence was a Taipei, Taiwan startup applying machine learning to metal additive manufacturing. Its focus was the deformation and shrinkage that occurs when metal 3D printed parts are sintered — the expensive trial-and-error step that keeps metal AM from being fast, scalable and cost-competitive — and it paired hardware with software, holding provisional patents on a machine learning method, a proprietary infill topology, and a method for varying the density of infilled sections. The company was selected by Taiwan Tech Arena as one of 100 startups showcased at CES 2021, and its LinkedIn page carries the slogan "Additive manufacturing, exponential progress." No first-party surface survives: the website the company itself declares on LinkedIn, www.additiveintelligence.com, holds an active registration on Google Cloud DNS but publishes no A record, so no host — apex, www, api or docs — can be connected to at all. There is no developer portal, GitHub organization, published package, or API of any kind.

providers.name: Ader
providers.description: Ader is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: AdKnowledge
providers.description: Adknowledge, Inc. was a performance-based digital advertising and marketing technology holding company founded in 2004 by Scott Lynn and headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri. It ran a response-based targeting marketplace that connected advertisers to consumers across email, search, domains, social and app inventory, and it exposed a publisher-facing AdStation platform with an automated offer engine and creative library. Ben Legg served as Group CEO from 2011 to 2016, during which the company consolidated a long acquisition run (Super Rewards, Miva, Cubics, Lookery, Hydra Group, AdParlor, Giant Media, TriVu Media and others) into video and social units that were then sold off; AdParlor was subsequently acquired by Fluent in 2019. Third-party company registries now list Adknowledge as out of business. It entered the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub via kleiner-perkins. Contemporary integration write-ups confirm a historical RESTful AdStation / Publisher Platform API, but as of this enrichment pass no live surface survives: the adknowledge.com zone is still registered (AWS Route 53 nameservers, Microsoft 365 mail with an SPF record) yet publishes no A record for the apex or for www, api, developer, developers, docs or publisher, so there is no reachable website, developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification from which to harvest provider artifacts.

providers.name: adludio
providers.description: Adludio was an AI-powered interactive mobile advertising company founded in 2015 in London by Paul Coggins (originally Future Ad Labs). Its "Sensory Ad Science" platform built rich, interactive mobile ad units using touch, motion and haptic interaction, sold on a cost-per-engagement rather than CPM model, with brand clients including Nike, Microsoft, Coca-Cola and Estee Lauder. The company was backed by Balderton Capital. Adludio is now defunct: ADLUDIO LIMITED (UK company number 08227542) entered administration on 2024-08-23 and moved into creditors voluntary liquidation on 2025-08-28. The adludio.com domain 301-redirects to permate.com (an unrelated partnership-automation platform), no api/docs/developer subdomain resolves, and the residual adludio.webflow.io marketing mirror now returns 404. Adludio never published a public API, developer portal or machine-readable contract; the only surviving developer artifacts are four abandoned first-party npm packages under the @adludio scope (interactive ad-runtime building blocks, not API clients), none released since 2019.

providers.name: AdMeld
providers.description: AdMeld was a New York City advertising-technology company founded in 2007 (by Ben Barokas and Brian Adams) that ran a supply-side platform / private ad exchange helping premium digital publishers optimize and monetize their ad inventory (serving 500+ publishers including FOX News and The Weather Channel). Google acquired AdMeld in 2011 for roughly $400M and folded its technology into the DoubleClick Ad Exchange. AdMeld no longer operates as an independent product and exposes no standalone public API; the admeld.com domain now serves a Google-maintained legacy landing page for DoubleClick Ad Exchange (Google nameservers, Google-hosted).

providers.name: AdNectar
providers.description: AdNectar was a social advertising startup founded in 2008 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, that built a sponsored virtual-gifts network for Facebook applications and other social platforms. Its product let agencies and brands run campaigns in which consumers gave branded virtual gifts drawn from a catalog, paired with an embedded rich-media landing unit plus viral distribution, optimization, and reporting, so social-app publishers could monetize their virtual-goods inventory. The company raised roughly $5.3M from investors including Battery Ventures before being acqui-hired by Lockerz in November 2011. AdNectar is now defunct; its original adnectar.com domain is parked and serves no live product, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record and is not an active API provider. Note that the unrelated adnectar.io (performance marketing) and addnectar.com (Addnectar Solutions) are separate companies and are not associated with this entity.

providers.name: Advanced Bio Development
providers.description: Advanced Bio Development, Inc. (ABD) was a New Jersey beverage and dietary-supplement company headquartered in Englewood Cliffs, NJ. It developed, produced and marketed X2PERFORMANCE, a patented all-natural liquid sports-energy supplement built around ATP, created by founder Dr. Ralph Ferrante as an alternative to conventional performance stimulants, and distributed in part through Anheuser-Busch InBev's AB ONE network. The company sold consumer packaged goods through retail and e-commerce; software was never its product and it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or developer portal. In March 2023 X2 Performance merged into the Don't Quit! beverage platform — ABD and existing X2 investors became shareholders in Don't Quit!, X2 CEO Mark French took the same role at the combined company, and Keurig Dr Pepper remained majority owner — after which the X2 brand was wound down. The brand domain x2performance.com is no longer controlled by the company: WHOIS lists the registrant organization as HugeDomains.com and the site 302s to a domain-resale listing, while advancedbiodevelopment.com does not resolve. This record is retained as an honest zero — a consumer-packaged-goods company with no API surface, whose only remaining public presence is third-party listings.

providers.name: Advanced Computer Communications
providers.description: Advanced Computer Communications (ACC), founded as Associated Computer Consultants, was a data networking equipment vendor based in Santa Barbara, California. The company began by building IMP interfaces for the ARPANET — initially for IBM 360 mainframes and later for DEC PDP-11 minicomputers — and grew into a maker of wide-area internetworking products for the interconnection and management of distributed computer networks, including carrier-class routers and integrated remote-access gear. In 1990 it sold its ACCES/MVS native TCP/IP stack for MVS to Interlink Computer Sciences. Ericsson agreed to acquire ACC in 1998 for approximately USD 285 million in cash and completed the acquisition that same year, after which ACC ceased to exist as an independent company. ACC predates the public web API era and never operated a developer program, public API, or developer portal; no successor developer surface exists under the ACC name today.

providers.name: Advent Solar
providers.description: Advent Solar was a silicon photovoltaic company founded in 2002 and headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico, that designed and manufactured crystalline-silicon (c-Si) solar cells and modules, pioneering emitter-wrap-through cell architectures and streamlined back-contact module assembly. Backed by Battery Ventures, EnerTech Capital, @Ventures and others across roughly $109M in venture funding (including a $70M Series D in 2007), the company's assets and intellectual property were acquired by Applied Materials in late 2009 / 2010. As a physical solar-hardware manufacturer that is no longer operating independently, Advent Solar exposes no public API, developer portal, or software surface; this profile is retained as a network identity record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Aepona
providers.description: Aepona was a telecommunications software company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Belfast, Northern Ireland, with additional offices in Dublin, the United States, and Sri Lanka. Its Network-as-a-Service platform let mobile network operators and cloud service providers expose carrier network capabilities — messaging, voice, location, identity, and carrier billing — to third-party developers through common-language REST APIs, and merchandize them through multi-sided business models. Backed by Amadeus Capital Partners and Sapphire Ventures, Aepona was acquired by Intel in April 2013 for approximately $124 million and folded into Intel's software and services group alongside the Mashery API-management acquisition.
