The company is no longer operating independently and its developer surface is defunct; this profile is retained as a historical record within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AeroFS
providers.description: AeroFS was an enterprise file sync-and-share and secure collaboration product built by Air Computing Inc., founded in 2010 out of Y Combinator with seed backing from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z Seed), SV Angel, Avalon Ventures, and angels including Chris Sacca, Maynard Webb, Jerry Yang, and Paul Buchheit. Its differentiator was peer-to-peer, private-cloud file sync that kept data on a company's own devices rather than a vendor's servers. Air Computing later pivoted to a team collaboration app called Amium. In 2017 the company merged with Redbooth (CEO and co-founder Yuri Sagalov became CEO of Redbooth), Amium was shut down on December 15, 2017, and the AeroFS technology was folded into Redbooth's product line. The standalone AeroFS product, developer program, and API are no longer operated; the aerofs.com domain is now a parked GoDaddy "for sale" page. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical/defunct-company record rather than an active developer surface.

providers.name: Affinity Labs
providers.description: Affinity Labs was a consumer social-networking company founded in 2006 by Christopher Michel (founder of Military.com) that built online communities for niche professional groups including firefighters (FireLink), police officers (PoliceLink), nurses (NursingLink) and the Armed Forces (HMForces.co.uk). Backed by Trinity Ventures and the Mayfield Fund, it grew past one million registered members before being merged into Monster Worldwide (Monster.com) in a $61 million transaction in January 2008. Its European operations shut down in 2012 and its domains and content were amalgamated into the Monster brand. The company is defunct and publishes no developer/API surface; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record. Not to be confused with Affinity (affinity.co), the unrelated relationship-intelligence CRM.

providers.name: Against Gravity
providers.description: Against Gravity Corp was the Seattle software company founded in April 2016 by Nick Fajt, Cameron Brown, Dan Kroymann, Bilal Orhan, Josh Wehrly and John Bevis that built Rec Room, a cross-platform social gaming and user-generated-content world for PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Meta Quest, iOS and Android. The company later renamed itself Rec Room Inc. and is tracked in this network under the rec-room record. Rec Room announced on 2026-03-30 that it could not reach profitability, took its game servers offline on 2026-06-01 and shut the rec.net community site down on 2026-06-09. It did run a real developer program: an Azure API Management developer portal at devportal.rec.net issuing subscription keys against api.rec.net. Both are gone — devportal.rec.net is a dangling CNAME to a deleted APIM instance and rec.net / api.rec.net answer TLS handshake_failure with no certificate. Only the legacy Squarespace marketing site at recroom.com is still served, so no live contract remains to harvest.

providers.name: AgBiome
providers.description: AgBiome was an agricultural biotechnology company headquartered in Research Triangle Park, Durham, North Carolina. Founded in 2012 by Scott Uknes, Eric Ward, Jeff Dangl, John Ryals and Paul Schulze-Lefert, it built the proprietary GENESIS discovery platform — a collection of more than 100,000 fully sequenced, isolated plant-associated microbial strains and hundreds of millions of gene sequences, screened with high-throughput assays for insect, disease and nematode control — and turned it into crop-protection biologicals. It commercialized the Howler and Theia biofungicides and had a third, Esendo, before the EPA, and it spun out the genome-editing venture LifeEDIT Therapeutics in October 2020 (acquired by ElevateBio in October 2021). Backed by Syngenta, Novozymes, Monsanto, ARCH Venture Partners, Polaris, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Pontifax and UTIMCO, the company nonetheless failed to raise further capital: it filed a North Carolina WARN notice in late 2023 covering its entire staff of 123, sold Howler and Theia to Certis Biologicals (a Mitsui & Co. subsidiary) in March 2024, and sold its platform assets to Ginkgo Bioworks in April 2024 for roughly $18.2 million in stock. AgBiome never published a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and agbiome.com no longer serves the company site — it answers from a Nexcess shared-hosting placeholder under a certificate issued to CN=nxcli.net. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: AgencyKPI
providers.description: AgencyKPI, Inc. was an Austin, Texas insurtech founded in 2017 by Trent Richmond and Bobby Billman, building a business intelligence and benchmarking platform for the independent insurance distribution channel — agency networks, independent agencies, carriers and wholesalers. The platform (marketed as Harmony) ingested, cleaned and normalized policy, premium and commission data out of agency management systems and carrier feeds, then presented benchmarking, collaborative planning and operational reporting on top of it, plus a managed insurance data lake for customer data teams. The company raised a Series A in 2020 from insurance industry investors and a Series B in 2022 that included Live Oak Ventures. As of 2026 AgencyKPI has ceased operations: agencykpi.com serves only a single-page service notice stating the platform has been discontinued effective immediately, and no developer, documentation or API surface remains reachable.

providers.name: AgentSquared
providers.description: AgentSquared was a La Jolla, California real estate marketing technology company, founded in 2013 by Albert Lopez and a team its LinkedIn page describes as "Internet pioneers who have founded, built and sold leading brand name Internet companies such as Media Temple, Miva, and Attracta." Its product was marketing automation for real estate agents and brokers: Instant IDX websites provisioned with a single click, single-property websites generated automatically for new listings, social sharing of those listings, lead capture and CRM, and Google Business Profile and Local Services Ads management. The company was notable as an API CONSUMER rather than an API producer — it was a RESO (Real Estate Standards Organization) member and one of the few vendors building on the National Association of Realtors Web API standard, using deep integrations and channel partnerships with MLS software providers to pull a broker's identity and listing data straight out of the MLS and stand up a fully populated website from it. It worked with RESO to help define and document the client portion of the RESO Web API certification program. AgentSquared never published a developer program of its own: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, or public package ever appeared on its site. The company reached roughly $961K in reported revenue without raising venture capital. Its web presence is now gone — see x-status below.

providers.name: Agillion
providers.description: Agillion, Inc. was an Austin, Texas web-based customer relationship management (CRM) company founded in 1998 by Steve Papermaster. It offered small and mid-sized businesses a hosted, continuously updated online database that consolidated customer information as businesses and their customers interacted, an early software-as-a-service CRM offering. The company raised roughly $40M from investors including Cisco, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley and is carried as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. Agillion has since been permanently closed; its agillion.com domain no longer serves a website and the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record.

providers.name: Agito Networks
providers.description: Agito Networks was an enterprise mobility and mobile unified communications (UC) company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, with a European presence in Reading, England. Its flagship product, the RoamAnywhere Mobility Router, was a network appliance that fused enterprise wireless LANs, carrier cellular networks, IP telephony, and location technology to extend PBX, deskphone, and unified communications features to mobile phones, providing handover between WiFi, 3G, and cellular networks while remaining agnostic to carrier and equipment vendor. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures, Castile Ventures, and ITX International. Agito Networks was acquired by IP telephony provider ShoreTel in 2010 for approximately $11.4 million, adding fixed-mobile convergence to ShoreTel's UC portfolio; ShoreTel was later acquired by Mitel, and the agitonetworks.com domain now redirects to Mitel. The company no longer operates as a standalone entity and publishes no public API, developer portal, or specifications.

providers.name: AgLocal
providers.description: AgLocal was a venture-backed food-technology startup (founded 2011 by Mike Hsieh and Naithan Jones, Kansas City / San Francisco) that built an online marketplace connecting small family ranchers and sustainable meat producers directly with buyers. It launched in 2013 as a ranch-to-restaurant marketplace serving chefs, then pivoted in 2014 to a consumer-facing monthly meat subscription service. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Chicago Ventures and others across roughly $3.8M in funding, the company shut down in 2015, stating it could not reach a self-sustaining business model. It is added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead; the company is now defunct and its domain (aglocal.com) is parked/for sale, so no live developer portal, API, or specifications exist to enrich.

providers.name: Agriprotein
providers.description: AgriProtein was a South African industrial insect-farming company, founded in Cape Town in 2008, that pioneered commercial black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens) bioconversion: it fed organic waste from food factories, supermarkets, farms and restaurants to fly larvae and processed the result into MagMeal insect protein for aquaculture, poultry and pet food, MagOil, and MagSoil soil conditioner. It opened the world's first full-scale BSF facility in Philippi, Cape Town in 2014 and raised USD 105 million in 2018 to build out a global factory network. Its UK parent, Insect Technology Group, entered administration in February 2021 and the group's assets, intellectual property and plant were sold in June 2021. The company is defunct; it published no developer program, API, or machine-readable specification, and the agriprotein.com domain has since lapsed to an unrelated operator.

providers.name: Ahlijasa
providers.description: Ahlijasa was an Indonesian on-demand home services startup founded in 2015 in the Greater Jakarta area by Jay Jayawijayaningtiyas and Made Dimas Astra Wijaya. It originally offered laundry, air-conditioning repair, and home cleaning before pivoting in late 2016 to focus exclusively on on-demand laundry by partnering with premium and traditional laundrettes to give them a digital storefront and online customer base. The company won Startup World Cup Indonesia in 2016 and raised seed funding in May 2017 from 500 Startups (500 Global), Fenox VC, and Indogen Capital, but secured no further funding afterward. Its primary domain (ahlijasa.com) now resolves to a domain-parking/for-sale page, indicating the business is no longer operating. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts were found for this provider during enrichment.

providers.name: AiBiotech
providers.description: AiBiotech (AIBioTech, American International Biotechnology) was a Richmond, Virginia contract research organization and CLIA/CAP clinical laboratory offering molecular biology, immunochemistry, protein expression, peptide chemistry, bioanalytical mass spectrometry, microbiology, BSL3 virology, genetic identity and forensic DNA analysis to pharmaceutical, biotech, academic and government clients. It was a wet-lab services business, not a software company, and never published an API, SDK, webhook surface or developer portal. Its domain aibiotech.com is now a HugeDomains for-sale parking lander answering HTTP 200 with the same sale page on every path; the last archived snapshot of a real company site dates to 2017. Laboratory directories list the operation under Granger Genetics, which makes no first-party claim to the brand, so no successor host is wired here.

providers.name: Aiden.ai
providers.description: Aiden.ai was a London-based marketing-analytics startup, founded in 2016 by Marie Outtier and Pierre-Jean Camillieri, that built what it billed as the first AI-powered marketing analyst: a machine-reading assistant that ingested large volumes of paid-advertising data to surface actionable insights, detect anomalies, predict campaign performance, and proactively act to improve ROI. It raised a $1.6M seed round led by Partech in 2018 and was acquired by Twitter (now X) on 2019-11-21. The company no longer operates as an independent business, ships no public product or developer API, and the aiden.ai domain is now parked and listed for sale (Afternic). This profile is retained as a Partech portfolio lead but is defunct: there is no live developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Aipingji
providers.description: Aipingji (爱拼机, also romanized Apin / Aipinji) was a Hangzhou, China travel-technology startup — legal entity 杭州爱拼机网络科技有限公司, incorporated 7 May 2015 in the Binjiang district — that built a C2B "intelligent group-buying" marketplace for discounted international air tickets. Rather than reselling published fares, it aggregated the unsold seat inventory of roughly a thousand Chinese charter operators (包机商), who buy blocks of seats from airlines in advance, and let consumers form 10-15 person buying groups against a specific date until the group filled and tickets were issued, taking a reported 5% commission from the charter operator. The app served 36 destinations from Hangzhou, Shanghai and Nanjing, and the company raised an angel round (Aug 2015, 天使汇), a tens-of-millions-RMB Series A (Apr 2016, led by 耀途资本 with 光合基金 and others), a ¥120M Series B (Jan 2017, 华映资本 and 弘帆资本) and a Series B+ (Jun 2017, 一村资本, 华映资本, Century Capital, Shenxuan Investment). No first-party surface survives: the domain cited as its site, apin.com, is now a parked listing offered for sale at ¥199,999 through the Chinese domain broker ename.com.cn and answers 403 on every path but the sale lander, the mobile app's last recorded update was September 2017, and there is no developer portal, GitHub organization, published package, or API of any kind.

providers.name: AirBand Communications
providers.description: AirBand Communications, Inc. was a fixed-wireless broadband provider for business customers, founded in 2000 by Andy Lombard and headquartered in Dallas, Texas. It delivered high-speed data, Voice over IP, security and managed services over a last-mile fixed-wireless network, bypassing incumbent local phone companies, and operated in metropolitan markets including Baltimore, Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston, Philadelphia and Phoenix. The company was venture-backed, raising roughly $119M across sixteen rounds from investors including Battery Ventures, M/C Partners and Crescendo Ventures, and grew by acquiring the fixed-wireless business of WindChannel Communications (2006) and Sparkplug (2010). Airband was acquired by United Network Services (UNSi) on 2013-05-15 and no longer operates independently. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass its former domains (airband.com, www.airband.com, airbandcommunications.com) do not resolve (DNS NXDOMAIN), and no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind could be found. This company is retained in the network as a historical/defunct record only. Not to be confused with Airband Community Internet, an unrelated UK rural broadband operator.

providers.name: Airborne Entertainment
providers.description: Airborne Entertainment was a Montreal, Quebec mobile entertainment company founded in 2000 that published and distributed premium mobile content and applications for carrier decks and early smartphones, including games, ringtones, ring-back tones, images, video and informational content, often under licensed consumer brands. The company raised a $22M round in July 2004 with participation from Insight Partners and Verizon, sold a majority stake to Japan's CYBIRD Co., Ltd. in 2005, was taken back by management in a 2008 buy-out, operated afterwards as Airborne Mobile, and was acquired by Bandsintown in October 2010. It no longer operates as an independent company: both airborneentertainment.com and airbornemobile.com are parked domain-sale listings, and the company never published a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as an API Evangelist network history record.

providers.name: Airbrite
providers.description: Airbrite was an early commerce-infrastructure startup (a16z portfolio) that offered a hosted order-management and payments/commerce backend API for merchants and developers, with JavaScript and Python client SDKs and an embeddable checkout. The product was later rebranded and pivoted to "Celery" (pre-order / crowdfunding commerce). Airbrite is now defunct: its primary developer domains (airbrite.io, getairbrite.com) no longer resolve and airbrite.com is a parked domain, so there is no live developer portal, API reference, or hosted API to enrich. What remains verifiable is the public github.com/airbrite organization and the client libraries still published on npm and PyPI. This profile records that residual, evidence-backed surface; most enrichment artifact types are legitimately empty because the provider no longer operates.

providers.name: Airespace
providers.description: Airespace, Inc. (formerly Black Storm Networks) was an American enterprise networking systems company founded in 2001 by Pat Calhoun, Bob Friday, Bob O'Hara and Ajay Mishra, manufacturing wireless LAN access points and the controllers that managed them. Airespace pioneered the centralized AP-controller architecture for rapid enterprise Wi-Fi deployment and authored the Lightweight Access Point Protocol (LWAPP), the direct precursor to the IETF CAPWAP standard, and was first to market with integrated Wi-Fi location tracking. It was venture backed by Storm Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners, Fidelity Investments and Battery Ventures, and shipped OEM equipment through NEC, Alcatel and Nortel. Cisco Systems acquired Airespace in 2005 for $450 million and merged its products into the Cisco Aironet line. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no API, developer portal or documentation; the airespace.com domain is parked and listed for sale.

providers.name: Airgram
providers.description: Airgram was a Singapore-headquartered AI meeting assistant founded in 2020 by Ryan Zhang. Its web app joined Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams calls to record and transcribe them in real time, then produced collaborative notes, agendas, action items, AI summaries and shareable clips, with exports to Notion, Slack and HubSpot and an automation connector listed on Zapier. It sold the product to end users on free and paid plans and never published a public developer program: no API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, webhook catalog or developer portal was ever offered, and the Zapier connector was the only integration surface. In early 2024 Airgram merged into Notta (notta.ai), the AI transcription company, and the Airgram service was discontinued from 8 March 2024; Notta hosts a "Airgram Has Joined Notta" welcome page and the LinkedIn company page is renamed "Airgram (merged into Notta)". No first-party host survives — airgram.io and www.airgram.io have no DNS record and airgram.com 301s into the dead www.airgram.io — so no Website pointer is wired. This record is retained as an honest zero: an end-user software company, absorbed into an acquirer, with no API surface to profile.

providers.name: AirMap
providers.description: AirMap was a drone airspace-management and unmanned traffic management (UTM) platform that provided airspace intelligence, flight planning, digital notice, and geofencing services for drones and their operators, exposed through a developer platform of airspace and flight APIs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07) the company appears defunct: airmap.com no longer serves a developer portal or API and now resolves to a parked Squarespace-hosted page with a mismatched TLS certificate, and the legacy developer.airmap.com / api.airmap.com / docs.airmap.com hosts no longer resolve. No live API surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Airplane
providers.description: Airplane was a Benchmark-backed developer platform for building internal tools, dashboards, and operational workflows by turning scripts into shareable tasks and UIs. It was acquired by Airtable in 2023 and the product was subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct: the website www.airplane.dev no longer connects, the airplane.dev apex resolves to a domain-parking IP, and the airplanedev GitHub organization was archived on 2026-02-03 with no public repositories. No live API, developer portal, documentation host, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Airvana
providers.description: Airvana was a Chelmsford, Massachusetts wireless infrastructure company founded in 2000 by former Motorola engineers Sanjeev Verma and Vedat Eyuboglu, building femtocells and small cells for 3G CDMA2000 EV-DO and 4G LTE mobile broadband networks. Its access points extended operator coverage inside buildings over consumer broadband connections, and the company was a founding member of the Femto Forum and an active contributor to femtocell standards. Airvana went public on NASDAQ (AIRV) in July 2007, was taken private in 2010, and was acquired by CommScope in 2015. It no longer operates as an independent company: the airvana.com apex serves no site, www.airvana.com now points into CommScope infrastructure, and there is no Airvana developer portal, public API, or SDK. Its femtocell and device management products were TR-069 based operator systems rather than public web APIs.

providers.name: Airware
providers.description: Airware was an enterprise commercial-drone (UAV) software and aerial-data-analytics company founded in 2011 by Jonathan Downey and headquartered in San Francisco. It began by building an operating system and autopilot for commercial drones, then pivoted to a cloud-based "Aerial Information Platform" that captured, processed, and analyzed drone imagery for enterprise verticals such as mining, quarrying, insurance, and construction. Airware acquired French drone-analytics firm Redbird in 2016 and raised roughly $118M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, GV (Google Ventures), Intel Capital, and Next World Capital. The company ceased operations in September 2018. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no live developer surface, API, or public specification is currently discoverable (the airware.com domain no longer resolves), so this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.

providers.name: AK Steel Holding
providers.description: AK Steel Holding Corporation was a leading producer of flat-rolled carbon, stainless, and electrical steel products, as well as carbon and stainless tubular products, primarily serving the automotive, infrastructure, manufacturing, and electrical power markets. AK Steel was acquired by Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. in March 2020 and now operates as a subsidiary.

providers.name: Alien Labs
providers.description: Alien Labs, Inc. was a San Francisco software startup founded by Cristian Strat, Mircea Pasoi and Liana Dumitru, and a seed-stage portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Under the Alien Labs banner the team shipped Summify, a social news digest acquired by Twitter in January 2012, and later Memo — "the wiki that's always up-to-date" — a Slack-native team knowledge base that let 8,000+ teams star a Slack message to save it as a searchable note, edit rich-text and code-block documents in context, and retrieve them with a /memo-find slash command. Memo stopped accepting new signups on January 16, 2018 and shut down on March 16, 2018; most of the engineering team joined Coinbase. The company operates no live developer portal, documentation, or public API today, and this profile is retained as a historical network record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Allegiance Telecom
providers.description: Allegiance Telecom was a competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) founded in 1997 and backed by Battery Ventures, providing local and long-distance voice, data, and internet services to business customers across major U.S. metropolitan markets. The company went public in 1998, expanded rapidly during the telecom boom, then filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2003; its network assets were acquired by XO Communications. Allegiance Telecom is defunct and operates no website, developer program, or public API surface today. This profile was surfaced from the Battery Ventures portfolio graph and is retained as an historical company record in the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no live API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Alluvium
providers.description: Alluvium was an industrial machine-learning / data-science startup backed by Bloomberg Beta and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. Enrichment on 2026-07-17 found no live API surface. Its domain alluvium.io now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale parking page (dan.com nameservers), indicating the company is defunct or acquired. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or package registry presence was found; alluvium.com is an unrelated active environmental-consulting firm and alluvium.ai is a parked domain. No scoring artifacts could be produced without fabrication.

providers.name: Alpharel
providers.description: Alpharel, Inc. was a Camarillo, California document-management and imaging company founded in 1981 that built turnkey digital document transmission and management systems (scanners, optical disks, terminals, LANs) for industrial, commercial, and government use. It acquired Optigraphics in 1993, renamed itself Altris Software in October 1996, and its business was ultimately succeeded by Spescom Software, Inc. of San Diego. Alpharel appears in the Battery Ventures portfolio list. The company is DEFUNCT under this name: it has no active first-party website, developer portal, API, or SDKs, so there is no API/developer surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Altra Energy Technologies
providers.description: Altra Energy Technologies was a Houston, Texas software company founded in 1996 by Williams and PanEnergy (later Duke Energy) that built neutral online trading platforms for the energy sector. Its flagship marketplace, Altrade, provided a real-time, anonymous electronic exchange for trading natural gas, crude oil, natural gas liquids, and power, backed by energy transaction management software spanning deal capture, portfolio monitoring, physical scheduling, and back-office reconciliation and settlement. At its peak the platform served more than 6,000 users worldwide. The company raised roughly $55.5M from investors including Battery Ventures, Austin Ventures, BP, Candescent Partners, and Capital Resource Partners. It ceased to exist as an independent company around 2002: its software operations were acquired by Caminus Corporation and its online marketplace by ChemConnect (recorded elsewhere as Supply Chain Connect). No live developer portal, API, or public developer surface exists for this defunct company.

providers.name: AltSchool
providers.description: AltSchool was an American education-technology company founded in 2013 by former Google executive Max Ventilla to build a network of small private "lab" schools around a personalized, student-directed learning model, using those campuses to develop a K-12 software platform for assignments and progress tracking. It raised more than $170 million from investors including Founders Fund, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Mark Zuckerberg's CZI, and Peter Thiel. In 2017-2019 the company closed or handed off its for-profit schools (to Higher Ground Education) and pivoted to selling the software as "Altitude Learning," with Ventilla stepping down as CEO. The venture is now defunct as an independent operation: the altschool.com domain no longer resolves and altitudelearning.com redirects to Guidepost Montessori. No public developer, API, or documentation surface was found; this record is retained as a historical VC-portfolio company profile.

providers.name: AltspaceVR
providers.description: AltspaceVR was a social virtual reality platform founded in 2013 where people gathered in shared 3D spaces for live events, meetups, classes, comedy shows and conferences. Google Ventures (GV) was an early investor. Microsoft acquired the company in 2017 and folded it into its Mixed Reality division, then announced in January 2023 that the platform would close, shutting it down permanently on 2023-03-10 in favor of Microsoft Mesh. AltspaceVR published no hosted HTTP API; its developer surface was the Mixed Reality Extension (MRE) SDK for building server-hosted 3D world extensions in Node.js, plus the earlier web-based AltspaceSDK. Every SDK repository is now archived and altvr.com redirects to microsoft.com. This profile is retained as a historical record of a terminated platform, not as a live integration target.

providers.name: Amazon CodeGuru Security
providers.description: Amazon CodeGuru Security is a static application security testing (SAST) service that uses machine learning to detect security vulnerabilities in your code. It identifies vulnerabilities such as injection flaws, data exposure risks, and infrastructure-as-code misconfigurations, and provides actionable remediation guidance to help developers fix security issues quickly.

providers.name: Amazon Elastic Transcoder
providers.description: Amazon Elastic Transcoder is media transcoding in the cloud. It is designed to be a highly scalable, easy-to-use, and cost-effective way for developers and businesses to convert or transcode media files from their source format into versions that will play back on devices like smartphones, tablets, and PCs.

providers.name: Amazon Lookout for Metrics
providers.description: Amazon Lookout for Metrics uses machine learning to automatically detect anomalies in business and operational metrics such as revenue performance, customer engagement, and user activity. It continuously monitors data from various sources including Amazon S3, CloudWatch, RDS, Redshift, Athena, and AppFlow, providing root cause analysis and alert notifications when anomalies are detected.

providers.name: Amazon Lookout for Vision
providers.description: Amazon Lookout for Vision is a machine learning service that spots defects and anomalies in visual representations using computer vision. With just a small sample of images, it builds a custom computer vision model to enable you to identify damaged products or issues before production issues arise. It supports projects, datasets, model training, and real-time anomaly detection.

providers.name: Amazon MediaStore
providers.description: AWS Elemental MediaStore is an AWS storage service optimized for media, providing the performance, consistency, and low latency required to deliver live streaming video content at scale.

providers.name: Amazon RoboMaker
providers.description: AWS RoboMaker is a cloud-based service that makes it easy to develop, simulate, and deploy intelligent robotics applications. RoboMaker extends the most widely used open-source robotics software framework, Robot Operating System (ROS), with connectivity to cloud services, providing tools for building, testing, and deploying robotics applications at scale.

providers.name: Amazon SimSpace Weaver
providers.description: AWS SimSpace Weaver is a managed service that helps you build and run large-scale spatial simulations in the AWS Cloud. It provides tools to run custom spatial simulation logic at scale and use simulation workloads for defense, urban planning, and other real-world system simulations.

providers.name: AMCC (Applied Micro Circuits Corporation)
providers.description: Applied Micro Circuits Corporation (AMCC) was a California-based semiconductor company founded in 1979, originally producing application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) for the military market before diversifying into commercial mixed-signal, networking, storage, and embedded processor products. AMCC went public on NASDAQ in 1997, acquired MMC Networks in 2000, and bought IBM's PowerPC 400 processor line in 2004. Under the AppliedMicro brand it later developed the X-Gene ARM 64-bit server-on-chip family. AMCC ceased to exist as an independent entity when MACOM completed its acquisition on January 26, 2017; the X-Gene compute business was subsequently spun out to form Ampere Computing. As a fabless silicon/hardware company (now defunct), AMCC published no public developer API surface, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: AMEE
providers.description: AMEE (Avoiding Mass Extinctions Engine, also styled Avoidance of Mass Extinctions Engine) was a London-based environmental-intelligence company founded around 2005 by Gavin Starks out of UK firm Dgen. It ran an open web-service API and cloud database that standardized carbon-emissions and energy-consumption data across 150+ countries, letting applications apply government emission factors to tracked activities. AMEE powered carbon calculators and footprinting for clients including Google, Morgan Stanley, Radiohead, Sun Microsystems, and UK and Irish government programs (notably the Act on CO2 campaign). It raised roughly $7.5M from Union Square Ventures, OATV (O'Reilly AlphaTech Ventures), The Accelerator Group, and Amadeus Capital Partners. AMEE was acquired by Pi (PredictX) in late 2015 / early 2016 and no longer operates as an independent company; the amee.com domain currently returns HTTP 502 with no live API or developer surface.

providers.name: Amiato
providers.description: Amiato was a Palo Alto, California big-data startup founded in 2011 by Nathan Binkert and Mehul A. Shah, originally incubated at Y Combinator in 2012 under the name Nou Data. Amiato built a real-time analytics pipeline around its Schema-lift technology, which extracted records from NoSQL data stores such as MongoDB and Couchbase, automatically inferred and transformed them into a relational schema, and loaded them continuously into Amazon Redshift so that unstructured operational data could be queried by conventional business-intelligence tools. The company raised roughly $2M from investors including Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz, Ignition Partners, Data Collective (DCVC) and angel Bobby Yazdani. Amazon Web Services quietly acquired Amiato in May 2014 (reported publicly in April 2015) in what was widely characterized as a talent acquisition; most of the team joined Amazon's database and Redshift product groups and Amiato ceased independent operations. The company is defunct: the amiato.com domain no longer resolves and there is no surviving public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich.

providers.name: Ampool
providers.description: Ampool is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Anar
providers.description: Anar was a B2B marketplace and business networking mobile app for small businesses, sellers, and buyers in India, operating from 2020 to 2023 before shutting down. At its peak it reported 1.6M+ registered businesses, 450k+ sellers, 1.1M+ buyers, and 7M+ business enquiries processed across 6.6M+ listed products. It raised roughly $6.5M from Accel and Elevation Capital plus angel investors. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio company; no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation was ever published, and the service is now defunct.

providers.name: Andera
providers.description: Andera was an online account-opening / digital-banking software company. Its domain andera.com now 301-redirects to Bottomline Technologies' digital banking product (bottomline.com/us/financial-institutions/digital-banking), indicating the company has been acquired and folded into Bottomline; no independent Andera developer, API, or documentation surface exists. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found no live standalone API surface to build on.

providers.name: Anki
providers.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: Anobit Technologies
providers.description: Anobit Technologies was an Israeli fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2006, that developed flash-memory Memory Signal Processing (MSP) controller technology to extend the endurance, reliability, and performance of consumer-grade NAND flash used in SSDs and mobile devices. Backed by Battery Ventures among others, Anobit was acquired by Apple in early 2012 and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer surface, API program, or live web presence, and remains in the API Evangelist network only as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: AnswerSoft
providers.description: AnswerSoft, Inc. was a privately-held computer-telephony integration (CTI) software company based in Richardson, Texas. Its Concerto product line automated interactions between telephony systems and business applications, covering smart screen pop, intelligent call routing, data mining, and early internet-enabled call centers. Davox Corporation acquired AnswerSoft in a stock-for-stock transaction in 1998 to pair AnswerSoft's inter-application automation with Davox's Unison outbound call center line, taking the combined company into the emerging CRM market. Davox renamed itself Concerto Software in 2002, merged with Aspect Communications to form Aspect Software in 2005, and merged with Noble Systems to become Alvaria in 2021. AnswerSoft has not operated independently for over twenty-five years, publishes no API, developer program, or documentation, and the answersoft.com domain is now listed for sale on the GoDaddy aftermarket. This profile is retained as a historical acquired-company lead only.

providers.name: Apcera
providers.description: Apcera was an enterprise container and policy management platform founded in 2012 by Derek Collison, offering a "trusted cloud" runtime that layered fine-grained, policy-driven governance over workloads, containers, and services across hybrid infrastructure. Backed by a16z and DCVC, the company took a majority investment from Ericsson in 2015, was fully acquired by Ericsson in 2016, and the platform was subsequently wound down around 2017. The company is defunct - its primary domain (apcera.com) no longer resolves to a company site (it 301-redirects to an unrelated third party), and there is no live developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or reachable API host to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record only.

providers.name: Apieron
providers.description: Apieron Inc. was a private, venture-backed medical device company headquartered in Menlo Park, California, formed in early 2001 to develop a simple-to-use, non-invasive monitor for the measurement of exhaled nitric oxide (eNO) as an aid in the management of asthma. Its patented biosensor platform enabled highly sensitive detection of selected analytes, and its Insight eNO System received U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance and launched in the United States in 2008. Following that launch Aerocrine filed patent-infringement complaints against Apieron and Apieron counterclaimed; citing the legal setbacks and a lack of financing, Apieron filed a Chapter 7 bankruptcy petition in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of California on 30 March 2010. At a court auction on 12 May 2010 Aerocrine acquired all of Apieron's business assets, including its patent and trademark portfolio, ending the litigation; the Insight product was discontinued and not returned to supply. Apieron was a clinical-hardware company and never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface. This profile is retained as a historical record of the Canaan Partners portfolio and is not an active API provider.

providers.name: App.net
providers.description: App.net (ADN) was a paid, ad-free real-time social networking and microblogging platform launched in 2012 by Dalton Caldwell's Mixed Media Labs after a public crowdfunding campaign. It was explicitly developer-first: the App.net Stream API exposed posts, users, follows, files, channels, private messaging, filters and a real-time streaming/subscription surface, all governed by OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens and a consistent data/meta response envelope. Third-party clients (Alpha, and many community apps) were built entirely on the public API. App.net announced in 2016 that it would not renew and the service was shut down on 2017-03-14; the live API hosts (api.app.net, developers.app.net) no longer resolve and the app.net domain is now operated by an unrelated apps directory. The API documentation (appdotnet/api-spec), terms of service, and official SDKs remain publicly preserved on the appdotnet GitHub organization, which is the basis for this profile.

providers.name: AppBistro
providers.description: AppBistro, operated by MMTG Labs, was an application marketplace for the Facebook Pages platform that let brands and page administrators discover, install, and manage third-party apps to boost engagement and reach on their fan pages. It also built AppGalleries, a white-label app-store platform. A TechCrunch Disrupt 2010 finalist, the San Francisco startup raised a $550K convertible note (Sand Hill Angels, 500 Startups, i/o Ventures, Zelkova Ventures, Seraph Group, and angels including Alfred Lin) and was acquired by mobile ad network InMobi on 2012-07-13, after which the product and its five-person team (co-founders Ryan Merket and Nalin Mittal) wound down. The company is defunct and appbistro.com no longer resolves; no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: appconomy
providers.description: Appconomy was a mobile-commerce platform company, founded in 2010 and dual-headquartered in Austin, Texas and Shanghai, China, that let brands, retailers, service providers, and mobile carriers add commerce functionality (daily deals, coupons, loyalty and rewards, mobile gifting, and merchant app generation for marketplaces such as Taobao) to their mobile apps. It was venture-backed with strategic investors including Qiming Venture Partners (lead of a $10M Series A), True Ventures, Neusoft Holdings, and WTI. The company is now permanently closed and publishes no live developer surface. The appconomy.cn domain does not resolve, appconomy.com returns 404, and no public API, documentation, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ endpoint could be found. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-graph record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: AppIQ
providers.description: AppIQ was a storage-infrastructure software company (founded 2001, Burlington, MA) making storage resource management and SAN management software for visualization, provisioning, monitoring, reporting, and policy-based automation, backed by Matrix Partners, North Bridge Venture Partners, ATV, and Intel Capital. It was acquired by Hewlett-Packard in October 2005 and absorbed into HP/HPE. It has no independent, live developer surface today: appiq.com now redirects to hpe.com and there is no public API, developer portal, documentation, or OpenAPI to enrich. Surfaced here as a Matrix Partners portfolio lead; enrichment found no active API artifacts.

providers.name: Applimation
providers.description: Applimation was a provider of application Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) and enterprise data archiving software for packaged applications including SAP (ERP, HR, CRM, SRM, SCM, APO) and Oracle environments, helping customers manage the full data lifecycle from test-data management through archiving of inactive data to lower storage and database costs and improve application performance. Informatica acquired Applimation for approximately $40 million in an agreement announced in February 2009, folding its ILM and database-archiving technology into Informatica's data management portfolio. Applimation no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer surface, API, or documentation.

providers.name: Appurify
providers.description: Appurify was a mobile app and website testing platform that let developers automate testing and optimization of native and web apps on real iOS and Android devices across OS versions and simulated network conditions. Founded and backed by DCVC and GV, Appurify was acquired by Google in June 2014 and its technology was folded into Firebase Test Lab (formerly Google Cloud Test Lab). The company no longer operates independently; the appurify.com domain now redirects to the Firebase Test Lab documentation and Appurify's standalone developer API and product have been discontinued.

providers.name: Apropose
providers.description: Apropose, Inc. was a Mountain View, California startup spun out of the Stanford University Computer Science Department in 2013 to bring data-driven software to web design. Founded by Ranjitha Kumar, Jerry Talton, Maxine Lim, and Arvind Satyanarayan, the company built tools for large-scale visual page search and web design analytics — letting teams track design trends, compare a site's design against demographics, and surface prevalent design patterns to inject concrete data into the design process. It raised a roughly $1.875M seed round in 2014 led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA) and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), with angels including Pat Hanrahan and Nick McKeown. The company has since ceased operations and is permanently closed; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and its primary domain (apropose.com) is now parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained as an a16z portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Apteligent
providers.description: Apteligent (originally Crittercism, founded 2011 by Andrew Levy, Robert Kwok, and Jeeyun Kim, rebranded to Apteligent in 2016) was a mobile application performance management platform that provided real-time crash reporting, diagnostics, service monitoring, and user-engagement analytics across iOS, Android, hybrid, and HTML5 apps. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Opus Capital, and Shasta Ventures (~$48.7M raised), the company was acquired by VMware on 2017-05-15 and folded into the Workspace ONE digital-workspace platform. Following VMware's 2024 end-user-computing spin-off, the technology now ships under the Omnissa Intelligence brand. The independent Apteligent developer surface has been retired: apteligent.com no longer resolves at the apex and www.apteligent.com 301-redirects to omnissa.com; there is no live standalone API, documentation, or developer portal to enrich.

providers.name: AquaHydrex
providers.description: AquaHydrex was a green-hydrogen technology company that developed a redesigned high-pressure alkaline water electrolysis system for large-scale hydrogen production. Founded in 2012 as a spin-out of the University of Wollongong and Monash University (ARC Centre of Excellence for Electromaterials Science), it opened its North American headquarters in Louisville, Colorado in 2015 and raised about $25 million, including a January 2023 round led by AP Ventures with Aramco Ventures. It filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in October 2023 (D. Colo. 1:23-bk-14706). It published no API. It was harvested from a Nasdaq Private Market listing, which an earlier pass mistook for the company and described as a liquidity and secondary-market platform.

providers.name: Arbor Software
providers.description: Arbor Software Corporation was an enterprise business-intelligence and OLAP software company founded in 1991 in Sunnyvale, California by Bob Earle and Jim Dorian. It created Essbase, the pioneering multidimensional online-analytical-processing (OLAP) server first released in 1992, and went public on NASDAQ under the ticker ARSW in 1995. Arbor merged with Hyperion Software in 1998 to form Hyperion Solutions Corporation, which Oracle Corporation acquired in 2007; the Essbase technology lives on inside Oracle. Arbor Software no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface, so there is nothing to enrich.

providers.name: Areteia Therapeutics
providers.description: Areteia Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company, formerly based in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, operating in the life-sciences sector. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company is no longer operating: areteiatx.com serves only a closure notice directing asset and general inquiries to contact addresses, and the company publishes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or other technical developer surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; retained for network completeness with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Argon Networks
providers.description: Argon Networks was a late-1990s networking infrastructure startup that developed a high-speed routing switch for what was then described as the next-generation multi-service Internet, combining IP routing with ATM switching in a single carrier-class platform. The company was venture backed by Canaan Partners (Series B, partner Eric Young), Matrix Partners, New Enterprise Associates and Greylock. Siemens acquired Argon Networks in March 1999 in a deal reported at roughly $240 million and folded the team into Unisphere Solutions / Unisphere Networks, the carrier-infrastructure unit later acquired by Juniper Networks in 2002. Argon Networks predates the public web API era: it shipped carrier networking hardware, never operated a developer program, and has no surviving website, documentation, SDKs or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical venture-portfolio record rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: ARIVE
providers.description: ARIVE (getarive.com) was an urban quick-commerce platform founded in Paris during the COVID-19 pandemic that delivered fashion, beauty, and lifestyle products to customers within hours. Operating across Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, and Paris, it connected more than 500 brands and 200 local stores directly to young, convenience-focused urban shoppers. Backed by Balderton Capital, LaFamiglia, and Triple Point Capital with roughly €31.7M raised, the company ceased operations in mid-2023 following a sale of the business. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or other technical surface was ever published; this profile is retained for network and portfolio-graph completeness.

providers.name: Ark.com
providers.description: Ark.com was a people search engine founded in San Francisco in March 2012 by Patrick Riley and Yiming Liu, and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2012 batch. Ark indexed over a billion public social network profiles — aggregating "ghost profiles" from Facebook, LinkedIn, AngelList and other networks — and let users search across them with filters such as hometown, current city, high school, college, employer and interests, to reconnect with classmates and acquaintances or find new business contacts. The company raised a $4.2M seed round in April 2012 from Andreessen Horowitz, Greylock Partners and SV Angel, and reached the finals of TechCrunch Disrupt NYC 2012. Ark is no longer operating: Y Combinator lists the company as Inactive and PitchBook lists it as Out of Business. As of a July 2026 probe the ark.com domain no longer serves the company — it redirects to www.ark-invest.com, the unrelated ARK Investment Management site — and no api., developer. or docs. subdomain resolves. Ark never published a public API, developer portal or SDKs, so there is no API surface to catalog. Retained as a historical a16z portfolio record only.

providers.name: Around
providers.description: Around was a video-calling application built for designers, developers, and product teams, known for floating circular "heads" that cropped participants to their faces so the call could sit on top of the work rather than dominate the screen, plus echo prevention that let several people call from the same room. Around was acquired by Miro in June 2022, operated for a period as Around by Miro Labs, and was shut down on 31 March 2025, with features such as echo prevention and reactions folded into Miro's own video collaboration surface. The around.co domain is now parked on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket and the product, developer portal, and any API surface are gone. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record; there is no live API to catalog.

providers.name: ArrowPoint
providers.description: ArrowPoint Communications, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARPT) was a networking company based in Acton, Massachusetts that built content switches — Layer 4-7 "web switches" that inspected HTTP content, cookies and URLs to route and load-balance traffic across web server farms, CDNs and hosting providers. Founded in 1997 and backed by Matrix Partners, North Bridge Venture Partners and Accel Partners, it IPO'd in early 2000 and was acquired by Cisco Systems in a stock deal announced 2000-05-05 and completed 2000-06-23, valued at roughly $5.7 billion. Its CSS 11000 series and WebNS software became a Cisco product line that has since reached end-of-life and been retired. ArrowPoint no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no documentation, no APIs and no SDKs, and the arrowpoint.com domain — still delegated to Cisco nameservers — serves no live web or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Matrix Partners portfolio exit.

providers.name: ArrowPoint Communications
providers.description: ArrowPoint Communications, Inc. was a Massachusetts-based content-networking company that built "content smart" web switches for server load balancing, content delivery, and web caching in the late 1990s. After a January 2000 IPO it was acquired by Cisco Systems in 2000 for approximately $5.7 billion in stock, and its technology became the basis of the Cisco Content Services Switch (CSS) product line. It has not operated as an independent company since the acquisition, and it exposes no public developer program, API, documentation, or other machine-readable surface today; this record is retained for network/portfolio lineage rather than active API enrichment.

providers.name: Artillery Games
providers.description: Artillery Games (also known as Artillery) was an early-stage technology startup backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) that built browser-based, real-time multiplayer strategy games and an associated JavaScript game engine. The company was acquired by GitHub in 2017 and no longer operates as an independent entity; its former artillery.com domain now redirects to a domain-sale marketplace. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead, but exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or other surface to enrich via the pipeline.

providers.name: Artivest
providers.description: Artivest was a New York-based alternative investments technology company founded in 2012 that gave financial advisors and high-net-worth investors a curated digital experience for discovering, evaluating, and subscribing to private investment funds, including its "Open Network" platform serving roughly 1,800 advisors and management of 28 proprietary alternative investment funds. iCapital Network announced the acquisition of substantially all of Artivest's assets — technology, operating platform, fund management, and enterprise relationships — on 2020-05-13 and closed the transaction in August 2020. The Artivest brand, platform, and public web presence were fully absorbed into iCapital; as of this enrichment pass artivest.co does not resolve and artivest.com is registered to an unrelated third party. Artivest never published a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts, and there is no live surface remaining to enrich.

providers.name: Ascend Communications
providers.description: Ascend Communications, Inc. was an Alameda, California manufacturer of wide area networking equipment, founded in 1988 and taken public in 1994. It developed, manufactured and sold WAN access solutions — remote-access concentrators, ISDN and frame relay gear, and the MAX family of access servers — to telecommunications carriers, Internet service providers and corporate customers worldwide, becoming a leading supplier during the dial-up internet build-out of the 1990s. On January 13, 1999 Lucent Technologies announced a definitive agreement to merge with Ascend in a stock deal valued at roughly $20.3 billion, and the merger completed on June 24, 1999, when Ascend became a wholly owned subsidiary of Lucent. The company has not operated independently since. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company; it predates the public web API era and publishes no developer surface today.

providers.name: Aserto
providers.description: Aserto is a cloud-native authorization platform providing fine-grained, policy-based access control for applications and APIs. Built on Open Policy Agent (OPA) and a Google Zanzibar-inspired directory, Aserto exposes REST and gRPC APIs for the Authorizer (real-time authorization decisions), Directory (managing users, groups, objects, and relations), and Decision Logs (audit trails of authorization events). The open-source Topaz engine carries the technology forward after the commercial SaaS control plane was wound down in May 2025.

providers.name: Ask
providers.description: Ask (Ask.com), formerly Ask Jeeves, was a consumer web search engine that operated for roughly 30 years before officially closing on May 1, 2026. The domain now serves a static closure/farewell notice and a Privacy Policy page. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network; enrichment confirms there is no public developer API, SDK, documentation, well-known discovery surface, or event/webhook surface to harvest — the site is defunct. Retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Associated Content
providers.description: Associated Content was an open content publishing platform founded in 2005 by Luke Beatty that paid contributors to publish articles, video, audio, and images on any topic, then distributed that library through associatedcontent.com and a network of syndication partners. At its peak it hosted over one million pieces of content from roughly 250,000 contributors and adopted Thomson Reuters OpenCalais for automated classification of that library. It raised a $5.4M Series A from SoftBank Capital (2006), a $10M Series B from SoftBank, Canaan Partners, and Tim Armstrong (2007), and $6M more in 2009, before Yahoo acquired it in May 2010. Yahoo rebranded the property as Yahoo Voices in December 2011 and shut it down on July 31, 2014, retiring the Yahoo Contributor Network the following month. The company is defunct: it never published a public developer API, and associatedcontent.com is now a parked domain that refuses HTTPS.

providers.name: Astrid *
providers.description: Astrid was a popular cross-platform social to-do list and task-management app (Todoroo, Inc.), known for its Android and web productivity service and a lightweight task-sync API. It was a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the consumer sector. Yahoo acquired the Astrid team in May 2013 and discontinued the service later that year; the astrid.com domain now resolves to Yahoo and the original developer surface (apidoc / api_keys) is dead. The Android client was open-sourced (todoroo/astrid) and later revived by the community as tasks.org (tasks/tasks). No live first-party API, developer portal, or documentation exists to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct portfolio lead.

providers.name: Atexto
providers.description: Atexto was a speech-recognition data company (self-described "the accuracy platform for speech recognition") based in Mexico City, founded around 2016 by Brenda Mana Pastrian and Esteban Gorupicz. It helped machine-learning and voice-assistant teams create, collect, annotate, transcribe, and benchmark audio/speech datasets, combining an enterprise data platform with a global paid crowdsourcing community that transcribed and labeled audio across roughly 24 languages and their regional accents. The company also offered a hybrid human-plus-machine audio-to-text transcription service and ASR training-data services. It was backed by 500 Global, Redwood Ventures, MC Capital, and a Start-Up Chile grant. The company now appears inactive: its former domain atexto.com has been repurposed to an unrelated third-party site, and no live developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification could be located. This profile captures verified historical identity only; no API artifacts were enriched because no live API surface exists.

providers.name: Athenian
providers.description: Athenian was a full-cycle software-development analytics platform founded in 2019 by Eiso Kant, with a seed round led by Point Nine. It integrated GitHub, JIRA, and CI/CD tooling to give engineering leaders end-to-end visibility into their delivery pipeline — lead time, cycle time, deployment frequency, PR review dynamics, and goal alignment — deliberately measuring teams and events rather than ranking individuals. The company has since wound down: athenian.com and athenian.co now redirect to github.com/athenianco and the production API host api.athenian.co no longer resolves. However, the OpenAPI specification (athenianco/api-spec, 79 operations, 218 schemas) and the open-source API implementation (athenian-api-open, MIT) remain publicly published on GitHub, which is why this profile is enriched from the real, still-available API contract.

providers.name: AtheroMed
providers.description: AtheroMed, Inc. was a privately-held medical device company based in Menlo Park, California, founded to treat peripheral artery disease (PAD). Its sole product was the Phoenix Atherectomy System, an over-the-wire, low-profile atherectomy catheter that uses a rotating front-cutting element at the distal tip to shave diseased material directly into the catheter, where an internal Archimedes screw continuously captures and removes the debulked material without requiring specialized capital equipment. The Phoenix system received FDA 510(k) clearance in January 2014 and CE Mark approval in Europe. AtheroMed was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and U.S. Venture Partners, and was acquired by Volcano Corporation in June 2014 for $115 million upfront plus milestone payments; Volcano was in turn acquired by Royal Philips in February 2015. AtheroMed no longer operates as an independent company, its atheromed.com domain is parked and listed for sale, and it has no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind. The Phoenix catheter is now sold as a Philips Volcano product.

providers.name: Atlas Wearables
providers.description: Atlas Wearables was an Austin, Texas fitness-technology startup founded in 2013 by Peter Li, Mike Kasparian, and Alex Hsieh. It raised over $500,000 on Indiegogo in 2014 for the Atlas Wristband, a motion-tracking gym wearable whose "Exercise ID" technology automatically recognized strength exercises and counted reps and sets. The company shipped the Atlas Wristband and Wristband 2 and historically promoted an open developer API and integrations with apps such as MapMyFitness and Fitocracy. Atlas Wearables was acquired by Peloton Interactive in late 2020; the company no longer operates independently and the atlaswearables.com domain no longer resolves (it is now held by Peloton Interactive). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a former Techstars-associated portfolio lead; no live developer surface, API specification, or documentation remains available to enrich.

providers.name: atSpoke
providers.description: atSpoke was a modern workplace service desk / internal helpdesk SaaS (formerly askSpoke) that let teams triage and resolve employee support requests across HR, IT, and operations. It was a portfolio company of Accel and was acquired by Okta in August 2021 for approximately $90M to seed Okta's identity governance (IGA) roadmap. The standalone atSpoke product and its entire domain footprint have since been sunset: atspoke.com, askspoke.com, help.atspoke.com and the former public API host api.askspoke.com/api/v1 no longer resolve or serve. This profile is retained as a historical network record; there is no live developer surface left to enrich.

providers.name: Auditude
providers.description: Auditude was a Palo Alto video advertising technology company founded in 2007 that let premium publishers, content owners and media companies manage, serve and monetize advertising around online video across multiple platforms and devices via its proprietary Auditude Connect platform. Backed by Redpoint Ventures and Greylock Partners with roughly $38M raised, its customers included Comcast, Sony Music and Universal Music Group. Adobe acquired Auditude in November 2011 for a reported ~$120M and folded the technology into Adobe Primetime (ad decisioning / ad insertion), since rebranded under Adobe Pass. Auditude no longer operates as an independent company: auditude.com does not resolve, and the only surviving public footprint is the legacy com.auditude.ads.* namespace inside Adobe's Primetime Player SDK documentation. This profile is retained as a defunct / acquired historical record; there is no Auditude API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Aurigin Systems
providers.description: Aurigin Systems, Inc. was an intellectual-property management software company founded in 1992 and headquartered in Cupertino, California. It built online patent and trademark information services and business-automation software for intellectual-asset management, raising roughly $54M in venture funding (investors included Battery Ventures) over its lifetime. The company operated under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection before substantially all of its assets were acquired by Information Holdings Inc. in May 2002. It is defunct, has no surviving website, developer portal, or public API, and was surfaced only as a historical portfolio lead from a Battery Ventures scrape.

providers.name: Automatic
providers.description: Automatic (Automatic Labs, Inc.) was a San Francisco connected-car company founded in 2011 by Thejo Kote and Jerry Jariyasunant. Its OBD-II adapter and companion mobile app turned almost any car built since 1996 into a connected car, adding trip logging, fuel and MPG tracking, engine-light diagnostics, parking recall, and automatic crash alerts. Automatic ran a public developer platform at developer.automatic.com built around three surfaces: a REST API exposing trip, user, and vehicle data; an Events API delivering real-time driving events such as ignition on/off, hard braking, acceleration, speeding, and location changes over webhooks and websockets; and a private-beta Streaming SDK that read raw OBD-II data from the second-generation adapter over Bluetooth. SiriusXM acquired the company on 2017-04-27 for approximately $115 million, and all operations were shut down on 2020-05-28. THIS COMPANY IS DEFUNCT — no API, developer portal, or documentation remains online, and the automatic.com domain now belongs to the unrelated company Automattic. This profile is retained as a historical record of a notable connected-car API platform.

providers.name: Avanex
providers.description: Avanex Corporation was a fiber-optic components manufacturer founded in 1997 and headquartered in Fremont, California, backed by Mayfield along with Crosspoint Venture Partners, JAFCO America and Sequoia Capital. Avanex designed and built photonic processors, optical components, modules and subsystems used to raise the speed and capacity of fiber-optic communication networks, and went public on NASDAQ in February 2000 raising $216 million. In April 2009 Avanex merged with Bookham Technology to form Oclaro, and Oclaro was in turn acquired by Lumentum in December 2018. Avanex is no longer an operating company: it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API of any kind, and the avanex.com domain is now a parked GoDaddy for-sale listing. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lineage record only.

providers.name: Avenue
providers.description: Avenue is an operations observability and workflow-automation platform that helps operations, RevOps, and support teams detect problems and act on them in real time. It connects to the tools and databases a business already runs on (Postgres, Google Sheets, Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, Linear, Asana, Notion), watches for issues using custom rules and thresholds, and routes alerts into a shared task queue where teams triage and resolve them. A drag-and-drop playbook builder and an operational AI copilot automate routine responses, while metrics track resolution over time. Avenue is used by operations leaders at marketplaces, fintech, and healthcare companies. It was founded in 2021 by Justin Bleuel and Jeff Barg, and was backed by Y Combinator, Slack Fund, Accel, Flexport, Lachy Groom, and Elad Gil. Avenue was acquired by Clay in January 2025 and the product has since been wound down: the marketing site at avenue.app is still served but frozen at "© 2024 Avenue", the application host app.useavenue.com returns HTTP 404 "Application not found", and the Intercom help center at docs.useavenue.com returns HTTP 403. Avenue never published a public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, MCP server, or agent card; the only developer- facing surface it documented was inbound and outbound webhooks.

providers.name: Aviate
providers.description: Aviate was an "intelligent homescreen" launcher for Android, built by ThumbsUp Labs (founded 2011 by Paul Montoy-Wilson, William Choi, and Mark Daiss). The app reorganized a phone home screen contextually — surfacing apps, contacts, and information based on time, location, and activity. It raised a $1.8M seed round in May 2013 from Highland Capital Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Freestyle Capital, and Draper Associates, and was acquired by Yahoo in January 2014. Yahoo discontinued the Aviate launcher on March 8, 2018. The company is defunct: it never shipped a public API, developer portal, or SDK, aviate.com is now a parked domain listed for sale, aviate.yahoo.com redirects to downloads.yahoo.com, and the ThumbsUp Labs GitHub organization has no public repositories.

providers.name: AVO
providers.description: Avo (avonow.com) was a New York City-based "building commerce" and workplace-amenity platform, founded 2017-2018 out of Y Combinator (S18) and backed by Insight Partners and Kleiner Perkins with roughly $84M raised. It offered white-labeled same-day delivery of groceries, household goods, alcohol and personal-care items into residential and office buildings with no order minimums or delivery fees, plus on-site and virtual event programming and corporate gifting and recognition services, serving apartment communities, corporations, hospitals and universities across New York, New Jersey, Chicago and Houston. Avo published no API, SDK or developer portal, and as of a 2026-07-20 probe its domain resolves to a parked lander with no operational hosts; Y Combinator lists the company as inactive.

providers.name: Axiall
providers.description: Axiall Corporation was a manufacturer and international marketer of chemicals and building products, including chlorovinyls (chlor-alkali, PVC resin and vinyl compounds) and aromatics, for use in industrial and consumer applications. Westlake Chemical completed its acquisition of Axiall on 2016-08-31 and the Axiall brand and website have been absorbed into Westlake; the company published no developer program or API.

providers.name: Azuqua
providers.description: Azuqua was a Seattle-based integration platform as a service (iPaaS) and no-code workflow-automation company, backed by Insight Partners and Techstars, that let business teams build integrations and automated workflows (FLOs) across SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Slack, Marketo and ServiceNow. Azuqua was acquired by Okta in 2019 and its workflow orchestration engine and connectors were folded into Okta Workflows (part of Okta Lifecycle Management). The standalone product is now end-of-life: azuqua.com serves an acquisition notice and the API is no longer available for purchase. This API Evangelist profile documents the surviving public developer surface (legacy ReadMe docs, changelog, llms.txt) and the product's lifecycle status.

providers.name: Babel Finance
providers.description: Babel Finance was a Hong Kong-based crypto financial services provider offering crypto asset lending and borrowing, asset management, brokerage and derivatives trading, and mining-related financing to institutional and high-net-worth clients. It reached a USD 2B valuation on an USD 80M Series B in May 2022 with backing that included Multicoin Capital, then froze customer redemptions and withdrawals weeks later in June 2022 amid the Three Arrows Capital and Celsius contagion. The company disclosed roughly USD 766M in losses, pursued a Singapore court moratorium and a scheme of arrangement, and floated a crypto-backed stablecoin to repay creditors. As of this enrichment pass the company is listed as permanently closed and its primary domain babel.finance no longer resolves (no NS delegation), so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct crypto-lending provider.

providers.name: Backtype
providers.description: BackType was a San Francisco social-media analytics startup (backed by 500 Startups/500 Global) whose BackTweets product helped publishers measure the reach and conversion of their Tweets and content for clients including The New York Times, HubSpot, bitly, and SlideShare. The BackType team also built Storm, the distributed real-time stream-processing system later open-sourced as Apache Storm. Twitter acquired BackType on July 5, 2011 and folded the team into its platform group; the standalone product and public API were discontinued after the acquisition. The company is defunct and backtype.com is now a parked domain, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: BackWeb
providers.description: BackWeb Technologies Ltd. was an Israeli-American enterprise software company founded in 1995 by Eli Barkat, Nir Barkat, Yuval Rakavy, Iftah Sneh and Lior Hass, with offices in Ramat Gan, Israel and San Jose, California. BackWeb pioneered "Polite" push technology — background delivery of software updates, patches, alerts and marketing content to desktops using only idle bandwidth so it did not disrupt the user or the corporate network. Its Polite Communication Server, Offline Access Server, e-Accelerator and Proactive Portal products were deployed by Cisco, Hewlett-Packard, IBM, Ericsson, Compaq and SAP, and integrators used the BackWeb Server Extension API and BackWeb Automation SDK to publish content from external data sources into the Polite server. The company IPO'd on NASDAQ (BWEB) in June 1999 after raising roughly $13M privately from investors including Goldman Sachs, Intel and Trinity Ventures, peaking near $38M in annual revenue. It never recovered from the dot-com collapse, was delisted from NASDAQ and moved to the OTC Bulletin Board, approved a voluntary liquidation in 2012, suspended operations and divested its patents in 2014, and began distributing remaining cash to shareholders. BackWeb is defunct: there is no operating company, no developer portal, and no live API. The backweb.com domain is a parked Afternic for-sale lander. This profile is retained as a historical record only.

providers.name: Baker Technologies
providers.description: Baker Technologies (Baker) was a Denver, Colorado based customer relationship management (CRM) and marketing platform built for the cannabis industry, founded in 2014 by David Champion, Joel Milton, and Roger Obando. A graduate of the 500 Startups accelerator, Baker helped licensed dispensaries grow revenue and build customer relationships through online ordering, loyalty programs, SMS/text messaging, and analytics, and launched an expanded integrations program with a developer API connecting dispensaries to 20+ ancillary cannabis services. The company raised approximately $11.75M (including an $8M Series A) before being acquired by TILT Holdings in 2018. The trybaker.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, indicating the product has been discontinued; no live developer portal, API documentation, or specifications are publicly available.

providers.name: Balanced
providers.description: Balanced was a payments API for online marketplaces and crowdfunding platforms, founded out of Y Combinator (W2011) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), SV Angel, Collaborative Fund, and angels including Brian Chesky and Ashton Kutcher. It offered a developer-first API for processing cards and bank (ACH) payments, paying out to sellers, and handling seller identity/underwriting for marketplaces. Balanced announced on 2015-03-13 that it was shutting down its payments platform and gave customers 90 days notice, striking a transition deal that migrated card, bank account, and seller identity data to Stripe by 2015-06-11. The company and its API are defunct; the balancedpayments.com domain is now a parked/lander page and the api/docs hosts no longer resolve.
