providers.name: BankOns
providers.description: BankOns was a San Mateo, California mobile savings startup founded in the summer of 2010 by Joshua Greenough, a former VP of Operations at PowerReviews. Launched in May 2011, the app connected a user's bank transaction history to their location, analyzing spending habits to surface the nearby merchant deals and rewards best suited to them, drawing on Foursquare and other local deals data. The name was a contraction of "bank" and "coupons". BankOns was seed funded by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) plus a friends-and-family round. In May 2012 Capital One acquired select BankOns software through a limited asset purchase agreement, and several team members including Greenough joined Capital One Labs. The product was wound down and the company no longer operates a consumer service or a developer platform. The bankons.com domain resolves to a GoDaddy parking lander with no content, and no API, documentation, SDK, or developer surface exists.

providers.name: Barneyscan
providers.description: Barneyscan was a San Leandro, California color imaging company founded in 1986 that built one of the first high-quality 24-bit color film scanners and related graphic-arts software for the press and prepress industry. It is best known as the origin of Adobe Photoshop, whose early version 0.87 shipped bundled with Barneyscan scanners as "Barneyscan XP" before Adobe licensed it. Backed by Battery Ventures, Bay Partners, and OSCCO Ventures, the company was acquired by PixelCraft on March 1, 1993 and no longer operates. It has no live website, developer portal, or public API surface, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: bash.gg
providers.description: bash.gg was a browser-based indie game marketplace built on Solana (founded by Kyle Zappitell, a former Xbox engineer) that let independent developers sell games directly in the browser without the ~30% platform commissions charged by Steam, Xbox, Apple, and PlayStation, with 10% royalties routed back to developers on resale. It entered the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead and was kept as a stub. Re-probed on 2026-07-20, the company remains defunct - the bash.gg domain is parked for sale on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket (NS delegated to afternic.com, null MX, SPF "-all"), there is no live developer portal, API, or documentation, and the company GitHub organization (github.com/bash-gg) exists but publishes zero repositories. Wayback captures show the site only ever exposed Next.js/NextAuth internal routes (/api/auth/session), never a public developer API. No provider artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived. No fabrication was performed.

providers.name: Battlebound
providers.description: Battlebound was a Los Angeles-based blockchain / play-to-earn game studio founded in May 2021 by former Riot Games technical artist Adam Hensel (pseudonym Damos), with a team drawn from Blizzard, Ubisoft, NCSoft and Riot Games. In March 2022 it raised a $4.8M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from Play Ventures and Dapper Labs. Its titles were Evaverse, a Steam-published social metaverse game using NFTs as playable avatars, and an in-development RPG codenamed Anterris (also referenced as "Project A"). The studio wound down amid the collapse of the web3 gaming market; as of 2025 it is defunct and the battlebound.com domain is parked and listed for sale. The company never published a public API, SDK, or developer platform, so there is no API surface to catalog or enrich.

providers.name: BeBop Sensors
providers.description: BeBop Sensors was a Berkeley, California smart-fabric sensor company founded in 2014 that designed and manufactured flexible, fabric-based pressure and touch sensors for OEMs across robotics, medical devices, automotive interiors, and virtual reality. Its best known products were haptic VR gloves and "intelligent sensing technology" surfaces that turned ordinary materials into multi-touch, pressure-sensitive inputs. The company raised a $10M+ Series A led by Bullpen Capital and shipped custom sensor hardware paired with bespoke firmware and integration software for enterprise customers. BeBop sold engineered hardware under contract rather than a self-serve developer product, and never published a public API, developer portal, or SDK. The company is no longer operating and its former domain has been repurposed by an unrelated third party.

providers.name: Bedrock Materials
providers.description: Bedrock Materials was a Chicago-based deep-tech startup founded in 2023 by Spencer Gore (CEO, previously Tesla and Enovix) and Rafael Vila (CTO, Stanford battery scientist) to manufacture engineered sodium-ion cathode active materials as a low-cost, easy-to-source alternative to lithium-ion — built from abundant sodium, manganese, iron and aluminum, and designed to drop into existing lithium-ion cell manufacturing lines for low-voltage, starter-lighting-ignition, micromobility and industrial-traction applications. It raised a $9M seed round led by Trucks Venture Capital with Refactor Capital and Version One Ventures. In April 2025 the company wound down and returned the majority of that seed capital to its investors: CEO Spencer Gore concluded that sodium-ion could not be produced cheaply enough to beat lithium iron phosphate (LFP) after lithium oversupply collapsed prices, and that energy-density gains carried steep trade-offs. Bedrock Materials was a materials-science manufacturer and never operated a developer program, public API, or developer portal; both bedrockmaterials.com and its former bedrock.inc website are now parked/for-sale domains with no company content. This profile is retained as a verified-defunct record in the API Evangelist network — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Beek
providers.description: Beek was a Spanish-language audiobook and ebook streaming platform serving Latin America and Spain, backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners. At its peak it reached over 4 million users who streamed nearly 200 million minutes of audio content, including its exclusive Beek Originals catalog. The service has since shut down: Amazon's Audible acquired a significant portion of the Beek Originals catalog, and Beek now redirects listeners to Audible to continue their libraries. Beek ran a private backend service (api.beek.io) but published no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation, so it has no consumable API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Believer Meats
providers.description: Believer Meats is a cultivated-meat company founded in 2018 in Rehovot, Israel as Future Meat Technologies by Hebrew University bioengineer Yaakov Nahmias, rebranded to Believer Meats in November 2022 and later headquartered in the United States under CEO Gustavo Burger. It grew chicken, lamb and beef from animal cells in a continuous fermentation process rather than raising and slaughtering animals, raised roughly USD 390 million across a 2019 Series A and a 2021 USD 347 million Series B backed by Tyson Foods, ADM, Emerald Technology Ventures, Bits x Bites, Cibus Fund and Menora Mivtachim, and completed a 200,000 square-foot production plant in Wilson, North Carolina billed as the largest cultivated-meat facility in the world. In 2025 it received an FDA "No Questions" letter for its cultivated chicken followed by USDA label and facility clearance, and then ceased operations in December 2025 after its largest investor withdrew. It was a food-biotechnology and manufacturing business rather than a software vendor: it published no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract, and its Webflow marketing site — last republished in October 2025 — now stands as an archive of a company that is no longer operating.

providers.name: Beme
providers.description: Beme Inc. (stylized "beme") was an American multimedia company founded in 2014 in New York City by YouTube filmmaker Casey Neistat and engineer Matt Hackett. Its mobile app, released on iOS in July 2015 and on Android in May 2016, let users capture and instantly share unedited two-to-eight-second videos without previewing or editing them, aiming at a more authentic alternative to curated social video. Beme raised a seed round backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Vayner/RSE, and CNN acquired the company in November 2016 in a deal reported at $25 million. The consumer app was shut down on January 31, 2017, and on January 25, 2018 the founders departed and Beme was folded into CNN Digital Studios. The company is defunct. Beme never published a public API, developer portal, or API documentation; its only public technical artifact is an open-source Go testing utility. The beme.com domain has since changed hands and now redirects to an unrelated company.

providers.name: Berry Plastics Group
providers.description: Berry Plastics Group was a manufacturer and marketer of plastic packaging products, nonwoven specialty materials, and engineered materials serving customers across consumer and industrial markets. The company was renamed Berry Global Group in 2017 to reflect its global operations and diversified product portfolio beyond plastics. As Berry Global, the company agreed in November 2024 to an all-stock combination with Amcor plc, which completed on 30 April 2025; berryglobal.com now redirects to Amcor's packaging site. It never published a developer program, an API, or a machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Beryllium
providers.description: Beryllium was a Singapore- and Delhi-based sports and trading game development platform founded in 2018/2019 by Amay Makhija, best known for its consumer product Sixer — a fantasy cricket game where users bought "Up" or "Down" virtual stocks in professional cricketers, with prices moving on in-game batting, bowling, and fielding metrics. The company raised roughly $3.6M across two rounds, including a $3M pre-Series A in June 2021 led by Bullpen Capital with Genting Ventures and Velo Partners. Beryllium was acquired by Dream Sports (Dream11) in October 2023. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct as an independent operator: sixer.gg no longer resolves in DNS, and beryllium.ai is a parked domain listed for sale on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket. Beryllium never published a public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.

providers.name: Binaris
providers.description: Binaris was a fast, low-latency Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) platform for running production Node.js workloads in the cloud. Founded in 2017 and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, its developer surface centered on the `bn` command-line tool and Node.js SDK (published to npm as `binaris` and to Docker Hub as `binaris/bn`), which let developers scaffold, deploy, invoke, and inspect serverless functions in seconds. Authentication was via a Binaris API key (`BINARIS_API_KEY`). The company later explored a "Shift" programming model (`@binaris/shift-fetch-runtime`). The hosted platform at binaris.io / binaris.com is no longer in service, but the first-party client packages and a 42-repository GitHub organization remain publicly available and are captured here.

providers.name: Binary Thumbs
providers.description: Binary Thumbs (operating name "Binary Thumb", Y Combinator Summer 2012) was a San Francisco startup founded in 2012 by Josh Leong, Michael Lin, and Matt Monson to reinvent the spreadsheet for touch devices. Its single product, Grid, was a collaborative grid-based spreadsheet and organizational app for iPad and iPhone that let people keep notes, pictures, people, and places in a freeform grid rather than rigid rows and columns. The company raised roughly $2.15M across a 2012 YC round and a 2013 seed, with participation from angel and institutional investors, and appears on the Andreessen Horowitz public investment list. Y Combinator now lists the company as inactive; Josh Leong led it as CEO from 2012 to 2016. Binary Thumb never shipped a public API, developer portal, or documentation surface -- it was a consumer iOS product company. Its lasting public technical footprint is the BinaryThumb GitHub organization and a handful of open-source React and JavaScript utility libraries published to npm.

providers.name: Bing News Search
providers.description: Microsoft Bing News Search REST API enables developers to retrieve relevant news articles, trending topics, and category-filtered news with image thumbnails and publisher metadata. The API provides search queries against Bing's news index, returning results with titles, descriptions, URLs, publication dates, and related media content.

providers.name: Binpress
providers.description: Binpress was a marketplace for commercial source code and open-source software components, founded in 2011 in Israel by Adam Benayoun (CEO) and Eran Galperin (CTO) and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global). The platform let developers publish, discover, buy, and sell SDKs, libraries, and code components on a 70/30 revenue split, growing to roughly 1,000 listings with GitHub integration and later adding hosted storefronts for digital goods. The company was acquired by CodersClan in 2016 and no longer operates as an active developer platform; the binpress.com domain has since been repurposed as an unrelated digital-business content site with no public API. This profile originated as a 500 Global portfolio lead surfaced into the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Bit.io
providers.description: Bit.io was a serverless, shareable PostgreSQL database platform that let developers spin up cloud Postgres databases in seconds, load and query data, and share them via a link, with programmatic access over the standard Postgres wire protocol. Founded by Adam Fletcher and Jonathan Mortensen and backed by Battery Ventures, bit.io was acquired by Databricks in May 2023; the standalone product was sunset on June 29, 2023 (database exports available through July 29, 2023) and the team moved to Databricks. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired network record — there is no live API, developer portal, documentation, or discovery surface to enrich.

providers.name: Bitcasa
providers.description: Bitcasa, Inc. was an American cloud storage company (founded 2011 in St. Louis, Missouri; later based in Mountain View, California) known for its converged/infinite storage model and, for developers, the CloudFS API — a white-label cloud-storage platform that let third-party applications integrate file management, secure sharing, media transcoding, instant streaming, and zero-knowledge client-side encryption. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), CrunchFund, Pelion Venture Partners, Horizons Ventures, Samsung Ventures, and First Round Capital, Bitcasa wound down its consumer Bitcasa Drive service in 2016 and shut down all services in 2017. The company is defunct and the bitcasa.com domain is now parked, so no live developer surface, API documentation, or specifications remain to enrich.

providers.name: Bitfusion
providers.description: Bitfusion (Bitfusion.io) was a GPU virtualization startup whose FlexDirect software pooled and disaggregated GPUs across a network so machine learning and AI workloads could share accelerator hardware on demand. VMware acquired Bitfusion in August 2019 and folded the technology into vSphere as "vSphere Bitfusion." VMware/Broadcom later declared End of Availability for vSphere Bitfusion effective May 2023, with end of maintenance in May 2025. The independent company no longer operates and the bitfusion.io domain no longer resolves; there is no independent, active public API surface remaining for this provider.

providers.name: Bitfusion Io
providers.description: Bitfusion (bitfusion.io) was an Austin, Texas startup, backed by DCVC, that built "elastic AI" infrastructure software. Its FlexDirect platform was a transparent GPU/CPU virtualization layer that pooled network-attached accelerators (GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs) across TCP, RoCE, and InfiniBand into a single elastic compute cluster for sharing, scaling, and management of AI/ML workloads. VMware acquired Bitfusion in 2019 and folded FlexDirect into vSphere as vSphere Bitfusion (subsequently end-of-lifed). The independent company no longer operates, the bitfusion.io domain no longer resolves, and it exposes no public API, developer portal, or discoverable artifacts. Retained here as a DCVC portfolio record; defunct as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: BitYota
providers.description: BitYota was a Data-Warehouse-as-a-Service (DWaaS) startup founded around 2011 in Santa Clara, California, offering a SaaS analytics data warehouse that ran on top of Amazon Web Services and Rackspace infrastructure and natively queried semi-structured JSON data. The company's team of data-processing engineers was acqui-hired by LifeLock in August 2015 for approximately $12.8 million, and the standalone BitYota product and company were subsequently wound down. The primary domain bityota.com no longer resolves (no DNS records), no public API, developer portal, documentation, source repositories, or client SDKs survive, and there is no active API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest. This profile is retained for historical/network completeness and is flagged defunct.

providers.name: Bix
providers.description: Bix was an online talent-competition community founded in 2006 by Mike Speiser (co-founder of Epinions), where users created and judged web-based contests across karaoke, dance, photography, writing, beauty, and comedy. Backed by Trinity Ventures, the roughly 16-person startup grew to over one million users within months and was acquired by Yahoo! in November 2006; Yahoo later shut the service down. This API Evangelist profile documents Bix as a historical, defunct consumer company with no live website, developer platform, or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Blekko
providers.description: Blekko was a web search engine founded in 2007 by Rich Skrenta, Tom Annau, and Mike Markson and launched publicly in 2010. It was best known for "slashtags" — user-applied /slashtag filters that curated and narrowed search results by category as a spam-resistant alternative to mainstream search engines — and it exposed a developer search API. Blekko was acquired by IBM in March 2015, where its technology and team were folded into the IBM Watson group and its consumer search engine was shut down. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical/defunct record; the company no longer operates a live website or public API (blekko.com resolves in DNS but no longer serves HTTPS).

providers.name: Blink Booking
providers.description: Blink Booking was a Madrid, Spain based mobile application for last-minute hotel booking, founded in 2011 by Rebeca Minguela and Miguel Ortega Rodriguez. The app presented travellers with a curated daily selection of four discounted hotels for same-day stays, working with more than 2,000 hotel partners across eight European countries, and competed directly with HotelTonight. The company raised approximately $2.5M in a Series A round in May 2012 from Ventech, Uncork Capital (then SoftTech VC), 500 Global (then 500 Startups) and Kibo Ventures. Groupon acquired Blink Booking in September 2013 to strengthen its Groupon Getaways travel division; the app was rebranded "Blink by Groupon" and was wound down over the following months. The company is defunct and publishes no developer surface, no API, and no documentation. Its former blinkbooking.com domain lapsed and was re-registered in August 2020 by an unrelated party; it now redirects to a third-party gambling site and must not be treated as a company property.

providers.name: Blissmo
providers.description: Blissmo is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: BlockChalk
providers.description: BlockChalk was a location-based neighborhood messaging service founded in 2009 by Stephen Hood, the former product lead for Delicious, and Dave Baggeroer of the Stanford Institute of Design. Users with GPS-enabled smartphones left short public messages called "chalks" pinned to a specific geographic point, and read the chalks other people had left on their block, so neighbors could ask, answer, praise, gripe, report potholes and lost pets, announce garage sales and organize locally. The company raised $1M in seed financing in May 2010 from Joshua Schachter, Battery Ventures, Founder Collective, Harrison Metal, Mitch Kapor, Josh Stylman, Tom McInerney and David Liu. BlockChalk published a small read-only public API on its developer page, offering XML, JSON and RSS interfaces that returned nearby chalks for a supplied latitude and longitude, later joined by a versioned GeoRSS endpoint. The product and the company are retired: blockchalk.com holds an active domain registration but its delegated nameservers no longer resolve, and no BlockChalk host answers on the public internet. This profile preserves the historical API surface as documentation.

providers.name: BlockFi
providers.description: BlockFi was a Jersey City, New Jersey crypto-financial-services company founded in 2017 by Zac Prince and Flori Marquez that offered retail and institutional clients interest-bearing crypto accounts (the BlockFi Interest Account), USD loans collateralized by bitcoin and other digital assets, spot trading, and a bitcoin-rewards credit card, growing on a USD 350 million Series D in March 2021 that valued it at roughly USD 3 billion. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in November 2022 in the wake of the FTX and Alameda Research collapse, and emerged in October 2023 not as an operating business but as a wind-down estate. Its customer web platform and mobile apps have been shut down, in-kind crypto distributions are administered through Coinbase and cash distributions through Kroll Restructuring Administration and Digital Disbursements, and blockfi.com is now a WordPress notice site carrying noindex/nofollow and dated estate updates rather than a product. There is no operating developer program: api.blockfi.com and every other developer, docs and app subdomain no longer resolve in DNS, the company GitHub organization holds zero public repositories, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, MCP or agent-card document is served from any surviving BlockFi host.

providers.name: Blockspring
providers.description: Blockspring was a data integration and enrichment platform that let developers and spreadsheet users run cloud functions and connect to hundreds of third-party APIs and data services from Google Sheets, Excel, and via its own API. Founded around 2014 and originally Y Combinator backed, it was acquired by Coda (Krypton) in 2017 and surfaced here as an a16z portfolio-associated company. All Blockspring services -- the website tooling, integrations, plugins, APIs, and data enrichment -- were permanently shut down on December 29, 2022, with active subscriptions cancelled and prorated refunds issued. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no live developer surface, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: BlockVigil
providers.description: BlockVigil was a blockchain / Web3 developer platform company, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the enrichment pass on 2026-07-18, the company's website (https://blockvigil.com) publishes only a wind-down notice stating that "BlockVigil has concluded its active service offerings," directing remaining custom-contract customers to their designated representative. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or well-known/ metadata are published; this profile therefore captures only live domain-security posture and the discontinuation status.

providers.name: Bloom
providers.description: Bloom was a decentralized identity, credit-attestation and verifiable-credentials company backed by Pantera Capital, built on Ethereum and IPFS around three products: BloomID (identity attestation), BloomIQ (a credit registry) and BloomScore (credit risk scoring). Its stated aim was to let traditional and digital-currency lenders serve people who cannot obtain a bank account or a credit score, and it announced a TransUnion partnership in 2020 for consumer credit monitoring. Bloom is wound down. Its integration SDKs were archived on GitHub in 2021, its API, documentation and status hosts no longer resolve, bloom.co now redirects to a domain-broker sale listing, and Bloom HoldCo LLC filed a Form 15-12G on 2025-08-14 terminating Exchange Act registration of its BLT token with holders of record stated as "none". What survives is open source: 40 public repositories under github.com/hellobloom and 19 unmaintained but installable npm packages under the @bloomprotocol scope implementing the W3C and DIF decentralized-identity stack (Verifiable Credentials, DIDs, Presentation Exchange, Credential Manifest, WACI).

providers.name: Blooom
providers.description: Blooom was an independent robo-advisor that provided automated, flat-fee management of employer-sponsored retirement accounts — 401(k), 403(b), 457, and TSP plans — analyzing holdings, rebalancing allocations, and flagging hidden fund fees on accounts it advised but did not directly custody. Founded in 2013 and backed by QED Investors, the Kansas-based company operated a consumer web application rather than a public developer API. The consumer service has since wound down: blooom.com no longer resolves to a website and the domain is now served by Morgan Stanley nameservers with a locked-down, mail-disabled defensive DNS posture (null MX, SPF -all, DMARC p=reject). Retained here as a historical wealth-management profile; no live API or developer surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Blue Flame Data
providers.description: Blue Flame Data was an early-2000s consumer-preference analytics company (founded around 2000 in New York City) that built web-based software for real-time measurement of consumer market preferences, marketed as TrueChoice Preference Technology for quantifying the preference structures of individual consumers and employees. The company appears to be defunct: its domain (blueflamedata.com) resolves to a parked/unresponsive IP and does not serve a live site. It was surfaced to the API Evangelist network via Battery Ventures portfolio mining. During enrichment no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, packages, MCP server, or other machine-readable artifacts could be located, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Blue Jeans Network
providers.description: Blue Jeans Network (later BlueJeans by Verizon) was a cloud-based video conferencing company founded in 2009 in Mountain View / San Jose, California. It delivered interoperable video meetings across desktop, mobile, and conference-room systems, and offered a developer surface that included the onVideo/Meetings REST API and a WebRTC Embed SDK for embedding live video into applications. Verizon acquired BlueJeans in 2020; Verizon subsequently discontinued the BlueJeans service and the bluejeans.com website and developer portal are no longer reachable. This profile preserves the company's published package artifacts, which persist in public registries even though the hosted service is retired. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Bluebox
providers.description: Bluebox (Bluebox Security) was an enterprise mobile and application security startup founded around 2012 that let organizations secure corporate data on employee-owned smartphones and tablets without managing the whole device. It raised roughly $27.5M, with Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) leading its Series A and returning for the Series B alongside Tenaya Capital, Andreas Bechtolsheim, and SV Angel. Its technology assets were acquired by Lookout on April 8, 2016, after which Bluebox ceased operating as an independent company. It was a packaged security product vendor, not a public API provider, and it maintains no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface today.

providers.name: Bluefin Labs
providers.description: Bluefin Labs was a social TV analytics company founded in 2008 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Deb Roy and Michael Fleischman, spun out of research at the MIT Media Lab. Its platform semantically interpreted public social media commentary from Twitter, Facebook and blogs and automatically linked those comments to the television shows and advertisements people were watching, producing audience engagement measurement for networks, agencies and brands. Its product, Bluefin Signals, gave media buyers a tool for accessing and analyzing social TV response data. The company raised a Series A led by Redpoint Ventures in 2010 and a $12M Series B led by Time Warner Investments in January 2012, with SoftBank Capital and Lerer Ventures participating. Twitter acquired Bluefin Labs on February 6, 2013 for a reported ~$100 million and absorbed the team and technology into its TV advertising and analytics products. The company is DEFUNCT: it operates no independent product, developer program or API, and the bluefinlabs.com domain no longer belongs to the company — it now redirects to an unrelated news site. This profile is retained as a historical / portfolio-graph record only.

providers.name: BlueKai
providers.description: BlueKai was a data management platform (DMP) and third-party audience data marketplace founded in 2008 that let marketers collect, organize, and activate first- and third-party audience data for programmatic advertising and targeting. Oracle acquired BlueKai in 2014 and folded it into the Oracle Data Cloud; Oracle wound down its advertising business (including the former BlueKai and Data Cloud assets) in 2024. The company operates no independent developer program today — the bluekai.com domain 301-redirects to Oracle's advertising pages and exposes no live public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bluelearn
providers.description: Bluelearn was an India-based community-driven learning and edtech startup backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears inactive - its primary domain (bluelearn.in) no longer serves a product site and instead resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander page, with no reachable HTTPS endpoint, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. No OpenAPI, SDK, or other machine-readable API artifacts were found to search, generate, or derive from. This profile remains a lead pending any revived public developer surface.

providers.name: BlueStripe Software
providers.description: BlueStripe Software was an application performance management (APM) vendor headquartered in the Research Triangle Park area of North Carolina. Its flagship product, FactFinder, provided application-aware infrastructure performance monitoring and end-to-end transaction tracing across distributed servers, letting operations teams map and troubleshoot how applications behaved across physical, virtual, and cloud infrastructure. The company was backed by Trinity Ventures and other venture investors before being acquired by Microsoft in April 2015, after which its technology was folded into Microsoft System Center and the Operations Management Suite (OMS) and the standalone BlueStripe product and developer surface were discontinued. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record; the company no longer operates an independent website, developer portal, or API.

providers.name: BMC Stock Holdings
providers.description: BMC Stock Holdings, Inc. was one of the largest professional building materials distributors in the United States, serving homebuilders, remodelers, and contractors with lumber, structural components, millwork, doors, windows, and installed services. The company was formed in December 2015 through the merger of Stock Building Supply and Building Materials Holding Corporation (BMHC) and traded on NASDAQ under the ticker BMCH, headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina. On January 1, 2021, BMC Stock Holdings completed an all-stock "merger of equals" with Builders FirstSource (NYSE: BLDR), creating the nation's largest supplier of structural building products to the professional homebuilding market. The combined company retained the Builders FirstSource name, BLDR ticker, and Irving, Texas headquarters. The merger had an enterprise value of approximately $2.5 billion and produced a company with more than $11 billion in annual sales, approximately 26,000 employees, and roughly 550 distribution and manufacturing locations across more than 40 U.S. states. BMC Stock Holdings no longer exists as an independent entity. The legacy buildwithbmc.com domain redirects to bldr.com, and BMC product lines and branches have been absorbed into the Builders FirstSource network. This profile is retained as a historical Fortune 1000 record (BMC ranked #677 prior to the merger) and as a redirect to the successor profile at api-evangelist/builders-firstsource. BMC operated as a commodity-and-services distributor and did not publish public developer APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal. No API surface is documented for this provider.

providers.name: Bolt Threads
providers.description: Bolt Threads, Inc. was a San Francisco Bay Area biomaterials company founded in 2009 to engineer protein- and mycelium-based materials. It is best known for Microsilk, a bioengineered spider-silk fiber; Mylo, a mycelium-derived leather alternative developed with partners including adidas, Kering, Lululemon, Patagonia and Stella McCartney; and b-silk protein, a silk-protein ingredient for beauty and personal care. The company went public on Nasdaq in August 2024 via a SPAC business combination under the ticker BSLK, halted Mylo production, was suspended from Nasdaq in January 2026, and now trades OTC Pink while deregistering with the SEC. Its website serves only a notice that the company is no longer operating. Bolt Threads was a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor, and never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Bon-Ton Stores
providers.description: The Bon-Ton Stores was a regional department store chain in the United States that operated stores across the Midwest, Northeast, and upper Great Plains. Founded in 1898 in York, Pennsylvania, the company sold apparel, accessories, cosmetics, home furnishings, and other merchandise under banners including Bon-Ton, Bergner's, Boston Store, Carson's, Elder-Beerman, Herberger's, and Younkers. The company filed for bankruptcy and ceased operations in 2018.

providers.name: Boost Media
providers.description: Boost Media (formerly BoostCTR) was a digital-advertising creative-optimization SaaS platform that paired machine-learning analysis with a curated marketplace of more than 1,000 human writers and designers to test and improve ad creative across paid search, social, video, and display campaigns. Its technology powered roughly $1 billion in paid-search advertising for around 100 global brands across retail, education, financial services, healthcare and insurance, gaming, auto, and travel. Backed by Battery Ventures (Series C, $19M, 2014), Founder Collective, and 500 Global, the company raised about $42.8M total before being acquired by AdLabs Technology in April 2019. The company is now closed; its former domain (boostmedia.com) has been released and now serves a GoDaddy parking lander, and the acquirer's own domain (adlabs.ai) no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a Battery Ventures portfolio record. No public API, developer portal, or specification surface exists to enrich — the Internet Archive record of boostmedia.com shows a WordPress marketing site and blog only, with no developer, docs, or API path ever published.

providers.name: Bop.fm
providers.description: Bop.fm was a music-sharing and playlist startup that let people share and play individual songs across streaming services — building a link for a track that would resolve to whichever service (Spotify, Deezer, SoundCloud, YouTube, Rdio) each listener used. Founded out of Y Combinator, it reportedly reached several million monthly listeners and raised roughly $2M before being acquihired by identity-protection company LifeLock in October 2015, at which point the website, mobile apps, and embedded players were shut down. The company is defunct: the bop.fm domain no longer serves the product (it now redirects to an unrelated parked site) and no developer portal, documentation, or API surface remains online. This profile is retained as a historical record within the API Evangelist network; there are no live API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Bowery
providers.description: Bowery Farming was an American indoor vertical-farming (controlled-environment agriculture) company headquartered in New York City that grew leafy greens and herbs in automated, pesticide-free indoor farms serving major East Coast metro areas. Once valued at roughly $2.3 billion and backed by investors including Bloomberg Beta and SV Angel, the company ceased operations in November 2024 and its facilities and equipment entered liquidation through 2025-2026. Bowery published no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or discovery surface; this API Evangelist profile records the company's identity and its probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Boxee
providers.description: Boxee, Inc. was a New York and Tel Aviv based consumer media company founded in 2007 by Avner Ronen, Tom Sella, Idan Cohen, Gidon Coussin and Roy Vulcan. Its cross-platform media-center software began as a fork of the open-source XBMC project and bridged local media libraries with internet streaming sources. Boxee shipped a Python-based application API in April 2009 that let third parties build Boxee apps in Python with XML-defined interfaces, distributed through the Boxee app directory and documented at developer.boxee.tv. Hardware followed with the D-Link Boxee Box (2010) and Boxee TV with a cloud DVR service (2012). Backed by Union Square Ventures and Spark Capital, Boxee was acquired by Samsung Electronics in July 2013; the cloud DVR was shut down on 10 July 2013 and Samsung wound down the Boxee team in 2015. The company is defunct and no API surface, developer portal, or documentation remains reachable.

providers.name: Boxy (ex-Storelift)
providers.description: Boxy, operated by the French company SAS Storelift (founded 2018 in Ivry-sur-Seine by David Gabai and Tom Hayat), built unstaffed 24/7 convenience stores inside 15-20 square metre shipping containers, using computer vision, weight-sensing shelves and an on-site compute node so a shopper could unlock the door with a QR code from the Boxy mobile app, take products off the shelf and walk out to be invoiced automatically. The company raised roughly 5M EUR in 2020 and a 25M EUR Series A in February 2022 led by Serena with CapHorn and LocalGlobe, targeting 1,000 stores. It shut its entire store estate by the end of April 2024, and SAS Storelift entered liquidation judiciaire on 6 November 2024 after sauvegarde and redressement procedures earlier that year; the store containers were auctioned in early 2025. The getboxy.co domain is now parked and returns HTTP 410 Gone on every path, and no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable contract was ever published. This profile records that absence.

providers.name: Brace
providers.description: Brace (Brace Software, Inc., brace.ai) was a Culver City, California fintech founded in 2017 by Eric Rachmel and Amr Mohamed that rebuilt mortgage default servicing as software. Its Default Management Platform covered the end-to-end loss-mitigation lifecycle for servicers, lenders and investors — a homeowner engagement portal, a centralized responsive application, a rules and underwriting engine, document classification and data extraction, and event-driven communications and reporting — replacing the paper-based, inconsistent default workflows used by top U.S. mortgage servicers. The company raised a reported ~$30M and was acquired by Boston-based mortgage technology firm Stavvy, announced 1 August 2023, folding Brace's loss-mitigation platform into Stavvy's eClosing, digital notarization and foreclosure suite. Brace does not survive as an independent surface: brace.ai now 301-redirects every path to stavvy.com/mortgage-servicing-solution, and no docs., developer., api. or app. subdomain resolves in DNS. No public API, developer portal, machine-readable specification or SDK was ever published under the Brace brand — the Wayback CDX index for brace.ai carries no developer or API path — so this profile records identity and exit rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Braid
providers.description: Braid Networks was a creator-economy startup that let creators build customizable landing pages unifying their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts and commerce links), build mailing lists, and engage followers via text and push notifications. Founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro, it raised a $6.8M seed round from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Initialized Capital. Braid was a consumer direct-to-fan product and never published a public developer API. The company was acquired by Laurel on 2026-01-01 to power Laurel's Signal product and has since shut down; the braid.network domain no longer serves a site.

providers.name: Brainient
providers.description: Brainient was a London-based advertising technology company founded in 2009 by Emi Gal that specialized in interactive video advertising and Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO). Its platform made online video ads more personalized and interactive by matching creative to real-time context such as socio-demographics, geolocation, device, time of day, and weather. Brainient was acquired by Teads in September 2016 and folded into the Teads Studio division; the standalone Brainient brand and its brainient.com domain are now defunct. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. No public API surface, developer documentation, or machine-readable specification was located for Brainient during enrichment.

providers.name: Brainshop.ai
providers.description: Make A Free A.I Brain

providers.name: Brewster
providers.description: Brewster was a New York-based mobile contacts startup founded by Steve Greenwood that launched an iOS app in July 2012 offering a "hyperconnected mobile address book" — it merged phone contacts with Google Apps, Facebook, Twitter, Foursquare and LinkedIn profiles, deduplicated them, and kept them self-updating in the cloud while surfacing relationship signals about who a user actually engaged with. The company was backed by Union Square Ventures and Slow Ventures. In October 2015 the founding team was acqui-hired by Restaurant Brands International (owner of Burger King and Tim Hortons) without the app or its data, and in March 2016 FullContact acquired Brewster's self-updating address book technology and shut the consumer product down within 30 days. Brewster never published a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI definition or developer portal, and no API surface survives today. This profile is retained as a historical record only.

providers.name: BrightFunnel
providers.description: BrightFunnel was a San Francisco-based B2B marketing analytics company founded in 2012 that built a revenue attribution and forecasting platform. Its Revenue Intelligence Suite gave B2B marketers multi-touch attribution, revenue-funnel analysis, account-based measurement, web analytics, and predictive forecasting so they could quantify marketing's impact on pipeline and revenue and align plans with business priorities. BrightFunnel was acquired by account-based marketing vendor Terminus in January 2018, and its multi-channel analytics were folded into the Terminus platform. It no longer operates as a standalone product: the brightfunnel.com domain now serves only a redirect, and there is no live developer portal, public API, documentation, SDK, or discovery surface (.well-known, llms.txt) to enrich. This profile remains a historical company stub, originally surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: Brightmail
providers.description: Brightmail was an email anti-spam software company founded in 1998 by Sunil Paul, best known for its network of "spam probe" honeypot email addresses that fed real-time anti-spam filtering rules to enterprise mail servers. Symantec acquired Brightmail in 2004 for roughly $370 million, and the technology shipped for years as Symantec Brightmail AntiSpam and later Symantec Mail Security; Symantec's enterprise security business was subsequently acquired by Broadcom in 2019. Brightmail today is a defunct brand with no independent developer program or public API surface — www.brightmail.com redirects to broadcom.com and the brightmail.com apex domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained for historical/network completeness rather than active API enrichment.

providers.name: Briko Robotics
providers.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

providers.name: Broadband Access
providers.description: Broadband Access Systems, Inc. was a Westborough, Massachusetts networking company founded in 1998 that built a next-generation Internet Protocol (IP) broadband access platform — a carrier-class cable-modem termination system (CMTS) that let cable operators and communications service providers deliver data, voice and video services over hybrid fiber-coax networks at scale. Matrix Partners was one of eight venture investors in the company alongside North Bridge Venture Partners, Norwest, Blueprint Ventures and Bowman Capital Management. ADC Telecommunications agreed on September 20, 2000 to acquire Broadband Access Systems for approximately $2.25 billion in ADC common stock, and the acquisition closed on October 2, 2000. The company was absorbed into ADC's cable and broadband business, which ADC later divested; ADC itself was acquired by TE Connectivity in 2010. Broadband Access Systems operated no public developer program and shipped hardware platforms rather than APIs; it has had no independent web, documentation, or API surface since 2000. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical venture-portfolio record only.

providers.name: Broadbus Technologies
providers.description: Broadbus Technologies was a video-on-demand (VOD) streaming infrastructure company based in Boxborough, Massachusetts. It developed RAM-based VOD streaming server technology (the B-1 server) used by cable operators to deliver on-demand video at scale. The company was acquired by Motorola in 2006 and folded into Motorola's Connected Home / cable video business. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As a defunct hardware and infrastructure vendor with no surviving corporate or developer presence, it exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or discoverable web surface to enrich.

providers.name: Brooktrout Technology
providers.description: Brooktrout Technology, Inc. was a Needham, Massachusetts telecommunications company founded in 1984 that designed fax and voice-processing hardware and software for computer telephony integration (CTI), including the TR114 and TR1034 fax boards and the SR140 host-based (software) fax product. Its developer kit, the Brooktrout SDK, provided C/C++ APIs for building fax, voice, and unified-messaging applications. Brooktrout was acquired by Excel Switching in 2000 (forming Brooktrout Technology / Excel), and the Brooktrout product line later became part of Dialogic, which continues to ship and document the Dialogic Brooktrout SDK. The brooktrout.com domain now redirects to Dialogic; Brooktrout survives as a legacy product brand rather than an independent company, and it has no standalone modern web-API developer surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead.

providers.name: buddybuild
providers.description: buddybuild was a mobile continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform for iOS and Android apps, offering automated builds, testing, user feedback, and over-the-air deployment to testers. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Kleiner Perkins, it was acquired by Apple in January 2018; the standalone service was wound down through 2018-2019 and its capabilities were folded into Apple's Xcode Cloud. The buddybuild.com domain now redirects to developer.apple.com/xcode-cloud/, and no independent developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface remains. Retained as a network record of an acquired/defunct provider rather than an active enrichment target.

providers.name: Bufferbox
providers.description: BufferBox was a Waterloo, Ontario startup that operated self-service parcel-pickup lockers for online shoppers, letting people route e-commerce deliveries to a nearby locker and collect them with a PIN. Google acquired BufferBox in November 2012 and wound the service down in early 2015. The company is defunct and operates no developer or API surface; the bufferbox.com and bufferbox.ca domains are parked (resolving to a Bizland placeholder host), so this profile carries no API artifacts. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical logistics / last-mile-delivery record.

providers.name: Builder.ai
providers.description: Builder.ai was a London-based AI-assisted software development platform, originally founded in 2016 as Engineer.ai by Sachin Dev Duggal, that let customers assemble custom web and mobile applications from reusable building blocks orchestrated by an AI assistant branded "Natasha." Positioned as a no-code/low-code "human-assisted AI" app factory, it raised large rounds from investors including Insight Partners, Microsoft, the Qatar Investment Authority and SoftBank's DeepCore. The company collapsed into insolvency and entered administration in 2025 amid a revenue-restatement controversy, and its public web and developer surfaces are no longer operational. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record; no live API, developer portal, or documentation could be verified during enrichment.

providers.name: Buildscience
providers.description: BuildScience Inc. (Y Combinator Winter 2015) was a PropTech startup based in Mountain View, California that built an operating-system platform for commercial buildings. Its software let building owners and facility operators deploy customized building-management solutions intended to reduce operational costs while improving tenant satisfaction, and the company reported deploying in a one-million-square-foot Class A office building. As of the 2026 enrichment pass the company appears dormant: the buildscience.com domain no longer serves a live product (the host returns a CloudFront default certificate that does not match the domain and a broken origin), no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be located, and the organization's single public GitHub repository was last updated in January 2020. This profile is retained as a verified-identity network record; no API artifacts could be enriched because the provider publishes no live API.

providers.name: Buildspace
providers.description: Buildspace was an online education platform and community that billed itself as "the biggest school in the world for people who wanted to work on their own ideas," running six-week cohort-based programs to help entrepreneurs and builders ship their own projects and startups. Backed by a16z, the company wound down its operations; its site now serves only a farewell letter and final video. It was a consumer education and community product, not an API provider, and exposes no public developer surface, API, documentation, or SDKs. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Bump
providers.description: Bump Technologies was a Mountain View, California mobile software company (2008-2014) behind Bump, an iOS and Android app that let two people exchange contacts, photos and files by physically bumping their phones together. Bump servers correlated accelerometer, location and network signals from two handsets to match the pair, then brokered the transfer. The company published a first-party Bump API and iOS/Android SDKs so third-party apps could embed the same proximity-matching handshake. Backed by Y Combinator, Sequoia Capital and a $16M Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz in January 2011, Bump was acquired by Google in September 2013 and both the app and its developer API were discontinued on January 31, 2014. The company's bu.mp domain still serves its shutdown notice and the archived SDK repositories remain public under the bumptech GitHub organization; there is no live API surface.

providers.name: Butter Systems
providers.description: Butter Systems was a San Francisco restaurant-technology startup founded in 2013 by Sam Brin and Jon Li and backed by Y Combinator (batch S13). The company replaced the paper restaurant menu with a locked-down tablet at the table, letting diners browse an interactive menu, place food and drink orders on demand without waiting for a server, and request the check, while restaurant operators adjusted menu items, pricing, and promotions on the fly through a web back office. Butter Systems raised roughly $120K across two seed rounds in 2013 from Y Combinator and Fenox Venture Capital, and shut down in 2014. Y Combinator lists the company as inactive, and its buttersystems.com domain is now a parked "domain may be for sale" page. Butter Systems published no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and none survives in the Internet Archive record; it is retained in the API Evangelist network as a closed-company reference only.

providers.name: Buysight
providers.description: Buysight, Inc. was a Silicon Valley advertising technology startup founded in 2008 that built intent-based audience targeting, retargeting, and Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO) for display advertising, using machine learning to select both the audience for an impression and the creative shown to that user. The company raised approximately $16 million from ONSET Ventures, Rembrandt Venture Partners, Uncork Capital (SoftTech VC / Jeff Clavier), Reid Hoffman, and AOL. On December 4, 2012 Buysight was acquired by AOL's Advertising.com Group, with the entire team joining AOL and the DCO and machine-learning technology folded into AOL's AdLearn optimization engine alongside Advertising.com, ADTECH, the AOL On Network, goviral, and Pictela. Buysight no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API, documentation, or SDKs. The buysight.com domain is held by MarkMonitor and redirects to a registrar placeholder page. This profile is retained as a historical acquisition record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Buzzer
providers.description: Buzzer was a mobile live-sports streaming startup founded in 2020 by Bo Han, formerly director of live content at Twitter. Its consumer app, launched in 2021, sold micropayment access — as low as $0.99 to $1 — to short in-game moments of live sporting events, targeting Gen Z fans who would not buy a full cable or league subscription. Buzzer secured streaming rights covering the NBA, WNBA, NHL, PGA Tour and ATP Tour, and raised roughly $44 million in total, including a $20 million Series A in June 2021 co-led by Sapphire Sport and Canaan Partners alongside a large group of athlete and team-owner investors. On 19 May 2023 the company shut down the direct-to-consumer app and pivoted to a business-to-business model branded "Powered by Buzzer", announced as API licensing, custom development and consulting for leagues, teams and networks streaming direct to fans. That offering never reached public availability: Buzzer ceased all operations on 30 June 2023, citing "recent fundraising developments and market dynamics". No public developer portal, API documentation, specification, SDK or package was ever published. The buzzer.com domain no longer hosts the company and now redirects to an Atom.com domain-for-sale listing. Retained in the network as a historical record of a defunct company; not an active API provider.

providers.name: CaaStle
providers.description: CaaStle Inc. was a New York based business-to-business "Clothing-as-a-Service" company that built white-label clothing rental, subscription and resale infrastructure for apparel retailers, operating tenant-branded storefronts and reverse-logistics for partner brands rather than selling directly to consumers. The company collapsed in 2025: its board confirmed financial distress and furloughed staff in April 2025, and it filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware on 20 June 2025 (case 25-11187), electing liquidation over reorganization. Founder and chief executive Christine Hunsicker resigned amid allegations of fabricated financial disclosures and later pleaded guilty to a fraud scheme prosecutors valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars. CaaStle never operated a public developer program, and the caastle.com domain has since passed out of the company's control.

providers.name: Cabletron Systems
providers.description: Cabletron Systems, Inc. was an American manufacturer of networking and network-management equipment, founded in 1983 by Craig Benson and Robert Levine and headquartered in Rochester, New Hampshire. It rose to prominence in the 10BASE5 and Ethernet switching markets, shipped the ST-500 transceiver and the LAN-MD field test set, built the SPECTRUM network-management platform, and passed one billion US dollars in annual sales in 1996 at a peak of roughly 6,600 employees. In 2000 the company announced a split into four businesses: Enterasys Networks (enterprise switching), Riverstone Networks (metro service provider), Aprisma Management Technologies (SPECTRUM software), and GlobalNetwork Technology Services. The Cabletron holding company merged into Enterasys, which went public in 2001, was taken private by The Gores Group in 2006, and was acquired by Extreme Networks in 2013. Riverstone was acquired by Lucent and later liquidated. Cabletron Systems no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API, or documentation: the cabletron.com and enterasys.com domains both redirect to extremenetworks.com. This record is retained as a historical company profile only.

providers.name: CAD Solutions
providers.description: CAD Solutions, Inc. is a historical Battery Ventures portfolio company that appears in the firm's all-companies list. Research during the API Evangelist enrichment pass found no operating business, no developer surface, and no live web presence behind the name - public records indicate the company was acquired by microCAD Solutions on 1995-05-29, and the closest matching domain, cadsolutions.com, now resolves to a GoDaddy parked "for sale" page rather than a company site. The many unrelated "CAD Solutions" businesses currently trading under similar names (CAD Solutions LLC, CAD Solutions Inc of Dassault partner fame, CADD Solutions, CAD-E Solutions) are separate entities and are not this Battery portfolio record. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Caffeine
providers.description: Caffeine was a social broadcasting and live-streaming platform founded in 2016 by former Apple designers Ben Keighran and Sam Roberts, and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Greylock Partners. Built on a proprietary WebRTC-based real-time video distribution network, Caffeine positioned itself as a low-latency, social-first alternative to Twitch for gaming, entertainment, and — in its later years — live sports, partnering with roughly 200 sports organizations and reaching tens of millions of monthly users. The company published open-source broadcasting tooling under its caffeinetv GitHub organization (libcaffeine, caffeine-rtc, an OBS plugin, and the CaffQL GraphQL code generator) but never shipped a public, documented developer API program. Caffeine announced it was ceasing operations, and its web presence is now a shutdown notice; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead and is archival rather than an active, integrable API provider.

providers.name: CakeHealth
providers.description: CakeHealth (Cake Health) was a San Francisco health-insurance management startup founded in 2011 by Rebecca Woodcock, pitched as "Mint for health insurance." Users linked their insurer logins so the service could aggregate health plans, claims, bills, deductibles, and out-of-pocket spending into a single consumer dashboard. It launched as a TechCrunch Disrupt finalist and was backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) and Kima Ventures. Inbox Health acquired the company for its medical-bill tracking technology in April 2016, after which the product was shut down. The company is defunct and no longer operates an API or developer surface; the cakehealth.com domain has since been repurposed and now redirects to an unrelated third-party site.

providers.name: CalAtlantic Group
providers.description: CalAtlantic Group was a U.S. homebuilder formed on October 1, 2015 through the merger of Standard Pacific Homes and Ryland Homes. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, it became the fourth largest homebuilder in the United States before being acquired by Lennar Corporation in February 2018, which made Lennar the nation's largest homebuilder. CalAtlantic no longer operates as an independent entity and does not offer public APIs or developer resources.

providers.name: Calxeda
providers.description: Calxeda was an Austin, Texas semiconductor startup — founded in 2008 as Smooth-Stone by Barry Evans, Larry Wikelius and David Borland — that built ARM-based EnergyCore system-on-chip server processors (ECX-1000, ECX-2000/Midway) aimed at low-power, high-density data center workloads. It raised roughly $90-103M from venture investors including Battery Ventures, and its silicon shipped in Boston Limited Viridis appliances and HP Project Moonshot systems. Calxeda ceased operations in December 2013 after a refinancing round fell through, and its ARM server IP resurfaced under Silver Lining Systems in December 2014. The company published no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts, and calxeda.com is now a parked domain listed for sale, so there is no live API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.

providers.name: Camiant
providers.description: Camiant, Inc. was a policy control and application-assurance technology vendor for broadband and mobile service providers, founded in 2003 in Marlborough, Massachusetts (originally Chameleon Solutions). Its Multimedia Policy Engine implemented 3GPP Release 8/9 Policy and Charging Rules Function (PCRF) capabilities and was deployed by operators including Verizon, Vodafone, Sprint, Comcast, and Cox. Tekelec acquired Camiant in 2010 for approximately $130 million, and the business was later folded into Oracle Communications. Camiant no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, API, or documentation; its former domain (camiant.com) is parked. Surfaced as a matrix-partners portfolio lead, this profile records verified public history rather than a live API surface.

providers.name: Campanja
providers.description: Campanja was a Stockholm-based advertising-technology company founded in 2010 that built a high-frequency paid-search bid-optimization engine. Its platform placed millions of automated bids per day across Google AdWords, Google Shopping, and Yahoo/Bing search campaigns, using real-time tracking and predictive big-data modeling to improve return on ad spend for large online advertisers while cutting media cost. Campanja raised a $5M Series A (Hoxton Ventures, DFJ Esprit) and was acquired by [24]7.ai in 2015, where its technology was folded into the [24]7 Customer Acquisition Cloud. The independent company is effectively defunct and campanja.com no longer resolves to a live site. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Canopy Labs
providers.description: Canopy Labs was a customer analytics and predictive marketing SaaS company founded in 2012 in the Toronto, Ontario area (Thornhill) by Wojciech Gryc and Jorge Escobedo, with an additional office in San Francisco. A Y Combinator alumnus, it built machine-learning software that helped businesses model and predict customer behavior, optimize purchase funnels, and personalize marketing across the customer journey. The company raised seed funding from investors including BDC Venture Capital's IT Fund and Valar Ventures. In 2018 Canopy Labs was acquired by Drop Technologies (the customer-loyalty app Drop), after which the independent product, website (canopylabs.com), and any developer/API surface were wound down. This profile is retained as a historical company record; the entity no longer operates independently and publishes no live API.

providers.name: Canvas Networks
providers.description: Canvas Networks was a consumer social media and image-sharing startup founded by Christopher "moot" Poole (the founder of 4chan). Launched in private beta in early 2011 at canv.as, the platform let users share, annotate, and remix images on moderated, topic-based boards, positioning itself as a friendlier, more creative take on imageboard culture. It raised roughly $3.6M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Union Square Ventures, SV Angel, Lerer Ventures, Founder Collective, Ron Conway, and Joshua Schachter, and later pivoted to the mobile drawing app DrawQuest. The company shut down on January 21, 2014, citing its inability to build a sustainable business model. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirms it is defunct with no surviving developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: CapMAC Holdings
providers.description: CapMAC Holdings Inc. (Capital Markets Assurance Corporation) was a New York-based holding company that provided financial guaranty and surety insurance for structured securities worldwide, primarily asset-backed securities, alongside structured financial solutions, advisory and structuring services, and investment management. Founded in 1973 and headquartered at 885 Third Avenue in New York City, it was a Canaan Partners portfolio company. MBIA Inc. acquired CapMAC Holdings in a stock swap valued at more than $500 million, completing the merger on February 17, 1998, after which CapMAC operated as an indirect wholly-owned MBIA subsidiary. Capital Markets Assurance Corporation was merged into MBIA Insurance Corporation during the third quarter of 2010 and ceased to exist as a separately licensed insurer. The company is defunct and operates no website, developer program, or API surface; the capmac.com domain is an unrelated parked domain listed for sale.

providers.name: Capriza
providers.description: Capriza was an enterprise mobility software company founded in 2011 in Palo Alto, California, backed by a16z and others across roughly $73.5M in funding. Its platform took a no-code approach to mobilizing workflows from legacy enterprise applications such as SAP, Oracle and PeopleSoft by driving their existing user interfaces, explicitly WITHOUT requiring APIs, new infrastructure or custom code. The company has permanently closed and never published a public API surface, so this record is retained as a historical network entry rather than an enrichable provider profile.

providers.name: Capsule Social
providers.description: Capsule Social was a decentralized-innovation company founded in early 2021 by cryptography researcher Nadim Kobeissi to build tools for a web3 future. Its flagship product, Blogchain, was a decentralized publishing and social platform — a Substack-like blogging experience with Twitter-like social elements — built on IPFS for serverless content storage and the NEAR Protocol for identity, digital-asset management, and tokenized community governance, letting creators own their content and monetize it behind optional paywalls. The company raised a ~$2.6M seed round from investors including Polychain, Naval Ravikant, Fyrfly, and former Coinbase CTO Balaji Srinivasan. The Blogchain product and the capsulesocial GitHub organization have been inactive since roughly October 2023, and the capsule.social domain has since been re-registered by an unrelated "social memory" consumer app — so the surviving authoritative surface for this entity is its open-source GitHub org, not the current website. There is no hosted REST API: Blogchain is a client-side web3 dApp (Vue frontend, NEAR smart contracts, IPFS).

providers.name: card.io
providers.description: card.io was a mobile SDK company that provided fast, easy credit-card scanning inside iOS and Android apps using the device camera, letting users capture card details by holding a card up to the lens instead of typing them. Founded around 2011 and backed by Uncork Capital (then SoftTech VC), card.io was acquired by PayPal in 2012. Its scanning SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native were open-sourced in December 2014 under the card-io GitHub organization, and the product was ultimately discontinued. The company operated no public REST or web API; its product surface was a set of client-side mobile SDKs, all of which are now archived. This profile is maintained for network completeness and historical/portfolio context.

providers.name: Cardmunch
providers.description: CardMunch was a mobile business-card scanning service that used human transcription to turn photographed business cards into contact records on iOS. Founded as a Y Combinator and 500 Global backed startup, it was acquired by LinkedIn in January 2011 for a reported sum under $3 million and operated as a free LinkedIn-branded iPhone app. LinkedIn discontinued the app on July 11, 2014, migrating its users to Evernote's business-card scanning feature. CardMunch never published a public developer program, API, or SDK, and the cardmunch.com domain was re-registered by an unrelated party in April 2016 and now hosts an affiliate content blog. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: CardSpring
providers.description: CardSpring was a card-linked offers and payments platform that provided an API for building card-linked applications, letting developers connect merchant point-of-sale systems and consumer payment cards to deliver digital coupons, loyalty rewards, and receipt-level offers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company was acquired by Twitter in 2014 and subsequently wound down; as of this pass every path on cardspring.com (including the old /help/developer_faq.html) 307-redirects to an Afternic "cardspring.com is for sale" domain-sale lander, developer.cardspring.com fails TLS with no matching certificate, and no first-party CardSpring packages remain on npm or RubyGems. There is no live developer portal, documentation, API, or OpenAPI surface to enrich. Sector: payments.

providers.name: Carmera *
providers.description: CARMERA was a New York City based road-intelligence and HD mapping company that provided "change-as-a-service" map maintenance for autonomous driving, mobility-as-a-service and consumer navigation. It used consumer-grade cameras mounted on commercial fleet vehicles as crowdsourced visual probes to detect permanent road inventory change (signs, signals, lane markings) and temporary closure events (construction), then regenerated both HD and SD maps in near real time. Its commercial offering was described as detection APIs that identify map-impacting events plus vector APIs that deliver map updates, layered over a customer-supplied or CARMERA-supplied base map. The company was backed by GV and was acquired in July 2021 by Woven Planet (now Woven by Toyota), the advanced mobility subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation. Its APIs were sold under enterprise agreements and were never published as a public developer program; as of this enrichment pass the carmera.com domain no longer resolves and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API artifact survives.

providers.name: Carpooling
providers.description: Carpooling.com GmbH was one of Europe's largest ridesharing / carpooling platforms, founded in Munich, Germany and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital. It connected drivers with empty seats to passengers travelling the same route across Europe. In April 2015 the company was acquired by the French ridesharing operator BlaBlaCar and its operations were merged into that platform. The carpooling.com domain and every developer-facing subdomain (developer / api / docs) now redirect to BlaBlaCar (blablacar.co.uk), and no independent Carpooling developer portal, API, or specification remains. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record; there is no live API surface of its own to enrich.

providers.name: CarServ
providers.description: CarServ was auto repair shop management software — marketed as "the operating system for auto repair" — used by single-site shops and multi-location repair groups to run repair orders, Digital Vehicle Inspections, technician and service advisor workflows, customer communication and payments. The company was backed by Techstars. It is no longer operating: carserv.com returned HTTP 410 Gone through late 2024 and now resolves to a registrar parking page delegated to Afternic name servers. CarServ shipped a read-only JSON:API v2 "Public API" covering repair orders, customers, vehicles, appointments, inspections, operations and their part, labor and sublet line items, authenticated by exchanging an API key and secret for a JWT bearer token. No OpenAPI definition, developer portal or documentation survives; this profile reconstructs the historical API contract from the company's own open-source Ruby client library, which remains public on GitHub.

providers.name: Cascade
providers.description: Cascade (www.cascade.io) was a no-code data analysis platform founded in 2019 by Jake Fuentes and Jon Brelig that let non-technical business teams import large datasets, transform and combine them with no-code tools, then visualize and present findings as interactive data apps (positioned as a cloud-native, collaborative alternative to Alteryx). The company wound down in 2023 after failing to reach breakout growth; www.cascade.io now serves a retrospective "What Cascade Did" page. As of the 2026-07-18 enrichment probe there is no public API, developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or documentation surface to enrich, so this profile carries identity only.

providers.name: Catalog
providers.description: Catalog was a music distribution and direct-to-fan platform that let independent musicians sell digital downloads while keeping 100% of earnings, collect fan emails directly, split revenue with collaborators, run referral rewards, and control private, public, or scheduled releases with zero marketplace fees. The company has ceased operations - its homepage now shows a closure announcement - and it never published a public developer API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Caterwings
providers.description: Caterwings was a European online catering marketplace connecting businesses with local caterers for office and event food ordering, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital. As of the July 2026 enrichment probe the brand appears to be retired: caterwings.com no longer serves a site (AWS S3 responds 403 AllAccessDisabled) and caterwings.de redirects to www.eatfirst.com, the corporate-catering platform operated by B2B Food Group of Berlin, which also runs the EatFirst and Feedr brands. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDK package, or GitHub organization could be found for Caterwings; this repo is retained as a historical network record with no live API surface.

providers.name: Causera
providers.description: Causera was an early-stage Palo Alto, California startup surfaced as a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. Enrichment probing found no operating public surface: the company's own domain, causera.com, resolves to a GoDaddy parked-domain lander rather than a product site, and the only verified live property is the dormant "Causera Engineering" GitHub organization (github.com/causera, created 2011-06-22), which holds a single public repository — a fork of mbleigh/princely, a Rails wrapper for the PrinceXML PDF library — last pushed in August 2011 with no public members. Causera therefore appears to be a defunct 2011-era company with no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no published specifications. This profile records the negative result so future enrichment rounds do not re-probe from scratch.

providers.name: Cell Design Labs
providers.description: Cell Design Labs, Inc. was a biotherapeutics company based at 5858 Horton Street, Emeryville, California, that engineered immune cells into "smart, living therapies" for cancer and other diseases. Its platform was a toolkit of proprietary molecular modules — including synthetic Notch (synNOTCH) receptors and programmable, combinatorial-antigen CAR-T circuits developed out of Wendell Lim's lab at UCSF — deployed inside an immune cell to program its specificity and control its killing force, so a therapy recognizes a disease signature and neutralizes it without harming adjacent tissue. The company ran an exclusive research collaboration with Kite Pharma (announced June 2016) on molecular on/off switches for CAR T-cell immunotherapies, and was acquired by Gilead Sciences, announced 7 December 2017. Cell Design Labs no longer operates as an independent company: celldesignlabs.com is dead (DNS resolves to a parked address, HTTP times out; the archived site shows an expired Squarespace subscription). It published no developer program, API, documentation, SDK, or GitHub organization, and none exists to enrich.

providers.name: Cell Pathways
providers.description: Cell Pathways, Inc.
