(CPI) was a development-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered at 702 Electronic Drive, Horsham, Pennsylvania, focused on the research and development of products to treat and prevent cancer. Incorporated in Delaware in July 1998 (as Cell Pathways Holdings, Inc., renamed Cell Pathways, Inc. in February 2001), it developed a class of compounds it called selective apoptotic anti-neoplastic drugs (SAANDs), designed to induce selective apoptosis — programmed cell death — in precancerous and cancerous cells without affecting normal cells. Its lead candidate was Aptosyn (exisulind), studied in precancerous lesions such as colonic polyps and cervical dysplasia and later in prostate, lung, and breast cancer; the company also imported, promoted, and sold Gelclair Concentrated Oral Gel into oncology and dental markets, and had previously marketed Nilandron. It traded on the Nasdaq National Market (Commission File No. 000-24889) and employed approximately 34 people full-time as of March 1, 2003. In February 2003 Cell Pathways signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger to be acquired by OSI Pharmaceuticals, Inc. in a stock-for-stock exchange; stockholders approved the merger on June 10, 2003, and the company filed a Form 15-12G on June 12, 2003 terminating its Exchange Act registration with one holder of record. OSI Pharmaceuticals was itself acquired by Astellas Pharma and deregistered on June 18, 2010. Cell Pathways predates the API economy entirely, never operated a developer program or public API surface, and no longer exists as an operating entity. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Celsius Network
providers.description: Celsius Network LLC was a global cryptocurrency lending, custody and yield platform, founded in 2017, that let retail and institutional customers earn interest on crypto deposits, borrow US dollars and stablecoins against their holdings, and — through the Celsius Partner API — let third-party partners embed that earning power directly into their own applications. The Partner (Wallet) API exposed per-coin balances, accrued interest, transaction history, deposit addresses, withdrawals, KYC verification and utility reference data across three partnership models: Omnibus Integration, Omnibus Treasury, and Segmented Integration, where the partner created and managed a Celsius wallet for each of its own end users. Celsius froze withdrawals on 2022-06-12, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 2022-07-13, had its plan of reorganization confirmed on 2023-11-09, emerged on 2024-01-31 and shut down its mobile and web applications on 2024-02-29 as part of the wind-down of its business operations. The Partner API and the developer portal are retired and their hosts no longer resolve. The reorganized bitcoin-mining business was spun out as Ionic Digital, a separate company that listed on Nasdaq under IOND on 2026-07-28. This profile preserves the API contract as a historical record, derived entirely from first-party artifacts that are still publicly resolvable.

providers.name: CenterForce Technologies
providers.description: CenterForce Technologies was a Bethesda, Maryland software company that built workforce-optimization, workforce-management, and performance-analytics software for contact centers. It partnered with Concerto Software for nearly a decade before Concerto acquired it on 2004-04-26 to pair CenterForce's workforce and contact-center management tools with Concerto's ACD, IVR, and email contact-channel products. Concerto was itself taken private in 2005 and rebranded as Aspect Software in 2007, absorbing the former CenterForce workforce-optimization product line. The company raised roughly $6.01M; investors included Battery Ventures, Piper Sandler, Aspect Software, and SightLine Partners. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead. Enrichment (2026-07-18) confirmed it is a long-defunct, acquired entity with no independent website, developer portal, or API surface; there is nothing to catalog.

providers.name: Cerent
providers.description: Cerent Corporation was a Petaluma, California optical-networking startup, founded in the mid-1990s and backed by Kleiner Perkins, that built the Cerent 454 — a compact next-generation SONET multiservice provisioning platform that collapsed traditional add-drop multiplexing into a far smaller, cheaper, data-aware box for carrier metro networks. Cisco Systems acquired Cerent in 1999 for approximately $6.9 billion in stock, at the time the largest acquisition in Cisco's history, and the product line shipped on as the Cisco ONS 15454, one of Cisco's most successful optical transport platforms. Cerent has not operated as an independent company since. Its hardware-era business predated public web APIs entirely, and it maintains no developer platform, documentation, SDKs, or API surface today — the cerent.com domain is now held by Cisco and serves only an acquisition notice. This profile is retained as a venture-portfolio historical record, not an active API provider.

providers.name: CES International
providers.description: CES International was a software company founded in 1989 and based in Alpharetta, Georgia, that built real-time software solutions for distribution utilities — including the Centricity operations resource management (ORM) system with outage-management capabilities and an energy delivery management (EDM) suite for network operations — serving utilities on five continents and more than 35 million metered accounts. It was acquired by SPL WorldGroup in May 2004, and SPL WorldGroup was in turn acquired by Oracle in November 2006, where its utilities software became the foundation of the Oracle Utilities global business unit. CES International no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface, and none of its historical domains resolve to a live company site. This record is retained as a historical / defunct entry in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ChangeTip
providers.description: ChangeTip was a Bitcoin micropayments and social-tipping service built by ChangeCoin, Inc. (San Francisco), founded in 2013. It let people send small bitcoin tips across Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, Twitch, Facebook, Slack, email, and text by replying with an amount, settling the micropayment behind the scenes to a hosted wallet. ChangeTip published an open API and first-party client libraries (Python and JavaScript) so the community could build tipping integrations and pair external wallets. The company raised roughly $3.5M and was backed by 500 Startups, Pantera Capital, and Gil Penchina. ChangeCoin was acquired by Airbnb in 2016 and the tipping service was discontinued in November 2016; the site now serves only a shutdown notice with balance withdrawal. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Charlie Finance
providers.description: Charlie (Charlie Finance Co.) was a Pasadena, California fintech company that operated a mobile banking app and debit-card program built specifically for Americans aged 62 and older. Founded in 2021 by Kevin Nazemi, the service offered Social Security deposits paid up to several days early, a FraudShield protection layer tuned to scams that target seniors, 3% high-yield savings, no monthly fees or minimums, a fee-free Allpoint ATM network of 55,000+ machines, custom photo debit cards, and seven-day-a-week human customer support. Charlie is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and raised a $7.5M seed round followed by a $23M Series A. The company discontinued service and permanently closed its debit-card program on January 22, 2026. Charlie is a consumer neobank and does not publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Checkin
providers.description: Checkin (checkin.cc) was a Bloomberg Beta-backed social-connection platform that brought thousands of people together for structured, timed 8-minute weekly one-on-one conversations intended to spark meaningful human connection. The consumer service ceased operations on June 30, 2023; the domain now serves a shutdown notice and the only remaining contact is support@checkin.cc. The company published no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this profile has no API artifacts to enrich beyond a live domain-security probe of the remaining host.

providers.name: ChemConnect
providers.description: ChemConnect, Inc. was a Houston, Texas-based electronic exchange (founded 1995) for trading midstream energy, feedstocks, chemicals, and related commodities such as natural gas liquids, refined and intermediate fuels, aromatics, olefins, and commodity polymers, serving thousands of member companies with e-commerce, market information, negotiation, and supply-chain collaboration tooling. It acquired rival CheMatch to form a leading commodity trading platform. The company is a now-exited Battery Ventures portfolio investment; it no longer operates and the chemconnect.com domain is parked and listed for sale (HugeDomains), so there is no live developer, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Chordiant Software
providers.description: Chordiant Software Corporation was an enterprise software vendor founded in 1991 and based in California, known for customer relationship management (CRM) and customer decision management software used by large banks, insurers, telecommunications carriers, and healthcare organizations. Its products included Chordiant Decision Management, Marketing Director, and Recommendation Advisor, delivering real-time predictive decisioning and next-best-action recommendations across customer channels. The company went public on NASDAQ (CHRD) in 2000 and was acquired by Pegasystems in 2010, with its decisioning technology folded into Pega's Customer Decision Hub. Chordiant no longer operates as an independent company and exposes no public developer portal or API; the chordiant.com domain now redirects to pega.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record and carries no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Chute
providers.description: Chute was a visual marketing automation platform (getchute.com) that helped brands discover, collect, rights-manage and publish consumer and user-generated visual content. Its product line spanned visual insights, digital asset management and content publishing, and it exposed a public REST API documented on Apiary (docs.chute.apiary.io) with first-party Ruby and Node.js client libraries. The company is defunct: the canonical domain no longer serves a site, the API and developer hosts do not resolve, the Apiary documentation returns 502, and the github.com/chute organization has been deleted. Only the abandoned package-registry entries survive. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record of a former API provider.

providers.name: Cimarex Energy
providers.description: Cimarex Energy was an independent oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with operations focused in the Permian Basin and the Mid-Continent. In October 2021 Cimarex Energy combined with Cabot Oil & Gas Corporation to form Coterra Energy (NYSE: CTRA). No public Cimarex-branded developer APIs exist; all current digital channels and any future API offerings are part of Coterra Energy.

providers.name: Cinta Networks
providers.description: Cinta Networks, Incorporated was a venture-backed optical networking equipment startup of the dot-com era, funded in part by Battery Ventures and led by CEO John Vaughan. The company built the patented WAVEJunction product family, an architecture that integrated DWDM optical transport with optical switching in a single network element for metro, regional, and long-haul carrier networks, claiming capital-expense savings of more than 50 percent and operational savings of over 70 percent through modular, port-at-a-time growth, universal transponder cards, and dynamic wavelength reconfiguration across ring and mesh topologies. Public activity is visible from roughly 2000 to 2002, including a January 2002 WAVEJunction field-trial agreement with Pacific LightNet and a component supply arrangement with ADC. Cinta Networks appears to have ceased operations in the post-telecom-bust period: archived captures of cintanetworks.com show the site replaced by a parked domain-search page by 2004, and the domain no longer resolves in DNS as of July 2026. Cinta was a hardware manufacturer and never published a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts, so there is no API surface for this profile to describe. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio record.

providers.name: Circle of Moms
providers.description: Circle of Moms was an online community for mothers, organized around topical mom groups, discussion threads and mom blogs, covering pregnancy, babies and infants, parenting and family health. It is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC) and was later operated under the POPSUGAR brand, whose branding appears on archived captures of the site. The service is no longer operating: the circleofmoms.com domain is still registered but now redirects to the POPSUGAR Family page on Facebook, and its DNS is administered under Vox Media, POPSUGAR's parent. Circle of Moms never published a public API, developer portal, or partner platform — web-archive crawls of the domain contain no developer, API-documentation, or OAuth paths, and no developer or api subdomain has ever been recorded. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface.

providers.name: Circular
providers.description: Circular was a Spanish hiring community that connected tech recruiters with software developers, describing itself as a "Hiring Community for Tech Recruiters & Developers." It operated a referral-driven talent network in which recruiters shared vetted candidates they could not place themselves, and developers received job opportunities through that trusted pool rather than through cold outreach. The company was backed by Point Nine Capital and ran its candidate and recruiter landing experiences on a Next.js application served from circular.io and static.circular.io. Circular has since shut down and merged into Manfred (getmanfred.com), the largest tech community in Spain, with its own migration notice stating "Circular cierra sus puertas para integrarse en Manfred." The circular.io domain remains registered to Singular People Europe S.L. but has been fully undelegated, and Point Nine no longer lists Circular in its portfolio. Circular never published a public developer program, API, SDK, or specification. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: City Reach International
providers.description: City Reach International Limited was a UK-registered telecommunications and internet-infrastructure company, incorporated 14 April 2000 at 8 Salisbury Square, Blackfriars, London EC4Y 8BB (Companies House number 03973748), classified under SIC 6420 (telecommunications) and 7260 (other computer related activities). It was a dot-com era venture backed in part by Battery Ventures, and appears on the Battery Ventures all-companies list, which is how it entered the API Evangelist network. The company was dissolved on 13 May 2014. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found no surviving corporate website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface: the candidate domains cityreach.com, cityreachinternational.com, cityreach.net and cityreachinternational.co.uk do not resolve, and cityreach.co.uk resolves only to a parked domain-for-sale landing page. There is no API, specification, SDK, or event surface to catalog for this company, and none should be fabricated.

providers.name: Clarity Money
providers.description: Clarity Money was a personal-finance and money-management mobile app founded in 2016 by Adam Dell (Oath Holdings / Dell family) that used data-driven analysis to help consumers track spending, cancel unwanted subscriptions, negotiate bills, move savings, and manage budgets. It was acquired by Goldman Sachs in 2018 and folded into the Marcus by Goldman Sachs consumer platform; the standalone Clarity Money app was subsequently discontinued. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. No public developer program, API, documentation, or developer portal was ever published, and the claritymoney.com domain no longer resolves to a live site (held by Goldman Sachs registrar CSC).

providers.name: Clean Urban Energy
providers.description: Clean Urban Energy, Inc. was a Chicago, Illinois cleantech company that turned large commercial office buildings into grid-scale thermal energy storage assets. Its technology harnessed the existing thermal mass of a building — concrete, drywall, furnishings — by pre-cooling during off-peak hours and coasting through peak demand, effectively operating the building as a multi-megawatt battery for demand response and load shifting without installing dedicated storage hardware. The company raised a reported $7 million venture round and appears in the Battery Ventures list of all portfolio companies. As of a July 2026 review the company has no live corporate web presence: the cleanurbanenergy.com domain no longer serves company content, and no developer portal, API, documentation, or GitHub organization could be located. It is catalogued here as an inactive, non-API-provider company record.

providers.name: Cleargraph
providers.description: Cleargraph was a Palo Alto, California startup building natural-language and graph-based search over data, operating under the tagline "Data Accessible through Search." It was backed by Version One Ventures and appears in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company is inactive - its primary domain cleargraph.com now 301-redirects off-site, its cleargraph.io website no longer resolves (connection refused), and its GitHub organization (github.com/cleargraph) was archived in April 2026 and holds only forked libraries with no first-party API, SDK, or specification. No live API, developer portal, documentation, or first-party package surface could be verified during enrichment, so no API artifacts were generated.

providers.name: Clearstory Data
providers.description: Clearstory Data was a big-data analytics startup (Menlo Park / Mountain View, CA) that built a cloud service for blending and visualizing enterprise and third-party data, backed by a16z, GV (Google Ventures), Kleiner Perkins and Khosla Ventures. It was acquired by Alteryx in 2016 and is no longer an independent company. Its former domain (clearstorydata.com) has lapsed and now 301-redirects to unrelated parked/spam sites, so it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/defunct portfolio record; no live artifacts are producible.

providers.name: Clementine
providers.description: Clementine (Clementine Labs) was a New York based enterprise communication startup founded in 2013 and publicly launched in September 2014, offering workplace messaging, chat, and conference calling that let colleagues reach each other without exchanging personal mobile phone numbers. It appears on the Andreessen Horowitz investment list and was acquired by Dropbox in April 2016, after which the Clementine service was shut down and the team folded into Dropbox collaboration efforts. The company operates no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs today: its primary domain, clementine.io, now issues an HTTP 301 redirect to dropbox.com. This profile is retained as a historical, non-operational record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Clinkle
providers.description: Clinkle was a Silicon Valley mobile-payments startup founded in 2012 by Stanford student Lucas Duplan. In 2013 it raised roughly $30 million in what was then reported as the largest seed round in history, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Peter Thiel, Marc Benioff, Accel's Jim Breyer, Richard Branson, and Intel Capital. The company promised a phone-to-phone payments technology but never shipped a viable product, launched a poorly received "Treats" debit-card app, cycled through multiple pivots and leadership turmoil, and lost its window to Venmo and Apple Pay. By 2016 Clinkle had quietly shut down with no official announcement. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a defunct a16z portfolio lead; it publishes no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface today (clinkle.com resolves to a suspended-account page).

providers.name: ClippPR
providers.description: ClippPR (later rebranded Primeloop) was a startup that helped brands and PR agencies clip and track their press coverage, measure the value of earned media, and re-engage audiences by turning clicks on shared links into targeted relationships. Founded around 2011 in Las Vegas and part of 500 Startups' eighth (first San Francisco) accelerator batch, the company has since shut down. Its primeloop.com domain is parked/for-sale, primeloop.co no longer resolves, and clipppr.com has been taken over by an unrelated blog. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI was ever published; the only surviving first-party surface is the company's GitHub organization.

providers.name: Clockwise
providers.description: Clockwise was an AI-powered calendar optimization platform that helped individuals, teams, and organizations protect focus time, reduce meeting overload, and coordinate scheduling intelligently. The platform provided REST APIs for managing focus time blocks, meeting preferences, smart scheduling links, and team calendar coordination. Clockwise was acquired by Salesforce and shut down on March 27, 2026.

providers.name: Clothes Horse
providers.description: Clothes Horse was a New York-based, data-driven size-and-fit recommendation company for online apparel shopping. It matched a shopper's body measurements and brand preferences against retailers' actual garment measurements to recommend the right size at the point of sale, sold to retailers as SaaS. The company merged with Fits.me in December 2014 to form a virtual-fitting-room solutions provider, and no longer operates as an independent entity. It exposed no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and the clotheshor.se domain now resolves to an unrelated Swedish fashion/lifestyle WordPress blog. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; enrichment found no live API surface.

providers.name: Cloud Peak Energy
providers.description: Cloud Peak Energy Inc. was an American coal mining company headquartered in Gillette, Wyoming, established in 2009 as a spin-off from Rio Tinto Energy America. The company operated three open-pit mines in the Powder River Basin (Wyoming and Montana) and held a 50% interest in the Decker Coal Company. Cloud Peak Energy filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May 2019 amid declining demand for Powder River coal in East Asian and US markets and is no longer operating. This profile is maintained as a historical record - Cloud Peak Energy did not publish public APIs.

providers.name: Cloudcoreo
providers.description: CloudCoreo was a Seattle-based cloud security startup (founded 2016, seed round led by Madrona Venture Group) that built a cloud configuration and vulnerability-assessment platform to identify and remediate misconfigurations across public multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP). VMware acquired CloudCoreo in February 2018 and folded the team and product into VMware Cloud Services, where it became the basis of CloudHealth Secure State. The standalone CloudCoreo service and developer surface have since been retired: cloudcoreo.com is now a parked/for-sale domain and there is no live public API. The CloudCoreo GitHub organization remains, hosting the now-deprecated first-party CLI. This profile is a historical/lineage record, not an active API provider.

providers.name: Cloudistics (Fungible)
providers.description: Cloudistics was a composable, hyperconverged cloud infrastructure software company whose platform managed applications, virtual machines, storage, and networking across on-premises datacenters via a REST API and an official Python client (with the ccli command-line tool). Fungible acquired the Cloudistics software team and assets in September 2020 to build DPU-powered hyperdisaggregated infrastructure, and Microsoft acquired Fungible in January 2023 to bolster Azure datacenter networking and storage. As independent companies both are now defunct: the primary product domains are parked, the public GitHub organization has been emptied, and the PyPI package has been removed. The one surviving public developer surface is the read-only Cloudistics API Python Client documentation hosted on Read the Docs. This profile is retained as a historical API Evangelist network record.

providers.name: Cloudpipes
providers.description: Cloudpipes was a Sofia (Bulgaria) and London-based iPaaS (integration platform as a service) that provided a cloud-based integration and workflow-automation platform for connecting SaaS applications and automating business processes without code. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups / 500 Istanbul), BrightCap Ventures and LAUNCHub Ventures, the company was acquired by Vista-backed Quickbase (Quick Base) in August 2019 and its standalone product and developer surface were subsequently wound down. This API Evangelist profile is a historical/portfolio record: the cloudpipes.com origin is offline (Cloudflare 522) and no live API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts remain available to harvest.

providers.name: Cloudsimple
providers.description: CloudSimple was an enterprise software company that ran secure, dedicated VMware workloads (VMware Cloud Foundation - vSphere, vSAN, NSX) as a managed service on public clouds, originally partnering with Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. Google Cloud acquired CloudSimple in November 2019 and folded the technology into Google Cloud VMware Engine; the standalone company, product, and developer surface no longer exist. The former domain (cloudsimple.com) resolves to a Google-owned IP but serves no live website, documentation, or API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and Redpoint Ventures and remains in the API Evangelist network as a historical / defunct-provider record; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: CloudSwitch
providers.description: CloudSwitch was a cloud-infrastructure software startup founded in 2008 by Ellen Rubin and John Considine and headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts. Its flagship product, CloudSwitch Enterprise, was a downloadable software appliance that installed into VMware and Xen environments and enabled enterprises to migrate and run existing Windows and Linux virtual machines in public clouds such as Amazon EC2 and Terremark without re-architecting them, preserving networking and security boundaries. The company raised roughly $15.4M across two rounds from Matrix Partners, Atlas Venture, and Commonwealth Capital Ventures, and was acquired by Verizon in August 2011 and folded into its Terremark cloud services unit. The company is defunct: it operates no independent website, developer portal, or API, so this profile remains a historical portfolio-lead stub with no live surface to enrich.

providers.name: Club Factory
providers.description: Club Factory was a Chinese-owned cross-border e-commerce marketplace app that grew to roughly 70 million users globally, with India its largest market at around 40 million users. In June 2020 the Government of India banned Club Factory alongside 58 other Chinese apps citing data and privacy concerns, and the company withdrew from the Indian market shortly after. It was originally added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead surfaced from Qiming's portfolio. Enrichment finds the company effectively defunct - clubfactory.com no longer serves a company site (it is parked for sale via Afternic nameservers and redirects to a /lander page), there is no live developer or API surface, no published SDKs, and no discoverable /.well-known documents.

providers.name: Clutch Wallet
providers.description: Clutch Wallet was a Los Angeles-based web3 startup building a non-custodial "social wallet" and web3 toolkit — a seedless browser extension and mobile wallet (leaning on account abstraction and seamless sign-in) paired with a dApp offering token search, three-click DeFi, a web3 social profile, a personalized crypto media feed, aggregated multi-wallet balances in a single dashboard, integrated crypto education, and community tools. Founded by Bec Jones (CEO), James Kouzinas (CFO/COO), and Sheela Vats (CTO), it raised ~$800K backed by Anthemis (Female Innovators Lab Fund), Emmeline Ventures, Everywhere Ventures, and Rogue Women. The company is now permanently closed: its clutchwallet.xyz domain is parked and it exposed no public production API. It remains in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile; its clutch-wallet GitHub organization (mostly forks of Zerion, Argent, and MetaMask projects) and one first-party npm library survive as artifacts.

providers.name: Codex Protocol
providers.description: Codex Protocol was a blockchain startup (founded 2018, backed by Pantera Capital) that built a decentralized registry for unique physical assets — fine art, wine, watches and other collectibles — on Ethereum, using ERC-721 Codex Records and an ERC-20 Codex Coin (CODX) token, plus a Codex Viewer dapp and a Codex Registry REST API. The company is now defunct: its API and dapp repositories are archived, its documentation host no longer resolves, and its original marketing domain (codexprotocol.com) has been repurposed by a third party and redirects offsite. The surviving, verifiable first-party artifacts are the codex-protocol GitHub organization (13 repositories of smart contracts, services, and tooling) and four @codex-protocol npm packages. This profile was surfaced as a Pantera Capital portfolio company and is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical / defunct record.

providers.name: Coho Data
providers.description: Coho Data was a scale-out enterprise storage startup based in Sunnyvale, California, founded in 2011 (originally as Convergent.io) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz among others. It built a software-defined storage platform that combined commodity flash and software-defined networking to deliver scalable NFS/object storage for private clouds. The company ceased operations and wound down in 2017. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is defunct: it operates no live developer portal, documentation, or API, and the cohodata.com domain has since lapsed to a third-party parked/content-farm site unrelated to the original company, so there is no public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Colfax Corporation (Historical)
providers.description: Colfax Corporation was a diversified global manufacturer founded in 1995 in Richmond, Virginia by Steven and Mitchell Rales. In April 2022, Colfax completed the spin-off of its fabrication technology business as ESAB Corporation (NYSE: ESAB) and renamed itself Enovis Corporation (NYSE: ENOV), refocusing on specialty medical technologies. The Colfax brand and corporate entity no longer exists as an operating company. This profile is preserved for historical reference and routes to the two successor entities. No Colfax-branded developer APIs were ever published; any successor APIs would fall under Enovis or ESAB.

providers.name: Color Labs Inc. (Apple)
providers.description: Color Labs Inc. was a Palo Alto, California social photo-sharing startup founded in 2011 by Bill Nguyen and Peter Pham. Its Color mobile app let people photograph and browse photos taken nearby, grouping content by proximity and social graph. The company raised roughly $41 million before launch — $25 million from Sequoia Capital, $9 million from Bain Capital Ventures, and $7 million in venture debt from Silicon Valley Bank — and reportedly declined a $200 million acquisition offer from Google. After a March 2011 launch that drew about a million downloads but fell under 100,000 active users by September 2011, the board voted in October 2012 to wind the company down and the service closed at the end of that year. Apple then acqui-hired the remaining engineering team in a talent acquisition reported at roughly $2–7 million. Color Labs never shipped a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, and it has had no live web or API surface since 2012. Its former domain, color.com, is today operated by the unrelated Color Health, Inc. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Bain Capital Ventures portfolio company; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Combinatorx
providers.description: CombinatoRx, Inc. was a Cambridge/Boston, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company (SEC CIK 0001135906, SIC 2834 Pharmaceutical Preparations, incorporated in Delaware) that pursued combination drug discovery — screening pairs of approved drugs for synergistic therapeutic effects. It registered with the SEC in 2002 and traded publicly following its 2005 IPO. The company was renamed Zalicus Inc. in September 2010 after its combination with Neuromed Pharmaceuticals, and renamed again to EPIRUS Biopharmaceuticals, Inc. in July 2014 after merging with EPIRUS. EPIRUS was delisted in September 2016 (Form 25-NSE) and its SEC registration was formally revoked on 2024-05-14. The company is defunct: it operated no developer program and published no public API, SDK, or developer documentation, and combinatorx.com is now a parked NameBright listing unrelated to the original company. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Canaan Partners portfolio company and has no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Commerce One
providers.description: Commerce One, Inc. was a Pleasanton, California B2B e-commerce software company and one of the defining names of the dot-com era, running the MarketSite marketplace and the Global Trading Web trading network. Founded in 1994 as DistriVision and renamed Commerce One in 1997, it went public in July 1999 and peaked in 2000 at a $21.5B market capitalization on $401M of revenue. It filed for bankruptcy in October 2004; its patent portfolio went to Novell subsidiary JGR Acquisitions and the Commerce One name to Perfect Commerce in 2006. The company no longer operates and has no live API or developer portal. What survives, and what this profile documents, is xCBL — the XML Common Business Library — a royalty-free library of 44 XML business documents across 9 namespaces, still published and downloadable from xcbl.org. Commerce One also created SOX, the schema language that influenced W3C XML Schema and JAXB.

providers.name: CommonBond
providers.description: CommonBond was a New York City based financial technology lender founded in 2011 by David Klein, Michael Taormina and Jessup Shean that refinanced student loans for university graduates and originated in-school loans for MBA, law, medical and engineering students, later adding Parent PLUS refinancing and a solar/green home-improvement lending product. It raised institutional debt and equity financing, including a $35M Series B in 2015 and a $150M lending partnership with Nelnet, and operated a consumer lending platform at commonbond.co with an externally documented Postman based API at api-docs.commonbond.co. The company exited student loan refinancing in 2022 after the federal payment and interest pause removed much of the refinance market, pivoted to solar lending, and subsequently wound down. As of this profile the commonbond.co domain is parked and every path on it, including the former API documentation host, returns HTTP 410 Gone, so no public API surface remains to profile.

providers.name: Compaq
providers.description: Compaq Computer Corporation was a personal-computer manufacturer founded on February 16, 1982 in Houston, Texas by Rod Canion, Jim Harris and Bill Murto, three former Texas Instruments executives. It legally reverse-engineered the IBM PC BIOS and shipped the Compaq Portable in March 1983, then built out the Deskpro desktop line, the LTE notebook line, the Presario consumer line, and the SystemPro and ProLiant server lines, becoming the world's largest PC maker by 1994. Losing ground to Dell's direct-sales model and hit by the dot-com collapse, Compaq agreed to merge with Hewlett-Packard on September 4, 2001 in a $24.2 billion deal that closed on May 3, 2002. HP retired the Compaq brand entirely in North America and Europe in 2013 and has since licensed it regionally to third parties (Positivo Tecnologia in Brazil, Grupo Newsan in Argentina, Triden Corp in Mexico, Ossify Industries in India). Compaq predates the public web-API era and never published a developer program, public API, or SDK of its own; the compaq.com domain is still registered to HP Inc. but serves no website. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Compaq Computer Corporation
providers.description: Compaq Computer Corporation was an American personal-computer company founded in 1982 in Houston, Texas by Rod Canion, Jim Harris, and Bill Murto. It pioneered IBM PC-compatible portable computers with the 1983 Compaq Portable and grew into one of the largest PC manufacturers of the 1990s, acquiring Digital Equipment Corporation in 1998. Compaq merged with Hewlett-Packard in 2002; the brand was gradually retired and its operations absorbed into HP. It survives in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company profile (backed by kleiner-perkins); it operates no present-day developer portal, public API, or SDK surface, as compaq.com now resolves to HP infrastructure.

providers.name: Computable
providers.description: Computable (Computable Labs) was a Pantera Capital-backed crypto startup that built the Computable Protocol, a decentralized data-market and "Datatrust" system letting participants create Fair, Free-Access (FFA) markets to pool, price, and share datasets on Ethereum. The project shipped developer client libraries (computable.js for JavaScript, computable.py for Python), a Datatrust API reference implementation, Computable Improvement Proposals (CIPs), and a protocol specification ("The Computable Book"). The GitHub organization and its repositories are archived and inactive (last activity 2022-2023) and the company's websites (computable.io and computablelabs.com) no longer resolve to a live property, so this profile documents the surviving open-source developer surface rather than a running service.

providers.name: Computer Sciences Corporation
providers.description: Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC) was a multinational information technology services and professional services company. On April 1, 2017, CSC merged with the Enterprise Services line of business of Hewlett Packard Enterprise to form DXC Technology, retiring the standalone CSC brand. This profile is preserved as a historical record; CSC did not publish any public developer APIs and the entity is no longer actively operated under this name.

providers.name: Comtravo
providers.description: Comtravo was a Berlin-based business travel management company (a TMC) that combined booking technology with human travel agents to handle corporate flights, hotels, rail and expense workflows for European businesses. It was backed by Creandum and other investors. As of this enrichment pass the standalone company is no longer operating: the comtravo.com domain returns a 301 redirect to navan.com, consistent with Comtravo having been acquired/wound into Navan (formerly TripActions). No independent Comtravo developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or public API surface could be found, so this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Con-way
providers.description: Con-way Inc. was a North American freight transportation and logistics company best known for its Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) carrier Con-way Freight along with Menlo Logistics, Con-way Truckload, and Con-way Multimodal. On October 30, 2015, XPO Logistics completed a $3 billion acquisition of Con-way; by May 2017 the Con-way brand had been fully retired in favor of XPO. This profile is preserved as a historical record; Con-way no longer operates under this name and modern shipping APIs are surfaced under XPO.

providers.name: Concho Resources
providers.description: Concho Resources, Inc. was an independent oil and natural gas company focused on the acquisition, development, exploration, and production of oil and natural gas properties primarily in the Permian Basin of West Texas and southeast New Mexico. On January 15, 2021, ConocoPhillips completed an all-stock acquisition of Concho Resources at a total enterprise value of $13.3 billion, retiring the Concho brand. This profile is preserved as a historical record; Concho no longer operates under this name and never published any public developer APIs.

providers.name: Concord Communications
providers.description: Concord Communications was surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. The July 2026 enrichment pass found no live company web presence and no API surface. The candidate domain concordcommunications.com resolves to a GoDaddy/Afternic domain-for-sale parking lander (no company content), and concord.com belongs to an unrelated business (Concord, the independent music company). No developer portal, documentation, API reference, specification, package, or /.well-known surface could be probed, and the APIs.io catalog holds no matching provider record. This profile is retained as an inactive historical lead; there is nothing to enrich until a live successor surface is identified.

providers.name: Concord Data Systems
providers.description: Concord Data Systems was a telecommunications equipment manufacturer founded in 1979 by Ken Miller (previously Director of Modem Development at Codex) and based in Marlborough, Massachusetts. The company designed and sold high-speed full-duplex dial-up telephone modems for transmitting digital computer data in analog form over the public switched telephone network. As the modem hardware market commoditized, the business pivoted from industrial data communications to the emerging market for network performance management software and was renamed Concord Communications, best known for its eHealth network management suite. Battery Ventures was one of thirteen investors in that company. Concord Communications was acquired by CA (Computer Associates) on 2005-06-07 for approximately $350 million ($330M cash plus roughly $20M of assumed net debt); CA was itself acquired by Broadcom in 2018. Concord Data Systems is therefore a historical, defunct entity: it operates no website, no developer portal, and no API surface today. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lineage record only.

providers.name: Conexant Systems
providers.description: Conexant Systems, Inc. was an American fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California. Spun off from Rockwell Semiconductor Systems in 1999, it designed mixed-signal and system-on-chip products for audio, voice, imaging, modem, and networking applications, and was best known for its dial-up modem chipsets, audio codecs, and far-field voice-input processors used in smart-home and IoT devices. Conexant's audio and imaging business was acquired by Synaptics in 2017 and the standalone Conexant brand has since been retired. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the company publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface (its former conexant.com domain no longer resolves to an active site), so there are no API artifacts to enrich at this time.

providers.name: Confer Technologies
providers.description: Confer Technologies, Inc. was an enterprise endpoint security company that marketed what it called the "Converged Endpoint" — a single lightweight sensor combining attack prevention, detection, and incident response across endpoints, servers, cloud workloads, and mobile devices. The product gathered endpoint telemetry across the enterprise and applied data science to analyze attacker behavior and adapt automatically, positioned as an EDR and next-generation antivirus alternative for organizations without large security teams. Confer was venture-backed (Matrix Partners, Foundation Capital) and raised roughly $17M before being acquired by Carbon Black in 2016. Its site at confer.net began permanently redirecting to carbonblack.com by mid-2016 and the domain no longer resolves to a host. Carbon Black was subsequently acquired by VMware (2019) and then by Broadcom (2023). Confer never published a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is retained as a historical record of an acquired company and has no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Conjectag
providers.description: Conjectag (Conject AG / Conject Holding GmbH) was a Munich-based German construction technology company founded in 2000 that provided cloud-based software for the built environment, covering project management, collaboration, document control, and construction cost management for the AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) sector. It was surfaced as a historical Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company. Conject was acquired by the Australian construction collaboration platform Aconex in March 2016, and Aconex was subsequently acquired by Oracle in December 2017; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no live website or developer/API surface. This profile is retained for network provenance rather than active enrichment.

providers.name: Connected
providers.description: Connected (Connected HQ, Inc.) was a social CRM and contact-management startup that pulled a user's address book, email and social accounts together into a single continuously-updated relationship manager. Backed by 500 Global, it was acquired by LinkedIn in October 2011 and folded into the LinkedIn-branded "Connected" product, after which the standalone service was retired. Connected never shipped a public developer program, API, SDK or documentation. The connectedhq.com domain is still defensively held by the acquirer (MarkMonitor registrar, Azure DNS and NS1 nameservers, SPF and DMARC p=reject, RFC 7505 null MX) but publishes no A record and serves no content. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Consona
providers.description: Consona Corporation was an Indianapolis, Indiana enterprise software company founded in 1986 as Made2Manage Systems and taken private by Battery Ventures in 2003. Operating a roll-up strategy, it acquired multiple ERP and CRM product lines (DTR, Cimnet, AXIS, Encompix, Intuitive, Relevant, SupplyWorks) serving small and midsize manufacturers and field-service businesses. On August 7, 2012 Consona merged with CDC Software to form Aptean, and the Consona brand was retired from commercial use. The company is defunct, has no live web domain (consona.com does not resolve) and no public API or developer surface; its former products live on inside Aptean.

providers.name: Contactually
providers.description: Contactually was a cloud-based CRM (customer relationship management) platform focused on helping real estate agents, brokers, and other relationship-driven professionals nurture their networks through follow-up reminders, contact bucketing, pipelines, and automated outreach. Founded around 2011, it was acquired by real estate brokerage Compass on February 27, 2019, and had already been powering Compass's own CRM. Contactually permanently ceased operations on March 31, 2022. It historically exposed a v2 REST API (api.contactually.com) documented at developers.contactually.com for contacts, buckets, notes, tasks, and webhooks, but that developer surface, the API hosts, and all SDKs are now offline. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct provider; no live API, documentation, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Convergent Networks
providers.description: Convergent Networks, Inc. was a carrier-grade broadband voice infrastructure vendor that built next-generation VoIP switching and signaling equipment for telecommunications carriers, including the ICS2000 and Commando media gateways, the PacketMatrix softswitch controller for call screening and number translation, and the ICSG SS7 signaling gateway. Venture-backed by Battery Ventures and Saints Capital (raising roughly $57M across two rounds), the company was acquired by Eastern Photonics, a subsidiary of Global NAPs, in 2003. It is defunct and publishes no active developer portal, API, or specification. This profile was surfaced from the Battery Ventures portfolio as a lead; the enrichment pipeline found no live API surface to harvest.

providers.name: CONXUS Communications
providers.description: CONXUS Communications, Inc. was a United States advanced-messaging and narrowband-PCS carrier, headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina, that operated the Pocketalk voice-messaging and Pocketext text-messaging services built on Motorola's InFLEXion protocol. Formed in the mid-1990s from a group of one-way paging providers and backed by strategic and financial investors, the company offered wireless voice messaging, guaranteed message delivery, automatic acknowledgment of receipt, error correction, longer messages, and subscriber-originated replies across roughly ten U.S. markets. Conxus filed for bankruptcy protection in May 1999 and ceased network operations on August 27, 1999, affecting an estimated 80,000-100,000 subscribers. The company is defunct and publishes no API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio record only.

providers.name: Copan Systems
providers.description: Copan Systems was an enterprise data-storage company founded in 2002 and based in Longmont, Colorado, known for pioneering MAID (Massive Array of Idle Disks) technology for long-term persistent and archival storage. Its Enterprise MAID architecture powered down idle disks to cut power, cooling, and floor-space costs in the data center. Backed by Battery Ventures and other investors, the company raised more than $100 million in venture funding before filing for bankruptcy in 2009; SGI acquired its assets in 2010 (that storage lineage now sits within Hewlett Packard Enterprise). The company is defunct and operates no public developer surface, API, or documentation, so there is nothing to enrich in the API Evangelist artifact pipeline.

providers.name: Copia Global
providers.description: Copia Global was a Kenyan B2C e-commerce and last-mile distribution company founded by Tracey Turner and Jonathan Lewis to serve middle- and low-income consumers across rural and peri-urban Africa. Rather than a consumer website, it ran an agent-network model in which customers placed catalog orders through local agents using mobile and USSD technology, and Copia processed, aggregated, and delivered goods within days. Backed by investors including DCVC and Goodwell, the company raised a $50M Series C in 2022 to expand, but suspended Uganda operations in 2023, entered administration in May 2024, and was subsequently placed into liquidation. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or specification; its primary domain now resolves to a parked page. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead for network coverage.

providers.name: Copper Mountain Network
providers.description: Copper Mountain Networks was a telecommunications equipment maker founded in 1996 by Mark Handzel and Joe Markee that led the 1990s DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) wave in North America, building central-office DSL concentrators (the CopperEdge platform) and customer-premises modems that delivered high-speed broadband over existing copper telephone lines. The company was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and InterWest, held its IPO in 1999, weathered the telecom downturn of 2001, and was acquired by Tut Systems in 2005 (later absorbed into Motorola in 2007). It shipped hardware and network equipment, not a public web/developer API; the company is defunct and operates no live developer platform today.

providers.name: Corillian
providers.description: Corillian Corporation was a leading provider of Internet banking software and services, headquartered in Hillsboro, Oregon. The company was formed in 1997 when CheckFree spun off InteractiveSolutions Corporation, and it went on to build the Corillian Voyager online banking platform used by many U.S. banks and credit unions for online banking, bill payment, and real-time financial services integration. Backed by Battery Ventures, Corillian became a public company and expanded through the acquisitions of InteliData Technologies (2005) and qbt Systems (2006). In February 2007 CheckFree agreed to acquire Corillian for approximately $245 million; CheckFree was itself acquired by Fiserv later that same year, after which the Corillian brand was retired. The company no longer operates independently and maintains no public API, developer portal, documentation, or other live developer surface.

providers.name: Corio, Inc.
providers.description: Corio, Inc. was an enterprise Application Service Provider (ASP) founded in September 1998 in San Carlos, California, and incorporated in Delaware, formed by acquiring the capital stock of Data Systems Connectors, Inc. Corio implemented, hosted and managed packaged enterprise business software from Oracle, PeopleSoft, SAP, Ariba and Siebel Systems on behalf of medium and large public, private, non-profit and public sector customers, delivering ERP, CRM and e-business functionality as a service from secure third-party data centers over IP networks. The company operated two lines of business — Application Management Services and Professional Services — and partnered with (i)Structure, XO Communications and Qwest for data center and network infrastructure. Backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (29.5% pre-IPO across the KPCB Java Fund, KPCB VIII, KPCB VIII Founders Fund and KPCB Information Sciences Zaibatsu Fund II, with Vinod Khosla and Ted Schlein on the board) and Cap Gemini Ernst & Young, Corio went public on NASDAQ in 2000. IBM agreed to acquire Corio on 24 January 2005 for $2.82 per share in cash via Nike Acquisition Corp.; Corio filed its Form 15 deregistration on 15 March 2005 and was absorbed into IBM. The company is defunct, publishes no API, developer portal or documentation, and corio.com is a parked domain — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cortina Systems
providers.description: Cortina Systems, Inc. was a venture-backed fabless semiconductor company founded in 2001 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, that designed high-speed communications and networking integrated circuits for optical transport, carrier Ethernet, framer/mapper and PHY devices, and broadband access (EPON/GPON and DSL). The company grew through acquisitions and was itself acquired by Inphi Corporation in 2014; Inphi later merged into Marvell Technology in 2021, and the cortina-systems.com domain now redirects to Marvell. Cortina was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a hardware semiconductor business with no public developer platform or API surface, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Coterra Energy
providers.description: Coterra Energy Inc. (formerly Cabot Oil & Gas, combined with Cimarex Energy in October 2021) was a Houston-headquartered independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company with positions in the Permian Basin, the Marcellus Shale and the Anadarko Basin. On May 7, 2026 Coterra completed an all-stock merger with Devon Energy; the combined company operates as Devon Energy (NYSE: DVN), Coterra's shares were deregistered (Form 15-12G filed 2026-05-19) and investors.coterra.com now redirects to investors.devonenergy.com. The coterra.com site has been reduced to a five-page holding site for interest owners. Coterra never operated a public developer program or API: owner statements are delivered through EnergyLink and production data through PDS Energy, both third-party platforms. The only programmatic access to Coterra data is the SEC's own EDGAR API, listed here as a clearly labeled third-party government API.

providers.name: Counterpane
providers.description: Counterpane Internet Security, Inc. was a managed security services provider founded by cryptographer Bruce Schneier, growing out of his Counterpane Systems cryptography consultancy. Counterpane pioneered Managed Security Monitoring (MSM) — outsourced, 24x7 human-staffed security operations centers that monitored customer networks and devices for intrusions, rather than selling security products. It was venture-backed, with Accel among its investors, and was acquired by BT Group in 2006, after which its operations were folded into BT's managed security business. The company is defunct as an independent entity: it operates no product, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface today. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe, counterpane.com resolves (209.17.116.163, Network Solutions nameservers) but refuses HTTPS on port 443, and plain HTTP redirects to https://www.schneier.com/ — Bruce Schneier's personal site. www.counterpane.com returns HTTP 404. There is no MX, SPF, DMARC, or CAA record on the domain. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Craftsvilla
providers.description: Craftsvilla was an India-based online marketplace for ethnic and handcrafted products — sarees, ethnic apparel, jewelry, footwear, accessories, beauty and home decor sourced from artisans, weavers and small sellers across India. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Mumbai, it was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, Nexus Venture Partners and Global Founders Capital before winding down its consumer operations around 2019 amid financial difficulties. It was surfaced as a Lightspeed portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment found no live public developer surface: the storefront domain now serves a broken AWS S3 redirect (www.craftsvilla.com is NXDOMAIN) and there is no API, developer portal, documentation, /.well-known/ discovery, or llms.txt to harvest.

providers.name: CrediFi
providers.description: CrediFi is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-18 and 2026-07-20 found no independent live surface for CrediFi — credifi.com redirects to actovia.com, a commercial real estate data provider — so this profile is retained as a historical record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Cross Access
providers.description: Cross Access was a data-integration software company backed by Battery Ventures that was acquired by IBM on 2003-10-17 and folded into IBM's information-integration portfolio. It is defunct and has no independent web presence, developer portal, API, or documentation surface today; DNS for candidate domains (crossaccess.com, cross-access.com, crossaccess.io) does not resolve. This profile is retained as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio record, not an active API provider, and there are no live artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Crowdery
providers.description: Crowdery was a consumer retail and e-commerce startup backed by a16z, listed on the a16z investment list. Its product inverted the traditional retail sales model: shoppers voted on product designs from a curated set, Crowdery assembled a personalized marketplace from each shopper's top picks, and the highest-voted products were opened for pre-order at a discount. For brands it offered consumer feedback loops, pre-production demographic analytics, and pre-orders intended to de-risk manufacturing runs. The company never shipped a public API or developer program. As of July 2026 Crowdery appears defunct: the apex domain crowdery.com serves a Doteasy hosting placeholder page, www.crowdery.com still delegates to a decommissioned Heroku prelaunch application that returns 404, and no developer portal, documentation, GitHub organization, or API surface could be found. This profile is retained as a historical a16z portfolio record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: CrowdForce
providers.description: CrowdForce was a Nigerian fintech that operated the PayForce agent-banking network, deploying point-of-sale and digital financial-services agents to extend cash-in/cash-out, bill payments, and banking access to underbanked communities across Nigeria. Backed by 500 Global, its PayForce merchant/agent business merged with FairMoney's Fusion in 2023. As of this enrichment pass the crowdforce.io domain no longer serves an active product or developer surface. The homepage renders an empty Cloudflare-fronted shell and the /payforce path returns unrelated third-party (gambling) spam content, so no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation could be verified.

providers.name: CrowdGather
providers.description: CrowdGather was an online forum and message-board network operator, surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. The company is defunct — crowdgather.com no longer serves a product and resolves to a GoDaddy parking lander, and no developer portal, documentation, API, or specification survives on any host. This profile is retained as a verified-negative record so future enrichment runs do not re-probe it from scratch.

providers.name: CrowdMob
providers.description: CrowdMob was a mobile gaming and app-monetization startup surfaced as an a16z portfolio company. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating API surface: the company no longer appears in the a16z portfolio listing, and the crowdmob.com domain is now operated by an unrelated affiliate-marketing publisher (AffiliateBay) as a WordPress "growth marketing agency" landing page. No developer portal, documentation, API reference, specs, SDKs, packages, or /.well-known/ discovery documents exist. Retained as a historical/defunct record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Cruise
providers.description: Cruise was an autonomous-vehicle (robotaxi) company founded in 2013 and majority-owned by General Motors, building self-driving technology and operating driverless ride-hail services in San Francisco and other U.S. cities. Backed by GM, Honda, SoftBank Vision Fund, Spark Capital, Y Combinator and others, Cruise suspended operations after a 2023 incident and, in December 2024, GM announced it would end robotaxi development and fold the Cruise team into GM's own autonomous and driver-assistance programs. As of 2026 the getcruise.com domain 301-redirects to GM's autonomous-driving pages. Cruise never published a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Cruise Technologies
providers.description: Cruise Technologies was a wireless thin-client computing company founded in 1997 and based in Arlington Heights, Illinois. It developed the CruiseConnect platform, which enabled server-class and wireless thin-client computing delivered through OEM and licensing partners worldwide. The company raised roughly $12M from Battery Ventures and Bessemer Venture Partners, was acquired in 1999, and has since ceased operations. It was surfaced as a historical entry on the Battery Ventures list-of-all-companies roster and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Enrichment confirmed the company is defunct: it has no live website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. The former cruisetechnologies.com domain is a parked HugeDomains for-sale listing, not a company property. This profile is retained as a historical record only and requires no further enrichment.

providers.name: CryptingUp
providers.description: Cryptocurrency data

providers.name: CubeTree
providers.description: CubeTree was an enterprise social collaboration software startup (founded 2008, Redwood City, California) offering a business social network with wikis, blogs, file sharing, and activity feeds. It was acquired by SuccessFactors in 2010 (deal valued up to $50M) and folded into the SuccessFactors Business Alignment suite; SAP subsequently acquired SuccessFactors in 2012 and the product was absorbed into SAP SuccessFactors / SAP Jam. CubeTree no longer operates as an independent company: the cubetree.com domain is parked under SAP nameservers with no live web presence, developer portal, documentation, or API. Surfaced as a trinity-ventures portfolio company; retained as a historical/defunct network record with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: CucumberTown
providers.description: Cucumbertown was a recipe network and food-blogging platform ("a Tumblr for recipes") founded around 2011-2012 in Palo Alto, California by Cherian Thomas, Chris Luscher, Arun Prabhakar and Dan Hauk, and backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) among other angel investors. It let home cooks and food bloggers publish, structure, and share recipes on a hosted network. Cucumbertown was acquired by the Japanese recipe network Cookpad in June 2015 and was fully shut down by March 31, 2017 for lack of a sustainable business model. The company is defunct and operates no public API or developer program. The cucumbertown.com domain now 302-redirects to Samsung Food (app.samsungfood.com, formerly Whisk), an unrelated successor product; none of the artifacts served on that host belong to Cucumbertown.

providers.name: Cullinet Software
providers.description: Cullinet Software (formerly Cullinane Database Systems) was a database and application software company based in Westwood, Massachusetts, best known for the IDMS/IDMS-DB mainframe database management system, the IDD data dictionary, and the ADS/Online application development environment for IBM mainframes. Backed by Battery Ventures, Greylock, and Morgenthaler Ventures, it was one of the first software companies to go public (1978) and was acquired by Computer Associates (CA) on June 30, 1989. The company is defunct and publishes no developer portal, API, or documentation surface today; this record is retained as a historical portfolio-graph node with no enrichable API artifacts.

providers.name: Curio Labs
providers.description: Curio (curio.io), operated by Curio Labs, was a London-based audio-journalism subscription app founded in 2016 by Govind Balakrishnan and Srikant Chakravarti. It turned articles from premium publishers into professionally narrated audio and later added AI-generated personalized episodes. Backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), EarlyBird, Draper Esprit, Cherry Ventures and Horizons Ventures, it raised over $15M before the founders wound the company down after eight years, citing AI and big-tech competition; they have since moved on to a new venture (Gibran). Enrichment probe finds no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface — curio.io now serves a closure/landing page only.

providers.name: cVidya Networks
providers.description: cVidya Networks was a provider of big-data analytics software for communications and digital service providers, best known for its MoneyMap product suite covering revenue assurance, fraud management, marketing analytics, and data monetization for telecom operators. Founded in 2000 by Alon Aginsky as an Israeli/US company, cVidya grew to roughly 300 employees and about $65M in revenue with deployments across Europe, LATAM, APAC, North America, and Africa. In January 2016 the company was acquired by Amdocs (reported at ~$30M) and absorbed into the Amdocs Revenue Guard and Business Assurance offering; cVidya no longer operates as an independent company and its cvidya.com domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record; there is no live developer portal or public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cyneta Networks
providers.description: Cyneta Networks, Inc. was a wireless data networking equipment company founded around 2000 and headquartered in Plano, Texas, with an additional presence in Cockeysville, Maryland. Backed by Battery Ventures, it developed intelligent hardware and software for wireless data networks — packet control, network element management, and network monitoring / service-quality optimization for mobile operator core networks — and accumulated a patent portfolio in wireless and core network monitoring. The company is a dot-com-era venture that no longer maintains an active public web presence: its former domain, cyneta.com, no longer serves a Cyneta site and its DNS is now operated by an unrelated party. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live developer portal, documentation, GitHub organization, package-registry libraries, or any API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record; there is nothing to catalog on the API supply side.

providers.name: Cyren Call
providers.description: Cyren Call Communications Corp. was a wireless communications company founded in 2005 by Nextel co-founder Morgan O'Brien to advocate for a nationwide public-safety broadband network. Its central proposal asked the FCC to reallocate 30 MHz of 700 MHz-band spectrum (freed by the 2009 analog-TV shutdown) to public-safety users, and it later served as advisor to the Public Safety Spectrum Trust (PSST) after PSST became the nationwide licensee for public safety's 10 MHz of 700 MHz broadband spectrum. The FCC dismissed Cyren Call's original petition as inconsistent with auction requirements, and the PSST advisory relationship ended in early 2009. The company is permanently closed. It never operated a developer program, public API, or SDK surface, so no API artifacts are available for enrichment.

providers.name: Daily Gobble
providers.description: Daily Gobble was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub sourced from the 500 Global portfolio. A 2026-07-20 enrichment pass found no operating company behind it. The dailygobble.com domain is a GoDaddy parked domain that serves a JavaScript redirect to a /lander page, carries no MX records, and publishes no content. The relevantmobile.com URL carried on the original stub does not belong to Daily Gobble; it now serves an unrelated Indonesian-language gambling and SEO spam site, and it has been removed rather than retained as a Website pointer. No first-party client libraries were found on npm or PyPI. There is no API, developer program, documentation, or event surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: Danger
providers.description: Danger, Inc. was a Palo Alto, California mobile computing company founded on December 9, 1999 by Andy Rubin, Joe Britt, and Matt Hershenson, all former Apple, WebTV, and Philips engineers. Danger built the Danger Hiptop, sold in the United States as the T-Mobile Sidekick, an early client-server ("cloud") smartphone whose downloadable application catalog prefigured the app stores later shipped by Android and iOS. Andy Rubin left Danger in 2003 to found Android. Microsoft acquired Danger on February 11, 2008 for a price reported at roughly $500 million and folded the team into "Project Pink," which shipped as the short-lived Microsoft Kin. Most former Danger staff had left Microsoft by October 2009 and the company was wound down by approximately 2011. Danger was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a historic Redpoint Ventures portfolio holding. It is defunct: the danger.com domain no longer resolves and there is no developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: DAOex
providers.description: DAOex (DAO Exchange, product-branded "Commune") was a web3 community relationship management platform positioned as an all-in-one tool for understanding, engaging, and growing DAO and NFT communities. Its advertised surface covered member directories bridging on-chain and off-chain data, referral programs with unique member/affiliate links, quests, contests and bounties as rewards infrastructure, Discord-native engagement and role assignment, and payouts of tokens, NFTs or Discord roles on Ethereum mainnet and Polygon via an automatically provisioned Gnosis Safe, with a points-and-CSV fallback for pre-token communities. Surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the company appears DEFUNCT: daoex.app no longer resolves in DNS (NXDOMAIN, no SOA), the site was a single-page Webflow marketing site last published 2022-09-22 and last archived 2023-03-21, and no API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, package or GitHub organization was ever published.

providers.name: Dapper
providers.description: Dapper was an advertising-technology and web-data company founded in 2006 by Jonathan Aizen and Eran Shir, seed-funded by Accel. It ran two surfaces: Dapper Ads, an intent-driven dynamic-ad product that pulled live product and inventory data from an advertiser's own site into targeted creative without IT integration; and open.dapper.net (the "Dapp Factory" / Dapper: The Data Mapper), a hosted tool that turned any web page into structured feeds, web services and widgets — XML, RSS, JSON, YAML, CSV, iCalendar, Google Gadgets, Netvibes modules and image loops — effectively letting anyone "create an API for any site" before providers published their own. Dapper was acquired by Yahoo! in 2010 and both surfaces were shut down; dapper.net now resolves to Yahoo nameservers with no host, and open.dapper.net no longer resolves. There is no live API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Dark Sky
providers.description: Dark Sky is a hyperlocal weather forecast REST API (now part of Apple) that provided minute-by-minute precipitation forecasts, hourly weather conditions, and multi-day outlooks powered by machine-learning models. The API delivered real-time and historical weather data for any latitude and longitude worldwide, including current conditions, 60-minute minutely precipitation intensity, 48-hour hourly forecasts, and 7-day daily summaries. It was acquired by Apple in March 2020; new developer signups closed immediately, and the API was permanently shut down on March 31, 2023. Apple's WeatherKit REST API is the successor service.

providers.name: Dashbase
providers.description: Dashbase, Inc. was a San Jose, California based developer of a next-generation log analytics and search platform, positioned as a lighter, real-time alternative to heavier log-management and observability stacks for DevOps and engineering teams. The company was a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (dashbase.io) no longer resolves / times out and its GitHub organization retains only a single archived fork, so the company appears to be defunct or to have been acquired and wound down; no live developer surface, API, SDK, OpenAPI, or documentation could be located. This profile is retained as a network record with only verifiable facts.

providers.name: dashmobile
providers.description: dashmobile (listed by Slow Ventures as "Dash Labs") was surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 found no operating public surface: the listed domain dashmobile.co has no DNS records at all (no A record, no NS delegation) and returns no HTTP response, and the Internet Archive holds exactly one capture of the domain (2022-05-24), which was itself a .CO registry domain-expired parking page rather than company content. The company therefore has no website, no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no discoverable artifacts of any kind. This profile is retained as a verified-defunct portfolio lead and is not a candidate for further enrichment unless the company relaunches on a new domain.

providers.name: Dasient
providers.description: Dasient was a web anti-malware company founded in 2008 in Sunnyvale, California by ex-Google engineers Neil Daswani and Shariq Rizvi with McKinsey consultant Ameet Ranadive. It sold cloud-based protection against web-based malware and malvertising, scanning customer websites and ad networks with its Malware Analysis Platform. It shipped a JSON-RPC over HTTP "Web Protection API" that let customers schedule and run on-demand malware scans of individual domains and URLs, with tiered pricing by scans per day. Twitter acquired Dasient in January 2012 for a reported $19.1 million; the product was retired, dasient.com went dark in late 2012, and the domain is now a parked defensive registration held by Twitter. This company is DEFUNCT and has no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Data Elite Services
providers.description: Data Elite Services, Inc. was a San Francisco company associated with Data Elite, a venture lab and early-stage accelerator for big-data startups and data scientists founded in 2013 at 135 Main Street, San Francisco, California. The entity was registered in California on 2013-08-27 as a foreign stock corporation and its filing status is recorded as forfeited by the Franchise Tax Board, indicating the business is no longer active. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live company website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. The dataelite.com domain resolves but redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale parking lander rather than a company site, and no other candidate domain resolved. This record is retained as an inactive historical entry in the API Evangelist network with no API artifacts to enrich; it should not be treated as an active API provider.

providers.name: DataGravity
providers.description: DataGravity was a data management and security software company founded in April 2012 in Nashua, New Hampshire by Paula Long (co-founder of EqualLogic) and John Joseph. It pioneered the "data-aware storage" category, shipping hybrid storage arrays that indexed, classified, and audited data in place so that security, governance, and search became properties of the storage tier rather than bolt-on tooling. The company raised venture funding from Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, CRV and others, won Best of Show at VMworld 2014, and began shipping in October 2014. In February 2016 it pivoted from appliances to a software-only behavioral data-security product. DataGravity ceased operations in June 2017 and its assets were assigned to a liquidator; HyTrust acquired the technology and roughly twenty employees, folding the product into HyTrust CloudAdvisor (HyTrust was itself acquired by Entrust in 2021). The datagravity.com domain no longer belongs to the company and now 301-redirects to an unrelated business (anomalo.com).
