No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification survives, so there is no API surface for this profile to describe.

providers.name: Datalogix
providers.description: Datalogix was a consumer-purchase and marketing data company that connected offline buying behavior to digital advertising audiences, enabling measurement and targeting for brands and ad platforms. Backed by General Catalyst and IVP, it was acquired by Oracle in 2014 and folded into the Oracle Data Cloud. The datalogix.com domain now 301-redirects to Oracle's acquisitions page, and no standalone Datalogix developer portal, API, or documentation remains publicly available.

providers.name: Datrium
providers.description: Datrium was a Sunnyvale, California enterprise infrastructure company founded in 2012 by Brian Biles and Hugo Patterson (both formerly of Data Domain / EMC). Its flagship DVX ("Distributed Virtual X") platform introduced an "open convergence" architecture that separated compute from durable storage for virtualized data centers, and the company later pivoted toward cloud disaster-recovery-as-a-service (Datrium DRaaS with DRaaS Connect and ControlShield). Datrium was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, NEA, and others, and was acquired by VMware in July 2020, with its technology folded into VMware Cloud Disaster Recovery. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no active developer portal or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record surfaced from Lightspeed Venture Partners' portfolio.

providers.name: DaWanda.com
providers.description: DaWanda.com was a German online marketplace for handmade, unique, and custom-made products, founded in 2006 in Berlin. It connected independent makers and small designers with buyers across Germany and Europe, comparable to Etsy in the DACH region. DaWanda ceased operations on 30 August 2018 and partnered with Etsy to migrate its sellers and buyers; the www.dawanda.com domain now redirects to Etsy Germany. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. No public developer program or API surface was found during enrichment; the company is defunct and retained here as a historical/portfolio record.

providers.name: DCHQ
providers.description: DCHQ (Data Center HQ) was a cloud automation and Docker container management platform out of San Francisco, offering both a hosted PaaS (DCHQ.io) and self-hosted on-premise editions for modeling, deploying, and managing container-based applications across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Rackspace, and OpenStack. The platform covered application modeling (Docker Compose / JSON), infrastructure automation, multi-tenant governance and access controls, and lifecycle management including monitoring, backup, and auto-scaling, with integrations for Docker, GitHub, and Jenkins. The company is now defunct — its primary domain (dchq.co) no longer resolves and dchq.io serves a frozen 2020 marketing snapshot with no live developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record; no live API artifacts were available to enrich.

providers.name: DCP Midstream
providers.description: DCP Midstream LLC was a Denver, Colorado-based natural gas gathering, processing, and NGL transportation company that operated as one of the largest U.S. producers and marketers of natural gas liquids. In June 2023, Phillips 66 completed the acquisition of all publicly traded common units of DCP Midstream LP for approximately $3.8 billion, taking its ownership stake to 86.8%. DCP Midstream and Phillips 66 Partners were subsequently merged into Phillips 66's NGL and midstream business; the standalone brand, public filings, developer surface, and corporate website have been retired. The dcpmidstream.com domain no longer resolves to a working site, and there is no public DCP-branded developer portal, API reference, status page, or changelog. This repository documents DCP Midstream as a defunct entity absorbed into the Phillips 66 midstream organization.

providers.name: Dean Foods
providers.description: Dean Foods was a leading U.S. food and beverage company and one of the largest processors and direct-to-store distributors of fresh fluid milk and other dairy products. After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2019, most of Dean Foods' assets were acquired by Dairy Farmers of America (DFA) in 2020. Dean Foods no longer operates as an independent company and does not publish a public developer API; surviving brands are now managed under DFA. This profile is retained for historical reference.

providers.name: DecisionPoint Software
providers.description: DecisionPoint Software was a San Mateo, California-based enterprise software company that provided packaged financial performance management (FPM) and financial data warehousing software, built primarily around the Oracle ERP stack. Its systems captured and moved continuously changing data from financial source systems into a data warehouse, automatically configuring the analytic environment as the source systems changed, and shipped as far as Release 11 with operations in both the United States and the United Kingdom. The company was named one of the 50 fastest-growing private companies in Silicon Valley in 2004 and raised a $5M Series B round from Battery Ventures that same year. It was acquired in December 2005 by NCR's Teradata data warehousing division, which folded the FPM and data warehousing technology into the Teradata enterprise data warehouse offering. DecisionPoint Software has not operated as an independent company for roughly two decades: it publishes no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface, and this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: deepfactor
providers.description: Deepfactor was an application security (AppSec / ASPM) platform for cloud-native and containerized applications. Its integrated approach combined software composition analysis (SCA), software bill of materials (SBOM) generation, container image scanning, and container runtime security into a single developer-security platform. Its differentiating capability was runtime software composition analysis / runtime reachability, correlating static scans with observed runtime application behavior so teams could prioritize vulnerability remediation based on true usage. Use cases spanned Shift-Left & DevSecOps, supply chain security, SBOM, container runtime security & compliance (SOC 2), and cloud-native application security. Backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07) the public website is offline — the apex domain (deepfactor.io) returns a Cisco 503 error page and the WP Engine-hosted www/docs hosts return "Site is not available", and DNS for the apex resolves to Cisco infrastructure; there is no live developer portal, API, SDK, CLI, GitHub organization, or published package to harvest.

providers.name: DeepSparks
providers.description: DeepSparks was a Bangkok, Thailand fintech offering a lending-as-a-service platform built on AI-driven alternative credit scoring. It analyzed non-traditional data to help financial institutions, microlenders, and enablers approve and acquire underbanked borrowers, and offered a data API, lead generation, and a rejected-applicant exchange. Founded in 2018 and backed by 500 Global and J Ventures, the company has since ceased operations (deadpooled); its official site at deepsparks.ai no longer resolves.

providers.name: Delta Tucker Holdings
providers.description: Delta Tucker Holdings was the holding company for DynCorp International, a provider of specialized mission-critical professional and support services to government and commercial customers, including aviation services, logistics, and training. DynCorp's operations were acquired and integrated into Amentum in 2020. Delta Tucker Holdings does not publish public APIs; this profile is preserved as a corporate-history index.

providers.name: Descartes Labs
providers.description: Descartes Labs was a Santa Fe, New Mexico geospatial intelligence company founded in 2014 as a spin-out from Los Alamos National Laboratory. The company built the Descartes Labs Platform, a cloud-native geospatial data refinery and analytics environment combining a petabyte-scale satellite imagery archive (Landsat, Sentinel-1/2, MODIS, NAIP, PlanetScope, SkySat, commercial radar, NEXRAD weather radar, plus client-uploaded data) with a Python client library, JupyterHub-based workbench, and distributed compute for training and running deep learning and remote-sensing models at scale. Customers in agriculture, mining, energy, defense, insurance, and the U.S. government used the platform to build production geospatial machine learning pipelines covering crop forecasting, mineral exploration, infrastructure monitoring, methane detection, wildfire response, and ESG reporting. The Platform exposed a Catalog (imagery, bands, products, blobs, events), a Compute service (containerised functions, jobs, schedules), a Vector service (tabular and geospatial features), Dynamic Compute (lazy raster algebra and tiling), Auth, and a `descarteslabs` CLI. In October 2024, EarthDaily Analytics — backed by Antarctica Capital — acquired Descartes Labs and the Descartes Labs Government, Inc. subsidiary, folding the team, customers, and platform into the EarthDaily Constellation programme. The product was rebranded EarthOne in 2025; the `descarteslabs` Python package has been formally discontinued in favour of `earthdaily-earthone` (v5.x), the github.com/descarteslabs organisation has been renamed to `dlarchives`, www.descarteslabs.com is now a parked domain, and the docs.descarteslabs.com developer portal has been retired in favour of EarthDaily-hosted EarthOne documentation. This catalog entry preserves the historical Descartes Labs Platform surface as an archive — see the EarthDaily / EarthOne profile for the active product.

providers.name: Destineer
providers.description: Destineer was a networking-solutions provider for telecommunications carriers, and an early-stage Kleiner Perkins portfolio company partnered since 1995. Per Kleiner Perkins' own partnerships archive, the company was acquired by MCI WorldCom and no longer operates as an independent entity. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live web presence: destineer.com, destineer.net, destineer.dev and destineer.us all return NXDOMAIN, there is no developer portal, documentation, or GitHub organization, and the APIs.io catalog lists no APIs for this provider. Because the company predates the public web API era and is defunct, no API, specification, SDK, or agent artifacts exist to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record in the Kleiner Perkins investment graph rather than as an active API provider. Note: the unrelated video-game publisher of the same name (Minnetonka, MN, 2001-2011) and the individual github.com/destineer account are not this company.

providers.name: Dharma Labs
providers.description: Dharma Labs was a decentralized-finance company that built Dharma Protocol, an open-source Ethereum protocol for tokenized debt and peer-to-peer lending, and later the Dharma non-custodial smart wallet. It was backed by Polychain and was acquired by OpenSea in 2021. The company is defunct: its developer surface at dharma.io is now a parked, for-sale domain with no live API, documentation, or well-known discovery endpoints. Real, first-party remnants still survive on the public registries — the GitHub organization dharmaprotocol (26 public repos, including the dharma.js client library, charta smart contracts, developer-docs, and the dapp-wallet) and the npm package @dharmaprotocol/dharma.js, which is published but explicitly marked DEPRECATED. This profile captures those honest historical artifacts; the provider ships no maintained API today.

providers.name: Diablo Technologies
providers.description: Diablo Technologies Inc. was an enterprise memory technology company backed by Battery Ventures. It developed Memory Channel Storage (MCS), an architecture that placed flash storage directly on the DDR memory bus, and productized it as Memory1, a flash-as-DRAM DIMM the company marketed as delivering up to 256 GB of memory per module and 4 TB per dual-socket server. Diablo positioned itself as a silicon and module vendor selling through server and storage OEM partners rather than as a software or platform company: it never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or any machine-readable specification, and no developer surface appears anywhere in the archived record of its website. The company appears to be defunct. Its corporate site is last archived intact in 2017, the domain subsequently served unrelated SEO spam, the diablo-technologies.com registration lapsed and was re-registered on 2023-10-08 through a different registrar, and the hostname today serves an unrelated consumer-gadget review blog with no connection to the memory business. No GitHub organization exists under either diablo-technologies or diablotechnologies. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface.

providers.name: Diamond Lane
providers.description: Diamond Lane was a hardtech networking-equipment company that built DSL broadband networking equipment, backed by Kleiner Perkins and listed on the firm's partnerships page with a status of acquired. The company predates the modern web API era and no longer operates an independent commercial surface: enrichment probes in July 2026 found no reachable corporate website (diamondlane.com resolves only to a domain-for-sale parking page and diamond-lane.com to a registrar default page), no GitHub organization, no published client libraries on npm or PyPI, and no developer portal, documentation, or API of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Digby
providers.description: Digby was an Austin, Texas software-as-a-service provider of mobile commerce and mobile engagement solutions for large retailers, operating under parent company 30 Second Software Inc. Its platform — including the Localpoint location-based marketing product — delivered branded mobile web experiences and native shopping apps, connecting digital engagement to physical stores for customers such as Cabela's, Kohl's, Catalina Marketing and Hasbro. Digby raised venture funding from Battery Ventures, S3 Ventures, Daylight Ventures, Relay Ventures and the BlackBerry Partners Fund. The company was acquired by fellow Austin mobile company Phunware in May 2014 (along with its Movaya subsidiary in Seattle and Chengdu), terms undisclosed, and the Localpoint technology was folded into Phunware's product line. Digby no longer operates as an independent company: digby.com no longer resolves to a live site (last Internet Archive capture February 2015) and there is no current developer portal, documentation, API, SDK or other public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Digital Market
providers.description: Digital Market was an enterprise-software company that built electronic-components B2B commerce software, backed by Trinity Ventures. It was acquired by Agile Software and no longer operates as an independent provider. It is not an API provider and publishes no live developer surface, documentation, or specifications; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio record rather than an active, enrichable API.

providers.name: Digitalk
providers.description: Digitalk, Inc. was an American object-oriented software tools vendor and a Trinity Ventures portfolio company, best known for Smalltalk/V — a commercial Smalltalk development environment first released in 1986 for MS-DOS, preceded by "Digitalk Methods" in 1983. It was founded by George Bosworth, Jim Anderson, Mike Teng and Barbara Noparstak, and its product line grew into Visual Smalltalk Enterprise. In July 1995 Digitalk merged with its principal competitor ParcPlace Systems; the combined company was later renamed ObjectShare, announced a shift away from Smalltalk toward Java in 1997, and active development of the Digitalk line ended shortly after. The final release, Visual Smalltalk Enterprise 2000, shipped in September 2000. Cincom retains the right to sell and support VSE 2000 for existing licensees and Seagull Software owns the virtual machine. Digitalk predates the public web API era and operates no developer platform, public API, or live web presence today; this profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Direct Revenue
providers.description: Direct Revenue was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead. A July 2026 enrichment pass found no live corporate or developer surface for this company: directrevenue.com resolves to an Efty domain-for-sale parking lander (domain registered 2002, held at Tucows, listed for sale); direct-revenue.com is a squatted domain that 302-redirects to baidu.com; directrevenue.co returns Cloudflare 522 (origin unreachable); and directrevenue.net, directrevenue.ai and getdirectrevenue.com do not resolve at all. There is no website, no developer portal, no documentation, no API, and no matching provider in the APIs.io catalog. This profile is retained as a historical lead record only and carries no API artifacts.

providers.name: Dirig Software
providers.description: Dirig Software, Inc. was a Nashua, New Hampshire software company that built application and system management software for eBusiness — agent-based performance monitoring and automated problem correction for J2EE application servers (WebLogic, WebSphere), web infrastructure, and hosted service-provider environments, sold both direct to enterprises and through OEM and service-provider channels. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures. Its web presence at dirig.com carried full product, partner, and support content through roughly 2003, degraded to a broken holding page under the name "Dirig Corporation" from early 2004, and by late 2006 the domain was a parked Sedo for-sale page. As of this enrichment pass the company has no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind; dirig.com now resolves to an unrelated third-party endpoint returning a bare "OK" health response. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network — there is nothing to enrich and nothing to score.

providers.name: Distelli
providers.description: Distelli was a Seattle-based DevOps and application-deployment company founded in 2013 by Rahul Singh and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It offered a SaaS platform and command-line tooling for building, deploying, and managing applications across servers and cloud infrastructure, later adding a Docker container pipeline and a Kubernetes (K8s) dashboard for managing container clusters. Puppet acquired Distelli in September 2017 and rebranded its products — the VM/CI-CD dashboard became Puppet Pipelines for Applications and the Kubernetes dashboard became Puppet Pipelines for Containers. The standalone Distelli company, product, and API no longer operate: the distelli.com domain is parked and the Distelli GitHub organization is archived and explicitly "no longer supported nor actively maintained." This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record (a16z) in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Divshot
providers.description: Divshot was a front-end and static web application hosting platform based in Santa Monica, California, and a 500 Global portfolio company. It offered command-line deploys of single-page and static applications across development, staging and production environments, with instant environment URLs, custom domains and SSL certificate upload, environment variables and app configuration, HTTP basic-auth protection of environments, cache purging, release promotion and rollback, and per-app webhooks. Divshot published a first-party CLI (divshot-cli) and a JavaScript API client (divshot-api) on npm, and open-sourced Superstatic, the static web server behind the platform. Divshot was acquired by Google in 2015 and folded into Firebase Hosting. The service is defunct - divshot.com no longer resolves and no live API, documentation or developer portal remains. This profile is a historical record built from the surviving first-party npm packages and GitHub repositories.

providers.name: DNA Games
providers.description: DNA Games was a social game studio founded in 2009 by Jon Lee and Shaun Haase in the San Francisco Bay Area, building technology for real-time social game optimization on the Facebook platform. The studio shipped Casino City, Bar World, and Slot City, casino and lifestyle simulation titles that together reached more than 20 million players, with Casino City becoming a leading casino simulation game on Facebook. The company raised roughly $2 million in venture funding from Battery Ventures and Bain Capital Ventures before being acquired by Zynga in May 2011, one of a rapid series of Zynga studio acquisitions during that period. Post-acquisition the founders and core team were absorbed into Zynga to seed a new internal game studio, and DNA Games ceased to operate as an independent company. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company publishes no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface; the dnagames.com, dna.games, and dnagames.io domains are all parked or listed for sale by third parties and are not operated by the company.

providers.name: doc.ai
providers.description: doc.ai, Inc. was a privacy-first enterprise artificial intelligence platform for healthcare, founded by Sam De Brouwer and Walter De Brouwer. It ran decentralized "data trials" that let individuals contribute and train models on their own genomic, pharmacogenomic, exposomic, wellness and hematology data, and it issued the $NRN (Neuron) token in a sale that closed in October 2017 — which is why it is carried in the Pantera Capital portfolio under the crypto sector despite being a digital-health AI business. Sharecare, Inc. completed its acquisition of doc.ai on 2021-02-23, absorbing the Unwinding Anxiety, Serenity, VERIFIED and Passport products and retaining both founders as executives. The doc.ai brand is retired: the apex domain no longer resolves to a website (last archived HTTP 200 on 2023-04-16) and no doc.ai developer portal, API, or specification could be located.

providers.name: Doelz Networks
providers.description: Doelz Networks Inc. was a data communications networking company headquartered at 9501 Jeronimo Road, Irvine, California. It developed data communication networks designed to be independent of media, speed, attached devices, or protocols, applied across both local area networks (LANs) and wide area networks (WANs), with additional locations in Columbia, Maryland and New Jersey. The company raised roughly $16.9 million from investors including Battery Ventures, Accel, J.H. Whitney, Citi Venture Capital International and Brentwood, and was bought out by its management together with a group of European investors in 1988. The company has since been acquired and is no longer operating: enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live corporate domain, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical record of a venture-backed networking vendor and is not expected to yield API artifacts.

providers.name: Domio
providers.description: Domio was a New York City hospitality and real-estate technology company that designed, leased, and operated branded "apart-hotels" — spacious, design-forward apartment-style accommodations aimed at group and extended-stay travelers. Founded in June 2016 by former Bank of America Merrill Lynch real-estate bankers Jay Roberts and Adrian Lam, the company used data analysis and machine learning to select buildings for its portfolio and distributed inventory through its own site and app alongside third-party channels such as Airbnb. It raised roughly $117M across five rounds, including a $12M Series A in 2018 from Tribeca Venture Partners and SoftBank Capital, a $50M joint-venture facility from Upper90, and a $100M Series B in December 2019 (half equity, half debt) led by GGV Capital with Eldridge Industries, 3L Capital, Cain International and Tenaya Capital. Airbnb suspended all of Domio's host accounts in August 2020, the co-founders resigned that September, and the company ceased operations in November 2020, selling its assets through an assignment for the benefit of creditors overseen by Sherwood Partners. Domio never published a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification. Its former host staydomio.com was re-registered on 2021-09-19 by an unrelated party and now serves a GoDaddy parking lander, so it is deliberately not wired as a Website pointer. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Donnerwood Media
providers.description: Donnerwood Media was an early-stage social gaming and social entertainment company founded in 2005 by Sean Ryan and based in San Francisco. It operated Meez.com, an avatar-building platform that let consumers create customized 3D avatars usable across the web as personal identifiers, alongside a portfolio of social game properties. The company raised roughly $15.7M from Battery Ventures, transcosmos, and Allen & Company. It is now defunct — the Meez service went offline in December 2017 and its domain expired in March 2018 — so it exposes no live website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: Dooly
providers.description: Dooly was a connected workspace for revenue teams that improved Salesforce CRM hygiene by syncing meeting notes, pipeline updates, and next steps back into Salesforce automatically. It layered a fast note-taking surface, deal vitals, real-time playbooks, and one-click CRM updates on top of Salesforce so account executives could keep their pipeline clean without manual data entry. Backed by Battery Ventures, Dooly was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. The Dooly platform was shut down on June 30, 2025; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and this profile captures the remaining public surface (website, privacy policy, terms) for the record.

providers.name: Door-to-Door Organic
providers.description: Door to Door Organics was an organic and natural grocery home-delivery service founded in 1997 and headquartered in Louisville, Colorado. It delivered fresh local and organic produce boxes along with pantry staples, dairy, eggs, meat, and bread to homes and offices across roughly 17 states in the West, Midwest, and East Coast (including Washington, D.C.). Backed by Battery Ventures among others, the company raised about $44.4M over six rounds before abruptly ceasing operations in 2017. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no public developer surface (no portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or API host); the company is defunct and publishes no API.

providers.name: Dooyoo De
providers.description: Dooyoo was a German consumer product-review and price-comparison platform built on user-generated reviews, best known for its "dooyooMiles" rewards program that paid users for writing reviews. It was acquired by the French shopping-guide publisher LeGuide.com in 2008, and the LeGuide group (Ciao, Dooyoo, and others) was in turn acquired by Kelkoo in 2016 to form Kelkoo Group. The dooyoo.de domain no longer operates as an independent brand and now 301-redirects to kelkoogroup.com; there is no active developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a defunct/absorbed portfolio lead with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Drawbridge Networks
providers.description: Drawbridge Networks was a network microsegmentation cybersecurity startup founded in 2014 in New York by John Terrill and Tom Cross. Its product, PathProtect, applied fine-grained, identity- and workload-aware security policies inside corporate networks to learn, detect, and automatically quarantine lateral (east-west) attacker movement before it could spread. The company raised a $1.7M seed round from Antecedent Ventures, Bloomberg Beta, and Bowery Capital, and was acquired by OPAQ Networks in May 2017 (OPAQ was itself later acquired by Fortinet in 2020). Drawbridge Networks was surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment finds the company defunct: no domains resolve, and there is no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Drippi
providers.description: Drippi (trydrippi.com) was a New York City-based platform that helped young content creators navigate the complexities of running their creator businesses. The company has been acquired and has closed its service to both current and new customers, directing its community to Instagram (@trydrippi) for future updates. It does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. NOTE FOR ENRICHMENT — this entity is distinct from the similarly named drippi.ai, a separate, bootstrapped Twitter/X cold-outreach DM automation SaaS (founded 2021 by Alex Penunuri, no venture funding); do not attach drippi.ai's API artifacts to this Bloomberg Beta portfolio profile.

providers.name: Drivetime
providers.description: Drivetime (Drive.fm) was a voice-activated, hands-free in-car entertainment platform founded in 2018 by Niko Vuori, Justin Cooper, and Cory Johnson (veterans of Zynga and Rocket Games). The consumer mobile app delivered interactive trivia games, storytelling, quizzes, news, and audiobooks designed to be safe to play while driving, running on Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, and partnered with the Jeopardy game show for a channel narrated by Alex Trebek. The company raised roughly $15M across seed and later rounds, with backing from Canaan Partners, Makers Fund, the Amazon Alexa Fund, Google Assistant Investments, Sinai Ventures, Fuel Capital, and Access Ventures. Drivetime was a business-to-consumer product and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; as of this profiling the drive.fm / drivetime.fm domain and the associated App Store and Google Play listings no longer resolve, indicating the product has been discontinued.

providers.name: Driveway Corporation
providers.description: Driveway Corporation was a dot-com-era online file storage and sharing service that operated driveway.com from roughly 1998 until 2001. Its consumer product let members "store and access files from any Web-connected computer" and share documents, photos and MP3s with friends and colleagues, with up to 100 MB of free storage on sign-up; it also marketed a white-label "Driveway Private Label Storage" offering to other websites. Battery Ventures lists Driveway Corporation as an exited investment. The company is defunct and no longer operates any web, developer or API surface. NOTE: the driveway.com domain today belongs to an unrelated business — Lithia Motors' Driveway online car marketplace — and must not be attributed to this company.

providers.name: Dubsmash
providers.description: Dubsmash was a video-selfie and lip-sync mobile application that let users record short videos set to a library of popular audio clips, quotes, and songs. Founded in Germany in 2014 by Jonas Druppel, Roland Grenke, and Daniel Taschik, it grew into one of the most downloaded social video apps, particularly among younger creators in the United States. Reddit acquired Dubsmash in December 2020, integrated its video-creation technology into the Reddit platform, and discontinued the standalone Dubsmash app on February 22, 2022. Dubsmash never offered a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; its consumer domain (dubsmash.com) no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical, defunct company record surfaced from venture-capital portfolio data.

providers.name: Dunzo
providers.description: Dunzo was an Indian hyperlocal delivery and quick-commerce platform founded in July 2014 in Bengaluru by Kabeer Biswas, Ankur Agarwal, Dalvir Suri and Mukund Jha, which grew from a WhatsApp group into an app-based service delivering groceries, food, medicines, pet supplies and same-city packages across up to nine Indian cities. Its Dunzo for Business (D4B) offering gave merchants last-mile delivery through a partner API and through multi-carrier aggregators. Backed by Google, Blume Ventures, Alteria Capital and Reliance Retail, the company was dissolved on 14 January 2025; the app and website were shut down and every Dunzo-operated host, including its merchant API, is now offline. This profile is retained as a historical record — Dunzo publishes no developer portal, documentation, specification or support channel today.

providers.name: Durata Therapeutics
providers.description: Durata Therapeutics was a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company founded in 2009 around anti-infective assets acquired from Pfizer's Vicuron division, headquartered first in Morristown, New Jersey and from 2012 in Chicago, Illinois. Its lead candidate was dalbavancin, a long-acting semisynthetic lipoglycopeptide antibiotic taken into Phase III trials from 2011 for acute bacterial skin and skin-structure infections and later marketed as Dalvance. The company was backed by Canaan Partners and was acquired by Actavis (now Allergan) on November 17, 2014 for approximately $675 million, at which point it ceased to operate as an independent entity. Durata Therapeutics published no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts; its corporate domain duratatherapeutics.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DWL
providers.description: DWL Inc. was an enterprise software company founded in 1996 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, with significant engineering and operations in Toronto, Ontario. DWL built customer data integration (CDI) middleware — its flagship product, DWL Customer, was a real-time master data hub that consolidated fragmented customer records from across banking, insurance, telecommunications, and retail systems into a single authoritative view, and served that view back to operational applications through a transaction-oriented services layer. Backed by Insight Venture Partners, AGF Investments, Nationwide Mutual Capital, Royal Trust, and Stone Point Capital, DWL was acquired by IBM in August 2005 to fill the CDI gap in IBM's information-management stack. DWL Customer was rebranded IBM WebSphere Customer Center and subsequently folded into IBM InfoSphere Master Data Management. DWL has not operated as an independent company for two decades, never published a public developer program or API, and the dwl.com domain now redirects to ibm.com. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Eargo
providers.description: Eargo was a San Jose, California direct-to-consumer medical device company that designed and sold rechargeable, virtually invisible in-canal hearing aids for adults with mild to moderate hearing loss, founded in 2010 as Aria Innovations and listed on Nasdaq in 2020. In 2025 Eargo merged with South Africa's hearX Group to form LXE Hearing, combining Eargo's direct-to-consumer platform with the Lexie and Go Hearing over-the-counter brands. In 2026 LXE Hearing began winding down its US operations after restructuring efforts failed, and the eargo.com website has been reduced to a single wind-down notice page. Eargo never operated a public developer program, developer portal, or documented API: the hearing aids paired with a consumer mobile application backed by a private, undocumented service host at api.eargo.com.

providers.name: EasyKnock
providers.description: EasyKnock was a New York based residential real estate fintech, founded in 2016 by Jared Kessler, that pioneered consumer sale-leaseback in the United States: homeowners sold their house to EasyKnock for cash and stayed on as renting tenants with an option to repurchase. The company raised roughly $430 million in equity and debt and rolled up several proptech businesses — Ribbon Home, Onder, Balance Home, HomePace and FarmlandFinder — before consumer lawsuits and state attorney general and regulator actions in Massachusetts, Michigan, Connecticut, Texas, Maryland, South Carolina, Pennsylvania and Ohio over its sale-leaseback disclosures. EasyKnock announced it had closed its doors on December 6, 2024. Its website is now a single static shutdown notice, its api.easyknock.com host answers Cloudflare error 1016 (origin DNS deleted), and it never published a public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Echelon
providers.description: Echelon Corporation was a pioneer in energy control networking and semiconductors, known for its LonWorks control networking platform and IoT edge computing products. Surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company (listed as an energy-control-networking milestone/exit), the company is no longer an independent entity — its product lines were acquired (Adesto Technologies, 2018) and now live under EnOcean. There is no live Echelon developer portal or public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Echopass
providers.description: Echopass Corporation was a cloud-based (on-demand / hosted) contact center technology company, headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area (San Ramon / Pleasanton, California) and backed by Canaan Partners among other venture investors. Its platform delivered multichannel, carrier-grade contact center and customer-interaction capabilities as a hosted service to enterprises. Echopass was acquired by Genesys in 2013 and folded into the Genesys customer-experience portfolio; it no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live developer, API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for lineage and portfolio-graph purposes rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: EcoMom
providers.description: EcoMom was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead for enrichment. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating company surface behind the ecomom.com domain. The domain's nameservers are ns1/ns2.afternic.com and every request to ecomom.com issues a 307 redirect to an Afternic listing headlined "The domain name ecomom.com is for sale!" with no published price. The host serves a wildcard soft-200 parking page - arbitrary paths, including a deliberately nonsense control path, all return HTTP 200 with text/html that redirects to /lander - so the 200 status codes returned for /.well-known/security.txt, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, /.well-known/api-catalog, /.well-known/ai-plugin.json, /llms.txt and /openapi.json are parking artifacts and not real documents. The api, developer, docs and www subdomains resolve to the same two parking IPs. There is no developer portal, no documentation, no specification and no API surface to catalog, so no enrichment artifacts were written for this company.

providers.name: EdgeSpring
providers.description: EdgeSpring is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins, lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Edgix
providers.description: Edgix (Edgix Corporation) is a former, exited Battery Ventures portfolio company surfaced from Battery's public list-of-all-companies page and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment stub. As of the 2026-07 enrichment pass no live web presence, developer portal, documentation, or API surface could be located: candidate domains edgix.com returns HTTP 404 and edgix.io / edgix.ai do not resolve to a live server (connection refused). Battery lists the investment as exited (marked with an asterisk on their all-companies list), and the portfolio harvest recorded is_api_provider: false. No artifacts were produced this round because there is nothing published to search, generate, or derive against without fabrication. This record is retained as a verified-defunct lead so future pipeline runs can skip it rather than re-probe.

providers.name: edisn.ai
providers.description: edisn.ai was an AI-powered fan engagement platform for sports and media, surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The enrichment pipeline found no public developer surface — no API, OpenAPI, SDK, package, or documentation, and no docs/developer/api subdomain ever archived. The domain expired on 2026-05-09 and is now in pendingDelete/clientHold with no DNS resolution; by 2024 it already redirected to fubo.tv. No provider artifacts could be captured because none exist to search or derive from.

providers.name: Edmodo
providers.description: Edmodo was an education technology company that operated a K-12 social learning network and learning management platform connecting teachers, students, and parents, and at its peak ran a developer platform and app store for third-party education apps. It was acquired by NetDragon in 2018 and the service was shut down in September 2022. Surfaced as a portfolio company of union-square-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the edmodo.com domain resolves only to a parked lander page and exposes no live developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: eduFire
providers.description: eduFire was an online education startup surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-19 found that the company's primary domain, edufire.com, no longer resolves (no DNS A or NS records), indicating the company is defunct. No live developer portal, API surface, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or any other artifact could be located to enrich, so this profile remains an identity-only stub.

providers.name: Edukart
providers.description: EduKart was an Indian online education startup, backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), that sold certificate, diploma and degree courses from partner universities and training institutes to Indian learners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company is now defunct — repeated probes of edukart.com find a parked hosting placeholder rather than a live business, and no developer, API, documentation or SDK surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: ElasticBox
providers.description: ElasticBox was a multi-cloud application management and deployment platform founded in 2011 by former Microsoft engineers Alberto Arias Maestro, Amadeo Casas, and Ravi Srivatsav (AngelPad-backed, offices in San Francisco and Madrid). Its "boxes" model let enterprise IT define, version, and orchestrate application deployments across more than a dozen clouds — AWS, Microsoft Azure, IBM SoftLayer, VMware, vCloud Air and others — with a self-service catalog, a REST API (token-authenticated, JSON), and a Jenkins CI plug-in. The company raised roughly $12.4M across three rounds, including a $9M Series A in 2014 with participation from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Nexus Venture Partners, Intel Capital and Sierra Ventures. CenturyLink acquired ElasticBox in June 2016 and rebuilt the technology as CenturyLink Cloud Application Manager (now part of Lumen). The standalone ElasticBox product, its developer portal, and its public API documentation have been retired; the elasticbox.com domain no longer serves the platform. This profile is preserved as a historical portfolio-lead record — no live, first-party API surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: element 5 AG
providers.description: element 5 AG was a German e-commerce and digital-distribution company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Cologne, Germany. It operated a platform that let software developers and publishers sell their products and licenses directly to customers online, growing to more than 10,000 clients across 150 countries and becoming one of Europe's leading software e-commerce providers. element 5 was acquired by U.S.-based Digital River (its direct competitor) for roughly $120M and subsequently absorbed and renamed Digital River GmbH, ceasing to operate as an independent company. It was an early Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company; this profile records its identity and exit. No live independent API or developer surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: elo7
providers.description: Elo7 was a Brazilian online marketplace for handmade, customized, and creative products — frequently described as "the Etsy of Brazil." Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Sao Paulo, it connected independent artisans and small makers with buyers across Brazil for party supplies, decor, crafts, and personalized goods. Etsy acquired Elo7 in July 2021 for roughly USD 217 million, then sold it to Brazilian firm Enjoei S.A. in July 2023, after which the marketplace was wound down and stopped accepting new orders. Elo7 published no public developer API or OpenAPI; its GitHub organization holds only small internal frontend (AMD) utility libraries. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and is enriched here with the real, honest surface that remains.

providers.name: Embark Trucks
providers.description: Embark Trucks was an autonomous-trucking company founded in 2016 and backed by Y Combinator, building a self-driving software stack (the Embark Driver) for Class 8 semi-trucks operating on interstate highway freight lanes. The company went public via a SPAC merger with Northern Star Investment Corp II in late 2021, but wound down operations in November 2023 after failing to secure additional funding; its autonomous-driving technology and engineering assets were subsequently acquired by Applied Intuition. Embark never operated a public developer platform, REST API, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile is an identity record rather than a live API. Its only surviving public technical surface is the embarktrucks GitHub organization, which hosts open-source robotics and autonomous-vehicle tooling (ROS drivers, LIDAR/camera integrations, and the webviz visualization libraries) rather than first-party API client SDKs.

providers.name: Emergent VR *
providers.description: Emergent VR was a San Francisco Bay Area virtual-reality startup backed by GV (Google Ventures), where it is listed in the portfolio with the asterisk GV uses to mark exited companies. The enrichment pass found no live company web presence: the former emergentvr.com domain now resolves to an unrelated third-party blog, and the company's GitHub organization (github.com/EmergentVR, created March 2015) holds only ten repositories, all of them OpenCV builds and a fork of Google's cardboard-unity SDK, with no activity after June 2016. No developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or event surface exists for this company, so no API artifacts were produced. Sector: consumer / virtual reality.

providers.name: Enbala
providers.description: Enbala Power Networks was a distributed-energy-resource (DER) and grid-flexibility software company (Concerto DER management platform). It was surfaced as an obvious-ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass the company has no live public developer or API presence. enbala.com serves an expired TLS certificate and 301-redirects to www.generacgs.com (Generac Grid Services), which no longer resolves in DNS. No OpenAPI, docs host, developer portal, SDK, MCP server, or webhook surface could be located. Treat this profile as a defunct/acquired lead rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Enevate
providers.description: Enevate Corporation was an Irvine, California battery technology company that developed and licensed silicon-dominant lithium-ion anode and cell technology — marketed as HD-Energy and XFC-Energy — aimed at extreme fast charging (roughly five minutes to a substantial state of charge), high energy density, and cold-weather performance for electric vehicles, with a licensing rather than cell-manufacturing business model. It was a materials and cell-chemistry licensor, not a software vendor, and it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or webhook surface. As of an August 2026 probe the company's own domain no longer serves a company website: enevate.com redirects to a "Website Temporarily Unavailable" domain notice stating the prior Enevate Corporation website has been retired and the domain is now under new ownership following an asset acquisition process, and that all previously published statements about products, services, partnerships and company operations should no longer be considered current. This profile is retained as a recorded absence with the probe evidence attached.

providers.name: Engine ML
providers.description: Engine ML was a machine-learning infrastructure startup (founded 2018, backed by Kleiner Perkins) that offered a hosted platform for distributed model training and experiment tracking. Its product surface centered on the `engine` command-line tool and the `eml` Python library, which let data scientists launch experiments, track code, system utilization, logs, and output files, and run image classifiers (PyTorch/TensorFlow/Keras) against datasets such as MNIST. The company appears to be defunct: engineml.com serves an empty page behind an expired TLS certificate (expired March 2023), the documentation site docs.engineml.com returns an empty S3 bucket, and the public GitHub organization (EngineML) has not been updated since 2020-2021. No live API, OpenAPI description, package-registry release, or reachable developer docs could be found. This profile preserves the historical identity and the still- live GitHub organization as the only verifiable surviving surface.

providers.name: Enjoy Technologies
providers.description: Enjoy Technology (Enjoy Technologies) was a "commerce at home" mobile-retail startup founded in 2014 by Ron Johnson, the former Apple senior vice president of retail and JCPenney CEO, and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company brought the retail store experience to customers' homes, dispatching mobile experts to deliver, set up, and demonstrate consumer electronics on behalf of partners such as carriers and device makers. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Oak Investment Partners, and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Enjoy went public via SPAC in 2021 and declared bankruptcy in 2022, with its assets subsequently acquired. Enjoy never operated a public developer program or API; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: EnvoyWorldWide
providers.description: EnvoyWorldWide (Envoy WorldWide, Inc.) was a Massachusetts-based automated notification and interactive multi-channel messaging company, backed by Battery Ventures, that sold hosted alerting and customer-communication services. The company rebranded as Varolii Corporation in the mid-2000s, and the envoyworldwide.com property was retired. As of this enrichment pass the domain has no A record and its most recent archived captures show a parked "Under Construction" placeholder rather than a company site. No developer portal, documentation, API reference, SDK, package, or GitHub organization could be located on any public surface. This profile is retained as a historical network entry with no active API surface.

providers.name: Eo Computer
providers.description: Eo Computer (EO, Inc.) was an early-1990s hardtech company, backed by Kleiner Perkins, that built the EO Personal Communicator - a pen-based tablet computer running GO Corporation's PenPoint operating system. AT&T became the principal backer and later shut the company down in 1994. The company is defunct: it has no website, developer program, public API, SDKs, or any published developer surface, so there is nothing for the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline to search, generate, or derive. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record of a dead, non-API hardware company.

providers.name: EP Energy
providers.description: EP Energy Corporation was an independent exploration and production company engaged in the acquisition and development of unconventional onshore oil and natural gas properties in the United States, principally in the Eagle Ford shale and the Uinta basin. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2019 and emerged in October 2020. Verdun Oil Company II LLC, an EnCap Investments portfolio company, completed its acquisition of EP Energy on 30 March 2022 for approximately $1.45 billion, with the Utah/Uinta assets divested post-closing under an FTC order. EP Energy is no longer an operating company. It never published an API, SDK, or developer program, and its corporate domain epenergy.com now redirects to the acquirer, verdunoilco.com. The unrelated hyphenated domain ep-energy.com is a GoDaddy aftermarket listing offered for sale and is not an EP Energy surface.

providers.name: Epsagon
providers.description: Epsagon was an observability and application performance monitoring (APM) company, founded in 2017, that provided automated distributed tracing for serverless and containerized applications — AWS Lambda, Node.js, Python, Go, .NET, Ruby, and Java — correlating traces, metrics, and logs to help teams identify and fix problems fast without manual instrumentation. Epsagon was acquired by Cisco in 2021 and folded into Cisco's observability portfolio, after which the product was sunset. The epsagon.com developer surface (docs, dashboard, and API subdomains) no longer resolves. Its surviving public footprint is the github.com/epsagon organization and the first-party instrumentation SDKs still hosted on npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Go modules, NuGet, and Maven Central. This profile captures that remaining, verifiable footprint.

providers.name: EQRx
providers.description: EQRx was a biopharmaceutical company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2020 by Alexis Borisy with a mission to develop and deliver innovative, patent-protected medicines at radically lower prices. The company went public in 2021 through a SPAC merger with CM Life Sciences III and built an oncology and immunology pipeline anchored by in-licensed candidates such as aumolertinib and sugemalimab. In 2023 EQRx wound down its drug-development programs and was acquired by Revolution Medicines in an all-stock transaction. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by a16z and GV); it never operated a public developer platform or API, and its web presence is no longer live.

providers.name: Equipe Communications
providers.description: Équipe Communications Corporation was an Acton, Massachusetts telecommunications equipment startup established in 1999 by a group of telecom industry veterans. It designed, manufactured, and sold data network switching equipment for large-scale facilities-based carriers and service providers — Incumbent Local Exchange Carriers (ILECs), Inter Exchange Carriers (IXCs), and international carriers. Its product line comprised the Équipe 3200 Multiservice ATM/MPLS Core Data Switch, Évail System Software, ÉvailNet Manager, and Élite LifeCycle service and support. The positioning was to let carriers scale an existing ATM core network while offering a gradual, low-risk transition path to MPLS. The company raised a $40 million third round in March 2002, was awarded the first of 74 patents in February 2002, earned ISO 9001:2000 certification from TÜV Management Service in February 2002, signed a sales agent/reseller agreement with Ciena in June 2002 and a services master agreement with Fujitsu in August 2002, and achieved NEBS certification for the É3200 in January 2003. Équipe was a carrier-hardware vendor of the pre-API era: it never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface. This profile is retained as a historical record of the Battery Ventures portfolio and is not an active API provider. NOTE: unrelated to equipe.com, a Swedish equestrian show-management software company (see x-disambiguation).

providers.name: Escher Reality
providers.description: Escher Reality was an augmented reality and computer vision startup founded in 2016 by Ross Finman (CEO) and Diana Hu (CTO), with roots in the MIT Sandbox program. It built cloud backend services for cross-platform, persistent, multi-user mobile AR — shared experiences that neither Apple ARKit nor Google ARCore offered at the time — letting multiple users interact with the same virtual objects anchored to the real world. The company raised roughly $3 million and was based in Sunnyvale, California. In February 2018 Escher Reality was acquired by Niantic (creator of Pokemon GO); its team and technology were folded into the Niantic Real World Platform (now Lightship), and the standalone company and its developer/SDK offering were discontinued. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record; there is no independent, active API or developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Estamp
providers.description: E-Stamp Corporation (eStamp) was a dot-com era Internet-postage company, a Canaan Partners seed-stage portfolio company that competed with Stamps.com to let users buy and print official U.S. Postal Service postage online. The company is defunct: on April 30, 2001 Stamps.com acquired E-Stamp's name, 31 Internet-postage patents, and the estamp.com domain, which today 301-redirects to stamps.com. There is no live company, product, developer portal, or API surface to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Evariant
providers.description: Evariant was a healthcare customer relationship management (CRM) software company founded in 2008, offering a Salesforce-aligned platform for health systems covering consumer/patient engagement, physician relationship management, marketing planning, appointment reminders, and service-line growth analytics. Evariant was acquired by Healthgrades in January 2020 and fully absorbed into "Evariant, a Healthgrades company"; the independent product and brand were retired. As of this enrichment pass the former evariant.com domain 301-redirects to a parked GoDaddy marketplace page, and Evariant publishes no independent public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Eve Com
providers.description: Eve.com was a dot-com era e-commerce retailer of prestige beauty and personal care products, founded in 1998 by Mariam Naficy and Varsha Rao. It raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners (1999) and reached a Series B before being acquired by Idealab in 2000, after which the business ceased independent operations. It is retained in the API Evangelist network only as a historical Lightspeed portfolio lead; it published no developer program, API, SDKs, or documentation. The eve.com domain is today operated by an unrelated entity (CCP Games / the EVE Online game universe) and is not a surface for this company, so no live API or developer artifacts can be harvested for it.

providers.name: Evelo Biosciences *
providers.description: Evelo Biosciences was a Flagship Pioneering-founded, GV-backed microbiome biotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing orally delivered investigational medicines acting on the small intestinal axis. Following clinical failures of its lead candidates EDP1815 and EDP2939, the company announced dissolution in November 2023 and has been wound down. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a dissolved life-sciences portfolio record: the evelobio.com domain now serves only a parked catch-all error page and the company publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind.

providers.name: Eventtus
providers.description: Eventtus was a Cairo, Egypt-based event technology company that built a mobile event app and attendee-engagement platform for conferences, trade shows, and community events. Its product offered event apps with agendas, networking and matchmaking, live Q&A and polls, push notifications, social feeds, lead capture, badge printing, online registration, and organizer analytics. Founded by Mai Medhat and Nihal Fares, Eventtus raised venture funding from investors including 500 Startups (500 Global), Vodafone Ventures, and Endure Capital, and was acquired by the community-events platform Bevy in July 2021. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no live public API, developer portal, or first-party SDK — the eventtus.com domain no longer resolves and the engineering blog is offline — so the profile is retained as identity only.

providers.name: Everclear
providers.description: Everclear (previously Connext) was a crosschain clearing layer for the intent economy. It netted bidirectional rebalancing flows between solvers, fillers and bridges across chains so that liquidity moved once instead of many times, cutting rebalancing cost by up to 10x. Rebalancers deposited into a Spoke contract on any supported chain and named the destination chains they wanted funds on; a Hub contract on the Everclear clearing chain netted those intents against opposing flow, and any intent that could not be netted became a discounted invoice that arbitrageurs could purchase — a dutch-auction style mechanism that kept the system solvent without a central operator. Everclear shipped a public, unauthenticated REST API ("Chimera API") that read indexed intents, invoices, supported assets, route quotes and settlement history, and that built unsigned EVM, Solana and Tron transactions for callers to sign with their own wallet. On 2026-05-21 the team announced the protocol, the Everclear Foundation and the labs unit had all been wound down; the protocol is sunset, the API host no longer answers, and this profile is an archival record of the developer surface Everclear published.

providers.name: Everdream
providers.description: Everdream Corporation was an on-demand desktop and IT asset management SaaS provider founded in 1998 and headquartered in Fremont, California. It offered hosted remote management, monitoring, and security services that gave organizations visibility into their hardware and software assets over the internet. Backed by Canaan Partners and other venture investors, Everdream was acquired by Dell in December 2007 and folded into Dell's managed-services offerings. The company is defunct; the everdream.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, and there is no active public API, developer portal, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: everyme
providers.description: everyme was surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating company surface: everyme.com no longer resolves to a company website but redirects to a GoDaddy aftermarket listing offering the domain for sale, its nameservers are Afternic (a domain broker), and its DNS publishes a null MX record and an SPF policy of "v=spf1 -all" indicating the domain sends no mail. There is no developer portal, documentation, API, or event surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical lead record rather than an active provider.

providers.name: Excite@Home
providers.description: Excite@Home (At Home Corporation) was a broadband cable-internet provider and web-portal company formed when the @Home Network merged with the Excite web portal in 1999. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, it delivered high-speed residential internet over cable partners and operated the Excite consumer portal, before filing for bankruptcy and ceasing operations in 2001. It is a defunct pre-API-era consumer company surfaced from a venture portfolio; it publishes no developer platform, OpenAPI, or live API surface, so this profile remains an identity-only stub with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Exelis
providers.description: Exelis Inc. was an American global aerospace, defense, information, and services company that produced communications systems, electronic warfare products, geospatial systems, integrated structures, and night vision equipment. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, Exelis was acquired by Harris Corporation in 2015. Harris and L3 Technologies then merged in 2019 to form L3Harris Technologies. No public APIs are published under the Exelis brand; developer resources, if any, are tracked under L3Harris.

providers.name: Eyeview
providers.description: Eyeview (Eyeview Digital) was a New York-based personalized and programmatic video advertising technology company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - its primary domain (eyeviewdigital.com) is registered on AWS nameservers but serves no website (no DNS A record) and no email (no MX record), and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or public GitHub spec surface could be located. No API artifacts could be harvested; this remains a defunct-company stub.

providers.name: Fakespot
providers.description: Fakespot was an AI-powered fake-review detection service, founded in 2016, that graded the trustworthiness of product reviews on Amazon and other online marketplaces through a browser extension, mobile apps, and website. Mozilla acquired Fakespot in 2023 and integrated its technology into Firefox as the Review Checker. Mozilla discontinued the product in 2025 — the Firefox Review Checker on June 10, 2025 and the Fakespot browser extension, mobile apps, and website on July 1, 2025 — and fakespot.com now redirects to a Mozilla announcement. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface exists; this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.

providers.name: Famebit
providers.description: Famebit was an influencer-marketing marketplace, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Los Angeles, that connected YouTube, Instagram, and Vine creators with brands for sponsored branded-content campaigns. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), it was acquired by Google in October 2016, rebranded as "FameBit by YouTube," and later folded into YouTube BrandConnect. The standalone platform has been shut down and famebit.com now redirects to a Google/YouTube Help support page, so there is no live public API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: FamilyLeaf
providers.description: FamilyLeaf was a private social network for families, launched in 2012 and marketed as "a place to share your life with your family" — a closed, invite-based space for sharing photos and updates among relatives rather than a public feed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-20 found no operating company: familyleaf.com is registered (GoDaddy, registry expiry 2027-03-09) but delegated to no nameservers at all, so it has no A record, no mail, no website and no API surface. The last live archived snapshot of the product (2014) carries a banner announcing that FamilyLeaf had become part of Origami; by the 2023 archived snapshot the domain was serving a registrar parking page. There is no developer portal, documentation, SDK, GitHub organization, or any other API artifact to capture. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Fanbread
providers.description: Fanbread is a defunct venture-backed company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Its primary domain fanbread.com no longer resolves to a live site — the HTTPS handshake fails and HTTP returns 410 Gone from a parking host — and no website, developer portal, documentation, API reference, or machine-readable API surface remains anywhere. The company's GitHub organization survives under the login FanBread but is now titled "Wild Sky Media FnB" and points at wildskymedia.com; its seven public repositories are forks and small front-end utilities with no first-party API artifacts and no activity since April 2020. This profile is retained as a historical record and a dead-domain marker, not as an active API provider.

providers.name: Fanbridge
providers.description: FanBridge was an email and SMS marketing platform for musicians, artists, bands, and creators, letting them grow and message their fan mailing lists, run newsletters, and capture subscribers from shows and social channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-19) confirmed FanBridge is defunct - it was acquired by Kit (formerly ConvertKit) and ceased operations on April 11, 2022, with active accounts migrated to the Kit platform. The domain fanbridge.com now 302-redirects to kit.com/fanbridge. There is no standalone FanBridge developer API, documentation, SDK, or event surface; the developer docs linked from the destination site belong to Kit, not FanBridge.

providers.name: Fanhouse
providers.description: Fanhouse was a creator-subscription social platform, backed by a16z, that let fans pay creators directly for exclusive posts, photos, and community access rather than through ad-driven feeds. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The original product operated at fanhouse.app, which no longer resolves to the company (it now redirects to an unrelated domain), indicating the a16z-backed platform is defunct. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API surface could be located for the original Fanhouse product, so no scored API artifacts could be produced without fabrication. This profile is retained as a company/lead record.

providers.name: Fanimal
providers.description: Fanimal was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Re-verified on 2026-07-20, the primary domain fanimal.com remains a parked, Cloudflare-fronted redirect — every path probed (root, /llms.txt, /.well-known/security.txt, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /.well-known/api-catalog, and the api./developer./docs. subdomains) returns HTTP 301 to https://tickpick.com/?fanimal=y. The ?fanimal=y attribution marker on a redirect into a ticket-resale marketplace indicates the property is defunct or has been absorbed by TickPick. No package was found on npm, PyPI, RubyGems, or crates.io; the github.com/Fanimal organization exists but is empty (0 public repos, no profile metadata) and cannot be verified as the same company. No independent Fanimal API, developer portal, OpenAPI spec, MCP server, or reachable /.well-known/ surface exists to enrich; there is no spec-bearing developer surface to ground any artifact against. The registered domain is still administered (live TLS, HSTS, SES SPF, Google and Klaviyo site-verification TXT records), which is captured in the probed domain-security artifact.

providers.name: Faraday Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Faraday Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was a Seattle, Washington clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 as a spinout of Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, built on the elemental-reducing-agent research of Dr. Mark Roth. It developed therapies intended to prevent and treat cardiac and skeletal muscle loss after acute critical illness, led by FDY-5301 — a proprietary intravenous formulation of sodium iodide designed to neutralize reactive oxygen species and limit reperfusion injury in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The company raised roughly $120M from an investor group led by ARCH Venture Partners and Polaris Partners. Its Phase 3 trial read out in late 2025 and failed to meet its primary or secondary endpoints, and Faraday announced in February 2026 that it had ceased operations and was winding down the business. Faraday never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and its faradaypharma.com website is no longer served. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Farmeron
providers.description: Farmeron was a dairy herd-management and farm-analytics SaaS founded in 2011 in Osijek, Croatia, that helped dairy producers track animals, feed, milk production, and farm operations through a web platform and data integrations. The company went through the 500 Startups accelerator and was acquired by the machine-vision agriculture firm Cainthus in 2016, after which the standalone Farmeron product was wound down. This network profile is retained as a historical/portfolio lead; the farmeron.com domain is registered but no longer serves a live website or API, so there is no public developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fashion, Inc. (Fab.com)
providers.description: Fashion, Inc. was the legal entity behind Fab.com, the design-focused e-commerce and flash-sale marketplace founded in 2010 by Jason Goldberg and Bradford Shellhammer after pivoting from the Fabulis social network. Fab raised roughly $150M across rounds led by Menlo Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and Atomico, listed Battery Ventures among its backers, and passed ten million members by December 2012 before layoffs and a collapse in growth. PCH International acquired Fab's digital assets in March 2015; the site was later repositioned around health and fitness goods and went offline in December 2022. The company is defunct and operated no public developer program or API. The fab.com domain is today registered to Epic Games, Inc. and serves Epic's unrelated Fab digital-asset marketplace, so nothing currently published at that host belongs to this company.

providers.name: Fashionara
providers.description: Fashionara was an Indian premium online fashion retailer that launched in 2012 as a curated "e-fashion mall" selling ladies, men's and kids apparel, footwear and lifestyle goods. It ran a flash-sale "events" model on a Magento storefront, carried more than 200 international labels alongside Indian brands including Kenneth Cole, Calvin Klein, Fossil, Adidas, Benetton, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Clarks and Arrow, and operated a quirky in-house sub-brand called F.lea Bazaar. It offered free shipping over Rs. 799, free returns, next-day delivery in eight Indian cities, a style-advisor booking service and an Android app (com.fnara.main). The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Fashionara never published a public API, developer portal, SDK or OpenAPI definition — a scan of more than 8,000 archived fashionara.com URLs found no /api, /developer, /docs, /swagger, /oauth or /graphql paths, and no api/developer subdomain was ever archived. The storefront went dark in mid-2016 and the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fauna
providers.description: Fauna, Inc. built a distributed document-relational database delivered as a cloud API, combining the relational query power of SQL with the flexibility of documents, global serverless distribution and strictly serializable ACID transactions over plain HTTPS. Fauna announced End-of-Service in March 2025 and shut the hosted service down on 2025-05-30; as of 2026-09-17 every Fauna service host returns NXDOMAIN and the apex domain forwards to an unrelated company. This profile is maintained as an archival record of the API surface as it stood at shutdown.

providers.name: FaxSav
providers.description: FaxSav Incorporated was an Edison, New Jersey internet-fax company that designed, developed and marketed store-and-forward and real-time fax transmission services over a hybrid telephony and Internet network, letting customers bypass international long-distance rates. Its products included the faxLauncher Windows desktop client, the faxMailer email-to-fax service built on the company's patented e-mail security technology, and Serverlink, a partner integration that let third-party fax software and application developers route documents through the FaxSav Network. FaxSav went public in 1996, renamed itself NetMoves Corporation in February 1999, and was acquired by Mail.com, Inc. in early 2000; Mail.com became EasyLink Services Corporation in 2001 and the business was acquired by OpenText in 2012. The company is defunct and operates no API, developer program, or public developer portal today. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: Fei Protocol
providers.description: Fei Protocol was an Ethereum-based decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol that launched in April 2021, introducing FEI, an algorithmic stablecoin backed by Protocol Controlled Value (PCV), alongside the TRIBE governance token. Founded by Joey Santoro, it merged with Rari Capital in December 2021 to form the Tribe DAO. Following the April 2022 Rari Fuse exploit, the Tribe DAO voted to wind down and dissolve the protocol later that year. Fei Protocol was backed by a16z (Andreessen Horowitz), Framework Ventures, and other investors. Its smart-contract code and documentation remain public on GitHub, but the protocol is no longer operational and its web properties (fei.money, docs.fei.money) are offline. Fei Protocol is an on-chain smart-contract system and exposes no public REST/HTTP API, so it carries no OpenAPI, SDK, or hosted API artifacts.

providers.name: ffrree
providers.description: ffrree (GitHub organization "Free") was an early-stage, Slow Ventures-backed mobile software company active around 2015-2016. Its only public engineering footprint is a GitHub organization of eight repositories - seven of them forks of third-party iOS and backend libraries (AFNetworking, jot, TheAmazingAudioEngine, protobuf-objc, redis-py, slack) plus an original CocoaPods "Specs" podspec mirror - with all repository activity ceasing in 2016. The company is defunct: ffrree.com now serves a GoDaddy/Afternic domain-for-sale parking lander, and there is no product, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface of any kind. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a verified dead lead rather than deleted, so the slug is not re-researched from scratch.

providers.name: Fidor Bank
