providers.description: Fidor Bank was a German digital challenger bank founded in Munich in 2009 and an early pioneer of Banking-as-a-Service and open banking through its fidorOS / bankOS middleware platform and public REST API, which covered Customers, Accounts, Transfers, Transactions and Account Information over an OAuth2 authorization-code flow. Fidor was acquired by France's Groupe BPCE in 2016; following years of post-acquisition integration struggles the bank ceased business operations in mid-2023 and entered liquidation. Its developer portal (fidor.com) is now a parked domain and the sandbox and production API hosts are offline. The surviving first-party developer artifacts are the archived official Ruby client (RubyGems: fidor_api, by Fidor Solutions AG) and the github.com/fidor organization. This is a retired provider retained for historical reference.

providers.name: FiftyThree
providers.description: FiftyThree, Inc. was a New York City-based technology company that built tools for mobile creativity, best known for Paper (Apple's 2012 iPad App of the Year), the Pencil Bluetooth stylus, and Paste, a collaborative presentation tool. The company raised a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) in 2013 and, in July 2014, shipped the FiftyThree SDK so third-party iOS apps such as Procreate and Noteshelf could integrate the Pencil stylus (pairing, palm rejection, surface pressure). FiftyThree's assets and patents were acquired by WeTransfer on August 21, 2018, and the standalone products and developer surface were subsequently wound down. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no live public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI to enrich.

providers.name: Fimio
providers.description: Fimio was a developer-tooling startup founded in 2022 in Oakland, California by Omoju Miller (formerly of Google and GitHub). Its first product was an ML-trained fraud-detection / malicious-smart-contract reputation API for Web3 builders (Ethereum), with data supported by Spice AI, released as an alpha. The company later repositioned around "collaborative tooling for serverful applications" and "reproducible builds made easy." Fimio appears to be defunct: as of the enrichment probe both fimio.xyz and www.fimio.xyz 302-redirect to google.com, the docs/api subdomains do not resolve, the blog returns 404, and the GitHub organization (fimio-xyz) was archived on 2026-01-27 with only Careers and feedback repositories and no published API artifacts. It was backed by a ~$2.19M seed led by Neo with Redpoint Ventures, Protocol Labs, The House Fund and angel investors.

providers.name: Fincentric
providers.description: Fincentric Corporation was a Canadian core retail and wealth banking software vendor founded in 1984 and headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia. It provided account processing, core banking, and wealth management technology to credit unions and financial institutions, serving roughly 167 clients worldwide and claiming a large share of Canada's top credit unions. Backed by Battery Ventures alongside BancBoston Ventures, HarbourVest Partners, Shasta Ventures, and Ventures West Capital, the company was acquired by US core-banking vendor Open Solutions in May 2007; Open Solutions was itself acquired by Fiserv in 2013. Fincentric no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live developer portal, public API, or documentation surface. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct entry — there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Finisar
providers.description: Finisar Corporation was a manufacturer of optical communications components and subsystems (optical transceivers, semiconductor lasers, and related fiber-optic hardware). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. Finisar was acquired by II-VI Incorporated in 2019, and the combined company was subsequently rebranded as Coherent Corp. The Finisar brand is retired (finisar.com issues a 301 redirect to coherent.com, verified 2026-07-19) and has no independent public developer, API, or documentation surface. No API artifacts are applicable to this stub.

providers.name: Fireglass
providers.description: Fireglass was an Israeli browser-isolation cybersecurity startup, a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners, whose remote-browser-isolation product removed active web content threats by rendering pages in an isolated cloud environment. The company was acquired by Symantec in 2017 and its technology folded into Symantec Web Isolation (now part of Broadcom); it no longer operates as an independent brand. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment probe the fireglass.com domain has been re-registered and now serves Technical Glass Products, an unrelated fire-rated architectural glass manufacturer. No surviving Fireglass developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, MCP server, or /.well-known surface exists to enrich; this stub is retained as a resolved Lightspeed portfolio lead.

providers.name: FitStar
providers.description: FitStar Labs, Inc. was a San Francisco based consumer fitness company that built FitStar Personal Trainer and FitStar Yoga, adaptive video workout apps that adjusted each session to the user's feedback and fitness level. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) and Trinity Ventures, FitStar was acquired by Fitbit on March 5, 2015 for $17.8 million and folded into the Fitbit Coach product line. The company is DEFUNCT: the fitstar.com domain no longer serves web content (last archived live October 2017), the FitStar apps have been retired, and no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface survives. This profile is retained as a historical record in the API Evangelist network; there is nothing to enrich beyond identity and domain posture.

providers.name: Fleetsmith
providers.description: Fleetsmith was a San Francisco-based startup (founded 2016) that provided cloud-based Apple device management (MDM) for IT teams — automated zero-touch setup, patching, app deployment, and security enforcement across Macs, iPhones, iPads, and Apple TVs. Backed by Menlo Ventures and others, Fleetsmith was acquired by Apple in June 2020; Apple subsequently discontinued the standalone product and folded its capabilities into Apple Business Essentials. The company no longer operates an independent developer program or public API, and fleetsmith.com now redirects to Apple Business Essentials. This profile is retained for network history.

providers.name: Fleksy
providers.description: Fleksy (Thingthing Ltd) was a keyboard technology company that built a mobile Keyboard SDK — a white-label, privacy-focused typing engine that iOS and Android developers could embed in their own apps. The SDK provided autocorrect, next-word prediction, swipe/gesture typing, customizable themes, and a plugin system, and the Fleksy keyboard once held Guinness World Records for the fastest typing. Fleksy distributed a native mobile SDK rather than a public web/REST API, so it exposes no OpenAPI, GraphQL, or hosted developer portal. Backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest, the company's public web presence (fleksy.com, docs.fleksy.com, fleksy.dev) no longer resolves and the business appears defunct; this profile captures the surviving public artifact — the first-party FleksySDK CocoaPods pod for iOS.

providers.name: FlightCar
providers.description: FlightCar was a United States peer-to-peer car-rental marketplace built around airport travel, surfaced into the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating company behind the name and no API surface of any kind. The domain flightcar.com is registered but publishes no A, AAAA or MX records, resolves to no host, and sits on Njalla privacy nameservers with a SOA serial dated 2026-07-18; the api, developer and docs subdomains do not resolve; there is no GitHub organisation at github.com/flightcar; and no first-party client library exists on npm or PyPI. The Internet Archive shows the consumer site returning 200 through May 2016 and an Internal Server Error by July 2017, with no successful captures in 2017 or 2018. FlightCar is therefore carried in the network as a defunct company retained for portfolio-graph and historical continuity rather than as an active API provider, and should not be re-queued for artifact enrichment.

providers.name: Flipagram
providers.description: Flipagram is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Flirtey
providers.description: Flirtey was a drone-delivery technology company founded in 2013 by Matthew Sweeny and Tom Bass, backed by Y Combinator. It pioneered autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle delivery, conducting the first FAA-approved drone delivery in the United States in 2016 (Nevada) and running early delivery trials with partners including Domino's (the first pizza delivered by drone, in New Zealand) and 7-Eleven. Flirtey developed the Flirtey Eagle delivery drone and portable landing/loading systems aimed at medical, food, and retail last-mile logistics. The company is now defunct: it did not maintain a public developer program or API, and the flirtey.com domain has since been sold and now redirects to an unrelated business (us-stemcell.com). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Flowdock (Discontinued)
providers.description: CA Flowdock was a team chat and shared team-inbox product originally founded as Flowdock in Helsinki / Tampere, Finland (Nodeta Oy spin-off, ~2010), acquired by CA Technologies in 2013, and operated under Broadcom after Broadcom's 2018 acquisition of CA. The hosted service and all public APIs (REST, Push, Streaming, SCIM) were discontinued on August 15, 2023. Broadcom's sunset notice directed customers to Microsoft Teams or Slack as successor products. This profile is an archival record assembled from the public api-docs repository and archived snapshots of the developer portal.

providers.name: FlowWise Networks
providers.description: FlowWise Networks was a computer-networking hardware company founded in 1996 and headquartered in San Jose, California, that built layer 2, 3, and 4 wire-speed, self-configuring router-acceleration products designed to boost enterprise network performance with minimal disruption of service. Backed by Alta Partners, Battery Ventures, InveStar Capital, Mitsubishi Electric, and TL Ventures (roughly $21M-$27.5M raised), the company was acquired by Network Equipment Technologies (N.E.T.) in January 2000. It is long defunct and operates no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this record is retained for VC portfolio-graph provenance only and is not an enrichable API provider.

providers.name: Fluid Truck
providers.description: Fluid Truck was a Denver, Colorado peer-to-peer commercial vehicle sharing platform founded in 2016 by James Eberhard and Jenifer Snyder, often described as "the Zipcar of commercial vehicles". It operated an app-based, self-service rental marketplace for cargo vans, box trucks and flatbeds across roughly 400 cities in 32 US states, and ran the Fluid Vehicle Investor Program (FVIP) through which individuals and small businesses bought fleets that Fluid managed and rented out. The company raised over $80 million in venture funding, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware in October 2024 after an $20.6 million cash loss in 2023, sold substantially all assets to Kingbee Rentals in December 2024, and the case converted to Chapter 7 liquidation in September 2025. The company is wound down: no developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable contract was ever published, and its own web properties no longer serve a valid TLS certificate.

providers.name: Fluidity
providers.description: Fluidity Money is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol that turns idle crypto into "Fluid Assets" (fAssets) — ERC-20-compatible wrapped tokens on Ethereum/Arbitrum and SPL tokens on Solana that pay instant, probabilistic rewards every time they are transferred (the Transfer Reward Function). Yield is sourced from lending protocols such as Compound and AAVE on Ethereum and Solend on Solana, and distributed through "utility mining." Fluidity exposes a public GraphQL API over its webapp and landing-page data, publishes EVM ABIs and Solana program/account structures for on-chain integration, and is governed by the $FLY token. Fluidity Labs sunsetted active protocol development on 2026-04-01 to focus on the Superposition ecosystem; docs, status page, and on-chain contracts remain live.

providers.name: Flutter
providers.description: Flutter was an early-stage gesture-recognition startup founded in 2010 by Mehul Nariyawala and Navneet Dalal and based in California. Its consumer app used computer-vision hand-gesture recognition over a built-in webcam to control media players such as iTunes, Spotify, VLC, and QuickTime; it launched in 2012, reached number one free app in dozens of countries on the Mac App Store, and was named by Apple among the best free apps of 2012. The company raised early funding from Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and NEA before Google acquired it on October 2, 2013, after which the product was discontinued. It has no active developer program, public API, or maintained developer portal today. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; there is no live provider surface to enrich.

providers.name: Flye
providers.description: Flye was a San Francisco social-audience and brand-marketing analytics startup (500 Global / 500 Startups Demo Day Batch 19, founded 2016) that helped brands build and understand their audiences from social data (an "audience fingerprint") and run targeted, personalized engagement campaigns using machine learning. The company appears defunct — its original domain (flye.co) has lapsed and now hosts an unrelated online-casino review/affiliate site. No developer platform, API, documentation, SDK, or other technical surface exists for this provider, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication.

providers.name: Focal Communications
providers.description: Focal Communications Corporation was a Chicago-based competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) founded in 1996 that provided switched local phone and data services to large, communications-intensive business customers in Tier I US markets. Backed by Battery Ventures, Madison Dearborn and Frontenac, it went public in 1998, filed Chapter 11 in December 2002, emerged from reorganization in July 2003, and was acquired by Corvis Communications (later Broadwing) in 2004. The company is defunct and operates no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this network profile is a historical stub and no live API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Foodspotting
providers.description: Foodspotting is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Foodzie
providers.description: Foodzie was an online marketplace, founded in 2008 and based in San Francisco, that let people discover and buy food directly from small artisan producers, and later ran a monthly tasting-box subscription service. It raised roughly $1M from investors including Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC) and Jeff Clavier, and was acquired by the video-commerce company Joyus in June 2012, becoming "Joyus Food" before the subscription service was wound down. The company is defunct; the foodzie.com domain is no longer operated by the original business, and no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: FORE Systems
providers.description: FORE Systems, Inc. was a computer network switching equipment company based in Warrendale (Pittsburgh), Pennsylvania, founded in 1990 by Carnegie Mellon researchers Francois Bitz, Onat Menzilcioglu, Robert Sansom and Eric Cooper (the "FORE" acronym) to build Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) network interface cards and switches. It was the first company to commercially ship an ATM switch (the ASX-100) in 1992 and grew through acquisitions (ALANTEC, Applied Network Technology, RainbowBridge, CellAccess) before being acquired by Britain's General Electric Company (GEC) in 1999, folded into Marconi, and ultimately absorbed by Ericsson in 2006. The company is defunct and has no active API surface, developer portal, or product endpoints; this profile is a historical/company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Forever Oceans
providers.description: Forever Oceans Corporation was a US offshore aquaculture company, founded in 2014 and headquartered in Virginia, that raised sushi-grade kanpachi (Seriola rivoliana) in deep water off the Pacific coast of Panama using a patented single-point mooring system that let its submerged pens orient with ocean currents. It raised roughly $170M and held a large Brazilian marine-aquaculture concession, with planned farms in Brazil and Indonesia. Its investors brought in restructuring and liquidation specialists in November 2024, and its corporate domain foreveroceans.com is now a registrar parking page that refuses HTTPS. Seafood production, not software, was the product: the company never published an API, developer portal, SDK or any machine-readable contract, and no such surface survives.

providers.name: Forrst
providers.description: Forrst was a community for designers and developers to share work in progress and give and receive detailed feedback, founded in 2009 by Kyle Bragger with seed funding from 500 Startups (500 Global) and other angels. It was acquired by Colourlovers in 2012, then by product-design firm ZURB in January 2013, and was shut down on April 14, 2014. The company is defunct; forrst.com now redirects to zurb.com and there is no active API, developer portal, or public API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Fortigo
providers.description: Fortigo Network Logistics Pvt. Ltd. (4TiGO) was a Bengaluru, India technology-enabled logistics and supply-chain network platform, founded in 2015, operating an online marketplace for freight/truck transportation alongside a Digital Supply Chain Control Tower SaaS. It was backed by Accel and Nandan Nilekani's NRJN Family Trust, raising roughly $23.5M across five rounds. As of this enrichment pass the company appears deadpooled/defunct: its 4tigo.com site is unreachable (connection refused across all hosts) and no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition could be located. No API artifacts were enriched because there is no live developer surface.

providers.name: FounderDating
providers.description: FounderDating was an online network that helped entrepreneurs find co-founders, advisors, and early team members to start companies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-19) confirms FounderDating has been merged into CoFoundersLab: the founderdating.com domain now redirects to cofounderslab.com, a founder-matching and startup-community platform. Neither the legacy FounderDating brand nor the CoFoundersLab successor publishes a public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, developer portal, SDK/package, or any /.well-known discovery surface, so there are no API artifacts to search, generate, or derive. The founderdating.com host is additionally unreachable over HTTPS (connection times out; DNS points at a parked Tucows IP). This profile is retained as a historical company record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Freejit
providers.description: Freejit (styled FREEjit) was an early-stage startup founded around 2010 in Newport Beach, California, that attempted to turn browser autocomplete into a marketable service. It was backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) and other early investors. Per public company registries the business is now closed/defunct, and its domain (freejit.com) no longer resolves. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; enrichment found no live developer surface, API, documentation, SDKs, or specifications to harvest.

providers.name: Freescale Semiconductor
providers.description: Freescale Semiconductor, Inc. was an American semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Austin, Texas, created in 2004 from the spin-off of Motorola's Semiconductor Products Sector. Freescale designed and produced embedded processing hardware — microcontrollers (Kinetis, S08), i.MX applications processors, ColdFire and QorIQ/PowerPC communications processors, digital signal processors, RF, analog, and sensor products — for the automotive, networking, industrial, and consumer markets. In December 2015 Freescale merged with NXP Semiconductors in a roughly $11.8B deal and ceased to exist as an independent company; its freescale.com domain now redirects to nxp.com. Freescale was a hardware/silicon company, not a web-API provider: it published no public REST/HTTP API, developer portal, or OpenAPI, so there is no live API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: FreshDish
providers.description: FreshDish (Fresh Dish, Inc.) was a Santa Monica meal-kit delivery startup founded in 2012 by Steve Goldstein (formerly SVP/GM at Provide Commerce, the ProFlowers and Shari's Berries operator). Incubated by Science Inc. and seeded with $500,000 from Battery Ventures, it shipped ready-to-cook dinner kits with chef-designed recipes and pre-portioned ingredients (two-person kits at $24, family-of-four at $32, free shipping). The company was deadpooled and is no longer operating; the freshdish.com domain now resolves to a parked/for-sale lander. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. FreshDish never operated a developer program, public API, or SDKs, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Freshplum
providers.description: Freshplum was a San Francisco data-science startup (founded 2010) that built cloud-based predictive analytics for e-commerce, gauging online shopper behavior in real time to surface personalized promotional offers and discounts to visitors who might otherwise abandon a purchase. During its private alpha it was already processing over 10M requests a day. Freshplum raised roughly $1.7M from investors including DCVC and GV (Google Ventures) before being acquired by ad-targeting company TellApart in July 2014 (TellApart was in turn acquired by Twitter in 2015). The company is defunct: it ships no live product, developer portal, documentation, or public API, and the freshplum.com domain is now a parked listing offered for sale via Afternic. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Friend.ly
providers.description: Friend.ly was a social question-and-answer service that let people meet and connect by answering fun, get-to-know-you questions, launched around 2010 by a team led by Ed Baker. It raised roughly $5M from Lightspeed Ventures, Balderton Capital, SoftTech VC (now Uncork Capital), and a range of angels, and was acquired by Facebook (now Meta) on October 10, 2011 — primarily an acqui-hire, with the founding team moving to Facebook to work on growth and new products. The consumer service was wound down after the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record for Uncork Capital; the friend.ly domain is now parked and the company operates no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Fritz.ai
providers.description: Fritz.ai was a Boston-based mobile, on-device machine learning platform, backed by Uncork Capital, that gave iOS and Android developers SDKs plus a hosted service for training, deploying, and managing ML models directly on devices. That original developer platform has since wound down, and the fritz.ai domain now hosts an unrelated AI-tools review and ranking content site (guides, glossary, interviews, and tool comparisons) with no public API, SDK, or developer program. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the Uncork Capital portfolio graph and is retained as a historical company record; no live API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Frontier Car group
providers.description: Frontier Car Group (FCG) was a Berlin-based startup, founded in 2016, that built, launched, and operated online and offline used-car marketplaces across high-growth emerging markets including Nigeria, Mexico, Chile, Pakistan, Indonesia, India and Poland, offering vehicle inspections, pricing guides, financing, warranties and insurance. OLX Group (Prosus/Naspers) invested up to $400M at a $700M valuation in 2019 and folded FCG into its OLX Autos brand; the Berlin operations were shut down in 2021 and Prosus later moved to exit the car-classifieds business. As of this enrichment pass the frontiercargroup.com domain no longer resolves (registered and ACTIVE through 2027 but serving no DNS A/NS records), the api.frontiercargroup.com host does not resolve, and the company publishes no developer, API, documentation, or other machine-readable surface. Originally surfaced as a Partech portfolio lead.

providers.name: Frontrow
providers.description: FrontRow was an India-based edtech company that operated an online learning platform teaching extracurricular skills and hobbies — such as music, singing, guitar, drawing, chess and other creative pursuits — to learners through recorded video courses and community-driven classes. The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of the last enrichment pass the product has shut down: its primary domain frontrow.co.in 301-redirects to a Medium shutdown announcement confirming "FrontRow shut down a few months ago," and no developer portal, public API, documentation, or SDK surface exists. This entry is retained as a defunct portfolio-lead record; there are no live API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: FTX Exchange
providers.description: FTX Exchange was a cryptocurrency exchange (ftx.com / ftx.us) that collapsed in November 2022 and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment probe, all FTX web and docs domains (ftx.com, ftx.us, docs.ftx.com, docs.ftx.us) return 301 redirects to the FTX bankruptcy claims portal at claims.ftx.com; the former developer/API surface no longer exists. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a web3 stub. It is DEFUNCT: there is no live exchange, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or API to enrich. The enrichment pipeline verified this and captured only real, probeable domain-security DNS/TLS data.

providers.name: Fuego
providers.description: Fuego, Inc. (maker of FuegoBPM) was an enterprise business process management (BPM) and service-oriented architecture software company founded circa 1999 in Plano, Texas. It was backed by Trinity Ventures among others (Series A, 2004) and was acquired by BEA Systems in March 2006, where FuegoBPM became the basis of BEA AquaLogic BPM; BEA was subsequently acquired by Oracle in 2008 and the technology folded into the Oracle BPM product line. Fuego no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: Fulcrum BioEnergy
providers.description: Fulcrum BioEnergy, Inc. was a Pleasanton, California waste-to-fuels project developer founded in 2007 that converted municipal solid waste into synthetic crude oil for refining into sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and diesel, using a shred-and-sort feedstock line feeding a gasifier and a Fischer-Tropsch conversion train. Its first and only commercial plant, the Sierra BioFuels Plant in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center outside Reno, Nevada, was designed to take roughly 175,000-219,000 tons of household garbage a year from an adjacent feedstock processing facility and began production in late 2022. The company raised on the order of a billion dollars in equity, debt and government support over its life, including strategic investments and offtake alliances with United Airlines, Waste Management, Cathay Pacific Airways, Marubeni and bp, plus a US Department of Energy loan guarantee, USDA loan guarantee and Department of Defense grants; E. James Macias led it as president and CEO through its build-out years, and it had announced follow-on projects including a Gary, Indiana plant and the NorthPoint facility in the UK. The Sierra plant stopped operating in mid-May 2024 after persistent equipment problems, the company laid off essentially its entire workforce and took its website down, and on 2024-09-09 Fulcrum BioEnergy, Fulcrum Sierra Holdings and Fulcrum Sierra Finance Co. filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware listing more than $456 million owed to over 200 creditors. A November 2024 auction sold the biorefinery to Switch, Ltd. for $55 million and the adjacent feedstock processing facility to Refuse Inc., a WM subsidiary; the plan of liquidation was confirmed in April 2025 and went effective in May 2025. Fulcrum was an industrial energy project developer rather than a software company and never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification — a Wayback index of its corporate site from 2008 through 2024 turns up no developer, reference, or spec path of any kind. Its corporate host fulcrum-bioenergy.com no longer resolves to any web server, and the alternate registration fulcrumbioenergy.com is parked on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket and listed for sale. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fungible
providers.description: Fungible Inc. was a Santa Clara, California startup founded in 2015 by Pradeep Sindhu (Juniper Networks co-founder) and Bertrand Serlet that built Data Processing Units (DPUs) — programmable microprocessors (the F1 and S1 chips plus the FS1600 NVMe storage array) designed to offload networking, storage, and security workloads from data-center CPUs. Its DPU cluster control plane ran Linux and exposed internal REST APIs for management, but Fungible never published a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK registry. Microsoft acquired the company in January 2023 (reported ~$190M), folded the team into its Azure data-center infrastructure engineering organization, and wound down the independent product line. The fungible.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fusebit
providers.description: Fusebit was a code-first, developer-facing embedded integration platform (embedded iPaaS) founded in Seattle in 2019, letting SaaS teams build, deploy and run third-party integrations inside their own products using serverless functions, managed OAuth connectors and an embeddable browser IDE. The company was acquired and the platform is retired: as of 2026-09-10 the domain fusebit.io is still registered but publishes no DNS A record, so the API, the developer documentation, the management portal and the asset CDN all fail to resolve. What survives is substantial and first-party — two published OpenAPI 3.0 contracts covering 89 operations, four dated release-note streams served from Fusebit's own GitHub Pages, 101 npm packages under the @fusebit and @fusebit-int scopes, and 35 public repositories across the fusebit and fivequarters GitHub organizations. This profile is a historical record of a retired API, not a callable surface.

providers.name: Fusion I/O
providers.description: Fusion-io (branded Fusion I/O) was an enterprise storage company founded in 2005 and based in the Salt Lake City area of Utah, best known for its ioMemory and ioDrive PCIe flash acceleration cards that placed NAND flash directly on the server bus to speed databases and data-center workloads. Steve Wozniak served as chief scientist; the company listed on the NYSE in 2011 and was acquired by SanDisk in 2014, later becoming part of Western Digital. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface today; fusionio.com no longer resolves to a live site. Retained in the network as a defunct a16z portfolio company for record.

providers.name: Futureadvisor
providers.description: FutureAdvisor was a Y Combinator-backed robo-advisor that provided automated, algorithm-driven investment management and portfolio recommendations to retail investors. It was acquired by BlackRock and folded into the firm's digital wealth offerings; the consumer FutureAdvisor product has since been wound down. As of this enrichment pass the domain futureadvisor.com is controlled by BlackRock (its nameservers resolve to blackrock.com) but publishes no live website, developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or any public developer surface. No API artifacts could be searched, fetched, or derived — this remains an identity-only record for a defunct/absorbed provider.

providers.name: Galileo Technology
providers.description: Galileo Technology was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1993 that designed and marketed complex semiconductor devices for high-performance embedded control systems, principally in the area of data communications. Co-founded by Avigdor Willenz (CEO), Manuel Alba (President), and Eyal Waldman (VP Engineering), the company completed an IPO in 2000 and was acquired by Marvell Technology, Inc. in 2001 for approximately $2.7 billion. It was an early Lightspeed Venture Partners investment (1995). The company no longer operates independently and exposes no public developer surface, API, or documentation; this profile is retained for network/portfolio lineage only.

providers.name: gammastar
providers.description: GammaStar (GammaStar Medical Group) is a Shanghai-based medical-device company backed by Qiming Venture Partners that develops, manufactures, and services precision radiotherapy and oncotherapy equipment, including rotary cobalt-60 gamma-ray radiosurgery systems, and operates a network of oncotherapy and psychosurgery centers. It is a medical-hardware manufacturer rather than an API provider; enrichment found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface, and the gammastar.com domain currently resolves to a parked "for sale" listing on Atom.com rather than a corporate site.

providers.name: Gantto
providers.description: Gantto was a web-based Gantt chart and project scheduling SaaS launched in August 2010, backed by Y Combinator and 500 Startups (500 Global). It let teams create and share project schedules in the browser as an alternative to Microsoft Project, with a customer base that reportedly included Twitter, Lucasfilm, and Fujitsu. Gantto was acquired by Dutch competitor Tom's Planner on July 9, 2013, and the product was subsequently discontinued, with users migrated to Tom's Planner. gantto.com now redirects to tomsplanner.com. This company is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record; it publishes no developer program, API, or technical surface to enrich.

providers.name: Garaji
providers.description: Garaji was an online auto-services marketplace based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, founded in 2018, that connected car owners with local workshops for routine maintenance and repairs. Customers selected a service and a vetted garage, and a Garaji valet or tow truck collected the vehicle, delivered it to the workshop, and returned it once work was complete. Garaji was a 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) portfolio company. The company is permanently closed, and its domain garaji.com is now a parked, for-sale listing served via GoDaddy/Afternic with no live product or developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct portfolio-lead record; there are no APIs or developer artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Garuda Therapeutics
providers.description: Garuda Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2021 by Sean Morrison and David Scadden and headquartered in Massachusetts (Cambridge, later Natick), developing off-the-shelf, self-renewing, HLA-compatible, transgene-free hematopoietic (blood) stem cell therapies intended to remove the dependency on a matched donor or on patient cells in the treatment of hematologic malignancies, sickle cell disease, beta-thalassemia and bone marrow failure. It raised roughly $184M across a $72M Series A and a $50M Series A-1 closed in March 2025, backed by OrbiMed Advisors, Northpond Ventures, Cormorant Asset Management and Kyowa Kirin. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it never published an API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification, and its website garudatx.com no longer serves company content and now resolves to a GoDaddy parking lander.

providers.name: GazeHawk
providers.description: GazeHawk was a webcam-based eye-tracking startup founded in December 2009 by Brian Krausz and Joe Gershenson, offering affordable eye-tracking usability and ad-testing services that ran on ordinary consumer webcams instead of expensive dedicated hardware. Backed by Y Combinator (S10) and 500 Startups, the company was acqui-hired by Facebook in March 2012 — Facebook hired the engineering team but explicitly did not acquire the product or technology, and the founders moved on to unrelated backend and product engineering. GazeHawk operated no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; the domain today serves only a legacy static marketing and blog site for the defunct product.

providers.name: Gemvara
providers.description: Gemvara was a Boston-based direct-to-consumer custom fine-jewelry e-commerce retailer, founded in 2006 by Matt Lauzon and Jason Reuben (Babson College), known for made-to-order jewelry customization software that let shoppers configure gemstones and metals on demand. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners among others, it was acquired by Richline Group (a Berkshire Hathaway company) in 2013 and shut down in February 2023. The company published no public developer API, and the gemvara.com domain no longer resolves to a live site. This profile is retained as a defunct-company record.

providers.name: General Galactic Corporation
providers.description: General Galactic Corporation was an early-stage web3 studio founded by Rob Mee (founder of Pivotal Labs) and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It built open-source Ethereum developer tooling published under the generalgalactic GitHub organization, including eip4361-tools for Sign-In With Ethereum (EIP-4361), the ERC721Sequential (ERC721S) gas-optimized NFT contract, an ENS registry (skyteller-ens-registry), and related SIWE authentication utilities. The company wound down its products and experiments in 2023; its site now runs as an ENS/IPFS page announcing the closure. This profile catalogs the remaining public open-source and package footprint. No hosted or public API is currently operated by the company.

providers.name: Gentrace
providers.description: Gentrace was a developer platform for evaluating and testing LLM and AI applications ("evals as infrastructure"). It provided pipelines, datasets, experiments, and test cases so teams could run offline and online evaluations, grade model outputs, track regressions, and observe AI features in production via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation. The platform shipped a REST API (v4) secured with bearer API keys, first-party Python and TypeScript/Node SDKs, and a documented object model of pipelines, datasets, experiments, and test cases. Gentrace was based in San Francisco and backed by Matrix Partners. The company has since shut down its hosted product, but its OpenAPI specification, SDK packages, and documentation mirror remain publicly available.

providers.name: Genuity
providers.description: Genuity Inc. was an internet infrastructure services company spun off from GTE/BBN, which filed for bankruptcy in 2002 and had the majority of its assets acquired by Level 3 Communications. Level 3 was later acquired by CenturyLink in 2017, which rebranded as Lumen Technologies. This repository tracks the legacy Genuity entity and its successor companies.

providers.name: Gestoos
providers.description: Gestoos was a computer-vision company that built a real-time gesture-recognition and touchless-interaction SDK, letting developers add camera-based hand-gesture and motion control to interactive installations, digital signage, kiosks, and embedded devices. Its public developer surface centered on an interactive SDK with sample integrations (including bindings for the Cinder C++ creative-coding framework). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment its primary web presence at gestoos.com is offline — the domain no longer resolves to the company and now redirects to an unrelated parked site — and the only surviving public developer asset is the gestoos GitHub organization, whose most recent activity dates to 2020. This profile is retained as a historical network record; the API/SDK product appears discontinued.

providers.name: Get Satisfaction
providers.description: Get Satisfaction was a customer-community and engagement SaaS platform that gave companies a hosted online community where customers, employees, and prospects could ask questions, report problems, share ideas, and offer praise in public topic threads. Founded in 2007, it popularized the customer-powered support community model and offered widgets, community moderation, and integrations that companies embedded on their websites and product pages. Get Satisfaction was acquired by the social customer experience management company Sprinklr in 2015 and folded into Sprinklr's platform; the standalone product and its developer program have since been discontinued. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record (backed by Uncork Capital); it no longer operates a live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Getaround
providers.description: Getaround was a peer-to-peer and connected car-sharing marketplace (merged with France's Drivy in 2019) that let owners list personal or fleet vehicles fitted with Getaround Connect - a BLE/telematics smart-lock kit - for keyless, app-based rental. Getaround historically ran a documented Owner API and webhook program for fleet-management partners (CarSync, FleetWire, Invers Fleet Hawk) plus a native Connect Blueforce BLE SDK for lock/unlock. OPERATING STATUS (as of 2026-07-03) - the company is winding down - it shut down U.S. operations (including its HyreCar subsidiary) in February 2025, sold its European car-sharing business to Denmark's GoMore ApS effective April 30, 2026, and Getaround Inc.'s board voted June 5, 2026 to pursue formal Delaware dissolution and liquidation (stockholder vote July 29, 2026, no distribution expected). The api.getaround.com API host no longer resolves and its owner API documentation page is now empty, so the API described here is historical/discontinued rather than currently operable.

providers.name: GetGlue
providers.description: GetGlue was a social-entertainment "check-in" network where users checked in to TV shows, movies, sports, music, and books to earn stickers and badges and see what friends were watching. Founded by Alex Iskold and backed by Union Square Ventures, it offered a public API and social graph for entertainment. GetGlue was acquired by i.TV in late 2013, rebranded to tvtag, and the service was discontinued. The getglue.com domain is now a parked lander with no live product, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Getsupp
providers.description: Getsupp was an India-based digital health and wellness platform offering supplement and nutrition product discovery, personalized health recommendations, and online consultations with certified experts (nutritionists, dietitians, and coaches). The company was a General Catalyst portfolio company and was subsequently absorbed into Eka.care. As of this enrichment pass the getsupp.in and getsupp.com domains no longer serve a standalone site: both resolve to Eka.io infrastructure (65.0.57.69, TLS cert altnames *.eka.io) and return HTTP 404 for all paths. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, /.well-known/ discovery, or /llms.txt could be found. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: Gimme Media
providers.description: Gimme Media is the Techstars-backed music company behind Gimme Radio, the heavy-metal streaming and live-DJ radio platform that later expanded into Gimme Metal and Gimme Country. The standalone streaming apps were wound down, and the brand now operates as a Shopify-hosted storefront at gimmemetal.com selling vinyl, merchandise, and exclusive releases to the metal community. As of this enrichment pass Gimme Media publishes no first-party public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation; the only machine-readable surfaces served at its domain are the Shopify Customer Accounts platform OIDC endpoints, which belong to the hosting platform rather than to a Gimme Media API.

providers.name: Gitprime
providers.description: GitPrime was a software engineering analytics and developer-productivity company founded in 2015 in Durango, Colorado, backed by Y Combinator and DCVC. Its product mined data from Git repositories, code review, and ticketing systems to give engineering leaders visibility into team throughput, code churn, and delivery health. Pluralsight acquired GitPrime in 2019 (~$170M) and rebranded it as Pluralsight Flow; in February 2025 Appfire acquired Flow from Pluralsight, and Appfire has announced that Flow will be discontinued on December 31, 2027. The independent gitprime.com domain no longer resolves and www.gitprime.com redirects to appfire.com/flow/info, so there is no standalone GitPrime developer portal, public API, or specification to enrich; any surviving API functionality now lives under the Appfire Flow product. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct company record.

providers.name: Glow
providers.description: Glow (glow.fm) was a podcast subscription and membership monetization platform that let podcasters run paid, listener-supported premium feeds. The standalone product has since been folded into Libsyn: as of this enrichment pass the glow.fm domain issues a 301 redirect to Libsyn's podcast-monetization offering, its TLS certificate has expired, and no active developer portal, API, documentation, or SDK surface remains under the Glow brand. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead (a16z, Norwest Venture Partners, Union Square Ventures) and has no live API to enrich.

providers.name: gohoo
providers.description: gohoo was a boutique e-commerce company based in Hangzhou, China (founded circa 2001) that linked high-quality goods to supplier channels by integrating the factory supply chain to reduce brand premium. It raised a seed round in 2018 and a Series A in March 2019 with backing from Qiming Venture Partners and Bertelsmann Asia Investments. The company is no longer active (deadpooled), and its gohoo.com domain now redirects to an atom.com domain-for-sale landing page. No live company website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists, so there is nothing to enrich beyond this honest identity record.

providers.name: GoInstant
providers.description: GoInstant was a Canadian (Halifax, Nova Scotia) real-time collaboration startup, founded in 2011, that provided a JavaScript API and backend-as-a-service for building multi-user, real-time web applications — shared browsing / co-browsing, live data synchronization, and presence. Developers embedded a hosted client library to add real-time collaboration (shared cursors, forms, and widgets) to a web page without plugins. Salesforce acquired GoInstant on 2012-07-09 (reported at ~$70M) and folded the technology into its platform; the standalone GoInstant developer service and website were subsequently discontinued (gone by late 2014). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record — GoInstant is a defunct provider with no live API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Good & Co.
providers.description: Good & Co. (Good&Co Labs, Inc.) was a Techstars-backed startup that built a research-driven psychometric and culture-fit platform for hiring and employee engagement, using Big Five-based personality assessments to match candidates, teammates, and workplaces via a proprietary FitScore. As of this enrichment pass the original company appears defunct with no live developer or API surface, and the good.co domain now resolves to an unrelated third-party logistics (3PL) fulfillment business.

providers.name: Good Technology
providers.description: Good Technology was an enterprise mobile security company whose Good Dynamics platform provided app-level encryption, data loss prevention, secure inter-app communication, and a secure application-development SDK/API used by ISVs, systems integrators, and enterprises to build secured mobile apps across iOS and Android. The company served more than 6,200 organizations, including over half of the Fortune 100. Good Technology was acquired by BlackBerry in October 2015 for approximately $425 million and folded into BlackBerry's enterprise mobility (UEM) portfolio; it no longer operates as an independent entity and its former developer surface (good.com) now redirects to blackberry.com. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Goodlegal
providers.description: Goodlegal was a Bucharest-based legal-tech startup founded in 2021 by Vasile Tiple (former UiPath Head of Legal Automation) building a legal infrastructure platform and "one-stop shop for legal compliance" — a drag-and-drop document builder, out-of-the-box document templates, an editor with text analysis, e-signature, workflow automation, and integrations aimed at standardizing legal work for individuals and organizations. It raised a ~EUR 1.2M pre-seed round in 2022 led by Earlybird's Digital East Fund. The company wound down and shut off its platform at the end of 2023 (per founder Vasile Tiple's "Final thoughts on Goodlegal" post), and the goodlegal.io domain is now parked / listed for sale. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API surface was ever published, and none exists today. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Google Optimize
providers.description: Google Optimize was a website optimization and A/B testing tool that helped businesses test variations of web pages and personalize experiences. Google Optimize and Optimize 360 were sunset on September 30, 2023. Google recommends migrating to Google Analytics 4 with built-in A/B testing or third-party tools.

providers.name: Grana
providers.description: Grana was a Hong Kong-based direct-to-consumer fashion brand founded in October 2014 by Luke Grana and Pieter-Paul Wittgen, selling premium wardrobe basics made from directly-sourced fabrics — Peruvian pima cotton, Chinese silk, Japanese denim, European linen, cashmere, merino and baby alpaca — online without retail middlemen. It raised roughly US$16M across seed and Series A rounds from investors including Alibaba's Hong Kong Entrepreneurs Fund, 500 Startups (now 500 Global), Golden Gate Ventures, MindWorks Ventures and the Bluebell Group. The company has since wound down; grana.com now resolves to a parked domain with no live storefront, developer program, or public API.

providers.name: Graphicly
providers.description: Graphicly was a digital-comics and e-book distribution and self-publishing platform, founded around 2009 in Austin, Texas, that let independent creators and publishers convert their work and distribute it across major reading platforms including Amazon Kindle, Apple iBooks, Barnes & Noble Nook, and Google Play. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) among other investors, the company was acquired by Blurb in 2014 and its distribution service was subsequently discontinued. The graphicly.com domain no longer serves a live product, and the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph and historical reference; enrichment found no live API, SDK, event, or security surface to harvest.

providers.name: GreenBytes
providers.description: GreenBytes was a data-storage and desktop-virtualization company (patented VDI IO-offload and inline data deduplication) backed by Battery Ventures, and was acquired by Oracle in June 2014. Its product line was absorbed into Oracle and the former green-bytes.com domain now redirects to Oracle Support. The company has no independent, active developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or public API surface, so the enrichment pipeline found no real API artifacts to add. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio-lead stub.

providers.name: Greenfield Online
providers.description: Greenfield Online, Inc. (Nasdaq SRVY) was an independent provider of Internet-based survey solutions and online market-research panels, headquartered in Wilton, Connecticut. Founded in 1994, it pioneered online panel sampling and data collection for the marketing-research industry, went public in 2004, and grew by acquiring sampling firms worldwide (including European comparison-shopping service Ciao). Microsoft acquired the company in 2008 for roughly $486 million to obtain Ciao, then divested the survey and sampling assets to Toluna in 2009. Greenfield Online no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer program, public API, or live web presence today. This record is retained as a portfolio-lead profile surfaced from the Insight Partners portfolio.

providers.name: Greyter
providers.description: Greyter Water Systems Inc. was an Ontario, Canada manufacturer of onsite greywater recycling and water reuse systems, founded in 2012 after acquiring the assets of the defunct Brac Systems. Its flagship Greyter HOME captured water from showers and bathtubs, treated it, and returned clear, odor-free water for toilet flushing, cutting a family home's indoor water consumption by up to 25 percent; it earned NSF/ANSI 350 Class R certification in early 2019 as the first compact residential greywater reuse system to hold that designation. A scaled commercial line served water harvesting and reuse for toilet flushing and cooling towers in multi-unit and institutional buildings, and the systems were installed in more than a dozen countries. The company raised roughly $13M through a Series B. Its only software was an end-user monitoring surface — the mygreyter.com portal and a consumer Greyter mobile app used by owners to watch water savings — and it never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhooks, or any machine-readable specification. Greyter Water Systems Inc. filed for bankruptcy on January 8, 2026, with GlassRatner Restructuring Inc. appointed Trustee and its intellectual property, patents and customer lists placed into an asset sale process. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Gro Intelligence
providers.description: Gro Intelligence was a New York- and Nairobi-based agricultural and climate data company, founded in 2014 by Sara Menker, that built a global food-and-climate intelligence platform on top of satellite imagery, weather models, government statistics and trade data. Its product was a normalized ontology — metrics, items, regions, frequencies, sources and units — over hundreds of trillions of data points, exposed through a read-only REST API and an official Python client used by traders, insurers, lenders and CPG procurement teams to forecast yield, price and climate risk. The company raised an $85M Series B in 2021 and was named to TIME's 100 most influential companies, then ran out of money, laid off 60% of staff in March 2024 and ceased operations that spring; Almanac (formerly Semios) acquired its IP and AI models out of liquidation in November 2024. This profile is a historical record: the API host, developer portal and web application no longer resolve, and the primary domain is a parked registrar lander.

providers.name: Grokstyle
providers.description: GrokStyle was a visual-search / computer-vision startup (a Cornell Tech spinout) that let users find products such as furniture and home decor from a photo, backed by Canaan Partners. It was acquired by Facebook in early 2019 and wound down. As of this enrichment pass its domain (grokstyle.com) is registered but resolves to no nameservers, there is no live website, developer portal, API, SDK, or GitHub organization, so there is no public API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GTR
providers.description: GTR (Global Top Round) was a mobile game accelerator program that annually selected roughly ten indie mobile game studios, providing them global publishing connections, real global game-market and network access, mentorship, and fundraising support through a six-month accelerator program and the Global Top Round global mobile game conference. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of enrichment (July 2026) the company website globaltopround.com no longer resolves (no DNS A/NS records) and GTR appears to be defunct; it exposes no public API, developer platform, documentation, or SDK, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Habeas
providers.description: Habeas was an email reputation and deliverability services provider that helped legitimate senders monitor and manage their sending reputation to maximize inbox deliverability, using a trademark-based accreditation and safelist model to certify permission-based email. Founded in the mid-2000s and backed by Canaan Partners through a Series B round, Habeas was acquired by Return Path in 2008 (habeas.com now redirects to returnpath.com); Return Path was in turn acquired by Validity in 2019. The company is defunct as an independent brand and publishes no live public API or developer surface, so this profile is retained as a Canaan Partners portfolio-history record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Hackpad
providers.description: Hackpad was a web-based real-time collaborative wiki and document editor, built on the open-source Etherpad codebase, that let teams write and edit documents together simultaneously. It was acquired by Dropbox in April 2014 and its underlying platform was released as open source under the Apache 2.0 license at github.com/dropbox/hackpad. The hosted hackpad.com service was wound down after Dropbox folded the team's work into Dropbox Paper, and the public service was discontinued in 2017. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hackpad as a historical, now-defunct portfolio company surfaced from the a16z portfolio; there is no live production API surface remaining, and the durable public artifact is the open-source repository.

providers.name: Hamptons Lane
providers.description: Hamptons Lane is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: hangtime
providers.description: hangtime is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Happs
providers.description: Happs was a live-streaming platform for creators and citizen journalists that let broadcasters produce real-time news and multicast a single live stream simultaneously to Facebook, YouTube, Twitter/X, Twitch and other destinations, with built-in studio tools and viewer monetization through tips and monthly sponsorships. Originally launched as a home for independent journalists, it expanded into a general creator social network and ran its live video on Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS). The company raised roughly $4.7M in a post-seed round led by Bullpen Capital and Crosslink Capital, and wound down operations around 2022. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record; no public developer program, API, or live web surface remains.

providers.name: havekarma
providers.description: havekarma is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Hawaya
providers.description: Hawaya is a Muslim-focused online dating and matrimonial app that began as Harmonica, an Egyptian matchmaking startup backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), and was later acquired by Match Group and rebranded as Hawaya. The service emphasized serious, marriage-minded connections with privacy controls tailored to Muslim singles across the Middle East, North Africa, and international diaspora markets, offered as consumer iOS and Android mobile apps rather than a developer platform. Hawaya was discontinued in 2023 and no longer accepts new registrations; it exposes no public API, SDK, or developer program. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a company record with identity and legal links captured from the provider's own site.

providers.name: hayneedle.com (formerly know as NetShops)
providers.description: Hayneedle (formerly NetShops) was an online retailer of home goods, furniture, and outdoor products, founded as NetShops in Omaha, Nebraska in 2002 and rebranded to Hayneedle.com in 2009. It grew into a large specialty e-commerce operator running hundreds of niche home-and-lifestyle storefronts, and was acquired by Jet.com in 2016 for roughly $90 million, becoming a Walmart subsidiary after Walmart bought Jet.com. The standalone brand was subsequently wound down and hayneedle.com now redirects into walmart.com. It was listed as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no first-party public developer surface (no API docs, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or event surface); the only signal captured is honest DNS/TLS domain-security data for the still-resolving redirect domain.

providers.name: Health IQ
providers.description: Health IQ was a venture-backed insurtech founded in 2013 in Mountain View, California that offered lower-cost life insurance to health-conscious individuals, later pivoting in 2019 to selling Medicare Advantage plans to seniors. Backed by a16z and others (~$200M raised), the company laid off staff in December 2022 and filed for Chapter 7 liquidation on August 30, 2023. As of this enrichment pass the healthiq.com domain resolves to a parked "domain may be for sale" page, and the company operates no public website, developer portal, or API. Retained in the network as a defunct a16z portfolio lead with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: Healthmode
providers.description: HealthMode was a machine-learning digital medicine company, founded in 2017 in San Francisco by Bradford Cross and Dan Karlin, that developed AI-enabled digital measurement methods to increase the precision and speed of clinical research. Its techniques improved phenotype understanding, streamlined screening and eligibility, enabled early detection of adverse events, and provided objective, low-burden efficacy endpoints for next-generation clinical trials. HealthMode was acquired by MindMed in 2021 and folded into MindMed's digital-medicine division (Albert); it no longer operates as an independent company, maintains no standalone website or public developer/API surface, and none of its former domains resolve.

providers.name: Heartland Financial USA
providers.description: Heartland Financial USA, Inc. (HTLF) was a Denver, Colorado bank holding company — formerly headquartered in Dubuque, Iowa — that operated a multi-charter family of community banks across twelve states, including Dubuque Bank and Trust, Illinois Bank & Trust, Wisconsin Bank & Trust, New Mexico Bank & Trust, Arizona Bank & Trust, Rocky Mountain Bank, Citywide Banks, Minnesota Bank & Trust, Premier Valley Bank, First Bank & Trust, Bank of Blue Valley and Signature Bank of Arkansas. Its business was commercial and retail banking, treasury management, and wealth services delivered through branches and third-party core banking platforms rather than through a developer program. HTLF never published a developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind. UMB Financial Corporation completed its all-stock acquisition of HTLF on January 31, 2025 — the largest in UMB's history — and completed the systems and brand conversion of every former HTLF divisional bank in October 2025, at which point the HTLF brand ceased to exist. The htlf.com edge configuration has since been decommissioned. This profile is retained as a historical record; any banking API surface for these institutions now lives with UMB and is tracked separately under the UMB Bank profile.

providers.name: HeartThis
providers.description: HeartThis was a mobile fashion shopping and discovery app, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and GV and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company appears defunct/absorbed: heartthis.com and www.heartthis.com now return a 301 redirect to an OpenSky content page (www.opensky.com/content/general/heartthis), the host serves a long-expired stale wildcard TLS certificate (CN wildcard auctivacommerce.com, expired 2022-12-16), and no api, developer, or docs subdomains resolve (NXDOMAIN). No public developer portal, documentation, or API surface could be found, so no API artifacts could be enriched without fabrication.

providers.name: Height
providers.description: Height is an AI-powered collaborative project management tool that provides a REST API for managing tasks, lists, workspaces, attributes, dependencies, and automation triggers. The API enables developers to programmatically create, read, update, and delete tasks and task lists, manage workspace users and groups, post activity comments, and configure webhook integrations for real-time event notifications. Authentication is handled via secret API keys generated from workspace settings, with OAuth 2.0 available for third-party application integrations. Height announced the shutdown of its service with a final date of September 24, 2025, making this a historical profile of the platform's public developer footprint.

providers.name: HelloFlo
providers.description: HelloFlo was a women's-health startup (a 500 Global / 500 Startups portfolio company) known for its subscription boxes and viral marketing. As of this enrichment pass its helloflo.com domain returns a permanent 301 redirect to theflowspace.com (Flow Space), a women's-health digital media platform owned by Penske Media Corporation. HelloFlo no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any technical / developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct/redirected network lead; there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Heptio
providers.description: Heptio was a Seattle-based cloud-native software company founded in 2016 by Craig McLuckie and Joe Beda, two of the original co-creators of Kubernetes, to help enterprises adopt and operate Kubernetes. It built a suite of widely used open-source Kubernetes tools including Ark (later renamed Velero) for backup and restore, Sonobuoy for conformance testing, Contour as an Envoy-based ingress controller, ksonnet, and Gimbal. Heptio was acquired by VMware in November 2018 and folded into the VMware Tanzu portfolio; the company brand was retired and most of its open-source projects were migrated from the github.com/heptio organization to github.com/vmware-tanzu. This profile is preserved as a historical/defunct-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Heygo
providers.description: Heygo (formerly GoGuides) was a London-based consumer platform for live, interactive virtual tours, where local guides livestreamed real-time walking tours of destinations around the world to remote audiences on a tip-based model. It was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Point Nine. As of this enrichment pass the public site origin is unreachable (HTTP 522 behind Cloudflare) with no mail (MX/SPF/DMARC) records, indicating the service is no longer operating; no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or other machine-readable API surface could be located.

providers.name: Heyzap
providers.description: Heyzap was a mobile-game advertising, discovery, and monetization company. It began as a social game-discovery network and pivoted into a mobile ad mediation platform, offering iOS, Android, Unity, Cordova, and Adobe AIR/ANE SDKs that let game developers serve and mediate ads across networks such as AdMob, AppLovin, Vungle, Chartboost, AdColony, and Facebook Audience Network. Heyzap was acquired by Fyber (RNTS Media) in 2016 and its brand was later folded into Digital Turbine. Heyzap never published a public REST API; its developer surface was the mobile ad-mediation SDKs distributed via GitHub (github.com/Heyzap) and package registries. The heyzap.com domain is now parked/for-sale and the developer documentation site no longer resolves; this profile preserves the historical, first-party SDK artifacts that remain publicly available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: HiCustomer
providers.description: HiCustomer (ハイカスタマー) was a Japanese Customer Success Management (CSM) SaaS built specifically for SaaS companies. Its platform aggregated customer data scattered across BI tools, CRMs, and chat tools to visualize product usage, communication history, revenue, and contract information in one place. Teams used configurable health-score rules to monitor account health across the customer lifecycle, and custom alerts to surface churn and upsell signals at the right moment, with time-series analysis to make customer-success outreach repeatable. The company also offered customer-success consulting, and later pivoted to a digital sales room product, "Arch by HiCustomer". On 2024-09-13 HiCustomer Inc. sold the Arch business to the Tokyo-listed adtech company Geniee, Inc. (TSE 6562), which absorbed it into GENIEE SFA/CRM and rebranded it Geniee DSR. As of this enrichment pass the hicustomer.jp domain no longer resolves to a live site (its authoritative AWS Route 53 zone is delegated but empty) and the product is discontinued; the last archived homepage (Oct 2024) is a STUDIO-built single-page "About the company" placeholder. No public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal was ever published — the Wayback record for hicustomer.jp contains no /api, /docs, /developers, /pricing or /status path at any point in its history.

providers.name: Hike
providers.description: Hike Private Limited is a New Delhi consumer internet company founded in 2011 by Kavin Bharti Mittal. It is best known for Hike Messenger, launched in December 2012 and at its peak one of India's largest homegrown messaging apps, which the company retired in January 2021 to pivot into the Rush Gaming Universe — a mobile-first skill-gaming platform that layered Web3 ownership and play-to-earn mechanics over roughly fourteen casual titles. Hike raised approximately $261M across seven rounds from investors including SoftBank, Tencent, Tiger Global and Polygon, and reached unicorn valuation in 2021. In September 2025, after India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act banned real-money gaming, the founder announced a complete wind-down of the company and of Rush. As of August 2026 hike.in still resolves but serves an HTTP 502 behind an expired certificate, and every developer-facing subdomain is NXDOMAIN; the company publishes no API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: HipChat
providers.description: HipChat was Atlassian's team chat platform, providing persistent group chat, video, file sharing, and an extensive integration ecosystem. Atlassian discontinued HipChat Cloud, Stride, HipChat Server, and HipChat Data Center on February 15, 2019 after selling the IP to Slack in July 2018 and committing to a joint migration path for customers. This profile preserves the historical API surface (REST API v2, Webhooks, Connect add-on framework) for archival and migration-pattern research; no live endpoints remain.

providers.name: Hitwise
providers.description: Hitwise was an online competitive-intelligence and audience-measurement company that tracked website traffic, clickstream behavior, and search-term data to help marketers benchmark share of visits, referral sources, and competitor performance across industry verticals. Originally an Australian firm, it was later owned by Experian and then Connexity. The Hitwise brand has since been retired -- as of this enrichment pass the hitwise.com domain no longer serves a live product (it returns a lapsed-host "Site is not available" page with a mismatched TLS certificate) and exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of insight-partners; enrichment found no active API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Hologix
providers.description: Hologix, Inc. (formerly MBA Technologies, founded 1989) was a Phoenix, Arizona software company that developed Attricom, a business-to-business eCommerce order management solution built for manufacturers with complex, attribute-based product lines in the metals, textile, and paper and forest products industries. Attricom streamlined configuration, quoting, and order management so large-scale producers could offer closer, self-service ordering relationships to their customers. Hologix was venture-backed by Insight Partners, Adams Capital Management, Integral Capital Partners, and Kemper Ventures, and has since ceased operations. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public API, developer portal, or product website is currently reachable.

providers.name: Holor Media
providers.description: Holor Media was an integrated immersive media technology company founded in 2015 and based in Los Angeles and San Francisco. It focused on 360/VR content creation and distribution, building augmented and virtual reality authoring tools aimed at the next generation of social, interactive XR (extended reality) experiences, including interactive 360 apps for the Transformers film franchise. It raised seed funding from 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), Skyline Ventures, and WI Harper Group. The company is now permanently closed and its former domain (holor.com) is a parked, for-sale listing on Afternic, so there is no active developer surface, API, documentation, or SDK to profile. This record is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Home Account
providers.description: Home-Account (Home Account) was a consumer financial-services startup focused on mortgage management and consumer credit-risk analytics, backed by Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC). Per its LinkedIn profile, the company built patent-worthy consumer risk-analytic tooling to help homeowners manage mortgages and understand consumer credit risk, operating in the Consumer Services sector with roughly 11-50 employees and a base in the Fort Mill, South Carolina (ZIP 29708) area. Its original website, home-account.com, no longer resolves, and Uncork Capital's portfolio record associates the company with Bills.com. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API artifacts were found during enrichment; this record remains an identity-only profile of a legacy/defunct portfolio company added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Homeboodle
providers.description: Homeboodle was a San Francisco rental marketplace startup that rebranded as "Lovely" around 2012. The product let renters search, apply for, and pay for apartments online, while giving landlords and property managers tools to list units, screen applicants, and collect rent. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) among other investors, Lovely (livelovely.com) was acquired by RentPath (the owner of Apartment Guide and Rent.com) for roughly $13M in April 2014. The company is now defunct as an independent product; livelovely.com issues a 301 redirect to apartmentguide.com and the former developer/API surface (hub.livelovely.com) is offline. This record is retained for historical and network-graph completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Homeis
providers.description: Homeis was a social networking platform for immigrant and foreign-born communities, founded in January 2017 by Ran Harnevo and Hanan Laschover with offices in New York City and Tel Aviv. The app matched users by country of origin and current city so newcomers could find their community for tips, jobs, dating, events, and local services, serving groups such as Israelis in the U.S., Latinos in Canada, French-speaking Africans in France, and South Asians in the Emirates. It reached more than one million users and raised roughly $16 million, including a $12 million Series A led by Canaan Partners and Spark Capital. The consumer app shut down in Summer 2021 and never reopened; homeis.com is now a parked domain listed for sale. Homeis published no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich for this profile.

providers.name: HomeJoy
providers.description: Homejoy, Inc. was an online home-services marketplace that connected customers with vetted house cleaners and handymen through its website and mobile apps. Founded in 2010 by siblings Adora and Aaron Cheung, the Y Combinator-backed company raised roughly $40M (Google Ventures, Redpoint, First Round, Max Levchin) and expanded to more than 30 cities across the US, UK, Canada, France and Germany. Battered by high customer churn, discount-driven growth and worker-misclassification lawsuits, Homejoy ceased operations on July 31, 2015; much of its product and engineering team was acqui-hired by Google. This is an archival API Evangelist profile of a defunct company: it operates no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, and its former homejoy.com domain now redirects to an unrelated cleaning service.

providers.name: Homigo
