providers.description: Homigo was a Toronto-based home-services startup, founded in 2016, that later rebranded to Setter and operated a concierge platform giving each homeowner a dedicated concierge to manage home maintenance and repairs — plumbing, HVAC, electrical, landscaping, roofing, pools, masonry, appliances, and handyman work — at the touch of a button. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Thumbtack in December 2020. Its website (setter.com) no longer resolves, and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation were ever published, so there is no live provider surface to enrich.

providers.name: Honey
providers.description: Honey was a modern intranet and internal-communications SaaS platform (honey.is) built to connect distributed teams, streamline company-wide communication, drive and quantify employee engagement, and replace outdated intranets. Launched in 2013, it was incubated by the design agency Huge and its parent Interpublic Group in Brooklyn, and raised a $1M seed round from Point Nine Capital in 2015; customers included Capital One, Coca-Cola Hellenic, Lowe's, and Sesame Street. The company is now defunct: the honey.is domain no longer resolves and it publishes no live website, developer portal, API, or documentation. This profile is retained as a Point Nine portfolio lead with no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: HotelUrbano
providers.description: HotelUrbano (later rebranded Hurb) was a Brazilian online travel agency founded in January 2011 by Joao Ricardo Mendes and headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, offering hotel bookings, flights, and flexible travel packages across domestic and international destinations. Once one of Brazil's largest OTAs and backed by investors including Insight Partners and Tiger Global, the company collapsed amid consumer-protection complaints: the Brazilian Ministry of Tourism revoked its Cadastur operating license on 14 April 2025 and the company ceased all operations on 25 October 2025. Its consumer domains (hotelurbano.com.br, hurb.com) no longer resolve and it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI. The only surviving public technical surface is its GitHub organization (hurbcom), which hosts engineering coding challenges and open-source utility forks rather than product APIs. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Houseparty
providers.description: Houseparty was a face-to-face social networking and group video chat mobile app developed by Life on Air, Inc. Launched in 2016, it let up to eight friends video chat together in shared rooms and play built-in games such as Heads Up! and trivia. Epic Games acquired Houseparty in June 2019, and the service was discontinued in October 2021 with its team folded into Epic. Surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company, it is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical consumer-social profile; the product is defunct and publishes no developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: HouseTrip
providers.description: HouseTrip was a London-based online vacation-rental marketplace founded in 2009 by Arnaud Bertrand and Junjun Chen, backed by Accel and Balderton Capital, that grew to roughly 300,000 European holiday properties before being acquired by TripAdvisor in April 2016. The standalone HouseTrip brand and its developer surface (formerly dev.housetrip.com) have since been retired; the housetrip.com domain now serves TripAdvisor's HolidayLettings marketplace. This profile is retained as a historical consumer-sector company record in the API Evangelist network; no live first-party API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published under the HouseTrip brand.

providers.name: Howard
providers.description: Howard was the world's first flex-use real estate platform, co-founded by Michael Jaindl (CEO) and Derek Lee, aiming to bring flexibility to commercial real estate. It was an early-stage (seed) company backed by Bloomberg Beta out of its 2016 fund. The company has since permanently closed and operates no public developer surface, API, documentation, or live host. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio record and is not an active API provider.

providers.name: Huddl
providers.description: Huddl (huddl.ai) was an AI meeting-collaboration platform founded in 2017 in Mountain View, California by CEO Krishna Yarlagadda and CTO Nava Davuluri. The product acted as a collaboration hub layered over Zoom, Webex, and Microsoft Teams, using automatic speech recognition to turn meeting audio into searchable text alongside real-time collaborative note-taking and AI-generated meeting summaries. The company raised roughly $8.7M in venture funding. As of this enrichment pass the huddl.ai domain no longer resolves (delegated to Namecheap parking nameservers with no A/AAAA/MX/TXT records), indicating the service is discontinued; no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or GitHub organization could be located.

providers.name: Humane
providers.description: Humane was a consumer AI hardware startup, founded by former Apple engineers, best known for the AI Pin — a screenless, wearable AI-powered device — and its companion Cosmos operating system and Humane.Center cloud service. The company was acquired by HP in early 2025, the AI Pin was discontinued, and its cloud services and humane.com domain were taken offline. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the company has no reachable web, developer, or API surface.

providers.name: Humanoid
providers.description: Humanoid was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass its associated domain speakertext.com no longer serves a live product. The domain resolves (HTTP 200) but sits on GoDaddy parking infrastructure (IPs 15.197.148.33 / 3.33.130.190, ns65/ns66.domaincontrol.com nameservers) and every path — including /.well-known/* and fabricated paths — returns an identical parking lander that redirects to /lander (wildcard soft-404). No API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or discovery surface could be found. The company appears defunct/inactive; there is no enrichable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Hundeland
providers.description: Hundeland was a German direct-to-consumer online shop for dog supplies — dog food, treats, accessories, and pet-care products — and a portfolio company of the Point Nine venture capital firm. The hundeland.de storefront has been permanently closed ("dauerhaft geschlossen") and now 302-redirects to Pets Premium (petspremium.de), operated by the same company, which carries the same brands and product range; former customers must re-register there. Hundeland publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs, so the enrichment pipeline found no API surface to harvest. This record is retained as a Point Nine portfolio lead with the real closure status captured; the only machine-verifiable artifact is the domain-security probe of the still-resolving hundeland.de host that serves the redirect.

providers.name: Hyperink
providers.description: Hyperink is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: I2 Technologies Inc (THINK SYSTEMS)
providers.description: i2 Technologies Inc was a Dallas-based supply-chain management software company founded in 1988 by Sanjiv Sidhu and Ken Sharma; "THINK SYSTEMS" refers to Think Systems Inc, a supply-chain planning software firm i2 acquired in 1997. i2 Technologies was itself acquired by JDA Software in 2010, which rebranded to Blue Yonder in 2020 and is now owned by Panasonic. This is a defunct/historical entity with no independent, live developer or API surface. The enrichment pass found no attributable API to enrich; the live i2group.com intelligence-analysis APIs belong to a different, unrelated company (a name collision), and the "insight-partners" backing appears to be an erroneous VC-portfolio match.

providers.name: IBEX Process Technology
providers.description: IBEX Process Technology was a semiconductor-industry technology company based in Lowell, Massachusetts, founded around 2000, that developed neural-network-based process control systems for semiconductor fabrication. The company raised roughly $6.8M across two funding rounds and is now defunct (deadpooled), with an Involuntary Revocation status on its Massachusetts registration. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub from battery-ventures data; enrichment finds no live website, no developer/API surface, and no machine-readable specifications to harvest.

providers.name: iBillionaire
providers.description: iBillionaire was a fintech startup (a 500 Global portfolio company) that built a mobile investing app tracking the public equity holdings of billionaire investors, and later launched the iBillionaire Index (ticker IBLN via the Direxion iBillionaire ETF). As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct - the ibillionaire.com domain is parked and listed for sale (307 redirect to forsale.godaddy.com), no docs/api/developer subdomains resolve, and there is no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: icerasemi
providers.description: Icera Semiconductor (icerasemi.com) was a British fabless semiconductor company known for soft-modem and baseband processor chipsets for wireless devices, and was acquired by NVIDIA in 2011. It was surfaced as a portfolio lead of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company no longer operates independently; as of this enrichment pass the domain www.icerasemi.com returns a shared-hosting error page with no live product, developer, API, or documentation surface, so there is nothing beyond domain-level metadata to enrich.

providers.name: Identify Software
providers.description: Identify Software Ltd. was an Israeli enterprise-software company founded in 1996 in Petah Tikva by Yochi Slonim, backed by earlybird (invested 2001). It built application performance management, software-testing, and business-process-automation tooling that helped IT teams reproduce, diagnose, and resolve production application problems, best known for its AppSight problem-resolution suite. It is a legacy portfolio entry rather than an active API provider: the identify.software domain is parked/for-sale, there is no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich, so this profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead only.

providers.name: IEX Cloud
providers.description: IEX Cloud was a cloud-based financial data platform from IEX Group offering market data, fundamentals, news, options, and reference APIs at https://cloud.iexapis.com/v1. The service was sunset on August 31, 2024 by IEX Group. The entry below is preserved as historical reference for migration patterns; endpoints are no longer reachable.

providers.name: Ihaveu
providers.description: Ihaveu (优众网, ihaveu.com) was a Chinese business-to-consumer luxury fashion e-commerce platform founded in 2010 by Sun Tongyu (a former president of Alibaba's Taobao) and Chen Xiao. Based in China, it sold curated high-end designer apparel and accessories from international couture brands such as Prada, Hermes, and Marc Jacobs to Chinese consumers. It raised a Series A of roughly $11M in December 2010 led by IDG Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners, followed by a Series B in 2012 that added The CID Group and JAFCO Asia. The company is no longer active and its ihaveu.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, so it exposes no live website, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record for a defunct Lightspeed portfolio company; it has no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Illustra
providers.description: Illustra Information Technologies was an object-relational database company founded in 1992 by Michael Stonebraker, Gary Morgenthaler and several of Stonebraker's students to commercialize the Postgres research project. Its DataBlade extensibility modules let structured and unstructured multimedia data (text, geospatial, web content) be stored and indexed as true objects. NASA selected it in 1995 to store millions of satellite images. Informix Corporation acquired the company in 1996 and folded the object-relational engine and DataBlades into what became Informix Universal Server; that lineage passed to IBM and is now maintained by HCL Technologies. Illustra no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no standalone website, developer portal, or API. This record was surfaced from a historical Trinity Ventures portfolio list; enrichment found no live API surface.

providers.name: Imara
providers.description: Imara Corporation was a lithium-ion battery technology startup founded in 2006 in Menlo Park, California, that grew out of research at SRI International. It designed and manufactured high-power lithium-ion battery cells and packs based on patented cathode materials science, targeting power tools, outdoor power equipment, hybrid electric vehicles, specialty applications, and power-grid energy storage. Backed by Battery Ventures and Nth Power, it raised roughly $15.65M and reached commercial cell production in 2009 before shutting down around 2010-2011 for lack of manufacturing funding. It is a hardware company with no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface, and is now defunct.

providers.name: iMedeon
providers.description: iMedeon, Inc. was a mobile workforce management software company based in Atlanta, Georgia, providing wireless web applications to optimize scheduling, routing, and the dispatch and management of mobile field workforces (the iM:Work suite). It was acquired by ViryaNet Ltd. in February 2002 (later rolled into Verisae) and no longer operates independently. The domain imedeon.com does not resolve and there is no live website, developer portal, or API surface. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a defunct/legacy company profile; there is nothing to enrich.

providers.name: imgfave
providers.description: imgfave is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Immunicon
providers.description: Immunicon Corporation (NASDAQ IMMC) was a Huntingdon Valley, Pennsylvania biotechnology company that pioneered immunomagnetic cell-selection technology for isolating and characterizing rare circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from blood. It developed the CellSearch and CellTracks diagnostic platforms, licensed to Veridex, LLC (a Johnson & Johnson company) for oncology use. Immunicon filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2008 and was acquired by Veridex/Johnson & Johnson; the CellSearch platform later passed to Menarini Silicon Biosystems. The company was backed by Canaan Partners and publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Immunity Project
providers.description: Immunity Project was a San Francisco nonprofit and Y Combinator company (batch Winter 2014, one of YC's first non-profits alongside Watsi) that set out to develop a free HIV/AIDS vaccine. Its approach studied naturally immune "HIV controllers" and applied machine learning to reverse-engineer the immune response, aiming to deliver a crowdfunded, virus-free vaccine via nasal spray. Founders included Reid Rubsamen, Naveen Jain, and Ian Cinnamon. The organization surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; enrichment found no developer portal, documentation, or API surface, and its former domain (immunityproject.org) has lapsed and now redirects to an unrelated third-party news outlet, indicating the project is effectively defunct.

providers.name: Impala
providers.description: Impala built a single, standardized REST API for the hotel industry — one integration to search availability, read rate plans, and create, amend, and cancel bookings across many property management systems (PMS), so any app could sell hotel rooms and earn commission per booking. Founded in London in 2016 and backed by Speedinvest, Lakestar, and Kima Ventures, Impala shipped a sandbox (with a demo hotel, "The Charleston"), a Postman collection, and PHP/JavaScript wrappers. The company is now defunct: getimpala.com / impala.travel and the API and docs hosts no longer resolve, and the primary domain is held by an unrelated party. This profile preserves the historical OpenAPI (apis.guru impala.travel:hotels 1.003) and pipeline-derived artifacts for the record.

providers.name: In-Fusio
providers.description: In-Fusio was a mobile entertainment company founded in 1998 in Bordeaux (Merignac), France, and one of the pioneers of the mobile games industry. In September 2000 it launched ExEn (Execution Engine), the first Java-based game engine dedicated entirely to mobile devices, competing with Sun Microsystems' J2ME, and partnered with Motorola on a client-side mobile gaming API for faster action and richer graphics. The company published games and community services across more than 70 wireless carriers and 140 handsets worldwide, with distribution deals including Verizon, Sprint, AT&T, Vodafone, Orange, Telefonica Moviles and China Mobile. It split its publishing and distribution divisions in January 2006, was acquired by Zenops in May 2007, entered administration in 2008, and went into compulsory liquidation in 2009. In-Fusio is recorded in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio company of Insight Partners; it operates no active developer platform or public API today.

providers.name: inbilin
providers.description: inbilin was a Shanghai-based social networking mobile app founded in 2013 that let users place voice calls to strangers, either dialing a person of interest or being paired at random for a live conversation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Public company databases (Crunchbase, CB Insights, Tracxn) record inbilin as permanently closed / deadpooled; the inbilin.com domain no longer resolves to a live site and no developer program, documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or public API surface could be located during enrichment.

providers.name: Inbound Health
providers.description: Inbound Health was a Minneapolis, Minnesota company that enabled health systems and health plans to deliver hospital-level and skilled-nursing-level care in patients' homes. It was spun out of Allina Health's own Hospital-at-Home and SNF-at-Home programs in October 2022 with $20 million from Flare Capital Partners, and was led by co-founder and chief executive Dave Kerwar, previously chief product officer at Mount Sinai Health System, with Dr. Chi Huang as chief medical officer and Dave Zimmerman as chief operating officer. The company raised a $30 million Series B in September 2023 led by HealthQuest Capital, and in February 2024 released Inbound InHome, a proprietary patient-management and analytics platform for advanced care in the home: AI/ML-assisted identification and eligibility screening of candidate patients, device-agnostic biometric monitoring across devices, wearables and in-home sensors, a virtual care module carrying real-time video, audio, text and alerting between patient and care team, a workflow application automating logistics across the care episode, supply-chain management, and integration points into multiple EMRs. Inbound Health ceased operations in December 2025 after regulatory uncertainty over the federal Acute Hospital Care at Home (AHCAH) waiver stalled its next financing round; MedArrive acquired its AI-backed care-navigation technology assets in March 2026. Inbound InHome was sold only under signed health-system and health-plan agreements, and no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP manifest or A2A agent card) was ever published on an Inbound Health host. Both inboundhealth.com and www.inboundhealth.com now fail at the origin behind Cloudflare (HTTP 526) and every api/docs/developer/app/portal/status subdomain has been removed from DNS, so there is no live API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: InBrace
providers.description: InBrace was the lingual orthodontics brand of Swift Health Systems, Inc., an Irvine, California medical-device company co-founded in 2012 by orthodontists John Pham and Hongsheng Tong. Its patented INBRACE Smartwires were programmed from digital scans of a patient's teeth and bonded behind the teeth, moving teeth continuously without relying on patient compliance; the product reached market in 2016 and was sold to orthodontic practices through a doctor-facing case-submission portal at portal.inbrace.com rather than through any public developer program. The company raised roughly $70 million in total, including a $45 million Series C led by Vivo Capital with Novo Holdings and venBio Partners in 2019. InBrace ceased operations in April 2025, citing tightening capital markets and slower-than-expected adoption, leaving providers with cases mid-treatment. Its intellectual property, production equipment and manufacturing assets were acquired by orthodontist Dr. Scott Schwartz, who relaunched the technology in August 2025 as InSmile Braces — an independent company operated by Lorelli Technologies and explicitly separate from InBrace. As of this profile inbrace.com and portal.inbrace.com 301-redirect wholesale to insmilebraces.com, so no InBrace-origin content is served from any host. InBrace never published an API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification, and none is served today.

providers.name: Industrial Safety Technologies
providers.description: Industrial Safety Technologies (IST) was a hardware-focused industrial safety platform, founded in 2011 and built by Battery Ventures through acquisitions of gas-detection and hazard-monitoring businesses including Gas Measurement Instruments (GMI), Detcon, DSA Detection, and Simtronics. Its products centered on fixed and portable gas detectors, flame detectors, and hazardous-environment safety instrumentation for industrial sites. IST was acquired by Scott Safety, a Tyco business, from Battery Ventures for $329.5 million in December 2014 and no longer exists as an independent company; the enrichment pipeline found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface to profile.

providers.name: InSparq
providers.description: InSparq is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: InstaEDU
providers.description: InstaEDU was an online, on-demand tutoring platform founded in 2011 in San Francisco that connected students with tutors for live one-on-one help across a range of academic subjects. Backed by Battery Ventures and Social Capital, the company was acquired by Chegg in 2014 and folded into the Chegg Tutors service, which Chegg subsequently wound down in 2021. There is no independent InstaEDU developer program, public API, developer portal, or live domain today (instaedu.com no longer resolves) — this profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: InstaPaisa
providers.description: InstaPaisa was an India-based personal-finance and lending fintech surfaced as a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct or absorbed — its domain instapaisa.com resolves (Amazon CloudFront) but redirects to InCred Finance (incred.com), an Indian digital lending / NBFC platform, indicating an acquisition or wind-down. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification was found for InstaPaisa, so no API artifacts could be harvested or derived; only live domain-security signals for instapaisa.com were probed.

providers.name: Instart Logic
providers.description: Instart Logic was a web application performance and security company founded in 2010 (originally as Zettata) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. It pioneered an endpoint-integrated cloud delivery architecture that paired a cloud service with a client-side JavaScript engine (the Nanovisor) running in the browser to accelerate web and mobile web applications, optimize and stream images (SmartVision), and defend applications with bot management and a web application firewall. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, Tenaya Capital, Greylock, Sutter Hill Ventures and others across roughly $140M+ in venture funding, the company's technology assets were acquired by Akamai Technologies in early 2020, after which the business wound down. No live developer or API surface remains: the instartlogic.com domain resolves to no website host and is served by Akamai nameservers.

providers.name: Intarcia Therapeutics
providers.description: Intarcia Therapeutics, Inc. was a Boston-headquartered clinical-stage biopharmaceutical and drug-delivery company, founded in 1997 and once valued at roughly $5.5B, that developed the Medici Drug Delivery System — a matchstick-sized subdermal osmotic mini-pump engineered to stabilize therapeutic proteins and peptides at body temperature and release them continuously for months from a single placement. Its lead candidate, ITCA 650, delivered the GLP-1 receptor agonist exenatide for type 2 diabetes over three- to six-month intervals. The FDA issued complete response letters on the ITCA 650 new drug application in 2017 and again in 2020, after which the company ran out of capital, laid off staff, closed its Boston, Hayward (CA) and Durham (NC) sites and liquidated its manufacturing and laboratory equipment at auction. Its remaining assets — the Medici platform and ITCA 650 — were acquired by i2o Therapeutics in August 2023, and FDA published a final decision refusing to approve the ITCA 650 application on 2024-08-23. Intarcia was a drug-device developer rather than a software company: its corporate site carried only Medici System, Pipeline, Newsroom, About, Leadership and Careers sections and never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind. As of 2026-08-23 both intarcia.com and intarciatherapeutics.com resolve to an Atom.com domain-broker parking page that offers the names for sale and returns HTTP 404 on every path, and no developer-facing subdomain resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Intellicare
providers.description: IntelliCare, Inc. was a specialty healthcare services and application software company founded in 1997 and headquartered in South Portland, Maine. It provided medical contact center outsourcing services and technology products, delivering telephone-based (telephonic) nurse triage and clinical decision-support services to health plans, providers, payors, self-insured employers, hospitals, and health management organizations. IntelliCare was a portfolio company of Canaan Partners (with Liberty Medical and Cutlass Capital) and was acquired by PolyMedica Corporation in 2005. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface; its former intellicare.com domain is parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Interana
providers.description: Interana was an event-based behavioral analytics platform for interactively querying large-scale event data (clickstream, product usage, and time-series data) at full resolution. Founded around 2013 in Redwood City, California by former Facebook engineers, it was used at scale by companies including Microsoft Bing. The company's team and technology were acquired by Twitter in March 2020; the standalone product was spun out and continued as Scuba Analytics (scuba.io), and the interana.com domain now redirects to its successor lineage. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical / defunct company record — there is no live public API surface, developer portal, or hosted documentation remaining. The only surviving first-party developer surface is the open-source Interana GitHub organization.

providers.name: InterPrice Technologies
providers.description: InterPrice Technologies, Inc. was a New York City debt capital markets fintech that gave corporate treasury teams a single web platform for new-issue financing decisions. Founded by Olga Chin and commercially launched in 2020, its treasury capital markets platform aggregated the indicative pricing that banks and financing partners supplied for bonds, commercial paper, loans and hedging, normalized it across currencies and products, and presented it in comparison dashboards so CFOs and treasurers could read funding costs side by side instead of collecting them by email and spreadsheet. The company was WBENC-certified as a woman-owned business, raised roughly $9.8M — a $2.5M seed in March 2021 and a $7.3M Series A in November 2022 co-led by Nasdaq Ventures and DRW Venture Capital with Bowery Capital participating — and named HP Inc., McCormick & Company and Takeda Pharmaceuticals among its corporate treasury customers. In March 2023 it announced bank API connectivity, but that was an inbound integration through which relationship banks delivered pricing indications into the InterPrice platform for its own tenants; no public developer portal, API reference, key issuance, or machine-readable specification was ever published, and none appears anywhere in the 983 archived URLs captured for the domain. The company wound down during 2025 — founder and chief executive Olga Chin left in February 2025 and is now a managing director at Tradeweb, the last Wayback capture of the site is 2025-01-26, and interpricetech.com now has an empty DNS delegation — so this profile is retained as a historical record and there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Interwoven
providers.description: Interwoven, Inc. (NASDAQ: IWOV) was an enterprise content management software company founded in 1995 whose flagship products were TeamSite web content management and WorkSite document management, with a strong presence in the legal sector. Accel backed the company circa 1998; it IPO'd, and was acquired by Autonomy Corporation in 2009 (Autonomy in turn acquired by HP in 2011; TeamSite and related products later went to OpenText in 2016). The company is DEFUNCT: interwoven.com no longer serves HTTP/HTTPS and there is no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface to enrich. This entry is a false-positive lead from harvesting Accel's historic portfolio and should be skipped by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: InVision
providers.description: InVision was a digital product design platform used by teams to build the world's best customer experiences. It provided REST APIs for managing prototypes, design documents, boards, comments, workflows, and design system components including design tokens and icons via the Design System Manager (DSM). InVision shut down all services on January 1, 2025, with its domain now redirecting to Miro.

providers.name: InVisionApp
providers.description: InVision (InVisionApp, Inc.) was a digital product design collaboration platform founded in 2011 by Clark Valberg and Ben Nadel. It built a suite of tools for prototyping, design handoff, and real-time collaboration — including interactive prototypes, Inspect/Specs for developer handoff, DSM (Design System Manager), Boards, and the Freehand online whiteboard. At its peak InVision was valued near two billion dollars and backed by Battery Ventures, Accel, Tiger Global, and others, serving product design teams as a challenger to Adobe. As Figma surged, InVision's business declined: it sold the Freehand whiteboard product to Miro in 2023, and wound down all remaining services on December 31, 2024, after which customer content was permanently deleted. The invisionapp.com domain now redirects to Miro. InVision historically exposed a public REST API with OAuth and webhooks for its design platform, but that developer surface has been retired along with the product.

providers.name: Inxeption
providers.description: Inxeption was a B2B "industrial commerce" software company founded in 2017 by serial entrepreneur Farzad Dibachi and headquartered in Silicon Valley (San Jose / Cupertino, California). It sold a cloud commerce platform that let manufacturers, distributors and wholesalers stand up a branded online storefront and digital product catalog, then manage quoting, contract-specific pricing, purchase orders, bulk and multimodal orders, freight and logistics, returns, payments and sales analytics from one place — a category it marketed as the "Industrial Commerce SuperApp". Its best-known product was Inxeption Zippy, launched in March 2019 with UPS after an equity investment from the UPS Strategic Enterprise Fund, which bundled UPS as the shipper of choice into the storefront. The company raised roughly $186M across its rounds, including a $125M Series E in January 2022. Inxeption shut down on 2024-08-15. It never operated a public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK or package was ever published, and its integration story was bespoke customer and EDI connections delivered under contract. Today only the apex domain resolves, and it no longer belongs to the company — it is listed for sale on the serp.domains domain marketplace. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: IRL
providers.description: IRL (legal name Get Together, Inc.) was a San Francisco social calendar and group-messaging app that let people share and sync calendars with friends and follow venues, organizations and notable figures. It raised more than $200 million in venture capital, including a $170 million Series C led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 in 2021 that valued the company at $1.17 billion. In June 2023 a special committee of the board reported that roughly 95 percent of the app's claimed users were automated or bot accounts, and the board voted to dissolve the company; the SEC charged founder and former CEO Abraham Shafi with fraud on July 31, 2024. The company is defunct: irl.com now serves only an asset-inquiry notice, the marketing and app hosts are abandoned Netlify shells, docs.irl.com (Postman-hosted developer docs) returns 404, and api.irl.com is a dangling CNAME to a deleted AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. No public API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer program remains.

providers.name: Iron Ox
providers.description: Iron Ox (legally Inevitable Tech, Inc.) was a San Carlos, California robotics company that built autonomous indoor farms — hydroponic greenhouses worked by mobile transport robots and a robotic arm that seeded, moved, imaged and harvested leafy greens and herbs, with machine learning used to spot pests and disease plant by plant. Founded in 2015 by Brandon Alexander and Jon Binney, it went through Y Combinator (W16), raised roughly $98 million in total including a $53 million Series C led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures in September 2021, and ran greenhouses in Gilroy, California and Lockhart, Texas. It cut about half its staff — roughly 50 people — in November 2022 and ceased operations in mid-2023. Iron Ox never ran a developer program: it sold produce, not software, and the only public code it ever shipped was internal ROS robotics tooling on GitHub. Its site, ironox.com, is now a GoDaddy parking lander and every developer subdomain has been removed from DNS, so there is no API, specification, SDK or documentation surface left to profile.

providers.name: Itemfield
providers.description: Itemfield was an enterprise data-integration software company known for its Complex Data Exchange (CDE) and B2B data-transformation technology, which parsed, mapped, and transformed complex, unstructured, and industry-standard message formats into structured data. Itemfield was acquired by Informatica in 2006, and its technology was absorbed into Informatica's B2B Data Transformation product line. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no surviving independent Itemfield developer surface: the itemfield.com domain now resolves under Informatica-managed DNS and serves no HTTP content, so there is no live API, documentation, portal, or specification to harvest.

providers.name: Iterum Therapeutics
providers.description: Iterum Therapeutics plc is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, focused on developing novel anti-infective medications to treat multi-drug resistant (MDR) bacterial infections. Its lead product, ORLYNVAH (sulopenem), is described as the first oral and IV penem antibiotic targeting gram-negative resistant infections. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Iterum Therapeutics is a pharmaceutical/biotech company and does not operate a public developer API; as of March 2026 the company entered liquidation following a High Court order in Ireland.

providers.name: Itzcash
providers.description: Itzcash (ItzCash Card Ltd, operated by Ebix Payment Services Private Limited, CIN U74999MH2006PTC160835, Mumbai) was one of India's early prepaid payment and digital-payments companies, offering prepaid/gift cards, utility and bill payments, domestic money transfer, insurance and travel payments, and an agent-assisted retail payment network across India. The company was acquired by Ebix, Inc. in 2017 and folded into the EbixCash financial-exchange business. The ItzCash brand has since been retired: www.itzcash.com now redirects to ebixcash.com, and there is no first-party ItzCash developer portal, public API, or OpenAPI definition. This profile was surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company and is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network. Any live API surface belongs to the parent EbixCash entity (an "Ebixcash API Hub" root responds at api.ebixcash.com), not to the ItzCash brand.

providers.name: Ivella
providers.description: Ivella was a consumer fintech company that built shared money-management and multi-account banking tools aimed at couples and households, backed by the fintech venture firm Anthemis. As of 2026 Ivella's products have been sunset and the team has joined EarnIn to continue building. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an Anthemis portfolio-company lead; the enrichment pipeline found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API surface, and the company is no longer operating as an independent product.

providers.name: Jam.gg
providers.description: Jam.gg, founded in Paris in 2020 as Piepacker and rebranded in 2022, built a browser-based social cloud gaming platform for playing retro and indie multiplayer games with friends with no download or install, on patented streaming technology the company said cut bandwidth requirements by roughly 15x. It passed 8 million users before pivoting to selling its cloud gaming technology B2B to game developers and publishers. Backed by Makers Fund, Serena Capital, LEGO Ventures, Kima Ventures and Kickstarter (~$15.4M raised) and a Y Combinator W20 company. Jam.gg never published an HTTP API: its developer surface was a native game-integration SDK plus a Compose Multiplatform virtual gamepad library, both shipped from the GitHub organization still named piepacker. Y Combinator's company directory now lists Jam.gg as Inactive, noting the business split into two entities in 2023 with Onibi emerging separately; the jam.gg web property no longer completes a TLS handshake and piepacker.com has left DNS.

providers.name: Jarden
providers.description: Jarden Corporation was an American consumer products conglomerate that owned brands across Outdoor Solutions (Coleman, K2 Sports, Marmot, Rawlings), Consumer Solutions (Crock-Pot, Mr. Coffee, Sunbeam, Oster, FoodSaver), Branded Consumables (Yankee Candle, First Alert, Diamond Match), and Process Solutions. Jarden was acquired by Newell Rubbermaid on April 15, 2016, with the combined entity rebranded as Newell Brands. As such, Jarden no longer exists as an independent company and does not maintain its own APIs.

providers.name: Jaunt *
providers.description: Jaunt (Jaunt VR, later Jaunt XR) was a cinematic virtual-reality and immersive-media technology company founded in 2013 and based in Santa Clara, California. It built end-to-end tools for capturing, stitching, streaming, and viewing 360-degree cinematic VR, including the Jaunt ONE professional camera and a cloud rendering pipeline, before pivoting toward volumetric AR/XR in 2018. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) among other investors, the company wound down its XR business and sold its underlying technology assets to Verizon in late 2019. This profile was surfaced as a GV portfolio company; the company is now defunct and its domains (jaunt.us, jauntxr.com) are parked/for-sale or reassigned, so there is no live developer or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Jelli
providers.description: Jelli was a programmatic advertising technology company focused on terrestrial and broadcast radio, building a real-time platform that let advertisers buy and manage radio spots programmatically across broadcast station inventory. Backed by Battery Ventures (among other investors), Jelli was acquired by iHeartMedia in 2016 and its technology went on to power programmatic and automated audio advertising. The independent Jelli brand is now defunct - the jelli.com domain 301-redirects to tritondigital.com, and no Jelli-branded developer portal, API reference, or public API host remains. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the enrichment pipeline found no live Jelli developer or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Jet
providers.description: Jet.com was an American e-commerce company and online marketplace founded in 2014 by Marc Lore and headquartered in Hoboken, New Jersey. It offered a membership-style shopping model with dynamic, real-time pricing that lowered the total as shoppers added items to their cart. Walmart acquired Jet.com in 2016 for roughly USD 3.3 billion and folded its operations into Walmart's own e-commerce platform, discontinuing the Jet.com brand in 2020. The jet.com domain now redirects to walmart.com; Jet operates no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation. This record is retained as a defunct portfolio lead for network completeness.

providers.name: Jet (Walmart)
providers.description: Jet (Walmart) was a US e-commerce marketplace founded by Marc Lore and backed by Bain Capital Ventures, acquired by Walmart in 2016 for roughly 3.3 billion USD and subsequently wound down. The jet.com domain now 302-redirects to walmart.com (confirmed 2026-07-19) and no standalone Jet developer portal, API, documentation, or SDK surface exists; the brand and its commerce technology were absorbed into Walmart. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is retained for lineage/graph purposes but has no live public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Jet Com
providers.description: Jet.com was an American e-commerce marketplace founded in 2014 by Marc Lore that used dynamic, real-time pricing to lower cart totals as shoppers combined orders. Walmart acquired Jet.com in 2016 for approximately 3.3 billion dollars, folded its technology and talent into Walmart's online operation, and fully shut down the Jet.com brand and site in 2020. The jet.com domain now redirects to walmart.com, and no Jet-branded developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface remain online.

providers.name: Juke
providers.description: Juke is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto-web3. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Julu Mobile
providers.description: Julu Mobile was a Shanghai, China based mobile advertising network that served targeted, personalized ads to Chinese mobile users by analyzing mobile interactions to profile user interests. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by Zhubajie on November 1, 2012 and no longer operates an independent product or developer platform. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, documentation, MCP server, or developer surface, and julumobile.com resolves to a Cloudflare block page.

providers.name: Jumbo Privacy
providers.description: Jumbo (Jumbo Privacy) was a mobile-first consumer privacy and security assistant founded in 2019 by Pierre Valade, the co-founder of the Sunrise calendar app acquired by Microsoft. The iPhone/Android app helped everyday users take control of their online privacy by automatically hardening privacy settings across services like Google, Facebook, Twitter/X, Amazon, and LinkedIn, cleaning up old social posts, monitoring data breaches, and bundling identity-theft insurance. It was explicitly designed to process user data locally on-device with no server-side processing, so it never exposed a public developer API, SDK, or documented integration surface. Jumbo was backed by investors including Balderton Capital and Thrive Capital before being acqui-hired by cyber-insurer Coalition in 2023; the standalone consumer app was wound down and fully discontinued by 2024. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record - there is no active API to enrich.

providers.name: JumpCam
providers.description: JumpCam was a consumer mobile video startup (San Francisco, founded 2013 by former Yammer/YouTube product leader David Stewart) that let groups of friends collaboratively shoot and edit a single video from up to thirty short clips. It raised $2.7M led by Google Ventures (GV) and shipped an iOS app. The company is no longer active and jumpcam.com is now a parked domain listed for sale (Afternic); no developer portal, API, documentation, or other public API surface exists. Surfaced as a GV portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirmed there is no live API to profile.

providers.name: Jumprope
providers.description: Jumprope was a how-to video creation app backed by lightspeed-venture-partners that let creators produce and share step-by-step, swipeable instructional videos. The company (formerly at getjumprope.com) was acquired by Snap Inc. in early 2021 and the standalone product was subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass it operates no independent website, developer portal, or public API surface — the getjumprope.com and jumprope.co domains no longer resolve, and the unrelated jumprope.com domain is a physical jump-rope retailer on Shopify (not this company). No API artifacts could be discovered or derived; this profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record only.

providers.name: Jumptap
providers.description: Jumptap was a mobile advertising and audience-targeting platform founded in 2005 and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It matched ads to signals such as time of day, carrier network, site content, and device type, helping app developers acquire users and helping developers and publishers maximize ad revenue. In August 2013 Jumptap was acquired by Millennial Media (valued at roughly $210-232M in stock); Millennial Media was subsequently acquired by AOL/Verizon and folded into what is now Yahoo. Jumptap no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API.

providers.name: Jungla
providers.description: Jungla, Inc. was a San Francisco precision-medicine informatics startup founded in 2016 by Alexander Colavin and Carlos Araya. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and IndieBio, it built a cloud-based Functional Modeling Platform (FMP), also described as a Molecular Evidence Platform, that combined functional genomics, computational biophysics, cellular engineering, and machine learning to produce auditable predictive models for clinical genetic and genomic variant interpretation. Jungla emerged from stealth in 2018 and was acquired by Invitae Corporation in July 2019 (approximately $59M), where its technology augmented Invitae's Sherloc variant-classification approach. The company is now defunct; its original developer surface (jungla.io) is offline and no public API, documentation, or SDKs survive. This profile is a historical record surfaced from the a16z portfolio; it carries no live developer artifacts.

providers.name: JustBook
providers.description: JustBook was a Berlin, Germany based mobile hotel booking startup that offered same-day and last-minute hotel deals at discounted rates, in a model similar to HotelTonight. Founded in 2012, it grew to cover last-minute inventory across more than 120 cities in Europe and the United States through its iOS, Android, and web apps. The company was backed by Creandum, DN Capital, and Earlybird Venture Capital (among roughly 21 investors, raising about $3.74M) and was acquired by UK luxury-travel company Secret Escapes in January 2014 to strengthen its German-market and mobile presence. JustBook no longer operates as an independent brand and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation; this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct, acquired Creandum portfolio company. Note: the justbook.de domain is now an unrelated book price-comparison site (BookFinder) and is not connected to this company.

providers.name: justyo
providers.description: Yo (justyo.co) was a single-tap notification app and "the world's simplest API." A service registered an API username, received an api_token, and could push a lightweight "Yo" notification to a single subscriber or broadcast to all subscribers, optionally attaching a link, plus read the subscriber count. The Yo API had effectively one job — fire a push — with an api_token for auth (an OAuth 2.0 page was documented but never enabled) and first-party client SDKs across Python, PHP, Java, Node, Ruby, Scala and iOS under the github.com/YoApp organization. The Yo service is now defunct: the justyo.co host is suspended and its api/docs/dev subdomains no longer resolve. This API Evangelist profile captures the historical Yo API surface for the record.

providers.name: Juxta Labs
providers.description: Juxta Labs, Inc. was a San Francisco social and mobile applications startup founded around 2011 by Jared Allgood and Jayson Ahlstrom, building social games and light-social apps for teens (titles such as Zoomed In, Shadow Shapes, and Pick the Song) that reportedly reached tens of millions of users. In June 2015 the company raised roughly $1.7M from investors including 500 Global (then 500 Startups), Monashees, Alta Ventures, and Atua Ventures, which is why it surfaces in the 500 Global portfolio. The company is now inactive/deadpooled and its site (juxtalabs.com) is offline, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. Note: an unrelated current company at juxtalabs.io (enterprise AI document automation) is a different entity and is not this 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Kadena
providers.description: Kadena was a layer-1 Proof-of-Work blockchain platform built around Chainweb, a braided, parallelized Nakamoto-consensus protocol that scales Bitcoin-style security across many chains for high transaction throughput, together with Pact, its human-readable, Turing-incomplete smart-contract language. Kadena exposed two primary public APIs: the Chainweb Node API (P2P and service endpoints for cuts, blocks, headers, payloads, the mempool, mining, and node info) and the Pact REST API (local, send, poll, listen, spv) for submitting and querying smart-contract transactions on mainnet and testnet. The developer surface includes the kadena.js TypeScript client libraries, the pactjs CLI for type generation, and extensive docs at docs.kadena.io. Kadena Eco supported an ecosystem of dApps, the Marmalade NFT standard, and tooling. NOTE: Kadena the company announced it would cease operations on 2025-10-21; Kadena Mainnet stopped producing blocks on 2025-11-15 and the kadena-io GitHub organization was archived on 2025-12-23. A community edition (kda-community) forked from mainnet on 2025-11-08 and continues the open-source protocol. This profile documents the public API surface as published.

providers.name: Kaixin001
providers.description: Kaixin001 (开心网) is a Chinese social networking website launched in March 2008 by founder Cheng Bingao, a former senior executive at Sina. It rose to mass popularity in 2009-2010 on the back of viral social games such as "Friends for Sale" and "Parking Wars" before losing ground to Renren, Sina Weibo, and WeChat. After the parent company was acquired by a listed company in 2016, the founder departed and the business pivoted toward enterprise services and internet finance, marginalizing the original social network. Kaixin001 discontinued its Flash-based social gaming on November 18, 2023, and now persists mainly as a low-activity nostalgia platform. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub of Qiming and exposes no current public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Kalpana
providers.description: Kalpana, Inc. was a Sunnyvale, California networking hardware company founded in 1990 by Vinod Bhardwaj and Larry Blair that built the first Ethernet switch, the seven-port EtherSwitch, and pioneered EtherChannel link aggregation and the Virtual LAN (VLAN) concept. The company was acquired by Cisco Systems in 1994 and has been defunct as an independent entity ever since, with its technology absorbed into Cisco's Catalyst switching product line. There is no surviving developer portal, API, or public developer surface associated with the original Kalpana, Inc.

providers.name: Kamcord
providers.description: Kamcord was a San Francisco-based mobile technology company (Y Combinator, Summer 2012) founded by Aditya Rathnam, Kevin Wang, and Matt Zitzmann. It offered an iOS and Android SDK that let game developers embed in-app gameplay recording, live streaming ("appcasting"), and social sharing to YouTube, Twitter, and Facebook, and grew to roughly 200 million device installs. The company later pivoted to a short-form mobile screen-content social network ("shots"). In November 2017 Lyft acquihired most of the ~15-person team, including co-founders Rathnam and Wang, and Kamcord wound down its consumer app, live streaming, and developer SDK by the end of 2017. The company is DEFUNCT and no longer operates any developer program or API. The kamcord.com domain has since been repurposed by an unrelated lifestyle/blog publisher and is NOT associated with the original Kamcord.

providers.name: Kanoodle
providers.description: Kanoodle was an online advertising network founded in 1999 by Kent Keating, specializing in search-targeted and later content-targeted (contextual) sponsored links, adding partners such as CBS MarketWatch in January 2004. In August 2006 it restructured under a new parent company, Seevast Corp - the search-advertising business kept the Kanoodle brand, the content-targeted contextual ad product was spun out as Pulse 360, and the newly acquired Moniker.com domain registrar ran as a separate unit. Listed here as an Insight Partners portfolio company, Kanoodle/Seevast is defunct and exposes no surviving public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation - the seevast.com domain now resolves to a parked-domain lander. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Kansas City Southern
providers.description: Kansas City Southern (KCS) was a transportation holding company that operated freight rail networks across the United States and Mexico. On April 14, 2023, KCS merged with Canadian Pacific Railway to form Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC), the first single-line rail network connecting Canada, the United States, and Mexico. CPKC operates approximately 32,000 km (20,000 mi) of rail and is headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, with U.S. headquarters in Kansas City, Missouri.

providers.name: Kaodim
providers.description: Kaodim was a Southeast Asian on-demand home and local services marketplace founded in 2014 that connected consumers with service providers such as cleaners, plumbers, electricians, aircon technicians, movers, tutors, and event professionals. Headquartered in Malaysia, it operated regionally under Kaodim.com (Malaysia), Kaodim.sg (Singapore), Gawin.ph (Philippines), and Beres.id (Indonesia), and raised venture funding from investors including 500 Global (500 Startups), Venturra Capital, and Square Peg. The company ceased all operations on July 1, 2022, citing prolonged COVID-19 lockdowns, labor shortages, rising costs, and weakened demand. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer program or API surface exists for the defunct company, so there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: KapStone Paper and Packaging
providers.description: KapStone Paper and Packaging Corporation was a producer of containerboard, corrugated products, and specialty paper based in Northbrook, Illinois. In November 2018, KapStone was acquired by WestRock for approximately $4.9 billion, ending its existence as an independent public company. WestRock subsequently merged with Smurfit Kappa in July 2024 to form Smurfit Westrock, the global combined entity that today inherits the legacy KapStone operations.

providers.name: Kashya
providers.description: Kashya Inc. was a data-protection software company providing continuous data protection (CDP) and heterogeneous, storage-agnostic data replication for enterprise disaster recovery and business continuity. Founded around 2000 with headquarters in San Jose, California and research and development in Israel, and backed by Battery Ventures among other investors, Kashya was acquired by EMC Corporation in 2006 for a reported ~$153 million. Its technology became the foundation of EMC RecoverPoint. The company has been defunct since the acquisition and operates no independent website, developer portal, or public API surface today.

providers.name: Katango
providers.description: Katango was a Palo Alto, California mobile software startup whose smartphone app automatically organized a user's phone and social contacts into intelligent groups (circles) using clustering algorithms, so people could share and message the right subset of friends without manually building lists. The company was backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (through its sFund social initiative) and was acquired by Google in November 2011, with the team joining Google to work on the Google+ Circles experience. The standalone product was discontinued after the acquisition. This API Evangelist profile was created as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio lead; enrichment confirms the company is defunct with no public developer surface, API, or documentation. The katango.com domain now resolves to Google-owned infrastructure with no live site.

providers.name: Katerra
providers.description: Katerra was a Menlo Park, California off-site construction and building-technology company founded in 2015 by former Flextronics chief executive Michael Marks with Fritz Wolff and Jim Davidson, built on the thesis that a single vertically integrated firm could design, engineer, manufacture and assemble buildings end to end — running its own architecture practice, factories in Phoenix, Tracy and Spokane producing cross-laminated timber and prefabricated wall, floor and bathroom assemblies, and its own supply chain and general contracting arm. It raised more than $2 billion across a dozen rounds, including an $865M Series D led by the SoftBank Vision Fund in January 2018 at a valuation above $3 billion and a $200M recapitalization in December 2020 that handed SoftBank majority control. Its only software product was Katerra Apollo, announced in February 2019 as a design-to-field platform (Apollo Construct, Apollo Insight, Apollo Connect) whose launch materials promised "open API integration" with existing construction workflows — but Apollo was sold to Katerra's own construction customers and never shipped a public developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification. The insolvency of its SoftBank-backed lender Greensill Capital cost Katerra its bonding capacity, and the company shut down and filed Chapter 11 in the Southern District of Texas on 6 June 2021. Its assets were broken up: the Apollo software went to Builders FirstSource for roughly $4.5M on 9 September 2021, and the factories were sold separately. katerra.com no longer serves a site — it answers a Cloudflare error 1001 on every path and cannot complete a TLS handshake at all. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface left to catalog.

providers.name: Kerros Health
providers.description: Kerros Health (Kerros) was a digital mental-health and wellness startup building clinically validated, mobile-based programs proven to improve mental health, positioned as an evidence-based consumer brand modernizing established treatments through mobile technology and design. The product began as a teen-created mental-health app (originating out of Scarsdale High School) and grew largely through word of mouth. Co-founded by Justin Ip and backed by Cowboy Ventures at the seed stage, the company has since exited. It was a consumer mobile app with no public developer/API surface; this API Evangelist profile is maintained as a portfolio-lead record and no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation could be found during enrichment.

providers.name: Kespry
providers.description: Kespry was an industrial drone and aerial-intelligence company founded in the San Francisco Bay Area that paired automated fixed-perimeter drones with a cloud analytics platform to turn aerial imagery into measurable data. Its product was used for stockpile and inventory volumetrics in mining and aggregates, construction-site progress monitoring and earthworks, and insurance roof inspection. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Kespry was acquired by Firmatek in 2020 and the brand has since been retired; the former developer and marketing domain kespry.com now issues a 301 redirect to firmatek.com. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for lineage and portfolio mapping, but Kespry publishes no live, standalone developer surface, API, documentation, or client SDKs of its own.

providers.name: Kevin.
providers.description: kevin. was a Lithuanian account-to-account (A2A) payments infrastructure company providing PSD2 open-banking Payment Initiation and Account Information services to merchants across 28 European countries. Its platform API let businesses initiate bank (SEPA) and card (hybrid) payments, issue refunds, read account data, and receive signed payment webhooks through a single integration to hundreds of banks, supported by an official Node.js SDK, a CLI, and a React UI component library. Backed by Accel. The company has wound down its public web presence - kevin.eu no longer resolves as of 2026-07 - and this profile is enriched from kevin.'s published npm packages and archived developer reference.

providers.name: Kiira
providers.description: Kiira (Kiira Health) was a student-focused digital health / telehealth platform that partnered with colleges and universities to bridge the gap between students and clinicians, providing online visits with doctors, nurses, and therapists, primary care and gynecological consultations, mental health support, and health literacy workshops and education resources through a patient booking portal. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this pass the company operated a consumer/patient web app only and published no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal, so there is no API surface to enrich. Its recorded domain kiira.io is no longer controlled by the company — it now redirects to an unrelated third-party site — so this profile reflects the company's last-known (archived, Dec 2024) state and is treated as a defunct / lapsed lead.

providers.name: Kik (Kin)
providers.description: Kik (Kin) refers to the Kin cryptocurrency created by Kik Interactive, the messaging company, as a blockchain-based digital currency for use inside consumer applications. Kin originally launched on a fork of the Stellar network and later migrated to Solana, shipping first-party developer SDKs (JavaScript/Node and Python) under the kinecosystem GitHub organization and a developer program at developer.kin.org. The Kin project is now defunct: the developer surface no longer resolves, every kinecosystem repository is archived, the published SDKs are deprecated, and Kik itself was acquired by MediaLab AI Inc. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and is retained as a historical record of a wound-down crypto developer surface.

providers.name: Kimono Labs
providers.description: Kimono Labs was a developer-tools startup that let users turn any website into a structured API without writing code, using a visual point-and-click tool to define data selectors that Kimono would crawl on a schedule and expose as JSON/CSV endpoints and RSS feeds. Founded in 2014 by Pratap Ranade and Ryan Rowe and backed by Cowboy Ventures, the company was acquired by Palantir Technologies in February 2016, after which the hosted cloud service at kimonolabs.com was shut down on 29 February 2016; a downloadable Kimono Desktop application was released as a farewell so existing scrapers could continue running locally. The company is defunct and operates no live API today; this profile is retained for historical and network completeness.

providers.name: Kinecta
providers.description: Kinecta Corporation was a venture-backed provider of software infrastructure for content distribution, funded by Canaan Partners and reaching a Series B stage. It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. The company is no longer operating as an independent provider and publishes no active developer surface, API, documentation, or developer portal, so there are no API artifacts to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio identity record.

providers.name: Kinnek
providers.description: Kinnek was a B2B purchasing marketplace that helped small and mid-sized businesses buy from suppliers. Buyers could describe what they needed, collect competitive quotes from vetted suppliers, read unbiased reviews, and get expert purchasing advice in one place, under the tagline "Purchasing Made Painless." The company operated at kinnek.com but is no longer active: the domain no longer resolves (no DNS A, MX, NS, or SOA records) and the site survives only via the Internet Archive (strongest snapshot circa 2017). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead (backed by 500 Global and Version One Ventures); the enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specifications for this provider.

providers.name: Kippt
providers.description: Kippt was a social bookmarking and link-saving service (kippt.com) that let people save, organize, and share bookmarks in lists and follow other users' collections. It exposed a public REST API over the kippt.com domain, which produced a small ecosystem of community-authored client libraries in Python, Ruby, and JavaScript. Kippt was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The service has since been discontinued: the kippt.com domain resolves to a legacy IP but no longer responds, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to harvest. What remains real and capturable is the set of third-party API wrapper packages still published on the public registries.

providers.name: Kitch
providers.description: Kitch was a Lisbon, Portugal based restaurant technology company founded in 2019 by Rui Bento and Nuno Rodrigues, both former Uber executives for southern Europe. After starting as a delivery-first "dark kitchen" operator, Kitch pivoted during the 2020 pandemic into a SaaS platform that let restaurants consolidate and manage digital orders arriving from multiple third-party delivery marketplaces — Glovo, Uber Eats, Bolt Food and Just Eat among them — on a single tablet, alongside their own direct-ordering storefront, so operators could keep control of their menus, pricing and customer identity instead of depending on the aggregator apps. Kitch raised roughly EUR 1 million in pre-seed funding led by Seedcamp and Mustard Seed MAZE, followed by a EUR 3.25 million seed round led by Atlantic Food Labs. The company was acquired by Barcelona-based delivery platform Glovo in a deal signed in January 2022 and announced in March 2022, and the standalone Kitch brand has since been retired. Kitch never published a public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or status page was ever published on kitch.io, and none appears in the Internet Archive's record of the domain. The kitch.io domain registration has since lapsed and now resolves to an unrelated third-party gambling site, so no live link is carried in this profile.

providers.name: Kitchen United
providers.description: Kitchen United was a Pasadena, California ghost-kitchen operator that built and ran shared commissary kitchens — branded "Kitchen United Mix" — where multiple restaurant brands cooked out of one facility for delivery and pickup, including a chain of in-store food halls operated with Kroger. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others, the company wound down its physical footprint: in late 2023 it announced it would sell or close all remaining units and pivot to licensing its ordering software, and on 2024-03-14 sbe/C3 founder Sam Nazarian acquired its intellectual property and ghost-kitchen assets into a new holding company, Everybody Eats, alongside C3 and Nextbite. Kitchen United never published a public developer API, SDK, CLI or developer portal, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or package-registry artifact exists for it. The kitchenunited.com domain still resolves but now serves a residual WordPress shell whose only remaining page is unrelated SEO spam, so it should not be treated as a live developer surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Kitchensurfing
providers.description: Kitchensurfing was a New York City marketplace that booked professional chefs to shop for, cook, and serve meals in customers' own kitchens, founded in 2012 and backed by roughly $20M from Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital, and Tiger Global. It began as an advance-booking platform for private dinner parties and pivoted in 2015 to a flat-rate on-demand model in which a chef arrived and cooked dinner within a fixed window. Neither model produced sustainable demand against better-capitalized meal-kit and delivery competitors, and the company discontinued service and shut down on April 15, 2016. It never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Its GitHub organization survives with eleven public repositories - open-source Ruby/Rails forks and internal hackathon projects, last active in 2016 - but contains no client library or API definition. The kitchensurfing.com domain was subsequently re-registered by an unrelated cooking-products affiliate publisher and no longer represents this company.

providers.name: Kitchit
providers.description: Kitchit was a San Francisco on-demand private-chef marketplace founded in 2011 by Brendan Marshall and Ian Ferguson. The service matched consumers with vetted professional chefs who shopped, cooked, served, and cleaned up a multi-course meal in the customer's own home, booked through the kitchit.com web and mobile storefront. In 2015 the company pivoted from fully customized menus to a lower-priced standardized product marketed as "Kitchit Tonight," priced around $39 per person with a two-person minimum. Kitchit served more than 100,000 meals across roughly five years of operation and reported a net promoter score of 87. It raised approximately $8.1M, with investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Crosslink Capital, Javelin Venture Partners, and Otter Rock Capital. The company announced its shutdown in April 2016, with the founders citing a finite investment runway that ended amid broad upheaval in food-tech, alongside contemporaneous failures at SpoonRocket, Dinner Lab, and Kitchensurfing. Kitchit is defunct: it operates no website, developer portal, or public API today, and no public API surface was ever published. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct provider record for network completeness.

providers.name: Klout
providers.description: Klout was a San Francisco social-analytics company, founded in 2008 by Joe Fernandez and Binh Tran, that scored individuals on their online social influence. The "Klout Score" was a single number from 1 to 100 derived from the size of a person's social network and how other people engaged with the content they published across connected accounts such as Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, and Google+. Klout operated a public REST API — the Klout API v2 at api.klout.com — that let developers resolve a social handle to a Klout identity, look up a user's score and score history, and retrieve influence graphs (who a user influences and is influenced by) and topic affinities; access was key-based and widely used by marketing, CRM, and social-listening tools, and a large community of third-party client libraries grew up around it in Ruby, Node.js, Python, and PHP. Lithium Technologies acquired Klout on 27 March 2014 for approximately $200 million. Lithium retired Klout as a standalone service on 25 May 2018 — the day the EU General Data Protection Regulation took effect — stating that Klout's AI and machine-learning capabilities were valuable to Lithium but the consumer service was not aligned with its long-term strategy. The Klout API was shut down with the service. Lithium has since been rebranded as Khoros, and klout.com now redirects into the Khoros website. The company is defunct and operates no live API; this profile is retained as a historical provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: KNO
providers.description: Kno, Inc. was a digital textbook and student learning platform founded in May 2009 in Santa Clara, California by CEO Osman Rashid (co-founder of Chegg) and CTO Babur Habib. Kno began as a dual-screen tablet built for students, abandoned hardware in 2011, and pivoted to eTextbook software delivered across iPad, Android, Windows and the web in partnership with textbook publishers. The company raised roughly $93 million from Andreessen Horowitz, Intel Capital, Goldman Sachs, FLOODGATE, First Round Capital, SV Angel, Advance Publications and GSV Capital before being acquired by Intel in November 2013 for approximately $15 million and rebranded as Intel Education Study, which has itself since been discontinued. As of enrichment the kno.com domain is parked and redirects to a third-party domain brokerage, and the provider exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other artifact surface to enrich.

providers.name: Knowable
providers.description: Knowable was a mobile audio-learning company that united world-class experts, thinkers, and storytellers to produce structured audio courses for curious minds — an "audio courses" take on online learning delivered as serialized lessons rather than one-off podcasts. Founded by the Bit Kitchen team and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z led its round in May 2019), Knowable published expert-led course series across business, creativity, and personal development. The company is no longer operational: knowable.fyi now serves a tombstone notice stating that Knowable has been acquired by Medium and directing former listeners to Medium.com. Knowable never published a public developer program, API, SDKs, or developer documentation, and its GitHub organization (bitkitchen) exposes no public repositories. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record from the a16z portfolio; there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Knowmia.com
providers.description: Knowmia was an education-focused video platform used by instructors to create, share, and assign instructional video and lessons. The brand was operated by TechSmith alongside Camtasia and Snagit, and was marketed as Knowmia and Knowmia Pro for classroom and campus video. TechSmith retired Knowmia Pro in early 2025 and now directs former Knowmia customers to TechSmith Screencast, which offers comparable asynchronous video sharing, commenting, and review and integrates with Snagit and Camtasia. As of July 2026 knowmia.com issues an HTTP 301 redirect to the TechSmith Screencast product page. Knowmia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, CLI, or machine-readable specifications; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a retired/absorbed entry for historical and lineage purposes.

providers.name: Kodit.io
providers.description: Kodit.io was a Helsinki-based proptech and "iBuyer" that used machine learning and automation to make instant cash offers on residential property, buying homes directly from sellers and reselling them, with operations in Finland, Spain and Poland. Founded in 2017 and backed by Speedinvest among others, the company rebranded to Rive in 2022 after a EUR 23M Series A aimed at simplifying home buying and selling across Europe. In January 2024 Rive (formerly Kodit.io) transferred its entire Finnish real estate brokerage business to Neliöt Liikkuu LKV, and the Kodit.io LKV entity subsequently entered bankruptcy proceedings in late 2024. The company operated a consumer-facing marketplace only; it never published a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts, and the kodit.io domain has since lapsed to an unrelated registrant. This profile is retained as a historical network record.

providers.name: Koinex
providers.description: Koinex was an Indian digital-asset exchange launched in 2017, describing itself as India's first and largest cryptocurrency exchange with more than one million users. It offered spot trading across multiple crypto assets with INR pairs before regulatory uncertainty around Indian banking access forced it to shut down all services in June 2019, asking users to withdraw their holdings by July 15, 2019.
