The company is DEFUNCT: koinex.in now serves only a single static wind-down notice directing former users to claim any crypto assets left on the platform through CoinDCX, with which Koinex partnered for the transition. There is no live product, developer portal, documentation, or API surface; the domain's TLS certificate expired in March 2025 and every path other than the notice returns 403. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record of a shut-down crypto exchange and as a Pantera Capital portfolio lead.

providers.name: Koo
providers.description: Koo was an Indian microblogging and social networking platform built by Bombinate Technologies, positioned as a multilingual, India-first alternative to Twitter/X with support for Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi and other regional languages. Backed by Accel and Tiger Global, it grew during the 2021 Indian social-media policy disputes before ceasing operations in 2024 after funding and acquisition talks fell through. Koo never published a public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs, and its domain no longer serves a site — this profile is retained as a verified-defunct historical record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Koru Careers
providers.description: Koru (joinkoru.com) was a Seattle-based predictive hiring and people-analytics SaaS company. Its platform built a per-employer "predictive hiring fingerprint" and scored candidates against the Koru7 Impact Skills assessment — Grit, Rigour, Impact, Teamwork, Curiosity, Ownership and Polish — via a 20-minute online pre-interview that produced a Candidate Fit Score, with the stated goal of increasing quality of hire and reducing screening bias. Products were marketed as Koru Hire and Koru Develop. The company was acquired by Cappfinity: between February and November 2020 joinkoru.com began redirecting to koru.cappfinity.com, where the Koru7 Impact Skills Assessment was carried as a Cappfinity product. That subdomain now redirects to cappfinity.com, which carries no remaining Koru branding, and the joinkoru.com domain has lapsed and currently serves unrelated online-gambling affiliate content. Koru published no public developer portal, documentation, or API; this profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct company and no live endpoints are catalogued.

providers.name: Kosmik
providers.description: Kosmik was an infinite-canvas visual workspace and AI moodboarding app for macOS and Windows, published by Lithium Media SAS in Paris and backed by Creandum. It organized work into spatial "universes" grouped in shared workspaces, and combined that canvas with a built-in web browser, web clipper, PDF reader, drawing and frames, real-time multiplayer collaboration, and AI features including auto-tagging, AI search and AI-assisted asset discovery. Kosmik was an early mover on local-first storage, shipping an on-device IPFS node with multiplayer in 2018 and a multiplayer web browser in 2022, before consolidating that work into Kosmik 3 in 2025. Kosmik shipped no public API, SDK, CLI or webhook surface, and the product sunset on 31 May 2026; the vendor now publishes in-app universe and workspace export instructions in place of any migration interface.

providers.name: Kosmix
providers.description: Kosmix Corporation was a Mountain View, California topic-discovery and search company operating from roughly 2005 to 2011. Rather than returning a ranked list of links, Kosmix automatically assembled a topic "home page for the web" for any subject, aggregating and categorizing content across health, science, food, sports, politics, travel, finance and other verticals. The company also shipped the RightHealth, MeeHive and Tweetbeat properties, the last of which filtered and organized real-time Twitter activity by topic. Kosmix was acquired by Walmart in 2011 and became the nucleus of @WalmartLabs; kosmix.com later 301-redirected to walmartlabs.com and the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record. There is no live Kosmix developer surface, API, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Kyte
providers.description: Kyte was a full-stack technology-operations company that delivered rental cars on demand to the customer's door, positioning itself for any trip longer than a rideshare — a car for a day, a few days, or longer — with no rental counters, no lines and no paperwork. Headquartered in San Francisco, the company combined a consumer mobile and web booking experience with its own fleet and delivery operations ("bits and atoms"), and at its peak operated in 14 US markets delivering tens of thousands of trips per month. It was a growth-stage portfolio company of Anthemis under that firm's Data, Tech and Infrastructure thesis. Kyte was a consumer-facing operator and never published a public developer program, API, SDK or developer portal, and as of this enrichment pass its web properties no longer serve the company.

providers.name: Lagoa
providers.description: Lagoa was a cloud-based 3D visualization, rendering, and CAD publishing platform built by TeamUp Technologies Inc., billed as the first web-based platform for photoreal 3D visualization and rendering. It let artists, designers, engineers, and architects import over 40 native CAD formats, build kinematic assemblies, produce photoreal renders in the browser via its MultiOptics interactive rendering engine, publish interactive 3D product configurators, and collaborate on scenes in real time — with no local hardware or installed software. Lagoa also ran a developer platform exposing server-side Platform APIs (geometry and image transcoding, asset management, thumbnailing, user authentication, versioning) alongside an Application Framework with Application, Collaboration, and Real-time Persistence APIs for embedding browser-based 3D into third-party apps. The company acquired browser CAD tool 3DTin in September 2013. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company is defunct: the marketing site (home.lagoa.com), support and API documentation (support.lagoa.com) and application host all stopped resolving, the github.com/lagoa organization is empty, and lagoa.com is now a parked listing offered for sale on atom.com. No live developer, API, or documentation surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Language Technology
providers.description: Language Technology is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Lanistar
providers.description: Lanistar was a London-based consumer fintech founded in 2019 by Gurhan Kiziloz, known for a heavily influencer-marketed "polymorphic" Mastercard debit card with an on-card keypad and display that generated single-use PIN and CVV2 codes. Lanistar Limited operated as an EMD agent of Modulr FS Limited under FCA authorisation, with cards issued by AF Payments Limited, and pivoted its consumer launch to Brazil where it offered a mobile account, Pix transfers and in-app crypto buying and selling. The company never operated a developer program: no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, or public GitHub repository was ever published. Lanistar Limited (company number 12091938) was placed into compulsory liquidation by a court winding-up order filed 14 April 2025, and its public surface has since gone dark — lanistar.com and lanistar.app no longer resolve to any web host, the lanistar.co.uk domain is listed for sale by a domain broker, and the com.lanistar Google Play listing has been removed. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Lateral
providers.description: Lateral was a Berlin- and Hobart-based AI research software company founded in 2013 that built machine-learning powered content recommendation and document navigation tools. Its early product was a conceptual text-matching and recommendation API that let developers insert documents and retrieve semantically similar content, with pre-populated corpora covering arXiv, PubMed, Wikipedia, news and SEC filings. The company later pivoted to an LLM-assisted research workspace for navigating information across large document sets, and published open-source research on hyperbolic-space word embeddings (Poincare embeddings, hyperplane hashers, WARP recommenders). Lateral was permanently shut down on 26 June 2025; the team pointed users to a successor open-source research platform at coordination.network. The public API, its documentation host and the application host are all retired, so this profile documents a historical API surface and the client libraries that remain published.

providers.name: LaunchGram
providers.description: LaunchGram entered the API Evangelist network from the 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio listing at 500.co/portfolio, which remains the only sourced record of the company. A July 2026 enrichment probe found no live company presence behind the name: launchgram.com no longer serves a company site but a Spaceship domain-marketplace parking page offering the domain itself for sale (listed at $2,588 outright, or lease-to-own), the domain publishes no MX records, and none of the conventional developer subdomains (api, docs, developer, developers, app, status) resolve. No developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable definition, SDK, or package-registry client library could be found, and requests to the /.well-known/ discovery paths return no response at all. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record for a defunct 500 Global portfolio lead; there is no API surface to enrich, and no artifacts have been generated for it.

providers.name: LaunchKit
providers.description: LaunchKit was a set of web-based tools for mobile app developers, built by Cluster Labs, Inc. in San Francisco and backed by GV. Its products included Screenshot Builder for App Store screenshots, Review Monitor for App Store review alerts, a Sales Reporter, hosted App Websites, and Super Users and Cloud Config delivered through the LaunchKit iOS SDK. LaunchKit joined Google in 2016 and the codebase was released as open source under Apache 2.0. There is no live hosted LaunchKit API, developer portal, or documentation today; the surviving surface is a self-hostable Django/JavaScript codebase on GitHub plus an unmaintained Objective-C SDK on CocoaPods. The original launchkit.io domain is no longer company-controlled and now serves an unrelated content site.

providers.name: LE TOTE
providers.description: Le Tote was an online women's clothing rental and subscription-box business founded in San Francisco in 2012 by Brett Northart and Rakesh Tondon, and a member of the Y Combinator Summer 2013 batch. Unlike Rent the Runway, which concentrated on high-end event wear, Le Tote rented everyday apparel and accessories through a rotating personalized "tote" driven by its own sizing and recommendation data. In August 2019 it agreed to acquire the Lord & Taylor department-store chain from Hudson's Bay Company; both businesses filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 2 August 2020, and Saadia Group bought the assets that October. Saadia Group was reported effectively shut down in March 2024 and the letote.com site went offline that spring. Le Tote is defunct: the domain no longer resolves, and the company never published a public API or developer portal. This profile is retained as a historical record of its open-source engineering output.

providers.name: Leade.rs
providers.description: Leade.rs, Inc. was a two-sided marketplace that matched keynote, motivational, and business speakers with the conferences, corporate events, brands, and press that wanted to book them. Event organizers could search a curated roster and create an event, while speakers maintained a profile covering their availability and topics — the platform's stated aim was to remove the cold-outreach grind from conference programming and surface newer and more diverse voices. The company was co-founded by Loïc Le Meur, the French entrepreneur behind the LeWeb conference and a Silicon Valley angel investor; at acquisition its network was reported at roughly 300 speakers across 11 core fields including crypto, AI, and entrepreneurship. ASX-listed Animoca Brands acquired 100% of the equity on 6 May 2019 for US$0.5 million upfront, intending to grow the roster into a mentor and investor network bridging East and West alongside its Zeroth accelerator, with Le Meur joining Animoca as a venture partner. The product did not survive the acquisition. Leade.rs never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable documentation, and as of the July 2026 enrichment pass the leade.rs domain no longer resolves — it remains registered through December 2026 and is delegated to EuroDNS nameservers, but the zone is not served, so there is no live surface of any kind to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Leaky
providers.description: Leaky was a US auto-insurance comparison service that operated from 2011 until 31 August 2013. It let consumers compare prices and plans across the nation's top insurers, model "what if" coverage scenarios, and keep all of their policy information in one place with alerts when they could save money. The comparison engine was built by reverse-engineering the pricing models of more than 100 insurers from publicly-available government filings rather than by selling user information to carriers. Leaky reported providing over $300 million of auto-insurance quotes and saving its users more than $40 million before it wound down the consumer business; its commercial-insurance business was acquired by Navion Insurance. The company was backed by 500 Global (500 Startups). Leaky is defunct — leaky.com now serves only a static shutdown notice, all user data was deleted at closure, and there is no developer portal, public API, SDK, or discovery surface to catalog.

providers.name: LeanMarket
providers.description: LeanMarket was a mobile advertising technology company headquartered in Mountain View, California, that brought real-time bidding (RTB) display advertising to small and mid-sized advertisers through a self-serve platform. Its pitch was transparency and operator control: advertisers could pull reports showing in-depth data on every mobile app and mobile website their ads appeared in — in contrast to blind ad networks — and could tweak, optimize and scale campaigns themselves through a self-serve interface with up-to-the-second reporting, rather than waiting on an account manager to make changes. The company went through the Y Combinator Summer 2012 (S12) batch and appears on the Andreessen Horowitz investment list, with seed participation also reported from Initialized Capital. LeanMarket is defunct and operates no live product, developer portal or API today; this profile is retained for historical and network completeness.

providers.name: LearnSprout
providers.description: LearnSprout was a San Francisco edtech company founded in 2012 by Franklyn Chien, Anthony Wu and Joe Woo out of the Imagine K12 accelerator. It built LearnSprout Connect, an API layer that unlocked K-12 student data held in student information systems (SIS) through direct database integration rather than the SIS application layer, giving edtech developers a single "once and done" integration plus a change-log endpoint for incremental syncs. It also sold a district-facing analytics product covering attendance, grades and college readiness, reaching over 2,500 schools across 42 states on roughly $4.7M raised from Andreessen Horowitz, Formation 8 and Samsung Ventures. Apple acquired the company in January 2016 and the public API was retired; learnsprout.com no longer resolves and is parked on Apple nameservers.

providers.name: LearnVest
providers.description: LearnVest was a New York personal-finance company founded in 2009 by Alexa von Tobel and backed by Accel, selling subscription financial planning that paired consumers with CFP professionals alongside budgeting, spending-tracking and goal tools. Northwestern Mutual acquired LearnVest in 2015 for a reported $250 million and terminated the subscription planning service on June 5, 2018, closing all client accounts. The brand was relaunched as a consumer financial-education content site, and learnvest.com today is an archived article library on budgeting, saving, paying off debt and career growth, operated under the Northwestern Mutual brand. LearnVest never published a public API, developer portal, SDK or sandbox, and no developer surface exists today.

providers.name: Legit Patents
providers.description: Legit (listed by Seedcamp as "Legit Patents", 2016 cohort, legit.ai) was a Cambridge, Massachusetts startup applying natural-language processing to scientific and patent literature, which it developed into an on-demand expert network for the life sciences. Its product let pharmaceutical, biotech and medical-device teams search a corpus the company described as more than two million experts backed by roughly forty million data points, then pay a flat fee per reply to message key opinion leaders directly instead of scheduling calls — marketed for R&D, business development and licensing (BD&L), strategic alliances and integration management. The company is no longer operating: substantive legit.ai content disappears from the web archive after 2021, its LinkedIn company page returns HTTP 404, and the legit.ai domain is now parked on GoDaddy/Afternic and listed for sale (Afternic nameservers, a null MX record and an SPF "-all" policy). No public API, developer portal, documentation or machine-readable specification was ever published; see review.yml for the full probe record.

providers.name: Lenda
providers.description: Lenda was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment on 2026-07-19 found no operating surface: lenda.com returns HTTP 200 but serves only a parked single-page notice offering the domain for sale via a contact form, hosted on AWS and registered through Amazon Registrar. Every developer-facing subdomain probed (api, developer, developers, docs, app, status, blog) is NXDOMAIN, the full /.well-known/ discovery surface plus /llms.txt, /openapi.json and /robots.txt all return 404, and there is no first-party package on npm or PyPI and no company GitHub organization. This company is treated as defunct with no API to catalog; no artifact pointers are wired because no artifacts genuinely exist.

providers.name: Lendsquare
providers.description: Lendsquare was a community-lending / peer-to-peer lending startup surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company is defunct. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass lendsquare.com no longer hosts a product - the domain is parked on GoDaddy/Afternic nameservers (NS1.AFTERNIC.COM) and every path redirects to a "/lander" for-sale page, so there is no website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog. The only surviving first-party artifact is the dormant GitHub organization github.com/lendsquare, created 2013-07-09 and last updated 2015-04-24, holding two Ruby repositories that are third-party libraries the team consumed rather than APIs it published - "area" (place / area-code / zip conversion) and "dwolla-ruby" (Dwolla's official Ruby API wrapper), the latter indicating Lendsquare moved money via the Dwolla API. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct record; no API artifacts were generated because none exist to capture.

providers.name: Lendtable
providers.description: Lendtable was a US consumer fintech that extended a line of credit so individuals could afford to max out employer-sponsored benefits they would otherwise leave on the table — primarily the employer 401(k) match and Employee Stock Purchase Plans (ESPP). In its own words: "Lendtable gives a line of credit to help individuals get their employer 401(k) match and ESPP." The product advanced cash against a user's paycheck contributions and took a share of the resulting gains, and was distributed direct-to-consumer and through employers via a Lendtable for Business offering, alongside an iOS app and a Zendesk help center. Lendtable was backed by Partech among others. The company now appears defunct: lendtable.com, the blog, and all product paths return HTTP 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED (probed 2026-07-19), the iOS App Store listing is delisted, and the last successful Internet Archive capture of the live site is 2024-12-06. DNS, Google Workspace mail (MX/SPF/DMARC) and the GitHub organization remain registered. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts were ever published by this company.

providers.name: LendUp
providers.description: LendUp was a San Francisco consumer-lending fintech founded in 2011 and backed by GV and QED Investors, offering single-payment and installment loans to subprime borrowers alongside a gamified "LendUp Ladder" program that promised cheaper credit and credit-bureau reporting as borrowers repaid. LendUp Loans LLC ceased lending operations in January 2022 following Consumer Financial Protection Bureau enforcement actions over misleading marketing and pricing claims. The lendup.com domain is now operated by an unrelated company, LendUp LLC of Dover, Delaware, which runs a consumer loan-matching and financial-education site connecting borrowers to licensed lenders for a referral fee; it states it has no corporate, ownership, or operational relationship to the former lender and no access to its customer data. Neither entity publishes a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or any machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: LendUp Global
providers.description: LendUp Global, Inc. was a San Francisco consumer-lending fintech backed by a16z, operating through LendUp Loans, LLC (formerly Flurish, Inc.) to offer short-term and installment credit to subprime borrowers. The company is DEFUNCT — LendUp Loans, LLC ceased loan operations in January 2022. It has no live developer surface, no public API, no documentation host, and no maintained code repositories. The lendup.com domain is now operated by an unrelated entity (LendUp LLC, Dover, DE) that publicly disclaims any corporate relationship to LendUp Global, Inc.; its properties must NOT be attributed to this company profile. Retained in the network as a historical a16z portfolio record.

providers.name: Level
providers.description: Level is a stablecoin protocol that issued lvlUSD, a stablecoin fully backed by USDC and USDT which were deployed into blue-chip lending protocols (Aave and the Morpho Steakhouse USDC vault) to generate yield. Lending yield was passed back to holders through an ERC-4626 staking mechanism: lvlUSD could be staked for slvlUSD, a yield-accruing token that appreciates as the protocol distributes yield into the staking contract. Both tokens were transferable and integrated across DeFi venues including Morpho, Pendle, Spectra and Curve, with LayerZero OFT adapters bridging them to Base. Level exposes no public HTTP API — its programmable surface is a set of audited Ethereum mainnet smart contracts (lvlUSD, slvlUSD, LevelMinting, LevelStakingPool, LevelUsdPointsFarm, LevelReserveLens) documented in GitBook and published on GitHub. In September 2025 the team announced it was joining the Sky (fka MakerDAO) ecosystem as part of Grove and that the Level protocol is being sunset: mints paused, redemptions made public and fixed 1:1, cooldowns cut to two seconds, final yield distribution on 2025-10-02, and the front end retired on 2025-12-15 with contract-level redemption remaining available indefinitely.

providers.name: Librato
providers.description: Librato was a hosted metrics, monitoring and analytics service for operational data — time-series measurements, tagged metrics, dashboards ("spaces"), charts, annotations, alerts and notification services — delivered as a developer-first SaaS with a JSON REST API at metrics-api.librato.com/v1. Backed by Cowboy Ventures among others, the San Francisco company was acquired by SolarWinds in 2015 for a reported $40 million, and its metrics platform was folded into SolarWinds AppOptics — released in November 2017 — which has itself since reached end of life. The librato.com domain and every product subdomain (metrics., status., www.) now 301-redirect to the SolarWinds AppOptics end-of-life notice, the metrics-api.librato.com API host no longer resolves in DNS, and the github.com/librato organization was archived on 2024-01-02. This profile is retained as a historical record of a well-regarded developer API: the API reference source, the first-party Ruby, Python, Java and Node client libraries and the collection agents remain publicly archived and are catalogued here. The successor product is SolarWinds Observability SaaS.

providers.name: LifeMed Media
providers.description: LifeMed Media was a consumer health media company that operated dLife, a diabetes-focused media brand spanning dLife.com, the dLifeTV television program, the dLife Foundation, a diabetes retail store, and a section for healthcare professionals. Its editorial surface covered type 1, type 2, gestational and pre-diabetes, blood sugar management, insulin, complications, nutrition and recipes, and diabetes lifestyle content, monetized through sponsored sections from device and pharmaceutical advertisers. The company was venture backed by Battery Ventures. As of a 2026-07-19 verification pass the business appears defunct: its corporate domain lifemedmedia.com is parked for sale on HugeDomains and dlife.com no longer resolves. No developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface has ever been identified for this company.

providers.name: LightLogic
providers.description: LightLogic was an optoelectronics company founded in January 1998 and headquartered in Newark, California. It designed and manufactured highly integrated optical modules — transmitters and receivers — for high-speed (10 Gb/s and up) fiber optic telecommunications equipment, specializing in the integration of lasers, micro-optics and high-speed electronics. Its marquee products were 10 Gb/s transponders providing optical-to-electrical conversion for SONET OC-192 and 10 Gigabit Ethernet applications, sold to optical networking OEMs building primarily metro-market systems. The company raised $57.5M and was backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Cisco Systems, Infineon Technologies, Dassault Developpement, Infinity Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners (then Weiss, Peck and Greer), Optical Capital Group, Ridge Ventures, Siemens Mustang Ventures and Viventures. LightLogic was acquired by Intel Corporation; by mid-2002 lightlogic.com redirected to Intel's optical transceiver product pages. This is a hardware component maker with no API, developer or software surface — historically or today — and the lightlogic.com domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: LikeWise
providers.description: Likewise Software was a Bellevue, Washington enterprise software company building storage, identity and security products that bridged Linux, Unix and Mac systems into Microsoft Active Directory environments. Its OEM line, Likewise Storage Services, supplied SMB/CIFS multi-protocol file access to network storage vendors including HP StorageWorks, Riverbed, EMC Data Domain and NetApp, while Likewise Data Analytics and Governance covered auditing, reporting and compliance (HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, FISMA) over unstructured data. Its Likewise Enterprise and Likewise Open Active Directory integration products moved to BeyondTrust. Backed by Trinity Ventures, the company was acquired and no longer operates: there is no live website, developer portal, documentation or public API, and the likewise.com domain now redirects to an unrelated owner.

providers.name: Lilium
providers.description: Lilium was a German eVTOL aircraft developer building the Lilium Jet, a seven-seat (including pilot) ducted-fan electric jet designed for regional air mobility with target cruise speeds around 175 mph and ranges in excess of 100 nautical miles. Lilium pursued concurrent EASA and FAA Type Certification and signed pre-orders with operators across Europe, the Middle East, the United States, Brazil, and Saudi Arabia. In October 2024 Lilium's board approved self-administration for its German subsidiaries after failing to secure a guarantee for a EUR 50 million Bavarian government loan, and in December 2024 the company ceased operations and laid off approximately 1,000 employees. A consortium called Mobile Uplift Corporation GmbH announced a partial asset acquisition in late December 2024, but in February 2025 Lilium's German entities filed a second insolvency after the promised takeover financing failed to materialize. As of this profile (May 2026) Lilium remains non-operational and the website and social channels may be intermittently available; this profile is preserved for historical and archival reference.

providers.name: Limbo Labs (limbolabs.com)
providers.description: Limbo Labs was, in its own words, "a small technical team in san francisco" whose products were to "begin launching in july 2010". The company surfaced in the 500 Global portfolio listing and was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no company to enrich: limbolabs.com carried a single-page placeholder from 2010 through roughly 2015 and never grew past it — an Internet Archive enumeration of the domain returns only eleven distinct captured URLs, all of them the one landing page plus its stylesheets, jQuery and four images. No product, developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or Swagger document, SDK or machine-readable specification was ever published or archived. By 2018 the domain served a JavaScript-wall parking page, and it now redirects to an Afternic "for sale" lander, so the brand is retired. The website URL carried on the inbound 500 Global portfolio record, readyforzero.com, is a mis-joined row: it belongs to ReadyForZero, a separate 500 Global personal-finance company, and it no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record with no active API surface.

providers.name: Linen App
providers.description: Linen Wallet, operated by Linen Mobile, Inc., was a mobile self-custody cryptocurrency wallet that used multi-signature protection built on Safe (formerly Gnosis Safe) smart-contract accounts instead of the single seed phrase used by most wallets. It began as a DeFi savings wallet earning yield on stablecoins through Compound, later adding Ethereum staking and Polygon support, and grew out of Bloqboard, a non-custodial digital-asset lending platform built on the Dharma, Compound and MakerDAO protocols. Linen was backed by Polychain, Coinbase Ventures, HashKey and Wyre, and won Aave and Polygon grants. The product is discontinued — since late 2023 every path on linen.app has returned a site-wide redirect to a single X post, and no documentation, developer portal, API or specification was ever published publicly. See lifecycle/linen-app-lifecycle.yml for the probed wind-down evidence.

providers.name: Link A Media
providers.description: Link_A_Media Devices (LAMD) was a privately-held fabless semiconductor company founded in March 2004 by storage industry veterans and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It built signal-processing and data-recovery technology — read channels, error correction and System-on-Chip blocks — that storage OEMs combined with their own proprietary logic to build custom controller SoCs for hard disk drives and NAND flash. Its product lines were MagLINK (magnetic/HDD) and FlashLINK (NAND/SSD), sold as IP and silicon to drive manufacturers rather than as a developer-facing service. The company targeted higher areal density, lower cost per gigabyte, improved drive robustness and higher manufacturing yields. LAMD is no longer an operating independent company: its website was live through January 2013 and the domain is today a parked for-sale listing. It never published a public API, developer portal, or SDK, so there is no API surface for the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline to capture.

providers.name: Listrunner
providers.description: Listrunner was a HIPAA-compliant clinical collaboration platform that let hospital care teams build and share living patient lists. Marketed as "a collaboration platform for clinicians," it targeted specialty practices, residency programs, hospital departments, and outpatient teams with shared sign-out/handoff lists, faster rounding, coordinated discharge tracking, task assignment, real-time lab and clinical data access, EHR integration, printable rounding lists, fully customizable per-team list fields, administrator-controlled user permissions and data access, audit logs and reporting, and a robust offline mode across web plus native iOS and Android apps. Listrunner no longer operates as an independent product: its brand domains listrunner.health and listrunnerapp.com are now served from Cloudflare and redirect (301 then 307) to commure.com, the healthcare-infrastructure company that merged with Athelas. The last archived standalone Listrunner homepage is from 2021-06-04. Listrunner never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or package; it is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical health-tech identity record and a pointer to its successor surface at Commure/Athelas, not as an API provider.

providers.name: Little Eye
providers.description: Little Eye was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment found no active API surface at littleeye.co. The historical "Little Eye Labs" was an Indian startup building performance analysis and monitoring tools for Android applications that was acquired by Facebook in January 2014 and is defunct; the littleeye.co domain has since been re-registered and now hosts an unrelated Arabic-language technology news, tutorials, and device-review blog with no developer platform, API, docs, SDKs, or webhooks.

providers.name: Local Bushel
providers.description: Local Bushel is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global, battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the company appears defunct - its domain localbushel.com no longer hosts a website and is listed for sale on HugeDomains. No developer portal, documentation, or API surface could be found.

providers.name: Local Motors
providers.description: Local Motors was an American vehicle manufacturer founded in 2007 by John "Jay" Rogers Jr. that built vehicles through open co-creation and distributed "microfactories" rather than conventional mass production. Its community designed and the company produced the Rally Fighter off-road car from its first Chandler, Arizona microfactory, the Strati — the first car to be 3D-printed live, in 44 hours at IMTS 2014 — and, from 2016, Olli, a 3D-printed electric autonomous shuttle whose conversational passenger interface ran on IBM Watson and which was piloted at National Harbor, Maryland and other campus and transit sites. The company operated microfactories in Chandler, Knoxville and National Harbor and spun its crowdsourcing community out as Launch Forth. Local Motors ceased operations in January 2022 after fifteen years, having failed to raise further capital, and its intellectual-property portfolio was acquired by drone manufacturer RapidFlight of Manassas, Virginia in July 2023. Local Motors never operated a public developer program: the archive of localmotors.com holds an internal django-tastypie JSON API under /api/v1/ that served the co-creation community website, but no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification was ever published, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The domain is no longer the company's — it now answers HTTP 301 on every path to a third-party affiliate article — so there is no live API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: lockitron
providers.description: Lockitron was a smart-lock startup (Bluetooth/Wi-Fi keyless entry, the Lockitron Bolt) that offered an open web API at api.lockitron.com and integrations with IFTTT, Pebble, Nest and others. It was acquired by Chamberlain Group in 2019 and its service and developer API were shut down on 2020-06-17; Bolt devices moved to Chamberlain's myQ platform. The company is defunct and its domain (lockitron.com) is parked with no live web or API surface. Surfaced as a slow-ventures portfolio lead.

providers.name: LogicLoop
providers.description: LogicLoop was a low-code / no-code operations-automation platform that let non-engineering teams write SQL-based business rules on top of their company data to trigger alerts, reviews, and automated actions for use cases like fraud and risk monitoring, logistics, and customer onboarding. Founded in 2021 by Jesika Haria and Jackie Xu, it raised roughly $4.5M from Accel and First Round Capital, offered an AI SQL Copilot (plain-English-to-SQL) and a REST API for managing rules, schedules, notifications, and embedded dashboards. LogicLoop was acquired by Hummingbird (risk and compliance) on 2024-09-18; its website (www.logicloop.com), docs (docs.logicloop.com), and API hosts no longer resolve, so no live API surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: LogicNow
providers.description: LogicNow (styled LOGICnow) was a global provider of integrated, cloud-based IT service management (ITSM) software for managed service providers (MSPs), best known for its MAX product suite — MAX Remote Management (RMM), MAX Backup & Disaster Recovery, MAX Mail, MAX Risk Intelligence and MAX Service Desk. On June 1, 2016 LOGICnow was acquired by SolarWinds and merged with SolarWinds N-able to form SolarWinds MSP, later spun out as the independent public company N-able. LogicNow no longer operates as an independent entity: its logicnow.com domain no longer serves a website (NXDOMAIN, MX only, handled by n-able.com) and it publishes no independent developer or API surface.

providers.name: Loku
providers.description: Loku was a travel and local-experiences recommendation startup, founded around 2010, that provided personalized recommendations from local experts. The company raised roughly $2.1M in seed funding and was acquired by Groupon in July 2013, after which the product was shut down. Loku is no longer an operating company. Its former domain, loku.com, no longer hosts a product and now redirects to an Afternic "domain for sale" listing. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; enrichment confirms there is no live API, developer portal, documentation, or product surface to catalog.

providers.name: Looking Glass Networks
providers.description: Looking Glass Networks, Inc. was a facilities-based telecommunications carrier founded in 2000 and headquartered in Oak Brook, Illinois. It built, owned, and operated metropolitan fiber-optic networks (approximately 2,000 route miles across 14 major U.S. metro markets, serving roughly 215 buildings), providing SONET/SDH, wavelength, and Ethernet data-transport services along with dark fiber and carrier-neutral colocation. Backed by Battery Ventures and Madison Dearborn Partners, the company was acquired by Level 3 Communications on August 2, 2006 and no longer operates independently. It exposes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Looly's
providers.description: Looly's PBC (doing business as WeTheTrillions) was a San Francisco public benefit corporation founded in 2013 by Lamiaa Bounahmidi that reengineered preventative healthcare through microbiome science, evidence-based clinical research, telemedicine, and plant-based food. It delivered fresh, ready-to-eat plant-based meal and snack bundles targeted at chronic conditions such as IBS/SIBO, diabetes and PCOS, plus a fertility program. Backed by 500 Global and part of the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead, the company is a consumer food and health business with no public API surface. Its primary domain (wethetrillions.com) no longer resolves and the venture appears to be defunct/deadpooled.

providers.name: Loop Crypto
providers.description: Loop Crypto is a crypto and stablecoin payment processor that lets merchants, billing software, and e-commerce platforms accept crypto and stablecoin payments end to end: charging a wallet, storing payment methods, accepting stablecoins, ERC-20 tokens, and Solana SPL tokens, and settling to merchants in either fiat or crypto. Loop offers payment links, an embeddable Pay/PayIn checkout component, a white-labelable Connect widget, and a REST API (v1/v2, api-key + entity-id header auth) covering customers, entities, merchants, tokens, payments, payouts, and webhooks, plus out-of-the-box integrations with Stripe, Chargebee, and OpenPay. Backed by a16z. NOTE: Loop is winding down and folding into Lead; the service was sunset on 2026-02-13 and is not recommended for new integrations.

providers.name: Loose Cubes
providers.description: Loosecubes, Inc. was a membership-based marketplace often described as the "Airbnb for shared office space" — it connected people looking for a place to work with companies that had vacant desks and coworking space. Founded in 2010 in Brooklyn, New York by Campbell McKellar (Walmsley) and Anna Thomas, it raised roughly $9M total, including a $7.8M Series A led by New Enterprise Associates with Revolution Ventures and Battery Ventures participating. The company shut down and permanently closed in late 2012. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead; enrichment found no live API surface — the business is defunct and the loosecubes.com domain is now held by an unrelated owner.

providers.name: Lowkey
providers.description: Lowkey (lowkey.gg) was a San Francisco social gaming platform that let players automatically record, review, and share their gameplay highlight clips across titles like League of Legends, VALORANT, and Among Us. Backed by Y Combinator and an a16z Series A, the company was acquired by Niantic (the developer of Pokemon GO) and the consumer product was subsequently discontinued. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no live public developer surface: the lowkey.gg domain no longer resolves/serves, and there is no public API, OpenAPI, documentation portal, SDK, or MCP server to harvest.

providers.name: LSI Logic
providers.description: LSI Logic Corporation was an American semiconductor company known for application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), custom system-on-chip designs, and storage/RAID controller silicon. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. The company was acquired by Avago Technologies in 2014 and its assets are now part of Broadcom; its former lsi.com domain redirects to broadcom.com. LSI Logic operates no independent public developer API program.

providers.name: Luvocracy *
providers.description: Luvocracy was a social-shopping and recommendation marketplace where people discovered, shared, and bought products curated by friends and trusted tastemakers, with the service handling the purchasing on the buyer's behalf. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) and Kleiner Perkins, the company was acquired by @WalmartLabs in 2014 and subsequently wound down; its website (luvocracy.com) now serves an archived static page announcing the acquisition. No developer program, public API, or SDK was ever published, and none exists today. This profile is retained as a network record of a defunct consumer startup. Sector: consumer / social commerce.

providers.name: Lynda.com
providers.description: Lynda.com was an online video learning platform founded in 1995 by Lynda Weinman and Bruce Heavin, offering courses in software, creative, and business skills. LinkedIn acquired Lynda.com in 2015 (~$1.5B) and folded it into LinkedIn Learning; the standalone Lynda.com service has been retired and www.lynda.com now 301-redirects to linkedin.com/learning. The brand exposes no public developer program or API surface of its own. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and enriched as a lead; the honest result is a defunct brand with no first-party API.

providers.name: Lytmus
providers.description: Lytmus was a technical-interview and coding-assessment platform for hiring engineers. Candidates worked live in a browser-based, fully functional Ubuntu virtual machine (Terminal, editors, Chrome) so recruiters could run pair-programming phone screens and evaluate real coding skills across languages and full-stack scenarios, priced in per-session plans. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment probing (2026-07-20) found no developer portal, API, documentation, or ./.well-known surface; the company was acquired by GitHub in 2019 and its product has since been shut down, so lytmus.io now serves stale content and lytmus.com is a parked, for-sale domain. No API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Lytro
providers.description: Lytro was a light-field (plenoptic) imaging company founded in 2006 by Ren Ng and based in Mountain View, California. It shipped the first consumer light-field cameras (the Lytro and the Lytro Illum), which captured the entire light field so images could be refocused after the fact, and later pivoted to professional light-field capture for cinema and VR with Lytro Cinema and Lytro Immerge. Backed by a16z, Greylock, NEA and Qualcomm Ventures, the company wound down in March 2018 with much of its technology and talent moving to Google. It is defunct and publishes no public developer program or API; the lytro.com domain now 301-redirects to an unrelated light-field vendor (raytrix.de).

providers.name: Makani *
providers.description: Makani was an Alphabet (Google X) moonshot developing airborne wind energy — "energy kites" that flew in crosswind loops to generate electricity and sent power to the grid down a tether. Backed within Alphabet and partnered with Shell, Makani wound down in 2020 after roughly 13 years of development. On closure the team open-sourced its full flight-simulation, autopilot controller, visualization, and avionics software stack under Apache-2.0 and published the Energy Kite Collection of technical reports, designs, and flight logs. Makani has no commercial or developer API surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company for network completeness.

providers.name: Makeably
providers.description: Makeably was an online marketplace for custom-made and handmade goods (apparel, jewelry, furniture, household items, wedding and arts products), later pivoting to a "remixes" model that let shoppers request variations of reference products rather than fully bespoke commissions. It raised roughly $650K in seed funding in 2013 from Great Oaks Venture Capital, 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and others. The company appears to be defunct — its domain no longer resolves and no developer or API surface exists. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub.

providers.name: Makelog
providers.description: Makelog was a product changelog and release-notes platform that helped software and product teams collect, curate, and publish product updates to communicate releases with customers and internal stakeholders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment (sector: productivity). As of this enrichment pass the makelog.com domain no longer resolves (DNS NXDOMAIN) and no live web, developer, or API surface could be reached, indicating the product has been discontinued.

providers.name: Maker Comms
providers.description: Maker Communications was an early networking-silicon company that designed high-performance programmable communications processors and related software for ATM and Internet Protocol data, voice, and video networks. Founded in 1994 and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (early investment in 1997, Barry Eggers), the company went public in 1999 on NASDAQ under the ticker MAKR and was acquired by Conexant Systems (NASDAQ CNXT) in 2000. It exists in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it is a defunct, fully-exited hardware/semiconductor company with no surviving public developer program, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: MaxPoint
providers.description: MaxPoint (MaxPoint Interactive, Inc.) was a Morrisville, North Carolina marketing technology company that built a hyperlocal programmatic advertising platform, matching neighborhood-level ("Digital Zip") consumer intelligence to online media buys so brands and retailers could tie digital advertising to in-store sales. It was funded by Trinity Ventures among others, went public on the NYSE as MXPT in March 2015, and was acquired by Valassis Communications in August 2017 for roughly $95 million, where it was folded into Valassis Digital. Valassis was later unified under the Vericast brand, which divested its adtech business in 2024. MaxPoint no longer operates as an independent company or product line: maxpoint.com and maxpointinteractive.com are dead hosts returning HTTP 403 on every path with a mismatched TLS certificate, api./developer./docs.maxpoint.com do not resolve, the github.com/maxpoint organization is empty and forwards to a handle now owned by an unrelated company, and valassisdigital.com is NXDOMAIN. There is no public API, developer program, or machine-readable contract to profile.

providers.name: MCA Solutions
providers.description: MCA Solutions was a service parts planning and optimization software company founded in 1999 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Its Service Planning and Optimization (SPO) suite helped aerospace and defense, high-tech, and capital-equipment firms reduce spare-parts inventory, lower support costs, and improve service levels across the service supply chain. Backed by Battery Ventures and Longworth Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Marlin Equity Partners in March 2012 and merged into Servigistics (later part of PTC). It no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: Mech Mocha
providers.description: Mech Mocha is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: mobile. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Medbelle
providers.description: Medbelle was a London-headquartered digital healthcare company, founded in 2016 by Leander de Laporte and Daniel Kolb, that operated as a "digital hospital" coordinating elective specialist care across the UK. It combined a technology platform (marketed as Medbelle OS, with a CareConnect virtual-first assessment pathway) with human Patient Care Advisers to route patients through consultation, diagnostics, surgery and aftercare, working with clinicians, hospitals, insurers, employers and case managers. Specialties spanned cosmetic, bariatric, orthopaedic and ophthalmic surgery. Medbelle ceased trading in 2026 and its technology platform was transferred elsewhere; medbelle.com now serves a single farewell page and every other path on the domain returns 404. No public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract was ever published, and none survives.

providers.name: Mediapassage.com
providers.description: Mediapassage.com is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: MediaSpike
providers.description: MediaSpike was an AdTech startup founded in 2011 by Blake Commagere and headquartered in Mountain View, California, that built a native monetization platform for dynamic, programmatic product placement inside social, mobile, and virtual-reality games. Its API let game developers surface contextual in-game sponsorships and brand placements, and the network reportedly reached roughly 20 million unique users at its peak. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Google Ventures, CMEA Capital, 500 Startups, and others (a $5.2M Series A in November 2013), the company ceased operations around June 2017. mediaspike.com no longer hosts the product and currently serves only a "coming soon" placeholder; no live API, developer portal, or discovery surface remains.

providers.name: Medly Pharmacy
providers.description: Medly Pharmacy (Medly Health Inc.) was a Brooklyn, New York digital pharmacy founded in 2017 by Marg Patel, a second-generation pharmacist. It operated a hybrid model — physical retail pharmacy locations paired with free same-day prescription delivery — supported by a consumer mobile app for refills, prescription status and pharmacist chat, and a prescriber-facing e-prescribing workflow it marketed to physician practices. The company raised a $100M Series B in July 2020, expanded into several US metros, and in 2021 acquired the health-and-wellness retailer Pharmaca. It never published a developer program, public API, SDK, machine-readable specification or partner integration reference; the platform was an internal product, not a product sold to developers. Medly Health filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 9 December 2022 along with 31 affiliates, agreed on 9 February 2023 to sell its remaining prescription files, inventory and intellectual property to Walgreens for $19.35M, wound down all retail and e-commerce operations by 31 March 2023, and converted to a Chapter 7 liquidation on 26 April 2023. In September 2024 the SEC charged three former executives, including the founder, in connection with the company's capital raises. The medly.com domain is now controlled by the acquirer and blanket-redirects every path to walgreens.com. What survives publicly is the company's engineering open source — the GitHub `medly` organization and its npm and Maven Central packages — none of which is an API client. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Medrobotics
providers.description: Medrobotics Corporation was a Raynham, Massachusetts surgical robotics manufacturer, founded as CardioRobotics, that built the Flex Robotic System — an articulating, steerable robotic endoscope platform cleared by the FDA in 2015 and CE-marked for minimally invasive procedures in otolaryngology, colorectal surgery and gastroenterology, and deployed at roughly thirty hospitals worldwide. The company was a medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: its product was an operating-room capital robot and its single-use accessories, and it never operated a developer program, a public API, an SDK or a developer portal. Medrobotics filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Massachusetts on 2022-01-24 (case 1:22-bk-10077), following judgments in the Endobotics litigation, and in June 2024 the Chapter 7 trustee liquidated the entire 40,000-square-foot Raynham plant at auction — 23 complete Flex and Flex360 systems plus roughly 22 terabytes of technical specifications, customer lists and other intellectual property. The company is defunct. Its domain, medrobotics.com, is now a parked page served by a domain-parking network and its registry nameservers are NS1/NS2.PENDINGRENEWALDELETION.COM. This profile is retained as an honest zero: there is no API surface to catalog, and there never was one.

providers.name: Mem Protocol
providers.description: Mem Protocol (mem.so) was a San Francisco based startup, founded in 2021, building tools for the social layer of web3 - a decentralized social-media protocol focused on user data sovereignty, portable social graphs, and verifiable on-chain identity. The company raised a ~$3.1M seed round in 2021 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z crypto), with participation from Balaji Srinivasan and Polychain's Olaf Carlson-Wee. As of this enrichment pass the project appears dormant/defunct - the official domain mem.so resolves only to a parking IP and times out, and the alternate domain memprotocol.xyz redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page. No live website, developer portal, API documentation, GitHub organization, SDK packages, or public API surface could be found. This profile remains an identity-only company record; there is nothing to enrich beyond the historical facts below.

providers.name: Meridian Data
providers.description: Meridian Data, Inc. was a Battery Ventures-backed maker of network-attached storage (NAS) appliances, best known for the Snap! Server workgroup NAS line and one of the industry's first storage operating systems for entry- and workgroup-level appliances. Quantum Corporation acquired Meridian Data in a stock swap valued at roughly $85M, completed June 1, 1999, folding its technology into Quantum's storage systems strategy. The company has not operated independently since and publishes no current developer or API surface; this profile is retained for API Evangelist network completeness as a historical, acquired entity.

providers.name: merXu
providers.description: merXu is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, point-nine, prosus-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ecommerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: MessageMe *
providers.description: MessageMe was a mobile messaging application built to explore expressive, fun online communication, and a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) in the consumer sector. The MessageMe team was acquired by Yahoo, and the product was shut down: users could access messages until November 7, 2014, after which accounts and personal information were erased. The messageme.com domain now serves only the shutdown announcement. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 confirmed the company is defunct with no live API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or event surface to catalog.

providers.name: Metacrine
providers.description: Metacrine, Inc. was a San Diego, California clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 to develop differentiated therapies for liver and gastrointestinal disease. It built a proprietary farnesoid X receptor (FXR) platform on a distinct chemical scaffold and advanced two oral, once-daily FXR agonists — MET409 and MET642 — through Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials in non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), alongside exploratory work in inflammatory bowel disease. Backed by ARCH Venture Partners, Polaris Partners, venBio and EcoR1 Capital, it raised a $36M round in 2015 and a $65M Series C in June 2018 before pricing an initial public offering on 2020-09-15 of 6,540,000 shares at $13.00, for roughly $85.0M gross, and listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market as MTCR. Equillium, Inc. agreed to acquire the company in an all-stock transaction announced 2022-09-06, but the two mutually terminated the merger agreement on 2022-12-23. The board approved a Plan of Dissolution on 2023-01-24; Nasdaq issued a minimum-bid-price delisting notice on 2023-01-31, trading was suspended on 2023-02-09 and delisting took effect 2023-03-13; the FXR program assets were sold under a February 2023 term sheet for up to $4.0M in cash plus assumed liabilities; stockholders approved the dissolution on 2023-03-23; and the company filed a Certificate of Dissolution with the Delaware Secretary of State on 2023-03-24, effective on filing under DGCL Section 275. Metacrine was a drug developer, not a software vendor, and it never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification of any kind. Its domain metacrine.com has since lapsed and is parked. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Metamarkets
providers.description: Metamarkets built a real-time analytics platform for the programmatic advertising industry, giving ad exchanges, DSPs, SSPs, and publishers an interactive dashboard over billions of daily bid, impression, and spend events. Its Real-Time Data Ingestion (RDI) platform ingests well-formatted, standards-based ad-tech event data (adhering to OpenRTB 2.5, IAB guidelines, and ISO date/country/language/currency standards) over an authenticated HTTPS streaming endpoint and surfaces it in the Metamarkets dashboard within seconds for querying and analysis. Metamarkets was acquired by Snap Inc. in 2017; the primary metamarkets.com site is now defunct, but the legacy developer documentation for the RDI platform remains live at docs.metamarkets.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: MicroByre
providers.description: MicroByre was a Berkeley, California synthetic biology company founded in 2017 by CEO and co-founder Sarah Richardson to "domesticate" wild-type bacteria — building an automated characterization and genetic-tool pipeline that made naturally occurring, never-before-engineered microbes tractable so they could ferment unrefined waste biomass into commodity chemicals, enzymes, food ingredients and probiotics at costs petrochemical routes could not match. It raised roughly $20.5M, including backing from Prime Coalition's Prime Impact Fund, and went out of business; Prime Coalition lists it as "no longer active" and C&EN reported the shutdown. MicroByre was a wet-lab platform company, not a software vendor: it published no developer program, no API, and no machine-readable contract, and its own domain no longer resolves to a web server.

providers.name: Microsoft Bing
providers.description: Microsoft Bing provides a comprehensive suite of search APIs that enable developers to integrate web, image, video, news, entity, and visual search capabilities into their applications. These APIs are part of Azure AI Services and provide intelligent search experiences powered by Bing's web-scale index.

providers.name: Mightytv
providers.description: Mightytv is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Milk *
providers.description: Milk, Inc. was a mobile application development lab founded in 2011 by Kevin Rose, Daniel Burka, and Jeff Hodsdon, and backed by GV (Google Ventures). Its only shipped product was Oink, an app for rating and discovering real-world things. Milk shut down Oink in early 2012 and the product team was acqui-hired by Google in March 2012, after which the company ceased to exist. It is defunct with no active website, developer portal, SDKs, or public API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; enrichment confirmed there is no API to catalog.

providers.name: Millennial Media
providers.description: Millennial Media was a mobile advertising / adtech company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The enrichment probe (2026-07-20) found the company is defunct: millennialmedia.com now CNAMEs to rc.yahoo.com via AWS Global Accelerator on oath.cloud (Yahoo / Verizon Media / Oath infrastructure, consistent with the AOL acquisition of Millennial Media), and every host returns HTTP 404. There is no independent millennial-media developer portal, API, developer.* or api.* subdomain (NXDOMAIN), and no /.well-known/ or /llms.txt discovery surface. No API artifacts exist to enrich; this record is retained as a historical/company lead only.

providers.name: MindSumo
providers.description: MindSumo was a crowdsourcing and open-innovation platform that connected companies with a community of students and young professionals to solve time-boxed business challenges for monetary prizes, generating ideas, market insight, and hiring leads. A GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company later acquired by MBO Partners, the platform distributed over $1.3M in rewards across 1,300+ challenges in 200+ countries before being permanently shut down after 13 years of operation. MindSumo never published a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile records its identity and the residual public web properties (terms, privacy) that remain live.

providers.name: Misfit
providers.description: Misfit is a consumer wearables brand — fitness trackers and smartwatches such as the Misfit Shine, Flash, Ray and Vapor — founded in 2011 by Sonny Vu, John Sculley and Sridhar Iyengar and backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, GGV Capital and Xiaomi before being acquired by Fossil Group in 2015. Misfit ran a developer program (the Misfit Cloud API, Device SDK and Scientific Library) at build.misfit.com with 30+ launch partners. Fossil discontinued the Misfit backend, Cloud API and companion app in spring 2023, so the hosted API and all misfit.com domains are now unreachable. The only surviving developer surface is the official Misfit-Developers GitHub organization and its unmaintained iOS SDKs on CocoaPods.

providers.name: Mitro *
providers.description: Mitro was a password manager for individuals and teams, founded in 2012 in New York City by Vijay Pandurangan, Evan Jones, and Adam Hilss (former Google/Serious Eats engineers). It let multiple people securely share and control logins to a single account, architected around cloud storage with password databases encrypted client-side using keys derived from the user master password. Mitro raised $1.2M in seed funding from Google Ventures (GV) and Matrix Partners. On July 31, 2014 the team joined Twitter and released the Mitro source code on GitHub as free software under the GPL. The hosted Mitro service shut down on October 6, 2015; its open-source successor is Passopolis. The company is defunct and publishes no live API, developer portal, or reachable domain today.

providers.name: Mixer Labs
providers.description: Mixer Labs was a San Francisco startup, backed by Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC), best known for building GeoAPI, a geolocation and geodata web API that let developers resolve places, points of interest, and location context from coordinates. The company was acquired by Twitter in December 2009, where its technology and team (co-founders Elad Gil and Othman Laraki) went on to power Twitter's location and geo features. Mixer Labs no longer operates as an independent company, its mixerlabs.com domain no longer resolves, and it publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface today. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record rather than an active provider awaiting enrichment.

providers.name: Mobcrush
providers.description: Mobcrush Streaming, Inc. was a Santa Monica, California live-streaming technology company, founded in 2013 by Royce Disini with James Hurley, Travis Rogers and Stephen Dao, that made it possible for mobile gamers to broadcast gameplay straight from an iOS or Android device with no capture card, no desktop encoder and no third-party software. Its differentiator was simulcast: a creator went live once and Mobcrush relayed the same broadcast simultaneously to Twitch, YouTube, Facebook, Twitter and Periscope at no extra charge, which turned the product from a competing destination into distribution infrastructure for creators who already had audiences elsewhere. The company added an advertising and sponsorship layer in 2018 ("Go Live, Get Paid") and operated Mineville, one of six official Minecraft server partners under agreement with Microsoft, reaching more than twenty million players a year. It raised roughly $35.9M across its rounds, including an $11M Series A in September 2015 led by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and a $20M round in 2016, with First Round Capital and Lowercase Capital also participating. Super League Gaming announced its acquisition of Mobcrush on 11 March 2021 and closed it on 2 June 2021 for approximately 12.6 million shares of common stock; the acquirer now trades as Super League Enterprise, Inc. and does not carry the Mobcrush brand forward as a product. Mobcrush ran a JSON web API at www.mobcrush.com/api/ that backed its own site and mobile apps, but it never published a developer portal, an API reference, a first-party SDK or any machine-readable specification, so there is no public API surface to catalog — and the mobcrush.com domain, while still registered, no longer resolves at all. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: MommaZoo
providers.description: MommaZoo was a mobile web application for parent-teacher and school-community communication, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Built as an HTML5 cross-platform app, it let parents and teachers centralize class posts, homework, sign-ups, reminders, documents, and multi-channel messaging across devices and languages. The company is defunct - public activity ends around 2013 and the mommazoo.com domain is now parked - and an enrichment pass found no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: Monedo
providers.description: Monedo, founded in Hamburg in 2012 as Kreditech and renamed Monedo in March 2020, was a German online consumer lender that underwrote short-term and installment credit in Poland, Spain, Russia, Romania, India and Mexico using a self-learning machine-learning scoring engine over thousands of alternative data points instead of traditional bureau scores. Backed by Peter Thiel, J.C. Flowers and Naspers, it was valued above EUR 230m in 2017. It marketed a business-facing Lending-as-a-Service / Credit-as-a-Service partner API that let retailers, telcos, banks and payment providers embed its credit products and point-of-sale financing, but that surface was sales-gated for its whole life: the company never operated a public developer portal, never published a reference, and never published a machine-readable contract. Monedo filed for insolvency in a Hamburg court in September 2020 and ceased operations in December 2020. Both monedo.com and kreditech.com lapsed and were re-registered by unrelated parties in 2022 - monedo.com is now a GoDaddy aftermarket listing offered for sale - so no company-controlled web or API surface remains.

providers.name: Moonfish
providers.description: Moonfish is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: MoPub
providers.description: MoPub was a mobile advertising and app-monetization platform providing ad-network mediation, advanced bidding, and a real-time marketplace/exchange plus open-source iOS and Android SDKs for mobile publishers. Founded in 2010, it was acquired by Twitter in 2013, then sold to AppLovin for $1.05B in a deal that closed January 2022. AppLovin migrated publishers to its MAX platform and shut down MoPub's mediation, advanced bidding, and marketplace on 2022-03-31, with dashboard/reporting retired by 2022-04-30. MoPub is now defunct: www.mopub.com redirects to applovin.com and the developer/API surface (developers.mopub.com) is offline. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct record; there is no live MoPub API to enrich.

providers.name: Morta Security
providers.description: Morta Security was a stealth-mode cybersecurity startup founded in 2012 by a team with backgrounds in threat intelligence and protecting national critical infrastructure (widely reported as ex-NSA engineers). The company was building a new paradigm for detecting and countering advanced, targeted cyber threats. Morta raised roughly $1.9M in venture funding from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), DCVC (Data Collective), Greylock, Norwest, and Wing Venture Capital, and was acquired by Palo Alto Networks (NYSE: PANW) in 2013-2014, where its technology and team were folded into Palo Alto's threat-detection products. Morta Security no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio record; enrichment found no API artifacts.

providers.name: Motion Math
providers.description: Motion Math was an educational math-games company (500 Global portfolio) whose products were acquired by Curriculum Associates and folded into the i-Ready learning platform. As of the enrichment probe (2026-07-20) the motionmathgames.com domain and every subdomain (developer/api/docs) return a 301 redirect to curriculumassociates.com/products/i-ready/i-ready-learning/motionmath-shutdown, and the site shares a wildcard TLS certificate with i-ready.com. The company publishes no independent API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface — this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct/acquired provider with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Mountaintop.gg
providers.description: Mountaintop (Mountaintop.gg) was a remote-first independent video game studio founded in 2020 by veterans of Blizzard, Respawn, Riot, and Bungie, led by Oculus co-founder Nate Mitchell. Backed by a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), the studio built Spectre Divide, a free-to-play 3v3 tactical PvP shooter featuring its signature "Duality" two-body mechanic. The game launched in 2024, but the studio wound down and Spectre Divide's online services were shut down in 2025. Mountaintop is a consumer game studio, not an API provider, and publishes no developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and its public web and support surfaces are now offline. It remains cataloged in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company with no active API surface.

providers.name: Movielala
providers.description: MovieLaLa Inc was a San Francisco movie-discovery and social-video startup (500 Global portfolio, founded 2012) best known for its GIF maker and a MovieLaLa Video Player. The only developer surface it ever published was a client-side JavaScript embed API for that player (a drop-in replacement for the YouTube IFrame API, loaded from assets-embed.movielala.com), documented in the github.com/movielala GitHub org. The company is now defunct — its last public code activity was 2016 and the gif-maker repo redirects to gifmaker.io. The movielala.com domain has lapsed and is currently repurposed by an unrelated third party (an Indonesian gambling site), so it no longer represents the company and is not wired as a website here. No REST/OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or hosted API surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Movivo
providers.description: Movivo was a London-based mobile rewards startup (500 Startups / Distro Dojo, HQ London) whose consumer app let users cover the cost of their mobile airtime and data by completing surveys, crowdsourced micro-tasks, and app installs, working with mobile operators across emerging markets. The company was surfaced as a portfolio lead of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct — movivo.com resolves to a parked GoDaddy for-sale domain, and no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or GitHub organization could be found. This profile is retained as a network record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Moxion Power Co
providers.description: Moxion Power Co is a mobile energy storage company (a Y Combinator alum) that builds trailer-mounted, zero-emission Mobile Power Units (MPUs) used as quiet, clean replacements for diesel generators on construction sites, film productions, events, and grid-support jobs. Moxion operated a REST Developer API that let fleet operators fetch device metadata, real-time GPS location, and time-series telemetry (state of charge, pack voltage, net/output power, energy available/capacity, cellular signal) for their Mobile Power Units, along with active fault codes. The API additionally exposed AEMP 2.0 (ISO 15143-3 v.20190501) compliant fleet-snapshot endpoints so telematics platforms could ingest Moxion equipment alongside other heavy-equipment fleets. Authentication used bearer tokens issued to Service Accounts. Note the company filed for bankruptcy in August 2024; the developer documentation remains online but the API host may no longer be operational.

providers.name: Mporium
providers.description: Mporium (Mporium Group plc, formerly MoPowered) was a London-based, "mobile first" data-driven marketing and advertising-technology company founded in 2012. Its proprietary IMPACT platform delivered software-as-a-service that helped agencies and advertisers identify and act on consumer "micro-moments" across search, social, and display media, reacting to real-time signals from TV, news feeds, sports, financial data, and social media to optimise ad pricing, timing, and selection. The group also acquired the digital agency Fast Web Media. Mporium was a portfolio company of the fintech venture firm Anthemis and was previously listed on the London Stock Exchange. The company is now defunct: it has been delisted, publishes no developer portal or public API, and its primary domain (mporium.com) is parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Mr. Draper
providers.description: Mr. Draper is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: MRU
providers.description: MRU Holdings, Inc. (operating as MyRichUncle) was a specialty education-finance company founded in 2001 and headquartered in New York that became one of the largest private student-loan providers in the United States. It ceased offering student-loan products in September 2008 and filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in February 2009. Battery Ventures participated in the company's 2005 PIPE financing. The company is defunct and publishes no live website, public API, or developer surface.

providers.name: mSpot
providers.description: mSpot was a mobile cloud-based content service provider founded in 2004 by Daren Tsui (CEO) and Ed Ho (CTO) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company offered a cloud music locker that let users upload their music library and stream it from PCs, Macs, iPhone, iPad and Android devices, alongside a full-length movie rental service with content deals across Sony, Disney, Paramount, NBC/Universal, Lionsgate, Warner and others. mSpot raised roughly $2.3M in venture funding from Trinity Ventures and was acquired by Samsung Electronics in May 2012 (reported ~$8.8M) to power the Samsung Music Hub. The standalone mSpot product and brand were subsequently wound down and folded into Samsung; there is no active mSpot developer portal, API, or product surface today. This profile is retained as a historical network record.
