Piestro shut down in January 2025 without shipping a production unit. It is a hardware and food-service company, not a software vendor: it never ran a developer program, and no public API, SDK, webhook, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind was ever published. This profile records that absence rather than inventing a surface.

providers.name: Pilota
providers.description: Pilota is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Pine Medical
providers.description: Pine Medical was a telehealth provider that offered a medication-supported weight-loss program pairing licensed clinicians with prescription therapies and ongoing patient coaching. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment probe on 2026-07-20 found the public website (pinemedical.com) announcing that Pine Medical wound down its medication-supported weight-loss program effective March 30, 2024, and redirects former patients to alternative providers and insurance-covered options. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found.

providers.name: Pipelinedb
providers.description: PipelineDB was a high-performance PostgreSQL extension for continuous, incremental aggregation of time-series data using continuous SQL views, avoiding the need to store raw event data. It also offered Stride, a hosted streaming-analytics API with first-party Python, JavaScript, and Go client SDKs, plus extensions for Apache Kafka and Amazon Kinesis ingestion. The company joined Confluent in 2019; the open-source extension reached a final 1.0.0 release (Apache-2.0) and is now archived, while the pipelinedb.com website and the hosted Stride service have been retired. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCVC.

providers.name: Pixate
providers.description: Pixate was a code-free, drag-and-drop mobile prototyping platform that let designers build sophisticated, fluid interactive prototypes running natively on iOS and Android devices. Founded as an interaction-design startup and backed by a16z, Pixate was acquired by Google in July 2015 and discontinued on October 31, 2016. The pixate.com domain now serves only a Google-hosted farewell notice; there is no product, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface remaining to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record.

providers.name: Placemeter
providers.description: Placemeter was a New York City computer-vision analytics startup (a Techstars company) that turned live video feeds into real-time measurements of pedestrian and vehicle activity in physical places, offering a data API for foot-traffic and movement counts. The standalone product and developer API are no longer operational: placemeter.com no longer serves a website (the apex domain has no address record, carries no mail exchanger, and is defensively parked under Netgear's corporate registrar, CSC Corporate Domains), so there is no live API surface, documentation, SDK, or event stream to enrich.

providers.name: Placenote
providers.description: Placenote (Vertical AI Inc.) was a San Francisco company that built a cloud-hosted persistent augmented-reality toolkit — a "Persistent AR" SDK that let developers save, reload, and share ARKit/Unity spatial maps so digital content stays anchored to a physical location across sessions and devices. It shipped native client SDKs for iOS (Swift, via the PlacenoteSDK CocoaPod) and Unity, plus multiplayer AR samples such as PlaceInvaders and web mesh-viewing examples. The product was consumed as mobile SDKs backed by a cloud mapping/localization service rather than a public REST API, so no OpenAPI or web API surface was published. The company is now defunct: placenote.com no longer resolves to a live product (the domain is parked) and the docs/cloud service are offline. The Placenote GitHub organization and the published SDKs remain the only live, first-party developer surface, which is what this profile captures.

providers.name: plated
providers.description: Plated was a meal-kit delivery company surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company was acquired by Albertsons in 2017 and later wound down; the plated.com domain now 301-redirects to safeway.com, and no independent developer portal, API reference, SDK, or well-known surface remains. This profile records the honest state of a defunct provider with no active API surface.

providers.name: Platfora
providers.description: Platfora was a big-data analytics company founded in 2011 by Ben Werther that provided in-memory business intelligence and data visualization directly on top of Apache Hadoop, letting analysts run interactive queries, build "lenses," and share dashboards without ETL into a separate warehouse. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Battery Ventures, In-Q-Tel and others, it raised roughly $65M before Workday acquired the company in July 2016 and folded the technology into Workday's analytics stack. The standalone Platfora product and platfora.com developer surface were subsequently discontinued; the domain no longer resolves and no public API or developer program remains.

providers.name: Plato
providers.description: Plato was a mentorship and leadership community for engineering leaders (platohq.com), operating from 2018 until its sunset on December 19, 2025. It ran a global network of 500+ engineering leaders and 1,000+ mentors, the annual Elevate conference, and dozens of meetups, webinars, and dinners. Its parent company Coda was acquired by Grammarly (rebranded Superhuman), which wound down Plato's programs to focus on an AI-native productivity suite. The company is now deactivated: platohq.com redirects to a Substack sunset announcement and no developer API, SDK, documentation, or integrations are or were published. Surfaced as a partech portfolio lead; enrichment found no API surface.

providers.name: PlayHT
providers.description: PlayHT, now operating as PlayAI, is a generative voice platform offering realistic text-to-speech models, AI voice agents, and a podcast generation tool called PlayNote. The platform centers on the PlayDialog and Play 3.0 Mini models, providing more than 200 prebuilt voices across multiple languages and accents with sub-second latency suited to conversational applications. PlayAI exposes REST and streaming endpoints for text-to-speech, voice listing, voice cloning, and voice agent management. It ships Python and Node.js SDKs and a hosted playground, and integrates with the major voice agent infrastructure stacks. The product is widely used to build voice assistants, IVRs, narration pipelines, and content production workflows.

providers.name: Plerk
providers.description: Plerk was a Mexican fintech startup offering an employee-benefits and perks platform ("beneficios para colaboradores") for companies in Mexico, backed by 500 Global. During 2023 Plerk merged with minu to consolidate the employee benefits offering in Mexico, and the standalone Plerk product was wound down. Its primary domain plerk.com no longer resolves (DNS fully lapsed; last web archive May 2023) and plerk.io redirects to the now-defunct plerk.com. Support was handled at soporte@plerk.io. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired lead; the surviving product and any API surface live under minu. No live developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists for Plerk.

providers.name: Pliant Technology
providers.description: Pliant Technology, Inc. was a data-center storage company that pioneered the introduction of high-performance enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs) into mission-critical data-center environments. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by SanDisk in 2011 and its product line was folded into SanDisk's enterprise storage solutions. The company operated as a hardware/semiconductor storage vendor and published no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer surface; its former domain now redirects to SanDisk. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Polyvore
providers.description: Polyvore was a community-powered fashion and lifestyle social-commerce website where members created and shared outfit "sets" by clipping product images into collages. Founded in 2007 and backed by Matrix Partners, it was acquired by Yahoo in 2015 (~$200M), passed to Verizon/Oath, and its assets were acquired by Canadian e-commerce retailer SSENSE in April 2018, which shut the site down immediately. The polyvore.com domain now 301-redirects to ssense.com; there is no live product, developer portal, or public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Polywork
providers.description: Polywork is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Pop Up Archive
providers.description: Pop Up Archive was a startup that provided audio and podcast transcription, speech-to-text, and searchable spoken-word archiving tools, making audio content discoverable and machine-readable. It was acquired by Apple in 2017 and its independent products, developer surface, and popuparchive.com domain were retired. The domain now resolves to Apple nameservers with no active host, so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API to enrich. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Bloomberg Beta and is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record; no live API surface remains.

providers.name: Populr.me
providers.description: Populr.me was a self-service website builder that let users create and host single-page personal and marketing pages on free and paid subscription tiers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found the consumer service permanently shut down on June 1, 2023 (users directed to Wix, Weebly, Squarespace, GoDaddy) and no public API, developer program, documentation, or event surface remains — only a static shutdown page on the domain.

providers.name: Portal Software
providers.description: Portal Software was an Accel-backed billing and revenue-management software company whose portal.com domain now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to Oracle WebCenter Portal, indicating the business and its assets have been absorbed into Oracle. It was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, but the enrichment pass finds no independent developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or published security program under portal.com — the domain serves only an Oracle marketing redirect, so there is no standalone API surface to enrich beyond the domain-level TLS/DNS security probe.

providers.name: Postini
providers.description: Postini was an email security and message-management company founded in 1999, providing hosted spam and virus filtering, email archiving, encryption, and web security for businesses. Google acquired Postini in 2007 (roughly $625M) and folded its capabilities into Google Apps (now Google Workspace); the standalone Postini service was discontinued and customers were transitioned to Google Apps by around 2012. The postini.com domain is now Google-owned and redirects to google.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; the company has no live, standalone API surface, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Powder
providers.description: Powder was a Paris-based gaming company, founded in 2018 and backed by a $14M Series A led by Serena with General Catalyst, Slow Ventures, Alven, Bpifrance Digital Venture and Secocha Ventures. It built AI-powered clipping software for gamers and content creators: a low-resource Windows screen recorder plus on-device machine learning that detected highlight moments in gameplay recordings and long Twitch, YouTube and Kick streams and turned them into short vertical clips, AutoEdits and automontages, with per-title models for 40-plus games including Fortnite, Valorant, Counter-Strike 2 and League of Legends, and NPU-accelerated local inference on AMD XDNA hardware. It was distributed as an end-user desktop app through Steam, the Microsoft Store and Razer Cortex, on a free tier with a $9.99/month Powder Pro subscription. Powder published no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract. The company has since wound down: its own apex domain now redirects every path to a first-party notice stating the app is no longer updated or maintained and that all subscriptions have been cancelled.

providers.name: PRA Health Sciences
providers.description: PRA Health Sciences was a global contract research organization (CRO) headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, providing outsourced clinical development services to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies. On July 1, 2021 ICON plc completed its acquisition of PRA Health Sciences in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at approximately $12 billion, forming one of the world's largest healthcare research organizations. Following the acquisition the PRA Health Sciences brand has been fully retired and operations were merged into ICON. The legacy prahs.com domain redirects to iconplc.com / icongroup.com and no PRA-branded developer programs, public APIs, SDKs, or technical documentation remain.

providers.name: Practice
providers.description: Practice (practice.do) was a Montreal-based all-in-one coaching and consulting business platform that bundled scheduling, client portals, forms, contracts, invoicing, and payments into a single tool for independent coaches. It raised a $10M seed round in 2021 led by a16z (Andrew Chen participating). The company shut down permanently on November 3, 2025 after a failed acquisition process; its domain no longer serves a product and it exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface.

providers.name: PredictionIO
providers.description: Apache PredictionIO is an open source machine learning server that lets developers and data scientists build, deploy, and serve predictive engines as web services. Originally the commercial product prediction.io from TappingStone, it was acquired by Salesforce in 2016, donated to the Apache Software Foundation, and graduated as a top-level Apache project before being retired to the Apache Attic. It exposes a REST-based Event Server for collecting event data and an Engine Query API for real-time predictions, built on Apache Spark, MLlib, HBase, Elasticsearch, and Akka HTTP, with official SDKs for Python, Ruby, PHP, and Scala/Java. This profile enriches the original portfolio-lead stub.

providers.name: Prelay
providers.description: Prelay was a deal collaboration ("team selling") platform that helped B2B revenue teams coordinate the internal stakeholders behind complex enterprise deals — sales engineers, legal, deal desk, finance, and leadership — inside a shared workspace that plugged into the CRM. Founded 2019 in San Francisco (Y Combinator W20), it was a SaaS application aimed at sales and revenue operations, not a developer/API product. The company has since ceased operations: Y Combinator lists Prelay as Inactive, Crunchbase records it as permanently closed, the github.com/prelay organization was archived on 2025-10-16 with zero public repositories, and as of 2026-08-14 prelay.com and www.prelay.com no longer complete a TLS handshake (the Webflow certificate has been deprovisioned) while app.prelay.com answers 404 for every path. No public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, MCP server or agent card ever existed, and no api./docs./developers. subdomain resolves. Prelay was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Prescient
providers.description: Prescient Co. Inc. was a United States construction-technology and manufacturing company that sold an integrated design, engineering, manufacturing and assembly platform for multi-unit buildings — apartments, condominiums, student and military dormitories, hotels and senior-living communities. Its product was the patented Prescient Solution built on the Unified Truss Construction System (UTCS), a light-gauge steel structural framing system manufactured off-site in panelised components and assembled on-site, marketed as a faster, greener and lower-cost alternative to conventional cast-in-place and wood-frame structures at heights up to roughly twelve stories. The "technology" in the offering was internal design-automation software that linked architectural design, structural engineering, factory manufacturing and field assembly into one digital model; it was delivered as a design-build service to real-estate developers and general contractors, never as a product a third party could integrate with. Founded in 2012 (some sources list 2013) and headquartered in North Carolina — Charlotte, later Durham — with manufacturing in Mebane, North Carolina and Arvada, Colorado, the company raised a large private round stack including a $40M Series D and a Series E led by Eldridge Industries at a reported $650M valuation; publicly reported lifetime totals disagree, with EquityZen listing $103M and Crunchbase reporting roughly $375M through Series G. The company contracted sharply: the Mebane plant closed in 2022 with 83 jobs cut, 50 Arvada jobs were cut in April 2023, and a Colorado WARN notice filed on 31 August 2023 announced the permanent closure of the Arvada plant and a further 60 jobs, stating that upon conclusion of the shutdown activities the company would be closed. Prescient never operated a public developer program, API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification, and prescientco.com has since passed out of the company's control. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Primary Data
providers.description: Primary Data was a software-defined storage and data-virtualization startup best known for its DataSphere platform, a metadata engine that abstracted files across heterogeneous storage tiers (flash, disk, cloud) behind a single global namespace and moved data automatically by policy. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors, the company ceased operations in 2017, with much of its team and technology continuing at Hammerspace. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass the company is defunct and primarydata.com is a parked domain (GoDaddy lander), so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Primesense
providers.description: PrimeSense was an Israeli fabless semiconductor and 3D-sensing company, best known for co-developing the depth-sensing technology behind Microsoft's Kinect and for sponsoring the open-source OpenNI (Open Natural Interaction) framework and its NiTE middleware for skeleton tracking and gesture recognition. The company shipped the PrimeSensor reference design and PS1080 system-on-chip for structured-light depth cameras. Apple acquired PrimeSense in November 2013 for roughly $360M; the OpenNI project and openni.org were subsequently wound down (openni.org now redirects to apple.com) and the company's developer program, website, and API/docs hosts are no longer online. Only legacy Apache-2.0 source repositories (the OpenNI sensor driver and NiTE controls) remain public on GitHub. There is no live web/REST API surface for PrimeSense.

providers.name: Prism Skylabs
providers.description: Prism Skylabs was a cloud-based visual monitoring and video analytics company that turned surveillance and IP-camera feeds from physical retail and commercial spaces into searchable, time-lapse imagery and business intelligence. Backed by a16z and Draper Nexus, it was acquired by Cisco in 2016 and folded into the Cisco Meraki smart-camera (MV) computer-vision line; the standalone company is defunct. The prismskylabs.com domain now 301-redirects to prism.com, an unrelated domain-licensing/holding page, and no live Prism Skylabs developer portal, API documentation, or API specifications exist to enrich. This profile is retained as an a16z portfolio identity record.

providers.name: ProgrammableWeb
providers.description: ProgrammableWeb was the original API directory and developer resource, founded by John Musser in 2005, documenting over 19,000 open web APIs and thousands of mashups and applications over 17 years of operation. It was acquired by Alcatel-Lucent in 2010, sold to MuleSoft in 2013, and ultimately shut down in October 2022 following Salesforce's acquisition of MuleSoft. The site's content is preserved through the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine.

providers.name: Props
providers.description: Props (Props Project, operated by Props PBC / Open Props, founded by YouNow's Adi Sideman) was a blockchain-based loyalty and rewards network that let consumer apps grant users a shared crypto token (the Props Token) as a stake in the networks they helped grow. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Borderless Capital, Venrock and Comcast Ventures, it raised ~$2M and was the first Regulation A+ consumer token qualified by the SEC, reaching over three million users across its app network. In August 2021 the team announced it would wind down commercial operations at year end, citing the regulatory constraints of running a qualified security, and open-sourced the Props Protocol contracts on GitHub. The propsproject.com domain no longer resolves; there is no live developer portal, API, documentation, or maintained SDK. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record.

providers.name: Prynt
providers.description: Prynt is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Pss Systems
providers.description: Pss Systems is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: PsyOptions
providers.description: PsyOptions is a decentralized options protocol built on Solana by Mithraic Labs, providing on-chain American-style options contracts originally designed for use with the Serum/OpenBook DEX. Rather than a hosted REST API, it exposes its functionality through open-source on-chain Anchor/BPF programs and first-party TypeScript client libraries (the @mithraic-labs npm scope: psy-american, psyoptions, market-meta, psy-token-registry, psy-metrics) plus a Rust crate. The project has since been sunset: its documentation and marketing sites are shut down, though the GitHub repositories and published packages remain available for reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. Sector: crypto / DeFi.

providers.name: Punchd
providers.description: Punchd was a mobile customer-loyalty rewards application for small businesses, founded in 2009 at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo by Reed Morse and Grantland Chew, that let merchants run digital punch-card loyalty programs. Google acquired the company in June 2011 and retired the product in June 2013, folding features into other Google products. The getpunchd.com domain now serves only a static Google-hosted closure announcement. The company is defunct with no active product, developer program, or public API surface; this profile is retained for network completeness as a historical record.

providers.name: Punk API
providers.description: Punk API is a free, no-auth REST API exposing BrewDog's "DIY Dog" open-source beer recipe collection — 325 detailed homebrew recipes crowdsourced and transcribed from the BrewDog DIY Dog PDF. The v2 surface (api.punkapi.com/v2) offered three read-only endpoints: list beers (with rich query filtering on ABV, IBU, EBC, brew date, beer name, hops, malt, yeast, and food pairing), get a beer by id, and get a random beer. Each beer carries a full recipe — ABV, IBU, EBC/SRM colour, target gravities, mash temperature schedule, fermentation temperature, twist, malt and hop bills, yeast strain, food pairings, brewer's tips, and contributor attribution. STATUS — DEPRECATED. BrewDog decommissioned the public api.punkapi.com endpoint in 2023 and the source repositories (sammdec/punkapi-db, sammdec/punkapi-server) were archived on 2023-06-28. The dataset and server source remain MIT-licensed and available; community-hosted mirrors and the `punkapi-db` npm package preserve the contract documented here.

providers.name: Pure Watercraft
providers.description: Pure Watercraft was a Seattle, Washington electric marine propulsion company founded in 2011 by Andy Rebele. It built electric outboard motors marketed as drop-in replacements for 20 to 50 horsepower gas engines, along with lithium-ion battery packs, chargers and Wi-Fi throttle controls, plus a consumer companion mobile app that pulled trip history and telemetry off the outboard over Bluetooth and pushed firmware updates to it. General Motors took a reported 25 percent stake in 2021. The company wound down and sold its assets in 2024, with the outboard line acquired by Raider Outboards and other assets going to a Seattle electric boat club. purewatercraft.com and the former companion-app host app.purewatercraft.com both now 301 to www.pureoutboards.com, the Pure Electric Outboard storefront operated by the acquirer. Pure Watercraft never published a public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; its telemetry cloud was private to its own mobile app.

providers.name: QEP Resources
providers.description: QEP Resources was an independent natural gas and crude oil exploration and production company headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with operations in the United States. The company was acquired by Diamondback Energy in 2021 and no longer operates as an independent entity.

providers.name: Qualtera
providers.description: Qualtera was a French software company, founded in 2010 and backed by Serena, that built high-volume big data analytics platforms for semiconductor test and manufacturing — giving IDMs, foundries and OSATs real-time observability, traceability and production control over test and assembly data across worldwide operations, processing the data of tens of millions of wafers and billions of parts a year. Its products included SiliconDash, an automated decision-support system for test, quality and yield analysis. Synopsys acquired Qualtera on June 10, 2020 and folded its analytics into Yield Explorer and TestMAX, which now ship as part of the Synopsys Silicon Lifecycle Management family. The Qualtera brand and any surface it once had are gone: qualtera.com now resolves to Synopsys nameservers and 301-redirects every path to the Synopsys Silicon Lifecycle Management marketing page, and the host refuses a TLS handshake on port 443 entirely. Qualtera never published a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK or package on any registry, and no machine-readable contract survives under its own name. This profile is retained as a historical record; the live analytics API surface, where one exists, belongs to Synopsys and is profiled there rather than credited here.

providers.name: Quantopian
providers.description: Quantopian was a Boston-based crowd-sourced quantitative investment firm and algorithmic-trading platform (backed by a16z and Bessemer Venture Partners) where members wrote, backtested, and shared Python trading algorithms against historical market data. The company ceased operations in November 2020 and its intellectual property was acquired by Robinhood; its public developer platform and hosted API are retired. Its widely-used open-source Python libraries - Zipline (backtesting), Pyfolio, Alphalens, Empyrical, and trading-calendars - remain published on PyPI and its GitHub organization stays live.

providers.name: Quantum Effect Dev
providers.description: Quantum Effect Devices (QED, originally Quantum Effect Design) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1991 by former MIPS Computer Systems managers Tom Riordan, Earl Killian, and Ray Kunita. QED designed MIPS-based 32- and 64-bit embedded RISC microprocessors (the RM5200 and RM7000 families) for networking and communications systems including routers, switches, and optical transport equipment. The company completed an IPO in 2000 and was acquired the same year by PMC-Sierra for approximately $2.3 billion. It has no independent operations, developer platform, or API surface today; the former corporate site (qedinc.com) is defunct. This record was surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company and is retained as a historical/no-API-surface entry.

providers.name: Queenly
providers.description: Queenly is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Quickoffice
providers.description: Quickoffice was a mobile office productivity suite (document, spreadsheet, and presentation editing for iOS, Android, and Symbian) that was acquired by Google in June 2012, folded into Google Docs / Google Drive, and formally discontinued in 2014. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment on 2026-07-20 confirmed there is no independent Quickoffice API surface. The quickoffice.com domain now resolves to Google infrastructure and www.quickoffice.com 301-redirects to google.com/docs/about/, developer.quickoffice.com does not resolve (NXDOMAIN), and no developer portal, documentation, or API remains. The product capabilities live on inside Google Workspace (Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides).

providers.name: Quirky
providers.description: Quirky was a crowdsourced consumer-product invention platform (founded by Ben Kaufman) that let inventors submit ideas the community helped design, manufacture and sell; it was backed by a16z among others. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2015. As of this enrichment pass the quirky.com domain is a parked "domain name is for sale" page with no operating product, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained as a defunct a16z portfolio-company lead; no API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Rapid Robotics
providers.description: Rapid Robotics was a San Francisco robotics-as-a-service (RaaS) company, founded in 2019 by Jordan Kretchmer, that rented pre-trained six-axis "Rapid Machine Operators" to small and mid-size manufacturers on a subscription — roughly $25,000 per robot per year — to cover repetitive machine-tending work such as pad printing, injection molding, heat staking, heat stamping, ultrasonic welding, pick-and-place and parts inspection. The robots shipped with grippers, computer-vision software and models pre-trained on CAD, and were set up and supervised through a proprietary no-code fleet console rather than through a developer interface. The company raised about $54.2M in total — a $12M Series A in 2021 and a $36.7M Series B co-led by Kleiner Perkins and Tiger Global — and announced partnerships with Universal Robots and Yaskawa Motoman in early 2023. Rapid Robotics subsequently wound down, and its assets — hardware, marquee customers and the US team — were acquired by Munich-based RaaS company RobCo, which used them to enter the US market and announced a new San Francisco headquarters on 9 September 2025. The company never published a public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification of any kind: 1,773 unique archived URLs on rapidrobotics.com contain no /api, /apis, /docs, /developer, /graphql or /sdk path. The domain is no longer operated by the company — it is delegated to ns1/ns2.atom.com and redirects to a brand-name marketplace listing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record; there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Rapportive
providers.description: Rapportive was a browser extension that added a contact-intelligence sidebar to Gmail, surfacing a person's name, photo, job, and social profiles alongside their email. Founded in 2011 and backed by 500 Global (then 500 Startups), it was acquired by LinkedIn in 2012 and later folded into LinkedIn Sales Navigator. The rapportive.com domain now 301-redirects to LinkedIn's "Sales Navigator for Gmail" feature page. Rapportive published no standalone developer API and operates no independent developer surface today; this profile records that defunct/absorbed status for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rapsphere
providers.description: RAPsphere was a mobile IT company that developed mobile information management solutions enabling CIOs to contend with BYOD (bring-your-own-device) in the enterprise and the critical need to protect corporate applications and data on mobile devices. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by AppSense in May 2012 and no longer operates as an independent entity. Its former domain (rapsphere.com) is now a parked / for-sale domain and there is no live developer surface, public API, documentation, or reachable web presence to enrich. This profile is retained as a portfolio-history lead and is not an active API provider.

providers.name: RCS Capital
providers.description: RCS Capital Corporation (RCAP) was a publicly traded holding company focused on the financial services industry, founded by Nicholas Schorsch and taken public in June 2013. The firm owned a diversified group of businesses including independent broker-dealers, investment banking, capital markets, and transaction management services. It assembled Cetera Financial Group to become the second largest network of independent broker-dealers in the United States, with approximately 9,100 financial advisors managing $220 billion in assets under administration for 2.5 million clients. RCS Capital filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in January 2016, citing $1.39 billion in debts, and emerged in May 2016 as Aretec Group, Inc., the holding company of Cetera Financial Group. No public developer APIs were offered under the RCS Capital brand.

providers.name: Ready Player Me
providers.description: Ready Player Me was a cross-game avatar platform: a hosted Avatar Creator plus REST APIs that produced interoperable 3D character avatars as binary glTF (.glb) and 2D PNG renders for Unity, Unreal, web, iOS and Android. The Avatars, Assets and Auth APIs covered draft/save avatar creation, template-based creation, wearable-asset equipping and discovery, colour palettes, render precompilation and anonymous/email-code user authentication, all scoped to a studio application via an X-APP-ID header. Netflix acquired the company in December 2025 and the public platform - Avatar Creator, PlayerZero and the developer APIs at api.readyplayer.me - was shut down on 31 January 2026. As of 26 August 2026 readyplayer.me publishes MX and TXT records but no A record, and api.readyplayer.me, docs.readyplayer.me and studio.readyplayer.me are NXDOMAIN, so every first-party developer surface is gone. Avatars already exported as .glb files still load in any glTF 2.0 engine; the readyplayerme GitHub organization and two npm packages remain public.

providers.name: Ready Robotics
providers.description: READY Robotics was a Columbus, Ohio industrial-automation software company, founded in 2016 out of Johns Hopkins University, that built Forge/OS — a universal operating system for industrial robots. Forge/OS presented one low-code programming and control surface across hundreds of robot models from ABB, Epson, FANUC, Kawasaki, Stäubli, Universal Robots and Yaskawa, and its Forge Edge product advertised a REST API with an OpenAPI/Swagger description plus client tooling for Python, JavaScript and C++, alongside the RAL2 (Robot Abstraction Layer 2) C++/Qt plugin interface used to write new robot drivers. The company ceased operations in August 2024 after a funding round collapsed, and its assets were liquidated through an assignment for the benefit of creditors. Every developer-facing host it operated — developer., docs., portal., market. and support.ready-robotics.com — no longer resolves in DNS, so no live machine-readable contract remains. What survives publicly is the marketing site behind a Cloudflare challenge and the GitHub organization, which still carries the RAL2 sample driver and the vendored C++ dependencies Forge/OS was built on.

providers.name: RecappED
providers.description: RecappED (recapped.io) is an AI-powered digital sales room and customer onboarding platform for B2B revenue teams. It consolidates the buying and selling process into a single collaborative workspace with mutual action plans, deal management, buyer-engagement tracking, AI deal intelligence, an AI sales coach, and structured handoffs from sales to implementation. Integration with CRM and sales tooling is delivered through native connectors (Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Gong, Clari, Zoom) and Zapier rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, developer portal, or public REST reference is published. The platform announced it is shutting down on 2026-07-31 and is not accepting new customers; probed again on 2026-08-13 the site and application were still serving, with the shutdown banner on every page. The one machine-oriented document the company publishes is the schema of the customer offboarding data export, in the github.com/Recapped organization. Surfaced as a CRV portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Red Beacon
providers.description: Redbeacon was a consumer home-services marketplace that connected homeowners with local service professionals — for home repair, cleaning, landscaping, handyman and similar jobs — letting people describe a job and receive quotes from vetted local pros. The company was an early venture-backed startup (with Mayfield among its investors) and was acquired by The Home Depot in 2012. The standalone Redbeacon consumer service was subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass the redbeacon.com domain still resolves (Cloudflare DNS, Google Workspace email) but serves no live website (origin returns HTTP 525 / 400) and publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio-graph node.

providers.name: Reinfer
providers.description: Reinfer was a London-based communications intelligence company, backed by Seedcamp, that built a natural-language-processing platform for mining structured insight and automation triggers from unstructured conversational data such as emails, support tickets, and chat. Reinfer was acquired by SS&C Blue Prism and its technology folded into SS&C's intelligent-automation product line; the original developer surface (reinfer.io, docs.reinfer.io, api.reinfer.io) is now defunct and no longer resolves, so there is no live public API to catalog. This profile is retained as a portfolio and acquisition lead for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Renoviso
providers.description: Renoviso is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: rentify
providers.description: Rentify was a London-based property technology (PropTech) startup founded in 2011 that built an online lettings and property-management platform for landlords, letting them list, market, price, and manage rental properties directly without a traditional high-street agent. It raised a Series A from Balderton Capital and later a crowdfunding round before ceasing operations. Surfaced as a balderton-capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface (the company is no longer operating and rentify.com no longer serves an application).

providers.name: Restorando
providers.description: Restorando was a Latin American online restaurant-reservation platform (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, and other markets), originally backed by Emergence Capital and later acquired by TripAdvisor. The Restorando brand has since been absorbed into TheFork: as of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass, restorando.com returns a 301 redirect to thefork.es and the standalone Restorando product no longer exists. It exposes no independent developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable surface to enrich.

providers.name: Revolv
providers.description: Revolv was a smart-home company that built a connected home hub and mobile application to unify control of disparate smart-home devices and wireless protocols from a single app. The company was acquired by Nest (Google) and the Revolv hub and service were subsequently discontinued; owners of purchased Revolv hubs were directed to Nest support for refunds through a deadline of October 31, 2018. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical portfolio record. The company publishes no active API, developer portal, SDKs, or public developer surface, so this entry carries only a domain-security probe of its remaining web presence.

providers.name: Rixty
providers.description: Rixty is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of uncork-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Rize
providers.description: Rize (Rize Money, Inc. / RizeFS) was a Banking-as-a-Service and embedded-finance platform that offered unified banking, brokerage, and payments APIs, letting companies embed savings, checking, and investment accounts directly into their own products. Rize was acquired by Fifth Third Bancorp in 2023; the standalone rizefs.com developer and API surface has since been decommissioned, with no live documentation, OpenAPI, or reachable endpoints found during this enrichment pass. The registered domain still publishes SPF and DMARC (reject) email records but serves no web or API hosts.

providers.name: Rockmelt
providers.description: Rockmelt was a Chromium-based social web browser startup founded in 2008 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), designed to integrate Facebook, Twitter, and web feeds directly into the browser chrome. The company was acquired by Yahoo in August 2013 and its products were discontinued shortly after. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment confirms the company is defunct with no live web, developer, or API surface.

providers.name: Rockset
providers.description: Rockset was a real-time analytics database company (Greylock portfolio, infrastructure sector) that was acquired by OpenAI in June 2024. The standalone product and API have been wound down: rockset.com now 301-redirects to OpenAI's acquisition announcement, and the former developer surface (docs.rockset.com, api.rs2.usw2.rockset.com) no longer resolves in DNS. There is no live public API to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Rohm and Haas
providers.description: Rohm and Haas Company was an American specialty chemicals manufacturer founded in 1909 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The company produced electronic materials, specialty polymers, adhesives, coatings, paints, and process chemicals. On April 1, 2009, Rohm and Haas was acquired by The Dow Chemical Company for approximately $18.8 billion in cash and stock. The Rohm and Haas brand has since been largely retired and its product lines, technologies, and businesses have been integrated into Dow (now Dow Inc., NYSE: DOW). Some legacy product brands persist under Dow but the standalone company no longer exists.

providers.name: RolePoint
providers.description: RolePoint was an employee referral, internal mobility, and talent-acquisition software company that helped recruitment teams source, refer, and redeploy talent through referral programs and internal mobility marketplaces, with a "Connect" API layer for integrating into ATS/HRIS systems such as iCIMS. The company was acquired by Jobvite in 2019 and folded into the Jobvite Talent Acquisition Suite; the standalone rolepoint.com domain no longer resolves and no independent developer portal or API surface remains reachable. It is tracked here as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Roll
providers.description: Roll was a social token infrastructure platform for the creator economy, letting creators and communities mint and manage their own branded ERC-20 tokens on the Ethereum blockchain. Founded in 2017 in New York City and backed by Techstars, IOSG Ventures, and Fabric Ventures (a $10M Series A), Roll offered developer APIs and OAuth-based integrations so third-party apps could query tokens and balances. The custodial Roll app and its developer API (docs.tryroll.com / api.tryroll.com) were sunset in April 2025 and permanently shut down on 2025-05-26; the company web surface no longer resolves. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; this pass confirms the company is defunct with no live API surface remaining.

providers.name: Rome Tools
providers.description: Rome Tools, Inc. was the company behind Rome, a unified, Rust-based developer toolchain for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, HTML, Markdown, and CSS, intended to consolidate the roles of a formatter, linter, compiler, and bundler (replacing tools like Babel, ESLint, webpack, and Prettier) into a single fast tool. Rome shipped as a command-line tool and VS Code extension rather than as a hosted web service, so it has no REST/HTTP API, OpenAPI, webhook, or event surface. The project's GitHub repository (github.com/rome/tools) was archived on 2026-07-21 as read-only, the rome.tools domain no longer resolves, and the effort has been succeeded by the community-maintained Biome project (biomejs.dev). Rome Tools was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirms it is a defunct open-source CLI toolchain with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Romit
providers.description: Romit was a bank-agnostic digital wallet and payment-gateway platform for the card-not-present merchant-acquiring industry, built by a team of ex-Robocoin (bitcoin ATM) founders and backed by the 500 Global (500 Startups) accelerator. The Romit Merchant Suite let merchants stop chargebacks, reduce fraud and resolve disputes, while its consumer wallet let customers securely store payment methods, view transactions and communicate with merchants. Its OAuth2 REST API (api.romit.io/v1) exposed Banking (cards + linked bank accounts), Identity/KYC, Transfer (authorize/capture/refund/void money movement), Subscription, Plan and Invoice resources. Romit (romit.io) has since ceased operations; this profile captures the API surface derived from the surviving public evidence.

providers.name: Rovilus
providers.description: Rovilus is a seed-stage hardware startup founded in 2018 by YenChe Huang and Katherine Kan, developing thermal management technology for industrial battery packs. The company raised roughly $150K from 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) and appears in that firm's portfolio. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass the company's website (rovilus.com) no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN, no NS/MX records), and no public API, developer portal, SDK, documentation, or other developer surface could be found; Rovilus is a physical battery-thermal hardware company with no API footprint.

providers.name: RTFKT
providers.description: RTFKT (pronounced "artifact") was a digital-fashion and collectibles studio founded in 2020 by Benoit Pagotto, Chris Le, and Steven Vasilev, known for NFT-based virtual sneakers, wearables, and the CloneX avatar collection created with artist Takashi Murakami. Backed by an a16z-led seed round, the company was acquired by Nike in December 2021 and operated as a Web3 / metaverse brand. Nike announced it was winding RTFKT down in December 2024, with operations ceasing by the end of January 2025. RTFKT was a consumer/collectibles brand and never published a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; its remaining web presence is a frozen static archive page. This profile records that verified absence of an API surface.

providers.name: SalioGen Therapeutics
providers.description: SalioGen Therapeutics was a next-generation genetic medicine company, formerly based in Lexington, Massachusetts, developing gene therapies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of d1-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a biotech stub. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass its website (saliogen.com) serves only a minimal holding page indicating the company is no longer operating; no developer portal, API, documentation, blog, or other public technical surface was found.

providers.name: Sampler
providers.description: Sampler (The Sampler App Inc., Toronto) was a digital product-sampling platform used by consumer packaged goods (CPG) and retail brands to run targeted sample-distribution campaigns, collect first-party consumer data and reviews, and measure the impact of sampling on purchase behavior. Founded in 2013, it acquired Abeo and AdMass in 2023 and served brands including Procter & Gamble, Unilever, L'Oreal, Nestle and PepsiCo. THE COMPANY IS DEFUNCT: it filed for bankruptcy on 2024-06-27 with CAD 12.9M in liabilities against roughly CAD 300K in assets, and ceased operations. As of 2026-08-12 the entire estate is decommissioned — sampler.io and www.sampler.io fail the TLS handshake outright, api.sampler.io retains stale DNS records whose hosts refuse all connections, and every documentation or developer subdomain is NXDOMAIN. Sampler never published a public developer API, developer portal, documentation host, OpenAPI, or machine discovery surface; the api.sampler.io/v1/ endpoints visible in archived crawls were the private backend of its consumer claim widget and admin console, not a documented developer product.

providers.name: Sandforce
providers.description: SandForce was a fabless semiconductor company (Canaan Partners-backed) that designed flash memory / SSD controller processors. It was acquired by LSI Corporation in 2012 and its flash-controller business was subsequently folded into Seagate; the sandforce.com domain now redirects to seagate.com. As a defunct, absorbed brand it operates no independent website, developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation, so there is no live API surface to enrich. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a canaan-partners portfolio lead; retained as a historical/company record.

providers.name: Santa Cruz Operation
providers.description: Santa Cruz Operation (SCO) was an American software company founded in 1979 in Santa Cruz, California, best known for its Unix operating systems for Intel x86 hardware — Xenix (developed with Microsoft), SCO UNIX, SCO OpenServer, and UnixWare. The company later reorganized as Tarantella, Inc. and The SCO Group, which became widely known for the SCO v. IBM Linux litigation beginning in 2003. The SCO Group filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2007, and its Unix product assets were subsequently sold to UnXis, later renamed Xinuos. The historic Santa Cruz Operation is defunct and operates no modern developer platform or public API; this record is retained for network completeness.

providers.name: Sapho
providers.description: Sapho was a San Bruno, California micro-apps startup (founded 2014) that let enterprises build employee-facing "micro apps" and workflow notifications on top of legacy and SaaS systems. It was acquired by Citrix in November 2018 and folded into the Citrix Workspace product line as Citrix Microapps; the standalone product, developer portal, and any API surface were retired. The sapho.com domain now resolves only to a MarkMonitor brand-protection holding page (HTTPS refused, HTTP returns the registrar notice), so there is no live public API, documentation, or developer surface to enrich. This record is retained as a portfolio-company history stub for bloomberg-beta and uncork-capital.

providers.name: Savedo
providers.description: Savedo was a German fintech operating a consumer deposit marketplace that let savers in Germany open fixed-term and savings accounts across multiple European partner banks from a single portal. Backed by Point Nine, it was acquired by Deposit Solutions in 2017 and is now a subsidiary brand of Raisin SE (WeltSparen). The Savedo customer portal was deactivated on 31 March 2022 and the brand no longer accepts new customers; existing balances are administered via flatexDEGIRO Bank AG. Savedo published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile is retained as a network lead surfaced from the Point Nine portfolio.

providers.name: Scanwell
providers.description: Scanwell was surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probing (2026-07-21) found no live API surface — the scanwellhealth.com domain associated with the Version One Ventures portfolio company (Scanwell Health, an at-home smartphone diagnostic-testing startup) now 301-redirects to an unrelated site, indicating the company is defunct, and the scanwell.com domain belongs to an unrelated freight-forwarding firm (Scanwell Logistics) that publishes no developer program.

providers.name: Schematic Labs
providers.description: Schematic Labs was a San Francisco consumer music startup founded in 2010, best known as the maker of SoundTracking, an "Instagram for songs" mobile app for sharing the music you are listening to. Backed by Google Ventures (GV), Accel Partners, and SoftBank Capital with roughly $5.9M raised, it was acquired by Rhapsody in August 2014 and wound down as a standalone company. Today soundtracking.com redirects to napster.com (Rhapsody's successor brand) and schematiclabs.com is a parked domain. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; this profile records the company's place in the GV portfolio graph.

providers.name: SCiFi Foods
providers.description: SCiFi Foods was a San Francisco Bay Area food-technology startup, founded in 2019 by Joshua March (CEO) and Kasia Gora (CTO), that developed cultivated (cell-cultured) beef blended with plant-based ingredients to make burgers close to the taste of conventional meat. The company used a proprietary platform built on gene-editing tools such as CRISPR to create and screen hundreds of animal cell lines each month. Backed by a16z among others, SCiFi Foods raised roughly $40M before ceasing operations in June 2024; its cell lines were later released to academia via the Good Food Institute. The company is defunct and exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical surface.

providers.name: Scoopola
providers.description: Scoopola was an early-stage consumer startup backed by 500 Startups (Batch 2, June 2011), pitched as "the HotelTonight for live music and theater" — a mobile app for discovering and buying last-minute, discounted tickets to local live-music and theater events. The company appears defunct; its associated web domains (getwillcall.com and scoopola.com) no longer resolve, and there is no surviving developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This record is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; the enrichment pipeline found no live API to catalog.

providers.name: Scoreloop
providers.description: Scoreloop was a Munich, Germany based mobile social gaming company that provided a cross-platform SDK adding social features to mobile games - online leaderboards, achievements, player challenges, friend invites, and in-game virtual currency and monetization. The Scoreloop SDK supported Android, iOS, Windows Phone, Samsung Bada, Marmalade/AirPlay, and Unity 3D, and at its peak was used by more than 3,000 game developers. The company was backed by earlybird and was acquired by Research In Motion (BlackBerry) in 2011; the standalone Scoreloop platform and its developer service were subsequently wound down. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead - there is no live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remaining (the scoreloop.com domain now serves a suspended page and no developer host resolves), so no API artifacts are available to harvest.

providers.name: Scout.fm
providers.description: Scout.fm (Scout FM) was a podcast-curation startup whose iOS, Android, Alexa and CarPlay apps turned podcasts into personalized, radio-like stations using AI-driven recommendations across genres such as news, sports and true crime. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, Precursor Ventures, Advancit Capital and Samsung NEXT (roughly $1.4M raised), the company was acquired by Apple in September 2020 and subsequently shut down, with its apps pulled from every platform. The scout.fm domain no longer resolves and the company publishes no developer, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as a historical network record; there is nothing left to enrich.

providers.name: Scripps Networks Interactive
providers.description: Scripps Networks Interactive, Inc. (NASDAQ: SNI) was a Knoxville, Tennessee lifestyle media company that owned HGTV, Food Network, Travel Channel, DIY Network, Great American Country and Cooking Channel, plus digital properties including ulive. Discovery Communications completed its $14.6B acquisition on 2018-03-06 and renamed itself Discovery, Inc.; the brands now sit inside Warner Bros. Discovery. Scripps Networks Interactive no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API or machine-readable contract. Its former corporate domain, scrippsnetworksinteractive.com, has since been re-registered by an unrelated party and now serves an Australian online-gambling affiliate site, so it must not be linked as a company property.

providers.name: Sears Holdings
providers.description: Sears Holdings was the American holding company behind the Sears and Kmart department store chains. It filed for Chapter 11 in October 2018 and its retail operations were acquired in 2019 by Transform Holdco LLC, which trades as Transformco (Transform SR Brands LLC), the entity that operates Sears.com, Kmart.com and ShopYourWay.com today. The live developer surface carried forward from that estate is the Sears Marketplace Seller API — a versioned XML-over-HTTPS integration for third-party sellers covering catalog and item management, item class and attribute libraries, inventory, pricing, purchase order retrieval, order cancellations, returns and partial or full refunds, ASN and shipment updates, order prep time, installation service items, and remittance, removed-item, content-match and processing reports. Every API is published with a downloadable XSD and a sample XML document, both fetchable without credentials from seller.marketplace.sears.com, and calls are signed with an HMAC-SHA256 authorization header rather than OAuth. There is no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP server or A2A agent card on any Sears, Kmart or Transformco host.

providers.name: Sears Hometown and Outlet Stores
providers.description: Sears Hometown and Outlet Stores, Inc. (NASDAQ: SHOS) was a national retailer of home appliances, lawn and garden equipment, tools and hardware, spun off from Sears Holdings in October 2012 and operating two segments: Sears Hometown and Hardware, a largely franchised network of smaller-format stores in rural and suburban markets, and Sears Outlet, which sold new, one-of-a-kind, out-of-carton, discontinued, obsolete, used, reconditioned, overstocked and scratch-and-dent merchandise. The company was acquired by Transform Holdco (Transformco) and ESL Investments in October 2019, at which point the Sears Outlet business was sold on to Franchise Group and rebranded American Freight. Sears Hometown filed for Chapter 11 in December 2022 and converted to a Chapter 7 liquidation in February 2023. The company is defunct: it never operated a public developer program, and its corporate domain shos.com is now a parked registrar page serving a wildcard *.hostgator.com certificate and a 404, so there is no API surface, documentation, or /.well-known/ document left to profile.

providers.name: Seculert
providers.description: Seculert was an Israeli cybersecurity company that provided cloud-based automated threat and attack detection, analytics, and breach-detection services, correlating outbound traffic and threat intelligence to identify compromised devices. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, it was acquired by Radware in January 2017 and folded into Radware's cloud security portfolio; the independent seculert.com brand is now defunct. This enrichment pass found no live independent API surface: the apex domain no longer serves TLS, www.seculert.com redirects to a dead HubSpot landing page, and no /.well-known, llms.txt, or developer/API documentation is published. Retained as a network profile of an acquired, now-inactive provider; DNS records (DMARC ruf to dmarc@radware.com) corroborate the Radware ownership.

providers.name: SeeCommerce
providers.description: SeeCommerce was a supply-chain performance management software company that provided analytics and management software focused on supply-chain visibility and problems. It raised roughly $47-58M across multiple venture rounds from investors including Insight Partners and Integral Capital Partners, and was acquired in February 2006. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct/acquired with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface (seecommerce.com no longer resolves to the company and other candidate domains do not resolve), so there are no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Seiza
providers.description: Seiza was a French social-recruitment advertising and recruitment-automation SaaS platform dedicated to frontline hiring — hospitality and restaurants, transport and logistics, agri-food, industry, retail, temp staffing, healthcare and construction. Founded in Paris in 2010 as Work4 Labs by Stephane Le Viet, Gautier Machelon and Matt Brown, it built its early business on sourcing candidates through non-professional social networks rather than job boards or LinkedIn, later rebranding from Work4 to Seiza. It raised roughly $22.8M in venture capital (Serena, among others) and served about 400 clients across Europe and the US, including McDonald's, Sysco, Ecolab and Veolia. The product was a recruiter web application — social sourcing campaigns, profile enrichment, one-click calling, a compatibility index, automated interview scheduling, SMS/messaging and reporting — plus a fixed catalog of 23 named ATS connectors (Bullhorn, Workday, Greenhouse, SmartRecruiters, iCIMS, Cornerstone, Recruitee, Talensoft, DigitalRecruiters, Beetween, Fountain, Paychex, CareerBuilder, Avionte, Acquity, Idibu, PivotCX, Talemetry, Gestmax, Scoptalent, Eolia Software, MyCVtheque, Hubspot), with anything outside that list handled as a bespoke integration through sales. No public API, developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, webhook catalog, SDK or CLI was ever published: a 557-URL census of the archived seiza.co site shows only marketing, blog, FAQ and legal pages, and every /.well-known/ path returned 404 while the site was live. Seiza was acquired by UK job-search engine Adzuna on 2024-11-18 and folded into Adzuna's social recruitment advertising line; Adzuna's own developer program is profiled separately in this network. The company domain seiza.co was still serving in May 2026 but no longer resolves at all as of 2026-08-17. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: SenSage
providers.description: SenSage was a security information and event management (SIEM) and log/event analytics company backed by Battery Ventures and Canaan Partners. Its platform focused on collecting, warehousing, and analyzing very large volumes of security event and log data for threat detection, forensics, and regulatory compliance reporting. SenSage was later acquired by KEYW Holding Corporation and the brand was retired; its former domain, sensage.com, now redirects to IgniteTech (an ESW Capital software-acquisition operator). This profile was surfaced as a venture portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. No active developer portal, public API, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; the company is treated as defunct with no live API footprint.

providers.name: Sentieo
providers.description: Sentieo is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Sentimoto
providers.description: Sentimoto is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Server Density
providers.description: Server Density is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine, seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Sessions
providers.description: Sessions (Session Technologies, formerly Flow OS) was a Bucharest-based unified communication and collaboration platform founded in 2021 by Radu Negulescu and Radu Tintescu, backed by earlybird's Digital East Fund (invested 2022, lead Dan Lupu). The product bundled voice, video, chat, webinars and meetings with third-party productivity integrations on a proprietary "Flow OS" framework at sessions.us. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07-21) the company appears defunct: the sessions.us domain no longer serves the product (it resolves to an unrelated parked/casino-spam page behind a bare-IP TLS certificate), the docs, developers and api subdomains do not respond, and no live developer, API, OpenAPI, SDK or documentation surface could be located to enrich. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead record; no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: Seventy Seven Energy
providers.description: Seventy Seven Energy Inc. was a diversified oilfield services company headquartered in Oklahoma City, providing wellsite services and equipment to U.S. land-based oil and natural gas exploration and production customers. It was formed in 2011 out of Chesapeake Energy's oilfield services arm and spun off as an independent public company, operating through affiliates including Nomac Drilling (contract land drilling), Performance Technologies (hydraulic fracturing and pressure pumping) and Great Plains Oilfield Rental (rental tools and equipment). After the 2014-2016 oil price collapse it completed a prepackaged Chapter 11 restructuring and recapitalization, emerging in August 2016. THE COMPANY NO LONGER EXISTS. Patterson-UTI Energy completed its merger with Seventy Seven Energy on 20 April 2017 in a transaction valued at roughly USD 1.76 billion, issuing about 47.5 million shares and repaying USD 472 million of Seventy Seven Energy debt at closing; Nomac was absorbed into Patterson-UTI Drilling and Performance Technologies into Universal Pressure Pumping. Seventy Seven Energy never operated a public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and there is no surviving entity to publish one — its own domain, seventysevenenergy.com, no longer resolves.

providers.name: SGI (Silicon Graphics)
providers.description: SGI, or Silicon Graphics, was a workstation, server, supercomputing, and computer-graphics company founded in 1982 and one of Mayfield's landmark early portfolio companies. It pioneered high-performance 3D graphics hardware, the IRIX operating system, and the OpenGL API. The independent company was acquired by Rackable Systems in 2009 (which adopted the SGI name) and that business was in turn acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in 2016. There is no longer an independent SGI developer program or public API surface; the historic sgi.com domain now redirects to HPE's high-performance-computing product line. This profile is retained as a historic Mayfield portfolio record; it is not an active API provider.

providers.name: Shelby.tv
providers.description: Shelby.tv was a Techstars-backed social video discovery startup that let people find, share, and watch videos surfaced from their social networks. The company has shut down; shelby.tv now serves only a founders' farewell page and no longer operates any product, developer program, or public API. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Shoppr
providers.description: Shoppr was a Malaysia-based consumer fashion-discovery mobile app (launched May 2015, often described as the "Tinder of fashion") that let shoppers swipe through personalized clothing recommendations. The founding team, led by Kendrick Wong, subsequently pivoted the business into Omnilytics, a B2B fashion retail market-intelligence and analytics platform serving brands and retailers. As of this enrichment pass the associated domain omnilytics.co is a parked domain (nameservers lander.d.parity.domains) and neither Shoppr nor Omnilytics exposes any public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal. This entry originated as a 500 Global portfolio lead and is retained for record; it has no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Shoreline
providers.description: Shoreline Software Inc. built an incident-automation platform for cloud operations, letting SRE and platform teams close the loop between detection and repair: an alarm defines when there is an issue, an action defines the command that fixes it, and a bot binds the two into an auto-remediation loop that runs without a human. The platform also shipped runbooks, notebooks, resource queries, file distribution and an Op query language, driven from a UI, a CLI, notebooks or Terraform. NVIDIA acquired Shoreline in July 2024 and the independent product surface has since been decommissioned — shoreline.io and docs.shoreline.io no longer resolve, and www.shoreline.io redirects in full to nvidia.com. The only first-party developer artifact still published is the Terraform provider, now archived.

providers.name: Shoreline Biosciences
providers.description: Shoreline Biosciences was a San Diego, California clinical-stage biotechnology company developing off-the-shelf, allogeneic cell therapies from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), principally iPSC-derived natural killer (iNK) cells and macrophages engineered for oncology indications. It raised roughly $140M, acquired Editas Medicine's iNK cell franchise and related gene-editing technologies in 2023, and signed collaborations with Kite Pharma (Gilead) and BeiGene with headline values above $4B. Therapeutics, not software, were the product: no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification was ever published. As of this profiling pass the company's own domain, shorelinebio.com, no longer serves a website — it answers HTTP 404 with a Squarespace "Website Expired" holding page — and the company is tracked here only as a secondary-market entity.

providers.name: Shunra
providers.description: Shunra Software (founded 1997, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) was an application performance engineering and network virtualization vendor whose products let teams emulate real-world network conditions to test application and mobile performance before deployment. Hewlett-Packard acquired Shunra's network virtualization business in March 2014 to expand its LoadRunner and Performance Center mobile-testing capabilities; the technology moved to HPE's software division and then to Micro Focus in 2016 (now part of OpenText). Shunra no longer operates as an independent company: the shunra.com domain redirects to HPE's domain-redirect 404 handler (nameservers softwaregrp.com) and there is no live product, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead but resolves to a defunct/absorbed company with nothing to enrich.

providers.name: Sibeam
providers.description: SiBEAM, Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company that pioneered 60GHz millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless technology and helped drive the WirelessHD standard for uncompressed wireless HD video and multi-gigabit data links. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment (sector: semiconductors). The enrichment pass found no independent public surface: SiBEAM was acquired by Silicon Image in 2011, and Silicon Image was in turn acquired by Lattice Semiconductor in 2015, so there is no live SiBEAM website, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Sidecar
providers.description: Sidecar (side.cr) was added to the API Evangelist network as a Union Square Ventures portfolio lead. The side.cr domain today hosts a transportation news and information content platform (self-described as "building the largest transportation news source powered by everyday people"), covering ridesharing, driving, delivery, safety, and automotive topics for riders and drivers. It is a reader-facing editorial site, not a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, OpenAPI, or any /.well-known discovery surface. The name echoes the pioneering peer-to-peer Sidecar ridesharing company that Union Square Ventures backed and that wound down in 2015, but the current content site states no operational or corporate ties to that defunct service. This profile is retained as a company/lead record with no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: SigOpt
providers.description: SigOpt was a machine learning experimentation and optimization platform whose API applied ensemble Bayesian and black-box optimization to tune model hyperparameters, run design-of-experiments, and track experiment metadata at scale. Developers integrated its REST API and first-party clients (Python, Java, R, scikit-learn, Spark, MATLAB) to drive automated hyperparameter search from their training loops. SigOpt was acquired by Intel in 2020 and its hosted API and platform were subsequently discontinued; sigopt.com now redirects to an Intel corporate redirector and the api./app./docs.sigopt.com hosts no longer resolve. The GitHub organization (github.com/sigopt) and the published client libraries remain public as historical, first-party artifacts, including an open-sourced server and optimization engine (sigopt-server, sigoptlite, libsigopt).

providers.name: Silicon Optix
providers.description: Silicon Optix Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company that designed image- and video-processing chips, best known for its Realta HQV (Hollywood Quality Video) processor for high-definition video scaling, de-interlacing, and noise reduction, and for the Teranex line of professional video processors. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners, it was acquired by Integrated Device Technology (IDT) in 2008 (IDT was subsequently acquired by Renesas). The company operated as a hardware/chip vendor and did not publish a public developer API; its historical primary domain (siliconoptix.com) no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a network stub with no live API surface.

providers.name: Silver Spring Networks *
providers.description: Silver Spring Networks was a smart-grid, smart-city, and IoT networking company that built wireless canopy networks and the SLV/Data Platform for utilities, offering RESTful Data Platform APIs (device registration, device metadata, sensor data, and webhook event notifications) plus an SDK on its developer portal at developer.ssni.com. Itron completed its acquisition of the company in January 2018 for approximately USD 830 million and rebranded it Itron Networked Solutions; the standalone ssni.com and developer.ssni.com properties are now offline. Enrichment pass 2026-07-21 found no live API surface: all legacy domains fail to resolve and the historical developer portal is no longer reachable.

providers.name: Silver Tail
providers.description: Silver Tail Systems was a website fraud and abuse detection company founded in 2008 in Menlo Park, California by Mike Eynon and Laura Mather, both formerly on the anti-fraud team at eBay/PayPal. Its product collected and analyzed real-time web traffic to deliver web session intelligence and predictive analytics that detected fraud, account takeover, and abuse on banking and commerce websites. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) among others, the company raised roughly $20M across three rounds before being acquired by RSA, the security division of EMC, in 2012 and rebranded as RSA Web Threat Detection. It no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no live developer or API surface.

providers.name: Simple
providers.description: Simple is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global, anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Simple Energy
providers.description: Simple Energy was a portfolio company of Techstars, surfaced and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07 enrichment pass, its domain simpleenergy.com no longer hosts a product site; it returns a static page stating the domain is owned by Uplight and immediately redirects to uplight.com. Probing found no public API surface for Simple Energy - no api/developer/docs subdomains resolve, no .well-known endpoints, no OpenAPI, no llms.txt - so this remains an identity-only company record.

providers.name: Simple Feast
providers.description: Simple Feast was a Danish plant-based, ready-to-eat meal company surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the consumer app host food.simplefeast.com no longer resolves and the root domain simplefeast.com is parked on one.com nameservers, so the company appears defunct. No developer portal, API, documentation, or other machine-readable API surface could be discovered during enrichment; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Skew
providers.description: Skew is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.
