providers.name: Skip Scooters
providers.description: Skip Scooters (operated by Skip Transport / Waybots) was a San Francisco-based dockless shared electric scooter (micromobility) startup and one of the early operators permitted in San Francisco, also running fleets in Washington, D.C. Backed by Accel, the company wound down and its assets moved to Helbiz around 2020. It is no longer operating: its former consumer app and rider domains (rideskip.com is a parked for-sale domain, skip.com now resolves to an unrelated retailer) have no live developer, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record; the enrichment pipeline found no public API to harvest.

providers.name: Skipjaq
providers.description: Skipjaq, Inc. was a machine-learning performance-optimisation startup that marketed itself as "Performance Optimisation as a Service" and was backed by Accel. Its proprietary automated workload-optimisation software ran repeated optimization tests against a customer's application (hosted in the cloud on AWS EC2 instances behind Elastic Load Balancers) and used machine learning to tune configuration for better application performance, throughput, and latency without manual, expert tuning. The product was delivered as a cloud SaaS and was offered under a beta test agreement. The company is now defunct: the skipjaq.com domain no longer resolves on any common TLD (.com/.io/.ai/.co.uk all return no A/NS records as of 2026-07-21), the last archived snapshot of the site dates to May 2025, and there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, first-party SDK, or live API surface. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio lead.

providers.name: Skybox Security
providers.description: Skybox Security was a cybersecurity vendor, headquartered in San Jose, California with R&D in Israel, whose Security Posture Management Platform combined attack surface visibility, network modelling and attack-path analysis, firewall assurance and change management, vulnerability and exposure management, and its own threat intelligence feed for large hybrid enterprise and OT networks. It raised roughly $335 million in venture and private-equity funding, including a $50 million round in February 2023, before ceasing operations on February 24, 2025 and laying off approximately 300 employees across the United States and Israel. Tufin acquired a limited portion of Skybox's business and technology and retained select personnel, but did not assume Skybox's customer contracts or support obligations; it instead runs an "ExpressPath for Skybox Customers" migration programme onto the Tufin Orchestration Suite. Skybox exposed a REST API and integrations (Splunk, ServiceNow, Elasticsearch) to its customers, but the reference lived behind customer/partner credentials at docs.skyboxsecurity.com and no machine-readable contract was ever published publicly. Every skyboxsecurity.com host now 301-redirects into tufin.com, so nothing served on those hosts can be attributed to Skybox any longer.

providers.name: Skyboximaging
providers.description: Skybox Imaging was a satellite imaging and geospatial-analytics company (founded 2009, Mountain View, CA) that built a constellation of small high-resolution Earth-observation satellites (SkySat) and the analytics to turn frequent imagery into commercial insight. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Bessemer, Khosla Ventures and others, it was acquired by Google in 2014 (~$500M), renamed Terra Bella, and its satellite business was sold to Planet Labs in 2017. The skyboximaging.com domain is no longer a live product surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph and historical reference.

providers.name: Skyport Systems *
providers.description: Skyport Systems was a cloud infrastructure security startup, backed by GV and other investors, best known for SkySecure — a hyperconverged secure server appliance that enforced workload isolation and firewall policy in dedicated hardware for critical enterprise data-center workloads. Cisco acquired the company on January 24, 2018 and did not continue the standalone SkySecure offering, so Skyport Systems no longer operates as an independent company. Enrichment found no live developer surface: skyportsystems.com is a parked/for-sale domain and skyportsystems.net now serves an unrelated cybersecurity news aggregator. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record (surfaced as a GV portfolio company) with no public API, developer portal, or SDKs to catalog.

providers.name: Slime Sandwich
providers.description: Slime Sandwich was an online gaming company that developed in-browser 3D games. It was founded in 2009 in Englewood, Colorado by Douglas Glover, Vadim Ugov, and former Photobucket CEO Alex Welch, and raised a $2.75M Series A round backed by Battery Ventures. The company has since permanently ceased operations and its slimesandwich.com domain is no longer active (now a parked/for-sale listing). It was originally surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; enrichment confirms there is no live company website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to profile.

providers.name: Slingshot
providers.description: Slingshot is a self-custody, multi-chain DeFi application and wallet founded in 2020 and headquartered in San Francisco, letting retail users search, send, receive, and swap tens of thousands of cryptocurrencies at aggregated best prices with 0% swap fees. It is available on Web, iOS, and Android with bridging support across Ethereum Mainnet, Arbitrum, Arbitrum Nova, Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, and Canto. Backed by Electric Capital, Slingshot combined centralized-exchange ease with the openness of decentralized exchanges. NOTE: Slingshot announced it is sunsetting, advising users to export their private keys before February 28, 2026; its GitHub organization was archived in January 2026. This profile documents a consumer DeFi product that exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: SLM Software Company
providers.description: SLM Software Company (SLMsoft.com) was a Toronto, Canada based developer of electronic payment systems and real-time transaction processing solutions for the financial services industry, founded in 1986. Its platform bundled a transaction management engine with application modules for Internet banking, IVR, debit and credit card issuing, ATM and point-of-sale network management, retail branch management, and e-CRM, along with brokerage portfolio management, e-health claims settlement, and e-government payment products, serving over 1,500 customers across 52 countries. The company was acquired by The InterCept Group (C$110 million) and is now permanently closed. It was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found no live API, developer portal, documentation, or other public developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: SLP InfoWare
providers.description: SLP InfoWare was a French software company founded in 1989 by graduates of Telecom ParisTech and based in Paris, France, providing customer profiling, churn prediction, fraud detection, and retention analytics to the telecommunications, banking, and insurance industries. Its flagship products included CHURN MINER and a Churn/CPS application that analyzed customer billing data to predict and prevent subscriber attrition. The company raised venture funding and was acquired by Gemplus International SA in October 2000 (Gemplus later became part of Gemalto, now Thales). No independent SLP InfoWare website, developer portal, or public API surface exists today; this record is retained as a historical / portfolio-lineage entry in the API Evangelist network and carries no live API artifacts.

providers.name: Smarterer
providers.description: Smarterer was a Boston-based skills-assessment company that used crowdsourced, adaptive tests to rapidly quantify people's proficiency across 400+ technical, social, and business skills. Backed by Google Ventures (GV), it opened a REST API in March 2015 that let partners embed tests, pull score data, and build leaderboards and profiles on top of its assessment engine. Pluralsight acquired Smarterer for roughly $75M in November 2014, absorbed its test engine into the Pluralsight learning platform, and wound down the standalone product. The smarterer.com domain no longer serves a site (defensively held via MarkMonitor, no DNS A record) and there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Snapette
providers.description: Snapette was a mobile fashion-discovery and local-shopping application that operated from 2011 to 2013, letting users photograph, share, and discover fashion items and nearby boutique inventory. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), it was acquired by PriceGrabber in 2013 and subsequently ceased operations. This API Evangelist profile is retained as an archival portfolio-company record; the company publishes no developer program, API, or SDK surface. The snapette.com domain now serves only an archival page documenting the app's history, founders, and business model.

providers.name: Snapfinger
providers.description: Snapfinger was an online and mobile food-ordering platform that let diners browse menus and place takeout and delivery orders across a network of restaurant brands. The snapfinger.com domain now 301-redirects to Tillster, the restaurant-commerce company (ordering, kiosk, loyalty, menu, and data solutions for 40,000+ restaurants), so Snapfinger operates today as a defunct brand absorbed into Tillster. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published under the Snapfinger name. It remains in the API Evangelist network as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio lead pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: Snaproute
providers.description: SnapRoute was a cloud-native networking startup, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Norwest Venture Partners, that built a containerized, microservices-based network operating system (its FlexSwitch / Cloud-Native Network OS) aimed at running switch software with the same DevOps tooling used for application infrastructure. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/snaproute) reflects that focus — OpenConfig and YANG tooling (pyang/pyangbind), OpenNetworkLinux, netlink, sFlow, and a Docker-based training lab — but it has been dormant since 2020 and ships no published REST/OpenAPI interface, SDKs, or developer portal. The company no longer operates independently: the snaproute.com domain now 301-redirects to infoblox.com, so there is no live API surface to enrich. This profile records the verifiable remnants (GitHub organization, domain posture) rather than a working developer program.

providers.name: Socialcam
providers.description: Socialcam was a mobile social video application (iPhone, Android, Windows Phone) for capturing, editing, and sharing short videos across social networks. Founded by Michael Seibel, Ammon Bartram, and Guillaume Luccisano out of Y Combinator (W2012) and backed by a16z, it reached roughly 16 million downloads and was acquired by Autodesk in July 2012 for $60 million. The consumer service was discontinued on October 28, 2015, and socialcam.com no longer resolves to a live web host (AWS Route 53 nameservers only, no A record), so there is no developer portal, API, documentation, or agent surface to enrich.

providers.name: Sockeye Networks
providers.description: Sockeye Networks was a network-management software company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. It provided intelligent internet routing and connectivity-optimization services, combining real-time global internet traffic data with customer-specific measurements to optimize enterprise IP connectivity for improved network performance, efficiency, and visibility. The company appears to be defunct or long-inactive; no active website domain resolves and no public developer/API surface, documentation, or specifications could be found during enrichment.

providers.name: Solar Mosaic
providers.description: Solar Mosaic, Inc. (trading as Mosaic) was a residential clean-energy lender founded in Oakland, California in 2010, originally as a solar crowdfunding platform and from 2014 as a point-of-sale financing platform for residential solar, battery storage and other sustainable home improvements funded through third-party capital partners. Mosaic originated loans through a dealer/installer channel and backed more than $15 billion in home energy loans across roughly 360,000 households. Its integration surface for installer and capital partners was the Mosaic Financing API, documented on a password-protected ReadMe developer portal at developer.joinmosaic.com. Solar Mosaic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the Southern District of Texas on 2025-06-09 and its loan portfolio was acquired in September 2025 by Solar Servicing LLC, which stated it would not originate new solar loans. As of this profile the joinmosaic.com website 301-redirects to solarservicingllc.com, the api.joinmosaic.com host returns HTTP 503, and the Mosaic status page reports "Page Inactive".

providers.name: Sold *
providers.description: Sold * was a consumer resale service (a mobile app that sold your unwanted items on your behalf, handling pricing, listing, and fulfillment). Backed by GV, the Sold team was acqui-hired by Dropbox; the service was shut down and no longer accepts items. The homepage at usesold.com now serves only an acquisition/shutdown notice. No developer portal, API, documentation, or well-known surface exists (all api/developer/docs subdomains fail to resolve; /.well-known/*, /llms.txt, and /openapi.json return 404). Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Soldsie
providers.description: Soldsie was a social-commerce platform founded in 2012 in San Francisco by Chris Bennett and Arrel Gray that let retailers sell directly through social media: customers bought products by commenting "Sold" on a merchant's Facebook or Instagram post, while a backend dashboard handled invoicing, customer tracking, and waitlists. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and e.ventures, it raised roughly $1M in seed funding and a $4M Series A (2014), and had processed over $25M in transactions across more than 1,000 merchants. The product is now defunct: the soldsie.com apex no longer resolves and www.soldsie.com returns a broken redirect, so there is no live developer portal, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Solid (Solid.fi)
providers.description: Solid (formerly Wise) was a venture-backed fintech-as-a-service / embedded finance platform offering banking, card, and payment APIs to fintech builders. Solid raised more than $80M, including a 2022 Series B led by FTV Capital. The company subsequently became the subject of significant legal trouble - including litigation with FTV Capital and reported customer disputes - and substantially wound down operations through 2023-2024. As of this profile, the solidfi.com site is not responding to requests and no active API or onboarding pipeline appears to be operating. This is an honest historical record; treat any API references as unverified / inactive.

providers.name: Sosh
providers.description: Sosh was a San Francisco-based social-discovery mobile app (founded 2010) that acted as a "social concierge," giving members a personalized collection of local activities, events, and places to do and share. It was backed by Battery Ventures and Khosla Ventures among others. Sosh was acqui-hired by on-demand delivery service Postmates in November 2015 and the consumer app was subsequently discontinued. Enrichment research (WebFetch) found no surviving product, developer portal, documentation, or public API; the sosh.com domain is now a parked "for sale" listing. There is no live API surface to enrich, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Spectra
providers.description: Spectra (formerly Spectra Experiences, originally Comcast-Spectacor Ventures / Global Spectrum + Ovations Food Services + Paciolan + Front Row Marketing) was a North American venue management, food services & hospitality, and partnership-sales company headquartered in Philadelphia, PA. Owned jointly by Comcast Spectacor and Atairos, Spectra was acquired by Oak View Group (OVG) in a deal announced August 31, 2021 and closed on November 15, 2021 after receiving U.S. Department of Justice approval. On February 25, 2022, OVG formally consolidated Spectra and OVG Facilities into a single, rebranded division called OVG360. The Spectra and Spectra Experiences brands were retired as a result, and the spectraexperiences.com domain is no longer resolvable. This apis.yml is preserved as an historical record only — Spectra never published a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal. Operational successor: OVG360 (https://www.oakviewgroup.com/ovg360-2/). Ticketing platform Paciolan, which had been part of the Spectra portfolio, was divested before the OVG deal and is now an independent Learfield subsidiary.

providers.name: Speechly
providers.description: Speechly was a real-time spoken language understanding (SLU) and streaming speech recognition platform from a Finnish startup, offering low-latency voice transcription, intent/entity parsing, written language understanding (WLU), batch audio processing, and audio/text moderation through a gRPC API with browser, React, iOS, Unity/.NET, Python and Go client SDKs and a command-line interface. Speechly was acquired by Roblox; the standalone product and hosted API have since been discontinued — speechly.com now redirects to roblox.com, the api.speechly.com and docs.speechly.com hosts no longer resolve, and the github.com/speechly organization was archived on 2025-01-07. Its open-source client SDKs and protobuf/gRPC API definitions remain publicly available and are cataloged here by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Spenmo
providers.description: Spenmo was a Singapore-based spend management platform for businesses, offering corporate Visa debit cards (physical and virtual), bill and invoice management with smart scanning, employee reimbursements and claims, and accounting integrations with Xero, NetSuite, QuickBooks and Jurnal. Operated by Digital Services SG Five Pte Ltd, it worked with MAS-licensed payment partners rather than providing regulated payment services directly. The company ceased operations on 14 August 2025 and permanently disabled customer access. No public API or developer program was ever published.

providers.name: Splitty
providers.description: Splitty (splittytravel.com) is a Techstars-backed online travel company that offered discounted hotel bookings by algorithmically splitting a single multi-night stay across separate reservations to surface lower nightly rates. The consumer service has since been wound down and now operates as "Splitty by trivago DEALS Ltd." - it no longer accepts new bookings and only lets existing customers manage their reservations, redirecting new hotel searches to trivago DEALS (trivago.DEALS). Splitty publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: SPLT
providers.description: SPLT is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of techstars and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: SpoonRocket
providers.description: SpoonRocket was an on-demand, prepared-meal delivery startup backed by a16z that delivered low-cost ready-to-eat meals on demand. The company has since ceased operations and its spoonrocket.com domain no longer resolves to a live website (AWS Route53 nameservers remain delegated, but there is no A record). It publishes no developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or public API surface. This profile remains in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead with no active API to enrich.

providers.name: Sqoot
providers.description: Sqoot is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Sqreen
providers.description: Sqreen was a Paris- and San Francisco-based application security company offering Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP), an in-app Web Application Firewall, and account-takeover and attack protection delivered through language agents for Node.js, Python, Ruby, PHP, Java and Go. Backed by Y Combinator, Greylock and Point Nine, Sqreen was acquired by Datadog in 2021 and its technology was folded into Datadog Application Security Management. The standalone sqreen.com product, dashboard and developer APIs have since been decommissioned; the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical company lead and has no live, independent API surface to enrich.

providers.name: St. Bernard Software
providers.description: St. Bernard Software was a San Diego-based web-security company (iPrism web-filtering appliances) that rebranded to EdgeWave and whose technology and domains now resolve to the successor cybersecurity provider GoSecure (gosecure.ai / gosecure.net). The St. Bernard Software brand is defunct: an enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 confirmed stbernard.com presents a *.gosecure.net certificate and edgewave.com 301-redirects to gosecure.ai. The successor company GoSecure offers 24/7 managed detection and response services and publishes no developer portal or public API. This company therefore has no independent, live API surface to enrich, and no API artifacts were created (attributing GoSecure's surface to this legacy slug would conflate two distinct companies).

providers.name: StackPath
providers.description: StackPath was an American edge computing platform provider headquartered in Dallas, Texas, founded in 2015 by SoftLayer co-founder Lance Crosby. It sold CDN, WAF/WAAP, DNS, SSL, object storage, edge compute (containers and VMs), serverless scripting and monitoring as a single edge platform, driven by a public REST API at gateway.stackpath.com with OAuth2 client-credentials auth and per-service OpenAPI definitions. The company exited the CDN business in 2023 (roughly 100 enterprise CDN contracts went to Akamai), sold its web application and API protection assets to Gcore in March 2024, then announced in June 2024 that it was ceasing operations and liquidating its remaining assets. All StackPath API, developer-portal, control-panel and status hosts have since been withdrawn from DNS and the company no longer publishes any machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Stamplay
providers.description: Stamplay was a backend-as-a-service and API-integration platform — billed as "Lego for developers" — founded in 2012 (Turin, Italy; later San Francisco) and backed by 500 Global. It let developers assemble application backends by visually wiring together third-party APIs, authentication providers, hosted data objects, webhooks, and static site hosting on stamplayapp.com, driven by a JavaScript SDK, a Node.js SDK, and the `stamplay` CLI. The product has been discontinued: the company was acquired (widely reported as Apple, 2019), the stamplay.com domain is now held via MarkMonitor and returns no HTTP response, every source repository in the GitHub organization is archived, and the npm SDK/CLI packages were last published in 2016. This API Evangelist profile preserves the historical developer footprint (SDKs and CLI) rather than a live API surface.

providers.name: Standard Treasury
providers.description: Standard Treasury is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Stateless
providers.description: Stateless was a Boulder, Colorado network-infrastructure startup (founded 2016) that built a software platform for network automation in the hybrid multi-cloud era, delivering network functions such as firewalls and load balancers through an "as a service" consumption model with an emphasis on simplicity, scalability, and evolvability. Backed by Speedinvest, the National Science Foundation, Drive Capital, and Matchstick Ventures, with its last funding announced in December 2022. The company now appears defunct — its former domains (stateless.net, getstateless.com) redirect to domain-parking "for sale" pages and no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface remains.

providers.name: Statwing
providers.description: Statwing was a self-serve statistical-analysis SaaS tool that let non-statisticians run and interpret analyses on survey and spreadsheet data through a point-and-click interface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-21) found no live company or developer surface. Statwing was acquired by Qualtrics in 2015 and the product discontinued, and the statwing.com domain now serves an unrelated Thai-language lifestyle site. No API, documentation, SDKs, or developer resources exist.

providers.name: Stay Alfred
providers.description: Stay Alfred Inc. was a Spokane, Washington short-term-rental and hospitality operator that pioneered the "travel apartment" — full apartments in walkable downtown cores, leased in bulk from multifamily building owners and operated with hotel-style consistency, cleaning and guest support. Founded in 2011 by Jordan Allen, who was named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year for the Pacific Northwest in 2019, the company grew to roughly 2,000-2,500 units across 28 to 33 U.S. markets including Denver, San Diego, Miami, New Orleans and Nashville, hosted around half a million guests, and employed more than 230 people. It raised approximately $62M in total venture funding, headlined by a $47M Series B in October 2018 led by Chicago real-estate technology fund Nine Four Ventures. Distribution ran through its own consumer booking site and the major online travel agencies, so Stay Alfred was an API CONSUMER rather than an API publisher; it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification. COVID-19 ended it: the company closed every property nationwide from 1 April 2020, a rescue funding round was withdrawn at the last minute, and on 20 May 2020 Stay Alfred announced it would close permanently, winding down through mid-2020 while it had been on track for roughly $100M in revenue that year. The stayalfred.com domain is still on its original 2013 registration but is no longer controlled by the company: it is privacy-shielded, Cloudflare-hosted, and every path now 301-redirects into a rotating chain of unrelated third-party sites. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Stockpile
providers.description: Stockpile was a Palo Alto, California consumer investing company — "the money app for families" — that let people buy, sell and gift fractional shares in stocks and ETFs, and that popularized the stock gift card, a physical or digital card redeemed into a brokerage account at Stockpile Investments, Inc. (a FINRA/SIPC member broker-dealer). Alongside custodial kid and teen accounts it sold Family Base and Family Plus subscriptions bundling debit cards and savings. The company wound down on April 17, 2026; customer accounts were moved to Public, Stash and Apex, and www.stockpile.com now serves only a Stockpile gift-card refund request form operated on the issuer's behalf by CIMI2603, Inc. Stockpile never published a public API, developer portal or machine-readable contract; its only public developer surface was an embeddable stock/brand modal, archived in 2016.

providers.name: Storability
providers.description: Storability Software was an enterprise storage resource management (SRM) company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Southborough, Massachusetts. It built software to simplify and centralize the management of complex, multi-site, multi-vendor storage infrastructures, raising roughly $67M from investors including Battery Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Madison Dearborn Partners. The company was acquired by Storage Technology Corporation (StorageTek) on October 11, 2004, and no longer operates as an independent entity. It has no surviving website, developer portal, or public API surface.

providers.name: Storicity
providers.description: Storicity Inc. was a Seoul, South Korea-based travel-technology startup, founded around 2020 and backed by 500 Global, that built Yoda Trip (Korean brand "여다") — an AI-assisted consumer travel-planning mobile app offering customized itineraries and mobile audio guides for tourist destinations, shipped on iOS and Android. It was a consumer B2C mobile product rather than an API platform provider. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 (web search plus a live domain/TLS probe) found no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK packages, GitHub organization, or other developer surface. Public records indicate the Yoda Trip service was discontinued in April 2025 and the company is listed as out of business; the yodatrip.com domain still resolves but serves a broken TLS certificate.

providers.name: Storigen Systems
providers.description: Storigen Systems was an Internet infrastructure company founded in 2000 and based in Lowell, Massachusetts, that pioneered the Distributed Storage Network — a class of infrastructure intended to improve the economics and performance of bandwidth-intensive applications by enabling efficient storage, delivery, and management of data across distributed environments. The company raised roughly $49M from investors including Battery Ventures, Charles River Ventures (CRV), Flagship Pioneering, and Pilot House Ventures before ceasing operations; it is now permanently closed. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no live domain, developer portal, documentation, or API surface — the company is defunct and publishes nothing to harvest.

providers.name: StratoScale
providers.description: Stratoscale was an Israeli software-defined data center company founded in 2013 in Herzliya by Ariel Maislos and backed by Battery Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, Intel Capital, Cisco, Qualcomm Ventures and SanDisk ($70M raised). Its flagship product, Stratoscale Symphony (announced December 2015), delivered AWS-compatible cloud infrastructure on commodity x86 hardware — an API-driven, hyperconverged platform exposing EC2-, S3-, EBS-, EFS-, RDS-, ELB- and EMR-compatible services plus Kubernetes and Docker, alongside OpenStack and vCenter compatibility for hybrid and multi-cloud operations. The company ceased operations at the end of 2019 due to insufficient funding; there is no longer a live developer portal, documentation site, or reachable API surface. Its public GitHub organization (open-source Go/go-swagger tooling) remains available.

providers.name: Strattic
providers.description: Strattic was a static and headless WordPress hosting platform that pre-rendered WordPress sites into static assets for improved security, performance, and scalability, while preserving the familiar WordPress admin experience via SFTP and WP-CLI developer access. Strattic was acquired by Elementor in 2022 and folded into Elementor Hosting; Elementor announced the sunset of its dedicated static hosting service in 2025, and strattic.com now 301-redirects to elementor.com/hosting/. No independent Strattic public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remains.

providers.name: StreamLoan
providers.description: StreamLoan was a digital mortgage software company offering a point-of-sale (POS) and loan-origination platform that connected loan officers, borrowers, and real-estate agents to convert leads into funded home loans faster. Its toolkit spanned lead management, borrower communication and collaboration, workflow automation, document collection, security/privacy controls, and a branded borrower experience aimed at cutting the 40+ day mortgage close cycle. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - streamloan.io is parked on a registrar IP and every developer/app/api/docs/portal subdomain is unreachable (DNS records remain but no host responds), and no public API or developer program was ever documented.

providers.name: Streamonce
providers.description: StreamOnce was a cloud-based enterprise collaboration platform founded in 2012 in San Jose, California by Ilan Twig and Ariel Cohen (who later co-founded TripActions/Navan). The product connected business systems into a social enterprise layer so teams could reply to emails, read documents, and post to Yammer and Chatter from a single unified interface. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (~$1.25-1.36M raised), the company was acquired by Jive Software in 2013, less than a year after its initial funding. StreamOnce is no longer an operating company and publishes no active product, developer portal, or API; the streamonce.com domain now redirects to a domain-sale marketplace. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record surfaced via Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Styleup
providers.description: StyleUp was a Y Combinator (Winter 2013) fashion advisory startup that delivered personalized daily outfit recommendations tailored to the user's local weather and individual style preferences, learning from feedback to improve suggestions over time. It operated as a consumer styling service out of the San Francisco Bay Area rather than as an API or developer platform. The company is now defunct and no longer operates: its former domain (thestyleup.com) has been repurposed by an unrelated third party and serves a Turkish sports-streaming site, so there is no live product, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface remaining to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical stub with no active API artifacts.

providers.name: Styvio
providers.description: Realtime and historical stock data and current stock sentiment

providers.name: Suborbital
providers.description: Suborbital was a developer-tools company building a WebAssembly-based extensibility platform: the Suborbital Extension Engine (SE2, formerly Suborbital Compute), a hosted service for running sandboxed third-party plugins; E2 Core / Reactr, a function scheduler for Go and WebAssembly; Sat, a tiny fast Wasm edge-compute server; Grav, an embedded decentralized message bus; and the subo CLI for building Wasm plugins and scaffolding projects. Suborbital was acquired by F5 in 2023 and the hosted product was subsequently wound down; the suborbital.dev domain has since been repurposed as an unrelated content blog. The first-party open-source client libraries (npm @suborbital/*, the se2-go Go client, and the subo CLI) and the 32-repo GitHub organization remain publicly available.

providers.name: Subspace
providers.description: Subspace was a real-time network-as-a-service platform delivering a dedicated, performance-optimized global network for latency-sensitive applications — WebRTC, VoIP/SIP calling, video conferencing, multiplayer gaming, and fintech. Its Product API provisions three services: PacketAccelerator (no-code global internet acceleration), SIPTeleport (SIP/VoIP call-quality improvement), and WebRTC-CDN (instant global WebRTC acceleration with ICE server configuration). The REST API uses resource-oriented URLs and JSON responses, versioned at v1, authenticated with OAuth2 client-credentials issuing 24-hour JWT bearer tokens via Auth0, and ships six first-party OpenAPI client SDKs. The company was a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company; its marketing site remains live while the API, identity, and status hosts have wound down operationally.

providers.name: SumAll
providers.description: SumAll was a New York-based social media and business analytics startup, surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct - its primary domain sumall.com no longer resolves to a live product and is parked/listed for sale on Afternic. There is no live developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface to harvest, so no provider artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Superpedestrian
providers.description: Superpedestrian was a Cambridge, Massachusetts micromobility company founded in December 2012 by MIT Senseable City Lab co-inventor Assaf Biderman. It built the Copenhagen Wheel electric bicycle retrofit (2017) and then the LINK shared e-scooter fleet (2020), whose differentiator was an onboard Vehicle Intelligence System running self-diagnostic safety checks on every ride. It raised roughly $185M (a $60M round in December 2020 and a $125M Series C in February 2022 with Citi Impact Fund and Sony Innovation Fund) and at its 2022 peak ran shared fleets in about 57 cities across eleven US states and seven European countries. Superpedestrian closed its US operations on 31 December 2023 and auctioned more than 20,000 scooters in January 2024; the European business was sold to Norway's SURF Beyond in February 2024 and subsequently folded into ZEUS Mobility. The company published no public developer program and no machine-readable API contract. Its only known machine-readable surface was per-city GBFS feeds served for host cities at mds.linkyour.city, which are offline. Both superpedestrian.com and link.city are now parked domains that answer HTTP 200 to every path with a domain-parking lander, and link.city is delegated to afternic.com nameservers and listed for sale.

providers.name: Sverve
providers.description: Sverve was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. During the enrichment pass the company's website (sverve.com) was offline — the origin returned HTTP 522 behind Cloudflare, and its DNS (NameBright registrar-parking MX/SPF and a "comingsoon.namebright.com" DMARC target) indicates the domain is parked and the company appears inactive. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or public API surface could be found, so there is nothing to enrich beyond a probed domain-security record. Left as an inactive lead.

providers.name: Sygate
providers.description: Sygate Technologies was an endpoint-security software company founded in 1995 in Fremont, California, and backed by Trinity Ventures among other investors. Its products included enterprise server and end-user firewalls (Sygate Personal Firewall), automated network discovery, network access control (NAC), and security monitoring. Symantec acquired Sygate in 2005 for its Universal Network Access Control technology; the end-user products were subsequently discontinued and the enterprise NAC technology folded into Symantec (now Gen Digital). Sygate is a defunct entity with no active company website, developer portal, or public API surface; this profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Symmorphix
providers.description: Symmorphix, Inc. was a materials-science company founded in 1998 and based in Sunnyvale, California, that developed and manufactured advanced amorphous dielectric and optical thin films for the optical-networking and communications industries. Its core technology was a proprietary wide-area physical vapor deposition (PVD) process performed at low temperatures, enabling deposition of a broad range of material compositions onto metal, ceramic, and polymer substrates for use as physical barriers, dielectric layers, and optical layers. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures and Crescendo Ventures and was acquired by Springworks on February 6, 2004. It is a defunct hardware/materials company with no public API, developer portal, or software developer surface, and is retained in the API Evangelist network only as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Synapse
providers.description: Synapse Financial Technologies was a San Francisco banking-as-a-service platform, founded 2014-04-14 by Sankaet Pathak and Bryan Keltner, that sold a REST API letting fintech companies open and operate deposit accounts, move money over ACH and wires, issue cards and run KYC/CIP checks through partner banks including Evolve Bank & Trust, AMG National Trust, American Bank North America and Lineage Bank. At its peak it served roughly 100 fintech platforms reaching about 10 million end customers, and it published first-party client libraries for Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go and PHP against its v3.1 REST API. Synapse filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 2024-04-22 with a $65-96 million shortfall between its records and its partner banks'; the sale of its technology assets drew no qualified bids and the case was later dismissed. The company is defunct: as of 2026-08-29 every synapsefi.com host returns NXDOMAIN, so the API, its documentation and its developer portal are all permanently unreachable. This profile records what survives — the first-party SDKs still published on npm, PyPI, RubyGems and the Go module proxy, and the public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Synplicity
providers.description: Synplicity, Inc. was a supplier of software for the design of programmable logic devices (FPGAs, PLDs and CPLDs) used in communications, military/aerospace, consumer, semiconductor and computer systems. Its tools provided logic synthesis, physical synthesis, ASIC prototyping and verification for FPGA and DSP designers (Synplify, Synplify Pro, Identify). Synplicity was acquired by Synopsys for approximately $227 million, with the transaction completed on 2008-05-15, and no longer operates as an independent company. The legacy domain synplicity.com now 301-redirects to synopsys.com. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners; it has no independent public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: SynQuest
providers.description: SynQuest, Inc. (formerly Nasdaq: SYNQ) was an Atlanta, Georgia based supply-chain planning and logistics software company that provided e-business solutions to optimize the financial and operational performance of the supply chain, including transportation, distribution, and inventory planning and simulation for customers such as Ford Motor Company. SynQuest reverse-merged with Viewlocity, Inc. in November 2002 (Viewlocity merged into SynQuest as the surviving entity) and was delisted from the Nasdaq SmallCap Market shortly after. Insight Partners (formerly Insight Venture Partners) was an early investor, which is why the company appears in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead. The company is inactive today and publishes no live website, developer portal, or public API surface; enrichment searches found only historical SEC filings and press coverage.

providers.name: Syntertainment
providers.description: Syntertainment was an entertainment technology startup founded in 2012 in Berkeley, California by game designer Will Wright (creator of SimCity and The Sims), Avi Bar-Zeev, and Anya Wright, emerging from the Stupid Fun Club collective. The company set out to explore the intersection of entertainment and reality, blending real-world data and player experiences with game-like interactive media. It raised roughly $5M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Mayfield, SV Angel, and former Electronic Arts CEO John Riccitiello. The venture never shipped a public consumer product and is no longer active; its website (syntertainment.com) is offline and it exposes no public developer program, documentation, or API surface. This profile was surfaced from an a16z portfolio list and enriched to reflect the company's real, historical status.

providers.name: Systems Center
providers.description: Systems Center, Inc. was a mainframe and enterprise systems-management software vendor best known for the NetMaster network-management product line. The company was acquired by Sterling Software of Dallas in a 1993 deal (approximately $185M), after which NetMaster was folded into Sterling's data-communications portfolio and rebranded (Connect:Direct lineage); Sterling Software was itself acquired by Computer Associates in 2000. Systems Center was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass (2026-07-21) searched for any live website, developer portal, or API surface and found none: the company is defunct with no independent public presence, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Tact.ai
providers.description: Tact.ai was a Redwood City, California conversational-AI and field-engagement company founded by Chuck Ganapathi that built an AI sales assistant ("Tact Assistant") unifying CRM, email, and calendar data into a voice- and chat-driven interface for enterprise sales teams, later concentrating on the life sciences vertical. It was backed by Accel, Redpoint Ventures, Upfront Ventures, Microsoft's M12, and Salesforce Ventures. In November 2023 its field-engagement and conversational-AI technology was acquired by Aktana and the standalone company wound down. The tact.ai domain no longer hosts a product: it resolves to an Afternic domain-for-sale parking page (nameservers ns1/ns2.afternic.com), and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal to enrich.

providers.name: Tactic
providers.description: Tactic was a cryptocurrency and digital-asset accounting platform founded in 2021 in New York and backed by Lux Capital. Its product aggregated on-chain activity and exchange/custody data (Coinbase and others) into a unified treasury view and crypto sub-ledger, automatically categorizing transactions, calculating USD gain/loss and taxable events, and reconciling the crypto sub-ledger to traditional accounting software such as QuickBooks. Tactic launched from stealth in 2022 (originally on choosetactic.com, later the exact-match tactic.com) and raised roughly $13.6M before being acquired by TaxBit in January 2023 to augment TaxBit's digital-asset accounting suite. The standalone product, developer portal, and API surface have been retired; the tactic.com domain is now listed for sale and no independent developer surface remains.

providers.name: Taggle Internet Ventures
providers.description: Taggle Internet Ventures Private Limited was an Indian online group-buying / daily-deals platform (taggle.com) incorporated in 2010 in Bangalore, Karnataka, that brought consumers together to purchase discounted products and services from merchants across food & beverage, wellness, and beauty. It raised an early venture round in 2010 and is now reported as permanently closed. The enrichment pass found no live developer program, public API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or documentation for this entity. Note: the taggle.com domain is now operated by an unrelated Australian digital water-metering company, Taggle Systems, which is a distinct company and not the subject of this record. This profile was surfaced during VC-portfolio mining and is retained as a historical/closed-company stub with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: TakeLessons
providers.description: TakeLessons was an online and in-person lessons marketplace founded in 2007 by Steven Cox and headquartered in San Diego, California. It connected students with independent instructors for music, languages, academic subjects, cooking, and professional training, handling scheduling, payments, and instructor discovery. Microsoft acquired TakeLessons in September 2021 to expand its edtech offerings, then wound the service down: the last day to book lessons was August 15, 2024 and the consumer site closed on November 15, 2024. The company is now defunct and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface; this record is retained as a portfolio-lineage stub for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TakeWheels
providers.description: TakeWheels (branded "Wheels", operated by Wheels Labs) was a shared electric micromobility platform based in Los Angeles, founded in 2018, that offered seated pedal-assist e-bikes and dockless light electric vehicles for short-distance urban trips. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital, which participated in the company's 2019 Series A. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable developer surface for this company. As of this pass the primary domain (takewheels.com) no longer resolves to the company: it issues a 301 redirect to an unrelated third-party site, indicating the business is defunct and the domain has been repurposed. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead with no active API surface.

providers.name: Talaria Technologies
providers.description: Talaria Technologies, Inc. was a developer-tools startup based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2011, that built a dynamic web application server and runtime infrastructure for web developers — notably a just-in-time (JIT) compiler and runtime for PHP intended to help developers build and run websites more efficiently. It was surfaced as an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) portfolio/investment-list company. Per public company-intelligence sources (indexed.vc, PrivCo, Bloomberg, CB Insights), Talaria was acquired by Google in 2013 and ceased operating as an independent company; it maintains no active website, developer portal, or public API surface today.

providers.name: Talko
providers.description: Talko was a mobile business-communications startup founded by former Microsoft CTO Ray Ozzie and backed by a16z. Launched in September 2014, its app let mobile teams call, text, and exchange voice and video messages, recording live conversations with in-call bookmarks, tagging, and asynchronous voice follow-ups. Microsoft acquired the company in December 2015 to bolster Skype, and the Talko service was fully shut down by March 2016. The company is defunct with no live developer platform, website, or API surface; it remains in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio record.

providers.name: Talkray
providers.description: Talkray (operated by TiKL, Inc., a Y Combinator W12 startup founded in 2012 by Zafer Ahmed in Redwood City, California) was a free cross-platform messaging and calling app spanning the TiKL Touch-To-Talk and Talkray consumer apps, which together saw roughly 28 million downloads. In 2013 the company announced the Talkray Developer API, a white-label cloud platform for embedding one-on-one and group text chat, group voice calls, voicemail, push notifications, and image/video transfer into third-party mobile apps and games. That API never left private beta and no public documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal were ever published. The company is now defunct (deadpooled) - active development ceased around 2018 and the app was removed from Google Play in February 2021. talkray.com currently sits behind Cloudflare and returns HTTP 403 for all paths.

providers.name: Tapingo
providers.description: Tapingo was a mobile ordering and pickup app for college campuses and local restaurants, surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures. It was acquired by Grubhub in 2018 and folded into Grubhub Campus; as of the 2026 enrichment pass the tapingo.com domain 301-redirects to onsite.grubhub.com and Tapingo no longer operates as an independent company or publishes any developer or API surface. Sector: consumer / food ordering. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; there are no live APIs to enrich.

providers.name: Tapsense
providers.description: TapSense was a mobile advertising and real-time-bidding exchange founded in 2011 in San Francisco, connecting app publishers to brand advertisers through a private mobile RTB marketplace, an advertiser API and publisher SDKs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company is defunct and the 2026-08-12 re-verification confirms it - the tapsense.com zone is now a parked domain held by Trellian Pty. Limited, serving a 995-byte "This domain may be for sale" holding page from a wildcard A record, so www, api and developer subdomains all return that same page and docs.tapsense.com fails TLS on an expired certificate. No OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, MCP, agent card, webhook or well-known document exists on any host, and no first-party package survives on npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Maven Central, CocoaPods or crates.io. The advertiser API and mobile SDKs the company once marketed went offline with it, so there is nothing to enrich beyond this identity record.

providers.name: Tara Ai
providers.description: Tara AI (Y Combinator W15, originally Gradberry) was a San Jose-based engineering efficiency platform that used fine-tuned LLMs over source control and project data to measure cycle times, benchmarks, and delivery velocity, integrating with GitHub, GitLab, Jira, and Slack. Backed by Aspect Ventures, Y Combinator, and Slack Fund (~$13M raised). As of July 2026 the company is listed as permanently closed on Crunchbase and tara.ai is a parked domain; no public API, developer docs, or SDKs were ever published, and the TARAAI GitHub org has no public repositories.

providers.name: TaskHuman
providers.description: TaskHuman was a mobile-first, on-demand human coaching platform that connected employees with live 1:1 video coaching across wellbeing, fitness, leadership, professional growth, sales and mentorship topics, sold to employers as a benefit and delivered through iOS, Android and web apps plus Slack and Microsoft Teams integrations. The San Francisco Bay Area company raised roughly $35M from investors including U.S. Venture Partners and Madrona and marketed a coach network spanning more than a thousand skill areas. The company ceased operations in 2026; as of this profile the entire taskhuman.com origin answers HTTP 401 behind an nginx HTTP Basic authentication wall and the product's API and application hosts no longer resolve, so no developer program, documentation or machine-readable contract remains reachable.

providers.name: Tasty Labs
providers.description: Tasty Labs, Inc. was a social-software development studio founded in 2010 by Joshua Schachter (creator of Delicious), Nick Nguyen, and Paul Rademacher. Backed by a $3M Series A from Union Square Ventures and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), it built experimental consumer products including Jig.com (a marketplace for needs), Human.io (a micro-task service), and Skills.to. The company was acquired by @WalmartLabs in May 2013, with its team and technology folded into WalmartLabs; the tastylabs.com domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record and exposes no public API surface, developer documentation, or specifications.

providers.name: TCF Financial Corporation
providers.description: Profile for TCF Financial Corporation, a former Detroit-headquartered regional bank holding company (Twin City Building and Loan Association, founded 1923). TCF was merged into Huntington Bancshares Incorporated on June 9, 2021, and the TCF brand was fully retired. This repository is preserved for historical record only — TCF Financial no longer operates and exposes no APIs. All banking, treasury, deposit, and lending services formerly offered under the TCF brand are now operated by Huntington National Bank under the Huntington brand. See the huntington-bancshares repository for current API surface (which is itself minimal; Huntington exposes no public developer portal).

providers.name: TD Ameritrade
providers.description: TD Ameritrade was a US retail brokerage that provided REST APIs for trading equities and options, accessing streaming market data, managing brokerage accounts, and retrieving historical and real-time market data. Following the Charles Schwab acquisition, the TD Ameritrade API was shut down on May 10, 2024. Schwab has ported much of the original functionality into the Schwab Trader API.

providers.name: TeachStreet
providers.description: TeachStreet was an online learning marketplace that, in its own words, "helps people find great classes, courses, teachers, and instructors who help them learn new things," while "teachers use TeachStreet to find more students" (teachstreet.com homepage, archived June 2011). Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company, TeachStreet was acquired by Amazon on February 2, 2012 and subsequently wound down. The teachstreet.com domain is now a dormant, Amazon-controlled brand-protection asset — MarkMonitor nameservers, a locked-down mail posture (SPF "v=spf1 -all", DMARC "p=reject" reporting to dmarc.amazon.com), and no A/AAAA/MX records — so there is no live website, developer portal, or API surface to enrich. This record is retained as a historical, defunct-company profile.

providers.name: TellApart
providers.description: TellApart was a predictive-marketing and cross-device retargeting technology company founded in 2009 by former Google AdWords-API engineers Josh McFarland and Mark Ayzenshtat. Its cloud-based customer data platform unified shopper profiles across channels and devices and used machine-learning scoring to power dynamic product ads and direct-response retargeting for retailers such as Neiman Marcus, Wayfair, Sur La Table and Pottery Barn. TellApart was acquired by Twitter in April 2015 for roughly $533M in stock and folded into Twitter's advertising business; it no longer operates as an independent company and the tellapart.com domain is now parked with no live developer or API surface. Surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: TellFi
providers.description: TellFi is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Tello
providers.description: Tello (Tello Applications, Inc.) was a customer-feedback and customer-service ratings startup founded in 2010 in Palo Alto, California by Joe Beninato and backed by 500 Global. It offered a free web and mobile application that let consumers rate and comment on their in-person service experiences at businesses (including feedback on specific employees), and sold businesses paid dashboard access to monitor how their staff were rated. The company has since shut down; no live product, developer program, or public API surface remains, so this record is retained as a defunct-company profile rather than an active provider for enrichment.

providers.name: TellTail
providers.description: TellTail was a community-first platform providing community, education, and business support to dog breeders, connecting certified breeders with families seeking puppies. Backed by a $3.4M seed round led by General Catalyst (April 2022, with Scribble Ventures and Companion Fund). Surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company has since ceased operations ("TellTail is closing its doors"); it operated a consumer marketplace and community product with no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or event surface.

providers.name: tenXer *
providers.description: tenXer was a San Francisco productivity-analytics startup that helped engineering leads measure and improve team performance by pulling data from the tools engineers already used (GitHub, JIRA, Pivotal Tracker, etc.) and turning it into manager-facing views, stats and insights. Backed by True Ventures, GV (Google Ventures) and Khosla Ventures (~$5M raised), the company was acquired by Twitter in April 2015 for under $50M and folded into Twitter's internal engineering-tools effort. The standalone product and public developer surface no longer exist; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. No live API, developer portal, or documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Terra Bella (fka Skybox Imaging)
providers.description: Terra Bella, originally founded in 2009 as Skybox Imaging (Mountain View, California), was a satellite imaging and geospatial analytics company that built and operated the SkySat constellation of high-resolution Earth-observation satellites. Google acquired Skybox Imaging in 2014 for roughly $500 million and rebranded it Terra Bella. In 2017 Alphabet/Google sold Terra Bella and its SkySat satellites to Planet Labs, folding the business into Planet's Earth-observation operations. Terra Bella no longer exists as an independent operating entity and publishes no independent developer portal, API, or SDK surface; its capabilities live on inside Planet Labs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners.

providers.name: test.ai
providers.description: test.ai (formerly Appdiff, Inc.) built an AI-powered test-automation platform that used computer vision and machine-learning element classification to make Selenium and Appium tests resilient to UI change. It published first-party Java, Python, Node.js and Ruby SDKs, a gRPC "Classifier" service that labelled UI elements from screenshots, an Appium classifier plugin, and OpenTestData — a free open database of automated test fixture data with its own REST API. The company raised over $30M and was sold; its founder has since moved on to other ventures. As of 2026-08-30 test.ai serves no website of its own: the domain has no HTTPS listener and every HTTP path redirects off-domain. The artifacts profiled here are the contracts and packages the company published while operating, all of which remain publicly retrievable from its own GitHub organization and from the npm, PyPI, RubyGems and Maven Central registries.

providers.name: Textaurant
providers.description: Textaurant was an early SMS-based restaurant waitlist and table-management startup founded around 2010 by Josh Bob in Waltham, Massachusetts, and later surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Its software let a restaurant manage its waiting list from a laptop and text guests when a table opened up, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative to pager-based systems from JTECH and OpenTable. The original company is defunct: its primary domain, textaurant.com, now resolves to a parked GoDaddy "for sale" landing page with no product, documentation, or API surface. A separate, unaffiliated live app reusing the name exists at app.textaurant.app (a small Twilio-backed Next.js application served through a personal proxy), but it publishes no public API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer documentation. There is no API to onboard against; this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct provider.

providers.name: The Backplane
providers.description: The Backplane, Inc. was a US social-network-builder startup (founded 2011) that built branded social networks for fan groups and organizations, most notably Lady Gaga's Little Monsters community, and later pivoted to the Place.xyz network-building platform. Backed by Battery Ventures, GV, Sequoia, Greylock and others, it raised roughly $18.9M before running out of money, going out of business in April 2016 and selling all of its assets (patents, code, trademarks, URLs). The company is defunct; enrichment found no live website, developer portal, API, specification, or SDK surface to catalog.

providers.name: The Echo Nest
providers.description: The Echo Nest was a music-intelligence company, spun out of the MIT Media Lab, that ran a developer platform and API for music understanding — machine-listening audio analysis (tempo, key, energy, danceability, valence), artist and song metadata, automated playlisting and taste profiles, and the Rosetta Stone service for translating artist and track IDs across music services. It was acquired by Spotify in March 2014 (reported at roughly €49.7M / ~$100M). Spotify consolidated onto its own Web API: The Echo Nest API stopped issuing new keys on 2016-03-29 and stopped serving requests on 2016-05-31, with developers directed to the Spotify Web API (whose audio-features and audio-analysis endpoints descend from Echo Nest technology). The developer.echonest.com portal no longer resolves; the echonest.com domain now redirects to an unrelated WordPress site. This profile was surfaced as a matrix-partners portfolio company; it is retained for historical/lineage reference and has no live, public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: The OK Company
providers.description: The OK Company was a consumer technology startup, backed by Obvious Ventures, best known for OK Play - a mobile app for iOS and Android that turned screen time into a catalyst for real-world, parent-and-child play activities designed to build empathy, kindness, and creativity in young children. It was founded by CEO JJ Aguhob and President Chris Ovitz (previously co-founders of the mobile video app Viddy), with developmental psychologist Dr. Colleen Russo Johnson as Chief Scientist. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - its domain theokcompany.com no longer resolves to a product site and instead redirects to a third-party domain-sale listing. The OK Company was a consumer mobile app business and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer platform, so there is no API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company lead.

providers.name: The Rainmaker Group Ventures (letitrain.com)
providers.description: letitrain.com was the corporate domain of The Rainmaker Group Ventures, LLC, an Atlanta-based hospitality revenue and profit optimization software vendor serving hotels, resorts and casinos. Rainmaker sold an "intelligent profit platform" built around three products: guestrev for transient pricing and science-based revenue management, grouprev for group pricing and evaluation, and revintel for business intelligence and reporting, with a demand forecast marketed to operators including Caesars Entertainment, Atlantis Casino Resort Spa and Two Roads Hospitality. The company was backed by Norwest Venture Partners and ran offices in Atlanta, Las Vegas, Singapore and Dubai. The brand is retired: letitrain.com now serves a blanket redirect to Cendyn, the acquiring company, its TLS certificate expired in December 2022, and no Rainmaker developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification was ever published or archived. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record with no active API surface.

providers.name: theBoardlist
providers.description: theBoardlist is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: thefacefeed
providers.description: thefacefeed is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: TheFind (Meta)
providers.description: TheFind (Meta) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: commerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Thing Labs
providers.description: Thing Labs was an early consumer social-software startup founded in 2008 by Jason Shellen (previously a product lead on Blogger and a co-creator of Google Reader at Google). The company built browser-based social tools including Plinky (daily writing prompts), Brizzly and the Brizzly Guide (a web-based Twitter/social client), and Let's Be Trends. Backed by SoftTech VC (now Uncork Capital) alongside angel investors, Thing Labs was acquired by AOL in September 2010, after which Shellen became VP of Product for AOL's AIM & Messaging group. Thing Labs no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no public developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ThinkUp
providers.description: ThinkUp was a social media analytics application, co-founded by Gina Trapani and Anil Dash, that gave individuals insights into their own activity across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, and other social networks. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, it ran as both a hosted subscription service and an open-source project (ThinkUpLLC/ThinkUp on GitHub, 3.2k+ stars) before its hosted service was shut down in 2016. The thinkup.com domain is no longer operated by the company (it now resolves to an unrelated coupon-code site), and no public developer API surface is available for enrichment.

providers.name: Thread
providers.description: Thread (thread.com) was a UK-based fashion technology company that combined AI with human expert stylists to deliver personalized clothing recommendations for men and women. Founded by Kieran O'Neill and Ben Phillips and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Balderton Capital, Thread's brand, technology and data were acquired by Marks & Spencer. The company subsequently entered administration and has ceased trading; its site now serves only a shutdown notice. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or event surface. This profile is retained as a network record of a defunct portfolio company.

providers.name: Thrive Earlier Detection
providers.description: Thrive Earlier Detection Corp. was a healthcare/biotech company commercializing CancerSEEK, a machine-learning-driven liquid biopsy blood test to detect multiple cancer types from a single blood draw. Spun out of Johns Hopkins technology and backed by Lux Capital, Bain Capital Life Sciences, Casdin, Google Ventures and others, it raised large early rounds before being acquired by Exact Sciences in 2020/2021 for roughly $2.15 billion and folded into Exact Sciences. This profile was surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. It is a clinical-diagnostics company with no public developer API surface; its former web presence (thrivedetect.com) is decommissioned.

providers.name: ThriveFantasy
providers.description: ThriveFantasy was a New York City daily fantasy sports platform focused on player-prop pick'em contests across NFL, NBA, MLB, esports, and other leagues, backed by Bullpen Capital. The company ceased operations in early 2024 after a failed funding round and a player-withdrawal crisis. It never published a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its legacy marketing site remains online.

providers.name: Thundra
providers.description: Thundra was an application observability and security platform for serverless, container, and VM workloads, best known for AWS Lambda monitoring and debugging. Its products included Thundra APM (distributed tracing), Sidekick (remote debugging), and Foresight (CI pipeline test observability). Founded in 2018 out of OpsGenie and backed by Battery Ventures, its assets were acquired by Catchpoint in April 2023 and the service has been discontinued — thundra.io now redirects to Catchpoint's acquisition announcement and the GitHub organization states "Thundra is no longer in service." Its open-source agents and plugins remain published on npm, PyPI, Maven Central, NuGet, and pkg.go.dev.

providers.name: Ticketfly
providers.description: Ticketfly was a San Francisco-based event-ticketing platform for independent music venues, promoters, and festivals, founded in 2008. It was acquired by Eventbrite in 2017 and, following a June 2018 data breach, was shut down in November 2018 with its music-oriented features folded into Eventbrite Music. The company is defunct: as of 2026 every Ticketfly host (www.ticketfly.com, developer.ticketfly.com) returns HTTP 301 redirects to eventbrite.com. No independent Ticketfly API, developer portal, documentation, or specification survives. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Timetric
providers.description: Timetric was a London-based data platform founded in 2008 for publishing, analysing, and performing calculations on large quantities of time-varying statistical data, later providing online market data, analysis, and advisory services to the insurance, construction, and infrastructure sectors. The Timetric Platform exposed an API with OAuth and API-token authentication for creating and updating time series. Timetric was acquired by GlobalData in March 2018 and timetric.com now redirects to globaldata.com; the company no longer operates independently.

providers.name: Tobira Therapeutics
providers.description: Tobira Therapeutics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Tomfoolery
providers.description: Tomfoolery, Inc. was a San Francisco mobile-app lab founded in 2012 by Sol Lipman (Chief Product Officer) and Kakul Srivastava (CEO), a team of ex-Yahoo and ex-AOL executives building consumer-grade, mobile-first collaboration apps for the enterprise. Its debut product was Anchor, a real-time conversation platform meant to be a central hub for work discussions, followed by an app called Action. The company raised roughly $1.7M (investors included Andreessen Horowitz) before being acquired by Yahoo in January 2014, after which the Anchor app was shut down. Tomfoolery is now a defunct/deadpooled company with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface. It was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirms there is no API to profile.

providers.name: Topl
providers.description: Topl was an impact-technology company founded in 2017 out of Rice University and based in Houston, Texas, building a proof-of-stake blockchain that let organizations prove ethical and sustainable practices on-ledger. It raised a $3M seed in 2020 and a $15M Series A in 2022, and shipped a real developer platform: the Bifrost node, the Genus indexer, the Brambl SDK family for Scala, TypeScript, JavaScript and Dart, and the brambl-cli client. In late 2023 the company rebranded to Apparatus and repositioned around Thunder, a Bitcoin Layer 2. It appears to have wound down after that — the last first-party artifact of any kind shipped on 2024-09-26, all ten remaining public repositories are archived, every documentation and API host now fails to resolve, and the topl.co domain lapsed and was re-registered by an unrelated owner on 2024-12-30. What survives, and what this profile is built from, is the contract itself: a 38-file proto3 module defining 6 gRPC services, 30 RPCs and 138 messages, still downloadable from the Buf Schema Registry, plus the published SDKs and container images.

providers.name: Torbit
providers.description: Torbit was a web-performance-optimization startup (real-user monitoring and automated front-end optimization) backed by 500 Startups, acquired by Walmart Labs in 2013. The product has long been discontinued; the enrichment pass found no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface. torbit.com no longer serves a site and now resolves to Walmart brand-protection infrastructure (MarkMonitor registrar, UltraDNS nameservers, Proofpoint mail), with both HTTP and HTTPS requests timing out.

providers.name: TotSpot
providers.description: TotSpot was a mobile resale shopping marketplace for kids' clothes, letting parents buy and sell gently used children's fashion (brands like Burberry, Nike, GAP, Gymboree) with peer-to-peer listings and a concierge selling service. A 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company, TotSpot appears to be defunct - as of July 2026 totspot.me serves only a web-hosting placeholder page, and no public API or developer surface was found.

providers.name: TouristEye
providers.description: TouristEye was a travel-planning startup founded in 2009 that offered web and mobile apps for discovering places, saving tips, and planning trips. A 500 Startups (500 Global) portfolio company, it was acquired by Lonely Planet in 2013 and the service was subsequently shut down. The touristeye.com domain remains registered (via GoDaddy Corporate Domains, through October 2026) but no longer resolves, the historical api.touristeye.com host is offline, and the company's GitHub organization has been dormant since 2014 — no public API, SDKs, or developer artifacts remain.

providers.name: ToyTalk
providers.description: ToyTalk was a San Francisco conversational AI company founded in 2011 that built voice and chat characters for entertainment, rebranded as PullString in 2016, and was acquired by Apple in early 2019. Its developer platform - the PullString Web API plus Converse and Author tooling for authoring conversational experiences - was shut down after the acquisition. Today pullstring.com and toytalk.com no longer resolve and both domains are parked on Apple nameservers, the github.com/pullstring organization has been deleted, and the only surviving first-party developer artifact is the orphaned pullstring JavaScript SDK on npm. This profile records that historical developer surface; there is no live API.

providers.name: Tracksby
providers.description: Tracksby (Tracks.by) was a music marketing startup that helped artists and their managers release new music and videos through deep Facebook integration, social launch campaigns, fan email capture, and YouTube/VEVO embeds, turning each release into a fan-growth campaign. Listed on the a16z investment list, the early-2010s company is now defunct - tracks.by no longer resolves, tracksby.com is parked for sale, the @TracksBy Twitter account is gone, and its GitHub account has been inactive since 2012. No public API surface was found, so this profile records an inactive portfolio lead with no artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Tradegecko
providers.description: TradeGecko was a Singapore-based cloud inventory and order management platform for SMEs, wholesalers, and online retailers, launched in 2013 with integrations into Shopify, WooCommerce, and Xero. Intuit acquired TradeGecko in August 2020 and rebranded it QuickBooks Commerce; the standalone platform and its public REST API were subsequently discontinued. Its API hosts no longer resolve and tradegecko.com is no longer operated by the company, though first-party Ruby client libraries remain published on RubyGems.

providers.name: Tradesy
providers.description: Tradesy was a Los Angeles-based online marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned luxury and designer fashion, founded in 2009 and backed by 500 Global among others. In March 2022 it was acquired by Paris-based Vestiaire Collective to accelerate that company's expansion into the US resale market, and the standalone Tradesy brand was subsequently wound down. The tradesy.com domain now redirects to vestiairecollective.com, and Tradesy no longer operates an independent website, developer program, or public API. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record.

providers.name: Traffix
