providers.description: Traffix Systems was an Israeli 4G network-signaling company, founded in 2005, that offered Diameter signaling products (routing, load balancing, and gateway functions) for telecommunications service providers. Bessemer Venture Partners partnered with the company in 2011, and in 2012 Traffix was acquired by F5 Networks, which absorbed its Diameter signaling technology. The company no longer operates independently: its legacy domain traffixsystems.com is parked on F5 Networks infrastructure with no web presence, and Traffix publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: Transcend Medical
providers.description: Transcend Medical was a medical device company based in Menlo Park, California, developing minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) devices. Spun out of the ForSight Labs ophthalmic incubator, its lead product was the CyPass Micro-Stent, a suprachoroidal implant designed to lower intraocular pressure in patients with mild-to-moderate glaucoma undergoing cataract surgery. The company raised roughly $89.8M across multiple venture rounds from investors including Canaan Partners, HLM Venture Partners, Finistere Ventures, Kaiser Permanente Ventures, Latterell Venture Partners, Morgenthaler Ventures, Split Rock Partners and Technology Partners, and was acquired by Novartis's Alcon eye-care business in February 2016. It operated no public API, developer platform, or software product; the transcendmedical.com domain no longer resolves following the company's absorption into Alcon.

providers.name: Transparent Systems
providers.description: Transparent Systems (Transparent Financial Systems) was a Seattle-based fintech startup advancing financial infrastructure through on-demand, 24/7 cryptographic settlement solutions built on cryptographically-secured distributed networks, backed by Pantera Capital and Vulcan Capital and active in US regulatory engagement (OCC comments, 2020). The company appears defunct: its website redirected away from 2021 onward and as of July 2026 transparentsystems.com is a parked GoDaddy domain listed for sale, with no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: Treecard
providers.description: Treecard was a Seedcamp-backed "walk to plant" climate consumer company that funded reforestation from everyday activity, originally through a wooden debit card and later a step-tracking mobile app. The company has shut down, and treecard.org now serves a closing notice thanking members and reporting 10,037,912 trees funded and 2,931,070 lifetime tons of carbon, pointing former users to Ecosia and Treekly while its planting projects live on at impact.veritree.com/treecard. Treecard published no public API, developer program, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Trooly (Airbnb)
providers.description: Trooly, Inc. was a machine-learning trust and safety startup that scored the trustworthiness of individuals using publicly available data and digital footprints, offering its Instant Trust screening service to businesses for trust and safety management, risk assessment, and customer relationship use cases. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Trooly was acquired by Airbnb and ceased operations on June 19, 2017, shutting down its external APIs; its technology was absorbed into Airbnb's trust and safety systems and Trooly, Inc. remains an Airbnb subsidiary. trooly.com is now a parked domain and no living API surface exists.

providers.name: TrueFlip
providers.description: TrueFlip was an international anonymous blockchain lottery with instant payouts, open-source draw code, and a transparent prize fund, launched in 2017 with an Ethereum token ICO and backed by Pantera Capital. The company's GitHub organization has been dormant since 2018, and the trueflip.io domain is suspended at the registrar (clientHold) with no DNS records; by early 2026 the domain was serving unrelated crypto-casino affiliate content. No public API, developer documentation, SDK packages, or machine-readable surface was found. Profile retained as a Pantera Capital portfolio record.

providers.name: TrueFort
providers.description: TrueFort was a zero-trust lateral-movement protection platform for enterprise workloads, providing real-time microsegmentation, service account protection, file integrity monitoring, and workload hardening driven by continuous application behavior analysis, with integrations for CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, and Armis. Backed by Canaan Partners and other investors through a $30M Series B, the company ceased operations on May 21, 2025. TrueFort never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: TrueLens
providers.description: TrueLens was a marketing-technology startup providing social media analytics and customer intelligence. Its product, Socialgraphics, helped brands target customers using data compiled and analyzed from multiple social networks for marketing campaigns. Google Ventures (GV) led a roughly $1.2M funding round in 2012; the company was small (2-10 employees). TrueLens now appears defunct: its former domain truelens.com 301-redirects to an unrelated retailer (misterspex.de), and no public API, developer portal, or documentation could be found. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Trust
providers.description: Trust (Trust Software Inc., trust.co) was a fintech and marketing-technology startup founded in 2019 by James Borow, backed by a 2020 seed investment from Lightspeed Venture Partners. It began as a corporate card and community giving digital businesses higher credit limits and extended payment terms on marketing spend, then pivoted to Market (withmarket.com), an AI marketing assistant that let Shopify merchants chat with their business data. As of July 2026 both trust.co and withmarket.com no longer resolve in DNS and the company appears to have wound down. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface was ever published.

providers.name: TryTry (穿穿)
providers.description: TryTry (穿穿, trytrytw.com) was a Taiwanese women's fashion e-commerce brand ("是妳，決定了這件衣服的表情" — "It's you who decides the expression of this dress"), active around 2015-2016 and surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company. The business appears defunct — as of 2026-07-21 trytrytw.com is domain-squatted (wildcard DNS to a parked Chinese web-design page, serving an expired TLS certificate issued for an unrelated host) and no developer, API, or documentation surface exists.

providers.name: Tsumobi
providers.description: Tsumobi was a Y Combinator (Winter 2007) mobile messaging startup founded in Boston by Joshua Wilson and Adam Bouhenguel, and later backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It built a programming language that sat on top of J2ME so feature-phone applications could be downloaded and updated on the fly via URLs, aiming to fix the painful install and upgrade cycle of late-2000s mobile apps. The company is inactive (YC lists it as Inactive; reporting describes the startup as shut down after raising roughly $2M), the tsumobi.com domain no longer serves a website, and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or specifications were found. This profile is retained as a historical a16z portfolio record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tugboat Yards
providers.description: Tugboat Yards Inc. was a San Francisco startup (product name "Tugboat") that built tools for independent publishers and media creators to raise direct financial support from their audiences, and was backed by a16z. The company is defunct - the product was live circa 2012-2014, the tugboatyards.com domain was reduced to a registrar parking page by 2016, and as of July 2026 the domain publishes no A/AAAA records. It did operate a real, documented publisher API at api.tugboatyards.com (key-check, pages, offers, subscribers, orders, checkout configuration, placements, and Instant Payment Notification webhooks) with a first-party Python client, pytugboat. That surface is offline; the artifacts in this repository are a historical record recovered from the provider's own 2015 documentation via the Wayback Machine and from the still-live pytugboat docs on Read the Docs. This profile is preserved as part of the a16z venture-portfolio graph in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Twice
providers.description: Twice was an online marketplace for buying and selling secondhand clothing that operated at liketwice.com, and it appears on the Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) investment list. eBay acquired the Twice team in 2015 and the marketplace was shut down; liketwice.com now serves an HTTP 301 redirect to ebay.com (verified 2026-07-21) and no longer answers HTTPS. The company is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a defunct a16z portfolio lead with no public API surface.

providers.name: TXN Solutions
providers.description: TXN Solutions (TXN) was a fintech startup founded in 2014 that offered a web application for consumer spending analytics, competitive intelligence, and surveys - capturing spending directly from the credit and debit cards of consumers who joined its research panel to give brands, investors, and researchers insight into consumer spending, merchant performance, and market positioning, including CPG and SKU-level data. It raised seed funding (announced November 2016) from a16z, Homebrew, Bloomberg Beta, and Social Starts. The company appears defunct as of July 2026 - its historical domain txn.com has been relinquished and is parked on the eName domain marketplace - and no public API surface is known.

providers.name: uBEAM
providers.description: uBeam was an ultrasonic wireless power startup founded in 2011 by Meredith Perry and headquartered in Marina del Rey, California. It raised roughly $26 million from Andreessen Horowitz, Upfront Ventures, Founders Fund, Mark Cuban, and Marissa Mayer to charge devices over the air using 45-75 kHz phased-array ultrasound. The company rebranded as SonicEnergy in December 2018 and went defunct on February 5, 2024, without shipping a commercial product. It published no developer APIs, SDKs, or documentation, and both ubeam.com and sonicenergy.com are now parked domains.

providers.name: uberVU
providers.description: uberVU was a social media analytics and monitoring company, backed by Seedcamp, that offered brand-insight dashboards and a metrics API before being acquired by Hootsuite in 2014. The company no longer operates independently - ubervu.com now 301-redirects to blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-analytics/, its former metrics API is retired, and its GitHub organization is dormant. This profile is kept as a historical record of a VC-portfolio company with no current public API surface.

providers.name: Ubooly
providers.description: Ubooly was a children's smart-toy company that made "The Learning Toy that Listens" - a plush toy that turned a smartphone, iPod touch, or tablet into an interactive learning companion for kids aged 4-8, with hand-crafted play packs and voice interaction. A 500 Global portfolio company, Ubooly is now defunct; ubooly.com was last archived as a live storefront in late 2015 and today 301-redirects to an unrelated third-party site. No public API, developer portal, packages, or GitHub organization were found.

providers.name: UCode
providers.description: UCode was a STEM coding-education company ("Where Kids Learn to Code and Create") that taught kids and teens ages 6-19 software programming through classes, camps, and online instruction, creating apps, websites, and games. A seed-stage Bloomberg Beta portfolio company founded by Scott Mueller and Michael Yang, it is marked as exited in the Bloomberg Beta Manual. As of 2026-07-21 ucode.com is a parked domain listed for sale, and no API, developer, or platform surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Ula
providers.description: Ula was a B2B wholesale commerce platform for small neighborhood retail shops (warungs), providing supply chain technology, inventory management, and credit access across Indonesia, India, and Singapore. Backed by Prosus Ventures, Ula closed its core operations in late 2023 and ula.app now hosts a retrospective of the company. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs were ever published, and no developer subdomains resolve.

providers.name: Ultra Safe Nuclear
providers.description: Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation (USNC) was a Seattle-based advanced nuclear company, founded in 2011, that vertically integrated fourth-generation nuclear power — the Micro Modular Reactor (MMR), the Pylon space reactor developed through its USNC-Tech subsidiary, and Fully Ceramic Microencapsulated (FCM) TRISO nuclear fuel manufactured at Oak Ridge, Tennessee. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware in October 2024 following the death of its principal investor, and its assets were sold in a bifurcated Section 363 auction: NANO Nuclear Energy acquired the MMR and Pylon reactor patents and demonstration partnerships for $8.5 million (court-approved 18 December 2024), and Standard Nuclear acquired the FCM/TRISO fuel business and the Oak Ridge facility for $28 million (closed February 2025). The company no longer operates. Its primary domain, usnc.com, is still registered and still routes mail on the Microsoft 365 US Government cloud but publishes no address record, so the corporate web presence is gone. As a reactor and nuclear-fuel manufacturer it never ran a developer program, and no public API, specification, SDK, or agent surface was found under its name.

providers.name: Unamo
providers.description: Unamo was a Warsaw, Poland based SaaS suite offering SEO monitoring, social media monitoring, and conversion rate optimization, formerly known as Positionly, and backed by Point Nine Capital. The company appears defunct as of July 2026, with unamo.com no longer resolving in DNS and the pre-rebrand positionly.com site serving stale 2017-era content whose API, signup, terms, and privacy pages return 404. No public API surface, client packages, or developer documentation remain online.

providers.name: Unikrn
providers.description: Unikrn was an esports betting and entertainment company founded in November 2014 by Rahul Sood and Karl Flores, headquartered in Seattle and backed by investors including Mark Cuban, Ashton Kutcher, 500 Global, and Pantera Capital. The platform offered real-money and token-based wagering on competitive video game tournaments (CS:GO, League of Legends, Dota 2, and more) and ran a $30M ICO for its UnikoinGold (UKG) cryptocurrency in 2017, which it later disabled as part of a 2021 SEC settlement. Unikrn was acquired by Entain in August 2021, and the unikrn.com betting site was permanently closed on October 20, 2023. The domain now serves only a farewell notice; the company publishes no APIs, developer portal, or public technical artifacts.

providers.name: Uninstall
providers.description: Uninstall.io was a mobile "uninstall intelligence" platform built by Songline Analytics (Bengaluru/Singapore, founded 2015) whose iOS and Android SDKs tracked app uninstalls, surfaced uninstall reasons, and drove re-install campaigns for customers like Snapdeal, Axis Bank, Zalora, and BankBazaar. Backed by 500 Startups India, Rajan Anandan, and Hive Data, it was acquired by Singapore healthtech company Mobile Health in July 2018. The uninstall.io domain is now parked for sale and no public API surface remains; the GitHub organization and first-party mobile SDKs survive as the public footprint.

providers.name: UNIsite
providers.description: UNIsite, Inc. was a wireless communications infrastructure company founded in 1994 that owned and operated roughly 600 wireless towers and 46 managed antenna sites, focused on antenna siting, tower site management, ownership, and build-to-suit development. A Battery Ventures portfolio company, UNIsite was acquired by American Tower Corporation in a merger consummated in January 2000 (total consideration approximately $198.1 million, including assumed debt). The company no longer operates independently and publishes no APIs; the unisite.com domain is now held by an unrelated web-based business software product.

providers.name: Universal Hydrogen
providers.description: Universal Hydrogen Co. was a Hawthorne, California hydrogen-aviation startup founded in 2020 by former Airbus CTO Paul Eremenko to decarbonize regional air travel. Rather than building a hydrogen pipeline network, it proposed a modular capsule model: lightweight hydrogen capsules loaded into aircraft with existing cargo handling equipment, paired with fuel-cell powertrain conversion kits for regional turboprops such as the ATR 72 and De Havilland Dash 8. In March 2023 it flew a converted Dash 8-300 testbed with one propeller driven by a hydrogen fuel cell. The company raised roughly $100 million from backers including GE Aviation, American Airlines, JetBlue Ventures, Airbus Ventures, Toyota Ventures and Mitsubishi. Unable to raise further equity or debt or to find a buyer, it ceased operations on 27 June 2024 and liquidated. It was a hardware and fuel-logistics business and never shipped a public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification; its domains no longer serve a site.

providers.name: Unlonely
providers.description: Unlonely was a crypto/web3 livestreaming platform founded by Grace and Brian Guan and backed by Multicoin Capital — livestreams on Base with token-gated chat, creator and temp tokens, the $VIBES on-chain interaction economy, and stream clips minted as NFCs (non-fungible clips). The product is defunct: the unlonely.app domain registration has expired and the hosted GraphQL API is no longer live, but the platform was open source and this profile preserves its real GraphQL schema (225 types) harvested from the public monorepo.

providers.name: uNow (UniversityNow)
providers.description: UniversityNow, Inc. (uNow) was a San Francisco-based higher-education startup founded in 2011 and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) that built competency-based, self-paced online degree programs for working adults. It operated New Charter University, acquired Patten University in 2012, and its learning platform was sold to Penn Foster Education Group in 2016 and National University System in 2018. The company is defunct and unow.com now redirects to a dead page; it published no public API.

providers.name: Unwind Me
providers.description: Unwind Me was a San Francisco on-demand massage startup ("Massage Made Simple — straight to your door, when you want, at an affordable price") that let customers book state-licensed, vetted massage therapists who arrived with a full "Unwind Kit" (table, sheets, oils). Venture-backed with Slow Ventures among its investors, it was acquired by rival on-demand massage platform Soothe — the transition notice "Unwind Me is now part of Soothe" was live on unwind.me by December 2015, with Soothe honoring outstanding customer credits. The company is defunct: unwind.me is now a parked GoDaddy domain, and it operates no website, developer portal, or public API surface today.

providers.name: Upcode Academy
providers.description: UpCode Academy was a Singapore-based coding school offering short bootcamps and part-time courses (SQL, Python, Web Development with Ruby on Rails, Data Science, Computer Vision, IoT) taught by industry practitioners. Operated by 40 Tasks, a 500 Global portfolio company whose earlier product was the LOCO location-based search app at 40tasks.com. The company appears defunct - upcodeacademy.com serves a Cloudflare 522 dead-origin error (a bare default server page by December 2025) and 40tasks.com no longer resolves in DNS (domain-squatted since about 2023). No public API surface was found.

providers.name: Upsight
providers.description: Upsight was a mobile analytics and marketing platform for apps and games — positioning itself as a "user lifecycle management platform" combining omnichannel analytics, integrated web and mobile marketing, ad optimization, and a DataMine SQL analytics product behind a single SDK for iOS, Android, tvOS, Unity, and Web. A Battery Ventures portfolio company, the platform is now defunct - upsight.com no longer resolves, the help.upsight.com developer docs survive only in the Internet Archive, and the GitHub org has been dormant since 2020, though the UpsightKit CocoaPods SDK and the doctor PyPI package remain published.

providers.name: Upthere
providers.description: Upthere was a consumer cloud-storage company backed by GV and founded by former Apple software engineering chief Bertrand Serlet. Its Upthere Home app was designed as "one home" for photos, videos, music, and documents, stored directly in the Upthere cloud with fast search, private sharing, and shared "Loops". Western Digital acquired Upthere in 2017 and later discontinued the service; upthere.com now 302-redirects every path to a retired Western Digital support notice. Upthere never published a public developer API, and no API surface remains — this profile records the company identity and the posture of the surviving domain.

providers.name: Uptime
providers.description: Uptime (Uptime SAS, Paris, SIREN 822006839) was a French elevator predictive-maintenance company founded in 2016 by Augustin and Amaury Celier. It fitted 4G-connected sensors to existing elevators and used the resulting telemetry to predict failures, dispatch technicians and report availability to building managers, backed by Serena and angels including Jacques-Antoine Granjon, David Amsellem, Yvan Wibaux and Antoine Martin across roughly EUR 10M of funding. The Paris Commercial Court opened a redressement judiciaire on 2022-07-26 and pronounced liquidation judiciaire with a plan de cession to SAS Otis on 2022-10-20; the elevator-maintenance activity and a minority of staff transferred to Otis. The company never published a public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification, and the uptime.ac domain has since lapsed — it now 301-redirects every path to unrelated third-party sites. This profile is retained as an honest record of a defunct company with no API surface.

providers.name: Urban Engines
providers.description: Urban Engines was a Silicon Valley urban-mobility analytics startup founded by Shiva Shivakumar and Balaji Prabhakar that built a Space/Time Engine for analyzing how people and objects move through cities, powering commuter routing and congestion insights for cities including Washington D.C., Sao Paulo, and Singapore. Backed by a16z and GV, the company was acquired by Google in September 2016 and is now defunct; it published no public API, developer portal, or client packages, and its former website is parked on Google infrastructure.

providers.name: Ureeka
providers.description: Ureeka was a community and mentorship platform for small businesses, surfaced as a Bullpen Capital portfolio company. The company no longer operates a standalone product - the ureeka.biz domain (www and apex) now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to zenbusiness.com, and no developer, documentation, or API surface remains. Probed 2026-07-21 by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: URX *
providers.description: URX was a San Francisco mobile deep-linking and app-search startup that connected mobile users to relevant in-app commerce experiences. Backed by roughly $15M from investors including GV (Google Ventures) and CyberAgent, it was acquired by Pinterest in May 2016 and its product was wound down. The urx.com domain is now parked and listed for sale on a domain marketplace, and no API, developer portal, or public developer artifacts remain. Profiled in the API Evangelist network as a historical GV portfolio company.

providers.name: Utopia Technology Partners
providers.description: Utopia Technology Partners, Inc. was a help desk software and IT support services company based in Larkspur, California, backed by Battery Ventures (listed as an exited investment). It was acquired by Royalblue Group plc of Woking, UK on May 11, 1998, expanding Royalblue's US help desk operation to the West Coast. The company is defunct - its California corporate registration is suspended and it publishes no website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: UUNET Technologies
providers.description: UUNET Technologies was one of the first commercial Internet service providers, founded in 1987 by Rick Adams in Virginia to commercialize Usenet and email, launching the AlterNet IP backbone in 1990. Backed by Accel Partners, Menlo Ventures, and NEA, it IPO'd on NASDAQ in 1995, was acquired by MFS Communications for $2B in 1996, which WorldCom bought that same year; after the MCI merger and Verizon's 2006 acquisition the UUNET brand was retired into Verizon Business. The brand is defunct today - its legacy domains (uu.net, uunet.com) remain Verizon-operated DNS zones whose web hosts only redirect to verizon.com/business, and it publishes no APIs or developer surface.

providers.name: Valiant Networks
providers.description: Valiant Networks, Inc. was a dot-com-era network testing, design, and consulting firm serving carriers and network equipment vendors, raising a $21M Series B in October 1999 and cutting staff (including its CEO) in the 2001 telecom downturn per Light Reading. It appears on Battery Ventures' list of all portfolio companies. The company is defunct with no surviving web presence or API surface; valiantnetworks.com lapsed and was later re-registered (2004) by unrelated businesses, and today does not resolve.

providers.name: Vamo
providers.description: Vamo was a San Francisco travel startup offering multi-city trip planning that automatically found the best combination of open-jaw flights, low-cost carriers, trains, buses, ferries, and hotels for international itineraries. Backed by DCVC and Slow Ventures, the team joined Airbnb on September 11, 2015 and the product was shut down, so no API surface exists; vamo.com is now parked at MarkMonitor.

providers.name: Vark (Aardvark)
providers.description: Vark is the Felicis portfolio listing for Aardvark, the social search / knowledge-market startup founded in 2007 by Max Ventilla, Nathan Stoll, Damon Horowitz, and Rob Spiro (The Mechanical Zoo). Users asked questions and were connected live with friends or friends-of-friends who could answer them, over email and IM. Google acquired Aardvark on February 11, 2010 for $50 million and shut the service down in September 2011. The company is defunct and published no public API. Its original domain vark.com no longer resolves, and the vark.io URL listed on the Felicis portfolio page now hosts an unrelated SMS meeting-reminder product operated by Saasology LLC.

providers.name: Vaunte
providers.description: Vaunte was a New York fashion commerce startup, backed by Battery Ventures, that let shoppers buy items directly from the closets of socialites, stylists, editors, and models (the 2013 site billed itself as "Shop fashion closets of socialites, stylists, editors, and models"). The original marketplace is no longer operating, and today vaunte.com hosts an unrelated fashion and lifestyle content site with no API or developer surface. Tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Vayar Vision
providers.description: Vayar Vision Ltd was an Israeli startup (company no. 514054972, incorporated 2007-11-26, Herzliya) that developed a visual search engine enabling search for images based on their visual characteristics rather than textual tagging - positioned as "a Google for pictures" turning images into searchable knowledge. A Battery Ventures portfolio company listed as an exited investment, the company has been wilfully dissolved (last annual report 2021) and its former website vayar.com no longer resolves. No API surface, developer program, or published artifacts exist.

providers.name: VDOnet
providers.description: VDOnet Corp was a mid-1990s streaming-media pioneer whose VDOLive server and player delivered some of the earliest video streamed over the web, alongside the VDOPhone video-telephony product. Backed by Battery Ventures, with Microsoft taking a minority stake in 1996, the company wound down in the late 1990s and its product line was sold off (Citrix negotiated a purchase of the product line for roughly $8 million in 1998). The company is defunct - its former vdo.net domain now resolves to a parked page listed for sale - and no API, developer portal, or other machine-readable surface exists to harvest.

providers.name: Vector Launch
providers.description: Vector Launch, Inc. (originally Vector Space Systems) was an American small-launch and space software company founded in February 2016 in Tucson, Arizona by Jim Cantrell — an early SpaceX executive — with John Garvey, Shaun Coleman, Ken Sunshine and Eric Besnard. It acquired Garvey Spacecraft in July 2016 and developed two LOX/propylene micro-launch vehicles, the Vector-R and the larger Vector-H, aimed at a high-cadence smallsat launch market, alongside GalacticSky, a San Jose based software-defined-satellite platform that produced more than forty patents and was marketed in 2016 with a promised suite of satellite SDKs, APIs and a satellite-optimised Linux distribution called GalacticOS. Those developer surfaces were announced but never shipped publicly: Vector operated no developer portal, published no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL or Postman collection, ran no public GitHub organisation, and distributed no client SDK to any package registry. The company raised roughly $22M disclosed (a $1M angel round from Shaun Coleman, then $21M in June 2017 from Sequoia Capital, Shasta Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners), flew suborbital prototypes from Mojave and Spaceport Camden, and won a $3.4M U.S. Air Force ASLON-45 mission in August 2019 that was cancelled days later on solvency grounds. Sequoia withdrew support in August 2019, Cantrell departed, operations halted, and Vector filed Chapter 11 in Delaware on 13 December 2019; Lockheed Martin took the GalacticSky assets by default for $4.25M when no qualified competing bid appeared, and a separate bidder took the launch-vehicle assets. A relaunched entity under Robert Spalding re-emerged on 29 October 2020, shareholders voted a wind-down in January 2021, and the residual business was finally absorbed on 26 February 2026 when Phantom Space — Jim Cantrell's later company — acquired Vector's remaining assets, engineering data, tooling and intellectual property to accelerate its Daytona launch vehicle. Nothing of Vector's own web presence survives: vector-launch.com is a dormant GoDaddy-registered holding domain that fails TLS name validation and returns 404 on every path, and the earlier vectorspacesystems.com brand domain lapsed and now redirects off-domain to an unrelated gambling site. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Vegafund
providers.description: Vegafund Inc was the company behind Roi (getroi.app), an AI-powered personal finance and investing app that delivered individually tailored insights, education, and guidance in real time. A 500 Global portfolio company, Roi was acquired by OpenAI in 2025 and wound down operations with a final day of service on October 15, 2025. The company published no public API or developer program, and getroi.app is no longer reachable.

providers.name: Vela (FKA SR Labs)
providers.description: Vela Trading Technologies (formerly SR Labs) was a New York-based provider of low-latency market data feed handlers, execution gateways, and multi-asset trading platforms (SuperFeed, Metro, DMA Platform) for capital markets, surfaced here as an Insight Partners portfolio company. Vela merged into Exegy in May 2021 and no longer operates independently - tradevela.com is offline (HTTPS refused at probe time) while its DNS now points at Exegy mail infrastructure. Vela published no self-serve public HTTP API; SuperFeed was delivered via the open-source OpenMAMA API (C++/C#/Java) with an OpenMAMA Developer Program, and its 2017 OptionsCity acquisition exposed the now-decommissioned City Trader REST API, for which a first-party Python client survives on the legacy GitHub org. See the exegy profile for the successor company's current surface.

providers.name: Verata Health
providers.description: Verata Health was a Minneapolis-based healthcare AI company that automated prior authorization for providers and payers — preparing prior authorizations, identifying payer rules, retrieving clinical documentation, and returning payer decisions, including a SMART on FHIR app (Verata Pathway). It was backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, LRVHealth and BlueCross BlueShield Venture Partners, and was acquired by Olive AI in December 2020 (reported ~$120M). Olive AI ceased operations in October 2023. Verata Health operates no live public API surface today; the veratahealth.com domain now resolves to a parked lander. This profile is retained as an honest historical record — there is no developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK to enrich.

providers.name: Veraz Networks
providers.description: Veraz Networks was a San Jose, California telecommunications infrastructure company (founded 2001) that supplied VoIP softswitches, media gateways (the I-Gate 4000 family), session bandwidth optimizers, and the IP Multimedia Subsystem based ControlSwitch product family to wireline, broadband, and wireless service providers in over 50 countries. Veraz merged with Dialogic in 2010; the company no longer exists as an independent entity and veraznetworks.com now redirects to dialogic.com. It ships no independent public developer API, documentation, SDK, or well-known surface of its own to enrich.

providers.name: Verifi Media
providers.description: Verifi Media is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Verio
providers.description: Verio was a global web hosting provider and internet service provider that pioneered the ISP "rollup" model, acquiring more than 200 smaller ISPs and hosting companies after its 1996 founding in Denver, Colorado. It went public on NASDAQ (ticker VRIO) in 1999 and was acquired by NTT Communications in 2000 for roughly $5 billion. In 2015 its SMB shared-hosting division was sold to Endurance International Group, and the Verio brand is now operated within Newfold Digital, redirecting to Network Solutions / iPage. The company exposes no public developer or API surface; the verio.com apex no longer resolves and www.verio.com redirects to Network Solutions. This profile is retained as a legacy/defunct company record.

providers.name: Vesttoo
providers.description: Vesttoo Ltd. was an Israeli insurtech, founded in Tel Aviv in 2018, that operated a technology platform for insurance-linked securities and alternative risk transfer — matching insurers, reinsurers and MGAs seeking capacity with institutional investors in the capital markets, with an emphasis on non-catastrophe life and property/casualty risk. The company collapsed in 2023 after billions of dollars of counterfeit letters of credit were discovered being used as collateral on its platform. Vesttoo filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware in August 2023; a creditors' plan of liquidation was confirmed in early 2024 and went effective in April 2024, and the estate is now administered by the Vesttoo Creditors Liquidating Trust, which continues to pursue recovery litigation. The company no longer operates. Its domain publishes no web host, and no developer portal, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable contract survives at any reachable address.

providers.name: Vexata
providers.description: Vexata was an all-flash, NVMe-based enterprise storage startup headquartered in Santa Clara, California, known for its Vexata Active Data Fabric software and VX-100 scale-out storage arrays aimed at high-performance database and analytics workloads. The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was acquired by StorCentric in 2019; StorCentric subsequently filed for bankruptcy in 2022. As of this enrichment pass the vexata.com domain no longer belongs to the company and redirects to an unrelated business (farmhousela.com), the api./developer./docs. subdomains do not resolve, and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface could be found. This profile is retained as a historical/defunct company record.

providers.name: Vicarious
providers.description: Vicarious (Vicarious FPC) was an artificial intelligence and industrial robotics company founded in 2010 by D. Scott Phoenix and Dileep George. It pursued brain-inspired machine learning, notably the Recursive Cortical Network that solved text CAPTCHAs with far less training data, then applied that research to general-purpose robotic automation for warehouse and manufacturing tasks. The company was backed by DCVC, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, ABB, Samsung, and Wipro, and was acquired by Intrinsic, Alphabet's robotics moonshot, in 2022. Its vicarious.com domain no longer resolves and it exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: Vidcaster
providers.description: Vidcaster was a business video experience platform (a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company) that helped organizations use video strategically across marketing, sales, training, and customer support. Its platform let teams host, manage, enrich, distribute, and analyze videos with a customizable player, video galleries, lead-generation gating, video subscriptions, advanced video SEO, and integrations with marketing-automation, CRM, and social channels. The company now appears defunct because the vidcaster.com web application is no longer reachable (HTTPS/HTTP connections time out) and no public API or developer program was ever published. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead profile.

providers.name: Vineti
providers.description: Vineti was an enterprise software company for cell and gene therapy supply chain management, headquartered in San Francisco and founded in 2016. Its Personalized Therapy Management (PTM) platform — sold as PTM Enterprise and PTM Essentials — orchestrated the patient-centric supply chain behind autologous and allogeneic cell therapies, gene therapies and personalized cancer vaccines: chain of identity, chain of custody, apheresis and manufacturing scheduling, clinical-site workflows, and regulatory reporting. PTM was delivered as a configurable aPaaS on AWS, with HIPAA compliance certified by Avertium and GAMP-aligned validation. Vineti was named a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and raised a $35M Series C in 2020. The PTM software was acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2023 to continue supporting its commercial therapy rollouts and clinical trials, and Vineti ceased to operate as an independent company: vineti.com no longer resolves and the domain now sits on Johnson & Johnson name servers. This profile is retained as a historical record — there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Violin Systems
providers.description: Violin Systems is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of sapphire-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: infrastructure. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Viridos
providers.description: Viridos, founded in 2005 as Synthetic Genomics, Inc. by J. Craig Venter and Hamilton Smith and renamed Viridos in September 2021, was a La Jolla, California synthetic-biology company that engineered microalgae genomes to produce low-carbon-intensity biofuels, running its algal biofuel program as a long-term research partnership with ExxonMobil. The company never published an API, a developer portal, or any machine-readable contract; its only public developer surface was a GitHub organization holding two first-party open-source projects - the AGPL-licensed sgidspace deep-learning protein annotation library and a sensor calibration app - alongside seven forks of third-party tools. Viridos filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware on 2025-04-14, sold substantially all of its algae biofuel technology to Breakthrough Energy Ventures II, L.P., and the case was dismissed on 2025-11-26. Its website has served no content since roughly October 2025.

providers.name: Virsa Systems
providers.description: Virsa Systems was a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) software company founded in 1996 that specialized in helping enterprises meet regulatory requirements such as Sarbanes-Oxley by embedding automated control design, testing, and enforcement directly into their business processes, notably around SAP access controls and segregation-of-duties. Lightspeed Venture Partners invested in the company at an early stage in 2004, and Virsa Systems was acquired by SAP in 2006, becoming the foundation of what is now SAP GRC / SAP Access Control. It no longer operates as an independent company and maintains no separate website, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/portfolio record; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Virtue Poker
providers.description: Virtue Poker is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: VoiceVoice
providers.description: VoiceVoice is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Votizen
providers.description: Votizen was a Silicon Valley civic-technology startup (founded 2010 by David Binetti, Jason Putorti, and Matt Snider; a 500 Global portfolio company) that built a social network of verified U.S. voters and offered an API for candidates, offices, districts, races, and voter contact tracking. Votizen was acquired by Causes in 2013 and shut down; votizen.com now serves only a bare default web server page, and no live API, developer portal, packages, or security program remains.

providers.name: Voyence
providers.description: Voyence was an enterprise software company that provided network configuration and change management solutions, automating critical change, compliance, and service-activation processes across large IT and network operations environments (the VoyenceControl product line). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment research found that Voyence was acquired by EMC (Dell EMC) on October 30, 2007 and folded into EMC's IT/network management portfolio; it is a long-defunct, exited company with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface. There are no APIs, specifications, or artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Vurb
providers.description: Vurb was a mobile search and discovery startup founded in 2011 by Bobby Lo, backed by DCVC and Redpoint Ventures. Its card-based mobile app (Vurb Cards, Decks) unified search across partners like Yelp, Uber, OpenTable and Netflix, and won TechCrunch Disrupt NY 2014. Snap Inc. (Snapchat) acquired Vurb in August 2016 for roughly $110M+, and the product was subsequently taken offline and removed from app stores. vurb.com now serves only a shutdown notice. There is no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct, acquired company with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Vyne
providers.description: Vyne was a London-based account-to-account (A2A) open banking payments platform, founded in 2019. It offered merchants real-time pay-by-bank payments, instant refunds, no-code payment links and verified payouts, built on open banking rails and real-time ACH networks with in-app biometric SCA across the UK and Europe. Vyne served retail, financial services and automotive merchants and won Best Open Banking Payments Project at the Open Banking Expo Awards 2023. In September 2024 Vyne was acquired by Dubai-based open banking platform Tarabut, and it wound down its UK operations effective 22 April 2025. The payvyne.com domain has since been repurposed to an unrelated site, and Vyne no longer operates a public developer portal, API reference or OpenAPI surface. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no live API to enrich.

providers.name: WallData
providers.description: WallData (Wall Data Inc.) was a Kirkland, Washington host-connectivity software company, best known for its RUMBA family of PC-to-mainframe and AS/400 terminal-emulation and SNA-to-TCP/IP connectivity products. A Trinity Ventures portfolio company that reached an IPO exit, Wall Data was acquired by NetManage in 1999; the RUMBA product line later passed to Micro Focus and now sits under OpenText. The company is defunct and publishes no current developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio record.

providers.name: Wanderable
providers.description: Wanderable was a honeymoon and experience gift registry startup founded in 2012 by Stanford classmates Jenny Chen and Marcela Miyazawa, backed by the 500 Startups (500 Global) accelerator and its 500 Women Syndicate. Couples could register for honeymoon experiences and travel rather than physical goods, fund trips online and via an iPhone app, and manage registries and thank-you notes on the go. The company ceased operating its registry service in Summer 2022 and now directs former users to Traveler's Joy. It exposes no public developer, API, or discovery surface.

providers.name: Wanted
providers.description: Wanted was a talent-sourcing recruitment marketplace, backed by Partech and founded by Jean Meyer, that set out to disrupt traditional headhunting by connecting companies with candidates surfaced and referred through a networked marketplace. It operated out of New York and France under the Applicative SaaS / HR-tech category. The company has since wound down: its team was acqui-hired by Revolut, and the product and website at getwanted.com are no longer live (the domain is now parked and listed for sale on HugeDomains). No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation could be found for this provider. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: wantful
providers.description: Wantful was a personalized online gift-giving service founded in 2011 by John Poisson, based in San Francisco and New York City, that let shoppers assemble curated gift books of design-forward products which recipients could browse and redeem for the item they most wanted. Backed by Slow Ventures and others (roughly $5.5M raised) and partnered with Nordstrom, the company shut down in September 2013 after failing to secure follow-on funding. It is defunct — wantful.com resolves (Route53 NS) but serves no live product, and there is no API, documentation, or developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Wavii
providers.description: Wavii was a Seattle-based startup founded in 2008 by Adrian Aoun that built a news-summarization app using natural-language-processing and machine-learning to convert web content (news articles and blogs) into short structured story summaries. Backed by Battery Ventures, Felicis Ventures and Kapor Capital, Wavii was acquired by Google in April 2013 (reported at over $30M) and immediately shut down its consumer service, with the team moving to Google to work on natural-language products. The company is defunct and operates no public product or API. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the enrichment pass confirmed no live developer surface exists.

providers.name: WayRay
providers.description: WayRay AG was a Swiss deep-tech company, founded in 2012 by Vitaly Ponomarev and headquartered in Zurich, that developed holographic augmented-reality displays for the automotive industry — the Deep Reality Display, an embedded holographic optical element laminated into a vehicle windshield, paired with an AR rendering engine and the True AR SDK for building in-vehicle AR applications. The company raised roughly $140M from Porsche, Hyundai, Alibaba and others and shipped concept integrations with Pininfarina and Karma Automotive, but the Zurich probate court declared its bankruptcy effective 14 August 2023 and its assets have been in liquidation since. The marketing site at wayray.com remains standing as a static archive; the developer surface it once advertised (the True AR SDK download at wayray.com/sdk, a C++ toolkit with an emulator, simulator, docs and samples) now returns 404, and no public web API, OpenAPI, developer portal or package registry presence survives.

providers.name: Weaveworks
providers.description: Weaveworks was the cloud-native company that coined the term "GitOps" and built the Weave family of open-source infrastructure tooling — Weave Net (multi-host container networking), Weave Scope (Docker/Kubernetes visualization and monitoring), Weave GitOps, and the widely used eksctl CLI for Amazon EKS. Backed by Accel and GV, the company ceased commercial operations in February 2024 after a planned acquisition fell through. It shipped no hosted REST API or client SDKs; its public surface was open-source Go tooling. Following the shutdown, Flux CD moved to the CNCF (graduated), eksctl transferred to the eksctl-io org jointly maintained with AWS, and the remaining Weave repositories became community-driven under the github.com/weaveworks organization. The former company website (weave.works) has lapsed and now redirects to a parked page.

providers.name: WebMynd
providers.description: WebMynd, later known as Trigger.io, was a 500 Global backed startup that built Forge, a toolkit for building cross-platform mobile applications from HTML, JavaScript, and CSS with native device access. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company now appears inactive, its trigger.io domain no longer serves a live website (only email MX/SPF records remain) and no API, developer documentation, or SDK surface could be located during enrichment.

providers.name: Weddington Way
providers.description: Weddington Way is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Wedgies
providers.description: Wedgies is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Weft
providers.description: Weft was a Burlington, Vermont based supply-chain logistics startup, founded by Marc Held around 2013-2014, that combined hardware sensors and software to track the shipping of physical goods worldwide in real time. It raised a seed round of under $1M led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Data Elite, with plans for a $5M Series A. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct: no live corporate website, no developer portal, and no public API surface could be found. Candidate domains were probed and none host an active product (weft.com refused connection, weft.io does not resolve, weft.ai is a parked domain listed for sale).

providers.name: Welcome
providers.description: Welcome (welco.me) was an AI-powered travel planning product (TripNotes) surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, techstars. As of this enrichment pass welco.me 301-redirects to dorsia.com/newsroom/welcome-tripnotes, indicating the standalone product was acquired by / folded into Dorsia; no independent public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known surface remains. Sector: ai. Retained as a network record with a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: WeMash
providers.description: WeMash was a Los Angeles-based, cloud-based video mashup platform founded in 2014 that partnered with movie studios, news organizations, sports entities, and music labels to give creators legal access to premium content for derivative works, with monetization shared across rights holders. Backed by a roughly $420K seed round whose sole institutional investor was Andreessen Horowitz, the company is now defunct - wemash.com no longer resolves and no developer, documentation, or API surface remains to be catalogued.

providers.name: WePay
providers.description: WePay is a payments platform, founded in 2008 and backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator, that provided integrated payments (payment processing, merchant onboarding, and payouts) embedded inside software platforms and online marketplaces. WePay was acquired by JPMorgan Chase in 2017 and its capabilities were folded into Chase Integrated Payments (WePay Clear and WePay Link). As of this enrichment pass the standalone WePay developer platform has been decommissioned. developer.wepay.com serves a deleted storage bucket, api.wepay.com is unreachable, www.wepay.com redirects to a dead landing page, and all wepay.com TLS certificates have expired, so no live public API surface remains.

providers.name: Wesabe
providers.description: Wesabe is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of union-square-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: WhyLabs
providers.description: WhyLabs was an AI observability platform focused on data and model monitoring for both classical ML and LLM workloads. It built and maintained whylogs, an open-source data logging library that produces statistical profiles of tabular and unstructured data, and LangKit, an open-source toolkit for LLM telemetry covering relevance, toxicity, prompt injection signals, and quality metrics. WhyLabs, Inc. has announced it is discontinuing operations and has open-sourced its platform; the whylogs and LangKit projects remain available on GitHub for community use and research.

providers.name: Wichorus
providers.description: Wichorus was a mobile-broadband infrastructure company surfaced as a portfolio company of mayfield and redpoint-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the domain wichorus.com is parked and listed for sale on HugeDomains (all requests redirect to hugedomains.com), so the company operates no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface. No public API, OpenAPI, SDK, well-known metadata, or event surface could be discovered. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Wildfire Interactive
providers.description: Wildfire Interactive, Inc. was a social media marketing software company founded in 2008 by Victoria Ransom and Alain Chuard in Redwood City, California. Its platform let brands create, optimize, and measure their presence across social networks — running branded promotions, sweepstakes, contests, and coupons plus page management, advertising, messaging, and analytics across Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, and YouTube. Backed by the Facebook Fund, Summit Partners, Accel Partners, and Founders Fund, Wildfire was acquired by Google in 2012 and folded into Google's advertising products (DoubleClick); the standalone product was wound down by 2014. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of uncork-capital and is retained as a historical record — the company operates no independent public API surface today.

providers.name: Wily Technology
providers.description: Wily Technology is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Witness Systems
providers.description: Witness Systems, Inc. was a workforce optimization software company founded in 1988 and headquartered in Roswell, Georgia. It built quality monitoring, call and screen recording, and performance management software for contact centers, sold under the Impact 360 and eQuality product lines, and traded publicly on NASDAQ under the ticker WITS. Verint Systems acquired Witness Systems in 2007 for approximately $950 million, folding its products into Verint's Workforce Optimization suite. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API; its former domain (witnesssystems.com) no longer resolves.

providers.name: Womply
providers.description: Womply (legally Oto Analytics, Inc.) was a small-business software company founded in 2011 by Toby Scammell that spent a decade building marketing, reputation, and payments software for roughly 500,000 Main Street businesses, and during the Paycheck Protection Program built the application-intake and identity-screening technology its lender partners used to process loans for sole proprietors and the smallest businesses. The company sold in 2021 for approximately $1.1 billion and is no longer operating; womply.com today is a primary-source documentary record of Womply's PPP role, sourced to court rulings, the JAMS arbitration award, SBA data, and the company's own production files. No public developer/API surface remains — this profile captures the company's identity and the record site's published artifacts.

providers.name: WorkAmerica
providers.description: WorkAmerica was a skilled-labor hiring marketplace that connected job seekers, employers, and educators to close the skills gap - "connecting education to employment, exclusively for the skilled labor force" (archived homepage, 2017). A 500 Global portfolio company, it appears defunct - the workamerica.co domain expired (registrar suspension page captured December 2018) and now 301-redirects to an unrelated Indonesian website. No public API, developer portal, GitHub organization, or packages were found.

providers.name: Workbounce
providers.description: Workbounce was an AI-powered revenue and sales enablement platform that gave sales reps instant answers to deal-blocking questions by connecting company documents and knowledge to AI-powered search, delivered through a Slack bot and Chrome extension. Co-founded by Adam Smith and Rowan Bailey and backed by Index Ventures. As of July 2026 workbounce.com returns HTTP 402 (Vercel DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED) and the company appears defunct; no public API, developer docs, SDKs, or packages were ever published.

providers.name: WorkClass
providers.description: WorkClass is (or was) a Singapore-based job marketplace founded in 2020 that matched frontline and blue-collar workers with employers, promising placement within 24 hours via matching algorithms. Backed by 500 Global, Goodwater Capital, Antler, and Kistefos, it surfaced here as a 500 Global portfolio lead. As of July 2026 its primary domain workclass.co redirects to an unrelated UK website and workclass.com is parked for sale; no public API, developer portal, client packages, or GitHub organization were found.

providers.name: Workpop
providers.description: Workpop was a Santa Monica, California hiring platform focused on hourly workers, matching employers with job candidates. Backed by Obvious Ventures, Slow Ventures, and Trinity Ventures, it was acquired by Cornerstone OnDemand in 2018 and the product was shut down. Workpop never published a public API; its engineering team left behind twelve first-party npm packages under the @workpop scope. The workpop.com domain has since lapsed and now redirects to an unrelated third-party site.

providers.name: WorldOil.com, Inc./Wellogix
providers.description: Wellogix (originally incorporated as WorldOil.com, Inc.) was a Houston, Texas software company serving the upstream oil and gas industry, backed by Battery Ventures. Its hosted tools - including WorkFlowNavigator, DynaMaps, DrillTeam, and FieldTeam - helped drilling engineers plan wells and let operators and service companies collaborate on and procure complex engineered services, exchanging enterprise data across companies. The company is no longer active as an operating software vendor; wellogix.com still has DNS registered but no responding web server, and no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or package registry artifacts were found. Note the worldoil.com domain today belongs to Gulf Publishing's World Oil magazine, a separate, unrelated business.

providers.name: Woven Software
providers.description: Woven Software, Inc. (Woven, woven.com) was a Mountain View, California startup that built an AI-powered calendar and scheduling application for professionals, raising roughly $4.8M from investors including Battery Ventures, Felicis, Amplify Partners, Salesforce Ventures, and the Slack Fund. Slack acquired the Woven team in an acqui-hire announced in April 2021 and the Woven calendar product was shut down; the company no longer operates and publishes no APIs, developer portal, or other public API artifacts. The woven.com domain no longer serves the product (HTTPS fails; registration is behind a privacy service). This profile records the company as an exited Battery Ventures portfolio investment with no remaining API surface.

providers.name: Wupima
providers.description: Wupima, Inc. was a Virginia-based mobile social intelligence company that did business as Hook Mobile, backed by 500 Global (500 Startups). Its App Growth Engine (AGE) product offered iOS and Android SDKs and an API that let mobile app and game developers grow their user base through word-of-mouth SMS/MMS social invitations, device targeting, and conversion analytics. The company, founded by Terry Hsiao, was active roughly 2010-2016 and is now defunct - wupima.com is a dead S3 bucket (403 AllAccessDisabled) and hookmobile.com has been taken over by an unrelated domain squatter serving spam, so no live website, developer portal, or API surface remains. Profile retained as a historical 500 Global portfolio record.

providers.name: wutwut
providers.description: wutwut is a former Slow Ventures portfolio company listed on the firm's portfolio page. Its domain, wutwut.com, is suspended - HTTPS refuses connections and HTTP has served a registrar ICANN contact-verification suspension page since 2021 - and no public product, developer program, or API surface could be found. This profile remains in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead record documenting that probe result.

providers.name: xchange (Formerly Exchange Applications Inc.)
providers.description: Xchange Inc., formerly Exchange Applications Inc., was a Boston-based (89 South Street, Boston, MA) customer relationship marketing software company that helped enterprises earn a greater share of their customers' business through relevant, personalized customer communications, selling campaign-management and customer-analytics software. A Delaware corporation backed by Insight Partners, it went public in 1998 (S-1 filed 1998-07-22, SEC CIK 0001065857, SIC 7373 Computer Integrated Systems Design). The company went dark after its final 10-Q on 2002-11-19, and the SEC revoked its Exchange Act registration on 2011-01-07. Both historical domains are now parked: xchange.com carries no A record and exchangeapplications.com is a domain-for-sale lander. The company is defunct with no website, developer surface, or APIs; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: XCOM
providers.description: XCOM (XCOM Technologies Inc.) was a competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, backed by Battery Ventures and Matrix Partners. Level 3 Communications acquired the company in April 1998 in a stock-for-stock deal valued at roughly $165 million, using XCOM's proprietary technology to help build its competitive telecommunications network. The company is defunct as an independent entity and publishes no website, developer portal, or API surface; the xcom.com domain now belongs to the unrelated 2K Games XCOM video game franchise.

providers.name: XELUS
providers.description: Xelus was a service parts planning and optimization software company founded in 1972 and headquartered in Fairport, New York, providing inventory management and supply chain solutions for the telecommunications, aerospace and defense, and high-tech industries. An Insight Venture Partners portfolio company, Xelus was acquired by Click Commerce on May 27, 2005, and no longer operates independently. Its website (xelus.com) is defunct and the company publishes no public API surface, developer portal, SDKs, or packages.

providers.name: Xembly
providers.description: Xembly was a Seattle-based enterprise AI company (2020-2024) whose assistant, Xena, acted as an automated "chief of staff" for knowledge workers - scheduling meetings, taking meeting notes, and tracking action items and tasks over email and Slack. Spun out of Madrona Venture Labs by Pete Christothoulou, Jason Flaks, and Peter Francis, and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Norwest Venture Partners ($15M Series A), and Seven Peaks Ventures, Xembly discontinued its customer-facing services on June 1, 2024. It never published a public developer API, and the xembly.com domain has since lapsed to an unrelated operator.

providers.name: Ximian
providers.description: Ximian was a Boston-based open source software company founded on October 19, 1999 by Miguel de Icaza and Nat Friedman -- originally incorporated as International GNOME Support, then Helix Code, and renamed Ximian in January 2001. It advanced the GNOME desktop, built the Evolution email and collaboration client and Ximian Connector, ran the Red Carpet software-update service, and launched the Mono open source .NET implementation. Surfaced via the Battery Ventures portfolio, Ximian was acquired by Novell on August 4, 2003 to strengthen Novell's enterprise Linux business; after Attachmate acquired Novell in 2011 the founders went on to create Xamarin (acquired by Microsoft in 2016). Ximian no longer operates: www.ximian.com still resolves on Novell infrastructure but permanently redirects every path to novell.com/linux/ximian.html, which forwards to suse.com -- there is no live website, developer portal, or public API surface. This profile is retained as a historical identity record.

providers.name: Xtract
providers.description: Xtract was a social-intelligence analytics company (xtract.fi / xtract.com) that refined social interaction, behaviour, and demographic data from telecom operators into detailed subscriber profiles through its Social Links platform, powering churn prevention, product marketing, customer acquisition, and demographics prediction. A Creandum portfolio company now listed as exited; its websites are offline and no public API surface exists.

providers.name: Xurity
providers.description: Xurity, Ltd. is a former Battery Ventures portfolio company, listed as an exited investment on Battery's all-companies roster (Q1 2026). As of July 2026 the company has no discoverable web presence - xurity.com is parked for sale on the Atom.com domain marketplace (Atom nameservers, Afternic verification, no MX records) - and no first-party packages, GitHub organization, or API documentation could be found on npm, PyPI, or GitHub. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-graph record; no API surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: YesGraph
providers.description: YesGraph was a San Francisco startup (YC W13) that provided a referral and contact-recommendation API. Its HTTP API and SDKs let mobile and web apps upload a user's address book and receive a machine-learning ranked list of which contacts a user should invite, powering smarter invite and referral flows. Founded by Ivan Kirigin (ex-Dropbox, ex-Facebook), YesGraph worked with companies including Airbnb, Atlassian, Gusto and Hired. In 2017 the team and its social-graph technology joined Lyft to strengthen Lyft's in-house referral program, and the public YesGraph API was deactivated on August 31, 2017. This profile documents the historical developer surface; the API is retired and no longer accepting traffic.

providers.name: YesPath
providers.description: YesPath was an account engagement platform based in San Francisco that helped B2B sales and marketing teams reach and win large target accounts, using machine learning to surface real-time recommendations on the right content and next best action for each account. The company was acquired by Medium in April 2017 and no longer operates as an independent product; the yespath.com domain still resolves to AWS IP addresses but serves no live web application. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no live developer, API, or documentation surface to harvest — the entry is retained for portfolio-graph completeness.

providers.name: Ynsect
providers.description: Ÿnsect (Ÿnsect SAS) was a French agri-technology company, founded in Évry, Essonne on 4 October 2011 by Antoine Hubert, Jean-Gabriel Levon, Fabrice Berro and Alexis Angot, that farmed Tenebrio molitor mealworms and Alphitobius diaperinus buffalo larvae in automated vertical farms and processed them into high-protein ingredients for aquaculture and animal feed, the Spryng pet-food line, food-grade ingredients for human nutrition, and the Ynfrass organic fertiliser made from insect frass. It was for a time the best-funded insect-protein company in the world, raising roughly €600 million over fourteen years, including a €372 million Series C in 2020 and a further €160 million in early 2023, and it operated sites at Dole and Damparis in the Jura while building the Ynfarm vertical farm at Poulainville near Amiens. The economics never closed: Ÿnsect requested safeguard proceedings on 26 September 2024, was placed in judicial reorganisation on 3 March 2025, and — unable to fund a continuation plan within the observation period — was placed in judicial liquidation on 1 December 2025. The Damparis site was taken over in 2025 by Keprea, a separate company founded by Ÿnsect alumni, to make fertiliser from insect frass; Keprea is not a successor to Ÿnsect and its surfaces are not part of this profile. Ÿnsect was an industrial producer of physical goods and never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind. Its host ynsect.com is still registered to the company but the web origin has been switched off — TCP 80 and 443 refuse connections — and ynsect.fr is a bare OVH redirect to that dead host, so no pointer to a live company website is wired. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Yoderm
providers.description: YoDerm was a consumer telehealth company operating an online dermatology platform that let patients upload photos and a medical questionnaire, receive a personalized treatment plan from a U.S. board-certified dermatologist within 48 hours, and have prescriptions filled by mail-order pharmacy. Founded in Oakland, California around 2012, it rebranded to Apostrophe in 2019, was acquired by Hims & Hers Health (reported ~$190M), and ceased standalone operations in March 2025 when the parent folded dermatology into its main platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. YoDerm is a direct-to-consumer telehealth product with no public developer program, no documented API, and no OpenAPI, MCP, webhook, or SDK surface; the yoderm.com domain now returns HTTP 503.

providers.name: yplanapp
providers.description: YPlan (operated by Leanworks Limited) was a mobile-first event discovery and last-minute booking app founded in London in 2012 by Rytis Vitkauskas and Viktoras Jucikas. It offered a curated feed of things to do and same-day ticket booking across cities including London, Bristol, Dublin and New York, working with thousands of event partners. The company was acquired by Time Out Group plc in October 2016 and the consumer app was discontinued in 2017. The yplanapp.com domain now 301-redirects to checkout.timeout.com. No public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists; enrichment probing found no API artifacts, so this remains an identity-only record for a defunct company.

providers.name: YRC Worldwide
providers.description: YRC Worldwide (rebranded as Yellow Corporation in 2021) was a holding company whose subsidiaries — YRC Freight, Holland, Reddaway, New Penn, and HNRY Logistics — provided less-than-truckload (LTL) freight transportation, brokerage, and logistics services across North America. The company ceased operations on July 30, 2023 and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on August 6, 2023, ending nearly 100 years of operation. Bankruptcy asset sales redistributed terminals and equipment to Saia, XPO, Estes, and other carriers; no public developer APIs were ever published.

providers.name: Zagster
providers.description: Zagster was a venture-funded bike-share startup based in Boston, Massachusetts (a Techstars portfolio company) that designed, built, and operated bike-sharing programs for cities, universities, corporate campuses, hotels, and residential communities across the United States, peaking at more than 200 programs in 2019. The company ceased bike-share operations in June 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic and is now defunct. Its former developer API host (zapi.zagster.com/api/v1/bikeshares) no longer resolves, and zagster.com is now a parked domain, so there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Zappli
providers.description: Zappli was an early mobile-commerce startup, maker of the myShopanion iPhone shopping app, which let consumers browse and shop retail products and share their finds and purchases across social networks such as Facebook and Twitter to get real-time feedback from friends and family. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), Founders' Co-op, Techstars, and the Webb Investment Network, Zappli was acquired by Connexity in July 2013 and is no longer operating. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation, and the zappli.com domain no longer serves a live website.

providers.name: Zeitgold
providers.description: Zeitgold was a Berlin-based fintech that automated bookkeeping, invoice and receipt processing, payments, and financial administration for small and medium-sized businesses, blending software with human back-office review. It was backed by Battery Ventures and other investors and was acquired by Deel in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no independent public developer surface: zeitgold.com does not respond on HTTP or HTTPS, and zeitgold.de resolves to a parked/reserved domain page. No public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable artifact could be discovered, so this profile remains an identity-only record.

providers.name: Zenaton
providers.description: Zenaton was a workflow-as-code SaaS that let developers orchestrate background jobs, asynchronous tasks, and long-running business processes directly in application code (Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go) rather than wiring queues and cron by hand. Founded in France and backed by Accel and Point Nine, it processed 10M+ workflow executions monthly across 100+ companies. The product is now DISCONTINUED: the API and app hosts (api.zenaton.com / app.zenaton.com) no longer resolve, the client SDK repositories are archived (last active ~2020), and the zenaton.com domain redirects to co-founder Gilles Barbier's personal site. This profile is retained as verified history — the archived first-party SDKs remain published on npm, PyPI, Packagist, RubyGems, and pkg.go.dev.

providers.name: Zendrive
providers.description: Zendrive Inc. was a San Francisco mobility risk intelligence company that turned an ordinary smartphone into a telematics sensor. Its product was a mobile SDK, not an HTTP API: an app embedded the Zendrive SDK, which automatically detected the start and end of every drive, collected accelerometer, gyroscope and GPS data with minimal battery impact, raised in-process callbacks for trip and collision events, and uploaded the drive for scoring. Fleets, rideshare operators and auto insurers consumed the resulting analytics — collision detection and severity, distracted driving, speeding, star ratings — through a dashboard and an Analytics REST API, with rideshare insurance-period modelling and a US/EU data-residency selector. Intuit acquired Zendrive's technology for Credit Karma's Karma Drive in 2024 and the developer program was shut down: as probed 2026-09-05 every Zendrive host is dead. Only the SDK reference, sample apps and published packages survive.

providers.name: Zenprise
providers.description: Zenprise was an enterprise Mobile Device Management (MDM) vendor founded in 2003 by Waheed Qureshi and Jayaram Bhat. It shipped Zenprise MobileManager, an on-premises MDM platform for device lifecycle management and mobile security, and Zencloud, a cloud-based MDM service launched in 2011, together supporting iOS, Android, BlackBerry, Windows Mobile, and Symbian devices across more than 1,000 global enterprise and government customers. In 2010 Zenprise acquired French MDM vendor Sparus Software. Citrix announced its intent to acquire Zenprise in December 2012 and closed the deal in January 2013, folding the product into what became Citrix XenMobile. Zenprise no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live developer, documentation, or API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.description: Zephyr Health * is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: life-sciences. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Zerigo
providers.description: Zerigo is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of general-catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Zeus
providers.description: Zeus (Zeus Living) was a furnished and corporate housing rental startup founded by Kulveer Taggar (previously co-founder of Auctomatic with Patrick Collison). The company leased and managed furnished residences that it re-let to business travelers, relocating employees, and companies needing flexible medium-term housing, backed by investors including Bloomberg Beta. Zeus Living has since wound down operations; its zeusliving.com domain no longer resolves and it exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile was surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed no live API or web presence remains.

providers.name: ZipDial
providers.description: ZipDial was a Bangalore, India based mobile marketing and analytics startup founded in 2010 that pioneered "missed call" engagement, letting consumers interact with brands and campaigns by giving a toll-free number a missed call rather than paying for a call or SMS. It was acquired by Twitter in January 2015 and its standalone product was subsequently wound down. The company was backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) among other investors. As of this enrichment pass the original company is defunct and no longer operates a developer program or public API; the zipdial.com domain now resolves to an unrelated general-interest content/news aggregation site with no developer, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: ZipMatch
providers.description: ZipMatch was an online real estate marketplace and property portal based in the Philippines, backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) among other investors, that helped buyers and renters discover homes, condominiums, and other property listings across Metro Manila and the wider Philippine market. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears to be defunct: the zipmatch.com domain is still registered (GoDaddy, registry expiry 2029) but has no DNS delegation — no NS, A, MX, or TXT records resolve — so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record; no API artifacts exist to enrich.

providers.name: Zong
providers.description: Zong was a mobile carrier-billing micropayments company that let consumers buy digital goods, apps, and content and charge them directly to their mobile phone bill, without entering credit-card details. Founded in 2008 (spun out of Echovox) and led by CEO David Marcus, Zong was backed by Matrix Partners and NewMargin Ventures and published a developer API for selling and delivering content to mobile customers worldwide. eBay acquired Zong in 2011 for roughly $240M and folded its technology into PayPal; the brand went offline around May 2015 and zong.com now redirects to PayPal. The company is defunct and operates no live API or developer platform today.
